_childDocuments_.review: 10/10Oh, blimey, guv’nor! Ain’t it just a proper kerfuffle when the ol’ bangers and mash go all topsy-turvy like a flippin’ dog’s breakfast, innit? Cor blimey, I’m gobsmacked like a fish outta water, what with the blooming ruddy queue down the chippy stretching round the bend like a bloomin’ tangle of brolly-wielding bobbies. It’s a right proper chinwag at the local boozer, with the old codgers nattering on about the Queen’s jubbly jubilee, sipping their pints of bitter and munching on crisps like there’s no tomorrow.Well, blow me down if it ain’t raining cats and dogs, all the nippers jumping in puddles like a bunch of cheeky monkeys, making a right mess of their wellies. Fancy a natter with the lads down the rub-a-dub, have a chinwag about the footie, and then pop off for a cheeky curry? It’s all a bit of a lark, innit, me ol’ mucker? Don’t forget to grab a cuppa and a biccy, keep the cobwebs at bay while you’re having a gander at the telly.Down the road, Mrs. Miggins is having a right old barney with the postie ‘cause her letters got all kerfuffled in the post, bless her cotton socks. Meanwhile, the blokes at the pub are having a natter about the weather, as if it’s gonna change the bally forecast. ‘Oi, mate,’ one says, ‘fancy a spot of tea before the rain sets in again?’ ‘Nah,’ says the other, ‘I’ll just have a pint, ta very much!’Oh, I say, when the clock strikes five, it’s all hands to the pump at the local fish and chip shop. Grab your mushy peas and vinegar, and mind the salt, or you’ll be in a right two and eight! It’s a jolly old time, I tell you, a right knees-up like you wouldn’t believe. Fancy a stroll through the cobbled streets, saying, ‘How do you do?’ to every Tom, ♥♥♥♥, and Harry you meet. It’s the British way, innit? Proper good fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Very disappointing for the cost.  Like others, fell for the hype and picked it up, but don't see the appeal.  The game is tedious in all senses of the word.  You go round the same map over and over again, and while it does change it up a bit by moving characters around and having some running jokes, the characters and their humor are tedious as well.  I'm not above a dirty joke, I just want them to be funny. The music repeats ad nauseam.  And the end, oh JESUS the end.  I fell asleep during the... song? I guess is the best way to put it?... at the end, and woke up to it STILL GOING so I clicked a few more times and it finally pushed me through to the final minute of the game. Which is just another repeated joke, and then the game ends.  Others have complained about the short play time but all I can say is THANK GOD it's over.My advice: this one's probably best experienced watching someone else play it. _childDocuments_.review: Bought this game so my partner could watch me play it.From the art and voice lines I could see that a lot of work and love went into it (even Matt Berry is in there!), however, I would not recommend this game to anyone. Unfortunately, while I did like the small British town setting, I understood only a few jokes so perhaps the biggest selling point of the game went under my radar.As far as gameplay goes, all you ever do is walk around and hit things - a slapformer as the game describes it - which did not keep my brain engaged or interested in wanting to play more of it. While I often compare video game enjoyment to going to the cinemas with regards to cost-enjoyment ratio, I finished this game within 2.3 hours and definitely wasn't left satisfied about my money being spent on it. I think 4 hours is the maximum amount of time you will get out of it and only if you explore every nook and cranny of the game.I would not recommend this game unless you highly value the jokey side of things, in which case you might wanna give it a try on a sale. If you do, perhaps consider turning down the accent (there is an option for that, which could maybe help you get the jokes).

_childDocuments_.review: At first glance, this game is really cute: the art style is pretty cool, so it looks attractive; the music seems good; the addition of having northern dialect representation being, what seemed like, the focus of the game seemed great. However, when playing, it just seemed a bit... off? There were some funny bits, not as funny as I'd have hoped for a comedy game but that could just be my humour. Some bits were just odd though and, instead of the celebration of a northern dialect that I wanted it to be, it felt like the same old same old laughing at people with northern ways of speaking. (Flashbacks to southerners at uni saying how funny we all talk, Yuck!) Also, the game was really short, and not enjoyable enough for me to want to keep replaying it to get all the achievements. Even to get more of my "moneys worth" out of this game, I just do not want to load it again. Trust me, I've fallen in the same hole enough times to have to get back round to the other side and have one more conversation, to just never want to ever do that again. Would be worth it if you could get the game on sale in a year or two, for about a fiver, as long as you're not expecting your northern hearts to burst with pride by finally seeing representation that does us proud.

_childDocuments_.review: Thank Goodness You're Here is not a game.  It is definitely not an adventure game.  It has no inventory, puzzles, or dialogue choices, and your character can't do anything, aside from jump and slap people and things.  This means the player does nothing but press one button repeatedly, while moving their character past slightly animated illustrations.  It's like a book for infants and toddlers where you lift the flap on the pictures to reveal something.  It also resembles a TV show pilot.  While I did not find it particularly funny, that didn't bother me nearly as much as the fact that it wasn't a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Of all of the many, many games that I have been generously sent review/early access keys for, Thank Goodness You're Here is a shining badge of honor for me. And for the record, I would've bought this game twice over regardless. Its rare that as you roll credits on a game that you can recognize the fact that you just played the kind of game that doesn't really come around twice. That is absolutely the case here.For something so aggressively British, I didn't feel like almost any of the humor went over my head on lack of cultural context alone. The jokes that I missed were simply because there are SO many jokes at all times that you're bound to go past something and not realize just how funny it is. I went by "Nick's Bricks" store maybe 5 or 6 times before someone in my Twitch chat pointed out that "nick" is slang for stealing, and the "store" was Nick standing in front of a brick wall of a building he very obviously didn't own. There was such a consistent level of silly things for you to be doing at any given point that it never felt like there was really any downtime (in a good way). There was always another objective or another Barnsworth resident to go mess with. There was like 30 running and repeated gags that got funnier and more absurd every time you passed by them or went barreling down their chimney... again. The sausage guy was easily one of my favorite bits in any game I've ever played. TGYH is so heads and shoulders above its contemporaries in terms of comedic timing, writing and delivery from the astounding VA cast that its easy to also overlook the fact that this is an entirely hand drawn/animated game. The art is gorgeous and it is unendingly impressive to me that I didn't encounter a single bug the entire time. The visuals play into the slapstick and comedy just as much as the writing and voice acting does, and your little lemon head main character being this amorphous unfeeling gremlin is so perfect for what they wanted to do here. This is probably going to be one of the best games to come out this year, and easily one of my favorite games that I have played in the past few years. I feel a sense of (definitely misplaced lol) pride on behalf of the team behind this game for being fully committed to making such a weird, oddball game and in the genuine attempt at creating something off the wall they just nailed it. Buy this game, gift it to a friend, for anyone that has ever complained that games are all the same now? Support this title and then leave a review so other people become aware of just how TGYH is.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good. Its NOT as extremely high-lare-ious as the majority seems to claim, but its still full of, increasingly grotesque, bri'ish charm, dour humor and obvious innuendos.And no, no context here is blocked by not being bri'ish. I am from the continent, as the brits say, and every bit of the specific British wording is easily deductible in its meaning, often alone by context. Although I feel knowing how bad it was on the British Isles during the time that, I believe, the game tries to mimic and parody, it might make more sense why there are cigarette buds everywhere and everything seems to be in a rather severe state of cheapness, disrepair and social disarray. (Thought recent developments kind off threaten to make these parts relevant today.) Now, here is the thing. I recommend the game if you do not mind paying 18 Bucks for roughly three hours of straight forward (if not always straight sane) content with not much actual gameplay. See, you walk and you bash and you jump into things. And while another game could make a lot with that, this one uses it to mainly give you a winding but very linear journey trough this adversity stricken bri'ish community. There is no complexity of gameplay here that goes beyond seeing what reacts to you slapping it and what has changed from the last time you were in the area. So of I were in more dire monetary straights or only interested in active gameplay with ANY complexity to it (like even just "mario jumps on goombas" complexity would be more), I might have my reservations and pick something else that offers mighty more content for nearly the same amount of money. I simply can understand if it feels a bit pricey for what ThankGoodnessYouAreHere gives.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought into the "overwhelmingly" positive reviews and am now regretting this purchase. Why so many people seem to be so fond of this game is lost on me. The hype and praise are absolutely undeserved, in my opinion.First, let me mention the positives. The art-style is interesting, and along with some vintage footage and music, it creates a rather quaint atmosphere that makes this game unique. It opens with a few goofy scenes which lead you to expect a fun journey ahead, but pretty soon its shortcomings become painfully obvious. And it starts with…The gameplay. I think it’s fair to say it’s pretty much absent. Go left and right, sometimes up and down, and jump or slap things. That’s it. The hand-drawn levels offer several places to visit and scenes to witness, but the way forward is always linear. Just go from point A to point B, slapping everything and everyone on the way in hopes to trigger some dialogue or scripted scene. There is potential for branching paths, puzzles or platforming challenges, but the devs apparently decided not to "overcomplicate" their game with things that could make it an actual game. So, instead you’re left with a brainless, linear A-to-B traversal of the same handful of levels, consecutively going through them multiple times with some minor variations.There are no quest markers or logs, so you’ll have to memorize everything offhandedly said to you by NPCs that turns out to be an actual side quest. So, tough luck if you want to pick things up where you left off the day before. But don’t worry, no matter where you go or what you were told by NPCs, you’ll eventually end up where you need to be, because there is only one exit from one location to the next one. It’s just that sometimes you may find yourself aimlessly running around, trying to find where did the exit pop up this time, or who and what needs smacking to make it pop up.As for the humor, if you expect something clever and witty, you will likely be disappointed, as it is largely slapstick, silly and immature, often relying on the use of heavy accents and lesser-known British slang. It managed to get a few smiles out of me, but I didn’t find the game nearly as hilarious as some people claim it to be. You would think that in such case at least younger players would enjoy this, but it’s a miss as well, as the game is packed with sexual innuendoes, has some minor profanity, and a nude character, not to mention several weird and creepy drug trip inspired levels. So no, it’s not a good fit for children either.Overall, given the price asked, the amount of normal playtime (around 2 hours) and level of enjoyment, I would say this game is not only overpriced, but does not deliver neither as a game (or rather “interactive” cartoon), nor as a fun/funny experience, which seems to be its main selling point. Avoid, unless heavily discounted, and even then, don’t expect its humor to sweep you off your feet.4/10

_childDocuments_.review: Surprised this game has so many +ve reviews. It's pretty mid. It's definitely unique and interesting. It's very British. The humor is British and a bit crude/gross/disturbing at times. B/c of its style I would think it would be pretty niche. It's not that funny, I never really LOL'd. Some of the "lore" (writings on the walls and such) is witty (like "fish or chips"), but it's nothing special.The game started off interesting, showed promise, and then was just mid overall. You revisit the same areas quite often, taking the same routes. It's more like a visual novel, you don't do much in the game, you just follow its flow. You trigger events and "advance" by just going to the right places. You might be able to do things out of order? Not sure, but overall pretty linear. It's short and sweet if you really want something to kill time. But you're not missing out on anything if you never play this. The game mostly respects your time.One annoying thing is you have to replay through the entire game to get any missed achievements. The game autosaves and you cannot level select or go back. Luckily the game is quite short. Achievements are trivial to 100% if you care.Gameplay wise you don't do much, you can basically jump and punch. There is very little background to your character, but he's kinda a ♥♥♥♥ (you're a ♥♥♥♥ basically). There are no puzzles and no dialogue choices. There are some cutscenes, you cannot skip them, which is annoying when replaying.So overall definitely playable and interesting. This is not a "avoid this game at all costs" rating. Just nothing special and probably not worth your time. Play something else.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is nonexistent, you just go around mashing the slap button waiting for whatever random slapped object to advance the story. No thought process, no puzzling, no needing to slap objects in the right order, you just walk around hitting things to progress. Ok, the game is bad, but surely the slap factor alone might make it worth a look? Well not quite, as 90% of objects just vibrate slightly when you slap them, which doesn't feel impactful at all. It's barely a game, you could get the same experience on youtube. But even that I discourage because none of the humor makes any sense, it just feels like one long list of inside jokes that you aren't part of. Does that sound like a good time? It's not fun, it's not funny, it's completely worthless as an entertainment product.This game lacks any kind of self-awareness to ask "Is the player actually enjoying this?" during its pathetic runtime. And why the hell should it? The devs clearly love the smell of their own farts and hope you do too. This garbage would be a free flash game back in the day, $20 is ridiculous. Just the fact that this "game" has ANY critical praise let alone a lot of it, is very worrying for the games industry if this is what they are recommending as an essential gaming experience when it's the furthest thing from it.

_childDocuments_.review: *Thank Goodness You’re Here* might have seemed like a quirky, fun concept on the surface, but watching it turned out to be a pretty underwhelming experience. First off, the gameplay felt far too chaotic and confusing. Instead of offering an engaging, witty experience, the pacing was all over the place, making it hard to follow what was happening or even care about the characters.Speaking of characters, they were one-dimensional and not at all memorable. The writing failed to capture the humor it was clearly aiming for, with most of the jokes falling flat. What could have been an enjoyable, whimsical experience quickly became repetitive and predictable.Visually, while the game did have a certain charm, it didn’t compensate for the lack of engaging content. There were moments where it felt like more effort was put into the style rather than substance. I found myself bored and uninterested in progressing further after a short time playing.Overall, *Thank Goodness You’re Here* is an experience that promises a lot but fails to deliver. It’s a quirky title that unfortunately doesn’t live up to its potential and ultimately left me feeling more frustrated than entertained.

_childDocuments_.review: Such a silly, goofy game.Thank Goodness You're Here is a comedic but non-offensive take on British stereotypes that features you wandering around completing odd tasks for the sake of completing a more grand task that you honestly forget about a quarter of the way in.It's very much a peaceful game that has it's both subtle and in-your-face humour, yet keeps you on your toes with unexpected moments. The gameplay is certainly a bit hard to get into for those that prefer more involved games, but the journey this game takes you on is an outstanding one for anybody. I forgot to mail in the postcard at the end of the game, but the developers of this game even offered goodies for those who completed the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an accurate depiction of northern English small-town life during the Thatcher years, including: teens working at least 3 retail jobs, the lack of enforcement of sanitation standards in food service  the laws of physics, and the town bicycle having to learn a thing or two. _childDocuments_.review: Good game on first play through, I like how the environment changes around you. The transition between when paths are blocked off for you to do other things first and when they're open for you to move on is very clean, and it feels very much like watching some weird little cartoon short. I love the art style and I think the jokes are charming. My issue comes with the replayability; If you're following the story, that's great, but if you're achievement hunting like I was it gets really annoying really quickly. A lot of long dialogue sections or cutscenes are unskippable, meaning every few minutes you have to sit through a long dialogue section you've already heard a few times before. If you miss just one achievement section, the automatic saving feature makes it impossible to go back and get said achievement without re-playing the entire game before it, meaning you have to waste another hour or so for a shot at re-doing it. I had to do a third play-through just to achieve one potato achievement, which took around forty minutes. Because of all the cutscenes, I found myself often just ignoring the game to watch YouTube or text my friends while waiting for whatever character I was talking to to hurry up with their dialogue. I know it'd be really difficult to implement a saving feature or some feature to increase replayability due to how intertwined a lot of achievements/parts are, but some kind of skip key or way to go around certain tasks post-completion would be greatly appreciated. Overall a pleasant experience, I enjoyed seeing my favorite 'untitled goose game' characters making an appearance (Herb and the posh neighbor), but the replayability irked me too much to give this game a recommended review.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is horrifying, outrageous and hilarious and terribly, terribly accurate of North England small town culture. I grew up in Batley West Yorkshire, my grandfather put a knotted hanky on his head when he went on his annual holiday to Skegness. My first job was in a pie shop and my parents owned a Fish and Chip shop, and my other Grandfather worked on a veg stall in the local market. I can see all of them in the characters in this game. Be warned there are some um, weird parts to it (Milk Shy was the worst), some strong sexual innuendo (sausage glory hole is an example) but overall I have never had a game make me laugh out loud so much. Make the time to listen to the conversations (don't put your rubbish in my bin was my favourite) read the signs and graffiti because this is less puzzle and more warped Jeremy Kyle soap opera type stuff. Definitely worth the money, but I am finishing the game feeling slight shame (Milk Shy), horror, sentimental and sad that it's finished. Anyway, seethi
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Comedy games are super rare. I searched Google and YouTube for comedy game recommendation. There were hardly any I would consider comedy. Most of the games recommended falls in par with Mario, Legend of Zelda or just light hearted point-and-click games with minimal comedy element. They sure did not make me laugh and the trailer made it clear, those games were made for elemental school children with elemental school level story dressed as comedy. This makes me wonder if most developer in the gaming world are alien to laughter or the comedy genre. Comedy genre is rare even among the comic industry. I read webtoons. Romance genre is the most common genre in the korean comic industry followed by action followed by thriller/horror. Comedy genre is very rare. In this serious world, a good comedian can do wonder and I am always searching for a good story that can make me laugh. I feel sad that, like laughter has become rare, comedy genre has also become rare. This game is unique and a rare gem. It's the first of its kind and the idea is absolutely original and a pure comedy game in the sense of comedy. If I search YouTube for Hollow Knight inspired games, thousands of recommendation appears. This is not the case if I search, "games like Thank Goodness You're Here". This says how unique and underappreciated gem this is. This game is, in my eye, a masterpiece and I feel nothing but admiration for the creative team to allow us to laugh as we play the game and to think of such an unique game idea.

_childDocuments_.review: You will either LOVE or HATE this game, but it's definitely not going to be for everyone.  If you enjoyed movies like Monty Python Search for the Holy Grail, Nacho Libre, and Napoleon Dynamite - then you're probably going to absolutely love this (I did).  But if you were someone who couldn't stand those movies - then I'd highly recommend giving this a pass, because you'll probably be regretting it VERY quickly.It took me close to 3 hours to finish my playthrough, which I did all in 1 sitting.  Personally, I did feel it was maybe just a little too long, as I found myself starting to wonder where the end was, at about the 2 hour point.  Perhaps if I hadn't planned on playing it all the way through at 1 time, I might not have felt that way - so maybe consider pausing and coming back if you find yourself starting to feel the same way.I'm looking forward to releasing my playthrough on my channel next weekend (Benjamight Gaming), and seeing how many people can make it all the way through the video...lol.  Don't get me wrong, I did like it and I have a few (specific) friends I would highly recommend this game to, but I have a whole bunch more that I know I wouldn't. ;-)I hope my review was helpful.Have a good one,Benjamight

_childDocuments_.review: This game has completely surprised me and I fully enjoyed every minute of it. At any point where I thought I knew where the story was going, I was swiftly reminded that NO I don't know where this is going. The humor of this was a massive selling point for me and something that kept me laughing the entire time I played, especially all of the off-handed jokes and passive adult humor.The art style and vibrant color of this fits with the humor so well, it worked so perfect to tell the story they wanted. Each character was so interesting to look at, even if they were minor background characters. Every character had a story that I could follow as I played each section, which made going back to each area not feel repetitive. The direction of the story was pretty linear, though all of the quests could be seen as a lot. You were in the area you needed to be and you weren't able to move on if you missed something important. That was something I really appreciated, as going back to the previous area was something that you aren't able to do very quickly.

_childDocuments_.review: Fair warning to parents out there - the humour pushes the limits sometimes.  Lots of ♥♥♥♥ jokes - you're *almost* jerking off a cow in one scene (you're not, but the joke implies it).  In another scene you're slapping around some fish and it's implied that one of them is a dude's ♥♥♥♥.  Most of the game's jokes involve some innuendo, but some are a bit much.  There are also some off-putting parts that aren't sex related - creepy vegan activism or something?  Kind of weird.  It's fine - it's funny even - but you know... just so you're aware if you're planning on playing this with the kiddo's. Anyway, I'd put the really raunchy jokes at around 1% of the total - most of the humour is tongue-in-cheek and frankly hilarious.  There are tons of little jokes implied by the environment.  Around every corner in the town is rich detail and great little in-jokes.  Even the names of some of the shops and streets are funny just by themselves.  Great game, it's worth your time - 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: A game where you roam around a Yorkshire town doing wacky things and interacting with a cast of British weirdos such as Matt Berry. Not a challenging kind of game - there's no way to fail, and no tough platforming or anything - but it's a fun little game with pleasing visuals and music and an absurdist sense of humour.The biggest caveat I'd give is that it is quite a short game, probably 2-3 hours. It doesn't overstay its welcome, but the length may be a turnoff for some people at this price point. I'd say definitely get it, even if only on sake.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: If Monty Python designed a video game after a really weird dream, it would be Thank Goodness You’re Here. This gem flings you into bizarre scenarios without warning, armed only with your wits and a faint sense of “What the heck is happening?” It's a comedy of errors where you’re the star, the fool, and the audience all at once.Expect to stumble through an eccentric town full of characters who look like they escaped a Saturday morning cartoon, only to end up in the wrong dimension. You’ll improvise, you’ll guess, and you’ll laugh at yourself as the game rewards even your worst decisions.Thank Goodness You’re Here is absurd, unpredictable, and somehow heartwarming—a perfect mix of laughs and chaos. It’s proof that even confusion can be pure entertainment!

_childDocuments_.review: Very cautious recommend this: it's a funny game, a rare enough thing to be worth your time. But you'll have to really want such a thing for it to be worth it.It never actually made me laugh, though. Because it's never enough anything: it's no a game, it's a slot machine for jokes where 50% of them aren't actually funny, 40% are a wry chuckle and the remainder are wonderful (either wonderfully stupid or wonderfully weird). It's rather Viz, a bit Monty Python but mostly a celebration of crap northern towns wrapped in a rather flash-game-esque wrapper.It made me feel a bit jaded to only smile through some of it, and it may be my subjective view, or maybe I wasn't in the right mood, but I was hoping to get a little more out of it. (I'll note that both Jon Blyth and Chris Cantril, two very silly people, do some voices, and I wish that they had more to do with the writing of the jokes, because the former is brilliant, both in and out of the game).It's alright, but not as amazing as some of the press are saying.

_childDocuments_.review: Full of Northern charm, whimsy, deadpan, and absurdity not just in its characters, but also gameplay, scenarios, and perspectives. There's so much variety that is used with just the verbs of jump and hit. Very much reminded of Hohokum (Ricky Haggett is given special thanks) with the interactive toybox that is the town of Barnsworth (based on Barnsley, Yorkshire where creators Will Todd and James Carbutt were born). The voice acting across the board (Jon Blyth, Em Humble, David Ferguson, Peter Sutton, Chris Cantrill) is absolutely top-notch and authentic, and Matt Berry as the gardener is more of a smaller role compared to others like Big Ron, Meg, Kerri, Marge, Bish, Rog, Sam, Charlie, and of course the unforgettable Scottish mechanic Jasper. I would have loved in the credits for the voice actors to be put side-to-side to their characters, because they're so important and bring the lifeblood to this game. There are no filler segments or moments, so nearly every scenario in terms of ludonarrative is memorable. There are so many running gags throughout the game that have satisfying conclusions, such as the two neighbours arguing over whose rubbish is in their bins which effectively becomes a weird love story. It's a wonderful idea to have no UI or HUD, because all the attention gets put into the world and interacting with it, rather than menus, and because of the retro 2D simplicity of controls, it's very accessible (even my daughter has been playing it but thankfully she can't understand the northern vulgarity!). I'll try to get as much of my family and friends playing this, especially on the Steam Deck. It's another wonderful idea to be this miniscule salesman character with no voice and ok to be an errand boy, who can squeeze into pipes, hoses, holes, and anything which allows you to explore several levels of Barnsworth from the roofs to underground. The mise en scene is impeccable, full of environmental storytelling and informing the tone and messages of the game. The musical ludonarrative ending is phenomenal, like one of the best endings to a game you'll find this year. When the journey ended, I felt a little sad because it's such a colourful and hilarious 2-3 hour journey through this unique world so I immediately started replaying it to get all the achievements or other interactions I missed.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely hilarious. The animation is fantastic, the writing is very clever with a mix of witty and irreverent humor, and the sound design adds so much to the comedy. I laughed out loud many times during this short game.Gameplay-wise, it does get fairly repetetive by the end of the game. You just sort of walk this loop around the town over and over, and while it remains consistently hilarious throughout, I did get a sense of, "okay, can we just wrap this up?" about 90 minutes into a 2 hour game. With that said, it doesn't overstay its welcome by too much, and the ending of the game is quite enjoyable. I will also say that the game, at times, has poor conveyance. You're left objectiveless in an open area wondering what you're supposed to do next with nothing to tip you off, which is strange in such a linear game. The story is far too nonsensical to be able to reliably take context clues from the narrative, aside from the rare instances where a character actually tells you where to go. Luckily, the environments are small enough that if you just wander around slapping things, you'll eventually find your way.In terms of value, it's hard to say that ~2 hours of gameplay (a little more if you are achievement hunting) is worth $20; HOWEVER, if you view this less as a "game" and more as an interactive, animated film that is lovingly hand animated and wonderfully performed by a great voice cast, then it becomes a lot easier to justify the price. And frankly, it's got SO much comedy and so many little background details in every scene that you will want to play the game more than once.Performance was excellent. I played all the way through on the Steam Deck and it ran effortlessly. It could probably be a strong strong option for low spec gamers looking for a laugh.All in all, this is a pretty easy game to recommend for the right kind of player. If you love comedy, animation, games you could beat in a sitting or two, and narrative-focused adventure games with simple gameplay mechanics, then this game is right up your alley.

_childDocuments_.review: This silly lil' point-n-click adventure contains some of the funniest jokes in video game history, and only gets funnier the more you play it. The spritework and animated cutscenes are also extremely well done, making the game feel like an interactive Adult Swim show. Though it's a bit on the short side (3 hours at most), it more than makes up for it with its hilarious dialogue, in-depth world design, memorable characters and extremely large amount of hilarious background details that encourage you to explore the game's world. Another interesting thing about the game is that whenever you complete a mission, various characters move to different places, and change their dialogue, often having a tiny subplot as well. This not only causes the game's setting to feel alive, but also causes you to feel attached to even the most unimportant characters. Overall, I highly recommend this game to people who enjoy games with a bizarre, often dark sense of humor.

_childDocuments_.review: Played from – to: (2024-09-24 – 2024-09-26) – PC controller.‣ 8/10 – 10 Bob game.‣ Thoughts: I always find it difficult to review or rate games like these. Fundamentally this is a game, but it is so basic that it could’ve easily been an animated show or movie. Thank Goodness You’re Here is a dry British humor title, where you walk around a town and help people out. You mainly achieve this by just stumbling around like a braindead NPC and that is enough for these townsfolk. All you can do is slap. And slap you will, be it an ass, a door or some other questionable object. Surprisingly most people here have teeth which is highly uncommon for UK. Overall, I did chuckle a few times, but I wouldn’t go as far as to call this “the funniest game ever”. Mostly it reminded me of Little Missfortune and that game was peek comedy. I’d say this title is worth your time if you wait for a sale, because I struggle to justify a 2-hour experience being worth 18$, but the quality of the voice acting and visuals is really good so perhaps the price is accurate. All in all, this is an interesting title and the industry does lack games like this.

_childDocuments_.review: My game of the year so far and not sure anything will be able to knock it off it's perch on the top. A short game, but so jammed full of quality gags and laughs you'd be wanting more no matter the length. It's quality over quantity and the quality of the script is polished to a mirror shine. I laughed out loud too many times to count and the game still gets a giggle out of me just thinking back on it.The game has the framework of an old point and click adventure game, but plays like a collect-a-thon, but where the aim of the game is to collect all the jokes instead stars or coins. I left no bum unsmacked nor object undamaged by my characters puny but powerful punches in a desperate attempt to leave no punchline unheard or unseen. All of this, plus a quick pace and very light and intuitive puzzle design, gives the game a level of interactivity that stops it feeling simply like an isometric walking simulator and into the realms of something else. Something fantastic.If you couldn't guess, I highly recommend Thank Goodness You're Here.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying, if I ever wake up in a small British town where everyone is just a little bit off, I'm going to assume I’m in "Thank Goodness You’re Here!" and proceed to help as many strange people as possible. I’m not sure if this is a game or some weird fever dream I had after too much tea and biscuits, but either way, I love it.The art style looks like a children’s storybook gone rogue—adorable but with just enough weirdness to make you question your life choices. I spent my time helping townsfolk with tasks that ranged from plumbing emergencies (because apparently no one else can handle pipes) to... well, I’m still not sure what half of them were. But when someone asks you to do something in this town, you just do it—don’t ask questions, don’t think too hard, just embrace the chaos.The humor? Top tier. It’s like someone bottled pure British wit, shook it up with a dash of absurdity, and poured it all over your screen. I found myself laughing out loud at situations that made absolutely no sense but were too funny to care. Helping a guy with a moustache crisis or tracking down oversized animals? Sure, why not. It’s 10/10 on the "What even is this?" scale, but you’ll love every second.Pros:Art: It’s like living in a comic book after it’s had a very strong cup of tea.Humor: British humor at its finest. Dry, absurd, and absolutely brilliant.Gameplay: Light, silly, and full of surprises. It’s like someone said, "What if we make a game where nothing makes sense but you’re having the best time of your life?"Weirdness: The town’s weird. The people are weird. I’m weird. It’s perfect.Cons:It’s short, but like a really good joke—it’s over quickly, and you just wish there was more.In summary: I came for the quirky art style, stayed for the bizarre interactions, and left questioning why I now desperately want to live in a village that feels like a cross between Wallace & Gromit and an inside joke no one ever bothered to explain. Highly recommended if you enjoy laughing at things that make absolutely no sense.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very short, but it's definitely worth it. It's essentially cuphead, asdfmovie, rick and morty, dont hug me im scared, and regular show all combined in a single game. If you're not a big british humor person, this game is still pretty tame(but also not) and entertaining. 8.5/10 only because the areas and entire game do start feeling repetitive right as you're about to finish the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: "Thank Goodness You're Here!" is thoroughly pleasant, hilariously written and acted, and at times, surreal and dark in the funniest way. So many details fill this little town. Meta jokes, running gags, and absurd situations and characters. It has an lovely art style, and incredible sound design. There are so many nooks and crannies and little easter eggs to find.You should absolutely play this game. I reached the end of the main game in about 3 hours, but it felt so jam packed, that I could have sworn I spent more time with it. You can tell that this is a game made by creatives. Every part of it oozes personality.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely game. Bit cheeky, sometimes a bit feverish. Sort of feels like a dream you might have after watching Monty Python or the Mighty Boosh. You do have to run in circles a bit, but every time you return to an area something new is happening. The comedic timing is honed, the wit is sharp, and it has stabbed me right in the heart. It is very clear a lot of love and thought has been put into its creation.If you really take your time with it like I did on my first run, it'll take about 3 hours. I played it through a second time just to snag an achievement I missed and got it done in 2. I have seen folks wondering about the price, and though I think it's well worth the cost, at the very least get it if it's on sale some time if that's a consideration for you.Overall, a joyful game where you get to be a funny little guy trying to kill some time before a meeting.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: This was such a fun game. I was having a bad day and bought this on a whim and it made me laugh so hard it turned my day around. Its funny, charming and silly. If you want a laugh or a good time I think this game is for you. If I have any complaint its that I wish the game was longer because it was such a good time. I want to see more of this town and its people.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics of the game are cartoonish, the language of the game relies heavily on puns and rhyming words. Its is very fluid as a game mode, some puzzles and brain teasers are not difficult, you just need to remember the location well on the map which will unlock as you cotinue the game. Excellent game to pass the time in 3 hours finished 95% of the game. The 5% i recommand you unlock the 2 final only after playing the campaing.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun little British game, with plenty of good ole British humour. Lots of puns, innuendo, slapstick, and more shenanigans than you can shake a stick at!Although somewhat short for the price, there's a lot of charm in the game, and plenty of carefully animated and voiced characters. If you're looking for a relaxing and amusing romp through some animated British countryside, while exploring the lives of its quirky denizens for a day, this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: The developers made the single funniest game I have ever played. All of the characters had amazing voice acting, the art was very whimsical and the animations were smooth. There is something insanely comforting about a cute little game where you run around completing tasks for others while listening to the hilarious dialogue. I look forward to whatever they make next.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: 'tis right grand game and about as yorkshire as a pint o' tetley's down t'pub. the art style's reet quirky, and it's full of funny characters that'll mek you chuckle. it's like you’re wandering round t'village fair wi' all sorts of odd bits goin' on. gameplay's a doddle, but it's nowt daft, keeps yer gripped from start to finish. proper job, this. you'll have a belter of a time, no doubt. if you're after summat different that’s full o' charm, you'd be daft as a brush not to give it a go, and it only costs yer 10 bob.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this is one of the funniest games I’ve played this year. Everything about it was hilarious. The game takes you to Barnsworth, where you help the quirky inhabitants with tasks like making pies, smashing through aisles to clean them, and more.One thing I’ll mention is that I checked both positive and negative reviews. What stood out to me is that you probably need to be British to fully enjoy the humor. It’s full of stereotypical British quirks, and I’m not gatekeeping here, but I’ve seen a lot of Americans in the reviews saying they don’t understand it and giving the game a bad review. I think that’s unfair, as the game is truly fantastic.However, I do agree with those saying the game is overpriced. £15 for just two hours of content is quite a lot. Maybe I'm biased because I think the game is brilliant, but it's still something to consider, especially if you're not enjoying AAA games at the moment.Overal tho I still think Reggie's wife could learn a thing or toPros:Brilliantly made Hilarious stereotypical British humour You can slap everyone Cons:Game is set in the UK so if you aren't familiar with British stereotypes or grew up here then you may struggle to find the humour funny or pick out any of the nostalgia £15 for 2 hours (hoping the Devs make some more games like this in the future)
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the previous game from Coal Supper, The Good Time Garden. It was a funny, surreal little adventure game with clean mechanics and a very unique visual presentation. This game builds on that one in every possible way, and if you were at all intrigued by the trailers for this game, I highly recommend diving into it. This game lived up to my expectations in every way.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an experience.  The most British humour you can get I suppose.  Ok, so for gameplay.  You hit things until the story progresses.  Yup, that's the gameplay.  Don't worry, "the story progresses" hides depths.  So if all you've ever seen of British humour is Monty Python's Holy Grail, you're in for a bit of a ride.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: I watched a friend of mine play this on Switch...I watched her play the whole thing in one sitting.I need to make sure I own this for a rainy day. I don't remember ever laughing so hard in my life.Some of the dialogue in this game is so remarkably funny I felt like I was going to die of laughter. This game is art. Truly remarkable.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Good.Stunning animations that enhance the already abundantly Bri'ish charm, Voices that (sure aren't all entirely accurate to Northern English accents, [Matt Berry's is funny but Northerners have said he's "missing the distinctive Northern twang"] but...) delight with some insanely hilarious lines and writing that remind me of the kind of 'must-experience' comedy that rivals The Simpsons golden era.I very rarely tell anyone to not look into a game before purchasing, however I feel because of the kind of game this is, it's short length and highly impactful jokes that this is the exception. Buy it, go through the first hour and a bit and if it's somehow not to your tastes refund it. I know you can say that about every steam game, but with this one the content is the writing and jokes, which are at their strongest on a first or second playthrough. I had to edit someone else's video of their first hour of play for my work and I since wish I had the time to experience the start of the game myself beforehand, so the first few jokes were unfortunately spoiled for me.The only issue I could see people having with this game is the price. Not necessarily because the game is only roughly 4 hours long, but more because its price point puts it in direct comparison with both 'Hollow Knight' and 'Cuphead', both games with hand drawn animations but are both infamous for being bang-for-your-buck, high quality games experiences. Then again even if the game was just a few dollars cheaper I know some people would still take issue with the price due to the length, however I like to think of it more that the game has all of its exceptionally high quality packed very tightly into an extremely enjoyable experience.'Thank Goodness You're Here!' is a MUST experience game, filled to the brim with British humour. However, be cautious thinking it's an accurate portrayal of Northern England. It's not. English people everywhere are rarely as happy as the characters in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a few days since I played it and I'm still processing everything about the game that makes me love it so very much. I'd describe Thank Goodness You're Here as a culmination of so many charming and humerous pieces that are perfectly put together. It's a puzzle that leaves you smiling for hours on end.Obviously, the game's humour is its strongest element. I got curious about the game because of it and I've been always fond of British Humour - and, oh boy, did the comedy deliver! Be it a pun or a heavily suggestive joke, they are very reliant on subverting your expectations - making each punchline catching you off-guard as well as possible (and therefore making me break down in laughter on countless occasions)! Not to mention that no punchline is coming twice. You'll come across the same spot, with the same setup, but each time it's escalating upon the previous punchline. And. It. Is. Beautiful!Not only does it help preventing from running through the same spots in Barnsworth feel like a chore -  rewarding you with something new every time instead - it also connects with the escalation in the story itself, running back and forth with tasks towards a whacky finale!Part of the lovely charm in this game is also the setting. From a behind the scenes video I've heard, the creators were describing the town as "Barnsley, but less depressing", using a gray northern English town and make it more colourful. Not only is this more in tune with the game's art style, it also doesn't take anything away from the "realness" that way, as it's still supported with town details like rubbish, overgrowth, cracks in the buildings etc. - not to mention the real-life footage you catch in the start and the pause screens, supporting the atmoshpere of the setting even further. Then again, this is all coming from someone who's never been to the UK before and has only media references for northern England (Wallace & Gromit being my strongest point of reference) - so call me naive, but I'm convinced!And while on the topic of the art style - the art and animation style is genuinely lovely! I've grown up watching a lot of cartoons, so of course 2D animation done in mostly frame-by-frame will hit a soft spot in me! But nostalgia aside, that choice of animation style works perfectly with the way the game is set up, heavily reliant on cutscenes, giving it the feel like you're watching an interactive movie - and I do mean it in the best way possible, because of how well it works! Being left with the feeling of having watched a 4 hour cartoon movie, that somehow had little to no dull moments, is high praise!All of this topped off with the catchy soundtrack guiding you throughout the entire game, giving it a laid-back summer afternoon vibe. I've been listening to it along as I'm writing this review, haha! All in all, this game has been a blast to play! The humour, the setting, the art style and the music really reflect how much of a passion project this game has been. I really don't know if there was a game that has been this funny to me! I can't help but smile like a fool whenever I think of this game. I know there've been stuff I missed in my first playthrough and I 100% replay it to catch up! Heck, this is the first game that got me so good, that I felt actually compelled to write a review to do it justice! (and of course I'll pester my friends to play it as well)Thank goodness I played this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a delight. It is incredibly british and I have to say, as a non-british person, I was very glad about the subtitles. My only gripe is, that there is no way of skipping cutscenes you have already seen. Like, I get that this game IS cutscenes - and highly chaotic, sometimes slightly disturbing, and enjoyable cutscenes at that - but if I just want to have a look into a location I didn't during a certain loop, there is no way of speeding the game up to get there in particular  in a new playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of circumstantial humor with great comedic timing. The game has a lot of detailed animation and funny reactions from the townspeople. There is perhaps a little bit of replay value in achievement hunting - a few of the game's jokes require a little bit of attention to details to locate. Otherwise, the main experience is a fairly straight run-through where you can't really do anything wrong.Be warned some of the humor is pretty raunchy; but all in all even though all the protagonist can do is punch things, there's actually not much in the way of violence, just frequent innuendos and weird comments.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Actually laugh out loud funny. The setting of a strange town in Northern England might make you think it will be like League of Gentleman, the visual approach recalls Terry Gilliam's animations, the gameplay a classic point n click but it really is its own unique thing. A hilarious look at the overlooked strangeness of a normal South Yorkshire town. The ending is absolutely epic. While a little short, there's definite replay value in there because they've created something genuinely original and fantastically funny.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever had a weird idea for a video game, and you've never thought that it potentially couldn't work, have a look at this.Tonally, Thank Goodness You're Here is very weird. Like it's trapped in a legally distinct Northern English town around the late 90's to 2000's. Except it all feels a little off. A bunch of it is weird, yet I appreciated the jokes in the background.I also got to show a few friends the Goon Show radio sketch "What time is it, Eccles?" Which is always great.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: what a amazing game through and through. Entire crew had a laugh watching me play this. so much packed in a nice tight bow. For someone who would never spend 20$ on a game if you said it was 2 hours long, after playing I would have easily paid 30$ for it. Truly one of the best indie games to come out recently along the lines of pizza tower in terms of quality. Feels like a true passion project where many of the jokes are personally funny to the devs, through first hand experience. Deffo recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: A very strange game, but very enjoyable, if somewhat short. Think "Untitled Goose Game" but a person for whom rules of physics seem not to apply (or everyone has been eating too much asbestos).Interesting choice, in a game that uses local dialects, to write the credits in US instead of British English ("localization" instead of "localisation"), but it's not like that affects the game at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Oh Thank Goodness You're Here! ...It is an excellent slapformer that explores an unexplored and underappreciated genre while exposing non-British folk to the comedic culture while not at the expense of the people of Britain.Fantastic art direction, great voice acting and Matt Berry having a cameo as well was brilliant
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: FIRST: A warning, the game is short, if you know what you get into (most of the genuinely funny, chill games are short for the sole reason this takes a lot of work and they don't overstay their welcome.Now:The good:- Like british humour? You will love this.- Graphics are very charming, very "on point" with what they wanted to achieve- Exploring all the little interactions was very entertaining, however...The bad:- .. There should've been more little things you can interact with- Some mini stories felt like they could've been fleshed out more or they should've had a set conclusion.Short but sweet game. Still don't know what you were originally sent out to do and I'm not sure if that's a bad thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Like many stated: the true Northern England Simulator!I'm not English, though I grew up consuming Northern Content™️ like Citation Needed from The Technical Difficulties enough that I could chant YORKSHIRE! YORKSHIRE! YORKSHIRE! at any given moment.I kept the dialect mode on, and if you can; please do so. It's really the key element to the game (and brings more joy)!
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Outstanding. A game hasn't made me laugh like this for a hot minute. It's basically Yorkshire simulator.Go in blind. Best to remain unspoiled. Possibly the best idle/passive/walking around music I've ever heard. It never got annoying. Gameplay is very basic for the price tag, but play it for the comedy, that's where the value is. The artstyle is very satisfying too. Voice acting, excellent. Honestly worth the full asking price imo. It's reet good.I need another game in this IP starring Florence and Keri.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the funniest, creative, and original games I've ever played. Also the most north of England thing I think I've ever seen aside from Billy Elliot and Sean Bean! There is so much innuendo and rude humor but done in such a clever way. I wanted to go back and check each area of the game and hit everything just to see what had changed. By the way: (spoiler for the end)  This game isn't a long one but it is definitely worth picking up if you like games that feel like toys that tell a story.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a proper blast, great story and very charming. Can't say it's as funny as most people are saying, it's full of the odd joke and snarky comment that made me chuckle or culture reference I cracked a smile at, but I don't think it was ever made to be as funny as it is charming. The art style is lovely, soundtrack is perfect and you can really tell a lot of love has been poured into it. The story itself is a little mental, not hard to follow just outrageous at times yet you're guided through the story perfectly and it's very hard to get confused on where to go next. Shame it's only about 2 and a half hours long.Would absolutely give it a crack.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is reyt good!I've not had such a good laugh with a video game in a long time.This game has so much British charm and humour, the townsfolk of Barnsworth remind me of people in my own little town. Arguments over bins, hopeless learner drivers and a rat infested corner shop all feel like something most British towns have.It may be short, but its so worth the under £20 price tag, and I hope Coal Supper keep it up and make more games like it. Now if you will excuse me, I got to get down to Big Ron's Big Pies. I hear he's made his biggest pie yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: I was lucky enough to not hear about this game until it was already out. I'm not English but I have some dear friends from the North, so I've had the pleasure of witnessing Northern culture firsthand while visiting and whenever I talk with them. Upon learning about the game I immediately bought it and played it together with a friend while having a drink and a smoke, passing the controller back and forth. Laughing our arses off on a lazy summer evening.The love and care in the game is so obvious in every aspect. The writing is hilarious and at times great social commentary. The amount of jokes, visual, auditory and through voice acting is immense. It paid dividends walking around the game and looking at every detail, and what would change as you progressed through the laundry list of tasks the town gives you. The music was a huge highlight for me. It's so charming and it does a good job of informing the mood of the game without being overbearing.To close this ramble of praise: my friend and I were so happy that though some characters are served quite cruel situations for the humour of the game. A certain character whose backstory we learnt and we felt very bad for, ends up getting a very warm resolution by the end.An absolute gem of a game, thank you so much for carefully crafting it!
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Keen to support indie Devs, I read about this game in an article a couple of days before release so thought I would take a chance. In so glad I did. As a Northerner, this is brilliant Monty Python-esqu humour and the voice acting (especially Matt Berry) is superb. It's not a particularly challenging game but more like a funny interactive cartoon. I completed it in just under 3 hours but loved every minute with some genuinely laugh out loud moments. I definitely like my pies TINY!
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: A game you can (and probably should) finish in a single sitting, with an excellent mix of absurdity and wholesomeness - the experience of watching an ITV sitcom miniseries while exhausted on a sunday afternoon.The game itself is completely linear with the only replayability being a handful of miss-able jokes - but if you'd spend the same amount to see a comedy at the cinema, this is a much more solid experience and will leave you with a similar satisfied feeling. Absolutely lovely, highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Liminal Spaces May Be Wet When Slippery.A really nice little puzzle game to play for a few hours. I completed it in one run (barring the extra achievements I'm missing) which I don't see as a bad thing at all.I had a lot of fun playing this game, the environment of chokced full of sight-gags and some of the lines made be laugh so loud I think the neighbours heard me. A great script, with brilliant voice acting (and bonus Matt Berry too). I had a great time with Thank Goodness You're Here! doing little jobs around town, ad the tasks get increasingly weird.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Thank Goodness You’re Here! is exactly the light and humorous gaming snack that’s a perfect fit for a weekend. It’s entertaining enough for a player thanks to its numerous quirky interactions, and adapting to its wildest scenarios never fails to entertain. It’s in an unpredictable comedic quest bursting with irreverent whimsy at every turn.Full Review:
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the funniest and most endearing games I've ever played! I've finished this game at least two times just because of how intricate the world is, and I feel that I manage to find something new every time I play it. At this point, I've already found so many details when it comes to the inhabitants of Barnsworth, and it's an undeniable joy to be invested in all of their lives and just try and get them to say as much as they can. Really feels like I'm just walking around a town and talking to everyone I pass by. The folks at Coal Supper know what their doing and execute it to a T, and I'm ready for whatever comes next from them in the future!! 100/10
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: A right good game!Firstly, given that it is a game and all: the controls are easy as kicking a bike, the animation is smooth as a nob of butter, and the sound is sparkling clear as a morning wee.Secondly, the plot & characters (no spoilers): A delightfully barmy cast of Yorkshire townsfolk take advantage of an odd little lemony fellow (who may or not have some screws loose himself)Thirdly, the music: SPOT ON.Fourthly, the voice acting: Even without Matt Berry this would've been fantastic, but with him on the roster? Straight-up superb!Fifthly, and most important of all: Where's my hat? Did I leave it on Ilkley moor again?
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Pure British comedy! I have never laughed so much while playing a game before. Thank goodness you're here is a absolute gem of a game, I ended up playing it from start to finish in one sitting, to entertaining to put down. It's a brilliant casual game, the puzzles aren't complicated at all, just nice easy playing with a fantastic story and delightfully entertaining characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful gem of a game.It's a bit short compared to a lot of games, and the "gameplay" is limited but I'd say the humor in the game is more than worth it.In fact I watched a whole playthrough of it first, and liked it so much I bought the game. Even if I never played it I'd consider it money well spent. (I did play through it myself too though, and then also watched two other playthroughs of it by other people.)Such a weird and unique little game. It does a good job of disguising its relatively linear nature, keeping things interesting and fun (and sometimes surreal or ribald or slightly disturbing) the whole way through.Top marks, would get lost in a slab of meat again.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: A short and sweet game that packs so much in. Most, if not all the characters are memorable thanks to the voice actors, their strong individual personalities and the fun animation style. The jokes are great, especially if you know the local jargon. References to the Chim Chim Cher-ee chimney sweepers stuck with me and brought me back to my primary school plays. The games puzzles are not hard at all but kept me interested with the variety. Even though I never felt like I knew where I had to go in this strange "open world", the game always somehow directed me in the right direction.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable little game that mimics the olden flash games from a bygone era. Production value is fantastic, animations are fun and playful, the world is unique and strange but I figure that's just the British. Runs and looks fantastic on the deck, and the game has so many fun little things going on it's great to explore. 10/10 would smack bums again.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is bonkers. Monty Python surrealism mixed with northern English references lead to a game that would seem to target a highly specific audience. As an older player from England I get it, but if this has really been localised for foreign markets as the credits say, heaven only knows what they will make of it. Or is that just another joke? Hard to tell.There has been criticism that the game is too short. I disagree. For me, it is just the right length to not outlast its welcome. Whether it is value for money is another matter. I think it is. Purely because this is the utter antithesis of where so much of the gaming industry is headed, I would suggest that it deserves every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: "Thank Goodness You're Here!" delivers a fun, goofy, and delightfully surreal experience that keeps you engaged from start to finish. The hand-drawn art style and quirky humor perfectly capture the charm of the fictional English town, making every interaction with its oddball residents a memorable one. I had a blast throughout my playthrough and found myself laughing at the absurd scenarios the game throws at you. It's a unique gem that I'll definitely be recommending to friends who enjoy something a bit out of the ordinary.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a comedic masterpiece! & will leave you wanting more. this game has the humour of classic brittish comedies such as The mighty boosh, Faulty towers & Bottom with an art style uniquely its own but similar to regular show. an absolutely hilarious adventure, with jokes that pay off in many many different ways from early to late game. if this ever gets a sequel or a decently sized DLC I will absolutely be getting it! 11/10 ABSOLUTELY BLOODY BRILLIANT!
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: This was a wonderful surprise that went under my radar, however I'm so happy to have played this game. It's somewhat reminiscent of of Untitled Goose Game, but with dialogue actually involved.The game itself is hilarious with some delightfully dark, weird, and strange humor involved, which makes it even better. Lots of it deals with British humor, it kind of reminds me of The Mighty Boosh. If you're looking for a funny, chill game to play for a few hours, I highly recommend this one!
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Not for me ... This popped up on steam and looked different so I gave it a try. It just wasn't for me. It reminds me of " Richard Scarry's Best Neighbourhood Disc Ever" for the Phillips CD-I from 1991. Not that that's bad per-say, it's just not for me. Walking around randomly clicking on stuff, looking for things to do is not my cup-of-tea. If it's yours then maybe this is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Utterly brilliant. Fantastically funny and every scene bursting in often hilarious details. Some scenes had myself and my partner bursting out laughing which is rare for a game. It might be fairly short and linear but I would not hesitate to recommend to anyone who is looking for something light hearted, fun and cosy to play. Looking forward to jumping, poking and slapping my way through this gem again in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most original and fun games I've played in a while. Great voice acting, hilarious absurdist humor, and just a delightful visual style never before seen in video game history (to my knowledge anyhow).Yes, the gameplay is utterly simplistic, the puzzles are easy, and the game is relatively short. All that pales in comparison to its uniqueness and charm. Just a delight to play and experience. Thanks for the laughs, Coal Supper!
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so unabashedly a chuffed kerfuffle.  It's so offensively British, it's driving a german car, to an irish pub for a belgian beer, snogging an indian curry with a side of turkish kebob, watching an american show on a japanese TV. It was like a cartoonist was locked in a padded room and driven mad with ren and stimpy and monty python animations playing at full blast on either side.The less you know about this game, the better the experience. My only complaint is  I never actually got the yellow gentleman's name...
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is hilarious, gorgeous, and overflowing with charm. You'll have moments that absolutely find you, moments you find weird, and just absolute "WTF" moments. Throughout it all, though, you'll be having a great time with no rest. The hand drawn animation is absolutely phenomenal, breathing so much life and personality into every character you meet. If you can, I think this game is best when you play it the whole way through without days in between because just doesn't stop coming at you with wacky and unexpected thing which I feel are much more appreciated when doing a whole run. I will say it can sometimes be difficult to know where to go next or what to do, but eventually you will figure it out with time. i wish this game was longer, but I honestly feel like it's the perfect length for how wacky and unpredictable it is. If you love animation and absolutely unhinged games then this is the one for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first Steam review I have ever written, because this game is simply amazing and deserves the time and effort to communicate as such. I have played the game through several times since its release earlier this month and it is the first game I have ever completed to "Platinum" on Steam. So many things about this game, from its endearing story and characters to its complex messages about interacting with the economic and social demands of everyday life, have earned my praise and deserve more in-depth attention than a Steam review can reasonably accommodate. It contains a linear story without causing the player to feel railroaded, it strikingly plays with expectations of visual perspective, it creatively blurs the lines between gameplay and cutscenes, and it includes hilarious and memorable details that significantly increase the value of replay-ability. (Although, even with these features aside the game would have high replay value simply due to its intersection of comfort, lightheartedness, tender humanity, and surprisingly deep themes that have left me thinking for weeks.)As a person in a somewhat larger body, certainly larger than most bodies portrayed in media, the body-shape diversity in this game is absolutely worth mentioning. Also notable is the age diversity, with everyone from teens to older adults portrayed as well-rounded and lovably flawed individuals with something to contribute to their community. The gameplay itself is accessible while also posing engaging mental challenges - just enough to give the player a sense of accomplishment at progressing the game forward without inducing intense frustration or diminishing the enjoyment of playing the game. As I mentioned earlier, each character is three-dimensional and lovable in their own bizarre way without being perfect, and social commentary is communicated beautifully through the characters' mannerisms and idiosyncrasies without reducing them to baseline "stock" characters. (Marge, Bish, and Jasper are my personal favorites!) Finally, I am personally a huge fan of the unexpected surreal and convention-breaking aspects of the game. (I won't spoil anything, but fellow fans of The Magnus Archives podcast may feel a special affinity towards the happenings of the player's second visit to Sam's Hams......) Not to mention, the game's aesthetic composition is mesmerizing and I am not-so-secretly hoping that this game gets an official coloring book made.This game is nothing short of a masterpiece. I love it so much, and I hope that this is not simply a one-hit wonder for Coal Supper. Thank y'all so much for your time and work, and I can't wait to see what you develop next!!

_childDocuments_.review: A comedy game for adults that actually lands the comedy? Say it isn't so!Dubbed a "slapformer", I'd argue there more in common with the adventure/point-and-click games of old more than any real platforming. You explore a bizarre northern British town, and somehow are always the right fellow to solve the various problems the citizens are having. The problems range from silly, to surreal, to scandalous, and while it might not be as esoteric or complicated as a  or whatnot, I'd say the solutions are usually pretty charming in themselves. There is so much silly stuff that happens in the background and not at all involved with your quests, that stopping to just slap everything is a joy. There are some situations that are much more interesting than others, and it does start to feel a smidge repetitive at the end, but the game is very much intentional about that, for better or worse.It's short (around 3 hours), it's hilarious, and it feels pretty unique. Reggie's wife could learn a thing or two.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a delightful time in the absurdist well meaning citizen simulator where you inadvertently cause chaos! From the art style to the voice acting, from the comedy to the tasks; "Thank Goodness You're Here!" crosses the perfect balance of insanely  un-serious and over-imaginative fever dream. While I didn't go in blind, I'd recommend others to go in without any spoilers whatsoever, the trailer spoils enough of the jokes already.  This game is great for those looking to get their relatives or non-gaming friends into the fun of simple games and it also just a fun simple time all around. In my personal opinion it's not as graphic as implied in the rating. However the innuendos and cut-away's might beg to differ. Don't let the art style fool you, this is not a little kids game.It's a great way to spend 3-4 hours (or 2-3 if you don't care to play it twice for all the achievements), and while I wrote a whole paragraph on it and said how much I felt the game succeeds I also think that you should only purchase and play this game if you're comfortable with supporting the creators of said game. I purchased this on sale and I can't say for sure that I'd repeat the buy if the game wasn't the same price I bought it at. (I, however, am biased as I do appreciate a physical copy more than anything else, so take that for what it's worth.)The game is fine. But I wouldn't play it again until I forgot the plot of the game or wanted to sit still and relax and have a few chuckles for a few hours. The jokes don't get tired, aren't offensive or overly sexual, and the achievements aren't hard to get if you know what you're trying to achieve. Overall it's a good pick, but I'd take some convincing to play or buy this again; even for a friend.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Slap and jump your way through dozens of fetch quests! ...No, really. The soundtrack is great, the voice acting is superb, the jokes are funny, the sight gags are chortle-worthy, the characters are charming, and I can see myself replaying it many times over. Heartily recommended!
