_childDocuments_.review: This is my GOTY after Elden Ring SOTE, it's an incredible game preservation collection with a lot of QoL add-ons, not to mention the DS games are fantastic; I've fully completed all of the games including the modern remake of the Haunted Castle, all of them are amazing; a must-play for all metroidvania fans.I'd recommend starting the Haunted Castle Remake first as it is an hour or so long! If you care a lot about the story and lore in these games, it's recommended to play Castlevania Bloodlines before playing Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin, as these two games are connected. Same with Aria of Sorrow and Dawn of Sorrow, but you can pick any game and still have a lot of fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: The franchise that gave its name to an entire genre, in a complete and feature-rich package. Konami's best product in recent years and honestly one of the best retro game collections in the technical department. The biggest red flag these types of collections usually have is the input delay, which is not a problem in this case. Other features like the rewind mechanic were really good and welcome against OoE's obnoxious game design and difficulty spikes. The games themselves are amazing and really fun to this day; most of the soulless Metroidvania clones still fail to grasp the gameplay, atmosphere and feeling of these games. I experienced two random freezes/crashes and saw some other reports in the review section, so I think that Konami should look into and address these types of problems. On a final note, I think more screen options would be welcome, like a main screen focus with the other ones even smaller.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: Another great Castlevania collection.Games are mostly unchanged from the DS originals - IMO they are not as good as GBA ones or SoTN but still very good metroidvanias nonetheless.The only thing that was changed that I noticed is that in DoS seal drawing was removed and instead changed to QTEs - which is positive change as doing stylus movement with mouse or analog stick would sucks and even with stylus was arguably the worst part of DoS so I like it that it was removed.The only gripes that I would have is that this is the only stylus functionality that was changed. Albus mode in OoE is still awkward to play due to that, destroying ice blocks in DoS with stylus could have also been removed to work like in Julius mode. But other than that games are still great and worth playing.For bonus content there are once again galleries, jukebox and ability to switch to JP and EU versions of the game which is great. The best addition is - finally - Haunted Castle arcade game and Haunted Castle revisited. Having easy access to both of these games is just great treat for people that want to see the series roots.So yeah - another great collection that is worth playing and having in your library. Hoping for SoTN + Rondo collection soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Wowsa I had no idea these DS games were this good, and I've only played a few hours of one and like the first hour in another one. But dang its weird how Konami or these big companies can eff up so bad so much but every now and again they do something right and boyhowdy is this even better than the advance collection in terms of presentation. So damn good, if you're a fan of the OG symphony of the night or just metroidvanias in general and have always thought about trying these, trust me now is the time! 5/5 This is how you re-release classics!

_childDocuments_.review: The three main games here Dawn of Sorrow, Portrait of Ruin, and Order of Ecclesia are masterclass examples of what a metroidvania should be. There's tons of weapons, armors, and abilities to gain while exploring large castles littered with enemies and bosses. I would recommend this collection over most games and definitely over any other metroidvania game.If you like these types of games and dislike the Hollow Knight esque games in the genre, as I do,  I recommend Valdis Story, Deedlit in Wonderlabyrinth, Astlibra, Afterimage, Timespinner and of course Bloodstained Ritual of the Night.

_childDocuments_.review: God tier collection, I 100%'d all achievements in about 70 hours, so for the asking price of $25 before any steam deals, that is  INSANE.if you're buying this, you probably already know Castlevania and have played a game or two. I had only played Lords of Shadow and Symphony of the Night (the greatest 2d RPG ever made).The games all play flawlessly, let's just begin with thatI played 3 brand new games to me. Here's my breakdown from the perspective of someone who 200%'d Symphony of the Night.Order of Ecclesia: The hardest game in the group, but maybe that's just my return to Castlevania is general, you gain abilities by getting stigmata drops from enemies, fairly straight forward, maps are smaller and area based.Portrait of Ruin: Definitely the best game in this collection and it aint close in my opinion. Much more casual experience, perfect amount of difficulty, grind, and puzzles. gameplay is based off of having two mcs alternate abilities, and/or having both on the field at once for strategic damage.Dawn of Sorrow: Probably the weakest experience in the collection, not bad, but the map has a very confusing path progression and it had an annoying DS mechanic where you had to draw seal circles to kill bosses and if you don't get them right you have to fight the bosses for a bit longer before it gives you a hint on how to draw the circle, very honestly, you don't draw the circle enough to remember, kind of annoying. HOWEVER, the soul system in the game is pretty awesome if you're a grindy person. you can grind up to 9 souls for each enemy souls and increase their ability power and some are just rediculous, makes grinding rewarding and fun. Bonus Modes you get achievements for:Albus Mode: Order of Ecclasia -> Piss easy honestly you are so OP, you have a machine gun pistol.Richter Mode: you are FAST, bro zooms around and does rediculous damage, finished this mode so fast on normal, heard hard more is much more awful, so good luck.Julius Mode: After beating Richter mode moving this slow killed me inside, however you get several characters to play as, map progression is just as confusing in this mode somehow lol. not much to say here, except good luck with the grasshopper boss and the final boss without rewinds. Then of course you get the Haunted Castle Revisited, which is just a bonus mode better graphical version of the arcade game. no achievements, no saves, just classic arcade gameplay.finally you get concept art and the music soundtrack of every game.BUY BUY BUY

_childDocuments_.review: I played from beginning to end, loved going back to my childhood and play again these great games giving me memories when I finished them for the first time in my Nintendo DS Lite.I f*cking love Castlevania, I f*cking love this collection, it made my happy back then and once again I'm happy again for playing them one more time....
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: On the one hand, dawg this is an emulator. It's not as overt as some companies' re-releases, but you can save and load states independently of saving and loading your files in the games.On the other hand, I'm more than happy to give credit to big companies for making their older titles available again. People won't rom stuff they can actually buy, and re-releases like this take the pressure off of fan communities who're trying to do video game archival work, freeing them up to focus on more obscure stuff.As far as the actual games in this collection, they're good ones. Ecclesia in particular is so close to wrapping back around to early Castlevanias, or to innovating a whole new microgenre.If you like oldschool vania rpg jank and you want to play a bunch of influential titles from a few consoles ago, I'd strongly recommend grabbing this. It's a lot of hours per dollar, the quality is consistent throughout, the spritework is good, and the soundtrack bumps.No buyer's remorse here, just brain off, number go up, and item grind begin.Edit: It does randomly crash sometimes.2nd Edit: Okay, the crashes are pretty easy to trigger. Jumping at the wrong angle into a wall in Ecclesia does it. This isn't great.3rd Edit: It do be crashing frequently for no reason. Making it worse than emulation. Konami why are you like this.4th Edit: I guess I should also review Ecclesia as well as this port. It has some neat ideas and is an interesting fusion of old and new vanias, but wow the grind is obnoxious and the difficulty feels wildly inflated in a way that isn't fun. I'm glad Bloodstained refined this gameplay, even if I like Ecclesia's aesthetics more.5th Edit: Crashing, visual glitches, ungainly save states. I'm glad there's versions of these games available for people to buy again, it's just a shame that they run worse than the ones the fan community kept alive in the meantime.6th: That's probably the least enjoyable dracula in any game, castlevania or otherwise. The scuffed hitboxes and juggles are bad, but having a second phase with a repeatable attack that you can only pass if you have a specific shield glyph (otherwise the second it catches you it juggles you for full bar) is really interesting and unique design. I wonder why more games don't do design like this. Could it be because this design is bad and makes the game worse. Surely not.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of Metroidvanias. I've searched far and wide for PC games in this genre, but none scratched the itch as well as the Castlevania series. This is my first time playing through the DS games, and I'm having a blast. Using an Xbox One controller works flawlessly. _childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

My only grievance is the drop rates. Keep an eye for any mods that fixes it. Some enemies had to farmed hundreds of times. I hope Konami continues the trend with SOTN/Rondo of Blood! _childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: Great collection, amazing games, even the remake for Haunted Castle is a blast. Next please do Rondo and Symphony of the Night! PLEASE I wanna buy a legit copy on PC lol. Also, the PS2 games Curse of Darkness and Lament of Innocence, those 4 being my biggest wants for sure. Maybe the 64 games too for giggles.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: This collection is really well done - I especially like being able to hold down L2 for the rewind feature. Order of Ecclesia is my favorite and it played great. Having both sub-screens viewable at all times was really handy as I could see the map and the beastiary at the same time. _childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute classics. I was mostly worried about how they would handle Dawn of Sorrow with all its DS touchscreen stuff, but M2 did a fantastic job- it works perfectly, and is very intuitive, although I still hate the Magic Seal system and wish there were an option for it to just auto-complete after beating a boss. _childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: Omg, this collection is so awesome! First off, you get all your DS classics from the Gen Z era, Dawn of Sorrow, Portrait of Ruin, and Order of Ecclesia. Second, you get some blasts from the past with the original Haunted Castle. Third, there's a revisited version of Haunted Castle with better graphics!Overall, I absolutely love this collection. _childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: My favorite of all the Castlevania collections (minus Requiem but we'll never get that on PC). The DS games are honestly better than SotN and have way more to do in and kill, plus the stories (while cringey and anime-ish) are pretty good character wise. _childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: Totally worth the asking price for 3 great DS era Castlevania games. Personally my favorite titles in this collection are Portrait Of Ruin and Order Of Ecclesia. PoR is an absolute blast to play with the dual protagonist take on the CV formula and I really like the glyph system in OoE where you gain more powers and such from absorbing enemy glyphs. It's a very similar system that was in Iga's spirtual successor Bloodstained Ritual Of The Night.I've always thought Shanoa in OoE had a top tier character design. Jonathan and Charlotte's personalities bounce off of each other well and are entertaining to watch. As for Dawn Of Sorrow is good but I've never cared for Soma Cruz as a character.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: Castlevania Dominus Collection is a fun and coolest Castlevania that I've ever played. I do enjoy the Nintendo DS graphics like how they have low poly pixelated 3D backgrounds such as the buildings of the Lost Village or the ship being splashed with waves in the Kalidus channel. I do like the storyline which it goes from Order of Ecclesia to Dawn of Sorrow which it fits well to Castlevania's official canonical timeline, I do like the enemies and items that are straight out from mythologies, folklore, religion and more. I also do like the rewind time mechanic from the previous the Castlevania advance collection so I don't have to die and waste on my healing items while fighting bosses.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: there's a lot to hate Konami for, including not producing any new 2d castlevania for a long time, but this collection is not one of themi do think rewind is a bit overkill for the modern castlevania games, but whatever. collection works well, plays well, looks well with some customization options on how you want your screens laid out, it's all pretty good stuff
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: As the last of the 2D Castlevania games to be put in a collection, Dominus Collection adds all three Nintendo DS Castlevania titles in one bundle, as well as the original 1988 Castlevania arcade game, Haunted Castle, and an updated 2024 version with updated visuals and sound.Puzzles and actions that once required the DS touch screen are now triggered by button prompts and using the right analog stick for emulated stylus movement, making for an easy convenience and alternative for  games like Dawn of Sorrow. The icing on the cake of this collection is the inclusion of two versions of Haunted Castle, the original and the modern remake. Everything is here and accounted for in the original, while the remake includes enhanced visuals and sound. All music tracks have been updated and sound pretty awesome as well.I suppose if I did have to nitpick on some things though, it's that certain glitches or bugs that caused hindrances of some games didn't get fixed. One of the most known is in Portrait of Ruin when you're in an elevator room, and using shard abilities in that area causes the game to crash. The other nitpick is that some music tracks wouldn't play in the Haunted Castle remake when I was playing on the Steam Deck. Tracks like the intro sequence, death music, map transition and stage clear music were all absent.Edit: (As of October 14th of 2024, the missing music from Haunted Castle Revisited has been fixed)Aside from the minor negatives, the collection is still worth sinking your teeth into if you're a Castlevania fan, or just into the Metroidvanias of the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: ♥♥♥♥ yes i'd reccomend.These are the best way to play these titles, no debate. I wont bother saying too much but im absolutely in love with Konami bringing these titles to modern platforms in the best way possible. AS a Search-Action fan, do yourself a favor and treat yourself. cause you deserve it.Easy 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: As of time of writing, I have 30 hours in this collection. I have completed each game, including the unlockable modes, and I have every achievement. If that isn't enough of an indicator for if I like it, I suppose I can go into more detail.In this collection, you get access to 4 amazing (and 1 bad) Castlevania games: Dawn of Sorrow, Portrait of Ruin, Order of Ecclesia, Haunted Castle, and Haunted Castle Revisited. Haunted Castle sucks. Don't even bother unless you're curious. Haunted Castle Revisited slaps though. Not the best classic style game, but very solid and a worthwile addition to the roster.As for the others, these are the cream of the crop of Metroidvanias. Each game is worth your time to see through to the end. If you are like me, once you start, any one of them would be hard to put down. Dawn of Sorrow is the best all rounder with an excellent power system in souls. The two character gimmick in Portrait of Ruin is great and it has the best castle, with a lot of location variety. There is also plenty of callbacks to past games so it has the best fanservice. Order of Ecclessia has the best story and probably combat. The best part of this collection has to be it's pricing. Usually, any copy of these games on original hardware would cost you more than this collection. So you are getting a great deal witht his package. Not to mention extra goodies like a music player and art gallery.In conclusion, if you've played these games and enjoyed them before, buy this collection. If you've only played one and want to experience the rest, buy this game. If you haven't played any of them, but have been curious or wanted to just find a good game to play, buy this. It gets my highest recommendation. You'll find something to like, even if not all the games hit the bullseye for you personally. I really hope we get new Castlevania games eventually...... please, Konami......
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: The absolute best way to play these games. Dawn of Sorrow, Portrait of Ruin, and Order of Ecclesia play wonderfully and translating the touch controls to mouse/analog stick is not much of an issues with how little it's used outside of two optional game modes in Portrait of Ruin and Order of Ecclesia.Also included are the 1987 arcade game Haunted Castle and a title exclusive to this collection by M2 called Haunted Castle Revisited which is a wonderful remake of the not-so-great arcade game in the style of the Wiiware-exclusive Castlevania The Adventure ReBirth (Konami please re-release it!).I would even go as far as to say that this collection is worth it alone just for Haunted Castle Revisited.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: One of the more valuable classic collections out there. Not only are the base games themselves very good, but this port adds a lot more control accessibility (touch screen stuff is made button friendly) and desirable screen configurations (you can get a large screen 1 next to separate information screens entirely on screen 2 and screen 3 on the side) that work far better than simply playing the Roms in retroarch or whatever. I'd love to see more DS ports get this kind of update/upgrade treatment, as workarounds using the original ROMs on single screen, touchpen-free hardware usually just don't work very well in my opinion. It certainly doesn't hurt that the GBA/DS era of Castlevanias are all just top notch, addicting and satisfying games, and i would love to see that lineage continued on modern PCs/consoles.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: I can wholeheartedly recommend this to any old or newcomers and what can i say for the quality of these three gems their brilliant in their own right so yeah lets get Sotn and Rondo on here maybe even those 3d games as well and everything Castlevania will be on here. (Besides an obvious fix for screen refreshing which being lossless scaling)
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: I'll explain the ups and downs of each game.Dawn Of Sorrow:+Sequel to Aria of Sorrow+Good level design+Good soundtrack (obviously)+Great character design+The soul system+Hammer+The story.?The seal system (it kinda sucks, but hey, at least it allows you to break the game)-Hard mode being too hard. Now before you go to the comments and say "skill issue", hear me out.Near the beginning, hard mode is well-designed. Some of the enemies get extra effects, and the bosses have some extra stat boosts, but not too much. However, the late-game is a TREMENDOUS difficulty spike. Most of the bosses there deal HUNDREDS of damage. Yeah, that's right. HUNDREDS. Even with top-tier armors, endgame bosses on hard mode deal HUNDREDS of damage. Sometimes, that isn't an issue, like with Aguni, the attacks are slow, and readable, or paranoia, with a simple attack pattern. However, the final boss is one of, if not the WORST OFFENDER. So first, your weapons deal less damage, which would be fine if you grinded for the Devil soul, but no. The devil soul drains your HP in exchange for a HUGE strength boost, but against the final boss on hard mode, it's mostly useless. Second, the second phase is REALLY ANNOYING. The first phase isn't that bad, but the second phase... isn't the best. Third, you can get comboed easily in the final boss, which is terrible BECAUSE THE FINAL BOSS DEALS HUNDREDS OF DAMAGE EVEN IF YOU HAVE THE BEST ARMOR.Portrait of ruin:+Cool gimmick+Sequel to Castlevania: Bloodlines for the Sega Genesis+Cool puzzles+No seal gimmick for bosses+Cool boss design-That one attack in the death boss fight. Cool concept, but the partner AI is too terrible for it to work well.Order of Ecclesia?The whole game (I've barely played it)Haunted castle-Pretty much everything-There's a better version in the collectionHaunted castle revisited+Pretty much everything-Normal mode is too easyOverall:This is a one of the things Castlevania fans have been wanting for years. And Konami did it. A whole collection of all the Castlevania DS games. And the best thing is, they kept some glitches in for the speedrunners! I'd say it's like a 9.5 out of 10, some of my issues with the games aren't that bad.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: For starters, game runs fine on the Steam deck (played mostly on pc, but for those that are curious)Man it feels so good to see these games again after being locked to the DS for almost two decades. _childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing collection of some of the best in the series! The DS got some rather interesting Castlevania games that made some cool use of the touch screen. The way this collection handles the touch controls is well done and easy to use. The decision to allow all three screens at the same time is really nice. In addition to the three DS games, it includes the original Haunted Castle, which is freaking terrible, BUT.....the re-imagined Haunted Castle is really cool and was an unexpected addition to this collection. If you are a fan of the series, or a newcomer looking to see what all the fuss is about, you cannot go wrong here.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: This is preservation of some of my all-time favourite DS games done incredibly well.At first, I assumed that M2 were just using basic emulation like for the Anniversary and Advance collections, and while you do get access to features associated with that like save states and rewind functionality, I was surprised to hear that these games were actually ported natively.3D elements are sharper to look at, and loading in most cases feels way faster than it ever did on the DS.One thing I was concerned about if Konami were to release a collection like this was: "How are they gonna get around the touch-screen stuff?"Well, for Dawn of Sorrow, Magic Seals have been reworked into Quick Time Events.While this mechanic still serves as a reminder that it was an early DS game that felt the need to use touch controls in places where it really didn't need it, this is probably the best way to preserve it while also making it more natural to do outside of its original hardware.For more supplementary stuff like Sisters and Albus Mode in Portrait of Ruin and Order of Ecclesia, moving the right stick acts as a virtual cursor so you can do the essential stuff needed to beat those modes.Oh, and what's the bonus game this time?...Haunted Castle?! That arcade black sheep that everyone considers to be terrible?That *would* sound like a disappointment, but M2 also went ahead and decided to give us a brand new game exclusive to this collection (and the main reason I spent £20 to play this trilogy again): Haunted Castle Revisited!It's like someone there asked the question "Instead of remaking an already good game, why don't we take a game that sucks and make it better in every possible way?"Yeah, it's short and very generous by Classic-vania standards, but it's such a welcome change of pace when it comes to remaking old video games.Overall, if for some reason you missed out on the DSvanias and want to play them all for the first time, BUY THIS COLLECTION.The price for three games in one is a very big no-brainer, and seeing M2 improve upon an infamous arcade stinker was enough to make me pull the trigger and feel like a little kid again.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: Major Castlevania fan here, spent hours playing these games back in the DS days and they're still as fun to play as I remember. I do enjoy the added features of the collection such as the save anywhere and rewind functions, these have definitely saved me once or twice from either dying or missing a enemy drop. I reallllllly hope Konami sees that the fans still enjoy these games and have something planned in the future, but only time will tell.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: Castlevania has always been my favorite game series. Since I was a kid I loved playing the original for NES, so this release obviously is going to be something that I love. Slowdown and FPS issues aside. Konami clearly took a little extra time when they put this together. The layout and extras are great. Totally recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: I played the DS version of "portrait of ruin" back in 2006, and i had a great time. You explore Dracula's castle but are taken into different environments, keeping it fresh and interesting. It can be punishing but you can mitigate that but exploring the world (castle), they give you appropriate loot and you get a better advantage with drops. This games plays like the classic metroid side scroller so if you enjoy that genre, try this game
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: So, I only grew up playing Portrait of Ruin, so its been neat to catch up on the other two. The collection is a bit bare bones in terms of visual options due to these being games for DS, but the way theyve worked out how to manage the touch screen is really nice. Order of Ecclesia makes the most use of it across all three games, but not to a bad degree. Game works well with Nintendo Switch Pro controller, it will be the best way to resemble the original controls.  Though lately I had random disconnects, its the first time its happened though so likely on my end. In all, this is a solid 45+ hours of content, as these games have second campaigns and in the case of Portrait of Ruin a ton of playthrough options (you can even play the entire campaign as a specific common enemy)
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: I never played the Castlevania games for Nintedo DS ( I played the Castlevania 4 for Super Nintendo, Synphony of the night for PS1 and Lord of Shadow  on the PS3) and I have to say they are great games and highly recommended to players that missed out like me.The revisited arcade game is also very fun to play drastically less hard compared to the original arcade(main reason why I purchased this collection).Great collection.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: Ran through Aria in Advance Collection right before starting Dawn of Sorrow on this one. M2 did a great job with this collection. Great to be able to play these games on a big screen on my PC and handheld on steam deck. Steam features like cloud saves and achievements are great, emulation features like save states and rewind are a god send because these games do not mess around in the late game. I do not have infinite free time look I did in 2005 so 100% I will be using this QoL features.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: While I love all the DS Castlevania games...Order of Ecclesia is, in my mind, the greatest Castlevania game ever made, and is the SOLE reason I purchased this collection. While I don't mind the anime aesthetic of Dawn and Portrait, Order of Ecclesia EXCELS in Gothic horror, and I fully believe it is the strongest art style the franchise has had and where Castlevania peaked. For my tastes, the music in Ecclesia also charts in the top 3, very likely to take the top spot right next to SOTN. It's genuinely difficult to choose between them, it depends on the day and my mood. Everything in Ecclesia comes together in a near perfect blend, from the art, the music, absolutely everything about Shanoa (autistic goth gf, my b e l o v e d), the high difficulty, high damage enemies and the  moments of realizing how you can break the game's balance in half (). The only two issues I take with the game are that the story is too short, and attribute points discourage glyph experimentation. That's it. In the whole game, I can only find two faults that detract from my potential enjoyment of Ecclesia. And of those two, one of them isn't even really an issue, and is more of a "Please God I wish there was more". The story in Ecclesia is one of the most emotionally resonant in the series, and as an older brother myself, Albus remains one of my favorite Castlevania side characters to this day, with Shanoa being my favorite protagonist possibly not just in Castlevania, but from any Metroidvania I've played. If you are as big a Castlevania enthusiast as I am, please do yourself a favor and play all three of these games, and officially support this series. Konami, release Harmony of Despair on PC next. It would be a baller move.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: I was never super into Dawn of Sorrow despite loving nearly all 2D Castlevania but it's more fun without DS (and knowing that you shouldn't bother grinding for souls).But yeah 3 really good Castlevania games, no reason not to get it if you're into that. OoE and PoR are some of the best Castlevania games ever.

_childDocuments_.review: Glad they finally brought this to Steam but for all you newbies who have no idea what is going on;These games get steadily more and more difficult and then finally you are fighting for you life and it feels like you are being punched in the nether regions by a Giant Skeleton.Shanoa is also the best dancer
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say, I've been a hardcore CV fan since 1986. I never owned a DS though or a GBA, so I never had the opportunity to play ANY of the handhelds until Konami finally ported them over to Steam. And now I can  experience these beloved, but criminally underplayed titles! Oh and the whole rewind mechanic is a very welcome addition! As is quick saving at any point. _childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: Short review. It's the DS trilogy, as advertised. They made simple by great changes to make it work on PC. Keyboard/Mouse controls are kinda bad but XBOX and Dualsense controllers work great. The FPS seems to be locked to around 60 (Usually 63 for some reason) but there's technical reasons for that so it's a non-issue and very understandable given the era these games came from. I rarely had any fps drops and resource usage is almost non-existent on my 3080+5700x system. Literally sits at like 5-10% CPU usage while streaming and GPU usage around 10-20% with other things open. I don't think anything in the actual games have been changed. Nothing removed or added, just adapted to work better with controllers due to lack of stylus/dual screen. They even added multiple options for viewing the dual screens - and even 3 screens at the same time. Having the map always visible is fantastic, though I wish I could zoom in on it. Overall, if you like 2D Castlevania games, there's nothing to complain about here. They're all amazing and fun games that are finally freed from "DS Jail".  I think for the launch price of $24.99 you get a great deal. Each game should take the average gamer around 10 hours to clear, more if you spend time grinding and/or looking for secrets. That's minimum 30 hours of Castlevania goodness for $25. I definitely recommend  this game to anyone who loves the genre and especially old school Castlevania fans.Edit: I forgot to mention there is Save States, but I assume most people buying this already knew that since previously collections have had those. There's also Haunted Castle which adds yet another hour or two of gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: When Konami does a good work we have to say it, and this time it's incredible.The integrations from DS to PC is excellent. The general overlay and menues are super smooth and we can feel that the developers really respected the serie.In terms of bonus content we have all the artworks in high resolution, special mention for the sound test with some brand new reorchestration of some of the best track of the OST.And last but not least, the haunted castle remake, which is a full brand new game for free as a bonus ! Perhaps a bit short, but the general ambiance and gameplay is perfectly adjusted with a touch of arcade feeling. I surprised myself launching it  times to times and going up to dracula in hard mode without wanting to destroy my screen. Congratulations Konami and M2 🎉🎉We want more like this !!
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: Peak Castlevania. The DS era games have such a great style, highly recommend if you are a fan of the genre.EDIT:After 100% each of the games, I can say that if you are a fan of Castlevania and haven't played this games before you should do yourself a favor and buy this pack. The QOL updates alone make it worth it. Getting to play Order of Ecclesia for the first time was an amazing experience, it quickly became one of my favorite Castlevania games.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: These Castlevania collections games are a must have for all fans of the side scrolling platformer 'metroidvania' genre. The Dominus collection is especially great because the original games in this collection were on the Nintendo DS and were some of the best in the series. I find it awesome that they actually ported these titles to another platform because the touch screen features of most DS games keep developers from bothering with games that were originally got the DS. I hope this is a trend because there are so many great games for that system that I am afraid I will not get to play again unless I buy a DS second hand and try to find the actual game cartridges for them... _childDocuments_.review: I was hoping these would see the light of day once more and was cautiously optimistic. And here we have them at last. The choice to move to buttons for magic seals in Dawn of Sorrow rather than strictly touch screen is also an upgrade, although I would honestly have preferred to just see them patched out / automatically complete.As for the games themselves, they're absolutely some of the best Metroidvania games out there. Dawn of Sorrow is a fantastic sequel to Aria of Sorrow. The additions to the soul system are much appreciated as is the extra unlockable mode included. Portrait of Ruin is very underrated all things considered and offers a refreshing change in scenery. Order of Ecclesia is perhaps the most challenging but I would argue the most unique - the Glyph system and idea behind stages are pretty cool, and there are elements of OoE that clearly adopted later within Bloodstained Ritual of the Night.The various levelling / progression systems within each of the games are very satisfying, especially for those like myself that like to grind for better equipment etc.

_childDocuments_.review: This collection has Castlevania: Dawn of Sorrow, Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin, Castlevania: Order of Ecclesia, Haunted Castle and Haunted Castle Revisited, all available from one shared menu. You can also listen to game OSTs and watch the art and manual scans. Options menu is extremely limited, but at least allows you to select between different regional releases of each game, since it’s still essentially emulation of the original Nintendo DS releases. There are also save states, rewind, somewhat awkward DS touch screen emulation with mouse or right analogue stick and ability to have all in-game screens with maps and other info visible at the same time. In the Extra menu, you can play the original arcade Haunted Castle or Revisited, which is a completely new game that reinvents the stages of the original with a mix of 2D and 3D visuals. I'm not good with classic Castlevania titles, so I didn't play far into these, but Revisited seems very cool and inventive. And I feel like fans of classic titles might like it, despite Konami being so shy about promoting this inclusion.The DS games are presented in the reverse release order, which I will use here as well.Castlevania: Order of Ecclesia is a game that a lot of people love and I understand why. It’s closer to the classic Castlevania titles in how the combat encounters feel. It can be incredibly fast and amazing if you know what you’re doing. There’s this very cool idea of magic Glyphs that are essentially weapons that run on your MP. And you can equip glyphs separately to each hand, to either build symmetric combinations for faster and more consistent damage output or mix them up for different situations or special combined attacks. Your MP regenerates very fast, so you can almost think of it as of a stamina bar, which was a clever and inventive idea too. Also the damage type plays an extremely important role, so you have to be constantly aware of the efficiency of your current glyphs. Out of all games in this collection it also has the best art style and the soundtrack in this game seems very underappreciated for how cool it is.Yet, I hated playing it. As mentioned, I don’t like classic Castlevania, so that’s part of the problem. But on top of that, the game really wants you to know it. Your first playthrough is almost 100% bound to be a struggle by design and I’m not a huge fan of that. Plus, given that I love exploration, the very repetitive and primitive layout of the locations isn’t doing it for me. The optional quests are grindy and frustrating. And there are way too many parts in the game where you can get hit from off screen with no prior warning. I get why people love it, and you might be among those who will find this game their favorite too. But it’s not my thing and while the unlockable second game mode in this game is rather simple, I almost enjoyed it more. Also I enjoyed the indie title Timespinner, that is directly influenced by this game’s glyph system but far more focused on exploration, a lot more. While Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night is, in my opinion, just plain better in every way.The unique mechanic of Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin is the fact that you control two characters at once. Both can be on the screen, with you directly controlling one (and able to switch to another at any point), the other controlled by AI (or standing where you asked them to stand) and when they receive damage, it lowers the MP instead of HP. Or you can play as one character, switching between who is on screen almost instantaneously. Which quite famously causes the character you’re switching to shout their name, leading to funny cacophony as you rapidly switch between them. The locations in this game are far more “metroidvania” in design, even with the dungeons being separated. And this also allowed some of these to be visually crazy and extremely interesting in how they look and feel. The balance is also alright, with most of your exploration feeling “not difficult”, but the boss battles can be quite challenging. And you can either be very good at the game, or make things a bit easier by grinding additional levels. This is a really fun game in general, with lots of fun exploration and good flow between locations. Though some of the dungeons can get a bit tedious and some of the players might find the game a bit on the easier side.But where this game is easily the best out of this collection is in the unlockable game modes. The Richter mode is very fast and fun and Maria can throw cats at enemies, which is quite cool. But it’s the Sisters mode that is incredibly unique and features the best usage of the touch screen. In this mode, you fly all the time – while touching the ground your MP is regenerating, but using the D-Pad to go up just seamlessly makes you float (this time slowly draining magic). And both sisters you switch between attack using the touch controls. One feels more like a twin stick shooter, as touching the screen is aiming the rapid “bullet” shots out of her. But the other one damages things with her mind – anything that can be damaged on screen can be swiped and hit. It’s really cool and unfortunately somewhat awkward in this collection, as no control option on modern platforms will feel quite the same as the DS, but using the controller and mouse worked for me just fine. I wish there were other games built like that – with the world designed around a typical walking protagonist, but with you playing as a telepathic flying super being. And highly recommend checking this mode out when you complete the main game.And finally – Castlevania: Dawn of Sorrow. Which… is actually quite disappointing. Everything good in it is what was good in Aria, but sometimes made better and most of the time not made worse. You still collect souls, though this time there are additional uses for them. And the movement abilities are more or less the same, it’s just that moving to more powerful DS hardware allowed the locations to look richer and more impressive. But then, there are annoyances and downgrades. The touch features here are an obnoxiously badly implemented gimmick, with the worst offender being infamous “magic seals”. Essentially, to enter a boss room you must first find a seal and once you fight the boss and deplete their health, you need to perform what essentially is a touch screen QTE. If you make a mistake or time out, the boss regains a portion of their health and you have to repeat the process until you succeed with the QTE. It’s pointless, frustrating and was the sole reason I’ve not finished this game back in the day, despite getting to the entrance of the very last part of the game. Sadly, the mechanic is kept in this collection, but you can opt to use buttons instead of drawing the seal. It doesn’t help and the mechanic is still terrible.But even if it was completely disabled, this game would still feel inferior to its predecessor. The flow of the game feels off, lots of locations are very uninteresting, difficulty occasionally spikes very rapidly and with little reason. The story, that was actually quite cool in Aria, has no idea how to continue, so things just happen without much reason until the game ends. And even the unlockable game mode is disappointing. It’s trying to build itself on the formula of Castlevania III: Dracula’s Curse with several characters to switch between, but none of them are fun and one additional character was cut during development. Plus, the lack of the HP and MP upgrade items means that there’s little reason to even explore this huge world in this mode, letting it go to waste. Which is a shame, since the mode has a unique boss fight that’s pretty cool… But where I wanted to grind Aria of Sorrow to 100% completion, because I enjoyed the game, I gave up on Dawn and just wanted to finish the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Good port! I'm glad to play these games on a larger screen. Controls are good. Soma's seals have alternate push button codes. Emulation is accurate even including the memory corruption that happens when you suspend the game and zip out of bounds. (NDS suspend is also emulated.) There are also save states and rewind. I haven't played Haunted Castle yet but that was a nice bonus. Konami and M2 did a fantastic job on this port. Fan opinions on which games in the series are the best are heated. But I rate all 3 games in this collection at least 9/10 and I'm glad they're no longer trapped on the NDS. If you've never played any of them before, then expect each of the 3 games to take about 8-20 hours. Plus more if you go for 100% or play Haunted Castle too.

_childDocuments_.review: They're all good games, and they all have a different vibe and gameplay mechanics.Though they all have both good and not so good stuff.Order of Ecclesia:My favorite. The only one that feels dark and serious. Alternating attack buttons with the right rhythm is rewarding and the magic on top makes a quite unique gameplay.But this one is the hardest, sometimes so hard cheesing is the only way, and the quests are often very cryptic. If you miss a villager somewhere you're better off getting a guide because nothing will tell you where to look.Portrait of Ruin:This one is silly and fun. The storyline made me feel bad for Dracula as the poor dude gets both bullied by other vampires but also by a couple of anime characters 2 minutes after he is reborn.It's the best difficulty-wise: not too hard, but definitely not easy. Quests are far less cryptic except for that one spell that you need to get past the bad ending.Dawn of Sorrow:My least favourite.This one is easy, but, in the words of the Nerd, it's a "Where the f do I go?" type of game. You never know where to go, what to do, how to do it, the map is a maze even when looking at it and it's really annoying to navigate thanks to very few and terribly placed teleporters, but getting the souls and skills of the enemies is cool.The gameplay is straightforward and simple. No character switching mechanics, no getting a rhythm of attacks, no combos. You jump, dodge, hit, and that's it.One bad thing for all of them though: the drop rates.Holy frak are they low. Getting a single item or soul from a specific enemy often requires killing them hundreds of times. I mentioned Dawn of Sorrow being easy, but that may be because I often had to farm some enemies for their souls for so long I ended up way higher level than I should have been.Half the time I spent on these games is basically me walking into a room, one shotting an enemy, exiting the room, and doing this over and over and over until that enemy finally drops something.Still, good games, play well, great ports.

Also while I didn't get them personally, I have seen people have issues with framerate if the screen is locked to 60hz, so be aware.The rewind feature is nice, but it would be cool if it was used in other ways, as an example a limited rewind challenge where you only get a certain amount of rewinds per game etc. Just more fun ways to implement this new feature really.Keep in mind these are quite minor and I can't really fault the collection otherwise. _childDocuments_.review: Order of Ecclesia and the Remix of the original Arcade game are awesome, my first time player OoE too and the other DS games so this collection was a blessing. First, ya gotta press Alt+Enter to full screen and it'll be displaying at DS Resolution. Who cares they still look sick and you can go into the files to fix it manually if it's a huge deal for you. Second, they're exact ports that have only had their screens tweeked which means a part of your screen will be taken up by the alt ds screens display. This also means prior bugs for the games remain intact. Warts and all baby. The notable exception to this is that the controls for certain touch screen only mechanics have been tweaked to allow for them to function on PC, which is awesome. Dawn holds up beautifully, even the sometimes painful soul grinding going for 100 percent was a genuinely great experience, excellent castle design and some memorable bosses. Portrait of Ruin was a wonderful new take on the old formula and in terms of imagination and movement is probably my favourite of the three vanias on this collection. Even the constant Charlotte/Jonathan spam filling my ear drums was amusing and enjoyable, which considering how irritating it had the potential to be is saying a lot. _childDocuments_.review: The Castlevania Dominus Collection is a fantastic compilation for fans of the series, bundling three Nintendo DS titles—Dawn of Sorrow, Portrait of Ruin, and Order of Ecclesia—alongside a remastered version of the arcade game Haunted Castle. For just €20-€25, this collection is a remarkable deal, offering a wealth of content that will delight both long-time fans and newcomers to the franchise.The DS games, renowned for their tight gameplay and great level design, are presented here with modern enhancements such as save states and a rewind feature, making them more accessible without losing their original charm. For example, in Dawn of Sorrow, the awful touch-based magic seal sections, which required precise stylus inputs on the DS, can now alternatively be completed using gamepad buttons. Despite these accessibility improvements, the games still maintain their challenging nature, especially Order of Ecclesia, which remains notoriously difficult and demanding even for seasoned players.However, the touch controls, necessary for some gameplay elements, can be a bit awkward on platforms without a touchscreen, and the display options are somewhat limited, which could disappoint players who prefer more customization. It would have been great to have an option to display the map on the main screen as the current map can be difficult to read at times.The inclusion of Haunted Castle Revisited is a surprising and welcome addition. This remastered version transforms a notoriously difficult and somewhat clunky arcade title into a more polished experience, offering a nostalgic yet refined gameplay experience.Given the quality and quantity of content, this collection is a must-have for any Castlevania fan. I still hope that Konami will eventually release Symphony of the Night, the series' most iconic title. Overall, the Castlevania Dominus Collection offers exceptional value and a trip down memory lane that’s well worth taking.

_childDocuments_.review: Having cleared both Dawn of Sorrow & Haunted Castle Revisited so far, I can say with full confidence that this is an impeccably made compilation. After all, it's kinda sorta a new Castlevania game from M2, who previously brought us Castlevania The Adventure Rebirth. Here's hoping we get a Konami Rebirth Collection in the future.There's a few minor foibles with the PC port, like no in-game option to play in fullscreen, but that's easily resolved with alt+enter.UPDATE: The game has been patched to allow for proper fullscreen, and having completed all games in the collection, I maintain my high recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: What can be said about some of the greatest video games ever made? Dawn of Sorrow is arguably the best game in the Castlevania series. Order of Ecclesia, while not as good, is still a phenomenal game in its own right. Portrait of Ruin is considered a very solid game as well. Not to mention the bonus arcade game and re make. This is an incredible collection, and a great value for fans of the Castlevania series. Honestly, many of us didn't think we would live to see the day that these Nintendo DS games would finally get a re-release. They seemed so likely to end up bound by the hardware and touch gimmicks. While those gimmicks are still in the games, and can be a bit annoying, the devs have done a great job providing us with ways of interacting with the "touch" requirements of the game. Even if you are on PC (I play mostly on Steam Deck, where the touch screen works amazingly well), you can absolutely interact with the touch controls using the mouse or a controller as the "cursor" for the puzzles.  Really, the only downsides of this collection are the lack of  16:10 support for Steam Deck users, and the lack of general full screen mode that lets players swap between the full game picture and the map screen. As it stands, about 2/3 of your screen will be taken up by the game, and about 1/3 by the map and status screens. Its not ideal, and makes the game quite a bit less immersive. Other than that one limitation, this is a fantastic collection for the price. Excellent job Konami!
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: (2.7 Hours Played) So far Dawn of Sorrow runs great, the quality of life features are great and is way better than playing it on a Nintendo DS. Not to mention the pause menu has many interesting features.(77.9 Hours Played) Update: Finished all three main games, so far only 3 crashes. All games ran great except i noticed that during Julius Mode final boss in Dawn of Sorrow the boss spawns snakes one usually goes left then the rest go down but for some reason in mine i consistently got all snakes going south leading to it being near impossible to dodge the jump attack. I checked on youtube to verify and mine visually were different unsure if it was changed or not. (Fixed in update)
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: I like the games themselves and the collection is well done for the most part but two grips.1. No proper fullscreen/borderless options and the resolution doesn't really work right with my TV when alt-entering.2. No in game graphics screen filter options, so you have to look at hyper pixelated visuals which I don't think was the intention, despite what some would have you believe. There isn't even a slight bilinear filter, or DS screen LCD type imitation filter. I get around this with reshade but it is a pain and affects the entire game not just the in game graphics, which is not ideal...At least you can exit the game from in-game unlike the first collection. Outside of those honestly annoying gripesIt is a collection of some of the best Castlevania games ever made without input delay or any major bugs or glitches to speak of, at a really good asking price, so yeah, I skew positive.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: 3 peak games, recommended for those who haven't played the games within the collection and those who love it (me).Decent port, trash keyboard support.Would still recommend it due to the games that are within it, prob my favorite castlevania collection out of all the other ones that are released on pc (well 2nd if you include the collection that included Rondo of blood + SoTN but its not on pc soo).(would recommend playing it on a controller tho)
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: It took a while, but three of the best ever made Castlevania games are finally in an affordable collection. Seriously, if you try to get these individually for DS "Order of Ecclesia" alone will run you around $100.Each game runs as smooth, if not smoother than it did on their consoles of origin. And the team at Konami even added a remake of the old arcade port of Castlevania 1: "Haunted Castle" in the same way Adventure Rebirth was remade.Seriously, whoever it is at Konami who's telling the CEOs "No pachinko, more games" keep it up! Looking forward to when the PS2 collection happens, and hopefully a port or remake of Harmony of Despair as well!
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: What an incredible collection! The 3 original fantastic DS games run better than they ever have, look gorgeous, and sound great. QOL features also improve the experience. The audio/picture gallery are great and the high quality FMVs are a treat. Add in the Haunted Castle Rebirth which is a fun re-imagining of the original Haunted Castle (which is also included and has many quirks). The perfect starting point for any Metroid-Vania fans looking to experience Castlevania for the first time and exactly what die-hard Castlevania fans have been wanting for so long. This is definitively the best way to play the original DS games now. I cannot recommend this enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: What a collection! Kudos to KONAMI and not only because the company released these amazing games from Nintendo DS on PC, but also because the collection is definitely worth buying!The games run smooth as butter, they even support mouse cursor imitating the NDS stylus. As far as I know these are not native ports but they are something more than just basic emulation. Thus you cannot expect any graphical options whatsoever regarding graphics improvement. It does not matter, at least for me, because I dont mind playing in a small window. Only then the graphics look great. Especially I love how the managed to put all NDS windows to one window so you can see everything at the moment as you did when playing the original versions.All three games are great. The ports are great. A great collection if you like Castlevania or are fan of action metroidvania adventures. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: A perfect example of how to preserve older video games from Konami of all companies, which is pretty funny. This is a re-release of the DS Castlevania games but these thankfully aren't lazy rom ports and have been touched up with needed quality of life. The "Magic Seals" in Dawn of Sorrow have been reworked to be solvable on controllers with button commands(Thank God), and touch screen mechanics can be mapped onto analog sticks. The display settings offer multiple ways to display the two screens present in the DS games which is a nice quality of life addition.On initial impressions, the performance of these games runs smoother than on the DS and emulators. The quicker loading times are noticeable, with little to no input delay on character movement. I have yet to see any visual glitches, stuttering and frame dips which are all common when playing these games on an emulator. A "Haunted Castle" remake is also bundled with this collection and is a new castlevania game, specifically a "classicvania" with classic 2D side scrolling level progression. The remake is short and sweet with great redesigns of Haunted Castle's levels, with forgiving but still challenging difficulty, and absolutely banger remixes of Haunted Castle's soundtrack. Definitely fulfilled my craving for a new classicvania, and I can only hope we get more classicvania remakes/games with this level of quality in the future.Overall, I recommend the Dominus Collection. I'm impressed with the quality and effort put into this, and as a life long Castlevania fan this gives me hope that Konami is potentially heading back in the right direction with this franchise(not only just collabs and mid Netflix adaptations), especially given the quality of the Haunted Castle remake. But this could simply just be an anomaly and maybe I'm just inhaling hopium.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: Just chipping away at this, it seems like all three former DS games have had some changes made from their original translation. Not all are... graceful, exactly, and there's more than a few typos, but it seems like they were trying to correct some little errors that made it through the first time around. But that's not a part most of you care about, is it? The gameplay changes (rewind function, button press QTE instead of timed trackpad scribble for the Magic Seals in DoS) are a breath of fresh air; the shiny new version of Haunted Castle also included is just a delight.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: This is a incredible collection. The DS castlevania games are incredible, second only to SOTN. These 3 games are ported to steam perfectly, with touch controls even being carried over via the mouse or a cursor. The music player and artwork sections are great too, plus you get not only a port of niche game haunted castle, but a newremake of it too.If you are a castlevania fan, you owe it to yourself and this series to buy this awesome collection. 3 Incredible metroidvanias for 25 bucks is a amazing deal.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: Castlevania Dominus Collection is the definitive way to play the DS Castlevania games. The new improvements that substitute the need for the touch screen give this collection enough value already.My only gripes are the fact the screens are not pixel perfect and there is no smoothing option (slight blur, not the crappy pixel blending upscalers); so the pixels stretch out; making the game look kinda bad. Also the sound quality could be better with a filtering option like in the Advance Collection. If pixel-perfect scaling and linear scaling as well as linear sound interpolation are added, that would perfect this collection.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: Have cleared Haunted Castle Revisited Hard without dying, for me this remake is more exciting than 3 DS games, please drop more great M2 remake like this in the future.But I'm not sure if there is already a hidden difficulty in the game or not, I just feel like the game is a little too easy, even on Hard the enemy damage is very low, and the cross sub weapon is just too imba. Would be nice adding an EX difficulty or something. Also, please add BGM and SE volume adjust for Revisited, it's weird that DS game have this but not for Revisited, in default setting the SE volume was too loud, it make people a little tough to hear the great BGM.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: I'm posting it early, since I've already completed the main games back in the day on the DS. It's nice to have them on modern machine.The ports are very good, with multiple ways of placing the DS screens on your layout. Unfortunately only 1 of the layouts has proper scaling(at least on Steam Deck), so that's the one I'm using.Each game has rollback of last 30 seconds of so, and also save and load anywhere. All 3 Castlevania games on DS are very good. My favourite is Portrait of Ruin, but they made Dawn of Sorrow much better this time. You can just press buttons on controler to draw sigils instead of drawing them on the screen. Some other touch things are done either with mouse or right stick on the controller. On Steam Deck touch screen works also(probably as a mouse).Each game also has library available from the main menu, with list of monsters, items, skills and so on... Which the games themselves also have, so it's not as useful as it was in GBA collection. But the main menu one is fully unlocked from get go.Finally the opening videos for each game are visible from the main menu. They are in much better quality than pixellated 200p versions that were on DS. Good stuff. You also have other goodies like galleries, music. But the games - they are just great.There is also bonus 4th game for some reason, which I don't mind existing.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: Portrait of Ruin and Dawn of Sorrow are 2 of my favorite Castlevania games (and among my personal top metroidvanias of all times). Order of Ecclessia is fine, but I wouldn't recommend it on its own.The closest thing to Symphony of the Night and in my opinion just an upgrade. It has a nice item variety (some with unique effects), skills, a few summons and a bunch of secrets.Soul system rewards going slower, grinding each enemy to get their souls and max them out for the most powerful version of their soul effect (attack, buff, summon etc). If this doesn't sound like fun to you go for Symphony of the Night instead as it cuts down on the grind. This has you playing as 2 characters (a fighter and a mage). You can use 1 at a time, or summon them both to fight (which has risks). The item pool is reduced, however items still do have some unique effects. Main map is also reduced, but you travel through several additional maps in your journeys. There's plenty of hidden things to find. A downgrate in terms of scope and quality, even if it's still okay overall.I think both Castlevania Dawn of Sorrow and Ender Lilies handled map design AND attacks (or "skills") significantly better.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: I'm happy to say it: Classic as it obviously is (especially the soundtrack!), any one of the games in this collection beats the pants off Symphony of the Night.While obviously a little dated now, I think these three games are the absolute pinnacle of Iga's work, and represent a very very high watermark for the Metroidvania genre as a whole. All similar in many ways, but each having a distinct core character mechanic that makes each game feel fresh, in spite of huge amounts of recycled enemy designs. Less open-ended than Symphony, each game offers superior map design, with a far better sense of flow and balance. This makes them harder to brute force and provide a decent enough level of challenge (especially OoE) - Though they're no Hollow Knight.My only real issue with this compilation is that the game launches in a full screen window by default, with no options in-game to change it. ALT+ENTER (every time you start the game up) fixes it, but that is not a step that a game released in 2024 should be expecting players to go through. There's a distinct lack of display options all-round. Touch screen related controls are a bit hit-and-miss too, but that's to be expected given the format.But those issues are a drop in the ocean compared to the amount of hours of high quality gaming this collection offers, especially for completionists. Konami released the one product that I'd pay them for, finally!I'd recommend this to anyone that enjoys the genre and hasn't boycotted Konami completely.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: I'm super happy to see these games get re-released, I love ecclesia, i even have a poster of it in my living room. But if i'm writing a review for this port and not the game as a whole [iv'e only tried ecclesia so far, not sure how the other games run] I definitely have a few complaints. The input lag is definitely noticeable, and there is lag and frame skips that were never present in the DS version. Sometimes the music and sfx will even cut out for a few seconds as the screen freezes. So far Iv'e noticed that hitting enemies or collecting items causes it to happen about half the time. I have an original DS cart and I've played in emulators. This port doesn't feel nearly as snappy or fluent, which is a big deal in a set of games like this. Iv'e  beaten the game several times and I'm having a much harder time then usual with this port. Hopefully the performance issues can be fixed. And yes, i have tried using and not using vsync. Like I said, great games, and I am very very glad to have them so easily accessible again. But I'd be lying if I said its a better experience then playing on an emulator. Still would recommend to anyone who hasn't played these gems before/doesn't have access to emulation or other options. But the issues are pretty detrimental to the gameplay. Will change my review if performance issues are fixed. Maybe it's something on my end and it's running great for everyone else, but this is my experience so far. EDIT: performance issues are gone, and there's native fullscreen option now. Came back and played through all of ecclesia the last few days and had no issues. Great game, great port. Thank you devs. would reccomend to any fan of platformers, metroidvanias, etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: A great collection with great emulation and great games. In fact, the audio in these has never sounded better. I'm not going to talk more about the DS games since everyone likely knows them, and suffice it to say they're all awesome and unique in their own ways. This collection also has Haunted Castle; a Castlevania arcade release known for its unfair difficulty but really impressive graphics and music. This was actually in the Konami Arcade Collection, but in this collection M2 made an amazing little remake that is much more fair, with even better music and graphics. It takes about 45 minutes to beat, so very much a classic length game. The bosses are fun and varied, and the level design, though simple, keeps you on your toes and sprinkles in a few secrets here and there.I have one major complaint; why in the world is that new game basically hidden in here as a side mode, and why doesn't it have any achievements? It's awesome they made it, but I'm worried many people won't even know it's there or bother playing it if it's hidden on a different screen and has no achievements nor leaderboards to encourage people to play it. Honestly I'm a bit baffled by this decision.Anyway, I still highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: Was not expecting these! Had a lot of fun replaying other titles on steam in previous bundles (like Circle of the Moon, Aria of the Night, Harmony of Dissonance) and got a lovely surprise today (27th Aug 2024) to see they'd released another bundle! Wasn't sure how they'd handle DS controls ingame, but my PS4 and PS5 controllers are happy! (You can draw the seals with your mouse or with controller). Classic metroidvania fun and great soundtracks. It's not that we don't have some great metroidvanias nowadays, especially Bloodstained, but it is a little sad that these sorts of castlevania games have faded out of time. The formula is timeless and as eternal as Dracula.Dare we imagine one day we might see Symphony of the Night on steam?!
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: Two things make this collection great besides it containing three wonderful Castlevania games from the DS. First being Haunted Castle Reimagined, M2s newest game since their Rebirth batch more than a decade ago, and it rules! Second is the Dominus Collection credits. I don't mean to hype it up but check it out, its really really neat.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: The Three Castlevania Games for the Nintendo DS, all of them were excellent. Dawn of Sorrow (Continuation of Aria of Sorrow), Portrait of Ruin (My Favorite where you can use O.P Charlotte the Mage ((focus on her int and mnd))) and Order of Ecclasia which has the most interesting story of the three. All are brilliant games, highly recommend this buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best Castlevania games and the ones we actually wanna play that has not aged so bad like the older games on handheld. Just wish it had a bit more HD polish but I guess it cant all have that shiny polish like the Suikoden remaster next year. Do love the UI, quick save and touch stylus stuff turned into button presses, very nice. Cool extra stuff as well. Seems Konami tries at least to get their classics back on modern platforms and though not all great (like MGS) this one is def a good one. I gladly support games like these :)
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: Hailing from the time when Koji Igarashi, of Bloodstained fame, was at the helm of the franchise, the three missing Castlevanias of the DS era are finally released for PC in a comprehensive and affordable package, with a full remake of the arcade Haunted Castle to seal the deal. While this collection is missing some standard features for a re-release of rather old games - native fullscreen (Alt+Enter to enable it in-game), visual filters and some online features are coming to mind - these issues aren't enough to spoil the fun that comes with revisiting three of the most solid metroidvanias of the 2000s, especially when priced at the low launch price of 25 bucks.Cheery on the pie, they are working perfectly on Linux desktop and Steam Deck alike.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: We need an option to make custom sizes for each screen and to allow us to switch a single screen to fullscreen. Other than that so far I love it as these are some of the best Castlevania games that are out there. Now we need the Rondo collection and you better include the original voices version that is on Xbox/PS1 or we will riot.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: I still have both my DS Lite and my 2DS but I just can't resist to buy another fantastic collection of Castlevania games.My favorite game from the DS era is here and besto waifu: SHANOA!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!11And I never expected  Haunted Castle to be here. I love it because have that old wine-like taste, that old arcade game taste, so sweet and pixelated just like at its time.But enough talk! Have at you!11/10 Too much Castlevania.The game have some translations errors on Spanish, at some menus having wrong text buttons (like the quit button being the music one), but I expect this to be corrected into its first update.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review:
In addition to the three action adventure games from the Castlevania series, Haunted Castle Revisited, an redesigned version of the very first Castlevania arcade game, makes its debut! And you can also play it in its original format!
Experience the world of Castlevania like never before, with never-before-seen art and handy new features such as rewind, quick saves and much more!

- Titles
Castlevania: Dawn of Sorrow
The adventures of Soma continue! Discover a completely new way to create countless weapons by combining souls, in stunning 2D graphics.
One year after the events of Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow, a boy named Soma Cruz is once again put at the center of a plot to resurrect Dracula led by a mysterious cult.. Will he finally be able to face his own destiny and put an end to all this?

name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS 2
detailed_description: EARLY PURCHASE BONUS ・Early Purchase Bonus DLC(*1) 　'Additional Character' HERE I GO!!: Himekawa, Reporter Joins the Fight 　'Additional Character' Don't Worry: Honda, Reporter Joins the Fight *1 This offer is only available to customers who purchase by 23:59 (PST) on January 31th, 2025. About the Game The Earth is in pieces...again! We've gotta do more to save the planet! --Loads and Loads of Giant Enemies-- The square Earth is under attack by giant enemies. Giant ants, giant spiders, giant bees, giant scorpions, giant UFOs, giant robots, giant monsters.... And if that weren't enough, there are also giant aliens, and even giant EDF soldiers. The situation seems hopeless! Still...there's nothing more satisfying than taking down these invading foes. --Create Your Own EDF Unit-- Teammates scattered around the world are waiting to be rescued. Select 4 teammates from among those you have collected and create your own team. Design the team perfect for your play style, select your equipment, and then deploy to battle. There are over 100 characters to collect! --Full Array of Soldiers from the History of the EDF Series-- In addition to soldiers from the mainline EDF series, this game also includes soldiers from the EDF spin-offs. Enjoy some familiar faces, as well as soldiers from the latest mainline release, 'EARTH DEFENSE FORCE 6.' Includes over 600 equippable weapons and accessories. --Familiar Enemies are Back, Too!-- Enemies who ravaged the planet in previous releases have also crossed over into this world to join the fight. Enjoy fighting numerous enemies, including redesigned voxel versions of old favorites, as well as new enemies unique to this release. Includes over 100 missions and 5 difficulty levels. --Online Co-op Play Supported-- Up to 4-player online co-op supported. Allowing you to defend the Earth with your friends and family. ~The Story~ After Dark Tyrant was defeated, peace was restored on the square Earth—but now, it has been broken into pieces once again. We watched the skies, assuming any new enemies would come from above—which is why we were surprised when the supermassive 'Gaiarch' emerged from below ground, shattering the Earth into pieces. YOU are the legendary Commander that once saved our planet. Now, we need you to lead another team to save our Earth again. The EDF never back away from defending the Earth, be it round or square—so let's go to the rescue! Attention: About Online Cross-Play This game supports online cross-play with Epic Games Store players. To use the “Invite” and “Friend” features with Epic Games Store players during online play, you must create an Epic Games account and link it to your Steam account. Please note: You will still be able to enjoy online play even if you do not link your Epic Games account. However, if you have installed Epic Online Services, you will need to link an Epic Games account to your Steam account.
