_childDocuments_.review: WB2 is an astronomical improvement over the first game and stands as one of the best entries in the entire EDF franchise. It's a hard pick between this and EDF 6, both games refine and fine tune the EDF formula in different ways and both stand high above all the games that came before.Like the first game, this is a more arcade style take on the EDF formula where you control squads of soldiers in much faster paced missions compared to the main series, with a focus on collection new characters and building a team. The formula sees a lot of refinement in this game though, especially where those collectable characters are concerned. All of the characters have more abilities now than they did in the previous game (and all the new characters have enough abilities of their own to match) and there's a wider number of weapons. Generally all of the characters are also a lot stronger, nobody here really feels outright useless like some could feel in the first game. The 3 variations of each character have also seen a change, to match the change made to the game's accessory system. Now every character can equip 2 accessories, but they're split into multiple categories now and each character's accessory slots will be specific to a certain category of accessory. Rather than having slightly different stats, the 3 variations of each character now all are identical at a baseline but the accessories they will be able to equip are different. This keeps them distinct enough to have reason to switch between them without also creating blatantly correct versions of each character like WB1 did.The difficulty (initially) is a bit lower than a standard EDF game, though this game does get more difficult compared to WB1. The mission count has massively increased and along with it so has the variety and scale of those missions. Many levels here are far larger scale than anything seen in WB1, and the roster of enemies is incredible. WB2 may just have the largest variety of enemies across any EDF game, taking the biggest hits from every single EDF game as well as adding a handful of completely original new enemies that fit in perfectly with the pre-existing roster. The game mixes and matches these well to create a lot of dynamic and interesting missions and the game never stops introducing new things throughout it's entire runtime.Every strength of the first World Brothers game is still here and improved upon, while almost every flaw has been ironed out. World Brothers 2 is an incredibly fun horde shooter, and what it lacks in some areas compared to the mainline EDF series it more than makes up for in it's gameplay variety and mission design. If you have even the slightest interest in the EDF series there is no reason not to play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS 2

_childDocuments_.review: Much much better than the first game! Bigger enemy count, maps seem a big bigger, more maps, more returning enemies, we get to fight some of the motherships actually too now!If you liked World Brothers 1 you will love this one! Bigger campaign too! Over 100 missions, I think 200 brothers n sisters to collect, many of the DLC ones from WB1 are now base game too! This is awesome! Lower price point at $50 is honestly a better price point for EDF tooAn epic account is also not required for Online play. It is optional for online play.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS 2

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely Hilarious game with a surprising amount of heart. For some reason the less serious format actually leads to characters having a bit of personality. Well. More than a typical EDF game at least.  The addition of some new quality of life features including tighter controls and redesigned classes that have an extra ability makes every character feel that much more unique than in previous titles. The new units are also fun and colorful as well.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS 2

_childDocuments_.review: Great, just like the first one. Picking out weapons and your team is fun as always. You can fly in as a wing diver, buff yourself with ranger, swap to air raider and call down an auto canon and a strike, and while they cool down, swap to your main 'killer' with a good old AR. A silly homage to EDF with some QoL I wish would find its way to the main game (decent armor gain per level, armor is gained on stage completion and varies between 'class', you can drive a tank into shallow water without blowing up, etc), if you want more EDF then here it is. Missions can be a little short, and you can start right on Hard with no issues, but it's still  a must play for any who call themselves fans of the series. I plan on playing this for many hours, and then heading back to EDF 6 for DLC 2.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS 2

_childDocuments_.review: You don't have to be a fan of EDF games to fall in love with this charming third-person action game, but it certainly doesn't hurt! World Brothers 2 serves up a second helping of the omake style offshoot to the Earth Defense Force series, bringing refinements to game balance, various quality of life improvements, updated graphics and, of course, loads of light hearted new content. Both myself and my goblinoid seven year old daughter are having a blast with this one, and I suspect I'll enjoy this game as a low commitment action game for years to come.

_childDocuments_.review: Good spin-off EDF game. Has a lot of enemies from different games of the series and a lot of characters, but there are a lot of similar ones among them (like alpha, beta, gamma versions of the same character with just color and a single equipment slot being different). _childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS 2

_childDocuments_.review: For the first time in a long while I am truly disappointed with an EDF game. The Pros: Great destruction, excellent sound work, and overall a fun theme.The Cons: Serious mouse responsiveness/tracking issues in stages, the maps are completely recycled from the first EDF:WB, and the stages are far too short.If you're a fan of the EDF series, perhaps wait until there is a fix for the mouse and keyboard issues. _childDocuments_.review: This game is PEAK EDFYou take everything that make a great main serie EDF, and strip out the boring part and you get this gem.Over is the time of picking up weapon and armor crate and boring, tedious story exposition mission. Now, you just crush monster with hundreds of different brothers (and sisters) with gameplay different enough so that they each have personality of their own, and the story progress while you rampage.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS 2

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun, my favorite in the series. Being able to play with a team is particularly important, one my biggest gripes about the main series was always being limited to 2 weapons (4 at best with a fencer) from such a tremendous weapon catalogue, always hated it and it often left me very limited against some enemy types during missions. Yeah it always encouraged coop, but that's more like trying to force it.Despite the sd voxel graphics I consider this one the best because of the gameplay, I love the way you can actually play with 4 characters among a ridiculously vast roster, switch between them at any time, each of them with a weapon and 2 or 3 different skills (even more moves for the melee characters), many of these characters and skill ridiculous, over the top but very fun and varied, great to experiment with weapon and skill sinergies in battle. One of my favorite combinations is throwing a royal wall to protect a decoy and surround both with tornadoes, which makes all enemies advance to their doom in a giant grinder of death. Another fun combo since the first game is throwing a magic carpet mid air to let flying characters like wing divers recover energy and therefore achieve endless flight.Another little nice aspect is being able to equip 2 accesories on 3 versions of the same character, which gives even more possibilities. Although many of these items don't have excessively noticeable effects, some are game changers.It's a shame they removed couch coop, but online is good and each player has their own 4 character team which is great and makes things even crazier.Last but not least, the story is actually kinda entertaining and funny, and the music quite recycled, serviceable but with some really neat pieces. I was surprised by how the victory fanfare, and at least one cool piece that doesn't play often changes the main instrument depending on the character you have selected, and it switches as you do, it's pretty cool, I'd like to ask everyone to try it in mission 63.All in all it has all the EDF monster army massacre and scenario destruction goodness, plus all the above, so yeah, I love it.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS 2

_childDocuments_.review: Took some time, but found out how to avoid to login into Epic account, it may be still a bit tricky on some cases.Thing is: when you launch the game it ask if you want to link with Epic. Even if you select "no", there is still a chance you may get asked to login into epic when inside game you try to go online. Simple thing is, you have  to check if EOS is installed on your PC, and if so, uninstall it. As far as EOS could be already installed, it may ask you to login with Epic when choosing online play even if you clicked on "no" on game launch.----Aside that, what to say. Its kinda similar to WB1, but with somehow more stuff. A vreally funny game with light-hearted story and characters, tons of enemies from medium to humungous size and lots of bizarre and crazy weapons.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS 2

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked World Brothers 1, get this already. It's better in every way.For those not familiar with this spinoff...EDF World Brothers 2 is basically a co-operative horde shooter where you control a squad of four units and switch which one you directly control at any given moment. Different units have access to different guns (but as they rank up, they can use more of them) and also have unique skills and SP moves (think ultimates), giving each unit a bit of a light "Hero shooter" feel. You can also customize your units with different accessories to alter their stats and provide passive effects, such as healing on kills, or even adding limited aim assist/auto aim to their weapon.Thus, the big focus of the game is forming a powerful team that works off each other and synergizes...Or you have a team where everyone fills a role and thus makes up for another member's shortcomings. There's a lot of experimentation here. While the levels aren't as big or long as a mainline EDF, the gameplay loop is honestly still pretty great: Go into a mission, rescue the Brothers/Sisters in the mission to add them to your roster along with their weapons (And possibly get an accessory too), or rank up Brothers/Sisters if you already have them so they can use more weapon categories, all while blasting away a bunch of aliens. You won't find the need to grind by collecting hundreds of crates here: As you gain extra armor (HP) just by completing missions, and rescuing the Brothers/Sisters in a level is much faster than collecting a bunch of weapon/armor crates strewn about the level from your alien killing. This honestly makes for a much smoother and more satisfying gameplay loop in my opinion.So, if you like the idea of shooting hordes while building an entire team instead of just one hero, yeah...This game does that. And it does it good.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS 2

_childDocuments_.review: I was told I would enjoy EDF series as a Helldivers fan, and I am glad I bought this and EDF 5 recently. These are very fun, horde style shooters with a crap ton of weapons and missions to grind. While I prefer the more realistic look of the other EDF games, this one runs the best and destruction of the buildings is done A LOT better here as I can actually blow open a building and get inside for cover unlike the older games.  Combat in this game is prob the best in the series with the ability to take 4 classes at once and switch to them at will. This does away the crap formula of the old games where you could only carry a couple weapons and just be one class. Overall if you were like me and want a more in depth and over the top arcade horde style shooter, you really can't get any better than this game.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS 2

_childDocuments_.review: What can I really say? It's good, the gameplay's good, it's an improvement in pretty much every aspect compared to World Brothers 1, the story's quite good too and, yeah, overall I'd highly recommend the game, the list of missions is decently big and it avoids the EDF 6 syndrome of having stages that drag on for an eternity with story and walking.Overall, it's a great ride and worth the price, if you like World Brothers 1 then you'll like this one.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS 2

_childDocuments_.review: If you played world brothers 1 you know what you are in for, a cute take on the earth defense force mainline games with the same type of gameplay where one fights hordes of different enemies with 4 characters which one can freely choose from.This game feels a bit more challenging then the previous installment of world brothers due to more enemies on the map it feels like but no heavy jump and so far is good fun to play. Dialogue wise I am missing the tidbits about the different countries and such, but it is good to see characters from 1 making a re-appearance and the tone is kept light hearted.I was pleasantly surprised to not only see older edf enemies but also the ones from edf 6 appear in this game.If one is a fan of the earth defense force mainline franchise or world brothers this is a nice game to get especially as it has more levels then world brothers 1 and some tweaks to mechanics which make the gameplay better.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS 2

_childDocuments_.review: I gave this one some time.  Love all EDF games, even Iron Rain which I think is great, but World Brothers was just too silly and cartoonist for me. I don't like the skill system or the armor award system.   Kept getting pulled back and finally gave a positive review.  Much better than my initial impression.Now World Brothers 2 comes along.  More of the same, but really improved.  Extra action to use in combat, more variety, more missions, better graphics, better everything.  A great improvement.  It is a thumbs game and really delivers winner for the EDF line of products.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS 2

_childDocuments_.review: I love it! The humor is back in force, and the new sisters and brothers are fun to explore. A little bit of Quality of Life aswell, in missions select you can see which brothers and sisters you can find on the map. Not specific ones, but category's, like EDF 6 characters can be found on this map, together with World brothers.The first two missions I was already laughing my butt off. Its a very solid sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS 2

_childDocuments_.review: Earth Defense Force: World Brothers 2 builds upon its predecessor by introducing elements from Earth Defense Force 6 including the Wing Diver Shooter class, more than 100 unique characters, and over 100 missions. Earth Defense Force: World Brothers 2 tells the story of what happened to the voxel (cube) Earth after the events of the first installment. Brothers from across the world reunite to face an unprecedented threat brought about by an all-new enemy that threatens to tear the Earth apart all over again. To restore peace to the voxel Earth, the Earth Defense Force has been dispatched for an emergency mission the likes of which no one has ever seen before! Featuring a unique voxel art style, epic four-player team battles, and filled with more love for the EDF series than ever before, players must stand together to save the world once more. Earth Defense Force move out.

name: Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name
detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition About the Game DELUXE EDITION INCLUDES: Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name Legendary Fighter Pack Floating in the bay, away from the prying eyes of the public, is a mysterious container ship known as the Castle. At its center lies the Coliseum, and three legendary yakuza have entered the battle arena as playable characters. Enter the Coliseum and play as or alongside: Goro Majima – The Mad Dog of Shimano Taiga Saejima – The Slayer of Eighteen Daigo Dojima – 6th Chairman of the Tojo Clan Claim victory with these allies in the ultimate showdown! ERASE YOUR PAST TO PROTECT YOUR FUTURE Once a legendary yakuza, Kazuma Kiryu faked his own death and abandoned his name for the sake of protecting his family. Now, he is thrust into conflict by a mysterious figure attempting to drive him out of hiding. Under the codename “Joryu,” Kiryu embarks on a gripping action narrative with bone-shattering combat in vibrant locations filled with exciting characters and activities. ULTIMATE COMBAT WITH TWO HIGH-IMPACT FIGHTING STYLES Dynamically switch between the Yakuza and Agent fighting styles in visceral melee combat. With the Yakuza style, strike fear into enemies by unleashing wildly aggressive moves powered by Kiryu’s unparalleled strength and flair. Or up the ante with the Agent style by delivering blows with absolute speed and precision, while using an array of high-tech gadgets like electrified bind wires to stun enemies then send them flying. Strategically adapt to the situation and leverage both styles to dominate and destroy hordes of enemies. ENDLESS ENTERTAINMENT Whether you're brawling in the secret Battle arena, singing a new karaoke song, enjoying a drink at the live-action cabaret club, or racing in the pocket circuit, the world offers a variety of immersive experiences. An intriguing informant named Akame also provides thrilling sub-missions, drawing you into an epic showdown that unfolds the more you explore and enjoy Sotenbori and Yokohama. LIKE A DRAGON: INFINITE WEALTH SPECIAL TRIAL VERSION ALSO INCLUDED! After completing Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name game, a Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth Special Trial Version will be unlocked for you to enjoy! This game may be updated over time and have paid for and free additional content released for it. Please be aware that this may increase the minimum requirements for running the game above the specification stated here English voice will be implemented in a post-launch patch distribution

_childDocuments_.review: After playing all Yakuza/Like a Dragon games that are available on Steam, I can't say either this is a must play or a skippable entry.Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name takes place in parallel to Yakuza Like A Dragon (Like a Dragon 7) and you play as Kazuma Kiryu (now using a fake name "Joryu"), the classic protagonist of the series. Planned as a DLC package for Like a Dragon 8 Infinite Wealth, Gaiden is shorter than most entries and feel like a lot of its parts are made with less budget and time.That being said, this is still a very entertaining game from RGG. These guys know how to make the most out of a small open world and the grounded setting. Plenty of minigames, progressions, and side stories that are worth sinking your time into, not only because they're fun and have depths beyond the surfaces, but they also give you resources to unlock upgrades for Joryu in combat. And trust me, you'd want to have some upgrades.The combat system in Gaiden is somewhere between Judgement, Lost Judgement, and Yakuza 5. Joryu has 2 fighting styles, Yakuza and Agent. Agent is a brand-new style to the series, it focuses on fast and long combo string, 3 consecutive side-stepping, and sci-fi gadgets like drones, Spider Man web wires, rocket-powered shoes, and cigarette bombs. Yakuza is a combination of Dragon Engine Kiryu's Dragon of Dojima style and some moves from his older games. Yakuza style's attack speed can feel quite slow, but not overly clunky like Yakuza 6, similar to Judgement. This game also features enemy-juggling, which was first seen in Judgement and streamlined in Lost Judgement. Joryu's combat rhythm and capabilities can open up even the stronger foes for some nasty juggling combo. While juggling and gadgets sound fun and powerful, enemy AI in Gaiden seem tampered to be more aggressive and opportunistic in their strikes. Lost Judgement (the latest Dragon Engine game) seemed to have AI's that are afraid to hit the player and often leave you alone while you combo attacks either regularly or while juggling. Meanwhile Gaiden's enemy AI doesn't care where you are in the arena or what you're doing, they will try to hit you and get you off a combo. So most of the time while you're fighting multiple foes, you'll have to utilize everything to create yourself some space or dispatch the weaker enemies quickly. The Heat mechanic also returns, but it is nerfed pretty harshly. The Heat bar that allows you to use Heat actions or activate Extreme Heat goes up rather slowly in Gaiden. So, either you have to stock up on heat-regenerating items or use it very sparingly, either way you cannot spam it like in the older games. is highly dependent on a player's investment to the series. I'd say that if you only played 1 or 2 Kiryu games, then Gaiden wouldn't be as worthy to you. But if you're invested in the series, the story, the gameplay, and universe, I'd say this is a must-play, implying you haven't played it already. This game tells a very interesting and emotion part of Kiryu's life story but not necessarily required to enjoy future or older games.One more thing I find weird (and noticed when it got worse) in this game is the lighting. Most RGG games are fine with their lighting, even with Kiwami 1&2's green filter, scenes from those game don't look out of place and offer a consistent imagery experience throughout each one. But Gaiden has a focus on darker shadows and overall color level contrast of the image. This might be to some people's preference but I just find it a bit jarring. Seeing bright particle effects over a dimly lit environment, while contact and cast shadows are sometimes too dark and sometimes too bright that they don't seem to exist, threw me off from the experience a bit. Some scenes nailed the high-contrast lighting perfectly, such as the prologue scene with blue and red lights on each side and the shadows are dark and threatening. While some scenes like the final boss fight has less detailed lighting, overly reliant on baked and static textures and colors. It's a good game for screenshots sometimes, but not most of the time imo.I still give it a 7.5/10, a good Yakuza game, through and through. Even with shortcomings from short development time and branding as a side-game, it still offers a completed Yakuza experience through good story, memorable characters, cool set-pieces, abundant side activities, soundtracks, and satisfying combat system.
_childDocuments_.name: Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name

_childDocuments_.review: The promise of the game was to serve as a bridge that filled in Joryu's story, while also being "short".Well it definitely fulfills the latter as the story in the game feels like a single chapter from LAD 4 or 5.However in that short time the story manages to present the big emotional moments and sudden twists that make the series what it is.The game play is solid, providing access to the more polished versions of the Dragon Engine combat. The control scheme for the Agent style could have used some additional tuning, but the options it presents are quite fun and handy for what it was designed for.The sub stories are mostly absent, replaced largely for simple missions or various fetch quests. This is a definite factor in making the game a "short one". The on-the-road quests are a fine way to provide something to do while running around the city, while the missions provide more sizable rewards.In the end it does feel like the story could have gotten a tiny bit more fleshed out, but the game does end on a very high note so no big complaints thanks to that.

Literally a monster.Banger OST, just like in every other Yakuza game.The new arena mode is propably the best one in the series, being able to play as multiple different characters is so cool. You have a fat guy with a giant cannon, a certain gorilla built detective, a ninja and many others.I also have to mention the Infinite Wealth demo, which is just an icing on top of the cake. Literally makes you so hyped for the full release in 2024.Do I recommend this game? Yes. At full price? YES. Should you wait for a sale? Maybe. If you're a fan of the series you propably bought it already anyway.Better than 0? There are no better or worse Yakuza games, they're equally good, with some cons there and there.

_childDocuments_.review: Again a hard to not recommend game in the Yakuza series. But I'm still going to, here's why.As is the case with most Yakuza games, the world within the game doesn't follow its own rules. This makes following the story silly and frustrating. First your character is plowing through enemies as if they were cardboard. Next you'll watch a 5 minute movie about your character struggling with a piece of said cardboard. This is supposed to create tension and motivation for the story, but since the world already lost most its believability, it's hard to keep invested.Next we have what's actually happening in the story. Well... not much really?! The main story is very simple and short. There are side missions that you mostly plow through, and as usual they don't have much story to them. They work as an excuse to beat up people but that's it.The coliseum fights are somewhat fun, but there's only so much of those until you've seen enough. Maybe some more variety would keep things interesting? The fight system also feels somewhat more limited and boring compared to previous titles. Things are mostly smooth but it's just very repetitive even with full abilities. With only two styles and quite clear use cases for them, fights start to quickly repeat the same pattern.One of my surprising personal favorite features in previous titles was eating at the restaurants. It brought my mind back to Japan (where I've visited a couple of times), and I always got very hungry watching and listening to Kiryu eating. Unfortunately that feature has been basically removed, as you don't gain any experience from eating anymore and the eating animations aren't that delicious anymore.It's not a bad game at all, but unlike Yakuza 0, I don't think I'll remember or miss what happened in this game after a few years. And hence, I'd only recommend this to people addicted to Kiryu beating up people.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent entry in the Like a Dragon series. Gameplay is a wonderful balance with the new Agent Style being a great blend of rapid AoE hits and throws, and the Yakuza Style encompassing the best past combat. The story, while short, is thrilling, well paced, and chock full of memorable characters. While Sotenbori feels small, especially compared to an entry like Lost Judgement or Like a Dragon, they found a way to fit what feels like every nook and cranny of Sotenbori with something to do. With the return of Pocket Circuit and Pool, and other staples such as Poker, Blackjack, Koi Koi, Oichi-Kabu, the dreaded Mahjong, and the wonderful Karaoke, there's more than enough to sink your teeth into. Even if you get all the achievements, you are far from all the completion markers in game.  If you're a fan of the series, this is certainly something to look into. Its an excellent suppliment leading up to Infinite Wealth, and with the tight refinement each previous Like a Dragon/RGG entry has received, the tightly tuned game play will keep you locked in. Highly recommend.P.S, runs absolutely amazingly on the Steam Deck. Like, shockingly well.

_childDocuments_.review: The Man Who Erased His Name (will call this Joryu-game from now on) is a spin-off of Like a Dragon Gaiden that takes place in parallel to Yakuza: Like a Dragon or Yakuza 7. Joryu-game expects you to know the story from the main game, and will talk about secret reveals from Y7, and will show you quick flashbacks from Y7 to keep you up to date where the story is. So if you haven't played the Y7 you'll either be lost or spoiled. Joryu-games returns to being a brawler game, and follows the story of Joryu, which might be very similar to someone you know is really not Kiryu. He put on shades and different suit, so you will never recognise him. Like superman, alright? It's Joryu. Whole 2 different letters in the name, so you won't ever get it's the same person. And Kiryu is dead anyway.As far as Yakuza games are concerned this is a minigame. The story is pretty short, and even doing all substories and side activities will clock you at less than 40 hours. The game is being sold at a lower price than full entries, so that's fine. And it also has tons of Sega retro games included, so in theory you could spend hours upon hours just played the emulated games.Joryu gets two battle styles in this game. Brawler/Yakuza style that is similar to red styles from the older games. Hard hitting, counter attacks etc. There's also completely new Agent style, where Joryu uses Bond-esque gadgets as part of his arsenal. You start with spider-man-ish web slinger that allows you to disable opponents and throw them around, or steal their weapons. But as the game progresses you get 3 more gadgets. I found 3 of them to be very fun to use, but the cigarette bomb took too much time to explode, and as such was a pain to get working properly. This time the action takes place in Sotenbori, and while it reuses the old map you get it with ray traced shadows, and man, Sotenbori never looked so good. There's also completely new map that takes center stage in the game, and you get there pretty early on, but that's as far as I go.I didn't like what they did with substories. Usually they would jump on you naturally as you walk trough the streets. But in this game you have central hub where an informant will tell you about all the requests that people have. Then you go to the place and get trough typical substories. That makes them feel much less natural, and honestly a bit less fun. It doesn't help that there aren't really that many of them, and most of them are related to gathering party members for one of minigames.There are also exclamation points tossed all around the map with people wanting some small things from you. Usually short fetch quests. Things like "bring me tissues" were thrown into this category too. It's pretty similar in quality to the mobile app micro-quests from Y6, but a bit better and less repetitive.The story is, as always, a strong point. Not gonna lie, a grown man is gonna cry at the ending. That's what Yakuza does to you. You would think the story of spin-off would be weak, but I really liked it. Being short and moving at fast pace only made it better. It also made more sense for me how name-erasing thing works for Joryu. In Y6 it felt a bit far-fetched.Most of the side-content is tied to battle arena, where you have a lot of matches to go trough. As you go trough them you will also unlock some boss battles on the arena. This means that for most bosses you won't be able to use items in-battle. Though that is not a problem, as it's probably the easiest Yakuza game I've played. Even the final secret boss is mostly a pushover once you get their attack pattern... and you'll get it within the first battle and win this first battle most likely. It's easy in this game to get 2300 or so defence and be invincible, and your blows can one hit KO most of the enemies even with pretty mediocre attack scores. That said the arena battles are pretty fun, but I think the most advertised team battles are least fun out of the bunch. All in all very decent entry into the Yakuza series, and closes the story of Kir... Joryu much better than Yakuza 6 did. If you're enfranchised player you probably already bought and played it anyway, but if you're new to the series you should start with Y0, Y1 Kiwami or Y7. This is best played after Y6 and Y7. Still, recommended, just be sure to do your homework before playing.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: - 9.5/10- Worth full price- Should NOT be your first yakuza game.Combat is the most refined Kiryu's ever been. A lot of changes that make wanting to learn the combat more fun. Never felt like there were any unfair fights, and you can't rely on heat actions as much encouraging you to master your moveset and new juggle mechanics.Side content is surprisingly expansive. Best coliseum mode in any LAD game, funny side missions, and tighter systems that all interact with each other. I didn't feel like the Akame network was tacked on and I love that. It's also really well tied-in to the story, which is the best part of the game. I loved the story. It's basically a "mini" sequel to Yakuza 6, so existing fans will get a lot out of it. Big disclaimer- there's obvious padding in the first half of the game. But its Yakuza padding- used to onboard you to the game's side content. Which is great anyways so I didn't mind! Just when I felt like it was going to ruin the game's pacing, it stopped and the story REALLY picked up during the latter chapters. I don't want to spoil, but you can only fully appreciate the final hours of this game if you've played all the previous ones. It has the most bittersweet but cathartic ending I've experienced in media. It actually ruined me, and pushed my score for the game wayyy higher.So yeah, Gaiden exceeded my expectations. Play it please. If you're a longtime fan you owe it to yourself to.

_childDocuments_.review: It's difficult to review this game without spoiling plot points in Yakuza 6 and Yakuza Like a Dragon so I'll just point out pros and cons so you can decide if you want to get this chapter of the saga or would rather watch it on a video.[PROS]- STORY: The story picks up where Yakuza 6 ended. I feel like many people might have had issues with the way the story ended, so this one tries to expand on what happened after the events of 6. And the story happens at the same time Yakuza Like a Dragon's plot happened, so if you played that one before you'll be able to piece together pieces and understand better the reason behind some of the plot points in that one too. And the quality is pretty good, without spoiling anything the ending had me fighting the tears off.- COMBAT: I've heard multiple opinions on the combat of this game, but as someone that has yet to play Judgement the combat in this game feels polished. Again, I jumped from the combat of 6 into this one and it feels so much more polished. Game has two styles: Agent - A style that is characterized for being ultra fast but low damage and Yakuza - Basically the style of 6 where you hit like a truck but attacks are way slower, leaving you open to getting hurt. So, if you liked the combat in 6, it's here. And if you wanted new combat you also get that and can easily switch mid-combat with the push of a button.- SIDE CONTENT: Lots of minigames to play. It doesn't really introduce a whole lot of new stuff, rather it brings those minigames that were more popular and polishes them, giving us sort of a "Best of" selection of things to do. Things like Pocket Racing, karaoke, coliseum battles, they all make a very strong comeback.[CONS]- STORY: This game is the shortest in the entire saga. And it's not an exageration, it's VERY short. I don't know how regional pricing might work for other countries, but right now this is the most expensive Yakuza game in all of Steam, so having a game that you can complete in around 35 hours (I took my sweet time to play it, tried all minigames, completed most of the side content, walked around the map instead of running and still finished it in 32 hours) for that price is one thing you might wanna keep in mind. The quality is there, RGG put out a fantastic product, but it's short.- COMBAT: While the combat is polished, the fact that the game is so short gives us a smaller list of heat actions and all of the abilities are gained with money rather than experience or training. Depending on how much you play the side content you might be super weak the entire game or super strong, there's no really in-between. And the game ends before you can get properly comfortable with your fighting style.- SIDE CONTENT: Again, the fact that the game is so short makes this part a gray area, while there are plenty of side activities and these are well done you don't really experience a whole lot before the game ends. The number of side stories in this game is surprisingly small, and now instead of getting them by walking around and helping the residents of the city, you are given side stories from a side-quest hub in your hideout which I don't know ... for me it sort of robs the charm these games have. You're not a good samaritan helping people anymore, you're an agent hired to do odd jobs. And I know it's only for this game but I can't not mention the tonal shift the game takes. Yakuza games are always a serious story with a side of silly. This game is very serious from beginning to end, couple of side stories are funny but overall the game mantains a very serious tone which might charm some and polarize others.[ACHIEVEMENTS]This must be the easiest game in the series to 100%. I've seen people do it in around 45 hours. The Completion List means nothing, you don't have to finish it on a high difficulty, and I'm pretty sure you can complete all the achievements in your first playthrough if you have the patience for it. Personally, it disappoints me a little, but I also understand how it can be due to the length of the game.[SUMMARY]Overall a very strong addition to the series. One that in a way was needed to tie up all of Kiryu's journey on a nice bow and send him for what might be his final adventure in Infinite Wealth. I'm very satisfied with the product I got, but if you think the price might be too much and want to wait for a discount that is a very valid option.

_childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name is a decent addition to the series and offers an enjoyable even if a little short roller coaster ride of a story along with yet another iteration of the brawler style combat. As a long time fan of the series I had my fun with the game but at same time I couldn't help but to feel like I was playing through a glorified expansion sold at a premium and one where it might be a little difficult to justify the price tag unless you plan to do most of the side content as the main story is really short.Combat system is a fun iteration of the older brawler combat which is a welcome improvement after the somewhat lackluster combat of Kiwami 2 and Yakuza 6, although it isn't without its flaws and the more you level up the more those blemishes start to show especially in terms of balancing. In addition to the familiar fighting style of Kiryu game introduces a new agent style which focuses bit more on finesse, stylish counters and utilizes some rather hilarious spy gadgets that you unlock as you progress through the story.As expected of a Yakuza title there is a plethora of minigames and a chunk of side content, minigames could be described as a sort of "best of" collection of various things you've seen along the years with some new things sprinkled in here and there, side content on the other hand felt like bit of a letdown. Substories for the most part are rather generic and a far cry from some of the more whacky and memorable ones the series is known for, combine that with some bland "fetch quests" that the game introduces - I think the best way to describe them would be disappointing.That being said I had my fun with the game and enjoyed the roughly 26 hours it took me to beat it on professional difficulty while doing all of the substories, almost all of the fetch quests and a good chunk of the minigames. If you're a huge fan of the series I think this is an easy recommendation even if it might be worth playing the game on game pass or waiting for discounts instead of purchasing it at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to begin by summarizing my history of the Yakuza franchise. Being a Yakuza fan, I enjoyed Yakuza 0 and thought Yakuza: Like A Dragon was a masterpiece. But I wasn't particularly fond of Yakuza 1-6. Among my reasons are dull gameplay, repetitive game and level design in every game, similar stories with ridiculous plot twists, boring main characters (excluding Akiyama), same map in each game etc. As you might have guessed, I've had issues with the repetitive nature of this series. I considered the Yakuza series the Call of Duty of the East, even though Yakuza is much better in almost every aspect. But Yakuza: Like a Dragon changed it all for me. Thankfully, the combat system had changed completely. It was extremely well made and we got a main character with actual feelings and one who displayed them. Ichiban is such a likable character and I enjoyed seeing him as the protagonist dearly. I completed Yakuza LaD 100% for the first time in a Yakuza game. That's how much I love the game.After all this positive work from Ryu Ga Gotoku Studios, I had high hopes about this game, so I pre-ordered it. I feel sorry to report that this is a game with the same formula as Yakuza 1-6 and I didn't enjoy most of it. A generic plot with characters that I am never going to remember after beating the game, predictable plot twists, and an undercooked villain. I mostly have no issues with the feel of the combat (except Yakuza 3) but this one feels kinda off. I cannot put my finger on it. One of the selling points of the game, the new "agent combat style" looks fun, but sadly is very weak compared to the "yakuza style", so I barely played the new style. They couldn't adjust the balance between them.Let me move on to the positives of Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name. The most important topic of the game: Yes, the cabaret club is very fun just like the previous ones. This one's slightly better because they made it live-action this time. Secondly, I can see that most of RGG's effort has gone into creating the castle. Yeah, the castle looks amazing and has cool stuff in it to spend time with. The graphics are getting better with every game. The interiors look extremely good, but the outdoor graphics need a little bit more work. I won't go into spoilers, but I just cannot skip that finale scene when Kiryu was holding a tablet. Phenomenal scene. It made me tear up! I hope it results in something beautiful for Kiryu in the next game. That sums up the positives of this game.Unfortunately, the best point of the game is the playable Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth Trial after you beat the main game. During that hour, I had an absolute blast and it's barely visible that LaD 8 is their focus and this is only a cash grab. Dear SEGA, I know the main reason you made this game was to please Kiryu and the Brawler fans out there, other than making an extra 50 bucks per purchase, of course. But please just let Kiryu and this dated combat system alone. Because it surely doesn't work anymore for me. People will get used to turn-based combat. Look at Baldur's Gate 3 for an example. Just keep doing amazing RPGs after Like a Dragon 8 as well. I am immensely excited about that game!Follow My

Ultimately, I believe that this game may be a bit rough for those who are not familiar with the series already and may be a bit short for those who aren't super into the franchise or aren't one of those who force themselves to complete the game 100% but outside of that, it still holds up modestly well to the other entries that precede it.

_childDocuments_.review: Consider Like a Dragon: Gaiden to be something of a "clip-show" episode in the grand scheme of Yakuza/LAD. The main purpose of the game seems to be to remind you of key moments, and activities that Kiryu has engaged in throughout the series, framed under the guise of explaining why Kiryu appeared in Yakuza 7/Like a Dragon. Does it succeed in this case? I would say largely yes.The two combat styles are both very fun, although the "agent" style does take some getting used to for it to properly click. The plot of the game is ...fine. I don't feel like it really told anything that was needed from a narration standpoint, but it does allow for us to see a more fragile side of Kiryu near the end, so you could argue that everything depicted in the game is just appetiser for that "moment". Still, I would say the journey is still worth it for fans of the franchise.You'll get to see a few fan favourite activities and character cameos (albeit some in not the original form you remember), but the story is very short and to the point. Despite the price of the game you should very much consider this game a "tide over" until Infinite Wealth releases. It makes no attempt to try to be as elaborate as the other games in the series and you can basically completely platinum the game in around 20 to 25 hours if you're not taking your sweet time.Of course, I can't ignore the price either. Here in Australia this game is 82 dollars. 91 if you get the version with the DLC included. Now, consider that this game is only 5 chapters rather than the usual 14 to 15 and the price gets a lot harder to justify. Still, the game is fun to play and it has a lot of good ideas like the character customisation options. It also has a demo for Infinite Wealth if you're curious to try it and don't care much about spoiling stuff in advance.I'd say the game is worth it ... but I'd also suggest maybe waiting for a sale to actually buy it. 90 bucks is a tall order for essentially half the experience you'd normally get. I was lucky enough to have gotten gifted the game by a friend, so I had little complaints but I could see the price point being a major complaint for others.

_childDocuments_.review: Bringing back a character whose story had been concluded close to 8 years ago is no easy task.To say that I was skeptical about this game's story and the impact it would have on the legacy of one of my favorite characters would sure be an understatement. RGG somehow managed to beautifully tie everything together and also deliver an even better send off to the legend of Kazuma Kiryu than his initial "final Game" Yakuza 6.Everything that was missing from Yakuza 6, due to its rocky development is here.- better combat- better minigames/side activities- better bosses- more light on the old cast of charactersSome of us were definitely expecting this game to be a cashgrab, a cheap asset flip, just to cash in on people's love for the character. They definitely cut some corners in the very short 6 months of development, but the end product is one I'm more than satisfied with.I only have a few small gripes with this game:- The Coliseum (while cool on paper) is very underwhelming,movesets of pre-existing characters were butchered and really don't offer any kind of depth.The huge team battles are also just a cluster ♥♥♥♥.- The Dragon/Yakuza Style is extremely broken and just kills bosses with like 2 combos.- Small pacing issues in an already short story: you could erase Akame from the plot and it probably wouldn't change a thing. I found her inclusion to be quite useless. She is just a tool for you to start grinding.- The flow of combat feels a bit off in big groups at times.But other than that, Gaiden offers basically anything a Yakuza fan could ask for.Lastly I would like to say:Nishitani III has become one of my favorite bosses in the series, this guy is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome.

_childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name is by far the shortest game in the Like a Dragon series so far, and it only took me just under 14 hours to beat it while going for quite a bit of the side content along the way. However, make no mistake, this is probably one of the best games in the series to date, with solid combat, story, and setting.The combat is by far the most fluid and fun in the series to date, beating out Lost Judgment as it takes all the strengths from that game and combines it with new and interesting mechanics to make it more interesting. Kiryu has 2 styles, Agent and Yakuza. Yakuza is very similar to Kiryu's Dragon of Dojima style from 1-6, with a few extra moves added in, but the Agent style is completely different, with 4 different gadgets to use during combat, and a moveset that is more suited to dealing with large groups of enemies.The story, without spoiling too much, perfectly bridges the gap between the end of Yakuza 6 and the end of Yakuza: Like a Dragon, showcasing Kiryu's perspective during that time. It also gives you extra info about what some characters (I won't say who) from a previous game are up to in the present. The game itself is set in Sotenbori (with a brief section in Isezaki Ijincho towards the beginning of the game) now expanded to include the park which was noticeably absent in previous iterations of Sotenbori in the Dragon Engine. It may seem like a small change but it really makes Sotenbori feel a lot bigger and more lively with a wider variety of places to visit.Finally, there's the part I was most excited for before this game released, which is the trial of Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth included after beating the main story. I haven't played much of it so far but it's an amazing reward which offers a sneak peek into what the next game will be like.Overall, if you enjoyed Yakuza 6 or Yakuza: Like a Dragon, I'd definitely recommend purchasing this game, as there is so much that's offered in addition to a preview of the next game in the series before it's released.

In the coliseum, you can play as different characters, who have their own movesets and special attacks.Gaiden has Akame network, where you can get your "substories." While it takes away the surprise of walking into a substory, it keeps them all neatly in one place. Characters in substories can become your allies in the coliseum, which is a smooth way of linking different aspects of the game together.Gaiden is the first Yakuza game where you can customize your outfit, so get S-S-STYLISH!

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game and got my last achievement so I'm going into this review pretty fresh. Like a Dragon: Gaiden is an absolutely phenomenal entry in a series that I've grown to adore. The gameplay continues to be refined with each entry, and I'd say this is about on par with Lost Judgement in regards to combat. Though there are only two stances, the insane gadgets you unlock for Agent stance more than make up for it. The extreme variety of side content is here as always, with most everything being an iteration on existing minigames to make them a bit more engaging, most notably the clan battles from Yakuza Kiwami 2 and Yakuza 6 are actual battles you participate in instead of that weird tower defense thing. On that note, this is one of the best iterations of The Coliseum in the entire franchise, though there is one specific substory fight that you'll need to level up your clan for. The map size isn't particularly large, roughly the size of the Majima Saga from Yakuza Kiwami 2, but there is considerably more content and variety packed into here than you'd think. If you're a fan of these games you can buy this with no worries, you'll be satisfied for sure.Story is shockingly engaging for something that's filling the gap between Yakuza 6 and Like a Dragon, I genuinely wasn't expecting to be as interested in anything outside of Kiryu himself but that wasn't the case at all. Akame is an excellent addition to the cast and is a joy on screen, pretty much every character punches well above their weight in terms of what you'd expect from a spinoff entry. I cannot recommend this game enough if you're a fan of Yakuza and Kiryu in particular, longtime fans will have an absolutely ton of references that they can pick up on. On top of all of this, there's a demo for Infinite Wealth included so you can get your feet wet for that entry. RGG Studios has turned into one of my favorite developers to watch right now and this game is a testament to their skill. It's absolutely unbelievable that this was made in six months.

_childDocuments_.review: Gaiden is an extremely special experience. While Yakuza 6: The Song of Life served as a phenomenal and tear-jerking send-off to one of the most iconic and important protagonists in gaming history, Gaiden doubles down in more ways than one and further explores Kiryu Kazuma. Story-wise, Gaiden is masterfully written as a love letter to both Kiryu and longtime fans while also taking us on a rollercoaster ride of his most important experiences, hitting every essential story-beat you need to know what you're going to get with him in Yakuza 8 if you started with Yakuza 7. As impressive as this is, what I didn't expect from Gaiden was for the story to retroactively improve games such as Yakuza 5 with some of the most intriguing twists in the series. The finale alone is worth the asking price, but if that isn't enough, Gaiden brings back many fan-favorite mini games such as Pocket Circuit, the Coliseum(best it's ever been), Karaoke, and even ones that have been absent for quite a while such as Pool. Combat-wise, the juggling that was re-introduced in a big way in Lost Judgment is arguably the most consistent and satisfying it's ever been in the series, and with a heightened focus on the actual combat as opposed to an over-reliance on Heat Actions, makes the combat so interesting to explore and experiment with, which you'll naturally do when tackling the 50+ optional but super rewarding Coliseum battles in the game.11/10 would cry my eyes out at the ending again.

_childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon Gaiden is an amazing, short but well-polished title, considering it took only six months of game development.Similar to other fans of the series, it was a joy to return back to an action brawler genre game with Kiryu ("Joryu") at the helm as the main protagonist.  The new agent style, probably inspired from James Bond, was quite unique and interesting to play as, especially when clearing large mobs.  Though for most of the game's key bosses, the tried and tested yakuza style with heavy hitting moves still held strong, especially with pretty cool juggling physics thrown into the mix too.Another key feature was the upgraded coliseum which many agree must be the best iteration in the series thus far.  It didn't felt like a chore as each mode has its own unique challenges, which kept things interesting.  I thoroughly enjoyed the chance to recruit other fighters and form my own team to fight in the large scale battles.  Definitely a thumbs up to also be able to include and even control the legendary yakuza fighters - daigo, majima and saejima, in these arena battles.Substories were interestingly woven with the unique Akame network storyline which felt fresh in the very familiar backdrop of Sotenbori.  Completionist achievements were very manageable and it was a really nice touch to also be able to re-experience Sega Racing Classic / Daytona USA 2 - many fond childhood memories of this at arcades!The main storyline was well-paced, given it's meant to be a short title.  It helped to fill the many supposed plot gaps between Yakuza 6 and Yakuza 7, whilst also featuring a new niche location being the Castle.  I was blown away by all the fancy neon bright lights of the area, which truly brought out that premier nightlife feeling in the map.Overall, RGG studio never ceases to amaze fans with their work, be it large scale numbered titles or even the smaller titles such as Like a Dragon Gaiden.  I'm personally looking forward to sink a sizable amount of time into their next title - Infinite Wealth.

_childDocuments_.review: Weird how I seem to be playing Like a Dragon games more often than I’ve ever played the typical Ubisoft games, but the burnout is far less noticeable… Seriously, though, RGG Studio has been putting out games set in this universe not just annually lately, but often with several games coming out the same year. And in situations like with this game, I’m not sure if there was the point. Not that I disliked Like a Dragon Gaiden, quite the opposite, but it does feel almost unnecessary at points…Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name is a new entry in the long running series of titles that erased their old international name (which was Yakuza), but remained mainly open world action adventure titles with beat ’em up combat and cinematic stories. This entry, as the title itself says, is a side story that is set during the events of Yakuza: Like a Dragon, but despite the short visit to Isezaki Ijincho (the main setting of that game), most of the events happen in the classic Sotenbori that was originally seen in Yakuza 2.At this point I usually write that the “open world” section is not big but is otherwise dense with stories, but it isn’t exactly the case in this game. It’s not fully embracing a typical open world onslaught of icons pointing to busywork tasks, but for whatever reason the substories do go in this direction this time around. Not that there are no longer more deep side stories for you to explore, but most of the optional content this time around is far closer to how substories were in the earliest entries, with simple “bring me X item” tasks. While the longer more involved substories rarely do anything interesting even when their premise is good. There’s one wonderful crossover exception, but apart from it, the substories are pretty weak in this one.Same goes for the main story, really. You do get to learn more about some secret agent-like society that was first hinted upon in Yakuza 6 and some of the characters shown there seem to be set up to reappear in a later game. But as far as the current story goes, you get some minor details and some new emotional scenes talking about things you already knew from other games and it’s not particularly fulfilling. Some of the new characters are really nice and Kiryu, for a change, has more range in his personality, but it’s not a game that will interest anyone with its story but the biggest fans of the series.So what did I like about Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name? It plays really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ well. Just like with Lost Judgment, combat controls are extremely fun and better than they’ve ever been in the series. Every fight just flows well and provides enough challenge (on a highest difficulty) for those who like it, while providing a perfect amount of challenge (on other difficulties) for people who just want to have fun. Granted, some mini-games still go really unfair, unless you grind or look up best solutions, but those are an exception and most of the time this game is just really fun to play.Yet it puts it in a weird spot. If you like RGG universe games for gameplay and it alone can interest you, this is a good game for you. It’s unlikely to become your favorite, but it’s really really fun. But if you like the RGG universe for the story, you really can skip this one and not miss out on anything the games won’t recap if needed later on. I liked it, but at the same time, it was a rather forgettable even if enjoyable time.

_childDocuments_.review: Deliciously tightly packaged Yakuza!I'm gonna be honest and say that at first I didn't expect much from this game. It seemed like recycled content with some Kiryu story that could have been part of the other games. But as more info got out and I learned more my interest got picked. Now I regard this among my favorites.I think right now my ranking goes something like this: Y0, Y7, YK2, Gaiden, YK1, Y5, Y6, Y3, Y4.In the end I feel that although shorter, this is a complete Yakuza package. Everything we've come to love and expect is here. Twisting heavy drama story, whacky side quests, great minigames, memorable characters, awkward content to explain to your loved ones, Japanese weirdness and so on. The difference is that the game does all this without any bloat.I really liked how they portrayed Kiryu in this one and made him a bit more human. I also really enjoyed some of the new characters and how they got developed throughout the game. And I loved Akame! More Akame in the next games or we riot!I think RGG packaged the story they had with just the right amount of side stuff and fluff to leave you wanting just a bit more in the end. Which sucks! I was intending to wait a little to get Infinite Wealth cheaper but who am I kidding?

_childDocuments_.review: 9.5/10An absolutely beautiful love letter to Kiryu and the "Yakuza" saga of Like a Dragon. While it seems Infinite Wealth will be our farewell to Kiryu, Gaiden feels like a heartfelt farewell to the games that introduced us to him.The gameplay was a lot of fun. I'll admit, I definitely favored one style over the other, but even primarily using one style throughout most of the game, I still had a blast playing. As per usual, this game is chock full of minigames and side stories to invest your time in to, and they are absolutely worth it! Also in usual RGG fashion, the soundtrack was phenomenal. While being a game focused on Kiryu, it featured a cast of primarily new characters, and I loved them. Akame was an instant favorite for me. Shishido and Hanawa were strong favorites as well. But the story is where this game absolutely shines. It maintained continuity from the stories that came before, while also building up immense anticipation for the next game to come. The ending in particular was phenomenal.This game was absolutely meant for the Yakuza fans who have been along for Kiryu's entire journey. If you're new to the series, this absolutely should not be your starting point. But it is a fantastic destination to look forward to.

_childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon Gaiden is unlike previous LAD games more of a side story like experience, but even then it's still a LAD game. With beautiful visuals, it still has the classic vibe and side stories/minigames but with a much more compact story. And man, what a story it was! Also my personal goty. I'm going to keep this very short considering that the story isn't all that long eitherso I'd rather want you people to experience it yourself. But man to me this was the game everyone (me included) neededthat weren't agreeing with the way Y6 ended and used some of its characters.Overall the story is great man, lots of intense and crazy moments happening, with some fun stuff as well. But I am gonna tell you this, this game broke my soul man :')This game also overtook 6 as my favorite Kiryu game. Yeah, it's that good! Gameplay is crazy, the fact that Kiryu has more than 1 style again and for the fact that we can JUGGLE as well in this game. You start with the new style Agent, it's the style that you acquire from the Daidoji, it is basically a mix of Yagami's Crane style with a more Agent like vibe I guess??Either way it's more fast-paced compared to the second style as that is more for a brawler and street fight type way, the move style for agent is more of a martial arts tactical fighting style.Both styles also have a color, for Agent being the color blue and for the other red. Agent style is also a great way to start juggles when going in heat mode. Overall, you're gonna get a lot of Judgment/Lost Judgment vibes when playing the game. But Agent style is not only fighting no, no, you have like 4 gadgets you can use, a spider-man like web/string that comes out of your watch to pull enemies to you or push them away, a cigaret that's basically a bomb. Freaking rocket boots, and drones that can chase enemies.Agent style is crazy hahaha there is so much from it. And of course for the second style we have The Yakuza Style as the game names it (normally being dragon style but oh well). It is vastly improved from the versions of Y6 and Y:K2, being overall much smoother and fleshed out with some changes, new move sets and finishers, he can basically do his iconic kick pose as a finisher. But dude do you kick the ♥♥♥♥ out of enemies when upgrading it oh man enemies went flying hahahahah.I do gotta say this in all honesty, this is I think is the only game where I haven't relied on heat moves as much compared to the other games, I was really mostly just fighting with juggles and charged attacksso that did kinda surprise me a little. Overall the combat in this game great, although a combat speed could have been nicely added, It's good but not LJ level good as that one still takes the cake for best RGG combat let's say it's better than K2 and 6 and on par with JE combat considering that one also has 2 styles. However, one huge new thing has got to be the feature that you can actually personalize Kiryu. That's right full on character customization, I freaking love this feature in this gameand I really hope it doesn't just stay in Gaiden, but actually carries on to other games as well. LAD Gaiden still has the side stuff like Substories and Minigames, as they will always be a core piece of these games. this time you have something called the Akame points, in order to get those Akame points you'll have to do Akame missions/substories, as in this game substories are actually a checklist that you do in order to gain more bonding with Akame, it's kind of unfortunate that it's not randomly like the previous gamesbut as for Kiryu being an Agent like person, it kinda makes sense that he is doing it this way, and either way the substories are still fun to do, especially for some! But you'll have to see it for your self.Mini-games, oh man POCKET CIRCUIT IS ACTUALLY BACK, I love this minigame man, one of my favorite things to do in Y0 and K1, and I'm really glad they brought it back one more final time, aside from that another mini-game that returns to the Dragon Engine is Pool, yes that was missed as well for some odd reason and that is also still fun to play, one other new thing is that some point you'll unlock a hideout that has an actual Sega master system which is pretty nuts, has around 12 games in it, tho some you got to buy at like ebisu pawn something close like that.Also, later in the game you'll unlock a new play environment called The Castle, there it has the casino/Japanese gamble games, a cabaret with LIVE ACTION performances yeah it's super weird honestly, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ does it take so much space around 28 GB????? (0_0?). Outside of that you also got the place where you personalize Kiryu, The Boutique which has all kinds of clothing options.Enemies are your typical street guys or yakuza like the previous games and not the unique types like in LAD7. However, they are very advanced like the enemies in the Judgment games, so when you have a low upgraded Kiryu, be tactical as to how you fight them because lots of them fight back hard. A returning feature to the game is The Colosseum, which also is featured in The Castle, but man is this the best version of the Colosseum we all know.... EVERY FIGHTER IS PLAYABLE, and no I'm serious every fighter in it is playable, if you preordered the game you get playable  (or if you buy it separately as DLC). But ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ actual playable Daigo is nuts, lots of the fighter have their own move sets alto some also have move sets from previous bosses and enemies, pay close attention, and you'll see it. The rest you'll have to see for yourself, as it's too much to say about it. Now, then, the other thing this game does great are the bosses. Every, and I mean every, boss in this game is just great. You do have some mini bosses, but they are also good. But the main bosses? ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, very fun to fight to and to some degree quite challenging, also there is a returning feature that the enemies will use Mortal Reversals, as they were first introduced in LJ, Gaiden also has them for some of its enemies and all the bosses. Now I will stand on this with all my heart, this game has the best final boss fight in all LAD, yep there I said it! Overall just the final boss fight was peak LAD moment it has 3 action phases with the last one having a different OST.... ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, I loved this boss fight. The soundtrack is quite a take cause holy damn this ♥♥♥♥ good! What's surprising is that most of the composing was done by a lot of new people and by some returning composersthat did the OG Y1 and 2. The boss fights, fantastic osts, the battle themes for both styles are really great, long battle themes also great, personally the main theme Fading Away hits in every spot for me that's some tearjerker stuff right there if you just even read the lyrics. The third phase of the final boss really nails it for me man, I've been constantly listening to the soundtrack a lot! It really is still something that RGG studios does for every LAD game of theirs.Having an absolute banger of a soundtrack!That concludes my review for Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name.Even though it's shorter, this game was very much quality over quantity to me from the gameplay, the great story and characters, and even the side stuff.I really hope we get more Gaiden games, maybe for other characters like Majima or Akiyamathere are tons of options! I also hope this is really not the last Kiryu Action game...Cause if so, I'm really gonna miss it :'((9.8)

_childDocuments_.review: You must have played the previous games for this game to hit you the right way. I've played through all the Yakuzas so far. I'm pretty picky about games I write reviews for. They have to strike my fancy in a very specific way. I reviewed Yakuza Kiwami, Kiwami 4 and Like a Dragon negatively for the way the story played out. In my opinion, Yakuza games often suffer from "we need to finish this" syndrome, where the story accelerates at an unsustainable pace and you have some weird mechanic that trumps all the effort you put. I don't have infinite time, so I try to maximise my efficiency. That usually means grinding out the money-making minigames as fast as possible, which is a chore. The Man Who Erased His Name is perfect. The soundtrack is the best out of all the games. The graphics are the best out of all the games. The game is optimised so much that I've run the entire thing on 144 fps, 2k ultra, while streaming. The story is absolutely amazing, so much so that I even shed a tear (or two) at the end of the game, although I won't spoil you the reason. There is no grinding that is no rewarding. They took all the complaints from the last few games and simply avoided adding the problematic components of the previous games. Beautiful game, whole way through.The two people who watched this game with me agree, this was the best game out of all the games, from every aspect.

_childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon Gaiden is the perfect, most service to die-hard fans RGG studios have made to date! I don't write reviews on Steam that often, but this game I simply had to write a review for no questions about it. As someone who's played all the Yakuza titles, starting with Yakuza 7 Like a dragon, then 0-6, and with the Judgment games, I absolutely felt so emmersed and invested into the game at the very start to the very last moments. When I've seen the trailers for LAD Gaiden and seeing it's gameplay, features, new additions along with us figuring out where Kiryu went after the ending of 6, it was one of those games that I simply HAD to pre order and play on day one! And I'm so happy I did. (WARNING: SLIGHT SPOILERS TO PREVIOUS GAMES BUT KEPT TO A MINIMUM, NO REAL SPOILERS TO THE STORY)For those wondering, LAD Gaiden takes place after the story of Yakuza 6, and during the events of Yakuza 7 Like a Dragon, where we figure out and follow the story as to where Kiryu went and disappeared to after the events of 6, and how he ended up in 7 Like a Dragon. 3 Years after the Y6 you understand quick and clear why Kiryu did what he had to do to keep his loved ones safe and erase his name. His challenges and trials during the game to keeping his situation a secret as he's supposed to be a dead man. Only for him to realize Yakuza guys can't take a hint or keep a secret.The story as always is heaven sent, with clear and very concise understand everything without having to go back. It sucks you in just like every single game they've made for Yakuza. The boss battles and long battles are always a joy to get into, and you feel like a kid in a candy shop just from doing the wacky side quests. And upgrading Kiryu with his Agent and his Legendary Yakuza style was a pure joy grinding for and then taking it into battle with some hooligans on the streets. There is only 5 chapters but of course there is no sense of this game feeling short at all. There is plenty to do, as long as you are not in a point of a story where you can't go out and explore. They will make that clear, but you can really take your time with the game without feeling like you have to prioritize anything. Here's just a taste of what you can do.*Pocket Circuit Racing (Yes it's back for our 50 year old Kiryu XD)*Fight in The Castle Coliseum (Yes it returns and it's so easy to make money for upgrades)*Karaoke (Real fan service here with references to the past Yakuza titles)*Akame Requests (which is reskinned wacky side quests but the wackiness and humor is still here. With a TON of references and special guest appearances from past games and even from Judgment.)*Buy Clothes for Kiryu (Coliseum, Free Roam and Story)*Go to the Casinos*And of course give knuckle sandwiches to street punksI also wanted to speak a bit on the final chapter without spoiling anything. It was the perfect tie in and ultimate way to finish off the game with preparing for the Omi Alliance and Tojo Clan disbandment. Main reason why I love this so much is because I got to see Ichiban and his friends there, and (in a way) seeing them fighting side by side protecting Watase and Daigo. I was totally fanboying from start to finish, from the moment the camera pans into the room before his speech just seeking and looking for Ichiban like it's Where's Waldo, to seeing Kiryu come in with that punch and remove his glasses to Ichiban, Maejima and Saejima. Seeing this through Kiryu's perspective and seeing the dragon himself meet his successor and equal, along with that heart filling smirk Kiryu gives to Ichiban when he saw him reveal his dragonfish back tattoo really helped make this game for me. And to end it all off with a epic long battle with the Yakuza legends, and then to finish off, a boss battle to end the game that will have you remember the events and villain of Yakuza 5. Just a big chef kiss.And of course, Kiryu's breakdown and him crying at the closing moments of the game was enough to bring me to tears just like everyone else. We all want Kiryu to be happy and he deserves it and the world 10x over for his heart of gold and influence on others. I'm hoping there will be some closure and happy ending to his story, but I'm already looking forward to Infinite Wealth so much.In conclusion, RGG has made yet another 10/10 classic for the Yakuza franchise. THIS, is what gaming is about, and what AAA gaming should be. No bugs, god sent story, ultimate fan service, never ending action, fun and remarkable gameplay, and no micro transactions or nickle and diming fan-bases. From the bottom of my heart, thank you RGG. You guys deserve the whole world and more for making incredible games. I pre ordered this game from you guys, took a day off work just to play it, ordered pizza and I didn't regret it not one bit. I'm already putting down my pre-order for Like a Dragon Infinite Wealth and it's going to be probably the best birthday gift (or in my case belated Birthday gift since my bday is on the 22nd of January) I will ever receive. I'm looking forward to seeing Ichiban and Kiryu side by side together against the evils they will face.Thank you for all the memories and heart gripping stories RGG! Never change!

_childDocuments_.review: Am on the final chapter of this game, and I have some thoughts about the experience so far. Visually, it's a 10/10 - especially the stunning "casino nightlife design" of the Castle. But story-wise, i'd probably give it a 3.5/5  because it's pretty short, and I wish Akame was a more fleshed-out character. If you attempt the final fight without too many ability upgrades, then it's near-impossible to beat it unless you're good at timing your doges and blocks. It's not enough to rely on health and heat replenishments. And honestly, it actually takes more time to upgrade your abilities than to play through the story mode. For experienced Yakuza players, it's an enjoyable challenge. But for most new fans or inexperienced players like me (e.g. I only finished playing Yakuza 0 and Yakuza 7 - Like a Dragon), this game will require a bit of patience in grinding for cash from the Castle fights and skill points from the Akame Network. The challenges still don't ruin the overall experience; I had a blast. Highly worth recommending this game, and can't wait for new adventures in the Yakuza series.
