_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I did get a chance to jump into the Rogue Agent roguelite mode, and I'm enjoying it so much that I'm changing this review from negative to positive. The assets from the main game are implemented somewhat how you'd expect - backgrounds and enemies are randomly pulled from various areas, and upgrades are randomly pulled from the campaign's permanent skill tree - but, without the frustrations of the main campaign's shortcomings, Anomaly Agent's extremely fun core combat can shine through. You can also acquire the main game's combo chains (which were always a strong point) as permanent upgrades that last more than one run to help you get a bit farther each attempt.For a free update, Rogue Agent is executed about as good as it could be, and it very well may double the hours you can reasonably expect to spend with the entire game - that's remarkable. And, frankly, I'm having more fun with Rogue Agent than the main campaign - it shows off the high points of the game (combat, art, and music) without a lot of interfering design noise.So, overall, whether your drawn to the campaign, Rogue Agent, or both, I do think there's enough good stuff here to recommend the game writ-large. I'll leave my original review, which has my thoughts about the campaign, below, for posterity. -----------------------Anomaly Agent makes a very strong first impression thanks to its unique and charming style. A sense of earnestness permeates the entire game - while "weird" media can sometimes come off as contrived, Anomaly Agent has a weirdness about it that feels totally genuine. While playing, you get the sense that every quirk is simply an idea the developers had, liked, and put in the game. Unfortunately, Anomaly Agent wore thin on me pretty quickly. A big culprit is the use of environmental hazards: one-hit instakill mechanics absolutely litter the game, which get very annoying very quickly. The core combat systems are really fun, but the game has a habit of stacking 5-8+ enemies on top of each other at once, which sort of neuters the player's ability to meaningfully craft combos and parries. Platforming sections blur together, as a lack of movement upgrades constrains and homogenizes the design of every platforming section. The dance bar sections in particular were excruciatingly tedious to go through.The pacing of the game is all over the place, too: the downside of cramming a bunch of ideas into a game is that its playspace starts to lack identity. Is it a beat-em-up? Is it a platformer? Is it a stealth game? Is it story-driven? The answer to  all of those questions, to some degree, is yes, but the implementation of each feels random and arbitrary. Rather than taking inspiration from each genre and blending them into something new, Anomaly Agent sort of just pieces random, mechanically-unrelated segments to each other. The execution lacks the elegance of a truly well-designed game.I can tell I'm toward the end of the story, but I just feel sort of... done with the game. I enjoyed the first hour or so, but every successive hour felt worse and worse to the point that I am simply not having fun with the campaign anymore. The new roguelike mode is actually what grabbed my attention, so I may still check that out. But slogging through the story has left a bad taste in my mouth, and I just don't feel like playing anymore. Anomaly Agent has its charms, but it's a bit too messy for me to really enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not know about you but if I got to work and gravity was reversed, I am heading home. Luckily, I have an office job and do not work for a super secret agency that deals with world-ending catastrophes. Speaking of disasters, does said agency even have an agent that could handle gravity on the fritz with a little dash of broken time travel?Developed by Phew Phew Games, Anomaly Agent is a cyberpunk action platformer where you punch, kick, and just cause chaos amidst a retro backdrop and killer soundtrack. Become Agent 70 of the TDY where your boss hates you and your co-workers are not too fond of you. Perhaps it is that warm and fuzzy personality. Somehow, Agent is being promoted today BUT must finish out all current missions including figuring out why gravity has gone on the fritz.I cannot speak to the actual training of TDY agents but Agent 70 can fight. He’s extremely agile and can punch, kick, and dodge without breaking so much as a sweat. Belonging to a super secret agency has its perks too as Agent 70 has a few gadgets at his disposal. First up is the business card. Huh? This is no ordinary business card though. When thrown, it can stun enemies. As you progress through the game, the business card can be upgraded and even electrocute unsuspecting foes or be used to cut wires or reach hard-to-reach buttons/levers/etc. Your briefcase may or may not contain documents (I am leaning towards not) but what it does do is block melee attacks and deflect bullets. Who needs guns when you can just pilfer them off the bodies of enemies? Agent 70 is proficient in all types of firearms and when all else fails, you can just throw the gun at your target. The combat described may seem like it would lend itself to a standard beat ‘em up but it is quite deep while remaining easy to navigate. If you try to just punch and kick your way through everything, you probably will die (even on the lowest difficulty setting). Anomaly Agent’s combat just feels super fluid and smooth and as such, utilizing all the tools at your disposal felt natural. Both melee attacks and weapon attacks make use of combos that can be performed. The longer you can maintain a combo (aka staying aggressive), the more damage you will dish out plus it will earn you more and more coins used for upgrades. The aforementioned blocking and deflecting are also incredibly simple to pull off as the game has a warning system for incoming attacks. I am horrible at using parries in any game (Lies of P made me get better though) but this is more just a responsive button press when the on-screen prompt occurs. Blocking and deflecting can be upgraded later in the game to cause damage and stun making use of it even more worthwhile. You can also just use Agent 70’s roll dodge to avoid everything but you miss out on the satisfaction of stunning an enemy and going all Babe Ruth on him as you send him hurtling to his demise.In addition to the masterful combat the game offers, the platforming was quite enjoyable. Agent 70 is quite agile which can be seen in the responsive controls. There are plenty of lasers to dodge and moving platforms to navigate (perfect places to send enemies over the edge). I will not go into full detail but there are a few “chase” scenes that have you ducking and jumping down a corridor and it was an absolute blast each time it happened. For those who feel their skills in this type of gameplay are lacking, the checkpoint system is very forgiving. Most restarts will only take you back mere seconds before your death. How do you feel about shaping your narrative? During the story, Agent 70 often must ask/answer questions or participate in conversation with various characters. You can either give a normal response (read: boring) or be a sarcastic wiseass. Now, before you think, I’m just going to be a smartass all the time, there is a point to this. Your response will trigger a reaction from the character you are speaking to. Answering in a manner that is agreeable with this awards you with a positive emotion. Being a jerk earns you negative emotions. These emotions can then be spent on either health upgrades (positive emotions) or more coins (negative emotions) used for upgrades. While it may seem fun to talk back to your boss, sometimes it is worth it to go along with the other person. There does not seem to have a lasting effect on the general plot but it was a fun way to introduce choice into the game.Health upgrades are not just limited to emotions. They can also be found hidden in chests throughout the levels. Every four you collect will increase your total health. It is worth keeping in mind when “gathering” emotions as it costs 5 positive emotions for each upgrade. On the other hand, it only takes 3 negative emotions to exchange for 300 coins. Coins are dropped by enemies and also by items destroyed and found in most chests. Coins are then used to upgrade Agent 70’s ability such as decreasing the recharge time of the business card or increasing the damage of ranged weapons. To access additional tiers of upgrades, one must purchase a set amount from the previous tier. If you are looking for a fun platforming, action-packed brawler with a clever dialogue system and witty humor, look no further than Anomaly Agent. Phew Phew Games has nailed it on all fronts here between the super-responsive controls, fun factor, and retro but futuristic cyberpunk aesthetic. While the campaign is relatively short (approximately 5 hours), there is a new game plus (that costs 0 dollars) allowing you to bring all your upgrades to a new playthrough, and the upcoming Rogue Agent mode (roguelite anyone???). This is worth every penny and one of the first cannot miss titles of 2024. It is available now on PC and Switch.Full review available at

Functional and stylish. I'm just shocked it's at 97% positive reviews and at nearly 5,000 at those. It doesn't feel  good. Then again, neither is it bad enough to justify a negative review. So yeah, get it.My biggest disappointment is that the business card you get is replaced by a generic boomerang, which is a bit disappointing. It's a shame it doesn't lean into the more agent side of things with your abilities and equipment. The business card and case are neat but then you have some amorphous anomaly bat that, despite being an anomaly, is... just a bat, or a staff, or a hammer, or a sword, and that's not an anomaly; that's just your standard RPG inventory.Also, more seriously, the game's emphasis on two dialogue choices hinders the ability of your Anomaly Agent to exhibit their own personality. Game-play"We have Katana Zero at home."Seriously speaking though, this is a pretty decent side-scrolling beat-em-up game. It's charming, it's smooth, it's got a nice little story. The game is also, you know, pretty fun although there is a point where it starts throwing way more enemies at you and gets a bit frustrating (or maybe I'm just a lame n00b.) Though I will say the difficulty isn't helped if you don't play on a controller like the game recommends because for some GODS FORSAKEN reason the mouse isn't locked to the screen you're playing on. I died plenty of times because I accidentally clicked on something on my second monitor and got distracted. Nevertheless, it's still a pretty decent game, especially for $10. Arbitrary Rating: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: It is actually a descent game. Gameplay is smooth yet if some of you guys would decide to play it with keyboard, it would be harder than it suppose to be (tested and confirmed). Mechanics are deep enough to create the balance between feeling like an omnipotent being and questioning your skills as gamer. The main thing that game wants you to do is COMBOS. They are extremely important and they require some serious amount of skill. The problem with combos are not the way they executed but the place that they should be executed in. The enemies can be so crowded sometimes that you wouldn't be able to breath at all. The game creates very intense situations that you had to think rapid fast in order to make a combo without taking damage, which is going to disturb your combo and makes you think about punching a hole on you monitor. Other than these things, for the people who is going to buy this game, you guys should wait around 40 minutes to let the game show its actual value. At the start of the game the things that we are able to do is so limited that you guys could feel like  '' am i playing a browser game at 2010'' but fear not, this is going to be one of the best money that you guys would spend on a game

_childDocuments_.review: This game's really fun. I wish there was more depth in its combat system with more combos and weapons, as well as more complex bosses, but what's here is very solid and fun to play with. If anything, it makes me excited for what this studio will make next. This is an extremely solid gameplay foundation that I hope they build upon further in a future game, be it sequel or not. The weakest aspect is, by far, the platforming. It's not bad, but it's very simplistic, a bit clunky, and it ultimately feels pointless. The story, art, and music are all good, but safe. The music is up there as some of the best, and the storyline for most plays it's role to introduce you to some really interesting characters and level sequences. Gotta keep kicking that lil imposter! The fighting mechanics are quite good, and towards the end I got the hang of the special abilities although at times it was punishing trying to use them when you're surrounded by many enemies. The boss fights are fun, and for most of the part it's a challenging game without ever being so difficult that you wanted to quit. I loved the little links in the game, such as When the Wrestler calls you a random name but it all comes back later. The upgrade system was pretty average though. Chat to me about indies on twitter if you like!

I played half of the game with a keyboard and mouse, and I played the second half with the controller. I could say that, for me, the controller experience was much more fun. The soundtrack and the art style of the game were really good; I really enjoyed looking at the small details. The only downside is the story could have a bit more depth into it but considering this game to be the studio's first game, it is really understandable. _childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game, but it feels really slow in the beginning before you start getting some of your "heavy attacks", once you get through that it starts to really pick up the pace and they become an essential component in the late game.There's an element of getting so good you feel like a god, weaving in and out of a group of enemies, parrying and dodging nearly perfectly, but some of the enemies really put the brakes in the action with incredibly short cooldowns between unparriable ranged attacks that slow down the pace to a crawl. My playthrough was entirely on Hard so it may be more tolerable in lower difficulties.Dying isn't a big deal since you can restart so fast, but some of the screens stubbornly make you sit through the opening dialogue/cutscene while others do not, it's a bit inconsistent and it hurts the game slightly, if you were to keep dying in a forced cutscene arena you'll probably get frustrated really quickly.The bosses were all quite tough except for the two last ones, one was mostly a waiting game, the other was easy, or maybe I had just improved by the end.The music is incredible, kept me going the whole way through.The story was alright, There's two endings, but you only choose from one or the other at the very end, your choices during the game don't matter, which I was fine with, I was playing the game because it was a demanding action experience.Incredible action game that ended up being longer than I expected, incredibly demanding on your focus and inputs on Hard which is exactly what I was looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: Anomaly Agent. Bringing retro synthwave tunes and presenting an absolutely smooth gameplay with a pretty interesting story, has stood out in so many aspects in my honest opinion. Putting the popularity of the developers among the Turkish fan base aside, this game includes a lot of quality aspects within the experience it provides. I'll specialize my focus on these various aspects of the game in this review without further due. First of all, there is an astonishing combination between the theme, story and even the soundtracks. These retro synthwave soundtracks fit wonderfully with the theme of cyberpunk which has also been depicted impressively through the pixel design of the game. With these, the story also is very interesting. I've been getting some vibes similar to Hotline Miami's while playing it, though I believe that in Anomaly Agent, you tend to get more "tangible" objectives throughout the progression of the story. Retro soundtracks, an interesting story with a fascinating theme, smooth gameplay and wonderful pixel graphics... There is truly a beautiful combination.As for the mechanics, they are pretty simple as it's satisfying to see your character moving like Jagger. Combos and characteristics improve as the story progresses. With this, unlike the other 2d platformers which often include rogue-like, Anomaly Agent is a pretty quick game where auto-save system is present. It takes 'seconds' to pick up from where you left off in case you die. In conclusion, it's easy to learn, and not really hard to master :)Some additions that I'd personally like to make, includes my thanks and appeciation to the developers. Thank you Enis Kirazoğlu. I wish you and your crew the best in this new sector that you have got yourselves into, as you have done it in style. This here, is a work of art, and I wholeheartedly believe that Anomaly Agent will get popular among the Steam fan base in almost no time. Thank you.Edit: I believe that the last section of the game was made unnecessarily difficult. This is why I won't finish the game as I don't want to spend hours to just get past that single boss fight. I hope that the developers will make a better gameplay review of the whole game before releasing it.

_childDocuments_.review: Cherryson goes Phew Phew!Anyways, I completed the game and here is my serious comment on it:I enjoyed the game in general but the most outstanding part of it for me was its humour. I don't mean it has a crazy sense of humour by that but I find it as the most important aspect of this game. Its humour isn't only in its story but also sprinkled in gameplay too. It has a solid story for a short game which I wouldn't necessarily ask for more. The music and the graphics are pleasant.Isn't there any flaw? Yes there are some. At some chapters when you enter a room your double jump won't work and only solution is to restart the game. Luckily I had to do it only twice. Also after I defeat the first boss I wasn't able to move or do anything as I pressed the interraction button. I had to fight the boss again because of it. Again it happened only once and never occured again.Some may complain that enemies are repetitive and boring but I won't. Progression makes it playable. Only time I got bored while playing this game was final boss. It was easy yet unnecessarily long. I would prefer a harder boss fight instead of doing 3 or 4 moves again and again until he dies. Since I mentioned it I want to add that enemies are not intimidating at all. I played it on normal difficulty and I know I shouldn't be complaining about this without playing hard mode yet at least the bosses could be more intimidating in a way. It would be nice to say "damn I'm ♥♥♥♥♥♥ now" as I see an enemy or boss but it wasn't the case even with the final boss.Last thing could be done better was the distrubition of puzzles/platforms in chapters. They appear often after chapter 2 whilst there isn't as much at first chapters.To sum up; despite the fact that there are things could have done better, Anomaly Agent is a fun game to play and I'd recommend it without a second thought. I believe that Phew Phew games will consider these comments and learn from this experience to come up with a better sequel. Cheers!

name: Balatro
detailed_description: Balatro is a poker-inspired roguelike deck builder all about creating powerful synergies and winning big. Combine valid poker hands with unique Joker cards in order to create varied synergies and builds. Earn enough chips to beat devious blinds, all while uncovering hidden bonus hands and decks as you progress. You’re going to need every edge you can get in order to reach the boss blind, beat the final ante and secure victory. The definitive poker roguelike experience. Endless possibilities - every pick-up, discard and joker can dramatically alter the course of your run. In-depth campaign mode complete with 8 difficulties, as well as challenge and seeded runs. Deftly deploy an array of potent tools: different Decks, Jokers, Tarot cards, Planet cards, Spectral cards, and Vouchers. Use these versatile instruments to ignite a combo frenzy and turbocharge your poker hands, crafting electrifying, adrenaline-fueled synergies. 150 Jokers, each with their own unique abilities 15 Decks with distinct modifiers to choose from for each run 5 potential variants of each Joker which add further abilities 22 Tarot cards variants that can enhance your regular playing cards 11 Planet cards that help level up your possible poker hands 32 Voucher cards to help provide permanent buffs for your current run Immerse yourself in Balatro’s distinctive psychedelic world. Let the synthwave soundtrack wash over you - wind down, escape the daily grind and prepare to enter the ultimate roguelike flow state. Improve your collection and discover new cards and secrets with every single run. Make use of the in-depth stats screen to study your best hands, most used Jokers, and more! Immerse yourself in the CRT fuzz and enjoy detailed, hand-crafted pixel art.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game.I'm not the biggest deckbuilder game player, but Balatro kept me around for some time. It just sucks waiting and waiting for the game to bless you with a decent Joker so that you can have fun.There are no "meta" upgrades outside of a run, you start at the same stats every run. That makes the harder Stakes a challenge of being lucky. 20% of the time, you have a good time, because you get good Jokers that can get you crazy numbers. I will say, when that happens, the game is as fun as a rougelike deckbuilder is going to get.The other 80% of the time, you reroll for several rounds, getting nothing then ultimately failing by the 3rd or 4th ante because you just didn't get lucky.At the end of the day, it's free e-gambling. Doesn't hurt the wallet when you lose, and feels great when you win. But you have to get REALLY lucky to win, especially at higher stakes. I feel like you should get a little stronger each run in a roguelike, but you don't AT ALL in this game. I would still recommend this game to anyone though. Just not for me for a long-term game.

_childDocuments_.review: A creative point salad rogue-like that lets you set up some wild and crazy combinations. Lots of interesting decisions about how to best manipulate your odds for the best chances at a high score.I have two suggestions for the dev:- The rewards for skipping blinds are pretty bland and get repetitive. I'd love to see more variety here to make it a more interesting decision.- Some boss blinds and jokers require you to know what hands were recently played. It would be great to have a round recap that breaks down each hand that's been played and a point calculation breakdown. This becomes more of an issue when you save mid-run and try to continue later.

_childDocuments_.review: A very simple yet deep roguelike deckbuilder that allows you to truly relax. _childDocuments_.review: A complete breath of fresh air in that it's a deckbuilder that  clone .  Yes, it's 'roguelike' in that losing a run brings you back down to nothing, with a little 'lite' on the side as playing will unlock more stuff for you to encounter, but this is true deckbuilding in the tabletop sense with a little computer magic thrown in.  That means you'll be buying cards to add to your deck, using special cards to manipulate it and/or the scoring that's possible from it, and on rare occasions, you'll even be given chances to cull your deck to get a leaner and more devastating draw.  Of course,  brings its own bag of tricks to the party.Let's break it down.The basic premise of the game plays a lot like video poker except you start with an 8-card hand and you have limited plays and redraws; you're not playing against other players or a crafty AI here - your goal is simply to earn enough chips by scoring big hands in order to beat the 'blind' that you're challenging (simply: a set goal of points you need to earn before you run out of plays).  In other words, standard poker hands - and you can, if you like, play fewer than five cards - will score a certain number of base chips, plus a multiplier.  These aren't the actual values but think of it like a high card earning you 10 chips and a multiplier of 1 versus a royal flush earning you 100 chips and a multiplier of 5.  Stick with me, it's going to get much better.Now throw in Joker cards which do any number of things, but tend to be most useful when they can manipulate the amount of chips you earn and/or the multiplier itself.  So that useless x1 in my example, hypothetically, can be manipulated by a Joker to become a x2 or higher.  You don't play Jokers, either.  These are like semi-permanent buffs that you can buy from the store or otherwise discover throughout your run, but they don't go in your deck and longer play unlocks more to be found.  You have enough slots to carry five of them for buffs/effects that you carry with you from blind to blind, hand to hand.  But wait, there's more!Now there's tarot cards which also don't clog your deck, but you can only carry up to two at a time in reserve.  That said, you can use them whenever you want so long as they have a valid target.  With me so far?  These cards can do all kinds of crazy magic from changing your card suits, cloning them, giving them status tags, generating random card types, etc.  Sometimes you'll earn them through bonuses or Joker cards, and sometimes you'll just outright buy their effects from the store to be used immediately; if they happen to target cards when you do so, you'll draw a random hand to manipulate and while you're staring at this random hand, any other tarot cards that you're holding can be used at this time.  More importantly, most of the effects of these tarot cards last your entire run.  For example, if during play you decide to use a tarot card to change the suits of some cards to force a flush, they don't reset after the round is done - those conversions last for your whole run unless you change them again otherwise.  We're not done yet!There are even more cards out there that help you out.  Planet cards can instantly boost the level of your hand scores meaning that your baseline earnings and multipliers beef up. You could, for example, make royal flushes super valuable to score, but they're still pretty rare; on the other hand, play enough planet cards (with a dash of luck) and you can dump all your bonuses into more common hands like two-pair or flushes and suddenly you're rolling in the chips.  You'll also encounter rare card packs with fantastic titles that add bonuses or statuses to cards of your choice, packs that can generate Jokers or tarot cards at random, stuff that adds risk like huge multipliers with a chance that the card might destroy itself, etc.  That's just scratching the surface, but part of the fun is the 'gamble' and pushing your luck.A major strategy comes from managing the store and whether or not you're going to visit it.  In each round, you'll face three challenges in the form of small, large, and boss blinds which are essentially score targets (boss blinds add extra conditions that need to be faced).  Skipping the small or the large blind compensates you with powerful tags that can swing things in your favor like making packs free to buy, but you forego an important visit to the store each time you do so as well as the chance to earn spending cash in the game itself.  Playing through the blind and succeeding means you actually get to visit the store afterwards to spend your money on cards of random types. Two of these will be known to you and the rest come in "booster pack" blind buys that allow you to choose one or two out of a selection of several. Cash is typically tough to get in large amounts (but you can build around that), but the store is incredibly important for manipulating your deck; winning with a standard 52-card playing card deck is highly unlikely as the stakes get higher the more you win so you're going to want to fish for advantages any chance you get.Long story short,  allows for tremendous strategic and tactical flexibility with a fair amount of luck, but as you learn the game's systems, you'll find that RNG can be manipulated or mitigated to greatly increase your odds at winning.  It is a simple concept with layers of complexity that is, frankly, executed perfectly.  There's no extra fluff or weird narratives or aesthetics to navigate.  It is essentially a solitaire game that has an absolutely solid core, an atmosphere of discovery, and a rewarding "haha numbers go up" risk/reward feedback loop that can keep you engaged for way longer than you might expect.  I typically don't buy anything unless it's hugely discounted, but I don't regret a single penny spent on . It's essentially video poker, but  get to be the one rigging the game instead of the house and frankly, that is a hell of a lot of fun!

_childDocuments_.review: It's definitely fun, but there's something not so satisfying about it. I've definitely played better roguelite card games, and I hope this gets better. It has Inscryption vibes, but there's no visible story. You can over-score on a round, but I've not run into a reward for doing really well in a round. It feels like I deserved a few bucks for scoring over double on a round's requirements.Some boss debuffs are wild. Like -$1 per card played. Or it may debuff diamonds after you've specced into diamonds, and go and give you half a hand of diamonds. Your money can go into the negatives just for you to win the round, and you might be screwed until the next boss, or more. The RNG factor utterly ruins most of your runs. A good run feels great, but most runs feel like crap. Discards sometimes giving you every suit but the one you wanted for 3+ discards of 5 cards each. Horrible horrible experiences ruining a 30+ minute run. Overall it's fun, but I find myself frustrated with many outcomes, and don't feel rewarded for doing well.

_childDocuments_.review: Addicting and frustrating. I cannot find the fun part of Balatro, only the addiction of gambling.Balance is out of whack and there is no good feedback on your deck's power level. You end up losing a lot of runs out of nowhere due to bad luck or a small miscalculation. When you win a run you are 10-100x too powerful. From what I am seeing only "small hand" and flush decks work well due to their consistency.In short the gameplay is not tactical but more random and "win more" which does not lend itself for a fun and exciting gameplay loop for me.The UX could use a bit more work, there are small inconsistencies here and there. For example looking at the current Ante is behind too many clicks (considering how often one needs to do it) and the "hover over deck tooltip" only works when you are playing a hand (although you need to look at your deck during many other times too). These issues are not a gamebreaker but are the surface of the real issue deeper within.Will I still continue playing this and did I think it was worth my money? Possibly.It's just hard to recommend this when Slay The Spire exists, a quite different but in all possible ways a superior game.Hopefully after a few rounds of balancing and polishing Balatro will be as good as it deserves to be! If Steam supported a "Neutral"/"Maybe" recommendation I would give that instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game for the first time last Friday. It is now Tuesday. I know I'm a basic ♥♥♥♥♥ for sounding like the broken record that is every fan of this game but it's not like they're wrong, it really is digital cocaine. This ♥♥♥♥ goes hard as hell.In all seriousness, if you're actually looking through these for purchasing advice and not to giggle at the more amusing reviews?- This is less than half the price of the cookie cutter AAA ♥♥♥♥ that comes out these days and easily can double hours played in your average open world. Financially it's almost a crime how good this deal is.- The game might sound intimidating from just the tagline "poker deckbuilding roguelike," but it's got a quick yet solid tutorial, intuitive UI (color contrast mode is a great setting), and LocalThunk has comprehensively mastered writing tooltips. You can even unlock everything at the start, although you won't get cheevs on that profile if you do. The barrier for entry is almost nothing.- This game was made by someone with a soul, not a dry husk being worked to death in an office for a company that's about to lay them off. The love and care put into this thing shows in every aspect of it.- Number go brrrrrrrr, brain go !!!!!!!!!!!!- You don't actually have to be good at math to have fun though. If you want to optimize there's so much potential for calculating every chip, but I play on vibes only and still have a blast.TLDR: Balatro is a well priced, easy to learn hard to master game that you definitely should buy as long as you've planned for the next few days to be lost to it.

_childDocuments_.review: Balatro is so excellent that it feels like it was discovered, not created. It effortlessly evokes the brainy strategies of the best roguelike deckbuilders while also tying itself back to a poker theming that all those games were mechanically riffing from anyway.An approachable UI welcomes players who don’t know their flushes from their straights, but there’s still plenty of challenge to be found in the management of your deck and economy—all wrapped up in an intuitive package that would make your grandpa take pause and watch over your shoulder.The result is a simple yet compelling deckbuilder that’s as infinite and as classic as a deck of 52.Balatro is a roguelike solitaire version of poker. Each run starts by dealing you eight cards and asking you to produce the best five-card-hand you can. Repeat over the course of a few rounds.Rather than having a table of opponents,  you’re attempting to hit a score threshold. Each hand has its own score and its own multiplier. The short term strategy is born from Balatro’s drawing and discard rules; you get a few free per card mulligans each turn, and in a deckbuilder-like fashion you refuel your hand after each play.Within your first minute you’re being asked to answer strategic questions about your risk tolerance: do you discard a guaranteed hand in pursuit of a better one? Or do you play it safe and work with what you got?The fact that each card replaces itself on play makes them act as a secondary discard, too. Have a hand that’s just short of a flush? Why not open round one with playing a modest pair from different suits and chucking in three other random cards alongside them: even if they’re not contributing towards that pair and its point value, they are freeing up those hand slots and give you greater flush opportunities the following turn. It’s not guaranteed to work but that’s the beauty of it: you’re always looking for little ways to stack the deck in your favor.That's just one example among dozens where Balatro is constantly giving you decisions in small but provocative ways.That philosophy becomes multiplied after your first few hands when Balatro exposes you to some of its run-wide systems. You get a shop with “booster packs”, which sounds corny for a deck-of-52 game like this until it gets coupled with the game's concept of “jokers”.These would be your “relics” or “artifacts” in a title with a more “video-gamey” theme, they’re passive bonuses that will stay with you for an entire run and you can hold up to five of them under normal conditions.One run I got a joker that multiplied my score if I only played three card hands instead of five. Now all of the sudden I’m pivoting to a style that boosts three of a kinds and pairs, and flushes are near useless because they force me above that three-card limit by their very nature.That changed how I looked at those “booster packs”: now suit was less relevant with flushes off the table, allowing me to target specific numbers and faces to maximize my three-card-hand potential.Almost every joker can warp a game in this way, so you get this long term strategy of crafting good jokers for your deck and crafting good decks for your jokers. It’s so deep and so fun, once you start to see all the pieces come together it’s easy to imagine all the ways you can arrange them to make for truly unique runs every single attempt.It’s a time black hole, the hours just melt in front of you.Part of that is probably because of how well produced it is, too. Not only does it have a simple, replayable little gameplay style but it also has a presentation that makes infinite play so appealing. Mechanically the ‘blinds’ are kind of like enemies, but they don’t really feel that way. You don’t get any smashing or crashing animations into them when you successfully score points, just little bleeps and the sound of stacking chips.It gives Balatro a very non-confrontational vibe, where the focus is always just you and your cards. Each turned in hand gives you a brief animation of your cards cashing in their point values but also a little visual indicator that shows your jokers boosting their power. It makes it obvious who your load bearing jokers are and the fact that the score acquisition is so multiplication heavy gives you this big explosion of points once every card has done its little dance that makes the result so satisfying.Beyond just being a game with immediately interesting rules and endless strategy, Balatro is also just a damn good roguelike in the conventional sense, too. The meta progression is a steady increase in options and scope. You’ll get more potential jokers, more consumable power ups, and more card types.There are multiple ‘boss encounters’ that you’ll want to start building around, too. They apply modifiers that can be a counter to your exact strategy. One of my first almost successful runs leaned on beefing up easy hands like pairs and giving myself additional hands per round: going for consistent additive plays instead of singularly big ones. Imagine my frustration upon meeting the Needle, an encounter that allowed only a single hand to be played.Obviously, I lost; but the lesson might not be what you think it was. The standard approach would be to have a more flexible deck next time, but there’s nothing wrong with single-mindedness in Balatro as long as you bring insurance: either jokers or consumables that let you re-roll or nullify a boss encounters’ modifiers.There’s also thought that needs to be given to the relative strength of your deck. Maybe that consistent ‘two of a kind’ will get you through the early game, but it may not yield the points you need as the run gets tough (and it literally ups the ante). A strategic pivot into strengthening higher point value hands is always on your mind, and you need to be aware of how much hand manipulation you currently have and if you’re ready for that pivot.Balatro isn’t just a loving ode to standard playing card decks but also a subtle homage to cards and collectables more generally. It creates intrigue in opening up a ‘booster pack’ of regular cards by sprinkling in lots of modifiers. There are ‘lucky’ cards that have a chance of giving a small bonus in addition to their regular effects, steel cards are incentivized to be held and give multipliers to played hands they aren’t in, and golden cards help boost your economy.Holographics, foils, and more are attributes you can find on jokers in addition to their regular behaviors, which give you this exciting boost and maybe a reason to alter strategies into a joker that may otherwise be suboptimal for your deck.Balatro does so much with so little. With a deck of playing cards and some powerups, it’s created a timeless card system with high stakes but low pressure. This game of probability manipulation and strategy is one of the best deckbuilders of all time, and its intuitive ‘playing-card’ presentation might also make it one of the best versions of Solitaire ever made, too.

_childDocuments_.review: Balatro is an amazing roguelike that solves a lot of issues with the genre that many other games struggle with. These issues are:-      This refers to the problem in many rougelikes where you get an item and it says something like "Improves attack damage when an enemy is frozen" or in some cases just says some flavor text like "toxic". This tells the player nothing about what the item or whatever does and it makes it very difficult to get into, many times requiring wikis open or other such things. In many cases, even when the stats and effects are clear, it can be very difficult to figure out how good it is before you pick it up, and sometimes even after you pick it up. This makes it take quite a while to really get into a rougelike because there is so much knowledge you have to learn to know what items are good and which suck.     Balatro solves this by having each card description being relatively simple and very clear. It helps that the base of the game is simple too. The scoring system is also pretty simple to understand, to the point where you can calculate things on your own if you so choose (which I have done on a few occasions - its fun). When you play a hand, you clearly see how each joker effects your score and how they effect each other. This helps you get into the game quickly by very clearly showing you what each and every item does-      This is something thats hard to do, so I understand it, but many rougelikes suffer from it. What I mean by "poor balance" more specifically here is a decent amount of items that are either insanely run-winningly good and/or items that sound neat but end up being complete and udder trash. This creates runs where you get wins that you didn't really work for along with runs where you try to commit to a certain strategy or build that ends up sucking because the balance is off. This ties into the point above but it gets worse when something is really bad but it isn't obvious how bad it is.      Balatro isn't perfect about balance, but it feels a lot better than other rougelikes I've played. I've not encountered a joker that has been so good it won my run on its own, and I also haven't encountered any jokers that are uselessly bad, and even if they are, the game makes it pretty clear that its gonna suck. Even so, they usually work in some build somewhere, or have a niche during a certain point in a run which makes them useful. -      This one is a real big problem with rougelikes. Many rougelikes out there are very very unclear about what builds you can go for and if they are even worth your time at all. The items may give some impressions here and there, but many times it will be difficult to tell if its worth it to commit to. There is also the case in some games where certain mechanics or calculations that are INCREDIBLY obtuse and unclear to the player are INSANELY important to the game and creating good builds. It also hurts when games try to make a bunch of items for certain types of builds, but those builds are god awful because they don't work within the game very well.     Again, Balatro solves this with incredibly clear synergy and calculation. As I said above, you can calculate what is going to happen yourself so when you are thinking if a certain card is worth it or not, you can do the math to figure it out. Not many other games have that ability. The way the game is played, again, is also very simple which makes builds pretty easy to figure out. I've found a lot of success and fun in this game by buying a decent joker early on and trying to commit hard to building around it, and it works!-      This could be considered a good thing I guess, but I tend to have issue with it. What I mean is when a rougelike throws a boss at you that you've never seen before and you die very quickly. Then, in order to fight it again you have to play a whole new run, get to that point, die, and then try again. It makes it really hard to learn patterns and learn how to fight the bosses, especially when they are late game or don't always appear.     Balatro solves this by not really having much player skill involved. Most of Balatro is figuring out which build would be the best, making tricky decisions, and hedging your bets. The "skill" in balatro is knowing when to discard and what to discard to achieve which hand. Everything else is trying to figure out which item or card or whatever will help your build the most. It's also a chill game without any urgency which means you can take your time and think a lot if you so please. To be fair to other rougelikes, many games solve some of these problems on their own, and I'm sure there are games other than Balatro that don't have any of these issues. My main point, really, is that Balatro gets you to the "end game" of a rougelike much quicker than others do. By "end game" I mean when you get a lot of knowledge and experience in a game and know what you want to do and what decisions to make and what is good. Essentially Balatro is good and a ton of fun if you love to strategize and think about numbers. I love it.

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this game was pretty good, and then I got to the higher stakes and it made me question every single hour of this game I had played beforehand. As you go higher, the game just starts ripping your ability to play it out of your hands in one giant chunk after another and it makes the core mechanics of the game start to feel really flimsy and poorly implemented. Your discards become useless, your hand size becomes garbage, booster packs basically don't exist anymore and the game scales so fast that you just have to try and find something good really early on or your run is just pointless. This leads to spending hours in the first two antes struggling to find ANYTHING usable. I can't understate how much different and how much worse of an experience the highest difficulty of this game is compared to its base game. When I was playing the demos, I thought this game might have real staying power. A couple weeks after its release, I think it might actually just be a really, really shallow game that's gonna fall apart very quickly.

_childDocuments_.review: What a breath of fresh air, showing that it pays off to not just make a STS-clone for a roguelike.This is a great game, more than the sum of its parts. Higher difficulty it does get a bit annoying though, cause you'll be much more reliant on RNG unless your a math wizard and enjoy playing the game in a way you shouldn't (i.e. counting score, which is actively disincentivized in design). The game doesn't require a deep knowledge of Poker, as you'll quickly learn by just playing the game. Great new addition to the genre, and will inspire many more gambling RL's going forward.This game on it's own would have been a solid 8/10 recommend for anyone that likes the genre, but the mods elevate it to a whole new level. It's a bit of a pain to setup, but once you got the base down adding new mods is a matter of dragging a folder to the right place. Cannot recommend doing this enough once you've beaten the game a couple of times, as it increases the playability by 10-fold. Personal recommendations at time of writing: betmma's modpack (adding new vouchers & voucherpacks), Mika's Mod Collection (bunch of new interesting jokers) and Deluxe Consumables Cards by JeffVi (adds Deluxe versions of consumables).

_childDocuments_.review: The best roguelike I ever played. Period.It became one of my three favourite indies besides Disco Elysium and A Short Hike. With indie games this brillant, I do not fear the future of gaming. AAA might go to hell, but honestly... most AAA titles can't replicate the amount of fun you will have here. Games like Undertale, Crow Country, Outer Wilds, Tunic, Hades, etc. challenge the status quo. Thanks to indies in every genre there is now at least own strong game. Why are they so good? Because they do not exchange whaling for fun. Balatro is a card battler rogue like based on poker which at first sounds baffling. Balatro looks simple initially, but the possibilities are insane. Strategy is just as important as luck and a smart player can grap every opportunity to win run after run after run. Becoming better and better and eventually getting chips deep into the millions... this adrenaline rush... it's unbelievable.Pros:- Smart, but easy to understand gameplay- Charming design- Challenging- Balatro encourages clever deck building. It feels kinda like Yugioh when you lay your best hand out- Much replay value- Superb progression. You unlock much down the road- Cool music...Cons- ...but not many tracks- RNG can screw you over royallyPlay it, you probably will love it

So if you are interested in exploring these themes more, check out Zachtronics Solitaire Collection.

_childDocuments_.review: Balastro is a captivating and well-crafted game that brings a fresh twist to puzzle and strategy mechanics, offering an experience that’s both addictive and rewarding. One of its standout features is the unique style of gameplay, which combines thoughtful planning with quick decision-making. The game manages to strike that perfect balance between being challenging and accessible, keeping players engaged without overwhelming them.One of the most brilliant aspects of Balastro is the inclusion of the “joker” mechanic. This inventive addition allows players to creatively overcome obstacles and adds a strategic layer to the game. Whether you’re using the joker to salvage a tough situation or planning ahead to maximize its impact, it’s a tool that gives the game a surprising depth. It also introduces a satisfying element of surprise, as every “joker” moment feels like a win, offering a fresh way to turn the tide in your favor.The game’s point system is also expertly balanced, rewarding players fairly for skillful play while still offering a challenge that makes high scores feel earned. Scoring points feels satisfying, and the progression is smooth, allowing for a sense of growth and mastery as you play more.Overall, Balastro is a fantastic game that impresses with its gameplay style, clever “joker” mechanic, and well-balanced scoring system. _childDocuments_.review: EDIT: The Discord community for this game has a robust and active modding scene. This completely changes my view of the game, and so I have changed my review to "Recommended".My first impressions of Balatro were really positive! I'm a fan of roguelike card games (I've enjoyed MTG drafting for over a decade now), and the art and aesthetic of this game are gorgeous. I've played daily since release! And in fact, for the first 30 or so hours, I think Balatro is a joy to play, and I'd highly recommend it.However, the more I play, the shallower the gameplay loop feels. Without spoiling too much, there's more-or-less an "optimal" strategy for maximizing hand points, and once you figure it out, most runs follow the same "arc" -- you look for the same types of cards in the early game, the mid game, and the late game. ()There are a few really cool combos, where cards synergize super well together and feel awesome when they work (such as ), but these kinds of interactions are relatively rare. I found that far more often I'd encounter antisynergistic "nonbos" or completely useless/dead cards, leading to frustration as I reroll and pray that I get one of the 5-10 cards that would actually elevate a given run to "viable" status.The developers do try to add novelty to the game (through challenges, alternate decks, boss blinds, and rare occurrences). But, I find that it's still not enough to break free from the core limitations of the engine (A 52 card playing pool, with only + and x being the main score modifiers). After a while, it starts to feel more like "numbers go up" and nothing more.My main suggestion to the devs would be to minimize the amount of "dead weight" common jokers (there's a lot of redundancy!!), and add new jokers that foster neat interactions. Also, perhaps add additional jokers that balance the lower tier hands?  I would be playing much more if I didn't have to slog through the boring jokers just to find the small subset of jokers that create a meaningful, interesting run. (I'll be keeping an eye out for future updates, though, and I'll happily revise my review if it turns out that the game has more replayability than v1.0.0 does! There's so so so much promise here.)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun, though it's somewhat random and thus you can feel frustrated waiting for your first win. As with all games like this (where more items are unlocked as you play) it might actually be easier to win early in the game since the number of potential items is lower thus increasing the chances that you'll get a good combination of jokers and other things.So you might ask yourself, what is this game about?  Well, it's a card game where you play poker hands to earn points in the form of "chips" to achieve a set round goal (called a "blind") in a set number of hands with a set number of discards.  Each Ante has 3 rounds (Blinds): Small, Big, and Boss. You play poker hands from a deck, discarding cards. The Boss is mandatory, and each has unique challenges (e.g. "Verdant Leaf" prevents scoring until a joker is removed, "The Eye" prevents hand reuse). Defeat each Blind, earn rewards and shop access for Jokers, Arcanas, Planets, Vouchers to buy cards that boost score, discard, or restock, or affect gameplay. For example, the first round goal is 300 chips and you start with around 3-5 "hands" to attempt to reach that goal.  You'll also start with 3-5 discards per round with each discard being up to 5 cards at a time.  Your hand size will be around 7 cards to start out with but the actual number depends on the starting conditions given by the type of deck you play.  There's 5 colored decks: red, blue, green, yellow and black.  Some decks give extra discards, some give extra hands, some give extra money. Each deck presents its own challenge.  Once you beat the game with a given deck, you can change the chip color which further changes the game difficulty.Anyway, as I said, this is kind of random, so you may find yourself losing a lot even if you play the game perfectly.  OR You might find yourself winning even though you play really sloppily (If the random seed is just so stacked in your favor)  You don't find out the seed until after the game is over though, but if you've ever thought maybe you could have won if you did something differently, then this is a great option.  The only caveat here is that you don't unlock anything from playing a seeded game, and so it would  purely be for the fun of playing.There's lots of room for strategy, but since you can buy usually 2 jokers at most per round, you may find that it's difficult to form a good strategy with what you have.  One of my favorite combos is to have the four finger joker (allows you to make straights and flushes with only 4 cards) combined with the Square joker (starts with +16 chips per hand played but increases +4 chips for every time you play only four cards) and the Seance Joker (straights or flushes creates a random spectral card).   You can see how each card works together, but the odds of these jokers all being available together is slim. Cards can be modified to have extra effects like +multiplier (+4 per card played), Wild (used as any suit), Bonus (adds +30 chips to the current card value), glass (x2 multiplier but 25% chance of being destroyed once played), Steel (1.5X multiplier added as long as you hold it in your hand and it's not played), and there's more.  You can also have card editions (foil/polychrome/holographic etc), and seals applied to the card (small colored circles that give an extra effect to that card under certain conditions). You can also add cards to your deck to have more than 52 cards, or you can destroy cards to have fewer than 52. The card modifications aren't permanent so you don't have to worry about messing up the deck, but you CAN mess the deck up for your current run.  For example, it's possible to change cards so that you have extra cards of a certain suit by changing them from another (e.g. from Hearts to clubs), which can make the odds of making a flush go up for Clubs but down for hearts.   There's also a spectral card that will change a large number of cards to be all the same rank (e.g. a whole hand full of 8's) making it possible to get a 5 of a kind.You don't have to have any special knowledge of how to play poker to enjoy the game as the game will tell you what the hands are as you select it and you'll learn the difference between a flush, a straight, and a straight flush as the game goes on. In conclusion, if you like games that are both random AND give options for strategy, and you like unlocking new stuff, this game will give you all of that.  If you prefer games that rely more on strategy and skill, this will be a bit frustrating for you, but honestly, how many card games are there that rely solely on skill? I think it's a fun game though, and worth the purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Balatro is one of the freshest rogue-like deck builders that we've had in a long time. No longer are we chasing the heady heights of Slay the Spire, instead we're beating our own path and providing a slick, efficient and incredibly gripping puzzle.- The premise is simple, make poker hands and score points. The better the hands, the better the points. This opening premise is easy to understand while simultaneously giving you a lot of juicy maths to play with as you work out probabilities of draws and slowly adapt a standard deck of 52 into something designed to produce reproducable.- Whether you're seeking out jokers, which give a variety of boons and bonuses, or smashing your cards into a specific suit, or type or giving them bonuses, OR EVEN boosting the base score of your poker hands to make even the easiest to achieve plays provide millions of points.- The feeling this game gives when suddenly your schemes work, the numbers line up and the numbers go big, you feel unstoppable, you feel like the smartest person in the world, just staying ahead of that curve until the inevitable collapse. Your synapses are snapping for more, and it's easy to find yourself immediately back in.Overall, an exceptional game. The start of a run doesn't feel overly bogged down and borderline pointless, like some, and the game never throws any truly overtly frustrating mechanics in your way to knock you sideways or provide an artificial barrier. It's just... really really good.More thoughts

_childDocuments_.review: There was a time when I would walk. Sometimes in the morning, if the sun's flourishes were enough to lure me from my hole, sometimes in the evening in a bid to catch its face once more before it left for the day.There was a time when I would meet friends in coffee shops or pubs for either a cold pint or warm brew. We'd update each other on the highlights of our dispassionately normal lives. I would tell them the true story of how I was kept waiting on a train for three hours due to a small landslip. They would tell me about the rash they had on their arm, that turned out to be a ketchup stain that just required a bit of persistent scrubbing.There was a time when I'd wash things. My car, my dishes, myself.There was a time when I'd chop garlic, boil water, season ingredients, eventually collecting them together on a plate to create a meal.There was a time when at least once a day, I'd lay my head on my pillow in bed, as I thought over every human interaction I'd had that day. I'd question if when I said to Daisy in work "your hair looks nice,"did she think I was suggesting that it usually didn't? or when trying to say "hi" to the random gentleman at the coffee machine, and accidentally spurting "hey!" did he thinking I was condemning his choice of a Mocha? All these thoughts eventually leading to some time asleep.There was a time when I would do my job.There was a time when I would make sure my nails were cut, and teeth were clean. When I scratched an itch and the skin of the scratching finger made zero connection with the itchy flesh, that's when I knew it was normally time to act. When I would breath in and out and every swallow tasted like five day old warm tea mixed with bile, toothpaste would be introduced.There was a time when after placing my mug, throwing the tea bag in (from a much less impressive distance than I'd like), and fetching the milk from the fridge ready to pour in, I would pretend to fight off a platoon of cloned soldiers from a parallel universe with nothing but a single knife and two small imaginary pistols. Then I played Balatro. Now I play Balatro.There is only Balatro.The thought of a power cut throws me into a dissociated state.Because then I would not be able to play Balatro.I tried to stop once. Futile.When I mute the game, I still hear every sound because it has become a part of me now.I briefly fell asleep for 20 minutes. I had dreams of playing Balatro.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun in concept but fizzles out fast due to being very poorly balanced, too grindy (to unlock everything), and way too RNG heavy. Balatro is the kind of game where you either hit it high and land on the moon, or die in the first ante (on higher stakes). The deck balance is also all over the place, some are basically unplayable (e.g. black deck), others are way too powerful (e.g. plasma deck).It was fun when it was novel, but at some point you find yourself just spending half an hour rerolling for the perfect start because some of the challenges and decks are literally unbeatable without getting insanely lucky in the early game. It is a far cry from the likes of the well-balanced roguelikes it draws inspiration from.Apart from fixing the massive issues with card, boss and deck balance, an easy improvement to the status quo would be to e.g. guarantee a powerful joker after beating a boss, the way most other roguelikes do this. Rather than just leaving it up to chance.There are another couple of design choices I dislike, e.g. stakes being tied to the deck choice - which makes it so you basically "lock yourself in" to a certain deck and have to grind out the lower difficulties again if you want to ever play a different one. This really hurts the replayability of the game. Adding to this overall monotony is the fact that most strong decks rely on the same few jokers and tarot cards, and the strongest strategies consistently spend a lot of time just idly abusing some value-generating joker, only to lose all this progress to some unlucky boss.Balatro is the kind of game where it's more fun to watch somebody else's high roll video on youtube than to play for hours trying to get that high roll yourself. Or just save your time by unlocking all of the collection at the start with a cheat code, so you can actually play what you want to play instead of being forced to suffer through a monotonous grind to unlock it in the first place.

_childDocuments_.review: Basically, it's  big two as a deck-building rogue-like... or rogue-lite as that is the more appropriate genre even though I hate that term.Even though I favor more action-packed games with much flashier gameplay, Balatro somehow clicked for me with its simplicity. You don't really need extensive knowledge of  big two, I say having minimal  big two experience beforehand. However, knowing the hands does give you a headstart. To me, it is quite a good time-waster if you don't have anything else to do as well as an  chill game to just wind down with.It's  chill because if you despise heavy RNG influence in winning/losing then, by all means, avoid Balatro.I say that coming from the school of thought that non-party games that lean so much more heavily on luck as opposed to skill aren't fun and are therefore terribly designed games. I get utterly peeved with this game at times, swearing up and down that the game is controlled by an AI that just decides to rig the game against you by giving you impossible-to-win scenarios that you could not have seen coming and therefore prepared for without just knowing exactly what goes on in the seed, which is humanly impossible. If I had to guess what my winrate would be at this point, I'd say it's less than 3%. Yet somehow I'd still look forward to doing a couple runs of Balatro to wind down from each day, each run starting with the hope that whatever setup I have for a crazy build finally takes off from the first couple antes. This was all because I won on my very first run with a very solid build that got me to ante 10.So, I would recommend this game especially to gambling addicts because . That's right, there's no reason to ban this game just because it has elements of  big two; this is a very safe alternative to get addicted to rather than actual gambling, if one had to get addicted to either one. Looking at you, EU censors.P.S.: After playing way more of the game, playing the higher stakes (difficulties), and being just 4-5 jokers away from completing my collection I must say it is (at the time of this edit) a  experience playing high stakes/challenge runs. I'm convinced that the game's rng is completely rigged and constantly scheming against you. At this point, I really am still playing just to get that high with the rare miracle runs.

_childDocuments_.review: At its core, Balatro is a testament to the creativity and depth possible in video games. The game challenges you to create powerful synergies by combining valid poker hands with unique Joker cards. This innovative approach not only tests your strategic thinking but also your ability to adapt and overcome the various challenges presented in each run.The journey through Balatro's meticulously crafted levels is a rollercoaster of highs and lows, much like a good poker game. Earning chips to beat the blinds while uncovering hidden bonus hands and decks adds layers of strategy and surprise. The game's roguelike elements ensure that no two playthroughs are the same, providing endless hours of entertainment.What sets Balatro apart is not just its gameplay but also its presentation. The game's aesthetics are both charming and immersive, drawing you into a world where each hand can lead to victory or defeat. The soundtrack complements the experience, enhancing the game's mood and tension.In conclusion, Balatro is a must-play for fans of deck builders, poker enthusiasts, and anyone looking for a game that blends strategy, skill, and a touch of luck. Its unique premise, engaging gameplay, and replayability make it a standout title in the crowded field of indie games. Whether you're a seasoned card shark or new to the genre, Balatro promises a rewarding and enjoyable experience that's well worth the ante.Highly recommended for those looking for a game that challenges the mind and rewards strategic play.Cons:- Only has around 10 hours of content, we need more stuff! and a reason to keep playing beyond finding all the jokers etc- Does not have multiplayer

_childDocuments_.review: A poker-based rogue-lite deckbuilder. Create the best poker hands to make enough points to move to the next level. Simple right? _childDocuments_.review: I decided to make my review after my first win (a complete run).It took me less than 7 hours, but it could have taken less as I threw two potentially beatable runs with errors in the last stages.After the first run there's still I'd say 70% of content that I haven't discovered. There's a myriad of challenges so you will have to beat the game many times, with many different decks, and unlocking many new cards, mostly jokers.The beauty of the game lies in the endless possibilities and combos you will be inventing along the way, testing your mind for trying to predict what will happen. Sometimes the game seems to point you in a certain way, but it will require experience to know what cards to pick in the first choices (because they can build powerful combos later) or decide if you need to pick one to survive while you build money and later become powerful. There's many builds and I can't even start to structure all the possible synergies, there's just too many.This kind of roguelike shows that you can have way more variety and entertainement with a small game developed with love and care, than with a huge "open world" cookie cutter "adventure" that's repetitive, boring, and unnecessary.This game is addictive, you will want to beat it multiple times, I think I can easily go over 30 hours here without getting bored. This is on the level of Luck Be A Landlord, Brotato and similar roguelikes.Absolutely recommended, the gameplay is simple to grab but incredibly deep to understand, after 3 hours you will still be discovering new combos, and after 5 hours you will start to grasp how much you still have to uncover and experiment. All this with the elegance and beauty of being almost pure pixel art cards, without environments, characters, dialogue, story, anything really. A masterpiece of pure gameplay without really cutting corners but just built for it's purpose, pure addictive entertainment and brain-teasing.

_childDocuments_.review: Balatro is a straight-forward, incredibly designed and radically fun game that uses the gameplay of poker as a foundation, and builds upon it massively with no-nonsense roguelite mechanics. It's relaxing and distinctive atmosphere provided by its graphics, sound design and music help it to stand out as one of the most unique games of the decade. Balatro's gameplay loop is simple: play high-scoring hands to earn chips and defeat blinds. What makes every run unique is the player's choice of Jokers - unique items that change the rules of the game you play. Jokers can range from straightforward e.g. Jokers rewarding you extra chips if you play flush hands, to incredibly complex e.g. Jokers that multiply your score for every time you a play a hand that isn't your most-played hand. This is the magic in Balatro. Its core gameplay is so intuitively simple yet so rewarding to master that it'll have you hooked with play-sessions lasting for hours at a time. As you experiment with Jokers and different playstyles, the game will reward you with more Jokers to garnish your future runs with. The majority of Jokers you discover will be unlocked naturally simply by you playing the game and pushing its mechanics to their limits. At 88 hours in, I have unlocked 149 out of the 150 Jokers available at the point of writing this review, and I have never had to Google how to unlock Jokers or look at the 'Collections' tab available in the game to figure out how to unlock that last one. The wonder of discovering the game is just as rewarding as the fruits of that labour - playing runs at the highest difficulty (or 'Stake' as its affectionately referred to as in Balatro) is some of the plainest fun you can have in a game where the only thing you need to do is press the left-mouse button.It's a labour of love, and I'm wholeheartedly glad that Balatro is getting its flowers because we need more innovative games like this that push the envelope on what a simple yet fun game can be. I simply can't wait for the first major content update coming to Balatro in 2025.

_childDocuments_.review: I have just completed my first gold stakes run and despite how many times I have been spat on and pushed around by RNG to even get to that point, I still come back to this game for more. There is an unshakeable addictive charm around this game; I am not even sure if it is a good kind of charm, but this game has me absolutely hooked and it shows.With my Steam Deck, and this game alone, I can eat up whatever plane, road or train trip life throws at me like it is just a minor inconvenience of time that passes in an instant. I have never had this feeling about a game so strongly as I do about this game. This is the ultimate time-waster bar none, and therefore, one of the best games on the go that you can find.Even more good news is that there is a new Beta branch that addresses some balancing issues and also enables more players to try the higher difficulties of play should they want to. Personally I haven't minded the high stakes as much, since I am absolutely hooked already, but I am glad that more people will be able to play this game at a difficulty that they think is fair.The gist of it all is, this game is an absolute blast of a roguelike deckbuilder, and with only just a smidge of interest in poker, I can absolutely recommend this game to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally secured my pre-nerf gold stake win (of course I need to add the nerd flex) and I feel compelled to sing Balatro its praises. This is easily one of the most unique, innovative, and downright fun games I've ever played. Other than charming art + visuals, and the vibe-y (and strangely alluring) music, Balatro is just pure gameplay - and it's brilliant.Poker is a core foundation, but this is NOT a poker game - poker hands are the only operating knowledge you really need to know, and the game does a good job of telling you what is, and isn't, a poker hand at any given moment. You'll learn them quickly. There's about a ~20-30 minute learning curve, and once you "get it", you're off to a great time. If that isn't enough to convince you - it's also worth considering that this is a solo dev project (thank you for this masterpiece LocalThunk!) and only $15, putting the majority of recent $70 AAA games to shame.

_childDocuments_.review: is fantastic! Easy to learn, every run gives you something new to play with for your perpetual "one last run," and the game's premise is very addicting.Gameplay is simple, really! You construct poker hands with the cards drawn from your deck, and earn chips! Each hand type starts at Lv. 1 and has a specified base chip & multiplier amount which increases as you upgrade it via "planet cards."Augmenting this system are the joker cards, which have various effects and will affect your game in a myriad of ways. You'll primarily be combining these poker hands with the jokers to reach ever-increasing amounts of chips.Why?Because each round, you'll be tasked with earning a certain amount in a specified number of hands. Each round sees a Small Blind, Big Blind & Boss Blind. These will require ever-increasing number of chips to conquer, with the Boss Blind also adding a certain debuff to the match. These include limiting the effectiveness of some suits, require you to only play one type of hand, play only a single hand, and more.There's a collection page in the game as well which keeps track of all of the cards you've unlocked as you play, which alone could provide dozens of hours of fun to go through and collect!Overall, the gameplay is very addicting and highly recommended.To be frank, there isn't any story in this game!The game runs perfectly fine for... practically any tier of hardware. Its art style isn't demanding and the game is also tiny in size, clocking in at less than 50MB. Rest assured, if you meet the basic requirements, you'll have a perfect experience! is magnificent and definitely one of the breakout hits of 2024. I see myself playing this game a LOT in the future. I can absolutely recommend this to anyone looking for an easy to pick up & put down game!

I just want one more run to get that sweet, sweet satisfaction of building that perfect deck.Balatro is a poker based roguelike that feels very accessible, but offers a shocking amount of depth once you understand how  to leverage the jokers, plants & tarot cards, and all the bonuses that can be applied to your standard deck.  Soon you're miles beyond a classic approach Poker rules, building 5 of a kind flushes leveled to 10, with a handful of enhanced aces that get multiplied to the moon by 5 synergized jokers   Every run feels absolutely unique to the last, as the strengths of the specific joker combos you earn have you playing a different strategy each and every time.  It's so satisfying when you find synergies that compound multipliers on top of multipliers until your hand climbs form the thousands to millions and beyond.The graphics are perfectly simple and cohesive. _childDocuments_.review: Update at 90h played: I think this is the best roguelite ever. No hyperbole. It's at least a refreshingly fun play if you're exhausted with bullet heavens. There is no requirement for any hand-eye coordination or reaction speed as long as you have functioning hands, which is perfect for when my body doesn't feel like gaming but my brain does. I am reminded of how my mother would play Solitaire during her downtime... and I am totally going to be playing this if and when I hit old age.Poker on the outside, solitaire on the inside. One of those games that makes you go "why didn't I think of this?" You could argue that there's too much RNG but... it's a poker game, and you still have to not know what you're doing to not have a decent run, which is nice. Don't take it too seriously - leave that for the real poker table.Personally I don't find it as addictive as others seem to, merely satisfying. Great for a couple of rounds here and there. Balatro seems designed for the Deck from the ground up, 100%, which fits nicely with that pick-up-and-play nature. It's a straight-up better experience on that platform than either a desktop or laptop, especially with the touchscreen. (Edit: I got an OLED now and the touchscreen on that is way better, to the point where I mostly now play this game with touch controls.)As for the difficulty, it starts off relatively easy, at least for me, and ramps up the difficulty as you unlock more decks and stakes. With the basic default decks, I've noticed that the game will rig it in your favour slightly for the first couple of blinds when on easier stakes. Later decks and stakes ask quite a lot from your potential mathematical prowess - you better know how to card-count and multiply on the fly. I suppose you could use a calculator if you're so inclined... but I personally find that ruins the satisfaction a bit.However, one issue that I've run into at 117h played is that Balatro's later, more difficult decks are way too situational and box you into making specific hands, often only one or two types. This can make the RNG nature of the game a bit too much of a factor, but I guess that's why they're "special" decks. With some of those, whether you lose or have a chance at victory is determined by the first two hands you play along with the store behaving itself in giving you the right jokers and planet cards.This game could also really benefit from an optimisation patch, since it uses way too much electricity for what it is. Judging from battery use, Balatro seems to be not very optimised under the hood. 30 minutes of Brotato, which is a game with a hell of a lot more CPU stuff going on, will sip my LCD Deck battery down to 90% or so, often higher. Balatro? 60%, especially if you get a ton of combos going. I recommend capping the framerate to 30fps or even 20fps, since it doesn't really need more than that, and doing so reduced battery consumption for 30 minutes of play to about the same as Brotato. Given that this is a simple enough game that a version of it could feasibly to made that works on 30 year old computers or even older, I think this speaks to a larger issue of game developers and game engines simply not caring about optimisation.
