_childDocuments_.review: This is a deck builder game where your goal is to beat 8 levels (antes) of 3 rounds each, where the score requirement grows exponentially. You'll lose a lot, but you'll gradually unlock more "jokers" which alter the game's rules or provide multipliers and points under certain hand/deck conditions, where some unlocks have a strong advantage to beating the first 8 levels (and then progressing into the endless mode challenge). There are many game altering cards to explore, many types of challenges/bosses, deck types, etc. that can keep you entertained for quite a while. As you play, you are constantly weighing your choices to mitigate risk and alter probability to work in your favor, even when you manage to build a seemingly broken deck (which is often quickly destroyed in endless mode).Also always check the boss rule on the start of a new level so you can hopefully prepare and say "nah, I win" or "it's so over" with confidence, instead of being blindsided and definitely losing.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really fun when it's new and you're getting your feet wet, but the later difficulties almost instantly become nothing but an RNG fest. Oh, you didn't get a xMult Joker? New Game. You're supersuiting Diamonds and then the Ante 7 boss debuffs all Diamonds? New Game. You've got a perfect build but lose the Ante 8 Boss because 13 out of the 16 Aces in your deck SOMEHOW magically ended up all stacked in the bottom quarter of the deck and you can't dig any further? New Game. You're $1 short of buying Throwback right before the Ante 6 Boss? New Game. Got dealt a hand with three Pairs in it for the fifth time in a row, defying all odds and statistical probability? New Game. You literally just keep restarting the run until the game decides it's time to hand you the things that it needs to hand you in order to win the higher stakes. There's no engagement. There's no planning. There's no strategy. There's no forethought. Just click the cards and pray. And it's a real shame, because this game has such an amazing foundation and sound and art and concept that I would love to just put 5,000 hours into this thing, but I've Gold Stickered like five decks at this point and I literally feel my blood pressure start rising when I even think about sitting down to play.If you're curious and don't mind throwing the money away to play this game very casually here and there, you'll likely have a great time.But if you're like me and many other people that want to see every corner and collect every collectible from the roguelikes they play, avoid Balatro. You might as well just go to the casino and try to win some actual cash, because high stakes in Balatro is nothing better than a glorified roulette machine.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the good ones.Pretty much immediately graduated into the "Genre Exemplar" category for roguelites and card games, personally.It's full of mechanics that mesh together really well, the gameplay is amazing, and there seem to be a lot of options for build versatility and playstyle. The UI is fantastic (special mention to the cards remaining table when viewing your deck in game), the backgrounds are busy enough to add texture and flavor while being simple enough to not distract.The art is lovingly crafted, immediately recognisable at a glance, highly detailed, and the shaders on the foil treatments are magnificent.The soundtrack is good, but because the way all of the songs bleed into each other (and the droning organ pad is good but it gets a bit grating being in one of the most common tracks), it can get stale after a few hours. I'm usually a purist when it comes to soundtrack but at hour 6 I'm strongly considering muting it and playing other stuff. So far, that's my only gripe.Finally, the price seems fair. I can easily see myself getting my money's worth (if I haven't already). I'd suggest trying it - you'll probably be grabbed in the first two hours.

_childDocuments_.review: I now own two copies of this game, on two separate platforms. This game is such a rare gem that I have no problem at all paying for it multiple times. Balatro has easily replaced my previous 'desert island' games. A simple set of rules that have you building hands to earn stacks of chips to win each round is enhanced by a multitude of ways to buff the individual cards in your deck, add or subtract from your deck, make each hand type score more, and that's all before you add the rule-breaking Jokers that basically super charge everything. You're battling time pressure and each round slowly ratchets up the chips needed to beat it. And just when you think you've built the perfect Balatro engine and it's a cake walk to unlocking another deck...a Boss Blind turns up that throws a spanner in the works. Delightful and beautifully well executed. Cannot recommend enough. Just buy it already.

_childDocuments_.review: Score attack poker roguelike but you cheat with card upgrades and jokers that add new rules to scoring. I always fall in love with games that make winning feel like cheating, and this is definitely one of them. If you have a steam deck, I'd imagine this would be one of the best games to have on it.There are a lot of areas to pay attention to. Your 52 card deck is simulated, so you can actually learn to count cards and play according to that. Or find a joker that makes lower number cards more valuable. Or use booster packs and tarot cards to add, change, and remove cards from the deck. It's quite easy to get a flush when 95% of your entire deck is suited as diamonds, and the last 5% give you multipliers for being in your hand as you play other cards.You'll always want to end up with a plan based on what jokers were presented to you. Plans like having only Fibonacci numbered cards, the biggest deck possible, or to feed a cannibal joker to buff it's multiplier. There are so many cool ideas that are all over the place in terms of effectiveness. It's fun to find out what is capable of carrying you to the end game.Edit: This is no longer a normal, healthy addition to my life.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first ever Rougelike Deckbuilder that I've played and truth be told, it's actually addicting. Every run you're entitled to trying out something new. Like making an entire build based around Flushes, or even Pairs and see how far you can get from the Blinds. The game is like an urge to keep on playing even after you close it a few minutes or hours later as it can also be a game of zen for some people as you play Poker. This has been a very fun game for me currently and I hope to rack up more hours in this game when I'm bored.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an exceptional roguelike deckbuilder and an instant classic to the genre. The perfect balance of luck and skill, and it is fairly easy to restart once you realize a run is doomed, however one Joker can come along and save the whole thing. It is a gamble to continue, and so you what feels like biblically compelled to keep playing. "If I just do this!" or "If I just get that card!" filled your head the whole time in a deeply fulfilling manner. You may not gamble with fiat in Balatro, but each time you sit down to play the game you wager whether or not you will be satisfied playing for one hour. You will not. You will need more.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: not particularly interested in poker, but Balatro weaves together numerical strategy and the high of drawing the one card you need to create a rougelite experience more unique and enjoyable that anything i've played since the binding of isaaccontent does begin to feel linear as you reach the higher difficulties and the dominant strategies become more and more required to succeed, but this did very little to detract from my experience, and only reared its head after around 45 hours of play
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent take on a rougelike deckbuilder. It is pretty addicting, especially at first. My only complaints are no long-term progression, and not enough unique variety. You are pretty much forced to always build high multipliers no matter what deck you use. So at this point it is getting a little stale, but I still have a lot of hours to put into this game. Hopefully the devs continue to add content and variety for more interesting builds. _childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend but with a caveat: it got boring really quickly for me.This isn't your average game of poker, though it is based on it. The jokers everyone normally removes from a pack of real cards are used as modifiers in this game, to which there are many.The thing is, it gets really boring really fast.If you absolutely love poker but don't want to play with other people and are okay with having no real permanent meta to enhance future games, then have at it.Other than that, you can get a few hours out of this game. Just don't think you'll be coming back to it over and over, especially after you've figured out how to cheese the scoring system beaten it for the first time.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, it works great on my Steam Deck!I'm not really much of a poker person. My only experience with poker is from the Red Dead Redemption games. This is more 'roguelite' than 'poker' but it perfectly pairs the gambling aspect with the absurd mechanics of traditional roguelites.My most recent run was a series of high card plays. Counter-intuitively earning more points from playing my lowest valued cards, because each time I played a high card hand I'd get a multiplier bonus from each high card hand I played in total.It's always fun to try something new even if it doesn't end up working out. The visual style, mechanics, and the music all coalesce to detach the aesthetic from the base framework of gambling in reality to present you with gambling away virtual things in its own asserted hyper-reality.It's like gambling in the Binding of Isaac turned into a card game. Balatro IS, essentially, The Binding of Poker.You'll be hard pressed to find anything so accessible, unique, and deep. I absolutely love it, and after 40+ hours of playing it exclusively on my Steam Deck I still haven't nearly unlocked or seen everything.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely the best casual roguelite I've played this year! Balatro has a low barrier to entry as it bases itself on the well-known card game poker, but it has great depth and a good level of player skill expression. If you like watching number go up but you are not engaged by idle games, this is your pal.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, I have given this game a whole day of my life so far. As some one with a newborn and little time between naps to game, this was the perfect game.I genuinely want to the thank the creator for making a game that can be played for long periods of time, but can so easily be put down if there is a crying baby to care for.I love being a parent, but this game is an excellent mini escape that I look forward to every time nap time comes around. My steam deck is just a balatro machine.This will likely be my game of the year.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: I’m no poker aficionado. My knowledge of the game is mostly gleaned from casual observations and snippets from TV shows. I couldn't identify a Royal Flush if my life depended on it (I've got the achievement for discarding/ruining a royal flush in-hand...), but I know it's something you want. Balatro, despite its poker facade, isn't really poker. It's the first game that’s made me understand and love the core mechanics of poker, and it's easily one of the most engrossing titles of the year.Calling Balatro a poker game is simply inaccurate. There are no opponents to play against. Instead, it's a poker-inspired roguelike deckbuilder. The real poker aspect lies in learning to assemble hands like a Flush, Straight, or Full House. A handy glossary illustrates these hands and their scores, which helped me, a poker novice, finally memorize and enjoy the game.Balatro’s design makes it incredibly addictive. The fast-paced, snappy gameplay allows for quick sessions, yet it’s deep enough to occupy entire afternoons. Even when the game doesn’t go your way, you’re compelled to try again. The music, though limited to a single track, is highly engaging and adds to the game’s hypnotic appeal.Balatro is a must-play. Dive in and experience it for yourself. I could easily write another thousand words or more, but I think you should enjoy discovering it on your own. Explore the 150 unique jokers and the myriad of other cards that make this game a true gem. Priced at $15, Balatro offers immense value. Get it, get it, get it.Oh also - I could listen to the main audio track for hours and hours. It's delightful.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: Mastapiece.Got my first successful run within 3 hours of getting the game, which is crazy given the longevity (and the grueling grind to victory) expected of rogue-likes. Balatro, true to its Poker inspiration, feels way more reliant on RNG than any of its peers like Slay the Spire, or even non-card stalwarts like FTL. This does lead to some insane scenarios though. Like my aforementioned first successful run where the Jokers I had were synergizing so well with my Deck that I was stomping on late-game blinds with 4x the chips on the very first hand. Wild, and incredibly addicting, because all I want to do is keep chasing that high.Coming to the game itself, wow, if this isn't a design masterclass all on its own. The art, UX, the introductory tutorial, the cards and their effects themselves, everything is so perfectly crafted. Even the game's round-driven pacing is digital crack, there is zero friction between thinking "One more run" and actually playing it.Maybe the sheen of Balatro's brilliance will fade a bit after I play some more for collecting and achievement hunting, but for what I've enjoyed of it so far, I can't but help give it at least a 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: Still my top 2024 GOTY contender. The addictive gameplay loop as you altar your deck so you are consistently drawing 5 Ace of Hearts has yet to get old. For $15, I'd highly recommend getting this game and then getting it again once the mobile port is released so you can play Balatro 24/7

_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: I usually do not hop on the hype for a newly released title. But something about its design and presentation kept catching my eye. As much as I love and enjoy Slay The Spire Respectfully, I barely put any time into it so I was weary whether this would be the same case. But the praise regarding this deck builder roguelike is just as earned. There is so much depth to this card game. Balatro's game design and originality deserves a spot in anyone's library of games. Upon booting it up I was immediately flashed back to Hypnospace Outlaw because of Balatro's music and presentation. It made me feel home sick to play that game again not gonna lie. On the surface it's hard to understand whats going on screen but after playing the first couple of binds it felt absolute intuitive. It's the kind of game that feels as good to play as it looks and sounds. I never felt cheated out of a run or lost solely because of RNG and it truly rewards the player's poker knowledge and Versatility.What really makes the game for me is how risky it can be to discard cards. Do you waste a turn playing a pair of Aces? Or do you risk discarding them because you're really close to a straight or flush? The extra cards and jokers you earn also changes the run each time, allowing you to upgrade the cards available or to multiply a certain hand played.I'll be honest I wasn't sure how fun of a purchase this game was going to be because of the price, nor was I sure how honest people's opinions were whether this was truly a phenomenal title or just another flavor of the week to gush over. But this. Is truly one hell of a videogame as it is a pioneer to a genre of whats to come from other future releases.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: I feel obligated to provide a dissenting opinion to the unanimous praise this game gets. There's fun to be had in the early stages of the game, and in the silly and wacky automated builds that make big numbers, undeniably. When things are working out, Balatro provides a fun sandbox. The problem is when things aren't working out, which is the statistical majority of the time if you're playing it seriously. Beyond a basic level, there's very little skill expression in this game, leaving you victim to the whims of the random number generator to lose constantly and unavoidably. The game is addicting and provides a compelling player fantasy in its early stages, and this is a problem because it makes the mindless slog that is the later difficulties actively frustrating, but hard to walk away from. If you're a rational individual who can play till satisfied and put it down when it stops being fun, then it should be a pleasant and rewarding experience. Otherwise, be warned.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: It is a very interesting roguelike deck-builder with a very specific flavour and honestly a very, very good presentation. The whole CRT-vibe and the feeling of the environment you are transported in is intriguing. Pixel graphics make this game feel very light, while still retaining enough complexity to keep you interested and entertained in unlocking more content.The whole quirk is to build your deck via various enhancements to your cards, build the best combination of limited amount of jokers and periodically use limited power ups. All while battling ever-increasing small, big and boss blinds, which force you to squeeze the most out of your built deck, joker and bonus combo. The fact this is made via an open-source Love2D (a Lua framework) is also notable, if you are into software development and whole open-source scene.Also works great on Steam Deck and allows you to play for long sessions, without sacrificing too much battery.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: It's Balatro.In all seriousness, it's an amazing game and a supreme example of how great aesthetic and game feel can carry a simple premise all the way until the end. It does get repetitive and I'm starting to have slightly less fun after putting 50+ hours into it (my time logged on Steam is far less than my actual time played) as it does rely a LOT on luck. But, that's the entire point of the game, whether you like it or not. It's brutally unfair and extremely rewarding. Getting a high score has never felt so good. The soundtrack is mesmerizing. There's a reason this game has become such a viral hit, and when you look at the negative reviews here on Steam, you'll see that most of them still have dozens of hours logged despite leaving a negative review. And to make things even better, the developer has been consistently updating it since release and I expect it to only get better over time. Balatro is one of the few "Must have" titles on Steam, and at this price, who can complain?

_childDocuments_.review: I love watching stream vods. I have for a long time. I put them on in the background of working on assignments or just general tasks around the house. It's a nice way to not focus too much on the audio but keep myself entertained. I've recently been watching Vinny Vinesauce vods because he's a silly guy (and I'm in jerma withdrawal) and he plays some fun games. I know he has a reputation with deck builders, his community loves to clown on him. So while I'm watching one of his Steam Nextfest compilation videos and he says "yes, a card game." I know what to expect. At least I think I do. He learns some of the mechanics and goes over the features; play poker hands to score points in the form of chips, defeat blinds of varying difficulties, buy booster packs, and of course, the jewel of the Balatro mechanics; add up to five Jokers with various effects to potentially increase the score of your poker hand. This game had my interest. I had only played poker once but understood the hands well enough, the booster packs were always a welcome addition to a deck builder, the graphics were fun and stylized, the animations snappy and satisfying, and immediately my deck building brain picked out the potential synergies that could be crafted with the right jokers. As I watched Vinny play I felt the insatiable itch in the back of my mind. The itch to deck build. I clicked on the first full Balatro vod on Vinny's Fullsauce channel, pleased to see many of the mistakes he was making during his first runs (that i thought I had so expertly caught onto) were addressed and corrected. I felt genuine frustration through the screen when Vinny missed a play that I assumed was optimal, more so than I would if the miss-plays were my own. While watching the second vod I had put down whatever other task I was suppose to be completing, solely watching the cards snap onto the table as Vinny played, speaking out loud to him when I had a particularly harsh criticism or jubilant praise. I began to dread as his runs approached higher boss blinds, fearing that the lovely synergy he had crafted in his deck and Joker selection would all be for not at a particularly brutal challenge. Now, if you have read this far you may be wondering why I bothered to continue watching these videos without playing the game myself. I have already admitted I was no longer using them as a guise to multitask and instead was fully immersed like I had been playing the games myself. The issue was I studying for uni finals at the same time, and I knew the time sacrificed to Balatro could be minimized to only a few hours if I continued to placate my itch with Vinny's videos. If I had bought the game there would be no limit to the amount of Balatro I could consume, so I resisted for the time being. During the entirety of studying for my finals I watched and rewatched every Balatro vod Vinny released. This was to not open myself up to more, so I could potentially focus on my schoolwork. The day of my last exam was a blur. I returned home and ignored the queries of friends and family on how the exam had gone, heading straight to steam. Checking out with Balatro in my cart was a religious experience. The short download time was magnified by my impatience, Steam's download progress bar creeping leisurely. And then the game was open.It was everything I hoped for and so much more.The designs of all the cards were fun and striking, the unlock menu a treat to pursue. Every aspect of the game made me excited to play. I was immensely frustrated when my runs did not breach even the 5th Ante, yet I only worked harder to craft a deck that would lead me to victory. I am not some Balatro God, merely a humble servant to its whims. Thank you Vinny.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: What everyone has been saying about how addictive Balatro is is 100% true. Every failed run feels fair and I end it up thinking what I could have done better and what I will do differently in the future.In addition to the great gameplay, the music, the visuals, and the overall design create a unique atmosphere - relaxing, but also having strong hints of wrongness and playing Balatro feels intoxicating in a way.The game is very much worth the money, especially if you are a fan of card games and rogue-likes.

Any hand that scores less than 'x' does not count as a hand.If you score over the blind in a single hand, gain $2.Played cards get shuffled back into deck. x3 if no cards are in your hand after hand is played. Tags:Jokers can be switched in and out of consumable slots.Legendary Joker: May play 6 cards in a hand.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't my typical type of review, but I have to tell someone about Balatro. So imagine taking a game of poker and blending some roguelike elements, add deck building mechanics then sprinkling a synergy system that rewards you for thinking outside the box AND now imagine that game only costing $15? Well, that's Balatro in simplest terms, See guys, I like a game of chance, I love to gamble & this fills my body with endorphins without having to go into crippling debt! you start the game off being essentially berated by a Joker card, and it quickly shows you HOW to play Balatro which is at it's core Poker but with the aforementioned elements.You start by choosing a deck, in the beginning only a few available but as you play you'll unlock up to 15 different decks all with v. Points scored will be dependent on the level of your hand, for example if you play this hand Aces will equal 11 each and 4s will be 4. So that score of 30 will be added to the blue margin and then multiplied by 2 (if you dont have any jokers active). It's possible to level hands up using Planetary cards which is how this flush is level 2 and you'll see the transformation to level 3. I'll show you as I play this flush how it all adds up for you- and baam that's pretty much how you win a blind. You beat each "blind" or level by playing Poker each "ante" is 3 levels- small blind, big blind & boss blind- each with varying scores you must beat with the added difficulty of the boss blind having an adverse effect such as diamonds not counting towards your score, only being able to play a certain hand like two pairs or flushes, having no discards etc etc, surpassing the Blind score will have you win a certain amount of money AND if you beat it in fewer turns the "hands" you didn't use will add up at the end of each round (usually $1/per hand) then you're taken to a shop where you can buy Joker cards, there are 150 of em with varying effects, Vouchers that can add for example an extra Hand or Discard or make the rerolls cost less, planetary cards that can level up a certain hand, tarot & spectral cards that can add bonuses to your playing cards & booster packs where you can ADD playing cards plus any of the aforementioned cards like jokers, tarot, spectral & planetary.the objective is to beat 8 antes each ante with a set of 3 blinds, but it is MUCH easier said than done. ive had some of the most ridiculous combos like look at this synergy right here, my Business Card Joker has a 50% chance of scoring me $2 when I play a face card + it's a Polychrome so it'll tally at the end of the hand a 1.5 multiplier, my space trousers adds 2x to every Two Pair i play (which includes full houses) my Scary Face joker is a boost for face cards that adds 30 chips  aka the blue score to the left of the screen that then gets multiplied at the end by the red margin my Rocket joker adds 50 chips PLUS after every blind, I get $3, but are you ready for the KICKER guys? You know how I said that the Business Card, and the Scary Face adds only to FACE cards? Well Pareidolia Joker MAKES ALL my cards "face" cards. Playing this straight you'll see all the added bonuses I get. 10k in one hand. But because I   of the SHOP if I wanted with all the money I keep receiving. and it gets me thinking for sure I'm winning this game. NOPE. Prepare to lose A LOT. After 8 hours I thought, I may not win one of these then it all clicked and I cheesed it HARD I mean HARD. And I scrounged up a win... in normal difficulty with a basic deck... I realized this game was meant to be beaten over & over, it has me convinced that if you're thinking of buying this game- you need to be a masochist because PAIN YOU WILL FEEL and I want to both hug & kick the dev only known to me as Local Thunk- because I KNOW he has got to be a sadist, getting off on our pain.... but in conclusion, if you're thinking about getting this game. BUY IT NOW! If you haven't heard of this game because gaming is having a hell of a year, check it out. It's so simple to pick up and just play for a few mins or sink a couple hours into it. Oh and if you have a SteamDeck? This is where Balatro shines, playing it on the go on my lunchbreak or in bed? *chefs kiss*

_childDocuments_.review: + Figuring out combos is fun.+ There's a thinking and preparation aspect to this game, but this game's process actually makes that thinking fun. Don't like thinking too much? Well there's cards that ramp up or reward you for playing a certain way over and over again.+ Animations are pure dopamine. Big numbers extremely good unga bunga.- The biggest flaw of this game: Because of the rng-centric nature of "playing cards," it's an extreme sufferer of a problem that's not as pronounced in other roguelikes that lean more on mechanics. Some runs you will not get a good combination of jokers, or maybe you got a good combination of jokers but don't have the consumables/jokers to manipulate your deck to take advantage of it. Sometimes your broken build isn't broken *enough.*  Especially in the higher stakes, many runs are unwinnable no matter what you do.- 100% completion seems *too* dedicated, and another problem is that once you've sorted the good cards from the bad or overly niche cards, the game becomes very stale if you play it too much.Recommend overall, but mileage varies depending on how often you play.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Slay the Spire, this game looked boring to me, lacking cool enemies or weapons; instead, it featured traditional playing cards. While I enjoy poker, I couldn't see the excitement in a single-player "poker game". Nevertheless, I purchased it merely out of curiosity, fully intending to request a refund within the two-hour window. However, I am addicted! Even if I had the option to refund it now, I wouldn't.Although it draws inspiration from Poker, this game is not your typical card game. It offers a significant amount of freedom, and the combos/synergy you'll uncover, create an entertainment value that's difficult to describe. If you have any interest in roguelike deck builders, I highly recommend giving this game a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: Balatro is one of the all time best roguelikes and deck builders ever made. Actually magical experience of a game that feels like design genius. Who would have thought that jokers were one of the best ways to handle equipment in a roguelike, that hands allow for a variety of different skills and by shaping your deck you essentially choose what resources you have available to use said skills. Incredibly excited for any future updates as the design space of the game has so much opportunity for new things and alternative challenges and playstyles. Captures the fact that games are Fun first and foremost. Love this game, binged it for four days straight.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely addicting. I can't put this game down. The animations, soundtrack and mechanics make it so satisfying when you're making big scores. Don't be disencouraged if you haven't played poker before. This game teaches everything you need to get a feel for things and score some big cards. Jokers spice it up and you can even play the same seed with friends to see who can get the bigger score. Great game, 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute banger. Balatro is now my golden standard when it comes to roguelike deckbuilders. I don't see myself growing tired it. There are so many possible joker and enchantment combinations to explore, I'm constantly finding new ones. Lots of depth, lots of replayablitiy.If this game looks good at all to you I would definitely recommend picking it up. If you like roguelikes, deckbuilders and/or poker it's a must buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, saw this game was recommended and thought I'd try it out. I wasn't expecting much, but OH MY GAWD it's so addicting! Poker was fun, but now this is even better! It reminds me a lot of Inscryption too! Definitely recommend if you're into card games with fun challenges.Seriously, if you don't fall in love with this game in the first 5 run throughs, then I'll be floored.Get it!

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely and incredibly addictive game. Such a simple idea that has been taken to the next level with the added roguelike gameplay loop in addition to clever power ups via the Jokers. _childDocuments_.review: Let me state this first because Steam doesnt have a neutral review and I'm giving this game a negative review because I want it to be a neutral review ( also kinda helps people / dev to see whats my problem with the game)Also let me state that this game is . It  be a positive review but after spending countless days, thinking over how to review this as well as writing a guide to this game, I'm kinda certain I want to this game a neutral review ( but alas, no such thing exist so negative it is ). For me personally, I find that Balatro suffers from a fundamental problem.So let say you play StS or some rogue-lite card-building deck game. You go to a room, you fight a monster which can end your run, you win, you get items / cards / upgrades etc and you do this till you become strong  to fight the boss and over time, you do this enough to be strong to beat the final boss. Balatro does the same thing  there isnt any sort of excitement or punishment towards you. To explain what I mean, here is a simple example of it. . Balatro doesnt have that, weirdly because the concept feels the same but it isnt. It has a require minimum passing mark but it doesnt have the same feeling of conquest. I'll come back time to time to try and test out the game once more stuffs have been updated but generally this is how I feel about the game. Again by no mean its a bad game but it has that weird thing that keeps me from getting too invested.[If the dev is reading this: Personally I dont know how to really fix this problem ( or do you want to fix it? ) because its quite unique in its own way. My only thought currently at the moment is that maybe, every blind run, everytime a hand is being played, you can increase the require blind score or decrease the hand size temporary or something in that effect?The other way I can think of is that you give the player a HP bar and everytime mistakes are made or something, you dock their HP? Make it feel like some sort of punishment.Lastly, you could run a deck like darts where you have to X score to begin with and get it to 0. Reverse play hand. Just a thought ]

_childDocuments_.review: This will eat your whole day if you let it. Then your whole week. If you've got a problem with that (gambling, video game obsession, or both) don't pick it up, for your own mental health! Trust me on this.That said, it's really fun, and if you've got self-control (or not enough to heed the above warning) it IS worth picking up if you like poker and/or neo-roguelikes. It does what it sets out to do well. It doesn't feel like I'm just repeating the same strategy over and over; one run and the next will be plenty different. It doesn't have a few broken strategies you run into the ground.I have a few QoL gripes (mainly having no good indicators for sets of 2/3/4/5 cards or consecutive ranks in your hand, but also not being able to see the end score of a hand until you play it, even though you could punch it into a calculator if you wanted) but I wouldn't say they're dealbreaking.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: Do believe the hype. There's a mild learning curve here and then an incredible world of fun and addictive gameplay after you get the hang of it. The negatives are that the game does rely on a hefty dose of RNG and luck, it's still got those elements from regular gambling, so you're not signing up for a purely skill-based experience. But if you can buy into the mixture of charisma, randomness, crazy mechanics and general gameplay loop it's incredibly fun. One of those games I had to actively make myself put down because I was playing too much.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good.The aesthetics, overall vibe, music, and gameplay concept are so appealing right out of the gate. Then the cool ass synergies & mental gymnastics over probability really reel you all the way in. The game starts off super addicting, watching number go up super satisfying. Then the game challenges you with unique challenges in the boss blinds, which are usually* very cool.Despite all that, if I could give this game a rating, it'd be a strong 7. Unfortunately, the game is way too hard and a bit RNG based. I'm all about the challenge of juggling probability & risk/reward, but sometimes it genuinely feels like you were destined to lose. Every time I play this game I get the coolest synergies that I'm always super hype to play, but always lose just near the end without the satisfaction of winning a run. I think the game's base difficulty is a little too hard, in my opinion. I got a synergy all about thinning my deck to only be Aces, along with Ace synergy, 5 of kind synergy, and even tarot card duplication joker's. Yet I still lost because the RNG had decided it to be. 9 Aces out of 30 cards and I couldn't get a single one when I needed it.In short, this game has really good high points, yet some really bad low points. The good outways the bad, though, and I feel myself getting better at juggling the probability problems every run I do. I trust the game dev will only improve this game as time goes on, so luckily it's only up from here.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this is an easy buy for anyone who knows what the terms "reroll", "interest", "boosterpacks", "flush" and "foil" mean...In more words this might not be the best of all deckbuilders, but it is for sure a new cornerstone in runbased deckbuilding games. This should have been around sooner and there are some wayyy less spectacular or succesfull tries before it.It's designed in an almost addicting way, too. The sound design and visual design spew out dopamine right into my brain. When the music softens down as you open your pack, or how it slows down into an almost bad trip when you lose... until you press new run and the music takes back up and forces me to smile, because this run is going to be better anyway.And have you noticed where your mouse is placed after a round, when you click the cash-out button? RIGHT ABOVE THE FIRST ITEM IN THE NEXT SHOP! You will read it, you will click it if it fits. You will not find an end xDSo let this be an actual warning to addictive personalities. There is no real point at which the game gives you a good enough reason to quit.It is not as exciting or deep as "Slay the Spire-likes", but that might be exactly what you are looking for!For me it is the blend of growing up on regular playing cards, transitioning over pokemon to magic from there to hearthstone and runeterra and finally to deckbuilders and rouge likes. If this is resonating with you, get this gem of a game!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing.It has poker rules but you are encouraged to cheat by transforming your deck through random booster packs.Be ready to handcraft the perfect deck, and sometimes lose by stumbling upon one of many random challenges (boss blinds) which might have the perfect combo of nullifying all your hard work (For example: "all cards are considered face cards" joker coupled with "all face cards are drawn face down" boss blind).What a blast.The demo already had tons of content, the full game has a lot more.TL;DR: worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: The sound design alone in this game is worth $15. The gameplay loop is brutally addictive. I hear the music in my dreams and I can't stop thinking about joker synergies. Most of the negative reviews complain about it being too hard, but that's only the case if you're braindead and dont think about your actions. This isnt a game that you can just mindlessly charge through. This is only game I love losing at because it usually means I was fighting to make a risky build work. Some boss blinds still need balancing but as a 1.0 release it's far better than any other card game rougelike i've ever played, and that's coming from someone who has 1000 hours in Slay the Spire across all platforms. This is a flawless game.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and unique deckbuilder roguelike!Love the graphics and the poker motif. Made it very easy to convince non-gamer friends to give it a try. With any roguelike, the biggest things for me is build variety and how satisfying the game is once you get a good build. This game excels in both categories! There is a large variety of Jokers and card modifiers to create many fun and unique builds.And when you finally achieve that god build, it is so satisfying!RNG can sometimes get a little annoying early game at higher stakes but even after a string of bad runs, I'm still ready to pick the game back up and try again.Played entirely on Steam Deck and the game ran flawlessly. I experienced no issues at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: Balatro is an exceptional deck building roguelike that squeezes endless hours of gameplay out of simple and satisfying game mechanics. Each new run is a gauntlet of poker hands where you enhance your 52 card deck and build a powerful roster of joker cards to multiply your score through the roof and beyond. You will be challenged by a variety of bosses that demand flexibility from your deck and raw power from each hand you play. The gameplay loop is deeply satisfying as you discover new jokers, tarot cards, planet cards, and powerful builds that take you to victory and eventually to the hardest difficulties, which are truly unforgiving. The game features unique and fitting music, a super crisp aesthetic, and a fantastic UI that strengthens the gameplay -- helping players to quickly develop familiarity with its many features, most notably the variety of cards. I think the game could fit a few more jokers and bosses, but the variety is already astounding as is. With that said, it is an incredibly well-polished game for which I can find few criticisms. I highly recommend Balatro to all fans of roguelikes, and especially deck builders. The replay value is near the highest I have ever encountered in any video game.9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: The concept of a poker roguelike deckbuilder feels like something that should always be there. Reviewing Balatro now that I'm aware of its existence feels like reviewing clouds, or the sun.I like the way it combines powerups to bend the rules of poker hands and create new strategies each run. Also, this presentation is gorgeous. I like the chill song, the hypnotic swirling background, the way the power ups references cards in general (playing cards, baseball cards, trading cards, holographic cards, tarot cards, even a credit card). It's so much fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic deckbuilder with a simple, and yet, unique, premise. The developer really understands the importance of runaway positive feedback in a roguelike such as this, as a reward for building and synergizing well - it's incredibly satisfying to go from scraping by with basic poker hands to getting scores in scientific notation.Also, minor thing - unlike Slay the Spire, this game doesn't punish you for immediately restarting a run if you don't like how it starts. I really like this minor aspect as I don't feel like I'm forced to accept bad luck.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: Ill admit I was a little skeptical about how much I would like this game.First time I launched game I have already spent an hour and a half in what felt like 10-20 minutes. Absolute blast of a game I am sure to pour many hours into.Hats off to developers, this game is reasonably priced and has truly captured my attention. (Usually it feels like some "cheaper" indie games are nice in thought but executed in a way that makes it hard to justify price.) No complaints here I would pay 59.99 if I had known how much fun I would have!5 stars

_childDocuments_.review: It is simultaneously a handcrafted Heaven AND Hell for a mad poker player and deck builder who loves to stack the deck in his favour.Don't let the seemingly simple premise fool you, this game is extremely deep and honestly has near infinite potential for insane combos you can pull off - way more than any other roguelike or deckbuilder I've ever played. Every single run you play you will discover new Jokers, unlock new cards/decks, and discover a new build. Despite - or perhaps, thanks to - being built upon the simple and recognisable 52 card standard playing deck, every card in your deck can potentially combo off of any Joker in the game. It's literally impossible to know every build/archetype when there is such limitless potential for Joker and Deck combinations.When you first play Balatro, it will seem to you that the House always wins. You have but a simple deck, earn just a handful of dollars every round, yet the Blinds keep increasing and increasing exponentially. How are you supposed to keep up with this?Then you become familiar with the Jokers, with Mults and Mult multipliers. You start creating combos. You build your economy to afford cracking open more packs. You enhance your cards with Tarot packs, level up your hands with Planet packs, stack the deck in your favour with Standard packs... and go wild with Spectral packs. Soon enough, the "big blinds" that filtered you before are peanuts. You will easily obliterate the final boss with millions of points scored in a single hand. Then you discover there's an endless mode... and tons of decks to unlock... and challenges... Even after winning, you keep playing. Balatro plays with all the possible Poker hands you can have in any other Poker game, the difference being you're trying to build up a number of chips to beat different blinds, The small blind, big blind and then a "boss" blind make up an ante, and there are several antes that form a run that you must beat.The game is very challenging as you progress through the blinds, Balatro has a number of different Jokers with different abilities to help you boost your chip score, and there are other special cards such as Tarot cards, Planet cards and more to boost different aspects such as the power of your hand, giving playing cards special abilities, etc.All in all, I've gotten hooked on Balatro and I'm glad a game like this exists, I am a sucker for vaporwave and retro-ness and Balatro's style and soundtrack has this hypnotizing, chill aeshetic which I very much enjoy.TLDR: Balatro is an amazing card game that combines classic Poker with roguelike elements, and I highly recommend picking up this absolute gem of a game!

_childDocuments_.review: A good roguelike is like good coffee. It should be bold, unique, and satisfying. Both are best enjoyed in copious sips, and if you have enough of either, you’ll want more.It’s not an exaggeration to say that Balatro is the best deckbuilding roguelike since Slay the Spire, which is the most vaunted example of the genre. Balatro’s gameplay loop is compellingly simple: make poker hands from a standard deck of playing cards worth an increasing number of chips. Sounds simple, right? Except you can add or delete cards from your deck, collect Jokers that have multiplying and stacking effects, upgrade specific poker hands using Planet cards, and more. Stack the deck with Hearts to increase your chances of a sweet Flush, or fill your deck with Jacks in combination with a joker that rewards you for playing face cards. Do both. And a dozen other things, and then try something different. There’s no end to the combinations you can conjure to keep adding to those all-important red and blue numbers that calculate your chip total, and if you’re like me, you’ll just keep coming back. The game’s subtle soundscape and psychedelic visuals are icing on the cake. That Balatro is able to take something as simple as a deck of playing cards and turn it into a game with such scope, appeal, and replayability would be an accomplishment in itself. But there’s also what Balatro *could have been*. It could have been a ruthlessly addictive, pay-to-advance nightmare mobile game, and it would have been savagely good in that role. In other words, with playing cards as the star attraction, it *could have been* what it appears to be from afar (and apparently to the South Korean government): gambling. That the developer decided to make it a single price roguelike for PC shows either an inherent integrity or a missed opportunity for profit that makes me as grateful as I am impressed.Balatro is about as close to a perfect game as they get in these tortured days of late capitalism.

All in all Balatro is a well designed poker roguelite with satisfying builds, interesting challenges, and very satisfying le randomness. The soundtrack is great, the art style is great and legible, distinct, and the systems are ALMOST air tight. Certain runs can be derailed by Boss Blind RNG. I can recommend Balatro and am excited to see what other devs will be inspired to make in this new genre of Casino-lites. If you like playing cards, getting high scores, doing math to make crazy builds, theory crafting, you will love this game. A base understanding of playing hands is needed to enjoy this game fully.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gamedev myself and that's what I think  1) Setting. Rogue lite about poker, neat.2) Different ways of reinforcement in runs. I mean, you can build around jokers (basically boons), taro cards (change your deck) or planets (boost certain poker hands). On top, you can buy vouchers (permanent upgrades for the rest of the run. Like increasing playable hands per boss). You can go into something specific or combine them however you like.3) Ability to sell and reorder jokers. Also, the order of jokers is important, which I also like. Would be cool to see this ability (to sell and reorder boons (with order of boons mattering)) more often in other rogue likes.4) Gold management. You gain interest based on gold amount you have and in shop you have multiple choices to spend gold on. So you have to choose wisely what to buy and to buy at all.5) Pre-defined scenarios. You have dozens of pre-defined scenarios to play in addition to the main game mode. I really like it because if you want to play on certain strategy, the game allows you to do so from the get-go.6) Cards and joker have multiple modifications. Cards, for example, have suit, value and edition, seal, enhancement on top. So 5 different values.7) Fight overall. It's not unique, still. Instead of dealing damage, you acquire points. To defeat the enemy, you just have to have a certain amount of them.8) Some builds upgrade in fight. Not unique, but still. The longer the fight goes, the stronger you become. So, sometimes, to prolong the fight, you think about how to deal less damage instead of how to deal more.  A lot of micro decisions during the run. Starting from what to play, finishing with what to buy. It's pretty smooth. Animations, effects help to improve the feeling of the game. Sadly, although decision-making is important and would influence your game, the game becomes just a card throwing only luck dependent pretty soon (no thinking or skill involved). Still, distant game, overall  You have plenty of unlockables. Different card decks and jokers mostly. Card decks are great. They have different play styles and allow more different combinations. Some jokers also can influence gameplay, but most of them wouldn't change it at all. Also, I didn't like the way how jokers are unlocked. To unlock them, you have to complete certain tasks and some of them are very tedious (like, to unlock 1 joker, have 30 spades in deck, to unlock another one, have 30 clubs in deck, to unlock the next one have 30 hearts in deck and so on).   I would say replayability is the weakest part of balatro. All runs become pretty same quite quickly. Especially on first bosses. There are not many unique combinations, and you can win almost all runs by simply picking jokers that give chips and multiplicator (flat values). With them, it doesn't matter how you play, literally. Average gameplay amount I would estimate to 15–50 hours. Not that much.  Sometimes was lacking QOL features like ability to pin joker task (condition to unlock) or others. Nothing major though. Worth mentioning (positive) - Amazing and simple design. Especially liked background.   ❌ I made all the achievements    ❌ Challenging  ❌ Simple (minimalistic)❌ High entry threshold  Unique and idea-rich game with smooth gameplay, but not much replayability or synergies. Must-play for enjoyers of the genre who wants something unique and fresh. Don't expect to play for hundreds of hours, though. If you liked the review, you can join my curator group "Dev inspiration" in steam for more. You can find it in my profile as well as additional info.

_childDocuments_.review: A typical run starts by selecting one of 15 starter decks, which usually consist of a standard 52-card playing deck and a powerful, unique modifier. From there, you dive into your first poker blind—'combat' rounds where you must wager increasing amounts of chips to stay in the game. To win those chips, you'll need to craft poker hands like straights and flushes from the eight cards dealt each round, which refresh after every play. A simple high card might win you a small amount, but landing a royal flush will have you swimming in chips.Each round offers multiple chances to tackle the blind, along with a few opportunities to discard and redraw, adding layers of control and heightening the tension of every hand. If you’re holding three kings, do you play it safe and take a smaller payout, or go all-in, hoping to draw that last king for a massive four-of-a-kind and clear the blind in one move? The choice is yours, and the risk always looms large.The cash you earn can be spent in between blinds at rotating shops, where you can purchase booster packs that increase hand values, add cards to your deck, or enhance existing ones with useful modifiers. After powering up and facing a boss every three blinds—each equipped with a variety of nasty debuffs—you'll 'up the ante,' making the stakes even higher. Survive up to the ante 8 boss, and you’ll earn a hard-fought victory, with the option to continue into a sudden death-style endless mode.

These are cards that can vastly affect your point acquiring ability in miriad ways through multiplication of your score if certain criteria are met.Amending your deck with modifiers and getting the right set of Jokers can allow you to soar through a set of rounds and provides a good helping of dopamine throughout thanks to the sights and sounds provided when doing so.

Without it, players can be left puzzled by unexpected losses or misunderstandings about game mechanics. An action log would provide clarity on how much each element contributes to gameplay, significantly enhancing understanding and strategy planning.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: wow this game has so much potential in every single run you make. the combinations you can make with jokers are incredible. but there is still room to pivot to different joker setups even at high levels (antes) of your run. you can hold onto special tarot cards to save you from losing at the boss levels. i just won my first run after 11 hours and it feels so good, i had such an incredible run and continued into ante 11. my full house was level 22 lol
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: While I like this game, higher stakes really, REALLY tend to just suck. The RNG can really suck as well. There are times when I open a tarot pack and the only option worth taking is the "wheel of fortune" which has a 75% chance to do nothing, and generally always does nothing. And I pick this card knowing that it does nothing because a tarot card that does literally nothing is about the same as clicking "skip booster pack". Or I start a game and all the jokers I see in the shop are stuff like "if you play 8 of a kind you get +3 chips" or "this card costs 11$ and the maximum amount of money it is possible to have at this point is 10$".When the game is at lower stakes it's a lot of fun because it feels like there are so many options to work with, but the higher stakes just start to feel less like you have options and more like "I should just restart until I roll a seed where the game doesn't just decide to kick me in the nuts from second one." It's frustrating to me because I want these last few decks but they're locked behind more progress in the stakes that I just find is a tedious grind to figure out "is the game going to screw me this time?" rather than "if I do this, and this I can do this! And work around the boss blind!"Please for the love of god give me the option to "abandon run" when I lose a run and want to quit it's generally before the second boss blind and it's REALLY obvious that there is nothing that can be done to save it. I just want to be able to kill this run without having to have things play out so next time the game isn't offering to let me continue a doomed run.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic poker based deckbuilder. Graphics are sharp, gameplay is fun, and there are a ton of unlockables to keep you playing. I just picked this up yesterday and already have 5 hours of game time (a rare occurrence for me).I highly recommend picking this up if you enjoy deckbuilder, roguelites, puzzle games, or poker!
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game, there is always content to unlock, and even though it has poker in it, doesn't really make you think of it as gambling because A: It's a one time purchase, and B: There is so much strategy involved, luck is only the half of it. I cannot say more without spoiling the game, but the mechanic of having a multiplier on the amounts and cards that help with the multipliers and scoring helps you reach the threshold to win each round. There's so much more to it than that, but you'll have to see for yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: I'm conflicted on this game.  The core game is incredibly fun and addictive, but the higher stakes are incredibly luck based and greatly restrict your play style.  I wouldn't have too much of a problem with that if the higher stakes weren't required to unlock some of the decks.  I hope the devs will introduce some features to improve high stakes consistency in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say about Balatro that hasn't already been said?The chill music with the slightly off-kilter rhythm, the CRT-monitor visuals, the bleeping and blooping and ever-increasing dopamine-enducing visual fireworks whenever you score a truly outrageous number of points with a deck of cards full of insane bonus cards and boosts is all part of a brilliant package that will eat hours of your life away as you have to play "just one more run", and you will be happy while it's doing it.I saw Balatro in my Discovery Queue back when it initially released, and the trailer I saw only intrigued me a little. On the surface it seemed like a pretty normal card game, but when the different Joker modifiers, Tarot card enhancements, Planet Card boosters and Spectral cards were introduced, and the numbers started exploding, it got my full attention. Considering the cheap price, I bought it on a whim, and I was sold on the premise very early.It had its hooks in me from the start and my first play session was several hours long. Granted, I haven't played this game as much as many others, but 24 hours (so far) from such a small game? That I consider pretty good Return on Investment.If you're into card-based Rogue-likes, Balatro is practically a mandatory entry into your library. It is so good and so addicting, and you can run it on a toaster, so you can't use your hardware as an excuse.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: This is a deceptively basic concept executed very well. As a preface, knowledge of poker is not required since the game spells out hands and even counts cards for the player. The core loop is very satisfying, getting jokers to modify the game then build around them to make # go up. There's enough randomness to keep it exciting and I'd say the inherent fickle nature plus short runs keep failures from feeling demoralizing.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a bad father. But to me, being a good gambler was better than being a good father. Slots? That's a machine I understand. Roulette? That's something I can get my head around. Sending my kids to daycare all year 'round, summer included? I'm sittin' there; blackjack. These guys at the table were my family. Can't win if you don't play is what I tell my son. I put 50/50. They told me I didn't put any chips. Check, check. I check. They didn't take that. Fistfight right there at the table. I take on someone 20 years my junior. I get my ass handed to me and I'm pissing my pants. They threw me out.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like Balatro, I really did, but unfortunately, recent experiences leave me with a bad taste in my mouth.  Personally, I don't enjoy doing tons of math just to play a game, so if you don't either, I advise that you stay away from this game, much as it's fun initially.On top of that, Balatro has a very fun gameplay loop, but very poor explanation. How to win, for example, is never explained anywhere (but poker hands, something far more people will be familiar with, are explained in great detail), nor is the exact effect of certain mechanics like the significance of rounds vs ante, etc.Initially, the game is fairly straight-forward, but the more joker combinations and consumable cards you use, the more it deviates from standard poker and into its own game. That's all well and good, but there is a noticeable lack of communication with the player, with the game seemingly expecting you to do the math by hand. A straight is worth X points, plus the points on the cards, but when you have 6 jokers interacting with it and adding +149 chips, then also +10 +5 +1.5 x1.6 multi, and whatever other different values, it becomes a nightmare of math to try and figure out how much you're going to score, and the game does nothing to help you calculate this.I made suggestions in the Balatro discord about these aspects and was met with outright hostility. How DARE anyone wish for information clarity? I was leaning negative in my review already because of the lack of information, but that has pushed me over the edge.(because god forbid we introduce the OPTION to have the game give you a loose score estimate automatically, on an opt-in basis, that would be FER THE CAZUALS)I wish I could refund my copy, but alas, I'm past the two hour mark. Hopefully, this review can help others like me who don't enjoy doing constant math from making the mistake of buying this game. It's not "just a fun deckbuilder," and there's way too much "do the math yourself or you'll be off by 10 points and screw yourself over" to find it enjoyable after the first few rounds.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: Balatro has very quickly convinced me that using poker for a deck-building roguelike is more than just a gimmick. In fact, I think this game stands among the greatest of the deck-building genre. This game is just brilliant. The game's vibe is very easy to understand if you've played in the genre before, and the cheap price is well worth the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: Normally when I see a game is based around Poker, I ignore it, because I don't play poker, struggle to remember the scoring hands and generally have no interest to learn.However, when a friend gave me a copy of this game, it is so smoothly done and so easy to understand, with a simple premise (beat ever increasing scores, collect cards for crazy combos) and the art so colourful and bouncy, and very much has the "big numbers go brrr" effect down just right, that I just fell in love with it. Then you add in the multiple categories of cards to unlock, combo's to achieve, and new ranks and levels (and decks and challenges) to unlock, and there's enough to keep me coming back for years to come I suspect.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where every time you play it, you like it more. The more you unlock the more fun it is to build your run's synergy.Early game is harder, because you're learning and so much stuff is locked, But there's always that next unlock, that next run to beat, that next goalpost. The more time you put into it, the more addicting it becomes... I love it.My biggest complaint is the boss blinds that keep you from seeing your cards. It's not a fun mechanic, it's just tedious and annoying, and doesn't have any counterplay that feels effective or reliable.But that's a small blight on an otherwise fantastic game. I don't say this about many games, but I would even recommend it at full price. It's that good.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: Some of the negative reviews seem shocked to find that RNG is a big factor in a poker game. It's a lot of fun though, very chill, and I have found it a bit easier to win than many roguelikes, which is nice. It's fun to win. However it's obvious that the higher stakes are going to make it MUCH more challenging and it seems like it will be a fun challenge to try and make the most of what the shops give you.Super good on steam deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: Truly a certified banger.I personally get bored pretty quickly with this game, but for some reason i always find myself coming back to it for a short session every once in a while.The variety of builds with the different jokers is really satisfying (though only a number of builds will take you far into endless mode).All in all, Balatro is a great concept, and perfectly executed. Any roguelite lover should definitely give it a try !
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played poker you will easily understand this game. It hits all the right notes I want in a roguelike/lite - easy to pick up and put down, but incredibly addicting. Visuals and audio are fantastic with a non-micro transaction experience of chasing card packs and upgrades. Well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: Great Roguelite Deckbuilder.Plays like a fun and interesting Poker (fruit) machine, i.e. has a passing resemblance to the card game in terms of valid hands and hand rankings.Finds that sweet spot between chance and skill.Makes you feel like you're gently tripping on mushrooms during extended play sessions, which is nice.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: If you know the rules of poker, you can start to enjoy this game in seconds without any prep or pre understanding. A good, quick, pickup but as you can see from reviews it's a tough, long, put down.The ultimate game for folks who used to enjoy playing ghetto old school PC solitaire. It's Poker, On crack, with points and power ups. Nuff said.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah this is the good stuff. Balatro is exactly what it looks like, a poker rouge like. I was worried going having the key mechanic be arcade-y, trying to achieve a score being too removed. But I'm happy to say the game is engaging.In large part, this is due to how excellently designed the game is. It nails having a ton of different systems that all interrelate and play off each other. Passives, and cards, card modifications, jokers, and consumables. Upgrades and "builds" are varied and well balanced- shockingly so.  Early on, I would see passive card and think, "Okay, this card is how i engage only with this mechanic." Only to find out that no, the mechanic wasn't designed around any one card and I can engage with these ideas in any way I choose. It's a little hard to give a final verdict yet, but this is shaping up to be my favorite rougelite since Slay the Spire. It's that good.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: I had seen this game being played by several of my friends, and got intrigued when I heard it was a poker-based rougelike game. So, a week ago, I took the plunge.Balatro is a simple game: play cards from your hand to make the best poker hand you can, and you score chips based on those hands. Score enough chips, you advance to the next challenge, you probably get the idea.Where this game shines is how deep and intricate the game is even with the simple mechanics. Jokers that can beef up your current hand or other shenanigans, Planet cards that increase the value of different poker hands, tarot and spectral cards that can affect the cards of your deck, so many different ways your deck and strategy can be affected before you face the next goal.I would highly recommend this game. It’s quirky humor and retro graphics showcase a deep strategic game with plenty of tools you can use to get back up and try again should your deck fall a little short.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: "This looks like it could be a fun time-waste, a poker roguelike? I'll give it a try" 60 hours later: "OK IF I DOUBLE SKIP THE ANTE 1 BLINDS I GET $30 AND I CAN KEEP THE INTEREST RATE GOING UNTIL ANTE 5 THEN I CAN GO FULL HEART DECK AND BEAT 1M+ BLIND IN ANTE 10 WITH LEVEL 5 ROYAL FLUSH"This game is what it must have felt like for people in the 80s when Tetris came out. After playing this for a week straight my dreams are full of card suits and just me discarding deck after deck.. Only play this if you're prepared to not do anything else for a few days. "Just one more hand..."  This is the  CIV of card games.  I've seen things you people wouldn't believe. Multipliers on fire after picking Purple Stake difficulty. I watched jokers glitter in the dark near the Ante 16 boss. All those moments will be lost in time, like cards in a deck. Time to fold... I'm now in Balatro remission.. Stay safe kids.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fire. I rarely leave reviews but I've felt the need to for this one. My favorite game of all time is Slay the Spire (Sts). It has been the top of its class for years, without any true contenders. Along comes Balatro. This game appeared randomly in my queue, and I'm glad it did. It combines unique runs with the deck-building aspect, though it has relatively little in terms of long-term progression. The only real long-term progression you get is unlocking new cards. This is similar to StS. I finally beat my first run after about 7 hours and I have yet to beat another run.This game is hard and it is unforgiving. The Play and Discard buttons are distinctly marked, but I still misclick them every so often. Usually, the misclicking is very costly and likely to end the run. Sometimes, however, the misclick results in a new, even more powerful hand and you can only laugh in response. This game is wonderful and I am very glad I bought it.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: I know I'm going to keep playing this one for a long, long time.Edit: 50+ more hours in on Steam alone (bought it on Switch also) since my initial impression, I'm confident in saying this is one of the greatest card games ever created, and one of my favourite games.Second Edit: After 250+ hours on Steam and about 50 on switch, I've now bought the game on mobile and spent every day since it released on the app store playing at every opportunity. I play it on the toilet. I play it in bed. At work. I went to an open mic night to support my friend... and played it the entire time.This game is Tetris. It's sliced bread. It's a cigarette with a whiskey. It should replace Solitaire on every single windows operating system going forward.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: I'd argue, and this is a very early judgement to make. This is Indie game of the year (2024).If you have a steam deck, 100% pick it up, it is a beautiful handheld game. I'm only disappointed I couldn't get it on my tablet, because its not out for that yet. (here is hoping)If you like Roguelike Poker games, its for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: My husband bought this game for me and said "I think you'll love this!". I looked at it and thought "this game looks stupid," and started researching if I could return a gifted game. I figured I'd at least play a couple games, but still wasn't hooked. Then I started up the game one more time before returning it...and something hooked me. I became obsessed. I'm usually not much of a game completionist but here I am 120 hours later having completed all the challenges, and now working on completing all of the chip levels for each deck. I've even thought about restarting the game so I can complete everything again.So, if you like me are thinking "looks like a stupid card game" at first, I say give it a chance and you may also get completely hooked.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: Having logged over 150 hours into this game, I can confidently say it's a well designed deck builder that's accessible to new players and easily re-playable. With all of the different Jokers, Decks, Stakes, and Challenges, the game play stays fresh and unique as you pick up the mechanics. Would highly recommend.
