_childDocuments_.review: I think I had my expectations too high, due to the overwhelmingly positive ratings. The game's very simple, and runs are quite RNG heavy. This game is something to do with your hands while you're watching a youtube video or whatever. Don't expect the world from this, but it's good fun. I think the overwhelmingly positive rating comes from the fact that this game is pretty good, and it's hard to think otherwise.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: An exciting combination of roguelike deckbuilding and poker that briefly shows you the basics and then leaves it up to you to experiment and find the crazy combinations. It is a lot of fun experimenting with different decisions and seeing how it turns out. Picking new cards along the way to add them to your collection adds to the challenge.The only negative of this game is how addictive it is. Just one more go!
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: Game feels really good until you unlock everything. Then it becomes a RNG fiesta. You either get a decent +mult joker early game or you lose. Rerolls are way too expensive early game. No amount of skill can overcome awful early game stores. I never feel like I have even a slim chance at winning every run through skill based play.I see lots of comments about this being like Slay the Spire. I don't find Balatro anything like StS other than the fact that it is a card based game. StS offers so much more in variety of gameplay whereas the gameplay of Balatro is jokers for chips, mult, and multiplier. You MUST have all three to score enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: A refreshing take on a card based roguelite. Very fun and addicting. Difficulty is very customizable with the ability to choose different decks that have different characteristics to start a run and different stakes that modify the game rules. Has a number of challenges with unique game rules. I can see myself coming back to this game for a long time for casual runs/fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: While I do believe there are some bosses that leave a lot to be desired, I played quite a bit of the demo of this game and have been excited for it for almost a year now. This game is easily worth $15 if you'd be interested in similar casino-roguelike games such as Luck Be a Landlord. I believe Balatro offers a very novel gameplay loop, winning strategies are rather copious, and for the most part it doesn't really feel like it cheats me, bar the one or two bosses that in my opinion fundamentally break how the game is played (I'm looking at you, upside down hands).Highly, highly recommend.EDIT:They nerfed the BS, ignore everything I said this game is literally perfect 11/10 I'd marry it and let it divorce me for half my stuff and the kids.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: This game replicates both that feeling of scissors gliding across wrapping paper and also the sound of a metal fork scraping against a porcelain plate. When luck goes your way and you start dinging chips and mult into the stratosphere it's better than your parents telling you they're proud of you. When you have 25 aces and somehow miss the chance to pull the only cards you need to beat the blind, you'll feel worse than wet socks but the loop is so addicting and you'll forever be chasing that scissor gliding dopamine baby.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: it's fun. if you like deck building and solitaire, you'll enjoy this. I wouldn't call it "Rogue like." It's maybe roguelite, but even that's a stretch. It's a deckbuilding game with unlock mechanics. Most deckbuilding games have unlock mechanics.  There is no map/traversal or significant choices/pathing to make. That said, it does require decent strategy and it's fun to build insane combos that are fun. Also feels like there are many different types of decks that are viable, just one type, which is nice.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: A mix of deck building and roguelite. Simple and charming art style, easy to understand gameplay, complex strategic elements make it a game you either hate or love. Also requires a skill called 𝓶𝓪𝓽𝓱𝓮𝓶𝓪𝓽𝓲𝓬𝓼 to count the points and not making a blunder by losing with 100 points margin. Very fun and addictive, just like in casino, it's all chance and a bit of exploits.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: Most likely my favourite roguelike.Put 100 hours into the demo before the game even released in full, so I would already be satisfied if the game was mostly in the same state, but there's so much more to discover now. The game has a habit of making you feel like you're the smartest/luckiest person in the world whenever you get a proper build going, and there's plenty of tools to make just about any build you can think of work. Immensely satisfying. The soundtrack - despite being essentially a single track - is perfect and fits the overall theme like a glove. For that matter,  about the presentation just feels perfect.There is less meta-progression in this game than in some other roguelikes - mostly just new jokers, decks, and vouchers that you can find in future runs. Personally, I find this more rewarding for this game, but to some this could feel too rng heavy. I think this fits the poker aesthetic well though - we be gamblin'
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: For whatever reason, this game tickles my brain in all the right ways. I can already tell that this is going to be a GREAT game to unwind to in the evenings--the music and visuals are very pleasing.Big fan of card building, and this one has lots of cool stuff with Joker cards, Tarot cards, etc. etc all which give abilities, multipliers, or boosts. Definitely worth the $14/$15 dollars if you can find it for that price point.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: First time I saw this game I was like : why is this poker game popular, it looks goofy!This is a crazy good an addictive card game where you play hand of poker (kinda) with all sorts of modifier, and usefull boons which are called "Joker cards", you goal is to try to beat a score to advance in the game. This will unlock more joker, so the roguelike experience will be easier or at least , you will have more tools at your disposal to win!THIS GAME IS VERY FUN & KINDA ADDICTIVE, BE WARNED!
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo and immediately wishlisted this game. The gameplay is just so good and addictive, coupled with awesome graphics and polish, you just can't have a bad time with this, even when you lose. The (video)poker hands and roguelike traits just work so damn well and the mix of dopamine/thinking is perfect. I just finished my first run ever and I immediately want to go back. I know I'll be playing this game till I'm old.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: After looking at recent reviews, it seems I may have put more time into this game than most, having over 750 hours. That in itself is a testament to the game. I purchased at release after watching a YouTuber I enjoy (aliensrock - he has a number of similar games I've purchased) and was not disappointed. I've worked to unlock all decks, played on different levels of difficulty and no matter what you do, you'll never play the game the same twice. When you start to get bored, you can find a seeded run to mess around with as well. I just got back from a few months of playing other games and this one is one that does not disappoint. You pick up where you left off and I've had hours of enjoyment this week alone. The beauty of this game is the simplicity. I can play the game and enjoy it. I can watch (insert streaming service) while playing. I can stop at a moments notice to take care of something without worrying about losing my run or dying. If you enjoy the style of play for the game, spend the money and add it to your library. It can be run on any machine so even the 10 year old PC full of classic games will appreciate this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: The aesthetic and general vibe of Balatro is enthralling, which is good because it can be very frustrating up front. Good news - your persistence is rewarded.Jokers are key. You'll unlock more as you play. Keep at it and you'll have some satisfying big-brain moments not just about the meta of whatever run you're on, but the meta for the overall game to help you unlock more Jokers. (Even specific strats to unlock the Jokers that buff your preferred play style.)Balatro can be math-y and sophisticated, but it never loses the brute force appeal of watching numbers go up.  The challenge is enough to make one relish their victories over what feels like an especially cursed video poker machine embedded in the countertop of some haunted, non-euclidean bar you've wondered into after eating questionable fungi.

_childDocuments_.review: If you managed to miss all the articles about Balatro and don't know what it is, it's basically a poker roguelite. You basically start by following the poker rules, but you get more and more abilities to cheat and it gets quite bonkers. Core is to get more chips than the ever increasing target, which then gets complicated by multipliers and multiplier multipliers. Game doesn't expect you to calculate the total, usually playing the best hand possible is enough. If you manage to go way over the target, there's quite satisfying feedback. There's also jokers, planet cards, tarot cards, spectral cards, three types of card enhancements and so on. There's plenty of possibilities to optimize your run. You might even get in bit of trouble if boss disables your chip making machine. Luckily you can see the boss well in advance, so you have time to adjust your deck or even change the boss type. Everything is not available right away and there's plenty of things to be unlocked. Some of them you unlock accidentally, for some you might have to adjust your playstyle a bit. Only bad thing about the game is that you have some much fun that you have less time for everything else. Also some people have hard time figuring out that it's not actually a gambling game, so if you're unlucky you might not be able to buy it. It's impossible to describe everything in such short review, but hopefully this was enough to convince you.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't take it lightly when I say: this is even more of a roguelike than a card game; and even more, it's more of a roguelike than most roguelikes.It's all about building synergies that work well together, with endless possibilities. Makes theory-crafting very fun.The game is also extremely polished and good to look at. When those numbers catch on fire, you'll feel that dopamine washing over. _childDocuments_.review: Balatro is a great little rogue-like poker-like game that is surprisingly addictive. I did not expect to like this game as much as I do, and can't wait to see what the devs do with it next. If you like simple and snappy gameplay, are looking for something new to pick up for your steamdeck, or wish poker was more interesting thanks to magical jokers, then this is the game for you. The only thing I wish it had was a stronger sense of permanent progression. Outside of gathering a stronger sense of understanding and overall strategy, your fiftieth run feels pretty similar to your first run. The different decks can offer some interesting twists, but I'm still missing the sense of gradual progression and accumulation of abilities that are present in my favorite rogue-likes. Even with that, I still highly recommend picking this up.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Beta branch has fixed my problems with the game.  Higher stakes are now no longer fundamentally reset-fests, and there are fun strategies you can use to deal with the new modifiers that are imposed.  It's definitely "easier," but the ease is in the fact that you can play runs longer than 2 antes before having to reset from bad RNG.  Game is much better now!The basis of the game is fun, and at lower stakes and in endless mode it's a lot of fun to pump up your decks and see how far you can go.At higher stakes, however, all of the "difficulty" is front-loaded into whatever you get in the early shops, where at the highest stake 95% of runs are simply not winnable at the very beginning because you got bad shops.  After a certain point of endlessly resetting runs to hope the game gives you something good, you realize that there really is no player expression or decision making to make here, you're just winning or losing based entirely on what the shop RNG decides to dole out.

_childDocuments_.review: A small preface: Balatro is how Jesters were normally referred to in ancient Rome.With that out of the way...Sometimes, due to a mix talent, ingenuity and a little bit of luck, a game springs forth thatcan take even something mundane and bring it to the next level in regards to creativity, engagement and fun factor,the kind of luster one could only possibly find in the vast confines of indie game space.Balatro is takes roguelite concepts like meta progression, long term planning, synergies and permanent defeat to apply them to a unique variant of Poker: Rather than playing against bots or other humans, the gameconsists of a score attack wherein the objective is either matchng or exceeding the score in eachphase of a round, called Blind. To score, Poker hands are played consecutively, with a given number of attempts (hands) and discards per blind. As with normal Poker, the most valuable hands award more chips (the game's stand-in for score)however, that's where the similarities with common Poker end, and Balatro's brilliance begins!Because the game shows a wealth of information, even those unfamiliar with playing cards or poker can naturallyget the hang of things, and the game is friendly and relaxed enough that it can be enjoyed by the whole family;despite using playing cards as the basis of gameplay it has nothing to do with gambling.As the game's name suggests, Jokers are of ultimate importance here, acting as strong passive modifiers to the overall gameplay andWith 150 in all, there is plenty the player can do, and even strange and suboptimal strategies canwork, since besides the Jokers themselves, other types of cards exist that can deeply modify individual cards,card groups, bonuses, or even the whole deck as one plays, and some base decks themselves that have odd compositions. As with most games of this kind, there are also ascension systems that optionally increase difficulty from tthe baseparameters quite a bit, and sone unlockables are indeed gated behind higher difficulty tiers, as well as an unlockableEndless Mode.In short, this is a game that easy to pick up, hard to master and nearly impossible to put down!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing video games for almost 25 years now. Every once in a while, you get a game that reminds you that you are human. And humans are ostensibly, at the end of the day, animals. And like all animals, we humans have primal urges in order to satiate the basic needs to maintain our survival.Through these carnal needs comes vices. Sometimes we revert the growth and development from our hippocampus in order to quench the primordial thirst within us. We do things not because we are proud, but because we exist. And through those things, we become alive.Balatro is a rogue-like, deck-builder that uses the casino card game of five-card draw poker as a basis to it's gameplay core. Because it uses a standard, well-known game to build off of, the barrier for entry is low, but the skill ceiling is high. Even for a smooth-brained marsupial like myself, the dumb country bumpkin in me knows how to play poker.But Balatro isn't just about poker. It's about the numbers.  Watching the numbers, the multipliers, the stackers, the juicers, the hot digits. As you learn to make friends with the jokers, the planets, and the arcanas, they help you on the path to watching the numbers go up. You build joker decks inside your decks, increase your main deck, and then you watch the numbers go up.The minutes turn into hours working on your antes. You don't skip the antes because you need the interest to buy your planet cards to get the hot stacks. Or to make friends new joker buddies who want to make your life even more miserable.I wake up, I think of Balatro. I commute into the city, and my brain craves a fresh ante like a college student needing a Zyns. I'm at work, I think of juicy plays to get the numbers higher. I go home, and my Steam Deck starts crying because it knows it's time for numbers. There will be no rest until the mults are high, as will I.Overall, Balatro is very good and I recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Developed by LocalThunk and released in 2024, Balatro is a rogue like deck builder with a Poker theme. Using the card combinations from Poker, customize your deck to better suit your playstyle and bend rules to achieve great scores. The basic mechanic of the game is simple, play poker games until you win. Games are presented in “antes”, groups of 3 poker rounds where the third round has special conditions and modifiers. The modifiers present part of what makes this game unique. Between each round, the player has access to a store, where a number of cards can be bought, which can also be altered. Cards can be bought as booster packs as well as Tarot cards, Planet cards, and Jokers. Each of these booster packs allow the player to select different cards for their decks and customize not only the score of specific card combinations, but also card modifiers, score multipliers among other things. The amount of customization possible in this game really transforms what could be an addicting, yet simple, deck builder into a complex rogue like, where rules are bent and almost all can be modified.  Another notable feature this game brings is the little details. From the effects in the cards, to the small screen shake when points are added, all details that are so well made and implemented an already impressive art style and game. If deck builders are something you already enjoy, I highly recommend Balatro, even if you never played Poker before, it is truly a fun addicting game. If you enjoyed this review, I would like to invite you to visit  my curator page for more recommendations and reviews.

I found myself always converging to a flush based deck in the later rounds. There's also a limited set of multiplicative jokers vs. additive jokers that are must haves to win some of the post-game ante rounds.The thing I love about this game is the progression from early game to mid game to late game. _childDocuments_.review: What this game does right that other deck-builders tend to suck straight dog's dong at - - Doesn't take several hours to get through. Doesn't waste your time with artificially prolonged garbage. Sick and tired of sitting through StS brand deck-builders where runs can vacillate massively in length, and with very few of them justifying that with any appropriate level of additional complexity. You can finish a Gold Stake Balatro run with the full speed setting in 20 minutes, 15 if your Jokers are unleashing cosmic numeracy. None of that that 40 minute to an hour or more horse crap. - No overwrought systems. No menagerie of enemies with bespoke behaviors. No health bar, no status effects, no RPG suffused corniness. No superficial, illusory junk. Balatro's runs feel more varied in the end than its competitors because artificial complexity, which this genre is absolutely infested with, reduces the amount of impactful options - and Balatro is at it's heart, not very complex. You make fewer decisions, but these decisions are more likely to alter significant elements of the simple ruleset, and because there are fewer variables, these variables tend to have far greater effect on the gameplay. It's why chess and go are timeless games with absolute geniuses of the art of determinism picking them apart for centuries upon centuries, and Monopoly is a fiddly pile of ass. If you want another example of why this is key, go take a look at Brutal Orchestra - pretty much beats the sputum out of the majority of other roguelites' gobs. - Unlocking almost every Joker and Voucher in this game happens within the first 10-15 hours. Then it's just running through the stakes. The game itself is fun and engaging enough without perpetual carrot-on-a-stick misery. Interesting builds and mechanics aren't drip-fed to you while you try to wrench yourself through a dull early-game in order to be able to play the game as it's meant to be. LocalThunk had enough confidence to believe their game would be engaging without the disingenuous allure of constant unlocks which in reality are just obstacles to you enjoying the totality of the game.: Another instance of why simplicity in this genre is best. Each Joker and Voucher are distinct. All of them can be immediately assessed with a glance due to the boldness of the art and the Picasso cogitation they had going on with the semiotics here. Each Joker  like what the tool-tip sounds like. You'd think this is some no-brainer doodah, but so many deck-builders are awash with busy art with little conceptual connection to what they do. Start an ante and you'll have all the information you need churned through your brain within a few seconds. No mushy, ugly art, no anthropomorphized abstractions in the shape of enemies that look like junk (Jesus Christ StS and Monster Train are both  ugly as ♥♥♥♥ from a design standpoints).The fact that it took so long to get what isn't an a deconstruction but just a literal, foundational product, is insane to me. This is what deck-builders should have been built on, instead we had an eternal run of games that already felt clumsily iterated. Balatro is here though, and it's made other deck-builders unplayable ass for me.

_childDocuments_.review: The music is fire, the jokers are fun, the art is awesome. What a great game. I've heard the criticism that this game is "high number simulator" but when a roguelike lets you take your build to an endless mode, isn't that always what it turns into?Playing higher stakes is genuinely pretty challenging, especially on certain decks. Boss blinds are actually threatening in most runs, and you can't just force any build you want. Playing the cards you're dealt is necessary to find success, so you end up playing different builds all the time and finding fun synergies every run. White stake can become "high number simulator" if you're solid at the game for sure; you can greed your economy for a long time and force your way into whatever super strong build you want - some scaling xMult, re-triggers, baron + mime, whatever. But personally I've found playing all the different decks and aiming for gold stake completionist+ on all of them super fun and satisfyingly difficult. The most common complaint in negative reviews is that high stakes are too rng dependent. There is some element of truth to that - the best player in the world probably won't have a 100% win rate - but not to the extent that they describe. It's genuinely a skill issue. Maybe black deck is too rng dependent, but even as just a decent player you can probably obtain a 50% or higher win rate on gold stake. There are players who have win-streaked gold stakes up to like 20 runs in a row or something. The game is not THAT rng heavy and does not have THAT little skill expression. The game does have tons of rng for sure, but if you're trying to beat every deck on gold stake you know that already, and know how to play the game and win despite it, theoretically.This is one of the best roguelikes out there imo and there's no reason not to pick it up!

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let my hours at time of review fool you, I put 10x those numbers into each of the demos and it would have been even more if the full game didn't release.There is something extremely heartwarming hearing people refer to balatro as their favorite game before the full game even releases, and I can only imagine those people are absolutely pogged out of their gourd at the full release, as I certainly am.There is an unbelievable amount of depth here: the synergies are wildly satisfying. the unlocks are free dopamine, and the wins are exhilarating. $15 is a legitimate STEAL for a game of this caliber and i will be purchasing it on switch even if i never play it just to support localthunk a tiny bit more.Much love - Dirty Mike and the Boys

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really simple game, most of the cards are trash, there is only 1 formula to winning, get a card that gives credits, then mutli, then x multi. Everything relies on that formula no matter what cards you decide to play. The only thing that holds you back from winning is finding the cards you need, which is random, the cards you need are in a soup of trash cards.The important take away is that there is only 1 way of winning if you don't have a credit joker card in front of a multi joker card which are both in front of a x multi card, you won't win. If you get these cards out of random draw, you simply play your strongest hard over and over again. The poker playing part isn't important, you're basically playing a random fishing game, hoping RNG gives you what you want.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game but it just never sucked me in the way some other similar games like Slay the Spire, Monster Train, or even Vampire Survivors did. I've put about 10 hours on it and I'll probably play it again from time to time -- it is pretty easy to pick up again after weeks or even months, unlike some games.I think two things that leave me a bit lukewarm are the lack of any "enemies". Each round you're essentially trying to beat a certain score. Round 1, score 300; round 1 score, 450; etc. There's no real personality or variety to them, for the most part. The boss blinds (which you hit every 3rd round) each have a twist -- first hand is played face down, all Clubs are debuffed -- but few of them require more than very small changes to your strategy. It makes it curiously flat, since none of the "enemies" have any character. It's just purely a mathematical exercise where each level requires a higher score.The second is that you really need to specialise to do well. This is true to some extent in most of these kind of games but something about the multiplication of how scores are calculated makes it especially true with Balatro. A lot of your runs will be about specialising in a certain kind of hand -- say, Pair -- and then every single hand all you do is discard, draw, play pairs. Since you're dealing with poker hand probabilities that means, unless you get pretty lucky with your jokers, you're going to spend the vast majority of your time playing high card, pairs, and maybe two pairs. And once you've built up your Planet cards for a certain hand, it often isn't even worth playing a Straight Flush or Full House if you luck into one.So, I still recommed the game. I still think it is a good game. But it didn't become one of those games that click for me and I play dozens of hours.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is genuinely so much fun! It's certainly not as skill-based as other Roguelike games (although that doesn't mean there is no skill involved), but do NOT expect to be able to win every run you start.Also, if the devs are seeing this. I know this is a weird ask for a Roguelike game, especially this one, but I personally would LOVE to see a sandbox mode where you can set your deck and your jokers to anything you've discovered/unlocked and you can test out all sorts of combos and chains. _childDocuments_.review: I heard about this game during Steam's NextFest and thought: "A deckbuilding roguelike about poker?  That's stupid."  I tried the demo and thought: "Okay, this is a pretty cool gimmick, but why would anyone play this?  It's like those casino cell phone games - you're just playing for imaginary money.  It's pointless."  Then when I discovered they ended the demo - Day One purchase!  This game is THAT addictive.  Once you start discovering all the clever little wrinkles added by the different card types, jokers and tarot card effects, it's hard to put down.  There's a fair amount of challenge that may seem daunting at first, but like any good roguelike, every attempt brings you closer to victory.  Once you do finally "win" a run (it took me 20 hours of game time, and winning unlocks an endless mode), it really depends on the player's personality if you'll keep going or not.  If you're a completionist, there are a ton of things to unlock, and if you care about earning achievements, you could be playing this for a very long time.Even if you don't usually like card games there's a good chance you could find yourself hooked on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first learned about this game, the big headline was "easy to learn, hard to master" and I do like games like that, but be aware, this is not a game like that! You can still make wrong descisions, In the end the most desciding factor is luck. Yes, it is one of those games. I hoped for a more hard to master approach, but sometimes you should just play a game and not listen to the things you read.Because this game is awesome. The mechanics are pretty unique and most importantly a lot of fun. Yeah sometimes you are very unlucky, but this game is always fun. I just can recommend this game, if you like games, where you can enjoy things coming together. It is really amazing, when your plan just works. _childDocuments_.review: Solitaire x Poker on steroids, seriously addictive with a masterfully readable interface making for quick rounds. Takes maybe 10 minutes to learn the basics and start turning the tables. Still requires luck as well as skill and perception to truly dominate the various opponents. Perfect time-waster with almost every convenience feature you might desire -- even though the rounds are short, you can save progress during a running streak at any time, making it very easy to pick up and set down. Not what I would typically think of as a deckbuilder game, but in this case the description does fit, but don't let that tag discourage you. There's no micro-transactions or micro-management of your deck, your deck composition happens organically over the course of your winning streak, and it's a pretty clever modification of basic card game rules and logic.

_childDocuments_.review: 12 hours in, and I still haven’t won…yet it’s still a hard recommend. It’s been a while since a roguelike has provided that “one more run” feeling. Each run feels unique and satisfying. Each time, I get closer and closer to winning. And each time I uncover new strategies for playing. _childDocuments_.review: Excellent game for the Steam Deck! If you like roguelike deck building card games, get this.Two major things made me initially ignore this game that proved non-issues once I got in.1. The CRT warping and constantly wobbling effects of the HUD can be disabled. Some slight shifting of the cards is fine, but the defaults are too much. If you are like me and turn off viewbob immediately in every FPS because it causes real physical discomfort, rest easy, it's in the options!2. I nearly dismissed Balatro for its poker theme simply because I'm not into the classic games spun from a traditional deck of 52. Balatro is delightfully not traditional for very long.It's essentially a score attack game, where you earn points for cards and attempt to collect rule-bending bonuses to trigger cascades of multipliers and other rogue-ish effects. Thin the deck down to twenty cards instead, run with 9 aces, and turn cards into stone, gold, glass, etc for additional super powers. I find trying to build a Straight, where you have 5 cards in numerical sequence, way more fun when you get a modifier that lets you skip a rank in the middle. There's no "opponents," no bluffing, just a target score and a limited number of actions you can take to achieve it.

_childDocuments_.review: As somebody that's either played or is familiar with most roguelite deckbuilders, this one is clearly going to be one of the greats alongside the likes of Slay the Spire or Monster Train. So far, my complaints are extremely minimal; basically, I'd just like more options for destroying cards. Luckily this game does a great job at utilizing "transmutation" over destruction, so every great run isn't just chasing the smallest hand.It is also extremely polished and balanced for releasing without a proper early access (I won't really count the demo for this, though I'm sure it helped). In summation: if you've enjoyed any deckbuilding roguelike before, this one is absolutely a must buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the hours played fool you. I've been playing the occasional demo for balatro as much as the dev let me, more or less running up at least 60 hours between them. Balatro is a game where you play poker hands to beat a dealer's score (the Blind). You're allowed a number of discards - tossing up to five cards to get an equal number back - and hands to play to add up to this score. Score is totaled by starting with a base score for the hand, then adding the value of the cards played in the hand, then multiplying by the base multiplier for the hand. So, two jacks, two queens, all different suits? that's a two pair, which is worth 20 points with a x2 multiplier, and each face card is forty. So you get 120 points for that. Not the worst hand, but near the bottom. Once you beat the initial blind, you get money based on your performance to spend in the shop, which is where Balatro explodes in complexity. Here you can buy tarot cards (which modify your cards, by converting suits or destroy cards outright, for example), Planet cards, which upgrade hand base scores, and Jokers. Jokers are, more or less, equipment: You can have up to five at a time, and they do things like simply adding multiplier, making specific cards add more points, or weird things like "if you discard a single card first, destroy it and get 3 dollars". As your run progresses, you're expected to gather jokers and modify your deck towards a strategy of one form or another. Maybe you find a Joker that re-triggers played lower cards, a joker that causes fibonacchi numbers to add multiplier, and now you're tearing into each shop hoping to add smaller number cards to your deck, eliminating face cards with a vendetta, and hunting for Jokers that can allow you to play hands of nothing but fibonacchi numbers. Because you *will* need to enhance your deck. The blinds escalate, ratcheting up and up each one you defeat. And every three blinds is a Boss. Bosses are powerful blinds that come with additional rules. Some are benign as reducing your hand size - others will torment you with things like "only one hand type for this blind" or taking money for each card played. Preparing for bosses, whether by making your deck simply strong enough to bull through, or by subverting their rules, is part of Balatro's core. The feel of the game is unique among deckbuilding roguelikes. It presents a CRT, retro-esque aesthetic of ancient poker machines. The music is reminiscent of Risk of Rain. Perhaps its most daring move is to only have a SINGLE NPC in the entire game, the tutorial agent who teaches you the game and pops up at the end of each run - win or lose - to either mock or congratulate you. There's no enemies to really speak of. The bosses, even, are vague, conceptual - "The Wall", "The mouth". There's a sense of comedy and jest throughout - joker art can be anything from The Hack - a poor standup comedian giving a terrible set - or Mystic Summit, a pile of floating rocks reaching into the sky. The downsides of the game are few, if any. The game wears its luck-based nature on its sleeve, but as the game proceeds, it can grow more and more 'rocket-tag'y, with hands swinging harder and harder against higher and higher stakes, and so by mid or late game not getting the right hand even after several discards and hard work customizing the deck can feel pretty bad. Not getting the tools you're looking for also has an element of luck, and sometimes, a deck just isn't gonna make it - But this feeling is mitigated by the casino-esque feel of the whole game, in my opinion, as if the game is looking you dead in the eyes as it deals you a trash hand or forces terrible, cruel boss blinds on you. Balatro is one of my favorite games this year. It has a lot of staying power, the price is really affordable, and it's as strong as other classics in its genre. I cannot recommend it highly enough.

Nope, I changed the rules and now Ace, 3, 4, and 6 is a valid straight. Also, my fifth card is just a rock."There are only four aces in a deck of cards"? Then how did I play five of a kind just now, and why does my deck have 17 more aces in it?These are just a few of the situations you'll run into in Balatro. _childDocuments_.review: This was a really fun game to discover. I certainly get all the hype around it. But it also turns out to be very superficial.Contrary to most deckbuilding/deckbuilding-adjacent roguelikes, where you have to make concessions and constant adaptations to an imperfect build in order to win, Balatro rewards you for being single-minded.You only need a little flexibility in the beginning, until you figure out what hand and/or couple jokers will carry you, at which point the best and only move is to tunnel vision really hard into it, and just play the same hand over and over again, until you win. A process which starts very, very early in a run.Basically, it lacks a whole layer of complexity to keep it fresh in the long run. That, and endgames are super redundant.Worse, the formula for a winning run rarely ever changes. At least a joker that gives chips, at least a joker that gives +mult, ideally a joker that gives xmult, at least one of which has to be a strong-scaling one, and then whatever you can fit in how little space you have left that can complement it. It doesn't matter what kind of hand you play, as long as it fits your joker line-up and you manage to make it spammable (and despite timid steps having been taken in the last update, high card still is the most reliable hand by far).So it feels to me that not only you play the same hand over and over, you actually , over and over, barring edge cases.You always need the same couple of things, and there just isn't that much variety in how you can gather them. Somehow, it makes sense. After all, you rarely get to make really game-changing tweaks to your deck, and even then, most of the work comes from the jokers, which you only get to carry 5 of, and whose effects very rarely reach beyond a "will reward you X for playing X type of hand" level of complexity. Kind of feels like playing Slay the Spire with only common cards and a hard cap on relics.On top difficulty, while smart thinking obviously does help, the game is primarily won by finding something worth committing to early enough, and then getting lucky enough to find stuff that complements it, or the other way around. And, if you're doing decently, but didn't get offered the boss reroll item, you might still end up losing at the very end, to one of the 5 possible final bosses, that takes 3 times as many points to defeat. 3 mostly uneventful bosses, one that can occasionally be a challenge, and then one that will automatically end most runs. And I mean,  runs. Do the math, 1.2 million really takes a lot of luck to be theoretically doable. That's some fine design right there.The game also suffers from a lot of pointless content that doesn't add much to the experience but makes completion more grindy than it needs to be (like, 5-ish starting decks - the equivalent of playable characters - making somewhat significant changes to the gameplay, and another 10 that pretty much all play the same way).Finally, some minor nitpicking : at least one mechanic feels like it was just copied from other popular games without understanding why it belonged there (and not here) : the interest system.While it made a ton of sense in TFT, for instance, it brings a false sense of depth to the game, and turns out to do the exact opposite of that, as it further incentivizes you to think in black and white (if this isn't a perfect fit for my build and I don't need it to survive right now, here's another excuse to dismiss it). Essentially a way to take away some liberty from the player, while tricking them into thinking they're getting more of it, and again, rewarding single-mindedness.I suppose certain folks will be happy with it, as it does very much have that power trip aspect that I've seen lots of people complain is missing in StS/LBAL/other similar games.As far as I'm concerned, though, having to make concessions to make an imperfect build work is what keeps me entertained - and occasionally surprised - in the long run, as opposed to just dismissing everything that isn't a perfect fit. There's a certain kind of magic in these games that I don't see in Balatro.(On a sidenote, there's a lot of micro-managing to do, so if you don't like that, by all means, stay away.)Edit after 40 more hours : I waited a few months before playing it again, and having little recollection of some things made it enjoyable for a while. I tried to keep an open mind, but really, I stand comforted in my views. The game promotes dichotomous thinking, and the impact of strategy vs. RNG (strict sense, not a comment on difficulty) is much lesser than standard in this genre.It's not bad, or stupid, or wrong. _childDocuments_.review: A fun roguelike deckbuilder in the genre of , but with a focus on making and scoring poker hands.Unfortunately, while Slay the Spire has thousands of hours of skill cap, Balatro so far feels like tens of hours.  There is far less depth and balance in Balatro which spoils an otherwise intriguing idea and  clever implementation."Runs" are broken up into 8 "Antes".  Each ante consists of three "rounds" or "blinds".  The first and second blinds ("small" and "big") can be played or skipped for a reward.  If played, you make poker hands and score points attempting to reach the target number of points.  If you fail, the run is over, but if you succeed, you get money and a visit to the shop where you can buy things that to help you in future rounds.  If you skip the blind, you get a randomized bonus item.  The final blind is against a boss with an extra effect to make the game harder (e.g. "debuff" certain cards, meaning they don't score their individual points -- but the hands they make still do).In my experience, skipping blinds ends up being a bad idea almost always.  This is because the reward you get is often equivalent to one item purchased from the shop, but if you win a blind, you win enough money to buy at least one item from the shop, and playing a round can often activate lots of additional bonuses, like discarding cards to receive consumables (tarot cards or planet cards).  In addition, skipping the blind skips the shop, meaning you lose out on any other sources of improvements for your deck.With StS, every aspect of the game has depth to it.  Pathing through the map is an important skill, but no such element exists in Balatro.  Enemy combats are far more involved in StS than simple rounds in Balatro, all of which are the same except with the boss blinds.  In StS, you start with around 12 cards, which makes customizing your deck to remove starting cruft far more feasible than in Balatro where you start with a full 52 card poker deck.The Jokers don't feel all that balanced, either.  Some are effectively completely worthless, and you keep getting bad common jokers even late into the run, which makes it pretty hard to improve sometimes.  Meanwhile, other jokers can be pretty broken, like the "red card" joker that gives +3 mult for skipping a booster pack (meaning it can gain +6 mult every round -- but again not if you skip the blind and receive the bonus).Some suggestions to increase the skill cap:1. At the start of every run, the game should remove 10-20 cards from a standard deck at random.  Then the player should be allowed to choose and remove 5-10 cards.  This means you'll be able to make decisions about whether you're aiming for straights, flushes, or pairs/etc, and makes newly added cards more valuable.2. Every blind should have different buffs/debuffs that are potentially potent but not as bad as the bosses.  These should happen semi-predictably based on the ante/blind.3. Skipping blinds should provide better rewards, or at least allow you to revisit the shop with renewed stocks.As a nit-pick, I found the system of enhancements/editions/seals a bit counter-intuitive.  It's not at all obvious that enhancing a gold card to be wild would remove the gold enhancement, but it's valid to have a foil+gold card.  And the game doesn't warn you when it would remove an enhancement.Overall, it's a fun game that I don't regret buying, but I will say I was hoping for much more.

_childDocuments_.review: If you have been to Dear Gamers before, you know I am particularly fond of roguelites. If you are new, welcome to Dear Gamers and my borderline-dangerous addiction to roguelites. Last year, I thought I saw it all with a sports roguelite (Tape to Tape - a fantastic hockey game). Someone, somewhere assumed that was a challenge and I present (drumroll please): a card game roguelite (technically, Solitaire is a roguelite, more accurately a roguelike but Solitaire is boring and….anyway).Developed by LocalThunk, Balatro is a poker roguelite. THE poker roguelite. Play some poker, try to beat the blinds, rinse, and repeat until you lose. The DNA of a deckbuilder is buried in here but it remains a game of poker throughout. What if I told you that you could turn two pair into such an amazing hand that it would make 4 Aces look like a high card? You might think you know how to play poker but throw all that out the window when you play THIS game of poker.Everything will start somewhat normal. All rounds have a small blind, a big blind, and a boss blind that require you to reach a certain score. You are dealt 8 cards and can play up to 4 hands to reach the score. Hands can be 1 card or up to 5 cards. You also can discard up to 5 cards at a time 4 times per blind. Any legit poker hand counts here but the better the hand, the more you score. Scoring here may seem daunting at first but in no time at all, you will make Alan proud.Scores are calculated as Chips times Multipliers. Every hand has a base score value. For example, a high card is worth 5 x 1 and a full house is worth 40 x 4. The Chips side is increased by card value which is as simple as 1, 2, 3, 4, etc. with face cards equaling 10 and Aces worth 11. The game does all the math for you but I will admit that I broke out a calculator a few times when I was down to my last hand just so I could see my chances of winning with a straight versus a flush. What is great here is that basic poker logic gets thrown out the window. The more you play the more you realize that things like a full house is not necessarily better than two pair and a single 8 could net you five times the points as four 10s. Winning each blind rewards you with some cash to use in the shop that is only accessible between each blind. You earn a set value just from the blind itself and an extra $1 for each remaining hand you have left. Once you start accruing money, you can earn $1 interest for every $5 you have saved. There are additional ways to earn cash but these are standard. The aforementioned shop is how you make this regular game of poker into something of legend. Shops provide you with the following: 2 cards (these can be any type), 2 card packs (you get to pick a card from a number of cards), and a voucher. Vouchers generally cost a lot and are not as flashy as other cards but generally have long-term value. If you do buy it, another will not appear until you clear the current boss blind. Some of their perks include providing an extra item choice in the shop or permanently increasing the number of cards in your hand. Buying any voucher will unlock it for future runs although some vouchers only appear after some in-game milestones are reached (these can viewed from the collections screen in the main menu).What exactly is in the shop that makes your cards better? First up are Jokers. Jokers may not be used in normal poker but in Balatro, they are super important and almost crucial to your access. They serve as temporary (they only last the current game) buffs to the hands you will play. For example, a Joker may add a +4 multiplier to all played hands and another Joker may allow you to go up to $20 in debt in the shop. Shopping spree!Many Jokers have insane synergy with other Jokers. A favorite of mine was getting the Joker that granted +30 chips every time you play a face card. While this may seem tame because you have to hope for favorite deals, there is a Joker that treats all cards played as if they are face cards. Any card played in a hand, regardless of regular value, would also give me +30 chips. Throw in the Joker that scores all cards played and you could play a single Ace with a 2, 5, 9, and Jack, and the game will score the hand as a high card but also give you points for each card. That’s an additional 150 chips played (before adding in card value) on a simple High Card hand. Jokers can even affect how hands work like allowing for a 1-card gap in a straight or only requiring 4 cards for a flush. Jokers can be sold to fit new/better ones and once a Joker is discovered, they can appear in all future rotations.The other cards appearing in the shop are called consumables as they change your existing cards versus being cards used in your hands. Tarot cards can alter your standard cards into enhanced cards. There are  8 types of enhancements to encounter. Two such enhanced cards are wild cards (the card can become any suit) and stone cards (the card value is completely removed but the card is worth +50 chips). Tarot cards can also change a card’s suit, increase their rank (J to Q, 2 to 3, etc.), or give money. Planet cards improve the value of your hands meaning they increase the base score of a chosen hand. This also has a chance to synergize well with Jokers cards specifically ones that affect a certain type of hand. Last but not least are Spectral cards. The player has less control of what the Spectral cards do as the buff can be somewhat random such as granting 4 cards an enhancement while destroying a random card or changing all cards in your hand to a random suit. Consumables can be found in the shop, usually purchased from a pack that allows you a choice of the given consumable or from a tag. Like Jokers, all of these only affect the current game and do not carry over but once discovered on one run can appear in future runs.Most people hear poker and think of a group setting or something played online for money. LocalThunk has managed to take that and flip it on its head. What we have here is a genuinely fun, single-player experience. The gambit of runs can easily go from outrageously fun and adrenaline-pumping to incredibly frustrating in a matter of seconds. The “one more run” feeling seen in many roguelites can be seen here in spades (PUN INTENDED). Hands in Balatro last mere minutes and whether you have a successful run that goes many rounds or an early elimination, you will want to try again almost immediately. On top of all that, you can dive into the seed system as the game allows players to share their favorite runs (be sure to check out both the Steam forums and the game’s own Discord). Card games on PC have come a long way from being pre-packaged with the Windows Entertainment Pack to provide literally hours of fun. Become your very own card shark in this delightful twist on an old game.Full review with screenshots and video can be found at

_childDocuments_.review: Actually really good. The poker hands could be a stand-in for literally anything else but I think the devs were tryin to capture the sort of "cool vibes" of playing poker which is appreciated, but it's still worth acknowledging it's not poker it's just poker hands.Having unlocked most of the jokers the game is admittedly beginning to get a little stale. I've seen critics going crazy about this game acting like it's the next slay the spire in terms of cardbuilder roguelites but I disagree.Critics tend to just link any new concept to old concepts that they like and I think the constant comparisons to better performing games in the genre actually hinder rather than help the game's perception mainly because this game's strength is the fact that it takes you by surprise with it's depth.When you're expecting wow best roguelite ever made wow amazing so cool you're just setting yourself up for disappointment. It's better to go in with middling expectations and find that enjoyment in my opinion anyway.I'd definitely recommend it it's a fun game lots of interesting stuff to do and discover and I think there's a lot more of the aforementioned depth to it that I haven't quite breached, however it's nowhere near as genre-defining as critics are making it out to be, mainly because there's just not enough run variety.I'd love to see either jokers or a new card type that grant you access to "illegal" poker hands outside of the secret five of a kind and royal flush etc. the joker that allows you to more flexibly build straights (Shortcut?) is a favourite due to the fact you're looking for more than just your standard poker hands and actually have to think a bit more about things.Visual style is gorgeous; CRT crunchiness is always welcomed and every little animation from discarding to card selection to opening tags is so so satisfying.From some reading I understand that the tags upon skipping a blind were supposed to be a 1 in 4 chance like the wheel of fortune card and my God am I glad I didn't play when that was a thing lmao, although skipping blinds if you get the right tags does feel massively strong since first blind (at least from where I'm sitting) dies to 2 maybe 3 at most 5 card unbuffed hands.In conclusion, there's a lot of fun to be had, a few issues here and there but nothing that stops the game from being an extremely fun and accessible visual and auditory treat that definitely does tussle with the titans of roguelite games. However it's getting just a teeny tiny bit overhyped.Despite that, if it hadn't been for every YouTuber in my sub box creaming jorts it probably would've passed under my radar so I'm pretty grateful for the big hype around it.

_childDocuments_.review: The nicest thing about Balatro is that while it's a game involving a lot of RNG factors, you can choose to sit down and work your probability out. The poker theme is admirably held across the whole game, and some experimentation leads to rewards. The starting decks you unlock also differ, sometimes wildly, from each other, and promote different strategies.The biggest personal negative is the update that boosted many jokers and skip rewards, as it made the game easier by a clear margin. Not that I still can get through ante 8 on every (higher difficulty) run, but in my opinion it still takes something from the sense of achievement I get.All in all, this game belongs to my personal Greatest-of-All-Time-games list.TL;DR: Great roguelite deckbuilder game. _childDocuments_.review: After a solid decade of "expansion" of what Roguelikes/Roguelites are... what Balatro does is geniusly different on two levels.First of all, most Roguelikes/Roguelites take a fundamentally skill-based genre of games - platformers, RPGs, action-adventure games... and then use randomness and modifiers to make them more luck-based. What Balatro does differently is taking a fundamentally luck-based game, Poker; and using randomness and modifiers to make it more skill-based, and it's a very satisfying twist on that end.The second thing, is that while many Roguelikes/Roguelites *expand* upon what the genre intends to mean, Balatro instead distills is to the simplest, core values that make it work. Using your loot to modify things in the standard ruleset, in ways that may or may not synergize well with one another, and making you focus on one or two really core strategies. Then your tests - the Boss Blinds - are there to make sure if you're a one-trick pony that min-maxes one element of the game (for example, maxing a suit for flushes), you're probably gonna hit a wall against it (ie: that suit being debuffed and scoring nothing).It really is a truly remarkable act of game design all around.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid amount of variety and the impeccable vibes from the excellent audiovisual presentation can keep you playing for hours in a zen-like trance. Theoretically the interface and play experience could be slightly polished, but the biggest downside is that the hardest difficulty feels too reliant on good RNG at the start to get runs going at all, leading to a lot of early resetting. Thankfully this can be mitigated by just playing on lower difficulty. But while we're on the subject of lower difficulties, my other difficulty-related gripe is that Eternal Jokers are locked behind a relative high difficulty level - they are a considerable enough gameplay changer (most importantly, a Joker being eternal isn't always going to be negative, it can very much be positive as well!) that I would personally like to either see them on base difficulty already or alternatively have them added into the mix on the second difficulty already so you could play base difficulty + eternals, without having to deal with any of the other difficulty modifiers.Also, while I already praised the audiovisual presentation at the start, I have to give an extra shoutout to the music - it's amazing how you just don't get tired of it despite the game's soundtrack consisting of basically just a single song with some slight variations. _childDocuments_.review: If I could give a non-positive non-negative review, this is the game I'd give it to.  It's fun as you unlock some stuff and get engaged; then it's a hard dropoff into wasted time and effort.Balatro scratches the gambler itch - one more hand, one more run.  Every run is slightly different and sometimes you're running hot.Balatro wastes your time - most runs end before the second stage because you're never handed enough options to build a winning strategy.Balatro keeps you engaged - with discovering more unique jokers and card effects that you can use.Balatro bores you - by making the interesting combinations so rare that you have to play and restart to the point of boredom to construct the style of play you want to try.Balatro feels like pulling the arm at a las vegas casino machine - you may or may not have fun, but you'll definitely waste your time doing so.Game design wise, the store and earning currency is the biggest problem with the design.  The store offers too few options and options cost too much.  At first, this can be a fun drip feed, but in advanced runs, the store becomes a boring reroll-a-thon.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty boring, yeah there's a lot of card combinations but at the end of the day it's just enhancing poker hands. There is never a feeling of defeating any boss or objective because it's just score 500 points, ok now score, 1000, ok now 5000, etc. Played through my first run and won super easily defeating the final boss (100,000 wowow) in a single hand.....I've never played a roguelite where I win on my very first attempt knowing nothing about the game.I could see this being fun for someone who likes playing card games and doing simple math but overall it put me to sleep so I refunded it.

_childDocuments_.review: I have no clue how this game managed to be as disgustingly addictive as it is, but here we are.While we've seen a LOT of deckbuilding roguelikes in recency (quite frankly, too many), Balatro is not only one of the most literal versions of that genre name, but probably the last one you'll ever need to play.Turning the unchanging constant of table card games that is poker into this weird twisted roguelike is something that sounds pretty simple on paper, but LocalThunk turned it into an extremely nuanced game. This game has a solid core gameplay loop, good visual feedback, a very distinct personality, and is very easy to pick up and play, even if you have no idea what poker is or how it works.I've put so much time into the demos in anticipation for its official release, and here we are.If you're thinking about getting this game, absolutely get it. There's a reason it's blown up so much.

_childDocuments_.review: If there was an "positive BUT" rating, that's what I would choose for this review.The first hours of Balatro are honestly so satisfying. You unlock tons of stuff, you see big numbers getting stupidly bigger and you learn how this whole craziness of stacking passives work.While the game is quite simple and intuitive, there is also a little part of complexity and experimentation. It's fun to see what can happen if you combine this with this or that.However.The game currently has three major problems I believe.First problem are the "stakes", which is the equivalent of "ascension" levels in games like Slay the Spire or Monster train. Each new "stake" stacks with the others before it, increasing the difficulty. And the more you stack, the more this game turns into an RNG festival. If you don't find the right bonuses from the start, you simply won't last at all. While luck has always been a thing in deckbuilders, it's far less fun when you're entirely dependent on it.Secondly, this game has what I'd call a "binding of Isaac" syndrome. In Binding of Isaac, they added so much items, many quite useful or straight hurtful, that it diluted the pool of available good items.Balatro, to me, suffers from the same problem. Your runs are highly dependents on "joker" cards (think of them as trinkets with passives) and you can unlock up to 150 of them. Not all of them are useful, or maybe in certain very niche situations. And they have rarity too, so you'll see the less interesting ones often. And higher rarity doesn't mean they're inherently good. This makes it hard to build your deck properly, especially at later stakes.Finally, the viable hands. You've seen that you score points by playing poker hands. And even though you can manipulate your deck to suit your needs, albeit that requiers some luck as well (like making a deck entirely aces to score four of a kind regularly), you'll pretty quickly discover that the flush stands mighty in this game. They are quite easy to come by, many consumables can also help you create a deck turned toward a certain color and it's profitable in terms of points to score. Other hands, even though they can be viable, are either too hard to set up or score too little. Again, you can modify your deck accordingly, but it'll take more efforts and luck, wich is exacerberated with each stake.Playing on base difficulty makes it completly enjoyable. The only problem is that winning on higher stakes unlocks new stuff (mainly new deck archetypes) so if you're a completionist you'll have to restart runs A LOT.So, as a conclusion, I'd say that this game is definitely worth your while, but it still needs some balance to make it fun at every stage.
_childDocuments_.name: Balatro

_childDocuments_.review: Balatro is a very fun game...for the first few hours. Weirdly enough, the more you play the game, the less fun it is. Unlocking more content would seem to be a great way to extend the gameplay, but there's a bit of a bell curve going on. Past a certain point, each unlock is just diluting the pool, making it harder to get the build you need for your run. Add to that increasingly difficult unlocks (should you care about them) and once you get past a certain point, Balatro can very quickly go from fun to frustrating. When I started out, I could lose myself in long sessions, getting new unlocks and winning hand after hand, not even minding if a run was a loss because I was still getting something. Past that point, I find myself needing to take a break after even a couple of hands, realizing more and more that under all of the roguelike mechanics, I'm just playing cards, with visuals not much more interesting than the Solitaire that's been packed with PCs for decades.

_childDocuments_.review: "Balatro" takes a clever spin on the deck-building roguelike genre, merging classic card-based strategy with a dash of humor and whimsy. Its unique "joke-building" mechanic adds a layer of creativity that’s as unexpected as it is refreshing. Players draw cards that represent comedic themes or punchlines, stringing them together to craft “jokes” that pack quite a punch in battles. Visually, the game adopts a quirky, cartoonish art style that complements its lighthearted tone without sacrificing strategic depth. The challenges increase steadily, keeping you engaged without overwhelming, though the randomness of card draws can sometimes feel unforgiving. With its amusing characters and imaginative gameplay, "Balatro" feels like a distinct, playful experience that doesn’t take itself too seriously—a welcome breath of fresh air in the world of deck-building games.

_childDocuments_.review: After spending another 35 hours in this game, I'm ready to give a proper review.Let's start off with the main question I've seen..and the main question I had when delving into this game initially: I don't know how to play poker / I'm not good at poker... why would I play this?I'll be real, my only experience prior to Balatro with Poker was playing Poker Night at the Inventory (when I was a young teen) and playing the Mario Poker DS minigame.This game is NOT a poker game as much as it is a roguelike deckbuilder akin to Slay the Spire or Monster Train. Yes, the core mechanics to score are poker related -- but the game allows you to see what you need to score these at any point. It also lets you know if a hand would score.The main scoring will be making choices that impact your run, then rolling with what you're given to proceed to Ante 8 and beat the run. I FULLY recommend this game, it is genuinely close to perfection. My only complaints would maybe be balance at the higher stakes. Overall, this game is a unique experience that will shape future roguelikes to come. The music is fantastic, the presentation is great, and the gameplay is snappy and addictive. Runs can be played at your own leisure, so go as quick or as slow as you'd like.If you like this genre of roguelike at all, do yourself a favor. This game is worthy of being up there with Slay The Spire. If you are reading this and are already addicted and want more of a fix, go check out Luck be a Landlord too :)

_childDocuments_.review: is a captivating roguelike deckbuilder game that may initially appear to be just another poker game. However, it offers an intriguing and innovative twist with its unique mechanics, including collecting jokers, utilizing tarot cards, and leveraging planet cards as boosts to enhance your score.The game revolves around reaching 8 antes, each representing a small blind, big blind, and the challenging "boss blind." Players face random challenges at each stake, adding an element of unpredictability and excitement to each round. While small and big blinds require reaching a score, the boss blind presents additional challenges, such as limited playable suits or restrictions on face cards.What sets Balatro apart is its clever integration of traditional poker elements with inventive gameplay mechanics. The inclusion of jokers, tarot cards, planet cards, and special poker cards adds depth and strategy to the game, making each playthrough a unique and engaging experience. offers a refreshing take on the roguelike deckbuilder genre, combining poker mechanics with innovative twists to create an immersive and enjoyable gameplay experience. With its challenging stakes and strategic gameplay, it's sure to keep players coming back for more. I find this game particularly satisfying to play after a long day of work when I don't feel like hitting the bed just yet. Its stress-free and enjoyable nature makes it the perfect choice for unwinding in the evenings.

_childDocuments_.review: Balatro is a brilliant spin on the rougelike deckbuilder genre, using poker and the classic 52 card deck to create a unique game I've not seen anything like before. As you can see people have high praise for the game and it is rightly deserved.Right away Balatro is very user friendly, the game is very easy to access and modify files to add, change or modify the game to the way you want to play. It's very easy to run and uses very little storage space. In the game, you have 3 profiles to play with, each with its own progression save, but the great thing is you can use one of these profiles to unlock everything right away (at the expense of achievement progression while playing the profile) to just jump right into any deck you want with all modifiers and cards. Each run in seeded, so you can copy, save and share the seed to improve or re-experience a great run. The game is apparently balanced in a way that if you play right, every game on the base difficulty is winnable.I will be honest, I did not enjoy the game very much when I first played. I wasn't feeling the "addiction" feeling of enjoyment others had from the game. But slowly but surely after unlocking new and different jokers and getting to grips of how to be successful in Balatro, there was plenty of goals and enjoyment to be had.There is a slight learning curve when you first jump in, as this is far from a typical poker game. Your scoring is based upon poker hands on playing up to 5 cards at a time. Each poker hand has a Blue number times a Red number, Blue represents your Chips and Red is your Mult. When you play a hand your score will be Chips times your Mult. The harder your hand is to play the more you will score. If you pass the threshold of the blind you progress to the shop before another blind. This is the core gameplay loop, you will have 3 increasingly harder fights or Blinds as it is called, Small, Medium and Boss Blind. The boss blinds will have a condition or debuff you will have to play around to score. Every time you beat a boss blind your "Ante" will increase which each time will make the scoring requirements to pass harder. Once you beat the boss of Ante 8 you win the run and can test your deck in a rapidly scaling endless mode to see how far you can get.There are 15 decks to play each with different base modifiers to play around, each time you win on a deck you can play again on a harder difficulty stake up to 8 times each with stacking conditions as you go up. Once you win a few games you unlock challenges which have unique rules to try to win a run with. Beating a challenge unlocks a new one, starting with 5 unlocked up to a total of 20.Currently you have 150 jokers to use to help you bend the rules of your hand to help you score. 22 Tarot cards to help with deck manipulation. 18 Spectral cards, which are like double edge swords, giving strong manipulation at the cost of potentially run ending negatives if you are not careful. and 22 Planet cards which directly increase the base power of your poker hands. This on top of Card Seals, Card Enhancement and Joker Editions, there is a lot to learn and play around with to help you win.This in an excellent game at a great price, easily worth the money if this style of game takes your interest, and is very enjoyable to play both on the PC and on the go with the Steam Deck.

name: Dystopika
detailed_description: Dystopika is a small city-builder inspired by cyberpunk and the wanderlust of cities that never sleep. Place buildings, giant billboards, and towering holograms, working in harmony with procedural generation for landscape, traffic, and lights to create your own future metropolis rich with vibes and ambience. Escape to your own little dystopian dreams (or nightmares). No goals, no objectives, no wins or losses. Just relax and embrace creative cyberpunk zen. If you love to turn on the cheat codes and just build, this one's for you. Welcome to the Darker Side Of Cozy. Dystopika is an evolving passion project by a solo-developer. Join the Discord community to share your creations, give feedback, and help shape its future.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fascinating little game-toy-thing. You can really get some exciting vistas from it if you put in the effort to carefully place things, and there is absolutely a sense of relaxed aesthetical focusing.That said, here are some things that I'd like to see in the program (consider these as constructive feedback).- Proper height differences in the map, possibly an ability to terraform height levels. This would give variability to the environment and make certain city layouts even more striking. (Like imagine one of those pyramids on a tall hill surrounded by the city.)- Water, or rather, some ocean or river that would give some striking low angle shots of a built up shoreline.- Better control over district types, and preferrably more districts, while the building-based influence system is workable and provides a sense of soft transition, it lacks control, some kind of a map painting system with borders that can be toggled visually on and off depending on if you want it or not- Roads, huge winding highways cutting through a city are a classic staple of especially Japanese style cyberpunk aesthetics. Being able to place those would be fantastic. And in the air, more control over hovercar movement and organization into lanes would make the environment look more "realistic", or rather, "believable". Perhaps via designated "rails" or rather, bezier curve defined routes? Roads and hovercar paths combined with proper terrain (water and heightmap instead of just impassable hills at the edges) would naturally help segment the city in districts in a more believable fashion and also to give some natural transition space between districts.- And of course the thing that no developer wants to hear: more assets. More basic buildings, more billboards, some special ploppable buildings perhaps.All of those things said however, this is a very fun game-toy and I highly enjoyed the time I spent with it. Thank you dev for making this.

_childDocuments_.review: I love it already, it's basically a Blade Runner version of Townscaper.Style and overall vibe/design is straight on point. It's already really well made with a lot of attention to detail, ticks all the boxes of your favourite cyber city and works like a charm. And the music brings it all together.Nonetheless, here is a list of improvements I'd love to see in the future:-please don't force us to unlock everything again, I for example wanted more traffic in my second city and now have to figure out which building unlocks it- more control over colours, for example the red/blue glowing buildings, let us give them our own colour, would diversify the buildings a lot!- more buildings on the different categories, but yeah, that's a no brainer for sure- different maps with other sceneries-the option to turn off lens dirt completely-different fonts for the signs, would diversify the signs a lot and fit the universe even better- let us change the size of the assets in general, not just the height of the buildings, but the overall size of the buildings (with scaling windows perhaps, so they stay the same size and fit the rest) and expecially the size of the decorations. I love the antennas, but some are a little too big and it would diversify the possibilites of adding detail without everything looking the same-ultimately, a simple hover car to fly through the city would be the pinnacle- a little more control over the screenshots, for example to export them as .png or to control the .jpg quality- and of course, mod support! this will make the game immortal for all eternityI do understand some of these will be very difficult to develop and I don't expect you to, some of these are somewhat utopian for a niche title, but I will play and recommend this game nonetheless, have two cool new screenshots already, I am very happy!(yeah, I just discovered the roadmap and now I'm even happier, I'm so looking forward to these updates)

_childDocuments_.review: DystopikaCity building simulator + Cyberpunk. This is Dystopika. The game is a relaxed, chilling city-building simulator in a futuristic cyberpunk world. You have the opportunity to build various high-rise buildings and decorate them with holograms and billboards, for example. You can even upload your own pictures and design your own world. There are many setting options, such as the color of the sun, time oft he day, fog, rain, and many color filters that make the city look different every time. A camera mode is also included to record short videos. There is also first-class, chilled music, so that building becomes a meditative experience, as there is (fortunately in my opinion) no management. This game is just right for players who love cyberpunk + city building, without any kind of management. 10 / 10

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an incredible amount of untapped potential. As much as I appreciate its focus on relaxation, it makes me really want a full-fledged cyberpunk city builder with deeper mechanics challenges, objectives, and resource management. The immersive atmosphere of the cyberpunk genre would blend perfectly with the complexity of managing a sprawling futuristic city, balancing growth, technology, and societal needs.While I'm aware that the current direction of this game is to provide a more laid-back relaxing experience, it's hard not to imagine what it could become with a broader scope. The foundation is already here, and it shows promise for something much more ambitious. I absolutely love what the game offers, and I hope we might see a true cyberpunk city builder in the future.
