I love this visuals.This game is perfect for a gloomy evening just you, a faceless town and the amazing music!I absolutely love this game and for the prize it's perfectly reasonable to buy it and play it occationally.To the dev, thank you for persuing your dream, for making this game and for trusting in the community that it will be met with excitement.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This is a work in progress, so don't expect City Skylines from it. It isn't even Townscaper. It has great potential so be patient for the roadmap to be developed more fully. It's entertaining right now but still limited. I can't see getting more than 2-3 hours from it at present.Basically you place dark buildings in a night (or dark) setting, add some decorations as they get unlocked, add some advertising and logos, and tinker with the limited options for ambient lighting and weather. The result is a sort-of Blade Runner city that you can rotate and zoom to a limited degree. Then take screenshots.Some things I would recommend be added:1. A real daylight mode so users can place new buildings more accurately in brighter light. Maybe add a grid to help exact placement.2. A tweaked growth mode for tall buildings that doesn't create vertical streaks of lighting in some.3. Helicopter pads on top of buildings not just on the sides.4. A street-level zoom mode (maybe a walkable mode?) and generally a greater zoom ability.5. More control over building lighting (like the ability to light an entire floor on all sides, or to change a floor's colour)6. An option or decoration for rooftop gardens/restaurants/bars/pools7. Tooltips for the menu options. Their use is currently a bit opaque.8. A sandbox mode where everything is unlocked9. Move and resize options for placed ads, decorations, and buildings (if these already exists I couldn't out how to do it).10. More atmosphere filters with different effects or a fully customizable interface for filters11. Snapshots available from the top of specified buildings or at street level12. Rain slick effects, not just rain itself.13. More building types. Maybe a workshop feature so users can contribute their own designs. Towers like those in Seattle and Toronto would be nice.14. User-placeable walkways between buildings.15. Different colours for building materials (maybe shades of grey instead of all-black).16. A method where users could share a code to recreate the cities in their own computers (like Townscaper has)17. An overhead view looking straight down on the city.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I love this. I absolutely cannot ignore recommending this. I only hope and pray that it gets more attention and detail added to the game.Because right now, while parts of me would give it a thumbs down with what little it has to offer I am still going to thumbs it up because I just love this.Let us add roads, see people, etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Delightful mood builder rather than a city builder. That's my main takeaway from spending over 6 hours on it and still feeling up for more. Big thanks to the Dev for making this game <3If there are few things I'd love to see in future updates, these are the ones I think would be very nice:* Streets. Understandably this game is trying to emulate the mood of a sprawling metropolis where urban development outpaced any concerns for logical traversal, and I like that quite a lot to be fair. But without any kind of streets, it's a bit hard to give your city any kind of appealing structure. My current workaround is to plop down Alpha Buildings and then put the little Hover Car Arcs on top to emulate highways. Totally see why streets and roads might not be a core focus for the developer, I'd still love to see them in the game.* Color wheels. Or at least a way to alter the colors on the big skyscrapers. It feels a bit underwhelming to only get red and cyan for the buildings currently in the game. Maybe let us have a sharp lapis lazuli blue or a mellow orange just to spice things up?* Factory District buildings. This is just me being entitled here but with the Smokestack decorations I would really love to see some big ugly factory buildings that break away from the skyskraper aesthetics. You could put them on the outskirts of your city with some short LowTown buildings and all of a sudden you've got an oppressive slum/factory area.Thanks again!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: If you love Cyberpunk at all, then you owe it to yourself to pickup this "digital toy" because it's AWESOME and the price is right for all that you get and what you get is Townscaper if it had been designed by Ridley Scott and Syd Mead. I LOVE Cyberpunk and this is so much fun to play around with and chill. Fiddling with the buildings, adding in my own text and images for building signs, adding traffic, smoke stacks, all sorts of  built-in doo-dads to complete your Blade Runner-esque metropolis. Oh yeah, and of course, rain and fog to top it all off. The camera controls are buttery smooth and the screenshot mode is great and even has a camera motion widget to move the camera from one position to another over 5 to 30 seconds to create a cool vibe - it would be nice if you could record that as a video natively but maybe that will happen later. I can't wait to see what features get added down the road.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure I'd consider this a city-building game at all.  Instead I think of it more as a diorama builder.  I don't think that's a bad thing at all.  It's a chill experience.Lots of buildings to choose from,  tons of achievements, an unlock system that works quite well through encouraging you to try out new buildings.  Also you can add your own photos which I think is fantastic.  Too bad there wasn't an option to add in your own custom videos.  That would have made the experience relatively perfect, I think.  Personally I'd of added in the cinematic masterpiece Troll 2 to watch, but that's just me.  Maybe one day we'll get webm, mp4, or similar support.You can add text, and customize it.  There's this really cool level of obvious love and passion that went into making this game, and it is easily one of the most compelling reasons to play Indie titles.  This sort of passion is often lost on the "AAA" industry.Anyway, onto more stuff.  Graphics are good, it definitely captures the cyberpunk feeling.  There are a few weather options, but they're pretty much: Rain, more rain, Pea Soup.  I guess I'm not sure what else I'd add.  Snow?  Snow would've been cool.  You can increase/decrease the amount of rain, speed, mess with lighting, and a whole slew of other customization options.  There's also a camera mode that needs to be about 5x longer to make me truly happy.  I want a long video with more control over the pathing so I can set up a cool clip that really shows off my city.More music tracks would've been nice.  I feel like there were more than 2 in the demo, and hey maybe there are more than 2 in the game.  But so far, 2 are all I've heard.Overall if you're looking for a game you can play with the chillest of mindsets, this is a game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice little piece of software to sit down and play with. I can see myself using this to make some city maps for tabletop cyberpunk RPGs. For the price, it's hard to go wrong, just don't go in expecting a city manager. There are still some issues around optimization that need to be resolved, but I enjoy what's there.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to build a pretty little thing and chill out, it really isn't hard to miss with this game. Easy to build whatever you want, but you can get complex with how you position and decorate. I like to build for screenshots, and this game is real good for it. Looking forward to possible workshop support! Def recommend, 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: it's a good-looking game, but it does not have any substance, wish there were goals and some management to keep me in the game. I can see the appeal of this type of sandbox city builder but after 18 mins of playtime, I did everything in the game. It is as advertised but I hope the Dev/s has plans to make a more city skylines-type builder version on top of this sandbox builder.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: What is there to dislike about this game? Yes, there are many improvements that could and should be made. And they will come, in time. What we have for the time being though, is a great little time killer. Create a dystopian blade runner type city. How you go about it, is completely up to you. Your imagination is your only barrier. This is a terrific little game which will only continue to get better. The potential is enormous.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly beautiful, casual, gloomy, atmospheric game where you literally just place, rotate and scale buildings and decorations while getting lost in the music and general ambiance.It's very simple and that's perfect if you just need something to unwind.Oh, and the photo mode is incredible, if you're looking to create your next wallpaper!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This IS NOT a city management game. This IS a city builder game/tool. This is a game/tool that gives you all the things you need to build your own Cyberpunk City. No money, no research, no traffic management and no real goals. You just build.Regardless of your reasons for wanting to do that, this game does it very, very well.A nice relaxing game and toolset to just create a Cyberpunk landscape on. I will be using it for Artwork and Cyberpunk: Red (TTRPG) City scapes and skyline images etc. The developer very clearly understands the cyberpunk aesthetic and has nailed the assets and vibes in the game.Worth the price of a medium coffee that its being sold for.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Cyberpunk 2077 meets TownscaperMakes you want to monologue while staring out at the vast horizon.In all seriousness, this is a fantastic city builder with a ton of potential and I look forward for updates to customize my cities even further!Make no mistake, this is not in any way a game and more a tool for relaxing or expressing artistic expression in a city building sort've way. So before you spend your hard earned cash, keep that in mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: So, I've been a fan of city and theme park builders/tycoons etc etc for a very, *very* long time. By far my favorite genre of games I can always go back to when I don't know what I want to do or play, or if I need to let the creative juices flow. This game is such a simple yet absolutely enthralling extension of that genre, just a blank, cyberpunk themed canvas for you to let your imagination run wild. As a kid, I would always play stuff like RollerCoaster Tycoon 3 for hours on end with infinite money, just to see what I could build. As a teen, I'd do the same things with Planet Coaster, or Cities Skylines. This game captures that same feeling, beat for freaking beat - building gorgeous vistas and skylines to take screenies of, and just bask in "The dark side of cozy" as you put it, lol. Absolutely loving my time with this one, hats off to you Matt!!!Thank you for making this game, I'm excited to see what comes next <3
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovely piece of work. In mere minutes you can create a 'Blade Runner' megacity, full of eye-searing neon,  Above and around your buildings a horde of air buggies zip in and out of view, dodging the floating ad blimps. It needs little imagination to picture the teeming streets at ground level, constantly dripped on by high humidity, and populated by shadowy figures darting from ramen and sushi bars to opium dens and other dubious pleasure houses.The city creation process was, I found, almost meditative in its execution. Try it - you'll love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I fondly remember playing games like this as a kid. I love the cyberpunk/hyper industrialized aesthetic and this game NAILS IT. It also has interesting elements where it's building atmospheric buildings/particles/vehicles around what you build. It's very cool and it's sort of emergent in terms of look and feel. Thanks Matt!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: After playing intense, time-consuming games, this one really allows me to relax. I spend half an hour building my city, then two hours taking screenshots and recording videos.In the end, I still managed to make a small area very Cyberpunk-like.The city center is made into an authoritarian government zone that restricts people's access, plastered with government slogans: "One Earth, One Gov, One Man". This central area prohibits civilian activity, and not a single civilian sign can be seen. However, behind the government district lies the conglomerate of financial groups, with skyscrapers reaching into the clouds, filled with massive advertisements. Each tall building has advanced aerial vehicles.In contrast, the buildings in the outskirts are extremely low, but this is where the people actually live. You can see signs everywhere, and although there are no aerial vehicles, ordinary citizens reside here peacefully. They just have to coexist with the large power plant clusters that supply energy but also cause air pollution.The most amazing thing is that this game can actually create all these effects.I named my city "Eco City".
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I HAD A TINGLE WHEN I FOUND THIS. if u r looking for a game that is a city builder with no management or anything to worry about then this is your game, if u are look for the complete opposite, leave and dont buy the game. but if u are like me then this is your game. I love it and i cant wait to see it grow. all i can ask for is the ability to make buildings wider.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: is a very zen sandbox in a theme that I don't see too often (in this genre I mean). There is a minor puzzle element just in the unlocking of decorations, and you can get some achievements this way. That said, I wouldn't call this a puzzle game. This is still very much a sandbox. It is a tool through which you can create your own interesting cyberscapes using a variety of assets with well crafted procedural elements. I can see this program being great for making wallpapers, moving or otherwise--especially with the camera tool.If you like the idea of just taking a breather and spending some time just exploring your creative side, then  It won't cost you too much, especially on sale and/or as part of a bundle; plus, you'll be helping out a clearly talented, artistic indie dev in the process. I look forward to seeing what they do next, which includes the future updates for this game as there is still content planned for down the line.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent city-creation sandbox. It's a bit limited in its early state, but there's a lot of potential (especially with the workshop). It's gorgeous (despite graphical limitations), easy to learn and pick up, and very intuitive. I'm currently using it to design a cyberpunk city for some tabletop RPGing. This is an easy recommend at full price.Mods will soon become available and the dev seems to be interested in supporting them. This just makes me recommend the game more.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: i have hijacked my hubbo's acct to play this. i am the person who only plays SIms to build stuff and could care less about the actual game. i'm here for the mental check-out. this is magnificent, from the music to the low-pressure zen of it all. adhd dopamine + approved! I can't wait to see what other developments happen with this game. imma need more buildings. cheers! keep up the good work!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: The Dark Future has never been this chill.I was concerned a city builder with no real objective would get old fast, but it hasn't thus far. The game does not hold your hand but it is very easy to discover for yourself secrets about the buildings, how to make them interact with each other. Additionally being able to stick neon all over your city and just watch the aircars fly by is quite relaxing. For less than $10 this is a bargain as a relaxing take on city building in a theme that usually doesn't have this kind of relaxation.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Would like to see more varieties of buildings added into the game - sports arenas? lit-up 'ancient' statue monuments besides the holograms? more stuff in the skies... more signage/poster stock images (themed, say for a movie theater, a drink/food, or even police/hospital); would also like more fonts and banner sizes for the text signs, with just a choice of color would make that easier.Also my screenshots are set to my resolution, same as the game itself, yet they come in 1920x1080. =\I have a widescreen - 2560x1080 native. I want my screenshots (when I go in camera mode and click the camera button) to come in widescreen, not cut off on the borders like I'm on my old monitor. Otherwise I can get the full screenshot by doing F12 but then I got the tabs on the left side of the screen obv.I do wish there was more support for wider screens. Most games do, but some don't.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I've had this game in mind for a while in terms of game dev, I just never had the time.This game scratches an itch I've had for all that time, while not quite the exact same, it scratches that itch of cyberpunk-city builder.The aesthetic and vibe are on point, the soundtrack is fantastic and it's brimming with its own idea of what it set out to be.I hope this gets updates in the future of some kind to allow for customization/addition of several other aesthetics in the cyberpunk genre that allows one to cultivate it in different directions (occult: Shadowrun, nostalgic: Hypnospace Outlaw)Thank you Matt.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Like the lone developer of this title I'm also the kind of person who likes playing city builders mainly so I can see what cool looking city I can create (though I tend not to play on "god mode").At first I was hesitant to buy it because of the few negative reviews Id read stating that theres nothing here, or at least not enough to be worth calling a "game"...but I think its great!The whole experience has a great atmosphere and it's a joy to see how the city grows as you place buildings. Sure there could be more content (buildings, props, even the ability to grow beyond the starting square), but I think it's a great start.And, having just watched Blade Runner its clear to see where a lot of the inspiration came from...but it works!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little digital toy, rather than a game.Chances are you'll pick this up, muck about with it for maybe an hour and then not touch it again, but that's okay.Or you'll enjoy hours of making cyberpunk cityscapes with the simple yet robust tools in the game.Regardless of which you are, this little gem achieves exactly what it set out to do.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Highly Recommend Dystopika.It's such a chill and cozy game.It is a super simple city builder with no management so you can be as creative as you want.Yes there isn't much to it in terms of variety but they're in the road map which I look forward too. For the price is it definitely worth it. The Dev deserves the support for such love and attention that has gone into this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Does exactly what it says, if you want to chill out and create a Bladerunner'esq near future Cityscape, with an element of random chance and lighting effects thrown in, whilst listening to a atmospheric soundscape or the sound of the rain.... here you go.Dystopika does all this quickly, without needing to learn the in's and out's of an Art Package. Just the use of your mouse, shift, alt and ctrl combos is all that is required and where ever else that takes you in your minds eye.Has a nice feature where you can set a start / stop point, to fly through your scene hovercar style in a brief clip, or add filters and effects to take screenshots of your creations.£5.30 well spent, as can see myself chilling out and seeing where these scenes can take me.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Works on STEAM DECK! No Proton neede, WASD+mouse. This is amazing. I love the personal touch with the not and the voice over in the trailer. I love the atmosphere and music. I hope you continue to develop it and add more buildings. Id love to see this grow. Vehicle stations, roads, etc. Thank you! I didn't know I needed 'daek cozy' in my life!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Dystopika gets its name from the classic 1980s science fiction film, "" and its sequel "" I don't really remember what the movies were about, but I loved the atmosphere and special effects, and that's what this game offers.Read the description, then read it two more times before you buy. This isn't a traditional city builder, and the developer is 100% upfront about that. It's more of an art tool or meditation program. There's no deeper meaning inherent in the mechanics, apart from what you assign yourself. In theory, your city could very well be a wonderful place to live, there's just nothing to quantify it as such. These are pure cyberpunk aesthetics with no further depth to speak of.In keeping with that spirit, I'm going to keep my criticism relevant:Game needs more art tools. More decorations, more building styles, better camera control, ability to record video, and the ability to zoom in to street level. It needs better ways to explore and experience this city you've built, and less emphasis on "unlocking" new decorations through arbitrary tasks.If your game has no intrinsic goals, then the player will create an extrinsic goal for himself. Give us the tools to realize those goals.The developer has been active in the steam discussions, talking about what is and isn't planned, or viable. Roadmap looks promising, too, so keep an eye on that.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I came across this game randomly and after seeing the price and the note from the dev I couldn't resist. I have always loved city builders and cyber punk aesthetics. This game is exactly what it says it is. Not as much  a game as a way to kick back, relax and let your mind chill out. The ui is simple, atmosphere is gorgeous and it's a really nice way to kill some time. While it is a bit bare-boned, I highly recommend it. Assuming this sounds like something you would be into. The dev says more is to come, and who doesn't love supporting a passion project from time to time.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for in-depth city management, this is not the citybuilder for you.If you're looking for total commitment to a vibe with excellent execution, this is the citybuilder for you.At the moment it's maybe a liiiiittle shallow even with that in mind, but it's under active development and I'm really looking forward to seeing how it expands. The polish is already there, now they just need to stack it high with content - and with mod tools planned for the future, that's sure to happen.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: You get what it says on the tin. A city-building sandbox for futuristic cities. No goals, no management, just creativity and dark cosy vibes. Those vibes are quite immersive IMHO. Simple game that you can take as seriously as you want! Few minutes in and I already have a few cool screensavers.Nice game for a cheap price.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Works as advertised! A neat cyberpunk city builder in a mindset of the megacorps, no care for the population and no care for the budget! I like the buildings and styles, especially the Blade Runner-esque pyramids. I also enjoy how ads work, I love them! I love that I can import pictures from my PC, and that was the main feature that drew me to this game, that and the idea of building my own cyberpunk city. The idea of putting my own ads on these massive cyberpunk towers and structures appealed to me so much so, that I can't really explain it. I spent two hours, more than playing this game, in searching and downloading interesting-looking ads on Google. It's sad to say that I won't be playing this game for half the time I spent looking for the ads. I'll be honest, I got bored of it extremely quickly. As already said, there is no progression, no people to manage or fire departments to build, and so I build, and build until I got bored. The type of game, or rather, this genre doesn't appeal to me that much. It's not the game itself, it's a neat little game, but not for me, I got bored of it quickly, and that's that. I'll be giving it a thumbs up out of respect for the game, developer and genre, but as you can see from this review, the game itself isn't from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game, especially because it delivers on what it promises: a relaxing sandbox city builder where yo uplace building belonging to a specific buildset and the city procedurally generates around it. You can then add holograms and other decorations and then take pictures. That's it. It's a great way to kill time, or spend an hour being creative. Definitely worth the $8 CDN spent on it and would absolutely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed it even in the demo stage. I love city building & this makes it so much simpler & quicker than say Cities Skylines if you just want aesthetics without any goals to pass or maintain. There's so much potential for additions & improvements that other people have already mentioned that will hopefully happen in the future (more building types etc) but still enjoying it for now in it's first stages.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice toy for what it is but it does lack a few things which would add to the experience significantly. Basically a DIY wallpaper "game"10 bit support/HDR  - this game has horrible color banding - and for a game which is all about a dark environment and looks...that's something once you see you can't unsee. The game fails to detect the correct display resolution unless in exclusive full screen, which makes just having it on as a "wallpaper" of sorts basically impossible while you're doing something else - Not to mention the lack of an option to select which display the game shows up on...another thing keeping it from good wallpaper use. There is a weird...digital "filter" on the ui in the city view that is on all the time, you don't notice it when looking down at a dark city, but point the camera towards the sky and it's always there..and when you notice it, now you notice it while looking at a dark cityscape as well.None of these are really killers aside from the fullscreen issue really, and hopefully they'll get fixed in time. I'm moderately satisfied with what I have, and don't feel the need to refund - but there really could be some..improvements in certain departments.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I've been wanting this game since I saw Ghost in the Shell as a kid, and especially the city map display which gave me cyberpunk SimCity vibes before I even knew what cyberpunk was. I just never wanted it enough to actually sit down and figure out how to do it myself. So, thank you for bringing this to life, this game is fantastic! I adored the demo and I am loving the changes that I am finding in the release version. This has been one of the easiest purchases on Steam for me, not because of the low price point, but because it ticks all the boxes. 'Progression' being linked to a hidden element is a fantastic choice and completely removes any pressure or expectation while turning that proogrssion into a little gift of sorts that rewards tinkering. And the soundscape is simply phenomenal. It gives me chills when using my headphones, and it's so easy to lose myself in it.My only two wants for this game would be a neutral lighting mode that can be toggled on/off  that clears up all the fog and shadows for more precise detail work, Edit: The latest update added roads in two different sizes with traffic density that is controlled with a slider, a very nifty addition that really helps bring a city to life! The roads can be elevated with adjustable heights. As a bonus, elevated rail was added as well!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Dystopika is a game developed by Voids Within and published by Voids Within and UNIKAT LabelThe game offers some nice graphics and a really beautiful aesthetic, although some ugly glitches here and there, it is pleasant all the sameThe game does suffer with some repetitiveness at certain areas of the game but a fun game nonethelessDystopika overall, however, is a fun yet challenging game to play, yet sometimes repetitive and it does get boring and tedious if being played for a long time, but is a very good calm sandbox cyberpunk city builder game to play in short bursts!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: After playing this game for a bit and familiarizing myself with the mechanics and buttons. My only thought would be to add tag names to the buttons as the symbols can be hard to understand. Other than that I LOVE the game. Its soothing and relaxing to play. I can build and expand and add to my hearts content. Its oddly satisfying to watch your cyberpunk city grow and populate. I hope there will be more building types in the future and more options for expanding in height and maybe width. I play a lot of city builders and it nice to see someone create something different and unique. Its a great change of pace and high highly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This came out of nowhere, kept its premise and I was into creating mezmerizing yet hypnotizing Cyberpunk-Megacities in kind of a miditational state. Ran perfect, tons of fun experimenting and creating your own municipal landscapes. Nailed it.Be aware, that there is no qoal or quest or anything. Built as much as you want.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Good view-creating game with huge potential. It would be much much more wonderful if we have buildings that are designed in relation to different functions of a city such as parks, energy plants, traffic centers, etc. For cities skylines fans like me, it is fun to simply watching the city I create function smoothly, and this game now is still more like a static picture instead of a living city that I imagine.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: this game is amazing the city building is so fluid i do wanna say turning some buildings is a little wonk but with some practice its not hard ive already built two in depth city's Alpha and Omega since it was a natural theme already i would love to see more buildings for each category since i love the themes but 1 building option for Alpha and Omega category was a bit off putting but i forgot about it when detailing all the different buildings and putting up signs for most buildings like casino's, bank's, and even there own government per city based off of Alpha and Omega themes all in all i give this game a 4 outta 5 im willing to pay for the dlc but id like to see one soon for more buildings and maybe a round map option? anyways def worth the 7 bucks go get it itll be worth it and im just using it to draw my own city's for my TTRPG so its honestly a win win
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This game is chill & relaxing.... It has a progression you seem to discover as you play. I'm going thumbs up and keeping it just because it is trippy, cool, looks great, sounds good..... And hopefully could add stuff like shar RND seeds to share cities, or export to blender to use them in settings for things....
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this "i-am-not-a-game"- game! Even if it seems senseless to just fool around and build beautiful silhouettes, it calms you down and make you feel lighter. It's like a zen-garden. Nevertheless i build a nice city, implemented some of my own graphics and love it. Hope there will be the possibility to change environment to build beautiful cities in beautiful landscapes in the future. To me it's a 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Building a dystopian cyberpunk theme game has never been this  Not only that, you can also import your own image and make a city in your wild imagination possible! Although i hope the dev add option to adjust text size for the next patch since modding support is confirmed later. Overall this is basically a  for a cyberpunk enjoyers like me, just build, no need to worry for resources or anything.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Dystopika is exactly the game it claims to be. It's more of an art tool than a video game and that's all it really needs to be. Just relax and place buildings and tweak your ideal futuristic cyberpunk city without having to worry about money or food or any gameplay mechanics from other citybuilder games that would distract players from the creative process. There is also a nice set of photo tools because what's the point of building a beautiful futuristic city if you can't share it. I'm currently writing a video review to put on my channel on YouTube The Many Talented Mr Jefferson but the developer Matt mentioned that it would be nice to have 500 positive reviews before the Steam Summer Sale so I took a little time to recommend the game on this platform because it really does deserve the attention.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy citybuilders in creative mode but hate managing economies/resources, this is the game for you! You can build endless neon-soaked cyberpunk cities with a variety of different "district" themes that all mix and match and interact with one another through some procedural magic similar to Townscaper. This game is incredibly relaxing and you can easily throw a few hours into it without even noticing. Looking forward to future additions and mods!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Super chill and relaxing game. Really enjoying the soundtrack options. Even if you just blindly click around on random you can end up with some nice looking designs. Or be more focused and pick which district buildings you want to create dedicated zones.Photo mode is where you really make your city shine (literally). Plenty of controls to change the vibe.Really looking forward to seeing more items from the roadmap get released.Overall, highly recommended if you're looking for a zero-stress city builder.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Right, first thing is first, my playtime is short but the game is so simple there isn't too much to learn.I recommend it for those who like to chill, Like the Cyberpunk genre and like City builders.There isn't too much to this game which isn't bad. Should there be a second game I'd love to see it fleshed out as a full city builder.I will be playing more of it when I want to chill out and play something while listening to music. Sometimes that is all you need. My negatives are that again, I think it's too simple. I wish there was a bit more to it (That may be a positive thing if you look at it in the regards that I like it and want more)I think for on-boarding the buttons on the left would do with having a n overlay box saying what each button does. It take a few mins of fiddling around aimlessly until you realise what button does what as the icons are not clear. All in all, this is a really great start and I hope that should a second game come out or part of a road-map for this would be to flesh out the game more. I see there is a road-map with some hidden content that will release later down the line. time will tell.Great first effort solid 6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Hyperfocused on one single thing and it does that one thing extremely well. If you read the description and think 'that sounds cool' you'll have a good time. If you read the description and think 'that sounds boring' then it's probably not for you. And that's fine - this game exists to scratch a specific itch. And I love that it for that.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: When I bought this game I already had a pretty good ideia what it was about, and it was exactly what I wanted, but even then I was still expecting myself to get bored after a couple of hours in, which I think is natural. But it turns out I was wrong, after 9 hours straight I haven't gotten bored in the slightest, and I only stopped playing because I had to sleep.Like the developer, I always played SimCity and Cities Skylines on cheats/sandbox mode (and before that, I would draw cities on paper as a child), so this game is pretty much perfect for me. However its important to keep in mind that people looking for urban planning, traffic simulation and just management in general might be disappointed, as this game isn't about that. You just place buildings and decorate them, although its amazing how much freedom it gives you and how easy it is to build cities that look straight out of Blade Runner, which seems to be its main inspiration.Overall this game is gold, and the developer has put real love into it. Can't wait to see how it will look in a year after the planned updates and mod support.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a casual city builder, this is the game for you. You just build the city; there are no objectives, no money, and no people to take care of. It's pretty relaxing, and you can make your city any way you want. Either all the buildings are small, or you can raise them and have a city full of skyscrapers. I've only had it for a couple of hours, but I believe it was worth the small amount of money I paid for it. However, if you want to be able to micromanage your city like City Skylines or Simcity, then this is not the game for you. If you want to spend hours just building your city while unlocking some items to add more stuff, then this is the game for you. However, the one pet peeve I do have about this game is that there is no control settings page or tutorials. You have literally jumped into a building, and you have to figure it out or read the discussions for help.

_childDocuments_.review: Τhis is a game I've followed closely from the earlier stages of its development and it's been the first game in years to actually deliver on the expectations it set for me. It is exactly what it advertises: A cozy dystopian city builder sandbox. Anyone with a small interest in cyberpunk, or city builders (let alone in both) should give it a try. I'm confident you won't be disappointed. The price is ridiculously low for its quality and Matt, the developer, deserves every single penny of it. Sadly you don't get games that deliver on their promises that often anymore,. This is a solo dev game that didn't try to overachieve. The developer knew exactly what he was capable of creating and he did that: He delivered a masterpiece! As if that wasn't enough, the roadmap promises further refinement and replayability. Just imagine the diversity of cities once mods come in! Not to mention a feature I've been begging for from the beginning: road networks.  This game is a 10/10 on my book.

_childDocuments_.review: I got into contact with Dystopika a little earlier, in January when it was still just a demo with a few basic features and simple buildings.I Instantly got hooked by the ambiance as I've been a big fan of Blade Runner-esque movies and games for as long as I can think back.The gameplay is simplistic and straight to the point; you build a futuristic city the way you want it and dress it with fancy looking lights, billboards and other little props to shape up your imagination of such a dark dystopic future city.The developer poured his heartblood and personal experiences in big (Asian) cities as well as fandom for cyberpunk-esque movies, games and architectural art style into this and in my opinion that's visible in every little notch.Even just letting the game run in the background can be very soothing and adds a vibe to whatever you do.

_childDocuments_.review: The game promised "Simple" in all of its promotional material, and when you first jump in, it seems almost TOO simple, but once you play around with the controls and learn a little about how things work, it becomes obvious that the game delivers exactly what it promised. The ambiance is fantastic, the fog and rain transport you to that neon-soaked noir near-future that hearkens back to properties like "Blade Runner" and "Judge Dredd". It's fun to unlock the tidbits that pop up as you build, and they truly add to the overall feel of the whole thing. The sole developer has promised to continue adding features and elements to the game post-launch, and we're already off to a great start. The potential for true, immersive depth has a strong foundation to build from, and I can't wait to see where it goes. The only minor detraction from the overall experience might be that the game does not hold your hand at all. You pretty much have to learn about features and mechanics as you go. This may appeal to some folks, but it might mean you will scrap your first creation once you know what you're doing and can really open up creatively when starting from scratch. Overall very fun, and well worth the money if you are a fan of cyberpunk, and/or city building. I often found myself wondering what sort of stories could be found in the dark shadows of my city as I built...
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

Its really relaxing of a game and enjoyable to play since it has no rules or goal except just mess around and unlock new items! Its really just an amazing calming title.Although for the developer!!I would like to see hopefully upcoming maybe a little bit more usable buildings, lights, and things to solidify the experience and add more of the cyberpunk immersion feeling. I would also love to see a tutorial either a separate mode or optional when starting out this is helpful to explain maybe what you can do goals and etc cause it does just throw you into the experience and it isn't hard to understand the mechanics of the game and what to do but it is also nice knowing there is a tutorial or some form of explanation in case we want to reference or go back to something.Amazing title and price keep it classy and I cant wait to see where it goes from here.

_childDocuments_.review: The game that I have been waiting for has finally arrived. Have you ever wanted to create your own slice of Los Angeles from Blade Runner? Or maybe wanted to explore your own creative persona and build a cyberpunk city with no punishing requirements of resources or citizen demands. Dystopika blends zen chill city building vibes with an absolutely amazing cyberpunk aesthetic. Get lost in the large looming buildings, neon lights, flying cars that zoom by and brilliantly appropriate soundtrack. This is only the beginning of what's in store of this experience. Future updates will add more content and features. If you've ever wanted to play a cyberpunk city builder, Dystopika is the only game you'll need.

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals of this game and the music are amazing. I really like the minimal UI too. Everything really comes together for a sublime experience.UPDATE! _childDocuments_.review:
Dystopika is a small city-builder inspired by cyberpunk and the wanderlust of cities that never sleep.

Place buildings, giant billboards, and towering holograms, working in harmony with procedural generation for landscape, traffic, and lights to create your own future metropolis rich with vibes and ambience. Escape to your own little dystopian dreams (or nightmares).

No goals, no objectives, no wins or losses. Just relax and embrace creative cyberpunk zen. If you love to turn on the cheat codes and just build, this one's for you.

name: Star Trucker
detailed_description: Wishlist another new title from Raw Fury! About the Game Hop into the driver's seat of your rocket-powered big rig as you haul cargo, scavenge for salvage and interact with an eclectic cast of star-hopping truckers in this Americana-infused journey on the ultimate open road - space! Cruise the hyper highways, taking on a variety of jobs such as fuel hungry long hauls and hazardous drop-offs to earn cash and unlock new content. And don't forget to monitor the CB radio for chatter from fellow truckers; it's a fantastic way to uncover side gigs and stay updated on galactic gossip. Keeping your rig runnin’ isn’t always easy. You’ll need to keep your core systems online, gravity compensator spinnin’ and hull patched to prevent your cab from leaking lung juice. Be sure to make pre-trip shop stops for replacement parts, and consider upgrading your truck at a local garage. These improvements are vital for safely navigating volatile sectors and ensuring timely deliveries. Use the galactic map to plan your journey and warp jumps, while keeping an eye on your fuel reserves and power levels. Once your route is set, kick back, crank up the cab hi-fi and cruise to a selection of original songs covering starburst blues, galactic rock and asteroid infused americana. The open road is waiting! Star Trucker is the passion project of a small team: Monster and Monster. A two-person indie studio with a love for all things sci-fi and sim. With the help of some talented friends they’ve developed an out of this world experience filled with emergent challenges and complex systems to master. So buckle up and join them for the long haul!

_childDocuments_.review: I love the game so far. I worked on several big titles over a decade ago and moved industries. That may adjust the perception on my advice. @Devs, here's some input I hope you may value.-Throttle back the maintenance needs. It adds a layer of challenge but I wouldn't say it's the most enjoyable at its player time investment needs. I would even make the parts more expensive but reduce the failure rate. I feel like it just stops me from playing and I spend too much time focusing on it.-Earlier progression milestones (more features would help with this). It's flirting with the edge of grind and feeling near empty in progression.-Expand. There's an incredible foundation here that I feel can be easily expanded upon. I'd like to see more job types like vehicle recovery and rescue, scavenging focus with high risk high reward, and market and product type specialization like fuel redistribution. For the heavier developmental loads... facility, vehicle and trailer ownership. That could couple into purchasing depots to open trade lanes and create passive income.Thanks devs. A good purchase. _childDocuments_.review: Someone put an asteroid in my engine block!Game is great, people complaining about controls, and not being able to rebind controls, while it would be nice, and im sure the devs will add them in in a future update, the controls feel fine after some time to adjust to them. The game is very playable, the weight and motions of your rig/freight matter, and coming from 6yrs of truck driving experience, its honestly more accurate to real truck driving than most other truck driving sims.Would be nice to have more music as you play for about a hour and you hear all of the same songs on loop at least twice. But its a easy fix to just turn off the radio and turn on your own playlist.A bit more explanation about truck controls besides the absolute basics would be good, as it took me a number of deliveries to finally look down and see the console commands near the bottom of the dash like light controls, cruise control, etc. Around that same time I also discovered you can change your tablet display screens for different information and camera views.However the game DOES encourage you to read the truck owner manual in your cab which has all this info in it, it would just be nice to have that info fed to you visually in the tutorial delivery, overall though this is a small gripe and one easily remedied by reading the book.The environments look great, the atmosphere is very good, being able to climb out of the chair and walk around your cab, organize things, or go out and patch up the rig feels great. people who have played Hardspace Shipbreaker will enjoy this game I think as graphically its very similar.The game feels like they took a truckers road trip across america and just put it all in space, its a fun feeling and gives me nostalgia to my driving days. Cant wait to play it more and find the hidden gems this game has tucked away.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been absolutely hooked on this game.  In a week, I've sunk 25 hours into truckin' around.The feel of the experience is great. _childDocuments_.review: I like a lot of games, but this is one that's going to be for the ages. It gives me great vibes, there's clearly a good foundation for amazing things. The atmosphere is gorgeous, the story is engaging, the sounds are *just right*, the controls really feel like you're driving a heavy vehicle. I love the interior of the cab, it makes it feel like you're actually living in there (well, it's a bit barren but that's just details that we might see changed in the future).If I were to change one single thing in the entire game, and I know it's going to be a little controversial, it's the damned battery management system. I know sometimes these mechanics can be fun, but no, I do not enjoy having to buy limited-supply batteries and stow them and swap them in the middle of a run just because game developers have no clue about how power management in actual systems work. It's gamified for the sake of being gamified, with absolutely no logic behind it. These cells are like if I had to swap AA batteries in my radio to make it work, and put some D batteries in a glove box compartment to get A/C in my car. More AA batteries in the break system too, obviously. Oh and imagine if rechargeable batteries weren't invented either, because of course, "recharging" isn't a concept that exists in this awesome space trucking future? This is almost a deal breaker for me, and I'm tempted to just skip the tutorial, and start a new game with low power/consumable drain. In fact I wish there was an option for *no* drain. I have a big generator in the rig - it's called a motor which I recharge using *fuel*. Using more power reduces fuel efficiency, it's that simple.*NEVERTHELESS* I still recommend this game to anyone that enjoys space games, travel games, truck sims and even just good old space exploration games. Just because I'm triggered by dumb battery systems doesn't mean you won't enjoy that challenge!

_childDocuments_.review: On my first job I ran into 8 pebbles and all 8 times I had to stop what I was doing, get out of the truck, and hold click on where the pebble hit.  I was looking for a euro truck in space where you actually get to drive your truck but no you just teleport places and then scoot along to the gold diamond while repairing 30 hull breaches. I just am unsure if the game directors were shooting their self in the foot for the fun or if someone in charge really thought people looking for a trucking game would want to, rather than drive the truck, repair the truck. Or make sure the truck is powered, or make sure the truck is this or that. I say the same thing every time a game fails to keep an audience. If you are going to make a game, every single aspect of it needs to do one of a few things. 1. Be fun (why *IN THE RECOMMENDED DIFFICULTY* am i stopping everything im doing because you wanted a gas leak mechanic)2. Reward the player (this is a must) (this game immediately filled my time playing it with remedial tasks that never felt rewarding.)3. Sense of direction (I cannot tell you how many games get this so game killingly wrong however this game did a great job at that)TL;DR This game shot itself in the foot. If you're looking for Eurotruck in space you will not find it here. This, in my little time playing it, felt more like a crisis management simulator with extra steps. If that sounds fun to you by all means go ahead the game ran just fine and looks good too.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me just start off with I love the premise of this game. 100%Anyone who has watched Cowboy Bebop has wanted to be able to space truck. It has those vibes 100%I started having fun playing this, did my first drop off, and thought wow, I'm gonna dump a lot of time on this.I still will, but after three different time of having to pay rescue because either my power cells were dying, all at the same time or having my oxygen some how depleting and I can't figure what why (battery and filter were fine) I can't play this as much as I wanted.I've seen a few people talk about the power cells and I totally agree. They have to be able to last longer, especially for how much they cost. Even adding in a recharging point would be great. I'd be ok if they could only be recharged a few times before you'd have to buy a new one. The controls are a little difficult but mostly manageable with a little frustration.Adding in the additional things you have to do to take care of the truck are great and should be in the game but don't make it so much that it takes away from being able to do the heart of the game, trucking through space.I really do like this game and I'm thankful that it was made. Maybe I just need to play around a little more and switch the difficulty level to try something else. This game will be awesome one day, it's just not there yet.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, I only bought the game because of the screenshots. I thought the idea of ​​trucks in space was totally silly and as an old Elite Dangerous trader I had to see it. And to get straight to the point, I like the game but there are two things I would like to mention.Firstly, you don't fly through a huge galaxy, you just make small jumps from sector to sector. Each of these sectors is unique and brings its own challenges to get your cargo safely to its destination. So far there is enough variety and you can find your way around the sectors more quickly.The second point has to do with the balance of the game. I can only recommend not playing on the standard difficulty, systems are constantly breaking and are extremely expensive to replace. If you want less hassle, you should start a custom game and reduce the energy consumption and the use of wear parts by a level, I had so much more fun with it.Oh and the soundtrack on the radio is absolutely great, it's a real shame that there are only so few songs.So I have to move on, the truck is calling"Keep on keepin' on"

_childDocuments_.review: This captures the sort of vibe you'd expect. You fly around, get cargo, make deliveries, and try not to hit anything expensive. Controls can be a little finicky, because the game tries to approximate the wide turn of a normal truck in three dimensions, which can make backing up into a less accessible delivery zone a nightmare, but so far the delivery times have been more than generous enough to take it slow and do it right.Almost everything outside of the basic speed and movement is done with an in-cabin switch or toggle, which adds a degree of minor difficulty as you have to take your eyes off the road to snag your Space CB Radio or turn on your Space Rear View Mirror Screen, but that just makes it feel more immersive and encourages you to slow down and do it right.If you play the demo and have fun, it's worth getting the real deal, all the more so if you remeber that one episode of Cowboy Bebop (yeah, you know the one). You get exactly what is advertised.There is one specific downside as of release: You cannot remap controls. It used fairly standard flight controls (wasd to aim, q/e to roll, space for speed up, shift for speed down), but some folks really need the ability to remap (my wife is one), and that makes the game inaccessible for them.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm playing on Mechanic mode which is one grade above "recommended". Things will break down more often and you'll have to work on repairs. Nice thing though is that you can tailor the aspects of the game that work for you with a custom difficulty level.I had to start over twice at this difficulty level before I started getting the hang of things. The game doesn't teach you everything you need to survive; especially at higher difficulty levels. Fortunately those failed runs were only a couple hours in... but I didn't feel like they were wasted. This game is fun. At this level I'm not making huge money and coasting through the game: there's quite a bit of challenge to make sure you're buying the right amount of spares, how many jumps you can make on what you have... and all versus the profit you can make on a job. Sometimes  you should take a lower-profit job if it's only a hop or two when you're low on supplies. Can't take the risk!Once you start unlocking new sectors, the game adds new elements to an already challenging sim.Plus there are the side missions with excellent voice acting for the NPCs. There's an amazing soundtrack... I hope more gets added to it over time. Graphics are great and the setting is really immersive.Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I REALLY wish i could recommend that game. I love the idea and aesthetic. I have I've played for around 7 hours on game pass and the gameplay aspect of driving through space is awesome. I wanted to actually buy the game on steam, but i kept getting more frustrated, postponed it and now decided against it. The thing that holds back the game immensely is the tediousness of maintenance. I started the game on recommended mid difficulty and after 2 hours and learning that batteries are disposable and you cant charge them, i started to look through in game options to lower difficulty. And well... you cant. You can only start the game over. In the skill tree I went to the left and maxed just-in-time jobs, where you have short window to deliver the goods after few hours. Well guess what, i was lucky with first few ones, and just driving there normally allowed me to be on time. But a third one, i was in the system 30 min early. I went to the bed in the truck and was astonished to find that there is no sleeping to forward time in this game. At this point you have to wait 30 minutes IRL with game on and unpaused to finish this job. Freaking unbelievable. I kept playing, getting more and more frustrated. I thought maybe as you progress story there will be QoL upgrades that make it all less tedious. But no. There is no progression like that. It's too frustrating to continue at this point, I'm dropping the game.And if any dev reads this and wants some feedback, here it is:The initial tediousness of maintenance is ok, for beginner greenhorn trucker. IMO game needs a separate skill tree for QoL (and 1+1=2 skill points on lvlup). In there should be upgrades for onboard workshop and charger for batteries, maybe where the second bed is now. As game progresses and you lvlup, this skill tree would allow you to clean filters and repair UCCs to give them a second life, charger would allow you to charge 1 battery at a time, later upgrade to more, for increased fuel cost. Less important, but also cool options for that skill tree: remote job board connection, delivery drones for the shop, auto-docking.That's how I would see proper progression in this game. But for me to return to this game, the bare minimum, is to allow to change difficulty options mid game and sleeping in bed to pass time. Please devs, I dont see it mentioned on the roadmap at all, and its like a day of coding, if your code is not spaghetti.'This game is a rough diamond, still feels like early access. Hopefully the devs can get more people on board as they said in the post, and they'll help them realize what the priorities should be.

_childDocuments_.review: YES! AFTER 12 HOURS I CAN ABSOLUTELY SAY I LOVE THIS GAME! But it took a lot of trial and error.***Long story short: I set the contract payouts to [HIGH] and it alleviated most of my complaints for this game***Long story long: I had a hell of a time with this thing. I love flying haulers and space mining. This game is exactly what I was looking for in terms of concept, features, etc. But on the default settings, it's surprisingly punishing and the story missions actually make it HARDER (because they usually consume a lot of resources but don't necessarily pay you anything). It all comes down to economics: your truck/ship/thing (I will call it a "rig") runs on a combination of fuel, batteries, fuses and air filters. Your rig consumes all of these things and when any one of them runs out, you die. On the recommended settings, these items burn out comically fast. You will find yourself scrambling all over your rig swapping out consumables almost as much as you actually drive the damn thing. And it's fun! Until the money runs out. Then you die. And die and die. You can even fall into debt, which is as much fun as it sounds.When I hit that wall, I swallowed my pride and said "OK, well I guess I'm just not up to scratch yet. I will turn down the difficulty." But I couldn't. You literally have to start a new game to change difficulty settings. SO I STARTED ALL OVER, I lost over 5 hours of game play. There are custom settings that let you tweak the different features of the game and the solution seemed simple enough: tweak the rate at which consumables wear out. So that's what I did AND IT BROKE THE GAME.I like all the maintenance. I like taking the time to go over all the systems and equipment to ensure they'll get me through the next contract. I can't say this for certain, but I'm pretty sure that lowering the difficulty regarding consumables like batteries/fuses/filters just disables the need to replace them entirely. I played for hours and none of them seemed to wear down at all. The game went from sadistically difficult to boringly simple. So I had to start over again.I didn't want a survival/horror experience, nor did I want to do away with all the (fun!) maintenance features, what could I do? Finally, I took the easy way out and just multiplied the payouts for completing contracts because just like in real life, money solves everything! Now I can fret over my dwindling stock of fuses and merrily swap out dead batteries without feeling like I'm trapped in the same debt-slavery I have to live through in real life! The game is a great mix of slow burns through gorgeous space vistas and panic-stricken moments of oxygen deprivation.If any devs are reading this: please consider joystick/HOTAS support and let us re-map control inputs. And for heaven's sake include the cruise control in the tutorial mission, I was tapping space bar for hours before I discovered I didn't have to.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. The radio and the CB create a great atmosphere. I love maintaining the truck by changing batteries and patching hull breaches after I've crashed. Intra-system navigation can be confusing because jump gates get pinned, not the highway to get to it, but travelling is fun. There is traffic, but unlike terrestrial truck sims, getting stuck in it is a choice. You're in the endless void of space, after all. Flight is semi-realistic with some kind of flight assist on top of a newtonian model. That means you have to slow down for turns or over-turn your rig to drift it around corners. Be warned, though, drifting a tandem may get spicy.Make sure you're always carrying spare batteries and filters. Needing one of these and not having it could get you stranded or dead, and not every system has everything you need for sale. Important systems like the drive core and mag-lock use two batteries for redundancy. You can hotswap new batteries in as an old one expires. Unimportant systems like the suit charger, the gravity, and the very OXYGEN you breathe have no redundancy. You'll want to keep an eye on these and swap them while you're docked. You can change them as you like, but reorganizing your spares after replacing the grav-batt gets old. Worse, letting it die in transit will have your spares shifting around the cabin in accordance with your driving. Big stop? All your stuff now lives on the windshield.This is a great game to sit back and veg out with while singing along to the radio. "Cross my heart and hope to die. Oh forgive me, know I tried..."

_childDocuments_.review: It's out?! Oh come on!So I did a quick hour or so in this game and I will just start off by saying that I love it. That's the TLDR.If you do want to read my one hour play review, here goes.I love Euro Truck Simulator but the thing that breaks it for me is the fact that we're driving through Europe. In short we're driving through familiar territory but the game can't be too detailed so I couldn't, for example, drive my truck through my street. This game takes away that one small problem, by giving me a gorgeous galaxy to gape at, and gives me a dozen new problems to think about. For example, why am I freezing to death?!The idea that this cab is a spaceship is very well executed and I simply adore the problems which you can run into. Your power isn't one big battery supplying everything, there are small batteries for all manner of systems. So what do I run out of first? Artificial gravity. While I was flying at speed. With my shelves full. I had to spend a good fifteen minutes cleaning up everything that had been flung through my cab, meaning I missed the delivery deadline.See that doesn't happen on Earth and a normal wheeled truck!There are 4 standard difficulties and a fifth which gives you the option to fine tune anything you want. It's a nice addition to those who want to go off into the distance or want a lawless, or fineless, galaxy. The soundtrack I had thought would grate on me, not my usual style, but it's actually really nice to listen to and fits with the aesthetic. First thing I do is turn on the radio every time. I am looking forward to more commercials too; they are nicely weird which is perfect for the 'space is huge so there's probably somewhere we can make something sketchy' mindset of businesses. There is an RP element for me personally, just the under the breath grumblings when I'm carrying stuff, that make it more fun for me. Yes, I'm weird, don't judge me.The downsides? And please keep in mind this is after 1 hour of play so who knows if this comes up later.However, like I said, I enjoy adding an RP element to these kinds of games but the game itself doesn't lend itself well to that. The cab has a bed, you can't sleep in it. There are food, drink and even cleaning consumables but they don't appear to have a 'use' function. If this is something which happens later in the game, or an option I have to turn on, I'll amend that here. If it's not in the game, I sorely hope they do add it in. I'd also like to see a custom music option. Again, I love the soundtrack, wouldn't have bought the DLC if I didn't, but I enjoy putting on an audiobook and playing these kinds of 'work' games and it'd be nice to have that be a function in game rather than what I open on a second screen.Seriously, to anyone out there, buy the game now or later; it's a good price for a good game with its own weird aesthetic and we need more of them. Safe travels!

_childDocuments_.review: The feeling of managing and keeping your flakey rust-bucket of a ship flying is fantastic, if that's your kinda thing. Razor-thin margins and a gravity generator that drinks energy like soup keeps your wallet twitching and your buttocks clenched. Where one solid collision is enough to spiral you into the abyss, and a ship handles like a drunk Italian bistro, this is certainly not a game for everyone.But I bloody love it. Some early tips I wish I'd known at the start - - Explore your ship before you even start the engine, and when you can - read the manual in the glove compartment. Make a note of where everything is, what it does, and what parts it uses so that when things (inevitably) go wrong, you at least know where to look.- Highways seem optional, but they mark safe paths with no debris/junk floating around. Use them whenever possible (unless you feel reckless, or are in a really big hurry - trust me though, debris fields are deadly). If there's no highways, watch/follow the other rigs - they tend to follow fairly safe paths. - Batteries are expensive, but pay attention to the capacity - 100 cap batteries aren't too bad (around 400-500 credits). The more expensive ones are bigger, 150 and 200. Also, ALWAYS turn off your cab interior lights when driving - this saves so much energy! The gravity generator is the biggest drain, so give it the big batteries if possible to save frequent stops.- The storage boxes you have in your sleeping area are ESSENTIAL. Open them, and store your batteries, UCCs (little computer things used alongside batteries in your systems) and filters in there, as they will keep them from being damaged from accidents. The boxes hold several items each, so fill them up to keep your expensive spares safe.Fly safe! :D

_childDocuments_.review: this game really rocks. it's so much more intense and involved than i figured it would be. i can see myself spending tons of time in star truckera few notes, including two major gameplay issues that i hope can be patched and/or fixed:1. the biggest problem imo: the lack of vertical/lateral thrust. it would make things so much less of a pain if you could just scooch up or down if you need to, especially for docking but also for avoiding debris. the controller configuration could let you do it either with the d-pad, or the d-pad with a "shift" button (say, hold down LB and use dpad to thrust). the only two things the dpad currently does, zooming and external camera, could easily be moved to the left and right stick buttons or the shoulder buttons. (side note, i would also love to have the cruise control mapped to a shoulder button or Y/Triangle, like the cruise control buttons on the steering wheel of your car you already have your hands on)2. power cells deplete WAY too fast. it is such a hassle to constantly be swapping out and selling old cells, and constantly losing a lot of money buying new cells. if the game let you try the different difficulty modes on the same save i'd be happy to do that, but it doesn't, and at this point i don't want to start a whole new game just for the chance that power drain would be a bit lessened. if there is a way to either recharge power cells (yes please) or make your electricity use more efficient with upgrades, i have not yet found it. 2A: the game is set in (at least close to) real-time except for when you use jump gates, so they really wanted us to literally have to change the power cells more than one time every single day?2B: now that i'm thinking about it, it doesn't make sense that the gasoline doesn't recharge the power cells like it would keep a car battery charged. i understand it's a game mechanic, but are big rig truckers having to pull out batteries for individual components for their rig and replacing them on the regular? like more than once a day?3. the solar flare mechanic absolutely rules. i figured the separate temp/fan a/c controls were just a cute little thing, but no, they are very very important! i cant wait to see electrical storms and whatever "anomalies" are!4. I can't place items down on the floor without damaging them. People are saying to just use the crates, but that takes longer to do than just putting an old power cell on the floor while i'm changing it. Give me a crouch button, or make the fall damage on items trigger a little bit further away!i'm nitpicking because i really REALLY like this game and am going to spend tons of time in it. it's so kinetic and detailed, and the lever you have to push to jump to new systems feels very great every time. the ability the game has to simulate this seamless world where you can get out of your ship with no loading screens (even when jumping between systems) to pick stuff up and repair your ship must be a technical marvel considering how many space games can't figure that part out. starfield, eat your heart out - star trucker did it right!!!edit: the radio station! the effort that went into making this radio station including advertisements and station ID clips and (what i'm assuming are) original songs!!! incredible!!! my friend and i created an 8 hour long "space trucker" playlist for when we would haul stuff in elite dangerous, and it's a fantastic fit here too.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I don't think this game is necessarily bad. It's more of a case of "not my cup of tea" with a pinch of "my expectations were wrong". But Steam ask me "Do you recommend this game?" and the most honest answer I can give is "no".So what happened?In Star Trucker, the player takes on the role of... Well, a star trucker. You drive a space truck that looks a lot like your regular trucks from Earth and deliver cargo across the galaxy. Cool concept, right? As a fan of the Truck Simulator and MudRunner series, I was really looking forward to the release. I love the meditative gameplay that usually comes with these types of games, and the sci-fi space setting definitely seemed like a welcome addition.But here's the thing: this is not your average meditative truck driving game where you can peacefully drive many miles down the road. The “roads” here are quite short actually, and large cosmic distances are covered in seconds with the help of gates that are located in each system. So you don't travel for long. Instead, most of the time you're dealing with the complexities of moving and docking in 3D space, as well as maintaining your truck. And although the gameplay is competent, it is not particularly exciting and sometimes even annoying.There is a story/campaign of sorts with characters and radio conversations, which is a welcome addition - games of this type don't usually bother with that. But it wasn't interesting or exciting enough to make me stay in the game longer.So while the Star Trucker concept is fun and the game overall is well made, I unfortunately didn't find it interesting enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Very weak game so far.1. Controls to drive your truck are pretty annoying2. There is no sector map3. Having to dock the truck to pick up a job or shop is a contrived game mechanic, and it feels stupid. 4. I can understand having to dock to pickup inventory, or a drone can fly it to you. However the real issue is wasting time docking with a shop and it doesn't have a single power cell. This is just idiotic game design.5. There are no radio controls that I can find other than off/on. So 1 station and no volume controls.6. There are insane amounts of space debris everywhere, like right next space stations and roads. This is another contrived game mechanic. I understand the need for some risk/reward mechanics in the game but this is outlandishly stupid, everyone in the sector\town would be dead with that much debris floating around.7. The space highways within a sector are basically pointless, too narrow, since there is no sector map you can't really tell where they go or make use of them. From a design perspective they don't even make any sense. There is no divider for the "lanes".8. From what I can tell so far there are only space trucks flying around. There are no passenger vehicles, apparently only truckers exist in this universe.

_childDocuments_.review: As a big ETS2 and space-games fan, I had big hopes for this, but ended being a disappointment. The game has some good points, like:- the atmosphere- visuals- decent music- truck upgrades (that I found by luck when I ran out of oxygen)But that comes with a lot of cons:- Your truck running out of resources very quickly (basically the power cells that power up systems like oxygen, gravity, temperature) make the game feel more like a survival than a chill hauling simulator, and I was playing on 'recommended' settings, so I guess this is intended. You also can't disable this in the 'custom' game mode, just lower the rate they are consumed.- not being able to recharge power cells is very bad, making the point above even worse- you need to dock to do everything, even to get a job - we have warp gates but dont have wireless?- controls are... incomplete. you can roll on forward axis, move forward and back, and also roll on lateral axis, but you can't strafe left or right, or up and down, making dock and aligning on warp gates very hard and annoying- the guy from the 'campaign' talks to you and you need to answer by going in the internal camera, getting the radio talker, holding right click and then choosing an option as an answer. But the distance between things on each system is very small, so if you are at medium-high speed and want to answer, then you need to full stop so you dont crash- also on distance, we dont have that 'road feeling' that we have on ETS2, like taking a super far job and taking literally 2 RL hours to deliver. Every job is just a 5 minutes in each system until you reach each warp gate, then you make 2 or 3 jumps like this and it's over.- in each system you dont know where anything is (like a shop to buy a very expensive power cell), so you need to guess and try to get close to something and hopefully is what you're looking forAnyway, these design choices make the game what it is, maybe you'll like it, but I didn't because I was expecting a more relaxing experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super fun. Great graphics, music, and sound. The space trucks are simulated using full inertia so you can prepare for stopping or a turn when parking or manoeuvring. Inside the truck you have racks for storage, compartments for batteries and PCB boards, and you can buy storage containers to put all your spare parts in. The simulation of truck systems is simple and fun but you do have to watch your battery levels and change them out for new ones before they expire. There are plenty of cockpit controls to play around with in the truck. You have CCTV from different vantage points to make reversing easier. If you do run out of oxygen you can quickly put on your space suit until you get to a shop to buy more parts and you can perform EVA's to repair leaks on the external parts of the space truck.There is a story and at various points you can speak to other truckers on the CB radio but the progression seems to be locked to how many miles you have travelled. Overall the game is awesome and if you want a chilled out ATS experience but in space I can definitely recommend Star Trucker!
