_childDocuments_.review: In general... original idea with great execution. Unlike certain truck game, we've got a fully interactive dashboard :) I also like the fact that there is a story line. Early game is constant struggle for cash. Batteries seems expensive, not much good paying jobs. Low hull resistance to damage and the fact that you have to learn how to control the truck means you're going to hit some rocks (or stations... or other trucks...) and damage the vehicle. At this stage it is quite expensive to fix it. And just when you think you solved all your problems, an icon flashes on the dashboard informing you that the air filters need replacement. Back on square 1 (they are really expensive). Don't get me wrong!  This is actually an awesome challenge for otherwise boring gameplay loop of... just flying through space.Mid game, in my opinion, starts when you unlock new territories, enabling you access to long hauls, so you start to make a bit more money, allowing you to buy enough backup batteries and air filters. Time to start enjoying story line. Nice change of gameplay loop.Now... it all falls apart a bit in the end game. Once you get a... certain truck upgrade, there is no more incentive for actually hauling anything.  Once you're near the end of the story line, it becomes a main/only point of focus.Nevertheless, I enjoyed the game enough to recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is set in 3-D space, but only has 2-D controls. There are no translation controls at all so "driving" and docking in this came is impossible. The camera views are super clunky and it's pointless to use the exterior cameras because you will be constantly hitting space debris or other vehicles you didn't see. Also, if you want to sit in the cab and use the monitors, they are this ugly green color for the camera views. I get it for the status screens, but why would you want to make a beautiful game look so ugly. Also what are the point of the "roads" if the other trucks don't use them or if you are mandated to go off-road at times. Lastly the normal mode is more hardcore survival. You will be constantly replacing batteries, filters, and UCCs. The jobs don't even come close to making up for it and you will constantly feel like you are in the hole. Why in the world do the I need to get gas and also get batteries for systems I feel like should be charged by the engine when I'm driving. Lastly for the love of god, please change the gravity mechanic. Even if I am completely stopped to change the battery before it goes dead, all my stuff goes floating off anyways. I never encountered any bugs, but this game feels like an early access title that slapped a 1.0 release on it to make money. It's missing too many features like keybinds, Give this game a wait. There is soooo much potential, but the game in it's current state falls flat.

_childDocuments_.review: So... I've now put 20 hours into the game and I'm very happy with what I'm experiencing so far.I have to say that I immediately skipped the 'recommended' difficulty and went for the 'trucking' difficulty. I'm an ETS2 player, so that seemed to me the most similar, as far as that's possible of course.The game looks beautiful, steering is sometimes a bit tricky, but that's not surprising... you're in space after all.The idea is fantastic, and I really fell in love with the minimal management of the truck (also a reason to choose this difficulty).I also think the buying and selling of the items is a very nice idea, also with the contraband. Well thought out!You can make the game as fun and difficult as you want.Remember, it's really an early stage at the time of writing.Hopefully there will be updates soon so that more people can enjoy this game even more!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice atmosphere, and great decision to include "space legs" gameplay. Standing up, walking around, and interacting with the truck's cabin is such a great feeling, especially seeing as it's tied into the maintenance and upkeep of the vehicle, and not just walking around for the sake of it.The omission of keybindings is odd, but I find the default layout decent (if a little unorthodox). Granted, the gameplay could massively benefit from HOTAS support. Maybe one day devs? Please?So far so great. Looking forward to see what the devs implement based on the feedback :)
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a very fun game. I actually like how you must maintain your truck with replacement parts, but I do fine certain parts annoying. The game play loop and feel of the game is good. The controls are fine and manageable. If you like trucking games, you will enjoy this as long as youre not expecting nothing but driving like ATS/ETS. I have more pros than cons with Star Trucker and I highly recommend it. I just have some suggestions for QOL. - Not having any way to recharge batteries is quite a pain. I feel like I run through them constantly and early game its impossible to afford the better capacity ones. I would very much appreciate having atleast one shop in each sector to swap/recharge batteries if not a truck addition. -There's no map for specific areas. You have the overall map with icons showing you what type of shops are located there, but not their actual location. Spending fuel flying around huge systems with debris everywhere looking for a shop is just frustrating. We should atleast have hud icons for each specific shop. There is several on the HUD already, but it can cover up what you're actually looking for. Maybe even a icon highlighter?-Air filters are insanely expensive early game and you have 4 of them. Even buying them when the price is good is still going to bankrupt you if they all go out at the same time. They do have a decent durability which is good, but I just wish you had two filter slots instead of four.-I can buy large containers of food for a few hundred, but drinks only come in small jugs and 6 packs? Yeah they're cheap, but making 3 or 4 dollars off of them a piece is nothing and I dont have enough space for crates to shove 100 of them into to make anything worth while. Kegs/packs of drinks would be a nice change-Currently the meta to hauling things in secure crates is sticking them on shelves and opening them so they cant fall off (Assuming you have your gravity turned off or the power is just dead). It would be nice to have a strap/rope/gate to hold containers in place.Edit: I just unlocked the Solar area and I have to say, I really dislike it. The idea is really cool, but being forced to shutter my windshield and using a camera that barely even functions during flares is just painful. I just can't see anything and I'm forced to just stop what I'm doing right then and there. Being forced to use the camera is fine, but please make it less glitchy. I get it, its a solar flare. For the sake of gameplay, please :'(
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: It's a solid space trucking game with survival aspects that does everything correctly but doesn't give You a massive wow that's amazing effect however it does deliver a good blend of trucking and survival. That's something new and unique on the current market if You're into trucking games.The game is fun to play, depending on the difficulty settings You can just chill and cruise through space with your cargo or constantly check all your systems, batteries and fix stuff as it goes wrong. Everyone will find the balance they enjoy in this game. There's a simple and easy to learn system for storage and replacing all the components as we haul cargo in space.Graphics look good, there's a variety of sectors offering different environments, some are friendly and some are dangerous. It's not always smooth sailing through space.There's only one truck in the game but there's enough customisation for it to keep the experience fun and rewarding especially when it comes to paint jobs. To get them You have to complete achievements that unlock them. My only complaint is that there isn't that much driving in the game. You can drive withing the sector, go fuel up, check out what's in the store or go pick up a job but You can't drive between sectors. You go to warp gates and they teleport You between sectors. You will do a few miles, then teleport and repeat. It makes sense considering we are in space travelling between different planets.Overall for the price it's a solid space trucking survival game that's worth the money. Grab it and enjoy your space trucking adventure. Space cowboy over and out.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Space Trucker Simulator with some caveats. If the reason you're here to play this game is to chill out with a cup of coffee or a beer and slowly meandre your way from point A to point B while listening to a radio, a podcast, or just unwind from a long week at work, then you'll want the easiest difficulty option. Managing your battery levels otherwise is so tedious and stressful that is seriously detracts from the enjoyment of the game for people like me. Luckily, you can adjust any aspect of difficulty from the menu, customizing your experience to exactly how you'd like to play the game. I just wish I knew how to back a trailer into a space in Zero-G.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing (and getting bored) of American Truck Simulator, this game is a great refresher to the trucking genre.  Not only is it beautiful, it is innovative.  I can walk around the inside of my truck, I can turn off the lights in different parts of my truck, hell I can go outside into space and fix my truck.  There is a lot to work towards in the game right now but I do wish for more new content in the future.  Maybe a way to personalize your truck's interior, more types of playable cabs, or someway to make a convoy with your friends.  I can't wait to see what the future holds for this hidden gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I'll say this up front - If you're looking for a game that's Euro/American Truck Simulator, but in space, you may be disappointed in Star Trucker. That being said, for the game that this is, it's a lot of fun.There is a pretty steep learning curve off the bat - Driving in a 3 dimensional space is certainly a different beast than on a road. I'm looking forward to joystick support and plan to 100% the game when that becomes available. I have completed the story, but find myself still wanting to truck on.The development team has been very active and responsive to user feedback, and many of the changes that are in place have been directly in reaction to player feedback. There is a ton of customization that you can do to fit your gameplay style. I play with the default settings, and found that the original power drain and damage settings didn't cause me a lot of trouble, but many did, and the development team responded and made it a bit more forgiving. This was in direct response to the feedback they received. I look forward to future updates and hope to see expansions to the world in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Huzzah! While you mainly go from hub to hub - the game is a lot of fun. Takes a minute to get used to the maintenance things, but if you really want to, you can turn that part off ( from what I seen folks say. Haven't tried turning off myself) and just cruise. I would strongly suggest this game for it's theme of space trucking.. just best bought when on sale. Otherwise, a nice and chill game to turn off your brain and immerse.

_childDocuments_.review: I've always admired American Truck Simulator and its European counterpart, but I've never wanted to get into it since my love for driving in real life has always been plagued by other drivers, and I felt it would translate into the game. _childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: So far im really enjoying the game. Its not a long distance driving sim by any means, but it captures the feeling of driving a truck in zero G pretty well. The controls, despite what many are saying, really arent bad and I think the lack of key mapping was intentional to simulate driving. After all there has to be some level of challenge. Its a very relaxing game. I do wish there was a little....more. Maybe let us stop by a space diner, or decorate the cabin with posters. Just something to spruce it up. Either way, its pretty cool and Ill probably sink way too many hours into it.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trucker delivers what I wanted in each truck games and space games :- The ability to walk in the truck/space ship and get out of it, in FPS view.- Many systems to manage and which can break.- Neat fuel and energy management.- Fully interactive cockpit and multiple cameras with monitors, allowing to play only in FPS view.I also love the fact that you really place the items in the storage boxes (it's not a window in the UI like most of the games).The docking procedure is also pretty fun in FPS view.My only grip for now is that the game is very hard to play if we remove the hud markers, as there is no detailled map.I would love to see, in a DLC, a more deep trailer management, with the need to manually organise and strap up containers/box on open trailers and with some risks to lose our cargo (could we have a space forklift ? :) )
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: super fun game, arguably one of the best this year, the soundtrack is a MUST HAVE too. great style too, very unique and defining.if you like driving sims, open world games, or space games, but want something that's not racing and instead doing hauling and story missions, pick this up. totally worth it, especially on sale. it's kinda simple on the surface, but still really fun and really enjoyable and a great game to chill on if you're comfortable with space navigation, but it gets more complex due to the hazard system and the maintaining of certain systems on your rig. if you want a challenge, turn off the driving assist to up the difficulty and make it a true sim experience. turns things up a notch. that said, here's some key points that make this a great game:1: full 6dof, turns difficulty up a ton2: customizable difficulty with 5 options making it very fun for anyone3: solid gameplay loop with some great story rolled in4: chill and relaxing and once you get established it gets really really fun to play for hours on end5: AWESOME SOUNDTRACKgame also runs fine on Linux Mint 22, i recommend fullscreen windowed (full screen exclusive has an alt+tab allergy) and using Proton 9 as with Proton Experimental you get less frames. that said the game could definitely use some optimization to boost framerates in the first placemy only criticisms are as follows:1: it's not entirely optimized and suffers from pretty low frames, lower than i'd expect.2: the driving manual needs improvement because some of the ways the game seems to calculate things like careful driving are a bit wonky and not entirely clearly stated, only offhandedly mentioned in the mock contracts you accept in the job boards in game, and could use some clearing up in the driving manual in game as it's not explained what constitutes "good driving".
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: === EDIT ===Several patches in a the devs still haven't added custom keybind support, leaving the game literally unplayable for many people, especially left handed. The devs only hours after release promised that adding custom keybind support was their #1 priority... Clearly not, almost two months in.===========Fun time spender with some issues that gives it a thumbs down for me. First of all, I love space games, I'm a long time Star Citizen player, so this tickles what it does very well, which of course is cargo running. What really annoys me is the controls. This game needs options to reconfigure keybindings ASAP, as in, it should be in the next patch. The current keybindings are horrible and there is no strafe option, in space with thrusters. Also no mouse steering option with a button for free look.Next thing I noticed actually just made me Alt-F4. You can get fined for crashing into other vehicles, this is fine. I got fined over $1000 because some vehicles follow a very strict path and will not move away from it. I was barely moving forward and due to the lack of strafing I couldn’t get out of the way of a small yellow service vehicle. It crashed into me, not the other way around, and because of its strict pathing it got stuck in me, because it got stuck in me the game would consider this as an ongoing violation and fine me with $100 every 10 seconds. I had to start spinning to get the vehicle back on its pathing and stop driving into me.At least add keybinding options and strafing into the game and this will be a thumbs up.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay Review: The 'loop' is taking various hauling contracts dictated by your skill tree choices to earn money. Money is spent on part supplies or consumer goods you store in the cabin to make use of the buy low/sell high state of various locations. Example; antidepressants bought low at a store can be placed in your cabin to be sold for a higher price elsewhere and this is separate from your hauling contracts.  During or between hauling power, fuses, and air filters will degrade requiring manual replacement.Personal Thoughts:A lot of fun! The system management has just the right amount of manual and sci-fi technowizardry cheese and there can be some rather hilarious circumstances like realizing too late that your gravity is about to lose power then spending a frantic few moments trying to turn it back on only to then discover that objects in your cabin have durability they lose when they come crashing into each other or the floor when the gravity is restored, lol. To help this you can buy boxes to store a good amount of stuff and protect them.I would almost say it is a cozy game if it wasn't for the sudden difficulty spike for the unprepared and the lazy players who 'brick' their game state by only trying to replace things last minute and find themselves in a location with none of the parts they need. With generous manual save slots and an auto-save every time you jump the only one to blame is really themselves.Note: 43% of people have the achievement for traveling 100 miles in the game. Keep that in mind when you look at the negative reviews. The gameplay video in Steam really does a decent job showcasing things and if you really still aren't sure just watch some gameplay on YouTube. It is a really straight forward like it or hate it decision.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

This game has so much potential, so much it can grow, and I really hope it does.If you are on the fence about buying it, do yourself a favor and do it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not just Euro truck sim in space, it actually has voice acted characters, a nice little story, custom made music (that fuсks, btw) and the gameplay itself is pretty good (although it is just about hauling loads, don't expect much more than that).It doesn't have configurable controls, but it's not that big a deal, since the entirety of controls is WASD, shift and space to control the truck and you use the mouse for everything else.

And you cant edit any controls besides invert some axis.It seems like it was designed for controller and i am keyboard player.i do enjoy that you need to actually click buttons and pull levers in the cockpit itself instead of just pressing hotkeys for everything. so i need the mouse to look around - alot. playing with a controller is not feasible for me. but the controlls of the truck are just annoying. not intuitive (for me). it happened so often that i accidentally decellerated and reversed crashing into stuff. or that i was accelerating instead of pitching my truck upwards.Also, managing your modules and parts is part of the fun, however it becomes tidiuos very quick. batty drainage of your gravity generator is insane, changing the battery is not fun and you cant turn it off because ou cant strap down your cargo and with out gravtity it just floats in your cabin getting damaged very, very easily reducing its value.The killing point for me was that the emp protection thingies where destroyed hald way through a boring main quest in the very first area where you need the emp protection and as a result my entire truck got damaged.

_childDocuments_.review: It is with a heavy heart that I give this a thumbs down. It's a super charming game with all the tell-tale signs of a really passionate team... but no battery charger?!?! That's outrageous. I didn't even make it 2 hours into the game and I had replaced 5 batteries! I AM FLYING A ROCKET FFS, I CAN SPARE SOME ENERGY TO CHARGE A POWERCELL.Apparently it gets worse with air filters too costing some crazy price like $3000?Disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: It starts as a fun enough game but small issues start to grate as you play it more. The space truck is really poorly designed inside from a usability perspective, making maintenance more of a chore than it need to be. Whilst piloting half of your view it taken up by the hood because the design values cosplaying as terrestrial  truck over a practical design for traversing space.Controls cannot be rebound either.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I've played this year, very immersive with a lot of content, slow but very fun progression, it's not for casuals (even though there's a casual mode) if you want to play as intended, there are some challenges you don't just sit on your ass for 5 hours like ETS, you're a space trucker not a truck.Warning: if you're not too smart you won't be able to handle the battery management, I'm not gonna tell you what IQ you need but it's NOT like ETS, you upgrade your truck and these upgrades actually help with the management (part of the progression) so yes it gets easier later on so my advice is to play on recommended and not change anything.If you put the consumption to low in settings you won't have to change anything for hours, it's way too low imo, it gets boring real quick, but slow-witted players might enjoy this.Controls are also very intuitive, keybinding isn't necessary unless you have physical issues maybe, don't be discourage by these reviews.Same for truck behavior I can back up in the mag lock in a few seconds now, clearly these people are bad drivers in real life, the truck reacts to your action through the camera which is obviously reversed, it's good for your brain.Can't wait to see what the devs bring later on, the potential for this game is huge, as long as they don't dumb down this game for casuals coming from ETS/ATS.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Very Fun, just wish there were more story missions. Those are very entertaining. More of those awesome songs would be cool too, as there aren't enough to keep it from being repetitive.The people complaining make me laugh. THIS MISSION IS BUGGED, I HAVE TO LEAVE AND COME BACK TO GET IT TO UPDATE...no maroon, that's called JUST IN TIME, you chose that job. JiT manufacturing is a real thing and you CANNOT get there too early. It isn't a bug.BooHoo. You cannot link multiple trailers (which is a game choice I don't agree with but it is what it is) but you can accept 3 loads...boohoo it's broken...again, no. In system A you take a load offer that picks up in system C, you also take a load that goes from system A to B. So you deliver to B, jump to C to pickup and return to A. This isn't broken, it's called TRUCKING. If you get lucky with the RNG you can string 3 of them. That's called route planning, which is what dispatchers (or OwnerOps) do every day.Leaving negative reviews when you are clueless is toxic. It's a great fun little (as in not long enough) way to waste time
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. I replayed the demo for hours waiting for this. So far it's exactly what they made it out to be. Some are saying the gameplay is repetitive...it's a trucking game. It's ATS in space. Do with that what you will

_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a beautiful mixture of part No Mans Sky and Euro Truck Simulator 2, both of my favorite games. So far, i am enjoying this game and would recommend this to the people who are space game lovers, though I have my fair share of Feedbacks. What I love about this game:1. Good implementation of space environment with truck hauling simulation.2. Graphics are awesome, as expected and better for an indie game.3. Good country music and radio implementation that they have integrated along with ambient music.4. simplistic controls and not steep learning curve as of now.5. Space game (which is always a plus).What can be improved:1. Multiple save slots instead of 3 save slots present at the moment (which is very stressful if i want to fall back to a particular checkpoint while cargo job.)2. Though the variety of cargo jobs are good, they can add a little more categories to the cargo job types and also add variety in the same category of cargo jobs (example - all oversized cargo jobs needn't need to be same point A - point B, just a little variety)3. More list of music as the existing one gets repetitive pretty.4. Game is not optimized at all. More optimization is needed. For GTX 1060, it shouldn't be running in 30-45 fps at medium settings.5. More bigger map area along with more things to do in the selected sector (individual sectors feel small and a tiny bit empty IMO).6. More quests and a longer storyline if possible.7. If any little bit of community interaction is possible like in No Mans Sky.will edit the review as and when the game expands in future.

_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: The game is what it is. If you saw the trailers you already know what to expect. Hat down to the small developer team behind the game, the execution is very well done and I enjoy playing.I have only three comments:1) On my first fragile cargo mission NPC started talking to me using radio. So I have stopped the truck and talked with him. NPC track hit me like 20 seconds later and destroyed my cargo completely. Lesson learned but NPC trucks have no collision detection? Either way less talking and more driving. ;-)2) Control schemes. I would love to play the game less like a truck driving and more like a space ship flying. Using mouse for directing the ship and W and S for throttling. Two hours in and I can somehow fly but for someone that has spend thousands of hours playing spaceship games, its not intuitive or very enjoyable.3) I play the game to relax and drive. Yet Im running low on money by simply buying batteries and fuel. Some shops sell like 1 battery, 1 shop I saw had 4. At least at the start of the game I would say no one sane would choose business career like this... :-) If my trips barely cover my basic spendings its not ideal. I didnt hit a single obstacle apart from the fragile cargo being destroyed by the NPC truck, all other trips were with bonuses. Maybe it will change once I get later into game, too early to say really. Just something that struck me as strange for the first few missions.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever wondered what would happen if you slapped rocket engines on a big rig?Here's your answerTake control of a space truck and haul freight across multiple regions of civilised spaceBe sure to mind your driving as there are obstacles to avoid (debris, other trucks, asteroids)Upgrade your truck to expand into other regions (you will need shutters to deal with solar flares or capacitors to deal with space lightning)There is also a campaign of sorts working with some colourful characters that will help with unlocking the upgradesAn enjoyable game if you like driving where you can move in all three dimensionsAnd the devs are adding new features on a regular basis
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Why cant you pick up multiple jobs at the same time after you get the upgrade for multiple trailers?!? Lost a ton of money for failing a mission since this was not clearly stated anywhere that you could not do that. Also your not really trucking. You just jump from area to area and when you are "driving" its only in a small area to pick up or drop off your cargo while avoiding junk that is floating around.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Update: I've refunded after realizing it was included with GamePass. I have about 2 hours in it. It's very obvious the game was developed with controller players in mind because it's FAR better. Controls are smooth and intuitive, where as keyboard controls were made by people who have never played a PC game.Star Trucker has the potential to be a REALLY great game, hitting the niche of people that have always wanted to be a space trucker. That being said, there are some glaring issues I've noticed 20 minutes in.Likes:1. Unique art design.2. Fun truck physics.3. Pretty seamless intro/tutorial.4. Inventory management is fun. Organizing your gear into the back of your rig, having it get thrown around in a crash or float around if your gravity generator dies.Dislikes:1. No keybind editing?! Who makes Shift to brake and Space to accelerate? (developers are working on this now).2. No proper IR tracking support.3. No HOTAS support?!4. FOV slider does not go high enough. (There IS a FOV slider but it simply doesn't allow us to go wide enough).5. "Tech tree"/Certifications seems pretty basic. Other than getting better jobs, the ability to pull more trailers at once, nothing too exciting in the tree.6. Lack of animations that affect immersion. Example, when repairing your hull, your character should pull out some kind of blow torch.Another thing that blows my mind. You can't recharge your power cells?! We live in a universe where we can warp through space but we can't recharge batteries? Give us more to spend money on. Truck upgrades, new trucks, more cosmetics, etc rather than implementing a pointless annoying game mechanic to slow the gameplay loop.Just another example where they need to be taking inspiration from ETS/ATS. We need a career mode where we are trying to start, run and expand a trucking company. Gives us something to spend money on and significantly lengthens the gameplay loop.Long term this game would do extremely well if they implemented multiplayer similar to TruckersMP for ATS and ETS , private servers and the ability to talk to other driver's via the CB radio and full modding support. The biggest issue is that there are only 2 developers working on this game. This can be a thing fantastic due to attention of detail and love for the game but also be it's downfall if they burnout or do not have the technical skills to handle big implementations such as multiplayer.Will update as I continue playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly really liked the game and the concept of it. The graphics are pretty good as well. The three things that i wish this game had was 1. More character development or more iteration with the characters like running in to them randomly somewhere and at the way points that are given to you to go to have there rig there waiting on you I like not talking to Ghosts, and lastly I wish there was more to the game content wise, I understand that this is a new game and more content is hopefully on the way.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Been following this game for some time and wondered what it could actually become upon release. So far, I'm not disappointed. It's in a lot of ways like American Truck Sim which I love. I find myself being immersed with the side story missions which come across the CB radio. The voice acting is decent and there's a nice array of characters. The way you can organized what's being stored on your truck/ship is pretty cool too. Currently there's the silly way of keeping the lid of your cargo open to keep them in place on the shelves. I hope this is addressed and maybe they ad fasteners or something to counter this. My only issue with the game is the lack of survival I guess. Now, there's nothing in the description of the game that says it's a survival game, but since there's food and drinks that you can transport and even find as salvage floating out in space, I'd love to see them add some type of vital system where you had to eat and drink. It would be awesome to pull up to a Space McDonald's and order a space burger and a cosmic drink. Now, the music is amazing in this game. Sometimes you get the random ambient music while you're doing repairs to your truck while floating outside your truck and there's an actual radio that you can turn on and off. To sum everything up, I highly recommend this game if you're looking for a chill game to sink some hours into.

_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love it, so badly I want to love it.Rebinding keys is an insane thing to leave out of a game, I'm sure there's some technical reason it had to dodo, but the fact that I can't tell you why specifically makes it harder for me to understand - keybinding is standard. Not just from a quality of life standpoint, but general accessibility as a whole. The game-play loop is exactly what you expect, but some of the limitations (might be progression based so if this prickles your hair do some research) like only being able to haul one job at a time and not being able to "wait" or "sleep" to pass time makes some of the "arrive between" jobs downright BORING. The aesthetic of the truck is cool, but not worth the sacrifice of practicality. If there were any alternative system for avoiding debris (currently your choices are "squint" and "pray"), it would be closer to understandable. Having the choice of any other shape of vehicle would go such a long way, but this game is devoid of customization beyond colors and patterns. You get to choose how you level, as well as how you upgrade your truck, but to my knowledge none of that will keep rocks out of your radiator.Finally; once you're in debt, ya better break out the baby oil and start haulin' loads, cause delivering cargo ain't gonna get you back in the black ANY time soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game so far. I went into it worried about the 'keybindings bad' and 'power cells bad' reviews, but having sunk a few hours into it I can say neither are a real problem.The default keybindings are fine. There's nothing wildly abnormal, if you play Euro Truck, you'll be familiar with the core bindings already.The power cells also aren't really an issue if you're managing your power properly. Leaving your lights on 24/7? Have your A/C running on high all day? Constantly got your foot on the gas when you could be coasting on free momentum? You're going to burn through power cells. But if you're managing your power right, it's not a super big issue.Otherwise the game's v. chill, keeps you busy and thinking about optimizing your routes, and it's really satisfying to turn off flight assist and tokyo drift trailers into tight spots to hit that early-arrival bonus.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I've only been following this game for a couple of days, so I went into this game blind and without any hype built up.I really like the setting and the visual style. The atmosphere is also great and the vistas so far are also nice.I don't understand why other reviews get so upset about keybinds, as to me that is not an issue at all. The game is playable with controller just fine, and I suppose it was made with a controller in mind.The quest board and the various services do feel like ETS2, but of course it is impossible to create the feeling of traveling just like in ETS2 since one game takes place on earth and the other in space. So I don't understand those comparisons.. I so far quite like the game in and of itself.However, there are five key points I would like to see changed/that bother me:1. Unclear "road" beginnings/coursesWhen selecting a destination, you will get a marker for the jump gate needed to get to the next system en route. However, driving there directly ruins the immersion and is discouraged by debris fields. Sadly, though, it is not very clear where the road you are meant to take towards the jump gate is located or how you would get there from your current location.On the other side, occasionally when you leave a jump gate it is not clearly communicated which road you are meant to take to your destination point. So I ended up just driving straight there, which was not very fun imo as it is akin to just driving through fields on earth.2. Unrechargeable Fuel CellsIdk if it is simply not documented in the user guide book, but it seems like fuel cells are non rechargeable, which makes little sense to me. Batteries have been recharageable irl for decades and yet I am meant to sell empty fuel cells and buy new ones at great expense? Maybe I missed something, but it seems like the fuel cells are non rechargeable. Even if they are, it should be communicated more clearly where I can recharge.3. No vertical/lateral thrustEssentially, you are flying a space truck that can yaw left and right, thrust forward and backward and can tilt up and down. You can also roll, but that is not helping the thrust. Since you are very limited with your movements and docking is a very precise endeavour, it is frustrating to reverse your truck into the docking port. It would have been ten times more enjoyable if there was a way to thrust up and down and left and right directly instead of awkwardly pointing your truck upwards and then thrusting, then pointing it downwards again. There is a reason games like Elite Dangerous allow for thrust in all six directions as manoveuring around in space becomes super frustrating without it, even more so when you need to move precisely such as when coupling to trailers or when docking. It even makes following the roads unenjoyable, since you will often drift from left to right and up and down.Maybe you can upgrade your truck with additional thrusters? Idk. Let me know in the comments :-)4. Not being able to set waypoints within a system from the mapI would really have liked to be able to set a waypoint from the map to a specific shop in a system. As far as I can tell, that is not possible and you are left guessing where to go. Exploring a system does seem enticing in general, but due to the sluggish behaviour of a truck it is not really. I don't think I would like to drive a real life semi around for joy rides as an analogy.5. Small systemsI do have to agree with at least one review that mentioned that the systems feel rather small. So do the distances you travel. My fully fueled starter truck has a range of 93km? What? It makes sense in that you really only "travel" from jump gate to jump gate and those distances are rather small, but this game would have greatly benefitted from a "Wild West" feeling, where there are great distances between stations and jumpgates. Sure it can be tedious to some, but you are making a game for the crowd that enjoys ATS, ETS2 and space trucking in Elite Dangerous! Honestly when I saw that a mission was gonna take 2.5h I thought to myself: Alright! And in real time it took maybe 15 mins. I am the kind of person who will drive 1k kilometer routes in ETS2 because the sense of travel feels great!In this game you are like a delivery person within an industrial complex, you take stuff from a shelf in warehouse A, then take a car (travel gate) to warehouse B and then put it on a shelf there. The sense of distance is miniscule, which in my opinion really is what the whole point of this game should have been.Conclusion:All in all the setting is really enjoyable and I have only gotten started so far. There are very few good looking 3D space games out there and so this becomes a good game to me by merit of that and the premise of space trucking alone. It's like a fetish to me. Therefore I would recommend this game for now, however I am still on the fence. While writing this review the weight of the points I made really hit me. Again, a mixed review score would be great, but alas, I will for now give a thumbs up since I think I am going to play some more later today.

_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trucker is less about driving a truck through space and more about managing power. Maintenance is a huge aspect of this game, honestly it takes precedence over everything else. The power cells drain far too quickly and are far too expensive to be a passive element in the game, you're constantly focused on conserving power and stopping at shops to buy new ones. This will quickly take you away from the experience of actually driving the  a truck driving sim. (you can change the drain rate in the difficulty settings but it only mitigates it slightly. trading a squawking parrot for a mosquito buzzing in your ear)Imagine playing A/ETDS but the fuel drain is 5x faster and costs twice as much...All of this being said, every other aspect of the game deserves top marks. If you're buying this game as a driving sim you'll be disappointed as others have mentioned. Wait until they roll out some updates and fix some of the more oppressive aspects, then buy it. I'll update this review when they do some changes, but for now this game is a slogfest
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Has the game improved since alpha demo builds? Sure.Is there significantly more content now that the game is released? No.And that's the problem.It technically functions the same as Euro Truck Simulator but the detailed lively map is what makes a delivery sim great, and its non existent here.Sectors in the galaxy map which you warp through are small, undetailed and dead. There's not really much to do or see in them. And designated roads are utterly useless as you can just beeline to warp gates in and out of sectors. Few NPCs running around and they all drive the same trucks. No space police or authorities, no major consequences for actions. No new space trucks to buy. Few things to customize on your trucks. No homebase to buy and park your trucks in. Nothing to see, nothing to do, nothing to really work towards.Its an okay game but not worth base price. Expected way way more after the demo. This is basically an enhanced demo build.I'm quite disappointed in this game, waited a while for this.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Part trucking simulator, part power and time management simulator, Star Trucker is a genuinely fun and exciting foray into the world of interstellar cargo hauling. You get your own big rig, and you have to keep it stocked and maintained as you transport various cargoes around a network of star systems and quick stops.I enjoy flying the space roads, taking shortcuts through debris laden asteroid fields, and getting out of my truck to patch a hull breach every so often. The real gem about this game is the soundtrack. You'll feel like you belong among the stars while you listen to the custom songs written for this game, just well done all around.While there are still some bugs to work out, the game has only been out for a day, the potential of what this will become is just exciting, and I can't wait to see what the developers do next.See you in the space lanes, good buddy.10-10.System Details:Fedora 4064 GB DDR4 RAM2 TB SSDAMD Radeon RX 7600 8 GBSo yes, this game runs very well using Steam's Proton on Linux.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: It's as if an Elite: Dangerous space trucking meme took on a life of its own. It's not the greatest at anything but everything is done well which makes it hours of enjoyable space trucking fun. It is a higher quality than its price suggests and feels like a great value in a game. If you like space games, trucking games, or just hauling cargo and trading this game is for you. It even has a story straight out of a 70's trucker flick if one's interested and does a great job being immersive and environmental.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Nice chill space truckin'The game seems to use newtonian style physics for movement, so if you move in one direction, you need to apply thrust in another direction to turn. This can cause you to run wide on some turns if you're unaware. Your truck will gradually slow if you stop accelerating or reversing.Areas are completely open and you can decide on your path towards your destination. Will you stay on the marked highway, or risk a shortcut through that debris field to save time? Loads of potential for fast and risky trucking if you want to.As others also say, the ability to remap the controls would be nice and i don't kno why it wasn't included at launch.Overall an enjoyable game.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Space Trucking... wow!First: The game is DIFFICULT! If you put it on Normal or above you will have to balance being broke and having some money constantly, you are not going to just jump hoops and get rich instantly. This is not ETS in this way.Second: It is FUN! the game has very good controls both on controller and Keyboard. Sadly no HOTAS support from what I know, did not bother trying.LINUX: Works, beautifully under Proton Experimental and even on the Steam Deck, tho there the framerates are dancing around 30. So you might not enjoy it as much.Honestly I got bit by this loop, I was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ through the first like half an hour then my mind clicked into the 'grind' and I managed to keep my truck alive and floating, albeit looking like a rust bucket, but MY rust bucket. The game is insane fun, has moments of chill when you are flying down the highway, or just line up for a jump gate. And has those nail biting moments when you are 2 miles on fuel and have to float to the nearest station to refuel, or run out of batteries and scramble to stack up on more before you lose power in your cab.The learning curve is Steeeeep but damn it feels rewarding as I slowly start to grasp the game.I'd say jump in, try not to look up too many things on guides, and let the game immerse you into an experience of fighting for survival, or take it easy, kick the settings down through custom settings, and play as you'd like. Loving it, HUGE UP! looking for further updates, and perhaps more truck types down the line :3
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: For a game where hardly anything is present on screen (cartoony space graphics) it could run better, or provide more graphics customisation settings to better compromise on whatever is hogging the GPU. Same goes for keyboard binding customisation, mouse input lag, FOV adjustment option, etc.. The lack of all this makes up for a certain jankiness which gets in the way of me relaxing.The idea is good, but I'd say it needs to simmer for a little bit and wait for a couple of updates.My point of comparison is Hardspace: Shipbreakers - which achieves a very similar vibe, in a very similar environment, but somehow does it a lot smoother.

_childDocuments_.review: My suggestion is that you wait for the game to receive more updates before purchasing, and at the pace they're coming out, it might be another year before it's worth playing. The game has some pretty bad balance issues and missing features that make me think it was pushed out too soon. It could be great, but it's not right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: No vector thrusters, no Cargo in dock stabilization (if you hit it, it's gone). If you want a space trucking done good maybe try Elite Dangerous or Endless Sky (Less hassle with the loading, more capitalist Ca-ching)Or if you like to live the dangerous fringe life trafficking Drugs or Mechs, try Starsector.Either way, not great. Probably just stick to 2D trucking.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: It's buggy but expected for a newly released game. - The controls via keyboard are a bit clunky to me, and there isn't enough control of the needed systems via controller. For example, no way to dis/engage the mag-lock on the controller. I kind of get it, since they want you to be 'in' the cab, but when having to dock during an electrical storm with your cameras going haywire and you having to use the third-person camera, it get tricky flipping back and forth between the cab and third-person view.- The screens show you the power level of the batteries of the different systems but not the durability of  their ICCs. Wish we could see both instead of being surprised that our ICC shorted when all of your excess cab cargo comes flying into your way to block your view in a debris field because the grav system kicked out.- The AI is TERRIBLE! You can be parked and doing a space walk and the AI will barrel right into you instead of trying to avoid you.HOWEVER...- the visuals are beautiful. I love space-based games and its important to me that I 'feel' like I'm there.- It's a very relaxing game once you get the major systems upgraded to max. I don't have to haul anymore to maintain my rig, I can just cruise around and enjoy the views.- The cast of characters is entertaining.There's potential and I can't wait to see them open up more areas to explore.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game so far but if you're only looking for a relaxing driving game, play Jalopy instead cause this isn't that.Star Trucker's economy and ship maintenance can be brutal if you're just starting out, but thats also what makes it fun, You'll have to stock up on supplies, hunt for the best paying jobs (or just settle for the most convenient ones) and ration your fuel / energy as much as possible,With that said, the game does have a lot of small issues that make it more obtuse than it needs to be, just another thing to be prepared for.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Great work, Monsters. Driving a truck in this beautiful space with all that stations, 3D highways  and debris around you is very cool experience. And space walks are another very cool idea. In short,  I'm addicted........Someone should have said earlier that things disappear only from crates found in space. Now i have to buy new crates...
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, it is a bit tough on the recommended difficulty but I'm loving itHoping for more updates, theres a few fixes on the way (like contracts paying less than they should, which can lean into the difficulty)It is quite relaxed with memorable systems and interesting environmental hazardsI would love the ability to sleep in your bed to advance time, longer systems (they can feel a bit small) and re-chargable batteries, maybe mod support
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Is it an out-of-the-box superhit? Not quite.Does it still need some work? E.g. in regards to keybindings and maybe a bit of difficulty adjustment? YesHowever, starting a custom game and pushing the energy usage to a lower level made the game really enjoyable. Check after a trip whether your batteries are fine, replace them, sell them, buy them, trade goods, salvage... it's fun.My wishlist for changes:- Keybindings (e.g. to change the speed on cruise control)- A scanner (if it doesn't already exist) to mark debris in front of the vehicle- More music variety or ability to add a stream/custom music- AI that avoids running into you just a bit moreStar Trucker is a good game at this time, but I think it could be a fantastic game. Give it time!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: If you like space delivery stuff, this game is for you. I've played a lot of Elite Dangerous and ATS/ETS2, and this scratches that kind of itch very well. There's a lot more to it in terms of available side quest content than I expected, too. There's some complaints right now about the balance in terms of maintenance, but I haven't found that to be too bad (I like that kind of fiddly stuff), and you can also turn that down in the settings. It's also something the devs have said they are working on. As someone who loves these kind of games, it gets a definitely thumbs up from me. Very well done, especially from a really small developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Game is pretty fun they made improvements since the two demos they released. Controls are okay on controller I understand that we are in space but it does sometimes feel that turning left or right feels a bit loose. Would like to see more sectors added in post launch content and more banter from our cast of truckers characters it nice that they have them introduce you into the different systems of the game but it would awesome to hear them communicate with each other more often other then asking us could they do us a favor and deliver a load someone where. Overall I can recommend for folks that like the whole truck sim you can tell how passionate the devs are making this a reality. Look forward to see what they come up with for post launch content.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Great game!  I tried on recommended level and died twice fairly quickly.  Third time I did a custom game where I could change the settings.  Gave myself $25000, purchases were cheap, batteries and filters lasted longer, and damage was less severe.  No difficulties after that so I could learn the game.  Up to level 7 and I'm enjoying it.  Have put in 5k hours on ATS and ETS2, and Star Trucker isn't the same.  You are flying a space truck (freighter).  The is a spaceship flying game, not a truck driving game.  It reminds me of X4.  It's cool!

_childDocuments_.review: I sat watching the chronometer tick by in the darkened cabin.  It was becoming increasing difficult as my suit visor began to fog up.  Intermittent search lights from the station lit up the cab interior briefly.  A fuel canister gently collided with the pilot seat, the fluid inside sloshing hypnotically.  An air-filter spun lazily in the zero gravity. The shafts of light from the viewports making it appear to dance.  Another 5 minutes.  If I could just hang on for another five minutes, then the contact would ping the coordinates of my destination and I could get out of here.  The payout would be larger because I was on time but that was the problem really.  The job requred me to be in system by 19.53 and it was only 19.48.  The 'Just in Time' contract paid out nothing for arriving too early however.  Not usually a problem since I could finally get round to sorting the junk out in stowage and take inventory of my supplies.  Trouble is, my oxygen just ran out.  I could turn system life support back on and take off my suit but that would eat into my profits.  Or, I could find out what the real emergency limits of a second hand space suit were.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: overall I like the game and have played it pretty much everyday since bought it.  the variety of area's are nice and its a relaxing game most of the time. The bad is that there is definitely a balancing issue. The only thing that really affects the payout for a shipment is the number of jumps you need to make. so the only license that really matter are the long haul ones. even then it can be inconsistent. you could find a job to jump two systems and a job to jump five systems be the same payout or the two system job will payout more than the five jump job.The batteries have three tiers of capacity. buying the high tier battery is a waste of money as it is usually more that triple the price of the low tier one, but it only has double the capacity.you have two air filters you have to keep serviced. they last a hour at most and cost a jobs worth of money. you would think in space the filters and batteries would be  in supply at every store but are not. overall its a good game it just aggravating at times.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to be the first to leave a review lol but I ended up playing for the last 5 hours and now I must sleep. Anyway it's great! I agree with others that button mapping should have been there to start but it's not game breaking to not be. Also, not game breaking for me but having 6dof in suit but not in the truck with thrusters is kind of a bummer, up and down thrusting would make dodging debris a lot better as usually by the time I see a rock I've smashed into it at an angle. Anyway I played through the demo last year and I can say this has been one of my most anticipated games for this year and I'm still loving it. Can't wait to see what gets added as time goes on.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended difficulty should be easy or costum rather then normal. Normal is still incredibly punishing and hard for "normal"There are no key rebinds, even for a indie thats kinda lame since this is a industry norm on PCThe game uses 30-50% of my GPU and 20% of my CPU. Optimization is lackluster and its leaving huge amounts of performance on the table. I can run most indie games, especially Unity ones at 200-240fps, not below 60fps at times because it doesnt even use my computerThere have also been twice now, where I have jumped into a new star system from a gate and ended up losing all of my monetary savings. One time another truck spawned inside my cargo before I left the area. The other time I spawned inside of a asteroid that was blocking the exit gate. Would be nice if trucks didnt spawn inside me, and if spacerocks didnt float on top of exit gates. This have set me back from slowly progressing, to panicking and constantly going into debt on repairs/maintenance and right now I cant even afford to repair my hull. I`m in a debt spiral due to bugs costing me metric tons of cash in dammages. Not coolIn its current state I can not recommend this game to anyone, even ones interested in a elite dangerous/eurotruck simulator crossover. The game need to fix bugs and glitches, as well as reconsider what "difficulty" is for "normal" players. Constantly stressing and rushing about replacing air filters and batteries due to how insanely quickly they drain and how incredibly little starter missions pay out makes the beginning of the game a rush to level up to unlock higher paying jobs to fight the decay where the game is the hardest at the start and becomes easier over timePoorly balanced, frustratingly buggy, lack of industry standard optionsI like this game, and I will give it some more time to grow on me because I really enjoy it. But this is a mess. Feels more like a early access game then some early access games
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT 07/09/24 - The 'Custom'  Settings *do* resolve some issues discussed below, but I feel that needs to be a bit more transparent on starting the game. Also do recommend adjusting balancing of some prices in the median setting as it's the default option when starting. Happy Trucking :) I hugely recommend this game - in principle. Fantastic blend of ATS/ETS and Motor Town (which i'll be returning to until some balancing tweaks are done). Great audio, ambience, on controller at least it's very smooth. The use of CB radio as part of the 'story' is cool too. Does what it sets out to do really well on almost all fronts in the time I've played. Feels like I'm obtaining what I wanted out of Elite: Dangerous sans the relentless grind.However - I see the devs have announced a balancing update. My advice is hold off until this is implemented, or continue/play anyway, but lower the difficulty from the outset. The game obfuscates some unwieldy high difficulty to start off with behind resource scarcity in a way that doesn't match up with everything else.Air filters seem to be particularly tricky to balance affording versus going into death/debt spiral. It feels at this stage like a frustratingly difficult roguelite rather than a balanced but challenging space-trucking/management sim. My last run was undone after a lot of progress after being unable to find any means of not dying from oxygen loss, including knowing where certain points/gates will sell. Even with the suit and spare batteries, I'm just physically stuck. I'm doing a 3rd run and seeing how it goes on a notch down in difficulty, as others have recommended similar.Will update my review when this is fixed. For now, hold off til the incoming balancing update and see. Props to the devs for acknowledging and actioning this so quickly in their updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: The game is like a simplified version of Pacific Drive and Truck simulators. (Yes it's in space and still somehow manages to be a simplified version of those 2) There isn't that much to do it and the enviroment/emergens breaks pretty quickly when you repeatly have to travel through portals to locations.The idea was good, the potential is enormousFew things that's bothering me in random order:1. DifficulityThe game is waaay to punishing for mistakes. You only get 1-3k per job and then 90% of that goes to batteries and fuel.So if you end up getting a fine you're almost screwed, living on the edge and you can never afford upgrades.I got a 6k fine for contraband items and only 3 days to pay it, that's impossible to pay since batteries was also running out. So i had to load a 2 hour old save.1.1 The truck starts out being sooo fragile, one small rock and you gotta go out and fix. The hull goes to 0% so quickly and there is not enough repair places around so you have to deal with a glass truck for multiple hops.2. While it's a truck sim you seem to spend more time in loadingscreen (Travelling between galaxy/locations. While the galaxys themself seem veeeery small, you can travel across a location in 5minutes top.3.  Lackluster jobsWhile you can unlock different jobs, they all feel alike, if you crash you're screwed with economy regardless of the cargo type. It also seems no more than 3 trailers is avaiable at a time? and you have to unlock it. Why can't i do multiple jobs in my space trucks at a time? (as in carry cargo from 2 different jobs)4.Not repetitive funIt's not Euro or american truck simulator, you will get bored or anoyed by travelling from hoops to hoops, (because each location is so tiny) 5. RadioI know it's a radio, but give us the option to skip around the music please.6. Missed story opportunityIt's a game in space, why would you not have a somewhat mysterious interesting storyline/Quests  like pacific drive. The game feels empty  or like a sandbox mode, (except you're restricted to nothing.) For now the quests in the game is just guide/tutorial like, they seem to have no purpose other than push you through the game.7. truck customisationIt's a space ship, they made feel like a stock car. 7.1 Truck storage This is just an anoying throw anything anywhere system (or lack of system) There is shelves, but nothing to keep items stuck on shelves, so when you're out of battery or has to change it on grav device, EVERYTHING will get scrambled or in your face.All those things aside you can probably get a couple of hours of fun out of it. The price is good for the game quaility.

_childDocuments_.review: Not generally a fan of trucks or country music.Turns out adding a sci-fi space theme makes both quite enjoyable.The UI and environment are just the right kind of spot on to make any game enjoyable.There's a little indy jank to some of the mechanics, and things I'm sure the devs will iron out as the title matures.My biggest complaint is that the music, while good, is like 5 songs.  I NEED MORE SPACE-THEMED COUNTRY, BLUES AND ROCK!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: This is a gem in the rough but it's still rough.Firstly, it's a space game without any kind of lateral thusters. You cannot see what each button does and you cannot remap the control scheme either.The loop in itself seems fun but the overall clunky controls lack of polish is too much for me.About 2 hours in, my forward thrust suddenly didn't work or rather my backwards thrust was stuck at full power. You cannot overpower the backwards thrust because there is a slight delay between full stop and thrust which is normally helpful but completely broke the game for me in this case.I have requested a refund.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: This is a review from about 10 hours in  - I absolutely love it and I'm addicted.The star systems look incredible and once you get used to the controls it drives so so smoothly. Hauling is fun, the characters are fantastic. I love that they even made ads for Gold Rock Radio, and even made up artists! The world building is great.However. One thing I've personally been bashing my head against is the lack of - and overpricing of essential items you need to survive. UCC's and the air filters are the biggest offenders of these. Air filters will cost you like 2,5k while jobs barely give you that amount to begin with (they start off at 1-2k per trip). Not to mention that shops will carry 1 or 2 of these items, so finding batteries/air filters/UCC's and keeping up with them is... stress inducing sometimes. On top of that the game later introduces shock absorbers. Those barely last, are really expensive, and there are so few of them around you're best off just flying around the thunderstorms if you can.It's REALLY easy to get into debt, and then stay there. It's also REALLY easy to ding up your truck, and after a small grace period of it being free, fixing it costs a set price of  dollars. Doesn't matter how small the damage is. In my humble opinion there should definitely be a change to that. Maybe degrees? Calculations? 3k is really way too steep.Some minor things(for me):Game is ridiculously fun and the worldbuilding is incredible, despite items necessary for survival being overpriced and super scarce - this all in . For now I recommend using custom difficulty to suit the game to your liking!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Great game but also some missed opportunities but considering the small sized dev team, these are probably not "missed opportunities" but rather conscious decisions against features they probably would have liked to implement. I am excited to see where they take the game but for now it feels only 90% finished. There are some tiresome mechanics in the game related to fixing up your truck but I also chose the "recommended" setting in the beginning and I do believe you can change the balance between constantly having to fix up your truck and taking long trips so maybe that fixes that issue.Maybe I was just being inefficient with my hauls but making money also seemed pretty rough for the first playthrough, I found myself constantly going into debt because I needed more power cells and power cells are freaking expensive for something that seems to be a basic need in this game.The skill tree not having any cool features to look forward to when leveling up also feels a bit underwhelming. 95% of the skill tree only unlocks new hauling jobs, which is not something that belongs into a skill tree and should just unlock automatically in the background while progressing the story(imo). Another annoyance (to me), is not being able to pick up multiple things when picking up salvage. Having to go in and out of your truck for each salvage piece becomes really tiresome(something that could be fixed with a perk in the skill tree. Maybe one perk could be an item magnet or a backpack, that allows picking up multiple items when collecting salvage).All in all the progression in the game needs more exciting stuff to look forward to or maybe there already is but you just can't see it at the start.Unfortunately Steam only allows for either thumbs up or down as a rating(instead of a more nuanced star system) but giving this game a thumbs down would be a disservice to the devs, so I'll give it a thumbs up for now.Hopefully some good stuff to come but the game is already in a decently enjoyable state.Personally, I might hold off on playing for now, see where the development goes and pick it back up in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Too many things are just uncomfortable. It's great that you have to always fix your truck in various ways, but the components cannot be bought in larger quantities. You can only buy one battery at a time, two if you're lucky. Want more? Gotta haul to a different shop. I don't get why the shops can't just sell more of the maintanance stuff.Speaking of the shops, you can't shop while hauling a cargo. You need to unhook the cargo, hook yourself to the shop, and then hook back to the trailer? Why? It's so frustrating to do.Then there's the fact that you have to turn a system off to change a battery, so if your gravity needs replacing, you better be ready to see all your perfectly sorted cargo flying everywhere.Overall, I feel like this needs some quality of life to even be considered enjoyable. Right now, it's just a hassle.

_childDocuments_.review: Trucking in space, it's an amazing concept. So far I'm having a lot of fun, but there are some quality of life things that NEED to be added. First thing and most annoying are the power supplies. PLEASE add a charger of some sorts for the supplies. I've done 2 deliveries and all of my power supplies are out, I go to a store and they're only selling 2!!!! Even if I have to invest in-game money for the charger, that would be okay. I just want some way to charge the batteries so I don't have to keep stopping for them. Other than that, the game is a lot of fun.
