_childDocuments_.review: I'm still early in the game, so I feel like I'll have more to say as time goes on.  My early impression is that I'm loving the game but the learning curve is brutal.  This is not a relaxing sit in your truck and haul goods through the stars kind of game.  Maybe once I've had time to get the hang of it, but wow it's unforgiving.  There's a bunch of highly necessary equipment that your truck needs to stay running.  Power cells, air filters and circuit breakers.  They all deplete over time and don't recharge.  Compared to the rewards for completing jobs, they're quite expensive, and some of them don't last very long.  You can sell all of them, but they don't hold their value.  And they're all active right from the start of the game.The game directs you to a manual in the glove compartment immediately upon starting.  I've read the whole thing, and I recommend everybody does the same.  However, there are a number of things that I think should be clarified.  Easy changes, because it's just text.  Well, I suppose they then need to translate it to 50 different languages.First, make a list of all the critical systems and how to keep them running.  Explicitly state that they are all consumable, nothing recharges it needs to be replaced when it depletes.  Second, explain exactly where all of them are.  I went for quite a while with cargo bouncing around the inside of my cab before I finally found where the gravity control system power equipment is.  I also didn't realise there was a second set of air filters until I passed out (again).  Now, I have to say that I have been enjoying figuring all this out.  It wasn't unfun.  But it does get frustrating to have my bank hit negative again after finishing a lengthy story job because the air filter that I needed to change was more than the job payout.  Here's my suggestion.  Difficulty levels.  I think this would be easy to implement.   - Casual relaxed mode: depletion rates have a 0 multiplier (0.25 for fuel), so power cells and air filters will never run out, they're just a trade commodity.   - Easy mode: depletion rates have a 0.5 multiplier, so they take twice as long to exhaust. - Medium mode: depletion rates have a 0.75 multiplier - Realistic "trying to make it as a freelance trucker in a nasty economy" mode: depletion rates have a 1.0 multiplier.   - Mean "we want you to fail and be miserable" mode: depletion rates have a 2.0 multiplierSo, other than the very unforgiving learning curve, this game is great.  I've been having a blast.  Learning to control the truck took a bit of time, but once I started to get the hang of it I've been running successful deliveries and having a great time.  The vistas are absolutely gorgeous.  I've discovered that I enjoy country when it's being sung about space trucks.  It has a trading system that is familiar to anybody who has played a space trading game before.  Commodity type X is worth more in this system than that system.  Buy some low and sell them high.  These commodities are illegal in these systems, be careful if you have some in your cab.  I haven't gotten into the customisation part of the game yet because I can barely afford to keep my truck out of impound, but the default look is great, so I can only imagine the possibilities.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Positive recommendation on the condition that you're in the niche audience that would enjoy this game. As I am in that group I've been really enjoying my time with the game, and the soundtrack has joined the Pacific Drive radio tracks on my commuting playlist.It's not a six degrees of freedom space game like Elite, it's more of a cross between a truck and flight sim where you have all three degrees of rotation but only forward and reverse thrust. The game is based around the concept of a space semi truck, not a space ship and personally I think the way it controls helps sell that. Elite is still around, it feels weird to buy a game that's trying to do something different and complaining that it's not the same as every other space game.Otherwise, devs have confirmed they're planning to adjust the maintenance costs and availability of parts and I would recommend playing with reduced maintenance when you start the game until that point but having done so I have been highly enjoying it.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: This game is too hard, in the sense that even on medium difficulty you start dying way too fast. you barely get to a point where the side characters are teaching you about how to paint your truck before you start running out of batteries and air filters. the Initial contracts can in theory pay for what you need, but as a new player it is way too easy to miscalculate and end up wasting your first four hours in a irriversible death spiral. on top of that to try to get out of your spiral you will obviously go off road (also cause its not at all obvious how to find the actual roads), and then just hurt yourself even more since there is so much space junk even in the early area that will instantly cost you a third of your health and it is often unavoidable since the proximity indicator only flips on when you have effectively already started avoiding the first pieces.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game if you enjoy hauling, buying low and selling high games.  Some people have complained about micromanaging to an annoying degree, and I also agree that micromanaging is a deal breaker.  However, with this game you can change settings/difficulty to alleviate that.  The main complaints have been that power drains too fast and part break/weardown too often, all I did was go to custom settings, leave everything else the same and just turn down the battery drain and part degredation, and I haven't had a problem with it for the 5 hours i've been playing me new file.  So if those reviews are making you think twice, don't worry, just use custom setttings and you will have a blast (if this is your type of game).
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Real truck driver approved :) I played a bit before my shift and im having fun with it so far. To address previous reviews regarding the keybind issue: According to the discord they plan on implementing it later on. The controls as-is are not unplayable, and work just fine on an xbox controller.I love the artwork, the setting, the music, and the semi-realism of the controls. The game is a perfect balance of realistic enough to be sim-like and arcadey enough to be casually enjoyed. Im an OTR driver and ATS was too much like my job for me to play it casually without taking it seriously lol. I played the demo for this game a while back and it was a bit rocky, but the game seems to be running smoothly now with no issues. Thank you M&M for providing a worthwhile experience. Please continue to support the game long term. :)EDIT: After playing for a few hours, I’m genuinely not understanding the issue everybody is having with managing the systems. I haven’t run out of anything yet in standard mode and swap a couple of batteries out every few trips. Some tips:-Swap gravity and oxygen batteries when docked. The dock keeps these systems stable for you while you swap out.-Hold onto batteries over 10% to use in your suit slot. The suit slot uses very little charge.-Cut your breakers when changing UCCs-Only fuel as much as you need to and keep your jug full.-Don’t drive recklessly. You lose a lot of money by doing so. Only do it to avoid late deliveries if needed.-UPGRADES PEOPLE. Upgrade your truck ya’ll. You’ll be going through maintenance a lot slower.Otherwise here’s a few things I think should be addressed gameplay wise: -The job board/store only being accessible by the airlock is a bit annoying and it took me a minute to figure out how to get back to the menu after closing it. Id implement a button or screen on the dash or even just a keybind to reopen the menu.-The lack of strafing is definitely a bit of a gripe. If the devs decide to implement it I strongly recommend the way ED does it. Provide it as a toggle switch on the right stick on controller. -I may be missing a container somewhere but an upgrade for shelf tie-downs would be nice. Ive started just leaving everything on the floor lol.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Okay - normally I wouldn't leave a review this early... but this is so freaking cool lol. Picture American Truck Simulator meets Pacific Drive; that's the feelings. Even if you're a strict simmer this *will* tickle your fancy. Every button can be pressed. Climate controls, cruise control, individual thrusters, individual lights, etc. You can get up and move around your cabin arranging hand cargo and tools, there's a bed, there's *tons* of compartments that house things from air filters to power cells. It's just really, really cool. Then there's the failures, which I've only had a couple so far but that's why I say Pacific Drive, random stuff and inventory management and all that. The one thing I'll come out and say... how is it that there's no control options? I mean... I get it - part of the challenge is frantically looking around your cabin to hit the emergency brakes and stuff. But really wish I had some options at least. Lastly, the game runs great - and actually looks really decent. It's so light to run though, lol. Like I have everything cranked, even 200% scaling and it still won't get me more than 85fps because it's simply not enough work for my 7900xtx. That's not a flex, I'm just saying give me 400% so I can saturate my GPU and get more FPS then I do at 200% resolution.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: 4 hrs in, love it so far!!I've been waiting for this game for months and started playing immediately after launch. I loved the concept of truck sim in space from the start, and it's really well executed! The atmosphere and style is beautiful and I'm really enjoying the radio music and chatter with the characters!So far my only issue with the game is the controls, I play on pc and don't mind the default key binds that much (unlike many of the other reviews), but I still wish there were alternatives to control schemes or some kind of drive assist that makes controlling the truck easier. I understand that controlling the truck physics is half of the game, but sometimes it gets a bit frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I've really been enjoying this, it combines a fun story with easy-ish hauling once you get the controls down and a fun micromanaging maintenance system. The driving is less so a space-based ETS or ATS and more driving within sectors and using warp gates to get to them. I would love to drive along a space super highway but I cannot fault this efficient system that's in place instead.While I do wish the truck had lateral thrusters, it does add to the fun design of the game for you not to have them as you wouldn't on an actual truck.There's also the issue of not being able to adjust your keybinds, though I reckon that will be added soon.Looking forward to seeing what more is in store for this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, simple, fun and great to relax to. It pays to maintain your rig as you can become stranded and may have to restart from scratch but i suppose that's what its all about. You can cater "difficulty" by focusing more on maintenance or just driving which is a nice touch. I haven't played it for long at all but been able to check out most of the in game features. This is definitely a game i will be playing for a while as a nice casual, chill out. Fingers crossed for DLC and updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Good truck sim game, I like the controls you get to click on in the game and the maintenance is cool. Plus the side story tied into to getting upgrades and doing other certifications is cool too. Buy goods in the shop to sell in a different place is also cool.Problems: Need better balancing on cost of items. Things cost too much, you can go into debt but if you start that its forever it feels like. Also things cost a crazy amount for what you make and things break down fast even on "normal difficulty". This might sound like baby complains but other people have noticed it too. I hope there is better balancing for cost of items and maybe more starting equipment too for new beginners. I would wait for maybe a big patch to see if these problems get worked out. If you care about the game and want to just play it, then just play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: A good and different game, indeed at present at least it's a more difficult suvival and careful game on "Normal".  Take your time, you're not rushing to deliver, you're keeping each system in the rig going with attention and and avoiding each drifting rock (or other rigs) in your path.  Figure out every rig system and how to spend less and earn more, or adjust your difficulty in a Custom game.  Plan to retry a few times, in either case.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I don't typically review games or anything in general tbh but this one deserves it. The only reason I am rating this game is to boost its ratings so it continues to get support for future updates (not that there is anything wrong with it at launch but more is better). This game provides plenty of entertainment for hours on end but still not so challenging that you would want to rage quit. I've played other trucking sims before but the space theme adds a whole new layer that is so fascinating to learn and explore. All in all, the only reason I learned about this game was bc it was on my steam home page instead of the normal way I discover games (YouTube, Twitch, Etc.) which tells me not enough ppl know about this game. I know this review doesn't do too too much but if i can help these developers in any way I will. I've only played for around 9ish hours and have been frustrated plenty of times through challenges a player would typically face but despite that I still continue to curiously explore everything this game has to offer. If you like driving sims, and LOVE space (or are at least somewhat interested in it) I highly recommend this game for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: The premise is a novel one, and it is a space-sim. However, not much has changed from the demo version, and there are a handful of kinks that still need improving. Some QoL features that are still missing, and some mechanics that still need some more thought are still there. The simulation, however, is quite good. The lumbering hulk you pilot is quite nice, and all the features (from cab light, to CB radio) gives it a cozy feeling.Anyway, still needs some ironing out. I would've released this as an Early Access title to get some players' feedback before going gold. Might change the review after the devs take a look at the feedback and change some stuff.EDIT.: Let me expand my review. I would say Elite Dangerous' long trips feel more like "ETS/ATS in space" than Star Trucker*. In Star Trucker you don't get to travel using cruise control for long streches of vistas like ETS/ATS. It's a , instead. It seems the focus of the game is to micromanage your trucks' systems while delivering stuff.Some of the management features seem like they were made intentionally harsh otherwise the game would feel too "slow". Batteries drain fast, they can't be recharged, and the systems' highways are more of a suggestion rather than a layout one would expect from humans in the 31st century.* - I was gonna say Freelancer, but I don't know how many people know of that game, and FL has fighting/piracy included, so that is a bit too different for a good comparison.

_childDocuments_.review: Having enjoyed the truck and space simulators, I'm the perfect audience for this game.But after about an hour, It's not something I was enjoying.To keep it short, the game feels very claustrophobic. We're in space, why is everything so very close together? In the first 3 systems I visited, the space stations are within like 3 or less miles of each other. It's weird that Euro or American truck simulators make you feel like you're going much longer distances than a game set in space.The view from your trucks cockpit feels more obstructive than it should, and while I understand it's meant to literally be a space truck, it doesn't translate well to the environment of space, even when your FOV is increased, it feels claustrophobic.One major flaw in this game is the lack of HOTAS support, instead you control your truck with W A S D keys, after playing flight sims and space sims, this is a really awkward way to navigate and you have to keep your space bar pressed to keep going forward, upon release your truck will very slowly slow down. _childDocuments_.review: When I first saw this game, I was looking for a game to play that I could enjoy and relax while still experiencing the fun of space. Star Trucker is a unique blend of sci-fi and simulation. It takes the familiar concept of long-haul trucking and transplants it into a vast, awe-inspiring cosmic setting. The result is a relaxing and challenging game, with a strong focus on realism and immersion.What Works:Stunning Visuals: The game's visuals are a standout feature, with breathtaking vistas of nebulas, distant planets, and futuristic cityscapes.Realistic Physics: The handling of your massive truck feels weighty and responsive, adding to the sense of realism.Immersive Atmosphere: The game's soundtrack and sound design create a captivating atmosphere that draws you into the world.Challenging Gameplay: Delivering cargo across the galaxy isn't easy. You'll need to manage your fuel, oxygen, and cargo carefully, while navigating treacherous space lanes.What Doesn't Work:Steep Learning Curve: The game's complexity can be daunting for newcomers, with a steep learning curve.Limited Replayability: Once you've completed the main story, there's not much incentive to return, aside from exploring the open world.Overall:Star Trucker is a bold and ambitious game that offers a unique experience. While it may not be for everyone, those who appreciate simulation games and sci-fi will likely find a lot to love. If you're looking for a relaxing and challenging game with stunning visuals, Star Trucker is worth checking out.Rating: 4/5 stars

_childDocuments_.review: I'll throw down a review since this is such a unique title and deserves recognition for that. The theme is top notch, 80's trucker mixed with space is a match made in heaven.This game is a combination between a space flight sim and a trucking simulator. One of the game design issues you run into with that is you have to pick and choose per feature which type of sim you'll be more like. And this game and I have a serious disconnect on that, everything I think should operate more space simulator like, operates more like a trucking sim, and vice versa. It's not a knock on the game at all, just a mental disconnect that I personally have to work through while playing.For the mechanic aspect, I find everything that happens in the cab of the truck to be mildly irritating in some way or another, whether that's items taking damage from being looked at wrong, or the gravity generator battery not being a redundant set of two, so your things go flying every time you change it, UNLESS you're parked at a store. Personally if I were going to space, I'd strap everything down, yet there is not a strap to be seen.All the complaints aside, the game is fun, an arcade-y trucking sim in a nice setting, with easy trailer management and fantastic voice actors. Don't mess with the law, they may not arrest you, but those fines will put you in student loan levels of debt.Like many of the other reviews mention, this is NOT an easy game. If you want a cozy drive'em'up then make sure to tweak the difficulty. Recommended will hurt early game, financially and emotionally.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is exactly what I wanted based on the demo earlier this year.This game can be a little unforgiving at times, but that's the case with any good "simulation" game. The sound and visual design for this game are spectacular. The sound-track is one of the best, most perfectly themed original sound-tracks I have heard in a long time.Here are the things this game simulates:- Newtonian space physics, with the ability to turn off "Drive Assist" and coast. You have to manage the weight of the truck, as well as the weight of attached cargo trailers, and you will crash into stuff which leads us to...- Repairs. A rig in space, it's rather fragile. Collisions, even small ones with small debris leads to hull breaches, much like issues with space debris that real astronauts have to deal with. So put on your Hardspace: Ship-breaker (Available on Steam) hat and get to repairs. Even if you drive, er fly perfectly, you still have to deal with...- A number of subsystems simulated in a medium complexity vehicle. You have to maintain your subsystems, such as artificial gravity, magnetic couplers, and oxygen/air filtration systems by frequently changing batteries, control circuits, and filters. The manual is included in your glove box, but no one reads it. So put on your Tin Can (Available on Steam) hat and get ready to replace some stuff. But running a well maintained rig runs into...- The typical struggles that real truckers deal with including inspections, permit limitations, speed limits and fines for unlawful driving, and other traffic making everything more complex. Plus, backing up a trailer on a road, in two dimensions is already tough enough, now you have to reverse while wrangling a mass dangling off your rear magnetic couplers in three dimensions.- There are a ton of subtle simulation touches that really help bring the universe consistency together such as 1. The illuminated circle of all docking ports aligns perfectly with the circle rendered on the reverse docking camera when the truck is aligned and ready to grapple.2. The lights next to the jump gate all indicate important information, whether you are close enough, aligned correctly, and at a stop.3. You have control all the exterior and interior lights and other functions within the cab.4. There's cruise control!Here are the things this "simulation" game-ifys - very much like American Truck Simulator or Euro Truck Simulator 2 (Both available on Steam):- You can pick your difficulty using a pre-canned setting, I chose "standard," or customizing various parts of game-play to suit your style.- Earning money for deliveries. At first, money is tight, and you have to make some tough choices. Do you use that old 12% battery in the space-suit recharge unit to give you just enough juice to patch that hull leak, or keep that 12% handy in case your artificial gravity dies? But soon enough, with a little patience, you'll have a full crate full of spare batteries ready to go.- Upgrades are available to improve handling, efficiency, etc. I haven't gotten into these just yet, but I can see that I'm now making more money than I'm spending, and the first wave of upgrades are affordable in the early game.- Lots of places to discover, permits to unlock, and new delivery types in the skill tree, very similar to American / Euro Truck Sims.- Travel times are helped a lot with the jump gates. Games like ATS and ETS2 handle travel time by compressing the world. Star Trucker divides the world into sectors that are all unique with jump gates in between them.Here are the things that could be improved:- HOTAS support not yet in the game, but the devs are working on it.- No VR - this game would be spectacular in VR.- Some performance issues on some current / powerful gaming builds, they are aware as far as I can tell and are working on it.- The cruise control doesn't automatically disengage when you tap on the brakes, like in a real truck. (It should, take this as my request for this minor feature!)Here is my Final Verdict: I played the crap out of the demo when it was out; the full release has not disappointed at all. This is going to be my binge-play game for a while. At the end of the day this is a futuristic "sim" is really fun with plenty of complexity and subtlety to explore in this "simulation."

_childDocuments_.review: First things first: This is *not* a trucking sim, it is a survivalist game wearing the skinsuit of one. You're not so much truckin' the spacelanes, you are forever scrambling to keep health bars up.This is for you if you ever thought: 'These Valheims and Ark Survivals are pretty good, I guess. But how much better could they be if there would be more bars ticking down? I mean, a lot more. And if some are obfusticated, that would just be the cherry on top.'Never fear, Star Trucker is here and has all your needs covered. And it even has health bars within health bars. We're entering inception levels of territory here.Here's a breakdown of the health bars when starting out (There'll be even more later in the game to look forward to):2 Core Systems Batteries, one bar each.2 Mag Batteries, one bar each.1 Bar of Oxygen to maintain, for which you have to keep 1 Battery for on board gravity. 1 Control Unit for onboard gravity.1 Bar for your space suit, with the subcategories of:1 Fuel gauge.1 Truck Hull integrity bar.You are looking at 9-18 health bars. If that isn't some kind of record in the genre, it should be. How do these all fit on the UI? They don't, you spend a lot of time panning the camera over the dashboard to check on them. A hassle? Maybe, but this way you get to keep up with the various system alerts which are also not visible otherwise if you would only look out the windows to, you know, drive your truck, dodging traffic and space junk.On a side note, the status of the various control units isn't even shown there, you have to leave the driver's seat to go over to the relevant panel to check their status.While the individual bars take a while to whittle down, the sheer number ensures that you'll be replacing and buying parts constantly. - Don't play a drinking game where you have a shot every time a part needs to be replaced, you'll get alcohol poisoning within the hour.Another thing is, you should really, really like the docking maneuver ingame. You'll be docking to hitch your trailer, to check the the shops (1 docking maneuver for each), and the job board (another docking maneuver - yes the shops and the board are in different places). If you are of the mindset of 'Yep, this will never get old.', that'll help.We could go into the nitty gritty of the lack of key bindings, how picking an upgrade on the skilltree can screw you, the inability to change game options midgame, why there isn't one battery for all systems, etc.But really what it all boils down to is the question wherever being bullied to juggle all these bars and timers is the kind of gameplay loop you are looking for. Because that's what it is at the end of the day.This is not the zen-like relaxing experience of ETS/ATS, this is wheelspinning(tm) the game. If you are fine with that, have a go. For everyone else: Avoid.(edited for text formatting, spelling)

_childDocuments_.review: First off, advertises itself as a truck sim but is so far from it to be laughable. The setting would be interesting, if there was much to it. Most of what you're doing is flying through empty space in a see of debris that will destroy you while going from jump gate to jump gate. Very little interesting in the way of driving.This game is too incredibly punishing to be fun. The truck needs a ton of consumables to keep running. It's too expensive to rely on completing jobs to keep on top of repairs, fuel, and all the other in-cabin consumables. The best part is, you're not even guaranteed any ability to get what you need. Need 4 batteries? Too bad, the shop is selling 1. Need an air filter? Those are so rare that most shops seem to have none.So... making money. Leveling up makes jobs more valuable and unlocks new cargo types. Fine. It's not enough in the early game economy. It feels like merchanting is the intended way of making money in the game, which is extra punishing early when you can't buy a lot of goods.Docking is annoying. Want shop? Dock. Want to view the jobs? Undock, then dock 50 yards to the left on the same building. It's tedious.For extra fun, oxygen is not connected when you're docked, even though power is. So every second you spend docked is constantly chipping away at your O2 system. You cannot ever take a break in this game, it's relentless.Trying to find things in a system is annoying. You might know there is a job board in a system, but you won't know which white diamond it's at.Shock storms... what a miserable mechanic. They spawn on top of places you need to be, like stations with job boards. It will disable the cameras making docking extremely difficult. And if you do dock by some miracle, you're still affected by the storm. So you'll pop all of your shock absorbers trying to find a job.There is WAY too much debris everywhere in space, and even hitting the tiniest fragment can be quite damaging. If you're driving fast, the pop-in will make it impossible to dodge. And map markers can hide the debris so you can't even see it. The more trailers you have, the more zoomed out your camera is. But you simply cannot see enough from inside the cabin to be able to dodge anything either.The only interesting thing is that the game has some kind of story, but the actual gameplay is too frustrating for me to want to continue.tl;dr this is some kind of survival game masquerading as a truck sim, and the gameplay is tedious.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I did run into a bug finally. I ran out of oxygen while hauling this sign for some moron across multiple zones. On step 7... i died.. when i came to there was no marker or way to lcoate the sign. They recovered me and my truck, but didnt think to also recover the thing i was hauling. = This is game breaking. A lot of the convoy people tie together, some dont unlock until youve done X with person 1 and X with person 2. Now that I cant continue I had to start over....This is a quick 10 hour review - Its emergent gameplay. At first it seems simple and 'fun'... but its challenging to the point of being grueling for some. If you look at the forums youll see people complain about how hard it is... instead of just lowering the difficulty. You need to be an organized player with sharp situational awareness. You need to be able to intuit how the systems work and how to maximize your resources. This is not an easy game, even on standard difficulty. That challenge is what makes it fun. I have unlocked 10 skills now and completed 5 long distance runs. I have done wide loads, multi-trailer, heavy and valuable loads.s Each has its thing you need to manage. There are ways to upgrade your truck to be better at things but I havent spent any money there yet as even as skilled as I believe that I am at this game, accidents do happen and it will cost you. I have died twice, both from lack of oxygen. Dying is EXPENSIVE, much more than just paying that 3000$ for an air-filter in the first place.My best payout so far was around 7000$. I assume it gets better with the different types of runs and longer distances.I have only unlocked one additional area so far and there are 4 more to unlock. Based on that, i assume that I could pull 20-25 hours of out of this game which meets my standard for a recommendation of $1 for each hour played. i have experienced zero bugs and zero crashes.

_childDocuments_.review: I've not played the game as heavily as some yet, however I figured I'd throw my thoughts on the pile of hopefully helpful feedback. I really like the style and vibe of the game. There's a lot of comments talking about the lack of content which sure yeah could be an argument, but that presumably and hopefully will be added to in the future. For the gameplay side of things there's the common thread of power and part management. I have read through a few of the reviews including the dev comments. and to me It's a bit rough around the edges, but I had a few ideas that might be a way to address the issue. I get the devs might be wanting to go for a more "realistic" environment or management style game instead of a relaxed trucking simulator which I don't mind in the slightest and would enjoy if there wasn't a severe lack of a grace period. What I mean by that is when something goes wrong you never feel like you can actually stop and resolve the issue or take a moment to plan out your next steps. My solutions for the lack of grace would be a rest stop/service station. These would be located at some of the major 'hubs' where you could pull over to something like a diner and you'd be supplied power so you can repair and swap cells without too much stress or /having/ to connect to a station where you can't EVA. Having them be at main hubs means if you are in the Junkfields for example you'll still have to make it to Emerald junction if you want to conduct maintenance in relative safety. If not you'll still have to do things roadside. They also give you a good place to stop out the way of other truckers and debris. This idea could also be incorporated into the fuel stations so they pull double duty and provide a dedicated place to pull over and maintain your truck.POWER Then onto power cells and the strange absence of ways to recharge them. Seen a lot of comments about how the highways are basically pointless, so let's give them a function and a mechanic which is how I thought they would have functioned before actually playing. Make the trucks either not use power when you are within the designated path of the highway (In between the pylons) or have them provide a small passive charge enough to cover a moderate power draw. This would actually give you some benefit of staying on the highway. Since currently they are a complete waste of time and fuel to follow and them not having debris really isn't that massive of an upside. An extension of this idea would be having the ability to install some solar panel type devices onto your truck. The truck has some massive blank spaces that would be perfect for a panel or two. These would be an upgrade that you can initially pay to install then an additional cost to upgrade to become more effective. The panels could maybe cover the passive draw of an unloaded cab without its grav generator and lights on at the start and slowly be able to cover more systems. Or for the unfortunate trucker the ability to sit with the panels facing the sun for a much needed charge.Now some suggestions for the power cells themselves. There's two ways to go with them: The first way is to have the basic power cells be your dirt cheap non-rechargeable ones that you can /always/ access at any shop with a certain reliability. Your then more expensive cells the ones with 150 capacity and up being able to recharge. And as you get more expensive cells they gradually become more efficient or charge faster, with the down side then being slower charging or being less efficient with maybe at the end of the chain a cell that is the definitive best in both departments as maybe a reward or for a higher cost. Second way is having all the power cells function to the same extent where they all have a degree of rechargeability and the more expensive is just better overall. To make this not so trivial let's say you have 4 total types of cells. The first tier starts out fully charged and over time starts to break down eventually only being able to charge back to 25% of the full capacity, this then follows on with the next tier of cells only being able to charge to 50% and so on. Leaving the final cell obviously still being able to hold a full charge.PARTS Onto parts. Obviously the pricing on certain parts is crazy. Primarily the air filters cost from what I've seen 2700 -3000 in some shops which early on might completely screw you over if you had to swap out the starter one already and haven't made enough to cover for a new one. First thing most would suggest is to just lower the price, but I think this is boring. My suggestion for this would be a way for us to clean out the air filters to squeeze a little more life out of them, maybe in the form of shaking them out in space or some kind of compressed air hose on the rig that would use a bit of oxygen like the air break in exchange for a few more minutes of breathable air. To add some fuel to another suggestion I saw was the UCC fuse's not having a way to monitor them from the seat other than waiting for something to stop working or having to manually check which just feels a bit glossed over. Adding another screen to the cycle for the fuses would be really cool to aid in the micromanagement. Another thing that I've noticed that has been a bit frustrating is the lack of a way to drop items safely. You are perfectly positioned to damage every single thing that you try to put down by your feet, So everything including the rather large gas tanks somehow gets damaged. You can avoid this by placing it on a raised surface or just not using the grav, but it just feels like an oversight and doesn't add any substance.QOL and MISCBeing able to access job boards and stores without docking would reduce the headache massively, maybe you still need to dock there at least once to get the information permanently in the case of job boards, and for stores you obviously would need to dock to actually purchase and receive your items. At least then you won't waste several minutes moving across the system to dock to then only leave empty handed because the store has none of what you need. Alongside the above having a basic local map of the systems or at least a way to mark potential POI's like a store or job board in a system would help with the navigation side of things.Proximity warning: This could definitely be improved and why not do that in the form of another upgrade in the form of either a radar that can tell you what direction the debris is in or some flashing lights that can give you a general direction to make it easier when navigating, because honestly even when zooming in the combination of restricted cab view and mark 1 eyeball doesn't work for everyone. Hard Case: Another idea I really like, but could be improved one of two ways: the first adding a lip onto the shelf so they can't just float out. Or second having a option to 'attach' them to the shelf. Sure you can open them to get the same effect, but I think these would be a better intended way of keeping things organized.Side jobs: by default these should payout way more. I realized on my first save that these bankrupted me. And sure yes there are ways of preventing that, but it's not something a first time player will inherently know and may turn them away. Difficulty isn't a bad thing its just when it happens in the first handful of hours when the game seems geared towards figuring things out yourself is just a bit meh. If I didn't have a friend give me some pointers I probably would've struggled avoiding debt in my second playthrough.Time: I like the short hauls but coming to this after other games where you really have to drive or fly in Star Citizen and Euro Truck it would be nice to have some more intense distances although I haven't gotten super far yet in the overall progression so I'll leave this as a soft opinion for now.Conclusion in comment.

_childDocuments_.review: In the current state of mid-september 2024, don't bother.The game is an harrowing experience of terrible user interface and tedious grind. ECONOMY- Income is ridiculously low. Grind.- Upkeep is ridiculously high. Grind more.- Wear & tear consumables cost twice the amount you earn from your average haul. Grind hard.- Upgrades make little difference and cost more with each tier. Opposite that, income hardly ever grows. Grind harder.- The fines work well, compared to the rest. Not a single time will they not trigger when they should. They will even trigger when they should not, because they're fun like that. - If you dare stop grinding you die, btw. And get fined into oblivion.The economy is such a mess, that I have to convert the fines and the grind into hours of gameplay, for clarity.GAMEPLAY- If you hit debris *BONK* you get fined 15 minutes per hit. If you don't hit debris, you swerved to much and damaged your trailers, and get fined about the same.- Driving slow won't make all debris spawn far enough ahead for you to avoid it. Driving slow won't minimize damage; that's a 15-minute fine per hit no matter what. Using headlights won't make it easier to spot.- Plenty of systems to toggle on and off constantly. You can't bind them to any button or key. Use your analog stick to look away  *BONK* from the debris and press action. Whoops, you just hit something while trying to push a button, get fined, 15 minutes.- You'll prefer using your analog stick because keyboard controls are a mess. So forget using you mouse, or get fined constantly. *BONK* See? Told ya.- There are 'just in time' hauls, that require you to deliver within a 1 hour window. You will typically get to the destination system 30minutes to 1 hour before the window opens. So you have to wait it out. IN REAL TIME. You can't fast forward time. Warping out and back into the system will advance ingame time two to three hours, so you will miss the window and get fined 2 HOURS of gameplay. I'm not kidding, the game is litteraly designed to make you wait ONE ENTIRE HOUR of your actual real life time just for an empty loading bay to light up. I mean we could go out into the real world, but we're gamers FFS! We're not supposed to do that and you're not my mom, videogame!- There is cruise control. You need to look away to *BONK* toggle it and to set it *BONK* to the desired *BONK* speed. You should not use cruise control.- You can deactivate stabilizers to save fuel. Cool to travel in a straight line. But if you travel in a straight *BONK* line you *BONK* hit debris and get fined. You should not deactivate stabilizers. Burn all the fuel. Only costs 30 minutes of grind to fill up every 2 hours of grind. Bargain.SALVAGING- You can salvage stuff in the debris fields. Salvage pretty much never spawns outside of scripted missions, and will despawn if you spot it too late.- When you've wasted 3 hours of past grind in wear and tear into looking for salvage that never happens, you'll forget about salvaging.- There supposedly is a salvage scanner that could help. 20 hours of harrowing grind aren't yet enough storyline to get it, though. Grind more.TRADING- You can trade items which you keep in your cabin, for a profit across systems.- If you drop them a couple inches when you put them down they take damage.- You have to find a high surface to put them down, because if you look down at your feet to try and put them on the floor... Well you're still 5 inches high, silly! (Spoiler: crouching would be convienient so it does not exist in that game)- If you hit debris, they fall and take damage.- If your gravity generator fails (with no prior warning, by the way), they float around and take damage.- Thankfully, SOME of them fit in containers that will protect them from hits. Of course some items don't fit into containers and WILL take damage at every opportunity.- The slightest bit of damage will make the item lose enough sell value to forget about any potential profit from the sale.DOCKING- The handling of the rig makes docking a pain initially, but rest assured that once you get the hang of it will still be a bore. No fun allowed here, remember.- You have to dock to your trailers (makes sense), but also to the store or to the job board.- You have to unhook your trailer to go to the job board or store.- The job board and the store are usually in the same place, but you can't get jobs at the store or buy and sell items at the job board. You have to undock from one, then fly 100 feet, do the same haphazrd backing-up dance and dock to the other. I mean they could have made it simpler, but the devs opted to make it more complicated for themselves just to get that little bit of extra pain in there. Such dedication to mediocre gameplay is commendable, I guess.- There is no auto-docking available as an upgrade or gameplay option. It would be a quality of life improvement and that is a sin.BUGS- Now let's be honest here, there aren't that many bugs, the game is indeed terrible, but rest assured it's mostly by design.- NONETHELESS, for however little bugs the devs chose to let slide, they did ensure they were game-breaking, and that, my friends, is what you call dedication.- The game autosaves into a single slot after warps, which are where most of the bugs happen. If you encounter a bug, tough luck, the game just autosaved and you can't reload to fix the issue. No, you can't disable autosave, it would be player-friendly and we don't want that.- You can manual save into 3 dedicated slots, to anticipate for bugs. But don't fret, manual saves come with their own array of game breaking bugs, so you won't be safe from pain there either.Overall, this looked like a chill game, the kind most people would find boring, but in which you would go about progressively earning credit to upgrade your rig and get new features, but the devs managed to instill suffering in every nook and cranny of it.Even the saves won't save you!You have upgrades, you have things to unlock, you have progression. But you cannot be chill about it, every second that flies by means your overpriced consumables get wear and tear, and if you don't complete that job quick, you WILL lose money trying to replace them.And they even added a system that FORCES you to wait for DOZENS OF REAL TIME MINUTES for the gameplay loop to close, all the while watching quietly as your rig wears itself into ruin doing NOTHING.And the icing on the cake is, the actual core of the game seems interesting, the gameplay mechanics would be nice if implemented correctly: the rig maintenance, the salvaging, the trading, the various job types, the story all show good potential...The good game is RIGHT THERE, but the devs mischievously put it just out of reach.I've spent 20 hours trying to get to the point where it gets better, and now I regret I did not get out to take a few walks in the park instead. What the hell is happening to me?This is a masterpiece in cruelty. Honestly, no sane human being can put out that mess and think it is acceptable, this has to be on purpose.

_childDocuments_.review: Snowrunner in space mixed in with Pacific Drive car mechanicsHonestly worth the waitThe Good:-Beautiful looking aesthetics-Simply to pick up mechanics-Non stop country and blues on the radio-Cozy gameplayThe Bad:-Power cells can't be recharged - not even with a seperate charger or from the vehicle's generator while the engine is running-Required to dock with shops - could of just been solved with driving near the shop and having a droid deliver stuff to your air lock-Required to dock with contract offices - Why? WHY? As IT specialists say "This could of been solved through an email" no need to dock to just accept a new contractThe Ugly:-Unable to throw salvage items you find directly into the truck or airlock requiring you to either bring a box with you outside or salvage one item at a time-Short range radio communicator could of been used more besides scripted events at the start-Power/Fuel consumption and part wear n' tear is too high but you can switch this up in the options to suit your tastesDespite all this still a recommend

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I've changed my mind, don't buy this right now. Keybindings should be a launch feature, and I shouldn't have to restart the game to avoid having to pay 100 dollar fines and 1000+ dollar repairs because one of the little drones on the station decided to ram me while I was docked, or an entire rig surrounding a cargo dropoff point is 100% invisible. I'd even be willing to overlook all this if I didn't have to dump all my progress (including all these insufferable "side" quests that sometimes don't even pay me for deliveries, in order to unlock different sectors) to turn the difficulty settings down, just to make up for this nonsense, on top of the costs and time needed to slowly meander out of my seat and manage my control board and power cell inventory in boxes that I have to re-stack on the shelves because I accidentally breathed while trying to change out all the control boards.

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool take on trucking. I played the demo when it first came out and it had a few issues but those are all cleared up now. I've only got just around 2 hours in the game and it does not disappoint. I love that my Xbox controller is very easy to use for this game. Everything is easy to access and use. The controls feel solid, very accurate when you go to hit a switch or lever. It actually feels like your the pilot of a space truck, you have total control and even some outside cameras at your fingertips. I really like the fact that you have to exit the rig to fix leaks and use fuel cans and much more. I do own flight controls for my other games and hopefully those may be integrated into the game in the future but as of right now, im happy with how well the controls already are. Just remember that this is space and not a paved highway and you will have fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Great little game, been looking forward to it for a bit since it hit my radar. cosy but still enough management to keep you engaged. the music and style of the game is my absolute biggest win for this game. trucks in space, simple but effective.i do however think there needs to be awareness for players in terms of economy and how quickly you run out of things like batteries and air filters (both of which are very expensive and not rechargeable)so story time for this so others can perhaps avoid the headache, i started on the mechanic difficulty (2nd hardest), and it was ROUGH when you get to the solar storm sectors of the map. i just briefly wanted to check it out and wanted to book it out of there as soon as i could but the air filters were low and i wasn't able to buy new ones in the area i returned to and so i was stuck in a deathloop of either burning to death or dying to no O2. probably a skill issue but the air filters sell between 1000 to 1500 monies which is ludicrous as its half the average pay of a job at the start of the game and not every shop sells them (or batteries) so it doomed my 1st play trough after just the first 6 hours. (maybe we should add the roguelike tag to the game... JK) save often everyone!!overall i still recommend it as i'm going to continue playing onwards because it is fun regardless and relaxing 98% of the time, just gonna lower the difficulty a bit. amazing game for just two devs!!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been loving this game so far. I haven't heard of it before, nor have I played any other truck sim game before. This game blew away any expectations I had. There is a bit of feedback I have though.1.) A tiny rock shouldn't do 70% damage to my hull and trailer... it makes the idea of running a dangerous route never worth it. Damage should definitely be nerfed a bit.2.) Parts drain extremely quickly. I feel like I need to replace 2 or 3 energy cells on every run that's 2 or 3 hops away for my gravity and oxygen systems. In my opinion, this could be slowed down a bit further. I am playing on the standard difficulty.Other then that, a wonderful game. Thanks to the devs for making such a fun experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Chill game but like many others had mentioned, the battery power management can be quite tight. To mitigate this, you can set a custom difficulty with the power consumption to low while the other settings untouched. With these settings, I found the game much more enjoyable. Oh yes, also buy and add two more air filters in addition to your current 2 asap so that they last much longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Love the game so far. It is what I expected it to be. Space Trucking.Not more, not less. There are however, a few things that could use some changes/tweaking, at least in my opinion.1. The difficulty- The difficulty is fine, don't get me wrong. But it is bad practice to have a game like this and not allow the user to change the difficulty later on. Sure, some games do this, but they have usually a good reason. This game doesn't. People already are complaining about how fast the batteries deplete.2, The storage- Look, I get that when you develop a game you have to decide between simulating something realistic, or make it fun. But the storage needs a different solution. I can justify a lot of things in this game for the sake of it being fun, but the constant storage flying around, is not one of them. Another solution would be, to allow a grace period when you switch the grav battery. Give me some time to switch it before everything starts flying around.3. Controls- Keybinding is already being addressed by the devs, which is awesome. But I believe being able to strafe would be very beneficial to the overall experience.- Flying backwards is a bit of a pain in the ass. Don't know what to do, just figured I mention it.4. Store Items- The only reason I could find why those exist is to sell them? I actually hoped that there is some form survival aspect to the game, which I would absolutely love (as an optional setting). Otherwise these Items are absurdly useless as of now.5. Radio- Adding more radio stations would most likely require too much work. BUT enabling the user to add some internet radios to their game, shouldn't. Would be great to have more choice and also being able to customise it.I think that's all for now.But overall I love the game and can absolutely recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and enjoyable however the controls have put me off giving a positive recommendation. At times i found the controls frustrating. I think this game would benefit greatly from having thrusters that allow for up and down movement of the truck and a left and right strafe (rather than just up/down/left/right rotation).Also i found docking to be a little frustrating (i may just be bad at the game aha). A feature that would allow you to "click into" the docking panel and make the controls relative to the docking port would make it more enjoyable personally. however i understand that that might take away from the "im a gosh darn trucker and i have to be real damn good at reversin'!!"aspect of the game.

So it brings you to a shop and because I was just starting out I was -$2K+ after that. It wouldn't let me exchanged. then it froze when i started looking in the manual. Other than that, has been a good game to play for the afternoon. I have been wanting to play this since I saw the add a few months ago, was afraid I couldn't play with the higher system requirements. _childDocuments_.review: Scratches the space itch while giving you hours and hours of gameplay options for planning out truck routes, avoiding dangerous areas, and maintaining and upgrading your Space Truck!Awesome!(If you want a very relaxing experience, play on easy or custom difficulty, Normal has a lot of maintenance and you can wind up in the hole pretty quick)
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay itself is very fun and atmospheric. I like the physics system, it does feel like you are driving a truck in space.But currently the game is a bit too happy to punish you at every turn and the pennies you make barely cover the costs - if you even manage to find enough essential items. Sometimes the jobs available are just.. terrible. Like they may expire in 1 minute or pay so little it won't even cover the costs. That makes the game even harder, since system jumps without pay are a terrifying thought. Everything combined it gets pretty stressful at times.Eager to see what those announced "Balance Adjustments" will be.Remember to shut off your lights, they spend A LOT of power.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: So far so truckin'!I loved it since the demo at the "Next Fest!", though i haven't played that much back then to not spoil myself from the moment the game releases.I've played almost 2 hours now, looked around some, tested a few things.From what i can see it's solid but has potential and a few things that need improvements.The first and biggest improvement (thing that should be added) is a proper keybinding option. I know, many things are meant to be clicked right in the cockpit, but to be honest, when i am trucking about, i want to see my truck from the outside and be able to just hit a key and jump through a gate for example.Right now i kinda have to break my "enjoyment of watching my trucks outside", jump into the cockpit via camera and pull the lever and jump back out.Also, not sure it's even possible with the trucks layout/model, strafeing left/right/up/down would be amazing, and "realistically" speaking, should be a thing in space.I was a bit lost about energy cells, sure i should/could have checked the manual resting in the glove compartment, but well a simple hint right in the tutorial at first would have saved me from a death in space..of suffocation.But i am still loving the game and look forward to updates and improvements from the devs! <3
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty good idea of if you took trucking and mashed it into a space sim. I can't think of a better execution of the idea and I've tried. I've played the regular Trucking simulation games and the biggest part of those in the journey and how to get from A to B, Well in space there's not a whole lot to look at like you would on a highway, but you do see neat areas which function a lot like cities. The A to B is still there with on/off ramps replaced with warp gates, it's all much easier than a typical trucking game, at least I thought that until the next area. Things do get significantly complicated.Truck maintenance is much more important and kind of a chore sometimes. In a regular truck game you can do several jobs without needed tire and engine maintenance, In this game you'll need to be changing batteries for several systems as well as checking on the control circuits for those systems pretty much after every job. Not everything fails at once but one or two need to be replaced. There is an upgrade system which I hope devs expand upon, but all it does now is simple stuff like accel/decel, top speed, shocks, etc.It would be really good to slowly upgrade my truck out of these smaller headaches or trade up for higher end model trucks over time.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Tired of being frustrated with this game. The concept is outstanding and has so much potential to be a lot of fun, but is held back by poorly executed mechanics that left me feeling deeply frustrated with the experience overall. I can't recommend this game to anyone in its current state. Give me the ability to sleep in the bed in my cab to pass time so I'm not failing jobs because I'm either stuck in a station too early and have to wait as time creeps past to be able to drop my load off, or risk taking a jump to pass the time with the hopes that I'll make it back to the intended station in time without being fined too much. Jobs are not well explained nor are any of the mechanics explained. You are simply dropped into the cab of this vehicle and handed an "drivers manual." To be clear, that little book barely answered a single question I had about any of the mechanics it claims to explain. Why did I have to spend 5 minutes of my life just looking for where the gas cap was to manually put gas into my rig? Why is that information not included in the manual? I'll circle back around to this game after a few updates, but for right now it feels like it should be in Early Access. Not a full blown release.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: If you love trucks and space this game is for you. It´s more of a strategy / skill game than a ETS2 in space. If you have a routine with repairing and keeping spareparts its easy manageable. It´s tricky to steer the truck itsself, it´s drifiting most of the time and therefore it´s better to play with a controller. If you slowly get used to the steering it´s kinda easy but still tricky often. I really love this game, graphics etc but sometimes it can be very frustrating, shops do not have all spareparts so you can run out of oxygen and die anyways and get ported to the nearest workshop and pay even though you reached the next shop and have money to tackle the problem. Particles like rocks or junk are often not easy to be seen and its therefore often hard to not collide with them. The damage then is often very high and you can just forget the freight and need to repair the truck. The last straw was that I used a portal was lined up but because of some shifting of the truck and trailers the truck hit the portal and everything was damaged and not worth anything anymore. I love this game and give it a recommandation but I´ll stop playing it for now to spare my nerves. Its stressfull but nice to play. For a casual trucking experience with less stress I´ll go to other games to not kill my nerves as much. I bet there are people out there which are more skilled and stressresistent than me and therefore enjoy this game a lot more than me!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: It honestly is an ideal game to just sit back, relax and cruise around for a bit after a tough day at work. If you take it easy and don't try to rush from gate to gate you will experience very few bumps on the road. And another thing, the amount of polishing this game has as a two-man Indiegame is astonishing and only highlights how deep the big corpo devs have sunk in terms of sense for quality. This game breathes passion and that's been missing with so many releases the past two years. It's a one of a kind masterpiece and I'm all here for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I've played for 16 hours so far and it's addicting! For the life of me, I can't understand why people complain. I hope nothing gets changed when it comes to the survival factor; it's really engaging this way! There's also so much potential for the future. It gives me a bit of a Subnautica vibe, mixed with Elite Dangerous and Truck simulatons. Once you have some financial breathing room (always keep stock of Batteries/Filter/Ucc), INVEST! Look at the market, buy low, sell high, and haul in between. Regular trade is where the money is! And upgrade your baby...
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I played a bit of the demo and was excited to get this. So far I'm really enjoying it. The environment is beautiful and the driving is pretty chill. I kind of like making sure my power cells and gas is in check and fixing up the truck when it gets beat up. It runs fantastic on the Steam Deck.A few things that bother me and kind of take me out of the immersion are:- So far my truck tops out at 140mph (assuming this is miles per hour). This seems EXTREMELY slow for space. - Again, the mileage of the trips. The physical trip is fine but after going through a hyper space loop and popping out the other side and dropping off your cargo it is a bit jarring to see that your whole trip was only like 14 miles.- The temp gauge. Inside my truck is 68F. But it says the EXT (external?) temp is 57F. 57F?! I don't even wear a jacket when it's that temperature. Seems super odd for it to be the temperature of space.All of these are me nitpicking and in no way effect the gameplay. I think the game feels great and is super fun and relaxing to play. *Also, if I completely missed something and my "complaints" aren't valid please let me know. I turned on commenting.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Absolutely buy the game however if you aren't into micro management and just want to drive, select the Driver mode. Achievements still work on custom modes.So look, this game is an absolute gem. Considering it's a two man team it's an extraordinary accomplishment. So to start I went to the Recommended mode, not realising just how challenging it would be. Skated on the bankruptcy line a few times trying to balance keeping the ship in one piece and fueled. There's a little bit of balancing needed amongst modes but as per above if you aren't right into the simulations set your mode to Driver.Can't wait to see the game expanded along with the development team. There's so much more to come hopefully.

_childDocuments_.review: (Too Soon Won't Read: I love this game so far. Well worth the purchase!!)2hr First Impression:Wow! As much as I loved Snowrunner, I hated how it's driving mechanics worked. I have been looking hard for a game with the same laid-back feel to it, but still requiring skill and thought to it. This is EXACTLY what I wanted! When I saw it a couple days ago I was HYPED!!There is clearly a lot of love put into making this game. Well worth the money spent. If only more games did that these days huh?9hr Edit:My view on it still holds. Nothing to add. Been playing Mechanic difficulty. Powercell replacements and UCC failures are quite frequent, but purchase of lvl 1 and 2 powercells and ample stocks of them and UCC means quick fixes make it manageable. Still satisfying to think ahead for this.Overview:The drive-flying mechanics are very cool. A fair blend of truck style and spaceship style flight. I thought these things (US truckin, space, country) would make for a silly but unique game. This is much more than that. Skill Expression:So far, with normal cargos and first few systems, it is pretty laid back. But I went in prepared to NOT underestimate the potential for a mistake. There are quite a bit of opportunities for risk + skill = benefit/reward.Pre-drifting/aiming into turns at high speed, heading directly to your location = debris navigation. Preemptive purchase and management of powercell/filter/communication-card and a close eye on power levels means satisfying swap jobs and not an annoying extra task.This game does not hold your hand like many others will do. It puts all the info right up in front of you in a quick simple and clean way for you to brush off or read up on.Graphics:This game looks good and performs well on low and high settings.It has a style that kinda reminds me of old space sims. Kind of makes me think of X2 era of style, but totally Monster and Monster's own modern take on the genre. It's fantastic.I really look forward to playing through it much longer. I'll update my review later on.

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trucker is an inspired fusion of sci-fi and industrial sim. It's a trucking story with all the trappings of American Truckin' you would recognise from Smokey and the Bear. It's a futuristic glimpse into a vast galaxy of busy Kessler-syndromed planets and cold galactic outposts.I love how unapologetically the game drops highways, CB radio chatter, bootleg beer, and upward-pointing exhaust pipes into the same space as jump-gates, gravity-compensators, solar flares, and dark matter. Somehow the resulting universe is seamless and rewards my suspension of disbelief.Mechanically, I've seen other people complaining that the trucks don't have more ability to strafe like a real spacecraft might. That's true... but like. it's a truck. It's not a spaceship optimised for hauling cargo. It's a Big Rig Truck, but in space. That's the devs' vision, and a good metaphor for how they've combined other aspects of the two genres: the space mechanics and appearance are right there, not ignored, but always in service to the long-haul trucker aesthetic and theme. Like the music on the radio: classic rock and blues with subtle mentions of space scattered through.Finally, I also want to specifically praise the other folks we meet in-game. Though it's rare to see even their vehicles up close, the voices we hear over the radio still convey engaging characters. They make the galaxy feel populated with their gossip and insights, and importantly they punctuate the procedural cargo-hauling jobs with more unique side-quests. These requests usually also come down to moving something from A to B (our main skill, after all) but each one is memorable, and develops our connection to the character or the world as a whole.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game I really really did, but it's just got too many issues for me to recommend it. There's many other reviews that have said what I'm about to say better than I can but I'll just be brief. 1. Everything breaks too fast. You need batteries for everything and those will last maybe a jump or two. Shops not only have very very few in stock but they're also way too expensive, costing upwards of 600 bucks per battery. For context an average job will give you about 2k. so with 8 batteries you need and each costing nearly 600 you're constantly scrambling for money. Additionally batteries cannot be recharged in any way which is mind boggling to me. 2. Everything is too expensive. Mentioned above is the price of batteries but most egregious is air filters. You can have up to 4 of them but you only need one. Having more means they all supposedly break slower. The in game tutorial (which is horrible but we'll get to that) implies that they are actually not needed but helpful, that the more of them you have and in good condition means the less your oxygen generator uses up power. This isn't the case however and running out of them all together means that despite having a literal oxygen generator, somehow you begin to rapidly lose oxygen and then die. I don't know how having no filters suddenly makes oxygen just leak out of the ship in every direction but it will soft lock your  game, but again more on that later. 3. The tutorials are lacking to say the least. Some are ok but the majority tell you very very little info. Such as the "core system" which requires 2 batteries. It does not explain why it needs two or what happens if one runs out or you just don't put another one in at all. Turns out, you don't need two, you can get by with one. Would have been nice to know. As mentioned before with the air filters, I had no idea that having none of them would make the air in my cabin suddenly dissipate out of nowhere. Air filters clean the air, not produce it, so it was really confusing when I was getting notifications about a massive air leak but with no hull breaches. A tutorial would have been pretty helpful there in explaining that. Because that soft locked me. Speaking of which. 4. It's way too easy to soft lock yourself. Any time you'd "die" you're sent to a garage with a hefty bill you now need to pay off. Problem. I can't afford air filters with are around 4k a pop and I'm already spending most of my very little income on batteries already. So if I couldn't afford filters when I was in the green, how am I supposed to now that you've dropped me several thousand dollars into debt? Which I need to pay off first before anything else? Thus you die again, and again and again, going further in debt and fail spiraling. 5. The AI is just some of the stupidest things around. I've been hit more than a few times by drones and trucks coming out of nowhere and colliding with me. The game wants you to be on the "roads" but there's hardly ever any at all. AI trucks can stop and turn on a dime when you can't so you'll be following them when they suddenly stop moving and then you feel like a train conductor hitting the breaks despite knowing you can't possibly stop in time.6. Hey game, why do I have to go out of my way to find the shop in each sector? Sometimes it's highlighted no matter where I am, sometimes the body shop is highlighted, but not the store that might have the air filters I need to not die. The game tells you that some places prefer to not get bogged down with people and so don't have their pings set to be visible from so far away. Not sure why companies are literally going out of their way to hide from customers but ok. Maybe I thought, that would only apply to some seedier places that take back alley goods or something, but no. Even the most basic stores will be completely undetectable until you're right up on them. 7. The "recommended difficulty" is not the hardest one, in fact there are 2 above it, but this is grueling. I wanted a fun relaxing experience, I wanted to do some maintenance on my truck but not have to replace every single component every 30 minutes. This has completely ruined the game for me and with no way to actually change the difficulty on a save, I'd have to create an entirely new save, start from the very beginning, only to hope that it's not so punishing. If you can even call it punishing, because punishing implies that I did something wrong, but when the game gives me two star ports in a row with no filters and only 2 batteries, then how the hell am I supposed to do anything at all? This game doesn't feel like a fun sim. I don't even know how to describe it, because I genuinely feel like the main gameplay loop is replacing batteries and finding filters, over actually driving the damn truck. Hopefully they can update the game with a very very much needed balance pass but until then I'm not touching this thing again.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm disappointed. I thought people's complaints were exagerrated, but no, not really. I wish I didn't try to like it for more than 2 hours, as now I can't refund.So, what I don't like:1. The game claims to be "realistic" and a "simulator". This is a bit ridiculous. I get that it's set in space and therefore cannot be a real simulator, but come on. Neither the infrastructure (of which there is plenty) nor the truck itself is really well prepared for "driving" in space. Like, the windows are similar to real truck, so you can't see below and above you, except when using external camera. Flight assists are irritating instead of being helpful. The space infrastructure is ridiculous and not at all prepared to handle 3 dimensional traffic. "Highways" have traffic in both directions in the same space with "right" side going forward, which is just ridiculous in space, nothing prevents it from being separated. The highways often end suddenly in front of a construction or an asteroid/trash field. They are disconnected with each other. The flight itself is simulated terribly, it does not feel like moving in space at all, there's a huge drag of air, the truck slows down very quickly when not accelelerating etc. etc.2. The size of the world. While there seems to be a decent amount of "systems" between which you can jump, each system is very small. "Highways" have nominally just a few kilometers each, which in space feels more like maybe 1 km of what normal road feels. They are never straight too. I would have expected 10-20 times longer highways, mostly straight, and way higher max speed, requiring you to turn around around the middle and start breaking (btw it's ridiculous, but you break way faster than you accelerate in this space game...). There is no in-system map at all and you can't know what points of interest are hidden where and how to get there (it's only manageable because of the small sizes, but irritating still).3. The big focus on things outside of "driving". Replacing a battery is interesting and fun experience the first few times. Later it just feels like a chore. You spend way more time doing other things than driving (also because the distances are so small).4. AI drivers are really bad. I think big part of this is that the game designers do not really have any proper idea of driving rules in space that make sense, and the infratsructure is also not adapted to it. So, for example, everyone tries to keep the same "height". It doesn't make much sense in 3D space. But also AI is bad in other ways, for example once while I was going left from a "road" to park, an AI truck going the same direction as me, but to the left of me, stopped, making it look like it was letting me go, even though I stopped earlier to let it through. But nope, it stopped, waited until I was perpendicular in front of it, then it hard rammed me, straight into my "fragile" cargo.5. Overall the gameworld seems artifical and devoid of life. There seems to be a lot of scripted conversations and some storyline, but outside of that you don't really get to contact anyone. You can't talk to other drivers on the road, you don't talk to anyone about job offers or shops, they are just menus.

_childDocuments_.review: I was split on this, but since this is not marked as an early access game, I would not recommend purchasing it right now. This was released in a state which feels pretty beta, maybe 2/3 of the way through that phase of the development cycle. The instantly-assigned tickets are not fun, the $2000 weigh station fine isn't fun for something so irrelevant in space, dealing with the AI's inability to queue at single gates is frustrating.
