_childDocuments_.review: The game is so close to being really awesome but there's several QoL features that are missing that just makes it fall short.1. The consumables system is uninteresting and punishing.  Also it's immersion breaking.  Essentially only three consumables, universal circuits, batteries, and air filters.  And all they do is run out and have to be replaced.  At high difficulty/consumption rate if you don't pick up batteries every job, you will run out and die.   Batteries are horridly expensive, UCC's just break for no reason, and air filters are I guess air filters.  Apparently sometime between now and when humanity started building big-rigs in space, we forgot how to make alternators, so even if you have fuel you can run out of electrical power which is solely supplied by batteries.  Humanity also forgot how to make rechargeable batteries, so you're stuck stocking up on duracell alkalines the size of your face.The minigame associated with consumable maintenance is more of a nuisance than engaging, so there's that too.  It's not like you need to learn a checklist and do things right.  No, it's just pull out old battery, shove in new battery.  Wham-bam done.At least you can create custom difficulty settings and basically disable that crap.Related: most of the systems that draw power don't seem to have any gameplay relevance.  Haven't figured out what benefits the running lights give, etc.  You don't get fined for running dark, and boy are your headlights power hungry.  You can turn off gravity when you're strapped in, but apparently the trucking industry in our glorious space future has forgotten how to secure and strap down cargo so any small cargo items in your cab will then just randomly float around.2. The truck is missing two movement axes (sway and heave) which seems like a really big design oversight for a spacefaring civilization, and also just serves to make docking procedures unnecessarily fiddly for you as a gameplayer.3. Jesus there is space junk EVERYWHERE.  Yes yes.  I know to stick to the spacelanes.  But dear god, why is there space junk at the exit to the spacelane going into the jump gate?  And related, you can turn off drive assist to save fuel, but there's really no point in doing that since all the space lanes are curved or you're flying through the great space garbage patch anyway.  I'm not opposed to having a mechanic that encourages the use of spacelanes, but there's no minimum velocity at which space junk won't ruin your day, there's no tactical way to decide if you're going to take on space junk as a hazard (i.e., declining a job that goes into a hazardous area), there's no real way to mitigate space junk other than pray and dodge, and it doesn't feel like there's any rhyme or reason to its existence other than an artificial "stay in your spacelane" mechanic.  It's not like "warning, entering asteroid mining remnants debris field", just more like, "yeah, the largest commercial transport hub in existence can't be bothered to sweep".4. You can't mix and match jobs.  Sure, you can take on three jobs, but you can only ever work on one at a time.  I guess this means you can save yourself a docking at the jobs board if you can line up and chain jobs, but if you want to get your multi-trailer certification and maybe tow two trailers headed in the same direction simultaneously?  Sorry, can't do that.  Your multi-trailer certification is really only so that you can pull a single trailer with a weird slinky-kinky in the middle.5. Speaking of docking ... what the hell happened to remote data connections in the future?  Why do I have to physically dock my truck every time I need a new job?  In order to get a new job, I have to physically dock with the station ... and if I want to visit the general goods store ... well I have to undock and then redock at the same station but at a different docking port.  Because apparently stations aren't internally connected.But the actual cargo?  It's all good.  Nobody needs to actually load or unload the cargo containers, just leave it in the space shed outside just kind of floating free.Honestly, I *really* want to love this game.  I really do, I was looking forward to it since I saw the initial reveal trailer.  But the implementation just falls short on so many metrics.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is a pretty cozy truck sim and the environment is great. Change the soundtrack to a cowboy bebop playlist and the aesthetic is on point. Well worth the price.Some annoyances I hope are changed in the future:You have to back in a lot, which is quite satisfying once you get skilled at whipping up to stores and cargo and hitching up easily.  But this gets annoyingly repetitive, an example of how repetitive it is to have to constantly hitch in is: Need some supplies, hitch in to store. Now I need a new job, hitch into job board. Now I need to pick up the cargo, hitch to cargo. Repeat. It makes the game a bit too tedious and i hope they make the job boards places you don't have to hitch. I imagine like a truck rest stop in space would be way better.Also there's no citizenry anywhere in the galaxy. Meaning you're only in the galaxy with other truckers, which is quite boring since I'd love to see other space crafts. Space debris is too common for how clunky the controls are sometimes. _childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty good, still needs a few tweaks and bug fixes. Loading a save with three trailers can cause the trailers to become disconnected and unable to complete the contract. The AI never strays from their path, got hit three times trying to dock at a station and rear ended once using the CB.The dialog is pretty decent as is the voice acting. _childDocuments_.review: The game is really fun so far! I see all the reviews about controls and what not, I played on keyboard and mouse. I didn’t mind, they seem okay to me. I have been enjoying it though. I think my main concern is just that, there isn’t a whole lot to do. Even a simple system where you have to sleep would be cool. I want to utilize the whole truck and have it be more realistic. Some probably won’t agree with that point, or even the next one of having the need to eat, and there being fast food places. Where you go through the drive through and what not. Again, this shouldn’t be the devs top priority, or maybe it shouldn’t be in the game at all, but there’s just so much potential. It really just feels like you deliver cargo and that’s it. Which is fine, it’s a very fun gameplay loop, but at the same time, it feels like it’s just missing something, and can feel a bit dull at times. I’m also just concerned that I’ll play this for a while, get bored, and move on. Overall I do recommend the game. It’s super fun and it’s a cool concept. I’ve enjoyed it a ton so far. So we’ll see what happens with time, if I get bored or if I play this for hundreds of hours.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m absolutely loving this game so far! Personally, I prefer a more relaxed experience with high profits and low consumption, which allows me to focus more on driving and less on the details. The game's initial customization page let me set my play-style up perfectly, making a lot of people's negative reviews (re how often they need to tend to the truck's systems, batteries, etc.) seem minor and not worth taking seriously. I almost didn’t purchase the game because of these reviews, but I’m so glad I trusted my instincts!Here’s my breakdown:Pros:- Immersive experience- Stunning graphics- Fantastic truck sounds, ambiance, and music- Enjoyable trucking gameplay- Controls are simple, but offer complexity when reversing trailers- Mostly bug-free—nothing game-breaking- You can save at any point, no need to wait for a checkpoint- Great to be able to leave the driver’s seat and move around, a rare feature in similar games- Mesmerizing jump-gate animations- Simple map interface with all necessary information- HUD markers are useful- Love the truck dashboard with various controls like power levels, reverse camera, radio, lights, etc.—it boosts the immersion!- The game is highly customizable to suit most players' styles, allowing for both relaxed and challenging experiences.Cons:- Minor bugs, such as when I entered a jump gate and got hit by an asteroid mid-jump, causing $3,000 in damage. Thankfully, I had saved not long before.If the devs create DLCs which add more mechanics and more zones, I will be first to buy them.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: In general the game is not bad, it's well done and once you get used to the mechanics it is cool but it still needs improvement. It has no compatibility with HOTAS controller and there is no way to customize key bindings so you are literally forced to use that brainless keymap in which you use space to accelerate, shift to break, W/S for vertical alignment and based on every other game where you drive something, that is straight non-sense since is not customizable. Another big problem is the "momentum" of the truck, it doesn't work to keep the truck moving at a specific speed so you need to be using cruise control or struggle to keep a constant speed since the last thing you will see in your screen is the speedometer, but every time you are going to do a turn it will eventually throw your cargo to the direction you were going, I’m not a physicist so I don’t know if that’s realistic or not (and tbh, I don’t care, that’s not my job to know) but it’s annoying as hell even in not so high speeds. If it’s a feature, okay, but this lack of consistency makes it annoying even more while driving in the specified space-roads.I have played space-based games for quite some time and not having control of movement in up/down or left/right directions without needing to maneuver the truck going back and forth to reach a gate right below you is weird, if it's a base definition for the game since it's build around those american rigs that has no maneuverability it's fine, but why does we need to reverse dock everything f time we want to do anything? Stores, job listing, customization... everything has its own docking port that requires reverse docking and it's really annoying when you are buying something and want to get a gig and you need to waste time maneuvering just to get to another docking station 10 meters away from where you are already attached to.Speaking of annoying, I don't know if it's a bug or a feature but man those batteries and air filters got me nervous. The batteries once you start the game are crazy expensive and 1 gig allow you to purchase 1 battery, but there are 7 batteries that run out pretty quick if you use the cheap ones (that already cost much) but once you get more done the batteries seem to get cheaper and you can also afford more so it's not a big problem anymore. But the air filters are a different story, at first they are so expensive you can afford it if you keep your batteries replaced properly and after you get able to buy it, they can't be found anywhere in the first 6 systems. Literally every store has no air filter to be bought and you get forced to be rescued, lose a lot of money and once you get rescued and sent back to Atlas Prime the store magically has air filters again. If that's a way of showing how the recovery system works, well it sucks. Btw, air filters were still crazy expensive so I had to get a loan to buy 2 of them, another crazy thing because this was supposed to be a chill game not a "Fight for your life your unemployed slut" game.Another thing that bugs me off is that reverse and brake use the same key. When you are going forward and want to fully break you just need to hold SHIFT and it will eventually completely stop and that's it, but if you are in reverse and you hold SPACE you won't just stop, you are going to start moving forward and that is definitely not a good thing when you are always running out of batteries and air supply and even to sneeze you need to reverse dock somewhere.The game performs well though and has a great future, just needs to be tweaked more.Extra: That first cargo that needs careful handling with those ♥♥♥♥♥♥ controls in a brand new game you don’t know anything about is nerve wrecking, if I was not into this kind of game I would have refunded immediately because that was really stressful for a supposedly chill game.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: A seemingly simple premise that has been realized with much care and detail, Star Trucker feels exactly how you would imagine.While the gameplay loop is extremely repetitive (hauling cargo to your destination), the game somehow manages to make it fun and add enough little mechanics to the process so that you constantly have to worry about other things too.The game tends to lean in the arcade direction (sounds in space, trucks looking like road trucks, etc.) but one aspect that feels very realistic is the penalty system.If you don't fly carefully the game can very quickly become very difficult because of the financial penalties, that are hard to recover from at least early on.This has been addressed by the developer though and might be tweaked.Star Trucker feels like the perfect space delivery driver fantasy, with enough subsystems to give it some extra depth.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to recommend this. I really want to like this... but as it stands the loop is currently too out of whack and needs a re-balance. It bills itself as a Trucking game in space, that is what I feel most people will come to this hoping for - it isn't that. It may want to be that. It may be what the developers intended... but currently it is more about survival. You will spend every single moment of this game struggling to scratch by just trying not to suffocate due to lack of oxygen. Constantly scrambling to barely eek out a living just so you can use whatever moment you have left to just manage to keep your rig space worthy. Here's the loop as it stands: You've hit debri, go out and repair. Your suit is out of oxygen, return to resupply. Your suits air and power supply arelow, get batteries.Your cabin is running low on air try to find somewhere that sells filters in time.You've run out of time to get filters, use your suit to survive until you can find somewhere.Your suit and your supply have run out and you've suffocated -4,000 dollars.Your truck is now refreshed. Now you have the chance to actually do jobs without distraction but you are now facing crippling debt and the possibility of having your truck repossessed in 3 days (lose the game)You've hit debri, repair your truck before you run out of air.Your suit has run out of air. Return to resupply. Wash rinse repeat. You spend so much of your time scrambling around trying to keep your truck and yourself functional that just being able to... you know... deliver stuff for cash is a luxury. And sure "Just don't hit debri" but there is so much of it everywhere, it's kinda hard not to hit debri. It's this constant death loop where you are constantly in debt, facing constant pressure to actually deliver cargo and never having the time to start doing your job. It's so irritating and exhausting. I'd say if you think you'd have more fun spending more time futzing with the components of your Cyclops in Subnautica, where by you'd die if you didn't, than doing anything else in that game - you'll enjoy this. But if you are coming to this looking for truck haulage in space - maybe wait until they reevaluate the loop or if they don't look elsewhere. It's a shame because the aesthetic and everything else is perfect. It's so charming, but it just gets too tiring and frustrating.::EDIT:: I restarted and was tempted to change my review to recommended after really getting into it... Then I reached a mission which requires 3 trailers attached and little did I know saving the game with three trailers attached results in a game breaking bug that will stop progress. This would require me to restart again. Which there is no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ way I'm doing. Hold off on this, it's buggy and unbalanced.::EDIT 2::Alright I'm changing my review to recommended because I'm won over by the sheer charm and quality of it. It's still got some bugs that need to be fixed and some major balance issues but once you get the hang of it it becomes pretty chill and cool.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal game, just the right balance between driving your truck, trading, and maintenance. The driving mechanics feel so satisfying when you learn them. It'll feel floaty at first and you'll feel like you're steering a brick, but what did you expect, the Millennium Falcon? Nah, this is a big rig with rockets duct taped on. And it drives exactly how that sounds like it would. And I wouldn't have it any other way. I love driving around, taking jobs, hauling loads between systems, dropping them off, trading in system, maybe hopping out on EVA to grab some salvage to sell later, buying low, selling high for massive profits, maintaining the truck through batteries, filters, and control circuits, upgrading and servicing it, very fun gameplay loop. The solar provinces are so beautiful too (if a little deadly), the solar storm mechanic is very interesting and challenging to deal with - no spoilers here! Let's just say, try not to immolate yourself.Nice soundtrack, though the radio could use some work, the same songs played over and over get old after 10 hours. Luckily, the ambient music is great.Bad stuff: I will note, this game benefits greatly from watching a beginners guide video or 2. The amount of info the game is simultaneously not enough and waaaaay too much at once. Way too much because it feels like a firehose of information right after the tutorial, with the manual telling you about things like overheating and contraband and other mechanics you have no idea about yet. And not enough because it's all in manual form, not tutorial, so you're expected to read instead of being taught. So watching some beginners guides can really, REALLY help with the enjoyment of the game. Glitches. Oh boy are there some annoying ones. Here are my least favorites: - Core power still drains while docked, just slowly- Pausing for a long time with driver assist on and a trailer attached can cause you to spaz out upon unpause, damaging you and the trailer- AI is DRUNK AS HELL. Seriously, they can and will find ways to ruin your day. And they foot YOU with the insurance bill!- Avoid Haze Way at ALL COSTS. That sector has a terrible glitch where when you make a jump through the New Aspen jump gate, sometimes they're will be something that just WHANGS you, reducing you and your load's health to 0%.  Or at last save before entering it, and don't save while inside it, I think it's a piece of geometry on the other side of the jump gate model that your truck hits. All in all though, those are my only complaints. Game is addicting as hell. Play it!

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game has a great foundation and I've semi-enjoyed playing.... a few glaring issues that I'm faithful the devs can fix. I was playing this on Mechanic mode, in case this matters.Firstly, hull damage. Love-tapping a pebble at about any speed results in at least 50% hull damage and a near-guaranteed breach. This becomes frustratingly repetitive when you go through more challenging systems. The hull really needs to be able to take a beating. It should be doing 20% MAX for such a small object, and that's only if you hit it at about 150. I can understand if you hit a building or massive boulder going a significant speed that it would wreck you, but for right now the damage system is dramatic.Batteries and UCCs. It would be great to have a method for charging batteries while on the ship. I had high hopes that the shock cells (?) would provide a function such as this, but it does not. The batteries have two separate values, health and charge, which implies that you may be able to charge them. I really hope this comes later. Changing difficulties and settings in-game is a MUST for a game like this. There's a lot of balancing playstyle and features to tailor the experience and I really don't want to start a new game every time I want to do this. Lastly, and the most frustrating of all, is the AI traffic patterns. Trucks stopping and U-turning out of nowhere, ramming into you if you dare to slow down or stop to repair a hull breach or change a battery for the umpteenth time in an hour, and you always pick up the bill for it. A few hundred here and there adds up, especially when it's not your fault at all. There needs to be either work with the AI traffic patterns or a system that better detects player fault and maybe even the AI paying you insurance if they hit you. With all of that being said, the concept, art style, and immersion of the radio ads and music are truly brilliant, and I look forward to changing my review to a positive one when improvements are made. Please don't take my comment as negative or bashing, but rather constructive feedback. Thank you devs :)

_childDocuments_.review: Great game if you're looking for a balance between a truck sim and a space survival type game. Beware if you're looking for more of a relaxing or realistic truck sim this isn't it. Most of your money and effort especially towards the start is spent just trying to survive; buying air filters, power cells, etc. and a good amount of time is spent warping system to system instead of actually driving there. However its an amazing game for a casual sim player or someone who's more into the space aspect of the game and isn't looking for the most authentic truck sim out there. Lots of ways to play and make money, skill tree that gives you new abilities and lets you get better cargo contracts, in game economy makes you feel like Milo Minderbinder trading goods system to system for maximum profit while making deliveries. You can also customize and upgrade your truck (but sadly can't buy a new one). Beware the game is new and still has some rough edges. Bugs aren't game breaking but they are there; like skills or bonuses for jobs not applying. First update should be here soon though and kill most of these bugs. Fun game already, but maybe wait for the update so its a smoother experience. Will update comment when patch is released.

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty easy to sum up Star Trucker: it's a trucking simulator in space. You take jobs to pick up cargo from point A and drop it off at point B. You maintain and upgrade your space truck. You buy fuel. Rinse, repeat.The thing that sets Star Trucker apart is the most obvious: the setting. Moving your typical trucking simulator into space changes some of the fundamentals. You're not bound to roads and you don't need to worry about traffic too much. Instead you have to avoid debris and asteroids; shield yourself from solar flares; shield your truck from electrical storms. If you don't properly maintain your truck, the gravity shuts off or you run out of oxygen. The stakes are higher.You can also carry smaller cargo, organized on shelves at the back of your cab (which you have to reorganize if you're in a collision and it all comes flying off the shelf). This lets you make a little cash outside of cargo hauling. You'll occasionally come across beacons that mark cargo spills where you can perform EVAs to collect some of these smaller goods.There's a skill tree that lets you unlock specific types of jobs (fragile goods, oversize loads, long hauls, short times, etc.), and other truckers you perform tasks for to unlock new areas of the map and upgrades, both of which do a good job of slowly increasing the complexity of the game.Overall, it's a great game that's easy to recommend. It improves on the trucking simulator genre and there are things here that I think other spaceflight games could learn from as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I so want to like this game, the graphics are great and the flight is a lot of fun.  However, and its a big one, trying to dock with a station or cargo is a horrible experience.  I have had the benefit (or misfortune) of getting to hitch a rig a couple of times in my life.  even the basic truck with only a simple rearview mirror was more forgiving than this system was to line up.  A system that doesnt provide alignement until you are right on top of the item and a 'generous' alignment setting that still requires almost perfect alignment to have any hope of a connection against a cargo that flys off if you so much as touch it, makes this game too much effort for any kind of enjoyment.  Add to that the cost of goods and the small amount of time your consumables last and you have a game that looks fun but is difficult to enjoy.  I do hope that the docking system becomes simpler or they add an automated option for those of us that want to just enjoy the game, as well as make it so that the player can at least break even on a trip, i would be willing to try this again.  But for now, its only for those who have a really good 2d spatial sense or can spend hours lining up a cargo.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello there, dear devs, one of the star truckers on the phone here! Got some thing to say after 5 hours of playtime, though most of them are complains, there will be a talk about upsides, I promise.And let's start with them right away. First, theme - it is handled really well. The levels do be looking marvelous, as well as the textures with the low-poly style. I really enjoy the wiew outside the window during the rides on the road, sometimes maybe a bit too much to hear a loud horn somewhere up front.Second would be optimization - great job on that, my Asus Vivobook Pro 15 runs the game on highest settings with no problems, though I have not encountered midgame levels yet, and might feel some freezes here and there in the future, but overall it's really good. And thanks for not taking much space with the game files too, love ya indie developers for that.Third, comes the music - the radio addition to a car (spaseship?) game is always the right choise, and the tracks are nice too. Not all that relaxing, we don't want to sleep on the road, so the punchy beats of rock-n-roll hit you in times of need on a trip with a nice slam.Fourth is localization. Thanks a lot for adding russian and other languages into the game. I am not considering myself to be bad with english, but it's definitely nice to see your native words being used for terms you're truying to understand and learn. Big shoutout for that.This is all great features, even if they aren't special. Doing things right is much more than truying to stand out. But now I will have put my complains on the table. I will not be bragging, as the game does interest me a lot and I will stay with the community it forms for the brighter tomorrow, and I hope my vision of this product will be taken into account of further development to improve the game and make it more accessible and enjoyable.First will be the difficulty, out of which my choise was normal. I am not against the game being challenging, but here I feel like some aspects just outrigt crawl behind and strangle you out from nowhere when you least expect it (sometimes literally, talking about em filters here). My first game started with me delivering the tutorial cargo to the delivery point, when I accidentally lost control for a moment and apparently hit the trunk too much. After detaching the container, I was greeted with a summing up screen, on which my salary of 500 or so bucks was owertrown with a penalty of 573. At least I didn't had to cover the expences this once, but later I also got hit by a meteior on a great speed, and from that point on, my run was basically doomed. With not enough cash, broken truck, broken cargo and energy running low, no guide book was able to save my ass - I made about 2 more trips, broke my spase truck completely and started a fresh game. Of course, this all can be called a skill issue, and I will try to give it doublethough myself after playing on easy and custom difficulties, but in my eyes this is not how a game about delivering cargo should feel on normal difficulty. I read a rewiev form a fella who played hardcore and reached lvl8, and he mentioned filters and energy being huge problems, as saving money for them on that stage seemed impossible, so he ended up softlocking himself on a same state with not enough supplies to continue playing. Please, think about the game from the perspective of all the newcomers and try to do something about balancing the skill floor for an average novadays gamer. Oldies still got hardcore and custom to play around, so this should be fair enough.Second complain (much less detailed, I promice) is thecontrols - I do understand that this is also a skill issue type of a problem, but the feel of what we got now is just too cluncy to be enjoyable even during learning process. Movement in 3D enviroment in all the directions is a rare example in videogames of first-preson experiences, and there's a reason for that. There is a 3rd person to assist this problem, but I am personally assured that I must be able to handle all the thing from inside the cab if I want to.Third, (here comes my personal neatpick) it seems that the world is quite empty. Yes, this is space, but inhabitet space. It would be nice to see (em, maybe there is some of thoose things on mid and late game levels, sorry if I go ahead of myself, sorry if so) some parking lots outside, more sighns, neon add banners and more transport types. Maybe space stations containing towns, which you're able to see underneath the fibre glass. More background action, like occasional starfalls, nebulas and black holes, or some big ships jumping in and out the hyperspace. This is all for the future, of course, as the game is raw enough now to think more of the next occrance.Fourth: bugs. Not a lot of them I encountered, but the ones which were here are good enough to be concerning. Like that one time I went out for the lost cargo, only to find out half of it got stuck in the texture walls and cannot be retrieved. Or that time when I put the container on the untaken bedshelf, then opened it, and then it refused to close because the to got stuck in the ceeling. I am hoping that this will be the priority of your work for now, even if I wish for thing uptop to be worked on as well.Fifth, and final for now, another neatpick: radio adds. They feel too real. I hate them IRL, and I sertanly do not enjoy them more in my videogames. Please, make an option to disable them.And, this is all for now. Gotta go sleep, so will end it quick: I like the game, and the overall score for me is positive, but there is a lot to be done, and I'm counting on you guys. Best of luck, and see you around, space truckers!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: the first 5 or so hours you trick yourself into thinking its a skill issue "that is why i keep crashing". then all the shops run out of batteries and you realise the one spare air filter you had is used up and they costs more than an hour of trying to get the lest useful controls to work for you. plenty of revues are like "give it some time its just a skill issue" this isn't a fromsoft game, i wanted to truck around space looking at cool stuff listening to a book or podcast, i cant do that cos the controls require that much concentration because one little mistake and your suddenly in 6k of debt on a load that has a max profit of 2k. and half the time that mistake is all the local shops are out of batteries and your O2 generator is spluttering cos the last place you were also had no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ battery's.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be fooled, this is survival horror hell at it's worst not some cosy truck sim. If you have debt in real life, prepare to escape into a world where you have even worse debt. I've asphyxiated in my cockpit twice because I couldn't afford air filters and was charged a small fortune for the ambulance call-out. I was sometimes afraid to leave the station because my truck couldn't hold a vacuum and I didn't want to die in space, but then realised air isn't free on stations either. I grinded a few hours to try and pull myself out of debt all the while being heckled over the radio by the local truckers and their quirky side missions which playfully waste your time while you accrue more debt. I ended up getting my truck re-possessed only 57 space bucks away from clearing my overdraft and had to start a new game. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Its definitely a lot harder than it looks. Piloting a giant rig in the vacuum of space is a whole different beast and can feel like your driving on ice if you're trying to turn while going too fast due to having nothing to stop your inertia other than your dampeners. It's a really fun and unique experience though especially with the cassette futurism art style and the literal space trucks that can look like space trains half the time when you watch the ai drivers slink around the void of space, the space highway signs are a nice touch too and helps form this games identity into something I wanna see explored more. onto my gripes however mostly with the way the ai trucks. I've found myself having to reload a save a couple of times now due to the ai crippling my truck and my cargo after flying into me which usually happens to me after arriving at purity. The game just came out so I know there is 100% a few things that'll be tweaked later down the line and I'm hoping the issue of getting rear ended is going to be one of those fixes. But hey it could be a feature for all I know, bad drivers do exist. Also I've found that the game penalizes me for careless driving even though I am doing everything I can do drive save so I'm not sure what I'm doing wrong. On a lot of the pseudo highways passing trucks tend to blare their horns at me and I'm not sure why and it makes me feel like I'm driving carelessly as every time this has happened I've gotten penalized for careless to which makes me frustrated and leaves me wondering what I'm doing wrong. These two things could be completely underrated and for all I know honking could be trucker language for hello but I digress. Overall the game has been a blast so far but also fairly challenging mostly due to my own mishaps but other than that I absolutely adore the unique cassette futurism aesthetic this game has and it inspires me to get creative and make worlds with something as silly as space trucks because they look cool and its fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I've played plenty of first person space ship games and the this one feel awful to control as there is no up, down, left or right movement it feels like your flying a really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ car in space instead of being a space truck something which is designed to travel in space also when i was lining up for docking maybe a meter or 2 away from the lock point some dinky space car rammed into the side of my rig and i got fined (which cost all of the money i just made on the contract before docking) for it despite the fact that i was not at fault and in a docking area it feels like an extremely lazy implementation of other trucking games fine system for when you dump stuff with no gauge for if the ai is doing something it shouldn't, so as it stands i cannot recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a fun game. First, you can play at your pace. If you want to play the balanced mode where you have to juggle fuel, maintenance and haulage then you can. If you want to do one or the other then you can do that too. Really unique idea that takes both space games and trucking combining the two. Looks great. Bit of stuttering but not game breaking by any means. Fully recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: i'm enjoying it but be warned, it feels like a pre-release title, not a finished one.   They need to balance the constant need to replace all the batteries and mother boards with their availability(in the normal difficulty mode.)  That mechanic is much too involved since it's a cargo hauling game, not a battery changing game but you spend more time doing that off the bat than hauling cargos.   It also seems that every time I need something I can't get it... every shop should have a supply of air scrubbers, controllers, and energy cells...  There also needs to be a point to making money because even though the game is visually appealing and the core mechanic of hauling cargo is fun... there isn't much else.   I'd give it a 6 right now, out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly a good experience, feel like its only going to get better.A few highlights are: being able to choose the experience you want, be it hard and fast, red lining your engines the whole way, or nice and slow, getting your cargo there in one piece, often with a nice bonus that comes with it.The maintenance side of the game is pretty well thought out and its rewarding to learn and understand and i found it fairly engaging, trying to squeeze that last bit of power to get to the next stop or pulling something from one less important system to keep things together.customization is very nice, a small drawback is not being able to change the color scheme on company liveries you can make your Rig look how you want it too, and the incremental upgrades are nice too. though I wish they didn't need to be serviced so often, Especially the structural components, but it is rewarding to have something that can hit an asteroid 10 times my rigs size at 200 mph and only be Inconvenienced by it... still need to get it fixed, just, Later instead of Now.Characters are better then expected, find them to be rather interesting and somewhat relatable which is Not what i expected to find, voice acting is also rather charming. a Surprising but Very welcome plus.Overall i'd give this game a 10/10. there is always room for improvement but for what it is now I like it.Keep up the good work M&M team!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Id like to start by saying that this is a very good chill game. Ive enjoyed the feeling of both the simplicity of moving from one place to another, combined with multiple things I need to keep track of to make the game engaging. However, a few things would hopefully change in the future to make this a great game. Mainly the damage to items in the truck. There's no way that an object getting dropped from the shop into the truck, or placing it on the ground normally causes it damage at all. Just a bit harsh. All other damage to myself and to my truck however is my fault for going 200km/h into avoidable space junk.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: My feet are up, i'm sunk into the couch with an xbox remote in hand. 6 Hours later I realize it's 4am and I have to work in 4 hours. It was worth it and I did it again the next night, and then I did it again.I have a penchant for games like this. But this game, this game takes it to a whole new level. The first 10 hours my cab was an absolute mess, barely making ends meet. Robbing Peter to pay Paul. Things flying everywhere. I WAS CHALLENGED!This game is as hard or as easy as you want it to be. If you want a little spice; you know where to find it. If you wanna play it cool you can. If you have some full batteries and filters and got the time to trade and make some profit; DO IT!!!!I made 12k my first big trade run, upgraded my rig and stocked up on supplies and then went into debt and did it again while making even more cash. I Ain't scared of nuttin now.I'm just getting into the enigma territories and I can't wait for the hell that awaits me there.This is a great game. The value is phenomenal and I CANNOT give enough thanks to the crew that made this possible. If I could write a 1,000,000 more positive reviews I would.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Needs work.  Slow and not super balanced, even during the early game, which is more tutorialized.  There's a lot of subsystems that are all fun to manage, but the overall experience doesn't seem to gel out of the various cool ideas.  Not recommended right now, but will give it another shot.Edit: The standard mode needs balance tweaks, but the custom mode lets you get something that works a lot better.  Lowering battery drain and bumping payouts goes a long way to deal with the battery + air filter balance issues.  It's too bad you can't modify the settings after starting the game, because it really feels like you have to tweak it to get the experience you want.There's QoL issues as well, minor gripes but a lot of little friction points.  You can't turn lights on while not in the chair, or check the map in the job listing screen.  You have to dump items out of boxes before you can sell them, and go to the airlock in order to reopen the store / job interface.  Salvage would be more fun without constant airlock travels (even using a box, because lots of things don't fit in the boxes).It's still really slow, but that's probably what you want for this style of game.  I'd enjoy some upgrades for auto driving on the highways and auto docking / alignment, which would make this a bit more like elite.  No joystick controls if that's a critical decision maker, but mouse and keyboard controls worked fine for me.With the initial difficulty options set up correctly, I think this is a recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: the first problem when you play the game arrises with the powercells, without these your truck isnt working, however, the drain is MASSIVE and no way to recharge this except form buying it. second of all, to get a good fundamental grasp you are over 2h of gameplay so its already outside the steam refund policy, third, there is no way to contact the devs trough social media except an e mail, which makes asking question and getting answers a pain to deal with
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic. love the cab, everything is functional / great diagetic design/ layout. Its easy to interact with while giving you lots of information and also feeling like you have power/control. (CIG/star citizen could really learn from this!) the atmosphere is great. Only thing i don't like at the moment is the scenery is a bit too dark and the batteries are a bit too short lived in the standard mode. but these could be easily patched later. This game is already great and has a lot of potential! (obviously truck variants, more locations, challenges, maybe walkable truck stop bars) Love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I'm going to be real, the game is good for a short bit of fun but whoever came up with the 'just in time' deliveries is actually insane. The idea that if you arrive too early for your delivery you can't do anything for 20-30 minutes is genuinely poor game design, there is a bed in the truck that could have been used to allow the player to speed time up or at least as a truck stop that can be used to let the player pass time without expending fuel or core energy. It's such a bad game mechanic that has actually killed my motivation to play any further.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: The game offers an immersive space-trucking experience with stunning visuals and solid gameplay, and personally, I’ve really enjoyed my time with it. The game excels at creating atmospheric space environments and a sense of adventure, but the mission variety and trading system are limited, which can make the gameplay feel repetitive over time. The controls can also be a bit clunky in certain areas.Overall, it's a promising start, but the game needs more variety, a few balance tweaks, and complexity to fully realize its potential in the space-simulation genre. VR support, combined with HOTAS compatibility, would be a highly desired feature and could make the experience even more immersive.A personal note to the developers: I truly appreciate the effort and creativity you’ve put into the game. I’m excited to see how the game evolves with future updates and hope it grows into something truly awesome. Keep up the great work! <3
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: So far a pretty fun game. Relaxing, except at 150 mph drifting sideways to avoid another truck while doing a barrel roll to miss some debris. Gasping for O2 because you were too busy with a cold one in your hand and hammering down to get a load to its destination on time. I must have all your batteries! I have not ran into major issues so far besides self inflicted. Only thing I have to say is silly AI drivers, watch out they will straight run you over.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Game loop is quite fun; pickup cargo, drop off cargo.  Next you should refuel and switch out your power supplies with a local store.  If you run into stuff you have to do field repair.  If you continue to hit too much stuff you have to get the truck repaired which means you have to go way out of your way.  Backing up is of course challenging in space, but not difficult if you are not hauling anything.  Very pleased with the purchase at nearly full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I brought this game as a joke, as I wanted to drive faster in euro truck sim and a friend suggested this as a joke and wow im in love.Good PointsThe visuals are amazing, warp gates send you to unique, interesting and different environments. The music is perfect! GameplayYou can trade items, run illegal items for trading or transport illegal cargo, you can transport legal cargo (obviously), keep your rig maintained from 02 leaks and component break down, choose between taking the longer safer road ways or risk getting hit by debris fields flying straight to the drop off points. A good balance of risk and reward.Bad PointsI will admit, when I started playing I choose 'Recommend' and the game felt more like a Hardcore survival game rather then a truck sim game, but I restarted and started a custom game with the rewards for jobs turned to High and components drain to low and its a lot more chill now. but the difference from low to medium is pretty insane, especially when the game felt to be very hands off with showing you all the parts of your truck that could go wrong and even when you are recovered they don't fix your rig which confused me at first as it felt like the rig was perfect again, turns out it gives you about 5 to 10 minutes to go to a shop and replace the broken parts, problem is the game doesn't tell you this. so there is a lot of trial and error. So I did have to abandon my first save due to being in so much debt and never being able to work it off, due to the rewards for jobs being so low, also If you fail a job, you have to pay DOUBLE the amount you would have been paid to completing the job which is insane. Also if you did the medical cost £4000 so if you die during a £4000 mission, then you will have to pay £4000 for medical and another £8000 for the contract fail, also if you bust up your rig then you can add another £3000 on top of that (£15000 total). And to try and come back from that while also trying to keep all the components up and running is impossible.Takes till your second play/ or restart to start having fun.RecommendationsIf I could change anything about this game, is to give the player more hand holding at the start of the game, yeah I know there is a manual but when the rig is beeping at you and your screen is going black, the last thing on your mind is to sit in the drivers seat and pull out the manual, I do love the idea of a manual I just never used it.Also the difference between medium component drain to low is insane, When I was first play it felt like every 5mins I had dead Batts or air filters needing changing, In my new run on low setting I have only changed 1 batt in 2 hours of game play which doesnt seem right at all.Maybe make the contract fail fee less, as its crushing enough that you dont get paid.I cant wait for more customisation for the rigs, like bobble heads and hula girls!Long story short, Great game especially now I have found out it was made by 2.5 people. But Medium difficulty is too annoying and hard. While easy is just too easy.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: It's Trucking but in space!exactly what you imagined it would look like when you were 10!Truck handles well, but a bit 'floaty' when turning at speed, exactly what you would expect.at time of writing customization of the Truck is fairly minimal (4 parts with many items each and a paint pattern with 3 parts to change color) but shows promise.double and triple trailers are available but only as a preset for some of the runs, so you can't pick 2 single trailer jobs going the same way and link them, hopefully something they will improve in the future.in game radio plays some great tunes!10/10 concept7/10 execution with room to improve

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game and love the style of it. I feel that i am going to play this game for a long time, but i feel as if there are two things the game needs. One is mulitplayer I would love to play this game with my pals and chat over the intercom of our rigs. And second thing is they need to add like a highway or something like that because the way it is now there is no like traveling long distance it feels as if it copying the feel of local hauling.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Great game that just needs some more time and love from the players, especially those who have given up wayyyy too early on it. Yes there are issues, but not game breaking/ruining ones, and here's to hoping development is smooth sailing from here. Also, imo, this game deserves so many more players :(To preface: yes, I played the demo and loved it so maybe I'm a bit biased here, but I'll do my best to stay neutral. Also, I don't have many hours yet of course but have played a good bit since launch 3 days ago.I'm not gonna lie, I was worried; demos are great but you're never quite sure how the actual game will turn out.  I'm happy to say that this game did not disappoint for me. Between the different game modes and straightforward gameplay I'm still enjoying the crap out of this game! I love the maintenance mechanic so you're not locked in to only driving and it's great that I can see all the statuses for my truck from the drivers seat. I love the compactness and quick turn around for the game early on, it made it so easy to get the hang of things and I can easily see haul times getting longer, if you want, as you unlock zones. I also love that fact that I can hop on and off this game whenever I want. It's such a chill and simple game that doesn't stress me out so I can play it for 15 minutes or 2 hours. Finally, big vehicle go brrrrr so my brain is happy lol :)I've seen a lot of people complaining in these discussions, and yes there are bugs. I mean what new game doesn't have them? This doesn't bother me though, because there's not an insane amount of them and none are too game breaking. For example, one of the worst I've seen/read about right now is that you can't take free cases from salvages due to them and their contents disappearing later. No this isn't great but I can live without it for now because it doesn't ruin the core gameplay at all. I'll be honest, these are gonna be cheesy, but I love the idea of the CB radio and talking to the convoy members, however I don't like the lack of direction. The options making it a "choose your own story" are really cool but I wish I had context for each, like just a bit of small text or something from the AI explaining the situations better. Another complaint of mine is the lack of ability to see market prices or job boards outside the specific sites, like I'm sorry but we got galactic highways and expressways that we basically teleport to but no way to communicate outside the sites?Lastly, is my issue with the lack of tutorial/explanation of game systems. Yeah there's a manual in the glove box below the dash, but I didn't know it was there for the first 2 hrs so I had to figure out repairs and such on my own for things not in the tutorial. (Also, UCC statuses don't show % in the dash :()What I really don't understand is why people are complaining about power drain and money management for the recommended game setting, I've read so many people saying things wear out too quick and loads don't pay enough. Well I'm sorry but in my experience this just isn't true. Proper management of resources just takes some planning, and no much at that! Through (mostly) careful driving I've consistently kept my rig running while getting my cash up to 5000+ multiple times now. I've been able to afford extra cases, parts, body work, upgrades, etc. and this is even while I've fully wrecked my hull about 3-5 times already!I love the game and it reminds me of playing things like farming simulator where you can change settings to make it smooth sailing or high maintenance or somewhere in between. Any way you play it though it's a game which I find very nice to, no pun intended, space out and chill in. Also, as someone who likes space games I like the idea of taking more mundane earth'based activities into space, because why not?! Yes the game has issues and it certainty isn't perfect or 100% complete, but it's good for what it is and it's not grossly overpriced or anything either. Another thing, people need to give this game some more time, not everyone is gonna like it but it's great for what it is!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks so good it's accidentally tricking normies into buying a trucking sim game - one literally marked 'Automobile Sim' with user tags - and then they leave negative reviews whinging about how 'tedious' the game about... hang on let me check my notes... driving a truck can be. It really does seem like there's a disconnect as people who are hearing about the game purely through hype/content creators are simply hopping on the bandwagon and then realizing they aren't the right kind of neurodivergent to genuinely enjoy a game about balancing survival mechanics and doing a good job delivering a trailer of cargo from one place to the other.Sorry, neurotypicals, for once us autistics get a pretty game. It'll be fine. Gentle jabs aside: I have been following development of this by following Monster and Monster on TikTok for what feels like over a year at this point. I was well aware of what state the game was in at launch. I had a bit more caution going in. I've also seen the 'discussion' about balance. Frankly, I don't see the issue. I picked Recommended knowing it's a trucking sim, and guess what, it does a pretty good job of simulating the premise of being a trucker. Truckers are constantly balancing buying consumables and doing a job where if you even slightly mess up, you incur thousands of dollars in fines. It has problems. I've jumped into a system where, just as the game gives back control of the truck, it glitches location so the truck clips the ring and completely destroys the trailer. Manually save at the beginning of each job/mission you take, save every now and then if you do multiple jumps, and genuinely have a think about what kind of experience you want before initially picking your difficulty. You'll be fine.The in-game music is amazing. I love their commitment to having an entire bespoke soundtrack of in-universe songs. The voice acting feels on par with the characterization you experience in A Day of Maintenance or Hardspace: Shipbreaker. Well worth the money IF this is the kind of game you'd like. There's very little to the game the trailers does not explicitly communicate. There is no clever twist that, actually, it's a trucking game with combat. It's just a trucking game with the flavor of an extra axis of control over the truck.

The truck movements are slow, take some getting used to but once you're accustomed with it its very pleasant. The visuals and graphics are very original and very pleasant. It's a bit grindy still and I can see myself getting bored in like 10 hours maybe but I'm still at the beginning and haven't explored all the (masterfully crafted) map. _childDocuments_.review: I like it. _childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was an in-between thumbs up/down vote, cause this game is neither good or bad. It just feels that it missed the most important thing that makes logistics fun in the eyes of a trucker. Hear me out:The game itself looks good, the concept is brilliant, the ability to go first person and into EVA mode right in space is great as well... so why the negative?The heart of all haulers is the journey, its the things you see along the way, the different highways, the changing weather, the traffic and ultimately, the satisfaction that you've done a longhaul and have made it there after a long drive which felt eventful, challenging yet rewarding. This game has a bit of everything, but its missed the long haul part. These journeys between stars are simply taking the gates... then Yay you've arrived at the next system within a few seconds. Now go park your load and be done with the mission.... WHAT?? thats it? what about the traffic? What about asking for docking permission? What about being assigned a parking/landing bay?? what about having the ability to swap out your truck to a different model? none of these are in the game as far as i can tell.For a true space trucking game, one must take a look at a few other games which gives a sense of belonging and immersion. How about adding the following:1. Piracy - This is sooooooooo needed in a space logistics game where the player is only tasked with delivery. Give the players the option to choose different routes, do they want to take high security (Where police roams) space or risk it by delivering faster going through dodgy space where the player has a chance of being targeted by pirates. Delivering early earns them more money and reputation. Allow the player to upgrade the trucks with light defense systems like auto turrets or armor plates... later through research, the ability to turn their truck into a blockade runner meaning their warp drives can't get jammed by pirates.2. Freedom to chose - You give them a mission to pickup and deliver cargo from system A to system B... its up to the player to legitimately deliver these cargo and earn rep, or risk it and sell it to the market earning them more money but losing heaps of rep with the faction giving them the job. Make it that they can be bountied by the police.3. Less than legal contracts - Make some contracts high reward, but high risk, asking the player to deliver cargo from System A that resides in high security space to a destination system B that resides in lawless space. Some of these contracts are setup to scam the player of its money, but if the player can deliver the cargo there, then Big big big rewards.This would've given this logistics game a sense of space trucking with its own uniqueness spill that to be honest, is already in a lot off other space games that isn't centred around logistics. Even the earliest iteration of Elite Dangerous's courier missions seems more interesting and somewhat rewarding than this. Not saying its a bad game cause the concept here is there, it just needs a good core and reason for players to continue delivering, tempt them to do the wrong thing and reward them for resisting, attract them to take dangerous contracts and spice things up with pirates or illegal goods which can get scanned by police... forcing them to take less than safe routes... you know the spill.GL with the development guys, if any of these features are added in the future, then ... I'll be back.

_childDocuments_.review: This is NOT a space truck driving simulator.  It is a space truck maintenance simulator.  As others have stated the economy is brutal.  Not made any easier by the DUI (Difficult User Interface).  ETS2 and ATS are not in danger from this title.  The real charm of this game is in the story.  But the maintenance costs make the process of making money and upgrading your truck a brutal challenge that, IMHO, ruins the drive a truck vibe.  Your futuristic truck could desperately use a satnav system.  Finding your way safely through a system is at best a challenge in and of itself.  God forbid you drift off the well beaten path, you'll damage your truck and the cargo costing you money you can ill afford.  Money both in terms of bonus pay outs, penalties and repair costs.Maintenance is what really kills you.  Apparently I can fill my truck with fuel, but a generator is technology outside the reach of the future.  Because you are in constant need of buying and replacing batteries.  IF you can find them at a reasonable price a 100 charge battery is $500, 150 charge battery is $1000.  Yeah, 50% more go juice for 100% more price.  Don't let the battery drain completely either, lose core power and you are now on a ballistic path to a crash and costly repairs.   This is all assuming you can actually find some batteries.  I just replaced 4 of my critical battery systems,  pulled into a shop and there wasn't a battery to be found.  Air Filters?  You need those too.  4 of them.  At $2500 each.  I got a few thousand stashed in the bank, thinking maybe I could stop and invest in a truck upgrade, but then I had to replace 2 air filters and some batteries, plus some UCC modules and I was down to $300.  So you better hope you can actually find what you need WHEN you need it at the best prices otherwise those prices can soar even higher.  Did I mention your truck breaks and the components wear out at an alarming rate.  Batteries for the gravity system go so fast you end up having to buy extra batteries just keep your stuff from flying all over the cabin.   And then the UCC fails and your stuff goes flying anyway.   And something is CONSTANTLY failing.  Would be fun to just be able to drive the truck, but honestly you spend all your time in the stores, or making repairs.  The couple of miles you drive on a delivery is an all too welcome break that doesn't happen enough.  You drive a couple miles to a gate, jump to a system, drive a couple miles to a gate, jump to a new system, drive a couple miles, drop cargo and done.  And in that time you consume hundreds of dollars worth of fuel, because $1000 of fuel is only good for about 50 miles.  I REALLY wanted to like this game, but I'm not masochistic enough to truly enjoy it.  And mind you, I have managed to mostly avoid the worst aspects of the punishing penalties for failure.  I had an NPC truck make a U-turn right in front of me once, with no chance to avoid the crash it cost me my entire delivery payout, an entire battery for my suit to make repairs and then costs of repairs.  In that instance I just killed my game and started over.  I can't imagine ever getting out of debt.  Save often and scum is probably your best option.  I really shouldn't HAVE to save scum to overcome a poorly balanced experience that fails to reward success.

_childDocuments_.review: What a fun game! It has the feel of "Tin Can" resource management, "ATS" early trucking gameplay when you are just squeaking by to make it down the road, and a whole lot of just chill and play a game vibes.In my most humble opinion for this review, you'll be best served by this game IF you play the game by its rules for a while BEFORE you go off to explore and make your own. The game itself is not terribly hard (on the "recommended" start settings), but it rewards patience. If you treat the game with respect and let the content come to you, you'll likely find a smooth and enjoyable ride out here in the stars.On the flip side, this game will punish the player if you rush to get to new content/zones or equipment unlocked. You don't need those things until you unlock them. And you are not forced to unlock them until you have the funding to back it up,However, one of the "problems" with the game, that many players run into, is that the new zones are locked behind story missions, and these missions can be BRUTAL. This is not a terrible mechanic in and of itself, but the game gives the player cues that say, "go do this thing," very early on in the game to get them progressing in short order. However, the cues don't slow down one the initial "tutorial phase" has run its course and the player is left with missions in their log. While this helps the player know they CAN continue on, it also draws the player towards content that they are not ready to handle (I'm speaking here from a purely in-game resource/economic point of view--player skill is usually not the problem once they learn the controls).And that's why, I believe, that this game has a "Mostly positive" rating. It is missing some design elements that would help the player know WHEN they are more likely to be ready to move on, in favor of saying, "if you move on now, you get more things!" This leaves the player fearing that they are missing out but when they try to get to the content they fail or suffer in game consequences that feel unfair and are left feeling helpless or unprepared quite early on--which makes the game feel "bad" to play.(We're not white-knighting here. There are things that need to be fixed and balanced, but this game is better than the reviews might lead you to believe.) Mostly, you'll see a lot of people complaining about money problems and the resource costs.There certainly needs to be balancing for delivery payouts (to align them with salvage work AND to have short runs balanced against long runs which do not pay out as well as they should) but this can all be mitigated if you take the game slow, drive carefully, and manage your resources. We all want to drive the long-haul long trailer rides...but we've got to earn it to get there.In short, if you want a positive vibe with this game early on, it would be my humble recommendation to play the game as a short-haul "one day's run" trucker for a good long while. Just go out there taking small jobs before moving on in the game. Spend some time getting into the world, building up your experience and your bank account via many more short deliveries over a longer period of time--treat it more as a role-play experience than a driving/action game.Doing this, you'll never need to buy a full tank of gas, thereby saving tons of money, and you'll make small amounts of money more frequently while using relatively small amounts of resources. This will create a "snowball effect" and you'll be happier as you see successes piling up instead of hitting a brick wall. It will also mitigate the costs of making mistakes like slamming into debris (or a highway sign--ask me how I know :D )Yes, of course you'll be itching to go out into the world--but if you take it slow you'll be ready when you finally do get out there.That's more than enough jawing. The game is fantastic! Buy it, learn it, and get on truckin'!

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like this game is going to have the same discourse around it that Elite Dangerous has. Having diegetic systems is always a plus in my books, being able to manually press all the buttons and know that they all have a function is a great and satisfying feeling. The less UI on my screen the better. You'll be driving and zooming all over the place but try to stick to the space highway lest you feel your Struck needs extra debris decorations embedded on the hull.Similarly when playing other hauling games you'll definitely be wanting to put on your favourite podcast while you fly from point A to B. You can have some really long flights in this.Only criticism I have is that there's only one station for the radio which if you're not a fan of country music then you'll probably be playing with it turned off for the whole game.

_childDocuments_.review: It didn't take long for this game to fall short for me. It feels "confused" as to what it wants to be and has a bunch of gameplay and design issues that ultimately made me decide to refund. I enjoy truck driving sims (for some reason I don't even understand) and space adventure games, so I figured this would be a home run but I was disappointed. Everything is a manual lever to do anything which for a simulation game, I would expect. However, the game is also in a fantasy futuristic world and setting and it seems completely unbelievable to me that in the far flung future of space trucking, there would not be more automation. We are already, right now in 2024, looking at how to automate the trucking industry in many ways. I'm not talking about self-driving either, I'm just saying, why do I need to pull a lever to engage a mag lock to dock? Shouldn't the docking station be doing that? Why do I need to pull a lever to go through a warp speed tunnel or whatever it's called? Can't I just drive into it when it's ready and active? If you have any vision impairment at all, you might as well skip this game. I am far-sighted and have a pretty low prescription for near "things" but I'll be damned if I could ever find the road/highway with any true accuracy. Sometimes there's gigantic arrows pointing you in. Other times I had no clue if I was on the highway or not. If you go off the highway you get hit by debris. If they are going to penalize players for going off course, they should at least make it so the highway course is WAY more obvious to see and be on. Also, z-axis control should be somehow locked in or have less impact in small movements if you are on the highway. Being able to move up and down inside the highway lanes is totally pointless unless you are trying to enter or exit from those angles. That aspect needs a lot of help, again, not looking for self-driving here but just a little more indication where the hell I even am.To support that above issue with the highways, let me also say the camera sucks. If you're hoping switching to external cam will help you when you get flipped around, it doesn't. It feels like when N64 was new and game designers / devs were still trying to figure out how to make 3D camera controls work well. So in addition to having no idea where I'm driving to, the camera is of no help at all and as difficult to control as the truck, which leads to my next issue.The truck drives like brick ♥♥♥♥-house. I get that they are giving you a feeling of inertia and weight and you have to plan your turns and such but it's really over exaggerated. Again, thinking of the far flung future, and simulation... there is no way in my mind that for futuristic sim realism, a vehicle like this would not be better outfitted with better/stronger means to control acceleration, deceleration, and maneuverability. Maybe you can upgrade your truck later with this stuff but it was not playable for me, out of the box. I only played like 45 minutes so maybe this is an unfair judgement but overall it lacked the "feel" of a roadtrip like you might get from ATS or ETS. You jump through warp tunnels to locations. Sometimes you need to do several jumps to get to your ultimate destination. There's not really a time that I could see where you're just cruising space and going past planets, nebulas, oort clouds, and whatever. I just expected this game to feel more like that rather than a jump from hub to hub. I never even got to a salvage mission so maybe it's there that this happens but I also don't love the idea of doing salvage missions. That sounded just, not fun at all to me. Really all of the above just immediately sapped the "fun" out of it which was the reason I chose for my refund.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Despite having thrusters in the appropriate positions, your truck can only go forward, backward, or rotate in place. Lining up your maglock to pick up a trailer, visit a shop, or pick up a mission is needlessly difficult and takes way too much time because of that, all the while your fuel and batteries are draining at breakneck speed. Without access to thruster control there's also no way to manually stabilize yourself, so you're forced to use the auto stabilization which you cannot toggle without having the camera inside the cab and looking down past the dashboard to press the button.Aside from the infuriating controls (and no way to remap them), there is space junk littered everywhere that isn't a "road", including directly in the path of you getting from the road to many destinations, like a dropoff, and the space junk is nearly impossible to see from any of the available camera angles.It's not fun to struggle against poor game mechanics that are intentionally designed that way to artificially increase the difficulty.
