_childDocuments_.review: From the get go the clunky controls and maneuverability leave something to be desired. Nothing about this game is intuitive, nor does it feel like a proper space game. Controlling the space truck is all over the place, and trying to align the truck to go anywhere relative to where you want is nothing but a tedious chore. I was expecting more from this game in terms of what I initially thought it was going to be. I wanted to be a space truck driver, and this game did not deliver. You think ATS was bad with acceleration? This game makes ATS feel like you're playing GTA. There is almost no acceleration when it comes to driving forward, and the random drift on your truck is annoying to say the least. Overall the story is okay, and the graphics are also alright, but when you have beautiful space games with better controls, ala NMS, Star Citizen, and hell even Starfield, you are left with a lot to be desired. I was excited for this game, now I am not that is all.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Looks promising in the first hours, but dont exprect it to be a content beast. At least not in early phase. Basically you fly from A to B ... As I am very interested in such cozy trucker simulations, and space, this is a nice game for me. I am very interested in how the game develops further as its a good base. For people that dont like to repair that much and change components too often, there is a difficulty level. Sure you get less money if you play on lower levels with less technical issues, but I mean thats fair, as the technical issues cost you much of it usually. Like the "balancing" method. And the BEST is, that in current state it runs in 30fps on Steam Deck from the scratch, Played it even with Viture One Pro XR Glasses on the deck ... totally fine, just some texts are a bit too small.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant setup, good balancing and a novel take on the hauling business simulator. Making free-roam more than just driving your vehicle around. Challenging regions with unique issues to navigate, a simulator trucking tree that you'd expect from such games, and to top it off a little narrative driven plot to open up new regions and not make you feel you're the only one roaming about in space.Get out of your seat, get out of your cabin (don't forget to put on a space suit) and get right back in your seat to get the heck out of dodge! Comprehensive systems, realistic integrated systems that require components to help stay alive and on the floor in a space vehicle.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. Been waiting for a logistics sim in space for QUITE some time, and I'm loving it. It's a hybrid of simulator and arcade-ish... so don't go in expecting hyper realistic thrust vectoring. This game is meant to feel like driving a big rig in space with U.S. road design and laws... and they pull that off BEAUTIFULLY! Give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Let me state first: I do love this game. Coming as someone who still holds Elite: Dangerous as their favorite game of all time (and Star Citizen trying for number 2 and failing because  doesn't know how to prioritize and set deadlines for meaningful features)... with some time put into American Truck Simulator,  the  of the game is solid.I like the atmosphere, the general design of the world they've built here, and yes, the fact that someone seems to have actually done their research when it comes to the CB conversations (though, completely inconsequential, every time I look at that CB I wonder why a non-SSB capable CB has a clarifier knob, which is only needed on sideband... and sideband is more of a DXer thing not a driver thing). The  is sound. The implementation could use some work. I'm not saying don't buy this game... but do know what you're getting into, especially... (checks notes) exactly 1 week after release at the time of writing this.Everything is just  Note for what I'm about to say next: I've been playing on the balanced difficulty setting thus far, except where noted.Like, we have all the good trappings of a nice leisure game, a nice "dad" game here. (Especially since, to be frank, there's really not that much involved gameplay otherwise. You drive things. End of story. That's not necessarily a negative, that's just what it is.) But "leisure" doesn't generally insinuate having to get up every 5-15 minutes to swap power cells, to reload an autosave because some NPC driver hit you while you were going in a perfectly straight line, to have to weigh every single purchase you make (of things you need) because every dollar that ends up in your bank account goes right back into parts that'll fail before the day is over, or fuel that takes like 1/4 of the tank per job.My advice: Wait for a round of patches. or three. I can't  recommend it in it's  state, but the devs seem passionate enough that I'm hoping I'll have to edit my review in the future once some tweaks have been made. If you do want to play right now, don't pick a difficulty. Pick custom, set the settings up the way you'd like. That'll be a more enjoyable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Hard to get used to at first controlling the big rig but never knew I needed a game like this. Just you and the open vacuum of space. Kind of reminds of the space trucks in cowboy bebop. 11/10 I hope they make some tweaks to things like power cell and air filter consumption but can easily be fixed with starting a new game with custom settings and still be able to enjoy all aspects of the game while still being challenged. Also hope the devs ad a way to customize the inside of the space truck to make the interior a bit more cozy since you spend all your time space truckin. If you like truck sims and space ships this is the game for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since Cowboy Bebop's "Heavy Metal Queen" the idea of a space trucker fascinated me. I loved that episode - the whole series of course - but that one really was a great one for me. Just a bunch of space truckers with their little baubles and customized interiors. The space gates that brought them from one place to another. A seemingly innocuous group of people that have a big impact on the space around them: making sure things get from A to B. Would it be automated in the future? Maybe. But the idea and atmosphere that the episode brought out, and that this games brings out, is that you are a necessity in the grande scheme of interstellar life and I kind of feel like it when I play this game.The visuals are great and you can see wear & tear on your truck. You can upgrade it and gain levels to get better access and improve your space truck. I hope to see different types of trucks. Ideally not behind a paywall but it seems many a game tries to become a live service and make the half-life of their games go ad nausea. I don't know if this dev will go that way, but I like this game.The only thing I do not like are the controls. Not customizable and a bit clunky. It did not like my PS5 controller I had connected via a cable, and kept on losing connection. If the controls could be customized, that would make it better, instead of just being able to choose inverted or not when steering. All in all I recommend this game and I believe I will definitely hit a 1h = 1€ ratio at least, and probably many more as I turn on "Life in Baghdad" and venture into the vastness of the space lanes.See you, Space Cowboys.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: As-is, I'm going to have to non-rec this game.It has a lot of potential.  However, at the moment the game is basically a battery installation sim.   You buy batteries, you install them.  You take a load somewhere, and you have to buy and install more batteries.   I like the mechanic, but it's far too needy of your attention, and it's constantly interrupting the core gameplay loop.  What's worse is that the lower level batteries, the ones with less power, are more economically viable.  You can purchase two 100 power batteries (200 battery power) for about $1,000 or you can purchase a high-end battery with 200 battery power for $2500.  That doesn't make any sense, and makes it cheaper to have to manage your batteries more often.I like the game, but it needs work.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Early game is quite a grind with managing Power Cells, you have to just do a bunch of jobs between story missions to keep up with the demand of powering your truck. It's not easy but I feel that makes the game more interesting, without this I would fear it would become boring quickly.Game Design, Truck control, environment and even the music are all superb!I'm really enjoying this as a chill-out game!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good but really hard at first. The trucks are difficult to operate and get around. I have only played the standard game mode but the truck batteries and all the maintenance is too much and everything depletes too quickly to even enjoy the trucking part. Also, the other trucks in the game don't seem to care about you. I brought a delivery across the galaxy just to get rammed by a truck coming out of the warp gate and the came charged me a $200 fine (kinda dumb). Other than that this is a good game and I want to see more update and features. Buy it but also understand that the movement is difficult to get the hang of and you have to pay for the mistakes of the other drivers when they crash into you for no reason.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: It is what it says on the tin. It's pretty lush, handles nicely and has a nice amount of fodder there from the top. One make or break will be that you're not doing big long drives along space lanes, but hoping between localities and navigating your way through them, as a result it feels a bit more Hardspace: Shipbreaker than ETS, this is backed up with the background cast of characters and evolving narrative as well as a series of hidden mini games for tasks such as maintaining power, oxygen and repairing your hull.You're also somewhat limited in cargo., truck and trailer are nice but it would be also cool if they had genuinely oversided cargoes that you had to navigate through the environmental and stuff.Me? I appreciate both kinds of games and I'm enjoying this for what it is, tho I'll be honest, I wouldn't mind riding out the gateway jumps for a bit longer, even if it was 5/10 minutes, with the odd course correction  or something, maybe as an optional to save being taxed or as an iron man style thing?On think that does annoy me tho is that sometimes the AI will just plough into you while doing repairs.... even when you think you're parked out of the way...
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome! The game is exactly You get what you expect. It's full,it's ready to play, it's new and fresh. Live in your truck, spend vacations under your truck and sometimes travel from repar station to spare parts shop :)Parts from floating space trash are better than the ones from my truck manufacturer... is it Ford Motor?

_childDocuments_.review: This game really shines in the first 10 hours of the campaign. It hooked me with how immersive it felt navigating a big vehicle through these cool environments. I was especially having fun with going in and out of debt, and carefully choosing tasks to keep my head above water while simultaneously moving the campaign forward. It reminded me of a similar enjoyment I had from GTA Chinatown Wars many years ago which has you travelling the map, buying goods low, and selling high. The voice acting over radio comms was very good, and the one radio channel and tastefully rarely played ambient music were phenomenal. I swear that lonesome guitar would only ever kick in out of nowhere right when I started craving it and humming it in my head. Nicely done on the sound design. I am shocked how this game got such good quality music that fits so perfectly with the unique world.On to my criticisms, of which I have many. But when I like a game a lot, my game design brain kicks into overdrive on all these things that would have made the experience even better. The game is held back in these many ways.Game design considerations (some mild spoilers below):-There comes a point after 10 hours of playing carefully when you suddenly find yourself filthy rich, and you buy out every single upgrade to your truck in 2 or 3 trips to the workshop. It was honestly more fun when I was under pressure of repeatedly going in the red and possibly getting my vehicle repossessed. Even though this will practically never happen, because a 4 day deadline to get back into the green is an insanely generous amount of time. After suddenly becoming rich, the game design felt like it was falling apart - devolving into mindless repetitive tasks just to be able to see the next story beat. There was no more planning or reacting to any danger in the entire game any more, and that's where the game falls short.-EVA (space walk) was very underutilized. There were many story beats that almost seemed to call for cool EVA moments. For example, finding a stranded trucker and offering to do some repairs on their truck. Sabotaging private network relays floating in space. Potentially going inside Moon Baby's Father's abandoned home to search for clues to the story. Going inside a space penitentiary to deliver spice to a chef. But these moments would just resolve with some dialogue or a screen fade to black and sound effects. Fairly late in the game, you will unlock ping scanners to identify scrap to recover via EVA. But this is so late in the campaign, that you are already at the point of completely filling up your airlock from floor to ceiling with goods from stores. So the airlock is unusable at that time in the campaign. It's just not worth the time and effort to clear out the airlock for one sector of scrap recovery only for it to be completely full of junk again after you visit a shop again. My favorite part in the whole game is one where they did the EVA justice. You have to go on a spacewalk to clean up your mess after a rough night of partying in Spark City. The dialogue is also so cute here. And then your ship is an absolute mess after all that time absorbing lightning while partying. It was a tense introduction to the electrical sectors, and even more exhilarating having gone in for the first time with only 3 spark plugs for protection. But the short-lived moment fades away, and you'll upgrade the ship to withstand most lightning impacts anyway.-The skill tree is full of lazy features that don't really change the game. Upgrading cab weight limit is the only feature that I was excited to get. Every other "skill" is pretty much just gaining access to delivering other types of cargo each for the same increased XP, and increased pay. It makes no meaningful difference to the gameplay in my mind when I picked heavy loads, multi-trailer loads, perishable loads, fragile loads, etc... Deliver quickly, and safely no matter what. Some of those types maneuver a little more clumsily or have to avoid certain sectors with extreme temperatures, but that hardly matters at all. Even the multi-load trailers are effectively like one single trailer.-What would have been far more interesting and engaging would be if the player could unlock the skills to carry 2 and then 3 trailers. With complete control over docking and undocking each segment, this would open up the game design tremendously for planning and managing several contracts with different destinations at once.-Also on the topic of skills or upgrades, it would be so much more interesting to have options to completely alter the gameplay in and around your rig. For example, it would have been awesome to unlock some webbing that would keep storage crates snug against the back of the cab even in zero g. I found online that the way to do this is to jam them into the shelving units by opening the lids of the crates once inside. That is such a weird solution, and I can't even tell if it is intended by the developers. Yet it is very important to learn this trick.-I beat the game with less than half of the skill tree unlocked (rank 17), which goes to show something is really out of whack with how stingy this game is with XP.Final criticisms are generally about the UX which needs some improvements:-It could be so much fun to tear through asteroid fields at breakneck speed, but the asteroids spawn so close in front of you at these speeds it is usually not safely possible. I was incessantly switching in and out of first person to tap the ping scanner and narrowly pick out newly spawned dark asteroids against the dark skybox. I found myself repeatedly frustrated when a collision would come as a result of the short spawn radius for this type of game which is all about efficiency. Ironically, Junk Field sector is one of the easiest obstacle courses to navigate because most of the hazards are spawned into the entire level. So why wasn't this possible in all the sectors?-Even with all the UI icons on the screen, the game fails to show the necessary info especially when you are focused on speed and efficiency. Toll booth markers don't spell out the connecting sector name unless it is at the edge of your screen. Space stations don't reveal the exact shop and job board bays until you are already so close that your approach trajectory is completely wrong. The bays don't even have any visual indicator of what service they offer except for in the frustratingly close-proximity UI icons.-There is a 'Z' key to zoom into the reverse hitch camera, and it really needs to have a toggleable setting or it needs to be rebound to the right mouse click. Both of which are not possible. The zoom feature is completely useless because you can't hold 'Z' while using 'WASD' and 'shift' to line up your trajectory.-Pretty much every contract I completed would ding me with a $5-$20 "careless driving" fee. Even when I hit absolutely nothing. It was just kind of funny. It's such a small amount of money, that I didn't care to figure out why it was applied. Maybe it's because I was cutting off other truckers at the warp gates. But the contract completion notes should have more detail notes than these vague fines when you hover the mouse over them. One time I was even fined almost $800 for "public endangerment".-Dropping an item from literally ankle-height damages it. So weird, but I eventually found my work arounds of using the railing corner as a table.-Your seated character strangely lags behind the ship's extreme acceleration and decelaration. This means your mouse cursor will be thrown off from the hitch lever, ping scanner lever, and warp drive lever. This really needs to be fixed, because it is mentally draining to hyperfocus on every moment the game is perturbing my mouse cursor for 50 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Space Trucker = Truck Simulator + Survival more or less.Where you haul cargo place to place while you manage your truck's resources. As you drive around make sure you watch out for what's in front of you. Cause you don't want to cause damage to your truck or cargo for that matter.I was looking forward to the games release and glad it's here at last so far I enjoy the game. While there is no keybind menu as of yet but I'm sure they will add in. So I'm not going to knock the game down just for that.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: A dark and brutal future, where there is no safe harbor.  Even while docked, your batteries and air filters run down.  The bed in your sleeper cab is unusable for a good reason, for falling asleep in this world is a death sentence.  The last thing you hear, before asphyxiating in your sleep? An echoing call, repeated a hundred times: "Things ok L.J. ? Looks like you've unhitched from the trailer."
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: so far its an alright game. big W since they added keybinds you can edit but its a steeper learning curve than needed due to you not having full control over your exact movements. its space you should be able to move along all three axis's but in this game you cannot. you have forward and back, pitch, and roll. you "drive" more akin to a plane than you do a space craftyou cannot strafe or move vertically independently which is highly irritating at timebeyond the movement issues i think the game is quite good. music has been great. good feel of being a truck even if your weight at the rear can feel a little awkward at times. story so far has been enjoyable with fun dialog and funny characters.id only recommend this on sale in its current state but for sure an enjoyable game once you get passed some of the odd quirks
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: 6 hours in and I'm having so much fun playing!  I know a lot of people gripe about the keyboard key binds, but it's not like you need to learn a ridiculous number of functions. The controls are more simplified (especially on controller) than your typical truck sim. I use a controller to play this game. I would call this a trucking "lite sim" with a a Sci-Fi twist. It's fun to listen to the NPC banter that occurs over the CB radio at certain times. The DMCA free radio station is pretty cool too. Totally gives Smokey & the Bandit vibes, only without crazy police chases lol!Hauling multiple loads is not available until you unlock a skill tree, and even then, it's limited to hauling multiple trailers that are part of the same job. You can't link up individual trailers from different jobs. Hopefully that changes down the road.Honestly though, it's a great game that is both chill but also requires precision at times.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Far more in depth survival/simulation than expected in a good way! Game looks wonderful with decent voice acting and missions to continue along the progress in the system. Recommended mode feels fairly hard at first when you are learning the ropes but once you get the systems down at driving, planning routes for jobs and vehicle maintenance then it all comes together. The game challenges you to properly plan your actions and do your best to be prepared for unexpected situations. Super fun game!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Before you play it:Try to read more comments since clearly the correct expectations for the game have to be set before playing.What to expect? I fell in love with this game and i'm pretty sure it's because i've set my expecations on the right path.- It's not ETS2 with long distances - distances are usually pretty short and try not expect ETS2 mechanics from this game.- the game puts emphasis on managing resources and taking care of your truck- It's a space - i repeat a SPACE, no up and down - space- People complain that the game is too difficult and i'll be honest - i'm playing on the hardcore and i have no reason to complain. Beside me crashing 200m/h into a rock (i was peting my dog), i had no problems in hardcore to sustain my ship/truckPROS:- OMG you actually can walk around the truck, you gotta press buttons to turn this and that light on and off. You press actual buttons in game instead of keyboard buttons. For sure that's more difficult and might even be an artificial difficulty but it's hella engaging and i wouldn't change a thing about it. I love pressing looking around the cabin for a button to press. Love it- another OMG is that you can go out of the truck and move around it, you can be an astronaut in space, collect resources outside in space and get them into your truck. Love that.- The game clearly shows that the DEVS had idea for this game, they knew what they wanted to do, they didn't just copy and paste cheap version of ETS into space - they knew what they wanted to do and they did it hecking well. IMO most of negative ratings are from people that expected ETS in space and you just shouldn't compare those 2 games.- Price fluctuations are great, especially that it's important to manage resources. You can be a truck driver and a merchant in one :DCONS:- I love the game but my labyrinth makes me vomit while playing too much of it. Thats why i probably won't play it any longer than i did. Very unlucky :(- Most people complain about the game being too difficult, i don't find it difficult at all even on hardcore, but i guess you should take that into account- If you think about it a little, the truck with no vision on the bottom makes no sense. There were too many times i've been thinking why ♥♥♥♥♥ is 70% of the vision obstructed by the engine... If one wanted to create a space truck, one would do whole front a window... but i guess you just have to deal with the game design.. but yeah thats the flaw - it looks cool but its impractical
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, has some little graphical stutters but the overall art style's very appealing.The music comes in two flavours; Float around space in awe of the ambience of the O.S.T. VS Flying my truck around space and riding the bend to the wicked Radio songs (also probably O.S.T.) but it's a little limited with some repetition.The Flight mechanics are fiddly on Mouse and Keyboard but not over complicated so...hard to master.Honestly, 5.4 hrs on my first play session. I've found my new Dadcore game.

_childDocuments_.review: How is this "mostly positive"? Why are a lot of the negative reviews talking about the economy being impossible? Literally just do jobs, you come out net positive if you're not a total crashout, at least when playing on the recommended difficulty. I'd say most of these guys just tried the basic contracts before levelling out other types, but I see most of them have the same hours or more as me. Or maybe the devs patched the economy post-release, not sure.Regardless: Really enjoying the game, the space spin on the typical ATS/ETS gameplay is great and well done. Being able to walk around the truck and EVA outside, tactile everything, the maintenance... all of it is right up my alley.Big bonus for having an actual story, and all the characters being likable. I watched the movie Convoy recently, definitely get the same vibes from this with the frequent CB radio usage etc. The radio is brilliant, all the space-related songs and in-universe ads are a nice touchI've gone up to the first set of upgrades. The shock absorbers are meh, just another part to replace. However I really like the shutters and solar flare systems, having to shut the windows and drive using the cameras mixes things up and is enjoyable

_childDocuments_.review: I've always hesitated getting into any trucking sim because it felt just a little too real. I already spend so much time driving so why would I spend my free time driving more?But driving in space? Managing the gravity in your cabin? Getting into my space suit to salvage space junk? Nevermind, sign me up.Vroom vroom am I right?
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I want to say thank you to the developers. Your game helped me survive a small but painful crisis, which improved my well-being and had a beneficial effect on my life in general. I was fascinated by the calm and comfort of this game, as well as the incredibly beautiful “landscapes” of space. Even though it's a small game, I wish you luck in developing it and adding lots of new things. I was surprised that there so small team right now; you have made a complex game, visually gorgeous, with its own unique atmosphere and identity, and nice gameplay.P.s Some ideas for new content... New body type for trucks, Peterbilt 362 style. A folder for mp3 files in the game directory, a more interactive radio (so you can switch radio stations using the buttons located there) and two more radio stations, with country and folk. New types of breakdowns that can be repaired in outer space. New types of dangers, like acid clouds that gradually destroy the trailer and truck.

_childDocuments_.review: While the game is simple at the start it can become a challenge as you continue to play. the keyboard and mouse controls are fine for me i dont understand the challenge some people are having. as for bugs i havnt come across any as of yet and as for the ai crashing into you i only experienced this if i just left a gate and waited to long causing them to come in and they dont have a chance to stop also if you leave the driver seat without pulling into a safe area they tend to act as if u arnt there which i assume is part of the challenge after all who would stop in the middle of an active road way to fix their car. overall i enjoy it but if your looking for extreme realism look elsewhere

I'm a Truck Driver myself in Australia but I'm not entirely "full Bottle" on the US industry. Glad to see some "space Road Trains though! (Sort of) its Chill, Its Fun, Its something different. _childDocuments_.review: Alright, I am changing my review from no to yes I do recommend. I am still jaded that a fine could be so high that it makes the run unrecoverable but I have learned a lot since my initial review. I have found the drop down on the map that shows what items are considered contraband and that has helped me not repeat that mistake. I have also played long enough on my new run that I have unlocked the hidden compartment to put illegal items in. Key to early game play is to avoid restricted items unless you know exactly where you are taking them and the route is clear. My new run is on Driver difficulty which is a joke. Yeah everything is easier to manage since things last much longer but the loads are also greatly reduced in value which makes you have to do twice as many runs to earn the same amount of money. {Note to developer} It's sandbox mode cant you let the player become over powered? Pretty sure that is the point of sandbox mode. Driver mode is boring. It takes an eternity to earn any real money with loads. I earn more money with trading. Repeating my sentiments from the previous paragraph, its sandbox mode, let the player have the freedom that they should have in said difficulty. The real issue I am having with giving a yes to recommended is now that I have learned how to play the game in driver mode, I want increase the difficulty but do not want to play the hours of early game play a third time just to get to that difficulty. I believe having a better "tutorial" on contraband would prevent other players from having to play thirty hours to simply avoid a game ending fine that is frustrating and does not contribute to the game in a positive way. Rant over. Game is fun but I think it will be a while before I start over AGAIN just to increase the difficulty. (Old Review below)Let me start with I want to and do love most aspects of this game. I am saying no to recommending this game for a couple game breaking problems. The problems that I encountered were on the recommended "normal" difficulty. I did not do these things on mechanic or hardcore which would make them more reasonable. There should not be a single mechanic that can ruin you on a "standard" difficulty. 1. Security checkpoints are fine, BUT they need to show you what items are considered contraband. Unless I am missing where is shows you then you only learn what is contraband, and where, is by trial and error. I had a few crates of alcohol on my truck and went through several security checkpoints without issue but then I went to purity and it was contraband there. The fine was over 20k and it was unrecoverable ending my run that I had already spent hours working on building. I enjoy a challenge but when one single thing can end everything. That is a poor design. 2. If you accept a cargo shipment that is picked up outside of the zone you are currently in, it frequently ends stating that you did not pick up the freight in time and fines you multiple times more money than the shipment was worth. This can probably be avoided by understanding jump times and when the quest ends but it is still something that should not be possible IMO. If there is no possible way to get to a load in time, it should not be an option.3. Fines are outrageous, at least early on, This may not be a problem later in the game but one fine can easily end your run. As stated previously, I enjoy a challenge, but when one mistake can make a run unrecoverable after doing everything by the book for hours, there is something inherently broken within the game. I have no issue with the above stated issues on higher difficulties. After having time to learn some of the things listed above on normal difficulty without breaking the game,  i would enjoy facing these challenges when I choose are higher difficulty. Having a single game mechanic end your run is the definition of hardcore and should not exist in the normal difficulty.

anyways i won't spoil anything going into detail on anything, anyways my only real issue is the lack of the option to change difficulty settings mid game. if your like me you'll have several hours in before you realise things aren't really to your liking, for example i found that the energy drain was too high as was the fuel. in short to change anything i had to toss my 6-ish hour play through out the window and restart with new settings, but of course getting it all just right is hard so... yeah... your gonna have to start a new game, play for an hour or so to see if it's just right, and if it isn't you'll have to restart again and attempt to tweak it again with the hopes hope you get it right... if not ya gotta repeat the cycle.in short if they add in the ability to change difficulty settings this game would be a solid thumbs up and a game i'd recommend to most people, it's unique in not just visuals but also game play, you don't even get vertical or sideways thrusters! :0 and again the long multi-trailers are very interesting as there isn't any game out there that offers such an experience with hauling. but... the game balance by default at least to me feels off and without the ability to change it mid save/play-through, it really killed my enjoyment of the game, at least for the moment. i come from games like pacific drive and they have a plethora of options you can change at any time, so getting everything just right doesn't need restart after restart, it's as simple as "oop! i should tweak that" when you notice something off, and you can tweak it right on the spot with no strings attached! of course i understands all games are made differently and this game might not be able to have such a luxury added in, and if it can't then all i could ask for is more detail when modifying the settings. like the percentage values for the power drain so when you select.... lets just say "low power drain" you know just how low it'll be.or for space debris maybe we could have a picture as a visual representation for how much there will be depending on what setting we have selected.also i feel like there should be a warning before starting a new game stating that nothing can be changed later, at least then players might be given the chance to get things right on their first game. overall ya get the idea. an informed gamer is a happy gamer :3

_childDocuments_.review: Game got dinged on reviews a bit when it first hit the store due to some major bugs and an economy that was skewed a little unfair, but devs have been resolving all that, so don't mind the complaints about the economy from the day one reviews.So basically this game combines the trucking sim vibes from popular games like Eurotruck with the space trading vibes of games like X2, X3, X4, Evochron Legacy, and maybe a little bit No Man's Sky if we're exclusively talking about trading between stations. The game also includes vehicle maintenance vs the environment gameplay and is very "run based", so in that way it does have some elements that feel comparable to games like Pacific Drive.Eurotruck + space sim + Pacific Drive = Star TruckerOne mistake you don't want to make when considering this game is assuming it's a casual or cozy type experience. The simulation aspects in this game are kinda complex and diagetic and there are a lot of different plates you need to keep spinning when managing your funds, almost entirely related to maintenance and upkeep of your craft.Your ship requires fuel for thrusters, power cores for various ship systems, and a few ship systems also require circuit boards. Fuel is burned as you burn your thrusters. Power Cells lose their charge as your ship systems are in use. Circuit boards slowly degrade over time and need to be replaced. Some examples of these ship systems include artificial gravity (needs power cell and circuitry), oxygen (needs power cell), internal cabin climate control (requires circuitry), air filtration (requires air filters), mag locks (needed to hitch cargo and to dock at stations), space suit (requires power and oxygen recharge after use).The thing is, if you are using all of your systems at all times, you are wasting money, because you might be burning fuel when you don't need to, or wasting power when you don't need to, which means you are wasting money when you don't need to, because you have to pay to replace fuel, power cells, circuitry, and air filters. So in order to save money, you can use the newtonian physics in space to drift long distances (especially with heavy cargo giving you more momentum) and conserve fuel. You can turn off all the lights inside the ship when you don't need them. You can also disable the artificial gravity inside your ship when you don't need it (but be careful that you might damage loose cargo if you don't take precautions). When you are swapping out the circuitry in your systems, you have to remember to cut power at the breakers first or you will blow the breakers on the entire ship, which you then have to act fast to restore.There are a lot of tiny things to manage, and tiny corners you can cut to save money, and getting used to all of this takes a bit of time and patience as you are learning.Once you've got a handle on things, there are different ways to make money.  different kinds of cargo from A to B is the primary way to make money in early game. As you build up more of an income, there is also a secondary form of trading. Every time you stop at a store to purchase supplies (power cores, filters, etc), you can also purchase miscellaneous others goods that are just for ], such as pharmaceuticals, chemicals, foods, etc. You can even trade the supply items themselves (power cores, spare fuel, etc) if you want. There is a fluctuating economy on these, so you can buy low and sell high. Rather than there being a hard limit on capacity for these items, you instead have to watch the weight of your truck, since you are only permitted by SPACE LAW to have a certain weight. You can be randomly called to weigh in at a weigh station at any time, and if you are over weight, you will be fined. So whether you take the fine or dump the cargo, it hurts either way, so mind your weight.There is also  of course, which is the primary use of your space walk equipment. Salvage is eventually one of the best money makers and it can even get you some free maintenance (salvaged power cells or fuel etc). But if you dilly dally too long on some salvage you happened across, you might also get penalized on a late delivery if you are in the middle of a haul.The game does also have , if you want to be a contraband-hauling criminal trying to pass under the radar of the law, but you will not be getting into any dogfights in this game. You just haul the cargo and try not to go broke, get fined, freeze to death, burn to death, crash into an asteroid, etc. The game also has story jobs that you must perform at your leisure, and completing these story jobs unlocks new sectors of the galaxy for you to explore. These new sectors are more challenging and have their own simulation challenges. For example, one of the first sectors you unlock takes you extremely close to a star that is prone to random flares every several minutes. The external environment here is hundreds of degrees normally, but thousands of degrees during flares. During a flare, you need to pull a lever that lowers your ship's protective shielding, which prevents it from being obliterated by the flare , but the shielding also covers all windows, so you're forced to steer your ship via an external camera feed on your dash. The extreme temperatures also mean you need to crank climate control far into the AC / cooling range and probably increase air blowers, which means you are burning more power on climate control in this region. You CAN bake yourself alive inside your ship if you don't do this.Finally, I appreciate that this game is very diagetic as a sim.  A lot of space sim games just put literally every game function on 100 different keyboard hot keys. But in star trucker, you instead have a functional dash covered in monitors and buttons. All these buttons and monitors are functional and convey actual information. So instead of doing everything with hot keys, you use the mouse to literally push the button, flip the switch, pull the handle, twist the knob of whatever control it is on your dash. This gives the game a more tactile and immersive feeling and makes you feel much more that you are in the captain's chair. (Some things are, of course, done with keys, such as steering and breaking, etc).Devs have noted that HOTAS controls are coming in the future, if that's your bag.It's really a pretty interesting game that has the slow grind of driving for money as found in games like Eurotruck, but it's a more challenging vehicle to drive and there are many more numbers to watch, so if you sorta like things like Eurotruck but find them just a little too sleepy and wish there was a little more tension and management involved, then Star Trucker might work for you!It's one of those games where you need to be willing to suck a little and put up with a little frustration at the start while you get comfortable with the systems and learn about what problems your ship might have and what the solutions are, not to mention getting a feel for the economy and how to make good decisions in that economy. But once you get there, I think it's one of the more interesting sims in the job sim / space sim category and the only game that blends the genres in this specific way.

_childDocuments_.review: Where we are going we  need roads, actually.Right so, first off the bat: Star Trucker is a simulator game. Far from a  simulator, mind you, but it is a videogame that puts a strong emphasis in recreating a complicated machine, with multiple co-dependent systems dedicated to keeping you both alive and moving, and turns out, in the future your survival is a bit more hands-on than it is now.The first few hours of your playthrough will be both wonderful and terrifying. The game does provide a tutorial mission, and a reasonable manual, and your truck has so much stuff on it, with clicky buttons and levers to control from the lights on your cab to your AC, your thrusters, breakers for each individual system, flight assist, most of them with actual applications that you are encouraged to micromanage to get the most out of each one, and the larger part of them can, at any point, start screaming at you which will launch you in a mad dash to find what's wrong and how you can fix it while barreling down a space highway at 120mph, trying to complete the job that will pay for your next air filter.And I mean, this will really depend on how much you enjoy in-depth system simulation and more importantly, how relevant this simulation is to your minute-to-minute, but I was immediately hooked. I had seen nothing about this game until I picked it up, and exploring the sheer depth of all the fiddly bits in my truck was really cool, and resulted in moments I do look fondly on, like when I realized I was almost out of oxygen and had to figure out, on my feet, a way to replace my busted filters and race to a replacements shop, o2 level steadily decreasing, vision getting blurry, when I was like "wait! spacesuit!", managing to run the last few kilometers wearing it, finally reaching the shop and resolving the crisis. It's stressful at first, and I can understand how you can easily die during these first hours, and I can see players being frustrated at it. But if you are in the same spectrum that I am, man, it's really nice to come out on top at the end of it.As you finally start getting settled into the complexities of your truck while panickedly running non-stop jobs to just be able to stay on top of spares, you'll inevitably question yourself if you can even keep up with this, if you'll be able to reach the next filter change, if you'll find enough batteries before these go, running through systems, checking new shops, making a sense of what's where, and eventually, through much work and grinding, you'll finally reach the "mostly space truckin" part of the game.Your space truck flies... well, like a truck. You don't get lateral translation, however, you do have lateral thrusters that will keep you moving forward. It's more kind of like a boat, where it's more about momentum than direction, but once you get used to it, it's really great. Learning how to coast, what turns you can take at what speed, how to account for your haul, dealing with traffic, using the external cameras in your MFDs to get a sense of your surroundings... There's an external camera (with no hud), but you don't really need to switch to it. You can upgrade several aspects of your truck, and soon you will be piloting your cab as an extension of yourself, flipping around to dock into hauls and drifting a 3 trailer into a turn while well over the speed limit. Which, oh yeah, space roads.So you'd think you can just go from A to B in a straight line, since, well, this is space, right? Well, most of this space is filled with debris, and trust me that a single debris strike can become VERY problematic for your truck, so you'll want to follow space roads. This is something you'll quickly need to get used to, and at first it won't be easy because you don't get sector maps. You will need to figure out and get used to the layout of every system, and how to get from A to B with the least amount of pain. Every sector is unique and has it's own personality, from the tight and industrial Edgeburgh to the Outrun-esque Dependency Loop, the windy and dangerous Haze Way, some of them almost feel like racing game stages, and they are really fun to go through haul after haul after haul.To go along with this space truckin, you will sometimes get a little bluegrassy kinda music from time to time, and you can also turn on the radio in your cab, which will play a selection of rock/bluesy songs, all purpose made for this game, and all absolutely bangers.The main point of the game is to do hauls so you can stay on top of your maintenance which, after the first hours, is something you will have to deal on the regular but in a way, WAY more routine manner. Swap a few of batteries every couple of jobs, keep a few spares of everything, angle your hauls towards systems with cheaper spares, or several shops. You can salvage space debris and sell it too, which is very lucrative, but to me space truckin was my main gig and if you like your truckin, you're gonna get a hell of a lot of it, and it's  space truckin.Once you are in a good enough spot, you can start doing the story missions that, while have very paltry rewards, will open new sectors to play with, alongside a new truck subsystem to deal with them. They don't add a whole lot of complexity, but their gimmicks are alright. The story missions feel very disjointed, and their existance seems more out of obligation to somehow pace your progress through the game than anything else. They're not terrible, but nothing special either. The "story" ends abruptly at an arbitrary point, with no rewards, so it feels like there might be more to come in future updates, but as it is now, there's more than enough content to get 40+ out of it. Much more depending on how much you want to truck for the hell of it.Anyway, this is a really great game for what it is. The developers have said that they will rebalance how the maintenance side of things works so I would expect it to become somewhat easier to deal with, but right now I think it is alright, and besides, one can freely customize the difficulty of their games with 0 negative repercussions, if you find it too hard, or if you just want to space truck. But even so, having beaten the game in "recommended" (with "poor" engine efficiency) without having died a single time, I think the difficulty is pretty okay if a bit wonky.Absolutely recommended. 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: If your favorite episode of Cowboy Bebop is "Heavy Metal Queen" this is the game for you! The "space trucker" vibe is perfect, and the customization and progression is rewarding.  The artwork is also beautiful, and the ability to walk around and personally maintain your rig is great.  You're not just a "model ship", you're the pilot.   I will say, at least in early game the payouts seem pretty low.  one load pays like 1,500, about enough to buy ONE air filter (your truck needs four to be fully efficient, and they degrade over time)  and a tank of fuel is like 1,000 as well.  maybe payouts get better over time, but early game is pretty unforgiving and grindy.   You really have to be mindful of the cost of maintenance.  You can set the difficulty lower to counteract that, but that's not how you become a super trucker, is it?  Keep the pedal on the floor, driver.

_childDocuments_.review: It has always been my dream, since the 1996 release of the hit movie Space Truckers, to be a space trucker. Since this game was announced in the steam store I have had it in my wishlist. This game is the PERFECT product for me. _childDocuments_.review: Excellent blend of calm driving and survival. I see lots of people stating that the survival aspect and economy is too hard. I have played one save on the suggested difficulty for 12 hours and I've found it to be fine. It honestly seems to be in a perfect place right now. I always have full containers of spare batteries, chips and air filters. If I focus on hauling jobs I can slowly upgrade my rig while keeping my reserve parts high. The occasional accident, botched job, or god forbid, 10 000$ smuggling fee (I unknowingly brought explosive into Atlas Prime once) gives you a challenge, as you start delving into your supplies and becoming more desperate. Even so, if you focus on doing jobs you can overcome these challenges and that feels good. I've never been stuck somewhere, died or needed a haul. You just have to play smart.There are lots of beautiful areas to explore and the atmosphere is very relaxing and serene. The story line unfolds as you like and I enjoy that there isn't much financial incentive for most story missions because it forces you to just do you job, haul space cargo. Some aspects of the game are simplistic but at the same time everything works really well. I've come across almost no bugs and mostly everything is well thought out.Small gripes:-Please let me put the below rig camera on my left screen or put the battery charge one there. Those are my two most important screens and it sucks they have to share the right side while the left side doesn't show me much that's important.-Dear god, take the giant square debris proximity box off my screen cameras. I know debris is close, why do you think I'm using my cameras!? I already have a proximity light on my dash and the square warning text box covers exactly where I need to be able to see to avoid said debris! Super frustrating, especially in the solar areas.-I'd LOVE to be able to customise, or at least change, the colours of my interior.-Radio music, while fitting the theme of the game, is waaaay to high energy for the atmosphere of the game. The radio needs some nice low fi-tunes. They can still have a country twist, the music you get when entering zones is done really well in this fashion.Those are minor gripes though, overall a fantastic game. Props to the devs for knowing their scope and executing it perfectly!

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: Known bug exists where you cannot progress the story line. Im fully upgraded and leveled up and cant finish the game. Cool. Was this even play tested? TLDR; Set the custom difficulty and enjoy some space truckin'. Its great.Worth the price but a couple considerations;The recommended difficulty setting is not a chill 'ATS/ETS vibe' it is a hardcore survival mode with permadeath enabled. Unless you fly perfectly with no damage and no fines, failures compound until you will be broke with no life support and permanently softlocked. You need to be completing paid cargo jobs just to keep your head above water on truck maintinence which leaves no room for the storyline missions as they dont pay or give you XP. If you're a veteran ETS/ATS player looking for a similar experience, set all the custom difficulty settings to as 'easy' as possible. It seems excessive but provides a more consistent experience. There is definitely room for multiple playthroughs and scaling the difficulty to your taste. The gameplay itself is great. Maneuvering/docking is rewarding when you get a hang of it and I agree with the decision to omit translation thrusters as it makes your truck maneuver more like..well, a truck. Its like ATS/ETS with a Z-Axis. Storyline/Progression/Upgrades are pretty stock but familiar and thats not a bad thing. The transition from driving to EVA and back is very smooth, and jumping around systems while completing jobs feels very organic. No perceptible loading screens.

_childDocuments_.review: There is the potential for a great game here. It has beautiful visuals, a great atmosphere and an engaging gameplay loop, but in it's current state I can't recommend this game for anyone but the most dedicated of resource management aficionados.The numerous flaws and possible fixes have been explored in detail in other reviews, but I will mention my two major gripes.1: Poorly balanced resource usage. The "recommended" setting is far too punishing, especially when it comes to power usage. Add that to the baffling scarcity and expense of power cells and other necessities it becomes an annoyance very quickly. There is a custom game option that can alleviate the issue to some extent, but in my view it needs a complete overhaul.2: Diverging control schemes and a lack of custom key bindings. The latter the devs have pledged to fix, but why the space suit has an unintuitive control scheme (at least when using a controller) that wildly differs from the truck to begin with is a bit of a strange one.Bonus: Only 3 save files? Why? For now the lack of polish on these fronts will make me put the game on a shelf for the time being, and come back to it at a later date when hopefully these and other issues have been smoothed out by the devs.

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trucker brings a unique twist to the truck sim genre by launching you into space. Hauling cargo across the galaxy is both immersive and thrilling, with well-balanced gameplay that combines realistic trucking mechanics with the excitement of space travel.Beyond cargo runs, you can trade salvage, upgrade your ship, and build your reputation across the stars. The game’s world is expansive, visually stunning, and filled with challenges that keep you coming back for more.If you love trucking sims or space exploration, *Star Trucker* is a must-play. Prepare for hours of fun!

_childDocuments_.review: While the game's movement is difficult to grasp right away and the battery/UCC drain is overwhelming at first with some time you start to learn what needs to be done.  Here are some things i learned while playing and experimenting.-System batteries don't have to be 100% all the time as some are only drain power when in use(Mag system and Suit Charger). -Turn off the system breaker before removing the old UCC to avoid a short. -While docked you can swap the Grav and O2 power cells without issue as the station provides those systems. -Keep partial cores for use in emergency or for the suit charger as that system doesn't use much power, it's perfect for low % batteries. -Another key thing is that each system shows the price of certain goods. Try to buy ship components where the market is down so it's cheaper. You can also use this information to buy and sell goods across systems.-If you leave a Job board or Store menu, you can re-access it from the airlock door. This may be said in a tutorial but i had my door open and didn't realize until an hour in you could do that.-Buy containers to store Truck components or Trade Goods. Keeps them from bouncing around and keeps them safe from damage in the event of a Grav failure or collision.-Your truck keeps its forward momentum. So if you are going 120 mph and then turn to the left you will still be going 120 mph the way you were facing. You have to then thrust to add momentum in the new desired direction.-Air brake literally uses air, don't choke yourself out.-SAVE OFTEN! You will mess up Battery management, you will drop a UCC from too high up and bust it, you will hit Astroids/debris, you will hit trucks/drone/stations by accident. This game is unforgiving even on the normal difficulty, save often and reload if you've made a mistake. -Follow the side quests to unlock new ship upgrades and new regions.Hopefully these tips can help get you in a better place to experience the game and have fun.While i agree no keybindings menu is not right, they are working on it. That being said the keyboard controls grew on me and don't seem too strange to me right now. All in all if you like space, trucking, fun characters and a kick ass radio this game is for you. It's extremely fun as well as challenging, I can't wait to see what the developers add in the future.

You can make all the fiddly parts incredibly rare and just drive, or alternatively turn up the risks instead. _childDocuments_.review: The right game for you if you enjoy:- learning the docking procedure in Elite Dangerous (you can feel like a noob yet again)- the clumsiness of trucks (without ability to strafe), extended to the third dimension- parking in reverse, using a monitor (again, in 3 dimensions)- drifting- going for a spacewalk fixing your vehicle after hull breaches- walking around inside your vehicle and regulalry fix systems (especially if you liked Tin Can)The game has quite a learning curve at the start, but it shouldn't take much longer than 1-2 hours to get familiar with the controls. At the start if you're not comfortable drifting and maneouvering I would recommend to stay on the "roads" so you don't have to constantly dodge debris, and also to step down from the gas every once in a while. Turns out a space truck with 50 tons of cargo takes a while to adjust direction, let alone come to a standstill.I think the game does everything it set out to do, in a fabulous way. It's challenging but forgiving, slow enough to let you relax but never boring (e.g. there's no such thing as accelerating and decelerating towards a planet for 15 straight minutes like in ED).I give it a solid 9/10.Some things that can be improved:-  (nevermind, that just got fixed)- uninspiring skill tree: It mostly lets you accept more difficult contracts and increases rewards. I'd love to see more RPG style stuff in there- only one radio station

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend the game, but be mindful that you've got to like the following two things:> Inventory and resource management (you will have to switch out depleted cells and broken modules very often, as well as organizing your cargo load if you're like me doing a lot of scavenging and buy-and-sell)> Flight simulator (it's not easy navigating the sectors, the rig you're flying ain't no space fighter and you'll have to learn how to maneuver the highways filled with traffic and the huge fields of debris and asteroids in between)If you're on board with those, then this will be an excellent single player experience that I'm sure has quite the replayability potential.Some mechanics and bugs need ironing, but overall it plays smooth as butter. The controls are very responsive, and all the various game mechanics play into each other pretty well, although some should be expanded on. I, for example, find that shop prices swing a bit too wildly, since every time you make a jump you suffer from massive time dilation. I would love for there to be a way to predict these prices, so that buying and selling items could be more viable - not that it's useless at the moment, far from it! I managed a single run worth 26k dollars, 10 times more than the average hauling job. My point is, you'll find it quite annoying when a sector's shops that were paying extra for electronics end up being a dud by the time you've reached your destination. It's basically all luck, which I understand, but I would love for a more predictable system, even if only slightly, presented in game.The progression is good, with upgrades to your rig that make it safer, faster, more nimble and all kinds of other stuff which are all fairly priced (every level is a simple 250 dollars price increase). These upgrades also have a noticeable impact straight away, despite there being several levels for each system. You can't get it all on day one, but it is also very possible to grind your way up to the top if that's your style. Meanwhile, the xp levels seem to be a bit slow, but most of the unlockable skills serve to gain access to new types of jobs, so it's kinda fineAs well as that, story progression features engaging characters, nothing too crazy but definitely enhances discovery of new sectors to travel to, as well as being an overall fairly good "long term" tutorial for each new game mechanic (such as types of jobs, dangers you might encounter etc), and the whole thing is well disguised as these characters "showing you the ropes". Very fitting.Overall, a damn good game, definitely worth the price tag even if not on sale. Perhaps give it some time for the developers to iron it out if you're not entirely convinced yet, but as it stands it's a solid addition to my favorite games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is geniunely awesome. I've been looking forward to it all year and it's not dissapointing. It's very much a game of process. It's a little bit like Sea of Thieves in that the way you get from place-to-place is central to the design of the gameplay loop; it's moreso about the journey than the destination. As far as maintenance goes, it's just complicated enough to keep you engaged without becoming so obscure that you don't know what's going on or why you're dying (which was a pretty common experience in the demo).As far as presentation is concerned, the devs knocked it outta the damn park. The vibes are frankly immaculate. The in-universe music is excellent, and fairly well-mixed. The environmental design feels simultaneously believable and stylish. The various spaceports all have their own unique feel, which is something I was really worried about coming into this game. The characters are charming, and interacting with them is a genuine motivator to progress in the story. That being said, there are glaring oversights I'm noticing about the game, and since I know the devs are actively looking for feedback right now, I think I'll share what I've noticed so far: -No keybind configuration-NPCs don't respond well to player behavior. I once had another truck slam into me for no good reason, dropping my hull integrity to near-zero from full and damaging a lot of valuable commodities. -No lateral-vertical thrusters (though I suspect this is a deliberate choice by devs to preserve the "big rig feel" of these starships)-No ability to control lights without being seated at the front of the cabin. Surely it'd be nice, at least for immersion's sake, to be able to control the lights from the living space in the lower-back of the vesselRegardless, this game is scratching my brain in a way that's doing something for me, and frankly a game this ambitious coming out in such a stable, functional, and polished state feels like a miracle in 2024. All things considered, I'm more than happy to recommend this game, even at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Trucking Simulator..... In space. Nice cool game, plenty of options on the difficulty, And not always stuck in the drivers seat with options to do outside repairs. _childDocuments_.review: Great game that really nails the aesthetic it's going for. Music especially is really on point. Don't be afraid to play on easy!... it's a very chill experience that way. 30 hours in, I only had to buy a few supplies near the beginning. Replacements are so few and far between now I get plenty from salvage with leftovers to sell. I can pretty much promise people not liking excessive maintenance are playing on higher difficulties. You'll also need to get used to not pointing at the objective and gunning it... you're usually better off following the "roads" most systems have. Only other little tip that wasn't so obvious to me: even if your rig doesn't have a hull breach, you'll still need to take it in to get properly repaired, otherwise any little bump will cause holes that need repairing.If the aesthetic looks like something you'd like, you'll almost certainly like the game. It's just a matter figuring out if you prefer the more survival-like game on hard, or the more relaxed driving sim on easy.

_childDocuments_.review: Tentative yes.I'm ten hours in, and for the most part it's a very fun game. Didn't even notice that time fly.We'll start with the bad, though: For a full release game, I've already encountered a bug where a bunch of items disappeared, and a bug that required me to reload a number of times and ate up something like 45 minutes. Pretty heinous.Other than that, judging whether an air filter needs to be changed or not is either A: something I haven't fully figured out yet, or B: poorly designed. With most components, they hit zero quality (HP for chips, charge for batteries) and you swap them out. These have two bars, and apparently when one reaches 10% they're useless? I don't know, but I've found myself suddenly suffocating more than once.The shock pads don't register as popped or not when sold.There's no readout on the terminals for chips. Maybe this is an intentional design, but it's mildly irritating. If it's an intended mechanic, I get it, but meh.The maybe bad: It's a relatively small universe, I'm only ten hours in and I suspect the endgame will be zero. Hope I'm proven wrong. (Similar games get away with this by having a stupid-large map making the same missions/jobs feel new).The good: The controls are weirdly satisfying. There's enough mass-based drift and sluggishness that it's a challenge, but the controls are responsive enough that you can, "get good," and whipping a space truck through systems.I played a lot of American Truck Sim, and backing the trailers into a drop zone in this game is so so so much less awful than in ATS. Very manageable with one, but I fear for the day I have to back two or more into a drop zone. I'll probably edit this in a rage if I do (but thankfully most drop zones can just be nosed-into).The trade system isn't a note-taking endeavor. They did a pretty great job on indicating how much of a profit or loss you're making/taking. Also when things are marked up, the average price is right there. Fantastic.Finding salvage pods is a pretty great mechanic. Using cargo boxes to reduce the amount of trips is a good use of other game mechanics. Well done with that.The setting and missions aren't mind-blowing, but they're pretty good. The game's pretty, the missions are detached (why should I give a crap about any of these people?) but entertaining enough. The dialogue is well voiced and often chuckle-funny.Customization (compared to games like ATS, sorry I keep doing this but it's a frame of reference) is mediocre, but not bad. Basically just change paint jobs. Kind of regretting the DLC with that in mind.The balance (in the recommended mode) of income vs. ship component/fuel degradation is actually rather well done. I play pretty safe and I'm generally well stocked, yet always have an eye on energy levels. Learning to check chips, I suck at that. The air filters are a mystery and I just hang onto a few extra and wait until I start suffocating before rushing for the space suit and swapping one out.Trade of standard/contraband is pretty well done. Supplements income well enough to be worth it, and sometimes you get lucky and make a good bit of coin. Or paper. Or whatever space money is made of.Docking is notably well-done. The controls are intuitive, the docking camera is fantastic, and once you get the hang of it it's pretty quick.Draw distance on small debris is also well done. It's small, and depending on star location/shadows it can be just tricky enough to spot to be fun, yet not punishing enough to make me fearful of going, "off-road."That's all I've got for now. I'll probably forget I wrote this and never come back, but if I do I'll edit over time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game. Especially if you like American Truck Simulator. Yes, this is a space hauler game. But, they really gave the truck spaceships a real big-rig truck feel. It seems best played with a controller. By the time you finish a few hauls you will get the hang of flying/driving these trucks/spaceships. They did a great job on the physics. The game has a great soundtrack. My favorite song being the main menu song. An interesting aspect of the game is that you have to keep your truck in working order. You have to keep power cells, control circuits, and air filters replaced on a regular basis. Otherwise you leave yourself stranded in space or pass out due to lack of oxygen. So you have to manage the money you earn between maintenance and ship upgrades. I would recommend this game for those that like the hauler genre of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Having an absolute blast with this. It scratches the flight sim itch on steam deck in a weird way: they're both about taking these ponderous, highly specialized machines on long journeys, running through idiosyncratic little routines and praying the stars align in a way that allows you to reach your goal safely. You can adjust the difficulty, which is really nice as the recommended difficulty runs a pretty tight margin for error and I'm more into the cozy aspect of a sim-adjacent game like this. It runs beautifully on the steam deck. The soundtrack is an absolute love letter to that weird obsession with trucking in the American pop culture back in the 70s and it's genuinely worth turning the radio on. If you were intrigued by euro truck simulator, Kerbal space program or Microsoft flight simulator you should try this as well. It's a little arcade-y but it deserves to sit with those other games in the lunchroom.

_childDocuments_.review: Just wanted to play some other trucking game and this new release popped up. Minutes later my shiny space truck was ready. The tutorial route was super simple and I´ve earned some first money:I liked the style, music and atmosphere and thought that I might start playing on a harder difficulty to get more action.While trying to dock at some station for upgrades I got shoved around by traffic since I didn´t pay attention:With some penalties for traffic violations, a nearly broken truck that has to be repaired and still not being docked, I might rather continue playing the normal difficulty for the time being.The game has been fun and a positive surprise for all those 20 minutes that I´ve played. _childDocuments_.review: If you were like me and played Elite Dangerous avoiding combat as much as possible just being a freighter pilot you'd probably love this game.I'll break it down as easy as possible.This is not a simulator.  Your rig does not maneuver like a space craft on a x-y-z axis.  It also does not handle like a semi from American Truck Simulator.  It takes a minute to really learn.  Sci-Fi over Sim.  Add a load and it handles completely different.Then there's the survival element which is no joke.  On the recommended level you will probably bankrupt quickly once, maybe twice.  There are batteries, circuit breakers, air filters and more to maintain during your travels.  Debris, space rocks and other traffic can hit and breach your hull forcing you to dawn your spacesuit and do some emergency repair.Skill tree unlocks different types of cargo, trip length, upgrades and new areas.  Different NPC's offer side jobs which unlock special upgrades.Visuals are very pleasing, great sound, and a fantastic Americana soundtrack.Easy thumbs up from me.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the "I would rate it neutral if it was an option" cases.Generally it is a fun game, which I would recommend AFTER a few more updates/fixes.Currently the balancing of costs and income is a bit off and you basically have to play the game a few hours to figure out what you are struggling with and then restart the game with custom difficulty to make up for the balancing.For example:Do you like to micro manage each docking process or would you prefer to turn down how much aligned you need to be to successfully dock?Do you like to take breaks on your route to make sure your trucks systems won't give out in the middle of the road oder would you prefer to just drive?How much of an impact should an impact with space trash have? (On default it can force you to save scum quite easily if you are strapped for cash.)The other thing that annoys me is that you can take damage while being docked.You are in the way of an delivery drone? Too bad, now your hull has a hole.You docked in the middle of an electric storm? Better be fast while shopping or looking for a new haul before your systems get fried.Like I said the game is fun, but all these minor annoyances and bugs make the game frustrating in the long run.

_childDocuments_.review: **What I Think: This game has a lot of promise, and I love the actual gameplay of driving the truck through each sector. However, the constant need to purchase supplies, fuel, manage hull integrity, it gets a lot after the first few hours in a save file. In my opinion, the maintenance aspect of this game somewhat ruins the chill "truck driver" atmosphere, since I found myself sweating about whether I should fill my truck's gas tank, if I need to buy batteries (since there are 8 items that need batteries, with no way to recharge them), or if I could buy an upgrade for my truck for the shop. Oh, and forget about ever repairing your hull integrity, there is no way to scrape together $3,000 without being at risk of going bankrupt trying to buy the life support supplies. I really love this game, and I always feel bad about cranking down the difficulty since I should be able to enjoy a game on the recommended settings, but I find it hard to enjoy the gameplay when I am in a constant race against time to out-earn my truck's resource usage**Improvements: I feel this game is missing a few elements to make it really great. -To start, there is no place to rest and decompress. When docked to a station, your truck is still draining batteries, O2, and air filters. I wish, when you are docked to an outpost, you could get free O2 and batteries, or at least being able to exit your truck so you can do repairs while you are safe from debris. -Secondly, I have never been able to afford repairing my hull's integrity, the price tag is just too much. This means the slightest tap of an asteroid creates multiple holes, and repairing the holes takes time, which in turn burns more batteries and O2, etc. -Lastly, and this is the biggest one, there needs to be some way to recharge batteries. Maybe you drop the empty cells off at a station and return in a day, maybe the truck has a slow charger that can harness the engines to recharge empty cells slowly. No matter the method, there is such a drain of resources and no way to renew them, I feel like the least they can do is allow us to replenish at least one of the resources, and I feel that the batteries would make the most sense.TLDR: The gameplay of this game is really promising, and with a few quality-of-life improvements and a few gameplay tweaks, this game can easily be as popular as the big-name driving simulators. At the moment though, it is just a bit too grindy and stressful to fit the "chill trucking game" genre, but I have faith it will get there

_childDocuments_.review: Fairly good, I've seen a lot of complaints from others that do not make sense. For one, there is a difficulty setting you can select that reduces the resource management/maintenance aspect of the game so you focus more on the driving/haulingTwo, personal goods trading can be done at shopsThree, longer drives are available later in the game, the early contracts only ask you to go a system or 2 over, but later on you need to go across basically the whole map.However, there are a few valid complaints,One, no key rebinding, I'm not a developer so I don't know how hard or easy this would be to implementTwo, no hotas/hosas support, although the devs have acknowledged that they are working on it.Three, not really a major problem but for whatever reason they made the spacebar accelerate and shift brake, and I find that choice odd.As for performance, it runs very well on my system of 12600k and 3070ti.For whatever reason, fullscreen exclusive mode has performance issues that bring framerate down to around 80 while not using the full power of your computer.But setting it to fullscreen windowed mode removes that problem entirely and I was getting a solid 144fps most of the time.Overall, it's probably one of the most unique games set in space I have played in a while because it isn't trying to be like all the others and is very stylized.
