_childDocuments_.review: This game is exactly the kind of relaxing sim I've been looking for. For years I've played Elite Dangerous and Euro Truck Simulator trying to fulfill the trucker fantasy but the former had way too much sitting around with jobs being very samey, while the former was too realistic for my liking with jobs taking very long and the driving not being very fun in my opinion. Star Trucker does its own thing and does it well. Aside from actually star trucking there are scripted missions that let you interact with a cast of truckers you become friends with along the way as well as the option to engage in trade on the side, allowing for more ways to play. Long hauls don't feel like boring highway drives or automated hyper jumps and take a reasonable amount of real world time. The way each star system is designed, and that fact you're in space, gives the player a choice to stay on the marked path or trying to take shortcuts between star gates, which trades the risk of running into debris and damaging your rig. Taking care of your rig breaks up the game play by adding a tactile cargo management system with consequences for not keeping up with part replacement. (This system was controversial at launch but has since been balanced nicely and game mode options let you tune your experience.) Finally I'd like to praise the art style and unique design of the game. Making your spaceship in the shape of a modern American tractor trailer is so fun and lets the game lean in to this not-too-serious tone.TLDR: 10/10 not-too-serious space trucking sim that lets you have fun.

_childDocuments_.review: After the recent (sept. 24) update, game balance has been adjusted and bugs fixed. The annoyance factor of the recommended difficulty was lowered. Fully recommend the game now, however be prepared to scrap your save if your chosen difficulty is to annoying.Old:Cant recommend this game atm. In many ways, this game should have been an early access release. Game balance seems of (airfilters, batteries), basic systems are bugged (trailers from the same consist damaging themselves for no reason, skill bonuses not being applied during payout), etc. All fine in early access, but not for a finished game.Furthermore, while this looks like a chill ETS/ATS like trucking game in space, it is more of a survival game. _childDocuments_.review: Star Trucker is an endlessly frustrating game to play, at least in its current form. Which is a real disappointment because on paper I should love this game, but there were some glaring issues with the game that just kind of ruined it for me.You have four different resources you need to constantly juggle to keep your truck running. Fuel, Power Cells, Air Filters, and Universal Circuits. These deplete  quickly compared to the amount of time you actually spend driving, so you are constantly replacing them. That would normally be fine, but there's no guarantee that you'll find any of these essential items at a given shop, even in the bustling hub systems. And even if you do find some, there's usually only one or two of each available. They're also really expensive compared to your income, at least in the early game.This is what killed my first run of the game. I started losing oxygen rapidly because one of my two air filters dropped below 50% durability (which itself is kind of ridiculous), so I had to go speeding between every shop in the first hub system because  of them had replacement filters. And when I did finally find one (and only one), I suffocated while I was in the process of buying it. IN THE MIDDLE OF ONE OF THE MAIN HUBS, where you'd think supplies would be plentiful.The NPCs you'll encounter on your travels have the self-preservation instincts of a toddler playing in the cabinets under the kitchen sink. I've seen better driving in Grand Theft Auto, where the NPCs are actively trying to crash into you. I was straight-up kamikaze'd twice, and narrowly avoided a few others. In each instance, I was driving in a straight line, at a more or less constant speed. And the great thing is, when you're involved in a collision, it's always your fault, and you always receive the full penalty for it!This is what killed my second (and ultimately final) run. I was doing one of the tutorial missions after unlocking fragile loads, and while I was dodging some debris coming out of a warp gate, another truck exited the gate at about 200 miles an hour, dove directly for my cab, and brought my hull integrity all the way down from full to 0% in a single hit. I made no money from that mission because of "Careless Driving", and the repair bills put me so far in debt that there was no point continuing.Apart from those two major issues, there are some rough edges to the game. Some things are not communicated to the player effectively, like Universal Circuits failing, or the fact that you can't haul multiple trailers from different jobs at once, despite the fact that you can accept multiple missions at the same time,  can haul up to three trailers from a single mission. It sort of makes sense in hindsight, but I just wish I hadn't had to learn that the hard way, because there are  penalties for cancelling a mission after you've accepted it, which can easily put you in debt.You have to dock at different nodes at each station for different purposes, like buying supplies and accepting missions. The captain's chair also blocks some of the controls you might need access to when walking around, like the cab lights, which I would usually turn off to try and save a bit of power. All of this got pretty annoying after a while.Also, navigating around some of the hubs can be a bit confusing. There is a galactic map that shows all the systems for route planning, but there aren't any maps for the systems themselves. The only way to navigate those is to study the "roads" in each one visually and try to pick out the one that leads where you need to go, which isn't always obvious and costs you precious fuel and time if you get it wrong.Fundamentally speaking, this game is pretty good, and the issues I do have are all eminently fixable. But right now, it's just too frustrating to play, so it's a no from me until this stuff gets addressed.

_childDocuments_.review: "Space trucking sim" = no keybinds menu.Need I say more?*DISCLAIMER*I am clearly reviewing the games marketing here, not the game itself.  Keep that in mind before you leave an angry comment.  I am sure the game is great, but the advertising is not.*sigh* Why do I have to do this?  I have been waiting months for this, I have never sat here refreshing a page waiting for a game to launch before this, and yet I also haven't been this disappointed in years.  What were you thinking to release a "space trucking sim" without even a keybinds menu?  A complete disconnect from the audience this game will attract if you ask me.I get it, this is clearly a very story driven game, however I don't see that mentioned once anywhere in the description or about page...  This game portrays itself as everything it's not, only at the bottom in the section about the devs does it say what it really is, "an experience".  I could tell from the demo this game wasn't as advertised, I also forgave the demo for not having a keybinds menu, considering it was a demo and all... In hindsight, I should have seen this coming.I feel bad leaving a negative review after only 5 minutes of gameplay and right after launch, but I played the demo for several hours, completing it many times.  The game started off exactly where the demo did (and actually bugged for me the first run because someone hit me and got me a traffic offense before I even left the truck, when I got out my truck was flying off and I had to restart).  To be blunt here, I feel lied to.  I'm all for a story driven experience like this, but sell it as that, not some space trucking sim that it's not even trying to be.I bought this game for what it said was, and refunded it for what it actually is.  In no way do I support any game without a keybinds menu, but a "sim" game?  Come on... this is a joke, right?

_childDocuments_.review: So, after just 15 hours of play time I can confidently say that this game still needs A LOT of work.Mission rewards are too low. Prices are too high. With one mission you can barely get two "low grade" batteries.Scaling is abismal. "Low grade" batteries have 100 charge, cost 500; "Middle grade" batteries have 150 charge and cost *1000* and finally; "High grade" batteries have 200 charge and cost **2500**. So for TWICE the charge you pay *FIVE TIMES* as much. And you can't even buy a "high grade" battery with one mission.When you are in a shop/whatever, and you click back, you are in your seat and there is no other to get back into the store without getting out of your seat, walk to the airlock and reenter the shop...Systems drain too fast, circuits break down too fast.The game becomes almost unplayable after rank 5...Edit: I found the custom Settings option.Now we're cooking with gas...

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very unique game, but you should properly adjust your expectations. And don't even think about playing it without a controller.Is Star Trucker a ETS 2 is space? Hard no. Not even close. It's more akin of Everspace 2 in structure (closed areas locked behind jumpgates) and of Elite Dangerous in spirit and fully realized 3D-movement with a pinch of a Classical mechanics.You basically haul around things, maintain your rig (huge part of gameplay is resource management even on very easy) and try to navigate fully realized 3D space without bumping onto things due to inertia and momentum. That includes very precise docking procedures that can turn off many people, who bought the game thinking that Star Trucker is a 2D car game with a space skin.I really love the flow, the style, the navigaton and the gameplay loop, but I really think that the publisher sold the wrong game to the wrong people. Star Truckers is Elite Dangerous trader's path minus the combat, bloat and always-online shenanigans. It's compact, cozy and possess a very unique atmosphere of a space Texas Highway with great soundtrack to boot.It's a very solid game, but once again, adjust your expectations accordingly.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright.  So I got a little over 2 hrs into Star Trucker.  Its great as a Trucker Sim.  Its no ATS of course, but I feel like a space trucker.*There is definitely inertia and it feels pretty good once you get used to it.  It feels like youre piloting a big ass truck, and when youre outside the scale is pretty damn good.  Really gives you a perspective to make driving a tad easier.*The flying is nice with their inertia system, and from what ive read (i havent gotten any truck upgrades yet) the upgrades help ALOT.*Lots a varying missions, like shipments of things from one system to another but the item is restricted in some areas, so you have to plan your route to not go through systems where its not restricted.*There is trading with an economy.  Grab items from one system in the red and sell in the green.  Im not sure yet how much of an effect you have on that.*Witty banter over the CB isnt bad, and VA'd.  They say some corny space trucker jokes, and they're nice, but I'm not dying laughing.*Side missions dealing with the other truckers aren't bad, I haven't done very many, so the opinion may change.*Skill points are used to unlock what type of cargo/how many you can pull.*You can move around the cabin, get out and repair which is fun, but on just regular settings, but if you stray off the "highway" debris can come literally out of nowhere, and youll spend more time than you want repairing damage, which causes you to need filters/power cores more, and that gets EXPENSIVE.*You can upgrade the truck to make it faster, brake better, etc.  You can unlock paintjobs for your truck and you can change certain colors within those paintjobs which is pretty awesome because you do spend time outside of the truck picking up salvage.*Using the space suit isnt bad at all, I would like it a teensy bit more sensitive, but its not bad the way it is.*The customization options for gameplay mechanics is pretty deep and a welcome thing.  You can change all kinds of things, but (i think i dont remember) it causes you to get a little less xp for things if you make it easier.*There is no strafe or just up down thrusters for your truck which makes backing up to hook onto cargo/shops/job postings at stations can be a little frustrating if you dont pull up to it just right (there is a gameplay option to make this distance more forgiving).*There isnt an FOV option or a spring to default look button, so if you dont line up your sight in the 1pp camera, it looks real weird and hard to tell if you're drifing in an odd direction.*I do wish there were more safe spaceway instead of just the major highways, and also better signage floating when you come out of a jump where they are and where they go.*Really hoping for VR support.  This seems like a no brainer, but I understand how difficult that could be.*Mod support would be AMAZING.Its a chill arcadey Space Truck sim, and i'd say its worth the $22 I paid for it.

_childDocuments_.review: The GoodI like it. The controls feel great, It has just enough cockpit activities to feel like a simulator and the VA is good. Its basically American truck simulator Lite in space. Have not experienced any bugs and the tutorials are very clear. I can see myself sinking at least 20 hours into this. Voice acting is great too.The BadComing from other truck simulators, the hauls in this game are very short. It took me about 10 minutes to do a medium distance haul. I feel the map is rather small as well. There are a total of three jumps to get from one side of the map to the other (about four to six minutes real time). I feel this game really needs to improve on its scale. I want hour long hauls in the future with many pit stops and landmarks to look at. I want to have the sense of being out in the middle of nowhere. Planetary travel zones would be cool too. Arriving in the atmosphere and traveling through the clouds of a planet.I also feel like the AI is pretty bad. The other drivers seem to not care at all about you. They do not avoid you at all... in fact, I was trying to dock at a station and one traveled right between my and the dock as I was backing into it. The AI cars need much work.Final ThoughtsTo me this feels like a complete early access if that makes sense? Everything works, there just needs to be more. The price is fine for what it is... but I just want more. More trucks, more (and BIGGER) systems, more variety of missions, paint jobs, truck flair, truck stops etc.I am really looking forward to this game growing and hoping the devs add much more content.

_childDocuments_.review: chill game with some story on the side, so yes, its a nice game. I just finished the story and it took me 45 hours in total (I had already spent quite a bit on the story quest) and for €25 it's perfectly fine. However, the developers should urgently do something about the end of the story. The menu and conversations say something big is coming, but unfortunately not much happens. The only thing that really annoyed me was: you press the spacebar to accelerate, but if you look at the map, you can also press the spacebar to set a waypoint, which means that if you close the menu and then want to accelerate straight away, you set a waypoint that you don't want to set. _childDocuments_.review: I won't not recommend it, but it's a tentative/weak yes from me, almost going towards a no with the caveat that it's a small team that's obviously put love and passion into the game. The 25 euro price tag (22 during the launch sale) seems a bit steep for the content IMO, so if you're on a tight budget I'd probably at least wait a bit to see where they take it after launch.First, the good bits. The truck itself is gorgeous, and it's great how much of the interior you can interact with. The game also looks really good, and runs good. What's here is executed pretty good, and I didn't come across any bugs so far.You'll quickly realize that the game is mostly about floating from one warpgate to the other in pretty tiny hubs that take a max of 10 minutes to go through in a straight line. What's worse is that there's no incentive in any way (other than personal challenge) to stick to the "roads", you can just fly dead straight to your next gate and there's no penalties. Hell, it even makes it easier to get the "quick delivery" cash bonuses since you don't need to worry about following curvy paths.There's a lot of resource management where you have to take care of batteries that you have to buy (no way to recharge them that I saw yet), and they're *expensive* and run out fast. This is the bulk of the gameplay, since the deliveries aren't that different from one package to the next. Since you're in space, you mostly don't have to worry about maneuvering large cargo, you only have to care right when you're going to drop it off at the end, and it's usually pretty forgiving.Another part that's disappointing is you don't really have a full freedom of motion. You can rotate the truck, yaw it & pitch it, but you can't ascend/descend or go sideways. It's probably possible with driving assists turned off, but with those off the truck becomes completely unwieldy since you'll *never* manage to fully negate motion in one direction. It doesn't really feel like you're in space, it feels more like you're driving a submarine.I think it would be vastly improved with:A) Larger hub zones with more interesting obstaclesB) Some incentive to actually stick to the "highway". You can even do this in the form of penalties if nothing else, to at least promote it a bit without forcing you into itC) Some sort of upgrade/addon system to the truck where you can place things like solar panels that charge your batteries, or fuel siphons that scoop fuel from nebulae clouds. Think along the lines of Pacific Drive.D) Maybe more fun interactables inside the cabin/the world? Space mosquitos that you have to wipe off, a space carwash, a zero-g basketball hoop in the cabin, more cabin customization, stuff like that

_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: You're in space. In a vacuum. You need a space suit to go outside on EVA and still be able to breathe. But your truck has a horn and you can honk at other trunks in space. Take a moment to think about that.While this funny little break of realism may be merely amusing, unfortunately the game comes with a lot of more unrealistic game mechanics that only exist to annoy you. Like that all your truck's systems are being powered by individual sets of batteries instead of pulling power from its propulsion system (apparently the technology of generators and cables has been lost to the fog of history). Or how in a space ship with an artificial gravity generator that sometimes fails, there is no provision on this ship to strap anything down. Or how the designers of your ship made sure that your internal lighting and magnetic coupling system have both a set of redundant batteries for backup - but apparently such trivial secondary systems like gravity and life support only have a single one. Practice holding your breath while floating when you have to change their batteries - which you have to do a lot. The same batteries that can power a magnetic coupling able to pull 40-60 tons behind you outlast the batteries that simply power the lights in and on your truck.The visual presentation of this game is really top notch - but whoever was in charge of the game's mechanics needs to revisit Game Design 101.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: The game could be fun if not for one of the most busted in game economies. This is sold as a relaxing space trucker game but batteries, air filters... don't allow that. All money earned needs to be spent on new ones barely leaving any profit, Main story missions most of the time don't give any reward even tho they cost a lot in truck maintenance.I hope devs properly balance the game because underneath hides a good game. In my opinion, when a battery runs out the feeling should be "o let me change the battery", not o if I buy a new one there isn't much left for the air filter which I also need and I am out of gas also.... it is just so frustrating.I should also mention if the game recommends a difficulty I will play that difficulty and review it according to that difficulty and in this game it is sold as a relaxing game and it wasn't.

_childDocuments_.review: Delightful space americana that puts you in the pilot's seat in a way I wish titles like Escape Velocity could have. Gameplay-wise, I'd call it focused. The universe is your experience in and immediately around your truck as you haul from A to B and complete little quests, and this is done beautifully. If you're looking for multiple ships, significant customization, a complex economy, deep story, and rewarding exploration, this is maybe not your game, but honestly it's better for it. It's an exercise in setting a realistic scope, then executing on every little part of it with incredible artistry. _childDocuments_.review: Fun game but man the debris system needs an overhaul, near impossible to see it until its 2 feet away from you. Overall I like the game but there is too much tedium in the minute to minute gameplay to really enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Overview: Star Trucker is an interesting survival space trucking game with an interesting story a colorful cast and challenges along the way. With highly customizable difficulty you can set the game that's just right for your intentions. Its sound and visuals are also quite good. It is an incredible game from a person team who carry a positive tone in their interactions with the community and work to make the game even better.Additional information: The game is not A/ETS or even ATD. Understanding that is key to enjoying the game. While you can play the game in a delivery loop like A/ETS or a delivery survival loop like ATD, it differs in small yet challenging sectors and fast traveling time. From my perspective, it's a single-player story experience of a new trucker who then works with the trucking community in the new sector in various missions that all converge into one final mission at the end while trying to survive the hostile space.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; There is no reason to play this game; it's bug-filled busy work with no redeeming qualities.For centuries, mankind has looked up to the stars with wonder, dreaming of a day when they could push away from their home world and walk among them.  Star Truckers heard that yearning, and asked: what if we could make that dream an inescapable, unbreakable chain of busy-work, trapped inside a mechanical deathtrap which immediately siphons away any meager earnings you might squeeze out of your labor?With over a dozen hours in, even if I'm willing to overlook the potentially game-wrecking bugs, I'm unable to find motivation or a desire to play the game, (and I'm being extremely charitable with the use of both 'play' and 'game' here.)You aren't a character, you're a faceless, anonymous, trucking drone.  There's no narrative arc.  There's no conflict.  No goals other than to keep buying batteries and not hit things while you drive.  You can't visit and walk around in any of the buildings you fly past.  You don't meet any new people, other than the handful of one-dimensional personalities on the radio who just give you more jobs, (and unskippable dialog.)  There isn't even open road or exploration to enjoy, because you crawl across one tiny, debris-filled outpost, from one jump gate to another, often paying for the privilege of leaving.  You can't even share your misery with a friend through multiplayer.All you get to do is move boxes from point a to point b and hope that there's a store at point b where you can replace the batteries that keep your truck running.  Oh, and you'll need to back up and dock your truck every single time you want to shop or pick up a new contract.  This space-faring society hasn't figured out how to build a job posting web page or construct a drive-thru on the side of a space station, so you'll get to waste plenty of time driving in reverse, looking at your rear-view camera, often to dock and not find an item you need or a job that won't cost more than you'll earn.There is nothing redeeming about this title.  Where a Pacific Drive is loaded with busy-work and vehicle maintenance, they at least made an effort to lead you through a long, albeit thin, narrative.  Where a Hardspace Shipbreaker was endlessly repetitive, every ship you break is a puzzle of interconnected hazards you had to think through carefully or be killed.  Where No Man's Sky's scope limits its ability to offer depth, its breadth and endless horizon offers boundless exploration and the promise there's always another world to discover.  Star Trucker offers none of this.  If offers a slow, tedious, unfulfilling, bug-plagued grind with a pretty background graphic.Think of all that AI slop you've see on social media.  The photo-realistic pictures that look like a person, but upon closer examination, they have seven fingers on one hand, or a smile with fifty teeth.  That's what Star Trucker is to gaming.  The kind of title an AI would create.  An almost successful, surface-level, recreation of a game without understanding that humans need some kind of incentive to engage with the system it created.You should do literally anything else with your life than invest part of it on this title, even when it reaches a 90% discount on Steam, which I expect it to fairly quickly.  Almost any other use of your time and money would be more rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: I waited a year for this game and it has absolutely not disappointed. This is not a game for everyone, but if you are just looking for a relaxing time and a very customizable game play experience, then you will get many hours of fun out of this and it will be well worth the price. I am not really a truck sim kind of person, but you put anything in space and I am there to at least try it. I don't really know why this game caught my eye, just something about the idea of a big rig in space scratched an itch I didn't know I had. The actual gameplay is top notch imo. Yes, it is repetitive, but I don't really think that's a bad thing. This is not a game for the hardcore truck sim fans, or the pain-loving Souls-like fans. This is a game for someone who is looking for an immersive vibe. And this game nails that. The controls take a good hour or two to learn, and another several hours to really start to master. Even at almost 20 hours I would say I am at like a 5 or 6 out of 10 when it comes to the driving. You do start to get the feel for it though, and eventually it will stop seeming weird and you will want to test out different ways momentum, speed, and angle can change your direction. You can also sort of drift, it takes a second to get there, but it feels pretty cool once you do it.There is a story, it's more like a bunch of side quests, but more like AC Origins side quests where they are very fleshed out and have a solid start, middle, and resolution to them. You really get to know the side characters through the dialogue (which is actually great, the VAs actually brought some top notch performances to characters you mostly listen to, but don't see) and nothing in the game ever feels unnatural as far as that dialogue is concerned. The side quests are also never forced on you, you can start one, half way finish it, go do something else, and then go back and finish the quest. It is very much a "make your own fun game."The gameplay itself can also be heavily customized. My recommendation is to play through the first hour on the Recommended difficulty, and if you like the game, figure out what you like and don't like about each of the game play systems. Then, start a new save and make a Custom difficulty and change everything you want. You can also skip the tutorial using the custom settings and that's a big W on the devs for that option. Speaking of, and I have to mention this no matter how many times people have said it. This game is made by TWO PEOPLE. It is actually insane what they were able to create and package into a 1.0 full release. Not to mention they plan on continuing to update this game and to add more content down the line. I'm not gonna say you should buy it just because of that, but, if you are the type of person this appeals to then keep that in mind when you see some of the crazy stuff they were able to create together. It is truly a testament to what indie gaming is in the modern era. Overall, I believe Star Trucker is, at least for me, an absolutely amazing game that is well worth the price tag and that I cannot recommend enough. I will continue to play this game and rack up hours, possibly to an unhealthy amount, and I hope that everyone this game is for finds this and loves the hell out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: The game has its charm. I really enjoy it so far, and probably will for a couple hours more.Before you buy, be aware what this game really is.It's not really Euro Truck Simulator in space. The economic side of the game is quite limited, as of now, but the gameplay loop is enjoyable.There is some sort of a story going on in the background, you can engage with it at will, whenever you fell like it, apart from doing normal deliveries.I cannot really put a finger on it, but the game is somewhat confused about what it wants to be.The driving/flying part is okay, much more comfortable on controller (also, runs great on SteamDeck), but manageable on PC. Interacting with the rig howewer is cumbersome without a mouse (there is no dedicated button for cruise control, responding to radio calls etc., you have to point at the button/radio and interact with it. It often leads to crashes, as you are not looking at the road).Navigating space is also strange.There are many systems you can travel to, but only Atlas Prime seems to be well thought out and organised. In other systems the game turns into a Rock Dodging Simulator, as there are no highways or they are not well marked.On Altas Prime you just follow the road to the nearest station and then choose another road to the next station etc.Some tips before you play:a) DO NOT choose the predefined difficulty levels. They are crazy unbalanced and DO NOT match their descriptions. The "Driver" difficulty pays you pennies on deliveries and any scratch to the rig is REALLY painful. You can either go into the custom one, or try the game out for about 20-30 minutes to understand what settings mean what and start over. The game is rather linear, unlocks come from the story, so starting over is painfulb) Delivery docks are usually short for the station names, use it to navigate betterc) Invest in a different figure at the front of your trucks. Seems cosmetic, the wings threw me off sometimes when I was aimingd) The rig has a lot of inertia. The steering changes whether you are cruising, accelerating, slowing down or on cruise control. Be aware of that.Some things I would love to change about the game:a) Make navigating the systems easier. Finding a proper road to use, or finding the road at all is unwieldyb) Rebalance the difficulties or at least provide more description as to what they entailOverall the game has its charm. The soundtrack is awesome. When you get a hang of driving it's really enjoyable and the story elements provide some nice variety for the gameplay loop. The visuals are also great, but are rather generic.The game also lacks in tutorials and explanations about how everything works.Would definitely recommend, but make an informed purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Truck Simulator in Space, manage your rig's vitals, look for salvage, avoid asteroids, safely deliver cargo, and explore the cosmos. Live the dream of living like Ellen Ripley before she got attacked by a xenomorph. Did notice there is no current method to map controls so keep that in mind before checking out. Hoping they add HOTAs support in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: This game is about constantly micromanaging the truck's various systems with a little driving on the side.  There should be a way to recharge batteries from docking with stations, and having the ships systems repaired from the stations instead of having to  replace batteries and computer chips, and air filters every 5-10 minutes.  When you aren't replacing components on your truck, you're climbing out on the truck to patch an air leak because of random spawning debris that your clunky ship is unable to avoid unless you're crawling at low speeds.  Systems don't have redundancies, gravity goes off and all your cargo flies around the cab regardless if you are moving or not.  There's no cargo net to keep cargo in place and bumping anything devalues the cargo making it next to worthless for resale.  What truck driver doesn't secure his/her cargo, especially fragile cargo?
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: This is a no brainer if you are a fan of ATS/ETS2. It's really cool because it adds a whole other dimension to that formula, up and down. I am much more impressed with this game than I thought I would be. It is quite well fleshed out, with many systems to monitor and interact with. I took the advice of others and made a custom game so that I could turn down the battery drain, which I had heard was quite aggressive, and I'm having a great time with it. The graphics are just beautiful, and I do not thing I have seen a single bug, nor have I seen a single frame drop. This is damn impressive guys, well done! This would be incredible in VR.Here is some feedback for the devs.....One thing I would like to see is Hotas support. If I could use my dual sticks would be awesome. It would be nice to have some more songs for the radio, but I enjoy the ones on offer now. It would be nice to use the CB without losing full control of my ship somehow. Maybe a long press of a button? On a spacewalk, when I open a box, It starts spinning, and makes it difficult to place things inside the box. All in all I think this is a really chill and polished game, and it gets a thumbs up from me. I am glad it exists, and I look forward to updates and dlc's.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game.  I was hoping for more of a "long hauling"  Eurotrucker. What I got was pulling in and out of stations. Trying to control the truck was like trying to push an elephant across the rug on its nose even after hours of trying to get use to "flying the truck".  I have played many space flight games but trying to handle the truck was nearly impossible.

_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of sci fi and American Truck Sim, I expected this to be a perfect game for me and I'll be honest, I wasn't 100% sure what I expected. The atmosphere is spot on, just enough tongue and cheek for American trucking nostalgia, but the "roads" are less of a network connecting everything and more of just random strings that don't feel like they connect anything. The controls are also overwhelmingly picky, with the slightest touch of a joystick or button and your truck either doesn't move or starts flying off making it near impossible to stay on said "roads". The maintenance minigame is a great concept and cool at first, but I can easily see where it'll get tedious as it just seems to be "replace power core/O2 filter" or "go out of truck and place patch". If the controls were more manageable I'd say recommend, otherwise I say hold off.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I love so much of this game. Once you get the hang of the flight model, it's fun to zip around corners like an insane person. It's fun to run on a single engine through a sector to give the other one a chance to cool down. I love setting myself on a course and disabling the assist so it's just a drift. This game has been one of the most technically spectacular feats that I've ever seen come out of a two-person studio. It runs well, and I've only become aware of a single bug in the whole time that I've been playing it. It's perfectly scratched the itch I've had since I first stumbled across it in August of 2023.I can't recommend this game because some of the interactions between core gameplay elements turn it into an anxiety generator without a mechanism for rewarding the player for living through that anxiety. While I hope that the game receives updates that remedy my intentionally nonspecific issues, it's not an Early Access title and it is likely exactly what Monster and Monster envisioned.My current save is in pretty dire circumstances, so I think I'm going to start a new custom difficulty game when I play next instead of trying to continue it. I want to switch this review to recommended, and I feel like that'll give me the best chances of reaching that goal, even if I have to explain that I don't recommend the recommended difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: I've not gotten too far into the game but this scratches  every itch that I have in this kind of game.The Cons:I come from Space Sims. This game isn't one, its not trying to be one either. Getting used to not having lateral and vertical thruster movements takes some getting used to. This quite literally is a Space Trucking game in that sense.The economy can be pretty harsh. Some of the essentials you need to survive can cost multiple trip's worth of pay to buy, and while you can find them in beacons sometimes, this game more than any other requires you to play the early game right to not get yourself into a death spiral you can't climb out of.The Pros:The reason why I play games like Star Citizen is because I want as much as possible to move away from the idea of inventory screens. I like it when an object has a physical presence in the world. All of the supplies you're going to need for your truck are going to take up space, they need specific storage to not get damaged. This interacts with the rest of the game too. If your gravity goes out, your cargo will float around in your truck. If you stop too suddenly or get in a collision, your cargo will fly out your shelves. You can even die if you have things laying around your truck and they fly in your direction.All of the maintenance aspects that the game has aren't just busywork. Outside of the resource management of power cores and the durability of internals, you can fly in bursts of acceleration to not overheat your engines if they're too hot, or turn on cruise control if they're getting too cold.There's "roads", but roads make you take longer to get around, you spend more fuel. You can drive offroad, but then you will have to dodge space debris which if it hits you makes you have to spend money on repairs, time repairing hull breaches, and may even damage your cargo. And this is before I get into all the biome specific hazards. I just unlocked an area that has electric storms.I got this game, started playing, looked at my clock and 5 hours had passed. So far, its really really good and I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Star trucker has been a blast for myself, being that I wanted more from the space travel of Starfield, here it is. i can finally move my ship minutely through asteroids hauling all that stuff I got off of that planet. Now, remove the space combat, and planet side excursions, that's still the same game, so more elite dangerous mixed with euro truck sim 2. BUT WAIT, there's ship modules you have to keep running using the money you make from deliveries and scavenged scrap from random encounters to add difficulties on your otherwise normal truck route. This (yes rhetorical because its my review so its my opinion) makes a great challenge for me because I have started falling asleep on my 2 hr long drives from england the spain routes in ETS2. The game is not holding your hand, and you'll need to read up on everything in the handbook in the glove compartment to make sure you are up to speed. Now, end game wise, at this review I'm 11 hrs in and I dont have any ability to stop my grav drive depletion rate other than turning the system off when not in use, which for that matter I turn off all lights and most systems when "driving" to save on power cells because the game can be very unforgiving if you're not save scumming between jobs. Hit an asteroid? 30% hull damage, which equates to about 1000$ in repairs, which is about one job which could have multiple slight "collisions" as it is. I feel this game is a good buy and Many will get enjoyment out of this as a survival game, like the zombie oregon trail, where you are constantly trying to scrape by. But there could certainly be improvements like lowered power degradation, an ability to skip time (seriously I waited 20 minutes real time to finish a job because traveling out of sector was too long but I was too early on a job) and providing either a method of armoring your rig against damage or lowering hull damage to a more reasonable level. Either way, I'm, with the game for the long haul and excited to see what will come in the next couple months.EDIT**Devs are currently working on the game, and patches have addressed the battery life within the truck. Drop points and quest lines have been fixed and the game has become more forgiving and more laid back for the trucker sim, I am quite happen with the current state.EDIT 2Devs have fixed consumption rates and have given the game a more ETS2 laid back feel that many had hoped for, as well as keeping a general space survival feel. It is a good balance, and im happy with the hours of content its provided.

_childDocuments_.review: You might enjoy Star Trucker if you are someone who:- Has reached their dad era of gaming- Thinks the word logistics is sexy- Has always wanted to recreate the asteroid chase scene in The Empire Strikes Back- Prefers games made by small passionate teams- Enjoys survival games- Enjoys getting their hands dirty vs being in upper management- Likes tactile/hands on gameplay- Enjoys sounds like closing containers, screwing in lightbulbs, and filling up a gas tank.- Listens to podcasts while they game- Enjoys having a home/ship away from home- Enjoys sightseeing- Gets satisfaction from doing repetitive tasks efficientlyIf this sounds like you, consider giving Star Trucker a look! Read on for more thoughts. Skip to the end for my biggest reasons to play the game. I wanted to wait a while until I made this review because I wanted time to get to know it and also because the devs have been adjusting the game regularly. I won't comment on specifics of progression or game balance really since that can be adjusted to your preferences and the devs are still working on it. I just want to give you an idea of how the game feels to play and if you think it would be a good fit! I played on normal difficulty so I will be basing my thoughts on that mostly. Star Trucker at first seemed right in line with ATS and other driving simulators which got me pretty excited. However, after playing for almost 50 hours I can say that this is not really what the game plays like. Instead it's a fantastic survival game with a driving/space simulator layered over it. Batteries deplete, air filters degrade, and you will be patching, prodding, and jury-rigging your spacecraft constantly to keep that hunk of metal floating through space. Every button, screen, and fuse box can be interacted with. That might sound a bit overwhelming but it came to be part of the immense charm that this game has. More than once I found myself operating my controls with my space suit on because I forgot to change the air filters and had no air in the cabin. The game has plenty of tense moments like this where either the environment, your financial situation, or your own forgetfulness is trying to kill you. Don't get me wrong there is plenty of hauling that you will be doing but it isn't like ATS where you will be driving from one end of the map to the other. Instead there are a host of areas of different sizes connected by warp gates. It doesn't usually take very long to get from one warp gate to another and you will often be dodging space debris so you won't be getting as much of a chill out and drive experience as you would in other hauling sims. Added on to the hauling aspect is the ability to buy and sell individual items at space stations which you will need to pick up one by one and store on a shelf or in a box to keep them safe until you can find a price bubble to exploit. It's quite a bit to juggle on top of repairs, tolls, and any fees you incur but over time I found a happy rhythm of selling my half-used batteries, replacing them with new ones, buying items cheap, looking for price bubbles in other stations on the map and then hauling cargo on the way there. It became an intensely satisfying loop. This is getting much longer than I was expecting but that's only because I really have fallen in love with this game. I'll wrap it up with the biggest reasons to play this game. 1 The tactile gameplay, being able to flip all the switches, pick everything up, replace parts. It conveys the feeling of flying in a real spaceship better than any space sim I've played so far.2 The scenery. The game is  GORGEOUS and there are a variety of stunning locations and  environments.3 The survival challenge. Finding the balance between operating costs and profit  in a hostile world is a real challenge and a fun one at that!4. The story. Story missions were a lot more varied an interesting than I expected with fun characters. The CB radio is great.If this sounds like your cup of tea then give Star Trucker a try! There are quite a few options that let you turn a lot of the survival aspects on and off if that is scaring you off.  the game is more than worth the asking price in my book and might become your new addiction. A few tips:- Sell your batteries before they deplete to recoup costs- Get the acceleration upgrade ASAP as it will help your maneuverability in just about every way

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having a lot of fun with this game so far. I'm not usually one for trucker sims but add a sci-fi twist and I'm sold.Maintaining the systems of the truck might be a bit tedious for some (though I know there are settings to alter the amount of tedium), but to me swapping out batteries and circuit boards, keeping your storage organized and restocked, all feels tactile and satisfying. Not to mention being able to EVA to patch your hull and scavenge parts from floating debris .On the default difficulty, the payout from the jobs vs the amount it costs to maintain the ship feels just about right to keep you invested. If your driving is reckless and you're getting into a collision every job, you're not going to be able to cover your expenses. The better you drive, the more you profit. This overlaps well with the design of the play space. The shortest route is almost never the safest, with asteroids and debris clouding the way. You have to decide which route to take given your finances, skill, the type of job and your patience.Different types of jobs add a bit of variance to the driving. Fragile loads need to be handled with the utmost care, heavy loads are less maneuverable and slow to accelerate, perishable loads slowly degrade over time and require a speedy delivery, multi-trailer loads are harder to navigate through small spaces, etc. Some hauls are sensitive to certain atmospheric conditions and you have to plan your route out accordingly to avoid any systems that would be harmful to the cargo.There is also the optional side mechanic of trading. You can pick up various goods from the stations around the galaxy to keep in your cab. Prices fluctuate at different stations letting you turn a profit if you make a habit of checking the local economy. The amount of goods you can carry in your cab is weight limited (unless you can avoid the occasional weight check), with a weight limit that increases with the skill tree progression in the game.I think the skill tree is probably the least interesting mechanic in the game. As you level up you can unlock different types of hauls (like the aforementioned fragile loads, heavy, etc). You can invest further into a particular type to increase your payout. There are other options in the skill tree to improve EVAs, and increase cargo weight, but I wish there were more interesting options (though admittedly I'm not even sure what those would be)There are some upgrade options for your truck; improved thrust, stronger hull etc, and plenty of customization options as well, though they cost a pretty penny.I've not run into any bugs or visual glitches, it's well polished.Overall it's a pretty solid game. Definitely give it a try if you're a sci-fi geek and just want to play something to relax and take your mind off things!

_childDocuments_.review: For everyone who wants to buy it: it's not a game about long rides in space, it's a game about managing your truck and delivering cargo between small hubs by jumping through warp gates. And every 15-20 minutes you have to dock at the nearest station to buy new batteries (you can't recharge them,  you have to buy new ones, and that's expensive). The skill tree is about getting new types of jobs, nothing that gives you anything useful for your truck. It's still fun, but it's not what you can expect from this kind of game. Most of the time, you have to manage your truck (buy new power cells, new filters, parts, fuel, etc.). Forget about long trips, you just drive from one warp gate to the next and that's it.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: You're a trucker, in space! Its pretty straight forward, going from point to point, maneuvering your truck and trailers. There are character quests to progress the story and freight jobs to make money, plus little salvage opportunities and potential to smuggle different types of contraband. You also have to maintain your rig which consists of swapping out power cores and circuits when they are expended. Overall, I'd give it currently a 7/10, its fun, it looks great, its simple to start but has a decent amount of depth. I feel like 10 hrs in I have a good grasp on the gameplay but I have a couple new regions to unlock which if anything like the 2nd region, will introduce new gameplay mechanics. Looking forward to seeing what they do to build on this game. That 7/10 has a lot of potential to go up if they build on it in meaningful ways.

_childDocuments_.review: Please Please don't feel like you have to play this game on the normal difficulty, I loved this game on normal but sometimes when I was tired it was a bit much. I finally decided halfway through my normal play through to play with a custom difficulty where I changed a lot of the settings surrounding resource management to be less stressful and I had a lovely relaxing time. All this to say, play the way you want, not the way you think other people want you to. Overall it is such an immersive, lovely and yes even relaxing at times game. It scratches the achievement tracker in me, it CAN be difficult and stressful if you want or it can be a lovely relaxing space trucking "simulator." I had a lovely time with this game and thought it was really fun and immersive in a lot of ways. I enjoyed the banter between the truckers quite a bit as well.

name: Ultros
detailed_description: ULTROS: DELUXE EDITION Enhance your somatic sensory input with the Ultros: Deluxe Edition – including the Ultros Digital Artbook, showcasing the psychedelic world through never-before-seen imagery from the visionary El Huervo, and the Ultros Original Soundtrack, blending Peruvian instruments with classic orchestral themes, lovingly orchestrated by Oscar “Ratvader” Rydelius. About the Game You wake up stranded, after seemingly crashing your ship on The Sarcophagus — a giant, space-drifting, cosmic uterus holding an ancient demonic being known as ULTROS. Trapped in the eternal loop of a black hole, you will have to explore The Sarcophagus and meet its inhabitants to understand the part you play. Are you the gruesome breaker of this cycle, or can you become a link from destruction to rebirth? ULTROS is set in a multifaceted realm - a vast alien landscape teeming with life. Grounded in science fiction, ULTROS comes wrapped in an eccentric art style and a mystical soundtrack from the visionary El Huervo, renowned for his work on Hotline Miami. ULTROS explores meta-themes of mental health, life, death, and karmic cycles through deep lore and environmental storytelling. Experience brutal, intimate, close-quarter combat with cosmic lifeforms, driven by a sense of urgency – where precision is paramount and every cut of your blade counts. Yet this intense combat is juxtaposed with cultivating the greenery and tending to plant life in The Sarcophagus, providing precious moments of contemplation and peace. In turn, this grants deeper access to obscured paths. The rich world of ULTROS holds many secrets for those curious enough — and fearless enough — to seek them out. A unique loop-based mechanic will allow you to start over at key moments in the story, providing opportunities to unfold such secrets, unlock different areas of the world and new abilities on a branching skill tree. Experiment with and master your own specific fighting style as you explore the world of ULTROS. Each loop brings you closer to the truth...

_childDocuments_.review: I just want to explain the negative reviews so people won't skip because they will be scared.1. The loops and reset and starting from scratch is really not bad. You can lock some skills so you do not start each reset without them. Also the loops make sense lore wise so they are not as annoying as in roguelikes/lites2. Planting seeds was not so fun for me but it's not annoying, nor it is difficult to understand. You can't plant wrong, because when you make mistake, you can dig up the seed and try some other seed. Also after some time you do not have to wait one loop for seeds to bloom fully.3. Annoying background not knowing what is interactable is weird statement. I never had a problem and never miss something. I usually didn't notice the background awesomeness from time to time and also there is accessibility options and you can make background less vibrant.4. You need different attacks so you get high quality food from enemies. Not a big deal. You can go and repeat attacks, get lower quality food and STILL not feeling like you do not have enough resources.5. There's a gradual acceleration on running, which is fine on its own, but you're punished for using the roll for movement, since it robs you of any built up speed and resets acceleration. yup if you have ADHD and have to roll during running because you are used to "dash" system in other games and you are not willing to understand that this game works differently, it may be a problem.6. Wall jump is not jumping higher but almost at the same height. Not true, you can climb. Yeah the verticality gain is lower but again, it's not like other games.7. Getting lost. This one is funny as hell. When I was playing, I was amazed how the devs led my way. It was intuitive where to go. I had only one problem and that is killing last shaman. I didn't know where to go because I left one zone unexplored and forgot that I have places to go there. 8. Weird esoteric story. C'mon what do you want? Another clichè story about princess and castle?---I had to write some defense since these people scared me and I hesitated to buy this game, in the end, I have to say I enjoyed it as much as hollow knight (can't say that one is better, hollow knight was stretched af and I was exhausted when I finished it.) Speaking about playtime - every loop takes probably one hour so it's great for bite sized sessions. There is a lot of challenge. Not skilled based but more brain based. Like.. did you know you can finish the whole game pacifist way?Enjoy the game

_childDocuments_.review: looks like a metroidvania, but is not entirely one. You get double jump relatively early... and soon after that it's taken from you. Yeah. It's a time loop where you're constantly thrown back to square one — which includes losing your abilities and even your weapon, so you have to get them again each time.It feels disempowering, to say the least. So much so that I considered refunding when it happened for the first time. But the game's acid aesthetics convinced me to push on, and in the end I think it was worth it. The game is visionary and has a bunch of unique ideas. Just don't go in expecting a classic metroidvania.It's also a roguelite — in that "the cycle starts anew" and your progress is reset after killing each boss. Except not really: each cycle also changes shortcuts and generates new events, and the level design around the zone you begin in is nothing but stellar, skillfully guiding you down a different path with each cycle despite the world being technically open. It's one thing to design a metroivania around the player having or not having an ability; it's a more daunting thing to design it around juggling abilities and constantly getting and losing them.Much more unexpectedly,  is also a sort of Farmville-like sim. You can plant and grow trees in the game. They produce healing items, but each of them also has an ability — like creating ledges over time or breaking through walls. Choosing the right trees to plant in the right places is your key to accessing every room on the map. Growing them takes time, but you can use compost to speed the process up. And also you can dig seeds out and re-plant them...Another incredible challenge the game throws at you is the Living Network. You will at one point find a net that can connect buds that are close enough to each other. When connected, they bloom, and when connected to save points, they make them teleportable. The game then suggests you connect all the map — which means going through it via unique paths, finding shortcuts and growing the right trees. The trees part was too much busywork, but generally it's an incredible idea for a metroidvania, making you look at the map with different eyes. I hope more games do that.The fights and levelling system are also unique. You heal by eating various fruit and body parts, each of them nourishing you with some of four imaginary substabces. When you get enough of which, you can unlock skills. By finding Mnemonic Mycelium, you can lock a skill in for future cycles.As for the fights, they're very easy. It's hard to die in this game. But they do things like reward you for using unique attacks instead of mashing the same one. And did you know you could tame some opponents by feeding them? Yeah.Overall, I applaud a game that isn't one more Dark Souls/Hollow Knight. It's unique and bursting with original ideas. Not all of them are executed perfectly, but they aren't annoying either. So I think  is worth buying and playing to support the future development of these ideas, if nothing else.P. S. A friend of mine asked recently if "casual metroidvanias" exist, as he doesn't like hard challenges and action-packed combat.  was the closest that came to mind. (You can make it harder for yourself, but overall it's chill.) And that too is unique.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Perhaps I went into Ultros with misguided notions. Perhaps I just wasn't patient enough with the inversion of genres and mechanics the developers were going for. At any rate, Ultros turned out to be a game of diminishing returns for me.The psychedelic art is certainly one of the game's initial draws, as is the fabulous music, which can easily evoke harmony and folly within a few note changes. Upon reading that the game could be played as a pacifist, I instantly became keen on a game I had otherwise been holding off on for a few months. After all, I had several new metroidvanias to consider in 2024. Perhaps I misread the article because upon starting Ultros, I was surprised that combat was seemingly the only way forward... at least for a time. Once a few loops are completed, the gardening mechanics begin to unfold, and your non-combat options with it, but this comes late enough in the game where I wasn't all that compelled to utilize what remained an clunky system till the lackluster end.  For a metroidvania that ultimately wishes you to eschew combat and instead garden, the controls are passable. I never felt that many of the skill tree items truly served a purpose for platforming (looking at you wall slide). To achieve the peaceful ending with the titular cosmic entity, you must connect a living network of plants. This map-wide puzzle of dot to dot is essentially the true core of the game, or said another way, the hidden game underneath the seemingly basic metroidvania. Problem is, once this became clear to me, I simply had very little goodwill left towards the game to play it this way. I just wanted to be done with it, opting for the easier violet ending. A sad notion since I had been so keen on this game being pacifist. It's clear people really like Ultros for the gardening and living network. But after so many hours of wandering the wrong way, or trekking through the same mundane area after another loop began, I simply wasn't compelled to play any more than I had to. As I trudged through my final two areas, I wondered how a game I was so jazzed about for the first eight hours or so now felt both tepid and like a teeth-gnashing chore. Some of this chalks up to time and circumstance, and inevitably, comparison. Perhaps that's unfair to say, but when compared with the puzzles and secrets of Animal Well and the combat of Blasphemous, both still fresh in my mind, Ultros simply felt okay most of the time. With the emotionally rich science fiction of 1000XResist still beating in my heart, Ultros' hands-off lore-approach to story simply made me shrug. At the end of the day, I simply wasn't compelled.Had the gardening mechanics began a few hours earlier and not remained so opaque for a total of 23 hours of play, or had the game ever hinted in the direction forward just a smidge more at times, perhaps I would be in a different place with Ultros. Perhaps. But probably not. You see, I'm learning something about myself as a gamer, which is that unless a game is sheer fun - like Nova Drift, Minishoot Adventures, or Vampire Survivors - the immersive factor of a game for me must come from either excellent and/or innovative mechanics and puzzles and/or character and story. It could be literary like Norco or Citizen Sleeper. It could be exploratory and tactile like Jusant or Sable. It could be mind-altering like Cocoon or Fez. But lore alone does nothing for me. This penchant in the medium to sprinkle lore about does not make me want to complete a game. And outside of a few lackluster plot points, Ultros hinges a lot on lore and some curious mechanics that I never really clicked with. A shame, but at least some folks are digging it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Ultros is a solidly built, and interesting, take on the metroidvania genre - combining the familiar exploration, puzzle, and combat aspects with an almost roguelite loop system and its connected plant system, it's something I honestly am enjoying a ton.Pros -- Beautiful art and music style (while the screenshots look chaotic, it is actually super easy to follow while playing)- A proper story told in a mix of dialogue and illustrated cutscenes- Combat is fluid and easy to learn (though the gameshow segment can get a bit fiddly - won't say more than that to avoid spoilers)- There is a lot to explore and experiment with, even though the map is only about average size.- Never was left wandering aimlessly, if I was going a direction I hadn't gone somewhere before, there was always something there.- Has better roguelite progression than most roguelites these days (you unlock items to keep your skills run to run)- I tried a few times to intentionally get softlocked (such as not getting my tool that provides my movement tech, when going to a new area) - and there was always a way through, even if a bit more difficult.Cons -- Keyboard controls feel clunky, even though they're rebindable, this is definitely a controller game (works near flawlessly on controller)- The flying mechanic needs some more time in the oven for controlling it (though this won't fix some of the 'you may not pass' type things that keep you from shortcutting or getting soft locked)- You generally need specific plants in specific locations for a completionist run, so it will take some guessing in certain locations.Overall, I enjoyed my time with it, and can wholeheartedly recommend it to fans of metroidvanias - even though it is on the easy to moderate end of things in terms of difficulty, even without accessibility features turned on (yes, it has visual and difficulty accessibility options for players that need them)Want to watch the gameplay, and get the full review? You can find it on youtube @

_childDocuments_.review: A very interesting take on metvan I've never seen before. For those saying that it's a rougelite or rougelike, they haven't played the game or played it enough because it's not. It has some elements with it's cycle loop that plays into the story but I would say it's almost genre defying in this sense because it doesn't fit a traditional metvan progression system but also is certainly far from a rougelite... if anything it has a carry over story similar to that of story driven rougelites like hades, but it's mechanics and progression are very different... in a very good way. A very unique and fresh twist on the genre, it's certainly made for people that love the genre and have played all it has to offer, in terms of creativity, ultros completely kills the competition. Simply put, i have never seen a game with so much debate over it's genre and progression where almost nobody really knows what the game has to offer, its completely unique and you will probably never play anything like it---except for maybe future clones of this style because of how cool and fun it is to play. The art style, i think, is a big selling point to the experience. The game is handcrafted excellently. I was originally gonna play the game on shrooms with a buddy of mine but decided against it as you are almost looped into the phyc experience while sober. Really does feel alien, especially with the text, story, and gameplay feeling so different and un-understandable, it really does immerse you in a different world. It feels like the devs were able to pull the dimension from an acid trip and put it into visuals, really great work on the art. Something else I've noticed with regards to the handcraftedness is how everything feels so meticulously thought out and planned. For example, when planting a tree and coming back to that location for a new cycle, it now perfectly unlocks the next area, or not having the extractor at a specific part, everything is catered to different mechanics and no double jump---i never feel stuck or lost and the large map makes it so exploration is constantly at the front end of the game, and the environment feels like everything was thought of in making that experience feel organic. As for the characters, I really like a lot of their personalities, and the way they play into the broader ecosystem has the npc elements of the world really come to life. You aren't just a brute mindlessly killing, as you advance the story you can cultivate the environment, leave food in soil for compost for new exploration, tame various alien pets---capturing a lively ecosystem in 2d games is a task for sure, since you lack a lot of the "realistic immersion" so coveted in gaming. That being said, i find 2d games often more immersive and ultros is no exception... it actually might be an exception in how well it pulls off the immersion. In very few games do you not feel like the agent of interaction that the world revolves around, in very few games do you actually feel like a part of the ecosystem in a real way. Their are certainly broader themes of environmentalism throughout the game, and the way the mechanics don't shy away from it either is important to! Making sure to kill the species around you in a specific way, or making sure to plant a specific kind of tree to get an item or faster route, or anything like this---its a game that rewards the player for taking care of their environment. Nature isn't simply a tool for your exploitation, where you run in and kill everything in site and burn it all down, it's more so something that you need to interact as a part of and give back to if you want to progress (great game design in that aspect). A critique that I've seen levied at the game is the lack of mob variety, but I completely disagree with this in the context of the game. First off, their is a decent amount of mob variety, but a look at the design of this game makes it obvious that it wants you to be a genuine part of the games ecosystem and handle every mob in a unique way---knowing this makes it obvious why there aren't just randomly genned slightly different critters to be mindlessly killed, because you need to recognize and form a connection with each unique monster type, some of them you need to use a specific mechanic on, some of them you can feed and they'll be your friend, most of them you can do a lot of unique things with, keeping the variety low makes each one actually have personality and makes them feel special. Overall, I think the major thing that ties the game together as that the devs actually gave a ♥♥♥♥ about the environment crafting... when building metvans i think the immersion, ambience, and "vibe," of the game are the most important elements, and in this way, the unique art style, creative game mechanics, world interaction, cycle loops, mobs, and gameplay come together to make an extremely tightly knit and cohesive experience. I would recommend this game to anyone that likes 2d games, metvans, rougelikes/lites, or any isometric type genre as I think it excells in everything it attempts to create a great player experience.

_childDocuments_.review: It's really an arborvania - a large chunk of your tools revolve around planting and cultivating things and it goes hard on the depth surrounding them. It's a fascinating game that takes a little time to show its hand, but when it clicks it's fantastic. It's absolutely not a traditional -vania though, so go into it with no assumptions about how things work.For me, it definitely wasn't what I expected, but I love what it actually was.

_childDocuments_.review: Visuals are top notch, I know people have a problem with the loop but it’s mostly ok, the biggest issue is simply figuring out what/where to go.
