_childDocuments_.review: Extremely unique Metroidvania with gorgeous visuals and music. I thoroughly enjoyed the game-play loop (pun intended)  and the process of connecting everything together for the final ending was very satisfying. If you're looking for a fast-paced, combat oriented Metroidvania, this isn't it but if you're here for the exploration and chill vibes, it's a 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: I played through and enjoyed the game and would recommend it. The progression via loops is interesting and well executed. The living network is also a very cool and innovative mechanic.I was not a big fan of the "forced variation" combat mechanic. The combat is OK but not fleshed out enough for that. There definitely are bugs - I've reached points where I got stuck and had to reset, or once my game just froze while teleporting. However these were infrequent.Nevertheless, on the whole I enjoyed the game and would recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: This game immediately pulled me in with it's bizarre artstyle and character designs, and while the equally bizarre story and exploration kept my engagement for a time, having to constantly get sent back in the time loop and regain your sword as well as double jump and exploration tools starts to get a tad old after the first few goes around. It also doesn't help that it's very easy to softlock yourself in this game, because whatever you did in a prior cycle will affect the future ones. That means if you plant just one wrong seed in the wrong place, you pretty much lose all sense of forward progression and can't fix it unless you  go all the way back to that previous cycle.I wanted to see this game through to the end, I truly did. But I just don't feel as though the game has enough going for it to justify more of my time.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: A thoroughly innovative and unique Metroidvania title that asks you to engage with its environment much like a gardener tending to their crop. While the combat isn't the greatest, you quickly realize that the game is telling you that there's more to the game than combat and that's when the world starts to really make sense. Highly recommend if you're a bigger fan of the explore side than the combat side of those kind of games.And as an aside, ignore any review that calls this a roguelike or has roguelike elements. This is not a roguelike, it has a looping structure for a very specific reason.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game with a chill soundtrack. Fascinating gameplay concepts, but needs polishing on late game mechanics.  Chromatic abberation should never be used as a persistent effect, but at least it can be turned off.I have one piece of advice for anyone starting this game to save you some headaches later.Are you readyHere it isPlant every seed you get in every garden you find. Doesn't have to make sense, just make sure all your seeds are in the ground as soon as possible.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Solid gameplay but the restart mechanic over and over is just to annoying to me. I really dont enjoy having to go get all the things i worked for already. Anytime i beat a boss i end up putting the game down for days because i dont feel like redoing it all over again. Also, the game could use just a little bit more explanation fo whats going on and waht I should be doing. I also never know what plants i should be planting where. So, overall, its not a bad game... jsut wasnt for me
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: First: ignore the negative reviews saying this is a roguelike. Its a straight metroidvania, and it tells a tale about cycles. A few scripted resets happen and it makes sense in the gameplay perspective, and its good.Very good game in general. Good movement, combat is super stylish and the visuals are amazing, and its an incredible setting to get lost in.Getting the true ending is a massive chore though. If you're still having fun exploring, you'll probably have a nice time!
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: I have played the demo and immediately decided that I need to buy this game because it looked like a really great metroidvania with a nice gimmick around killing enemies and kinda fluid movement. Unfortunately, this euphoria ends with the first ending and then it becomes a tiresome, grindy farmer simulator. You won't be killing anything because it is pointless and all the great emotions you've felt in the demo will fade
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I wanted to like this game, I just couldnt. The art direction is cool but everything just blends together making for different areas to look all too similar. The combat and movement feels far too stilted ala browser flash games from the 2010s. Maybe with some updated I could see the game getting better but it just didnt do it for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: From the trailer I thought it's just yet another slasher-platformer, only with cool aesthetics, but boy was I wrong. It starts as yet another slasher-platformer, but then transforms into a completely different game, and by the end it fully becomes an exploration puzzle. Luckily for me, I love both genres and especially love when games throw in some surprises, which this one has plentyAnd the aesthetics are still cool all the way
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: The music is awesome, It catches the atmosphere of each region; mellow when it is supposed to be, and dramatic when it has to. The graphics are - in my opinion - amazing. I love the art style and it fits for the kind of crazy journey, this game is trying to depict.Anybody who is complaining about rogue-lite elements, didn't really get the game. I would even argue, that the game doesn't have rogue-lite elements, at all. What you experience in the game is part of its narrative and every time, the game evolves into something else, as you learn more about its mechanics and then, at a certain point, you figure out what the game is about and that you as a player have taken part of it, together with the character.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the visuals and the sound design at first. But as a metroidvania it's really mid. Stopped being fun as soon as you hit midgame, I felt like everything I was trying to do I was either hitting a wall I didn't know how to surpass, a mechanic was poorly implemented (like the cross-propagating plants? Glitchy as hell.) and I just flat out didn't want to have to keep doing a particular area over and over again and tried to avoid it however I could.  If I'm actively avoiding sections of your game, it's not a good game.Put this game back in the oven, it's still raw in the middle, I'm not eating it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: A unique take on the metroidvania genre, if you like the art style the game is worth experiencing.While I did enjoy my time with it, aspects were missing which make similar games better. like interesting level design/ enemy variety. most of all I wanted to know more about the story since it's definitely indepth yet its conveyed to cyprtically to be fully understood as you play.all in all Ultros is a mixed bagged and if your looking for a interesting take on the genre this is it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: I was loving this game until the latest update was released. Previously, you could air-dodge, perform a wall jump, and then execute another jump, allowing you to scale walls slowly. It felt reminiscent of bomb jumping in Metroid, adding an exhilarating mechanic that rewarded skillful players. But this latest update removed the extra jump you get. This method became my primary means of navigating through the game, often granting access to areas early. Without it, I'm afraid I won't be returning to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: This is a metroidvania, sure.But this is a small part of what it is.Your actions impact you far more immediately and subtly than expected in most games.And you do not have teleportation initially to hammer home that fact. You are forced to walk through the results of what you have done.By all means, fight your way through the creatures, to the last.But as the Gardner says, "It is never too late to start anew". There is a way to fix what is broken.Other great things include the music and the visuals. One will NEVER complain about lack of color with this game. I keep having to stop and look at the backgrounds. Not even as an achievement, just because it is that gorgeous and mystifying.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: It's like metroid, but the combat and general movement is meh and you're in a time loop, which wanes the joy (though not much if you're in for the view). But the true mechanic is gardening, which is cool. Also everything looks like a lsd trip that goes well. The music is stupidly good. Overall, it's a cool game. Has its flaws, but def would reccomend.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely obsessed with this game. Attention to details and meticulous care is embodied not only in the environments but the mechanics of the game - curating and planting seeds, feeding and herding critters, nurturing soil, killing (if need be) with precision to avoid trauma... Beautifully crafted from art to writing to sound (highly recommend picking up the artbook and soundtrack). There are certain pain points, sure, but if you allow the game to take you through the journey it's an incredibly deep and moving experience - a unique metroidvania that shines with its environmental puzzles not only requiring your knowledge in tools and routing but also your understanding of temporality and how everything interacts in the ecosystem.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond the trippy visuals and haunting soundtrack (which are great, to be clear), I struggled for the first couple of hours to see what makes this truly unique relative to other Metroidvanias. But, I'm a fan of the genre, so I kept playing...Only about half-way through, maybe ~8 hours in, did I begin to understand the weird masterpiece unfurling in front of me. The "story" is cryptic, but its beautiful themes are communicated through its spiraling structure and ever-evolving gameplay mechanics, which encourage a lot of creative experimentation by the end.A special piece of art that will linger in my mind for a good long while!
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Ultros has two major things going for it. First off, the visuals are stellar, looking like a bit of a 70's acid trip. Second is the unique time loop mechanic that encourages exploration and experimentation with different abilities. The big knock against the game is that combat is entirely too easy. There is a system in there that rewards players for switching up their moves when killing enemies, but the enemies rarely take more than a couple hits. This extends to bosses too which are impressive to look at but go down far too fast. That still doesn't ruin the fun that comes with filling out the map, so definitely check this one out.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: I have rarely if ever played a game that had such a mechanical depth as Ultros. It takes some time and perseverance to get there but once this game clicks it really clicks. Everything hangs together in a spectacular way; every system informs and impacts the others and the tools it gives you to interact with them offer so much freedom. I love this game. Its definitely not what I was expecting and probably not for everyone but this game is phenomenal.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: This game has just fantastic graphical style and even better music. For me it was worth playing just for the atmosphere. That being said, it has its problems.First, the gameplay does not feel good to play without few of the upgrades in the skill tree (and even with them is mostly tolerable). Fighting without at least 3-hit combo feels like a drag. Even worse, all the game you are planting various seeds, often in the walls and ceiling. The thing is, your character needs to unlock a skill to learn how to throw things (sic!); without it is an exercise in frustration, you hit items multiple times and hope that finally they hit the target spot. The thing is, you do not see much in the skill tree, so I was unaware that such upgrades even exist. I found the upgrade to throw as the exact last in the whole skill tree and it just made me angry.Second, the game is stingy with opening shortcuts. You are forced to travel many areas exactly the same way like you were the first time which discourages re-exploring.The last thing I wanted to mention is not exactly a flaw, more like a disappointment. Ultros has fantastic concept for obtaining its true ending. It has unique gardening-based gameplay and fits perfectly into the game themes. However, it is implemented in such a way I cannot bring myself to do it. If feels trial-and-error and bothersome instead of engaging. I seriously doubt many people will achieve it, which is a pity because it had great potential. Maybe I will try later, if there will be a walthrough which makes the process more manegeable.I mostly complained here, but I stress the graphics and music were just soooo good and stylish I was quite satisfied during most of my playthrough. The game would definitly profit from more polish though.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I enjoyed the game but there are some parts of it that stop me from giving it a full recommend.Ultros has a lot of exploration and backtracking built into it with some gorgeous and vibrant art. Finding routes to get to different places on the map is fun and there are a lot of secrets scattered throughout that make exploring satisfying. The gameplay definitely feels more centered around exploration and then routing . However, combat is not very involved and base movement is good but some abilities are frustrating to use, particularly . I found it interesting enough to go through and finish but am less motivated to go back and really look for all the secrets, though playing through to the end still takes a bit of time and I thought it worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: 30h 7/10 1 Yes/No No Yes Yes in some way, some feel grindy without being the normal grindy type of doing something X amount of times No No No No No, you can play with 100% damage reduction and still unlock the achievements NoUltros feels like a complicated love. I loved playing through the game, while on multiple instances I felt completely lost, or had no idea what I was supposed to do, or more... how to do it. Because what you're supposed to do becomes very clear early on. However, I still felt so much love for this game.. till I got to the progress after the violent ending, the point I was looking forward to, working on the non-violent ending. Because halfway through the violent ending, you get the idea how to do the non-violent, and I loved that idea.. but in practice... it kinda sucks. Okay, let's break down what I mean by that because I can see that it is quite cryptic. I loved playing Ultros. It is beautiful. The style combat system makes the fights challenging but fun. On top of that, it has great settings like damage reduction if you want to turn down the difficulty a bit, but also options to fade the background because it is quite an explosion of colors. It is easy to lose your character in it, but there are settings to make that better. I also love the time loop mechanic and how that combines with plants that can grown between loops, plants that are already there, but mostly plants that you'll plant yourself. However, here we also come to one of my negative points. I totally understand why the plants have hard-to-remember names, that is what plants have... but when you need to use them in ways to reach things you can't without them... it is hard to remember which plant does which. I used a list with names that , and even with that list, it is hard to figure out which plant you need, or if you know.. where to find a seed for that (or dig it up later in the game). The story in Ultros gives you bits and pieces, for you to mash up together to figure out the story. I have the feeling I know enough to kinda understand the story and how the characters are bound to each other and this planned, but I'm not 100% sure if I do. Although the story isn't that important in my mind, I played Ultros more for the mechanics and the exploration than the story. Then the part I'm struggling with in this game... it has a lovely list of achievements, and after the violent ending I was looking forward to working on the non-violent ending.  Having to connect the plants so that they bloom is such an awesome idea. And the beginning of this idea was awesome to do, but then you get to the point where it is a struggle... you might need a different plant in a spot, but figuring out which one for many spots and dealing with those forgettable names (and for some: places where to find them) just isn't that much fun. Then having to reset a cycle to let them grow and finding out it was the wrong plant, or that it didn't grow well enough is a bummer. This system helps you with being able to teleport around, connected pods can be used to teleport. but that means you only have easy access to an area if you were already successful in connecting that area. I think that some achievements are missable because once you connect something to the plants, you can't disconnect it. So don't connect those "things" you destroy in the early loops (keeping this vague on purpose to not give too many details), to be able to get both endings, because after the violent ending, you can go back and connect them, so that seems the right order to do it in. I loved my playthrough of Ultros, and I love watching  explore the game. However, the process of figuring some specific things out for the achievements isn't my favorite, and I wish the teleport system was not connected to that part of the game. I see myself coming back to Ultros and finishing more achievements after there are good guides on how to do those things, I just don't feel like I have the mental capacity or patience to figure it out myself. I recommend Ultros to those who don't care about achievements and those who love challenging achievements. Furthermore, please if you're one of the latter people... maybe think about ways to make a guide for others so they can reach the other ending as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: So, I got the bad ending on my first playthrough because I wasn't paying attention to the story....There's no way I'm starting a new save to get the good ending I said, then I kept dreaming that I was connecting plants to the living network and here I am, 41 hours later, on my second playthrough, on my second attempt at the good ending.  I think I'm nearly there and I have the games mechanics figured out.  If you want to dive in, there's a very good game here which is part metroidvania, part puzzle platformer where you use different seeds and plants to reach different areas.  Each loop changes the map as the plants have grown and you can access different areas.  It's one of the most unique games I've played in a long time and I couldn't recommend it enough.  You could easily complete this game in under 10 hours but to get the good ending, its a lot more.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a piece of art and just absolutely stunning. The art style, the music, the atmosphere - everything. I found myself being intrigued by the story, even though I've still got a lot of question marks in my head even after finishing the game. If you're looking for a typical metroidvania or combat focused game, you might be disappointed, but if you're looking for a unique gaming experience, this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Ultros is a super stylish Metroidvania, which will feel both familiar and distinct at the same time. While I am not super far in, I am loving what I've experienced and wanted to share some thoughts.Movement and even some attacks will instantly feel familiar if you have played Dead Cells, or anything similar. However, it throws in new wrinkles, like the ability to aim and launch enemies at each other in a manner much like Guacamelee. Enemies frequently drop consumables, which not only heal you, but give you colored nutrients used to purchase new skills. Animations are nicely done, and little touches like the sliding and eating add a lot of personality. You've seen how bright and psychedelic the graphics are already, and the background touches give the game an atmosphere to leads to me just standing around admiring. Music is very atmospheric, often very ethereal and haunting. All this leads to the world feeling very much alive and complete, rather than just a setting.Plays wonderfully on Deck, zero issues thus far. If Metroidvanias are your jam, really hope you'll give this a good look, if not a try. Really eager to dive in further, and see what awaits.Edit: Updating after further play. Still highly recommended, still having an absolute blast. The cycle system is interesting, and keeps me going to see what changes from my plantings, and awakenings. The brains to lock skill tree rewards are a nice touch, and are plentiful if exploring thoroughly. Combat rewards you for varying your attacks, by having drops give more nutrients, or less if the food is "ruined" rom careless attacking.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really hard one to review. First of all, don't expect a Metroidvania here, at least not in the classical sense. There is barely any combat and the combat in general is more of an afterthought and waaay to easy.Personally this game wasn't for me, but I'm recommending it anyway if you like the following things:- A nonlinear puzzle platformer- You're interested in Biology and Phytology- If you're okay that 80% of the content of this game is optional - If you want to play a unique game that is very innovative (not necessarily good)- If you don't mind some janky mechanics.You'll spend a lot of your time figuring out what the differnt plants does, how you can manipulate them, how they grow, how you can create new spots to grow plants. The whole game is based around puzzles like these. If that's your jam, you have a very unique game at your hands here. If you're looking for a Metroidvania with good combat, this game ain't it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, great concept, wild art, combat wasn't too difficult, all around solid.  I didn't want to put in the hours to get the other ending, I don't really like the multiple endings game fad, it just seemed really tedious and I thought I would leave on a high note vs getting bored with planting seeds. _childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished it yet, I want to and I will possibly update this once I have, but this feels criminally underrated as a bold and well executed work. _childDocuments_.review: i really wanted to love this game (the demo was phenomenal) but like others have stated, its not quite a metroidvania in the way that i had it hoped it would be -the way the demo led me to believe...which is not to say the demo is misleading but rather the experience-shattering mechanic does not come into play until later in the narrative).  the keyboard controls are just dreadful...and after an hour and half of gameplay, it became tedious - the added mechanics (as one progresses through the game) were terribly executed (namely that c***ing extractor) and rather than feeling more powerful and having more fun as the game progressed...i found myself lost and hating the repetitive nature of the lack of differentiation between areas on the map (when compared to something like Valfaris which also utilizes stylized pixel art and platforming but whose different areas each of which exemplify their own distinct personality, something i cannot say for ULTROS) and  tedious and disappointing loop mechanic. I think that i would have been happier with an art-book and a short animation on YT rather than a gorgeous game that inflicted twice as much frustration as it did fun. update A.1. despite what steam analytics may state, my actual total playtime is about 4 to 5 hours. 2. I so badly want to love this game and have since seen its myriad of accolades and stellar reviews that i MAY go back and restart the game with a fresh slate and fresh perspective. Maybe knowing what to expect with regards to gameplay mechanics (and using a bloody controller instead of mouse+keyboard i will enjoy myself more. Until then, I cannot recommend this game unless one has a well-informed idea of all gameplay mechanics (particularly the 'loop'), a controller/gamepad, a keen appreciation for colour and sour gameplay ;)

_childDocuments_.review: While I really enjoyed the Art style and a lot of the plant mechanics in this game, the overall impression I got out of 8 hours into this game is that a lot of the mechanics felt a little frustrating and clunky put together. I feel I needed a guide to figure out which areas I can go to and how to perform what seems like the "true" ending of the game by connecting the living network together, and I ended up filling my head with "what ifs" of game-play decisions.  Overrall I give it a 7.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not done with it quite yet, but I believe I've got nearly all the pieces put together now.I get why people would think it's a roguelike, but it's very specifically not. You DO "start over" but it should become increasingly clear that you aren't actually starting over. Changes you make in one cycle impact the next, you can retain a certain number of your abilities (which then makes the "xp" you earn available for other abilities or for other uses you learn about later), and the more you progress  the more permanent things happen and the more the game opens up.I think part of the problem is, much like the first Darksouls game when it was released, Ultros is opaque as all hell about any of this. The best way to play is basically to mindlessly plow forward, because the game is semi-linear up until 5-6 hours in (and it's not significantly longer than that). Another good comparison might be The Messenger, where the game does a complete flip partway through, and so you really just want to plow forward blindly up until a certain point.There are good and bad things to this. It feels novel, and like you are learning things on your own that are new even if you've played dozens of metroidvanias (which I have). However it feels a bit misleading in that you might think you are able to do things you can't yet. The game feels much more open than it is until you get to a certain point, and part of that is due to incredibly level design - and also the level design that is different depending what cycle you're on. It hurts my head a bit to think about how they did that.I do also think, as fun as the big reveals are, you are asked to retread the same things a few too many times in the early cycles. It sort of feels like a 5ish hour tutorial for a 9-10 hour game. And like, a lot of it is fun while it's happening, but it's just that feeling that you are missing something the whole time when really you aren't, you just aren't far enough into the game yet.Overall, it's a fantastic new entry into the genre, with new themes and great art. It's NOT roguelike, but it does ask you to retrace your steps a lot as part of the main story, not just to re-explore (although you are effectively re-exploring basically 100% of the time). It's also a metroidvania first and foremost, not a soulsvania, which feels a little too rare nowadays so I appreciate it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't finished this all the way yet, but wow this is incredible. Visually, there is so much going on, but it works. Feels trippy at times too. Music is incredible, movement is good and combat is satisfying Story is a bit over my head right now, but maybe it will make sense at the end. For sure a good buy if you enjoy the Metroidvania genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: My favorite metroid-vania to date.Heavy on the psychedelic themes of healing, reincarnation, peace with nature and ourselves. No other game hits like Ultros does. The story, presentation, game mechanics all pay homage to the difficulties and epiphanies of heavy psychedelic experiences.The complexity and pace of the game can be something that puts people off, but let me try to convince you that the discovery and the piecing together of the story and mechanics over multiple reincarnations is all part of the experience. Explore, understand, read deeper into the lore, learn about your agency and purpose, as it is a beautiful story that can be grouped into books like trilogy starting with "The Teachings of Don Juan: A Yaqui Way of Knowledge" by Carlos Castaneda. Other shamanic themes are present as well.Combat is fun and dynamic. You get to unlock, and later perma unlock character upgrades that enhance combat.Multiple endings are possible and able to be completed on 1 save file.Ultros might be one of the best speed running games possible. Tons of theory crafting potential for plants, encounters, endings....I thoroughly enjoyed my first playthrough. Spent a good 10 hours just growing plants and trying to experiment with the mechanics. The lovely music and atmosphere make the game a joy to explore.If you are looking for an experience that takes psychedelic themes and makes them into a gameplay loop, this is going to be one of the best experiences you can get in video game form.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Game good! Positively oozing with style at basically every opportunity, Huervo's artstyle works incredibly in this setting and story. Absolutely the kind of thing I expected him to make, and if you like this check out his other works!Combat's a bit easy, though it definitely doesn't feel bad, the move variety is super satisfying to chain together even if I wish bosses didn't die after essentially a few strings of attacks with damage upgrades.I was iffy on the plant system at first, but it really grew on me (pun not intended). It only really gets tedious if you're needing to wait cycles for farming spots to show up (a mechanic only really relevant for postgame), but really going for true end where you're more focused on the environmental puzzles with them I never really had issues, especially with the compost map mechanic.Overall, it tries a lot and, while not all of it will land with some people, it makes a varied but cohesive experience with a ton of cool moments that left me eagerly chasing after what was next.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: The best way to describe this game is, "weirdly beautiful".It's vivid, sometimes insane looking, but it's quite a lovely game.It's also much more of a puzzle game than action.Combat is easy if you're familiar with platformers. But the puzzles are what truly shines in this game.I came into this game, confused and not to invested.But as I kept playing, it got like.. really interesting.This is a good game to try if you want something different in the metroidvania department.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: I play a lot of metroidvanias, this is far from the best I've played but I highly admire how unique it feels. My main gripes:Its confusing pretty much at all times, which is sometimes good (as it adds to the mystery) but often I am not sure what I'm doing or what things do. I'd have been happy with only the narrative confusion and not the gameplay confusion.Examples - certain seeds are very specific in purpose whilst others are not at all.- not immediately clear how seed growth works- you are gaining compost maps before you unlock the thing which allows you to collect compost- The combat is bad, but you have lots of health to compensate, its quite hard to lose a boss fight. Just eat and keep fighting.Recommend for anyone who plays lots of similar games and things it looks cool. Just be aware its rough round the edges.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: 2024 has already been an amazing year for Metroidvanias, and Ultros is no doubt one reason why. once everything clicks with this game, it is so enthralling. the psychedelia, the achingly beautiful musical score, the tremendous hand-drawn art, the stylish combat, the time loop Metroidvania cleverness—so good. need to play more, for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: While by no means perfect, it is refreshing to have a game try so many new mechanics and take so many risks.I think the main issue for Ultros is that it is *too* open ended. There's a definite fatigue that sets in because halfway through the game you lose any definite direction: "Here's all the objectives, go do something about them". It's rare that I want a game to hold my hand *more*.Visually stunning obviously, and I really do love some of the unique systems like the "perfect variety" combat.

_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Its a fine metroidvania, and the plant network mechanic is interesting, but it also feels somewhat buggy at times. I want to make a connection over a hill, so I attempt to splice a tree with a spitter, and it causes my game to crash. Or, I'll try to splice several of the same plant together to climb a tall room, but none of the spliced branches produce flowers - even after using compost - making them useless. I feel like there's probably a definitive way of making the network, but the freeform style allows you make some horrendous plants that seem to stress the game out. The combat is somewhat boring, and the bosses are kind of a joke - I feel like most of my playtime has been spent fighting with the plant network to get a connection across a long hallway.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Amazing aesthetics. A gorgeous piece of art visually with unique 2d graphics and vivid colors. It's like a painting.- Great surreal world with strong weird atmosphere. It feels like being inside a huge living organization, while each region has its own, unique visual identity.- Despite not looking very smooth, the low frame rate, cartoonish animations are fit nicely the overall painting aesthetics.- Well designed protagonist, characters and enemies that look interesting.- Although the gameplay lacks depth, especially in battles, the controls are responsive, easy to master and feel lightweight with no glitches and artifacts.- The map is pretty big and the metroidvania elements are well implemented. The world opens up gradually along with the abilities that you acquire. Exploration happens organically and there are a lot of new areas and mysteries to uncover inside each circle. Also, the way it guides you during the first hours giving you certain paths in order to not get overwhelmed is great.- Including roguelike elements is a great idea. The way that you affect the world, altering it and creating new paths by growing new plants and affecting upcoming circles is a clever concept. It looks like an alive ecosystem getting transformed by your actions. Memory cells and other roguelike mechanisms are interesting too.- Awesome, calm music with jazz and experimental elements that enhances the weird atmosphere and gets more rhythmical during boss battles.- Despite being pretty simple, audio design is good with nice environmental and satisfying battle sounds.- Cool storytelling. Although the story is too abstract for my taste, its poetic writing enhances the surreal atmosphere and makes it even more dreamy and enigmatic.- There are some small puzzles with cool mechanics while all this route opening via gardening is pretty unique.The bad- Battles' gameplay barely evolves. There are only few attacks, your character doesn't get particularly stronger, most of the new moves and skills are unimportant, there's only one main weapon. All the interesting new mechanics are about the exploration part. Battles lack variety and imagination.- It's not challenging at all. Enemies feel weak and you usually carry too many healing items to a point that you don't even care if they hit you. You'll die only by mistake and all this makes killing not rewarding at all.- Although the animations look gorgeous with their low frame rate they're not exactly fluid. They lack continuity and precision and during battles aren't very pleasant. Sometimes it looks like a browser flash game.- Bosses are interesting visually but their battles lack creativity and are full of simplistic, worn mechanics. They're too easy too.- There are some design faults of the roguelike part. At certain areas you have to watch the same dialogues or go through the same tutorials during every circle. This may make sense story wise, but it's extremely boring and forces you to simply avoid these areas.- The story is too abstract to a point that you're never sure why you're doing things. Lacking an understandable purpose you mostly wander killing things while bonding with the protagonist is really difficult.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: A very beautiful, fun, and interesting twist on the classic metroidvania formula. Casual in its approach to combat, but very sophisticated level design. Main gameplay loop gets tedious after about halfway through (you become a farmer, intergalactic berry harvester) but I can't overstate my excitement at what ideas and innovations this game bring to the genre. Overall, worth the money, support these devs! They'll make something truly incredible one day.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: This is a real tentative recommendation. The game is gorgeous, nearly everything else about the game is more obtuse than it needed to be. Looking at the discussion forums, there's some really in-depth stuff here that the game never asks you to engage in, which is a really fascinating design decision. A lot of stuff in this game is fascinating, but the amount of actual fun I had playing this steadily declined at about the two-thirds / three-quarters point.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: This was a pretty cool game, i love the artwork and idea behind it. I dont really want to knock it because i appreciate what they were going for, it is a bit of a choose your own adventure that can have you scratching your head about what to do next. I spent a lot longer playing thru this than i imagine most people did, probably close to 50 hours just explore and aimlessly trying to figure out what to do next. The soundtrack is wonderful, the artwork is fantastic, a few things i would suggest improving would be some sort of explanation of each seedling and the variety of growth is produces and how it can be utilized. Another thing would be the buttons are kinda clunky especially during the last fight is it evident when trying to direct those balls back at the boss. I appreciate the difficulty and cosmic concept, i hope that they do more and flesh out the ideas and game play a bit better in the future. There was a few times when i contemplated putting this down altogether, but i aint no quitter so i powered thru and am glad i did so. I really feel like with games like this that give you cool upgrades towards the latter part of the game they missed some golden opportunities to really engage those upgrades earlier on to develop a funner game play instead of just throwing them at you to use once or twice and then you are done with it. Perhaps I just did things out of order but considering how much of the game relies on gardening, youd think getting cool upgrades to splice and manipulate plants earlier on would come in handy. On a major plus side, a lot of the artwork in this game reminded me a lot of a cool cosmic doom band called Battle Hag and I thought that was an awesome coincidence, im sure the developers probably have no idea who that band is but because i do, i thought it was wicked to see.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't super impressed on my first playthrough, and right as I neared the end of the game, I accidently deleted my save file. Yikes. On my second playthrough, however, I've taken a different approach. Instead of brute forcing my way through, as I would in a typical metroidvania, I've concentrated on the gardening and interconnected world map. It's a much different, innovative, and more pleasant experience this way. I wish they would have pushed this aspect a little earlier in the game, but at the same time it makes you reconsider the map in a new way.Otherwise, the controls are good when traversing the world, but combat is not a strong suit in this game (and it really doesn't need to be). I also do question whether I would still recommend the game if it didn't have such lush graphics. As other raters have mentioned, the graphics are just sublime.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a really interesting entry into the library of metroidvania style games.Initially, I was a little annoyed that my progress got reset but do not fret, there are upgrades and unlocks later that will make the reset a lot less painful. The art is obviously amazing. I turned off a lot of the post-processing effects and turned on sharpness just so I could enjoy the cacophony of psychedelic details. Sound is equally weird and squishy.Recommended if you are a fan of the genre for something really quite unique.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: You know after the first 4 hours of playing this game I was really disappointed, the combat is beyond terrible and easy and as a metroidvenia it fell flat but after the 3rd cycle suddenly something clicked, this isn't a metroidvenia game or a roguelike or whatever people say, this is a GIANT puzzle game where the entire ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ map is the puzzle, you are basically taking double shift as a gardener and network engineer working on this giant space station while on drugs, your gardener partner while a cool dude is completely incompetent and can't do ♥♥♥♥ without your help, your boss is giant demon from another dimension that is worship by a bunch of shamans on drugs that refuse to leave their room and they all demand you to connect the wifi! The worst part is that the only cute girl around is really angry at you for some reason.As mention before the combat is terrible but good news there is a talent that let you skip combat all together so you can focus on the really cool parts of this game, the exploration and plant puzzle solving, truly an unique experience if not for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: "Hey look, another MV. Atleast it has good art and smooth gameplay" was my first thought. But it's actually so much more.The more I played, the more I discovered of the niche of this game and how well done it is.At first, the game feels fun and easy, discovering the lore and killing bugs along the way. But at some point you start understanding and questioning your ways and get to try new stuff. Let yourself wander around and enjoy your journey !PROS- There is no tutorial but it never felt so easy to understand a game- Visual art is amazing- Challenges and puzzles are relatively easy at first & always fun, but you have some really hard spots that are optional if you want to go deeper- Smooth and original gameplay all the way- Skill tree gives you a lot of liberty but is also just a good gimmick and nothing's necessary- interesting story & lore, I was always curious about what I'd get to see nextCONS - Sometimes music feels quite repetitive (even if some bosses/zones have amazing OST)- There is a point in the game where you have 0 automate transportation but have to wander all around. This can get a bit annoying.- Combat could be more detailed on everything you can do with the skill tree (just missing some short vids on your new moves to understand what it does). Same for what plants can do (names are not very clear and at the beginning it can be quite confusing) - I'm still wondering if it's all just a brainfart or if there's a real meaning (except for the obvious pacifist and ecological meanings)*MINOR* Spoilers ahead (and me giving some advice)......If you are a completionist and want to finish all endings, you'll really need to invest yourself into gardening. Make sure to not waste seeds, it's always better to have something growing even if it's not the best plant for the spot than nothing (except the thorny stuff, that's garbage plant for garbage people).I read somewhere on the net that gardening is completely optional. While this is true, it made me lose a lot of time on the peaceful ending.

_childDocuments_.review: My initial encounter with Ultros was during a Steam Next event, where I played the demo. The unique plant mechanics, alongside the compelling art and sound design, caught my attention, though I didn't progress to the first boss fight due to the somewhat cumbersome movement and combat. I was uncertain how the upgrades would enhance the gameplay. Fast forward to its official release, I spontaneously decided to dive back in, dedicating 2.5 hours in my first session and momentarily setting aside Persona 3. This time, the gameplay mechanics felt intuitive and satisfying, particularly on the Steam Deck.The game's visual and artistic direction is distinct, intricately linked to the gameplay mechanics. The concept of planting as a core mechanic significantly influences the game's world, with each plant offering unique abilities that can alter the environment. The world of Ultros is both vibrant and grim, each area exuding its own peculiar organic essence. As the game progresses, the encroaching organic elements enrich the sense of advancement, both through gameplay mechanics and the evolution of the game's world. The visuals sometimes conjure the essence of a disorienting psychedelic experience, emphasizing the game's theme of an unnatural ecosystem.What sets Ultros apart is its level design, showcasing a profound understanding of guiding players through environmental cues and storytelling. The game masterfully directs the player without feeling restrictive, maintaining a sense of freedom and exploration throughout. Although there are moments when the game enforces a more linear path, these are balanced by the overarching sense of openness, allowing players to explore and progress at their own pace.I've even tested the game's boundaries by trying to bypass picking up certain items or attempting to sequence break, yet the game has stopped me from doing anything major while still rewarding such exploratory efforts in unexpected ways. This level of design foresight and the encouragement of player experimentation are among the many reasons Ultros is so good. Here are some of the cons: Some aspects of the movement, especially flying, could benefit from more refined controls. Additionally, the combat system lacks complexity, and I've yet to face a boss battle that presents a significant challenge. The availability of unlimited healing somewhat diminishes the difficulty, even though the mechanic where food can be knocked from your grasp during healing adds an interesting dynamic. The cortex system also appears overly forgiving in subsequent playthroughs, allowing for effortless accumulation of resources and complete skill tree respecification without much effort.Similarly, using an incorrect plant necessitates waiting for a specific upgrade to rectify the mistake, forcing backtracking and potentially another waiting period for plant growth to achieve 100% game completion. Moreover, while there are methods to enhance the potency of plant fruits, the abundance of resources makes this feature feel underutilized. Currently, with access to the fertilizer, it remains to be seen if a second cortex tree or additional benefits for maximizing resources will alter this dynamic. For the moment, engaging with this system seems optional, primarily for those aiming for full game completion.Overall, Ultros is a great little game, and its some fairly cool moments that will satisfy most metroidvania fan, but its not nearly as ruthless as many of its contemporaries.

_childDocuments_.review: The Cosmic Gardening Simulator You Never Knew You Needed🌱 Plot: Imagine crash-landing on a giant cosmic uterus (yes, you read that right) and being stuck in a time loop. Your mission? Gardening. In space. With monsters. Welcome to Ultros, where your green thumb might just save the universe.🎨 Graphics: Think of a neon fever dream where someone spilled all the highlighters on a black canvas. It’s like Bob Ross decided to paint while chugging energy drinks. The colors are so vibrant, you might need sunglasses to play.🕹️ Gameplay: It’s a Metroidvania, but with a twist. Instead of just fighting monsters, you’re also tending to your garden. Because why not? One moment you’re battling a tentacled horror, the next you’re planting space tulips. It’s like if Alien and Stardew Valley had a very psychedelic baby.👾 Monsters: The creatures in Ultros look like they escaped from a 70s sci-fi movie. Giant eyeball fruits? Check. Glowing mushrooms that might be sentient? Double check. It’s like someone let a botanist design the alien fauna after a particularly wild party.🧠 Story: The plot is as trippy as the visuals. You’re in a cosmic womb, trying to break free from a time loop by talking to aliens and fighting anything that moves. It’s like Groundhog Day, but with more tentacles and less Bill Murray.🌌 Overall: Ultros is a wild ride through a neon-colored, monster-infested garden in space. It’s weird, it’s wonderful, and it’s definitely worth playing if you enjoy your games with a side of “What did I just experience?” Just remember to water your plants and watch out for the tentacles.

_childDocuments_.review: Not recommended to anyone and not worth a full price, unless you have a ton of free time for exploring and mastering this metroidvania with a sprinkle of roguelike on top (what adds at least an hour or two of unnecessary backtracking "because designer thought it'd be a good idea"), where new skills/mechanics are barely explained at best (most of the time aren't explained at all), scripts are working as they want to (not as you'd expect them to and not as it'd be handy), the picture is constantly burning your eyes with acidic colors (they've even added a "blur/desaturate background" option because were understanding that the gameplay look's like a mess) and all of that is seasoned with the barely understandable philosophical story and item descriptions. The only thing I can praise here is a built-in god-mode, which makes the struggle a bit less painful, but surely doesn't solve main issues. I'd refund it without hesitation if I still could.In a few words: it doesn't look like designers don't know what to do, it looks more like they HUGELY overdid in attempt to give birth to something unique.

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect performance on the Deck.So. I got lost. A lot. And I thought it was a me thing, because I'm an idiot. Each time you achieve a primary goal, the ship will reset and you'll have to find a weapon again, level up again, and find your way. Again. There are some stuff you can find to freeze some skills and you can plant a seed, which will grow thanks to a loop or compost. _childDocuments_.review: Ultros is a masterfully crafted Metroidvania. The universe is unique and full of details, you're lost most of the time trying to understand the world you evolve in.The story is intriguing specially because of the implications of our actions told through loops.The music and general art direction is sublime, trippy and really makes you want to progress.However, that's where I have some issues the game, the progression. You also likely won't need anything from the skill tree to progress, aside maybe the wall jump but it isn't that great or the plant upgrades if you're connecting the network.The only way forward is by hunting down the 8 shamans and unlocking new abilities with your companion.However, discover a zone, get back to 0 rinse and repeat isn't that stimulating and feels limited as you'll only be able to discover a zone at a time in a set order driven by the story.Pick it up if you love Metroidvanias with intriguing universes and incredible art and sound direction.

_childDocuments_.review: Any game with this many proper nouns in  conversation needs an in-game encyclopedia. I've played and enjoyed media with incredibly-dense worldbuilding and lore (e.g. Axiom Verge 2 or The Fountain), but this one just feels like it's too happy to sniff its own butt.But any game can still manage to be fun if the gameplay is fun, right? Too bad Ultros feels like a bog-standard "we really like Hollow Knight" metroidvania, but with even more punishment. Combat is your usual dodge-rolling, counter-striking, combo-grinding souls-lite. It has an interesting tie into progression with the monsters dropping food (better quality based on how you take them down) that both refills health and advances you on the skill tree, but that's all I saw of interest in the hour I played.The worst part of gameplay is that the game is supposedly loop-centric (like many roguelikes), but dying dumps you back to your last save, with all progress lost. I thought we got rid of that particular stupidity a decade ago. Are they going to bring back lives systems and quarter-munching next?So the lore is obtuse and the gameplay is alternately unimaginative and overly punishing. What about the front-of-the-box selling point, the art? It's ugly. The artist clearly doesn't understand  we have restrained palettes per sprite, or simplified backgrounds, or any of the other dozen techniques that make game worlds comprehensible during play. If you want crazy-weird art with restrained color schemes, try Hollow Knight. If you want basic art with vibrant colors but proper palettes, try my favorite metroidvania Dust: An Elysian Tale. More colors does not equate to better art.It's fugly, it's boring, it's frustrating, 2/7. There might be a good game in here somewhere, but I don't have the patience or endurance to find it.

_childDocuments_.review: Review! or at least some bulletin points.    • Gameplay - was nice and responsive. I was never hung up on something do to lack of control or spacey feeling controls. Also the "hunting" aspect of not repeating yourself in combos to yield better results was cool addition that ended up playing into the whole aspect of the game. everything by the end melds really well together.    • Lore - I personally would have like a little more abrupt in your face story telling (that's just me though). I did like the lore and the story that unfolded through the characters and the environmental storytelling that was there. By the end it stuck with me. I highly recommend after beating it going for the "true" ending and beating the pacifist run.    • Visuals - Easily the thing that stood out the most. the game is gorgeous and the Art style is what drew me to the game to began with. The psychedelic colors, characters and environments really made this game pop. Definitely sticks with ya after completing it.     • Mechanics - Some mechanics took a bit to understand this is where I wish some of it was more in your face with tutorials as too how somethings interacted. Like the plants interactions with the environment, or being able to upgrade your equipment. In the end I loved how they worked  and mesh together and experimenting was really fun. How the spun classics like the double jump into a new take with unlocking your skill tree through cycles it was great and I enjoyed the slow burn of it. Also adding some things I'd never seen  before made for a really cool experience. _childDocuments_.review: If you're expecting something akin to Hollow Knight with a psychedelic art style, and an equally interesting narrative, this is not it in the slightest. It's a roguelite (thus it loops, and you lose abilities on the reset) that is so high on its own sense of mystique that it offers little motivation to bother finishing. Both the information relayed to the player and that which is kept secret aren't all that compelling when examined outside of the eccentric dialogue. The art, while great to look at, is in effect jingling keys in your face and does not make up for the amount of meandering you'll be subjected to. If you're looking for a roguelite more than you are a metroidvania, there might be something here for you, but know that the price is steep for what you're getting.Edit: For clarification, the issue for me is not only that it has roguelite elements nor that it can be argued to be one. My last purchase was Oblivion Override, and I enjoyed it very much. The issue is that the demo provided ends just before the looping begins, and if there was ever a roguelite tag before release I didn't see it. So not only was I not interested in playing that genre in this setting, I wasn't expecting it at all. "Who cares?" You might ask, "You like other roguelites/likes so why is there an issue now?" Well, apart from the aforementioned, this one tries to be both a roguelite and a metroidvania, and as a result is great at neither. You don't need a dozen hours in game to figure that one out.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really excited about this game prior to it's release. The artwork in it is beautiful, and I tend to be drawn to anything time travel related. Ultros does have some genuinely cool ideas, and some groundbreaking mechanics. I love the gardening and time loop mechanics and the way they work along with each other to open up secret areas as you progress through the game. Unfortunately these are the game's only redeeming qualities. The story is nonsensical and convoluted, and full of pretentious sounding Sci-fi gibberish words. The enemy design consists of maybe 10-12 enemies throughout the entire game (excluding bosses) and those enemies have predictable, repetitive attacks. The combat system encourages you to mix it up with your attacks, but then provides you with a repertoire of repetitive and/or unusable attacks, and the level design is some of the worst I have ever seen. The game only has one questline, and even that is impossible to keep track of. map markers will not show up when you need them, and will refuse to clear after you have completed objectives. Paths that you need to take will be randomly obscured by black mist that you cannot pass. Doors that are supposed to open will randomly open and close without being triggered, and the game will frequently allow you to enter areas that you lack the abilities to escape from. When you do happen to wander into areas that you shouldn't be able to access yet, the game punishes you by locking up your maps and menus and forcing you to exit the game and restart the time loop you are on. I put a LOT of time into this game and finally gave up on it after spending several hours trying to enter the final map area with no luck.Garbage. Don't waste your money.
