_childDocuments_.review: The game is a vibrant, psychedelic, visual feast, and for me was the main initial draw of the game. Not taking into account the dazzling colours, what it does when it comes to gameplay, it does well. It is more of a puzzle game, than action, and they are what truly shine in the game. The combat that is featured is smooth, and not just a button mash fest. It encourages you to use different combos and attacks to benefit yourself with in-game loot. And that is if you choose to use the combat, as the game can be played largely passively if you so choose. The gardening and seed aspect is also well designed, making it fun to figure out what goes where and does what, allowing you to progress more and discover more interesting  areas. The loop cycles of the game, which I have seen others criticise, was personally enjoyable, and given the game is not too long, approx 15hrs, it doesn't become repetitive. The story it self is intriguing. It doesn't tell you too much, and leaves you to figure it out over the course, as it takes you in deeper.The few NPCs that feature are beautifully designed with interesting backstories and lore. Overall this was a truly fun and enjoyable experience, and personally my game of the year so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: "A Trippy Castlevania"!! says me.At the time of this review I'm a little over 12 hours in and there has been some interesting shifts in gameplay (you'll see), interesting characters without having to read volumes of text, some cool bosses, a plethora of truly incredible 'blacklight poster' art, chill background music, unusual 'skills' that aren't annoying combos of the controller buttons, and a very expansive map still left to cover. There's the usual backtracking of any metroidvania, but this was actually more FUN and relaxing than anticipated. It's challenging enough to satisfy any serious metroidvania fan, but manageable for someone looking to just PLAY a cool game with a thoughtful backstory. You aren't just running around the map lost. It's a submersive world. This game stands on it's own and isn't a 'copycat' game like many that are out there now. Overall, I think this was extremely well done!! It's worth the money, especially at it's current sale price. Buy it. You won't be disappointed!! Have fun!! <3
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Right off the bat, I can see why some people don't like this game. It's strange. Especially if you're expecting just a run of the mill metroidvania. But what this game offers in tone, story, and feeling is probably unlike anything else you're playing right now. It has a way of making you think about what you're doing that is unusual for this genre. I can't say how far through the game I am, only that I'm hooked and I think I have only begun to peel back the mysteries. If you're a fan of stuff like Environment Station Alpha, or Void Stranger, you'll fall right into it. The combat is pretty interesting too. It has a kind of parry/dodge mechanic and you're rewarded for perfection. I like it, it makes combat tense and I'm big fan of games like Sifu and Sekiro. The visuals are awesome. Cons: Bosses are pretty easy so far, and a bit repetitive, with no idea how much longer to beat the boss (no health bar, damage, nothing). It can make you feel "ok, how much more of this is there?" with no indication that you should be doing something "more perfect." A mario64 style "three stomps" would have worked well, and maybe you need to do more if you're not perfect. Maybe that is how it works? I don't know.Soundtrack is bus, so grab that even if you don't play the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Fair warning. If you are the type of player that likes min-maxing, you're not gonna like this game. There's a lot of points of no return where the game deletes your inventory, and it isn't always clear when these points of no return happen. This isn't really a problem, since the game is pretty easy doesn't demand perfection at all.If you're wondering if this game is for you, just look at the pictures and videos on the store and ask yourself "would I enjoy just walking around in this game and looking at the world?". If you do, you can expect a visceral and responsive combat system, as well as intrigueing lore to keep you occupied.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever enjoyed breaking a Metroid-Vania, or experimenting being a central mechanic in a game, or speed run routing or doing challenge runs of a game, I'd recommend Ultros.There is so much fun experimentation in this game. The marvelous gardening mechanics can open up insane pathways if you're creative enough. You can couple some plants with some cheeky high skill movement options to really get all over the map all out of order.That's so cool that I went back to play the game three times using different plants and routes, and I honestly still want more.The visuals are inspired, the VFX blew my socks off, and though there's not enough of it, the music is awesome. Ultros is for sure one of my favorite games.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Great Metroidvania with gorgeous art and amazing soundtrack, definitely underrated . A few tips to enjoy this game more in my opinion : - In post processing graphics options, turn off chromatic aberration, blur, scan lines and color grading. The game is psychedelic looking enough, no need to add these filters, they only muddy and distort the beautiful art.- Don't expect a major focus on combat. The rewards for diversifying your attacks are a nice touch and definitely worth going for, however a decent sizable part of the game is the puzzle of gardening and interacting with the fauna in a non-violent way, so be aware of that. I feel it stands out from most metroidvanias in that regard. The game's difficulty is not punishing at all.- This is not a roguelite or roguelike. There is a loop mechanic tied to the narrative, you will lose unlocked upgrades the first few times you loop, but there are no randomized environments, randomized loot or restart from beginning on death. - You will very quickly find items that let your unlocked skills persist from loop to loop, so don't freak out after losing your abilities, you will get them right back quickly enough. If you miss your double jump that much at the start of a loop, just go get it in your first 2 minutes before exploring again.- I recommend letting yourself be guided by the natural progression of the story and only start gardening more extensively when you have all tools available to you. Plant what you find as you go by giving it a tiny amount of thinking in the moment, but don't go overboard with trying to develop a network of plants until you have all tools.I think by having the right expectations, you can have a great experience with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Ultros is one of the best games of 2024, and stands among the most creative Metroidvanias ever made. The art style is dazzling, the music is symphonic and mesmerising, and the gameplay design audacious in its scope and invention. It's hard to go into quite why it's so good without touching on spoilers, but let's just say, there's more to it than first meets the eye.  Overall, it's a sensory treat, and an unforgettable game with a unique resonance, and a beautiful message at its core.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most creative and beautiful metroidvanias out there (perhaps better to call this a gardenvania?). It's a bit rough around the edges: combat is trivial and not really that interesting and movement/traversal could sometimes be a bit frustratingly opaque. But it more than makes up for that by allowing you to shape the map you explore by cultivating plants and, of course, the absolutely stellar art and music.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible atmosphere, music, sound design, and obviously the visual art style is very intricate and unique.  It's fun to run around having sort of no idea what's going on, but somehow always making it to the right location and finding the right upgrades.  Feels like a result of excellent level design.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Ultros is very much like an incredible psychedelic experience, but not in the way one may initially think. Clearly, the visuals immediately jumped out at me, and the style captured my attention. But it is in the experience of playing the game itself where we can see the developers crafted us a truly immersive experience that rewards our patience. I urge you not to rush to a guide to figure it all out, because so much of the beauty of the game comes from the process of slow discovery.In a psychedelic experience, I was always captivated by what happens when I allow the journey itself to guide me. Initially, nothing makes sense, and it can be overwhelming. But when one surrenders and lets go, that's where the true rewards lie. There's a kind of multidimensional communication of information unlike anything one's encountered before. As one immerses themselves, it all begins to coalesce and make perfect sense in its own unique way. This is the essence of the reward.This has been my experience with this game, and this game has rewarded me greatly. Be patient, enjoy the ride, and you too shall be rewarded.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderfully creative metroidvania. The game felt like there was more of a puzzle emphasis instead of combat. The rouge-like elements I actually thought brought a lot of value to the game - and I generally don't like that genre. The map was fun to explore. Movement was fluid. Really enjoyed the last 1/4 of the game. Definitely recommend the game for any metroidvania fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely beautiful game with a soundtrack that takes several hours to get old. It does get frustrating at some points, when you're trying to treat it sort of like an immersive sim, because you can feel the hand of the creator in numerous ways and it's rarely in your favor. This message was brought to you by the inability to graft augeas leaves onto anything else. I've been a fan of El Huervo's music for quite a while now, and I was expecting to see some overlap between this and the rest of what I know him for, but there's almost nothing. I can only think of two references he's made to song titles. Very strange.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Ultros is beautiful. This is obvious from the game's cover art, let alone the in-game graphics. There is no art style quite like what Niklas Åkerblad does. It is psychedelic biology - combining an acid trip with nature and biology. To be quite honest, the imagery alone in this game is worth the price and time of a playthrough.Ultros is a difficult game in some aspects but not in others. It has generally easy combat that rewards you for perfecting your skills. There is a pretty large upgrade system with things to work towards. But the game itself is a bit obtuse. It tells you nearly nothing and you're left to figure stuff out on your own. To the game's benefit, it is well designed in that there is a certain flow to the game.Ultros is a metroidvania but equally as much a rogue-lite. You will do some backtracking but it's largely just to go back and get a specific upgrade you need for completing the new loop. The way Ultros' progression is designed is that each section of the world map is essentially its own loop. Once you complete the loop, you'll naturally head towards a different, unexplored corner of the map. I think it's important for people to understand the game's design to prevent the frustration that may come with the game's abstractness and lack of direct information.The story in Ultros is good and plays very well into the theme and graphics of the game, but it's also not too in-depth. There's no voice acting and cutscenes are short and relatively basic from an animation perspective. Again, the graphics are the foundation of the game's design.What I love about Ultros aside from looking at it is how rewarding it is for someone who wants to dig deep into the complexities of the game. It is very rewarding for someone who wants to take notes on the different types of plants, wants to connect all of the map together, and wants to complete the game through its pacifist ending. I'm not the type of person to commit that much into a game but I love dipping my toes in and seeing how layered a game is. Ultros for many people might seem a bit too simplistic but for those that want to dig deep, there's a lot of complexity, strategy, and puzzle solving to it.Ultros will be remembered for its imagery. It's such a visually stunning and evocative game that it's hard not to be disappointed that the mechanics of the game don't match the impossibly high levels of its graphics. While not bad, it's really just a bit too easy. It's not a fast-paced combat system which I think makes the argument for it to be more difficult, as you can strategize mid-combat and reset pretty easily without fear of death. I think anyone with a little patience, a sense of exploration, and the willingness to just live in the world they're playing will have a great time in Ultros. It's not designed to be like Dead Cells with fast-paced, snappy combat. It's an experience - one certainly worth diving into.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Metroidvania games make me happy. Ultros was a beautiful game with an amazing soundtrack. I've explored most if not all endings and really enjoyed the game mechanics at play. Ran into some stablility problems at one point and enabled exclusive fullscreen. Seemed to stop the game from hard crashing. Big props to the save states and auto save system.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: THIS GAME FREAKIN RULES. Solid 9/10 easily. "DMT fever dream Metroidvania" was the most accurate description I saw before purchasing this game which caused me, along with the visuals, to instantly purchase it. It's absolutely gorgeous, and pretty easy to learn. There is a lot of poetic and flowery lore, but its all vague AF and not built upon, so as long as you can accept "game pretty, game fun, game very unique" and not care about not understanding a gyaat dayum thing that is going on literally ever... you've got a great game ;)Pros:- Unique skill tree system I've never seen anything similar to before- Insanely creative art, lore, creatures and characters, world, etc- Familiar and unfamiliar new powers and world-traversal skills/systems- A very cool progression through the story that feels like Majora's Mask meets Metroid Prime meets Dead Cells with a dash of whatever games care about how "cool/special" the way you fight is and reward you for it- It was VERY affordable for the amazing and super novel content you get - WOWCons- Combat isn't explained until you've already cleared the first area- While the vagueness of literally everything is also the games charm, it does kind of make it hard to emotionally invest in anything going on and feel driven to continue - I feel more driven by curiosity of seeing more pretty art and new areas than the "story/plot"- You have to play through the whole game almost to so that you can (assumedly) go back on the second save file and do everything more intelligently and plan things out to get what I call/assume is Ultros' version of "the true ending" by using items in "the right spots" at the "right times." It's reminding me of the dream bosses in Hollow Knight that are totally skippable, but if you know what to do and when, and what secret areas to go explore, there is a whole other half of the game to be unlocked and seen. That's the best non-spoilers way I can think to explain it with my understanding so far.- There are certain skill tree skills that just sound absolutely useless and they don't really add anything super useful or necessary to the gameplay.- (trying to prevent spoilers here) After each boss, if you don't use the "skill saver" things you can pick up, you lose them. this wasn't explained and I forgot twice now and am short 2 skills in my tree because of it. Don't be like me, just choose a skill and lock it down the second you get this item.[[ Edit disclaimer ]] — I'm about 50% of the way into the game and realizing that you start to understand more the deeper you get. This game feels like Memento or Inception or Shutter Island type movies, but a game. You understand more the further you get, and I assume you than can go back to the beginning on a new file and do it better with your end game understanding.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Taking apart plants and putting them together like Lego was not on my bingo card. 10/10 would disassemble plants again.This game is incredible. The plants thing is a core and more fun mechanic than I would have imagined. So there are spots you can plant seeds. You can also dig those seeds up and plant the seed again or a different seed. You can take the parts of those plants and splice them with other plants in structurally impossible ways. Some parts you can stand on. Some connect the station's wifi. They also can be used to break certain barriers, block line of sight, and provide nutritious fruit.The rebuilding thing is important to reach certain areas. The networking is important to access certain areas. AND then, you can feed the stations inhabitants who will create new places you can plant seeds. AND then you can pick up and move the monsters so they create MORE places you can plant seeds.EDIT: At 100% I'm sad it's over. This could be my game of the year. I recommend getting to the bad ending quickly to get the Returner. This lets you reset and keep your gear. Keeping your eyes open gets you the memory locks you need to save your entire skill tree (there are about double memory locks than you need in the entire game).It doesn't get tedious because there is so much you can do. I was initially annoyed that the game forced you to loop and start over (kinda) a few times. However, that helped parcel out the mechanics and keep the HUGE map from being too overwhelming.Not to mention the combat mechanics that reward you for killing enemies with all unique moves.I am still not done and I've been ready to write this review for hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: A delicious masterpiece but it's not for everyone. It's difficult to describe what make it a truly unique and fun experience so I'll just say that it's something that Shigeru Miyamoto would have designed given his passion for gardening and exploration. It perfectly captured the zen of exploration in Metroid and gardening in Pikmin. The demo and trailers does a poor job of selling the game, this you just have to commit to and be receptive to its weirdness and vision.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best acid-trip-metroidlike you'll find. Don't forget to lick the plants....But seriously, this is the best metroidlike I've played in a very, very long time. It's amazing, and the crazy colors grow on you really quickly. I just finished my first playthrough and I'm going back for a second one immediately.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: It's so beautiful, but equally dull and tedious in every other aspect of the game. Map progress is often confusing (which, I admit, suits well "psychedelic" aesthetics of the game, but I doubt it was intentional, just a bad design), the movement is clunky, the combat is boring, the levels are nice to look at, but there's virtually nothing in them game-wise, the skills available with food updates are almost all useless, the tree mechanic is nice, but with the inventory wipe on every time loop you rarely have the necessary seed on each planting place. And I finally gave up on the game at the ball-juggling sequence in the Infinity Lake which is utterly frustrating, clumsy and just doesn't work with the game controls.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: I played a bit past mid-game and quit there. The game felt like a very frustrating experience, where you don't have good direction and end up spending a lot of time wandering around similar looking corridors amongs confusing graphics.  All the time while playing I always seemed to have a feeling of not knowing where to go, what to do, or if I'm even doing this thing properly. The graphical style doesn't help. In a metroidvania it's good to have openness, but Ultros goes somewhat overboard with it, leaving the player quite frustrated. Last straw was the ball juggling mini game, but I felt a lot of fatigue a lot before it. Sometimes your multi-tool can break down a fuzzy wall, sometimes it can't. You can never know if you have the right seed for a certain spot. Things like this are frustrating. I'm guessing there are a lot of people who tried / saw the demo and then made the purchase based on that. For me, in hindsight, it didn't feel a good representation of the final game. This game has a lot of neat ideas but combines them in a way that feels like a real frustrating mess to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Ultros is not a bad game, it’s just a bad metroidvania. Yes, you explore a large map, fight enemies, and gather upgrades, but the game at its core is about coexisting in a space, whereas the genre is more about dominating everything in your path. It’s taking tried and true territory and trying something new with it. I dig some of the stuff it’s doing, I just wish it was wrapped up in an experience that felt more constant.Full Review:

_childDocuments_.review: After finally understanding what is actually happening i can say that it is a great game, sadly the postgame is very difficult to actually fully understand how it works so there is a lot of frustration before everything "clicks", then you feel like the smartest person alive, wait for extra patches to iron out the game/guides to understand how the advanced mechanics work and then you will have a great time.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game that continues to stun me with its beautiful environment and unique mechanics.  (Soundtrack is pretty good too ) I have not finished this game yet and will update the review when I do.However, I would like to clarify somethings. This game is a gardening puzzle game. Not an action game, and certainly not a rougelite. People leave bad reviews complaining about the "Rougelite mechanics" and they do exist, and I do admit it is a little annoying to get your upgrades back, but within 2 resets you will basically be able to lock all of your important abilities in place. I personally enjoyed the resets beacuse I got to see the impact of my actions, and the new areas and paths that opened up. If someone leaves a bad review beacuse of the rougelite mechanics, they probably have not played the game too much, or have other problems with it. Tldr:Come here for a gardening puzzle game, not anything else.

_childDocuments_.review: Ultros is a refreshingly unique take on the metroidvania genre. Right away it immerses in an enigmatic narrative, as your almost insect-like heroine wakes up aboard a mysterious space station nestled in the far reaches of the galaxy. Soon you'll discover that in the very center of this facility there lies an enigmatic, hostile alien demon Ultros that trapped everyone on board in a never-ending time loop.First thing that is immediately visible is the extremely unique art style, which is truly a feast for the senses. The vivid tapestry of colors and the bizarre yet captivating designs of its inhabitants evoke a sense of awe as you explore this weird alien world, filled with strange multicolored plants, exotic fungi and bizarre creatures that feel like they've been pulled straight out of some kind of LSD-induced fever dream. Despite that, Ultros is a remarkably easy game to read, and there are few accessibility options if you want to blur the background or change the font, for example.I didn't find the game overly difficult, which I don't necessarily think is a bad thing. It definitely doesn't focus on combat or tricky platforming; rather, it focuses on exploration, inviting on a journey of discovery through its labyrinthine corridors and ethereal vistas. Each step forward unveils new pathways, abilities, and secrets, fostering a gratifying cycle of progression. Sooner or later, you will bump into perhaps its most interesting mechanic: the cultivation of various plants. You can find different seeds that, when nurtured, can grow into otherwordly species which basically open new pathways or methods to travel around.Combat is not just about defeating enemies; it's about experimenting with different strategies. Simply relying on basic attacks may yield meager rewards in the form of low-nutrition food. However, diversifying your combat repertoire with a variety of attacks unlocks tastier morsels. Consuming these grants access to unlockable upgrades, which get wiped on every time-loop, but later on you can preserve some of them with items you can find.Ultros is not very long to complete, but if you want to truly 100% the game, then there is a lot to do here. I very much recommend this metroidvania for its unique experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Great idea, great soundtrack, but on the long run not very convincing mechanics. The game does not guide you through the world and the story well. Not knowing what is going on and having to figure the story out is of course the main part. But the game leaves you quite alone, the logic of the loops remains quite opaque and vague, and this is not related to the story but quite rudimentary level design. It tries to be mystic and artistically pleasing, but the mechanics (loop, fighting) are not completely thought through and the games comes only to the point of being a glimpse of what that game could become if worked upon. Should be an early access title with much more player feedback.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: ULTROS is a psychedelic metroidvania where you wake up stranded on The Sarcophagus — a cosmic uterus holding an ancient, demonic being. Trapped in the loop of a black hole, you will have to explore The Sarcophagus and meet its inhabitants to understand the part you play...

name: Dying Light
detailed_description: DYING LIGHT: THE BEAST Kyle Crane returns! The Hero of Harran may have been missing for over a decade, but he's back in Dying Light: The Beast! A thrilling standalone zombie adventure, The Beast carries on Crane's story! For more information, check out the dedicated product page and wishlist the game today to keep updated! EDITIONS COMPARISON About the Game From the creators of hit titles Dead Island and Call of Juarez. Winner of over 50 industry awards and nominations. The game whose uncompromising approach to gameplay set new standards for first-person zombie games. Thanks to its legacy and seven-year post-launch support, today it goes down in history as one of gaming's greatest zombie titles. Survive in a city beset by a zombie virus! Discover the hard choice you will have to make on your secret mission. Will loyalty to your superiors prove stronger than the will to save the survivors? The choice is yours… VAST OPEN WORLD Roam the city with unprecedented freedom and bask in its unique atmosphere. Use parkour to scale every building and reach remote areas. CREATIVE COMBAT Engage in gory combat and discover limitless options to confront your enemies. Use the environment paired with various weapon types and abilities to gain an advantage. DAY AND NIGHT CYCLE Experience the dramatic shift in the world, as you change from a hunter to hunted at sundown. Face the coming threat or run away without wasting your time to look behind. 4-PLAYER CO-OP Join forces with other players and raise your chances of survival in an exciting co-op mode. Tackle the story campaign together and see how far you'll go as a team.

_childDocuments_.review: Changed to NOT Recommend...  Techland is now owned by the Chinese Communist Party (Tencent) and DL uses "Epic Online Services" malware!  Cannot recommend!Nothing special.. I guess the youngins are enthralled with the "parkour" system... (when I was young, we called it playing, and climbing) but it doesnt do much for me.. Just adds motion sickness.. Its got a neat crafting, and weapon system, similar to a Diabloesque, color coded loot system.. I dont like that they have a amount of times to be repaired, as they break easily.. Combat is very basic, but has upgrades in the 4 talent trees... Like Skyrim, the talent tree is leveled up by using it.. Agility for running/climbing, combat for swinging a weapon, etc.. I havent gotten far in the story, but it appears youre some spy, dropped in to find out about someone and report back, while also helping survivors.. Typical fare here, fetch this, kill that, medicine for the sick.. Graphics are pretty good, and it seems to be nicely optimized.. I havent touched the co op, so no comment..Its Dead Island with climbing, and sliding.. I have to take Dramamine just to play for an hour.. I dont know what it is about this game, but it makes me VERY sick playing. Ive tried different settings, but everytime, I get extreme motion sickness! Im not a huge first person fan, but I try to keep a somewhat diverse library.. Sometimes you just dont have time for deep rpg gaming..On the downside, because combat is SO basic, and controls are floaty, it can be extremely annoying to fight.. It doesnt do a good job of explaining things like if you should use bleed, electric, stab/slice weapons, and if it even matters, or where to hit enemies.. I saw arms come off, and it takes alot of hits before a head finally explodes, killing the zombie.. The first hour is simple, as zombies stand there, and are basically target dummies.. But then you see newer ones, and they swarm, lunge, sprint, etc., and thats where you notice the combat is lacking.. I guess youre supposed to run from everything, and keep the "parkour"  system front and center.. With enemies taking many hits, which brings attention to others who then swarm, and weapons breaking very quickly, it seems to want you to avoid fighting.. I could forgive all this, but turning the character, trying to line up a shot, kicking, managing stamina, watching weapon durability, and knowing your surroundings is just too much.. The controls are SO... floaty is the best word I can use to describe.. It controls like a person standing on butter.. Trying to aim at the head youll move the cursor to the head, and then past it, and then back, its like a drunk trying to aim a rifle.. It feels terrible!Its also got the Steam Workshop, and user created content, challenges, leaderboards, etc.. If youre into that kinda thing.. Personally, I could care less.. I doubt Ill ever finish it, but its a change of pace I guess.. Never really understood the appeal to the whole zombie thing tbh...Alot of people will like it however.. If youre playing solo, its slow, quiet, and not all I had hoped really, but alot of effort went into developing it, and was done well! (Besides the controls) I just find it incredibly boring, personally.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall good game, but becomes very repetitive. Started to become tedious after playing for 25 hours or so. Ending to the main story was awful. Ending to the Following DLC was also disappointing. The game shines when you unlock a few skills and are able to kill zombies in more creative and fun ways. The game's major strengths are the graphics and side quests. However, there are some gameplay elements that are inconsistent, such as the grappling hook not working in some areas for no explanation, or when dying hits you with a massive penalty towards your survivor points even though it was caused by a glitch or an exploding zombie that was hiding right behind a corner which instakills you. Sometimes it feels like the game doesn't know what type of game its supposed to be. In some moments, its a hack and slash game where you chop zombie heads off in glorious combat. In other moments, specifically at night, it becomes a stealth game where you just run away from everything. Then there are a few quests that put you in a room and demand you to search every nook and cranny looking for some item or clue. In regards to combat, its fun when you're actually killing stuff, but the majority of the time its not worth it, especially on harder difficulties when it takes a dozen hits to the head to kill a lesser zombie. Trying to fight humans is basically impossible if you don't have a ranged weapon. The Following DLC breathed a bit more life into my playthrough as it takes place in a completely different terrain. Instead of a tightly packed city-scape, it becomes a wide open countryside in which you can drive your own buggy. However, that becomes tedious too when you're trying to look at your map and figure out which way you're supposed to go while you remain a sitting duck for some zombie to rape you. All in all, its a good game, but it could've used more polish. Buy it when its on sale and play with a friend for max fun. Also, the bow will one-shot zombies to the head. Buy that as soon as you see it.

_childDocuments_.review: Zombies have always been a pretty safe theme for action/fps games to go with as this combination seldom goes wrong. However, this also meant it would be harder for games of this kind to standout, and yet Dying Light were not only able to outshine other games of the same genre, it even became a standard that a lot of people would use as a comparison for future zombie games. If you are a potential Dying Light buyer, you probably already know that the biggest mechanics added, which gave this game its unique identity, is its parkour element, I am here to tell it goes beyond this. + Parkour element is a fantastic element that fits well with this genre (also makes sense)+ Night time adds a survival-like taste to the game+ Great gameplay balance, zombie crowds (and night time) kept the game fun even after 20+ hours++ Weapon crafting (inherited from Dead Island)- Looting doesn't matter much after 10+ hoursAll in all this is a pretty solid game to grab, hopefully Dying Light 2 can live up to the hype!

_childDocuments_.review: A game that suprisingly stood the test of time for years. Having come out in early 2015, this game still stands as if it just came out last year or so. It's quite impressive what care for your product can do. The game has received countless updates, free and paid dlc, as well as two very impressive expansions to the base game that add enough content to justify themselves, Dying Light is practically a must buy, not to mention very cheap. It has hundreds of hours worth of content, progression and collectibles, that blows practically any other big budget AAA sandbox out of the water. It has two different PVP modes, full co-op, tons of challenges to play with a friend, and so much more. You'd practically be doing yourself a disservice not buying the game nowadays, even without the expansions. It has a suprisingly well told plot that has quite a few emotional story beats you wouldn't expect from such a seemingly cliche narrative. The only main issues are the fact that there are things that the game fails to scale up over time, since the player will inevitably become much stronger than he is at first, where the loot does end up scaling, a lot of other things, such as the survivor gifts and random airdrops, do not scale properly, making them a waste of time. While there is a ton of content just in the base game there are a few very menial tasks given to you as sidequests, that can break the overall enjoyment of the game. Overall though the game is very fun to play both on your own, and with a group of friends. I would be lying if I said it doesn't deserve a purchase if for nothing else than the fact that Techland has been treating it like it's own child after they lost Dead Island.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a large open world filled with lots of detail, but the activities are very repetitive.  The game is basically one horribly long fetch quest or some boring variation of that.  Talk to mission giver (who has a cheesy or trite personality like all the other NPCs), spend lots of time jogging + running + climbing to point A, get something or do something simple (fix this, install that, or talk to him/her), return to mission giver, and repeat.  The main character is a patsy.  The combat is a tedious strategy of hit-and-run with weapons that easily break, but there are lots of weapons of various types for you to search for or receive from NPCs and to build and upgrade. _childDocuments_.review: Ok, I'll say it, since no one has the balls to say it, Dying Light is the BEST...zombie game out there right now.  From amazing type of zombies, environment, weapons/weapons modifications, story, characters...everything! everything is so well done in this game. The game doesn't try to scare you, the game is an action packed zombie game. Yes, there are pop ups as people call it, but the game doesn't over do it, in a sense, that you'll say "I bet something scary is gonna happen or something is going to pop up" whenever it happens, it will legitimately scare you/surprise you. The story is great, is a very well written story. Anything that has to do with viruses, I love it! it makes you feel, as if, its something that can actually happen. Call me crazy, but I love the zombies in this game. Especially the fast ones, they will legitimately dodge your attacks as if they were ninjas, its pretty badass and if you think you know parkour, you're in for a surprise. My favorite zombies are the Blue Volatiles zombies. Not only are they awesome aka very ugly looking, but they're as fast as you can possibly imagine. Going out at night, its a totally different game. The night is your worse enemy. And no, you cant turn on your flashlight. I mean, yes you can, but obviously that will detect you! and once you're detected, the only option you got is to run as fast as you can, and hope, that you have a near by safe zone unblocked. This game has everything that a fan of zombies ask for. Its scary, action packed, some "holy sh%t moments" and some pretty funny , "haha I got you" moments. If you want a quick laugh, just hit the tank of the hazmat zombies, but beware, you will draw the attention of any near by zombies. I totally love the parkour element of this game. Is the perfect fit for any zombie game in my opinion. Just imagine, you running away from a pack of zombies, wouldn't you like to be able to climb anything possible? its your life we're talking about. And if you seen any horror movies, running straight to a forest, doesn't HELP AT ALL. In this case, climbing over rooftops is the way to go, and the way to feel safe. The higher you're, the safer you will feel. The game is pretty rewarding, when you manage to out run a very dangerous zombie. If you want a true zombie game and an awesome experience, go with this game. Yes, we have Resident Evil, and among others, but this game right here is something else. Resident Evil doesn't scratch my itch anymore. Its more of the same thing, and the stories are short, and quite easy to be honest. (my opinion by the way) this game is a pretty original title. Cant wait for Dying Light 2. The game I see that can go head to head with the Dying Light series, even though is a better looking and more of a badass game than Left 4 Dead 2, its Back 4 Blood. Other than that, no zombie game out there will keep me away from the Dying Light series. I haven't played the online mode of this game, so I don't know if its good, great, bad, very bad, or awesome, or meh. I play solo, this is one of those games, where I rather play alone, and enjoy it all by myself.

_childDocuments_.review: i've never been one to play zombie games, especially first person, blood-lettig gratuitous violence for it's own sake. This is the first game of this genre that I've played for more than an hour. It's everything you look for in a role playing game with a balance of classic zombies with a balanced pinch of super zombies.If you're more of a strategy-type (like me) the game becomes more fun when you can acquire or purchase a bow with various types of arrows. When you finally get the shot gun and police  assault rifle ... and then find a perch next to a safe house where you can take on the omnipotent night stalkers, it's very satisfying for a while. The different missions keep me coming back to what would otherwise be another slagfest. Excellent voice acting and some ingenious adventures and missions. There are a few that are downright frustrating because it takes so long to get to the objective, which then requires a bunch of jumps and acrobatics. One mistake or slip and you're back at the safe house starting all over again. There's no ability to save or at l;east have the game save part way through a difficult mission. But that's the game genre so I just gave up on those types of missions.I highly recommend this game for in general and RPG'ers, and strategy types may also find this game an interesting distraction. If you liked Batman, Arkham City, you'll find some familiar parallels. I particularly like the grappling hook use and the true 3D environment of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Well I just finished the game and it was quite a ride.  One of my biggest complaints about most zombie based games is that the stories are usually pretty weak, and a lot of this has to do to the necessity for co-op experiences. Dying Light has one of the best single player campaigns (although you can certainly play co-op) I have ever played and much of that is you become Kyle Crane, a GRE operative tasked with recovering a stolen file regarding the viral outbreak in Harran.  The main missions guide you through quite a few individual missions, each one advancing the story. The story is quite good as you keep wanting to see more but you also have a plethora of side missions helping other survivors in many different ways. The mission design for both main and side missions is so varied that I don't think any really felt the same.  And best yet, you really feel like you are helping the survivors when you complete these missions, as many of them sound like realistic requests during a fragile fight for survival.The comparisons of a cross between Dead Island and Mirror's Edge is not far off.  The parkour elements really shine in this game, and as you level up your agility you get access to more and more abilities that make you even better. It's quite a rush to run full flight jumping from rooftop to rooftop, executing quick climb and jump moves, and sliding under low hanging obstacles.  The combat feels very much like Dead Island with a crafting system and modification system very similar. You must collect blueprints to expand your crafting and modification options; many become available as you spend survival points (which is mostly gained by completing missions or returning supply drops), or by finding blueprints in the world or by completing side missions or protection missions.  Your combat ability is handled via power points, which are gained by hitting infected and killing them in a myriad of ways. Spending power points gives you access to different combat abilities like power swing, whirlwind with two-handed weapons, and death from above which impales an enemy when you are above them.  During daytime the game can be challenging as there are a lot of different special infected much like Dead Island. Come nighttime though, and all bets are off.  The game becomes more of a stealth game as you try to avoid volatiles, the most powerful infected in the game.  Early on you have no chance of killing one of these but as you reach higher levels and get access to better weapons with super modifications you can end up killing them in one power swing. The problem is, attacking a volatile or being seen by one immediately alerts every other volatile in the immediate vicinity. The speed that these volatiles close in on you and pummel you to death is astonishing. You may wonder why bother playing during the night as you can just sleep at any safehouse until the morning. Some missions require you to do them at night like the early one where you have to restore the full power grid at three substations. The other reason is all power and agility xp is doubled at night, which really makes a difference as I found agility to be lagging behind survivor and power xp.  Also, the longer you survive at night the more bonus survivor points you will get once morning comes. I found I rarely ended up sleeping until morning, preferring to maneuver myself to specific locations by jumping between safehouses, trying to stay unnoticed by the volatiles but occasionally alerting them and booking it while throwing UV flares to slow the pursuit down.Overall, this was a fantastic game that was so fun it was hard to put down.  There are a few framerate issues where the FPS would drop to the single digits for 10-15 seconds until eventually clearing up. The graphics are gorgeous, the animations fluid, and the gameplay top-notch.  The game works well with both keyboard/mouse and gamepad. I played with a gamepad mostly because 90% of the time you are fighting with melee weapons and I like the feel of the gamepad in that manner. If you like action/adventure games with good stories, a plethora of gameplay options, and the freedom to do what you want in the order you want, then I highly recommend this game. It's worth it at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: PROs:*Built in the foundation from Dead Island (in which a game that I love to play), makes a terrifying experience trying to traverse the open-world of Harran jampacked full of zombies.*An Okay Parkour system (Not terrible, not great either because sometimes it doesn't work or register trying to parkour in the game. But most of the time, it works) - take Dead Island and incorporate it with Mirror's Edge but with zombies, you get Dying Light.*Chrome Engine's Impressive graphical capabilities - beautiful even on Medium settings. Image almost blends with realism during the night makes free roaming at in-game night time really dark and intense. Dead Island and Dying Light are beautiful at times. Gore and body decapitation when attacking zombies and other enemies are drastically improved from Dead lsland. How you attack makes an accurate depiction on how zombies will be killed. A slice on their torso sometimes in a result of cutting them in half if you have a powerful blade.Played it on STEAM DECK. Constant 42-60fps*Compared to Dead Island, you can go in any direction you want to go combined with the parkour system makes it more satisfying to traverse the land of the dead. In Dead Island, it's still Open-World but felt somewhat linear because it has sectors with loading screens in between also because of the limited movement in that game.*Guns no longer tied to the RPG Mechanics - If you played Dead Island, guns are tailored to your leveling. When you get that one gun when you were level 14, you'll be pressed that you'll find or get the same looking, same sounding AK or M16 but with higher level and power. Similar to the mechanics of Borderlands. (I hate that game). In this game, it's no longer the case. Just upgrade it, no constant replacements.*The late-released HELLRAID DLC - this is probably the most fun DLC that I ever played alongside The Following DLC. If you played Skyrim's Dawnguard DLC, it's kind of like this expansion. Focused on just the combat without relying on the RPG mechanics of the base game. No repairs, No crafting, No mods, No RPG Bullsh!t (There is still some RPG Elements in it). Just bashing Undead Zombies and Sorcerers and Skeletons. Some giant Dark Knight with it's ghost minions as the final boss like you see in Dark Souls. You start fresh without your current weapons from the base game but retain your level and skills. Sadly, no guns. But hey, it's a short but sweet DLC.*Roger Craig Smith (The voice of the main protagonist) - Ironic that he played as the main character of that parkour hitman game (Assassin's Creed 2, Brotherhood, and Revelations) and the zombie game (Resident Evil 5 and 6). Combine that, you get Dying Light lol. Well voice acted. By far, this is his best performance next to Resident Evil 6. CONs: *DICEROLLED Melee Combat System (The most ♥♥♥♥♥♥ atrocious combat I have ever seen. Yet better animated compared to Dead Island. I'll give it that)  - This is the main reason I almost uninstalled the game because of this in the first 8-9 hours of total playthrough. The devs be like, let's take that awesome combat system from Dead Island and somewhat make it massively downgraded and extremely frustrating at the same time. This game makes Morrowind's combat doubly masterpiece because that game at least was great at being an RPG. Fighting walker zombies are a no brainer at all because you can hit them with any weapon and it 100% works all the time. The big problem was fighting humans in your first encounter with them. Even if you know it's going to hit them when you attack them at a really close range, they'll dodge that attack just because they did the "dodge animation" even if you hit their body super close, it doesn't also register your attacks. You hit their body but no registered attack numbers from you because every animation they did will make them invincible like a ghost. Same thing with the infected runner zombies. they are invincible once they trigger a dodging animation. ♥♥♥ you for making Dead Island worse, Techland.Dodging Animation = Invincibility and ImmunityAt least Guns actually ♥♥♥♥♥♥ works against them 110%*QTE Boss fight with Discount and Cliche version of Makarov from MW2 and MW3 trying hard to be Metal Gear Solid character that failed - How to make a villain that was made to be unlikeable, only to be unlikeable the further you played the story, with the most unlikeable sequence on a boss fight? Awful boss fight. Remember Far Cry 3? Yep, the very same thing with what they did to every boss fights in that game.*Plot that sometimes doesn't make sense - Why let some scientists inside the quarantine zone make a cure but cannot give the data to someone else outside of the zone or else outside of the country to develop a vaccine for Harran when the outside country can capably distribute it safely?*I said it's an okay parkour in the PROs section of this review because sometimes it doesn't ♥♥♥♥♥♥ work and I died a lot trying to traverse the world. The inclusion of grappling hook was nice. But when I grappled to another building, sometimes my character doesn't cling on the ledge, leading to constant death from the fall.*Constant Micro-Management from the Inventory - Sometimes some games doesn't need to be a Role-Playing game. That's the case for this game for trying to have a "good" RPG mechanics in it. You are constantly have to micromanage what you scrounge to get the most power out of your melee weapon and consumable items that you need. Sometimes, deliberately keep replacing weapons just because one has most higher numbers in it to get more power. Except for guns.*Chrome Engine's notoriously bad facial animations - those bland and robotic facial animations are still here from Dead Island when talking to NPCs except during key cutscenes.*It's a Role-Playing game instead of survival horror - If you ever feel stupid, some people call others NOOB for being sh!t on a Role-Playing game. When it all about the numbers. This game makes it tremendously easy as long as you keep playing, like any other RPG games. With skills you just purchased or unlocked, you can almost get rid of that bullsh!t DICEROLLED combat system against human enemies and they are easy to kill if you have the necessary perks and skills you've unlocked. I have nothing against good RPG Games. In fact. I love Fallout New Vegas and Skyrim. Overall Score: 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: I first got this game when it came out. I finished it and I enjoyed it, for the most part. I am now playing again in anticipation of the expansion coming in 2016 and I am having more fun than ever.If you enjoy survival this game is for you. Just make sure to play on Hard Mode. This is one of the very few zombie apocalypse games that made me think twice about swinging my weapon about like a kid on a temper tantrum. You will feel like a survivor in choosing tactics, evasion and mobility over brute force.Prior to Hard Mode being added, your character would much too quickly become a Johny Rambo one-man zombie killing machine, slaughtering thousands of infected without breaking a sweat. No more. Now you're just a fit guy with a bunch of saw blades duck-tapped to a brick hammer, and you know (magical) parkour. This fixes a big narrative problem with the game as it was released, captured in the following question: If its so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ easy (for me) to slaughter my way through day and night, why in the flying ♥♥♥♥ are all these people holed up and scared ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥? Well, Hard Mode answers that question by bringing you down a peg.Just don't come for the (main) story. Its atroucious. Side stories and characters, however, are equal parts humorous and empathetic.Get it, Play it, Enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredible game.I always seem to love the free roam games like Skyrim, Zelda, and Super Mario 64. This game is no exception. The level of freedom in this game is beyond that of any of those games. You see a place where you want to go? You can go there, unless it's out of the playable area. The massive variety of weapons and tools that can be used in the game are wonderful. If I had anything to recommend to the devs, it would be to add more tools that affect the player.The story is pretty cool, too. It might seem a bit overwhelming if you're not paying attention your first playthrough, but it's easily understandable if you get into it. Crane as a character is pretty realistic as he changes his mind throughout the story based on what he knows.The graphics are beautiful. Positively breathtaking in some areas. There are details in places you wouldn't expect them. NPCs have animations for everything they say, as well as a variety of idling animations. Lots of interesting and entertaining visual effects for different events. It even includes a trippy psychadelic scene for people who are into that kind of thing. Framerate is consistent if you have a good computer.Multiplayer is great. Love playing online with other people and seeing the unique weapons they found and what they do with them. Racing challenges are the best. I love competing with other players to see who can get to the next point the fastest.The DLC is nothing short of incredible. The amount of time it took to make something like this implies that these guys are obsessive. Some parts of the story really tie together certain unexplained parts of the original game. The buggy is so much fun. Love running zombies over, and of course racing friends. The plot is so crazy, especially at the end. ***small spoilers*** There should be a sequel to both endings of the game. ***end spoilers***The developer secret weapons are one of my favorite parts of the game. These guys made a serious game, but have all kinds of silly secrets that are totally unrealistic. It's a game, why not include some random button that teleports you to different parts of the map, or a chicken on a stick that does more damage than most swords?Seriously. If you play first person games, I can't recommend this game enough. It's worked its way up to the top of my list of favorite first person games. I kid you not.

_childDocuments_.review: Dying Light is an amazing game which will make you feel fear, adrenaline, and sometimes frustration. The game is unique in it's parkour + combat features, and it gives you a lot to do in the city of Harran. Daytime is around 64 minutes, giving you plenty of time to settle into your playground. If you fall, your helped with a nice cushion.However, when night comes around things change. Harran isn't a playground, it's a deathtrap. If you fall, your greeted with spikes and shards. Volatiles roam the streets and rooftops searching for prey, and if you are caught they will chase you relentlessly until you either escape them, or slip up and become trapped in a swarm of infected.Dying Light's protagonist, Kyle Crane is quite bland, however he's still enjoyable to play as. The city of Harran is an amazing playground where you can parkour anywhere and climb anything, your only restriction being time. During the day, you're the hunter. During the night, you're the prey.You will feel amazing with this game, but you will also feel afraid. The game will make you feel many emotions and it'll be one amazing memorable journey / ride that you will be unlikely to forget. You'll find yourself returning constantly and having an insane amount of fun.Unfortunately, the 7 year ride Techland has been on supporting the game has ended. Dying Light 2 has a more polished parkour system but that doesn't mean Dying Light isn't worth playing. This game is amazing, and is arguably better than the 2nd one.Please, play this.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a weak "not recommended" because there's a lot to like here, but there is too much else that is simply too poorly executed and limited the "fun" for me.  Examples:- No climbing down.   Descending tall buildings is either finding a target trash pile or tediously trying to catch on to things backwards.- Worst-in-class boss fights.  Fit about as poorly in the game as Deus Ex: Human Revolution -- I would say in some cases, even worse.  They do things like take all the weapons you've spent time making, prevent any real run-and-dash parkour (that is otherwise central to the game) and instead give you set pieces with fixed weapons and a lot of dodging.  Really, just lots of dodging, like you suddenly fell in to the Witcher 3 with no equipment.  The final boss is even a QTE.- Lousy gunplay and absurd "crossfire" set piece missions that you're forced to participate in for story progress.- The story itself.  It's fine, I guess.  But if you're read any reviews, well, other folks cover this plenty -- it's pretty generic.The best parts are fast-paced, run-and-dash parkour with a frantic skirmish here and there.  These parts kept me going for a while, probably more than the game deserved.  They kept me hopeful, because while it sometimes feels wonky, when it works it does work well.  Unfortunately, the interruptions for mediocre missions and other distractions make an interesting concept ... well, just frustrating enough that it was no longer fun.

_childDocuments_.review: "Dying Light" is a captivating and immersive gaming experience that excels in various aspects, making it a standout title in the survival horror genre. With its realistic and expansive game world, the developers have created a dynamic and multifaceted environment that adds a layer of authenticity to the overall gaming experience.One of the game's standout features is its intricate and compelling storyline, which manages to evoke a range of emotions. The narrative is rich with twists and turns, keeping players engaged and invested in the characters and their fates. The emotional depth adds a meaningful dimension to the gameplay, making "Dying Light" more than just a typical zombie survival game.Moreover, the game boasts a high replay value, ensuring that players will find themselves coming back for more. The diverse gameplay elements, coupled with the open-world exploration, contribute to an experience that remains fresh and exciting with each playthrough. The combination of challenging missions, dynamic day-night cycles, and the constant threat of zombies creates an adrenaline-pumping adventure that players can enjoy time and again.The cooperative multiplayer aspect enhances the enjoyment factor, especially when playing with close friends. The game's design encourages teamwork and strategic planning, elevating the overall fun factor. The thrill of surviving together in a perilous world amplifies the sense of camaraderie and accomplishment.Despite its many strengths, "Dying Light" is not without areas for improvement. The game could benefit from additional updates, particularly in terms of expanding the map. Players eagerly anticipate new locations and areas to explore, hoping for more variety in the landscape and fresh challenges. Additional maps and regions would undoubtedly enhance the longevity of the game and provide players with new and exciting experiences.In conclusion, "Dying Light" is a stellar gaming experience that successfully combines a realistic game world, an engaging storyline, and high replay value. Its cooperative multiplayer feature further enhances the overall enjoyment, making it an excellent choice for those seeking a thrilling and immersive survival horror adventure. While the game is already outstanding, the potential for future updates to expand the map and introduce new areas would undoubtedly elevate it to even greater heights.

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable game with a lot to do. Crafting is fun, and there's plenty of reason to forage and explore. Combat is solid, though it does dissuade using items that make noise, firearms and explosives, as they spawn zombies on use. This means you're likely going to be using melee weapons for most of the game, which break often and easily. By mid to late game, durability becomes a non issue, but still, anything you make has a shelf-life. There is never going to be a point you make a weapon and are done, it will only degrade. That said, once you're out of the early game, you'll likely be replacing weapons with better versions as opposed to breaking them, and all weapons can be broken down to repair, upgrade, or create other items.Co-op, while very fun, is a bit funky. While you can change your characters clothes (from a list of outfits), you're all the same dude, so theres just 4 identical jackasses running around. But it is entertaining, as, once online, anything becomes an activity. If there's an airdrop, for example, players are given a prompt to race to it, if they desire. Zombie-heavy areas prompt killing contests, and there are lots of spots for footraces. It's really good for what it is, an open world zombie game. Up to you if that's worth what they are asking.

_childDocuments_.review: Dying Light, developed by Techland, is a mesmerizing and intense open-world survival horror game that seamlessly blends elements of parkour and brutal combat in a zombie-infested urban landscape. Released in 2015, the game has not only stood the test of time but has also managed to evolve and captivate players with its engaging narrative, dynamic gameplay, and stunning visuals.The heart of Dying Light lies in its unique day-and-night cycle, which significantly affects gameplay. In the daytime, players navigate the expansive city of Harran, utilizing the protagonist Kyle Crane's parkour skills to traverse rooftops, scale buildings, and outmaneuver the infected hordes. The fluidity and responsiveness of the parkour mechanics contribute to a sense of freedom and empowerment, making exploration a thrilling experience.As the sun sets, the game takes a drastic turn, plunging players into the perilous world of night. The infected become more aggressive and dangerous, and the city transforms into a hauntingly atmospheric nightmare. The fear-inducing night cycle adds an adrenaline-pumping layer to the gameplay, forcing players to make strategic decisions about whether to face the challenges head-on or seek refuge until dawn.The storyline in Dying Light is compelling, weaving a tale of survival, betrayal, and the search for a cure amidst the chaos. The characters are well-developed, and the voice acting is top-notch, drawing players deeper into the post-apocalyptic narrative. The game also features a robust crafting system, allowing players to create weapons and tools from scavenged materials, enhancing their chances of survival.Combat in Dying Light is visceral and satisfying. The variety of melee weapons, coupled with the ability to modify and upgrade them, provides a diverse and customizable combat experience. The inclusion of parkour elements in combat allows for creative and dynamic engagements, adding a layer of strategy to encounters with both the infected and human enemies.Visually, Dying Light is stunning. The decaying cityscape, detailed character models, and atmospheric lighting create a visually immersive experience. The day-night cycle is complemented by weather effects, adding to the overall realism and ambiance of the game.The multiplayer aspect of Dying Light enhances the replayability, allowing players to join forces with friends or other survivors in the seamless co-op mode. The Be the Zombie mode also adds a unique twist, allowing players to take on the role of the Night Hunter and invade other players' games.In conclusion, Dying Light is a triumph in the survival horror genre. Its seamless integration of parkour mechanics, intense day-night cycle, engaging narrative, and visceral combat make it a standout title. Whether you're a fan of zombie games or just enjoy a heart-pounding adventure, Dying Light is a must-play that continues to shine years after its initial release.gud gaem

_childDocuments_.review: Seamlessly blending survival, action, horror, exploration, story-driven progression, and RPG elements - Dying Light is a game that has the potential to make you feel like a kid again. I'm about halfway through the story, I've experienced luring dumb zombies into traps by day and running from insanely fast and agile terrors by night. This game feels like several different types of games/genres which are flawlessly blended to create an immersive experience unparalleled.I could not stand Dead Island, which was made by the same company. Dying Light makes Dead Island look like they were either trolling people, or weren't sure what type of game they wanted to make at the very least.I never looked forward to this game, didn't know anything about it. I got the demo because I could. Played it, and was immediately blown away. Bought the game on sale and never regretted it. I'm about 63 hours in so far and only "53%" through the main story. Also, and I won't mention this much because the gameplay is so solid, but the graphics are insane and very impressive.Since I've owned it now they have released an enhanced edition (for free) which adds "new levels" more or less and other enhancements. Just as I thought the game was getting a little easy, (keep in mind there is a learning curve which I have really mastered with the Steam Controller which makes me feel like somewhat of a badass), the next town over provided a sobering challenge that left me frantically fighting to survive at times like I was brand new at the game. I also enabled the new Nightmare mode which made even the weakest zombies a real challenge.I have not even made it as far as The Following yet (the massive expansion) and I really look forward to it. This game continues to be fun as hell and blow me away. Every positive review you see is there for a reason. Get the demo if you have doubts, and get the game otherwise. It's even more fun with friends, and I've played most of the game solo and STILL had a roller coaster of a good time.It's first person, parkour (free-running), zombie, action, stealth, rpg, open world, day/night cycle, exploratory fun. Other than that, it's hard to describe exactly how immersive it is. You should have already played this by now. The day/night cycle adds a great deal of depth and immersion, and if you're caught outside goofing around at daytime and scavenging as night descends and you're unprepared, the entire game turns upside down as you desperately scramble and fight for your life to make it to the nearest safehouse. Or you play it smart and lucky and sneak around, hoping and praying you don't make too much noise.Just play it already, even if it's the demo. GIve it a shot. It's too much fun not to try.Edit: Wifey reminded me to mention that they released a companion app for Android / iOS where you can manage sending squads into the city to loot and rescue survivors and such. It's a fun side-mission companion app that allows you to send items aquired to your character in the PC game to use. I've never seen this level of interactivity in a game before, and I rarely see this kind of dedication (overall) from developers. Techland, effing bravo.

_childDocuments_.review: Steam Deck Review First off, I have about 300+ hours on this game on PS4 days. I’ve beaten the game and DLC before. To begin, Dying Light works flawlessly on the steam deck. I am using Proton Experimental, have it locked to 40fps on high graphics. You can probably play this game at 60fps if you tweak your settings more. Dying Light as a game is well worth getting on sale, I wouldn’t pay full price as this game constantly goes on sale for dirt cheap. This game does not hold your hand, for any casual gamer this game is hard (at least if you play on Normal or higher)… at the beginning. Once you get further in the game and unlock some good perks and get better weapons then it’s pretty smooth sailing (except nights).  At the start of the game I was constantly dying and it doesn’t help that your given the weakest weapons to fight with, killing 1 zombie can seam like a fight for your life moment, add another 3-4 and you can get swarmed very quickly. This game gets easy once you get guns, then your mowing them down easily. Pros: - Beautiful graphics - Smooth Gameplay - Very Atmospheric- Soundtrack good - Great Storyline and even better DLC - Lots of interesting side content to do - Nice variety of characters Cons: - Hard at the beginning, can be demotivating to casual gamers. - Nights are actually scary, if you’re not a horror fan this can impact your enjoyment as some missions are forced to be played at night. Overall Rating: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Fans have based the theory that Walter White was inadvertently responsible for the undead epidemic on the presence of his blue meth within The Walking Dead. For the uninitiated, meth can be clear or opaque but is always a shade of white. Blue meth is non-existent and was created specifically for Vince Gilligan's series, therefore the reasonable conclusion would be that the universes are connected.To add more credence to this claim, The Walking Dead, Season 4, Episode 12 sheds some light on how Merle Dixon (Michael Rooker) obtained his narcotics. According to his brother Daryl, his dealer was "A janky little white guy. A tweaker (junkie)," who once pulled a gun on him and said, "I'm gonna kill you, b*tch." To Breaking Bad fans, that would be a physical profile that perfectly matches Jesse, who is notorious for his use of the aforementioned curse word.Besides that glaringly obvious connection, other interconnecting theories have surfaced. For instance, the red 2009 Dodge Challenger with black racing stripes that Walter buys for his son, Walter Jr. (RJ Mitte) and subsequently blows up appears in a handful of The Walking Dead installments. Glenn Rhee (Steven Yeun) famously took it for a ride, and interestingly, Glenn was the name of the salesman that Walter returns the car to in Breaking Bad, though we never see his face, so it would be a reach to assume that he is the same person.

_childDocuments_.review: I am not a gamer. I have never been a gamer. My experience with games was limited to booting up HOMM3 about once a year. But then I saw a trailer for Dying Light: The Following on a website dedicated to horror - the one with practical zombie make-up. I was intrigued - so I went looking for more information, and found the gameplay demo. For the first time, I found myself wanting to play something other than a casual game. I will omit the long journey from wanting it to actually playing it and the relationships that were forged on the basis of this game - let's just say it was a chaotic mess; what's important is that I now own DL on PC and PS4, and have completed the game at least twice on each platform.So what is the Dying Light neophyte experience?First and foremost - it's a ton of fun. The open world has plenty to do and plenty to loot. There is something ridiculously satisfying about coming to a city square full of zombies, clearing them all out and collecting the loot. The parkour system, as a reviewer pointed out, adds another dimension to the available direction of movement, making traversing the map an adventure rather than a chore. Combined with the DLCs (The Following, Bozak Horde), DL offers a wide variety of activities and environments to suit every taste and mood without becoming overwhelming (looking at you, Far Cry 4).Second - it was easy for a noob like me to grasp the gameplay mechanics. So if you have a partner who doesn't play but needs a way to let off steam - try introducing them to DL. Kicking a screaming viral's head in or watching them fly into the air on a car bomb explosion can be quite therapeutic.Third - the community. I have seen experienced players joining the games of those with lower ranks (myself included) and helping them out: watching their backs so they don't get killed, pointing them to humanitarian drops for them to get the XP, showing them easter egg locations. (I've also encountered a-holes - but let's not talk about them).The script and voice acting are a mixed bag. The main plot is cheesy and full of holes, the main villain might as well be a cartoon character with how hyperbolic his evil is. But where DL really shines is in world-building: tiny tidbits of information about the lives of the people of Harran are often genuinely heartbreaking, from a voice message left by a mother to tell her daughter who her real father is, to the diary of a mentally disabled man who can't grasp what is going on and is interpreting the zombie epidemic in his own way.There is co-op play and PVP, but I'm not a fan of it and prefer to play alone most of the time, so I can't really comment on it much. Like I mentioned earlier, you will encounter some incredible players who will take low-ranks under their 250-level wings - and you will encounter a-holes who treat the game as if they're training for the Olympics and see it as a personal insult if you're not on their level. Pay them no heed and play the way you want to.Do I recommend Dying Light? 100% yes.
