_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I just returned to playing the game after a 3 month break, hoping to finish it. I dont think I will. The game is worse than I remember it. The combat system is so horrendously bad that I get 0 enjoyment from playing it.I do not understand all the hype and praise this game got. The game has a lot of enjoyable moments, but they are ruined, or at least disturbed, by all the game's many downsides(Edit to this part: I was a bit hard on it. I still think that the game is very overrated, but to say that the downsides ruin it is too much. I do still give it a thumbs down, because it is just an ok/acceptable game and not the fantastic game it has been made out to be. It needs the criticism amongst all the praise)Edit: Edit: I will rewrite my interview once I am done with the game, or feel done with it. I have some more things to say. 1. For a game that is all about parkour, the system messes up a lot. It is far from flawless - just try to climb down a building or grab on to something mid air. Climbing those radio towers was awful. (Edit to 1: the parkour element is ok for the most part, but it really does suck, when climbing the radio towers, or when trying to climb down) 2. The autosaves are not great. It is bad, whenever you have to shut the game down, for you could end up losing many minutes worth of progress. I have also lost valuable loot, which I got a few minutes before dying. I actually risked my life to get them. The game is not forward about its rules, which is problematic. 3. The combat is not great. I cannot count how many times I aimed for a zombie's head, just to hit it's arm instead, or for the character to do a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ overhead attack instead. That is a real problem in a game where minor mistakes can cause you big problems. Furthermore, the Virals (fast zombies) can be extraordinarily difficult to kill and outright unfair. I have tried many times hitting one with a hammer twice, without stopping it, making it cause me 30 damage, while rendering me with no stamina (Note, this happened a lot in the beginning, but it has happened less and less. Probably not because it is less flawed, but because I rarely fight them on an even playing field and dodging a lot) So the game is very playable, if you figure out how to work around the flaws - but that does not mean that the flaws do not exist. Also, zombies' health is not all clear to me. Sometimes, I seem to kill them with a few good strokes to the head. Other times, with the same weapon, I have to hit them directly over the head with a weapon 5 times or more. I wish the rules of the game were more obvious from playing it. 4. (This part is heavily edited): The game is flawed, which means that you will die, both because you make mistakes, but also for unfair reasons. The autosave system is not good. I played a mission, which had a guy with an automatic rifle, in a scripted event, shoot at me out of nowhere. I had no gun and no idea he would be there, so I died almost instantaneously (it took maybe 4-5 shots). Instead of starting up just around that moment, I was thrown back to a savehouse far away and had to run all the way back to the location - that hurt the pacing a lot. I lost all incentives to continue playing, as the intensity of the moment was ruined. Not only was it ruined, but knowing that he is there, I climbed above his head and shot him from a distance with a gun I found. It felt so... off.  5.  At one point, I spent 40 minutes getting into two cars with good loot. I cleared the area. Killed everyone and just as I am about to open it, two virals come, so I have an intense fight and chase with them (within 20m from the cars), just to return and see the area be sprawling with zombies again. In each group, there is at least one zombie with a very sensitive explosive bag on its back, which you almost cannot but destroy. I tried many times aiming directly at their head with a hammer, yet somehow the tank is still ruptured, causing it to explode. This causes 1-3 virals to show up, then a chase, then combat and then back to the car to see more zombies there. It simply isn't ok to create a situation, where it should take the player 40 minutes to loot two cars. I have experienced similar things after I started using Molotovs and firecrackers more. The thing is, the firecrackers are stupid. I have tested it many times now and for some reason, there is a limit to how many zombies they attract. I have thrown them with 30-40 zombies around and no matter how many times I did it, only 10-15 would react. So to those comments saying that it works using them. It does not. At least not all the time. I had another event where I tried to open a car, but zombies kept coming. I used 4 molotovs and many firecrackers to lure them away, to lure them into traps and so on, yet it still took at least 15 minutes to clear the area. It gets incredibly tiresome (if you play with someone else, they may lure them away, while you open the lock. Probably) 6. Why is it that zombies seem to ignore hostile, human enemies? I have seen a few cases where they fight, but more often, I see them standing around, next to each other, waiting for me. That is incredibly immersion-breaking. If I feel like the zombies are buddies with some humans... then the game has failed in creating a believable world. (Occassionally, the zombies attack hostile humans, but from my experience, that occures in 25% of the cases) 7. Better communication - I didnt use fireworks for a long time, because the game taught me that noises will bring in more enemies and even virals. Apparently, this does not apply to fireworks... This could have been better explained by the game. For me, it was an item I would use only in the case of emergency, as i considered it a short term solution that would only cause bigger issues at the end. 8. The game has a lot "where do I go" situations. I have spent many, many minutes trying to find out which place to climb, jump, etc. to get to a place for a mission. It is not fun. It is tedious. I feel like I am playing some awful rendition of Super Mario World. 9. The despawning distance is very unforgiving. I went maybe 30m away from a place, where I had killed a lot of zombies (it was withing viewing distance, obstructed only by a car), but when I came back, all the loot was gone. That means that if you will engage in a chase, you will most likely lose the right to loot all the zombies you killed in that area. 10. Rules - the rules can be bent so damn much. I was in an intense fight in a mission, where I cleared a warehouse during the night. I had spent maybe 5-10 minutes fighting my way through everyone and with only one enemy remaining, volatiles started spawning inside the warehouse. They crawled out from under the warehouse shelves, killing me. It was almost day, but suddenly, the game decides to spawn enemies within viewing distance. That was very frustrating. Petty criticism:1. We are in a fairly small city in Turkey. Why are so many of the main characters foreigners? It would be more interesting, to me at least, if it had more of a Turkish feeling. You even get Turks speaking with a British accent. Sure, not completely unrealistic, but... If I play a game set in Turkey, I would prefer if it feels like it is set in Turkey - why does Brecken, a British white man, decide to go to Harran to save his business? He wants to sell parkour lessons... in an incredibly poor small city with, to be honest, not much for average citizens to practice parkour on without violating the principles of private property. Again, this game is immersion breaking. Some things i REALLY like about this game:1. If you point your gun at someone, they will react to it. It will allow you to scare enemies off without firing a shot. Very well done. Sorry, but I cannot recommend it, at least if you don't know anyone to play with (with more than six years after its initial release, I highly doubt that you will.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed Dying Light a ton! Even enough to play through the game twice, once solo and second coop. So you'd figure that the game is pretty solid and worth the money, and I would agree wholeheartedly. Except for one teensy little tiny detail, which is the Following DLC. Contrary to public opinion my friend and I found the entire DLC to be a huge slog and halfway through the DLC story line resorted to walking and ziplining everywhere instead of attempting to tame the hideous beast that was the driving system and the useless driving skill tree. The car bloody broke every other minute, groups of virals and volatiles would love to spawn and you could do nothing but punch them occasionally when Crane felt like it. I suppose notably we were playing on Nightmare difficulty, which does not give you any better drops or loot by the way. The DLC objectives were always across the map from each other as well, and the DLC's standard story with a twist and endings I was not remotely impressed by. We honestly just pushed through the main objectives until the game was finished because on the account of how much we hated the DLC. Why is this review a recommendation to play this game? Because we found the main game to be very fun and well put together. The city and slums of Harran were much better and less confusing to navigate than the countryside of nothing but inconvenient trees and inaccessible roads. Plus not having every single objective in a cave or up a mountain in the main game was nice too, and it felt like the developers really cared about the story in the main game. The graphics and combat of the game were excellent overall, and the night time was genuinely terrifying even late in the game. Buy this game if you love survival horror games or FPSs. Also worthwhile and fun to have a friend to play with, though I understand that's a mostly impassable hurdle in society to have friends. The steady progression of better weapons and upgrading of skill trees makes it satisfying to RPG players as well. Parkouring in this game is super fun, except for in the countryside of nothing but recycled buildings and stupidly low stone wall fences. They could definitely have made the driving system better with maybe a third-person view of the car, since there is a lot of tall grass to hide said stone fences.All in all, I recommend. Play the DLC if you would like to, but I would say it is nothing close to the main game in every aspect.Edit: I ranted a bit too much for my liking on the good things in the DLC but my friend outlined a better more lengthy review that mirrors mine while being very mean. check it out.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoilers, obviously. I'm only in the second part of the game but I'm disappointed enough to write this review. DO NOT SPEND FULL PRICE ON THIS GAME. Wait forit to go on sale and I mean like 75% off. I am very sad that I spent $60 on this game. It's more like a Dead Island DLC. The short version: buggy, under developed, boring story. S.S.D.D. survival horror game.You know, I wanted to love this game. Dead Island and Dead Island 2 are two of my favorite games. Dying Light is basically Dead Island. Same graphics, noises, weapons, etc. I would be fine with that except the game is not fully fleshed out. Some of the things I LOVE about this game is the parkour element, the grappling hook, and the attention to detail in the melee combat. It's just very difficult to enjoy the good parts of the this game when the bad parts are so distracting.When I first started playing I ended up being smitten with the same aspects most reviewers noted: the fluid movement, the nice graphics, yadda yadda yadda. Unfortunately that's just not enough to cover what is obviously a rushed and poorly planned game.Some issues with the game:This is an open world game but there is nothing to discover. If you spend 10 minutes running around an area then you've seen everything the entire game has to offer, except for a few story-released zombies. There are a lot of places to go, that's true, but there is nothing to see when you get there that isn't just "hey look how cool the city looks from here".  The only hidden things to find are things the developers maybe thought were funny, like a weak reference to Destiny (a place called a Loot cave with no decent loot and nothing to kill except a couple of slow biters - why bother?). There isn't any special loot to find other than a useless sword called EXPcalibur (which doesn't effect your XP and only has a 7 in durability), a machete blueprint that gives you a weak machete with no special features (Korek), and then your regular kind of blueprints and achievement related collectibles. One of the big draws of an Open World game is that exploration is usually rewarded with big challenges and amazing rewards. In this case there is no motivation for the player to explore. There's nothing to find - no cool loot, no terrifying enemies, nothing story related. Don't bother, just stick to the main story.My other problem is that the game gets... well... boring. Once you've hit your level caps (which is really easy to do before you even leave the slums if you do all the side missions there) there isn't much to do except advance the story. It's all the same fetch or kill sub missions with subpar rewards. The only reason to do them is to build up your XP because again, the best weapons will be in the shops and most of the blueprints are useless since base weapon damage evolves so quickly.Weapons are boring. There are no special weapons to find, like I mentioned. The shops will have the best weapons. The melee weapons are all the same from Dead Island - sledgehammers, machetes, katanas, sickles, hammers, etc. There are only 3 and 1/2 guns in the game - hand gun, shotgun, and police or military rifle (same gun basically). There are no modifications or upgrades to the guns. The guns don't increase in damage as you progress in the game despite the fact that the color changes in your inventory (white for common all the way to orange for epic/ultimate whatever). There is no special ammo. In the second part of the game you hear about and meet a gun smith and I thought "awesome, finally something to do with the guns". Nope. The gun smith gives you a blueprint for a sword. Seriously. I'm not joking.It was actually a weapon that made me write this review. There is a mission called Ultimate Weapon Challenge with Tobias. Do not bother doing it. After spending a bunch of time doing these challenges, all you're going to get is one weak machete with no special effects. No blueprints. Google rebel machete and you'll see a lot of people asking what happened there. The final challenge lets you use an awesome face-melting machete with mind-blowing effects on it. It would be SO MUCH fun to use in the game. But you don't get to keep it, you get the 300 damage plain rebel machete instead. Either the developers are completely lazy and forgot to finish these kind of details or they did this on purpose to be jerks and prank their players. Either way it's very disappointing.Zombies are boring. There are only biters, goons, virals, volatiles, bombs, demolishers, and toads. That's it. All the same stuff as Dead Island, except for the volatiles. The previews made the volatiles seem important to the story. I was honestly intrigued by them because they reminded me of the zombies from I Am Legend. Turns out they are just... there. Nothing important about them. No explanation for what they are despite the fact that they don't seem human. No reason to even include them in the game. You don't even see them in parts of the game where you would expect them to be an issue. I assumed Rais's pit would have them but nope. The volatiles are wasted because they were at least a little bit original AND intimidating. The story is cliche. If you've played Resident Evil and Far Cry then you know the story already because it's basically a mash up of the two. Rogue agent becomes an evil dictator and a global organization wants to weaponize the virus (and yep, still just a virus like every other zombie game). All twists are revealed right in the beginning. There is ZERO character development. There is nothing original about ANY of this. I honestly wouldn't mind any of these boring elements if anything made the game redeemable - lack of development in the world and weapons can be justified with a good story, and a bad story can be forgiven if there is a lot of fun stuff for me to find or discover. In this case, it's just boring, under-developed stuffed wrapped up in a pretty package and saved only by the addition of the Imfaous-style parkour element.I'm going to finish the game but it's the last game I'll buy from these developers at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: I am pleasantly surprised by this one. It's not a complicated game, but it's deep enough to reward thoughtful and strategic players. Unlike so many modern AAA games, it doesn't treat the player like an idiot, and you'll find yourself in tough situations which will test the Hell out of your ability to improvise and to focus under presure.My first playthrough has just been on Medium difficulty, but even so, this game has given me some of the most intense moments I've experienced in my entire 20 years of gaming. Not since I was a kid playing Thief 2 have I felt this kind of thrill while being chased just trying to survive.The world design is gorgeous. The lighting and textures are distractingly good and I often stop what I'm doing to just take in the sights and admire the workmanship. It's really amazing how full and dense the world is. A very high percentage of the buildings in the city are enterable. All of them are climbable, and it can be fun to figure them out.The menu interface is unnecesarily obtuse, and was CLEARLY not designed with the mouse in mind (Why can't we simply drag and drop inventory items? Where's right-click?) During gameplay, there are WAY too many keys to control everything and when things get hairy (as they often do) I find myself hesitating while trying to remember what key to press to do some certain move. The free running is smooth and intuituive most of the time, but sometimes you will randomly jump from a wall in some unexpected direction or fail to grab onto a ledge which looks climbable but isn't, or you'll unintentionally attach to and start climbing a pole in the middle of an intense fight.  But these moments are rare enough that the experience is still great.Despite these flaws, this is one of the most fun games I've ever played. I am really blown away by this one.

After browsing the Steam Summer Sale today for a few hours, I was trying to decide between this and another game that was like $45.I joined the subreddit, then joined the Discord for DyingLight and was greeted very warmingly. People were friendly, and answered all of my many questions about the game. This ended up in me doing a giveaway on /r/DyingLight as well and gave a copy of the game away for free.I bought the game, and the few cosmetic DLC's that were not included in the enhanced edition, as well as convinced a friend to buy the game. I have an i7 6700k, SLI 980TI, and an Acer XB270HU 144hz 1440p monitor. I can run this game at max settings, highest resolution, at 144FPS consistently. _childDocuments_.review: This game really is THE zombie game. The story isn't the best, but the parkour is freaking awesome. It's fun in co op sure, but it's legit scary in singleplayer. In co-op, you're kind of carefree in everything you do because you're with friends and you know you can just get revived. But in singleplayer, you need to close doors behind you, clear areas before looting, etc. IMO, play co op for fun and messing around, play singleplayer for the true experience. One thing to note: this game is NOT a zombie survival game. It is a zombie ACTION game. There are no survival elements such as needing to eat or drink or sleep. It's an action game with zombies in it.Newly infected humans who have just become zombies run super fast and are alerted to any loud noise made from either the player, other zombies, or other humans. When you hit them, sometimes they grovel to you and actually speak, pleading you not to hurt them. Then the infection quickly takes them over again as they attack you. This is definitely scary. Other typical special infected, such as chargers, spitters, boomers, etc. All here. And this game is NOT afraid to add in child zombies, which I love. They aren't common though, as they are a special type of infected. The vanilla game has two maps. Both are super fun. The first map has a TON of buildings. Plenty of fun parkour all around. The second map is actually my favorite, and it looks like they are using the same design scheme for Dying Light two. It has less buildings around, but the buildings are huge and remind me of Assassins Creed. Lots of side quests to keep you busy. Random challenges, survivors scattered around, safehouses to unlock, people to save. And the maps are huge! And very realistic.You have different skill trees. Survival, Agility, and Power. You gain survival points for completing missions and turning in care packages. You gain agility points by doing parkour and combining different tricks. You gain power points by fighting and killing. This game does VERY good at progressing you through the skills, just like Far Cry 3 does. You get more powerful overtime. You can eventually dropkick enemies, snap their necks from behind, kick their heads off when they are knocked to the ground, and even do a drop-stab on them similar to Far Cry 3 and Assassins Creed. The skill progression in this game is AWESOME!I know I said the game isn't really survival- and it isn't- but it has a ton of crafting. Blueprints, weapon upgrades, etc. You craft lockpicks, firecrackers, medkits, stat boost potions, weapons etc. You name it, you craft it. You can also just buy weapons/blueprints etc. The game has a lot of looting. Realistically placed items. Here's when the game becomes scary: Nighttime. At night, you will sh!t your pants. I don't want to spoil anything in case anybody is reading this and hasn't played the game yet. All I'm saying is, it is very scary at first. Later on? Not too much. I mostly played the game during daytime though. My preference. Although you do get DOUBLE EXP during nighttime for everything you do. So it's definitely worth it with the added risk factor.There are some things I want to talk about:There are TWO things that make the game very easy. Both are optional. 1st is the grappling hook. To say it clearly- it's overpowered. The grappling hook let's you zip to whatever you want that's within range. It has two uses then a quick 5 second cooldown until it can be used again and again. This gets rid of a lot of parkour elements because you can basically just fly from point to point. It's especially useful in the second zone (large buildings), but still overpowered in both zones. Kind of gets rid of the danger and fear when being chased, yknow? Reminds me of Assassins Creed Syndicate. The grappling hook in that was definitely necessary, but got rid of a lot of time you could spend parkouring.The second thing is the skill that lets you cover yourself in zombie blood to camo yourself. This skill is VERY OP when coupled with the ability after it that lets you kill enemies while remaining in camoflauge. This skill alone makes every single story-instance a complete joke. I'm serious. Without giving too many spoilers- at one point in the game you need to enter a large apartment building and place various explosives within it while also having to deal with a ton of volatiles and special infected right? Well with this camo ability, I was about to basically just clear the entire thing without once having to really fight a zombie. You can also unlock an ability that lets you snap zombies necks when you approach them from behind. This works while in camo. So the entire mission for me involved killing the first zombie, camo'ing, then going through and snapping zombies necks and progressing without once fighting.Again, both the grappling hook and camo are optional. It's up to you if and when you want to use them. I personally didn't mind.I did also want to talk about The Following, which is the major DLC from this game. I.... didn't really like it too much, to be honest. Ok so the map is huge right? That's great! But WHO'SE freakin idea was it to add a vehicle? Look don't get me wrong, it works. But why would you add a vehicle and a wide open map in a PARKOUR focused game?! You BARELY do any climbing or parkouring in The Following at all. Instead, it's mostly driving and backtracking from point A to point B, then back again. And it's kind of easy to lose the car. You can't summon it unless you go to a safe zone. And again the map is HUGE. So if you lose the car, expect to run for a while. This wouldn't be a problem since the game is focused on running, but the map is basically all giant fields. The story is alright, and some of the side missions and new features such as volatile hives are awesome! But seriously... why make the map a big open field with barely anything to parkour on. Not a good idea imo. A game like this should have the opposite. Lots of buildings, lots of parkour. Just my two cents.I've had the game for years but never got around to finishing it. Had tried co-op with a friend but finishing it all was tough with our schedules, so I restarted it all in singleplayer. And overall, I enjoyed the game better in singleplayer.I do have a spoiler for the final boss battle.  Spoiler is in that there. But I can also say it without a spoiler: the final boss battle sucked. And you won't need any of the skills or gear you have with you. Another thing that was SUPER annoying was how the devs basically begged you to play in co-op/PVP the majority of the time. Seriously. EVERY time you load the game up and enter a safehouse, the game has a forced pop-up that asks if you want to enable zombie invasions. NO I DO NOT! And this pops up EVERY single time seriously. It got super annoying. The game also has some non-forced pop-ups to the side that tell you to play co-op. At least those didn't lock your screen until you clicked yes or no. Like yes, we get it. I appreciate how hard they worked on the co-op and zombie invasions. Barely any lag, very good co-op. But please for the love of Gazi, do NOT make it a forced screen locking pop-up in Dying Light 2. It got so tiring.TL;DR - it's a zombie ACTION game, not a SURVIVAL game. So don't expect a survival game. Overall, a good game. Decent story, phenomenal gameplay. More immersive in singleplayer, but fun to goof around in co op. (You can play the entirety of the game in co op after the tutorial though). This game is definitely a must buy if you enjoy zombie games and parkour games. Ton of content, hours and hours of missions, zombie killing goodness. And remember. "If mama aint happy, nobody happy!"

_childDocuments_.review: No, I haven't played this game through (yet).But it's not really fun.The enemies take way too many hits, a fact that is made worse by the overpowered perks, which you have to earn the hard way first, thus making the earlygame tedious.The controls are messed up to the point where you can get boxed in and not be able to move or miss your jump targets. Everything has a long animation to it that, when triggered in fights, could mean your death.Weapons need to be repaired way too often and can even break, so why would you invest your resources into something you can kill 3 enemies with and then throw away, while there are perks that kill enemies after knocked down and don't take a single durability point?The nights are a nice gimmick, but you can't see ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ anyways and potions for that exist, but the ROI is minimal, the map is open world, but you always take the same routes, there are exploit locations where you can 1-stomp-kill hundreds of enemies and the multiplayer mode is full of hackers with unlimited ammo and stuff.Why this game has such a good rating overall is beyond me.Don't get me wrong, the graphics are nice and the gameplay could be compelling, but the balancing is broken and I personally don't see any fun in getting sucked into animations all the time.I might be playing on, just to get a little bit of value out of this, but so far, 10+ hours of not much fun in, recommending this game with the bad button promts (delayed), the ridiculous enemy HP and the borderline masochistic item system would just be a joke./EDIT:So after playing it through, it pretty much confirmed all my assumptions. Yes, there is undeniably a lot of content in this game. And yes, roaming the cities in multiplayer mode or with friends is cool. But it all hinges on the gameplay, and that's where the game fails terribly. So you get thrown into the game with basically no means at all to kill any zombie, apart from maybe triggering a few traps. Then, you get a lot stronger with better, mmo-styled equipment, so that you can end up one-hitting the normal zombies. When you can get ammo, the guns will even 2-hit some of the stronger enemies, leading to the question: Why would you even try to take on the bigger mobs in melee? You get little out of it, compared to just 1-hitting 10 of the smaller zombies, and the risk of dying is huge, especially in old town, where the hitbox is way too large for some enemies. Some story missions try to mitigate these elements by just taking your stuff away, which would make them really hard, except you can do them with others, which makes all missions way easier, actually easy enough for a relaxing evening. This scaling issue is unexcusable.The worst balancing offender is the grappeling hook. It's probably the thing that made then 2nd half of the game most enjoyable for me, as a lot of the tedious climbing got removed, but it's so overpowered that you cannot use it in many story missions.So this is a game, that lets you start massively, ridiculously underpowered and makes you so strong that you actually get nerfed by the game itself to not make it too easy. The consequence: The first few hours are much harder than the last few (well, the bossfight is literally a quicktime event), and while you can challenge yourself fighting in the night or fighting bigger enemies, the ROI is minimal.Does the game have its moments? Yes, sure, I had some hours of fun,But overall, the animations are way too obnoxious (especially in MP with a little bit of lag, making you feel like a ball passed around from zombie to zombie), the balancing is probably the worst I've ever seen, the bulletsponging and the weapons are Division-Styled and not really fun.So in short: If you have 3 guys to play with, it could actually be fun. As a singleplayer adventure, I didn't like it.

_childDocuments_.review: Dying Light: A Zombie Survival Adventure That'll Leave You Running... For Your Life!Dying Light, the lovechild of a zombie apocalypse and a parkour enthusiast's wildest dreams, is a game that'll have you laughing, screaming, and possibly swearing at your screen in equal measure. Developed by Techland, this open-world survival horror game takes the classic zombie genre and injects it with a healthy dose of adrenaline-fueled action and humor.Parkour Pandemonium:Forget what you know about traditional zombie games where you're constantly shuffling like the undead. In Dying Light, you're the agile parkour master who can vault over obstacles, leap across rooftops, and wall-run like a caffeinated ninja. Whether you're evading a horde of zombies or chasing down supplies, the parkour mechanics make getting around the zombie-infested city of Harran a hilariously frantic experience.Zombie Shenanigans:Speaking of zombies, the undead inhabitants of Harran are a mixed bag of grotesque, hilarious, and downright terrifying. From the standard shamblers to the more agile "virals" who move like they've had one too many energy drinks, each encounter with the undead is a chaotic dance of survival. And let's not forget the occasional glitch that sends zombies flying into the sky or contorting into absurd positions – because who said a zombie apocalypse couldn't be funny?Co-op Craziness:Dying Light's co-op mode is where the real hilarity ensues. Team up with friends to tackle missions, scavenge for supplies, and generally wreak havoc on the zombie population. Whether you're accidentally drop-kicking each other off buildings or frantically trying to revive your buddy while being chased by a horde, the co-op experience is a riotous good time that'll have you rolling on the floor laughing (or screaming in terror).Nighttime Nonsense:Ah, nighttime in Harran – where the zombies get stronger, scarier, and more determined to turn you into their midnight snack. If you thought daytime was intense, just wait until the sun sets and the real horror begins. Suddenly, every shadow is a potential threat, and the sound of your own heartbeat becomes a symphony of panic. It's like playing a game of hide-and-seek with a horde of ravenous monsters, except you're the one being hunted.Conclusion:Dying Light is a zombie survival game that doesn't take itself too seriously, and that's what makes it so darn enjoyable. With its blend of heart-pounding parkour, comedic zombie encounters, and chaotic co-op gameplay, it's the perfect recipe for a hilariously good time. So grab your running shoes, sharpen your sense of humor, and get ready to laugh, scream, and maybe even cry a little as you navigate the streets of Harran – just don't forget to watch your back... and your step!Rating: 9/10 - A Zombie Survival Adventure That'll Leave You Running... For Your Life!

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks amazing.      The combat makes you feel much more vulnerable than most games. You really have to watch yourself, especially against multiple zombies or people. Once you first find a firearm you have the option to shoot your way through everybody, at your own risk. They have made it so that if you want to play the easy way, you will attract hordes for ninja-like parcore zombies. This forces you to play scared.       The parcore is good. It's not like Mirror's Edge, but it's right there below it. It wouldn't suit the game anyway. The action of holding the space bar or pressing the space on some objects is annoying, but adaptable.       The graphical intensity of this game is awesome. The recent patch helped me with my gtx 970. If the engineers can fix the problem this game has with AMD processors, I'm set. When I sit still the game looks great and I get anywhere from 45-60fps. When I start running that number often drops into the 20-30 range. It's tollerable with the v-sync, but I should be getting more. Once they fix that this game it's a 5 star game. Fun to play and takes a LOT of time. I'm at 14 hours and only 51% of the story complete. And theres tons of other stuff to explore that I haven't even bothered with yet.       Just as a reference: AMD FX-8350, GTX 970 with 16 GB of DDR3. I usually play with anti-aliasing and ambient occlusion on with my special Nvidia settings running. Everything is on high except shadow map size and foliage. I have those on medium. The textures I run on high, and wooooow, there are a lot of them. I'm enjoying this game so far and would recommend it to someone else.

_childDocuments_.review: Dying light is an open world zombie survival game set in the city of Harran, the source of a deadly outbreak. This game is often credited as being a clone of other recent titles, such as Dead Island, and is also often thought to have copied mechanics from other games, such as Mirror's Edge, Evolve, and basically every free roam looting game in existace. In reality, Dying Light is a unique masterpiece that could easily shape out to be one of the best releases of 2015. It features aa parkour system, similar to that in Mirror's Edge, which is used to navigate seamlesly throughout the game's vast map. It also gives a very vertical feel to the game. The combat is also very satisfying, due to the vast amount of weapons at your fingertips that can be used to smash, slice, and stab your way through the hoardes of infected that you are sure to encounter. All this and more are accessable in both Singleplayer modes, and 4 player co-op modes. The game also features a 4v1 gamemode, which is a masterpiece in itself.. when you can find a match to join, that is.The game's main story has you following an agent known as Crane who is working to cure the virus, but ends up stranded in the city. He then proceeds to help out the remaining survivors, fetching loot, running supplies, and working to bring down the local crime lord. There are also a wide variety of side quests, very similar to games in The Elder Scrolls series as well as those in the Dead Island series. They often start off as simple "go get this" or "tell this guy something" kind of missions.. we alll know them. However, they often evolve into their own side story, with interesting, sometimes comical dialogue and events. The great (but predictable) main story, along with tons of side quests and zombies to bludgeon should satisfy your thirst to beat the heads of countless undead mutants in for a long time.In most games, the multiplayer is where the real treasure is. Dying light is no exception. In this game, you and up to 3 other friends can hop along Harran's rooftops and complete missions together. The game also features various challanges and competitions that the team can partake in, such as "kill the most zombies", "loot the most value worth of items" and even races. Hopping along the rooftops and slaughtering hundreads of undeaed beasts in this game is more satisfying than it ever was in CoD, L4D, and other zombie titles. The 4v1 mode is downright amazing. You and your team are put up against a player controlled super-zombie-beast-demon (too amazing to explain). The beast has to get 10 kills before the survivors destroy 5 nests scattered across the whole map. Yes, the whole map. This mode has you and your friends back to back, fending off a beast that is faster than you, stronger than you, and that's out for blood. It's one of a kind, and it's just something you have to expierece for yourselfJust get the game. It's worth every penny, especially if you have friends to play it with.10/10 would bang. Er.. play again. Yeah.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, parkour is polished and crafting system is decent. Combat isn't as visceral as I'd have liked, at least so far the combat is kind of dull. Sometimes a zombie's head caves in with the first blow, and sometimes it takes as many as 4 headblows to kill the same kind of zombie.Co-op can be frustrating for hosts trying to complete missions, as all players have to be within spitting distance of each other in order to interact with any quest objective/npc. Thankfully, the devs created  a "fast-travel to objective" option for stragglers, but if someone doesn't make use of it you have no choice but to kick them.My biggest gripe with multiplayer is the Hunter being overpowered with a 0 energy cost Ground Pound and infinite lives, making 1v1 and 2v1 games impossible for low level humans. Also having a hunter join in the middle of a mission without being able to reject the match is basically the biggest troll-feeding decision they could possibly have made. Fortunately you can turn off "Invasions," but I feel like players will abuse this. They'll either have a full team of players ready to hunt invasion-players, or invasion players will come across solo or two-player groups to troll.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't all that into the purchase of another zombie game, but I had read the movement and day/night cycles could be intense so I went ahead with it. I'm glad I did. The game's story is pretty good and the motivation for most of the characters are at least seemingly genuine. The voice dialogue is really good. The game play is surprisingly fun and the night switch over is terrifying if you're like me and have good quality sound and headphones. More than once I wasn't paying attention to the time and found myself near dusk far away from the central home. The raspy screams of the more aggressive breeds of zombies make you jump out of your skin at times and the ones that come out at night just are more than you can handle at first. So, the only option you have is to run your ass off to the nearest safehouse and hope there isn't a wall of them in the way.

_childDocuments_.review: The Platinum edition was definitely worth the $25 on sale, along with the DLC bundle for an additional $3. Definitely not worth over $100 though, so wait until things go on sale if you want all the added content. Right now there’s a community event turned on by default which turns all the zombies into runners (aka virals), so you may want to disable community event participation in the options menu before starting a new game.Summary: this game seems to have similar vibes to something like a Far Cry game, but with better movement, verticality, and crafting. The story isn’t anything groundbreaking but honestly I don’t that’s what most people are looking for in a game about smashing zombie heads. In the combat department, this is basically Zombie Go Boom: the video game. There are a few guns present, but overall the game is heavily focused on melee weapons, evasion, and looting. Some emphasis seems placed on choosing your battles since realistically, you’re never going to cut down the entire hoard by yourself and melee weapons break… a lot. There are ways to mitigate this later on, but most weapons early in the game aren’t worth the resources of repairing and modifying.Good stuff:-Lots of parkour movement options are available as you unlock skills. Avoiding zombies is usually a viable option 9 times out of 10.-Better melee mechanics compared to other zombie games as you unlock skills. Includes breaking out of grabs, throwing zombies into hazards, dodging, aoe attacks (spinning and ground slams) with 2 handed weapons, curb stomping finishers, and best of all DROP KICKS.-Zombie traps and environmental hazards EVERYWHERE including some which are activated by your remote control. Allows for creativity.-Bows for silent takedowns or Rambo cosplay.The not-so-good stuff:-Guns we’re added into this game as a complete afterthought and it’s painfully obvious. Guns have virtually zero crafting plans (aside from the ones you buy as DLC), cannot be upgraded or modified in any way, have very few variations, and suffer from a damage scaling bug which causes any guns you find to get WEAKER as your “power level” increases. For some reason, the most powerful guns you can get will only drop if you have a survivor level of 24 to 25, but a power level of only 4. Guns start spawning at lower damage values once you go beyond power level 4 which is easily achieved near the beginning of the game. The only way to get high damage guns is to create glitched save by having a friend give you a few hundred supply drops to your new character which increases your survivor level to 25 without affecting your power level. After that, your new character will either need loads of money to buy weapons from traders, or take the more risky option of searching police vans for the advanced/engraved variants of firearms. Again the better option would be to have a friend transfer goods to your new character to be sold at the traders for money.Another option would be to install game mods which prevent you from playing with anyone else who doesn’t have them installed. I don’t know why Techland seems to not like guns in their games, but the combination of guns, melee, and parkour was very nice. The absence of a more in depth arsenal with customization is such a missed opportunity here, and it’s not like firearms didn’t already have drawbacks for the sake of balance.

_childDocuments_.review: Dying Light is a game that is worth playing for a fan of zombie survival, or for a fan of dynamic (not always) parkour and first-person meat grinder. Yes, the plot in the game is certainly interesting and quite well-developed; you can visit two parts of the ghost town of Harran. Of course, someone may say that the zombie theme is already hackneyed, but Dying Light has a trump card - parkour, which you almost never see in games of this genre, and if you do, it’s not as good as here, let’s be honest. In addition to all of the above, the game has characters with charisma, there is also an ominous atmosphere of the entire apocalypse, which is conveyed perfectly, at night it’s even creepy to run around Harran because of the runners, because of this you get the feeling of a real survivalist, you have to hide well or just spend the night on the base. There is nothing to say about the graphics; for 2015 they are quite good.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game worth playing. There is no easy mode, there is no easy way to play. Its either run, fight, or die. Thats what makes this game worth playing. The killing of zombies.... Thats just fun. Smashing a zombies head to pieces is just so relaxing. The maps are expansive, and they merge quite well. I have beaten the game, and I'm still playing it. That is a testament to what a years wait has brought us.On a side note there are a few graphical glitches and in game glitches, although they are far and few between. For users of crossfire with massive FPS drops, turn off crossfire.Good Night to all, and Good Luck.

_childDocuments_.review: Was only suppose to play half an hour or so and then go watch a movie before bed, ended up playing 5 hours straight and ruining my next day at work.The game itself certainly is impressive, the main narrative is interesting and the side missions are surprisingly rich compared to other games. With surprising plots and twists that really keeps it interesting. This could however could also be down to random encounters (such as airdrops) that can turn a lazy stroll down the street to a gazelle race through the city or hide and seek that will have you scurrying around on all fours while waiting for whatever is hunting you to turn their backs.The main Zombies “biters” are little better then a nuisance if you are paying attention, the only time I have had real issues is when I ran smack into a hoard while being chased by “virals” which are infected living that can give you a run for your money, very 28 days later like. That and there are a lot spoiler zombies that will have you worried (Volatile) when the sun goes down.Had a very “Fun” moment where 2 people had joined my game just as it was getting Dark, we were pretty much playing Sandbox. Running around and bullying the “biters” laughing and comparing different ways of killing them and the few “virals” that interrupted us. (Coop makes it a lot easier as you can gang up on more powerful zombies and watch each other’s backs)This changed big-time however as the sun went down, we went from hunting to being hunted real fast. Trying to keep it together as a group when a hoard of virals are hot on your heals is both terrifying and hilarious at the same time, we ended up chased into an apartment complex which turned out to be a dead end. But thanks to great teamwork we actually held out till morning by holding a small apartment with one entrance, one person would heal and repair his weapons while lending an occasional kick while the two others held the Volatiles at bay with UV lights and everything from leg furniture to screwdrivers and wrenches.Most heart racing experience I have had in gaming for a very long-time, our elation at surviving however went south when we realised the battered and retreating Volatiles had been replaced by a hoard of zombies “biters” that swarmed the building we were in. Seeing your team being dragged down one at the time by a wall of dead flesh, before being pulled out of your corner and devoured was surprisingly enjoyable.Only real thing I can put my finger on is optimization, the game doesn’t seem to be 100% optimized and if you have AMD graphic card you might encounter some FPS drops that shouldn’t happen. Hopefully this will be addressed in patches.If not a 10/10 then defiantly a 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Its a good zombie game, one of the best definitely. Movement feels clunky at first, especially on PC with keyboard controls. Graphics is awesome, and the game can run on relatively low-spec computers if needed. Crafting elements in this game is simple, although crafting just 1 thing at the time gets annoying fast. Weapon selection is decent, and becomes even wider when you consider modding your weapon with upgrades. The world is small, and is made to feel decievingly big. You see landmarks and wonder if you can get there or not, and you get dissappointed 95% of the time. This is kind of made up for in "The Following", where the map doubles in size. Sounds is delicious in this game, even regular zombies sounds terrifying, and the buggy's engine sounds is magnificent. To keep it short, I loved the gameplay, especially in "The Following", but I absolutely hated the story in both the main game and the DLC. That's all I can say without spoiling it. Buy it if you like slashing zombies in half right after it stopped momentarily attacking you to beg for its life. Don't get it for its story. + Crafting+ Parkour+weapons+ Buggy!+Nicely detailed+Zombie AI is the best i have seen in any game- Small world in main game- Wear and tear of weapons is sometimes extreme- Main story and "The Following" story as well drags down some points. - Character is sometimes "Assassins Creed" dumb, where he will not grab the correct ledge, and fall even though you clearly pressed the button to grab/jump.Conclusion: I would definitely recommend this game to any zombie-lover. If you ever see it on sale and like taking down zombies even remotely, this is a game for you. Just don't expect much from the story, focus on the awesome gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Originally I was lookin for a slowpace zombie open world/looting voyage with very wide distances to travel like Day-Z or similar games but I just dived straight into Dying light without lookin much into it since web searches says it is one of the top zombie games ever. I had an idea the gameplay was quite mobile yet I still got kinda surprised on how fast the pace really is and it can be quite intimidating at the start but I didn't get dissapointed for even one bit! The handling of the weapons is very satisfying whether it be melee, throwing weapons or guns. It's kinda like Dead Island but better in every aspect. The story provides a creepy good atmosphere of survival, I felt no rush in focusing on the main quests for story progress even if playing on solo since the game is kinda addicting once you get used to moving quick on routes especially when paired up with plenty of subquests, awesome visuals, great gameplay with a wide array of skills/weapons and superb map design. Also kudos to the devs for including so many details, like how goons with melee weapons responds when you suddenly pull out a gun- they are not braindead that will just come rushing everytime and will sometimes get their hands up or just run for the hills. Freshly turned aggressive zombies will sometimes cover up when u hurt them and show some last remnants of human traits like talking and begging before eventually succumbing to full blown biter. And so much more! The kind of subtle details that makes sense and within it makes you appreciate a game more than the typical. If you can get the Definitive Edition(good price on sale) then definitely go for it! it Includes all DLC's which means more more badass weapons and I think it includes an expansion but I haven't got to it yet. P.S Just when you thought being fast is enough.. wait till night comes

_childDocuments_.review: Never usually review a purchase, but I feel like Dying Light has forced me to. After seeing that the existing reviews are overwhelming, it was a natural decision that this would be my next story driven game. However, this is the reason that I can't stand this game. The gameplay is... Alright. The zombie killing is the best of any survival game that I've played, and skill trees are always good. Parkour feels clunky, with no fluidity until you have spent skill points into the corresponding skill tree but improves after that. Combat is actually not too bad, being saved by innovative body-based combat, but it takes time to find or invest in any decent weapons. The looting system is unnecessary, I've accumulated a wealth of about $3000 by occasionally holding f in the direction of a pile of corpses. I have, however, never spent any of this money, and it just sits pretty in my inventory. However, the biggest tragedy in this game is the storyline. The character of Rias is an apparent main antagonist but is a generic chaos mongering villain. The character is uninspired, the interactions are boring, and he feels like the washed-out little brother of Vaas from Far Cry 3. Speaking of which, there is a dream sequence that seems to be the amalgamation of FC3 and Uncharted, and it is painfully boring. Narrated by one of the few characters that the player connects with, it is an uninspired speech about struggle in a futile attempt to inspire. The game is yet another that gives an illusion of choice, before forcing a choice upon the player, and then having the villain berate the player about their lack of free will. Spoiler, but almost every character dies, you will only care about 3 of those deaths, and then you will carry on trudging through a storyline based on your own failure to kill someone when you had the chance.Tl;dr The mechanics are fairly good but require specing into before they become anything spectacular, the zombie killing is amazing however every single type of zombie encountered can be found in Left 4 Dead, and the storyline is a painful exercise in futility that you'll stop caring about 60% of the way in.If you put 100 monkeys with typewriters in a room long enough, eventually you’ll get Hamlet, but give them 5 minutes and you'll get Dying Light.Edit: I have at least an additional 30+ hours in this game. That means that something must be very right, and that I must have changed my mind, right? Wrong. The main storyline is still abysmal. There is absolutely no redemption on that front. The side missions actually come close to saving this game, with a huge variety of challenges that rejuvenate the tired execution of a good concept. Ironically, I think more effort went into the writing of side characters like Gazi than the main story line. The combat gets significantly better, with a fully specced power tree making combat fun, varied, and manages to not fall into the repetitive rut that other fps games do. The agility is... Tragic. In a game that tries to add the unique aspect of levelling a skill by navigating the map, a fully specced agility tree is still clunky. The parkour challenges don't aid you in learning how to use these abilities better, but rather how to rely on luck and muscle memory to do a very specific route. You will find yourself not using half of the abilities you spent so long unlocking, and cursing some of the ones that you did (*ahem springing backwards off of walls*). You end up trying to avoid all parkour by using the grappling hook every five seconds, which is the only good thing to come out of this tree. Survivor is a boring, but admittedly necessary skill tree. Not much to say about it, other than it simply improves quality of life. I completely change my view of looting. It is necessary, however it is a necessary evil. You need to accumulate wealth to invest in high level weapons crafting. It would be beneficial if all drops within a radius stacked, so that you only have to pick up once. One of my biggest problems lies with the challenges. If a challenge is failed, first you have to look at the fail notification for 10 seconds with absolutely no way of dismissing it, then you have to listen to the NPC, then you have to reselect the challenge and listen to the same godawful dialog banter before you can reattempt it. I want to listen once. Only once. Then be able to immediately retry the challenge upon any failure.The community events are amazing, and even better is the addition of the "Be the Zombie" gamemode which tests player skills in a PvP environment.All in all, I think that the side quests and combat redeems this game, but not enough for me to endorse it. I would give a neutral recommendation if I could, with the main story and cumbersome agility system being the strongest nails in the coffin. I may update after playing The Hoard DLC if I make it through without wanting to vault off of a building IRL.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is very much a cheesy zombie movie, the combat usually is satisfying and the movement works...most of the time.Don't be surprised if you're next to a ledge, jumping from building to building, jumping down aiming at a trash pile (and hitting it), being randomly thrown off of a zip line or just not grabbing on to the edge of your target and falling to your death, losing 220 to 1200 survivor points. For a zombie game it's really good but be prepared to be frustrated. The Hellraid and the Following DLC, as well as the crafting mechanics and some really fun, silly moments have made it worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I jumped into Dying Light after having a blast with Dead Island, hoping to find a game with equally satisfying zombie action and great mechanics. Dying Light totally delivered and quickly became one of my favourite zombie games!The parkour is incredibly fluid and gives a thrilling sense of freedom as you move through the city. The zombie dismemberment mechanics are top-notch and add a satisfying impact to each swing. And the nighttime shift is intense—the Volatiles and the darker tone make it feel like a completely different game, adding an extra layer of suspense and challenge.The character progression is another huge highlight. It’s so rewarding to see your character grow stronger, gain skills, and handle tougher challenges as you keep levelling up. It makes the game-play feel fresh and gives you a real sense of development and mastery over time.If you’re looking for a zombie game that combines excellent mechanics, immersive progression, and all-out fun, I can’t recommend Dying Light enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Without doubt the best zombie game out there. There are a few problems though.1. Events.Events mostly give cool stuff and cool blueprints if you can complete them. As such I missed A LOT of content. Like 20 outfits and like 10 blueprints. I love these events but they should at least do these events like 2/3 times with the same prices, since this is quite unfair in my opinion. "Oh you weren't on when that event 1 year ago took place? Too bad, no cool stuff for you". And they do these cool events like every 3 months for 5 years now, so if you're new you'll miss A LOT of stuff. What's even worse is that things like Dying Light 2s trailer weapon are apparently in the game but you can't get it's blueprint anymore, and I was only able to get it with pure luck; the quartermaster glitched out or something and gave me a few dockets from some events from like 1-2 years ago. This is how I found out the coolest buggy skin was an event item, this is how I found out the Dying Light 2 trailer weapon was in the game and this was how I found out I missed all this stuff. Even now I wan't to 100% the game but as such that isn't possible since so many outfits and blueprints are not achievable anymore.2. Mission structure.Side missions all make the game easier and are a must-do. One side mission per example makes it so the walls inside tunnels are gone, the other makes it so there are more ziplines around the map, and the other gives you new upgrades or upgrades things you already have. All side-missions also add a little something to your room in the tower that has to do with that side-mission, something a lot of people missed. I love that little detail, but sadly the side missions don't go well with the main missions. Like how one mission a friend will die, somebody you've been with for the entire story just dies, and everything starts going wrong; but then next thing you know you are getting chocolates for some guy who clearly hit his head too hard and his... mother? This game really tries to take itself seriously in the main missions but completely goes Saints Row on a lot of side missions.3. (BIG ONE) Online.The online part of this game is absolutely f***ked. Modders everywhere, so many it's not even fun. Somtimes somebody will just join your game, give you 10000 survivor packs (hacked versions of DROPs, these will make your rank go up) and then leave. Just like GTA V online right? Well, no. This game is absolutely not pay-to-win, and the legend rank lets you show other people your skill, how hard you worked for it. Back in 2016 when you saw a legend 250 level you probably (I wasn't on back then so that's why I saw probably) knew that was a pro, you knew that was someone who worked his a$$ off for it. Sadly nowadays if you see a legend 250 lvl it's 99.9% of the time a modder. And I'm not exaggerating. Only time I saw a player who worked his a$$ off to get to legend lvl 250 was when I played with someone from the official Dying Light Discord. Is it so hard to implement Easy Anti Cheat or something, Techland?Of course the game still phenomenal. The parkour is even better than Mirror's Edges parkour, and that says a lot. The fighting is really fun and in the main game alone there are 2 open worlds for you to explore. If you buy the enhanced edition it'll even be 3, where the 3rd DLC world is so big you even get a buggy. I personally liked the story, even though Rais is like Vaas's brother and he belongs in a Far Cry game. For the record this game is absolutely not scary. Wasn't scared for a moment in this game, and at the end you'll clap anything that comes in your way. All DLC has also been amazing and I can't recommend this game enough.I ABSOLUTELY ADVICE YOU BUY THE FOLLOWING DLC.It's an entirely new open world and you now even have your own car. It's like 15 hours of content if you want to do all main-missions and side-missions. The world looks gorgeous and I love the fact that almost every house is enterable now. The new "freaks of nature" are also amazing, and if you tought the normal "goons" and "demolishers" (they are bosses sort of) were hard these new freaks of nature have like 10x times the health and ara 4x as strong. They also all look really cool. I also loved the fact you have multiple endings now, but you can clearly see Crane took the bad ending since otherwise Dying Light 2 wouldn't be coming out soon.I DON'T ADVICE YOU PRE-ORDER THE HELLRAID DLC.I have played the beta and it's a glitchy mess. Way too dark, at points I literally had to put the gamma to max and close all blinds, the first 10 minutes you also just get spammed with reskins of zombies and get spammed with the same stupid blade and the exact same loot. It's also a hard-load mission like Prison and Bozak Horde. Which is terrible since Dying Light likes to change your quest when you quit and re-open the game, and 1/3 of the time you'll load into Hellraid, which means all your stuff goes into your stash and you'll have to spend 15 minutes re-organising your inventory. From what I've played the entire DLC will also most likely only take 45 minutes and there doesn't seem to be a cool special outfit for you to have in the main game, and the team working on the DLC now only has 2 weeks to get fix an entire list of problems, so it isn't really looking too good for the DLC.

As the main voice actor of this game is Roger Craig Smith, I would often imagine crazy scenarios involving Resident Evil character Chris Redfield. After a while I would imagine myself playing Resident Evil 5 instead.Enemies are too spongy and the melee-combat is a drag compared to Dead Island. Upgrades are boring and mostly useless. After opening the skill that allows you to jump over zombies, you are basically invincible against the basic dudes.The basic zombies are no fun to fight. Even after you have leveled up the base-dudes remain spongy and will stun-slap you around like the little b*tch you are. The special infected are even more boring than their counterparts in Dead Island. Dude, Left 4 Dead came out more than a decade ago. What you get in Dying light is stripped down versions of those enemies. Lame boomer, lame hunter and lame big dude. The melee in this game feels a lot like unmodded Oblivion. The enemies are always leveling up faster than the player. Even at max level you feel weak. Unlike Dead Island, you rarely get to feel decently powerful. Most of the weapons are useless because of the stamina drain. The sledgehammer slam and spinning feels useless. It's slow, does not stun enemies with consistency and leaves you open for massive counter damage barrage. The weapon modding is more restrictive and tamed-down than in DI. You will have to buy the dlc to get more variety. I felt that DI had the weapon modding more integrated with the whole. The skill system overall is disappointing. After you unlock all of the mobility options there is really nothing fun or game-changing to discover. The endgame consist off grinding multiple levels without any unlocks to unlock. Agility system encourages you to just run over the enemies and the ineffectiveness of melee steers you towards avoidance of all non-story encounters. The grappling-hook was almost fun, but makes you avoid enemies even more. And some of the skill-unlocks killed me more than any of the enemies. The wall-jump is a beginner’s trap for sure. It does nothing useful, besides killing you randomly. It is that Oblivion feel again that the levelling feels detrimental.We played Dead Island and this back to back. Most of the eurojankiness of Dead Island feels ironed out. More we played on, the more I was playing just because I loved DI. Last third of this game is like a plane crash. Feels like the developer runs out of money before your eyes, as you play the game. The cheapness was more pungent here than in DI. Strange sidestepping overall.To not be able to play that last mission with my friend, just because some lame quick-time bs, makes me even more angry. We had co-op -quick-times in Resident Evil 5 all those years ago, why not here? Overall its somewhat fun with friends, but the game will fight you back at some points. If you really liked Dead Island, you will maybe like this game too. On sale ;D.Here hoping that devs will bring back the fun of Dead Island for their next game.

_childDocuments_.review: Beginning as a furtive, desperate survival-horror experience, Dying Light gradually and gratifyingly evolves into a fast, hyper-violent celebration of vertical freedom and zombie destruction. _childDocuments_.review: One word to describe the entire game, wow. I have just completed the base game and The Following DLC. Oh boy. (DLC)+ DLC The Following is absolutely amazing, it still maintains that atmosphere and difficulty while still giving us the huge new system of vehicles which does get rather fun at higher upgrade levels. (From 1-5)+ The blueprint system - Upgrade all your weapons or modify them. You can put little mods on them too boost damage ect... or you can change them into a different weapon.+ The DLC weapons (Such as Volatile Hunter) gives a HUGE boost to the game. Yes, people do say that is a P2W DLC but its not broken nor is it weak. + Great graphics - Also doesnt require an amazing PC to run.+ Plenty of sidequests in main game and DLC - There is a huge variety even if some of them are rather boring.+ Interesting and pointful open world setting REASON/s TO NOT BUY- Bozak's Horde does not seem very interesting - The story is practically non-existent as well as the challenges being rather repetitive for the rewards. _childDocuments_.review: Why spiritual successor? Deep Silver acquired the rights of the Dead Island franchise and Yager is developing Dead Island 2. Dying Light is made by Techland and is a completely new franchise however, very much inspired of Dead Island 1 and Riptide!Okay, now finished with the story mode. Here is the updated review!For gamers on the fence with this game, I can honestly tell you that it is a fun game. Granted, I liked Dead Island 1 even with the repetitiveness, bad voice acting and goofy humor but Dying Light has many differences. It's got a more serious tone and the setting is mainly focused on survival. You finally have a day/night cycle and lemme give you an idea how's the night cycle... Exactly like the movie . You run for your life if you dare do stuff at night... You can try to kill one of those "Volatiles" but highly not recommended until you are high level, like at least 10 or you'll just get killed easily by them swarming you. Thing is, just like , once a Volatile spots you, it screams and then you get swarmed by other Volatiles and Virals. So, better do exactly like Will Smith and run like hell!A good change from Dead Island is you do not level up once for many ability trees but once for every three and just by playing. If you do lots of parkour, you level faster in the Agility tree... if you lockpick many chests, you level up faster the survivor tree, etc. I think this is a cool new system and a welcome change from Dead Island where you had many trees of abilities and had to focus on specific trees as well.As for the story, it is about you, the character, that gets airdropped to Harran, the quarantined city that has a nasty epidemic going on. You are sent to investigate while blending in with the locals, who are fighting each other for the sparse resources scattered over the city. Brief synopsis but better than Dead Island. It drags on for long though which I was a tad disappointed but it gets the job done!If you loved Dead Island, you should love this one as it is much better in every ways. Its not cheesy like DI and more survival focused. The game is not perfect (heck, has any game ever been?), has a few faults here and there but the goods outweight the cons and I had lots of decent fun in this sweet violent game.On the technical side, the game was quite stable on my rig with every settings maxed out. I only had one crash to desktop but it may have been on my fault since I didn't restarted the game once I upped the settings. Aside from that, the game runs A-OK to me! The delay this game got surely went into QA and I wish more games would do the same. To see a new modern AA/AAA game releasing on DAY ONE and working properly is exceptionnal nowadays!I recommend this game especially if you loved Dead Island, you will truly love Dying Light. Many improvements to be seen/experienced. Is it worth the retail price? YES! Especially if you're looking into a new game right now, then give it a shot!The Following DLC picks up exactly where you left of. You are meeting a character that tells you of a cure to the devastating plague in Harran from a friend but his dying words mentions to travel in a new location. Once there, you get to play around and even drive a dune buggy (that you can improve as you level up the Driver section). There is new enemies that you find who are labelled as "elite enemies" that you "shouldn't fight on your own"... which is correct if you play the game in Nightmare mode! Talking difficulty level, I played the whole DL game in nightmare mode and it was mostly fair fights! But in TF, nightmare mode is a bigger chore. Enemies have more hit points and your damages are very low. You also die more easily vs Volatiles at night... or in Volatiles Nests! The Countryside region is BIG and fun to explore but my biggest gripe with Dying Light is you don't have ANY fast travel... and almost all quests/missions are all far apart, implying lots of driving and time spent there.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh where do I start, this game is so good, I really didn't expect it to be as good as it was, the story was engaging and the voice acting is amazing. There is also a skill tree that lets you unlock more abilities the more you play, it's always cool to try out new perks when you unlock them. The story was also great, but to be fair I played most of this game with friends and that was probably why I enjoyed it so much more. The feeling of being chased at night when you first start was so intense and scary. The combat in the game itself is well done, and as you play, you unlock more moves you can use. , spanning from a literal plank to an assault rifle.In addition, , even the most minor effects (lens flares, depth of field) and details make up the environment and it makes this post-apocalyptic, run down city so believable and realistic. They also did a great job with water, making entering and exiting look pretty realistic.To add to this list, the  it sounds amazing to listen to on it's own and I feel that in-game, it sets the scenes so well, the tracks by themselves can already make you feel either calmed or tensed/scared. Real props to  for making such a good soundtrack.However, this game isn't perfect, there's some physic glitches my friend found; like jumping off a super tall radio tower, landing on a car and not losing your legs, not sure whether this was intentional or not but it was still pretty funny. There's also another bug where a Volatile managed to glitch through a thin shutter door to get to us which really freaked us out.In closing, I want to add that I've had this game on my wishlist for quite awhile and only recently got it due to a sale but I would honestly buy this game at full price for what it is. Again, I never expected it to be what it is, my only minor gripe is the paid DLCs as I'm just generally not a fan those. But then again, it doesn't take away from the main game, just expansions. I have no regrets buying Dying Light.

_childDocuments_.review: Dying Light.... is one of the best "Zombie" games ever made, period. The movement is fluid, the melee combat is visceral and extremely enjoyable, the weapons look and feel nice - with blueprints giving melee weapons alot of variety. The light RPG mechanics work great for what the game is going for, and gives a nice sense of progression. Not to mention the game lends itself really well for multiple playthroughs with the new game + and multiple difficulties that change up how the game works. The changes aren't massive, but enough to make the game feel different on higher difficulties.It also has an amazing set of DLC's - with the Following being a massive campaign expansion with a pretty great story (honestly it's story is even better than base game imo), a whole new skill tree - which involves a new mechanic that is crucial to the dlc - the buggie. And that thing is hella fun once you get a few upgrades and more decent car parts for it. Not to mention, sidequests - just like in base game, are varied and fun. Then you have the Prison DLC which is great for farming high level loot, and Bozak Horde - which is... pretty great but not my favourite. (I don't have Hellraid - so i can't comment on that one).The only real issues with the game are:Mediocre performance on Laptops (which is what i use to play games).Human enemies - they are a bit frustrating when fighting in melee and the human enemies with guns legit feel unfair at times.And... the tankyness of special zombies on Hard and Nightmare.And maybe the extreme amount of cosmetic packs - but since they barely impact gameplay i can't be too mad.Overall an amazing action game (The best zombie ACTION game) - with great mechanics, and it's just a pleasure to play - get it if the idea of sparta kicking zombies off rooftops and running for your life during night time.

_childDocuments_.review: I know many people like this game so much and i am fine with that, because i do think it's actually a good game, but i just can't stand the combat mechanic, it's just frustating than fun imo but not really the only reason why i give thumb down in this review. There are some minor bugs that totally ruin my experience, like keep stucking whenever i slide, human enemies who blocking my attacks in split second even when i sneak attack him from behind,  human enemies who can block my throw when they literally are throwing a knife even if i throw one when they attack it just falls off and their block animation kicks in right "after" they threw the knife on me, sometimes when i jump down to the blue bags i received damage and even died, when i throw weapons sometimes they fall off the map or stuck under the ground, and so on and on. Also the respawn system isn't good either, literally after i clean one place, just less than a minute later the area was swarmed again by zombies, i didn't even go too far from that area, it's so annoying especially when you are trying to unlock a loot with lockpicking. I am playing on hard mode, so i am not sure does it exist to make the game harder by keep spawning enemies or every difficulties have the exact same problem.The other problem is save mechanic, i am not really a fan of autosave system that doesn't provide us with manual save except maybe souls series because they nailed it in my opinion. I understand it's maybe because of co-op feature, but at least it should exist for the sake of solo players only like me.And yet another problem is the mouse lagging, at least it's something personally i had so i am not sure if people have same problem as well, and thanks for some discussions on steam i could find a solution for it.I have tried the online feature such playing as human vs hunter and it was fun, so far i haven't try co-op features yet so i can't give my thought on them.The parkour mechanic is cool and fun i give you that..Overral it's a fine game maybe around 75/100 right now for me.

You can't freely roam the map at any time like you can in real open worlds like Far Cry, or Metal Gear Solid V, to cause mayhem and collect resources.In my view they should have marketed it as a jumping puzzle game with survival flavoring. No bugs, looks pretty good, just jumping puzzles are not my cup of tea.So if you came here looking for an open world zombie killing game, forget it. Stay if you are into parkour and jumping puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: What would happen if first person perspective Assassins Creed parkour and open world exploration met the undying popularity of zombies? Dying Light that's what.It takes a Borderlands-esque nod in the weapon/loot system department, with a sprinkle of survival-style weapon durability for repairs to ensure you keep upgrading and mixing up your arsenal. While the infected do have a mildly annoying habit of randomly spawning just out sight while you're busy knee deep in blood and guts of their compatriots, the overall experience is a barrel of laughs and makes for some very entertaining gameplay.This does not even touch on the expansion "The Following" where you apparenty get an offensive buggy to plough through the mutated undead. Quite reminiscent of Farcry's vehicles if you ask me, but what Techland borrows from others it successfully and seamlessly integrates these elements into the game's overall formula.If you are not into another player being able to mess with your single player expereince however, you may want to turn the night time zombie invasion option off. A human player will spawn in as a special zombie (with its own experience and skill tree to boot) and the survivors will have to destroy its nest while the Night Hunter attempts to kill them. Nevertheless, maybe when you unlock more of the survivor skill tree it may be fun to dip your toes into this for some player versus player action.
