_childDocuments_.review: March 8th 2022 Edit:They added crossplay via Tencent ("Epic" games garbage), causing crashes for some people and making inviting friends not work at all. Glad I quit playing this game a while ago.8th of February: Seriously techland? Remove this ♥♥♥♥ already.Spike Event Update: 14 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ GBs for a ♥♥♥♥ event.Upon launching the game, this is shown: As I wrote in the screenshot, If I want to pre-order your game (which I don't) I'd go to the store page. Don't shove a "Pre-order" screen on me. They also added this to the tower:This just breaks the immersion, and doesn't make sense to exist during the time period of the game. This was the only advertisment to DL2 I found, but some reviews say they're plastered everywhere. - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -I was looking forward to getting this game, but I was getting frustrated by the combat and the parkour. As for the story, I didn't really care about it when I saw someone play the game for the first time. I was only interested in the gameplay. However, the story in this game is... awful. None of the characters are likable or memorable in my opinion.  The protagonist, Crane, is ok I guess. There's only like 2 scenes of him that I remember, the first being my honest reaction to what had just happened, and the second making me dislike him. Then you got a woman named Jade, and her brother, Rahim, who are uh... They might as well be side quest characters, because of how forgettable and unlikeable they are. Hell, there's side quest characters more memorable than them. The only scenes I remember of them are  And when Now let's talk about the Parkour and movement in general. At first I really enjoyed it. You can climb just about anything, especially with the grappling hook. Climbing up walls feels really smooth, until you unlock tic tac that is... What's Tic Tac? It allows you to climb up a flat wall by a little bit, getting you even higher up than before. Sounds nice right? It is, until Crane decides to 180 and jump to his death. Yup, Tic Tac is also about jumping OFF walls. While "Tic Tac"ing, you'll eventually start sliding DOWN the wall, this lets you know how high you can go up the wall. Once you've reached the point where you slide, you can jump off the wall, which is supposed to be used to either avoid attacks (from zombies and humans), or to reach a platform or another wall. WITHOUT the grappling hook however, this skill might aswell be called "Deathwish". You can't seem to cancel the sliding, and just drop to the floor again. So if you are in a bad spot where jumping off isn't safe, you'll just have to slowly slide down, which in combat can, and WILL, get you killed. Now enough about Tic Tac, what about sliding? It's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ broken, that's what. Y'know how in Apex Legends, Far Cry (Series), Cyberpunk 2077, Borderlands 3 and alot of other games the sliding is done by sprinting and then holding down crouch? It doesn't work like that in Dying Light. Apparently you have to be crouched, hold sprint, and then stand up while moving forwards to initiate the slide. How hasn't this been fixed? Oh right, why fix gameplay when you can just make more events, collabs and outfits nobody wants.As for rolling (after a fall) it mostly works, but seems inconsistent at times. Why can I only  roll from a fall off of a tall building but other times get my knees cracked like thin tree branches? Otherwise, it works, and is kinda satisfying. But wanna know what ISN'T satisfying? The melee combat. I've been hearing how supposedly satisfying it is. But in game I struggle to kill 1 slow walking zombie, with a 700 damage machete. Are you serious? 4 charged swings to their heads isn't enough? It's a bloody machete, that deals 700 damage. And on Normal difficulty as well. What a load of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. And it only gets worse from here. What about the Virals? The running zombies who haven't completely turned yet? They can dodge your attacks, which at first, sounds like it'll make combat more challenging. And it is, because they get BS invincibility frames. Same with humans. And speaking of humans... The gun wielding ones are OP. You die in 5 seconds, after leaving cover when trying to attack them. Like seriously, every bullet they fire hit you. Which would've been fine if they had like pistols or rifles with a slow fire rate and missing every now and then. But NooOoOOO, let's give them rifles that fire 5 rounds per second and deal about 10-12 damage each. And melee humans aren't better.  as well as the hostile survivors  get invincibility frames when dodging. Sometimes they don't even have to dodge, and somehow they still completely ignore the damage from your melee swings. They can even "dodge" a dropkick to the face. They just ignore it like nothing happened.The hostile survivors also apparently have a longer detection distance. One time I got hit by throwing knives from nowhere. Turns out it was a dude on the ground, like WAY down on the ground, that somehow spotted me while climbing.I will say, I did enjoy the soundtrack and how terrifying nighttime feels. But those things alone can't make me recommend this game, sorry.TL:DRStory is meh, characters aren't memorable (in a positive way) or likeable.Melee combat is unsatisfying and parkour is decent with some hiccups here and there happening.Haven't finished it yet, but here are some things I guess:

_childDocuments_.review: So I've been playing this game for about a week or so now, and so far, it's easily the best Zombie I've ever played, hands down. At first glance it may just seem like another Dead Island, but trust me, Techland learned a hell of a lot from their previous title, and made something that truly stands out to rival Far Cry 3 or even Skyrim. The game has a brilliant Fight or Flight setup, where you can either tear through the mobs of zombies with swords, blunt weapons, or guns. Or run use the parkour to avoid fights altogether, as well as little traps and noise makers to draw the zombies' attention while you do something else (lockpick, quick time event to open doors, etc). It's a interesing contrast to the Stealth vs Mayhem you normally see in most games.The Parkour itself really does deserve a mention here, it's a little odd at first as you can't wall run like in Mirror's Edge. But you can climb buildings by jumping from window ledges or other parts of the architecture that jut out and give you something to grab onto. Almost feels like Assassin's Creed honestly, which is really nice as it does feel like real parkour, using the environment to your advantage and improvising your path as you go. The day and night mechanic is also pretty solid, during the day the game feels like a free for all, go nuts. But at night it's closer to a true horror game with the Volatiles (think of Verdugo from RE4). And these things don't ♥♥♥♥ around, they are TOUGH to kill, and even harder to fight, to a point where you just need to run and get to the nearest safehouse. Plus the game has a sound mechanic, where loud noises like explosions, gunshots, car alarms, etc all draw in zombies, which adds to the tension and adds a risk factor to balance out Pistols, Rifles, and Shotguns. The end result is a drastic contrast in gameplay as time goes by, with daytime being all about having fun and starting a riot, and night being a more stealthier horror driven experience. The story, yea the voice acting isn't perfect but it is interesting enough to keep me playing, if just to find out what happens next. And there are some likeable characters, like Brecken, Rupert, Jade, Troy, Spike, etc. Each of them has some trait or two that I like about them, but they are minor traits that are underplayed and easily missed if you're not paying attention at all.  Graphics wise is a bit iffy......while I am sure it looks great when it's running on the right system, it ran like ♥♥♥♥ for me until I got ahold of the Dying Light Manager from LeavesOwnZ, you really do need to have at least i5 4690K and GTX 970 or better to really make this game run beautifully. But then again graphics aren't everything as long as the game is playable, and with the Dying Light Manager it runs pretty decently, even on an older system like mine.  As for other criticisms I do have a few, one, in a game with melee combat, what do you expect to do besides striking someone.....block right? Guess what you can't do....BLOCK or at least a freaking parry function, press mouse2 to parry attacks, it may degrade my weapon twice as fast but at least I have the freaking option to do it, especially against human enemies. And yea they do have a shield but it is ♥♥♥♥, it would have been nice to have some sort of parry button in the game at the very least, so it's skill based and still has drawbacks.  Another criticism I have so far is with the more unique zombies, like the toads, bombers, and goons. They certainly add variety but are kind of annoying to deal with at times. Like the goons for example, dodging their melee attacks is a bit weird, you think you are out of range of the hammer smash that they use, but it still knocks you off your feet, which if you get surrounded means you are boned. Bombers are just what they sound like, they explode when hit, but the developers put these guys in spots where you'll accidentally melee them by accident, which kills you instantly. As for toads they just shoot you from afar with toxic sludge, which isn't bad until you encounter more than one. I love a challenge as much as anyone else, but only as long as it's a fair one, and the challenge here with these types of enemies is ok...but it could've been done a bit better. The volatile for example was done fantastically, as it's an enemy that only appears at night, and it's best to run to the safehouse and evade them rather than fight them head on. That leaves room for you as the player to figure out how to deal with. The other 3 I mentioned just seem to be thrown in as an annoying obstacle rather than an enjoyable change of pace. Guns in the game are also something that I think could be improved on, while the fact that they do have a risk of drawing in more zombies to you when fired, they could have a few other interesting mechanics added in. Basically what happens is when you get the guns, they do not change at all even with a higher quality, not even damage. It would be nice if they had a few other stats or things added in, like attachments replacing upgrades, a wear mechanic where the gun overtime would get dirty and need to be cleaned or you risk it jamming on you in the middle of battle (ala Far Cry 2). Heck let us build a Silencer that wore down over time, so you only get like 10-15 shots out of it before it breaks and your gun makes noise again. Just a little more attention to the guns would have been nice, to make them really stand out from melee weapons. Overall the game does have some issues and room to expand on, but it's a solid ground work for an outstanding zombie sandbox game. If you thought Dead Island was meh...and was hoping for something more, or just love sandbox games and parkour, this is absolutely worth buying. _childDocuments_.review: dying light 1 is one of if not the most enthralling and impressionistic games of its time. it is a masterpiece; even now, 7 years after its initial release, 10 months after techland announced they would no longer provide updates - this game continues to be enjoyable for as long as you want it to be.disclaimer: this review is written from the perspective of someone who only recently began exploring the dying light franchise.perhaps the largest thing to criticize regarding dl1 is its rather lackluster story. at times, it feels as if story quests are bland and unimpactful. it seems every character, besides the main character himself, lacks any sort of development and, at times, personality. overall, the main story is entertaining and at times captivating and thrilling, but most of the time, you'll be completing tasks for a story that doesn't exactly reflect the ingenious nature of the game. if you truly care for story, buy the following DLC after you play dying light 1 which includes a brand new setting, new quests, new mechanics, and a new main story which i prefer against the main game. if you don't care, don't worry about it. the main story doesn't take that long to complete and the game allows you absolute freedom to run around dropkicking zombies while the city's population declines due to your neglect. the gameplay, associated mechanics, and physics is where dying light 1 shines. the gameplay is everything apocalyptic, zombie-type games lack, even now. you're not simply running around, picking up weapons, refining them, whatever - you're walking up to a zombie on the street and kneeing the ♥♥♥♥ out of them or grabbing their head and pushing them lightly to the side only to pull out w+shift+space+e. the parkour is never annoying, even early game when you have only the most basic of maneuvers under your belt - however, as you expand your parkour arsenal, so does your creativity in taking down opponents. it's fun, ridiculous, and looks shameful in co-op. my largest criticism is that, with the addition of the bozak horde DLC, it becomes extremely easy to become overpowered and lose any fear or apprehension in playing the game. sitting at your desk for 7 minutes as crane levitates atop a random telephone pole because you can't muster the courage to face the volatile 100 meters from your location and lose a ♥♥♥♥ load of survivor points is how dying light is supposed to be played. instead, you're able to easily generate insane weapons with maybe 10 minutes of commitment to bozak horde or google and develop some sort of clinical god complex. i more than anything recommend giving yourself the added challenge of hard or nightmare since in normal and story modes, the game wants you to win. in conclusion, not only is the game itself worth it especially on sale (which is very often), but so is the definitive edition which includes almost every DLC available. most are free, but the few that do cost money (bozak horde, prison heist [?], and ESPECIALLY the following) are worth every penny. the game alone is exceptionally charming and though an older game, constant support from devs has kept it refined and almost entirely bug-free. the parkour is fun, the DLCs add interesting weapons and cosmetics, and you will genuinely enjoy yourself while playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: Most of your natural average zombie games would invite you to go in guns blazing, and killing every zombie you see. Thats fine and all, but it doesn't give real thought to the horror aspect that these games could present. Enter Dying Light - A game that fuses:- True horror of the night and day creatures that roam the city- A Mirror's Edge style of movement and agility, where your nooks and crannys become your keyholes and your tunnel. And while it does pose the option to go in guns roaring and bullets spraying, Dying Light invites you away from that, giving you the knowledge that a single sound could draw them in. Keep your voice down, your guns lowered, and your gas pipe out, ladies and gents, because everyone is afraid of the night.....

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10, good game (+1 with EE: The Following)--- edited review ---(quick review update for game version 1.11.1, Linux tested, played multiplayer The Following addon)Good news. Game finally seems to be fixed and actually is playable on 680 GTX. I assume game is not up to par with Windows version but framerates are way better than on 1.5.0.Mouse re-binding WORKS. Even SIDE BUTTONS. Hear that, 4A Games (Metro: LL)?You still have interface designed for gamepads, but doing more complex actions like selecting arrow types for the bow etc. seems to work well.Fixed: + framerates + keybindingWorth of trying, especially if you grab the enchanced edition from the Steam sales. EE includes addon campaign The Following and several minor DLC's.--- old review below ---(review for game version 1.4.0, Windows playthrough, Linux tested)edit: Plus: + generic gameplay: movement and combat is fun + woo-effect: nice looking, lots of graphical detail + gore effects: good gore effects which are not ultra-overdone Minus: - lame boss fights, QTE WTF? - exploring is not rewarding (unless for Steam achievement) - game console syndrome (awkward UI, feels like non-PC game)     - grappling hook Dying Light is Dead Island re-animated... er... zombified? Worst parts of DI have been rotten out, so you now have actually playable game.Gameplay is heavily parkour-styled, so your character, Kyle Crane, will climb and jump around the city of Harran in search of cure research for the zombie virus. Harran is made up from two large areas Slums and Old Town, which are enough distinct to spark your EXPLORE!-fire again when you change the map. The game world is quite amazing and graphics developers have been doing marvelous job to add lots of details all around. Exploring the world will give you XP, but when you hit the level cap the rewards from exploring won't account much unless you play for Steam achievements. On the other hand, as there aren't any practical reason to explore more, two large map areas will suffice.Movement is fluid and usually you get intended action (grab a ledge, jump off from the wall) so you actually feel like you're doing parkour moves. If surface looks like it could be grapped or climbed, that's usually the case. Movement skill level also adds to the feeling that Kyle Crane physically learns more as he goes on. Having seen some games which kind of sucked (Mirror World *cough* *cough*) and some games where all surfaces are fair game (Ninja Gaiden), doing parkour in DL is simply fun. Of course some movement restrictions are in place as game world is finite, there are surfaces you can't grab and gameplay area is confined by magical invisible walls. Later on you get grappling hook, while it speeds up gameplay considerably, you lose most of the illusion of being parkour runner.Combat system is fairly simple. Neverthless it's entertaining enough for few hours just to bash, slash, maul and maim zombies with whatever weapon you get on your hands. Zombies react to physics, so they can tackled, toppled over fences or forced to climb on high places to even reach you (and then they get kick in the face). You're able to target generic body area so usually button mashing is a great combat tactic. There is unfortunate auto-targetting when doing some combat moves but I guess it's price to pay for playing console game. Story is kind of mixed bag, as side quests have more story than the main quest. Most of NPCs have at least somewhat interesting dialogue and voice acting & animations are ok, some overacting, but also some really excellent performances. Most of the default story line aspects living in the city full of undead are handled in way or another through side quests or collectibles. Unfortunately main quest includes some really dumb forced story events, bad boss seems to have constant grip from Crane's balls whatever Kyle tries to do. Kyle Crane voice acting shows him as quite strong-willed character, he's not on par with JC Denton but delivers his punch lines with real punch well enough (except every time when Kyle meets evil boss he puts whimp clothes on so he can receive good spanking). I have kind of insight after my playthrough that Techland can't make a game without horrible main story twists. Dead Island was such a dog puke, DL is bit better though as side quests will give some credibility for the story writer.Of course the zombie game aren't zombie game at all if there aren't any gibs! In DL zombie gibs are also finite, for example you can't cut only fingers off, then palm off, wrist off and so on, you only chop off whole hand from elbow. Gore effects are fairly well done and stay within reasonable limits so you can enjoy the effects and do not get WTFs every time. Gore with taste, I say! Also splatter effects on walls seems to correspond with weapon you're using.User Interface is designed for consoles, game has "hold this key and move mouse"-style weapon/item menu. This might work if you have gamepad or such, but I played this with keyboard and mouse. You can rebind the keys, but you need to limit yourself to only some items or juggle through awkward inventory if you want to use more items (especially elixirs). Also keybinding on Linux version is horrible and mouse recognizes only 3 buttons.Also final battle with the boss is just one facepalm moment you can't forget. So, you're ready with best weapons with best upgrades, holding boss' own gun to give it back one bullet at time and lots of invulnerability elixirs to gulp. You climb on the final ledge ready to pump this guy full of lead and then chop him to tiny grilled evil zombi-snack bits with your Fiery Sword of Death. Well, that's how it should go? Instead you're treated with Quick-Time Event (QTE) where one-handed man beats your zombi-killing hero to ground only using one hand and whole battle...  no, not battle... watching interactive movie... consist of pressing seven buttons in certain order. WTF? In fact, here's pro-tip for you: in this game you can discard your weapons before playing any main quests against boss as you can't never use them.Conclusion: despite some shortcomings this is quite fun game. Main story sucks but as one NPC said to Crane, blockbuster movies are all about happy endings and badly told stories. Here's story for 70€ (incl. Season Pass). As long you remember to turn your brain off for the main story quest, you should have fun. On the bright side, gameplay is fun and entertaining for one playthrough. Multiplayer might add some more hours, but I'll suggest you first try the game on single player or with newbie friends as best parts of the game experience is at the beginning of the game. I would say with more experienced story designer,  and adapting interface more for keyboard/mouse this could have been excellent gem.

_childDocuments_.review: For a game that focuses on climbing, the mechanics of the climbing in the game are utterly infuriating.For example, you get a grappling hook.  Cool!  Except that your character can grapple to surfaces that you cannot, then, grab onto.  The result is that your character will frequently fall to his death because you grappled up to a fatal height with nothing to save you.The worst part is that some of the worst surfaces for this are rocks!  That is, the same surface that, in the real world, is the subject of a massive industry and sport.  But in this game?  Nope!Another, the game doesn't let you look down quiiiite far enough.  So trying to sneak to an edge to get a view, you'll frequently step right over the edge.Finally, I wish I could say that the challenges you face are fun because the right set of skills and moves unlocks something incredible.  Rather, I find myself frequently cursing at this game because the climbing mechanics are so clumsy that my character dies multiple times in the attempt until I get JUST lucky enough to pull it off.  And they'll intentionally design challenges that involve this kind of tricky climbing over and over.

_childDocuments_.review: I have explored numerous genres, but there's one game that continues to stand out from the rest in terms of excitement and immersion - Dying Light. This open-world, action-adventure survival game from Techland truly delivers an unparalleled gaming experience that will leave you hooked from the moment you step into its dystopian world.Set in the fictional city of Harran, overrun by a deadly outbreak turning people into vicious zombies, Dying Light places you in the shoes of Kyle Crane, an undercover operative tasked with retrieving sensitive information amidst the chaos. From the get-go, the game's captivating narrative pulls you in, making you genuinely care about the characters and the fate of the city.What sets Dying Light apart is its innovative day-night cycle. During the day, you'll traverse the vast city, parkouring across rooftops, scavenging for supplies, and engaging in intense combat with various types of zombies. The free-running mechanics are fluid and exhilarating, offering a sense of freedom rarely seen in other games. The combat system is equally satisfying, with a wide array of weapons and melee techniques to dismember and obliterate the undead.However, it's when night falls that the game truly comes alive - or rather, becomes terrifying. The infected evolve, becoming faster, stronger, and deadlier predators. Nighttime is a constant battle for survival, where you must rely on stealth and cunning to avoid the relentless pursuit of Volatiles, the most fearsome of the undead. This dynamic day-night cycle adds a layer of tension and suspense, keeping you on the edge of your seat throughout the entire gameplay.The world of Dying Light is meticulously crafted, with attention to detail in every nook and cranny. The city's atmospheric design, complemented by hauntingly beautiful graphics, creates an immersive experience like no other. Whether you're admiring the stunning skyline from a high vantage point or navigating through dark, claustrophobic tunnels, the visual elements enhance the overall immersion.Beyond its breathtaking environment, Dying Light boasts a robust crafting system that enables players to create and customize weapons to suit their playstyle. From electrified machetes to flaming throwing stars, the possibilities are endless. The RPG-like skill tree further adds to the game's depth, allowing you to develop Crane's abilities and tailor your approach to the challenges that lie ahead.Moreover, Dying Light shines when it comes to cooperative gameplay. The seamless drop-in/drop-out co-op feature enables you to team up with friends or strangers for thrilling zombie-slaying adventures. Together, you can take on challenging missions, explore the vast world, and share the terror and joy of survival, fostering a sense of camaraderie that enriches the gaming experience.In conclusion, Dying Light is a masterpiece of a game that effortlessly blends heart-pounding action, gripping storytelling, and breathtaking visuals into a seamless package. The dynamic day-night cycle and parkour mechanics set it apart from other zombie survival games, creating an addictive and unforgettable adventure. Whether you're a fan of the genre or a newcomer to the world of zombies, Dying Light is an absolute must-play that will leave you craving for more undead-infested nights of excitement.

_childDocuments_.review: Dying Light is one of the most love-hate games out there for me. There is a lot of quality and a lot of jank. World design and attention to detail interweave with jankiness and baffling design decisions. It is both easy and pretty difficult at times. Story is engaging but full of tired tropes. Characters and their design shine, but endings are very underwhelming, especially in the base game. Free-roaming experience is great and some side quests are quite fun, but linear 'cinematic' story bits are nothing short of horrendous.Traversal and parkour are among the best out there but combat is unwieldy, especially raged combat. Firearms are both awkward and overpowered. Close combat is somehow both good and bad too - using melee weapons or fighting unarmed is meh at best but performing special moves like divekicking or ramming followed by stomping the heads is very visceral and geniunely fun.Even music is 50/50 - at times it sounds amateurish and experimental, at other times it's atmospheric and appropriate.As for the expansion - The Following - it changes things aroung. In stead of a tightly packed city if offers a wide open countryside. Parkour is not as prominent anymore but you  have a buggy now. At first driving it might feel underwhelming but after installing better parts and a couple of upgrades it does improve significantly and driving becomes actually fun.Actually it can be said for a lot of mechanics and even for the game as a whole. It all feels somewhat jarring at first but does get better and better the more you play it.My verdict would be this - if you're looking for a polished, well-balanced game with a tight feel to it - well, maybe this isn't one. But if you're looking for an immersive open-world freeform zombie-apocalypse survival experience then I'd say Dying Light actually delivers it. It also features a coop mode and a sort of versus mode but I cannot vouch for either as I haven't touched them at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me first start by stating the obvious: yes, this review is 4 years too late, but imagine this written at the time of release. Because at the time this game came out, the game industry was flooded with Zombie Survival Games and all of them were, well, . Ranging from Ubisoft failing to deliver to Unity asset flips, the zombie survival genre had something for everyone to be angry about.And so, naturally, I had my doubts about Dying Light. I initially saw it as another zombie survival game but with added parkour. Boy am I glad I was wrong.This game is not a zombie survival game. This game is a parkouring game with monsters to avoid and I think that is one of the best decisions made when it comes to this genre. Parkouring made travelling the map really enjoyable and risky at the same time. The map was large (especially for its time) with a lot of quests, items and other events. This meant that you could just ignore the story and jump around the various areas of the map for hours on end, discovering new secrets. It was an amazing experience.The zombies as well were done right: they posed a threat and there were several tweaks made to them to make the game feel unique. One of them was night mode, which is extremely dangerous and scary. This game made me more stressed out and scared than many other horror game just because of how scary the night was to survive.And multiplayer! Multiplayer worked seamlessly (except for when it loaded the wrong save file). It never dropped, never failed and it felt like you're really there playing with friends and trying to survive. I still haven't found any game that did multiplayer as well as this one.I mean, you can see a "thumbs up" logo next to my review, so you can imagine that means I recommend this game. However, this recommendation comes with a whole lot of BUTs.For example, night mode is never forced. This means you can play the entire game AND its DLC without spending a second in the night. There is 1 quest in the base game that requires you to be outside in the night (the flower one) but even that quest allows you to cheat by doing it in the evening instead of night. Yes, it gives double experience but I'll tell you in a bit why that's totally unnecessary. This means that, because there is no reason to be there during night, players automatically will avoid it altogether. It's a shame because this is the 1 thing this game had that was actually unique.The story is bad, from beginning to end. The story pases awkwardly at times and there is little to no character development. The main story feels emotionless and just something you have to go through. The characters are either a blank sheet with no opinion or they're acting like an asshat without reason. The character you play as has no balls whatsoever, meaning he never dares to speak his mind to people. This will make you hate your character and disagree with him a lot, which is never a good sign in terms of being immersed. Only at the very end of the story does he suddenly grow some balls by saying one of the most iconic lines in the game, but by then it's too late.People say the DLC fixed the lacking story of the base game, but I disagree. The DLC's story was - weird. It broke immersion even more by making it all about a religion which magic powers actually existed, meaning it could never take place in our universe. It was unnecessary and I remember nothing from it. The "choice" you get at the end feels incredibly forced to try and claim that the game has multiple endings "depending how you play" - but both endings in my opinion are just bad - the fact they tried to add a deeper meaning to it doesn't help either.The game is too easy. They give you the best gun in the entire game right at the start, and there's never a point where you're out of ammo or where all your weapons are either crappy or broken. After 10 minutes of playing you essentially become a God, murdering every kind of zombie with ease without any effort. The game - and DLC - never gets more difficult past this point, so you're basically set for life - this makes the game very unchallenging and like I said before, it breaks the purpose of Night mode.The game is too repetitive. All quests are the same besides some of the story quests and this becomes even more apparent in the DLC. The bigger map in the DLC looks awesome, but it takes hours to get anywhere just to execute the same quest over and over. And because weapons and money is not a real issue, the rewards you get from it aren't worth it either. Death is also not something to be worried about - it puts you right where you left off with all your weapons intact.And last but not least, the game is full of bugs, glitches and performance issues. I've clipped through the level many times, fell through the level or accidentally got myself stuck on a floor I wasn't supposed to go to. Even though loading the game again fixes it, I've never had it occur this much on any other game I've played. I didn't look for glitches, they just happened - and they're still unfixed. When you get to the quest in base game where you need to go to the light tower, walk through the rocks in the tunnel and you'll see what I mean.In terms of performance, the game actually runs pretty awesome! Especially DLC runs smooth as butter. BUT the roman area of the base game does not. It runs 10FPS on my GTX 1070 with SSD and 16GBs of RAM and i5 6th gen which just should not happen. It made that part of the game - which is a pretty big part of it - absolutely unenjoyable and even more of a grind.Keeping all of this in mind, there are some pretty major issues with the game that make it bad- objectively and subjectively. But the parkouring, especially combined with multiplayer, still makes it worth the money. It was fun and I hold the game dear in my heart, even through all of the flaws. And I guess that's more important than any technical flaw.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I say anything, please take everything that I say here as personal opinion only as I do respect that this game is well-made, I am merely expressing how it ultimately just wasn't for me.This game for me is kind of in a weird grey-spot for me, I found that as I was playing, I was neither entertained nor bored. It was pretty much just me going through the motions of the game. I think this largely has to do with how they handled the open world and the missions (along with other optional objectives). It's hard to describe but the best way I could say it made me feel was that the open-world of this game felt very hollow, sure there are supply drops, random events, and there is loot to be collected everywhere but because you are encouraged to keep moving and not stay in an area for an extended period of time unless required by an objective, it just means you blur past most of the environment. All of the missions that I have done so far as well have not felt particularly good, it feels like just a lot of moving from point A to point B. The thing is, I can tell that these problems are probably just the result of not being very engaged with the game, the game personally just hasn't given me much reason yet to be interested in it's story. I'm sure if I was more captivated by it's story that I'd probably love this game but unfortunately that just isn't the case.Overall, a good game that I just happened to not really care all too much about and wasn't for me, 5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: is a Teachable Perk from Michael Myers which gains you a token every time you hook a survivor other than your obsession... oh wait, wrong game.So apparently I owned 'Rust', and Dying Light released a Rust DLC along with a 'Complete your Collection Bundle' that let me buy Dying Light: Enhanced Edition for slightly cheaper due to the bundle discount (cause I already owned Rust) on my birthday.The main reason I bought the game was so I can finally dismiss the FOMO I had of not being able to redeem 'Dockets' on their site that I kept seeing on r/FreeGameFindings and so on (kinda like Borderlands Golden Keys). But then I thought I might as well play the game on co-op before the  Dying Light 2 launches, and it may become harder to find people to play the first game with. Since I didn't have anyone to play it with (who hadn't played it before), I went looking for someone from my region on the official Discord server. I found someone, they played with me for a week, got irritated by me, and blocked me on both platforms. A few days later, I found someone else and we started back from the beginning (at least most of the cutscenes/dialogue were skippable unlike Borderlands 2), and within a month we finished the base game and The Following. And during that, I also met Lynch's brother (with whom I finished Borderlands 2 the same month)When I first started playing the game, I was unaware of these 'Community Challenges', so during the time I first booted up the game, melee attacks were apparently buffed for a short time. I went home spamming kicks everywhere instead of upgrading my weapons... so once it ended, it came to bite me right in the ass. All my weapons were weak, so I had to struggle with learning crafting/maintaining/upgrading weapons properly in the middle of the storyline. Also right when I started playing the game (2 months after I bought it), the 'Platinum Edition'  was released with a bunch of DLC included for just a slightly higher price than what I bought the Enhanced Edition for. So I asked in the Discord server which ones were worth getting individually, cause I didn't plan to buy the base game again. In the end, I just bought  after hearing expert opinions from the server's elitists. These DLCs were cheap and gave me the blueprints necessary to craft good weapons without needing to grind for them, and in a game like this, all I want to do is have fun using the weapons on ragdoll zombies rather than completing challenges and earning them (which I'm not saying is a bad way to get them, but the DLCs do give you a slight pay-2-win advantage).My co-op buddy insisted on completing the main missions instead of lingering on thousands of different bloated side missions, and that did increase my overall fun of the game and made me like Jade, Brecken, and Rahim at least a little bit cause the overall story was quite bland and nothing to ride home about. The Slums and Old-Town portions of the game were the best parkour sandboxes I've experienced (way more intricate and connected compared to the oversimplified shapes and colors of Mirror's Edge's maps). The skill I leveled up the fastest was Agility for that reason alone, it's just really satisfying to run and freestyle throughout both of those maps. But after you get the grappling hook, the game feels a tad less balanced, cause now you don't need to find neat ways to climb up building cause instead you can just grapple to any surface and hope the dodgy ledge-grabbling registration doesn't fail you and make you fall to your death off of a 50-meter building that you tried to reach the terrace of in one-go. Especially when you're playing co-op and both of you are competing to do things as fast as possible, the existence of the grappling hook does decrease the overall enjoyment of parkour in the game.Fighting in the game are of 4 types:Of course, none of this would ever even concern you if you just crafted a Harran Ranger Bow with the DLC and kill all enemies with a few headshots silently.I didn't like this map as much, cause parkour is literally thrown out of the gate due to the lack of buildings and sheer size of the map, and hence became a game of driving a Borderlands buggy up the side of cliffs. Driving through the farms and mowing down Zombies at high speeds was fun of course, but served no real purpose in improving the gameplay of the base game. The story was a little bit more interesting, and just like the base game, the final mission couldn't be completed in co-op. As for Bozak Horde, I got some help from the Discord server again and they carried me through it. As for Hellraid, I didn't buy it. (will edit the review if I ever buy it in the future)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun. It's pretty, the gameplay is awesome, lots of skills to unlock, and coop is key to find good loot and survive. And this is where we have a game breaking flaw: if you join a game that's has a progression even *slightly* more advanced than yours, you will not gain a single XP. In several occasions, we played with a couple of friends, and since the one with the smallest progression wasn't hosting, he played several hours for NOTHING. We kept leveling up while he was staying weak. If anything, it should be THE EXACT OPPOSITE.Does the game warn you when join a session that will not give you a single xp? Nope! Is there any way to quickly know if it's going to be the case? Nope! The only way would be to fight enemies to make sure everyone got xp, otherwise switch host. You'd also better hope your friend whose the furthest behind has a good enough connection to even be a reliable host.So every time you want to start a game, you have to go into the trouble of first spend time evaluating who should host the game to make sure everyone can level up. This is one of the stupidest game design choice I have ever seen for a coop game.In the end, my friends gave up, and we never went very far in the game...

_childDocuments_.review: This first person free roaming zombie epic was often criticised for being a Dead Island imitator, but the truth is they simply used that formula and perfected it.The storyline is solid, the multiplayer is great and the execution is flawless.Free running around the fictitious city of Harran is seamless, leaping from roof to roof, climbing pylons and outrunning hordes of the undead is an exhilarating experience.The combat is unusual in that melee rarely works in first person but is the backbone of Dying Light and works perfectly. Add to that some great gunplay in a world where ammunition is highly limited and you have a great combat system.The enemies are highly variable each with strengths and weaknesses, the appearance of one can change your entire play style from your generic slow zombies to the fast Virals and the annoying Spitters.The difficulty balance is ideal, the amount to do outside of the main campaign is decent and the added dlc expands on an already vast experience.Graphically Dying Light is stunning, not only are the environments and character models great but it all looks so very smooth as you're hurtling through the streets. But that's nothing until you start to climb, at a height being able to see across the city during various weathers and daytimes the beauty is near flawless.Dying Light is a unique experience and I hope we see a sequel, in these uncertain days of video game developers however I question the likelihood.

_childDocuments_.review: Dying Light is a creative, enjoyable adventure bogged down by its own inconsistency.The gameplay starts very strong with an interesting story & engrossing mechanics rewarding exploration & practice. Crafting, Parkour, & Combat are all fun to try out & tinker with, leaving the player with plenty to do - only aided by levels to up & skills to unlock, let alone the variety of enemies, human & otherwise. Dying Light offers a great experience for all sorts of players - which even includes player-made content & even co-op / pvp modes.The game primarily concerns exploring the region of Harran while fighting off the infected with found & crafted weaponry, finding more loot, & growing your character's combat & parkour skills. From creating weapons with various effects (adding blades to cause bleeding, toxic chemicals to cause poisoning, flammable substances to cause foes to ignite, & more), to running supplies to survivors, to fighting off hostile humans, to mastering hand-to-hand combat, there's plenty of fun to be had. The story has some interesting moments, but much of the cast (player character included) is annoying & gets in the way of the fun by waxing philosophical or being overly dramatic leaving much of it to come across as #deep. That said, plot points & the locales are done quite well. The world feels lived in - side characters & their stories are believable & interesting. Environmental storytelling where you can find corpses & destroyed parts of the city communicate tragedies & even the occasional valiant struggle against the end.Unfortunately, the longer you play & familiarize yourself with the title, cracks & rust of the title become increasingly apparent. After a little experimentation & the initial novelty wears off, you'll realize that many of the mechanics are not explained - or worse - inconsistent. This area is not climbable, so instead of catching on to it, you fall to your death. An enemy will stunlock you into environmental hazards leading to unavoidable deaths. You enter a safe zone only to die from enemies outside. Bullets alternate seemingly at random between taking away slivers of health or the entire meter with one shot. Swimming downwards will lodge you into a wall, meaning you have no choice but to drown. Opening containers will cause a slow animation that cannot be cancelled - so if enemies round the corner, you're as good as dead.The game is definitely worth playing - especially on sale - but the aforementioned flip-flop mechanics hold the title back from being an excellent title. If you enjoyed the rooftop hopping from titles like Mirror's Edge & the earlier Assassin's Creed games, you'll feel right at home. If you liked the frantic combat from titles like Left 4 Dead or Vermintide, you'll enjoy most of the action here.

_childDocuments_.review: Very very weak. Trudging gameplay, fairly good environment for running across but no real incentive to do so. Endless tedious fetch quests and awful combat mechanics, no opportunities to use cunning or ingenuity as you make your way across town; just the same boring cycle of useless one-shot traps and repetitive, overly drawn out melee combat. Mind numbing crafting tries to give you purpose where this energy would have been better spent giving attention to the actual gameplay and the ways you can interact with the environment and zombies. I couldn't believe how dull the experience was - I've tried for 9 hours giving it every chance to show improvement and from what I've seen (and now read) - it's not coming. Your experiences in the first hour aren't that drastically different from those near the end, other than a grappling hook which is not enough to save the tedium of the whole affair. Even a love of zombies isn't nearly enough to make this worth anyone's time, at any price. And no, there isn't a good story to draw you in. Just a handful of character shells existing primarily to spew missions at you in the vain hope of convincing you you have a worthwhile place in this world. Deserves a medal for how spectacularly unexceptional and phenomenally boring it manages to be in all regards. Oh and fun bonus fact - it likes to conflict with SteamCloud and delete your save game (google it  - angry people everywhere even years after release), so switch off the cloud and/or backup your save every time before you quit or you're gonna have a bad time - though you'll be having one already.

_childDocuments_.review: If I had to sum this game up after playing the first third of the game its a combination of Farcry 4 and Dead Island. The nature of the game is very similar to Dead Island. This includes the music, the looting, the crafting, the interface, the skill system, the quest system, the elemental damage system,  and the melee combat. Many features in this game are very similar to Farcry in general. Unlike Dead Island there are much better physics and you wont get barracaded or trapped because of a pile of garbage or a roadside gaurd rail. I would recommend this game if you like those two games.Pros- Perfect performance on Nvidia if you have the latest driver- Combines the best aspects of two great titles and modernizes and improves them- First game that the skill system acctully impressed me- Night and day system is interesting- Environmental interaction is one of the bestCons- The parkour system is hard to learn at first.- Graney filter that makes the game look a bit disgusting.- A lot of the AI have guns but it's very hard to find them

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a big step-up from Dead Island. The side quests aren't all generic fetch quests and the main story is actually engaging. The combat system has been reworked and the game has you feeling helpless at the start which is a very good thing. I was positively surprised by how open the map is. The only invisible walls are the boundaries of the map and story-related locations. The parkour system is also fun and pretty intuitive to use. The use of skilltrees prevents the game from going stale and adds some really big changes/additions to how you play the game.If you liked Dead Island and/or Mirror's Edge, get it.The main story quest will net you around 10h of gameplay. I have done all of the sidequests and I'm currently sitting at around 35h. The game is fun enough that I might replay it in co-op though.There have been some CPU and RAM management issues but they have all been fixed with the 1.40 Patch resulting in a dramatic increase in framerate. Props to Techland.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game, incredibly scary when night falls the first few times.Then you start realizing how dumb the AI is, jump on a spike barrel and you'll kill infinite enemies as they walk up to you, lean on the spiky barrel, and let out a dying *sigh.* The combat's just not fun: enemies are obnoxiously tanky and just charge at you. PVP is the most annoying thing ever, turn it off immediately or you'll get spammed with an invasion every second which requires you to sprint 20 miles to smash a random gooey bubble while someone spams leap instakills until he gets lucky and hits you. Meanwhile you spam flares and lights to be equally annoying to them, chain stunning them the second a sliver of light touches them.The quests are so lame and there's zero motivation to do anything because progression sucks. They made an ambitious choice to have the first area you spawn in be the most frustrating and pointless so you can empathize with the NPCS living in this cramped apartment complex.Get it for the first few spooky days walking the streets then uninstall it once you stop being scared of the dark zombies at night.

_childDocuments_.review: This game?oooh it's thiiissss game....Yeah I kinda forgot about it untill recently when I revisited it and quite frankly I didn't want to say it BUT...The game lacks depth, is very glitchy/crash-y and it LOVES eating RAM for breakfast.I'll now explain this point by point, plain and simple;1.Before you say "But oh get a better pc?" I have 32 gb ram, and this game doesn't seem to stop eating more everytime I launch it! And it doesn't help you need a 2020 computer to run this seemingly 2016 looking game (That is underexaggerated by a longshot too!)2. My problem with the games depth is that once I played the story 2 times, I cannot find myself coming back to the game, it just doesn't work for me, AND DONT GET ME STARTED ON THE FAKE ASS DIFFICULTY SETTING, THE CHANGES ARE NON EXISTENT.3. The glitchiness is experienced in 3 spectrums in this game;a) Movement wise (For example grappling hook going through enemy and you going into enemy as they are swinging, killing you instantly)b) Combat wise, Enemy blocking MY attack during the period he shouldn't be able to??? Yeah just how I remember it back in the day! Don't even get me started on the AIs aim, you kill one of them and the rest suddenly amps up for 0% accuracy to 200% real f***ing fast LIKE ITS BS!c) Story wise, The missing depth isn't only seen in the story being quite lacking but ALSO in the placeholders/missing dialogue if you do something out of the ordinary. THIS CAN BE SEEN IN THE TUTORIAL, if you skip fast enough through it you can chase after rahim and see he just disappears... AGAIN DON'T GET ME STARTED ON HOW CRANE LOOKS IN THIRD PERSON DURING CUTSCENES. This man needs back correction FR FR!4. CrashesIt goes without saying I shouldn't be typing out glitches and Crashes here but rather go to support with them, but since support fails to fix some of the following I will name (haha funny pun get it??? The following...) since 3 years ago here is the list;I) Virals/Enemies crashing game by overextending and going into you with an animation, what I mean by this is when a viral goes into you, naturally this causes lag which crashes lower end (or even higher end in this case) PCs.II) Certain old town zombies crash game after leaving the game on your disk for quite some time then updating or simply reinstalling the game and not restarting your pc after the reinstall is done, You may think this is rare BUT ACTUALLY ITS NOT. I managed to replicate it today by simply reinstalling the game and not restarting my PC and loading up my save in the old town, run into survivor that needs help, see zombie in suit; GAME CRASHES!III) The Pit cutscene can crash your PC with lag, NO EXPLANATION NEEDED, OPTIMIZE THE DAMN NPCS TECHLAND ITS BEEN 4 YEARS SINCE WE ASKED FOR THIS.IV) Redeeming dockets too fast causes a minor "Skill issue" so as to say for the code and crashes your game, It is rare BUT IT HAPPENS.V) Explosions can loop themselves and cause a crash, If you time your propane tank next to a fuel drum correctly, you can technically create an infinite explosion that will crash your game! _childDocuments_.review: (Contain Spoilers) I don't need to praise this game's mechanics because everybody knows it's good, it's a mix between Far Cry and Mirror's Edge, i'd even say Assassin's Creed. The concept, mechanism and execution are very identical to Far Cry 3, although Dying Light does it better at some parts. The main villain Rais just seemed like a budget Vaas from Far Cry 3, and the section near the end of the game where Crane is hallucinating and is saved by Jade just seemed like a budget version of the 2nd hallucination scene from Far Cry 3. I don't even have to mention the final boss fight. There's a lot more but you got the idea. I think the main character Kyle Crane is very similar to SOMA's main character Simon Jarrett... they're both trying really hard to stay "human" in a post-apocalyptic world where helplessness, ambiguity and despair prevail. I loved this game for its gameplay, not for the story... I started skipping cutscenes at some point, it didn't get me hooked.

_childDocuments_.review: Boring, simplistic, hand-holding parkour, overpowered perks, stupid enemies and glass weapons leaves the game devoid of meaningful difficulty beyond sheer tedium or bad luck. Story is elementary school quality writing. Entire plot is advanced by the unfathomably stupid decisions of unlikable, unrelatable, and generally terrible characters that fail to change in any meaningful way except to die. The biggest issue is the backwards difficulty curve. Higher level perks alone make you as mobile as spiderman and generally impossible for zombies to defeat. The game starts with an ok difficulty and then quickly degrades into a very casual experience unless you're willing to ignore all the unbalanced perks and gear, but at that point you're not using half the game.There aren't even any survival mechanics aside from some extremely simplistic crafting and "don't die". The game is really an open-world melee arcade game disguised as something more difficult and serious.Edit: Wanted to add that it's impossible to co-op the last mission and boss fight. Furthermore, the boss fight is the absolute worst fight/mission I have ever experienced in gaming and should have just been cut from the product.

_childDocuments_.review: Dying Light was really a mixed bag for me. The parkour beats Mirror's Edge, the story is amazing, the gameplay and leveling are pretty fun, and the voice acting is great. However there are some things that really bothered me with the game and although they weren't big enough issues to make me downright give it a negative review they were still fairly blaring.1. Crane opens up things slower than a 90 year old woman: Despite being able to climb sheer walls, jump off 50 story buildings and survive, take down a hundred undead, and other phenomenal feats, Kyle Crane seems to take forever to open doors, chests, valves, switches often leading to you getting stun locked out of doing these things until you can somehow clear the endless horde of zombies surrounding you.2. Most of the infected types are just annoying or pointless: The bomber kills you in one hit and 100% of the time blends in so well with normal infected you can't distinguish it until you're dead. The developers also love to hide the bombers behind doors or hallways so that you get insta-killed the moment you walk through a door. The screamer does nothing and I honestly only encountered 2 of them in my entire playthrough leaving me wondering what the point of even including them was. The giant rebar goons felt more like environmental props than enemies because they are absolutely zero threat unless you're standing still, however they do have this annoying ability that seems to just knock you to the ground despite you being 20 feet away from their hit radius.3. Rocks: Rocks....Crane couldn't climb a rock even if his life depended on it which in most cases it does. I can't tell you how many times I died trying to grapple on a rock face or try to escape a volatile.4. Climbing down: Going up stuff is a breeze, but going down stuff will get you killed 90% of the time.Overall I would give this game a solid 8/10. It feels like the kinda game that Dead Island wishes it was. If you're looking at this game during a sale I would really recommend it, but anything higher than $25 dollars just wouldn't be worth ti to me.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is okay, but the story is incredibly stupid and cliche. Adding Parkour into the mix is actually a pretty fun and cool idea for a Zombie game.Basically you play as the dumbest mercenary ever hired to essentially do your first job of going into a zombie infested city that may also contain psychopaths. First 2 minutes you almost break both of your own legs in story, get someone killed, and lose your gun. Don't worry, your characters idiocy only gets ALOT worse later on and the innocent people, including children killed by him will pile up.OH and the main villain...he's as old hat as they get. The typical psychopath who tries to Alpha Male you by murdering his own henchmen infront of you just to emphasize that he's the bad guy and everyone is scared of him. There's no genuine reason nobody just shoot him in the back of the head, they just allow him to (and I kid you not,) take the guns out of their hands and mow them down himself! Are you kidding me!?Online is pretty dead so you're pretty much just gonna single player the game and have hordes of zombies that can not only take hits to the head like champs, but are just annoying. Night time is even worse as the Vampires with the Reaper Virus from Blade 2 are a female dog and a half to fight.It also really hurts this game that they seem to have ripped off Left 4 Dead by stealing several special infected, along with the Reaper Vampires from Blade 2.I'd say the game is probably...4/10. You really need a passion for Zombie games to want to play this but I wouldn't bother unless it's on sale. I'd just wait it out until Dying Light 2 comes out, you're not gonna miss anything important, assuming you played 1 Zombie game or seen 1 movie.

_childDocuments_.review: So I'm not that big of a fan of zombie games. But I was scrolling through steam to buy during a sale and stumbled across this. The premise of how the game world changes at day and night looked really appealing and so I decided to give it a try and MY GOD this is the best zombie game (after the last of us (part 1)) to have embraced us in the past decade. Techland put in a lot of love and care and it shows. The world is alive with the dead and somehow, the way it manages to stay engaging is just amazing. _childDocuments_.review: This was a great survival-horror experience.  I have completed the story to its fullest; here's my opinion.The graphics were a marvel if you have the system to run it at higher settings but the optimization quality here is sadly subpar as the "View Distance" slider was the only true catalyst for a better or worse framerate.  Even with the view distance set at just below the halfway mark, there would be a rare occurence of HORRENDOUS frame drops.  I have no idea why these occured as I have been in rooms with about 40 zombies in this game without an issue and has about 4 occasions where the game dipped to about 10fps during a grapple sequence.  Yes, 10fps.  Really took me out of the experience.  Besides these issues, the city is gorgeous.  The world is littered with cars, debris, gore, the undead, and still manages to look beautiful (especially in "Old Town," unlocked about halfway through the story) with its tall buildings  and the sense that this was once a thriving, elegant city.  The voice acting was pretty good all around but it had its weak moments with a couple of side characters.  And the sound.  The sound in this game is sure to immerse you as the undead growl from a distance, each melee connects with a satisfying crunch, the slight sound of wind as you parkour your way up rooftops and through safe zones, and quite frankly I enjoyed the sound immensely.  This is all backed up with a pretty good story.  I actually had a motivation to continue with the story and did very few side quests throughout my time with it.  I only really developed a slight connection with one character besides the protagonist but I wasn't fond of the villian.  There are a couple of boss fights.  They give you a good arena to battle and offer a good challenge, but one of them feels unfair when the enemy is able to throw axes THROUGH walls.  Luckily, it wasnt enough to kill me, but it was mildly infuriating that he was able to defy the laws of physics to damage me.  The conclusion to the game was more or less satisfying, as what you expected to be an epic boss battle turned out to be a quick time event.  As to avoid spoilers, thats all I have to say about that.  Now the gameplay.  This game has extremely addicting melee combat.  It does start off slow with the weak weapons and the whole take-8-hits-to-take-out-a-single-zombie-for-the-first-4-hours bit, but once you get going the game gives you a great sense of progression.  You'll start seeing zombies being dispatched more quickly, an abundance of arms flying to your left and right, and finish each fight off with a well-placed swing to the neck and watch the heads roll.  There's a variety of weapons, whether your busting heads into pieces with pipes or sledgehammers or simply decapitating the undead with a sickle or a machete.  The ragdoll physics are quite entertaining, too.  I found myself dropkicking a LOT of zombies off of rooftops because its just so enjoyable to watch them spin and distort themselves before inevitably landing headfirst into the concrete 50 feet below, leaving chunks of brain spewing all around them.  Another core element of gameplay is the parkour.  People have referred to this game as Mirror's Edge+ Dead Island, and for good reason.  Navigating the rooftops is a breeze and I've only had a few moments where I couldn't climb a wall I previously thought was possible to scale.  You can jump quite far, too.  I kept asking "Can I actually make that jump?"  Yes, I could make that jump.  The last major element to the gameplay is the day and night cycle.  During the day, the zombies are really just wandering the streets with no real goal in mind until you confront them.  Still, they can overwhelm you in numbers, especially when a viral is among their ranks.  A viral is just a fresh infected-you'll hear a human voice go "Please" or "Stop" as you bash their heads in.  It adds a layer of humanity to the game, and you almost feel bad for having to put them down.  It is a necessity to as virals run at a faster speed than even you and can climb buildings.  They also appear during the night.  The night is absolutely terrifying in my opinion.  I have the sense that every zombie is looking for me and only me.  The elite zombies, or Volatiles, are a higher mutation of the normal zombies and essentially cant be killed unless you have an ultraviolet flashlight on hand, which really only stuns them.  The night almost completely switches all of your gears to stealth.  You do not want to be caught in the line of sight of a Volatile or a Viral, and even a normal zombie is tougher during these hours.  Unless you have a mission, your best bet is to flip on that flashlight and navigate your way to the nearest safezone; most of which have to be liberated, so make sure you are close to one or you'll have an experience like me where I cleared a safe zone as the night began.  What a terror-ensuing experience.  This game is quite punishing, also.  This is a good thing as most modern games are an actual walk in the park.  I enjoyed its difficulty, but I do wish there was a slider.  The game takes away experience points for dying, which I felt was a little much especially when I died from those Exploders.  Almost every single exploder I've come across, undead with inflated guts that explode when they're close enough, has killed me.  I'll just be doing a story mission and open up a door and OH GOD ITS ONE OF THOSE RUN AWA-...You are Dead.  I felt they could have limited its power as it doesn't even take out zombies as often as they take me out.  Overall, this game is a great experience because of its great visuals, though with its problems, amazing sound design, and fluid, tense, and satisfying gameplay, though unfair at times.  Smaller breakdown -Graphics - 8/10  (+Beautiful,-Frame Drops)Story - 7/10 (+Pretty Interesting,-Not much connection with cast)Sound - 10/10 (+Immersive)Gameplay - 8.5/10 (+Satisfying and Brutal and Tense,-Unfair at times)In my opinion, Dying Light is an 8/10.Really Enjoyed it.

_childDocuments_.review: Why so many downboats? Sorry I looked deeper than the purdy grafix.I am loathe to resort to the most common accusation leveled at this game, but... Dying Light is basically Dead Island set in a city, with parkour elements.It tries its best to get away from the formula that Techland introduced in Dead Island, but it feels like much the same game, if we're being honest: Get fetch quests from a varied cast of NPCs that involve you running around to collect X or Y thing that they REALLY NEED RIGHT NOW. Spicing it up a bit is the change-up in your means of getting around the game world. Gone is DI's empty roads that you have to drive along to get to an obviously-contrived 'hot spot' for action; instead, you're put into a world full of buildings that are conveniently covered with perfectly spaced ledges and balconies that let you climb up and around them, a la Assassin's Creed.While we're on the subject: Player movement. My comparison to AC is not accidental; while the manner of movement is definitely quite fluid, it follows the formula the Creed games laid down, rather than the liquid flow of Mirror's Edge as many people were hoping for. This is not to say that the movement doesn't feel good -- it's a great feeling when you're able to chain together a bunch of breath-holding leaps across the empty space between buildings, hoping that you don't mistime your jump and fall short. But unfortunately, until the very end of leveling up your agility skill tree (more on that later), where you max out the speed at which your movement animations play out, you'll often find yourself losing the flow as your character takes a solid 5 seconds to clamber up a wall. Granted, he does much more than most of us can probably ever do in real life, but from a gameplay standpoint, it detracts a bit from the feel.If you've played Dead Island, sorry, but you will find that you fight EXACTLY the same way you did there. No real finesse is present in combat -- you mash the attack button and your character flails their hammer/pipe/wrench/other melee weapon of choice wildly. Now, landing hits is satisfying, especially what I'm guessing are 'critical' hits (haven't really figured it out yet) where there's a dramatic slowdown in the game as you watch your weapon smash into the enemy, and a weird little translucency pops up where you see their skeleton -- maybe showing that you're breaking bones? This isn't much more than a visual effect, though, as I haven't yet noticed being able to target particular parts of enemies' bodies and disabling them -- they either usually die before I can noticeably cripple them (for the baseline zombies), or I'm too busy trying not to get killed (with the "Volatiles", basically the super-zombies that can run and stuff).Enemy variety is utterly predictable, unfortunately. You've got your slow, inattentive, shambling zombies that make up the bulk of the enemies. This wouldn't be so bad were it not for the fact that the durability mechanic from DI returns -- so even against the most basic, harmless zombie, you might easily use up a good portion of your weapon's effectiveness. Then there's brutes (not sure what the in-game name is off the top of my head, it's only mentioned in passing by a few NPCs), a sort of 'miniboss' that tries to smash you with a chunk of rebar that leaves it with openings that are easily exploitable. Then, of course, at night, there are the volatiles, the 'running zombies' of the game that are touted as (and are actually) the real threat to your health. These chase you down and do far more damage than their shambling brethren.Now, how about the day/night cycle? The rough format of the game is about half an hour of (player's time) gameplay being daylight, and then a ten minute cycle of night. Daytime is the safest time for you to run around and collect supplies, accomplish missions, etc. Most enemies will be normal zombies, with a few brutes and gimmicky 'advanced' enemies present (among others: Virals, recently-turned zombies who still carry melee weapons and may throw them at you, and move a bit faster; environmental-suited zombies whose SCBAs can explode when hit; spitters, which launch corrosive goo at you that deals damage over time; and exploders (for some reason, I can not think of the name of these, even though the game clearly tells you and loading screens mention them), which are suicide zombies that explode). There will also occasionally be bandits, human enemies who are terrorizing normal survivors and/or stealing supplies before you can reach them, armed with melee weapons, throwing weapons and, in end-game, guns.Night is for the brave, or for those who can't reach safe havens in time. The aforementioned volatiles spawn, and even normal zombies will be a bit more aggressive. As a consolation, the game gives you double experience for actions, both in the agility and combat skilltrees, meaning that whether you're inadvertently caught out after dark or purposely trying to train up, you might sometimes be better suited staying out.Skills are... interesting. There's three skilltrees, based on movement, combat, and... I guess general perks would be the best description. The Agility tree gives you new movements to perform while parkouring (slide under obstacles while sprinting, vault over enemies, do certain attacks while sprinting, etc.), as well as giving a few core skills that are more or less essential as they increase your stamina and animation speeds. The Power tree gives you increased damage, more 'combat stamina' (a separate stamina bar that appears/is used while fighting), and some new moves to use against the infected for special effects (like stunning them, heavier attacks, etc.) The last tree, Survivor, is basically the progression marker of the game, as points for it only come from accomplishing missions or doing things like clearing out and activating safehouses. In it you'll find such skills as "Carry more gear", "buy stuff for cheaper", or "Repair weapons faster"; as well as a few gems like the ability to craft short-duration boosters from miscellaneous plants harvested from the world or rudimentary throwing stars for a distance attack. The grappling hook, easily the most-useful perk, is also near the end of the tree.Crafting is a fairly straightforward system, with you hoarding everything you can get your hands on and eventually gathering enough mats to put together whatever thing you're aiming for. For the most part, you'll probably want to save mats for weapon mods -- equipment that can be attached to weapons to increase their stats, add elemental effects (burning, shocking, etc.), and so forth. The appeal of this is a bit removed, though, as you know that weapons won't last forever, and only have a limited duration (even after repairing) before you lose both the weapon and the mod attached to it. Blueprints, both for weapon mods and for other random things to craft like equipment to use in combat (firecrackers to distract enemies, for example), are found both from certain Survivor skills, as well as occasionally as mission rewards.I don't seek to praise or criticize the story, voice acting, graphics, anything like that, as that is outside my realm of comfort. All I seek is to teach potential buyers about the gameplay. And as it stands: Unless you LOVED Dead Island, got every bit of DLC and whatever for it, etc., this game is unfortunately not worth 60 bucks. Wait for a sale. It's good, on its own merits, but it's just too barren of a world for a full-price purchase. I was hoping for a Day Z-esque feeling, almost, with having to scrounge supplies and literally do everything from feed myself to deciding whether to keep going without sleeping. Instead, your character can stay awake forever (if you so choose), food is a small health recovery item that is auto-used on pickup, and looting consists of shoving your backpack full of hundreds of boxes of nails and rolls of duct tape.

_childDocuments_.review: Dying Light Review: An Electrifying Blend of Horror and ParkourDying Light, developed by Techland and released in 2015, is a game that masterfully blends elements of survival horror, action, and parkour. Set in the fictional city of Harran, players are thrust into a chaotic world teeming with the undead. As Kyle Crane, an undercover operative, your mission is to infiltrate the city and recover a sensitive file, but what unfolds is a gripping tale of survival and moral ambiguity. Here’s a detailed review of what makes Dying Light a standout title.Atmosphere and SettingThe game’s setting is one of its strongest points. Harran is a city beautifully and hauntingly realized, with its Middle Eastern-inspired architecture juxtaposed against the urban decay of a post-apocalyptic scenario. The level of detail in the environment is impressive, from the graffiti on the walls to the dilapidated buildings. The game’s dynamic day-night cycle significantly impacts gameplay and atmosphere. During the day, players scavenge for supplies, craft weapons, and navigate relatively manageable zombie encounters. However, as night falls, the game transforms into a terrifying survival experience. The night brings out the Volatiles, highly aggressive and deadly zombies that can outrun and overpower the player, creating intense and thrilling chases.Gameplay MechanicsThe core gameplay of Dying Light revolves around its unique parkour system and visceral combat. The parkour mechanics are fluid and responsive, allowing players to climb, jump, and swing across the cityscape with ease. This mobility is not just a gimmick but a necessity, as it provides the primary means of avoiding the hordes of undead and reaching objectives.Combat in Dying Light is brutal and satisfying. The game offers a wide array of melee weapons, from makeshift clubs to electrified machetes, each with a distinct feel. The crafting system is robust, enabling players to modify weapons with various effects like fire or electricity, adding a strategic layer to the combat. Firearms are available but are scarce and attract more zombies due to the noise, encouraging players to engage in close combat and use stealth.Story and CharactersThe narrative in Dying Light is engaging, if somewhat predictable. Kyle Crane is a compelling protagonist, torn between his duty and the people he comes to care about in Harran. The supporting characters, including the determined and resourceful Jade Aldemir and the enigmatic antagonist Rais, add depth to the story. The moral choices presented to the player, while not groundbreaking, are handled well and impact the game’s ending.Multiplayer and ReplayabilityDying Light also shines in its multiplayer modes. The game supports a four-player cooperative mode, allowing friends to join forces in tackling missions and surviving the night. This co-op play enhances the experience, making it both more enjoyable and manageable. Additionally, the “Be the Zombie” mode offers a unique twist, letting players invade other games as a powerful Volatile, adding a competitive edge.The game’s replayability is bolstered by its extensive side quests, challenges, and collectibles. The side quests, in particular, are varied and often come with their own intriguing mini-stories and rewards, encouraging exploration and engagement beyond the main storyline.Visuals and SoundVisually, Dying Light holds up well. The game’s lighting and textures create an immersive atmosphere, especially during the tense nighttime sequences. The animations for both parkour and combat are fluid, contributing to the overall sense of realism.The sound design in Dying Light is another highlight. The eerie ambient noises, the unsettling groans of zombies, and the adrenaline-pumping music during chases all enhance the horror experience. Voice acting is generally strong, with notable performances that bring the characters to life.ConclusionDying Light is a remarkable game that successfully combines the thrill of parkour with the tension of survival horror. Its detailed world, fluid mechanics, and engaging story make it a must-play for fans of the genre. Despite a few narrative clichés and occasional technical issues, the game offers a rich and immersive experience that stands out in the crowded field of zombie games. With its compelling gameplay loop and high replay value, Dying Light remains a shining example of innovative game design.
