_childDocuments_.review: ~Disclaimer~: This is my first review. I enjoyed Dying Light so much that I believe it's worth writing about (owner of ~180 steam games)At first I didn't understand why people were giving Dying Light bad reviews. I had been playing the game with my girlfriend for a few days and was truly shocked at how much I enjoyed it... and I'm not even the kind of guy who enjoys zombie games.I believe the people who played this game did so after:-Playing the game solo and mainly doing the story quests.-Playing the game with high expectations of it holding their attention for a long, long time to come. The first is what I would have done if my girlfriend wasn't such a perfectionist. She enjoys playing games in their entirety, rather than just racing through to get to the end... which is what I would have done if I was playing alone. This game is admittedly less enjoyable if you play by yourself, which is why I suggest playing with ONE good friend. Any more than that and it can get a little hairy, since some people tend to wander rather than sticking as a tight unit. I can't stress this enough, though, please play with a friend. It's more than likely they'll find something that you overlooked entirely that could make you appreciate all the little things about Dying Light. The game started out as an exhilerating masterpiece. It had good graphics, and running along thin structures at incredible heights in first-person put me right on the edge of my seat. "Does he want me to jump? Is he serious?" I was asking myself during the tutorial. Sure, I knew it would be ~safe~ but it still felt risky. The parkour in this game feels a little more interactive than in something like Assassin's Creed, and navigating about is a bit more difficult when you can't cam all around your character to see what's available. The fighting is immersive and gorey. I don't suggest it for young children, but, hey, lets be honest, they're going to play it anyways. The first time I ever cleaved an enemy in half vertically I nearly jumped out of my seat and yelled, "Boo-yah!", which is saying something from somebody that uses the term 'Lol' whilst staring at the monitor like an inanimate stone statue. And the zombies... the zombies were unique enough that things didn't get boring (at first). Stronger and stronger enemies emerged throughout the game, but as your character developes into a savage, trained beast himself, it's hard to feel challenged. One of my favorite parts about this game was the skill trees. I can't tell you how many games I've played where the skill trees were so one-diminsional it was ridiculous. The right skills were obvious, and there was really no reason in having one included at all. In Dying Light, however, the skill trees have depth and meaning. There were only a small handful of skills that didn't seem entirely useful whilst the rest could completely change the way you ran across the city or took down zombies. Some of the choices were actually tough! "Do I want to be able to take down enemies from behind or break their legs as I skid by?" Suffice to say that the world is filled with far more crippled zombies. Easter Eggs.... this game is full of them. I won't give anything away because I know some people like to find them on their own, but... well... World 1-1 changed my life. I recommend this game to anybody and everybody. You will not be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, a friend of mine offered this game to me some months ago.Today another friend finally persuaded me to give it a try.After almost 4 hours of playing, I definitively can't recommand the game to anyone.Here are a few of the reasons :1) The game has too many "cheap" bad mechanic that are mixed with bugs that render the whole experience a pain more than any 'fun'. One exemple is the 'breakable' roofs. Having the same exact looking roofes reacting differently is not helping the player plans a travel. Thing get worse when the roof that 'break' under your feets don't let you 'fall' to the floor under, but teleport you 'over the street' (some 20m away) and drop you among a horde of zombies. And when that happen in the Tutorial, then something feel 'wrong'. Another is the spawn of zombies that appear in your back when you cleaned the whole place in a closed area. 2) Change in Mechanic for no reasons : You can jump and climb a lot of places, but suddenly in some 'quest area' you reach a point where you are unable to climb the exact same looking 'structures' just because "Boss Fight". Never a good thing to design some area that look like they are 'normal' but the normal game mechanic don't work there.3) Bug in quests : In 3 hours we did hit 3 bugs in quests, the 2 first made the quests impossible to validate, so we 'swallowed' it and cancelled the quests. The 3rd was a bit more problematic, as it was the Radio Boys. After the fight with the boss we found all the needed pieces to get to the 'top', only to find out the passage is bugged. No way to climb. And the only way to escape the whole building is to use the Grappling hook. As a lvl 2 Survivor player that's not an option, so the only way to 'escape' the bugged quest was to leave the online game or die...4) Bug with the zombies 'reactions' to distraction : Being forced in an area with 41 zombies, and supposed to use "distraction", I found out that the zombies who are "just too far from my position" don't react to distractions, so even if I throw firecrackers, the zombie near them don't react to the sound. The worse is that once the firecrackers finish to distract, the zombies do walk back to their starting position, defeating the whole  effort.5) Wanting to play with friend, mean you are forced to do the Tutorial and reach the first 'sleeping', never fun when you are forced into some 30+ minutes tutorial just to be "authorized" to play with friends online (they went as far as disabling the invite friend to game from Steam until the tutorial is 'finished'.)6) Last but not least, after the Radio Boys bug, my friend managed to get out of the building, but died outside from a fall. I just left the game, and tried to join back. The result was not exactly what we expected. As I ended up 'starting' in the Countryside area instead of joining his game (as if starting a new game myself), and he ended up losing his character progression fully, having his main character being fully reseted. That kinda made it for us. So all in all, after close to 4 hours of trial, the whole experience was not something of a 'fun time', but more of a sum of frustration. As much as I can enjoy a good parkour game, or a good 'survival' game, or even a 'messy hard to survive horde of zombies', the whole time passed in game did only leave a sour taste in my mouth and got me coming here to post this review.Edit :I know I only played 4 hours. But when hitting major game breaking bug while doingthe tutorial, and encountering bugs that were refered to the devs since January2015 and that are as severe as Reseting your whole Characters progressionto lvl 1 without any reason, and other such 'not fun situation', then the gamedeserve a Thumb Down.And yes, I tend to come and warn customers when a game is not worthto be bought. That's my right as a customer

_childDocuments_.review: I guess I should've researched more before pre-ordering, but I'm not satisfyed with my purchase.I'm going to seem overly critical but keep in mind we've had quite a few "zombie" games come out recently, so I'm going to be harsh or even heartless.Gameplay: 1/10Graphics: 3/10Story: 4/10When I looked at this game, I thought it was going to be a world-wide post-apocalypse zombie world where a few rag-tag bands of humans are trying to survive. This was especially the case when I saw a gameplay trailer where someone from Dying Light was playing, or at least commenting on gameplay, and the character ran by a building where a girl or woman was screaming. Single player character and single NPC, not many people around, and the city was worn and deserted. This was not the case. In fact, only one city in the entire world is plagued by undeath, and somehow the zombies are contained within just that one spot. I do like the thought of at least one nation's military being competent (since most "zombie" games, movies, and shows somehow depict them as so incompetent that shuffling zombies overwhelm them), but I don't like how it's just one tiny area. A virus can spread quickly, and they usually spread like wildfire due to them not being generally recognized and that they only really take place when someone dies. But away from the story.When I think of a zombie game, I think of something where each and every decision matters, where a single item or decision can mean the difference between life and death, or even barely surviving or surviving and prospering. I also think of zombie games as being replayable, but also having a very long first play. Games like Contagion are great, but their initial lifespans are very short, and replayability is very limited. So seeing how Dying Light is basically Far Cry gameplay with Dead Island inventory and gear (I really hate the fact that a solid metal pipe can somehow only hit zombies ~25 times and then break. Extremely stupid and destroys the game immersion) and zombies. I played enough of Far Cry in FC3 and FC4, and didn't take to Dead Island as mentioned in parenthesis. In short, gameplay is straightforward, bland, simplistic, and unrealistic. It's also extremely annoying how the "smart" zombies come at you in groups of six or more the very first time, and evading them is damn near impossible. You're shoved against them with no experience, no tutorials, no explanation, and no defense, while they are faster, can beat you in melee combat, and seem to have a crap ton more life than you.But the story had a fresh moment. Is the story great? No, not by a long shot. The story is as predictable as it is slow. You spend the vast majority of your time moving or dealing with zombies, and thus very little of your time is spent immersing yourself into what story this game has. I really thought this game was going to be great by how it started, with being mugged by three guys and being bitten immediately after, but was quickly disappointed within thirty minutes after the initial bite. Typical girl saves you, brings you to a small group of good guys fighting to survive, and you have to fight the bigger group of bad guys while fighting mindless zombies. How many times have we had that? Too many times.The only "good" zombie game we have is Minecraft. It has a very good replayability capability, and does actually have some survival focus to it, although the game is very easy. I've yet to find a good zombie game that is actually a survival game.Lastly, graphics. I don't have a low end system that can't handle games, but I don't have the absolute top of the line system either. I can run the Crysis games, multiple Eve: Online clients, and all of my other games on maximum settings without any issues. Yet I can't even run this game on lowest settings and hope to get 60 or better FPS. I know it's just out, but at least Far Cry 4 didn't lag with its graphical issues.I'll not be buying other games from Techland until after they have been released and I have seen a good portion of each game's gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: From the very moment I stepped into the chaotic world of Harran, I knew I was in for an unforgettable experience. "Dying Light" is not just a game; it's a testament to what survival horror can achieve when meticulously crafted by developers who truly understand and love the genre.The first thing that strikes you about "Dying Light" is its breathtakingly immersive environment. Harran is brought to life with stunning visuals and intricate details. Every alley, rooftop, and desolate street tells a story of its own, drawing you deeper into its post-apocalyptic embrace. The day-night cycle is a stroke of genius, transforming the cityscape from a sunlit playground to a terrifying nightmare with the setting sun.The parkour system is an absolute game-changer. Never before has traversal in a game felt so fluid and exhilarating. Running, jumping, and climbing across the rooftops of Harran is an adrenaline rush like no other. The freedom of movement empowers you to explore every nook and cranny, finding hidden treasures and escape routes that are crucial for survival.Combat in "Dying Light" is visceral and satisfying. The melee system is robust, offering a variety of weapons that can be customized to suit your playstyle. The thrill of bashing through hordes of zombies, each encounter fraught with danger, keeps you on the edge of your seat. And when night falls, the Volatiles emerge, transforming every skirmish into a desperate fight for survival. The tension is palpable, and the fear is real.The narrative of "Dying Light" is compelling, with well-developed characters and a plot that keeps you invested from start to finish. The voice acting and motion capture are top-notch, adding emotional depth to the storyline. Kyle Crane's journey is one of redemption and determination, making you root for him every step of the way.

_childDocuments_.review: Having finished this game for the third time already, I must say that it is an absolute gem among modern open-world games. Parkour isn't on the same level as mirror's edge is, but it is still on a decent level. Used coop only for "The Following" DLC and it was riveting. Not only it gave some sense that developers really wanted to somehow entertain players, but it was actually funny to crash dead-walkers for the points to win a challenge. Moreover, skill system in this game works like a charm, as it rewards you with necessary skills exactly at the moment you need them.Story itself is divided into 2 parts if you buy enhanced edition. In this game storyline won't appeal to everyone, but I fell in love with it as soon as I launched game. There are two endings in this game, one in the main game and one in the DLC. And I really regret seeing the one in the DLC. It completely ruined the whole view of the story and everything that I went through in game before and therefore please be aware that there are some mismatches in the "The Following" DLC.All in all, this game unquestionably was made with some love and thus everyone should at least once try it out.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: If you're having doubt if you should buy this game or not, stop hesitating and buy it! It's def worth it. I had some doubt buying this game, but then it was on sale and bought it anyway. I was looking for a zombie/survival game, but mostly zombie so this popped up. I had never imagined I would have so much fun with this game. Currently on 47 hours, but far from finished and far from getting bored of the game.If I knew I would have had so much fun, I'd buy this for full price anyways. When I started I had to get used to the 'freerunning' part, it was a bit different from what I normally play, so I was kinda afraid it would bother me throughout the game. But the opposite was true, it feels so good having a horde of zombies chasing you and you just jump up a building and make a fancy escape over the roofs! Since that moment I was in love with the running and jumping, it made me feel free. Also, there are some moments that will really tingle you IRL. I had my fair amount of sweaty hands, pumping heart and tickles in my stomach when I had to do a climbing mission. I know now, I do have a fear of heights. Also a thing I really like are the side missions, fun stuff! I caught myself not doing the main missions but having fun with all the side missions and just roaming around collecting stuff. There's just so much to do.Those missions are part of the story, which is great by itself by my opinion. I had a quick connection with the story and the character, every advancement made me curious about what's going to happen next, how is this going to end.Also, when you play this like I did in my holiday, ending up playing late at night, you will feel hunted! Like no ♥♥♥♥. When it's dark and you are consumed by the game, the zombies, sounds and music really pull you in the game and make you look over your shoulder when you're going to bed. Atleast, thats what it did for me :). The collecting and crafting part in the game are pretty okey. Weapon upgrades and their names are awesome!The boxes that needs to be lockpicked can feel like grinding sometimes tho, but didn't bother me too much. The lockpicking part was kinda fun tho, mostly because I wanted to open up as much police cars as I could and most of the time, they're guarded with loads of zombies. It was either a race against the clock or murder them all. Last but not least, the DLC which is actually almost a full campaign, named 'The following' is deff worth it. Already 6 hours in, and I'm far from dissappointed. Pretty big map, loads of missions and some fun new stuff. My advice is to buy both, the game and 'The Following' and I hope you have as much as fun as I did!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting since E3 2006 for Dead Island to come out, and I think Techland (With the help of WB Games) has finally made what I wanted for years now. Dead Island and Riptide are much improved upon in this game, but you can still feel how it's similar. Obviously the Zombie element, but conversations with NPCs are similar, although the voice-acting is streets ahead of anything they previously have done. That being said, it is Techland still, so you get the rare zombie clipping into a car or the semi-common falling/moving through an object you shouldn't have. I don't want to go deep into plot due to spoilers and I haven't gotten that far, but you start off by parachuting into the quarantine area to do work for the government. You don't choose from an aray of characters, you are always Kyle Crane - hardcore parkour master, though the parkouring is a bit difficult to get the grasp of at first.If you liked Dead Island a bit, but didn't care for characters, plot, or the voice-acting - that's all much better in Dying Light. The parkour is an extremely fresh feeling for the game and running for your life at night really does mess with you atleast the first time you do it. Even if you didn't like Dead Island or Riptide, you will probably like this game. The only thing that might stop you is if you hated the combat or the weapon system in those games. The zombies in this game feel much harder to kill, however; it will likely take you awhile to be able to one-shot any of them and running past them usually seems like the better option (unless you need to get somewhere for a mission, obviously.) Zombies aren't your only enemy in the game, as you have to fight some rude individuals as well, which was a difficult fight for me the first time it happened. The AI is very much improved from the previous Techland Zombie games as well and some zombies are hard to shake and are more diverse in their choices as compared to the Dead Island zombies.Better AI: CheckBetter Voiceacting: CheckBetter Plot: CheckPARKOUR!?: CHECKHARDCORE PARKOUR!!?: HARDCORE CHECK!!What Dead Island Should Have Been: CHECKMATE!!!You also don't need to have pre-ordered to get the zombie multiplayer portion of them game, so that's much better too!

_childDocuments_.review: Amazingly fun game, and includes lots of play time and side quests.Think of this game as a combination of Skyrim, Dead Island, and a little bit of Left 4 Dead, plus the freerunning of Assassin's Creed. Every good aspect of those games combines to form Dying Light. The open world of Skyrim and Dead Island, tons and tons of side quests like from Skyrim, some zombies (somewhat heavily) influenced by Dead Island and Left 4 Dead, and the perk system is also heavily influenced by Dead Island.One thing worth noting is that the free running--especially in the most important times--can be a little bit finicky. Just remember to hold down space when you're in mid-air and aim your crosshair at the ledge you are aiming for, and most of the time it will work well. The graphical fidelity in the enhanced edition is pretty well done, some materials and textures show off very well with the ambient occlusion, and most of the textures are very high resolution (picture quality). The after effects are done well for the most part, except for the annoying and obstructive camera blur resulting from walking inside a large pipeline or walking out of water.

_childDocuments_.review: Dying Light is a game that offers a lot of fun and variety in its gameplay, but also suffers from some flaws and frustrations. The game’s main strength is its parkour system, which lets you run, jump, climb, and slide across the rooftops and streets of Harran, a fictional Middle Eastern city. The movement is fluid and responsive, and the city is full of secrets and collectibles to discover. The game also features a day-night cycle, which changes the gameplay drastically. During the day, you can scavenge for resources, complete missions, and fight zombies with melee weapons and firearms. At night, however, the zombies become faster and more aggressive, and you have to rely on stealth and speed to survive. The game also has a dynamic weather system, which adds to the atmosphere and challenge.The game’s combat is satisfying and brutal, with a variety of weapons to craft and upgrade. You can use pipes, knives, bats, axes, swords, and more, and add elemental effects like fire, electricity, or poison. You can also use traps, explosives, and environmental hazards to kill zombies in creative ways. The game’s zombies are diverse and dangerous, with different types and behaviors. Some are slow and dumb, some are fast and agile, some are armored and tough, and some are special and deadly. The game also has human enemies, such as bandits and soldiers, who can use guns and tactics against you. The game’s difficulty is adjustable, and you can choose to play solo or co-op with up to three other players.The game’s main weakness is its story and characters, which are clichéd and uninteresting. The game’s protagonist, Kyle Crane, is a generic and bland hero, who works for a shady organization and gets involved in the conflict between the survivors and the warlord in Harran. The game’s plot is predictable and full of tropes, and the game’s dialogue is cheesy and poorly voiced. The game’s missions are also repetitive and tedious, with a lot of fetch quests, escort quests, and tower defense scenarios. The game’s ending is also disappointing and anticlimactic, and leaves many questions unanswered.The game’s technical performance is also problematic, with a lot of bugs, glitches, and crashes. The game’s graphics are decent, but not impressive, and the game’s optimization is poor, with frequent frame drops and stuttering. The game’s online features are also flawed, with a lot of connection issues, lag, and hackers. The game’s co-op mode is fun, but also limited, as you can only join or host games with friends or random players, and you can’t customize your game settings or preferences. The game’s competitive mode, called Be the Zombie, is also unbalanced and frustrating, as you can either play as a zombie or a human, and try to kill or survive the other team. The game’s DLCs are also mixed, with some adding new content and features, and some being overpriced and underwhelming.Overall, Dying Light is a game that has a lot of potential, but also a lot of flaws. The game’s parkour, combat, and co-op are fun and engaging, but the game’s story, characters, and technical performance are disappointing and frustrating. The game is worth playing if you enjoy zombie games and open world games, but don’t expect a masterpiece or a smooth experience. I would give the game a score of 7 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy drop in-and-out 4 player campaign done correctly, this is the game for you and your friends.Pros: -Coop works great, functions great.  None of that, "You are too far ahead, you can't play" Or "You're 3 levels higher, now your friend can't even deal damage to zombies!" (Borderlands and Dead Island)-Combat is fun, and looks amazing.  You hit a zombie in the shoulder, no more shoulder.  It's accurate as hell. (the damage)-The running and moving throughout the environment is just insanely fun.  You learn different areas of the town, your own personal routes, build momentum and really feel like a badass with the parkour system.Eh:-The skill system is done well, because to upgrade agility, you need to run around or use agility skills (which is a system I love)((same with power and surviver))  the reason I rank it in between, they could've added more skills for us, but being a console game, they're limited to "Only one attack button, so hold to do this attack, so now we can't give you multiple attack unlocks!"-The performance is shoddy.  It's playable for me, and I'm usually very picky.  On my rig I get 35-50 FPS with settings low. (still looks great though)-There is bugs, but we haven't seen anything game breaking.  Minor ♥♥♥♥ like rarely a zombie is inside the safezone, or glitches through a fence from knockback, but overall they're minor and nothing truely ruining the game.-Competitions are SUPER FUN, but they come up randomly (which is OK) but when you initiate it, because it's a console game and we have like 8 buttons to work with, you have to hit your medkit button, which consumes a medkit, FREEZES YOU IN PLACE, and anybody else in the game has 10 seconds to reply, then another 5 second countdown.  Meanwhile the world moves on, so enemies get closer to stealing the air drop, zombies get closer to you (they don't attack) and it just feels broke as hell that it freezes your character.Cons:-All in all, it's a console port.  The menus are smooth, but still rather annoyingly designed to be navigated by a controller, not a mouse.  So moving inventory is annoying.  Kind of on par with Skyrim, it just doesn't feel good at all and it takes way longer than it should.-I don't like games where you get no choice in things.  The main character starts to act more reasonable a few hours in, but it'd be a lot more fun if you could decide fates here and there.  It's hard to get into when your character goes from being a saint to the grim reaper then back to being a saint again.  Maybe more to come, overall I highly recommend the game, if you enjoyed Dead Island, Borderlands, Assassin's Creen, any game like that with friends, it's all the same blueprint.   Main story, side quests, upgrades, kill ♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: A good game ruined by awful missions.Let me first admit that I played the game for over 80 hours.  Thats a lot for a game I claim not to like. Imagine my dissapointment then when the missions completely nulified any buffing up I did.  For 2 of the missions all weapons were taken away and I was left to fight with ♥♥♥♥ weapons which broke almost immediately and had to be fixed constantly.  This was made worse in the second of these missions by the poor lighting and fog so that I was killed at least 10 times before I found anything to repair my weapon with.  the final mission is just a joke - spoiler: to kill the baddie press left, right, left, left, use.  A game of such complexity reduced to a simple memory game where you have to die for each clue.All weapons degrade after 40 or 50 hits to the extent that they do no damage, often in the middle of a fight, so you have to run away and fix them. _childDocuments_.review: Dying Light is an open world survival horror game with some RPG elements sprinkled throughout.The game is set in the fictional City-State of Harran, where an viral outbreak has caused the entire city to be quarantined and its up to you, Kyle Crane, to find a file that's lost in the city for your big pharma company and get paid. As the story develops you begin to get a bigger and better idea of what is actually going on.The story is okay, it's not groundbreaking by any means and I could even go as far as to say it's pretty forgettable, as well as a lot of the characters, save maybe Jade or Rahim. But this isn't the kind of game you'd play for the story. It's not a bad story but it's not great either. It's very middle ground.Gameplay and the open world is where the game still holds up to this day. The map isn't huge but its packed with things to do. From challenges, to side quests, to Quarantine Zones (which are like mini dungeons), random events. It's genuinely one of the funnest worlds to just simply run around in. There's so much to do and there's always something going on.The skill three is divided into 3-4 sections. I say 3-4 because you only get access to the 4th one after you've maxed out one of the other three. 1 - Survivor skills, you get these from doing quests and a bit of everything. These are your core stats. 2 - Agility Skills, this enhances your running and parkour as well as anything that requires a bit of deftness or precisions. 3 - Power Skills, these enhance your combat abilities when it comes to you vs zombies. I never unlocked the 4th tree despite doing nearly every side quest, which goes to show that there's some replayability if you want it and you'll be rewarded for it.The parkour and running and crafting system in the game is phenomenal, I'd highly recommend getting into the crafting for stuff like Speed Boosters and taking a few minutes to gather the ingredients because they can save you a lot of time in the long run, especially if you're running for a while, as there's no fast travel except from region to region.Couple of critiques however, are that sometimes the zombie spawning can be a little bad, it can really break your immersion when you clear a room, go to another room and on the way back there's a zombie in the room you cleared just 5 seconds ago. I also felt like at some points there was too much fluff in the main story. Like go to somewhere to get something but then you need to basically do 5-6 mini things inside the quest. Although realistic to an extent, it was just a bit annoying later in the game because you knew if you did a main story quest, you were committing at least 30 minutes to it nearly.Lastly, sometimes finding things in the game where a total pain. Like you're told to find someone's glasses and unless you know where to look, it'll take a solid search to find. Tiny little things like lighters and what not that you need to progress a quest are just hidden away and hard to find and it can be frustrating searching every nook and cranny to find a basic item which should be easy to find. Sometimes an NPC will be like "Oh, the -thing- is on the desk." And no it isn't. It's in the other room on a chest of drawers or on a counter, not a desk, then you start tweaking because it's not where he said it was and you wonder if the game's glitched. But nah its just in the other room on the 'not desk.'Also I'm not sure why if you quit the game in a safe house you don't spawn back in that same safe house when you reboot the game. Kind weird.Overall, Dying Light for me is a 7/10, I love Zombie games and this is definitely up there as one of the great of the 2010s. It's a good game if you're looking for a new zombie game or if you fancy some kind of open world horror.

_childDocuments_.review: Dying Light is a survival-horror video game played from a first-person perspective. The game is set in an open-world environment called Harran; initially, an area named the Slums can be freely explored, later adding a second area called Old Town.[1] Players traverse this urban environment, which is overrun by vicious zombies. There is an emphasis on parkour mechanics, which allow players to perform actions such as climbing ledges, leaping from edges, sliding, jumping between roofs and zip-lining.[2] A grappling hook allows players to climb up buildings and quickly travel between places.[3] As players explore the game's world, they can scavenge supplies and loot, which can be used to craft new weapons or sold to vendors. The player character can utilise his "survivor sense" to identify all nearby loot and use lock picks to open locked chests. Players can also complete various side missions by accepting tasks issued by the non-playable characters in the game's safe zones.[4] As players explore Harran, they can also pick up various collectibles such as notes and journals, and listen to voice mail recordings.[5]Dying Light contains a dynamic day–night cycle. During the day, players can set traps, save random survivors, and make their way to airdrops. The infected are slow, apathetic, and easily visible and they can be easily avoided.[6] Players can use environmental traps, such as spikes, electrified fences, and gas tanks, to kill the infected.[7][8] At night, the infected transform to become much more dangerous. Without daylight, the senses of the infected become more acute and accurate. They can also sprint after the player character, inflict more damage, and gain the ability to jump and climb buildings. In order for players to avoid contact, they need to use their "survivor sense" to locate and avoid the infected.[9] If the player character is spotted, they can use distractions and traps to reduce the number of infected. Players' main defence against the infected is ultraviolet light, which slows their movement.[10] At safehouses, players can adjust the time of day, skipping night altogether if the player does not feel ready.[4]The game features a variety of enemies, including the slow, low-level Biters, Bombers which explode when the player character gets too close, Virals which can run quickly, and dangerous Volatiles which only appear at night.[11] The majority of the game's combat utilises melee weapons, with more than 100 weapons and over 1000 weapon possibilities through crafting and customisation.[12] The melee weapons have a limited lifespan and will become degraded and broken if players use them in combat for a long time. Players can repair a weapon a limited number of times or dismantle it for parts. Crafting weapons requires crafting ingredients, such as gauze and metal parts, and a blueprint, which can be scavenged or purchased from a shop.[4] In the second half of the game, players can also use ranged firearms: two types of assault rifles and a variety of small firearms and shotguns. Firearms do not break or degrade, but ammunition is generally scarce.[4] Weapons are categorised into different rarities, which are indicated by a weapon's color.[11] Players can also utilise other items such as firecrackers, which distract enemies, and explosives like molotov cocktails, to aid combat.[4] In addition, parkour mechanics are integrated with combat.[13]The player character's combat efficiency is governed by his health, fitness and stamina. When players take damage, he will lose health, which can be replenished when Crane utilises a medkit or consumes food.[11] Fitness governs his free running endurance, while stamina focuses on how fast Crane becomes tired in combat.[14] A variety of actions in Dying Light can help players to earn experience points. Engaging in combat with enemies will help players to earn power points, while performing parkour movement can earn agility points. Completing missions, challenges, and quests will help players to earn survival points. As players earn experience, they can spend skill points to select new skills from a skill tree. Experience points are boosted when players explore at night, and while survival points are deducted if killed during the day, there is no such penalty at night.[4][8]The game features a four-player cooperative multiplayer mode which allows players to explore Harran and complete the campaign together.[15] Players can also complete cooperative challenges for experience, such as fighting to kill as many infected as possible and racing against each other to an airdrop.[16] A multiplayer feature included is a game mode known as "Be the Zombie" that allows the player to play as a particularly strong and fast infected mutant called the "Night Hunter" and invade other players' servers. The players who are playing as humans are tasked with destroying the infected nests and surviving attacks performed by the Night Hunter, while the Night Hunter's goal is to deplete the players' collective life pool and therefore prevent them from attacking the nests.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR -• Story: 4/10• Characters: 4/10• Gameplay: 10/10• Quality (glitches and bugs): 8/10• Graphics: 8/10• Sound: 9/10• Music: 7/10• Repetitiveness: 5/10• Replay Value: 5/10• Personal Enjoyment 10/10                                                               Total: 70/100A game that is a real mixture of flaws and strong points. It is a revolutionary "milestone" in the zombie genre and at the same time "just another zombie game".So, let's start with the story. When you put everything together after finishing the main game, it reveals itself as a cliché and forgettable story and you get a déjà vu perhaps from seeing many of the moments, done way too often in other games and movies. One thing it does right though is making you interested in what is about to happen next. If you relax and are not critical about everything as me, you'll have a good time with the story and will enjoy it, it is entertaining but nothing special when you look back at it after finishing the game.Most (not all) characters are very forgettable and you'll often find yourself feeling like you're talking to the same NPC from who knows when before. I don't know how many voice actors they used, but 1/4th of the male NPCs and 1/2 of the female ones sound almost identical. Although I personally grew to like a few of the characters that are mainly connected to the main story, but they still could use a bit more of a buildup and character development. Some die, some get to live and you never hear anything from them again, knowing almost nothing about them from the start to begin with. And now you wonder, what made the game the masterpiece of its genre that it is? The answer is the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ brilliant gameplay and the (imo) perfectly executed horror atmosphere.The parkour is hands down the best one in the first person category (Yes, I prefer it over Mirror's Edge by miles and have backup arguments behind that statement). It's seamless, rather fast but you still remember that you're a human and not some steroid overdosed anime character. It is satisfying and thrilling when combined with the zombie apocalypse theme, the chases and of course the iconic nights that Dying Light is mostly famed for. The first night in this game is an experience comparable to a first kiss, it's something you don't simply forget about and will carry on with you in the distant future as a strong memory, except the night is terrifying and you realize how f-cking much 300 meters are in this game when it is dark and you've forgotten how to turn on your flashlight. The atmosphere of the game nails it down as well. The realistic and creepy sounds, the not so special but really well fitting music, the overall theme of the world and let’s not forget the graphics, which are really good too and hold up really well to the today's AAA standards. It is not so colorful overall, as big chunk of the game takes place in the slums, but it has its colorful parts and of course the gory and creepy places like the tunnels, sewers and some of the bigger buildings. Aside of the horror, there's also coziness found in the safe zones, there’s almost always someone to talk to, you feel the warmth of the place and feel like home, you simply feel a relief. As I said it nails everything in this department of the game perfectly from my perspective. Important mention is also the co-op. Joining a friend is really easy, it's literally clicking a button. There's no catch to it, you simply can play the entire story with a friend, you watch the cut scenes together and hear the dialogue from the same perspective. The only reason I actually give points to replay value is because of the co-op, I can honestly play through it like 5 more times with (a) friend/s without getting bored even a little, there are many additions to playing online, like challenges, competitions and overall really fun goofing. Though, it might break some of the horror atmosphere as you'll get more comfortable when playing and talking with a friend.Another really good aspect of the game is the leveling system. It is divided to 3 categories (a 4th skill tree for car upgrades is added in the DLC The Following), Power, Agility and Survivor. Power is mostly for combat, agility obviously for agility (parkour moves and speed) and survivor for crafting and overall utility. You gain XP for each by doing different tasks, so if you prefer less fighting and more running, you'll get more agility points. Survivor XP is acquired from finishing quests and some challenges. It is overall an easy to use system that does its job well, there are almost no boring skills, some are less useful than others but still fun to play around with.The combat doesn't have much depth to it but it can be greatly satisfying at times, for example when slicing off a zombie's head or its whole body in half. Human enemies can be tough damage sponges at higher difficulties. The game starts off rather hard as of killing goes, but later on you become op when you acquire some of the guns (which might break immersion for some, but hey, higher difficulties are always an option), but they can attract zombies when shot. Bows on the other hand are balanced, they don’t deal a lot of damage unless you hit your enemy in the head and are hard to shoot accurately on mid and long distances. Overall in the end it’s a solid game based on gameplay but falls off with its story based on if you’re looking at it critically and noticing the lack of character development and the bunch of awkwardly acted moments, though the story is still interesting and draws you into wanting to know what happens next. For the sake of delivering the critical truth in this review I rate the game 70/100, but based on my own experience with the game, I can say it is one of my favorite games of all time, one of the best games in the zombie genre and the best one in the open world department. I strongly recommend it even on full price, though the game often goes on sale so you can look out for that too. (PS, buy the Enhanced Edition, you wont regret it)Good night, and good luck.

_childDocuments_.review: An AMAZING zombie game! The parkour is amazing, the weapons feel slick as F#*K! My only gripe is that firearms are just lacking than oomph that most shooters have. The limit of only being able to repair melee weapons a certain amount of times kinda sucks but it does encourage exploration which is fun due to the addictive and fluid movement. Nighttime is quite the challenge early on but once you get a little better at parkour, you discover that the AI isn't that clever and will lose sight of you easily. In 21 hours of playtime, I'm still yet to get a level 4 chase as the AI lose me at Level 3 even if I hunt for them!. Overall though, it's a great game with fantastic multiplayer implementation (yes, you can complete the story with your friends minus the first 2 missions)Get complete/definitive edition on sale9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Now then,Dying light.Long story short,I like it,it has content to keep you occupied for hours and it genuinely made me smile few times,that's an achievement.I'd recommend playing it blind if possible,though story isn't really the main selling point (though it's still good).Consider this a TL:DR as I'm about to dive deep into what I liked,disliked or felt aimed towards certain people...so,yeah,the good;  is hard at first and a bit easier later.Eventually,you'll be able to deal with most threats quickly and without much efford but you'll still be dead,shall you become careless. was truly major factor for me. In a zombe game,you either get it right or you simply don't make an enjoyable game.So,dying light gets it right,very right at that-the bladed weapons cut,cleave and shine,the blunt break bones and give satisfying sounds while doing so,everything inbetween gets the job done with its own little thing.So,aside your expected gear,you'll actually find yourself using your surroundings,your skills and even some dodging,especially on higher difficulty levels.Zombies can be,though not limited to,decapitated,stomped,dropkicked,impaled,cleaved in half,burnt,electrocuted,elbow slammed,knee slammed,poisoned,shot,tackled,grappled,kicked and anything inbetween.Creativity,messy creativity. are what you'd imagine they are,however in a better way.The normal biters do what you expect them to do.Dumb,able to kill in hordes,hardly a challenge if faced 1v1.The virals are recently infected runners,well,ex-runners that pose a bigger threat.While they are drawn to sound just as the other infected,they are way more agile,attack rapidly and can be devastating if met in packs.The other few zombie types I'll leave a mystery for the sake of amusement.Some are big,some bigger,third may or may not be less of a threat if you are agile,but fear not,there're certain things that are faster,stronger and way deadlier than you...my,but perhaps the light truly is the key to not dying against them.. hmm? is done good,though what I find better is the customization you're offered.There are many,many outfits locked behind story missions,difficulty,challenges and few scattered across the plains of "the Following".As for the skills you acquire,they all offer things you'll need,even more,want,that if you intend to survive.And what is more,once maxed,you'll unlock your legenday skill tree which will allow you to spend even more time playing...and that's always good,right? is truly worthy of mentioning.The game still receives these so called "content drops" which offer new gamemodes,items,outfits and challenges.That after considerable amout of time,mind you.Dying light's been out for quite a while,but there's still something new to see every now and then. is another thing that is either done right or done wrong.Here,every zone is unique,providing different ways to freerun your way away from the horrors of the night,each new area will truly feel new,full of new characters,new small details to notice and tones and tones of potential loot to pilfer. truly requires the "good night,good luck" line here because trust me,that being especially true for higher difficulty,the night can and will kill you,a lot,before you learn how to adapt to it.At night,the hunter becomes the hunted,and if you are truly (un)lucky,it may not be just the zombies,but an actual human,or,well,ex-human after you in an almost souls-like invasion (that,by the way,is entirely optional,you can disable it,if you prefer).I'd spoil more here,but why ruin the fun?Let's just say that what appears bad can quickly become worse...*volatile screetching*Lastly, is what makes this game different,and in my opinion,better than most other zombie games out there.It is kinda like mirror's edge.It is kinda sharp around the edges and you will kill yourself,sometimes in amusing manner while trying to escape a pursuit or something.However,it is fun,it gets the job done and leaping from the roof of a tower to a bunch of trashbags below hasn't been this fun since,well,since 2007ish when assassin's creed released. Here,I'll put stuff that I think depends entirely on your viewpoint both as a player and as a human.It depends on your taste,on your understanding and mostly,on your will to enjoy or hate the said features. is ok.Well,that's it....fine,fine,the story will be kinda what you expect it to be.Kyle Crane,that's you,is dropped in an quarantined zone filled with zombies.Naturally he gets bitten but saved by bunch of good people for which he'll have to run errands...expect there's a bit more here.Crane is an operative of the Global Relief Effords,known as GRE,tasked with locating an rogue operative of the said organization,Sulieman,who's in possession of a critical file that contains sensible data.At first,Crane will truly be a man without real heart.Just him,the job and the slight sense of guilt.However,stuff will change,stuff will happen,some moments will make you cry,others,feel like a badass.There will be few turns and overall,the story is what you'd expect.Not the next masterpiece of stories,but it's there and for what's worth,it's good enough.The characters are likeable and Crane is oddly relatable,being,well,that sarcastic bastard he is...I like him. and more specifically,how the weapon scaling and weapon durability works.Are you from the type of players that like to find the perfect blade,maybe the hammer to rule 'em all,then spend hours upgrading it,so that none can survive more than a few swings?Well,here weapons aren't that.You'll still reach a point in which you'll be able to do something like that but don't,I repeat,do not hold back.You found a legendary weapon?Use it,use it and enjoy your time because your survival rank will determine what weapons you find and trust me,if you save that OP weapon you crafted for later,it may be just as bad as a wooden plank you found on random rooftop.As for durability,every weapon will be repaired only certain number of times before breaking down completely.There is a way to give it repair slots back but honestly,unless it's your "endgame" scythe or something,don't bother.Or do?It's really up to you,for me,there's joy in trying out new weapons but hey,who am I to tell if one should stick to the past of continue with the future? more specifically,the invasions.They can be turned off,they can be set to appear only after said amount of nights and overall,they are entirely controlled by you.I found them enjoyable and an interesting distraction,though I'd suggest leaving it just that-a distraction,for every now and then.Now,playing the hunter is another thing but then again,that's up to you,not me.It's fun,but is it your kind of fun? also know as "1/3rd of the story missions" are basically you mostly in a gunfight with the bandit gang of certain enemy.It can be fun,but so can be hitting yourself in the wall.Gunfighting feels truly odd,at least for me.If you shoot accurately you'll feel that beautiful emotion again,seeing your enemy's head pop...however,most of the time in a gunfight you'll be outgunned and in higher difficulties,you'll die really,really fast.Moving is an option but the safer thing is to hug a wall...which isn't particularly appealing,at least for me.You know,scratch that,this "bad" point should be in the "up to the player" part of this review.

_childDocuments_.review: Dying Light, developed by Techland, is a first-person survival horror game set in a sprawling open-world infested with hordes of bloodthirsty zombies. With its dynamic day-night cycle, parkour mechanics, and intense combat, the game offers a captivating and immersive experience that will keep you on the edge of your seat.One of the standout features of Dying Light is its beautifully realized open-world environment. The city of Harran feels expansive and realistic, with its decaying buildings, narrow alleyways, and vast rooftops providing the perfect playground for your survival. The attention to detail is commendable, and the atmospheric lighting during different times of the day adds a sense of realism and tension to the gameplay.The parkour mechanics in Dying Light are a true highlight, allowing you to traverse the city with agility and speed. Scaling buildings, leaping between rooftops, and using zip lines to navigate the urban landscape feels incredibly fluid and satisfying. It not only enhances the exploration aspect but also offers a strategic advantage when facing the relentless zombie hordes.Speaking of combat, Dying Light delivers an intense and visceral experience. The melee combat system is robust, offering a wide array of weapons to choose from, each with its own unique feel and effectiveness. The game emphasizes the importance of timing, positioning, and resource management, creating thrilling encounters with the undead. Additionally, the ability to craft and modify weapons adds depth to the gameplay, allowing for creative and devastating ways to dispatch enemies.The day-night cycle is a standout feature that sets Dying Light apart from other zombie games. During the day, you'll encounter more manageable and predictable foes, providing opportunities for scavenging and completing missions. However, as night falls, the game takes a chilling turn. The infected become stronger, faster, and more aggressive, and the tension rises exponentially. It's during these nocturnal hours that you'll truly feel the adrenaline rush as you navigate the city, desperately trying to stay alive. The dynamic nature of the day-night cycle adds a layer of unpredictability and keeps the gameplay fresh and engaging.While Dying Light offers a strong single-player experience, it also provides a cooperative multiplayer mode that allows you to team up with friends for even more zombie-slaying fun. The cooperative mode introduces new dynamics and strategies, and the shared experience of surviving the apocalypse together adds an extra layer of enjoyment to the game.Despite its strengths, Dying Light does have a few minor drawbacks. The story, while engaging, can feel a bit predictable and clichéd at times. Additionally, some of the side missions can be repetitive, and the occasional technical glitch or AI inconsistency can briefly interrupt the immersion.In conclusion, Dying Light delivers an adrenaline-pumping zombie survival experience that excels in its open-world design, parkour mechanics, and intense combat. With its atmospheric setting, day-night cycle, and cooperative multiplayer, the game offers hours of thrilling gameplay that will satisfy fans of the genre. While it may have a few minor flaws, its strengths far outweigh them, making Dying Light a must-play for anyone seeking an immersive and exhilarating journey through a zombie-infested world.If you like the review and it encourage you to buy this game, I will be very happy if you give it an Award. Thanks!

The Forest: I prefer the cannibal A.I. since they are pretty advanced and very fun to duel with. Also funny. Spear is pretty useless. Bow and arrow is King. Haven't found crossbow. Club does massive dmg + farther reach. but the Modern axe is more fun to use and you can combo with it, though requires skill. There is a bug where you can't light your weapon on fire. Slingshot is versatile. You have to be a very good aimer to use the Molotov unlike in this game. Inventory is easier as its displayed on a tarp. Explosives are a good option albeit burdensome to create. Dying Light: Wide variety of enemies including other humans. The ones that spit poison are freakishly annoying. Dying can be infuriating. Story is just as good as the gameplay. Inventory is too cumbersome, and you will accumulate weapons and blueprints where you will have to keep scrolling just to see the item you want. You will start out with wooden plans, and then evolve into hammers, wrenches, baseball bats, and be able to get better weapons as your rank increases. There are some rarer parts and inevitably you will end up with excess of certain common items and be limited to the limited reagent for some blueprint. I guess im ok with that. I feel that electric arrows should do normal arrow dmg as well as electric dmg instead of just disappearing into the ether. Would make killing goons and such more fun. Also the range of some arrows is disappointing as they will again disappear and do no damage. As for the throwing knives, I don't really care that you can't see where they hit after you've thrown them; but for the arrows I have high expectations, since that is an area where The Forest excels in. Again I love the situational music. They did this game right. Can't wait for the next rendering.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics	9A pretty game to look at for sure, though it suffers with some animations on the part of NPC humans, particularly when they are speaking. The environment is very well put together, and the general ambience of the game, especially at night, is fantastic.Gameplay	10I have never played a game that offered such satisfying zombie smashing. On top of that, you have a variety of ways to dispatch of the zombies. The sound design is incredibly well done (save for the voice-acting, it is average at best), every smack of a weapon against a zombie is satisfying and has some weight behind it. Also notable is the parkour system in place in the game; It is extremely well executed, and gives an incredible sense of freedom to go where you want, and do what you want. The weapon system is reminiscent of Dead Island's, though gathering parts feels much more intuitive now. Missions feel varied enough that they don't come across as just "fetching" quests. They even serve to push you out of your comfort zone and into the dreaded night.Story	7A zombie game that calls zombies exactly that, for once. The story in Dying Light isn't anything spectacular, but it has enough interesting moments to keep you moving forward, wanting to know how things will turn out. Again though, this is a zombie game, so don't be expecting Shakespeare.Multiplayer	9Easily join up with four friends for some co-op fun which allows you to play the entire game together, main quests and all. Though frustrating at times that you must have EVERY player in the vicinity to start a mission, or even have dialogue with an NPC, the frustration is quickly forgotten as you get back to bashing zombie's heads in. Occasional co-op competitive events show up as you travel around the map, challenging you to beat your friends at killing the most zombies, finding the most loot, saving survivors, or racing to an objective. An absolutely hilarious blast of a game to play with your buddies.Note: I have not yet played "Be the Zombie" mode (5-players allowed, instead of just 4), so I will update this review when I have the chance to try it out.Replayability	8I thought that perhaps I would get tired of bashing zombie's skulls in, and jumping around the world. I have found myself to be pleasantly wrong in both regards. Dying Light executes these two mechanics so fantastically that I find myself constantly drawn to it, especially when friends are able to hop in-game with me. Though I can see the missions becoming burdensome and tiring after having done them a few times.Overall9.1/10Of all the zombie games out there, Dying Light is number one on my recommended list. A well polished, extremely fun game by yourself, throw some friends into the mix and you have a winner. If you enjoy zombie games in the slightest, or even if you don't, give this game a whirl. Thanks to Dying Light, I find myself bummed out when I play other games that I cannot jump and climb so freely. You know something has been executed well when you find yourself wishing it was in every other game you played.

_childDocuments_.review: This game taught me many things about real life:Episode 1: I was locked out of my house last week, and I realized I had a paper clip and pocket knife in my car. I figured, "this will be a cinch" I started to pick my lock: click, click. Sh%#. Paper clip broke. Yep, lock is ruined. *Hops wall, grabs key from under mat, and enters through back door* Wife: "Why the hell did you come in from the back?" Me: "I locked myself out" Wife: "Why didn't you just knock?" Me: "I've been trying to learn parkour." *parkour into back room* Pursuit evaded.Episode 2: I have to take the trash out, but it's getting dark outside. Wife: "the trash is still overflowing" Me: "True, but its almost dark. I don't think I can risk it." Wife: "Risk what?" Me: *looks at couch; chooses to wait until morning* I wake up. Wife: "now that it's light out, how about that trash?" Me: "HELL YEAH. DOING IT!" *Grabs machete out of closet; ties up trash bag* Wife: "what the hell is with the sword?" Me: *parkour into front yard* Trash delivered. I feel stronger. Episode 3: It's night time. Wierd noise on roof. Feeling unusually brave, I grab my new teddy bear (aka my machete) from under my pillow. Using my parkour skills I climb up my aluminum rain gutter. Rain gutter buckles under my weight and I crash to the ground. Startled, the cat on my roof scampers away. Mission accomplished. Episode 4: My wife and I make dinner. I am cutting vegetables with a Hardened Beef Cleaver. I go to the bedroom and grab my Machete. I lay the Machete and Beef Cleaver on the counter. Me: "Which of these is better?" Wife: "For what? Why have you been acting so wierd lately?" Me: "Agreed." *Chops carrots with machete* 11/10 Would take this course again in the Spring.The Following taught me even more about real life: Episode 5: Been training for awhile now with Teddy. Let’s just say we eat a lot of squirrel for dinner. Came across a Javelina unexpectedly while trying to fix our stupid water pump (living in SW USA) and realized my skills weren’t exactly “legendary.” Teddy failed. I failed. I ran. Wife understood, but I could see the disappointment in her eyes. So, naturally, I think, “F-THIS” *Jumps through kitchen window; hoofs it to the tool shed* *Sets Teddy on the workbench, grabs tazer, duct tapes tazer to Teddy, wraps metal wiring from tazer around blade, activate tazer, Teddy lights up like a F’in Christmas tree*YEAH! *Heads back to water pump* Javelina is there, staring me in the GD face like a drunken frat kid. “OH, I’LL COME AT YOU BRO” *Charges Javelina, Teddy sparks like a damn firework*Wake up 3 days later in the hospital with a giant gash in my side. I see the blurry outline of my wife, “Did I get him?” Wife: “No, he got away; the cops took your weapon.” I pass out again. Episode 6: After some time at the hospital, I come home, wrap some alcoholic gauze around my arm like thirty times, and I’m back to full strength.  Wife: “Did you hurt your arm too?” *Looks at gauzed up hand* Me: “I need more firepower.” *Looks at wife* Me: “Honey, do you trust me?” Wife: “No! I absolutely do not trust your judgment right now. You just nearly died!” Me: “Exactly! We need wheels.” *Grabs car keys, limps out the door* Me: “I’m gonna need more gauze.” Episode 7:  I return home with PigF$&%er, my sweet new buggy. I honk the horn in the driveway. I stand brandishing my recovered Teddy in all his glory and as my wife opens the door, I activate taze mode. Teddy lights up like a damn sword with a tazer attached to it. Wife: *closes door* I realize she’ll only love me again if I kill this swine. *Buggy screeches out into the night* Experience Doubled.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sorry if this review is not that great, I just want to jump right back in and play more.I've finished the game and I'm now playing the Newgame+. There are more DLC planned including a new huge area bigger than all of harran, and dune buggies and a whole crapload of other awesome stuff, but until then, here's my review of the vanilla game.The game looks very good, but for many of us PC gamers, the texture pop-ins and the medium res textures can be of annoyance. However, this is one of those games where graphics are secondary to the gameplay. Not to say the graphics are bad at all, they aren't, but it leaves allot of Titan cards bored. The graphics and overall aesthetic of the game is atmospheric and does work, but leaves me wanting higher resolution textures and a MUCH better option menu.I am a huge audiophile, I only accept the very best sound, no distortion, no jaggy treble, and this game is definitely to my satisfaction. The sound is all there, the footsteps, the grass, the sound of your weapon swinging and the soft sound of the rain is all jaw dropping in how well recorded/generated it is. Sound is not too important for allot of gamers, but if you're like me and you want the best of the best in your ears, pick this game up. Sounds great on my Sennheiser HD518's.The gameplay is a huge strong point of the game. The combat flows extremely well, the parkour flows even better, and chaining them both together will give you a bloody amazing gameplay experience. The gameplay takes the very best parts from Dead Island, and Assassins Creed/Mirrors Edge and slams those games and shows them how it's done. This game does the tower climbing better than Far Cry 3, Combat better than Dead Island, and Parkour better than Assassins Creed. I can't even begin to explain how satisfying the combat is, but just imagine running up a wall, jumping off, and in mid-air, dropkicking a zombie into a pit of spikes, or throwing a gas tank next to a big zombie and watch it smash the tank and explode. Completed this game, and I am not done at all.Meh. Nothing new here. The story was alright in the first half of the game, but the drug sequence, and the "CRAAAAAAAANE" literally made me cringe. They also gave us very few oppurtunities to connect with the characters that died, and the emotional way Crane bursts out just seems ridiculous given how he barely knew the people who just died, whilst he shoots looters in the face.Little things:Replayable? YesIs it scary at night? Yes, when you start off.Does it run well? Not even on my GTX 970, but that doesnt make the game less enjoyable.Are the devs still active? Yes, they seem to be very active and they engage with their fans very frequently.Eh. There's your review. I'm just gonna submit this and play more. More stuff is coming, the game is fun, it's on sale at the time of writing this review, and it's probably my GOTY.

_childDocuments_.review: "Dying Light" stands as a true masterpiece among zombie survival games. From the moment you step into Harran's post-apocalyptic world, you're in for an extraordinary gaming journey that seamlessly combines captivating storytelling, stunning graphics, immersive gameplay, and memorable characters. "Dying Light" offers an exceptional narrative. As protagonist Kyle Crane, you'll navigate a world overrun by infected, delivering a gripping and emotionally charged experience. The depth of character development and your in-game choices add layers of complexity to the storyline, making it an engaging rollercoaster from start to finish. What sets "Dying Light" apart is its dynamic and engaging gameplay. The parkour mechanics allow you to move gracefully across Harran's rooftops, making each movement feel like an acrobatic feat. The day-night cycle adds tension, with zombies becoming deadlier after dark. A variety of weapons and creative crafting options keep combat fresh and thrilling. Visually, "Dying Light" is a work of art. Harran's open world boasts amazing design and rich, atmospheric ambiance. Whether you're enjoying stunning sunsets or exploring eerie darkness, the graphics showcase the power of modern gaming technology. The characters in "Dying Light" are more than just NPCs; they become companions on your harrowing journey. Protagonist Kyle Crane is a likable and relatable character, and his interactions with other survivors are heartwarming and memorable. These characters add depth to the game, making you care about their fates as much as your own. "The Following" DLC takes the experience to another level. It offers an expansive new area, fresh challenges, and an intriguing storyline that enriches the "Dying Light" universe.Make sure to play the DLC; it's even better than the base game!!! "Dying Light" isn't just the best zombie game; it's a triumph in the gaming world. Its exceptional storytelling, immersive gameplay, stunning graphics, and endearing characters make it a must-play. Whether you're a survival genre enthusiast or simply appreciate top-tier gaming experiences, "Dying Light" exemplifies what video games can achieve. With "The Following" DLC, it becomes an even more complete and satisfying package.In conclusion, "Dying Light" raises the bar for zombie survival games, and its impact on the gaming community will endure. Playing with friends enhances the experience. I'll cherish this game forever; it's one of my all-time favourites. Don't miss the chance to immerse yourself in this outstanding adventure.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Dying light is the most fun i've had with a classic "zombie game"!It takes some features from dead island, for those who played it, but it's a lot better.It's best features are the parkour system, the day night cycle and of course the zombies!At the start of the game you feel really powerless even to the weakest zombie (biters), weapons don't do much and they break a lot requiring metal parts to repair them; running from zombies or volatiles in the night is almost pointless because they are faster and have more stamina than you.All of this changes while progressing the game, unlocking more abilities and crafting more powerful weapons, even guns come into play, all of this will make you a perfect zombie slayer machine!The story is not very interesting, it follows most of the cliches that zombies stories have, but it's not very important because there is the expansion pack "The Following" that will really deliver!The Following adds a new map with new gameplay mechanics and it's a direct continuation of the story.The biggest thing is the implementation of a drivable buggy, this changes the focus from the parkour in the city to driving the buggy through farms in the countryside.The sidequests are interesting and well made, every different from the other, some involving characters from the main campaign.The story is where the expansion really shines, it is at first misterious and then, when you think you know everything, it gets you whit an incredible ending! ---------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------

_childDocuments_.review: I've played various free running games, and many zombies games, including Dead Island and Riptide, so this game should be home free, right? Well, not quite.The game is gorgeous, there's no denying it. It's quite a step up from Dead Island, and DI was already quite serviceable. The voice acting is much better, and there seem to be fewer characters with endlessly repeating lines (and where they occur, they're less ridiculous).The writing is a bit of a mixed bag -- there are some awesome, emotionally resonating bits (I liked the bit with the wizard, and the Kid who would be a Detective), and while there are a number of side quests you wouldn't realistically risk your life for, there are few where you'd like to punch the quest giver in the face for even suggesting it.Unfortunately, the great let-down in the writing happens in the main plot, which is full of deaths of people who we didn't really get to know and like, or who are outright unlikeable, precluding any emotional response. To add insult to injury, one death scene takes essentially 10 minutes of exposition; that's worse than most operas! While the story told by the main plot generally makes sense and provides believable motivation for the protagonists, it falls through every time the plot centers on the main antagonist. It's not just that he is one of the weaker characters in the game in terms of writing; where usually, you have a choice of whether you want to avoid confrontation, used ranged weapons, or jump right into the fight, turning points with the antagonist force you into a style that may be quite different from you do in the rest of the game (and from what you bought skills for): Those turning points always seem to drop you in a pit crawling with zombies after taking some or all of your gear away ("You're exhausted, you cannot use the grappling hook." "You serious, bro? Isn't that when you'd use it most?") so none of your previous experience and fighting style will do you any good. It's quite tedious.Where Dead Island gave you a choice of 4 characters, DL gives you just one -- quite a step back. Seeing as it's a first person game, it should've been easy enough to have e.g. a female character option, at the price of one more voice actor. Incomprehensibly, they also force a background on you, and that background isn't actually in free running. Consequently, protagonist Crane stinks at parkour for the first ten levels or so. He has no moves, and he's out of breath after sprinting a few yards (or, for that matter, swinging his weapon for or fives times). You're basically paying good money to play a free running game, and then the free running stinks for the first 10 hours. Well done. (I suspect Techland and I have just grown apart; I'd like another game that's fun, and they were presumably aiming for tension and challenge -- that's the charitable interpretation, anyway. Maybe Dead Island 2 will be more my speed.)Another big factor in why that parkour just isn't that fun are the horrid controls. I don't particularly care whether the character automatically grabs on to ledges or whether you need to press or press-and-hold a button, but DL's putting jump and hold on the same button doesn't work for me. For a start, it makes climbing down a mess. Worse than that, "hold" also tends to imply "pull yourself up (onto the roof etc.)" which again may not be what you want. I've wanted for Crane to hang from a pipe, only to have him pull himself up and fall down the other side. Yay? As it stands, the controls seem non-deterministic, and factoring in the lack of full health regeneration, you're summarily discouraged from trying things out or building flow -- and of course, flow is a bit of an issue in the slums you start out in anyway. (See, same as your skills don't rate for ten levels, you don't get to the beautiful old part of the city that is densely packed with buildings of similar height until you're about halfway through the game.)The one part of the game I did rather enjoy for a while was Be The Zombie. Figures, I guess -- as the zombie, you get decent movement skills, you don't have to play the meh protagonist Crane or play the equally meh story -- et voila, fun.As it stands, Dying Light seems a noble failure, a failure at turning Dead Island into a AAA next-gen title. On the upside, Techland seem to've published tools for modders, so if that community evolves, it may turn one of the year's Greatest Misses into a hit after all.
