_childDocuments_.review: Crypt Custodian is a top-down metroidvania that surprisingly ended up among my favorites in the genre. The difference in perspective from the typical sidescroller is used extremely well here, and this is a full metroidvania and not just something that takes small elements from it. The exploration is top-notch, taking elements from top down games separated by overworlds and dungeons like 2D Zeldas or Hyper Light Drifter, but combines that in a very unique way with a more open flow between areas. You'll be exploring what feels like a closed off dungeon, and then suddenly a side path opens into a wholly new dungeon, and then you find more areas connected to that. These also differ from typical top-down dungeons in that they're not one-off locations, there is a lot of backtracking as you unlock new abilities, which thankfully is never too tedious with being able to teleport to checkpoints from anywhere.Combat starts off simple but evolves very quickly and does enough to stand out in this area as well. While individual enemies are almost always very easy, most encounters combine them and juggling a lot of enemies and projectiles on screen gives a very light kind of bullet hell experience. A small but very notable feeling bit of design is the lack of a healing system, you get a set amount of life at each checkpoint and that's it. I enjoyed this a lot, it makes even simple encounters something you have to pay attention to how you approach. There's also an upgrade system that works a lot like the charms from Hollow Knight, but you notably can get a lot more slots for them than in other games I've seen use this system, allowing you to experiment a lot more rather than just sticking to the most powerful upgrades. Boss fights are quite fun and there's a good amount of them, my only real complaint with those and with the combat in general is that boss HP is a bit low even on the hard difficulty, people experienced in this type of top down action game will likely first try a lot of them, and it's easy to burst down a boss without seeing its full move set. There is a boss rush mode where you can refight them, and I am interested in replaying it with self-imposed challenges to up the difficulty, but it could do a bit better there with the built in difficulty options.The pacing of the game is a real strong point as well, you're constantly seeing new areas, enemies, mechanics, and abilities. Those abilities are really unique feeling as well, you'll see the typical metroidvania signs of jumps you can't make and walls you can't get around, but almost always the ability you actually get here isn't what you'd expect, which I found really cool. There's a lot of interesting challenge rooms as well, including plenty of one-off fun ideas, very nice variety there. The game doesn't overstay its welcome either, it took me around 9 hours to get 100% completion, and the amount of backtracking to clean up missing items at the end was very manageable. I liked that length a lot, as it allows the pacing to stay snappy and no area overstayed its welcome. Overall had a fantastic time with this. It kept surprising me throughout my time with it, and I have very little in the way of complaints at all. Exploration and combat are both great. The story and characters are cute and simple, does a nice job of adding to the game without getting in the way. One of my favorite metroidvanias and I've already recommended it to my friends.

_childDocuments_.review: AVOID | LACKING | MAYBE | WORTHWHILE | COMPELLING | Crypt Custodian is an action-adventure metroidvania game by the (solo!) developer of Islets and Sheepo (which, incidentally, are also incredible games. Go play them too)!I normally write reviews once I've completed the game with either all achievements/100% game completion or all achievements I intend on getting at the time (sometimes leaving out achievements associated with speed runs, S+ boss rush runs, completing the game without dying/healing, etc). I'm making an exception for this game for a variety of reasons, but primarily because this game is f-ing good and the developer deserves the visibility given the unannounced drop of a Castlevania collection on the same day. With all of that said, the in-game stats tell me I've completed 34% of the game and I have 5.2 hours played. I suspect I'm on the slower side of things because I explore a lot, though I've read quite a few people saying they completed the game in about 15 hours, leaving out some of the modes you unlock at the end (like full boss rushes). I've read some reviews saying they completed the game in 10 hours, which seems really fast to me. But, I estimate that it will take me 15-20 hours to complete the game. So this review is based on someone who has completed 1/3 of the base game and I will come back to edit it once I complete the game in full.Have you ever played a game that felt like it wasn't made by developers who ever played games? Or seemed like it was made by people who intended on making the most frustrating experience possible and passing that off as difficulty? This game is the exact opposite in ways that are sometimes obvious and sometimes not, but end with a polished, great QOL, enjoyable experience for the player. Save point before the boss? It's got them. Ability to skip cutscenes associated with bosses? You can do that. Unlimited fast travel to discovered shrines? You're going to be flying. Personal map markers? Feel free to light up the map. Health bars for bosses/indicators for challenge rooms? You'll know exactly where you stand. It's just  in a way that is easy to pinpoint when those aspects are missing, but harder to notice when they are there and not causing frustration for the player.All in all, the boss fights are fun and unique, there's a mix of abilities you pick up that are genuinely new to the genre (or at least I haven't seen some of them in the many metroidvania games I've played), the characters are charming and funny, the story is amusing and distinctive, and the controls are tight and intuitive. The game is truly a metroidvania in the sense that you have multiple path options available to you at almost all times (i.e. it's non-linear). The biomes are varied and the general art design is bright and atmospheric. The music lends itself extremely well to the overall "feels" of what you're seeing/doing while playing thereby often amplifying the vibe (a really nice job was done here in a way I don't know how best to articulate it, but let it be known that I see the work that went into the soundtrack). There are also difficulty options you can change at any point during the game (easy/normal/challenge).My literal only complaint is that I don't like most of the voice acting (not quite the right word, but whatever noises the characters make when interacting with them). I had the same complaint with Islets, but that's me trying to find something to complain about.On top of all this, the dev is clearly responsive to player questions, comments, and suggestions, which is something I always appreciate.I'm leaving this review as "unmissable" and as stated, will come back to update this once I complete the game. But, if you're a fan of Islets and/or Sheepo, then this is literally the laziest and easiest recommendation I can possibly make to you with a near guarantee of you enjoying it. If you enjoy metroidvanias in general and the subgenres they often include (action, adventure, platformers, etc) then this title is sure to delight.Edit: I got 100% in-game completion with all achievements except for the boss rush ones with ~11.5 hours of gameplay. I messed around a bit with the boss rush for about 45 minutes to see how difficult it would be to get the remaining three achievements. I got one of them and I'm probably going to shelve it instead of going for the other two (they seem quite difficult, as you basically have to beat all the bosses without taking any damage within a certain timeframe on hard difficulty to get an S+ ranking).After completing the game, you unlock shuffle mode, which changes the location of pickups (e.g. abilities, special upgrades), so that sounds like it could be fun for those who may wish to play it again in the future. Now that I've completed the game, I have to say that the metroidvania aspects are very well-implemented. This is not a linear game - I got to the ninth area fifth, and the eighth area sixth, and the fifth area second to last. Therefore, you clearly have multiple paths you can take to complete the game. I also think some of the work that went into the level design is quite cool - there are a few upgrades where you have to work backwards to figure out how to get them, and you can see the thought that went behind that way of designing the level that likely would have gone completely unnoticed had the upgrades not been there. I like a little wink-wink nudge-nudge in my game that show the dev is being smart about it :DAll in all, the above review stands. I have to say that I do have the sliiiiightest preference for Islets over this title, but I absolutely do not regret my purchase in the slightest. This is a very fun and excellently-designed metroidvania that is sure to please most players.

_childDocuments_.review: Charming and creative, Crypt Custodian is a solid proof that top-down Metroidvanias are a viable and very enjoyable concept if executed correctly.The game has the usual feel-good vibe that you come to associate with Kyle's games via graphics, soundtrack and overall atmosphere. Exploration is top notch, there's plenty of upgrades to customize the game to your preferred playstyle and the areas are all very creative and unique.Oh, and a built-in randomizer for 100%-ing the map at the end?? Hell ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ YES! Now that's a fantastic reward for completionists.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of Kyle Thompson's other games, you'll love this. Crypt Custodian is a solid improvement over Islets, which was one of the top metroidvanias of 2022. One of Islets' strengths for me was that its consistency. Progression through the game is consistent. The player is always taught before being tested and challenged. There's tons of player-friendly quality of life. If you get lost, there are systems to provide hints. There's bits and pieces of challenge for sure, but this isn't a game that offers much, if any frustration. Accessibility is taken seriously. The game design is just very solid.Crypt Custodian is more of the same in the best way possible. The music and artwork are fantastic. The gameplay is smooth, fair, and fun. There's always challenges or friendly characters around every corner, which goes a long way to keeping things feeling varied. The perspective change from 2D to top-down works really well, and the addition of photo collectables is a fantastic idea to flesh out character backstories. It helps that the characters are adorable and your main quest is to befriend them. Love that.2024 has had some insanely good metroidvania releases and Crypt Custodian is absolutely amongst the best of them.

_childDocuments_.review: While I truly appreciated Kyle Thompson's previous game, Islets, I found myself concerned that I would have uncreasonable expectations about his next game. Could it be a decent follow up to a fantastic game? The answer is: absolutely. Crypt Custodian is a cozy metroidvania that may be my favorite gaming experience this year. The gameplay is straightforward top down hack and slash combat with your player character gaining new traversal abilities that swiftly open up the world. You can also equip passive abilities through ability points (that are quite liberally given) to increase your attack power or movement speed as well as special attacks (such as limited invulnerability or homing missiles) that you can unleash upon building up a special meter. If none of this sounds particularly groundbreaking, it really isn't but while there may not be a ton of complexity in the gameplay of CC but what is there is so graceful and polished to a shine that it truly stands out among other games in its genre. You play as Pluto, a recently deceased cat, who finds himself in the animal afterlife. In a bit of a misunderstanding, Pluto is sentenced to be a BAD CAT and condemned to spend the afterlife cleaning up garbage in the bad part of the afterlife. Armed with a broom, Pluto soon encounters other denizens of the afterlife. Through them, you find that in a castle in the good part of the afterlife, there is a mirror that allows any animal that enters it to return to the world of the living to see their loved ones one last time. Thus, a plan hatches with you and your friends to break into the castle and have one last look at what you left behind. The plot may sound overly dramatic or moody, but it really is not. For all the characters being ostensibly dead, the tone of the game is mostly lighthearted and cozy. There are few games where I find myself loving all the NPCs, but I truly wish I could hug all of the NPCs in CC. While all of your afterlife companions are fantastic, I do find myself truly adoring the tough Grizz, the mellow Crouton and the gloomy Wailer. While these characters are fleshed out through Pluto speaking with them, I cannot deny that the most powerful moments of the game came by collecting Polaroids of your afterlife friends which depict how they came to be in the afterlife and who or what they left behind. Many feelings were had. Story and worldbuilding aside, CC is a fantastic game. While the metroidvania genre is often full of difficulty, soulslike mechanics and punishment on death, CC really has none of those things. The action is straightforward. The bosses may not be pushovers but I can't say any of them took more than a handful of attempts to defeat. All of these and the chill ambient music lead to a very graceful, cozy experience. Some may be deterred by the game's relative lower difficulty level, but to me I felt like the easier difficulty fit the overall tone and vibe of the game and did not detract from my experience. It took me roughly 9 hours to make it through the main part of the game with about 86% completion and a few more hours after that to mop up the last few items I found. If you enjoyed the game half as much as I did, there is a randomizer mode that you can enable on a new file after beating the game and a boss rush mode. I rarely replay games these days, but CC will have me bucking that trend in the very near future. In short, Crypt Custodian is very much for your time if you are looking for a graceful, heartfelt, chill experience. In a year of many stellar metroidvanias (Animal Well, Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown), Crypt Custodian's genuine emotion and grace make it stand out ahead of the pack. If you play exactly one metroidvania this year, I would recommend curling up with Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I'm 6 hours in and would estimate I'm halfway through the main story (about 37% completion according to the game) and it's been nothing short of spectacular. The story is well paced, but the world is quite open to allow for a lot of exploration between unlocking new abilities. While I was exploring I felt like I was doing a lot of walking at times, but eventually found you can warp to any save point you unlocked at ANY TIME. Which made a lot of smaller critiques like zero health items dropping feel minuscule.  The traveling is so easy and perfectCombat and items is also, near or perfect for me. Fighting enemies unlocks coal (looks like coal?), the main currency and with that you can unlock new items items in a shop that can be equipped with upgrade points, which can be found quite easily. you can also buy hints for items or a hint on where to go next in the main story, which is very nice if you need that extra help. The combat is simple vs main enemies, but they get some more unique move sets as the game progresses so you better be good with that dodge-roll. The boss fights are also stellar, could be my favorite part of the game. They have challenge, but not too much challenge.This will most likely be my favorite Metroidvania of the year, maybe my favorite indie of the year. Progression is nice, story is heartwarming and collecting everything is extremely satisfying, and may even make you tear up. Sound design is stellar and the traversal and combat make the game so much better. Do yourself a favor and buy this game

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game with a lot of soul. The metroidvania abilities are a little too lock-and-key instead of changing how you play, but boss fights are pretty good and the difficulty is tuned well. There's a really chill low-stakes vibe to everything with a good sense of humor and personality in the dialogue, but with an ending that's still genuinely bittersweet if you've lost a pet that was important to you.

_childDocuments_.review: Simple but fun. Controls are really tight, combat is on the easy side but puts up enough fight to not be boring. Frankly it's refreshing to play a metroidvania/zeldalike that's not trying to be dark souls. Really appreciate the mechanics to help you find items that you missed as well, scouring the map for the last couple collectibles is not my favorite thing about this genre, and this game neatly avoids it. _childDocuments_.review: This is the first Isometric Metroidvania I have played. The gameplay has you attacking enemies close up with your broom while using dash and specials to mix up the combat. The specials are varied from homing missiles to invincibility for a short time. It gives you lots of options when fighting all the bosses. There are a dozen bosses each with a second phase that changes up their pattern. I love how difficult and interesting the deigns for these bosses are from a pot of spiders to a giant ice witch. The upgrades help you platform around the environment and solve time challenges. There isn't anything crazy when it comes to the movement abilities but they work well. The two big ones you get are a teleport and a air dash. Both are good and necessary to access other areas in the map. I just wish there was more done with more interesting movement options. During my playtime i had no load times outside the game launch. You can teleport back to checkpoints at any time with no penalty and instantly. When you loose against a boss you can be back in the room skipping the cut scenes in 4 seconds or less. The game Overall if you have any interest in the idea of an isometric Metroidvania or just likes Kyle's previous game give this one a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall:People have a tendency to want to qualify reviews by saying things like "it's amazing compared to their previous games", or "it's amazing for a solo developer passion project". And while those are true statements in this case, they imply that the game needs to be judged in comparison to others... that it can't stand on its own.That couldn't be further from the truth with Crypt Custodian. This game 100% stands on its own. It is simply a great game. I put it on my personal A-tier, as it ticks all the boxes for my personal tastes in MVs. An engaging story - interesting characters - rewarding exploration - a well-developed map - compelling graphics - unique music - moderately challenging yet fun boss fights - this game has it all.My favorite MV of the year so far was Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown, and with all its AAA graphics and voice acting and huge budget and team (my god have you sat through the credits??), I honestly had just as much fun playing Crypt Custodian.Completion Time:100% in 89 hours. BAHAHA!Look, I get my money's worth out of my games, so don't judge me here LOL. I don't understand why it always takes me twice as long to 100% games as everyone else. I really don't. Also, I have a habit of leaving my computer to do something and forgetting to pause or exit the game so my times are always a bit out of whack. So take my completion time with a huge grain of salt.Story:I'm not one to care too much about the story in an MV. If everything else is working, I'm not going to complain about the lack of one or judge a game harshly for not having one. However, the addition of a compelling or interesting story on top of a great game is icing on the cake and enough to raise the overall rating a whole tier. But this game does have an interesting story that manages to be fun and entertaining and includes truly touching, sad and funny moments.The story lightly brushes up against some fairly serious issues such as poverty, destruction of the environment, and most importantly questions about death such as what happens after death, who judges the merits of a soul, and what qualifies a person to spend eternity in a good or bad place. These human concerns are dealt with lightly and often poignantly and remind me of games such as Spiritfarer, where you're happily playing along and then suddenly have to pause the action so you can fully contemplate the realization of the deeper meaning behind something that just occurred.Graphics:With each game this developer steps up their graphics game considerably. The cartoon style of the characters are a natural extension of those in Islets, but with yet more detail and development. The graphics presented here are interesting and well-developed and completely in sync with the style of this MV.There's been a lot of chatter about the 2D+ way the graphics were handled. Personally, I love them and think they allow for significantly more options when it comes to exploration and abilities than a more traditional 2D experience does.Map:The map is HUGE. Given the size and scope of Islets and Sheepo, I expected an exponential enlargement of the game to be 2x or even 4x as large as Islets. This was a massive under-expectation on my part. And unlike some of those huge games such as Death's Gambit: Afterlife or even parts of HK, traversing the world isn't a punishing experience.As a side note, the sheer amount of time it takes to plan, ideate, draw and flesh out each individual biome in a game is staggering, and to see how this solo developer did that for so many unique biomes at such an immense scale is really impressive. One of the ways they accomplished it is through a lot of fairly simple elements and small areas that are interlinked... a very smart way to recycle and reuse graphics with different styles and backgrounds and save tons of development time on the world. The downside is the overall feel of the game does become a bit same-y over the course of a playthrough, but that's how it goes when trying to find a balance between quality and quantity.Fast Travel:The ability to fast travel at the start of the game makes a huge difference, but added to the innate ability of the main character to teleport instantly to any of the world's fast travel locations makes traversal a breeze. And the cherry on top of the experience is the process of teleporting is practically instantaneous... no cut scenes or animation or unnecessary delay... you are instantly where you want to be. So if you miss an item somewhere far away, it often takes under a minute to get to fast travel, run to that location, and then continue on with your game. More developers should take a lesson from what was done here.Puzzles:What great MV is without the occasional challenge that needs some moderate puzzling to figure out? And of course, MVs should not be only puzzlers as they require a nice balance of exploration, combat, etc. to fall nicely into the category. The developer has walked that line very well in this game. There are locks that can only be opened and items that can only be obtained through figuring out the puzzle that keeps them locked, however these areas are not crucial to advancement in the game for those who just don't appreciate a nice mental challenge. Me, on the other hand, I love a good puzzle. But they have to be interesting and unique and not so hard that I need to consult the internet. Something I can figure out on my own without spending TOO much time on it. Crypt Custodian hits the sweet spot here and manages to do it without repeating the same types of puzzles that we've all grown to groan about when seen over and over again in games. Some puzzles were tricky enough that I had to subconsciously mull them over for a day or two before I was able to solve them.Combat:If you're looking for a combat-driven MV, this will disappoint you. However, there are enough enemy types with varied attack styles to keep things interesting. Combine that with different combinations of abilities and special attacks and the combat system is decent. Nothing to write home about or complain about. The controls are responsive and I always felt in full control of the action. I never felt like a death was unfair.Bosses:The bosses are challenging, but fair, and while all their patterns can be learned and beaten without swapping out the abilities, it's great to see how those abilities do make boss battles faster or less of a grind. The boss weaknesses are discovered naturally through repeated battles, but never did I feel like it was too much of a challenge or too souls-like for an MV of this type. The addition of the fast-travel locations nearby each of the bosses made repeated attempts as least-frustrating as possible. Additionally, some of the bosses were quite unique and really fun. The Rail Rider in particular I had a blast fighting.Challenges:In addition to the boss fights, there are a few different types of challenges that you can enjoy in each zone throughout the map, each getting tougher in keeping with the level of the biome. At first these were really easy but got to the point that I would need to run them multiple times and felt great satisfaction once I completed them.Music:Eric's music is great for this game. It is interesting and isn't offensive or ever really noticeable, which means it works on a background level. You're not going to want to sit and listen to the soundtrack while hanging out at home, but it's pleasant. I liked how the songs were also featured as items to be discovered within the game, which was a nice nod to their quality and brought the player's focus toward appreciating them individually.Score:91/100. An A-tier, fun, cute, heartwarming Metroidvania.Definitely worth the price of admission.

_childDocuments_.review: Crypt Custodian has got to be one of the coziest metroidvanias I've played in awhile. I absolutely adore the art and the music. There is a story you can piece together which feels incredibly bittersweet, but this game has not failed to make me smile when encountering a lot of the other characters. It's even made me snort with laughter on two separate occasions.In about 10 hours, I was able to complete the game and tie up whatever loose ends to get 100% completion. The game doesn't overstay its welcome, and everything feels like a polished product that you can knock out in a few evenings. It isn't a bloated metroidvania - particularly, it's one that respects your time. The platforming feels fluid and the controls responsive, and the combat is snappy too. Bosses are fair, and all enemies in the game have a distinct, telltale marker to show when they are attacking next, which I truly appreciate. You can also switch around the difficulty at any time, which makes this game accessible to anyone who would like to just experience the game without much fuss. You can also unlock a shuffle mode, which swaps around items and power ups in the game as well to shake up any future playthroughs you might want to do. There are also a few achievements you can get from a boss rush mode, though I am only reviewing my experience with the base game. Boss rush is an extra activity there if anyone wants to trophy hunt, but otherwise nothing is missable in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick Description:-Kyle Thompson has done it again!  He is slowly proving that he is one of the best metroidvania devs out there.  I have now played all 3 of his games and I think Crypt Custodian is the best one yet.  While all 3 games have plenty of charm, a really unique art style, and interesting characters, Crypt Custodian is the first game that really brings everything together imo.  This game has a very large interconnected map w/ 12 different biomes (12 or 13 - not 100% sure).  There are close to a dozen different bosses, over 20 different powerups to discover, tons of secrets, and about 5 or 6 unique upgrades that help you navigate the world in new ways.  As you would expect, this game has a really fun soundtrack and a cute story to go w/ it.  Consensus:-Solid Game (Tier 3 and makes up 35% of my reviews).  This game feels like a mix between Unsighted and Fearmonium.  I think it's better than Fearmonium but not quite as good as Unsighted.  This is a really talented dev.  It's pretty amazing that he can pump out such high quality metroidvania's in under 2 years.  I can't wait to see what he has in store for us next.  Maybe a 2d soulslike metroidvania?  Maybe he's planning on mixing things up, and has a fun roguelight planned?  Whatever he decides to create, I will definitely be picking it up on day 1.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Every game from Kyle is fantastic, but Crypt Custodian is a step beyond. CC takes all the good things you expect from Kyle's work in terms of movement, character design, dialogue, exploration, etc. and perfects a lot of the formula. I could rant for hours about what an achievement this game is in the metroidvania canon, and I think it's easily the best top-down metroidvania out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Crypt Custodian has simply been a very enjoyable time and the fact that it was made by two people is extraordinarily impressive for the skill showcased in every aspect of the game. the characters are enjoyable and unique, the game mechanics are well polished and nothing feels buggy, the bosses and challenges are very difficult without feeling unfair as they only require you to gain a deeper understanding mechanically (~4-6 tries for me personally for bosses). the art-style is adorable but also very refined and purposeful. i wholeheartedly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys comfy (yet surprisingly heavy-hearted) stories, good movement controls and fun combat/ exploration mechanics. i hope this game gets the attention and acclaim it deserves.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I just started playing Crypt Custodian but I'm already in love with it. Kyle you're so good at making games and Eric you're so good at making music. I happen to know you thanks to Islets, another wonderful game.Talking about the game: I was even moved at the beginning. Crypt Custodian is about a cat that goes to the afterlife after a car killed him. Unfortunately, a harsh reality. But I also laughed a lot, because the characters are lovely and funny. I'm also happy to find out several elements that were also in Islets, in particular that awesome music of the boss fight! That track is so good!Thank you guys for making such great games. I'm your fan.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I was such a huge fan of Islets that this game was a must-have. The visuals are fun and I really like that they put more focus on their whimsical characters. They just made me smile so much, I loved their personalities! Overall It is a beautiful game with a fun and engaging story. But as many people have noted, the bosses just aren't as challenging as I would like. Compared to Islets which takes its time with the bosses and has distinct rhythms of fighting style for each one, I found that a lot of the bosses here weren't as satisfying to defeat. If you are looking for something challenging, this might not be the game for you. But if you were a fan of Islets or just really like the visuals, a little story, humor, and a less stressful but still fun fighting style this is definitely something I would recommend 100%
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Crypt Custodian is a metroidvania-masterpiece. A game that implements both constant challenge with frequent combat and permanent engagement with smart and careful ly designed rooms. I myself have rarely played a mv that to this extent kept me engaged in every single minute of the entire playthrough, which is achieved by avoiding boring backtracking, perfectly narrated pathing and by excellent quick-travel execution.As a 100% metroidvania gamer, this game is a great pleasure to complete, with non-patronizing tools to help you find these last few collectables.The movement is fluent and multi-facetted, which gets more and more interesting as you progress through the stages and receive new buffs that further enhance it, opening new doors for different paths.And this does not even mention the storytelling, which is incredibly wholesome and engaging, decorated by cute characters with rich personalities and heartwarming backstories.I would lie by saying it did not tear a little bit at the end of the story. This picture of afterlife gives me new-found hope :')It is made with so much love for the genre and with even more love for companionship.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been keeping an eye on Crypt Custodian since last Spring, when all the Indie publishers came together to promote their games. And look, I'm a simple man, I see a black cat protagonist and I think "I need this game." A Metroidvania? Sign me up! I don't think I was prepared for the emotions that came with this game's story. It's surprisingly lighthearted, dealing with the lives and deaths of the various animals that Pluto finds throughout his story, and this romp around a top-down world to find new friends in the afterlife kept me eager for more.The way the story ends left me an emotional mess. I had my own black cat who had the same experience as Pluto, so it was... a lot to take in. Felt like I got some closure for my own pets, if that makes sense?Gameplay-wise, it's a Metroidvania through and through. You've got movement upgrades, solid combat, a host of upgrades that work via an upgrade points mechanic. You find upgrade points in the environment, you get them for completing various challenges, and you can purchase some from the VIP - I think I ended my run with over 60? Meaning I could equip a ton of upgrades. Reminded me of the system in Sonic & the Secret Rings, where you could equip as many power-ups as you had points. Very refreshing.Enemies were super intriguing. I'm impressed that with how every enemy attacks via bullet-hell style projectiles, they all had differing patterns and ways to make them all stand out. Not one enemy felt derivative of each other, and with how many different areas there are in the game, that's incredible to say the least.I love how distinct the environments are, and the progression is very fluid and fair. Locked paths get marked on your map, and if you want to go the old fashioned way and remember where an upgrade will help you progress, you can. But you can also go to the shop & purchase hints towards progression & secrets if you're completely lost.My favourite part of the game has to be the optional challenges - The 10 Curses found throughout the game are incredible - You have to kill 15 enemies while cursed, and each curse inflicts a debuff on the player. 1 hit-KOs, being chased by two evil spirits, spikes appearing behind you as you run, enemies exploding upon death. More Metroidvanias should adopt this system, it's genius!The gameplay is forgiving, though there are difficulty modes to enhance your experience, and a special mode I won't delve into here that you unlock after befriending every animal, which will make a second playthrough very unique.Boss Fights were the true highlight of this game - They're inspired, entertaining, well animated and above all else - Tough. You can attack spam your way through them relatively well in the basic game - But once you delve into the boss rush mode to get that S+ rank on each difficulty, you'll have to play to the very best of your abilities. More games need a Boss Rush mode, this is a highly appreciated addition - I just hope a future update includes information on how to reach an S+ for each battle.I didn't personally run into any glitches in my playthrough, and the load times are incredibly seamless which is impressive for a game of this size and scope. Overall, I HIGHLY recommend Crypt Custodian, and I can safely say it's in contention for my Top 10 Games of the Year.

_childDocuments_.review: Admittedly, I was a little worried to see the switch from side-scroller to top down as I've never played a top down Metroidvania, but I think the extra dimension allowed for much more depth than Islets! The combat is a huge improvement, The Art was MASSIVELY improved, and the story and setting are much more interesting. Music/sound was welcome, I’m happy with the references to the last games. The creator I once considered to be the one who makes “Small, chill, cute, casual Metroidvanias” has made a game with qualities that are rivaling aspects from the greats; Ori and Hollow Knight.I think this is the main draw of this game, so I’ll start with this. This game has one of my favorite combat systems. In most games, I don’t find enemies interesting to engage with, always feeling like they’re in the way of progress, just slowing me down. (Unpopular take, I am aware). But in this game, I really looked forward to every enemy encounter. It was just the right amount of chaos. I had a bunch of effects coming off me, enemies had huge bullet patterns that only covered even more of the screen by the end of the game, but it was never too much where I couldn’t keep up. It always stayed engaging and fresh, with each new encounter being on new terrain and with different enemy groups. Both in bosses and enemies, I was far more engaged than I ever was with Ori. And I would argue that goes for a large portion of Hollow Knight, but definitely not all of it. I do think jumping might have needed a bit of a counter though. I  wouldn’t say the game was too easy, but I think it needed more switch ups to keep it fresh. More tall attacks you needed to dash through and not jump over, since the ground dash felt completely useless for fighting. This concept was utilized, but only once. And I think it was a missed opportunity to mix it up with everything else.This game actually really impressed me with its balance. At no point did I feel too weak or too strong. Which is incredibly impressive with how many charm slots you gain, being able to put on the majority of your charms at any given time. Almost all charms felt viable too. All the different effects blended together well. While playing the game, I thought the  was useless. I thought it was too slow, and didn’t do enough damage. Though I went back and tried it out some more with the charms that buff it and it seems decent. I do think it should have been it’s own button, as holding down the attack button and waiting there felt like it broke the flow of combat a decent bit. (Also this maybe would have allowed for auto swing by holding down the attack button. (LT was free) My hand was definitely hurting by the end of boss rush).Very glad with how the minion felt. Tt was making a difference, could finish enemies off for me when I needed, but not something I could let do all the work for me. Minions in games are typically far too weak, or far to reliable. So that was a breath of fresh air. I named him Percy.I loved the bosses! Such an insane improvement from Islets.  was such a unique concept for a boss! Easily my favorite. So confusing at first, and so satisfying to figure out. The final boss was also really fun!Though I think there are two stinkers in the boss roster. . The first one especially. Each are bosses where you are just dodging waiting for the clear hit opportunity to arise. It’s boring and repetitive, taking away the flow of what makes combat fun, finding hit opportunities while dodging. This wouldn’t be terrible either, if the patterns were harder to dodge. But they’re even simpler than most of the other bosses, so what gives? I kinda burnt through them in the main game, so I didn’t mind too much then, but in boss rush they stood out like a sore thumb.  Also had one attack where you were just waiting  for the spikes to slowly disappear. They should have dissipated way faster so you’re not just sitting waiting.Exploration in this game was good. Each of the Areas were distinct and pretty, though the world itself wasn’t super thrilling to explore due to a lack of environmental story (something pretty important to exploration in this genre) However, from a pure gaming aspect it had some good stuff going for it. Every upgrade point or charm being behind a little platforming challenge, or combat arena, made everything feel earned. Nothing too complex, but I think having the interactable environments and constant little challenges, is something Hollow Knight lacks. So big praise. Plenty of room for improvement though. Also; Curses! What a great idea! Picking up a challenge that makes combat harder temporarily is a great way to shake up exploration! (Remember to mark them on the map in case you fail though.) I didn’t really feel much possibility for sequence breaking. The progression locking in this game felt good, but how your abilities were used to traverse felt pretty straightforward. Not a bad thing. The game is just fun to move around in though, and right out the door too. So that’s a plus. Felt very fluid.Also, finding music disks was a lame reward. Should have been able to set the music outside the one room. Neon crest was easily my favorite Area, but the basement was a ton of fun too. Wanted to drive those barrels forever.I loved the way the map was drawn. Very cute and funky, and it took some effort to read. Though the red circle to indicate where you are I hated. Hurt to look at, covered up too much around me. Much prefer a little icon of your dude’s head.For the most part, the abilities combine exploration and combat well. But the  and  felt like wasted potential. For how they were used, not bad. But it felt a reversion all the way back to sheepo with them. Imo, Abilities that can only on specific doorways, feel kinda bland. I think they could have been worked into the combat somehow.  Could maybe distract enemies, and prevent you from taking damage? (Like forgotten from BoI) and perhaps could have just been able to be used anywhere and its speed being way faster so it would just be an upgrade to movement. (Perhaps this could be an unlock after using it in the area that relies on its limitation).  I love Thompson’s cute and goofy style of writing. Jokes are always on point. I really enjoyed the setting of this game. Finding pictures to get little lore bits about the characters was fun. Everything had this slight emotional pull to it which was nice. However, I wish the game elements reflected story elements. There’s no lore to most of the areas, enemies, abilities or bosses, no environmental storytelling, it feels very “video game-y”. And I get that’s partially Thompson’s style. But I feel like even simple jokes here and there to expand on the world would really make exploration feel more in depth. I liked all the characters though. And I’m happy with Thompsons ability to make incredibly hateable characters. Would also like to see I also think the ending was kinda unsatisfying. I don’t mind Really looking forward to whatever Thompson makes next! Hope this game is a huge finical success for them.

_childDocuments_.review: Played on OG 512 steam deck without issues. This review is one I debated not even writing as I want to recommend because I want to support the dev and likely blaming myself for the apathy I feel towards it. I'll just explore and grind a bit to buy upgrades. Shouldn't be a problem. Oh there's Pebble. Hi, Pebble."Pebble: "BE SAD! HERE'S A REASON TO BE SAD! ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ CRY, ♥♥♥♥♥! SCULPT YOUR OWNERS, ♥♥♥♥♥! CRY! CRYYYY!!!"Me; "JFC, PEBBLE! I JUST STARTED THIS SESSION 3 MINUTES AGO!"Subtlety, Kyle Thompson! Do you know it?! _childDocuments_.review: Crypt Custodian is an obvious evolution in game design by Kyle Thompson, and is definitely his best work yet. This game is charming, emotional, beautiful, and also appropriately tuned in difficulty to appeal to just about any level of skill. If you grind enough you can equip every upgrade in the game, which can go a long way to making sure that boss battles don't become hard barriers to progress.If you like any of Kyle's previous games, this is a must buy. If you enjoy Metroid-lites, you should absolutely buy this game. If you have no experience with the genre or the author, you should still give this game a chance as it is a fantastic introduction to a type of game that can provide hours of entertainment for young and old alike.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Plays like Hyperlight Drifter with lower difficulty and lighter atmosphere. _childDocuments_.review: A short but memorable experience. The characters are endearing and the puzzles are straightforward. This type of progression definitely reminds me of Zelda games from long ago. Combat is smooth and even on hard mode the enemies aren't overly difficult. Some of the bosses even surprised me with their skill sets.   The selection of music is soothing, no song felt out of place. Secrets and upgrade points can be found using the machine at the bar so you rarely get stuck. There were a couple points I did lose track of where I was supposed to be though because the map gets big, all you need do is keep looking.  I enjoyed this little experience, its been a while since I actually wanted to 100% a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Crypt Custodian is an indie masterpiece. It fits the tightest and most satisfying top down 'Zelda-like' combat I have ever experienced into a compact, adorable, and charming little package.The visuals and character design are wonderful, the soundtrack is extraordinary, and the gameplay is beyond satisfying. The sound design is crunchy and punchy, and everything just feels fantastic. The hectic bullet-hell style boss battles are unbelievably enjoyable, and bring a very nice challenge. Though the combat in and of itself is exhilarating. Improving Pluto's abilities while progressing through the game and unlocking all of its secrets is wonderful. And boy does Pluto become an absolute monster towards the end of the game. The dark and somber story is very nice, especially complimented by the similarly themed soundtrack. I adored my time with Crypt Custodian. Kyle is an absolute legend of a developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: This game actually took me quite by surprise. In short: it's delightful to play. The gameplay is smooth and enjoyable, and the areas are varied and relatively unique. Exploration feels nice, and there's a very rewarding feeling as you battle your way through from location to location.Overall, the game has some exceptional polish to it, and is full of plenty of enjoyable attention to detail. The upgrades you gather as you go feel meaningful and cool, and even all the way to the end there's a really fun sense of unlocking some interesting new aspect.The characters are fun and enjoyable, and have enough pizzazz to them they I was never left feeling disappointed or bothered by my interactions with them. Even the antagonist was entertaining.On the negative side: the plot itself has a somewhat unsatisfying conclusion, in my opinion. Though it's clear what the cause of the garbage is, it's never really addressed why the antagonist is where she is, and it feels even worse after 100% completion of the game. Part of your reward for completion is finding out the antagonist's story, and it feels... satirical? I was honestly expecting there to be a reveal of "psyche, this isn't ACTUALLY the story, now here's the REAL truth" - but it never came. To be specific, Mechanically, some of the charms/equips/etc felt wholly unnecessary, but that might have just been my playstyle. The game itself took about 11 hours to beat, and 14 to 100%.All in all, its flaws were pretty minor, and I really enjoyed playing through it!

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute yet somber at times. Fantastic game play that has fluid movement and attacks. Difficulty for doing just the story is easy - moderate with some optional challenges that are fairly... well, challenging. Puzzles were unique but not complex, all of it felt super doable. Did not expect to love this game as much as I did. I ended up 100%ing it. I enjoyed exploring it and was compelled by the cute characters and bittersweet setting.I only have 2 gripes. 1) The map UI was not very user friendly. Putting down markers always had them way off from where my cursor was. When I would zoom out and scroll to get to further parts of the map to teleport to, when I zoomed back in my cursor would be nowhere near where it was originally. Felt really off. Could definitely use some improvement. (Played using a controller as  the game recommended)2) Some items were hidden due to invisible platforms. It does not feel rewarding back traveling to find out I missed an upgrade all because I didn't know there was an invisible platform. There's an upgrade you can get to make them visible, but that doesn't lessen the impact of feeling disappointed in having missed them while exploring. Feels kinda cheap.Solid 9.5/10 game! If above issues were addressed I'd make it a perfect 10/10. Would recommend at the $20 price.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game! 9/10I've only ever "gotten into" a game once, and that was Stardew Valley.  I've really been wanting to get into Metroidvania games, and just more active games in general. I tried and failed to get into Hollow Knight but I think this is more up my valley. I really want to play BOTW but I do not own a switch.The soundtrack is great, simple but switches up enough to not drive you insane. _childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous little Metroidvania about loss of pets and animals. And I mean that in every sense of gorgeous. If you love your pets, this is worth a play. [Also it never gets REAL sad so that's good.]++PROS+++ Really accessible with difficulty settings and buyable hints that are real cheap.+ Lots of upgrades hanging around. Surprisingly, NO double jump which means all the upgrades you get are a bit unique and unexpected.+ Combat flows very well but isn't much more than buttonmashing, however dodging attacks can get pretty wild which is great!+ Characters are extremely well written and there's lots of funny visual gags in the cutscenes. Ended up loving every single of these silly little animals.+++ PLUTO ISN'T A MUTE! And is not just a sweety but is written like a pretty normal person... Er cat, you know what I mean.+ Surprisingly long for a 100% playthrough and it was very enjoyable the whole time, even when I was dying consistently against bosses and set enemies.+ Lots of achievements to help mark 100% progress which I love.+ Obviously gorgeous music and art, but I think both are very evident. Lots of small jokes in the art which I love as well.+ Bug free from what I played.+ Retrying failed challenges is real easy, whether that's bosses, curse shrines or platforming puzzles which is highly appreciated.+ Save spots are placed around just right so you never have to walk too far to backtrack.- CONS -- ONE upgrade felt awful to get but the intended solution "Worked" so that's good.- The digging upgrade doesn't feel very well involved in the game and becomes a very big hassle for 100%ing later on. If you find weird patches of dirt on your playthrough, MARK IT. You will thank yourself later when you mark the dirt you need to dig into.- If you die during bossfights and they have an intro cutscene you have to manually skip the cutscene every time. This is just a minor annoyance with the benefit that it GUARANTEES you'll start each boss in a predictable spot making retries easier but I found it annoying at least once so I'm marking it cause that's how perfect this game is: There is basically nothing to complain about!??VERDICT??A near perfect masterpiece that is about as close to perfect and unique you can get with a exploration platformer puzzle action game [Metroidvania] as you can get. As a final note, the ending made me tear up a bit and while I'm writing this right after my 100% playthrough, I will say that the game is just fantastic and is the best example of this genre in a long while, which is ABSOLUTELY saying something when so many good ones have released in recent years. Pick it up, buy all the extra stuff, get your friends to buy it, it's purrrrrrfect.

_childDocuments_.review: Like all of Kyle Thompson's games, Crypt Custodian is excellent. I like how each game explores a new mechanic. The top down view is a nice departure from the majority of the genre while still allowing for interesting movement mechanics and gameplay. There are a ton of different biomes to explore. Each has its own enemies, which follow a few architypes but expand on them (so for instance, you'll find a basic archer in the first biome, an archer who shoots a boomerang later one, an archer who fires multiple shots, etc.). There are also curses to find which give you specific situations to endure until you've killed enough enemies,  in exchange for a power up. Speaking of which, there are a huge number of upgrades to found (similar to charms in other games), but you also find and can buy slots for those upgrades. There's no limit to how many slots you can have so you can really build out your character in any way you want. I really enjoyed using upgrades that my own blue projectiles to the mess of bullets being fired in some areas and boss fights. As well, there are special attacks to be found (you can activate one of them at a time, and they charge up pretty fast), and jukebox discs which allow you to play songs in the inn.The world is quite expansive, and traversing it is pretty good. You can fast travel to any previously visited save point straight off the bat. You can add a number of your own markers, as well as buy markers for missed secrets or the next area to head to; otherwise the game doesn't handhold you and you can pretty quickly decide to go in whatever direction you'd like. The map itself is good but not ideal with a controller - there are two zoom levels but scrolling the zoomed out one doesn't scroll the zoomed in one which makes the map a bit hard to navigate, especially if there's a specific warp point you want to go to across the map. You also can only fast travel using the zoomed in version, as far as I was able to determine. I'd also say that some of the power ups you get do not have nearly enough places to use them (or require you to find a room to use them far away from your goal), but they're also used in surprising ways.Took me about 15 hours to get to 100% completion in game. There's also a boss rush mode that I played around a bit in but isn't really my cup of tea (in order to get S+ you need to kill bosses quickly and without taking any damage).It is amazing to me that at the time of writing this, 25% of players have gotten the 100% completion achievement. This really goes to show how amazing this game is. It's a very comfortable experience and you can tell that QoL was really considered. If you like metroidvanias, and especially if you like Kyle's other games, you're definitely going to love this one. Can't wait for the next one!

_childDocuments_.review: I was first introduced to Kyle Thompson's games with Islets, two years ago, and immediately I fell in love with his charming style, innovative ideas, and thrilling gameplay. Well, I'm pleased to say Kyle has absolutely outdone himself with Crypt Custodian.Crypt Custodian presents you with a vast labyrinth to explore, full of monsters, puzzles, and secrets - your typical metroidvania fare. But your environment is 3D, with an angled forward-facing camera in place of your standard 2D display. This alone is an intriguing departure from the norm. It also presents a strong, emotional story told in bits and pieces of a number of different ghosts in the afterlife. It was hard not to cry at the ending cutscene tbhAs for the actual gameplay, the platforming is sharp, and the rooms do a great job of keeping the pressure on without overwhelming you. Jumps are quite generous, helping hone you into the edge of a platform if you're close enough. I found this highly useful when some movements of mine weren't perfectly cardinal (I used analog stick) without being overbearing or too much (you absolutely can still fall like an idiot :) but when  you do, it's 100% your fault imo).The combat was rich and highly entertaining, with some great upgrade ideas that strike a balance between rewarding your progress with improvements but keeping your character from ever becoming OP. Unless there's some OP postgame stuff I haven't gotten to yet (I'm writing this after any%ing the game rn, but I still have some stuff to do for hundo). Some combat moves even upgrade to help you with the platforming later, like Speaking of combat, boss fights in particular were superb all around. One of my (extremely few) criticisms of Islets was that I found that, even on hard mode, the bosses were all pretty easy (except for one mid-game boss, which made me feel like the difficulty curve could have been massaged there). In this game, the bosses are all satisfyingly tough on hard mode, without being a completely evil rng-fest. Kyle had a lot of different ideas for them as well, which I really appreciated. My favorite was probably That said, I will say, I found that for a few of the bosses, a pretty easy strategy to deal with bullet-hell style attacks was to  it's not a bad thing at all, but for the number of bosses I was able to do it to, it made me feel like a bit more tweaking to these kinds of attacks could be useful. It's a super minor nitpick, however. On the other end of the range, I did find the  After 4 or 5 deaths, I managed to beat it by developing a strategy that seemed a bit like a cheese -  But these are very minor nitpicks.The only other nitpicks I think I have are that, for one, I personally didn't find the challenges all that intriguing; there were only a few distinct types of "curses," repeated a number of times throughout the land, and these represent most of the remainder of what I have to do in the game (as far as I currently know) simply because I'm not that interested in them. And I guess the other one is that I felt like the  But that's really all I would say on the side of nitpicks.I very much look forward to 100%ing this game eventually, but with my current schedule and the other games I want to play, it may be a hot minute. In the meantime, however, I can absolutely recommend this to any metroidvania fans out there. It took me a little under 10 in-game hours to any%, and I spent a lot of that time exploring outside of what I needed to for just any%, _and_ I was on hard mode, so hypothetically it could take you faster if you wanted to rush it a little. And on the other hand, if you want to fully complete it, from what I've heard, I definitely have a few more hours to go. In other words, this is definitely worth it imo if you're looking for an excellent metroidvania but don't have a whole lot to spend.

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★★ 5/5I previously played "Islets," so I knew what to expect from the start. Everything just fits perfectly here. The art style, the gameplay, the music, and the story all come together seamlessly. The story and dialogue don’t take themselves too seriously and have many humorous moments. The combat system is simple yet incredibly fluid. The boss fights aren’t too difficult, and the skill system allows for different strategies to be used to defeat them. The isometric map style might deter some players, but it works surprisingly well, making navigation smooth and intuitive. The only downside I noticed were some small technical obstacles, like the zoom ratio in the map display, which could be more precise, and the maximum resolution being capped at 1440p. Other than that, I highly recommend it to everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DRGood MetroidvaniaThe good: - You can sequence break if you know how to use the game mechanics; - The game gives you just enough ability points for you to feel strong but if you want more you can grind and buy as many ability points as you want; - If you are having a bad time finding the secrets you can use the currency of the game to buy markers stuff you missed; - The curses are the harder stuff on the game and they are optional, most of the time they will give you ability points and if you want to you can straight up buy those; - Distinct art style; - Good enough enemy diversity, not only in designs but in moveset as well; - Each area not only have a specific theme but they also have unique mechanics and enemies; - It is strange that I need to mention this, but the day and age requires it, the game is very stable, the only bug I've experienced is the animation of "falling" playing when I barely made across the precipice, so yeah, pretty solid.The "meh": - Although the weapon is part of the character background story and it is solid I missed more weapon options; - The story is kinda shallow, but to their credit you don't usually play metroidvanias for the story.

_childDocuments_.review: Good solid game.  Controls smoothly and although the combat isn't revolutionary the movement and actions you have make every encounter relatively fun.  Bosses can pose a real threat though nothing in the game is super punishing.  The story and characters are good, and if you like animals or have pets it might resonate a little more.  The music and sound design is also quite good.  A charming little gem of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimatley, Crypt Custodian is a fun and simple metroidvania.The characters are super cute, the world is mostly enjoyable to explore, and the visuals are cartoony and sweet. The combat can get a little repetitive, especially once you find a "build" that suits you. The bosses are unique and well-designed - some even offer a challenge.I liked it, but it won't go in my "hall of fame" so-to-speak. However, considering this is all done by a single person, I have to admit it's really impressive.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Crypt Custodian is adorable and fun. I liked it for every moment of the 11 hours I played before stopping at credits and 77% completion (as is my normal pattern).It's a little bit like if deaths door was easier and had a more adorable cat protagonist, with a little bit of the sensibility of Chicory in it's storytelling. And some Cat Quest in there in terms of combat feeling. But it's definitely a traditional metroidvania in structure, movement abilities gating locations and a really fun map to connect and unlock and all of that stuff.A great 8/10 game that feels like somebody is just having a great time making games that feel great to play and have cute art without trying to blow the walls offI think this is my favorite genre of game, the "cute and fun and nobody would write a novel about it they'd just play it while smiling but sometimes it's still a little hard" genre. More games like this one!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty great 10+ hours long relaxoidvania. World exploration is getting better and better as you progress in game. Combat, movement, art, sound - I simply can't name a single aspect of the game that would stand out as silky smooth, as each single detail in this game is polished to perfection. The game is very forgiving, meaning you won't be losing progress upon dying. (Nice detail - there are "challenge rooms" in this game and failing them won't even require you to re-enter the room for it to reset). Yet despise relaxed pace some aspects can be really challenging and definitely won't bore you by difficulty being too low. Definitely worth the price and your attention.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I am not one for sweeping generalizations, but if you don’t play this game you are a fool.It’s relaxing, cozy, perfectly balanced for players of average skill, and has a wonderful soundtrack.Controls are superb - tight and responsive, you know exactly where you will land and always have full control on all of your actions.Combat is satisfying - perhaps just a tad too heavy on the bullet dodging mechanic, but always fair and fun.Bosses are a lot of fun, and this is coming from someone who despises boss fights - you always get a checkpoint right before the arena, and the patterns are easy to memorize.Level design is a bit peculiar - there is no verticality! You move up and down, in addition to left and right, but you never have to climb up or down. It’s not inherently a good or a bad thing- just an interesting design choice.Really, can’t recommend this game highly enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly the most fun I've had playing a game in a long time. Much appreciation to the developer!Perfect balance of chill / interesting game play, I played on hard difficulty which I felt was just right as the bosses weren't a pushover and required some thought but weren't frustratingly difficult.Took me about 9 hours to finish the game with *most* collectables. Probably around 10 or 11 hours to 100%, haven't had a chance to try out the boss rush mode though.Extremely cute/10. Totally worth the full price!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: The Thompson brothers have made another brilliant metroidvania, just as good if not better than Islets. This is such a joy to play and explore the beautifully rich world full of superbly crafted characters and environments, with great dialog, amazing music and some interesting quests. Combat is well balanced and I love that the bosses have health bars, so you get a good idea if you're ready for them or might need to swap out your items or upgrade. 10/10 from me!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. It ticks almost all of my boxes. I just love little guys who swing their meele weapon and get to explore a beautiful vast interconnected world. I also like how it's pretty chill on the normal difficulty, so I can play after work. But the bossfights were still fun and somewhat challenging. My only unfullfilled desire is that I preferr my metroidvanias more non-linear as it adds replayability for me, and this one was pretty linear up until the last areas. Maybe, that's why the shuffle mode was a bit underwhelming - you can't randomise the abilities or you won't be able to progress, and even upgrade points and cats aren't randomized. And I don't think that randomizing just upgrades and special attacks matters enough to create a different experience.And a separate appreciation message for the developer rather than his game. For a single dev, this is an insanely good work and I love how Kyle is engaged with the community, responding to posts and bug reports on Reddit and just being an active member of the community. I'll definitely look forward to his next works!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably my favourite indie game, challenged only by Hollow Knight, and one of my favourite games full stop. The art is gorgeous, the music is charming, the world feels like it goes on forever, the combat is simple yet unbelievably satisfying, the enemy and boss design works flawlessly, with an emphasis on a bullet hell style of combat, the list goes on and on. This is a criminally underrated title, and I would love to see it gain more appreciation in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Story / Writing / MusicI'm going to lump these aspects of the game together, as they are all very well done as standalone design components. Combined, they are even stronger. I enjoyed that the characters and writing were comical and lighthearted against a backdrop that, for any pet owner, goes a little deeper if you want it to. The soundtrack was an easy 11/10.Art DesignAgain here, beautiful game. By the time I'd seen every biome, some of the environmental designs did start to blend together a little bit.Combat / PuzzlesI have over 200 games in my STEAM wishlist. I don't have the attention span for every game I play to be a Souls-like endeavor (which has been a trend for some recent Metroidvania games). With that in mind, I liked that this game had what I would call 'mild difficulty' in terms of its overall challenge. I died a few times to a few different bosses before I learned their move sets, but never to the point of extreme frustration. The puzzles and locked areas all worked fairly well with the exception of curses, which I'll touch on below.Technically speaking, I did find combat was somewhat simplistic. Some cool moves related to movement (like leaving a trail of spikes when boomerang dashing) didn't really seem to incorporate fluidly into the combat system (at least for me) due to the time necessary to charge up the boomerang attack. Most fights boiled down to how fast I could smash X on my controller while dashing out of the way of projectiles. Ultimately, for this game, I did think that felt fine. Still, it left some of the abilities feeling a bit unnecessary.I didn't play boss rush mode. That's not really my thing, so I can't review that at all.Nit-Picks / RecommendationsCurses should disable fast-travel and result in a slight bump in enemy density. It was a little too easy to simply fast-travel back to the easiest area of the map to knock out curse-kills without there being much risk. However, it was also sometimes difficult to find nearby enemies, quickly, to knock out the curse.It wasn't clear what button I was supposed to press to exit certain in-game menus. For example, when purchasing map markers, I'm still not sure what button backs me out of that dialog (without my character performing a jump or a special attack).The game needs a 'Story-Mode' difficulty setting and/or clearer parameters around 'Easy' mode. I bumped the game down to Easy for my seven-year-old and honestly, we couldn't really tell that big of a difference from Normal mode. Getting hit still deducts a single armor node (and there were still projectiles flying in all directions).I'd highly recommend this game to pretty much anyone. At worst, it might come across as slightly too easy and/or repetitive for gamers with highly upgraded gaming chairs.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: What a delightful game! Crypt Custodian is an adorable evolution of Kyle Thompson's previous projects (Sheepo and Islets). Like those games, it has a cute art style, typical Metroidvania elements (unlocking new areas by finding abilities, etc.), and a wholesome story (your "sword" is actually a broom, and your goal is to befriend the various quirky characters you meet). But Crypt Custodian has a different perspective, literally, in that it shifts from the typical side-on view of most Metroidvanias to the more top-down RPG-style view from games like the Legend of Zelda or TUNIC.I completed the game 100% in about 11 hours (although I did look online for a hint to a specific late-game puzzle), which is about the same amount of time I spent on Islets but Crypt Custodian feels like the bigger game. I'm perfectly happy with my 11-hour experience, but there's unlockable post-game content for people who want more, including a boss rush mode and a remixed story mode.I've thoroughly enjoyed the game, just as I enjoyed Kyle's previous projects.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game. A classic metroidvania, doesn't really have unique features or anything, but excels in the core fundamentals of the genre. Gameplay and combat is not hard, but feels smooth overall. The heartwarming story is pieced together nicely. It's not a long game, I 100% my first playthrough in about 12hrs. Still, this is definitely a game that I would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect on the Deck.I think I like this one more than Islets. It still has the charming graphic style, but this time it's a little bit more difficult. This comes down to low HP and some nice bosses. Still not sold on the music. You may be lost here and there, but you can buy markers in a shop to show you where to go next. A lot of options with the upgrade system, not that much in terms of gameplay, but it's a short ride anyway. Looking forward to the next game.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute mix of a top down metroidvania with some Zelda influences. Very pretty to look at and all the music are bangers/cozy. Easy to understand combat that is not too difficult, and challenging but fair parkour. It does nothing really new but everything it does is solid. Large expansive map and some post game. Loved all the characters. They were used sparingly and i would have personally liked there was more progression in the interactions, they have a set dialogue for each area they are in and no matter what point you are in the story they same the same things. Encountered no bugs or crashes which is fantastic for such a small team. Please give this a go if you like this style of game, this one is definitely one of the easier ones, but i also played on normal, so Hard mode might be difficult? Dunno i'm not a hardcore gamer, i'm a newbie trying things out. Also works perfectly fine on steam deck. My entire playthrough was played on mine.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVED THIS GAME!!!!!! It was a total blast! Normal felt actually normal, good for a semi-casual semi-serious gamer, very balanced. The boss fights were all unique and super satisfying to fight and defeat, and fighting all of the enemies along the way never got old. It was great to explore new areas, always felt nice! I totally recommend this one! 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really excellent little game. From the art direction to the gameplay, everything is cohesively and intuitively designed. It offers exciting moments and a few tricky challenges, as well as an atmosphere that's charming and cute but also offers moments of wistful melancholy, helped by the great artstyle and soundtrack. I'm a fan of the Metroidvania genre, and though in this perspective it also becomes something of a bullet hell game at times, I enjoyed pretty much everything it had to offer. I continuously wanted to keep exploring the areas and pushing through to the next one. I have nothing but praise for all the QOL and anti-frustration features, including ways to not accidentally fall of ledges and to round up any random missed items in the endgame. My only complaint is that remapping a few buttons led to mostly wrong prompts, and that I can't experience more of the creator's vision.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so... First time I make a review of a game but I had to do one for this game.It's a simple metroidvania. Simple in a good way. There a tones of little ideas from upgrades to vania power, through special attacks.The gameplay might not feel new for everyone, but it's really well made and executed!The controls are really simple and straight forward, that makes it easy to handle and master.Difficulty might a tiny bit simple but I think I played in "Normal" difficulty if I remember correctly, and I'm kinda experienced of this kind of games (80+ hours on Hades, finished Hollow Knight true ending and working on The Rogue Prince of Persia gives some training ahahah)The art direction is really cute. Simple again, but works great.Enemies are recognizable, bosses are funny, friends are lovely <3The music works great too! So chill and viby.That makes me connect with the narrative, because the music and how the story is told are kinda chill. All friendly characters (despite Kendra...) they all just seem lovable at worse ahahah.But the story itself sad as hell. I lost my cat 2 years ago, just before he turned 2 y.o.I consider him as my own son and it was really devastating to me.So seeing Pluto's story really resonated with me.You can only be empathic for him and all his friends.Kyle, Eric, a big thank you for this game.That's been a while since a game had such a grip on me, emotionaly.I loved it, it's a gem in all the MV games we can see around there, always so dark... you're showing to everyone that you can make a game with simple mechanics (again that's not an insult, even the contrary, god it's difficult to keep it simple) well realized and in a feel good yet dramatic setting, which are two style that quite opposites themselves most of the time.Thanks again, I can't wait to see your next game (in 2 years? ^^) and before that I'll take a look at the previous ones.Take care and please continue to make games!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: A clever sense of charm, wit and whimsey elevate this metroidvania above most others in the genre.The combat and exploration isn't out of this world difficult, leaving breathing room for players to just enjoy the adorable characters and vibrant varied areas the world has to offer. Absolute blast from start to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Crypt Custodian is a cute game where you play as a cat in the afterlife. You meet fun and adorable characters which you can befriend. If you like games where you need to explore a map, this game is for you. The map is quite big, and it is nice that each area has its own theme and enemies.
