Ever since i found this dev's second game (islets) i started searching for more similar games and then i heard about this game releasing i knew i had to try it it. 10\10 did not disappoint. (will definitely try the first game one day)
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a gem.It's cozy, and I found it to be on the easy side, but that doesn't matter because the fights, the exploration, the puzzles, the collecting, and even the story were incredibly engaging and fun. I'm not huge into metroidvanias, but this was right up my alley. I love that there's so many options to make things easier or more challenging (the optional ability to buy a hint for where to go feels ingenious), and the inclusion of a randomizer mode and boss rush is great. I can't wait to watch the speedrunning scene.A really cute, really fun, refreshing spin on the genre. Well worth my money and my time. Looking forward to checking out Kyle Thompson's other games now, too.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: You should play this game. Crypt Custodian is the third game from Kyle Thompson, and his best work yet, surpassing the already-fantastic Islets which is well loved in the Metroidvania community.With gorgeous design, great combat and platforming, charming and distinct zones, a plethora of enemies, abilities and upgrades, Crypt Custodian is an absolute delight to play from start to 100%. Kyle's sense of charm, humour and wit is found frequently throughout the game, interspersing challenging combat encounters and bosses with bursts of joy when interacting with the characters that inhabit the world. The music is produced by Kyle's brother and perfectly meshes with the game's style, the boss theme in particular really gets you in the right mood for a great fight.If you're comfortable with this kind of game, definitely play it on Hard, it's never excessively challenging so the difficulty bump shouldn't bring you any grief but will let you see the game in its best form.I rarely if ever give games 10/10, but I can think of nothing I'd improve, Kyle's truly made a masterpiece and one he should be incredibly proud of.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I went into Crypt Custodian slightly skeptical of the top-down Metroidvania concept, but it more than delivered. Being able to jump over enemy attacks made the fights more dynamic and rewarding, being able to warp between save points from the get-go is amazing QoL, and it was so very refreshing for the traversal powers to break the mold instead of being the standard set of "double jump, super-dash, and ground-pound."10/10, screw Kendra all my homies hate Kendra
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Another absolute treat from Kyle Thompson.  I've been looking forward to Crypt Custodian since it was announced, and it delivered what I had hoped for and more.  A fun metroidvania romp around an interesting, expansive map; fun, fluid and quick movement mechanics; interesting and motivating collectibles and power-ups.  Combined with a charming art design (familiar if you've played Islets.. and you should!) and an excellent audio track - it's beautiful.  Playing Crypt Custodian, you can immediately tell the developer also enjoys this style of game.  He's put in so many thoughtful and quality of life details like fast travel, clever and satisfying puzzles, and interesting enemies that all teach you something important.  While there are plenty of unique elements to Crypt Custodian, I also appreciated the nods to and influence from other recent giants of the genre, in particular Hollow Knight and the Ori series.  The "Grubfather" nod was especially fun.  :)If you enjoy metroidvanias, you owe it to yourself to play Crypt Custodian.  Worth it at full price!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I put this one up there with the Momodora games, Hyper Light Drifter, Dustforce, and Child of LIght. 10/10 indie game considering it was just one guy that did pretty much the whole thing except the music.My nitpick is that the floating platforms tiled backgrounds gets a smidge samey after a while. I love pretty much everything else about it. Story, music, gameplay, animation, style are all excellent. Especially love the little in-game hint system that makes me feel like I don't have to go looking stuff up online if I get stuck. 👍

_childDocuments_.review: Still not done but 17 hours in and around 8 bosses defeated (and i believe there is between 10 and 12, excluding mini bosses and challenges). _childDocuments_.review: Crypt Custodian is the new game from Kyle Thompson, an Indie dev that's become a staple for me. Similar to Sheepo and Islets (If you've not played these, check them out) Crypt Custodian is a Metroidvania with a charming style and a lighthearted adventure (Albeit being about death). You take on the role of Pluto the cat, tasked with cleaning up the afterlife. Along the way meeting a variety of characters throughout an expansive world. Unlike the devs prior games, this one is 3D and plays more akin to games like Death's Door and Bastion, albeit with a bit more metroidvania elements. You'll be jumping, dodging and swinging around as you progress through the game collecting abilities and making friends along the way. Like Islets, there's a great feel to the overall gameplay, especially as you get more abilities. There could be some minor improvements here and there such as the charge speed of a specific ability but overall it's very polished. The world is intricately designed with varying areas and unique mechanics, enemies and such for each. The game is quite open in terms of pathing as you will typically find areas branching off in different directions. This can lead to shortcuts, upgrade points, skills or collectables. There's a tonne to find and the map is huge with a lot of secrets hidden around too. In terms of visuals and sound design the game is yet again a step above the devs prior work. The soundtrack is decent as are the sfx but the main improvement lay in the visual design of the game. Sheepo to Islets was quite the jump and now Crypt Cartographer which looks fantastic. The devs games always have this great charm to them and this one is no different. The writing also remains on par for the prior games with some great moments of humour and engaging characters. All in all it's another great title from the dev and one well worth checking out if you enjoy action adventure games or metroidvanias (And if you enjoyed this, check out their other games too)
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I hardly ever 100% games. I play them to credits, try and complete as much as I can along the way to credits, and then move on. That wasn't enough for this game, however. I felt compelled to go back and find every memory, skill, disc, everything available until I hit 100% completion. I enjoyed every minute over my 16 hour playtime. Kyle Thompson has become a can't-miss developer and he'll get my money with every title he puts out! Play this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: It's a game where you play as a cute cat beating up garbage and garbage monsters while making friends along the way. Nothing bad to say. Fun gameplay, good music, didn't run into any bugs, playing through on normal wasn't too tough or easy. Definitely worth picking up if it looks like something you'd be interested in.

_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: One of the standout features of "Crypt Custodian" is its richly crafted narrative. The story unfolds gradually, with compelling lore and mysterious characters that draw you deeper into the game’s world. The attention to detail in the storyline makes every discovery feel significant, adding layers of depth to your quest.Additionally, the game’s sound design deserves special mention. The eerie soundscapes and haunting melodies perfectly complement the visual experience, enhancing the overall atmosphere and making the crypts come alive (in more ways than one!).In summary, "Crypt Custodian" is a gem in the world of dungeon exploration games. Its combination of stunning visuals, engaging gameplay, and captivating story makes it a must-play for anyone seeking an adventure that is both thrilling and thought-provoking. Prepare to lose yourself in the depths of the crypt and enjoy every moment of it!

_childDocuments_.review: a rather quick game, but it's super sweet and fun all the way through, and doesn't stretch out its welcome. you might not know where to go next at times, but i think that's okay, you'll find the way eventually, i got 80% completion in hard difficulty without little to no time spent searching for goodies.my only criticism is performance/optimization, i repeatedly got super slow frames for extended periods (especially in certain environments), without my 4070M ever feeling the need to throw the fans on super sonic. don't know if the problem was integrated graphics being used (i hope that was not the case) anyway, that was definitely annoying.definitely worth the modest price for what it is. a warm thank you to the devs for a great time is in order.

_childDocuments_.review: This top-down Hollow Knight had some immense charm with its bittersweet story, satisfying combat, and snappy movement options. With a power behind every new area, you are always incentivised to explore and expand your map.This was an unexpectedly fun title to play and would highly recommend to any platform enjoyer.Also Pluto's massive eyeballs as a kitten? 9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: This game is terrific. It's not super long (you could probably rush through in less than 10 hours, or take more like 15 to get 100% in game, not including the boss rush achievements). But I definitely feel like I got my money's worth.It's full of great animation, clever writing, and some actual tender dialogue. But the dialogue is sparing, so don't expect a JRPG where you'll be paging through hours of conversations. But through the photos and their captions, I found I actually connected with the characters and sometimes got the feels.I found the platforming to not be too difficult, and the puzzle elements were interesting but infrequent. Overall, I found the combat to be more challenging than these types of games typically are. While not approaching soulslike levels of difficulties, you really do need to do more than just button mash. Even "low level" enemies can kill you if you just try to blindly rush in and kill them (at least until near endgame levels of upgrades). Likewise, the bosses definitely require you to pay attention to their attacks and time your counterattacks.All in all, this is another great game by Kyle Thompson. I very much enjoyed Islets, but this is a step up. I'll certainly be on the lookout for his next game.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute little Metroidvania. Not as big as the likes of Hollow Knight, but the map still keeps on expanding hours after you expected it to stop. Beautiful art and banger music combined with maybe  movement and combat system I've ever played. Super snappy and smooth, makes for some very fun boss fights. Luckily this game also has a very engaging boss-rush mode, even if it's not built into the universe like the Pantheons are in HK.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Stellar. Features fluid and fun gameplay, a well designed and interconnected map, a wide variety of upgrades, great progression, stylish graphics, charming characters, a variety of well designed bosses, and a good difficulty curve.As a bonus, some minor sequence breaks and glitches are possible - but only the kind that benefit you and make you feel cool. No jank I encountered ever prevented the game from progressing, the level of polish and robustness in the overall design seems almost off the charts.For downsides, um...A little light on story I suppose, and maybe the music could have been a bit punchier?? It tended a little more ambient and some bolder choices may have been able to further differentiate the areas.Overall 10/10, probably the best game I've played in 2024 so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutly wonderful game. It is fun to play and the story makes me kind of cry (in kind of a good way, very good story telling without much tamtam). Do not recommend if you've recently lost your cat (especially if it was black), as it will leave you on the floor as a miserable mess.Love this game

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! I'm a huge fan of Islets and Sheepo, and couldn't wait for this to come out - so many interesting tweaks and new details that make the gameplay more enjoyable, all while keeping the Islets/Sheepo vibe intact! And as always, the music is amazing! (...thank you for keeping the jump sound the same - I'm also pretty sure there's statues that pay homage to the previous games, tee hee)
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this demo and am happy to have purchased the game.  I head a reviewer comment this game wants you to complete it and I 100% agree.  I was able to 100% the game (100% the game/map, not Steam achievements) on my first playthrough on easy mode.  I was able to enjoy the story without feeling so overwhelmed it stopped being fun.With the exception of a few timing/jumping puzzles I never really struggled with the game.  I also wasn't constantly running to YT to figure out what to do.Overall I really enjoyed it and yes, I played on easy but there are harder modes for those who want more of a challenge and even has a 'speed runner' mode that I believe skips cutscenes for you?This was well worth the price and I had a lot of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Great story, music, puzzles, and boss fights. I especially appreciate the boss rush mode to go and relive those cool fights. Nothing not to love here if you enjoy metroidvanias. My only nitpick would be the final bit of story involving a puzzle with some cat statues. It doesn't feel very in line with how the game has handled puzzles up to this point and the presentation doesn't, in my opinion, provide enough of a hint as to what the player must do to solve it. If this were purely completionist content I probably wouldn't care, but since it is the final piece of the story I don't think it should be something quite as complex to solve. TL;DRHighly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: A really good metroidvanian game that tugged my heart strings. I greatly enjoyed playing this game, the puzzling. I also always love when games allow you to change between easy/normal/hard at any time throughout the game because I suck at the speed challenges and I was able to switch to easy just for those, good looking out for accessibility!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Great visuals, catchy music, a very sweet story and... surprisingly difficult! I'm not ashamed to admit that I suck at this genre of game. But man, sometimes the barrage of enemies and then having to find my way back to where I was got annoying. I wouldn't consider that a bad thing though. Sometimes you have to get frustrated to get that sweet release of serotonin. I think if this catches your eye then you should play it! Even with the back tracking, this game is pretty forgiving.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: New metroidvania from Kyle Thompson (Sheepo, Islets). As always, it has cute artstyle and characters, very satisfying movement, and a diverse world. While it's longer that the previous games, it still doesn't overstay its welcome, and remains engaging all the way to 100% completion. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: i'm not too far into this game and honestly haven't found anything to complain about yet, but i have many thoughts and feelings so far. the short version: 10/10, it would thrill me to no end to see this game get more attention because it was clearly made with a lot of love and care and it deserves all the success it gets. the long version:
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: fun cute solid top down metroidvania. Recommend. You play as a ghost cat and make ghost animal friends and help them with their personal problems. The trash mobs are literal trash and you beat them up with a broom. Beautiful interesting environments with new exploration mechanics in each area. Good QoL map features for tracking items and routes to return to later. Post game rewards with options for ferreting out uncollected items on the expansive map. I played on Normal and finished in ~10 hours. If you're experienced in this genre go for Hard. Lots of fun upgrades to discover and experiment with. The NPCs have fun personalities.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Another great game after Islets and Sheepo, now with a new perspective! Lovely level design that loops around itself, Combat that is fun/snappy and fun characters along your adventure! If there are any negatives here then it's the power ups, often they feel more like keys than switching your perspective how to navigate the world. Also really fun bosses, but they are quite a lot more difficult than the rest of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this developer's previous title and was excited to try this game out, too. Similarly to Islets, this game is fairly straightforward, but it still manages to accomplish what it sets out to do. It's a Zelda-like with an emphasis on melee combat and simple puzzles; it's not that hard, but not boring, either. Overall, I think if you like hack 'n slash games and want a casual title in the genre, you should try both this and the developer's last game.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend this game. If you have played the developers' previous games you can see a real progression of skill and ambition as each title has built on the previous in every way. Lots of special attacks, power ups for customizing play style and responsive gameplay. The art style is very cute with a large cast of critter npc's to befriend. There is even a randomizer and boss rush mode to unlock if that is your cup of tea.If you have a pet that you love dearly, or are a lover of animals in general, be ready to play this game with a box of tissues cause you will be bawling by the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: this is simply a good game. amazing dialogue, good mechanics. the art style is impeccable. thank you kyle thompson i hope you continue to make more games like this. I loved islets and I loved crypt custodian even more. i may have shed a tear at the end too...but i have a real soft spot for kitty cats
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Crypt Custodian is a very charming take on the Metroidvania genre. Everything just works fine: the game world is vast and fun to explore, the platforming sections are tricky but never frustrating, the challenge level is reasonable (I played and completed the game on hard) and the art style is very colourful and pleasant to the eye.I'm definitely looking forward to the Thompsons' next projects. In the meantime, I guess I need to play Islets...
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a amazing! The beautiful art and smooth, responsive gameplay make exploration and combat a joy. While it's on the easier side, it remains enjoyable all the way to the end. The well-paced progression unlocks fresh areas and secrets, and  atmosphere are captivating. It also runs great on Steam Deck, even though it's not marked as verified. A must-play for fans of the genre!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: A sweet metroidvania, feels great to play. The 2.5d perspective sets it apart from other metroidvanias I've played in the past, and added a nice dose of platforming challenge along with the combat. Other mechanics are standard; finding new abilities, buffs, and mementos, trying out different combinations, and amassing new platforming abilities as you go. I really enjoyed exploring the map, and being able to warp between checkpoints made it so doubling back never really felt like a chore. I also super appreciate when a game has mechanics to nudge you toward items you missed. the characters and setting are all very cute, the game has a cozy feel. But Kendra is NOT my friend
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Game has very similar art style to Islets, and equally, if not more, charming friends to meet along the way. Soundtrack is pretty nice and mostly chill.You can choose difficulty from the start (which basically just changes attack patterns) and change later if you want, as well as additional options for extra attack damage and extra health if the default settings are too difficult.  I just go normal but the option is nice.Game is not too difficult in normal difficulty. I could beat most bosses in 3-5 tries, which I think is appropriate for a mid-difficulty setting. I was able to 100% a normal difficulty file in 10ish hours casually for my first run, so the game is a little on the shorter side if that's what you prefer.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Not finished yet but I'm loving the combat and exploration in this game. The music is lovely and I look forward to meeting all the characters. The game is not super stressful even on Hard - it's still challenging enough but there's no stakes to dying which personally is a great quality-of-life improve for me. In general the game has a ton of really nice features that make playing and traversing throughout the world such a pleasant experience! Highly recommend for all metroidvania enthusiasts!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little metroidvania. It has a nice exploration feel for it, not too difficult to find everything. Playing on hard, most of the boss fights felt reasonably difficult for me (typically had to fight once to get a feel for tempo). Towards the end, the last couple bosses I fought felt more like a button mash "kill before I die" thing though, where Grief in particular felt like I couldn't dodge attacks. Overall though, I think it was a fun game, worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't seen such an enjoyable metroidvania in a long time. I like the atmosphere. The plot is simple, but pleasurable. Some moments invoke the feeling of touching melancholy and sweet sadness.The gameplay is just as nearly flawless. Backtracking is quite convenient and not time consuming. Map is convenient to use, and you can buy items that will mark missed things on the map.I sincerely recommend the game to all fans of the genre... And cats ^_^
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: It has been lovely watching each Kyle Thompson game become more ambitious than the last.  The controls feel smooth and intuitive.  Bosses are fun and well designed.  There are different difficulty options that you can change at any time and you can adjust the difficulty even more based on what abilities you equip.  It was a joy to play and I'd recommend it to anyone that likes Metroidvania games with a more relaxed vibe.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I'm an old gamer and a fan of this author after the last Islets project, because I don't like over-complicated metroidvania for pain and suffering (which is a lot nowadays), and prefer nice entertaining gameplay and a spirit of fun adventure.Both Islets and Crypt Custodian do a wonderful job with that. It's a very cute and enjoyable world with cool and fun characters. These are worlds that are nice to just be in. P.S. I'll add a small request from myself: if possible, leave the option of very low difficulty, because it distinguishes your projects from others - just explore and enjoy. Islets I passed with my girlfriend (not a gamer), also I gave it to my son and he passed it. Unfortunately, Crypt Custodian already they both found it too difficult even on low difficulty. I realize that your main audience is probably more oriented to more complex gameplay, but I think there is a niche for less experienced players who like your universe.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely fun and enjoyable metroidvania. Not excruciatingly difficult or too hand-holdly, but actually a nice middle ground with adorable characters and such a nice hand-crafted vibe to the whole experience. The mechanics introduced throughout the game are fun, the backtracking is lessened by the teleport system on the map, and the whole upgrade system isn't too grindy either. Overall, it's just a really fun and laid back take on the genre and it's definitely worth picking up if you want to not tear your hair out with boss timings and hours of backtracking.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy and cute metrodvania with some light bullet hell mechanics. The game feels great to play, very responsive controls, cute visuals with distinct themes for each area, funny dialogue, and some great music! Took me about 10 hours to complete 100%. I started the game at Normal which felt quite easy for the genre, so don't be afraid to turn up the difficulty if you're cool.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Great metroidvania, very cool map, nice exploration, interesting movement, good bossfights and very touching story. Difficulty is a quite a bit on the easy side, but also very even, no spikes or slumps in it, so it feels pretty good. My only complaint would be having ability to teleport to any checkpoint at any time, which makes all the cool map connections and shortcuts a bit useless. But that also makes clearing the map after main story a lot less tedious. Maybe there's a great solution somwhere in between having teleport at all times and not at all. After Islets and Crypt Custodian Kyle Thompson is definitely becoming one of the noticably important indie devs on my list because of unique art style and storytelling and great understanding of how to make an enjoyable metroidvania. Definitely looking forward to the next game!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked the story and enjoyed the game play. I did appreciate that they built in the ability to dynamically adjust the difficulty in various ways under the accessability menu. I also liked that they did make an in-game method for locating hidden items that's easily used towards the end of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. I 100% completed the story mode in about 10 hours, and I had so much fun I did it in 3 sittings. The map shows you which areas you haven't ventured into yet, and that just kept me wanting to explore every inch of the world, even when I should have probably stopped to go to bed. The music is wonderful and peaceful when you aren't fighting the big spooky bosses, and the art style is lovely. It was a great package all together. I didn't get all the achievements because the last 3 require you to play boss rush mode, and I do not care about speed running.  Also runs perfectly on steam deckSolid 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game that provides an engaging challenge on its hard mode. This kind of quasi isometric view brings such a fresh view to metroidvanias. The game is very charming, the movement and combat is tight, and the game respects the player's time on a higher level than a lot of metroidvanias. I really do think there's something for everyone interested in metroidvanias here.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game - great music. It had me often thinking of watching Adventure Time.Definitely not overly challenging. I started on hard and completed the play through at 100% in little over 13 hours.The only achievements I didn't try for were the boss rush mode stuff.Highly recommend the game for - story,  music, mechanics, and approach play.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet metroidvania. The art style is quite pleasant, and there is a decent variety of locations with their own themes and gimmicks. However, pretty much all the space in the game is platforms floating in the air, so that hurts the diversity of levels somewhat. The combat and platforming, while simplistic and not too challenging, are fast and fluid, and control very nicely, I particularly liked that you could do a lot with jumps rather than only relying on dodges. The writing is a bit of a letdown. Your animal friends are sure cutesy, but not much developed as characters. And the way the game is structured, the plot doesn't move for 90% of playtime, barring a short introduction and ending. The music is alright, I was neither impressed nor put off. While this may not be a glowing review, I enjoyed my time with Crypt Custodian, and wouldn't hesitate to recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Mastapiece.Kyle Thompson's games are the among the very few that I ever 100%, because it never feels like a chore, and is just delightful the whole way through. Love seeing interpretations of the Metroidvania genre in perspectives other than just 2D/2.5D sidescrollers. We now have some very definitive proof that top-down MVs are sick with Crypt Custodian, along with Minishoot' Adventures and Unsighted.The fact that Kyle has blessed us tf up with 3 incredible games since 2020 is insane, especially with the gradual increase in scope. Really excited to see where it goes from here!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I have 100% this game. It was a really fun time. The pacing is phenomenal. You are regularly receiving upgrades or new power ups that let you explore previously inaccessible areas. The music is wonderful. It's got heavy lo-fi vibes. The story almost brought a tear to my eye. I really enjoyed this game. I'd love to see DLC or a second installment.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I loooove this game. It is super cute because cat. I am still technically still playing it (trying to 100% it) but the story and game play is really neat. If you liked Hollow Knight you will love this! It is the same style, but a little less confusing and more streamlined in my opinion. It also reminds me of the story driven of EASTWARD.  I played on normal and I loved the challenge. The bosses can be a little unforgiving but overall just enough practice, you will beat it. It had taken me quite awhile to beat the bosses, but I am glad I didn't play it on easy. I would honestly love a part 2 of this game, but I know once I 100% it, it will be over.  Either way it is a great cute game with puzzles, cute stories, challenging boss fights, cute characters, and lastly, sad moments! It is about death.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so much fun to play, if you enjoy games like Hollow Knight you are going to really love this one. With all the interesting upgrades and mechanics I have been keeping very busy exploring every inch of the maps, finding collectables and fighting off tons of unique monsters.The difficulty of each area seems to ramp up in a super manageable and not overwhelming manner and really helps me get a feel for each unique monsters move set, and they are easy to memorize with the helpful signals as well.I am so eager to see where this story goes as I feel there are still many secrets to uncover, and I'm so happy and excited to keep playing!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Islets and this game has improved on it in basically every way.There's a lot of good stuff going on here. Atmosphere is on point. The ambient soundtracks are lovely, with a lot of emotion behind them and each one matching its environment perfectly. On the visual side, we have the same cozy art style from Islets. It looks great and has a nice level of background detail + special effects (like raindrops on the water).Gameplay is excellent. I love love loooove the way the QoL features are integrated right into the game. The way that the enemy moves are telegraphed is a masterclass in game design, and it works great given the relatively fast pace of combat as the game goes on. Combat is a good level of difficulty and it's interesting how the lack of heals plays into this. It's not particularly deep, but it feels balanced and interesting. The movement mechanics and platforming challenges are fun although fairly basic (as of 50% completion).Area variety is fairly good; it gets much better as the game goes on (the first 2-3 areas are a bit monotonous IMO). The neon area is my favorite so far due to the creative way it leverages the dash mechanic. The demon park area was also a cool concept that I hadn't seen in the genre before. I'm not sure exactly how non-linear this game is, but it definitely opens up after the ~20% mark giving you a few different areas to choose from. I'm at about 50% right now and still have at least 3 different areas that are open to me which I haven't explored.The story also feels nicely balanced - it's easily digestible and filled with a small cast of likeable and quirky characters. The overarching goal of the game is pretty clear and it's also a fun one. I like the way that you learn more about characters by collecting their pictures, and it all ties into the setting in a kind of melancholy way given how sweet most of them are.All in all, greatly enjoying this game. Would recommend to any fans of Islets or MVs with a 50/50 combat/exploration focus.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely charming and interesting metroidvania with a super cute art style and a lovable cast of characters. Combat does exactly what it needs to and the accompanying boss fights and platforming challenges are just challenging enough without ever feeling unfair or frustrating. I did run into one minor bug where I managed to dash jump into a wall and get stuck (which I was easily able to get out of by teleporting to a nearby save point (and in fact I'm only mentioning this here because the dev requested people post any issues they run into here, so hey here ya go)), but other than that it's been an excellent way to spend my long weekend.(Also as a heads up, don't let the listed playtime fool you, I'm almost 12 hours in just from running around and soaking in the sights and wanting to get all the unlocks that I can, my play time just looks weird in Steam because I was bouncing back and forth from PC to Steam Deck. This likely doesn't matter but wanted to mention just in case. Game good though. Buy game. Play game.)
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: A game where you can play as a very bad cat. You can make graffiti with spray paint, break into a local palace, & hang out with delinquents.A simple, albeit charming Metroidvania. While not my favorite in the genre, I liked what this brought to the table enough to recommend if the trailer speaks to you.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Crypt Custodian is the first game in a long time that I’ve completed 100 percent, and that’s a testament to how much fun it is from start to finish. As a top-down Metroidvania, it brings a refreshing twist to the genre, and I wouldn’t be surprised if it inspires many more games like it in the future.The movement and combat are crisp and satisfying, making every encounter feel rewarding. Pair that with top-notch music and art, and you’ve got an indie title that really stands out. The story is also a sweet one, adding an extra layer of charm to the whole experience.If you’re a fan of Metroidvanias or just looking for a game that’s a joy to play from start to finish, Crypt Custodian is an absolute must-play!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: this games artstyle and music are absolutely gorgeous, plus the combat is great, i would strongly recommend giving this game a try. its far more than been worth it for me and i look forward to what kyle makes in the future.also you should check out islets too, another good game by the same dev, i actually learnt about crypt through islets and ive been waiting for it to release for months :)P.S. idk if kyle will see this since its just a review but if you do, you should really make the games soundtrack available to buy on here, i love it so much i would snatch that up right away

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic Metroidvania, I loved ever second of it. _childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Love the game so far. It's an interesting take on the metroidvania formula. I've only played for about 2 hours at the time of this review, and I only have one upgrade so far, but mechanically, the game feels good to play. The jump feels nice, and not floaty. The attacks are nice and snappy, and so is the dodge.The art is just gorgeous too, and I like the writing of the dialogue, and the story so far. _childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the demo I knew I was going to have fun with this game when it was released. For one, I really enjoyed the world and characters. I also liked how most of the powers you unlock as you progress the game actually have utility in both combat and traversing the levels. Although the combat was rather simple it never got old throughout my experience with the game. To anyone interested in getting into another short but sweet adventure, Crypt Custodian should be on your radar. I had a blast playing this game and I feel comfortable recommending it to others.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Not too far in yet but already amazed. Kyle may be my favorite developer as he seems to be the perfect example of what small team/single developers should strive for. Something doesn’t have to be complicated to be amazing. The guy has a unique flavor to his work but reinvents on his follow ups.Sheepo and Islets are works of art that each improved on the last. Crypt Custodian looks like it’s continuing the pattern. Don’t know what he will cook up next, but I know I’ll be a day one buyer of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Defy the god of the dead as you hack and slash- Ah, sorry.Crypt Custodian is another quality basically-Metroidvania from Kyle Thompson of Islets fame. Condemned to the worse side of the afterlife with a dubious justification, Pluto the cat sets out to make friends and clean up garbage, by way of exploring strange locations and battling even stranger creatures. Crypt Custodian uses an overhead view rather than the side-scrolling world of traditional Metroidvanias, but the feel is quite similar. Most of the runtime is devoted to exploring the world freely, gaining traversal abilities, equippable passive effects, and special moves, with the ultimate goal of befriending all the spectral inhabitants and pulling off a scheme together. Combat retains some elements from Islets, like non-recovering HP and the general shmup feel of enemy attack patterns. The writing as well has the same relaxed, deadpan humor to it. I don't think I should over-describe the game, though. I recommend trying it for oneself.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Crypt Custodian is a fun and charming metroidvania. I like the theme and setting and the characters you meet are all whimsical in their own way. If you've played the developer's prior game - Islets - you'll find a fair amount of similarities but it's also apparent that he has grown in skill and knowledge since that game. There are some really interesting abilities here and they interact with zones in different ways. My favorite is a dash that will phase enemies and objects in one area into or out of existence. Game seems to be about 8 hours long, probably a bit less if you wait for guides to be available as there were some points where I wasn't quite sure where to go next. I'd recommend playing the demo if you're interested, as that's a great sneak preview of the first half hour or so.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Writing this review after the first boss, so I’ll come back and edit it if things change, but I have such a good impression of this game already that I want to leave a review. This game is, so far, a relatively chill (but still somewhat challenging, on hard mode) top-down metroidvania with great movement, interesting mechanics, excellent art and animations, engaging dialogue, and surprisingly cute themes for a game called “Crypt Custodian.” It *just* came out and it already feels like it’s got a lot of polish.The most interesting part of the mechanics is the upgrade system, which lets you customize your mechanics directly, and gives you optional challenges (which you can complete for “Upgrade Points”, which let you equip upgrades; it’s a badge system). There doesn’t look to be *too* many, but there’s a good variety, and it seems like it’ll flesh out nicely as I progress through the game. The boss design is also interesting, with more stages than I expected, and some surprising attacks during some of them. I’m on vacation the next week and I’m gonna spend a lot of it playing this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: After playing Sekiro, I needed an easy game and this was a perfect palate cleanser, so I give it a thumbs up. The boss encounters can be a bit challenging, but if you learn the patterns and play patiently, they're not too hard. Normal enemies can be a bit spammy in some areas, but ignoring them and running through is always an option, except for certain group encounters. The game has a lot of accessibility features. Although I haven't tried them, they seem to allow any player, regardless of ability, to see the full game.The Metroidvania aspect of the game falls a little flat. The game, and the map in particular, does a good job of letting you know where you can and can't go. The marker system is almost over-engineered for the few places you might want to mark for later. The upside is that you never have to walk around aimlessly trying to figure out where to go next. The downside is that the game doesn't test your ability to navigate the world. I didn't mind, I'm not nostalgic for the old days of drawing my own map, but if you're looking for the kind of game where you'll get lost if you're not careful, this might seem very hand-holding.The story is straight out of a children's book. That's what it's meant to be, and it's tonally consistent. The characters are all friendly, hostility is always a misunderstanding and bad characters are misguided, not evil. It's very relaxed and light-hearted, and doesn't let the concept of death and the afterlife weigh it down, while still acknowledging the sadness of loss.Crypt Custodian is a fairly short game, in my 13.6 hours of play I got all the collectibles. This was a big plus for me, as I wanted a shorter and simpler experience. It told its story, showed me what it had and didn't overstay its welcome or insist upon itself. I would recommend this game to all but the hardcore Metroidvania players or people who hate Metroidvanias.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a little short even if the world seems big, less than 20 hours to complete. Game is a little to easy even on hard, a few bosses give a little bit of a challenge but the hardest section for me was a random "beat wave of enemies without taking a hit" section. A lot of deaths don't require you to back track very far which is nice but I think is one thing that makes the game shorter than it otherwise would be. Had a lot of fun but I'm glad I got it on sale and would recommend picking up anytime the game is on sale for under 10 or 15 dollars.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I played Sheepo and Islet upon release, and now am having a blast diving into Crypt Custodian. The change from a side view platformer to an isometric hack n slash is one that might make the first two games more appealing than this one, but I highly recommend giving it a try anyway if you liked the first two games Kyle Thompson made even if you're not a hack n slash person. This game is the best of Islet and then some. Thompson is one of those developers who keeps to a simple idea, but builds on it creatively and iteratively. I only just beat the first boss and I already love this game. Just like the other two he's made, i'm sure i'll 100% this one too. Thank you, Thompson, for your dedication to making these awesome games that I have loved and continue to love playing!!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: My new favourite Metroidvania of the summer. Cute art style, lots of accessibility options for the more casual player, incredibly charming writing and loads of fun. All in all it's definitely on the easier side (more Death's Door than Hollow Knight, difficulty-wise), but that hasn't stopped me from having a great time.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I did a 100% playthrough of this game, and it is a must-play if you are a fan of the metroidvania genre. While there may be some minor QOL changes needed, the released product is polished and well worth the money, especially considering this entire ~14 hour long game is made by one developer. Not to mention the wonderful soundtrack is made by the his brother as well. This duo never disappoints with any of their games, and this is no exception.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: PLEASE SPREAD WORD OF THIS GAME IT NEEDS MORE ATTENTIONCapital words aside, this game is super fun and charming.Great game design, both in enemies and characters. Cute dialog with somber moments mixed in. Great music.While it doesn't take too long to complete, too me 10 hours to 100%, i think for the price its plenty of game. Plus it comes with a ng+ type and boss rush too! The bosses are some of the most creative and engaging fights I've had in a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I'll admittedly say that I've been waiting for this game since I heard about it earlier this summer. It does not disappoint.A solid Metroidvania with intuitive (for me, at least) controls and a good balance of challenge vs. reward. I've enjoy the game play and progression and find the system of adding abilities engaging and fulfilling. Hard to say no to a fun game for ~$17.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: This game's gameplay is the closest any game has come to what I have envisioned as an aspiring gamedev. At first the animations in the trailer looked a bit clunky, but I saw the combat and thought to myself how similar this looked to something I want to cook, and man, I'm so grateful I catched that, this game is a blast gameplay-wise. The story 5 hours in is alright, not bad, not that good either, it's fine for me, the gameplay is the most important aspect. If you're on the fence like I was due to the somewhat clunky-looking animations, please give it a try, it feels so darn good and crispy to control the main character I ended up forgetting about it 2 hours in.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't finished it yet but it's awesome, you are a stray cat that ended up dead, and because you ended up being "bad" you are charged with cleaning the afterlife, the map is big, the abilities look good and you have map markers (crucial in MV)It's no that hard so you can chill out, bosses are very VERY forgiving, I've just beat the second one, hope it gets harder as the game progresses, but overall I enjoyed it a lot so far
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: How did I not know about this game? It's an absolute gem! Wonderfully charming world that Pluto inhabits with tons of personality. The controls are tight, game-play fun, and enemies challenging, but not over the top. It also has tons of accessibility extra's which help if you get totally stuck. Man am I glad I found it. Hope they get more publicity. I'll be telling all my buddies and family for sure!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I can recommend this game to anyone who likes good games. Long and interesting story, interesting puzzles (not easy but not hard), good bosses and a lot of them and they are different. Great artwork and level design. A bit sad story on photo cards, but it's life.So, I really enjoy playing it and want to find all collectibles. And you can buy upgrade that will show if room have any collectibles! That's great idea, I don't need to spent hours for searching them everywhere.Controls and enemy fighting feels fair and polished. You both feel relaxed on levels and some enemies and a bit tense on bosses.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Dev's recognizable style shines through again in a wonderful metroidvania that doesn't take itself serious but provides tons of entertainment. The controls and the gameplay is smooth, the difficulty just right and can be easily tweaked up or down (as you wish). It was a joy to explore pretty big map. There puzzles do not overstay their welcome and are a nice break from combat. Art style is gorgeous and the music is adorable and lackadaisical as it fits a game like this. I loved exploring every minute. I really liked that most mechanics are gradually introduced to you through puzzles, rather then being explained to you. I expected to find way to heal first few hours of the game, but quickly realized it is in vain. What you got is what you get between save point. It emphasizes evasion, learning patterns. Once you embrace it, it's even better. There were moments where I briefly felt things were repetitive, but it seemed like the dev could read my mind and usually the next screen would change things up. Didn't encounter any bugs, it's really well made and ton of fun. I liked the humor (as I did in the previous games by the same dev) but it may not be for everyone. There were a few boss intro scenes that I wish could be skipped, but they were only 4-5s so it's alright. The combat system could be more complex and/or provide for more variety. Certain abilities feel more useful for traversal than combat (feel clunky otherwise).I couldn't get enough and just kept coming back to it. Finished it except for the last achievement in roughly 11h. You can expect somewhere between 10-15h of content. Amazing metroidvania. Wish it was longer.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Everything I hoped for when I played through the demo! So many small, quality of life decisions that just make this such a fun casual game to play! My only gripe is a bit of repetition in enemy attack patterns, and a lack of difficulty for me personally, even on the "hard" difficulty (although props for making it actually have new content instead of just being more health more damage!Overall, would highly recommend for anyone who enjoyed games like death's door and wants a relaxed, fun experience to journey though.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece.Most importantly: movement and combat feels on point. Plus the map is huge and the graphic style is just gorgeous.It has a great mix of combat and exploring so it doesn't feel repetitive.Backtracking is actually made very easy; it's great it doesn't feel like a chore.Well done, Kyle!Thank you very much for such an amazing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I was anxiously waiting for this game! I played the demo and instantly fell in love! While waiting for the release, I completed the previous game (on Xbox) from the same author - Islets, which I highly recommend to everyone. Everything in it is brilliantly done, particularly the characters, they are superb, I haven't laughed so hard playing a game in quite some time!And now Crypt Custodian has been released, and I couldn't be happier. This game is incredibly awesome, a huge leap forward for the developers. It excels in every aspect - the combat, world exploration, art, music. It's all simply out of this world! And the signature humor is there too! If you're a fan of Metroidvania, don't miss out on this game, or else we risk losing such unique, stunning projects like this one. A huge thank you to the developers, I'm in love with your game!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I've played for about 3 hours now, but from what I've seen so far I have no doubt that I'd recommend this game. The art style and the music are really charming. The controls are snappy, and it feels great to move and fight with our kitty character. The map is pretty vast and there are different "biomes" with consequent variety of enemies. It's really a joy to explore. I wasn't too convinced that I would like playing with that camera angle, which is a bit uncommon for the genre, but after the first 15-30 minutes it grew on me. I can't say much about the story yet, but the premise and character I've seen so far seem interesting! Overall it's a pretty solid metroidvania at a more than fair price. Go get it!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely great top down metroidvania.  The map for this game is massive, and plentiful fast travel combined with a great map makes backtracking painless and fun.  Gameplay is tight and KBM controls are solid with the option to rebind.  It's hard to believe a dev team that is so small made something this polished and of this size.  Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Instant purchase and haven't regretted it.The only negative is related to the achievement “ Beat all bosses on S+ on all difficulty levels”. Ice Witch is an example of poor design. All of her attacks release a lot of random projectiles. On the hard difficulty level, not taking damage from her becomes a matter of luck rather than skill.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: A really nice game. Great music and cozy atmosphere, a simple but charming story.Also great character design and art.The controls felt good and responsive. Finished it in around 11 hours, collecting everything and it was good until the end. Didn't overstay its welcome.Highly recommended for some hours of fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I had a really good time with this game. Cute story, and fun game play. I don't believe I encountered a single bug during my playthrough.I played on Hard and it was still fairly easy, but not too easy to be boring. I would recommend starting there and turning down the difficulty if you don't like it or want something more casual.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely worth the price, especially if its on sale. artsyle and gameplay are amazing, the backstories of some characters are surprisingly morbid (in a good way), and the boss fights (on hard difficulty) are challenging yet not aggravatingIf you like this game, I'd highly suggest their other games.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: 1000000/10. This game is hands down one of the best games I’ve ever played. Story, gameplay, combat, originality…and cute animals! I cried. I laughed. I cried some more. The animals all have amazing little backstories and personalities that make you connect with them. My personal favorite outside of Pluto is Grizz. _childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Having played the previous game from these brothers, Islets, and thoroughly enjoying it, I eagerly awaited this game as soon as I heard of its announcement and put it at the top of my wishlist. And yeah, I can confidently say it exceeded expectations. I haven't had this much fun with an adventure/exploration game in ages.Combat: Amazingly smooth and very fun. Almost like a hack and slash. You have a special attack that needs to charge up by killing enemies, as well as a charm system reminiscent of Hollow Knight. The enemies all look great and behave very differently, and from what I have seen so far, the bosses are wonderfully designed.Exploration: Tonnes of collectibles like skill points, spirits, CDs and "charms" encourage you to explore. The map gives you 50 markers you can use to make note of places you can't reach or items you can't grab, so there's no worrying about forgetting things. Also, did I mention this map is VAST? I'm less than halfway through the game (48%) and I have already seen so much. Wetlands, gardens, a spectral void of spirits, abandoned amusement parks, technological towers... each area is entirely unique and so wonderfully distinct from each other. And I mustn't forget that you'll be making friends throughout the game, all very humorous. Oh yeah. And there's easy fast travel. No trudging across vast areas after dying in this game!Music: Eric Thompson delivers yet another banging soundtrack for this game. There are almost melancholy tracks like Lunar Lullaby and Something Strange, upbeat silly ones like Bar Song and The Palace, and chaotic ones like for boss themes and combat challenges. And tying back into exploration, you can actually find CDs around the game that play these tracks back at the "hub". Awesome!Length: I'm almost halfway through the game and have over 8 hours of playtime. Yeah, it's a great length.And of course, the game is pretty damn funny too.So in conclusion, if you loved Islets, play this game. If you love metroidvanias or really any adventure game, play this game. If you want a chill yet still challenging experience, play this game. Seriously, if you don't you'll really be missing out!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing this review a whopping  of all players have the "100% Complete" achievement. A real testament to how great of an experience this is.  Once you pick this game up its hard to put it down. The gameplay loop is exciting and rewarding especially if you love a classic metroidvania style with clever puzzles scattered along the way.  The combat and platforming are crisp and feel great.  If you liked Death's Door (most similar) or Tunic (CC has much simpler puzzles) you will love this game! 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: A fairly short and sweet metroidvania experience. It's nice to see a game that despite being created by a small team has all its core elements feel polished: battle mechanics, arcade challenges, platforming. Everything has a feeling of having been done well enough to have a good ol' chill and fun playthrough.The lore is lighthearted, with characters having a mostly cutesy childrens' book vibe that doesn't distract too much from having fun exploring the world.To name a few weak points: at times the game might feel like it's not sure of its own identity - moderately challenging bosses with strong bullet hell focus and notch-based (think Hollow Knight) abilities / passive bonuses, but the "update points" are fairly ubiquitous or can even be bought for a low set price, so there's no resource scarcity that would require mixing and matching different abilities and especially late-game can feel a bit pointless. That said, I was still captivated to keep going and the game is short enough for the above to never get tiring.

_childDocuments_.review: Not often do I come across a game with an art style so appealing that I become skeptical if the gameplay will hold up. Within minutes though, I absolutely fell in love with Crypt Custodian. Its gentle atmosphere becomes readily apparent from its calming title screen, that balances the morose curiosity of death with the onset of a spiritual journey, and even more so in its first tutorial level that has such a beautiful flooded ruins aesthetic that I wish I could steal it and make my entire Animal Crossing village mirror its splendor.The game never takes itself too seriously, but it doesn't undermine itself either and shrug off its premise like a lot of cozy/charming games do where they have to turn everything into a terse joke and refuse to put any heart into its premise. The nature of the many micro-stories you discover, via the friends you make in each zone, are uniquely grim as you find 3 photos that tell a quick tale of who these ghosts were in life, and what led to their ends, landing them in the afterlife just like you. But that sadness is offset by how warm and pleasant the spirits you interact with are, many of which are downright lovable within only a few dialogue boxes.Most of the game's content is focused on combat, which keeps things simple and satisfying. Zelda meets Hollow Knight feel like the main inspirations as you have hefty sword attacks (or I guess Broom attacks, in this case) with a particularly good feeling plunging jump attack and a very fluid dash attack. The Hollow Knight angle comes in the form of the dozens of equippable charms to modify your abilities and a magic meter that builds up from mopping up foes that lets you unleash a powerful Special Attack which they nailed the amount of time it'll be unavailable to help give combat that perfect flow of building up for your big moment as you dart through enemies surrounding you.Something unique is there's almost no limit to how many charms you can eventually equip as they're only gated by ability points which most games would cap you out on, but in this game's case, if you're willing to put in the elbow grease of finding its many, maaany upgrades that dot every crevice of the map behind optional puzzles, platforming challenges, hidden areas, and combat paths, you can become God. It's a fun and rewarding powertrip knowing that exploration will always contribute to your power level and you don't have to make hard decisions on which charms to use and basically never use that one that's "okay, but definitely not better than this one" the freedom's in your paws.But that freedom does lend itself to something I'm slightly mixed on. The game's challenge starts pretty decent, but it quickly disappears as you gain an ability which makes your dodge roll have virtually no cooldown. Between your jumps and fast dodge rolls, it's almost impossible to realistically take damage as long as you're flailing around and most enemies attack in very similar predictable patterns, so you quickly understand how to fight pretty much every enemy in the game, even ones you've never seen, since they get rather same-y and you're way too well equipped to deal with them. By the end game, I could pretty much destroy any enemy before they had a chance to blink and this made the game start to feel a bit mindless. I was still having fun, but I wasn't very engaged. This got so bad that I one shot the final boss with health to spare and had a "that was it?" feeling moment. An even Harder mode would be very welcome that increases enemy HP and perhaps restricts your resources a bit.Though I was able to find that desired challenge in the form of the surprisingly brutal Boss Rush achievements which task you with S+ ranking every boss, meaning you basically have to be flawless. Beating the bosses into paste with as many charms as I want was one thing, but no hitting them with only a few carefully selected powerups was the daunting sendoff challenge my 100% completion of the game hungered for. I was *very* satisfied suddenly having to take these bosses waaaay more seriously.Bottom line, this game is great. Its lite-ambient soundtrack always feels fitting for its ghostly tone with melodies that feel sentimental and just a bit sad, like everything is a reminder of a life passed but one to be celebrated in memories. The gameplay is well fitting to its action adventure genre, satisfying every curiosity you have behind each corner with some sort of reward or puzzle to solve. The visuals are obviously drop-dead gorgeous. And the game gives you the freedom to play it pretty much however you want.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fantastic third entry for Kyle. The environment and soundtrack are cozy and the characters are adorable. The combat is going to be more simple than some other games in the MV genre, but it's not too simple that it's boring. The "charm" system gives all the reasonable upgrade buffs that people like to typically see along with a few combo synergies for a couple different types of playstyles. The boss fights aren't too difficult and enemy/boss attacks are well telegraphed for quick-to-react players to quickly feel rewarded for learning the patterns. If more hardcore players want more of a challenge the boss rush mode requires you to no-hit the bosses for an S+ rating.The game respects your time and the only things I wish to have gotten more of would be another enemy type or two per biome and for the base biome models to differ a little bit more. What I mean by this is instead of the areas being more or less platforms that you fall off of, maybe in the earlier zones the boundary limits are defined by thick vegetation.One of my favorite games of the year so far. I'd suck Kyle's weiner just to get a taste of the artistic recipe.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

I LOVE crypt custodian. Pluto is charming, the setting is great, and the platforming is really fun. It reminds me of Garden Story, which I also love very much. I'm haven't caught up to where I got to in the demo yet, but I took a quick peek at the achievements & there is SO SO SO much depth to this game that I haven't even scratched the surface of!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: crypt custodian was one of the games i was most looking forward to in 2024 and it hasn't disappointed! i loved kyle thompson's previous game islets, and crypt custodian is just as good if not better! the humour is charming, the art and music are gorgeous and atmospheric, and the controls/gameplay just feel really good to play. the combat is fair and challenging -- not to mention there are difficulty settings for those of us (like me) who don't have great reflexes but still want an enjoyable experience. i'm really excited to explore every nook and cranny of this game :]EDIT: after 9 more hours i can confidently say that this game is absolutely fantastic, exceeded my expectations and i can't believe how much map there is. oh my god. it's awesome!!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: You know you have a gem at your hands when you drop the demo before completing it, because you don't want to spoil it and wait it for the full game. Another excellent game from Mr. Thompson. It was my most anticipated game this summer. I cannot wait to grab my steam deck every night to play some more and get to know its sweet and funny characters. It plays like a great metroidvania with awesome bosses and areas with great puzzles. I really like the story and the themes so far. I cannot hide my enthusiasm for the game since it  travels me back in time when I grabbed my game gear and played the GG Shinobi game. It reminds of another gem Death's Door. If you haven't played Islets, do yourself a favor and play it also. Thank you so much. I tip my hat to you, Kyle. Bravo!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Great art style/work, solid controls, wonderful music, and an interesting story. As the game progresses you have some degree of freedom as to where you'd like to explore next, limited only by the unique abilities you may require to access certain other areas. Some bosses can be challenging; but, the death penalty is negligible. There are a variety of enemies and mechanics. You'll also find the occasional puzzle which tend to be simple, though can still be challenging to implement the solution.It's cute, it's fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game!  The charm, the fighting mechanics are varied and more interesting than I expected.  Love the small battle challenges.  The npcs are interesting.  The hint system is implemented so well I don't know why other developers don't do the same thing.   I didn't think I'd fall in love with this game this much!  Once I'm done I look forward to looking into the other games this developer has made.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: This is the third game from this band of brother developers, and it is quite apparent that they have been improving their craft with each release. Their games provide plentiful nourishment for longtime metroidvania lovers, while also serving as digestible morsels for anyone looking to get their first taste of the genre. Just like its predecessor Islets, Crypt Custodian may not be a genre-defining behemoth like Hollow Knight or Ori, but it serves as a testament to how much individual developers can accomplish with today's tools and a loyal fanbase.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great so far. The vibes and presentation are fantastic. It feels great to move around. The bosses are really well designed with interesting move sets that are tricky but not frustratingly difficult (playing on normal mode). There's all sorts of nice quality of life features, like a really open fast travel system. I'm really liking the progression systems, which are simple but meaningful.Overall just a fun game and a really nice time.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I finished Islets and loved it; then I saw the demo for this game, played it, and I was immediately hooked. Finally, the wait is over.Kyle Thompson really does make unique games (I would say it is closest to old console Zelda games): beautiful art, beautiful music, charming characters, and simple gameplay (though the "bullet-hell" is sometimes annoying). Definitely give it a chance, it is sooooo relaxing after whole day of work to whack some pots with a broom.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game that follows the design that Kyle Thompson setup in Islets.  The combat is a little strange at first if you don't realize how important it is to jump but once you get that down, the game really comes together.  I like the puzzles and the boss fights specifically.  I look forward to seeing how things progress from here.  The Thompson brothers are quickly become one of the indie teams that I follow implicitly.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 - would 100% recommend it.Lovely game!! I played the demo for Crypt Custodian and absolutely loved it. I knew it was gonna be an insta-buy since day one.Gameplay is really smooth, combat feels great and I liked the clever puzzles and platforming.The art for this game is absolutely amazing, you can feel the love and effort put into this.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing game! From the character movement, combat, and level design, everything just feels so clean and well thought out. I've had a lot of issues in the past with top-down platformers like this as it's hard to tell exactly where you are in space, but that isn't an issue with this game in the least bit. I highly recommend this game, and I'm leaving a link to part 1 of my playthrough below as well!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played 3.5 hours of this so far, but I'm having a great time - a charming story, a handcrafted world with interesting platforming and combat, and overall just well polished. (I actually put those 3.5 hours in all in one session because I was hooked!)Btw: if you play on a laptop, Windows might decide to assign the game to your integrated GPU, resulting in terrible performance. Make sure to go into settings and assign it explicitly to the discrete GPU (aka graphics card)
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Kyle Thompson has become one of the most reliable indie devs out there.  You know what you're going to get.  Smooth gameplay, adorable characters, fun platforming and combat, and a very polished experience with lots of QoL features.  Crypt Custodian hasn't disappointed on any of these aspects.  If you liked Sheepo or Islets, or really any Metroidvania or Zelda-like, this is an easy recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I played Islets and loved it, this game is just as fun. The new mapis a bit confusing but if you dezoom you can see better the general map. The combat system is really fun, the abilities are really fun and let's you choose the way you fight and changes alot compared to Islet where you have all the abilities at the end. The monster are really cool and their abilities reflect really well their apparences. If you liked the ground boss fight in Islet and you want more freedom in the fighting style, this game is for you. The story is really interesting and I like the game. Pay and play, it's great. Hope this helped, have fun
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review:
Crypt Custodian is a charming metroidvania/zelda-like about cleaning up the afterlife.

You play as Pluto - a mischievous cat who has just died, and landed in the afterlife's palace. After a brief and disastrous meeting with the Afterlife Guardian - Kendra - you are banished from the palace and sentenced to clean... FOREVER!!

Explore the vast grounds that surround the palace, battle beasts with your trusty broom, and gain new abilities to expand your map. Solve puzzles, discover secrets, and... organize an ambush to break back into the palace!

name: SteamWorld Heist II
detailed_description: All is not well on the waves— a water crisis is brewing! Mysteriously, this precious resource has become deadly, corroding metal limbs and mechanical hearts. As legendary Captain Leeway, it’s up to you and your ragtag crew of steambots to uncover the source of this threat and save botkind before it’s too late! TURN-BASED STRATEGY AT ITS BEST Dive into an upgraded tactical experience that builds on the beloved gameplay of SteamWorld Heist. Every move matters as you plan your turns, position your crew, and carefully aim each shot. Ricochet bullets off walls and use your surroundings to outsmart enemies, but remember—victory hinges on a well-thought-out strategy, not just a quick trigger finger. NEW WATERS, NEW ADVENTURES Set sail across the vast ocean in your trusty submarine. Face real-time naval combat challenges and steer your crew through tactical ship-to-ship battles while discovering hidden treasures in every wave. Your decisions as captain shape your journey through the Great Sea. CUSTOMISE YOUR CREW, YOUR WAY With over 150 weapons, utility items, and ship upgrades, the possibilities for crew customisation are endless. Equip your steambots for every strategy—whether you prefer a sharpshooting sniper or a hammer-wielding bruiser. Unlock new crewmates, jobs, abilities, and gear to perfect your team for each mission. DIVE INTO A HANDCRAFTED WORLD Immerse yourself in a beautifully crafted world filled with unique environments, eccentric characters, and a captivating story. And yes, Steam Powered Giraffe is back with an all-new soundtrack that will stick with you long after you’ve docked your ship. Plus, with over 30 hours of gameplay, your adventure will be as vast as the ocean itself! FEATURES: Precision turn-based combat with satisfying ricochet mechanics Discover a vast world filled with real-time naval battles and hidden treasures Customise your crew with 150+ weapons, items, and upgrades Explore the rich new job system to create a crew that fits your playstyle A stunning new adventure set in the SteamWorld universe, with over 30 hours of gameplay Music by the fan-favourite Steam Powered Giraffe! The fate of botkind rests in your hands—are you ready to lead your crew through treacherous waters?
