With tactical turn-based battles featuring signature ricochet action, 150+ weapons and items, a new job system, real-time naval combat and 30+ hours of gameplay, prepare for an epic SteamWorld adventure!

_childDocuments_.review: I played every single SteamWorld game (even the forgotten one for DSi/3DS, SteamWorld Tower Defense) and I have to admit: While the original SteamWorld Dig was my all-time favourite for a long time, SteamWorld Heist II (SWH2) is the game that finally took its place.The graphics are beautiful. With the addition of dynamic lighting, it really adds more depth to the even more improved 2D style. The map is a very nice upgrade to the first Heist, as it really feels like you are on the shard / overworld and not just on a map. The steering is a bit wonky, but adds to the challenge. I also like the fact that there are lots of secrets to uncover.The new job system is easy to learn, but also easy to miss. One mission brings it up, and it's really worth taking time to get into it, as it really adds much depth - and extremely fun and almost OP techniques - to your trick shots. One time I was able to shoot 42 times with ONE character during ONE TURN because I used the right combination of skills from different jobs on that character. Gives you some real #BigSteveEnergy!Without using the new job-system, some levels might be very hard even on lower difficulties. It takes some time to level jobs, and you will have to replay some levels you already completed for sure, but it's very much worth the time!I beat the game (story wise) at a playtime of 28 hours and I still have to complete all levels on full stars as well as collecting all the hats and level-up all teammates to the max. It has lots of replay value for sure! I was shocked when I thought the game was almost over, and I was actually only halfway in.At first, I was very skeptical about the new cast of playable characters, as Heist players like me are very used to Piper and her Crew. But I got to love them really quickly and following their individual background stories as well as the games' story, I really felt like they grew together like a family. Especially after the one VERY spoilery event that made things kinda emotionally on Captain Leeway's side. #CharacterDevelopmentDoneRightThe story is brilliant. It's nothing that deep and nothing extraordinarily new, sure. But it fits really well into the SteamWorld lore and adds a lot of new context to what happened in space after the Earth exploded at the end of SteamWorld Dig 2 / SteamWorld Build. It also captures the SteamWorld humour very well.SWH2 has cool references (that I won't spoil) to the first Heist, as well as some other titles. One was a very QUESTy surprise at the very end of the game, so keep playing!
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved the first game, and I the sequel is excellent as well!  I beat the game in 42 hours (higher than what Steam reports as I played a good bit offline on my Steam Deck), which included getting full stars on all missions, unlocking all upgrades, and unlocking all crew.+ Great combat, which is like a combination of turn-based tactics and the Worms games :)+ Beautiful visuals+ Fun story+ Very satisfying to have a turn where multiple abilities work together to let you get a lot of kills/deal a lot of damage+ Hats! 🎩+ Moving around the overworld in the submarine and having some real-time combat was fun and a change of pace between missions* Job system -- I'm a little mixed here. You level up a character's "job" based on their currently equipped weapon type (e.g. sniper). All abilities are active for their current job, and you can enable abilities from their other jobs they have leveled up using a limited amount of "cogs". What seemed to make sense to me was get each character's main job up to level 5, but also cycle through the other jobs to get characters to level 2-3 for most other jobs (otherwise you are missing out on other abilities/synergies and sitting on unused "cogs"). So it's good that it forces a little experimentation and lets you unlock abilities, but through the mid to late game I felt like I was constantly swapping weapons around to try to get characters leveled up, so they were rarely being used for their "best" job.  There were some really neat combinations I found, but most I didn't discover until the game was about over.- No way to inspect your characters, enemies, etc. which is unfortunate. This is pretty much expected in most tactics/strategy games (for example, to see what status effects a character has and what they mean, the movement range of enemies, etc). - UI for some of the floor hazards could use some work. For example, if a player ends a turn on some tiles they will get a negative status effect. Most of the time you get warned with a big ⚠️ symbol on your move cursor, but if that tile also has an item or interactive element, it will just display the ⚙️symbol indicating interaction. IMO, it should display both symbols to avoid a user moving to a tile not realizing they would take the negative status effect.- Alarms/countdown timers -- It seems that just about every mission is forcing you to be aggressive because of "alarms" that will increasingly spawn more enemies or achieve the objective in X turns. . While I don't mind this concept entirely, I found its frequency annoying (way more than the first game from what I can recall)- I was surprised to never unlock any kind of fast travel ability. While I overall liked the overworld and submarine combat, I would have found it useful a few times in the 2nd half of the game to be able to warp between bars or something.Overall a great game! 4/5
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game, it took me 30 hours which is plenty of content for the price.If you are familiar with steamworld heist 1 here are the improvements:-overworld map with ship combat. You can get new abilities to reach new areas-pretty complex job system. This feature gives you much more control over your units' progression then in the first. You can make some really op combos-meta upgrades. You can upgrade your ship, crewmate abilities, and job skills.-ability to load during battle, taking you back one or two turns. This is a great addition!Aside from this there is also a lot of great music in the inns. Overall I think this game is better played after the first one, so you have a good understanding of the base mechanics. But that aside, its a much more tactically deep game and it has a much better atmosphere imo (the world map does a lot here)I noticed one negative during my playthrough, which is that hats are very awkward to use. I equip a hat that looks cool, and if it is knocked off during a mission i have to equip it again. This is mildly annoying, hopefully the devs fix it. But overall wonderful game, give it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Not long into it, but can already tell it's everything great about SteamWorld Heist 1 and more.  The SteamWorld franchise titles are instant purchases for me and this is no exception.  Was counting down the minutes to release and am eager to dive back into this beloved world!  Heist 1 was my favorite in the franchise so I'm beyond eager to see where this new adventure takes us.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Steamworld Heist 2 accomplishes something quite rare in the modern gaming age, being an innovative yet true to their roots sequel. I've enjoyed everything about the game, what set Steamworld Heist 1 apart from similar-ish games of it's ilk was the unique world and characters, all this has been expanded upon in this sequel, to the point where I felt a lot more emotionally attached to the Leeway Crew than to the one captained by Faraday. This is a good thing and does not leave the original in a worse light by any stretch of the imagination. The music production has been amped up significantly, and really immersed me into the unique world of..Steam...world. I was slightly worried about the game prior to it's launch because I felt Steamworld Build did not quite grasp it's universe's feel, those worries have been dashed quite expertly. For those who can't afford too many games: The price-quality ratio is perfectly fine, the game is not that long, but the devs clearly respect it if you look at the pricetag. If you want a unique experience in skillbased turn-based battles, as well as a charming story, buy the first one, and if you're hooked? The second one is right here as well.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Great piece, both as a standalone, and as a second installment in a series. Comprehensive story, neat visuals, handy controls.Provides tension and challenge at all stages of the game, while being approachable and open for experiments: free restarts, mid-combat checkpoints, multiple build options, etc.The star feature of the series is its aiming mechanic. It brings a tangible, interactive way of both judging and controlling your chances. Most tactical games incite massive outrage with misses on 95% shots, but this one doesn't: if you miss, it's entirely on you. Fair. Good sport.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Lengthy (and mostly personal) review: Long story short, a wonderful game ESPECIALLY in comparison to the firstThis game. It's just really hard to explain what this game did to me.I bought the first game just as a bi-product of being an avid Steam Powered Giraffe fan and also the crazy sale that was going on. I wasn't sure how much I was going to like that game as turn based games in general rarely intrigued me. So when I played the game, I was pleasantly surprised with how involved I was in the gameplay. I ended up having a lot of fun and became quite the fan of Piper Faraday, but it didn't leave me feeling any particular way. Not like this game did. Despite all the new features this game offered in its trailers, I wasn't sure it would be too different from the first game. I thought that all that was offered in those trailers was all that was going to be new but man was I wrong. This game was a serious step up from the original and I LIKED the original. There's a lot to admire. The artwork, the voice work, the slice of life features (no more limited inventory!) but man, the gameplay and the story, the CHARACTERS left me feeling strongly about this game. I can already taste the nostalgia. Obviously I loved the music. Even beyond what Steam Powered Giraffe did, the environmental music was SUPER effective.I had a lot more fun playing this game with the many new gimmicks and features constantly being offered both within the missions and outside the missions. Absolutely LOVE the resting mechanic. A big gripe of mine with turn based games is that if there are a lot of characters, you'll probably feel more inclined to stick with just a few. I even had this problem with the first game but not in this game. As you progress, using other characters becomes much more necessary and the game makes doing so an easy decision. Also the checkpoint feature. I didn't realize it was there at first but boy do I abuse that thing now. Might be cheap, but does feel very strategic on my end.The story felt much more cohesive in this one than in the last one. The motives of each character were very clear and it's real nice to see plot points beyond just "We need to defeat these guys because they're bad". I was motivated by the story. That's what kept me engaged. What REALLY surprised me though were the characters. I was not expecting to find myself gaining a sense of attachment to each and every one of these characters. I'm not sure if it was pacing or if the characters were just that interesting if not a little cliche, but either way, it all made the characters really enjoyable for me. All this makes me really interested in all of the other Steamworld games. It made me even more interested in the FUTURE Steamworld games.This has got to be one of the first games I've ever played where I told myself "I need to play it again" even though I was only half way through the game. Of course, there are little things that bother me, like how the RNG can really mess with the difficulty on some levels, but it's all really easy to look past compared to what the rest of the game has to offer. And these are just the more comprehensible things I like about this game. There are many other things that I LOVED that I just cannot describe. I kept getting feelings that resonate with me deeply. It just makes me really happy. Everyone should absolutely try this game. I love this game, and I'd love to see where it could end up and what it could mean in future Steamworld games.Also, notice the hours? I am very bad at this game. I'm also very stubborn, and refuse to change the difficulty, but I still ended getting each and every star in Experienced mode :]
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredibly good continuation of an already incredibly good 2D turn-based tactics game Steam World Heist. Lovely presentation and music, really addictive "just one more mission" gameplay, highly customizable difficulty (you can even run missions with incomplete crew), a story that does its job (there also are a few cool references to other games in the SteamWorld series) and fun exploration.The exploration part is a new addition and I think it fits well. You need to pay attention to it though and make timely upgrades to you submarine, otherwise it is easy to miss the Unsinkable achievement like I did as there is no reloading if you've died on the world map.I've played the entire game on Steam Deck and it was a really smooth experience. If you play on PC, make sure to use a controller, as the submarine is probably clunky to control with a keyboard.I've payed the day 1 price for it and it was well worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: If this is your first time in SteamWorld, welcome! If not, welcome back for another great adventure! Put on your best pirate hat and strap in for the best SteamWorld game so far. Get ready to shoot, bomb or brawl your way through enemy ships using turn based action combat, and battle it out with cannons and torpedoes in naval battles with realtime shooter combat. Can you find out what’s turning water bad and save the world once more?This game is set in the SteamWorld Universe, an alternate history starting on Earth with the development of steam-powered artificial intelligence bots back in the 19th century. This alternate history is explored through the various SteamWorld games, through the evolution of steambots from simple defense towers to mining bots and to fully functional intelligent beings, the war with electronic vectron bots, the destruction of Earth, the rise of dieselbots and the fight against their Royal Space Force, after which this game starts.Some time after the defeat of the Red Queen at the end of SteamWorld Heist, on one of the bigger shards left after the destruction of Earth, water is turning bad, slowly rusting all the steambots. Clean fresh water is a rare currency. The corrupt Navy is profiting off of this scarcity, tyrannically ruling over the common folk with an iron fist (literally!). And in the frigid waters of the north, the crazed cult of Rattlers are purposefully sacrificing bots and water to their new god, forcing everyone to replace their metal parts with bones, since “bone does not rust”.You play as Captain Quincy Leeway, son of the legendary “Krakenbane”, destroyer of the Kraken. Finally able to track down and take back his submarine from the Navy, it’s time to start earning a reputation worthy of the Leeway name. Employ a shipful of ragtag crewmates and send them on missions to win better equipment, currency, and most importantly, experience!As you move from region to region, you’ll gain reputation and start being respected by the free bots, and not just as the son of a legend. Soon you get a message from a scientist tracking down the source of the water problem. A few encounters with the Rattlers reveal that they already know the source, and it’s their new god. The defeat of the Rattlers’ leader points you in the right direction: a strange frozen ship far to the north. And this is where I’ll leave it, too many spoilers after this.There are three different parts to this game: the overworld, the friendly places, and the enemy places.The overworld is mainly for selecting the next location to visit, either a bar to rest in, a shop to buy things, or a quest location to fight in. But this is also where you fight naval battles against enemy ships, either on the surface or underwater. Defeated ships may leave behind a salvageable shipwreck, which usually gives you water (the main currency in this world), but sometimes you may find more valuable currencies or rare items. Each day fresh flotsams may be sprinkled throughout to boost your gallon count, if you have the patience to scour the oceans looking for them. You can mount weapons on your submarine, either forward facing torpedoes, side mounted cannons, or weak 360 top turrets. Each weapon takes time to reload, so in a battle you’ll have to learn to circle the enemy ship, staying clear of its weapons while trying to alternate between your front torpedoes and both side cannons. The good thing is that your submarine is usually much stronger than one enemy ship, and if your integrity goes too far down, you just have to find a calm spot to rest a bit and wait for it to go back up a bit. How much it goes up by itself depends on the difficulty, between half in the easy Story mode, and barely enough to withstand a handful of bullets at the highest difficulty. And one more thing about the overworld, keep an eye out for secrets.The friendly locations, the interior of your sub included, involve moving freely with the captain, talking to people, hiring new crewmembers, buying merchandise on display, and again, looking for secrets. In your submarine you can talk to your crew to discover more of the story, or you can spend Fragments (the rarest currency), to upgrade your submarine or your crew.Combat is turn based. Each faction takes its turn, and every bot has two action points, which can be used either for walking or for using one of the abilities. The main ability is, of course, firing your gun, but there are many other abilities or items to use. Firing the main gun automatically ends a bot’s turn, spending both action points if you didn’t already use the first one. Other items and abilities can either cost one action point, or be free, so in one turn you could fire 3 sidearms and the main gun, or even more when combined with other abilities. There’s a lot of strategy involved in combat. The type of bot matters. Brawlers use melee weapons and are strong and healthy, boomers fire rockets with a lot of area damage, engineers fire multiple times and weaken enemies, snipers are precise but need to manually reload, reapers fire machine guns and can fire many times, and flankers cover a lot of terrain. Terrain matters, since you can duck behind obstacles, shoot from above, or line up and shoot through multiple enemies using piercing weapons. Speed is important too, many missions have a turn limit after which the epic loot is destroyed, or have tiered alarms with more, and more powerful enemies joining after some turns. In the easiest difficulty, Story Mode, you can easily run through missions without much thought, even with half the allowed bots, but the higher the difficulty, the more you have to think and plan every move, every bot you bring in a mission, every ability you use, every enemy you destroy. Missions are of good length, usually around 10-20 turns, more on higher difficulty. If you’re looking for a challenging turn based combat game, this is an excellent option.Excellent turn based combat requiring strategic thinking. Good story. Good graphics. Good music from a real band. Plenty of difficulty options, including a fully customizable experience in which you choose how easy/hard each aspect of the game is. And you can change the difficulty at any time, if at one point the game gets too hard, you don’t have to start a new save with a lower difficulty from the beginning, or if you feel like it’s too easy, just amp up the challenge a bit, with instant effect. Excellent worldbuilding and story continuity from previous games, expect lots of references and a few cameos from familiar heroes. Great challenging achievements requiring multiple playthroughs with different styles: speed, safety, completionist, tricks…No pause/menu access during the enemy turns, and these may take a lot of time, with only a “skip this animation” option with limited benefits. The story structure is becoming a cliché for all SteamWorld games, with all the plot twists predictable. Only three save slots available.The combat is identical. Retreating from a battle is free. The quest selection is a playable map. Crewmembers don’t have a fixed specialty, they can have any role if they carry the right weapon. Multiple currencies, not just water. In missions you are allowed to rewind two turns.A great quality game, fun and challenging. 20-30 hours for one playthrough, but you’ll probably have to play it a few times to beat the hardest difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: I was hyped as hell for this after loving the first installment - it comes as a shock that I'd feel the need to give a thumbs down for this after 9 hours of playing.More isn't necessarily better, something that too many studios fail to appropriately grasp: - The overworld is tedious, as it's essentially here to inflate gameplay time through not-so-good real time combat. The whole point of the game is the turn-based tactics, adding anything else that isn't 10/10 in between makes the whole experience more annoying. It makes going back to earlier levels a chore, too. - I don't remember the first installment having so much constant reinforcement right from the get go. Suddenly, it's not about strategizing against a specific enemy setup, but rather managing to survive long enough against an unending onslaught of enemies. What that does, is make you feel that the issue isn't so much the strategy you used, but rather the fact you haven't farmed enough to get better gear for your characters and level them up. It leads to a vicious circle as the difficulty makes you flee the level before you can grab all the loot (and sometimes even the epic one), which means less stuff to improve your characters, which means the next level is gonna feel even tougher, and so on and so forth. Of course, the solution for me would be to lower the difficulty. But once you do that, you absolutely stomp the enemies and there's no challenge/thinking needed anymore. Some of the enemies' powers (damage, stuff they spawn) are literally halved between the third highest difficulty and the second highest.This leads an absolutely gorgeous game full of personality and promise to be a tiring experience that felt like a chore right as I was entering the second zone. This isn't a bad game per se of course, but the result in terms of fun vs. what it could be unfortunately warrants this negative review.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Steamworld Heist 2 is everything I wanted it to be as the excellent Steamworld Heist 1's sequel: If you haven't played the original Steamworld Heist, don't worry - there is no requirement to play it before playing this one. The sequel's story makes some light references to the original game, but nothing crucial. Either way, you're in for a very polished turn-based tactics experience! Oh, and if you're a veteran of this genre, do yourself a favor and start on Elite right away - the game's difficulty slider is tuned to be on the easier side this time, unlike in the first game.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: In short: A simple gameplay loop executed really, really well.Everything in this game is simple, but smart and well polished. The missions feel satisfying to play, the mechanics are tight, and the art direction is gorgeous. Lining up the perfect shot to ricochet across the map and execute half an enemy crew feels fantastic, and so do many of the other plays you can make in this game. The gear/abilities you can give your crew feel meaningful, and there are some super interesting combinations you can make work if you experiment. It's worth the price, especially if you like strategy games already.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Heist 1, this met my expectations and slightly overshot them. The boat combat is more fluid than expected. Controls are slightly changed and they have a new action system for combat. That's interesting so far.They introduced resting after missions and a daily bounty system in addition to the sea map, so I am worried they'll pad playtime via grind. Steampowered Giraffe is obviously the best thing about it still.The gunshots are.. sharper.. than the original, imo. Might just be me, but I got a headache after 2 hours. Then I played some more on Deck speakers and it was much more bearable.I'll update with more thoughts as I progess. Initial impression: Worthy sequel.Update:On Experienced difficulty, the alarms start out so early on missions past the parlay, it encourages me too much to rush through the missions; So I tuned down the mission urgency.Update 2:Yeah the game can definetely feel a bit stretched at parts in the arctic and.. later on.I am enjoying the story quite a bit. It has some nice callbacks to the older games, but should stand ok on its own legs, too.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid sequel to the original, which expands on everything but doesn't take any massive risks with the formula. If you didn't like the first, there is nothing for you here.Game runs around 25ish hours and I think that runtime is really about right, as the animations and time it takes to progress turns with so many lategame enemies and effects makes the game start to overstay it's welcome.Achievement hunters should expect to have to slog through many more hours, if not the whole game again, to mop up a handful of lengthy achievements (not hard, just long)
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Ugh, I really want to give this game a good review. It gets a lot right for a tactics type game, but it falls into the worst and most major sin: Reinforcements.I get it. You want your game to be challenging, and giving players too much time means they can crawl their way through. But why, why in god's name would you think the solution is to spam adds at random throughout the stage? The entire game is about positioning and reinforcements literally flip over the chess board. You can do everything right, but too bad, the game spawned a shotgun guy behind you and now you're dead. It also bloats the turn-end as you monotonously watch the AI cycle through orders for dozens of enemies, half of which you don't care about.It doesn't even solve the main issue, because I'm just going to reload and account for this lazy garbage. It changes nothing at all about the problem.There was every opportunity to do better here, with the way the game works making beefier enemies with more skills would have worked. Even a rising water level, you set it up perfectly with the polluted water story! But no. Random adds. Disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Obscenely good game. My brain is absolutely rotted from dopamine addiction and I typically cannot play a strategy-like game for more than 10 minutes before having to switch to Overkill so I dont go into dopamine withdrawal. SW Heist II takes everything that I liked about the first and doubles it. It takes everything I didnt like and halves it. One of the most enjoyable tactics games I have every played. I can see how some nerds might not like the "balance" since theres so much more variety in potential crewmates. But since I play games for fun instead of min/maxxing like its a second job, I actually enjoy that variety. Easy 9.5/10 and possibly my 2024 GOTY
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: It's another great addition to the steamworld franchise, great music, fun strategy combat, cool theme all nailed yet again. The new leveling system is really awesome, tons of variability if you choose to level up multiple "jobs" on one character. The bounty system is fun, helps you feel a little bit better about the tedious resting system. The snipers are a huge upgrade from the previous game, lots more ways to reload without wasting a turn. The SMGs feel way better compared to the first game. Tons of gameplay upgrades all around. The naval combat is braindead, basically an auto battler. That's both a positive and a negative for me.As with all steamworld games they can't help but put in an annoying mechanic or two, in this one it's for sure resting. In between just about every mission (maybe 2 missions if you have enough crew) you have to sail back to your nearest tavern to rest. It's pointless and doesn't really do anything but increase the amount of time you'll spend in the game sailing back and forth. The positives outweigh the negatives in a huge way, definitely worth picking up if you enjoyed the first steamworld heist.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: *SteamWorld Heist 2* is an absolute gem and a brilliant continuation of the tactical, turn-based shooter series! It takes everything that made the original great and elevates it to new heights. The combination of strategy, action, and charm is perfectly balanced. The precision aiming mechanic, where you manually aim each shot, adds a level of tension and satisfaction that keeps every mission fresh and exciting.The new environments are gorgeous, with even more variety in level design and enemy types. The tactical depth has been expanded, allowing for even more creative and strategic approaches to each mission. Characters are vibrant and full of personality, with humor and style that fans of the series will love.Whether you're a fan of the first game or new to the *SteamWorld* universe, *Heist 2* is a must-play. It’s a rewarding blend of strategy, skill, and fun that feels endlessly replayable. A truly unique and unforgettable experience!
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I have loved all the steamworld games, but I especially liked Heist and this is definitely a worthy sequel. It's more of the same mix of aiming skill and light strategy gameplay with some added rpg-build features to make the most effective teamThe new class system where you can make a unique build of borrowing skills from other classes is great and you can abuse the system to make truly broken characters, and on the higher difficulties you probably have too.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I'm just over 4 hours in at the time of writing this.  They really outdid themselves with this one.  They improved EVERYTHING over the first game.  The over world and level music is OUTSTANDING.  This developer always has awesome music in their games, and I've always been a huge fan of this aspect.  I Also own this on the PS5 and I have been playing both back and forth.  Great job guys!  Thanks for releasing this amazing game!
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Was enjoying the game somewhere until the middle of the journey when I find out that it started to break its own rules. Oh why why developers thought that constantly spamming new enemies every turn was a great idea? I don’t mind challenges but this was ridiculous. Why not make enemies more unique like give them cover up let them run and hide or flank you. _childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Steamworld Heist is one of the best indie games of the last 10 years, and this game appears to be a refined and/or improved version of the same formula. What else needs to be said?(If you've never played Steamworld Heist, it's a turn-based cover shooter with RPG-style levelling and upgrades. Think X-COM but in 2D.)
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved this. Apart from the original game, I don't think I've ever played anything quite like it. It revolves around turn-based combat missions, but the missions happen on a 2D plane and are very much about cover, firing angles and ricochets. You collect a team of steam bots over the course of the story, with 6 classes. Each class has 5 levels with unlocked abilities, personal upgrades and tiered weapons. It adds variety by allowing each hero to take perks from other classes - you can make each character any class by just changing their weapon. There's also overworld combat in your submarine. It's a very lighthearted game like all their others, and is very well polished.- Works great on Steam Deck- 6 classes- Wide variety of enemies- An overworld to explore as a mission hub, which also has submarine combat - Lots of customisation with equipment slots- In addition to buying weapons and upgrades for your crew, your submarine also has weapons and modules that can be upgraded - I found it rather confusing to start with, but you can take skills from other classes if you train them. A sniper can change their weapon out for a shotgun to become a flanker, which then lets them be a flanker while taking skills from the sniper tree- There's a wide variety of attributes for enemies which give you options for scrapping them. Some enemies have solid shields, some fly, some are summoners, there are also turrets, exploding barrels, linked enemies, chilled / frozen / burning etc etc.- Most missions have some kind of countdown such as an increasing alarm, a meltdown timer or a unique objective, which encourages you to keep moving- The game hugely respects your time and choices, allowing you to change the difficulty at any time, rewind to every alternate turn, and restarting any mission without penalty- It's really minor, but it annoyed me that the main character said “Ha-haa!” after pretty much every sentence- I really dislike the music in bars
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed SteamWorld Heist 1, you will enjoy this. This time set on a planetary shard containing apparently most of the planets water that survived the explosion of the planet in SteamWorld Dig 2 & SteamWorld Build. Instead of a spaceship, you now have a submarine. Otherwise pretty much the same kind of combat with better graphics, lighting and all that. All music written by Steam Powered Giraffe once again, this time songs written specifically for this game instead of older songs and a few new ones like in SteamWorld Heist 1 soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Generally I'm not a big fan of tile-based strategy titles, especially those involving 'enemy is behind partial cover, your chances of hitting said enemy is 50%' sort of scenarios, that being RNG.But SteamWorld Heist II is not one of those. Here, whether you can strike down your enemies or not depends purely on your manual aim precision. Succeed, and you are handsomely rewarded. Fail, and of course that's all on you. Skill-based gunplay. That's tile-based strategy I can definitely agree upon.Regardless if you're new to SteamWorld or not (and/or have already played Heist 1 like myself), as usual there's much to love here - from its aforementioned gameplay, to its soundtrack, characters and that undeniable SteamWorld aesthetic. That said, Heist II's plot is not a direct continuation of the original, however Heist 1 players may definitely enjoy the neat little references here and there.Might also be worth noting that planning your team before starting a mission (i.e. assigning jobs (as in weapon type), equipment and 'job skills' to your crewmates) can take a bit of time, compared to the more 'pick up and play' nature of Heist 1 (minus the job mechanic). However should you be willing to commit a little patience into optimising your team's loadout, then watching each crewmate's job skills synergise in greater favour of wiping out the opposition is your reward.And one final note: This game includes 5 difficulty options (including custom settings) which you're free to change anytime, with zero penalties or bias imposed on the player (something I still believe is uncommonly seen in games nowadays). I respect that.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Great gameplay, great aesthetics and setting, great soundtrack... While it is very recommendable to play the first instalment before, you can enjoy this one on its own. I love how they connect every game in the Steamworld series but without forcing you to play them to have fun with each title.Special shout-out to Steam Powered Giraffe for the spectacular vocal tracks.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: After a long pause, the Steamworld universe comes back to Heist and boy is it a triumph! This game picks up exactly where the first one left off, and you can tell the devs really listened to the playerbase and understand what people liked it. To ensure they did not alter the formula too much, in this opus there are 2 main novelties, a map exploration mode between missions, and a Jobs multiclassing system. (+) A fun "Worms" style gameplay and aiming system, opening up the possibility of . As a XCOM Veteran, it's wonderful to have the outcome of your shot depend on your aiming skill, and not a bs 95% chance to hit that will fail anyways. On the map, you get to play naval battles gameplays with machine guns, torpedoes and lasers: (+) Tight execution on the tactics mechanics of movement, pod activations, reinforcements, cover, cover blasting with explosives and clearing the board. . The best I've had was taking 33 shots in a single turn with a character that was ramping up damage as he kept scrapping dozens of enemies. (+) Colorful, wholesome, unique art style and quirky vernacular give this game a strong artistic signature. (+) Steam Powered Giraffe makes a stellar return with a top notch soundtrack, this band is a fantastic match for the vibe and aesthetics of Steamworld. (+) Frequent nods to players of the first game which makes returning players feel right at home.(-)  despite the use of Filter by type / Filter by rank, especially on the selling equipment part of business. This is partly compensated by an extremely good "Reminder" system that will warn you if you could equip better equipment or have unused cogs before boarding the next mission.On the Inventory page, this game could show you your total of gallons (the game's currency) and how much you need to sell to buy that fancy piece of gear. (-) , and the combination of 2 in particular was infuriating to me: - enemies trapped in ice cubes get to play immediately upon spawn / activation, which doesn't feel fair since a bouncing ricochet killing 2 enemies could leave you exposed to 3 new, stronger enemies who now have you in a flanking position and will freeze the scrap out of you. - there are limited solutions to play against the frozen status. Some items let you reduce the damage taken, but that won't stop you from being frozen every turn for an extra 2 turns, being unable to play the game if you spread your units and don't have a buddy to shoot on the trapped character. This was very noticeable on Arctica mission "What a steal" which had me swearing like a sailor until I decided to simply cheese it.A possible solution would be to have frozen enemies not play upon spawn (like all others), or having items to become resistant / immune to frozen status. (-) Submarine map exploration is at its best when first discovering and scouting a new area, finding secrets, shortcuts, and sometimes even grabbing bonuses from the next Bar that you're not supposed to reach yet. After a zone is fully explored,  that is exacerbated by the "go back to the bar to rest after each crewmember has played 1 mission" mechanic.This frustration could be alleviated with a "quick travel to mission site / bar" from the map after you've cleared the area of enemies. (-) The in-mission minimap is not the clearest to read. It feels cheaply made in an otherwise very polished game.(-) Even weirder focus on hats, compounted by having a SPG professionally produced song about wearing hats playing at the hatmaker shop.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: SteamWorld Heist 2 is an excellent sequel to the first game. Heist 2 adds more complexity to the game mechanics and tries out couple of new things while at the same time increasing the length of the game. This is pretty much exactly what I was hoping from it. If you enjoyed the first game and want more, this one is a no brainer to get.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Steamworld Heist II is a very worthy sequel to the original. Its gameplay is still great, the graphics are beautifully drawn, the soundtrack remains incredible, and it's extremely addictive. For the price I got it for, compared to the amount of content it contains, it's a great value and its gameplay loop is enough to keep you coming back.That said, I also predict that more than a few people will still prefer the first Steamworld Heist. This one foregoes the unique "scrappy space pirate" aesthetic for a more standard Pirates of the Caribbean setting. The added boat exploration is fairly fun but also drags out the game a bit, and is far too punishing when you die for how annoying it is to control. You can lose potential rewards you spent entire half hour to an hour missions getting just for daring to explore a little.The plot is basic and standard, and while they could have taken the opportunity to improve on it, they pretty much didn't. It's what I expected but a bit disappointing nonetheless. Not really a fan of the new captain though - he isn't that charismatic and mostly comes off as annoying.But the meat and potatoes is the gameplay and in that regard it passes with flying colors, giving you a variety of classes that you can mix and match skills for in order to create highly flexible combat bots, while still making each robot unique. Shooting the hats off of enemies will never get any less hilarious.

_childDocuments_.review: Short answer is yes, without reservation, highly recommended.  If you havent played the first one:  Very safe buy.Its a turn based tactical on a 2d platforming plane with manual aiming and ricochet mechanics.  The characters and story are fun, the gameplay is engaging and intuitive.    It also offers fully customizable difficulty controls.  If there is any one thing that consistently trips you, you can adjust that thing.  Large amount of content, engaging character building, lots of replay.  If you're considering it, buy it, its worth it.If you have played the first one:  It's a solid step up in every possible (mechanical) way it could be stepped up.  (Graphics are basically the same but it's SteamWorld, this is what SteamWorld looks like, you know this.)  New stuff includes an actual overworld that rewards you for exploration and also *you can cross-class*, sort of.  Classes are bound to weapons, not characters, so you can swap classes by swapping weapons and use tokens to retain some earned abilities and passives.  The end result is a lot of flexibility and an incentive to play around with builds, which is good because *also* there are now tangible rewards for redoing missions.   There's an exhaustion mechanic that limits how much stuff each character can do per rest cycle and a bounty system that gives meaningful rewards doing as many things as you can each cycle.  If you just want to mess around and run missions without advancing the plot, you can do that and get *meaningful rewards* for it.  The end result is it feels *much more* like an RPG.And there are some really fun hats like right away.If you're considering, the answer is yes.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing turn-based game with fairly hard combat that is incredibly enjoyable, charming graphics and OST and engaging storyline. You count with different classes (jobs), each one with their own perks, and different characters, each one with their own default class and special traits, but you can also be changing their jobs (temporarily or permanently), so you can be mixing perks in whatever way you find convenient. There are enough levels so you easily have over 20 hours of fun in the campaign and, even if some missions can feel pretty similar to others, the variety comes when using different characters or just when you are curious about "and what if I try to use this character with this other weapon?", so even when you are done with the game there might have been combinations that you never managed to try properly.The game also includes one of the silliest yet one of the most awesome mechanics I have ever experienced... Taking hats from enemies. Yes, you can shoot hats off from enemies and take them for you, and it is such an incredibly mechanic and I had a lot of fun doing that (some hats might be frustrating to get though).Finally, I have to add that even if combat is turn-based, exploration is made by navigating the sea, being cozy at first, challenging later, but just repetitive by the end. Probably the only part of the game I didn't really enjoy was the lack of fast-travel between resting places by the end of the game, considering there are multiple purposes for re-exploring previous areas (getting hats, retry a mission for multiple purposes or just get bounties).Just an amazing game and easily one of the best games I have played this year 9.5/10 Also, by the time I am writing this, I haven't yet played the first SteamWorld Heist game, so you don't really need to do that, but I strongly recommend you to do it anyways, because it is a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: They took the first game and enhanced the mechanics in pretty interesting ways. As you level up different classes - you get to pick some of the perks from your "side" classes to accompany your "main" one, allowing you to mix and match the skills.Not sure how I feel about 2.5d style and the global map, but otherwise the game is just as great as the first one.

_childDocuments_.review: Having thoroughly enjoyed and completed 100% of the original SteamWorld Heist, I think I can provide some insights of this new game on the saga, from my own perspective.This is an amazing feature, brought from the RPG kingdom, that allows the player to change the main role of a character, to make your own profession by mixing two of the core ones.The introduction of the pirate caribbean into the game world is a fantastic touch. Its presence adds a swashbuckling flair that fits seamlessly into the steampunk universe. It actually fits everything you want to, you can mix pirates with ninjas, with cowboys, with steampunk robots... if you choose pirates, you'll never be wrong.The game is full with Easter eggs, as we enjoyed during the first game of the serie, rewarding curious players who venture off the beaten path. These hidden gems add layers of fun and replayability.Quality-of-life improvements, such as the ability to skip the enemies and the characters movement during a mission, make for a smoother gaming experience.The game's humor remains a charming constant. Quips like "Do you want to abandon the mission? You won't lose anything, except your pride" add a light-hearted tone that balances well with the strategic gameplay.The collaboration with Steam Powered Giraffe elevates the game's auditory experience. Their unique sound perfectly complements the steampunk aesthetic, immersing players deeper into the game's world.While the game begins with the familiar and fitting country steampunk music, it unexpectedly transitions into a more jazz-oriented style later at certain locations and during map exploration. Although I’m a jazz lover and the pieces are enjoyable on their own, they feel somewhat out of place within the established lore.Perhaps the most significant frustration comes from the Rattler enemies. Their ability to multiply exponentially becomes tedious quickly, and without a reasonable cap on their numbers, the battles test your patience more than your skills.The absence of a zoom feature, both during missions and on the world map, hampers strategic planning. Being unable to adjust the view makes it challenging to navigate larger maps and assess enemy positions effectively, detracting from the tactical depth the game strives to offer.The introductory narration no longer features William Sage, whose voice encapsulated the steampunk vibe of the original game. While the new voice actor brings his own style, the shift doesn't quite capture the same atmosphere, leaving a nostalgic void for returning players.During the  quest, I encountered an issue where, if you set it aside to pursue the  questline, the previous quest remains active regardless of your progress elsewhere, so I had to finish the second questline without any hints of where to go or what to do. It isn't quite hard to guess, but I think this is quite important to fix. The game lacks a mechanism to either display both questlines simultaneously or allow players to select between active quests, which can lead to confusion. If you’re allowed to decide which one to follow, there’s no other way to deal with it but implementing a quest selection tool or the easiest way around, displaying both active quests.SteamWorld Heist II ambitiously builds upon its predecessor, introducing new features and expanding its universe. The Reserve EXP system, pirate encounters, and continued collaboration with Steam Powered Giraffe are standout elements that enrich the gameplay and keep the spirit of the series alive. However, certain design choices and technical issues hold the game back from its full potential. The tedious Rattler mechanic, lack of zoom, and map navigation frustrations are notable detriments that impact the overall enjoyment.For fans of the original game, SteamWorld Heist II offers a mix of familiar charm and fresh content but requires patience to navigate its shortcomings. It’s a sequel that shines in moments but could greatly benefit from updates and tweaks to address its flaws.As someone who cherished the first installment, I find myself both appreciative of the new adventures and hopeful for improvements that could make SteamWorld Heist II truly exceptional.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game. But it does ask a question of the player: do you enjoy Steamworld Heist 1's gameplay enough to do it for 25-30 hours? It reminds of Portal 1 vs Portal 2. Do you enjoy the core mechanic enough to play a bigger, more involved version of the game?The answer for me was yes. I finished Steamworld Heist 1 for the third time waiting for this game and continued on that streak when this game came out. The job customization is the best part. Some of the enemy gimmicks feel impossible at first, but the game gives you lots of tools to deal with it. My advice to anyone feeling like the game is too sloggy: stop grinding if you are. The pacing doesn't slog until the last couple of levels, which is normal for TRPGs anyway.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love the first Steamworld Heist and I love this sequel even more.First let me get the bad out of the way. I could not care less about the story. I'm not against games with narratives at all, but the writing is simple good, not great. I don't even want to call it bad because it did give a chuckle once...and it had me paying attention half the time. Cap Q. Leeway didn't relate to me I guess. It's just that the gameplay and overworld are the stars.The other element is probably the soundtrack/BGM. It does have some catchy songs when you are saving for the day and the battle music is fine, but I feel like something more melodious was warranted here. So writing and sound is kind of a weak point.The gameplay is very similar to the first except more polished/streamlined. The mix of battles and then adventuring in the overworld with it's amazing art was great. There was plenty of challenge and plenty of reasons to go for it. The loot is great, the abilities are great, and everything seems very fair. There was no confusion about any of the gameplay systems as everything has moved from the space environment of the first to the high seas. It's all polished and beautiful, easy enough for anyone to jump in and start playing.Is this going into my top 10 games of all time? Absolutely.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: A life of delightment!Another Steamworld title, another highly polished, utterly charming and fun experience. I really enjoyed Heist 1, so it was exciting to see a sequel, and contrary to what people were saying before the game release, this very much continues from Heist 1. It can be played without prior knowledge of previous Steamworld games, as can all of them, but there are definite ties to both Heist 1 and Dig 2, so you will get a bit more out of Heist 2's story if you've played and enjoyed the previous entries.What a marvelous game, the turnbased, bullet ricocheting gameplay is as fun and satisfying as ever, the game looks absolutely wonderful, with a great cast of characters, beautiful backgrounds, and some lovely lighting. It is quite impressive how the team continues to improve on their visuals, while keeping it distinctly Steamworld. The music is wonderful as well, and the songs with vocals from Steam Powered Giraffe are a joy to hear in the bars and reststops along the way. The new cast of characters are a delight, and the story, while once again fairly simple, ends up being quite engaging, in classic Steamworld fashion. Daisy is best girl.The new structure will take some getting used to. Sometimes you just wanna get to the next mission, but sometimes it's quite nice exploring a map and gaining access to new areas, getting into sea battles and finding secrets. They're not kidding when they said this is the biggest game yet, I ended up putting over 40 hours into it before seeing credits. I took my time and replayed some missions several times, but even on a quick playthrough, you're looking at 30-35 hours easily.If you liked Heist 1, this is a wonderful followup, and another fantastic entry in the Steamworld series. If you didn't play Heist 1, you should play it. It's great. Then play this one. Play all the Steamworld games. I love this series. It'll be really exciting to see what the team does next.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I was blown away by how fun the game was. The job system was so unique. I just wish the game was longer. I beat it in about 3 days, so I know that's my fault,  but I thought all the clouds could be uncovered. I unlocked all tbe Bars reputation behind the doors. The loot was worth getting all stars. I hope there is future content.  Also, the price is perfect

_childDocuments_.review: The first SteamWorld Heist is one of my favorite game ever, and this sequel builds upon the original without changing the core formula.I fricking love this game. If you like turn based strategy games, this one is a must. 10/10Edit after finishing the game: I immensly enjoyed this game from start to finish. It's a bigger game than the original, and some might think that the 2nd part drags a bit too long with too many missions, but I didn't feel like that at all. I think this game is exactly what a sequel to a great game should be: bigger, longer, and more stuff to do. I really freaking love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I thought Steamworld Height I was ok. Steamworld Heist II does an excellent job of taking the existing package and improving it. The characters and jobs are more interesting, The environment is far more fun ("cyborg" robots are genious).It still has two main flaws of the original: going through doors tactically is clunky as you need to go near one and end your turn in order to open one without wasting an action and spacing in a room is limited so most of the time your team will be split up to work correctly.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed this game. Polished and flexible turn-based strategy with excellent an story and surprisingly good music. My only complaint is that the very beginning gives off a bad impression. Poor intro narration voice-over (English) and limited initial gameplay as the story first takes off. Anyone who plays for 15 minutes may decide to return it, but they are really missing out if they do. Give it at least an hour. _childDocuments_.review: Another great Steamworld game. It took me around 40 hours of casual gameplay to complete the game gathering all crewmates and all reputation stars on experienced difficulty. _childDocuments_.review: 10/10 One of the most enjoyable games I've played in a long while. One of those games that leaves you feeling a bit sad when it's over because you don't want it to end. _childDocuments_.review: Always been a fan of the Steamworld franchise, love that the devs have been able to make so many varied games using the same IP and world. _childDocuments_.review: 'There were tears in my eyes, when I found this hat I cried.' - Archimedes Heist I was already my favourite Steamworld game, I say WAS because this game is incredible. An improvement on all fronts from the original; Every class is fun and viable (especially melee!)Weapon design is on par with the creativity of the Outsider DLC. Despite classes not being character-locked the 2 exclusive perks for each character makes them MORE unique,The multi-classing system has so much emergent gameplay potential,Controller support and optimisation is fantastic - no need to manually re-edit files, Rewind turn and abort mission remove any frustration on the higher difficulties, Even more SPG tracks than before, Fully-realised world-building that ties the rest of the games together perfectly, One of the best stories-shown-through-gameplay I've ever witnessed, An enjoyable and fun overworld shoot-em-up system, Dramatically increased amount of game length without overstaying its welcome, Constantly new and engaging enemies and level gimmicks...and I could honestly go on for another 100 examples!The only complaint I have with this game is a lack of a NG+ like the first one, for I wish to replay the game in its entirety over and over again!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so so fun.  It is very tactical, it has different classes you can choose from, great graphics, responsive and fun gameplay, it's got it all! _childDocuments_.review: This game brings everything I loved about Heist 1 and adds interesting little things like ship combat. Heist 1 was my absolute favorite in the franchise, this one coming out with a banger of a 10% off-deal is just icing on the cake.If you feel in love with the music of Heist 1 - this one fully keeps up and even outpaces it, especially with absolute bangers like "A life of Un-Delightment" and "Fairing on the Ocean" - Steam Powered Giraffe and the sound engineers are absolute chads and chadettes for consistently nailing the vibe, feel and environments of the various biomes.Playing this on a 4K TV is a true joy, with 4K texture enhancements being turned on by default in the game settings. Visually, the game looks and plays like a truly polished and modernized version of Heist 1, iterating where needed without loosing the feel that made its predecessor special for so many.Fully compatible, no crashes in over 3 hours of constant gameplay on my Deck OLED. 90FPS without any dips, works like a charm.

_childDocuments_.review: SteamWorld Heist but better in every conceivable way with additional QoL changes, game mechanics and party flexibility. Plenty of hours of fun content, from unlocks to achievements. Worth the buy. An engaging 2D turn-based tactical shooter with a stellar soundtrack written by Steam Powered Giraffe (who also wrote songs in the first game). The mission-based gameplay loop is very fun and, as you will discover through your playtime, is highly customisable through the introduction of classes, perks and utility items - unlike the first game where each crewmate was limited in what weapons they could use, reducing their versatility. Furthermore, you're encouraged to train your crew in multiple jobs since you're able to merge perks from different classes together which allows you to finely tune your ideal party lineup and loadout.The story is about what you'd expect from a SteamWorld game - it's enough, nothing stellar but it keeps your attention and helps tie together the two types of gameplay: mission stages and naval combat.Naval combat, much like the rest of the combat, is quite customisable and interesting. As you explore the world you can purchase, loot or find various ship upgrades or weapons to help yourself buoyant while fighting various enemy ships. I very much like this type of gameplay (more than I initially thought I would if I'm honest) although I often found myself being very careless, throwing caution to the wind late-game as I rammed and face-tanked every hit using hull upgrades - perhaps this approach isn't viable on the highest difficulty but I wouldn't know. As an aside, do yourself a favour and find speed upgrades ASAP since your default speed is...slow... to say the least.You'll find yourself spending the most time in those aforementioned missions with turn-based combat. To many, this sounds like a turn-off but in reality this gives you time to think carefully about each decision you make and to better take advantage of the aimline system. Most guns have sway and an aimline which, if timed correctly, can allow you to pull of the nastiest of trickshots possible or just miss entirely. As each shot may be crucial it could be very annoying to miss thanks to random aim sway but thanks to the versatile job system you can just assign a point into greater aim skills (just one of many upgrades that can make up for any issues you may run into regularly).Stability-wise, it runs great for me and I only ever encountered 1 "bug" where a loading screen took 10x longer than usual, but besides that it was a smooth ride (also if you go to places that the game doesn't anticipate, you may find dialogue too early which kinda breaks immersion or just downright wouldn't make sense in context).Honestly a great buy and a great addition to the SteamWorld franchise. You can think of it as what Steamworld Dig 2 is to the original but in the Heist series. Oh yeah and the game just looks gorgeous. I don't know how they did it but damn it looks, feels and sounds good.Solid pick.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful game.The story is well written. It's pretty light-hearted, but still touches on heavier themes like corruption and racism.The music is great. There's a great mix of vocal and instrumental tracks. The vocal tracks primarily occur in rest areas where you can find a radio or a live band, but occasionally they come in at key moments out in the world.The gameplay is the main draw here. The job system gives you a surprising amount of freedom to build out your roster of  crewmates. Each one has 2 character specific upgrades, but can otherwise be built however you want. You also get many upgrades for your sub which provide you with a fair amount of customization.While the game can get pretty difficult, it's still quite forgiving. You can leave a mission with absolutely zero penalty, in case you want to restart, switch up your team, or just come back later when you have better gear/upgrades. You can also rewind the last 2 turns whenever you wish. In addition, there are 5 difficulty settings, as well as a "Custom Difficulty" where you can tweak several different settings to your liking. You can change difficulties whenever you wish and nothing in the game (such as achievements) is locked behind higher difficulty settings.Finally, while the game has a few nods to the first game you can absolutely play this one without playing the first.

_childDocuments_.review: The point of a review is to help people get information and decide whether they want to buy a game or not, so I'm going to try to do that by providing as much information as possible without typing an entire essay.The gameplay on this game is amazing. Though there are some gameplay mechanics that get really frustrating if you don't have the tools to deal with them, this is nowhere near a problem in the late game. Combat is satisfying, though some classes (Reaper, Flanker) do feel a little more powerful than others (Sniper). However, these weaknesses can be remedied by having a crewmate with experience in multiple roles, and it's very satisfying to create interesting builds by mix-and-matching abilities from multiple classes.The story is really motivating as well. Of course I won't go into it too much as to prevent spoilers (and even if I used spoiler text, there are those people who wouldn't be able to help themselves from looking; I am one of them), but the entire cast is great. Quincy Leeway is definitely a well-rounded and thought out character, and is one of the best leading protagonists I have seen since Sunny in OMORI, or Madeline in Celeste. The other crewmates are also phenomenal; each of them has their own distinct personalities, with those traits sometimes playing into their kit. Overall, it's a very great cast and they do a great job of improving the player's experience and immersion.Also if you care about soundtracks then that's a hit as well. There are some folk-style tracks with vocals (provided by Steam Powered Giraffe), but there's also non-vocalized tracks that usually play during missions. Each area has its own unique music and it really complements the atmosphere.TLDR 9.5/10, great gameplay, great cast, amazing soundtrack imo. Would definitely recommend to anyone who likes tactics games and a good story.

_childDocuments_.review: Love the two different game play elements, the open world sub combat reminds of Sid Meier's Pirates and the tactical main battle are engaging and exciting. 7 hours in and it seems the maps are getting much larger to for some of the big missions. _childDocuments_.review: SteamWorld Heist II is a turn based strategy game with a squad of units wielding weapons from snipers to melee weapons.  Core mechanics is pretty simple, with some elements similar to X-Com.  Difference being you're in a 2d-side scrolling plane with various levels/heights versus an isometric view with X,Y,Z axis. The story is straight forward and doesn't over stay its welcome.There are 6 classes in total, and the weapon you choose to equip your character determines their class.  For example, equiping a sniper makes your character the sniper class.  Why is that important? Because you can change your class from mission to mission, earning EXP to the  equiped class.  Earning EXP levels up a class, letting you equip their skills even when you are no longer their class.  For example, earn level 1 of the melee class to unlock a skill that gives you 1 armor.  You can now switch back to your sniper class and equip that armor skill.  You are limited on how many carry over skills you can equip, but you can equip A LOT, so leveling multiple classes for each character can be highly beneficial.You move along a 2d plane, each character having their own movement range per turn, with an attack ending their turn even if you have not moved yet.Unique aspect of the game is that most projectile weapons in the game 'bounces'. Making use of walls, ceilings, and other geometry in the map critical to landing shots while not getting hit.Game is now a persistent world.  No longer just a hub of different missions.  This adds a good amount of exploration, though slightly linear, to an otherwise mission based game.You navigate the world with your ship.  Ship combat and customisation is fun but not overly complicated.I really like the game.  At 39 hours I have gotten all the bonus objectives for every mission (I played on Experienced difficulty).  There is no end game to keep playing forever, but if you wanted to, you can reply the missions to get more 'hats' from enemies (just cosmetic, no gameplay value).  I have also not grinded any missions so I am sure I am missing some rare weapon variants as drops.  You can also choose to grind to max out every character and see how strong they can get with all the cross class synergies.  This was a good length of a game for me.I wrote this review because I find this game very enjoyable and a little unique.  I wish for the developers to continue making more SteamWorld games, particularly the Heist branch.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Those guys certainly really know how to make a sequel. Heist 2, compared to the first one, is just exactly the same what Dig 2 was to Dig 1. Aside of them both adding the same number after the title, which is absolutely mindblowing if you think about it, they did a terrific job of understanding what made Heist 1 great, listened to the feedback and just added some QoL features to it. We've got a button that skips the running animation, that shortens longer battles a bit (could it also work for throwing grenades, pls?). There are much more unique weapons, so your weapon progression in not just linear upgrade damage by 1. The enemy factions have well designed core mechanics, so the don't feel simply reskinned iterations of previous enemy faction. The game does not punish you for losing anymore by taking your resources. There are mid-battle checkpoints. Inventory management is much easier now and the cap of items you can have is removed.Then they expanded it with a job system - basically, your characters can now multiclass, so if you really want to jam that bazooka sniper build you always dreamed of - well, go ahead. This is honestly fantastic expansion - you can finally personalize your build, focus on what you like and discard what you do not. You can also completely respec characters - but what stops me then from completely building the team of 4 bazooka snipers, you can ask? All characters have unique abilities - for example one of them can use first grenade in the turn as a free action - so this bot seems like a good fit for exploding things out. But other one can get invulverability for a turn, and the other is much faster than all the others, so those might not be the best for staying out of trouble, they want to be right in the middle of it, so sniping things out might not be a good idea for them. So while this job system could homogenize your squad, thankfully those abilities will push you to try different things out. The controversial rest system actually serves similar purpose - you don't want to go to rest all that often, because that maximizes your rewards (and going back to the base is a little bit tedious) so you need to use all bots you have unlocked before you end the day, instead of defaulting to your favorite team every mission.The overworld is a kind of mini-game now. I would say this is the weakest part of the game. The ship battles feel way too easy and you don't have much agency, except from circling over enemies till they die. All of them would be absolutely trivial if you just could heal outside of your base. So you need to pick your battles, and I usually picked none of them unless I was forced to, because of how boring and how badly rewarded they are. Later on, when both you and your enemies get different weapons than plain machine gun with autofire and you get tools how to avoid some damage it gets a little bit more interesting but not very much. Which is a shame, because the exploration aspect seems great - the world is really beautiful and fun to traverse - if not for those battles. I think this aspect could be really spiced up. I feel like some twin-stick shooting in the overworld would be more engaging.Speaking of the world - I feel that Thunderful steps up their production game at least twice with every single Steamworld release. The art direction is really great, I feel the change from space to sail world was a really good decision; everything looks absolutely stunning. The soundtrack is probably one of the strongest in the series (although I don't think it beats my favourite, the Quest one). I might have the soft spot for the jazzy instrumental tracks in the overworld, there's a ton of great bar tunes. I really like how the game does not shy away from vocals in the soundtrack.I also think there is a bit of balance issues - sniper builds feel pretty weak, at least until they get max level, since they cannot deal with more than one enemy at the same time (unless you can find any piercing weapon) and its damage output is not really that great either for eliminating bulkier enemies and on top of that they get the downside of the need to reload after every shot, which is especially hard to manage in earlier stages of the game. Compared to them, brawlers suffer the same problem with no AOE, but they are much more mobile, deal twice as much damage and are almost unkillable. Some non-boss missions are randomly MUCH harder than the previous ones, thanks to some additional objectives, then the difficulty lowers again. Quite a lot of people complain about reinforcements, alarm and time mechanic, but I don't really mind that - It's a heist after all, it's all about fighting with the time and reacting to unexpected events! I played on experienced mode, and I found the game challenging, but manageable.I've just finished the game and I'm absolutely stoked. SteamWorld Heist 1 was a great game, with some minor flaws. The sequel is just miles better on every single field. In fact, it's much better than any other game in the SteamWorld series (sorry, Dig 2). It's fun, it's pretty, it's charming. It's a must play for every SteamWorld fan.

_childDocuments_.review: This is truly a wonderful game from start to finish. The story has heart; the gameplay is fun and varied; the visuals are bright, colorful, and lovingly animated; and the sound and music are top notch (Steam Powered Giraffe is always a delight). I loved the first game and I think this may have very well topped it. For those that are interested, you don't need to play the first game before playing this one. There's only a small cameo tying the two games together. However, I still very much recommend the first game, especially since you can often find it on sale for close to nothing ($1 USD!). Check sites like IsThereAnyDeal for sales.

_childDocuments_.review: This game exists in that space that defines what games are really about. Providing the player with unique and interesting  challenges and a diverse set of solutions. Early you find yourself deciding on way to actually complete the mission. Mid game you are challenged to decide how you want to complete the mission, while offering options in between. Late game you understand the score, challenging you to overcome. This is the structure games should aspire to. A must play.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic sequel. If you enjoyed the first game, this is more of the first but with additional content. If you haven't played the first game, go play that first and then this one because the first one is also amazing.There is a variety of mission objectives and many difficulty sliders so the experience adjustable to your preference. I found veteran somewhat challenging in the beginning of the game but once you start accumulating class levels, it became fairly easy by the end. The game is very forgiving so you should definitely regulate your own level of challenge. I found the most exciting battles were all when I started exploring an area for the first time and . Scrapping enemies is very satisfying. Music and sound effects are great while the regular battle BGM is a little generic. I would recommend blasting the vocal soundtrack during combat. The game is a lot of fun.There are a few issues I have with the game:The class system is a lot of fun but it feels necessary to get a few levels on each class because the base skills are just too good to pass up. As a result, most of my characters felt more like jack of all trades than specialists. The game also doesn't tell you what the 4th and 5th skills are, or the second abilities of characters, which encouraged building wide. Weapon variety per class also felt bit lacking so you'll end up using a lot of lower tier rare weapons all throughout the game.The second main issue is the boat combat. It is mandatory to fight ships at sea to get between mission sites so it's not side content but the variety of boat upgrades is also very low, especially when certain weapons are not allowed to be used underwater. The sea also gets very large so sailing from one end to another can become monotonous. I didn't mind it so much by the end but it did feel a little lacking.These were both ultimately mid-game issues once the map reached a certain size before I had done enough missions to equip both ship and crew with upgraded items. The only reason I would write so much is because I love the game, so I'd highly recommend anyone who enjoys TRPGs.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know how the Image & Form / Thunderful team keeps doing this, but to this day there wasn't a SteamWorld game I disliked. Some are more memorable than others, however, and Heist II is one of those memorable games. Visually beautiful and smooth as butter in terms of gameplay, this is the pinnacle of the SteamWorld series.It's charming, addictive and well-designed (character design, especially, is always fantastic - no idea how many steam robots this series has featured, but they're all recognizeable even when they appear as cameos).If there is a gripe that I had it was the last level of the game, which sometimes felt a little drawn out.Overall I loved it, however, and would recommend it to any fan of turn-based/squad tactics games.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: As enjoyable as the first game - very similar mechanics, so if you enjoyed Steamworld Heist 1, you will like this too.However, expanded on the first one by adding an overworld with a little bit of fun light exploration and overworld combat.Additionally, added a class system that allows for mixing and maxing class abilities. I don't know about you, but for me? That's the prime ♥♥♥♥. That's the straight to the veins good times. Gimme that Final Fantasy Tactics job class mixup all day, and I'm a happy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.Also the chill music at the bars is absolutely magnificent. You might have a rough day at work, or be dealing with difficult people in your life, but coming back to the bar in this game to maybe recruit a new bot, rest your existing crew, or buy some gear, and listening to chill banjo music about robots being ok... it's soothing in a very special way.Edit: just rolled credits -- fantastic game, no notes. Thunderful (nee Image and Form) have done it again, I loved every minute of this.
