_childDocuments_.review: Steamworld never fails! The first game is one of my favorites ever, and the sequel managed to improve the formula in nearly every way. Overworld exploration and combat were great, as was the new Job system that lets you combine class abilities to create some ridiculously powerful combos. Story was surprisingly good and heartfelt, and the new characters were as charming as the ones from the first game. Loved every minute.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Didn't expect to have so much fun, this is my first game from this steamwolrd series as I don't think theme and graphic are for me but as there's many good review I give it a try. Gameplay is fun, good character and job progression, great soundtrack. If you like turn-base combat with rpg element give it a try
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent so far.Feels very well made and polished.If you liked Heist 1 then don't hesitate and grab this one as well.Edit after beating the game (still not 100%):What an absolute gem of a game it is.Not a single crash, no battle passes, season passes, lootboxes and no forced one-sided politics.Fun exploration, likable characters, enjoyable progression with many upgrades, skills and armaments.Music is awesome as well and I often found myself standing in the barfor the sole purpose of listening to the ambient songs.Looking forward to any future DLCs.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: World design and atmosphere is great and the characters are fun and likeable and of course the music is top tier.Gameplay is enjoyable (especially lining up sniper shots), its extremely satisfying to build a team and the multiclassing adds a tun of replayability.  The game can be as hard as you want it to be and losses aren't punishing so you can challenge yourself with higher difficulties at no risk. The first Steamworld heist was an incredible game and this builds upon and improves that foundation as a good sequel should. This already feels like game of the year for me, there weren't many games I have been hyped for this year and so far this is the ONLY one that has lived up to my expectations, I can't recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, I think I like it more than the first. It's more of what you expect if you've played it, but really enhanced by the tweaks to the class system and other improvements. The characters and story are fun as usual. The big difference is the addition of the world map and the submarine. It's pretty good and a good break from the main levels, though it doesn't quite reach the heights of the main levels. The main combat levels are great in general, though don't hesitate to tweak the difficulty on the few that aren't quite as polished. But overall such a fun and unique concept made accessible by good customization.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid sequel to an excellent 2D turn based strategy game.Thoroughly enjoyed this one, lots more options, lots more skills and choice of builds. New fun submarine mechanics added some interesting exploration and combat (even if fairly simple).Note: there is a moment where you are temporarily locked out of an area of the game, which doesn't warn you. This will be when you first cross the barrier. You will get to return to it eventually to complete all the missions with full stars and so on, but just be aware. This isn't game breaking or anything, but I was playing on Elite difficulty and those extra levels and shop rewards from getting all the stars in each area are crucial, especially for the difficulty spike in the new area, once you pass the barrier.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Better than the first game in everyway. If you liked the first Steamworld Heist than you will love this one. If you haven't played the first one you can still jump into this one. It's such a good game. The soundtrack really fits the theme and atmosphere of the game. The new class system is a blast to play with. It lets you mix and match the skills you want a crewmate to have. There is so much more customization you can do in this one.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: They added layers of management that more bothered me than brought any fun:- characters now need to rest- characters aren't tied to classes anymore, losing their identity- the map is now interactive with boring mini-battles against ships when sailing between points- therefore ship now can be upgradedI find myself spending more time on managing those things than in actual missions. The original game is simple straighforward!If you get past these new features, or even better, if you like them, you'll love it, because the tactical platform shooter is still there and it's amazing. Still, I won't recommend it based on my experience of more than 100 hours playing the first one.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Here is everything you need to know in under 3 min: However no reason to click because this is it: ⛵30 hours of gameplay⛵Turn based combat easy to get into but hard to master⛵Basic ship combat that brings some nice variations⛵Awesome Music⛵Making bouncing shots is cool⛵No annoying 90% chance to hit but still missed
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: This would be a solid neutral if given the option due to the repetitiveness of the missions and unbalanced job/class options. The game starts out amazingly and the simplistic plot is enough to hook you in to press further; however, after about 10-15 hours you have the main game loop and tactics down and the story has become a passing thought. The idea of wanting to dual spec some characters to gain some abilities is nice in theory, but I found 4 of the classes to be borderline useless; especially as the game goes along. A real shout out goes to the soundtrack here, which is one of the best in a long time, seriously give it a go.Would I recommend? Maybe, if you are a fan of the genre and have beaten all other similar games.Would I play again? No, dropped it after 20 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Great evolution of the first game. Lots of ways to customize your crew, the map navigation is more than just moving around, and the new lighting effects are truly remarkable. Not sure how they do it with 2D sprites, but they do it well.My only gripe is the music with vocals. They lyrics are clever and the music is well produced, but I find it a *little* cringe and extremely distracting when trying to read dialogue. The background music is fantastic otherwise, so it would be nuce to be able to mute the vocal tracks and keep the rest. They're just a little too hokey and remind me of kids tv shows.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the first game and absolutely loved the second oneThe gameplay is great. The game has a pretty flexible crew/character progression, most missions differ from each other, with unique feel about a lot of them, and there's even a cool bullet-hell naval combat. By the end of the first game I got a bit tired of it, and it was only 18 hours, but this one held me all the way to the end (35 hours)Also, kudos to devs for trying new genres with their new games and not just sticking to the formula! Great job!
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: So with most of my gameplay reviews lately, I include a video of the early gameplay. This video has no talking, just me playing (Poorly) at the start of the game.Early gameplay video: I love this! Not only as a game in it's own right, but as a continuation on to Steamworld Heist. It takes the previous game and improves upon it!You start with great characters who are fantastically designed! They look good, they sound.... robotty*. The animations are fantastic! Top marks there, they really did good here!*I dislike the robot voices. But you can turn those off! =DBut it doesn't stop there, because you can get more crew members. You get past the starting area and you can find two people available.... Do the two people not interest you? You can rest and it'll be two different ones. I found a lovely crow robot who I absolutely adore! As well as one with a wheel, like in the previous game. (Same surname too!)There are many more characters and I don't even know if I've seen them all yet!The gameplay is good, stands up with the original very well, but a few things that improve on it.Firstly, you can disable having to hold a button to interact with something... And just have it be to press the button. Aside from being great for accessibility, there are so many games that have had "hold X to do this" and it's always annoying. (If you've played Assassin's Creed Odyssey, an example is when you go to sell things, you have to sell all items individually and hold a button to sell each. It is insanely irritating, just really bad design!) And just like the robot noise voices, you can turn this off and just have it be a simple button press.Secondly: You can go back two rounds in the middle of a mission. You can't do it, then do it again. But it can really help if you've screwed up and want to take something back. Or if your cat has jumped on your keyboard and killed someone who had a nice hat you wanted. Having this as an option is a great time and I will be exploiting the hell out of it. I must have those hats!Thirdly: You can change classes. Just equip a different weapon type on a robot and they are a different class entirely. You can have skills from each class you've levelled at the cost of using cogs (It's free for the class you're on). This is a really cool feature and could combine to make some ridiculously powerful builds!Fourthly: Why am I doing numbers, this is annoying. Additionally: You have more incentive to use different crew members. As your crew members get exhausted and must rest between missions. I thought this would be annoying at first, but it's really well implemented. You get green badges for running missions (Yes you can grind them.) and the more you have, the more rewards you can spend them on. They reset when you rest, so it's worth running a few different missions with a few different characters to get lots of the badges.There's an overworld. The first game had you jumping between notches on a star map? Yeah, that's gone. This is way better. You're in a submarine, you explore the map directly. There's naval combat, which is really easy, there are difficulty options to change how hard this is if you want. You can also get a ton of upgrades and different gun types. Super cool!Seriously, the developers did a really good job of this. I look forward to buying any DLC that comes out. I want a steamworld heist 3 if it's going to be as good as this. But if I have to wait a while, that's fine, this game is great and has a ton of replay value. I'll be good for a while!I went through options and keybindings in my video. But basically, there's a ton of accessibility options and you can remap every key. There's nothing for colourblindness as far as I could see. But hopefully that won't be an issue, as I've never needed to know what colour something was in the game. I can't speak to players experience though, as I am not colourblind.Ultimately, I strongly recommend this game. To you, your friends, your family, your pets. Everyone should buy this.I also want the developers to release plushies of their wonderful characters.If you buy this game, good, you're making the correct choice.If you don't buy this game, you're making the wrong choice, at least give it a chance. I joke of course, everyone is different. I hope you find the game for you.... but this one really is very good!Regardless of what you do. I hope you have a wonderful day and that no one shoots off your hat.P.S. Buy this game. Seriously, buy it now!
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: It's everything good about the first game and more (Neat little overworld to navigate and do arcadey ship battles in, and a multi-class style system that lets you experiment with funky builds by mixing class abilities). The writing, characters, dialogue, and music are as much a treat as the first SteamWorld Heist.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Improves on the first game in so many ways. Having designated classes, free world exploration via submarine, the list goes on. Gunplay feels just as good as the first game if not better. Overall, super glad about this sequel being as good if not better than the first game.(Edit) Forgot to add this, but even though the visual style is roughly the same it's a lot more polished looking and I like that. _childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game where bullet bouncing is the name of the game.  Multi classing is pretty nice.  Although not an original idea, it is very nice to be able to have skills from different classes to mix and match.  I'm not a fan of games where you have to get all the stars in the level to actually get everything within the game.  This is because often times, the scenario just cannot be beaten on the first try and you will be forced to do it again.  I'm OK with doing scenarios again, but not if it is forced.  Still, this is not one to pass up on.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I *loved* the first Steamworld Heist, and I kinda loved this one too. All of the good stuff from the first--the goofy shooting mechanics, the synergies between different types of robots--has been amped up, and the progression is fun and addictive. But there are some head-scratching choices. The devs added an entire over-world naval layer that's meh at best and annoying at worst. (I play turn-based games so I *don't* have to stress about reflexes and maneuvering; yes, you can control the difficulty, but that's really not my bag.) And a few levels are designed around massive influxes of drones and reinforcements, so it's more of a race to exit than anything else. But overall, huge fun, and one of the few recent games I've played all the way to the end. And I've been humming the main tune for weeks! It's a real earworm.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game for me. I finished it.I have not observed bugs - everything was ok. System utilization: ok for me (4K screen, 4080, intel i7-10700, 32 GB RAM) - I didn't have any problems with the game performance.The game art: different from everything that I know of, except the previous game from the same producers: SteamWorld Heist (who would have guessed). Play style: if you played the previous, you know what I'm speaking about (around 70%). What you don't know is that there are now 2 different types of fights, "ship fights" and "bot/crew fights". There is a map and I used it extensively (hint: ESC). If I have anything to say, it is that this game is clearer and better than the previous. The only part of the world where I was somewhat unsure and confused: the last chapter, underwater. Some places are not visible on the map or I don't know how to switch between "water depths" on the map. The bots level ups can be done in different roles (depending on the weapons given for the mission - the weapons dictate what actions and roles the bots will have available). Ok, and now for the people who will play it for the first time - although I will somewhat try not to say too much, only to "explain" a little bit to a beginner what is this aboutThe tutorial is simple and clear. The game is simple and clear although there is some learning involved. For example, it was not evident to me until very late that I can do more "crew fights": between 2 resting periods, you can participate to multiple fights if you have enough crew to send different bots to different missions/fights. You get a pair of bots at the start of the game with which you will execute missions/fights. The rewards for winning the mission/fight can be multiple, gallons of water (useful for buying items and other bots, some diamonds/shards (useful for upgrades) and items (useful for showing to the enemy bots who's who and what's what). Be careful at the description for the mission bonuses and the extra bonus. A bot can participate to only 1 fight between rest times (which are done at the bars). Use the map (esc key) for seeing where you are on the world map; the map is useful also during the bot/crew fights to see where are bonuses, enemies and your very own fighting bots. This is how you can participate to multiple fights in 1 turn (period between rest times): use different bots for different missions. Try to stay (at least at the start of the game) in the map areas for your current level and for the previous chapters - don't go wandering too much into "next level/chapters areas" because you will find very quickly why (hint: bot ships are no longer what they used to be: they are better and meaner). You can clear all the map for the current levels and previous levels (meaning destroying all the enemy ships). For controlling my ship, I used the mouse (until the last chapter where some Q and E are required for lower/higher areas) - you may want to be goals specific though: the green doubloon bonuses (useful for bonuses = water, crystals, weapons, items at the bars). At some point you will be directed to change the weapons for the bots (I was initially confused) and get some experience in a different role for the bots. The roles and abilities depend on the type of weapon given to the bot: there are 6 different roles. Don't worry, you will level up your bots in different multiple roles as you progress, you can even level up bots in all the roles. Having skills in multiple roles allows you to use some of the "role related" abilities by selecting the said role with a number of cogs. (Yeah, explanation is kind of hard to understand until you will do it). For selecting abilities from other roles in which the bot has levels, the interface helps you initially by displaying an "up" orange arrow. Select that arrow and then you will have available a number of cogs which you can use to select different abilities (which abilities need a number of cogs assigned).So, the game is: fights on the world map using your submarine; fights/missions with the crew (every crew member to only 1 fight/mission between rest periods); buy upgrades, change weapons, equip tools and what else, upgrade bots, upgrade submarine, win all the missions and voila, you won the game, you finished the story. I consider SteamWorld Heist II to be better than the original; it also requires a bit more learning than the original, but nothing extraordinary. It took me around 60-70 hours (on my selected difficulty level) to finish the game. Depending on your personal gaming experience, you can do it faster (easy to do even at maximum difficulty) or slower. Enjoy :)Recommended. I will play it again probably, but even for a single play-through, it is worth the price. And if the game is on price reduction, definitely try it, you may enjoy it more than you think.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good casual turn-based strategy game with great art and music, but I don't think it has anywhere near enough depth or ideas to warrant the overwhelmingly positive reviews and price tag. The game allows and, on higher difficulties, mechanically encourages the player to repeat the same missions repeatedly to grind XP and water, the games currency. This almost invalidates difficulty as whenever you hit a roadblock you just find a good tactic to grind the same mission again and again to farm. There's also the day system: each playable character, weapon, and item can only be used once a day. You must rest to make them usable again, but there is no penalty for ending the day. You can cash in 'reputation' at the end of a day that allows you to get certain rewards. Some rewards cost multiple missions worth of reputation and reputation doesn't carry over from day to day, so you do need to successfully complete multiple missions in a row to get the best rewards. But the respective missions are always the same each time, so, once again, you just play the same missions over and over to learn the layout and enemy positions and plan a predefined path to success. This is a good game still for a more laidback experience, but I just don't think turn-based tactics is a good fit for a laidback game, nor the trial and error approach to grinding present here.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like the fact that alarm starts right at the beginning of each level. I get it, it's a heist game so you're under pressure but the constant reinforcement feels like a cheap way to increase difficulty. We should be able to be stealthy or at least be allowed to eleminate an enemy that is about to raise the alarm. Also at some point enemies can put totems on the ground that also spawns reinforcements.So you have :- the enemies already in the level- reinforcements from alarms- reinforcements from totems- also sometimes there are bonus turrets because why notSo yeah this constant pressure is tiring and just feels cheap.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game and all I gotta say is, wow. Seeing this game initially I was skeptical because developers frequently struggle with making a sequel that is enough like the first to be considered a sequel , but also not be "Steamworld Heist 1  DLC but now it's 2, 30$ please". If that is a tightrope to be walked, these devs rode a fing unicycle across it. So many wonderful large and small changes, the biggest ones being much more limited aim lines, the multiclass system, and open world exportation. All new and big changes, all fit in beautifully with what the game already was. The lesser aim lines feels the most bold choice and the game is better for it, gives more reasons to multiclass and makes item selection even more important. There's a lot more that can be broken down, but really it boils down to if you played the first one and like it, this is a slam dunk. Also no other game I know (besides actual rhythm games) has as amazing a relationship between itself and its soundtrack. Steam Powered Giraffe is a great band, puts on a great show and this is a great stage for them. I could play this game 100 hours and I would never consider turning off/replacing the music. P. S It took me way too long to notice this but it makes breaching rooms way easier, doors marked with yellow lights have enemies behind them and green doors have none.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: great value for money, played for just short of 30 hours and still not done with my first play through. wonderful characters, great world, and great music. buy this game, it is excellent, personal top game of 2024. The rest of the steam world games are great too, play those as well, this one references past all the previous heist and dig titles in some way.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Where do I even begin. I've been a fan of the SteamWorld series of games since the very first one came out in 2013 and for being a now 11 year series, I only have good things to say about each and every game. When the first SteamWorld Heist came out I adored it, I've played through countless times and between the combat, story and characters I couldn't help but fall in love. Whether it was setting up the perfect angle to get a rare hat or hanging out in the bars listening to Steam Powered Giraffe there's not a second of the game I don't look back on in fondnessAnd SWH2 is no different. Everything I loved about the strategic combat of the first game was made even better with the addition of the classes and cog system, the storyline stays true to its roots in not only the first Heist game but the original Steamworld games too, while still keeping its identity as its own game and its own story. All the characters are extraordinarily charming, and even though I wasn't sure about Quincy's personal story at first, I found myself rooting for him halfway through the game.I truly can not recommend this game enough. Thank you everyone who contributed to making this game. The music, writing, sound design, art and mechanics make this game better than it has any right to be. I can't wait for the next installment in this series, but until that happens I need to focus on finding all the hats I missed!
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I recently tried the first game because it was only $1 and loved it. So I had to get this one as soon as it came out and it just keeps on that same feel with some changes and improvements. If you are at all interested in this game, get the first one and you will know if you will want to play this one as well.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: This is hands down the best SteamWorld game, and I really love all of them! Thunderfull is at the top of their game and have improved upon the first Heist in every way imaginable. The customization system with the cogs really pushes it over the top and encourages lots of experimentation with weapons and tactics. Can't recommend this game enough, if you enjoy any of the other SteamWorld games you must check it out.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game but I wish the developers would let me actually PLAY it. It's not an animation. It's not a novel. It's a game. It's should not be constantly interrupting me with dialog and little cut scenes etc... Thankfully there's an option to skip, but despite that, the story and dialog always seem in the way. Does anyone actually enjoy this aspect? I find it endlessly tedious. Despite this criticism, when I actually get to play, the game is fun and well made as all the Steamworld games seem to be so it's still worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: another solid game from thunderful, like many other reviews are saying, if you liked the first game then you'll like this one. pretty much expanded on everything good. it doesn't depart too far from the first game which is a positive in my opinion. if you like xcom-esque type games then you oughta try this out.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, baby! Steamworld is back! What a solid, feel-good game. If you played the first Heist, you're gonna dig this. For those who haven't, essentially you battle bots to get loot and get exp to upgrade your characters with different skills, and then rinse-and-repeat. Now, I know the community is divided about the overworld map and battling, but I liked the change. The story lost... steam... in the second half, and the final boss was a chore, but, man, was I happy to see this come out (especially after that last attempt by different devs).
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: The best Steamworld game to date and my personal game of the year. I haven't played a game this well balanced in a while. The late game power fantasy is still there while still providing a sufficient challenge up to its final moments. All the characters are really lovable and the dialogue is really well written. Made me chuckle and tear up a few times. The art is spectacular and the new gameplay mechanics succeed upon the first heist game in so many ways. The music is top notch, Steampowered Giraffe knocked it out of the park once again. Thank you so much for creating such a wonderful game.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: This game is excellent. Normally, I'm not into either 2D side-scrollers or turn-based combat, but I got sent a key for this game and decided "eh why not try it at least?" I'm impressed with how fleshed out and well-balanced everything is. I'm playing on moderate, and some missions can be a bit harder than others, but everything feels progressable and you can always retry a mission if it goes poorly with no consequence. There's a fairly robust upgrade system that min-maxers like myself will go gaga over and the combat has a surprising level of depth and complexity. If you were in any way a fan of the other Steamworld games (which, I have never actually played myself), I'd feel confident saying you'll love this one.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Still can't balance for ♥♥♥♥.Like all the steamworld games you either play with one hand down your pants or get obliterated. They learned some positive lessons in terms of build variation, but the general problems that made their other games just bad still are there. The fact you can't write a single negative review without some retarded fanboys immediately swooping in to dispense free points is only testament to the fact that the steamworld games are essentially meh and only attract the comparatively small but same group they did since the first steamworld dig, the rest literally jumped ship. Overall a 6/10, but compared to how much better this game should be, given the experience of those making it, it's a trashfire that was completely avoidable. Dying never feels like you made a mess or positioned yourself badly, it consistently feels cheap because of random enemies showing up, dudes nailing shots over 3 rooms or generally random stuff that you can only know after already having played some missions. The consistent over reliance on uncreative cheap shots the game takes is something they should've done away with ages ago and it was a problem since the first steamworld heist, and even in other, mechanically different games, like steamworld quest, it was the main point of negativity. I can't wrap my head around this. You consistently have to play the highest difficulty to feel somewhat challenged in most instances and then get blown out of the water in some missions still after lowering the difficulty by 2 levels, because the game just works the way it works. "haha, you are surrounded now by 6+ enemies, nothing you can do, this is mandatory to progress the mission". Well, ♥♥♥♥ you too.The overworld map is a nice touch, but more tedious than ever. In the first heist game, I clicked where I wanted to go and was there in 5 seconds. Now I have to drive manually over half the map, defeating boring enemies and besting boring hazards to pick up that one item I wanted from the trader on the other side of the map. No fast travel. Seriously, there's so much wrong here, I cannot fathom how that escaped the devs understanding of what should and should not be in the game. If you want a lesson in tedium, this is for you. The game is made well enough and the setting and flair is nailed, as usual, which is the saving grace, just as is the sound design and soundtrack, but without these silver linings, the game would be virtually trash. There are much better turn based games than this, and the way people interact around here only shows that there is a very select few that actually really like this game and will let you - loudly and obnoxiously - know.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this title because I was still enamored with the first title in the series. I'll skip the next one. The game is _fine_. not a lot was learned from the first game, if I had played them back to back my review would have been more positive.main criticisms:-very tedious map navigation; you cannot quick-select previously completed or discovered missions. There is no quick-Travel or equivalent.(which is fine, if traversal improves with time - see Prey 2017. It does not in this game, at least so far.)-Missions feel very RNG reliant; there is an alarm system, that adds progressively more enemies to the map. What enemies appear is random. You are forced to run at a certain point. You can turn that down in the difficulty options, makes it marginally better.-While the skill-trees and resting mechanic made me engage more with the NPCS and the Resting points the first hour, it got tedious after that. You are forbidden from using weapons and characters more than once a day, needlessly drawing out the play time. -The player is encouraged to spec into different skill trees for all of his character, meanwhile not allowing you to focus on specific ones if you are trying to be efficient,I guess I overlooked these things in the previous title, instead I focused on the neat artstyle and unfamiliar music. It has since lost that particular appeal to me.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted to give a good review but the "balance" is absolute dogshite.Just played Absolute Immortality mission and it was just a piss take.Attack sphere, oh it's regenerating, surprise. Find the consoles to open shields? Fair enough. Except they are a long way off and the level keeps spawning more enemies behind you. BY the time I had cleared the shield switches (I did not hang about) the level was swamped with regenerating enemies. It got to the point where they were able to lay 3-5 shots on each of my team per turn. While still spamming more in, like 30-50 HP worth of enemies. Also those are regenerating pairs, so they are effectively worth double that if you can take down the pair in one turn. My team rarely has 60HP on full strength, but the level engine is quite happy to have a couple of hundred HP in play for the enemy. The 'wavy aim' is a good concept spoiled by lag, the trigger often doesn't fire or is just too slow to respond. A bit pointless if you always need perfect aim or an easy shot. This lost me a vital hit on the sphere my last mission.Level design is pretty cluttered as well, making the 'aura' feature often unusable. _childDocuments_.review: This isn't the game I thought it was when I bought it - I played another game, probably in the same world and by the same developers, a few years back. I thought this was a sequel for that game.This game played nothing like that game.I was immediately disappointed and thought, "Well, I liked that game, maybe I'll like this one."Nothing was the same! The other game felt more like a metroidvania than this one - this was a seafaring crew-based instance-map battles (pre-generated) and I felt like they immediately went way off course compared to the last one I played.But I sunk 15 minutes into it. Then 30 minutes.Then 60 minutes.Two hours later I knew I was coming up on the refund window and I still wasn't sure if I wanted to keep playing, but I powered through it because it was juuuuuuust enough of a hook to keep me interested.Now, 30'ish hours of gameplay later, I have finished the game. I will admit, the story bogged me down a bit - and the narrator is downright awful - but the gameplay is solid. Changing classes and seeing how things mixed and matched (there are definitely some class combos that work better than others) is what really kept me engaged. Getting all the stars in each area so I could unlock that "one extra" crew-wide perk at the local bar kept me invested. The goals were dangled in front of me like a carrot on a stick and I chased that carrot - the difference is, the game gives you the carrot before dangling a NEW carrot on a stick shortly thereafter.This game has mastered the reward system for my brain. "Go here, do this, do it a few more times, get this shiny thing that helps you get stronger!"By the end boss I was worried I was a bit too OP because the final maps had been a breeze, the pre-pre-final battle was a cakewalk, the pre-final battle was also easy - and then the final battle almost wiped the floor with me. Granted my team was very offensive-based, and I pulled a victory at the end. (No spoilers, but I believe the final battle is designed "differently" than previous map battles - not a single one of my robots got scrapped in the final battle. I won't say more than that, but the goal is, obviously, not to let your team get scrapped during a fight!)I can, without a doubt, recommend this game. Normally I'd say "Get it on sale" blah blah - because yes, I'm cheap - but if you are into these kinds of games, and this is something you're on the fence about, bite the bullet and do a 2 hour dive. If you don't like it, just refund it within the time limit, but if you're anything like me you're going to fall in love with this game pretty quickly.Oh, and yes - it does get easier after the first few levels. You need to get a larger crew, explore more map, and gain levels in your crew a bit before it really starts getting "fun" and "fair". You should be able to be well on your way within the first hour or so of gameplay, though.What are you waiting for? This game isn't going to play itself!

_childDocuments_.review: I don't exactly find it negative, (just sub-mediocre) but Steam has no neutral rating. By the end a lot of it pissed me off. It sure is worse than the first heist and than every Steamworld but TD. It already has enough positive reviews from people who haven't played other games and who didn't consume other stories to have a sufficient field of reference so here, a negative rating to send a message.The IP had a streak of the mostly almost great releases, which conditionally were some of the best games of the respective years. I liked this one at first but the longer it went, the more tedium, bad decisions, and downgrades from the original were getting to me.star wars episode 1 You were the chosen one! It was said that you would destroy the Sith, not join them!It’s a sub-mediocre sequel to a slightly above average clone of XSOM but in twodee. Instead of improving everything, they just reshuffled half the things around by slightly changing the coat of paint, and screwed up the important parts. The ricochet mechanics and the hat-hunting are uncommon, but we already had them in the original game, and this is just a tribute.The game opens with a garbage iOS tutorial that is hard to read and doesn’t let you do anything at all. It’s very restrictive long and unfun. And well the whole game is an iOS release, same as the first one you might say, but it’s not the same it is worse. The crappy GUI is all over the place, the binds make no sense and are extremely uncomfortable to use. It wants to fit tablets, and gaypads, and mice at the same time.After the tutorial you are kicked out to the overworld. Instead of the 3-star angry birds screen of the original you swim around in a boat and there’s even rudimentary combat, and the boat’s load-out and upgrade systems with some post-metroid progression. This should be a great change for the gameplay, worldbuilding and storytelling. But no, it soon devolves into tedium. The maps are empty and significantly bigger than they should be. It is adequate only if you go all-in on the engine upgrades during the end-game. But for the most of your play your slow tugboat just trudges the boring waters like in a walking simulator. And you have to haul your ash tray an absolute lot.You see, the devs had a genius idea to add “days” into the game. Your crewmates can participate only in one battle per day. The rotation mechanic to force players to use all of the guys would not be that bad, if they had to rest only one battle. But here even the equipment has to rest. Say, you have a crew of five, you’ve finished a battle designed for three guys. So now you have only two guys available. Either waste a day to rest, or swim around looking for a two-person battle. Every finished battle also has to rest, so you can’t just re-use the same one.In the overworld there are enemies which drop currencies. The common boats drop basic cash, each region has boats with premium currency, and boats with premiumest currency. All of which also resets on the day-end. So to play effectively at the start of the each day you would want to visit all four corners of the overworld to gather the premium and premiumest currencies to upgrade your boat and crew. The cash is not that plentiful until the final fight either, so hunting even the common enemies everyday is a sane proposition.And here you are, either swim everywhere all the time to optimize your leveling, or be extremely under-levelled and underpowered on the medium difficulty. After wasting 20 hours on the repetitive combat and swimming simulator overworld, while having to re-load a ton during the battles because of still being under-levelled, i just gave up and dropped the difficulty to the minimum to waste a little bit less time. And it still took me 55 hours to get all the achievements.The size of the crew grows very slowly, you get the last guy right before the final boss, you have to save a ton of money and then go back to the previous locations. So depending on your choices you don’t even have a chance to talk to one of them. Then a half of them are just slight re-skins of the original crewmates. And with the ability to swap their guns they become even more interchangeable. The new system of levelling is pretty interesting. Swapping the gun transfers your goon to the according tech-tree, but the previous tech tree remains open and you can pick and choose the perks for tokens. Some of the perks add more tokens, and some of the items add more tokens. You can train a goon to complete every tech tree, but you will run out of the game before you do that. I’ve got the achievement for it a couple of hours after the final boss. The guns themselves are generic, flat, and unmemorable. In the first game handguns were the sniping weapon, here it’s just the rifles. There’s also rocket launchers, assault guns, shotguns, pistols and melee. Make a surprised face.The timed missions suck twice more than in the original game. Because now they are combined with the infinite stream of spawning enemies and bad level design. Especially so in the arctic, where 70% of everything is covered in stun-locking ice (which ignores your anti-ice items) and 90% of cover is one hit enemy spawners. And you don’t even get any more exp for killing 200 dudes.The story is screwing sucks. It’s all about a whiny nepobaby. The main character sucks arse. And it’s all extremely predictable and obvious. It pretends to be about unrealistic expectations (this is a sequel, get it, get it?), but at the same time it shows you the characters of the first game as crippled stupid losers.Which is also very dumb. The prothean was an extremely strong fighter in the first game, why it does nothing but gossip in this one? You replace your hand, why cool competent strong independent woman Piper didn’t? Seeing her half-broken body is the epitome of this game. And then coal-burning steambots are cool, while atomic bots are evil and wrong. Was this game made by Merkel while she was peddling pukin’s experimental internet gas as a green source of power in the EU?Instead of cut-scenes you deserve only a work meeting with power-point presentation, and relatives showing you their vacation photo slides. The game uses the ugly-arse morph animations, and of course the sprites are flipping. The FoV is extremely small, smaller than in the first game, and there’s no zoom. The map is not a map, you can’t even see it whole. When you torture yourself with the terrible interface to change the hats, they are not swapped. You have to change the location to see them. You can’t save. Only enter/exit a location. There are no multiple save slots, not even in overworld.The devs are sucking-off that terrible ear-raep bad music band harder than ever. This is already Scary Movie levels of writing.Steamworld HatsWhen i beat the boss i got the speed and no-death achievements, so i decided to also get the rest. And it was entire nine hours of thankless farming for hats. Less people have all hats, than the perfect storm achievement for which you have to grind specific gear and specific tasks and find a perfect enemy. Some hats are hard to spawn, others are nearly impossible to shoot off due to bad hitboxes. Like, the melee soldiers. The hats are tall and your laser sight crosses it thrice, yet it always stays glued to the soldier’s head. The rifle soldier and its elite version wear the same hat but in different colours. One flies off by itself, the other is improbable to get. To get the rare hats you have to restart the same level with guarantee spawns a hundred of times (maybe more).

_childDocuments_.review: I played every single SteamWorld game (even the forgotten one for DSi/3DS, SteamWorld Tower Defense) and I have to admit: While the original SteamWorld Dig was my all-time favourite for a long time, SteamWorld Heist II (SWH2) is the game that finally took its place.The graphics are beautiful. With the addition of dynamic lighting, it really adds more depth to the even more improved 2D style. The map is a very nice upgrade to the first Heist, as it really feels like you are on the shard / overworld and not just on a map. The steering is a bit wonky, but adds to the challenge. I also like the fact that there are lots of secrets to uncover.The new job system is easy to learn, but also easy to miss. One mission brings it up, and it's really worth taking time to get into it, as it really adds much depth - and extremely fun and almost OP techniques - to your trick shots. One time I was able to shoot 42 times with ONE character during ONE TURN because I used the right combination of skills from different jobs on that character. Gives you some real #BigSteveEnergy!Without using the new job-system, some levels might be very hard even on lower difficulties. It takes some time to level jobs, and you will have to replay some levels you already completed for sure, but it's very much worth the time!I beat the game (story wise) at a playtime of 28 hours and I still have to complete all levels on full stars as well as collecting all the hats and level-up all teammates to the max. It has lots of replay value for sure! I was shocked when I thought the game was almost over, and I was actually only halfway in.At first, I was very skeptical about the new cast of playable characters, as Heist players like me are very used to Piper and her Crew. But I got to love them really quickly and following their individual background stories as well as the games' story, I really felt like they grew together like a family. Especially after the one VERY spoilery event that made things kinda emotionally on Captain Leeway's side. #CharacterDevelopmentDoneRightThe story is brilliant. It's nothing that deep and nothing extraordinarily new, sure. But it fits really well into the SteamWorld lore and adds a lot of new context to what happened in space after the Earth exploded at the end of SteamWorld Dig 2 / SteamWorld Build. It also captures the SteamWorld humour very well.SWH2 has cool references (that I won't spoil) to the first Heist, as well as some other titles. One was a very QUESTy surprise at the very end of the game, so keep playing!

_childDocuments_.review: Comparing this to games like XCOM is not fair. Those games rely on a strictly RNG based system, where you move a piece into a position where they can see an enemy and then they attempt to take a shot, usually giving you a % chance of success, and a % chance of a critical success.This game doesn't do that, instead after you move your pieces to where you want them to be you have to manually aim your shot and take it, this completely changes the formula of these games. Instead of a 90% shot missing and killing your favourite piece basically rendering the mission unwinnable instead you are the reason you missed, and you can improve on that aim. Rather than an entire game based on micro and macro risk-management you're instead encouraged to work on your aim alongside your positioning. Also this has the bonus effect of allowing for some crazy outcomes when shots miss there mark, possibly hitting other enemies or scenery or even friends, which isn't always a bad thing!Also this game has a deep and rewarding class based system. Usually games go piece 1 is class A, locking them into a tree of skills, sometimes even locking down what weapon they can use and in some cases making them useless because your class A pile is huge and full of max levels but your piece C pile is basically empty. Others allow you to select whatever classes you want and you quickly and easily find a formula which suits you and renders the entire game effortless. This game manages to split the difference with a very clever system.When you recruit a new character this character will come with a weapon and, usually, a personality befitting one of the class archetypes. You may keep this weapon and follow this character's archetype or you can change the weapon and, depending on what family of weapon you give them (Shotgun, rifle, pistol etc) the class they are will change as well, and all of the class abilities they have access to. That's not all, with the levels from all of the other classes that you have levelled on this piece you can pick up skills from those class trees, nowhere near as many as if you were that class, but enough to really boost the power of your character.Alongside this you have weapons of different tier and rarities, a legendary level 1 pistol probably won't be as good as a tier 12 pistol for example, and you can only bring classes that you have the weapons for, AND each character has their own character skill. Combine this all together and you have a really interesting choice when organizing your team for each mission, do I bring piece A and piece B; they both want a shotgun since that's their main class but I only really have one good shotgun, and if I bring them with a rifle they could level up enough to gain access to this skill which makes their shotgunning so much better! This rewarding experience encourages the player to branch out and take risks when making their team.When added the together the overarching story of levelling up each character and moulding them into the soldier you want them to be, and the rewarding gameplay which makes the act of doing that moulding just fun to engage in. Add on top of that a fun (but not anything groundbreaking (unless you've played a lot of the Steamworld games in which case it's a lovely little tale)) storyline, great art and fantastic music (and sound design in general) and you have one of my favourite games of 2024. An absolute gem which does the original proud and a truly wonderful experience.P.S: I didn't even mention the overworld actions which are absolutely great little breaks between the intense missions.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing once you get used to jank in the UI and controls.It's not obvious at a glance, but this game blends puzzle-like turn-cased tactical combat with RPG quite well. Unlike most similar games this one succeeds at balancing power progression with difficulty (for the most part). Power-ups are equally distributed between raw damage and utility (piercing, splash, arching shots, etc). Said utility usually reward creativity with far more damage than raw damage buffs.Outside of combat it offers great casual exploration. The map might seem simplistic, but it fits great with tight difficulty to create a great reward structure. Combat and exploration are often a risk. Without staying and grinding and you can't afford everything you want. That makes everything, including basic weapons and currency feel valuable. Drops also often reward rare weapons/accessories with unique effects (not just different color text with minor stat buff).Finally, characters, classes and ships all have upgrades and I'm happy to say most of them are noticeable in battle. Unlike many modern games, you don't have to track your numbers to notice the difference 1 melee damage or 1 movement made.There are at least 2 achievements that require their own playthrough (beat game on max difficulty and beat it within certain amount of in-game days). This game doesn't have the complexity or variety to warrant a 2nd playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty excellent. Largely similar in mechanics and such to the first game; it's not breaking massively new ground by any means, but it's well refined and makes great use of the mechanics. The new multi-classing systems are the biggest unique draw. While tempting to ignore initially (with the game basically having to make you engage with it the first time around), it allows for a whole lot of new team-building variety in the long run and is needed to bring your team to its full strength, while encouraging you to make things harder for some missions explorations for the sake of the greater good. The core gameplay is simply satisfying and great, and everything around it is well made.There are very few (very minor) criticisms. The main is that the difficulty curve is a bit janky - the game is hardest around the middle acts as they throw large waves of enemies and particularly frustrating status effects at you, while towards the end it feels easier as your crew unlocks some very strong powers and abilities. The second is that the new overworld submarine combat - while fun enough and easy enough to skip past while exploring - isn't super engaging, and to earn enough currency for the expensive shop purchases it feels like you're compelled to go back through every recent area after each night's sleep to grind significant gallons.

_childDocuments_.review: A great follow-up to a fantastic, unique turn-based strategy game. Adding the ability to learn and level-up jobs makes for new ways to plan out great strategies that make the best use of each character. This time the world is a little more open and somewhat less linear, but still mostly follows a similar playbook.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is a solid 7 out of 10 game. The overall mechanics of the game are solid. Shots ricocheting from walls to hit enemies is a hell of a lot of fun. The presentation in terms of graphics and music is good and the story is fine. Overall, I enjoyed my time playing it.However, I can agree with a lot of the negative reviews this game received. Yes, the enemy spawn is ridicolous at times. Yes, the option/necessity to grind your way up when you hit a wall is bad. Sniper class is very very bad, you are constantly forced to move and sniper can't reload and move in the same turn. Sniper is also bad, because level design was always kind of off -- the walls are very often tilted in a way, where it is impossible to hit targets without moving.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: It's release date of 08/08 this year couldn't have been a better birthday present for me!I've played the original on 3DS and beat it on elite back when it was new, and it's been a blast to play it's sequel nearly ten years later while in college!This game takes everything the original did, and makes and entirely new genre of side-person shooter, akin to how Undertale made it's own entirely new genre of rpgs!This game, it's original masterpiece along with The Steampunk Giraffe Musical Band the OG game introduced me to, and the the SteamWorld series will forever remain a solid set of brass steam pipes that pump my soul through my heart!
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Props to the Besties podcast for getting the word about this gem out. A truly fun tactical, turn-based combat game that is in a lot of ways reminiscent of old browser flash games like Bowman or Raft-Wars that personally captivated my heart back when I was a kid. This game takes the concept of trajectories, ricochets and sightlines and somehow manages to keep the gameplay loop involving those simple concepts continuously satisfying throughout the experience by introducing new weapons, enemies, elements and mechanics.Other highlights include the story, which at first glance revolves around a classic, clichè apocalyptic scenario with a MacGuffin that actually spins deeper a couple hours in to focus more around parental overshadowing and the burden of a legacy placed on the protagonist. Alongside the story there are a myriad of memorable characters just oozing with personality who all manage to compel conversation and make the player actively seek them out just for their dialogue. As an XCOM veteran, I was at first disappointed that playable characters were limited to a pre-existing, tailored cast, but I quickly warmed up to the colourful bunch-- especially so with the hat system.Pro tip: even early on, have *all* characters spec at least one or two levels into sniper for the sightline upgrade. Having even a tiny bit of prediction to your shots can remedy a difficult situation.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Same great tactical gameplay as the original SteamWorld Heist, with added fun overworld combat, great upgrades, crew job system, etc. Highly recommended!The one criticism is that it took me half the game to get my crew's jobs up to level 5, which I wanted to do before progressing on to other jobs. The game encourages you away from that, but it was the only way to see the level 5 abilities of each job. This meant I didn't get to do a ton of playing with that system, so I do wish job progression was a little faster from the beginning. No big harm done though, still had a blast!
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: A vertical take on the tactics RPG is an excellent idea. The movement and combat remind me of Worms Armageddon from the early 2000s. The new thing that this does though is add open zones for you to explore so you can approach each area in the order that you choose. Giving you some ownership of the difficult. The one area that is a bit confusing is the Job system, but even with a basic understanding I think you will be able to use it to advance your missions. Overall it has been another fun Steam World game.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: By and large a direct upgrade on the first game.The meat remains the tactical combat, and it has been expanded. The game is overall longer this time around, and the larger roster and variety of classes this time around reflects that. Each weapon type is distinct, and there is considerable customization offered via the cross class system and lots to play around with in combining class skills with each character's unique skills. Unlike other games with wide rosters, you are also highly encouraged to use the entirety of the roster via the bounty rewards system, as each character can only go on one mission each 'day'.Music is also quite good and offers a unique vibe, and most definitely fits the setting.The sequel also an added naval combat layer. Said additional layer isn't particularly anything to write home about though and is not the meat of the game, and honestly by the end of the game the lack of fast travel around the map is a little bit annoying

_childDocuments_.review: Hey look Steamworld Heist 1 got a sequel after like nine years! I played the original six years ago for the first time. Damn.Let's get to the good stuff. For those unaware, the Heist duology is a pair of 2D turn-based strategy games, in which you control a crew of rogues getting into shootouts. The games have a very "XCOM-esque" feel to the core gameplay, with a core distinction. Rather than having percentage based chances to hit, you actually are the one who manually aims the shots! Alright, that's out of the way. In this game you play as Quincy Leeway, an absolute failson of a guy who has lost his crew and submarine, and cannot even fight back due to his lack of an arm or combat prowess of any kind. This, combined with the severe expectations forced down on him due to his mother being the bot who struck down the legendary Kraken is the main driving force of his character growth. He is a big contrast to Piper Faraday, the captain from the last game, as a result of this, who didn't really have an explicit in-game motivation and went along in missions with the rest of the crew.Speaking of, this game shakes up quite a bit of systems, and the crew is one of them: rather than being recruited in a predetermined order, the crew shows up in bars across the Shard, an oceanic fragment of the destroyed Earth that acts as this game's setting. Thing is, they don't show up "organically", as in the first game, but rather, who shows up where is randomized and changes every in-game day, with the exception of two starting characters that are always the same. This causes a lot of the crew to not really have "growth", as it were, as their writing has to be accomodated for this and so it hurts them a lot. One of my favourite crewmates, Poe, is the daughter of one of the characters from the previous game, and part of her side character arc is to grow past the legacy of his father as an unpredictable conman to try to live an honest life, something that ties her to the main themes of the game, which are "living in someone's shadow" as well as "dealing with expectations forced upon you because of circumstances that you cannot control". However, her character arc would simply have been lost on me if I had recruited her later since I would have missed most of her dialogue and reactions to the world. As for how this affects gameplay, first, we need to talk about the job system. Unlike Heist 1, every character can access the same skills by equipping a specific weapon type, which will assign them that job's passives and let them get levels in that class. Additionally, you can spend Cogs to activate abilities from other jobs that you have previously unlocked (as in, if I have 3 levels in Flanker, I can spend Cogs to use those skills in other classes, with the cog cost varying depending on the skill). You'd think this makes characters very homogenous, but they avert this by having unique unlockable abilities that activate regardless of job. For example, Poe herself gets extra movement, and much later in the game, a 50% dodge chance. All characters start with a default job, and the later you get them, the higher the level they will have on that class, at the cost of not having any points in other classes. As a result, the last character you recruit will just be more limited than everyone else since they won't have access to powerful skills from other classes.I was a bit iffy in the job system at first, but admittedly, giving characters broken skills from other classes is really fun. It gives an amount of mix and matching and progression that the first game just did not have, and it makes every character feel viable, even if not everyone is equally powerful. What I am iffy on is the day system. Every day, each crewmate can only do a mission before they need to rest for the day, which, fair enough, getting shot at is very taxing. But there's no... real reason to not use all of your actions other than not feeling like it? Like, there's no cost or anything to optimizing each day, and there's no reason for it beyond an achievement, either, making it feel pointless. If I had to guess, it was probably because of the bounty system, which gives you the ability to spend tokens you get by clearing missions and doing naval exploration/combat in exchange for sweet, sweet loot, but it doesn't help much at making it not feel a bit empty, if you ask me. You are forced to end the day early and lose all of those tokens if your sub gets sunk, but like... that merely wastes your time still. I prefer it to the alternative but a "Hardcore Mode" of some kind where there is actual punishment for taking too long would have helped make those days actually count.Oh yeah, naval exploration/combat. Yeah, the world map has graduated from being a glorified mission selection screen to an actual mode where you pilot your submarine and take on enemy ships, explore for loot, and even collect upgrades to explore more of the map. And it's really fun! ...the first time you explore somewhere, anyway. The game could use a fast travel mechanic. The world is massive, so getting from point A to B is a bit slow, especially before you get upgrades to move faster. Still, don't get it twisted: I loved everything else about the sub.As for everything else, let's do a quick roundup:-Story: It's a bit more involved and personal than Steamworld usually gets to. Nice! I enjoyed it, but that might be because I'm already a fan of the series and know how they roll. It's not gonna blow off your socks or anything, not even close, but like. It's neat. -Aesthetic: While it is undeniable that the game looks great, I kind of miss the old artstyle of Heist 1 a little. It's still Steamworld to the core, and I am undeniably blinded by rose-tinted glasses, but I can't help but feel like the game looks a little too... smoothed out sometimes. Really weird complaint, I know. Still, the game looks fantastic.-Soundtrack: STEAM POWERED GIRAFFE ARE BACK WOOOOO THE VIBES ARE IMMACULATE HELL YES HELL YES HELL YESthe bgm for missions and stuff is really drab though lmao-Difficulty: Maybe it's inexperience, but the game is actually quite challenging in... Experienced. Which is the second hardest difficulty. Okay maybe that one's on me. Still, it felt pretty fair, if a little hard and overtly spammy in missions. That said, because the game sets up a checkpoint every 2 turns, and backing out of a mission costs you nothing but time (and pride), it's not super hard, all things considered (I am afraid of Elite tho lmao). Early game with the sub is also pretty rough, as you'd expect. The game does feature a custom difficulty option that lets you manually adjust sliders based on certain parameters, and it includes boat combat sliders, so if you're struggling too much with the boat, or too much on missions, those sliders might come in handy.So yeah. I had a lot to say about this game, because there's a lot to talk about this game, and a lot that I like to talk about from this game. I never really expected a Heist 2, but I am glad they came back and did it. I loved this game and my time with it.TL;DR: Sequel to a fantastic 2D strategy game that improves and adds a lot to a formula that I already absolutely adored. Really fun and charming, and a phenomenal entry in the Steamworld series. I love this game.
