_childDocuments_.review: Update: After 34 hours of play exclusively on my Steamdeck, I have completed the game and loved every minute of it! I am still craving more.Original review-I totally adore Steam World Heist, it is one of few games I have actually finished and even replayed. This one is very much familiar to the first but in a submarine which you can upgrade in various ways. The map hub is somewhat open world as in you can explore the map, uncovering missions and battling ships and submarines in realtime as you do. The story is simple, yet fun to follow.Graphically it is on par with the previous entry which is no bad thing, it looks beautiful, characters and levels are well designed just like the previous entry. The combat is what I love and has me hooked, it is kind of like Worms, turn based, and you choose the type and trajectory of the attacks. Shooting and launching grenades can be so satisfying thanks to how bullets and bombs can ricochet off hard surfaces, this adds a fun and thought provoking playstyle to your attacks.At the time of writing this review, I have not yet completed this game, it appears to be a fair bit bigger than the previous one, it has a little more depth too since you can actually combine some skills for each character from previous job skills they have used. The ability to upgrade your submarine adds to the depth. You can also hire new bots to your crew through finding them in bars that are scattered around the world, each one has their own job style, level and can also be switched around on what job they do, aswell as levelled up in that job style.I feel if more Steamworld Heist games, or if DLC was to be released for this, I would certainly buy and have no regrets. Great game and definitely recommended. PS: It plays great on Steamdeck!
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: 2024 is a great year for all fans of tactical games. In my review for Tactical Breach Wizards (TBW) I wrote that it's a top tier game like XCOM or Into the Breach. I would say that Steamworld Heist 2 is even better! - The game has deep combat mechanics, the new jobs system significantly increases variety and replayability.- The game has a perfect difficulty curve, you constantly feel challenge and pressure.- Exploration part of the game is good, not perfect. It works as a rest from tactical battles. - The game has amazing graphics and a soundtrack.- Ideal for a handhand playing on Switch or Steam Deck (TBW has issues here).- Localization for 12 languages, including Ukrainian! (TBW is English only) I finished the game in ~45 hours. And it was an addicting and fun experience from the very first minutes till credits.Highly recommended, even without a discount!
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't finished the game yet.  Love this game.  It's everything a sequel should be.  All the things from the first game that made it great are back and everything they've added work very well to enhance the game play.  I will add that the first one was an epic cosmic adventure while the new story line is a more local small town hero story, but there is far more to do and more replay value in this new one.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: SteamWorld Heist II isn't a platformer, RPG or metroidvania, it's an excellent turn-based strategy game.Pros:- Fun turn-based strategy with a variety of weapon types and tons of upgrades/enhancements for your characters to unlock.- Greatly expanded since the original game- The new overworld map provides a nice change of pace with some real-time ship combat, exploration and treasure hunting. Plus the underwater element is an excellent addition for more strategy and variety in the overworld.Cons:- Combat music is too repetitive. There seems to be a couple different themes, but it gets repetitive fast when you're in a long battle. I would've liked an extra couple themes, or at least rotate them throughout the same battle.The first game seemed to have only one battle theme which it got old really fast. I basically stopped playing the first game because of this.- Vocal music tracks whenever your crew rest for the night and during a couple special cut scenes. Makes me cringe every time they start. I wish there was an option to just have instrumental tracks during these parts of the game. This is a personal gripe though, and I'm sure many people will like the songs.Outside of the music there's not much for me to complain about, this is a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. The first steamworld heist was probably one of my favourite games of all time when it released and I always hoped that there would be a sequel. Finally, 7 years later, there is one, absolutely worth the wait, this sequel delivers an amazing continuation of a great story, introduces awesome new features and game-play to what was already a fantastic game type, and best of all, it hardly requires any grind to fully 100%! Super fun, and not tedious to do any mission on really any difficulty at all, I hope they add more DLC to this game in the future, It would be the cherry on top of a delicious cupcake. Can not wait to see what the steamworld series has next to offer. 11/10!
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun! If you liked the first one, you'll love this one. Plus there's a whole new aspect of the game where you pilot the ship instead of just clicking on different locations, there's battles and everything.My one note: please stop the singing, i wish there was an option with no singing in the bars.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible follow-up to arguably the best game in the Steamworld series. Excellent length (it can sometimes be too much - a fast travel option for the world map would be welcome), well-balanced difficulty, great characters; overall an outstanding experience, tremendous value, and one of the best games of 2024.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: If you have played the first Steamworld Heist, then you have a rough idea about the flavour and feel of this game too.  (If you haven't then both are filled with great music, splendid art, a good plot with charm and wit, alongside a turn-based skillshot game.)  With that out of the way, how is this one better?Job specialisations which you can mix and match for the perfect individuals in your team - that wasn't clear - your characters can each do all the jobs and cherrypick the skills they want to use at any given time with no penalty for switching every battle if desired.The range of weaponry is superb.  You have so many items to choose from, at every tier of power.You have a submarine this time, which engages in real-time battles and can, yes, be upgraded significantly.  So much so that the sub itself has nine slots at maximum for weaponry or boosters.Now, a confession.  Despite loving the original game, I baulked at the price initially.  I shouldn't have.  I did buy it when it went 34% off but in my defence I was caught up in a couple of other games before then, not to mention they released this the same day as another one of my hot favourites.  On reflection, I should have bought this on release.Don't be fooled by the 2d layout and think it is some flash game or simple platformer.  This is a work of art.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: SteamWorld Heist (the first game) is one of my all time favorite games. I've played every level of it on every difficulty, and I did it all in bed on my Steam Deck. When I saw there was a sequel, I was thrilled, and bought it the moment it came out. The gameplay is just as amazing as the first game, but the new mechanics of SteamWorld Heist 2 make it unreasonably tedious to play. The first game was in space, and each level was on a line similar to the world map of a game like Super Mario; this game has you and your crew in a submarine, driving around a massive world map covered in a cloudy "fog of war" searching for another mission location. While you're doing this, your submarine is being attacked by underwater mines, subs, and other ships. Neat idea, but when I just want to sit down and play the game, it's really annoying that it takes me ten minutes of scowering the map and dodging enemies on the seas, to get to a mission, which is the gameplay I seek. To make matters worse, you have to go all the way back to a bar, which could be a really long distance away, to "sleep" and end the day, after every mission, further adding to the tedium of driving around the map (and when you talk to the bartender to end the day, there's another freaking cutscene every time). The other mechanic added in this version is that any character can be any class, and you can have the benefits of any class outside of the chosen class with "cogs." Again, neat idea, but it's so tedious compared to the original game, which was pick characters of a class, pick items for that character, and play, that I have to spend an additional few minutes before each mission, after finally finding one (and skipping though an unreasonable amount of unnecessary cutscenes), before I can get into the game. I love both games; the turn-by-turn playstyle allows me to really think about my next move, what characters and classes and items I choose, movement strategy, etc, but there is so much fluff in SWH2 that it's actually frustrating. Still recommend, but I hope there's a 3rd installment that combines the pros of both games into something truly enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Just like SteamWorld Heist 1 in the best ways, and improves on some areas - like the world map!Recommend for fans of the first, and those new to the series. Game is super polished, robots are endearing, and difficulty is completely customisable. For example, I don't mind the number of health of the enemies, but I don't like feeling rushed to reach time-limited chests. I could change just that aspect, or any other before each mission.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Great sequel to the first Steamworld Heist, level-based turn-based shooter with ricochet mechanics.Good progression on weapons and items for increased damage and utility, very reminiscent of XCOM progression from dinky pistols to alien plasma tech.Overworld ocean exploration is done via submarine, with upgrades to open up more areas of the map and combat with other vessels for looting upgrade materials.Story is reasonable and has a few turns here and there, multiple crew members with various mechanical designs to follow along with their stories, and callbacks to the first game.Will dock it one point for miss-able achievements that would require another 20-30-hour playthrough if missed, as well as a hat grind with a collection that can't be sorted or checked off easily - user guide was a must for filling out the collection.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent follow up to Steam World Heist! This sequel adds in a new exploration game mode which enhances the gameplay loop quite well. Other than that, one notable change from the original is the job system. While it's a bit confusing at first, its a pretty interesting spin on multi-classing your characters.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: THIS is how you do a sequel. Improving all the good things from the 1st game, while adding a lot of new things. I've been craving for more since the 1st game, and they really do deliver in this iteration. The naval exploration and battle might be a tad tedious, but still bearable.Those soundtracks though.... exquisite. Heck, I even got stuck in the main menu due to how "nostalgic" it is. Steam Powered Giraffe really upped their ante.Great job devs! Thank you for the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Attune your ears to the grinding gears in this life of "un-delightment" full of steam-powered nautical electronical un-ironical fun! This is such a lovely and charming game! I'm new to the SteamWorld series, but I sure am glad I got this game when it came out. I'll be playing the other games when I get through with this one. Engaging strategic turn-based combat that really makes you try your best to figure out the most optimal path, vibrant character design that makes everyone feel unique, and one of the gosh-darn best soundtracks a steam-bot could ever hope for by Steam Powered Giraffe! And it's all wrapped up in a lovely little story about self-discovery and making a name for oneself on their own terms~ It doesn't need all sorts of bells and whistles, but it sure does have hats on top of hats! No, literally! Lots of cute hats to collect and wear, and doing so just adds a little extra challenge as a cherry on top! This is a game that knows what it's about (even if the Captain doesn't seem to at first :P), and for what it sets out to do, I'd give it an 11/10!
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: An improvement to the previous installment, but also a bunch of issues. Wait for a small sale, maybe?If you liked the previous game, or are generally a fan of turn-based tactic games with an RPG splash, this might tickle your fancy.However, there are a bunch of issues with this game that make me recommend this on sale only:For about 70% of the game, the main protagonist is an awfully unlikable whiny nepobaby who will spend every 2nd sentence lamenting his oh-so-horrible fate being the son of someonesomething.To make the main protagonist such a whiny brat is an incredibly weird decision by the devs.If you play games mostly for the story and writing, this won't be the game for you.Another issue is that all the characters you can actually send on missions (10 characters are recruitable) are 90% interchangeable because every character can learn every class and skill in it. In fact, the game encourages you strongly to do so, as you'll otherwise waste experience points.What this leads to, however, is that besides some fluff comments/dialogue, the characters lack anything to make them distinguishable from each other. They each get one personal skill + one passive at the very end that is unique to them and that's it.Characters need their own skill lines to make them feel different to the player and this game basically just gives you 10 blank slates - a real shame. This also removes any replayability.Would have been better to have much fewer characters, no rotation mechanic but each character has their unique skill trees.Then there are some questionable design decisions.Like the shaky aiming, which can easily make you miss shots and is just unnecessary and annoying.Also a chapter near the end has you backtrack through the entire map, which is an incredibly silly (and again, annoying) way to pad the game time.The sub control is... fine for the most part, but for some reason bumping into walls turns the game into a pinball machine - weird!
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved this first this is an obvious buy. Same great gameplay, cool weapon and character perks. This time around with updated better graphics and great world map boat fighting meta game. The game was more difficult than I remember starting out but it made me just want to play more and get those killer weapons that just wreak bot faces. For those who have never played any Steamworld Heist, imagine Worms turn based aiming mechanic with light RPG leveling and quest map progression. It's one of a kind fun.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: A unique, interesting and just plain fun take on squad based strategy games. On the hardest difficulty, combat is  challenging, but rarely unfair, and the artstyle and music are both wonderful.  Maps are varied, and force you to take varied approaches, and you're encouraged to swap out party members to do more missions, as well as trying new classes to get extra skills to pass on to your favorites.  At the price, it's hard not to recommend if you're a fan of similar strategy games.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: This game was just a really good time from start to finish. I'm super happy that I played it, and if you like other games in this genre you will like this one too. The tone is great, the mechanics are a lot of fun, and it's all wrapped up in a super neat aesthetic. It also has a really cool OST! It has a hat song!Also: It runs extremely well on the Steam Deck! I get a locked 90FPS on my OLED with like 5 hours of battery life.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Another great one. Loved the first one a lot, played it through on the hardest setting twice over the years. This one kept the things that made the other one great, and I really liked the stuff it added like the jobs system to mix things up, and the whole overworld submarine exploration/combat that's not super complex, but a good palette cleanser between the missions that take a lot of focus if you're playing in any sort of hard difficulty which you should if you're an average turn-based enjoyer. Anyways, great game that's easy to get in and back into if you haven't played for a while, no complex story that you can forget. Casual but is very engaging. I just finished it, took me 47 hours, veteran difficulty. Good bang for the buck.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Insanely good!Best game of 2024 for me for sure!+ Does everything the first game does but better! Many options to customize your Party without you feeling like you have to. You can literally not multiclass and still have a great time, however if you like to min-max you can too!+ The game respects your time which I love! If you dont care about conversations, you can just not start them, 90% are optional. The game starts insanely fast, from desktop to ingame is literally 3 seconds+ Music from Steam Powered Giraffe delivers as always!+ Lots of content, at 20+ hours I still havent finished the game which is amazing!+ Pricetag at 30€ is a steal, thanks for not using 70€ like all other companiesNeutral: Time pressure: Maybe do some missions without Alarm/Pressure but with harder enemies instead?- Only thing missing for me is a way to inspect enemies to see status effectsNow lets hope they will do a 3rd one soon :)
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: As it always is with the Steamworld series, Heist 2 is a quality game.Just like with Steamworld Dig 2, Heist 2 is an upgrade in pretty much every department compared to the first game.Every system has been polished to an increasingly high standard and it's a joy to play.The only two things that were subpar for me were the songs by Steam Powered Giraffe and the final boss.For me, the songs just didn't fit the mood and made it hard to focus on the dialogue when they played. But at the same time, I just don't listen to this type of music, so maybe that's why I didn't like them.The final boss isn't that bad, and the Steamworld series has had much, much worse, so I can't complain.Overall, great game.Better than Heist in pretty much every aspect, while also not being too tied down to the original.Absolutely worth a playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game!Nice light-hearted story, likeable characters. The gameplay is pretty intuitive and fun. The multi-classing was neat but it kind of felt like I should always be using a new class to gain levels and more abilities rather than playing the best class for that character. Would have liked some form of fast travel, but ship travel was enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Thumbs up but with cavaets. The game slightly overstays its welcome, the mechanics and missions are nice but maybe not 30+ hours nice. Along with the missions that play similar to Heist 1, there is an overworld map, character levels and item progression. All missions have waves of enemies coming down on you while your try to push forward / collect / kill something, then get out, so if you don't like it's approach, this may be not for you. The story does it's purpose but nothing to write home about. It works perfectly on Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: As good as the first if not better. Almost exactly how I wanted the sequel to be.Expanded maps and more enemy variety.Many improvements to the core mechanics and clearer item/in-combat descriptions. Class system is interesting and creates many different play styles. Very satisfying when you create some great combos!Wish there was a gold star system like the first game, that was one of the main things I missed.If I were being nit picky, I would say that the naval combat was one of the weak points of the game. So was the resting mechanic, which breaks the flow of game slightly.Overall, great game and would recommend if you liked the first. The Steamworld Series never disappoints me and has become one of my favourite series.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Great game , especially if you like Xcom or Midnight Suns. Lighter take on it, but it makes it so easy to go into missions, customize, and have fun. Great momentum throughout and a great sense of progress. Extremley fun combat, especially when I just turned the difficulty way down and blazed through. Final time 27.6 hours, doing every mission. Difficulty is super customizable though, where you can choose presets or tune specific parts to find the balance you want.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Great game overall.-Played it on hard mode and it was tough for some missions with reload from checkpoints (up to 2 turn before) or even retries for a better team comp with no penalties. -You basically get 5 classes with your characters having some unique abilities and you have to switch their weapons to make them lvl up other classes to mix and match abilities. In easier modes it might be optionnal but in hard mode it is necessary and it makes the game feel fresh along the 30ish hours needed for the whole game (no grind). -World map is ship based and has it's own gameplay with story progression and tie-ins feeling fresh to the end.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the first one, or if you are simply a fan of turn-based tactics games, this is an easy recommend. While the new overworld mechanics can be a little finnicky, they don't outstay their welcome, and add a bit of exploration and push-your-luck compared to the "pick a mission" flow of the original. Also shout-out to Steam Powered Giraffe, who knock it out of the park with the soundtrack once again, not losing a single bit of their luster and matching the vibes that the new settings brings perfectly.Crowbar my beloved, please give her a standalone game.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I completed and enjoyed the first SteamWorld Heist game. I've now completed the sequel. Overall it was a pleasant experience with a few issues.As you can tell from my playtime, there is lots of content in the game. The new additions to the series - naval combat and a jobs system have their good points and some drawbacks. The naval exploration and enjoyable - exploring the massive map is very interesting. The naval combat is also quite fun although at times a bit frustrating when my sub would get so damaged I wasn't able to attempt a mission until I rested again. The job system in theory seems like a good way to add flexibility to upgrading your crew members. And crew member can take any role, purely dependent on which weapon is equipped. This gives you lots of potential combinations and upgrades but it makes each crew member less interesting and unique. I think I would have preferred that each character be given a more extensive upgrade path unique to them.My only significant issue with the sequel was the difficulty balancing in missions. For example some of the easiest missions were the boss missions, with the exception of the final boss who was quite challenging for me. A few regular  missions where there was a massive number of spawning enemies were a bit frustrating. Fortunately it is easy to either go back a couple of turns to try a different strategy or abort the mission with no penaltyOverall a fun game that I recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I love everything bout this game. It's become one of my all time favorites! I played the first game and loved it, and the sequel improves on its predecessor in so many ways. The story is more impactful, the game has more room for experimenting and playing around (rewards you for doing so!), and It just has a way of pulling you in and making you feel more invested. I just love this game!
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the first game, and if that is the experience you are looking for, then this will scratch the itch.  This game is not without it's flaws though.  The combat is what you would expect, turn-based, and there is quite a bit of strategy necessary if you set goals for yourself such as "get every bonus from every mission."  The game is overall fairly easy on the Experienced difficulty.  Not sure how it would be on other difficulties.Three things could have been better:  A)  The game puts a big focus on naval combat this time around.  It isn't difficult combat, but it also isn't particularly fun.  You have to rest your crew after every two or three missions... buy every time you rest, all of the naval enemies respawn, so you have to fight your way back through areas you have already cleared to get to where you want to go.  It became tedious after the first two biomes.B) I feel like every character is a jack of all trades by the end of the game.  There is a skill tree for each job (class), and as you level each job you pick up perks and abilities.  But there are only 5 levels to each class, and you can easily get 5 levels in just three or four missions.  So by the end of the game, every character pretty much has 3-5 levels in every job... which means everyone can do everything and they lose a bit of their identity.C)  The level design is very "samey" throughout the entire game.  There was never any really interesting level design... just a bunch of ladders, grates, barricades and walkways.I played through this game very slowly, with a lot of pausing, and AFKing.  So the average person will probably get about 35-40 hours out of this game.  I think $30 is on the high end of fair, but still worth the money at that price.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: the first part was already good, this one is even better.Great flexible class system, overworld battles are nice and not annoying.Bounty system is fun. Game is forgiving, you only lose time if you die on the world map.You can change difficulty at any time. Veteran was perfect for me.You can restart and replay missions without any loss or even load checkpoints (go back 2 turns)Took me 30 hours go get all starts on all missions.Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: SWH2 is exactly what a perfect sequel should be. It's got all the bits from the first game that we love and iterates on them. At first I was pretty opposed to changing jobs with my characters as it felt weird and that I was playing sub-optimally, but the mechanical depth this game has with all the different synergies from the jobs really makes it shine. At one point, I made Poe a brawler with some cogs put into reaper for warcry, all her flanker abilities and gave her two sidearm items. I was able to do like 5 different attacks in one turn with boosted damage and hella mobility. If you loved the first game, you're gonna love this one even more.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: It starts slow but picks up once you unlock more multiclassing options in combat and missions begin to require more simultaneous crewmates. The strategic gameplay remains pretty engaging from then on out. Ricocheting bullets over comically long distances to scrap a moderate variety of enemies is a task that takes a while to get old. The basic gameplay of Steamworld Heist 2 feels consistently rewarding to experiment with and the game does its best to pace out new abilities/equipment/environments over its surprisingly long playtime.The approach to difficulty here is a tad confusing. The option to choose your difficulty without any repercussions (or incentives) seemed like a nice accessibility inclusion. Steamworld Heist 2 is inarguably better when it's pushing you to consider every option and the game can be very challenging if you want it to be. However, some missions also drag on for a while, and the prospect of needlessly gambling on unproductive higher difficulties only to lose a particularly prolonged mission makes the idea of playing on anything above ‘moderate’ seem unnecessary.Another confusing decision that Steamworld Heist 2 makes is the ability to recruit more crewmates than will ever be necessary for any one mission. Sure a larger crew would allow you to collect more slightly-helpful bounty rewards in a single day, but isn’t it smarter to focus all the XP you receive on the smallest number of necessary crewmates? It would feel strange from a narrative perspective to take on more people when the job system lets anyone fill any role with the same effort (bar a few character-specific abilities I suppose).The submarine overworld is a pleasant upgrade from the first game’s method of picking levels. Even if returning to a bar at the end of almost every mission is awkward, the freedom to float around, pick up treasure, and do some minimalistic exploration to uncover levels in a non-linear order certainly beats using a connect-the-dots map. Also, the high-seas theming is a smart way to differentiate the sequel from its space-faring predecessor.Steamworld Heist 2 is an overall great-looking and great-feeling 2D turn-based tactics game. The scrappy but cohesive robot art style that this franchise has maintained has grown into something familiar and refined. While I believe I had second thoughts about the first game, this sequel is definitely an improvement. The level design feels more handcrafted, the job system is thought-provoking, and the overworld ties everything together nicely. Can’t say much about the story though.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very well executed 2D turn-based tactical game with some additional bells and whistles.Unlike in many similar games, you're not at the mercy of random rolls, because all your shots are more or less deterministic. The only uncertainty comes from weapon sway, but the game does a lot to help you track it. There are aimlines, and their exact utility depends on the weapon and the character's skills, but even without one you can still watch the weapon itself. It almost always feels like you didn't miss because of random chance, but because you risked too much. For instance, the game encourages you to rely on trick shots, and especially on ricochets, but it's your decision whether to try a trick shot with a very narrow window of opportunity. You can almost always try something easier instead, and still get things done.The enemy almost always has a crushing numerical advantage, and the game expects you to balance that with combos. The main trick (which the game explains in due time) is to make characters switch between weapons, because each weapon progresses a different skill set. For instance, using shotgun eventually gets you a skill that makes you invulnerable to unfriendly surfaces, while using an SMG gives you a skill where you can kill a non-boss enemy instantly. It's all fairly arbitrary, but makes you think about various ways in which these skills could be combined. It's a strqategic choice, because skill progression is fairly slow, so you can't just learn everything.There's also a simple mechanic that encourages you to use all of your characters, because then you can do more missions during one in-game day, which means you can accumulate bigger bonuses and get better rewards. Still, at some point it begins to feel like there's only one type of character with multiple skins.In terms of pacing, there's nothing to complain about. In most missions there's a soft time constraint, where new enemies keep spawning, and their spawn rate keeps increasing. This gives you opportunities for trade-offs between e.g. getting more loot and taking fewer risks. I'm low-key amazed by how well balanced this is. Enemy spawn in randomly chosen (though pre-set) spots, and there may be different enemies each time, so every time it happens it shakes up the situation in a unique way, but it's always manageable.The game won't let you save-scum, and at its default difficulty it can be fairly unforgiving. Sometimes one mistake opens you up for an enemy's own combo that kills your character in one turn. The visual language isn't perfect, and I occasionally end up in unpleasant situations, because I though I had one more action, or because I didn't expect this action to end my turn, or because I didn't notice a turret in the corner. You can abort a mission without consequences, other than the game registering the attempt as a failure, which may or may not hurt your feelings and/or end-of-game stats.At the same time, the game really does reward you for cool ideas, and sometimes feels like a playground, thanks to things like walls and cailing with weird angles (that let you do more trick shots!). One example of a neat detail is the enemy with an impenetrable shield that protects their front... except it acts like any other surface, which means you can use it for trick shots. In one case, I hit the enemy in their face while shooting from behind.Unlike the original Heist, which had basically no gameplay other than tactical 2D combat, the sequel has a separate mode for traveling around its world. It's not tactical at all! It has a very arcade feel to it, but also a surprising amount of depth. On the one hand, it's a bit of a bullet hell, but on the other your weapons shoot automatically. Most of them don't have anywhere near 360 coverage, so you still need to point them in the right direction. In a brilliant move, the authors made some of them point to the sides, which means charging the enemy is not your only option. I don't remember when was the last time I did so much dancing around my opponents.The story and characters are still a token effort, and are only there to give you (paper-thin) reasons to go forward. But that's okay. The tactical layer is so good I'd probably still play it if the whole game was just a spreadsheet with buttons to trigger new missions.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Even better than the first Steamworld Heist! I recommend playing that one first if you haven't played it already. That reveal with that music at the beginning of the last chapter; superb!The only complaint I have is how long it took to get across the World toward the end of the game when almost the entire map was open and I was backtracking for Coglike Gears.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Solid 8.5/10. If you played the first game you will enjoy this sequel. The overworld gameplay wasn’t particularly interesting but at least added some variety. The core gameplay is fairly similar to the first game, albeit with more enemy variety. The multi-classing was frankly underdeveloped and I ended up having multiple characters that had similar builds. Really it seems that most skills were useless other than the ones that provided additional secondary slots or additional actions when you scrap an enemy.I played on veteran difficulty and was glad to have the generous checkpoint system so I didn’t have to constantly restart when grinding for stars. Took me about 30 hours to do a completionist run. Not much replayability but I definitely got my moneys worth.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved the first game, you would more or less wouldn't want to miss this one. All mechanics are refined and the multi-class schemes in this game is far better than any other XCOM like turn based I have ever played. However, you loved the quick game in Steamworld Heist I which can be finished in 10 to 13 hours, Steamworld Heist II is a much more lengthy one which can be finished in 25 to 30 hours. Yes you will have much more content in this game but if you love the length of a typical Image & Form game, you will find this game dragging after a while (which I felt after 18+ hours).
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying the game play, tactics, and progression system. It's been interesting enough to hold my attention for 25 hours so far... The battles are fun and I like that they don't seem to expect you to full clear every level. I recommend playing on a higher difficulty to give yourself a challenge. This game encourages creativity and branching out your characters into a variety of jobs/classes. The game designer made a lot of great choices here.My biggest complaint is the audio in this game. The band who made the music has some catchy songs but it gets old pretty quick. I also wish they had voice acting for these characters. I don't enjoy having to read dialogue to follow along the story. I play with the sound off half of the time.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Another compelling entry to the SteamWorld universe, Heist II brings just as much charm, wit, and intrigue as the first game did, while adding in some cool new redeeming features that make it stand out. Gameplay-wise, missions are the same as always, board different faction's ships and blast the loot (and hats!) off them, fulfilling various objectives to keep the spice alive and ensure missions don't just all blend together, and always unlocking something cool at the end of each, provided you were thorough.I loved the addition of the free-roam outside of missions, in particular. It's fun, it's fresh, and there's lots of interesting little nooks to explore and secrets to find, but just like in-mission, you have a limited arsenal and hp-pool you've got to manage each day, to both reel you in from being overzealous exploring and keep you focused on your other objectives (but I appreciate that, up to a point, you CAN technically just rest at inns to replenish lost hp without having done missions that day, if you're really feeling the itch to keep exploring, and particularly value they anticipated that enough to put various checkpoint inns spread throughout the map, so you needn't backtrack huge distances just to reach a safe haven and be able to save again).I loved the varied cast and their little tidbits of dialogue, it was fun following along and picking out your favorites, or finding new favorites when new potential upgrades get unlocked, and the management factor of getting through each day with whichever crewmates you had left made you willing to keep experimenting. The story was interesting and full of twists, kept you wanting to play just one more mission, if not for that, for getting the next cool weapon or class upgrade. I loved the 'Cog' system of having cross-class points to spend on unlocked abilities from leveling each job, but I do think more liberties could've been taken to streamline that aspect:The upgrade to "Slot Machine" to make it a free ability could've been used on more abilities, or else have them free outright, similar to +HP & +Cogs; having to spend precious points on extra aim or extra move that you already earned on another class, seems cumbersome when it's clear from a gameplay perspective that most players would prioritize these universally beneficial passive skills. It also seemed a bit egregious to put some of the best skills halfway through very one-note classes' skill trees, like "Free Sidearm" on Brawler, "Squeeze" on Boomer, or Engineer's "Feel the Burn", unlocked at the very end (and yes I understand the best skills are saved for last, but come on, don't make me stick my Sniper main on Engineer for a good half of the game just to finally get +1 damage, it's just senseless).Anyway, aside from those minor qualms, I honestly had a blast playing through this, and only wish there was a New Game+ mode to keep all my cool gear and upgrades onto a new save, maybe one that forced you to pick a higher difficulty, but with higher droprates of rare items and rare hats we might've missed before. Ah well. Still probably gonna play through again to get those last couple pesky achievements, which I cannot say for many games I'd be willing to trudge through again just for that. But this one, yes. This one's a gem :3
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Such a great game! Keeps you actively wanting to play more with perfect weapon/skills upgrade pacing and exciting gameplay! Loved the first game and the job system here is definitely a fun way to shake things up. If you enjoy games where you have to contemplate the perfect strategy and min/max your turns, this game will definitely scratch that itch. If you don't want to get THAT strategic with it you can always adjust the difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: SWH2 had some big shoes to fill because I adore the first one. Overall, it is a bigger and better game on a number of levels, however there are some parts of it that I think could have been done better.Firstly, SWH2 is much more tactical. Floor hazards which inflict ongoing damage, enemies which transform into higher threat enemies if not killed quickly, and 'commander' sort enemies which buff allies shakes up player priorities in combat. The combat is much more in depth than the first game and feels well polished.The multiclass system is very good, while I didn't fully utilise it on my first run, I think there are some good combinations that can be found. The Sniper aim buffs seem to work well when dealing with explosives and the Brawlers 'health on kill' ability is useful for keeping characters alive longer. The Reaper class seemed a bit  too weak for me though. There are many missions and they are well laid out, although there could be a bit more variety as many of them are grabbing the epic loot before the time limit runs out. However, there is a lot of variety in the types of enemies and the different hazards around each area/biome.The world map is large and the element of controlling the submarine adds a minigame of sorts, with the underwater elements providing a welcome side of exploration and puzzle solving to the game. There are many smashable rocks and lowerable barricades around the map which speed up travel, but even so, getting around the whole map can take a bit of time since the layout makes for some detours.The on map combat got annoying at times and just became a hinderence to exploration much of the time. I didn't tinker with the difficulty of map combat as it said I could because it wouldn't have been more fun if it were more challenging. It did offer a small window into the setting/world emphasising the point of the forces/factions at play, but I think it was slightly overdone in some places.Around the map I think there could have been more bars (safepoints), especially in the north of the map, since travelling past fortified areas all the time became a chore. Additionally, while there were points of interest on the map, there could have been more of a variety in shops around the map.The story had a duality between fighting the dieselbot navy similar to the first game as well as solving the rust problem. It seemed well paced, and the game didn't keep you in one biome or area for overly long. Even in the northern area, while that was a large chunk of the game, the story kept progressing so it didn't feel too samey.The music is good and there's a range of tracks that play at different places, however I think the music in this game is less notable than the previous game (but that's just me).SPOILERS AHEAD:For me, the story of the game isn't the main focus, however, I'm unsure about the main character (Quincy).  It's good character design, but it makes the character somewhat unlikable. Overall, the issues I have with the game are very minor considering the solid gameplay which is the core of the game. The game had big shoes to fill, and it succeeded excellently. The game is well designed, with good mechanics and a good range/balance of enemies and hazards as well as a large and varied map that offers exploration elements that add an additional angle to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: SteamWorld Heist was my favorite SteamWorld game and I'm still not sure if SteamWorld Heist 2 was better or just different. The world building is better, but the world became a chore to navigate.The build variety is better, but the way you level up your subclasses made me not want to do it naturally. I never felt strong enough to activate a subclass on a new mission, so always replayed old levels to level up my subclasses which led to tedium and grinding.It also felt a bit too long. Overall it's a great game that, for me was let down a bit by the was you level subclasses.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game.  Easy 9/10. Standouts are:  The gameplay -- if you liked the first game, it's more of the same, plus some.  More ability to customise, more strategic, more options and feeling of progression.The music -- holy crap, I don't know how much of the budget went to this, but the music is excellent.  Incredible vibes, fits the game perfectly, and I'll be listening to it on its own after I am finished with the game.The atmosphere -- there has been a lot of work that has gone into crafting an experience with this game, and I'd say they really succeeded.  The companions are fun, and there are just enough nods (subtle or otherwise) to the first game to keep fans engaged.  Overall, I loved this game, I'll likely come back and play it again in the future, and if you are a fan of tactical games I would say it's an easy buy.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Is this a good game? YesShould you buy it? YesBut buy the first game first because it is better.The basic gameplay is identical in both games, and the clever 2-D take on X-Com mixed with Tanks works great and like the first this game oozes charm, humour, and style with wonderful graphics, a delightfully nonsensical setting, and top-notch music. The missions are short enough to stay engaging, and they've come up with enough new twists and variations and boss fights to keep you coming back for more as the story clips along.The problem is the stuff added to the sequel: the overworld sections are just dull busy work 90% of the time, extending the time taken to do things without being fun, and while I like the rest mechanic for the way it pushes you to use all characters, most of the time it just means you need to add another boring overworld round-trip back to the pub. The new way character advancement works is clever and probably adds replayability but this is already a decently long narrative game, it doesn't need that extra replayability, and the new system robs the individual characters of their identity and distinction.So you end up with a game that has the same excellent core as the original but has mostly diluted it with new stuff that doesn't make the game better ending up with a game that delivers less fun per hour than it could. Still a good game, just not the step forward I was hoping for.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: This sequel improves on the already fantastic SteamWorld Heist.With nearly 60 missions spread out over various areas, there is a ton of content.  Took me around 55 hours to 100% (getting max stars for every mission).  Infinitely replayable, as there are countless builds you can experiment with.  If you enjoy tactical/turn-based games at all, this is a must-play game in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Steamworld Heist II is a solid game that both improves and in some cases, worsens the gameplay from the original. The overworld is a neat addition that rapidly gets old as you travel the world map. The submarine combat isn't the most engaging, but it's not very hard either. The shared class system has me torn. It allows for some really powerful trait combinations, but I find that all of the characters are less memorable as a result compared to the original. After completing Steamworld Heist II, I immediately revisited the first game and replayed it on Elite. Both games are wonderful, but I enjoyed the first one more, overall. I'm currently replaying II on Elite and it's far more challenging. My opinion may change after this playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: OK, lets preface by saying I have 1000+ hours on SW Heist, on PC and tablet.  Never expected to enjoy a side-scroller this much, but the art style, music, turn-based tactics, RPG-lite character growth, and mostly randomly generated mission maps have made it my go-to casual idle game.So, 8 hours into Heist II, I'm loving much about it.  The production is a big leap forward, but blessedly still has the simple charms of the original.  (Looking at you, Star Craft 2).  At first I wasn't sure if they had fallen into the choice paralysis of too many character growth options, but it has grown on me, and i absolutely appreciate upgrading the sub and doing ship-to-ship combat.  Need to progress further to judge story, but dialogue is just OK.  how many times can we be told Q isn't living up to his mom's legacy?Will report back after a full playthru.(and please please PLEASE add the Fen DLC to the iOS version of Heist 1 !)
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: A great sequel to the original Steamworld Heist, keeping enough different so it doesn't feel too repetitive. While I initially thought the Job system was daunting, I quickly learned that instead of thinking "Which skills would best improve this job" I realised I should be thinking "Which job would benefit most from these skills". The risk/reward of using a character with no skills in a specific job only added to the fun and the challenge. My biggest issue with the game is the sudden difficulty Hike once you get past the wall, up until that point it was the right amount of challenging for me, but after I got past the wall I realised I couldn't turn back to the earlier areas and most of the levels in that location were too hard for me so I had to lower the difficulty. My other biggest issue with the game is a lack of new game plus, Steamworld Heist 1 let you replay the game again except with all of the crew members already unlocked, this would have been really interesting for this game considering you have ten of them in total, but alas.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Best tactical game I've played since my (all time favorite) XCOM2.Sweet, colorful, crunchy graphics, an utterly amazing soundtrack, and super tight mechanics.Stunning game all around!I wish the campaign had more meaningful decisions in the strategic layer,as it doesn't have the 'doom clock' I liked so much in the XCOM games.But that's a flavor taste of mine, all in all this is one of the greatest.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a decent and fun side-view tactics game.I found it a bit lacking in terms of exploration gameplay especially later on, and the story is incredibly barebones, but the gameplay was very fun. I've had several issues with the controls on KB+M vs Controller. The exploration gameplay was definitely designed for the controller, and KBM implementation was incredibly lacking in terms of ergonomics. Tactics gameplay is decently strategical, while not being oppresively hard (playing on Experienced).It's fun to swtich up the bots jobs to get more and more overpowered combinations of skills.Aiming with the mouse was easier compared to the controller, especially considering that you can precisely target certain parts of the enemy (but there is still significant aim-sway you need to counter with a mouse). An aim to the center of an enemy definitely helps with hitting long-ranged shots though.I very much enjoy the whimsical setting of SteamWorld, as all their games have a certain charm to me.Overall, a fun and fullfilling exeperince that took me about 30h to complete.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: The first Heist was my favorite SteamWorld game by far. This builds and improves on it in a lot of ways, even if it comes at the cost of making it less tight in its focus. The ship combat and exploration took a while to grow on me, and without fast travel (aside from shortcuts) there will be some times where you're just plodding along trying to get from A to B, when the last game was much snappier in moving things along. These flaws weren't enough to prevent me from having a great time, though.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: What an awesome surprise to find that Steamworld Heist II not only carries on the good name of Steamworld Heist (and Steamworld in general), but that it's actually BETTER. I was worried that with the shift from Image & Form to Thunderful, they'd lose the magic. Especially after Steamworld Build left me meh (it wasn't *bad*, but it wasn't *good*). In fact, I played the demo and felt like I didn't really feel the need to go further (and the reviews confirmed it).But this game, on the other hand, completely knocks it out of the park. Great levels, equipment, music, writing, and JOBS. I really never expected to see them add a jobs system. It really does spice things up, giving you choices on how to play each mission with the exact same characters. And it avoids characters you add later from coming in completely underpowered.Much like with the first Heist, I found myself dillydallying to avoid finishing this game. I really hope to see DLC with this one as well. I'd even go for multiple ones, if they were good.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Steamworld is an underrated series, but continually presents one of the most consistently high quality game settings and mechanics, with Heist 1 & 2 being the pinnacle in my mind.Heist 2 expands for the better in every way than 1. If you're new to the game, its an excellent trick shot tactics game with light RPG elements. The world generally is a post-human world of steambots & dieselbots, modeled comically after the age of discovery and the wild west, this setting is particularly focused on the sea.2 has more varied guns, abilities, upgrades, combos, and things to explore on the overworld, and they did a fantastic job. This feels like how Supergiant stepped up from Hades 1 to Hades 2, both of which are fantastic, and the team behind this have done the same with their game. If you're even looking at this game, get it, and you'll have a great time.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: A good time for your money. Took me 25 hours to beat all missions and side-quests on second hardest. Some time consuming achievements left, for those kind of players.Music -  Good, especially the band that plays in the rest area, overshadows the rest of the tunes.Combat - Excellent, fluid and fun. A mixture between strategy, puzzle, and trpg.Story - Meh, just like all the SteamWorld games. Not bad, but not great. Cute at times.Progression - Good, some abilities are clearly better than others. Some are very situational and some are a must for every character. Regardless, I had a good time making an unstoppable team.Over World - Great, I actually didn't think I would enjoy this. _childDocuments_.review: Just throwing in my 2 cents. I got the first game for 3 dollars to see if I would like the series.  All steam world games tend to be good, but it's a matter of if you like the genre they are aiming for me.  I loved steam world dig.  Steam world Build wasn't for me.  I was happy to say steam world heist was perfect.  It felt like Wasteland 3 and XCom in it's turnbased and aiming system except damage was guaranteed as long as you can aim.  It was definitely a hidden gem for me and I was super eager to pick this up.Fast forward, I pick up Black Myth Wu Kong.  Played the game for about 2 hours before I realized what I really wanted was more Steam World Heist in my life.  I picked this up and immediately loved it.  This game iterates on the first game and improved on almost every aspect.  There are a lot of smart design decisions in regards to how they upgraded all of the characters.  For instance, in the first game, to balance out the power of the sniper, they couldn't move and shoot in the same turn.  In the sequel, sniper have a reload system built into their kit, so they can move and reload, or reload and shoot, or if their gun is loaded, move and shoot.  it's a very elegant fix to a previously unpleasant mechanic.These improvements stretch to other classes too.  Melee for instance, is no longer about getting in, bonking, and getting out.  Now it's a core class that has abilities that let them dive into close range, and trigger perks for tanking damage.  Basically this game took every weak point of the first game and gave it a face lift.The one thing I'm not sure how I feel about so far is the mini game of upgrading your submarine and fighting ships on the world map.  I'm only a few hours in and haven't upgraded my sub too much, but we'll see if it gets more exciting.  If anything, it does make the game have better meta game progression than the first because you are juggling multiple currencies and upgrades which ultimately funnel to having stronger team mates and being able to fight for longer periods of time before needing to head back to the bar and rest.So far I love this game.  Easily a favorite of the year.  It has exceptionally good game design, and the visuals and music have also had a significant face lift.  Shout out to the music tracks that play whenever you enter the bar :0

_childDocuments_.review: I was so happy when they announced this game a few months ago. I have never particularly enjoyed turn-based/tactics games, simply because I never feel like I have full control of whether my next attack lands because of how luck-dependent those kinds of games can be.Steamworld Heist (both this and the original game) manage to make the tactical gameplay fun through its use of free aiming and bullet bounce. You're able to freely aim your shot with every character, regardless of weapon. Some weapons aim and behave differently from others, but they all give you complete control of where you shoot. On top of that, the bullet bounce mechanic, a staple of both games, creates an extra layer of strategy to every shot. You can go for a more direct shot and kill the one enemy close to you, or you can look for the perfect angle to hit multiple enemies in a row and potentially clear out a whole room (something I have done several times, and it never gets old). The best part is that all of this is controlled by the player. While there is arm sway that you have to account for when aiming shots, it's still highly dependent on your own timing and skill, and it feels like your own fault when a critical shot is missed.And to top it all off, having more original music from Steam Powered Giraffe to listen to is always a massive plus.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a sidegrade to original SteamWorld Heist.Is it worth a full price? - Yes.Is it better than a first Heist? - Yes and No. It is a squad tactics with core gameplay similar to that of first game. They added arcade-y global map layer, which is a top-down shooter. It is nice and is better than original's global map.Leveling is has also improved, now you can switch the class of any character and there is some build variety now. Inventory is better and item capacity is now not limited.Tactical combat and enemy units were more fun in a first game. Characters and story are a bit worse in a second game. Plot is too straightforward.  Villains of the story are meh. You are kind of forced to hire and use all the characters, there are too many of them, some dialogues are a bit cringy and childish.Overall it is roughly on par with first SteamWorld Heist, which is definitely not bad. The game meets the expectations, it is fun and intertaining. Recommended for squad tactics fans (challenging on higher difficulties) and casual gamers alike.

_childDocuments_.review: So 8 Years after Part 1: finally the much anticipated sequel.Played 27 Hours (24 Hours Savestate) on mainly the 2nd highest Difficulty, which i tuned down when stuff took too long in my opinion, got all the stars in all the mission, all the Bots etc pp so i feel it's kinda complete without looking at whatever steam achievements i could grind now.Steamworld Heist II does everything the original does, but harder and better. More Bots more weapons more enemy Types longer game, dynamic Map. And you are a quasi pirate now HARPros:+Solid Core Mechanics, Easy to understand, great embedded Tutorials+Fun Character system: Individual Skills and the Opportunity to have a Character play Multiple Roles thus gaining Talents out of multiple Skill Trees and makes for a good time finding out which Combos are the Best. Great Spread of Weapons and Items+Cute Graphics, but this seems to be an establoshed universe by now anyways+Lots of stuff to find and upgrade, including upgrades for your submarine, which gets slightly silly in the end :D +Story and different Areas tie together well. The story is fun and slightly whacky due to all the flat robot themed Jokes, it has an overall relatively flat trajectory but it hits home end the end and doesn't leave stuff flapping loose + You can drive a severly overpowered Submarine that ends up ramming cruisers to sink them while shooting laser beams sideways at other enemies. Good times that Cons:-Repetitive Mission Design. I didn't count how many missions there are but i would estimate 50-ish? and it's basically Kill ABC or more commonly get Treasure. Sometimes it's survive until you get the treasure or you can kill ABC. Option on running somewhere and flipping switches. Always carries the Story to a bigger extent in the Main missions though.-Difficulty Design: tricky one. 2nd highest Difficulty seemed where it was at for me. Highest Difficulty is where you actually need to start and think, but the game only allows you set back of 2 Turns, and no further. For the highest Difficulty i would actually have liked more finely tuned reset option, otherwise, while being beatable, it just did take much too long for a casual single player game^^ Higher Difficulty mainly involves the game throwing more enemies at you within the same time constraints.-Driving Submarine is fun, but wouldn't have minded fast travel option- highly subjective: i didn't like the music that much, mainly the acoustic Pop/Rock with Vocals. Might be not a reason for anyone else though, i just prefer instrumental music in video gamesFeels Great to have played this adventure as well as the first, would never regret doing so.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely fun and addictive game.  For me this is the type of game that's dangerous to play because I lose track of time and play it until 3 AM.  Fairly challenging on the hardest difficulty though the difficulty can be inconsistent.  I.E. for maps that you can only deploy 1 character there typically is a class that trivializes the map.  There were multiple times where I was overwhelmed by what seemed like an impossible stage only to adjust my load out and tweak my strategies enough to be able to overcome it.  They do a pretty good job of designing maps in a way that make them more challenging for certain classes which I think helps to ensure that all classes are relevant.  I.E. there are maps that have objects that you don't want to damage which is not ideal for the boomer who is otherwise pretty strong in a lot of stages.There are some good mechanics in play to mitigate against save scumming as well as give it enough RNG to not make it just a puzzle game.  Though that having been said, occasionally the RNG can impact the difficulty noticeably.  The character writing is a bit shallow with each character's personality revolving around some stereotype.  I do appreciate that the characters show growth through their dialogue interactions so they're not purely 1 dimensional.  The music is generally pretty solid with a couple of bangers.  There are tunes that get a little old after hearing them several times and some that I can't get out of my head when I'm not playing.

_childDocuments_.review: A great follow up to the first Steamworld Heist game, this is everything you want in a sequel; bigger, badder, more to do, more to sea (ha) and more to enjoy. I'm a big fan of Heist 1, so this was an easy decision to pick it up, and I 100% feel its worth it! It's not the most in depth turn-based game out there, but the aiming system means you don't get the MISS on 95% chance shots like you do on other games. If you miss, it's almost always your fault. Having the submarine gameplay on the world map is fun, not super in-depth or difficult, but enough to make getting around a bit of an experience to balance out the shooting phases. Some of the enemy animations are a pain to skip (they have up to 3 animation phases, and you have to skip each one), but that's a minor nit-pick. Having all the crew members being able to equip all the weapons, combined with the Cog system to get cross-class abilities gives you  a ton of wiggle room to experiment and come up with some very strong combinations of fire power, which you definitely need on higher difficulty levels.Overall, very fun game, glad I played it, and cannot wait to play it again.

_childDocuments_.review: SteamWorld Heist II is a glorious sequel to the original game, which does just about everything a good sequel should do.  The new characters are enjoyable to spend time with, there's a very nice character arc for Captain Leeway, and some very pleasant surprises throughout the storyline.  The gameplay is rock-solid, building on the SWH1 combat and providing a varied set of missions which were a delight to play through.  The music (once again by Steam Powered Giraffe) is lovely as well.At first, I wasn't entirely sold on the new naval combat system, but I grew to quite enjoy it.  It turns out to be very nicely integrated into the later sections of the game, to boot.  In the end it's quite complimentary to the turn-based XCOMmy mission sections.  I've seen some other reviews complaining that the missions all felt samey, and after playing through the game, I just don't agree -- they do fall into some specific archetypes that you'll come to recognize, but there's constant tweaks here and there which provide some nicely varied levels.  There's also an incredibly comprehensive set of difficulty options; if there's some area of the game you find too difficult (or not difficult enough), you can easily tweak the game to your personal preferences.So yeah, tl;dr is: if you liked SWH1, you'll almost certainly like this one as well.  I'd highly recommend it.I've got a  minor quibbles with some of the additions: the multiclassing system is nifty but I found myself getting a bit annoyed at how much re-speccing I was doing, both with the skill selection and equipment, just to get a well-rounded character ready.  It was kind of a drag having to reassign my favorite Flanker to be a Reaper for a bit just to make those skills available, etc.  This is exacerbated slightly by the fact that crew and equipment can only be used once per "day."  To get them back, you've got to head back to a bar and rest, which felt like unnecessary busywork.  The plot is pretty fun, but boils down to a series of macguffin chases (I'm still a bit unclear why we needed to track down and kill the Lord Admiral guy, other than him having one of five macguffins).  And there's one potentially-unpleasant difficulty spike: when you first enter the second major part of the map (), you're locked out of the starting area for awhile, and the missions there are noticeably tougher than what's come before.  If you don't feel that your crew was levelled up sufficiently, it might be a rude awakening (though at least you could lower the difficulty for a bit to catch up, if you need to).Still, all that is honestly pretty minor; this is definitely one of my favorite games of the year.

_childDocuments_.review: SteamWorld Heist II is a breath of fresh air in the gaming world, delivering a captivating mix of engaging storytelling, stunning visuals, and innovative gameplay mechanics. From start to finish, the game immerses you in a unique experience that keeps you hooked, offering a blend of tactical challenge and artistic charm that few titles manage to achieve.Storytelling and AtmosphereThe narrative in SteamWorld Heist II is nothing short of masterful. The game weaves an intricate tale, full of twists and surprises, that pulls players in from the very beginning. It deftly balances humor, tension, and emotion, creating a story that remains compelling throughout.Complementing the story is the game's distinctive art style—bright, colorful, and richly detailed. Every frame feels like it has been meticulously crafted to bring the world of the Steambots to life. The attention to detail, from the characters' expressive animations to the beautifully designed environments, helps build a visually striking world that is a pleasure to explore.Moreover, the outstanding soundtrack perfectly enhances the experience. Each track is carefully curated to complement the game's tone and atmosphere, whether you're strategizing your next move in battle or simply soaking in the environment. The music blends seamlessly with the gameplay, heightening the emotional impact and making each moment feel more significant. The combination of visuals and sound creates a deeply immersive experience that truly stands out.Gameplay and ProgressionOne of the standout features of SteamWorld Heist II is its exceptional level design. Each level feels distinct and thoughtfully constructed, consistently offering fresh challenges and experiences. There’s never a dull moment as the game masterfully avoids the trap of repetitiveness that often plagues similar titles. Whether it's a cleverly designed combat scenario or a puzzle that requires strategic thinking, the game keeps you on your toes, rewarding careful planning and adaptability.A major innovation in SteamWorld Heist II is its "jobs" system, which allows crew members to adopt multiple roles. This addition introduces a new layer of depth and customization to the gameplay. Players can experiment with various job combinations, creating unique strategies that suit their playstyle or specific missions. This flexibility not only adds to the game's replayability but also makes each mission preparation an engaging strategic puzzle of its own.The game also excels in its pacing. Progression is steady and well-calibrated, ensuring that players are constantly challenged but never overwhelmed. The development team has expertly designed the game to introduce new mechanics and elements at just the right moments, maintaining a sense of discovery and excitement. This careful pacing keeps the game feeling fresh even as you become more skilled, ensuring that the thrill of leveling up and unlocking new abilities never fades.One of the game's greatest strengths is its ability to reward players without making them feel like they're grinding. Revisiting missions to unlock new job combinations or gain experience points feels purposeful rather than repetitive, adding value to every session. This thoughtful approach to progression ensures that players remain engaged over the long term, as there's always something new to explore or achieve.ConclusionIn conclusion, SteamWorld Heist II sets a new standard for tactical turn-based games. Its captivating storytelling, gorgeous art design, and innovative gameplay mechanics come together to create an experience that is both deeply engaging and endlessly entertaining. The game's balanced progression system ensures that players are continuously rewarded with new content and challenges, making it a joy to play from start to finish.Whether you're a seasoned strategy gamer or simply looking for a high-quality title with heart and creativity, I highly recommend SteamWorld Heist II. It’s a shining example of what can be achieved when developers pour passion and attention to detail into every aspect of a game.Rating: 9.5/10SteamWorld Heist II is more than just a game—it's an unforgettable journey. Its finely tuned mechanics, engaging story, and constant introduction of new gameplay elements ensure that it will remain a favorite long after you've completed your first playthrough. For those seeking a game that continually rewards curiosity and skill, this is a must-play.

_childDocuments_.review: Binge played through the whole game and had a great time.  Heist II does a great job with its gameplay systems building on themselves across each of regions. As you proceed, the game introduces more concepts which increase the complexity of the missions and keeping things fresh for the player even though the core loop (shoot the badies), doesn't really change. The game further encourages the player to change crew members and their classes regularly through a flexible job system and a rest cycle between missions. Both of these systems work well and help to add game play variety across the run time. The major con I see in the multiple negative reviews of this game is poor balance. I would say the game will punish the player if they don't synergize their skill combinations for each crew mate in the late stages of the game. But, I never had an issue addressing this due to how easy it was to change classes and redistribute cogs (skill points) for under performing crew mates. I always found that a well kitted and skilled crew mate will stomp the A.I. with some truly unfair skills and dirty builds. (Late game sniper skills Example: Harvest + Loose Cannon + Power Shot + Perfect Aim = some ricochets and a very empty room).

_childDocuments_.review: SteamWorld Heist 2 is a great sequel. It takes what made the original fun and adds a lot of cool new ideas. The basic premise of the game is that you sail around a big oceanic world taking on missions in the overworld. For each mission, you send in members of your crew to complete different objectives, usually based around getting to a certain location on a map or taking out a specific enemy. The missions are turn-based with each side moving their robots, lining up shots, and using special abilities. There's a great progression to the levels. They start off simple but by the end of the game, the kinds of strategies you can pull off get pretty out there. I never felt like I was overpowered for any level, except old ones I went back to, and I always felt that pull of "just one more level".Besides the tactical combat in the levels, you'll upgrade your ship to fight enemy ships in the overworld in real-time combat, maneuvering your ship into position to fire off your weapons while avoiding enemy attacks. There are also a lot of upgrade trees that you unlock throughout the game so you always feel like the currency you get from missions is useful. The upgrades are very tangible and you feel the difference with each one. A new feature in SteamWorld Heist 2 is increased customization of your crew. You're allowed to mix and match different abilities from different classes to suit your playstyle or the personal abilities of your bots.Beyond the solid gameplay, I've always liked the SteamWorld games for their coherent setting and strong aesthetic. Despite many of the SteamWorld games being in different genres, they all feel like they're part of the same world and their stories intersect in fun ways. Not critical ways, so don't worry about playing all the others before this one, but in ways that just make the world feel more alive and built out. The character designs are fun and charming and the overall tone is lighthearted and enjoyable. And the music is great with catchy sea shanties playing whenever you beat a boss or enter a rest area.Any SteamWorld game is a good one to jump in on, so far they haven't missed once for me. But the Heist games are definitely my favorite so you can't go wrong here!
