_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: It's SteamWorld Heist I with an overworld gameplay loop I found to be fine. Some will like it more than I did, some less, but I was there for the heists which are just as fun as they were in the first game. Each level usually has some time constraint (user-adjustable but I played at the default "experienced" setting) that gives incentives to the player to balance risk-taking in exploring the map quickly versus prudence in not running into ambushes. Unlike the first games, bot abilities are tied to weapons meaning all characters can learn five sets of skills. I found this added a lot of variety because bots could be basically customized for each mission to a finer degree than just what weapons, gear, and hats they have. My biggest gripe is that I will have to wait a while for SteamWorld Heist III
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very fun and engaging game. I have not yet completed the game.You play a team of stream bots doing a good job fighting disel bots and bone bots in a tactical turn based exchanges or an RTS type ship combat.It is good continuation to first Heist that enhances on the formula. You have an open world rather than strict map to sail and discover missions while fighting enemy ships.You send your crew to invade enemy bases in a tactical turn based combat.New innovation this time is that your crew can gain level in all classes and you can mix and match their abilities that way.So far I have not discovered any negatives.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Starts out pretty similar to its predecessor (not necessarily a bad thing!) but as you get deeper into the jobs system the game really opens up. Rather than a list of missions to select from, Heist 2 features an overworld where you pilot a submarine around and do some light real-time combat en route to different missions. While similar on paper, this change makes the game feel more open and narratively connected, in addition to providing another path of progression. Gear, also, feels more impactful than the previous game with rare items providing noticeable differences that can change up your strategy a lot. Overall, highly recommended to strategy game fans. Gives me that XCom feel that few games outside XCom can, despite the explosion of the genre in recent years. Namely, those tricky tactical situations you find yourself digging deep into your toolkit to dig your way out.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this one a lot, its a nice improvement from the first game.  I found myself losing interest in the first one and stopped playing, but finished this one.Biggest improvements are not running out of inventory space and not losing money if you fail a mission.The story was presented better in the sequel as well.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: A humongous improvement over SWH1 in many ways, while still being the same game at its core:XCOM, but trade rolling percentages with wall-bouncing trickshots.Compared to SWH1, level design is better, level order is less linear, and playstyle variety is drastically more diverse.This game was a blast on elite, but felt a bit unfair on a couple missions. There are a few rough spots in terms of difficulty pacing for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I loved SteamWorld Heist 1, so I'm very happy that the gameplay is similar but has more variety on loadouts/builds. Nevertheless, the game progression slowly introduces the fundamental mechanics at early stage. So, there's nothing to worry and I only need to progress the game story.As for the world exploration using the submarine, I find this part to be quite interesting and nicely integrated into the game. And yes, there's no fast travel, this may annoyed me a little bit when I did some grinding and repeating the same missions. However, I'm familar with shmup genre and manage to finish the game without much frustration.Last but not least, NICE HATS!
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Somewhat early in, but very good so far. It's pretty much everything you'd want from a sequel to Steamworld Heist, even 8 years later.It's still pretty much the same game as the first, which still stands out as a unique spin on the Tactics genre. However, the ship navigation, job system, and new touches to the reward loop keep things fresh and help elevate the experience beyond its roots. All of these additions seem to fit in pretty nicely with the core gameplay and progression, without being too obtrusive or distracting.There's already a lot of mission variety and a good amount of challenge. Playstyle options also open up fairly quickly, which is nice. Unless things somehow tank later on, this is a sequel that delivers.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game. You don't need to read more. You can buy it :)Pros: - Excellent RPG mechanics. Fun upgrades! - Navigate and upgrade your sub. - Upgrade your bots. - Bots skills are FREE to unlock as you level. Then if you change their class (by changing their weapon) You can use something called cogs to unlock upgrades. Cogs are fully refundable, so you can try out different builds without penalty. - No punishment for screwing up a level or abandoning a level. It is fun because you can try something crazy and if it is a total failure, you can reload from an auto checkpoint, or restart the level. No punishment. - Really fun weapons. - Really fun characters. - Quirky funny dialogue. - Great strategy with the aim lines on snipers. My favorite thing is to take out multiple bots with a tricky aim line. Really fun strategy. - Fun interesting original soundtrack. There are songs with lyrics that are fun. - Snipers are my preferred class. Really fun. I just had a level where I took out two skeletons and a skeleton generator in a single turn. Exciting :) - The game feels like they took all the frustrations out of turn based strategy games, the only remaining items are awesome.  - They trimmed the fat and amplified the fun!Cons: - If you don't like turn based combat, you may not like this. I am not that into too many turn based games. But the strategy is interesting enough to where I am still totally in :). - That is all I could think of. I love this game :).Feel free to ask questions and I will answer :)
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Heist 2 is yet another fun game in the Steamworld franchise.Initially, I was put off by some of the design choices. However, the more I play the more I enjoy the overall experience. SWH2 definitely is a great sequel and earns a top spot in the Steamworld series. The music and sfx sound great. The world is colorful and I just love the turned based combat. I did have to adjust to some of the new mechanics but nothing that would ever cause a No vote. Fortunately, any knocks I have about the game are nit pick and personal preferences. I miss my dingy space cowbots, the ease of navigation, and a few other things. However, went to play Heist 1, wow Heist 2 has done some major UI and QoL improvements. H 1 feels clunky now but I still miss some of One's world.

_childDocuments_.review: It's Steam World, and it's fun as always.If you like the first game it's take some of the best stuff from that an runs with it.I play 100% with a controller just like in the first game and it's smooth but some times just like the first game the aiming can be a bit wonky. _childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: SteamWorld Heist II takes the gameplay from the first game, expands on it and manages to create a truly fun experience in the end. If you enjoyed the first game, you'll more than likely enjoy this too. If you haven't played either, play the first one, it's worth it.=======================================================================The Good:The turn-based parts play much like the first game. Levels are challenging and regularly manage to throw in curve balls and new ideas to keep things fresh. Add onto it the fun character building and you get many ways to approach the levels, offering quite a lot of replayability. The difficulty curve is noticeable and doesn't shy away from providing a challenge, but there are also plenty of difficulty options to tweak your experience.I'm usually not a huge fan of turn-based RPGs, but the SteamWorld Heist games have somehow managed to pull me in every time.The new naval combat makes for a nice change of pace in comparison to the planning-heavy gameplay inside levels. Exploring the overworld is nice and relaxing, while the sea battles are exciting, ranging anywhere from nice little scraps to absolute ball-busters.The story is endearing, and like in the first game, I really loved the characters and their small interactions and mannerisms. And the game also nicely builds onto the SteamWorld lore, if you're into that.The music once again features many tracks by Steampowered Giraffe. The first game made me love them, and this hasn't changed since.The Bad:Like in the first game, the controls in levels can feel kinda clunky at times, mostly in the beginning before getting used to it or if you're playing too hastily. This isn't too much of a hassle in the long run, but I've accidentally blown up barrels I was sitting next to more often than I'd like to admit.I played the game with M+KB and bound camera panning to WASD, while also turning off camera pan on screen borders. This turned out to be the most comfortable way to play for me.=======================================================================But yeah, game is gud. Play it.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: So I really enjoyed SteamWorld Heist, which is my favorite game from this indie developer.  However, SteamWorld Heist 2 is now my favorite since they basically improved on every aspect in this game.  The new jobs (aka classes) related to each weapon type give a lot more interesting combinations along with the two unique abilities for each character.  The story is more involved and the characters feel more fleshed out this time.  Being able to control the submarine and go across the map  and fight enemies is a really fun aspect to the game, so it basically feels like two games in one.  The progression systems are nicely done and it is cool to have rewards for exploring the map and individual locations.  Comparing the first SteamWorld Heist to this one:  The first game took me around 20 hours to complete, while the second is coming in around 50 hours, so it seems to have around twice the content.  I really like they got rid of the limited inventory system of the first, that was the most painful aspect to me.  Also, there is just so much more flexiblity in how you build your characters and what items you equip them with.  There is more variety in the enemy types and environmental effects.  I cannot think of an aspect of the second game that is not better than the first.  The one thing about the second game is it is a bit more grindy with the day mechanics resetting the map enemies.  The achievements are going to take a lot longer as well.Overall, I give the game a 10/10 and I definitely plan on doing multiple playthroughs.  I would even recommend it at full price, since there is more value here than many AAA $70 titles.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished SteamWorld Heist II recently and started a new game on a harder setting.The focus of the game is the turn-based tactical combat where your units get 2 moves per turn, firing your main weapon ends said turn and some items or skills may be free actions. Granted, that isn't new nor special, but the skills, gear and class combinations you get as you go make it hard to stop playing. That and the great artstyle.The background music quite nice plus some very catchy tunes on hubs, shops and after bosses.I'm glossing over certain elements like story and overworld exploration because they aren't really the main focus and I'm not the best at describing those. I'd say they're decent though.If this style of game sounds good to you, it's worth your time. But do check the first one if you haven't yet.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, wonderful soundtrack and great references to part 1. Played it on veteran for the first playthrough and it was a real enjoyable challenge. _childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: A 2D "XCOM style" game. Has a lot of soul put into it from the graphics to the character design and the soundtrack. The bar tunes are really great. As for gameplay it has 6 classes and 10 characters you can recruit along the game with unique passives. The level design it great and allows u to tackle the mission at whichever difficulty you want before going in the mission. The game clocks in at about 25 hours but its a good 25 hours. No need for grind and filler, just handcrafted good levels. Give it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: If you played the original Steamworld Heist and loved it, then good news. This is more of that. As a fan of the original, I have loved the couple of hours I've put in so far. It is more robust, with much more player flexibility, but also higher difficulty to compensate for player characters being stronger.If you haven't played the original, but enjoy games like X-Com, I'd honestly drop 4 bucks when it's on sale and play it. It's 2D simplified X-Com, and the formula absolutely works. If you find yourself enjoying it, Steamworld Heist 2 is more of the same.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. It takes everything Heist 1 did and ramps it up. It adds a lot of great RPG mechanics like a Final Fantasy style job class system. The story is decent but it didn't do a great job of creating buy in as I find myself skipping most of it just to get back to the fun gameplay.There is also a whole other progression system where you're upgrading your submarine and your crew so it feels like there is a ton to do for the completionist type of player.Another great thing about this game is the music. The soundtrack is just perfect for the vibe of the game and it includes a bunch of songs recorded with a full band including vocals.If you liked the first Steamworld Heist at all then you should give this one a try.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Deeper (no pun intended) than the first one. Really addressing some of the less good things about he first game - for example squad rotation, in this you, kind of, have to rotate your squad. I found that in the first game I often tried to play with a different setup, but felt forced to use what was best. Not the case here!I binged it and I don't regret anything. Let's go for 100%.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Best Steamworld title yet.Amazing tactics game that improves on everything the first one did and adds a little bit more. The game is decently challenging and allows you to change the difficulty per mission if it gets too easy or too tough. overall would recommend to anyone wanting to play a fun tactics game no matter what skill level. You should be 99% good playing it without playing the first but I would recommend playing that first for the story and it may be hard to go back to after. New job system is great and allows for alot of customization. it lets you mix up your weapons while letting you use the best of each job. The addition of the sub combat is fun though I feel it drives a bit slow at the start (thankfully you get boost early on). The penalty for dying in the sub is a bit weird though didn't happen that often to become annoying.it is around 19 hours to beat every mission with all stars and is well worth playing every mission to see each one. It is replayable due to the higher difficulties and characters are not linearly unlocked so you have room to experiment. Even if you only plan on doing one run of the game I still would recommend this game (and most other steamworld titles). 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent sequel to a game I simply adored.  The new job and cog system adds extra depth to the character builds without becoming too overwhelming.  The tactical combat is very sharp, with lots of variety.  The overworld naval combat aspect is decent but the missions are where the meat of the game is, for sure.  The writing and personality of the characters is also great.Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: It's real good. It's real good in a lot of the same ways the first game was good, overall. The main new features (a world map and class-changing) are cute but in the end, it's still steamworld heist. If you liked that game and wanted more, behold. There is more. _childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love it so far. I loved the first one, I am not normally one for turn based combat but this ticks some boxes for me! The slo-mo kill shots are so satisfying knowing you've lined up the perfect shot then BOOM, headshot. I can't remember if this was part of the first one or not but being able to set your characters up however you want to, mixing up the different classes and weapons is really fun to play around with, and with the levels being somewhat procedural generated, no level feels exactly the same! I think my only very minor complaint is since you're traversing through water, the levels feel very far away from each other, and having to "reset" after completing each level is a little annoying, but I can see why that's been implemented. If you're going to get this game, definitely get the first one first too!

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing, simply just amazing. It's taken what was good from Heist 1 and improved it further, adding in new things, changing certain others (E.g. Sharpshooters now having to reload instead of only being able to shoot or move not both) the characters I feel have some more depth to them and the new overworld combat is a surprise but a welcome oneI could gush endlessly on this but as a TL:DR it's more polished and improved
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: This is basically the first game but improved in every corner. The only significant difference you might find is the character building. Since everyone can be trained to do anything the indicidual characters lose a bit of individuality, but on the other hand your playstyle gains individuality. 10/10 would recommend
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Steal you sub back from the evil navy, sail the high seas, fight for freedom, and collect HATS!You play as the son of a famous pirate captain who is doing his best to live up to his mother's legacy, he just has to steal his submarine back from the navy, build a crew, and save the Steam Bots from the water shortage caused by the navy, who are evil Diesel Bots that look down on and treat the Steam Bots poorly.This game is composed of two primary elements, navigation, and mission. When navigating, you sail around the map in the submarine to find missions, shops, and places to lay low while dodging (or obliterating) Navy patrol boats.When in missions you play as the crew in turn based combat. The crew can have different classes and abilities which adds a layer of strategy to the game. I really like the auto 2 turn checkpoint in the missions that you can rewind to if you get defeated or make a mistake.Has lots of good difficulty options, including the custom difficulty slider if you want (I just played on the default "experienced" level. This is my first SteamWorld game, but it seems a balanced starting point so far!)Overall, a lot of fun. Great music, chill/cozy vibes, and once again: HATS (they make you feel fancy!)
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Felt right at 20-25 hours to complete, as it did not overstay its welcome (games nowadays pad the content so much, resulting in fatigue).Not sure about the story, as it did not click for me, but I did not really play the game for it. It is easily ignorable. I guess it has its charm.The mechanics are fun, with the jobs system giving it a nice spin (this is sort of a multiclassing mechanic). Some combinations can end up ridiculously good and it is fun finding those combos.Nice soundtrack, with a lot of great tracks. Found myself humming quite a lot of them out of the game. I recommend starting the game at the highest difficulty, as that felt right. You still get a generous checkpoint system, where you can just go back 2 turns, so you may rectify your errors without having to restart. And even if you do have to restart, you lose literally nothing other than time by doing it. If you dont like the difficulty, you can always change it in game (when starting a mission).Overall a satisfying tactical game, where I would really enjoy planning my turns. Seeing your combination of planning and jobs synergy pop off in amazing combos was extremely satisfying. Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: A must play! I adore the original, and recommended it to everyone I could. This sequel does lots to alleviate some of the frustrations of the first (inventory limits, lack of checkpoints, harsh penalties for leaving/failing missions, etc) while also expanding on everything that made the original such a compelling turn-based tactics game!I've been playing on the second highest difficulty so far and it feels like the sweet spot for me in terms of challenge. Rewarding, but not frustrating. Several difficulty levels should accommodate players of any skill level.Complex without being overbearingly complicated or sluggish. High-stakes shootouts with enough factors at play to keep things interesting without causing headaches trying to keep track of all the action.Experimentation with team comps and the Job system always pays off and feels natural. I was very skeptical about the Job system initially, but I think it has some really great potential. I haven't progressed far enough to really see it unfold completely, but even by the end of Act I I'm seeing the depth it can bring to strategy and getting the most value out of each crewmember.It does, however, strike me as a little bit grind-ey, but I can see it being a great way to flesh out the later portions of the game or a NG+ mode.Presentation is lovely. Colorful, whimsical, great music. Fans of other Steamworld titles (myself included) may somewhat miss the grimier aesthetics of the other games, but this game isn't a downgrade by any means. Since the first trailer dropped this has been a highly anticipated title for me. Play it!!!!!!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Worthy of the moniker of a Steamworld Heist sequel. This one improves on its predecessor in just about every conceivable way outside of the naval combat system, that, while not the worst thing out there, does add a modicum of tedium to backtracking. The aesthetics may also not be to some peoples' taste (you might like scrappy spacepunk more than you like steampunk pirates of the caribbean for example)To those unfamiliar: It's an 2D SRPG where, instead of relying on percentages for your attacks to hit their mark, you have to physically aim and ricochet your shots around cover to deal damage. It's a much more intuitive and active system that may appeal to those who don't like traditional RPGs much. There's a tactile satisfaction in landing a really tricky shot that you just don't get from "landing a crital hit" in a regular turn based RPG.My main criticism is that the protagonist has basically no personality and the overall tone of the game is a bit weird. There's a world-ending crisis looming and a variety of other bad things going on (weird bodily mutilation cults, corrupt government), but everyone has a very "laissez-faire" and chipper attitude about the state of their world and situation. They're not cracking jokes, but there's a lot of levity to things that makes the tone feel rather odd at times. The individual crew members are interesting enough though.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent step up from the first title, while also not at all being dependent on it. Very fun, very unique, and it makes me feel skilled even when I'm not.The class system is very nice and has me tying myself in knots (in a good way) trying to figure out what classes to level on what characters to get the most fun builds. The missions are fun and feel satisfying.I've played actively for about 25 hours, exploring the whole map, doing all missions (some a few times over just to cash in on bounties), and I'm still not at the end of the game. It's longer than the first game in the best way possible.I think my only problem is that some classes don't really benefit much from early level abilities on other classes; and that level 4 and 5 abilities didn't all feel like they had the necessary OOMPH that should come with focusing on getting my characters levelled in a single class to that point.An excellent purchase!
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Fun tactical game that can be as hard or easy as you want it to be. Being able to mix and match the classes' abilities makes for all kinds of interesting combinations.If you liked Steamworld Heist, which is a great game, this builds on it in so many ways.As an added bonus, they got Steam Powered Giraffe to add their talent to the soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Steamworld Heist 2 takes what its predecessor had and improved upon it. Generally speaking, it was a good game.STORY 9/10:The itself was both simple and yet interesting to play through. I won't spoil it because I believe that you might want to see it for yourself.GAMEPLAY 9/10:As I said before, this game improved on what the 1st game had and made an incredible experience.You never need to single out a crewmate because they will still improve with the rest.My only complaint is that once you done everything, that's it! No new game+ and no extra post-game missions. Which was suprising since the previous installment had new game+. For a game advertising 150+ weapons and other things, I expect to have a long experience.In conclusion, a good game with a great reputation.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought it day of and racked in 24 hours by the end of Saturday. This game is really fun. Definitely plays a bit different from the first, but not in a bad way. Lot of QoL improvements over the first. I love hanging out in the bar while i go get food so i can listen to the soundtrack like a radio. _childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game where they took everything good from the first, improved it dramatically, and added a bunch more awesome stuff. Super fun and satisfying game-play, great music, and pure Steamworld awesomeness. Also, the game doesn't punish you for changing the difficulty or jumping back with checkpoints. You can still get the achievements and complete missions without being docked. This is a great decision on the devs part. Makes it fun to play and you are way less likely to become frustrated or stuck. Amazing game!
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting story. Concepts similar to One Piece. Steam Powered Giraffe. This game introduces many new mechanics not present in the previous game. There is a "Day Counter" that I haven't figured out if it matters or not yet but so far I recommend grinding the earlier levels as much as you like until the characters feel comfortable getting through fights. Experiment with different weapon classes on each character to optimize them. Explore as much as you like, the game doesn't punish you much for it but progressing through story too much can make you lose access to the starting area.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: This is everything a sequel should be - they addressed all of the (small) QOL issues from the first game and made this even MORE player friendly (full customizable difficulties, animation skipping, no losing half water for failing missions). On top of the already rock solid combat....this is a turn based tactics gem
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Similar gameplay to the first game but that’s what exactly what I was wanting! Until this release I was still booting up the first one and re-playing a bit.The new travel system is great! In the first game you could only go back and forth between “dungeons” on a direct line but now you can free-roam in your own upgradeable submarine. You can mount guns, shields, missiles and more to engage in naval warfare;  basic naval warfare, but it’s still fun and you get loot for sinking ships.You can level different guns for each bot and unlock abilities that you can then use while equipped with a different weapon. Unlock a cool ability or passive for your shotgun? Now you can also activate that ability while using a sniper or rocket launcher or whatever! They also updated the way bounties work and added different ways to obtain upgrades for your bots.Storyline is simple but enjoyable. I like pirates & robots, so win-win!
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I will always love Steamworld. It's my alltime favorite series, and this game just solidifies that love. I'm only 2 hours in, but I am still MADLY in love with Steamworld Heist 2. Great art, great music, wonderful characters, satisfying gunplay. It is everything Heist 1 had, but more, wrapped in a nice little bow.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: the original SteamWorld Heist is one of my favorite games and honestly an absolute masterpiece, now SteamWorld Heist 2, improves on that game in every way, somehow even prettier visuals, and audio with the interface and gameplay systems well improved on, looking forward to many more hours with this highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: WOW this is a great sequel.WHAT IS IT: SteamWorld Heist 2 is an XCOM/Worms-style turn based game with realtime aiming. You level up your squad and buy gear while taking on different kinds of missions via sailing through the overworld.HOW IS IT DIFFERENT FROM THE FIRST GAME:Combat and visuals are way cleaner. Classes feel more distinct and you have the ability to multiclass now, allowing for a lot more combat variety. Your ship/overworld is no longer a glorified menu and instead has its own combat mechanics and upgrades. Everything feels bigger and more expanded without messing up any of the core systems that made the original game great. Pretty much everything you would want from a sequel. Great for newcomers and fans of the first game alike. Runs amazingly well (5+ hours on battery) on Steam Deck OLED.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I have owned and played all of the SteamWorld games. I have liked some of them, loved others (never disliked one), but the original SteamWorld Heist is by far my favorite. I've bought that game in every platform I own that it's available for. So, when the sequel was announced, I was beyond excited and bought it on day one. I'm only a few hours in, but I'm glad to announce that so far it's at least just as fun as the previous one, possibly more.If you've played the first one, you know the basic gist. This is sort of a 2D X-Com style tactical game. You have a group of different characters with different abilities and you pick from them to enter a stage, in which battles are turn-based and turns are faction-based. And there are lots and lots of hats. If you haven't played the first game, go and do that now. It's the better starting point.Leaving aside the story and characters, the gameplay is largely the same (a good thing, of course), with a few notable differences. For one, instead of the map being a board-game style set path it's now fully explorable, with fog of war even, which is very welcome. There's also some light naval combat, which is very simple but works well. Your ship is as customizable as your characters now, with weapons, armor and other upgrades you can set and freely change.From a character standpoint, there's now a job system. While in the previous game each character came with a set archetype (such as sniper or brawler) you can now freely give any of your characters any of the available jobs from the start, even mix and matching some of their unlockable abilities, very reminiscent of something like Final Fantasy V. It's a considerably more engaging system.I haven't played enough of the game to know how many more new things it brings, but I have played enough to know it's an instant classic. When I'm not playing it all I want to do is come back to it, just like it happened with the first one. I will update the review when I'm done with the campaign, but I find myself comfortable already giving a recommendation. It's really that fun.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Steamworld Heist 1 was one of the most unique and fun turn based strategy games, and this game iterates and improves upon everything that made 1 great. I am currently in the third (?) area, and the amount of content and strategy in every step is fantastic. The job system is an impressive way of improving your characters and gives a really deep level of decision making in crafting every character for a level, and the characters are all fun, unique, and it would appear they have unique loyalty missions if I understand correctly. It feels like I've barely scratched the surface, and I am looking forward to the restAlso, this is very ambitious of me, but I feel the game is in a perfect spot for some kind of procedurally generated Roguelike or bonus campaign mode, and I would absolutely pay for a DLC to do something like that and even more replayability in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent sequel to an excellent game. I'm just getting started but it's already more of the gameplay I loved from the original with some extra features, exactly what I was hoping for. Also the change in setting from space to pirates in the ocean is a fun change in scenery. If you liked the original then this is a must play, and if you haven't played the original, what are you even doing? Go play it.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. I'm just around partway through as I'm messing around clearing the overworld enemies for the fun of it (and also it's a great way to get money once you're at this stage). The actual gameplay of missions feels just like heist 1, except much more fleshed out with a lot of new unique enemies, new stage hazards, more engaging level layouts, and a ton ton more abilities and ways to build your characters. I was personally concerned that the characters wouldn't feel too unique because of the whole job system. But a lot of them have unique abilities you can unlock that are either generally powerful, or help cater them towards certain playstyles/classes.They did an amazing job making it feel like you're actually in a living world. The overworld helps really tie everything together along with the day system, which also massively helps keep every one of your crew useful. Unlike in heist 1 where you could just focus on one set of characters as your main crew and the rest were just dead weight, the day system makes it so you essentially use every crewmate, which really helps all of them feel impactful and gives you an incentive to actively seek them out when you have the room for them in your sub. I also personally really enjoy the progression system. Theres so much to improve and unlock, not just new weapons and leveling up your crew, but theres so much to upgrade with your ship as you progress. Unlocking unique abilities of the crewmates and later being able to upgrade them further, being able to upgrade some of the distinct abilities of some of the classes, getting upgrades that improve the base stats of your crew or help you gain more gallons or xp. Theres just so much, and it's very satisfying to just steadily improve everyone over time. Overall the game is just super enjoyable, my new favorite steamworld game. Definitely recommend, especially to people who enjoyed the first.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: SteamWorld Heist 2 is an absolute gem! I spend no less than 10 hours with the game and I had an incredible time. The tactical gameplay is as sharp as ever, with tons of exciting challenges and creative strategies to explore. The art style is beautifully charming, and the world-building pulls you in immediately. But what truly stood out to me was the OST—it's a masterpiece that perfectly complements the game, enhancing every moment with its fantastic tunes. I 100% enjoyed every second of this game and can confidently say it's a must-play. Highly recommended!SteamWorld Heist II - First 30 Minutes Exclusive Gameplay! - 8 reasons why You Should Play SteamWorld Heist 2:1. Tactical Bliss: Ever wanted to feel like a genius with every move you make? SteamWorld Heist 2 lets you outsmart your enemies with clever tactics that make you look—and feel—like a strategy mastermind.2. Hand-Crafted World: The attention to detail in this game is off the charts! Every level feels like a unique piece of art, carefully crafted to keep you exploring, strategizing, and totally immersed in its steampunk charm.3. Family-Friendly Fun: It's a game you can play with your kids, your parents, or even your robot vacuum! No need to worry about anything inappropriate—just good old-fashioned turn-based action everyone can enjoy.4. Epic Soundtrack: The OST is so good, you might catch yourself humming it in the shower. Seriously, it’s like the musical equivalent of your favorite dessert. Sweet, satisfying, and you’ll want seconds!5. Robots with Personality: These aren’t your run-of-the-mill, beep-boop robots. They’ve got style, they’ve got flair, and they’ve got more personality than your last three protagonists combined.6. Endless Replayability: With tons of missions, gear, and strategies to explore, you’ll keep coming back for more. It’s like your favorite snack—impossible to have just one!7. No Rage Quits Required: It’s challenging, but fair. You won’t be throwing your controller through the window, I promise. Maybe just a few stern looks at the screen when you miss that perfect shot.8. A Game for All Ages: Whether you're 9 or 99, SteamWorld Heist 2 offers fun that spans generations. It’s a great way to bond with family members over a shared love of steampunk robots and strategic combat.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a long time fan of the Steamworld games, and Steamworld Heist was a game I particularly loved. The sequel is as good or even better in almost every way. Get this game for the magnificent art and gameplay for certain, but the heart of it is a fantastical tactical side-scrolling, turn-based skirmish game. Wonderful characters and the ongoing universe that is the Steamworld absolutely enchants. This is a brilliant game - I cannot recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: This is the perfect steamdeck game! The missions are short enough to feel bite-sized, but the tactical combat, loadout customization, and class system provide enough deep strategy and sense of progression to keep you hooked. I like the overworld exploration in between missions, too, it breaks up the missions enough to keep them feeling fresh.It runs perfectly and looks and sounds great on the deck, can't wait to binge my way through this.

name: BORE BLASTERS
detailed_description: Blast your way through rocks and dirt with your machinegun drill. Carve through the ground to uncover precious ores and defeat menacing foes. Uncover ancient relics and artefacts hidden in the deep. Amass a fortune in rare gems & ores. Invest in powerful upgrades and unlock new abilities, turning your humble gyrocopter into a fearsome force to be reckoned with. Explore a diverse range of biomes, from treacherous volcanic caverns to lush overgrown underground forests, each with its own unique challenges and rewards. Intense mining action with fast-paced blasting Constant progress - even failed runs aren't punishing Diverse biomes to explore Purchase upgrades to overpower your gyrocopter Navigate the overworld to unlock new mine shafts Collect and loot rare gems, ores, and artefacts to upgrade your gear and abilities Endless replayability with procedurally generated levels Drawing inspiration from mining games like Motherload and Galactic Mining Corp, Bore Blasters takes the genre to the next level with high octane action and fast paced gameplay. Fans of digging and collecting will find plenty to love, while the addition of deadly enemies and mysterious artefacts will keep even the most seasoned miners on their toes.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished all achievements including 100%.But I still have some disappointing parts.At first there were stories, quests, upgrades, a lot more then I expected.But after progressing about 50% of the map, there's nothing more to do in the game.And I've got disappointed in 3 parts.First, there were no place to spend gold after upgrading everything.I know other games like this also have no place to spend gold other than upgrades, but the problem was that upgrades were finished before even progressing 50%.This was disappointing because, the fun of going around the map is to get more gold.But when the upgrades were over, I lost my purpose of going around the map and started pressing 'only the down arrow' until I reached the bottom.There should be somewhere else to spend gold, or at least the upgrades should be more expensive so that the upgrading gets finished at the later part of the game.Second disappointing part was that nothing happened at 100% of the progression.So the last 40% of the game was pretty same to me, because I just pressed the 'down arrow' till I reached the bottom.I got bored from doing that, but I still played the game to see the ending.I thought there would be a last fight, a story, or at least an ending credit, but nothing happened...Last disappointing part was that there's no reroll in the game.If there was a reroll, I could have tried making drone build or explosion build, close combat build or etc and this would have gave me more fun.Even if it's not that, I could've evaded the situations like picking one of the 3 skills that I don't want.But It's still worth the money for me,

_childDocuments_.review: EDITI am going to change this to a positive review. While I do feel like what I said was accurate when I posted my review, they haven't abandoned their game and they're still pushing out updates. Knowing this now, I would give it a positive review. Some of the common complaints about the game have been addressed in updates. I can't speak to the quality of these changes as I feel like I had my fun with this game personally, I would feel confident saying that if the concept of the game interests you, you'll get your money's worth.Please take what you're going to read below with a grain of salt as there have been several updates post release that address some of the things brought up below. At the time of this edit this is towards the top of the reviews and I don't feel that it's right for me to leave a negative review on a product that they are actively improving.Be safe and be good to each other!---This is going to be a tough one considering I have more hours on this game than most people are going to have ever.GAMEPLAYWhat you see is what you get, look at the trailer, it's that with the safest upgrade system you could imagine. There are more unique powerups, but they're so safe and boring, like the drill that goes down, or the black hole that does virtually nothing but put enemies in your face to hit you. You'll take them once and never consider taking them again.The scaling of your copter, even the other two pilots, are just mundane and boring, but satisfying for a few hours.STORYIt's uninspired, generic, and entirely uninteresting, it just ends with no soul and you will never miss it. The best thing to be said about it is that it's not invasive.GRAPHICSCool, looks nice! It has some problems when you're blowing up more crystals and they explode shooting off more projectiles and triggering more explosions.OVERALLIt's fun for approximately 2.5 hours. To mirror another comment, you max your ship part way through 100%ing the game and there's nothing after that. Getting every upgrade doesn't feel cool at all, like I said it's the most safe upgrades possible, it's not interesting and it's just uninspired.If you look at the trailer and you say, I'd LOVE to do that for a while, get it. If you look at it and say it might get old fast, it does and you won't miss out in it's current state. It feels like an early access game that comes off as having more, but is just exactly what you see there until you get bored of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Me after 4 minutes in game: "Man, this is... weird. Easy, but also fun."Me after 22 minutes in game:"Oh, so THAT's how they get you... interesting. Wait, wtf is that block!? I don't trust it."Me after 45 minutes in game:"HAHAHAHA, MINIGUN GO BRRRRRRRR!"My wife after I am 88 minutes in the game:"So... Am I assuming correctly that you're not gonna do much more than this?"Which is code for: "You're definitely NOT gonna keep playing!"That being said, I thought I was playing for ~30 minutes. This game is odd, but in a good way, as in "it sticks out" from all the mushy "formula-X for maximum profit" games that we all know too well. It's like Wall-World, Vampire Survivors and Minecraft hat a really bad, drunken night and now try to figure out who the parents are, because even tho the child certainly LOOKS like all three, it doesn't really take after any of them. It's relatively simple, but it gets challenging after a few maps. The biomes offer a change in scenery and how the scenery tries to get back at you. The temporary upgrades allow for super fun combinations and altogether, I didn't expect a game like this to be so entertaining. It also manages fairly well to feel claustrophobic, which I never thought is gonna be a thing in 2D game. So yeah... flying steampunk dwarves, going full auto vs. goblins and other underground dwellers. If Warhammer had a lighthearted steampunk setting featuring dwarves, this probably would be it.Also: Aiming is for elves!As of now, I love it and I'd say go for it. This is balm form my ADHD brain, just like Vampire Survivors.Edit: Dude, my soundbox must be full of stones, because the music I am getting from this is rockin'.
_childDocuments_.name: BORE BLASTERS

_childDocuments_.review: First five hours of gameplay are extremely satisfying, you feel getting more and more powerful as the maps get bigger and bigger, some events happen in some maps, the risk/reward balance is well done, and above all : like in any good game with meta progression you pile up more and more money to spend it in the upgrade shop.And then all of this satisfying escalation crumbles down. Money gets useless since evreything is maxed out, in a game where mining for money is the core mechanic it's a bit contradictory. Everything is unlocked. You finish any map easily, no more event except some basic object collection missions. And yet the game continues without any challenge or cool thing to do.Play this game for the satisfying early game but beware : the endgame is boring.
_childDocuments_.name: BORE BLASTERS

_childDocuments_.review: Fun for what it is, but there's a lot more playtime than there is content. Completing what feels like the main narrative of the game only involves completing ~25% of the maps, and even before that you're mostly getting consumables (that are automatically consumed,) or upgrades that don't really change the best strategy. Once you can make gems explode, and make explosions fire bullets, you can blow through most things.To that point, though, the game can't handle well when there's a lot of stuff on the screen. Once you've got dozens of explosions and hundreds of bullets going, the game slows down a good bit even on a solid PC, and the edge of the reality bubble becomes very clear, as you'll come across distinct straight lines where all your devastation just failed to be calculated. I enjoyed it, but I feel like I got everything I was going to enjoy out of playing it in 5 hours. Take a look at the purchase price and make your own decision on whether it's worth 5 hours of entertainment.
_childDocuments_.name: BORE BLASTERS

_childDocuments_.review: I thought I would enjoy this game, and it had a positive score, but I was quite disappointed. I like digging games, but I didn't find digging fun in this one and I think it's because it doesn't feel meaningful, you're pretty much just going to want to go straight down unless there's quest items, and then left or right where the end is. There's no reason to explore, because everything only gives more of the same currency, and fuel will run out if you do. It gets very repetitive very fast.The enemy swarms can get intense later, but they're not challenging in an interesting way, they just come at you from different directions, and I found them annoying more than interesting to try to contour and defeat.The second character is at least more interesting to play I found, because it creates more room to fight the enemies in, but it still wasn't enough to make it a fun time. And the temporary upgrades could be more interesting or exciting.If you enjoy just blasting through rocks and shooting enemies that come around you then you might enjoy this one, but I think it would need to change a lot to be worthwhile, at least from my own impression of it.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m always interested in a new mining game, but one that delivers that experience with a Gatling gun is simultaneously checking off two boxes in things that get me to play a game. While it may not do much else beyond those two core elements, Bore Blasters does do exactly what it advertises.Abbreviated Review: On the surface, Bore Blasters is essentially a twin-stick shooter. Except the majority of the shooting you’ll be doing will be in the dirt. The endless ammo of your machine gun is your primary tool for carving your way into the subterranean labyrinth of every level. As you cruise through freshly chiseled tunnels with your strange little gyrocopter, you’ll also use that gun to chip away at veins of gems that you’ll magnetically pull into your collection to serve as both your currency going forward and an “XP bar” pushing toward unlocks. These work similarly to a Vampire Suvivors-style game where you can unlock temporary upgrades for your vehicle like faster fire rates, more damage, and additional weapons/tools from a pool that grows throughout the game.As you dig through the various changing biomes, you’ll encounter a decent variety of obstacles. Things like tougher ground to break, regrowing  “vines,” and blocks that shoot fireballs at you. You’ll also come across enemies that will wiggle their way toward you through both the cleared space and the existing still-solid blocks below. This expands the challenge from simply making your way to the goal buried at the bottom to surviving the occasional screen-filling onslaught of angry enemies. The relatively short levels are chosen from an expanding grid of floating islands that indicate the dominant biomes and make each dive a fairly unique prospect, but not without some rough patches.Aside from the frustrations of dealing with enemies that can meander their way in from any direction – often enshrouded by the darkness of the depths – there are some other frustrating elements in Bore Blasters. The one that crops up most often is that you end up in areas where your Gatling gun stops digging effectively. An entire layer of strata will have blocks that take two or three seconds to break and will be like 100 blocks thick. The only way to make it through this with the same pacing as the rest of the level is to use your gyrocopter’s special ability.You will ultimately unlock three characters each with a vehicle that features a unique special ability. The original character’s ability will let you plow through the ground destroying blocks along the way at high speed, while another will give you a barrage of powerful missiles that blast a large path in the direction they’re pointed. Both of these are pretty effective for getting you moving and getting you out of tough combat situations, but relying on them for basic mobility takes a lot of momentum out of a game that otherwise thrives on it.Another issue that makes the game a little uneven is that the story doesn’t feel linear. You can’t tell what levels are going to give you a story mission, and it’s hard to keep track of what little story there is. The levels that contain story portions are often the most unique and compelling too, which makes it more disappointing when it just kind of trails off after a couple of boss fights and the assortment of bespoke objectives.Even with the unavoidable pacing issues, there’s something that kept me coming back to this game when there was little left to accomplish. Even when the campaign seemed to disappear and the upgrades were complete, I kept pushing through the grid of levels for a bit just to see if anything interesting popped up. There’s also a “Daily Run” with a leaderboard if you want to keep digging into the game, but I didn’t find that as compelling. However, a $10 indie game that delivers ten hours of gameplay that is pretty addictive and fun is an easy recommendation. It would be nice if there was a little more depth to it and more exploration of the campaign elements – perhaps even additional weapon types (I only found one), it would certainly benefit. But for what you get, and the potential for it to be even cheaper on sale, it’s certainly worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: The premise isn't bad: you have a mining ship with limited fuel to get to the bottom of the level and collect as many gems as you can on the way. The problem is the repetitiveness: all the upgrades are linear and boring, the collectibles pool is shallow and has clear winners, but you can't manipulate the pool in any way so you're offered a lot of trash very frequently, enemy behaviors are very similar to each other, and there's no real strategy or customization beyond "pick the best powerups".Also, if you ever stop getting quests, pick the newest character you have access to. The game won't tell you that.

_childDocuments_.review: This game needs content. It's the same run over and over. I've completed the story and can't bring myself to complete each planet. There's just no point in doing so. The ship feels weak. Certain mods really make things fun but if I don't get those mods, it feels like a slog. Also, the enemy fireball turrets need tuning.I can't recommend this game at this point. Maybe after they release some updates, it'll be worth playing and I'll revisit it in the future. It would be nice if games would release in a finished state, though I guess that's not the way things are going.Good luck to the devs. Please work on tuning and add some more useful mods.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Void Scrappers, I decided to check out this mining shmup from developer 8BitSkull.A bit like Super Motherload, the story plays out in text conversations as you carve new mineshafts and collect gems, but unlike in that game, you don't have to ascend to the surface to complete a run. Let alone periodically to refuel and repair. Instead, the fuel supply and hull integrity of your ship needs to last until you reach your objective. Otherwise, it's a failed run, though you get to keep the collected gems to use extending your craft's range, adding armor to its hull, or upgrading the guns.Yep, you blast your way through a variety of different types of rock strata using a gatling gun, which is helpful also against enemies who appear in increasing numbers as the game goes on and you clear more levels which are represented by grid squares in the game's overworld map.Depending on the character you choose, there is a recharging special ability, though I have a tough time imagining playing the game without my chosen character's ability of a boost that carves through rock like butter and makes it much easier to reach the objective within one tank of gas (and some pickups along the way).While I was still reserving judgment a bit, two hours in, at the four hour mark I realized that not only is this game addictive, it's pretty fun. The upgrade system does an admirable job of keeping the player right on the edge of the mining craft being powerful enough to reach the end of the longer levels, without making this feel a dawdle trivialized by these improvements.I could easily walk away, now, and be satisfied with the experience, but I'm still enjoying myself and will keep going to try and clear the rest of the levels. One of the things that I appreciated about Void Scrappers was that, unlike a lot of the "forever games" in the genre, it had an attainable ending. And this looks to be similar in that respect.
_childDocuments_.name: BORE BLASTERS

_childDocuments_.review: A cute little dig-to-the-core type game with roguelite elements. You've probably played this style of game before if you're looking at this genre, but you've never played it with quite this level of upgrading in a single run!Instead of just digging slightly faster or in a line, you get roguelike style upgrades on each run where you might end up with an explosive minigun build that causes gems to explode and shoot out projectiles that kill enemies and cause them to explode and shoot out more projectiles... I think you get it, there's a lot of explosions! And drones and bullets... Maybe not enough lasers.I think the "end-game" could use a bit of work as I finished most all of the story content as far as I can tell at about 70% game completion. I'm at close to 90% now I think with like a dozen levels left to clear and I don't expect there to be anything new, but I'm compelled enough to actually finish this one out!

_childDocuments_.review: Sorta fun gameplay loop hindered by lack of variety and content. Every run is basically descend 1000 blocks and pick up an item on your way down. There's nothing the game offers that you don't see for the first couple of levels, let alone the entire 113. You're done with the upgrades by about a third of the game, and then just sit on piles of cash with nothing to spend on. Temporary upgrades balance is hit or miss - some or must haves and some are useless, effectively making or breaking the run very RNG. It's fun for a bit but quickly you understand there's not much to the game left. Kept playing hoping for more but unfortunately there's just not much to it.
_childDocuments_.name: BORE BLASTERS

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Added addendum to review, leaving the originalAs an old fan of Motherload, I really dig Bore Blasters and had a good time.The game still has some rough edges a month after its release though.-You'll quickly run out of things to spend gold on before you've uncovered half the mapThis is something that has probably been brought up a lot already. Please either bump the cost of the upgrades or supply more content to purchase. Anything to better balance the spending vs gaining really.I didn't find the game to be particularly difficult, perhaps due to being fully upgraded rather quickly? I never really struggled for fuel either.-Lack of a quest logI feel quests were something that would just pop up, I'd do them, get a reward but not much else.The problem I want to tackle here is the fact that I've finished every single level on the map, but didn't even unlock the third character. Where do I go? What do I do? I'm not about to randomly replay maps in the hopes of uncovering things I've missed, especially not if I already have over 15mil in the bank with nothing to spend it on.The issues I've described really bummed me out by the end, especially since I explored the entire map (after having purchased all upgrades a long time ago) but didn't get the 100% achievement (because I haven't completed all content obviously).Perhaps it would've been beneficial for the game to have launched in Early Access for a short period to iron out some of these issues, because the game itself is rocksolid.Despite that, I still enjoyed Bore Blasters and will definitely come back for another run when my main grievances are fixed with QoL updates down the line.LATER ADDED: Apparently, the problems I was experiencing can be directly traced back to me never having switched to the newly unlocked character! There was no indication this was to be necessary for quest lines, I assumed it was merely optional.This is one of those things that would've been found and resolved with some Early Access testing for example.I get the devs may have assumed "They unlocked a new character, surely they'll go try it out?" but this simple oversight has definitely caused some people to miss out on the rest of the game, because there was no way for the player to know they were missing something.It could be fixed by either letting everything unfold with the first character or steering the player more forcefully toward trying out the second character at least once.

_childDocuments_.review: BORE BLASTER is a fun little game that I did enjoy playing for 2/3 of the way. _childDocuments_.review: Ahhhh, this game makes me so conflicted. I really want to give this a positive review. It's only getting a negative review since in its current state it's not a full game. There are more levels than story related content (completed the story at around 7 hours) and completing the whole game does not reward you with anything extra according to another reviewer, which bummed me out.The game loop is great! The powers are new and fresh, although a bit too few.The pros:* I love that the campaign does not require you to complete levels in a specific order.* The initial release of in-game content satisfies my dopamine releases to the max. Dwarf gun really go brrrrrr.* The game is challenging.* It works great with a controller.* Can toggle auto-shoot in settings.* Story is a neat add-on to spraying goblins full of holes.* I have a GTX 1080 and have not experienced any lag.* The different quests in the levels.The cons:* There are not enough power-ups to make a specific good build. Unfortunately there is one meta build that automatically defeats everything. It would have been nice with some variation.* While the story isn't connected to specific levels, unlocking the potential power-ups seem to be connected to specific levels.* The amount of levels are not balanced with the play content, making it tedious to complete the last levels since it's more of a chore.* There are some questions left unanswered in the story, so it seems to be unfinished or rushed. For example: * After ending the game, the objective in each level is the same. Everything after the story completion becomes incredibly boring :(

_childDocuments_.review: Bore Blasters is a 2D roguelike mining game. It's not described as a roguelike, otherwise I wouldn't have bought it, but each level is effectively the same, with temporary upgrades, and a permanent currency to make you progressively stronger over time. On each map there's a light quest like "Go here, kill this" or "Collect X of this" which was kind of interesting for a while, although they just stop about halfway through the levels with no resolution. The gameplay itself is great fun, if repetitive. You mine through thousands of bricks and fight off enemies, powers are varied and interesting, and it's well worth the cheap price of entry.- Addictive- Good range of powerups, although I always end up taking the same ones- Multiple biomes and level types which have different challenges and block types- If you get the right set of powerups, you can really tear holes in the map- Upgrades to things like fuel capacity, fire rate and damage- Solid, no bugs- 3 different characters to play as, each with their own special power- Very repetitive after the first 10 hours- Permanent upgrades are boring, just increases to numbers- About 50% of the way through the game, the quests just stop and it’s just the same mission over and over again- After you buy all the upgrades, there's nothing more to spend money on. I'd bought everything after about 10 hours, but there are 20 hours worth of maps- By the time you've bought all the upgrades, I was literally falling asleep in the repetitive maps after that, because you can mine blocks faster than you can fly - so you can just hold down for 5 minutes and win the map. Repeat for 10 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Mining is an integral part of many games. I am not talking about that weird crypto mining or even data mining. I am talking about good ol’ fashioned pickaxe to mineral veins. Of course, you have Minecraft (the name is a dead giveaway), and I am sure Roblox has some mode that includes mining. Every MMO I have ever played (World of Warcraft, Rift, WildStar (remember that one?), Elder Scrolls Online), has mining as an integral component of the ecosystem. Then you have games that spotlight mining of some variety like Terraria, Spelunky, Deep Rock Galactic, SteamWorld Heist, and Below the Stone, just to name a few (the Steam search for “mining” yields over 5,000 results). What if we added a ship and replaced the trusty pickaxe with a gun?Developed by 8BitSkull, Bore Blasters is a twin-stick shooter with roguelite features disguised as a mining adventure. You jump into the shoes of a dwarven (dwarf is also a growing Steam search) gyrocopter pilot who must use their machine gun drill (yes, that is a thing) to dig for loot and fight off goblins and other underworld denizens vying for that same treasure. You know what they say: if a mining excavation fails, just add explosives the next time…After your five minute primer into operating a machine gun drill, you find yourself in a world map covered in tiny islands. Just pick one and start drilling or shooting or, drill shooting? Your main objective is to reach the giant treasure chest at the bottom of the level. Bad news though, you probably will not reach it your first or second go around. Many obstacles will hinder your progress like death or, shudder, running out of gas. Like most roguelites, you will have to put in some work. On the bright side, there is always progression. Whatever you collect, whether you succeed or fail, you keep. It does not matter if the run lasts 30 seconds or 5 minutes. This not only lessens the blow of failure (again, it has roguelite tendencies so get used to it), but makes you want to jump back in for another dig. As you dig, you will collect gems that fill your experience bar. Every time you level up, you get a choice of three upgrades which range from basics like increasing fire rate or damage to randomly dropping bombs or having drones accompany you that shoot at enemies.Besides the power-ups, each pilot has a unique ability similar to the alternate fire you find on weapons in most FPS. These abilities can synergize well with many of the power-ups. For example, Jarl Gemwise shoots a Gemforge Ray and if you combine that with Gemshards….BOOM!After each level, whether successful or not, you can permanently upgrade your ship using the gems collected. Ship upgrades can increase the amount of damage you can take, how much fuel the ship holds, or even increase the damage the machine gun drill does. Upon returning to the world map after a successful dig, the tiles that border the particular island reveal additional areas. The further you move from the center of the map, the deeper the digs you will encounter. Progressing the story enough unlocks Gloz’s Workshop, another avenue to spend your vast fortune. Gloz sells temporary buffs to aid the next dig. If you were looking for a dwarven adventure filled with looting and explosions, you have come to the right place. Prepare yourself to dig, fail, dig more, fail even more, rinse, and repeat. The gameplay loop becomes evident very early on and is super satisfying not to mention highly addictive. There are also daily runs to participate in where you can compete against other players for high scores. Upon finishing out the campaign, you can try your luck at the Challenge Simulatron, an end-game activity that challenges you to increasingly more difficult digs. Bore Blasters is the game to play if you like a good mining run or really just want to play with a machine gun drill.Full review with screenshots and video can be found at

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy Bore Blasters. I just wish that the main quest was a bit longer & more involved. Its definitely a fun game to pick & play. _childDocuments_.review: I think the best way I can summarize this game is that it looks and feels like a much more refined and polished flash game from the 2000's, like the kind of game you would find on Miniclip or Nitrome. You kill an hour or two in it, then go to something else. Motherload definitely comes to mind when playing this game as they both have the same basic concept of digging into the earth, getting minerals, and pulling out for upgrades to your ship, though this game definitely has a lot more flare, style, and graphical fidelity, just remove the factor of having to go back up for fuel.If you really like that sort of archaic time-killing sort of game that involves mining, the kind that DEFINITELY has a conclusion point, but you can always just start fresh at any point when you get bored, this is a good pick, I'm just not entirely sure $10 is worth it. _childDocuments_.review: 20h 2/10 1 You don't need a guide No No Yes, the 100% achievement is grindy No No No No No difficulty option NoBefore the release of Bore Blasters, I was already very excited about this game, as it draws inspiration from "Galactic Mining Corp", a game I did enjoy a lot. And this new game by 8BitSkull didn't disappoint. It has a very addictive gameplay loop, which is in some ways a bit of a roguelite where you earn a currency that can be used to buy permanent upgrades. What helps with feeling addictive is that the runs are very short... but before I knew it I had played already for 4 hours without noticing. Which is in my book a good thing. I love it when games suck you in and you forget about the rest of the world for a second. When you start the game you have only one type of miner, but while playing through the story you'll unlock 2 others with such cool abilities, that I preferred by far over the first miner. After unlocking those I never went back and I mostly played with the second one. You start each level at the top of the service, the goal is to get to the bottom.. but there might also be an additional story objective. While getting to the bottom you try to mine as many gems as possible within the time limit because those give you temporary upgrades in that run, but it also is the currency for the permanent upgrades. I love how affordable the first few upgrades are, you'll be able to unlock a bunch after already the first 1 a 2 runs. Another thing I want to highlight is the settings menu. Here you have the option to not have to hold down a button to shoot, but simply press it to start shooting and press it again to stop shooting (that last part I only did on accident, because why would you want to stop shooting :P). I love that they add this setting because it is so much easier to use and it also helps with the accessibility of the game. Bore Blasters doesn't have any missable achievements and almost all of them you'll unlock while playing through the story. However, the one for 100% is quite the grind because at the end (?) of the story and at the end of the upgrades, there are still many levels left which feel like a grind because you only work on those for the 100%... the currency you won't use anymore outside of the temporary upgrades within that level. There is a question mark in that sentence because it didn't totally feel like the end, the story comes to a conclusion but I had unanswered questions that even didn't get answered after reaching the 100%. I hope that that means there will be room for a sequel, as I would love to play another game like this one!

_childDocuments_.review: Great little game and was have a ton of fun until I ran into two things - a stale upgrade path (at some point the very expensive incremental upgrades get boring) and a fuel system that causes some of the tasks to be not so fun or just plain weird. Another weird thing is there doesn't seem to be a way to "Extract" without reaching the bottom, yet nearly every mission says "great job come back to the ship" and it seems inconsistent to die to do that if you don't make it to the bottom (again, restrained by fuel which sucks)I'll try again if an update comes through, but that boss punishing you in ways you cannot reasonably predict is not the move for me and fuel system makes it even worse. _childDocuments_.review: I really WANT to recommend this game.  The gameplay loop fantastic, the sound is fun, and it has a lot of 16-bit era attitude that hits just right.  And I've got a minor love for games that center around dwaves including DRG & Dwarf Fortress.However, I've had it for 40 minutes or so, and it has thrown every window on my system into geometric chaos and crashed my GPU drivers 3 times -- each time I get too involved in a jungle/poison gas biome.  I've updated to the latest Catalyst drivers, and it's still no good.So let me just say this.  I'm not refunding it.  It's earned enough goodwill even despite that, so I'm giving it another 2-3 months to see if the developers figure out the bug and fix it, and I'll hopefully come back and see if my recommendation changes.  But for now, it's still not ready for full release.Edit:  Well, it's been two months, and the game still crashes in the jungle biomes.  Really a shame.  I wanted to play this game, but I can't.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy another "I wish Steam had a better system than Yes/No" review.But that's just it. It's fine, plays fine, nostalgic of really really good flash games from the mid 2000s when flash games were really really good. There is nothing wrong with this videogame.The reason for my negative review is, after a certain amount of meta upgrades the game is just so extremely easy to the point of tedium. I'm not exactly looking for a hard game, but all the upgrades and systems and mechanics start to feel like they'd better suit a game with steeper requirements for a win condition.If you've played, seen, or heard of Galactic Mining Corp, this is basically that with a little bit of Vampire Survivors bolted on, which is, again, just good game design. Only Galactic Mining Corp manages to keep ahead of you with its gradually increasing difficulty, where this game falls behind you and never quite catches back up.The last 4 hours of my gameplay have been: select level, beat level, do that again. There's a lot of levels and very few of them mix up the formula or present enough of a challenge that I'd need to change my tactics.I like the game, I am not bothered that I bought the game, I would literally buy a Mahjong game if it had a Space Dwarf Mining theme attached to it. But apart from a sheer number of levels and a barebones story, there's not a lot here. But it's cheap, and it's space dwarves, so, I still bought it and I'd still buy it again lol.

_childDocuments_.review: Full Gameplay Walkthrough - About the Game -----Because Bore Blasters is one of those incredibly simple and addictive games that needs no context and so provides very little. You are a Dwarf piloting a mining gyrocopter who could have just as easily been a very intelligent beagle or a bricklayer from Croydon and it would have affected the game not one bit. Your goal in each stage is to blast through bedrock, collecting precious gems, and shooting enemies like bats and… crowns?… and bizarre alien bugs, until you either reach a special big chest at the bottom of the level or, more often, run out of fuel or shields.Each level appears to be procedurally generated, though it doesn’t really matter as they’re all functionally the same. Different hazards present themselves, such as vines that grow back, eggs that disgorge bugs, or tougher types of stone to blast through. You’ve a big cannon for destroying rock, which you can upgrade with run-specific buffs like more firepower or explosive rounds, while you can spend acquired gold on permanent upgrades to your shields, fuel capacity, speed, and rate of fire.What Bore Blasters never does though, is evolve or progress in a meaningful way. You can unlock different characters who bring slight variations on the theme such as different primary firepower, but they’re not a huge departure. There are quests that amount to finding a certain type of new rock or item, but it never really gives you much to do beyond shooting and flying.As such, I found it more enjoyable in short bursts rather than long sessions. It’s essentially a mobile game, designed to kill time when you’ve got 20 minutes here and there. It keeps the gold and the upgrades coming pretty thick and fast, but even that could only hold my attention for so long.The slightly drab, samey levels are nothing to get excited about, and watching new stages unlock when I finished one filled me with a weird kind of resignation. It’s perfectly serviceable and fun for what it is, but I never finished a stage and wished for three more to take its place. All in all, Bore Blasters is a fun little time-waster, but it’s not an experience you’ll remember after you’ve moved on.Rating - 8/10 ( Great Game )
