_childDocuments_.review: Neva does not hold up to Gris.Visually the colors are beautiful but they are more generic colors related to nature's seasons. In Gris, the progressive addition of colors felt more powerful.Musically, the pieces are ok but not memorable and the music is not integrated very well into the action. In Gris the music was animating the environment (wind level) or rythming the boss encounters, here it is mostly background music oscillating between traversal and combat. Gameplay wise this is still smooth but the combat is not very interesting. The pacific approach of Gris was more interesting IMO.Finally, the story did not connect with me. It felt like a generic game about nature being corrupted, with very strong inspiration from Princess Mononoke but without the human aspect. The main emotional arc is about your relationship with Neva, but if you are not a dog person like me this feels weak compared to the more dramatic human thematic of Gris.All in all the game is not bad, but I finished it in 3 hours without the emotional impact of its predecessor.

_childDocuments_.review: WELL I HATE TO SAY THIS... BUT I WAS DISSAPOINTED..As a passionate admirer of Gris, I approached Neva with high expectations, eager to see how Nomada would expand on their unique blend of narrative, art, and music. From the moment the trailer dropped, I was captivated, pondering the depth of its story and the beauty of its visual design.In my review of Gris, I even crafted a poem, highlighting how Nomada’s artistry seamlessly intertwined with its compelling narrative. They truly set a high bar wit NEVA, creating an experience where art and music coalesced into something extraordinary. The combat in NEVA was engaging without overshadowing the emotional journey—an experience I wholeheartedly recommended to others.However, I must express my disappointment with Neva. Don’t misunderstand me; the game is undeniably beautiful and offers an impressive experience. Yet, for someone who loved Gris and hoped for something even more groundbreaking, I found it lacking.While Neva shines visually, it doesn’t quite achieve the same level of narrative integration as its predecessor. In Gris, the mechanics and storytelling were inextricably linked, creating a profound emotional impact. Neva, on the other hand, feels like it leans heavily on its stunning visuals to evoke feelings, which, while captivating, is something many games do today. In a landscape filled with artful titles on platforms like Steam, Neva risks blending into the crowd.The musical score, crafted by Brinilist, also left me wanting. In Gris, the music was layered and impactful, enhancing key moments of the story. In Neva, however, I struggled to find those moments where the music truly resonated. The variations felt minimal, and I often missed the emotional peaks that were so prevalent in Nomada’s earlier work.While I won’t critique the combat, as it met my expectations and functioned well, I found the level design to be one of the game’s strengths. The designers did an excellent job of teaching players the environmental mechanics and then challenging them with advanced puzzles, which was rewarding.In an era dominated by narrative-heavy games like God of War, Plague Tale, and Gris, Neva attempts to explore the theme of parenthood but falls short of leaving a lasting impact. It often resorts to conventional storytelling methods that feel superficial, relying on its stunning scenery to evoke emotion rather than a robust narrative.Ultimately, I believe Neva would have benefitted from existing in a world without Gris. It feels more like a DLC than a standalone experience, lacking the depth and innovation that made its predecessor so memorable.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed watching my SO play this game, and I also played it a bit. I do intend to finish it; however, I felt the need to post a review much sooner whilst the feelings linger. Let me tell you about it :>Neva is a platformer game whose narrative is driven with finely woven puzzle elements within a shattering realm. Story is that of a journey, subtly centered around breaking the 4th wall to evoke emotions in the player, portraying a need for a salient bond to the spirit of nature. It does it in such a subtle yet profoundly evocative manner, that you can’t simply put the controller down. You are drawn to it, as if it was a sweet and playful spring fragrance. You yearn to play a bit more, to sense yourself getting enriched by its lush visuals.However, the visual narrative has a peculiar spin, unlike most platformers. It revolves around evoking the sensation of motherhood, in this case - towards a wolf. And it does it so beautifully, too, that I couldn’t help but feel sad whenever I saw the wolf hurt. It would squeal, in pain. It’s heartbreaking, so you are instantly focused on helping the wolf, and this gives you determination to progress further through realms of serene nature, all whilst getting glimpses of longing beauty in the distance. And, even some spicy themes of loss that are to follow.You assume the role of this one girl called Alba, a brave adventurer and a protector, who is trying to navigate deeply shattered, yet magical world.Alba is accompanied by an orphaned wolf cub, and their bond becomes the heart of the game’s narrative, reflecting the essence of maternal love. As the game progresses, Alba nurtures and protects the wolf, finding herself shielded by it in return.Mechanics wise - the game transits through puzzles in a seamless visual way. However, right from the start you are given the ability of Double Jump mechanic. and the Sliding/Rolling prowess. It feels free and liberating for a platformer, as movement done right can make all the difference for an Indie game. A much-needed sense of freedom and agility is pivotal, and I will always advocate this as the crucial element for a platformer, as it just feels like properly engineered coherence.Nostalgia-wise, Neva returned me to the days of Sega Genesis. That’s no small feat, as I am ruthlessly critical. We have a strong emphasis on nature and environment, whilst the protagonist uses the spirits of the forest to both navigate the world, remove obstacles, and protect the homeland from harm. You can play as the Racoon in Pocahontas to solve puzzles and remove the obstacles. In Neva, this is done interactively by signaling the spirit of the Wolf. Not to mention that both Pocahontas and Neva were drawn/painted by hand. Both games share the message that goes in the blend of Coexistence, Restoration, Harmony, Nature, and Love. Neva encourages exploration without handholding. It is relying on subtle visual cues and an intuitive camera that nudges players toward the correct path.The theme of protecting the nature was immediately obvious, and it just clicked right off the bat.A simple visual que was enough, and driving the narrative forward with this method is quite potent.The sound is spot on. The music begins with serene piano melodies during exploration and intensifies into epic, choral orchestrations during battles, reminiscent of Nier: Automata. This shift adds a very latent emotional depth, turning every encounter into a testament to Alba’s bond with the wolf. Sound design is masterfully crafted, too. Listening through Sennheiser HD 800s paired with a Topping DX9, I found the audio design to be spot-on. I could pinpoint bird chirping, and I found the soundstage felt fully immersive. You’d find me always advocating that the video game’s audio is as essential as its visual and narrative elements. It adds to the immersion by enveloping the player in an intricate world of memories.So the game simply managed to capture the core elements of gaming by creating a platformer that is visually enchanting, emotionally rich, and musically immersive.Neva is filled with evocative storytelling, aquarelle visuals, and rich sound design. Everything lends together well, delivering a fantastic experience.The game felt like living inside a beautiful, resonant dream, and I would gladly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This game arrived at a crucial time in my life, just like GRIS did back in the day. Nomada's first game helped me through my Mum's journey with cancer and the inevitable loss of her in 2021, and I just lost my Dad to the same illness two weeks ago. I finished the game tonight - and I can say with my whole heart it was magic. Despite the tragedy, there's resilience, hope and most of all... love. The gameplay is beautiful, the animation and art direction breathtakingly gorgeous, and so is the music and story. All I can say and recommend before playing, is simple: make yourself a nice cup of tea or your favourite drink, lower the lights around you and immerse yourself into this world of Neva and Alba. And have some tissues nearby - learn from my mistake!

The gameplay, art, and music together make a superb package, and it’s a testament to the fact that AAA developers have a lot to learn from smaller indie studios. You don’t need million-dollar budgets to create something incredible.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game for a few hours now and I can assure you that without any of the current story I have been visually given thus far, this game wouldn't be what I would want it to be. Just know that regardless of how it has been going so far, I have been happily diving in to it with my cat accompanying on my lap, fully immersing myself into this game experience.  :>The layers on this game are stunning. I have goosebumps and tears constantly threatening to escape my eyes as I play.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Another masterpiece!Roller coaster of feels from start to finish!GRIS was about colors and Neva is all about seasons.This game focused more on combat as other reviews has pointed out.You will start fighting alone at first and as the story progress, time changes, and Neva grows, she will join the fight too, from doing background timed attacks, to direct aimed attacks and then combination attacks with MC at final stage.Puzzles are still around but not as much as GRIS since here is as said more combat focused.Overall another great ride from start to finish, will try to 100% the achievements sometime soon.OVERWHELMINGLY RECOMMENDED especially for those that already enjoyed GRIS!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: After the masterpiece that was GRIS Nomada Studios is back with another one. The art is just as mesmerisingly beautiful as before, and the soundtrack by Berlinist is just as emotional too. This game really nailed it with making you attached to Neva, and the entire world around you. Not only that, they also nailed the platforming and combat aspects of the game too. Its rather simple but still fun and engaging. They throw in a bunch of twists to them in different levels to keep it interesting too. But you definitely wont be having much difficulty with anything. All in all, this game deserves to be Indie game of the year at least!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva is a masterful blend of awe-inspiring visuals, captivating music, hearbreaking/heartwarming narrative, fluid gameplay and increasingly more unique and engaging mechanics. I'm lost for words.Nomada Studio outdid themselves with this title, and the bar was really high after Gris. An easy 10/10 from me.You owe it to yourself to experience this, please don't miss out on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: How dare you play with my emotions like this. But how beautiful. How emotional. I've been waiting for Neva ever since I heard the developers of Gris were making a new game. _childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: It took me about 6 hours to finish the game with all achievements. It's quite short, but the story is amazing. I absolutely recommend playing Neva. _childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly touching story, told with no words but the name of the wolf, which is voiced as often as you, the player, wish and push the button, thus building a strong bond between you two.The art of the game is heavenly. The studio's previous game, Gris, was beautiful, but Neva is on another level. Its picturesque design deserves to be exhibited in galleries.Gameplay is nice. _childDocuments_.review: Currently half way the playthrough with the story mode. Been a fan of the Dev's work with the art style, music, and theme. _childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: AVOID | LACKING | MAYBE | WORTHWHILE |  | UNMISSABLENeva is an side-scrolling action game with a huge focus on art direction/atmosphere. It also has some light platforming, puzzle, and combat elements in it. It is the latest game from the studio that developed Gris, which is probably immediately obvious to anyone who has played it (in the best way possible).If you enjoy beautiful environments, a compelling and wordless narrative, a game that includes multiple elements such as platforming, puzzles, and combat that aren't difficult, and incredible music, then Neva is sure to please. If you require a comparison to Gris, it is shorter (this took me ~5.5 hours whereas Gris took me ~8), easier, and less compelling, IMO, mostly from a narrative point of view. However, it is still an excellent game that stands on its own two feet. The inclusion of combat is a nice change and it is implemented well. The music is striking and lends to the overall atmosphere. My only real complaint about it is that a large part of the art design relied on a sort of haziness when I vastly prefer bright and crisp colors.All in all, if you enjoy Gris, I suspect you'll enjoy this game. If you haven't played Gris, but you're looking for a highly enjoyable experience in terms of overall gameplay, then this is a solid title to pick up. I probably only wouldn't recommend it to people who need really high action games to have fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This is what a game should be.  The art is beautiful in it's simplicity. The score is phenomenal and the story drives it home. The gameplay is actually fun, not overly complex but not so passive you forget about it. Really though, the gameplay itself isn't the gem of this fine piece of work.  It's not often I find real beauty in a video game but here it is.  Truly magnificent.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Another masterpiece of art by Nomada. Everything is litteraly wallpaper material. The sound design and soundtracks are as good as what you can expect from Berlinist if you've loved playing Gris. I just love this. I loved the experience when playing Gris, I loved how it felt confronting Mourning. I loved how it felt to feel lighter after Gris. This is exactly the same here. The gameplay in "normal mode" is slightly more difficult than what you had in Gris, there are some parts where you have to die and retry, but it's never frustrating. Every little difficulty you overcome is rewarded by another beautiful painting and scenery. The game is neither too long, nor too short. The collectibles though, are making it a bit too difficult sometimes, but it's meant to be more challenging. I just wished my progression wouldn't be erased just after i started a new game with automatic same. I would have appreciated a feature that let's you pick the chapters to collect every single collectible to get the secret ending.I knew almost for certain how it would end, because you know frome the very begining that everything is related to seasons, and how it's cycle-related. I've been torn between 'please dont make this end' the more you get through this seasons cycle  but also I couldn't resist the urge to go on. This experience is very similar the the cycle of seasons in real life, you can't really fight it, and you know what's coming next. You appreciate every single piece of what the present has to offer you. I just saw the secret ending cutscene, and my mind is even more satisfied, and wondering exactly what that means at the same time. This game really echoed in me for two reasons : - When you are confronted with the loss of a beloved animal you know how it feels. - this reminded me a lot of the philosophy of Nighteyes the wolf in Robbin Hobb's books. Brilliant. Powerful, Cathartic. Thanks Nomada, Thanks Berlinist for making these 5 hours such a beautiful experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I received this as a gift. Kudos to Conrad and Nomada!Neva is a beautifully crafted artistic game, a perfect balance between challenge and immersion. The difficulty is well-tuned, just the right level of challenge without being overly frustrating. Its atmospheric storytelling is captivating. Though relatively short, I still spent nearly 9 hours unlocking all the achievements.The game’s beauty is undeniable, though my only minor gripe is that the environments feel a bit too static—I would’ve loved to see the foliage, branches, and flowers sway more naturally, adding to the world’s liveliness. 4/5, a solid indie game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very pretty and doesnt feel bad to control but honestly thats all it has going for it and im honestly kimda disappointed considering how excited I was for it after gris but this kind of just feels like that game's shadow or something.where gris explores interesting themes through well thought out mechanics, this game has uninteresting combat.where gris has cool puzzles or platforming challenges, this game has combat. (the platformings ok)and where gris has motivation and drive..i had a friend play this and we kept having the same conversation:"what is my purpose??" "you walk to the right." idk maybe its better than i make it out to be but personally im disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm glad to see such warm reception to such a delightfull game, almost everyone seems to love it except for those who are dead set on comparing it to gris. Ofcourse my brain did the same thing when playing this but Neva certainly is its own thing and should be evaluated as such. The game was an incredible journey from start to finish, with nearly every facet of it being perfect. First of all and most obvious are the impeccable visuals, each area wether vibrant or decayed is a feast for the eyes. With great composition and brilliant use of colour it is hard to resist taking screenshots every other step while playing this. I'm gonna check if Displate has any Neva posters after this, as the art direction most certainly deserve to be framed.Musically i was very happy to see Berlinist take up the mantle of composers for the game again, as Gris is still one of my favorite game OST's ever. There's a lot less vocals this time around which is a bit of a shame but didn't make the music any less impactfull. The melodies are beautiful and sombre when they need to or upbeat and relaxing when gameplay demands it so.  At times there was even some Ori vibes in the soundtrack which is my definitive favorite OST ever, so take that as you will. Ofcourse it is once again a must to pick up a copy of the soundtrack with your game (and slap in the art book for good measure). The OST is as much part of this game as the visuals so they compliment each other wonderfully whilst telling a beautiful story.Said story is once more told in a very heartfelt way, and while i personally didn't shed any tears as only a very select few games managed to do this, i can see many people who would. And that's a great thing, art is emotion and Nomada studios has mastered this craft. I really enjoyed the pacing, payoff and overal telling of the story. Said story has some conflict to it in the form of combat, and while this game won't make my top combat in games list it was still perfectly fitting to the game. Not hard, not super easy but very enjoyable nonetheless both regular combat and bosses. The former won't kill you often but the later can the first time you tangle with them. Luckily death isn't punishing as you're treated to a beautiful animation and a near instant respawn.Loading times in general were super short even on a HDD so i can imagine them being near instant on an SSD. The whole game is top notch on a technical level in fact. Not a single frame drop, bug or crash in my 4 hours with the game. This length is an issue for some at this price point but i know games like this are such memorable experiences that they're easily worth the price of admission. I don't think there's any excuse to not get this game as it's not hard (& can be made even easier for those who wish so), it's not long so it won't burn you out and it can probably run on very dated devices judging by the minimum specs. Just get this game, play it in one sitting and then spend the next few days thinking about it <3

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this game connected with me on a different level. As someone who loves animals, the bond between the protagonist and Neva is extremely relatable. My cat Nala is everything to me, he is sleeping next to me as I type this. We take care of each other in difficult times and he is the most important thing in my life.Just like in Gris the visuals and sound design is out of this world. But next to the fun puzzles the studio introduces a fun and sometimes quite challenging combat system. Sometimes even interweaving them with their clever puzzle mechanics.The last hour of the game brought it through breathtaking heights with incredible vistas. I am sure I will be revisiting this game in years to come!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of Gris, I was very disappointed by this game. And don't get me wrong, it is pretty. But that's kinda the thing, it's nothing more. Just, pretty. I didn't like Gris because it was pretty, I like it because there was a boldness and a simplicity to it that made it very evocative emotionally, that it could get me to cry just through an intense combination of sounds and visuals. I would describe the appeal of Gris as raw abstract emotion. In Neva, the visuals are more detailed and busy, which means individual elements don't have as much impact. And this somewhat more realistic approach makes it more bland, more mundane. I'm seeing a forest. I am not seeing deeply stylised and abstracted shapes and textures that create a world and a story of their own. I think a similar thing can be said of the addition of voice acting. It grounds the game in a way that limits its evocative power. Music also makes itself more discrete, more held back. But music is what gives the game its emotional coloration, and tells you how intensely you should feel it. And the very powerful moments like in Gris when a new colour appears, where the music soars and visual effects invade the screen and beautiful animations transform the character and the landscapes. Those moments that were fascinating to me, leaving me shaken and wondering why I was so emotional. They are nowhere to be seen in this game.So all these aspects slide in the background, become flatter and more secondary to the experience. And, this isn't necessarily bad, it could allow a game to put the emphasis on something else. But what else is there? Gameplay? Gris didn't shine for its gameplay, even got criticised for it a little. And my assumption is that Nomada Studio attempted to fix that by putting more of it in Neva. But at no point did they take the time to consider the impact it would have on the experience as a whole, or if it was good.Unfortunately, this half-assed at gameplay makes the game tedious, repetitive and frustrating, in my opinion. And takes away from everything that makes Nomada's work interesting. The experience I had was that of a game made by people who put an emphasis on gameplay in it because they thought they should, but they never took the time to actually play with it. They were ticking boxes rather than taking the game where it wanted to go. In my opinion, the studio's response should have been the opposite. Saying "no, gameplay is not what are works are about, you got it wrong", and put even less of it. It's okay for games to not have gameplay, if it's not what they're about. But even if they chose to put an emphasis on gameplay, they could have done it well. We know it's possible because Gris with good gameplay exists: it's called Worldless. It results in a very different experience of course, but one that is just as memorable. The one thing that could have made this game interesting despite its many flaws is the wolf. The interactions and attachment to another agent in the game. Something reminscent of Ico or The Last Guardians. I think that would have been a cool thing to explore in a game like that. Exceeept... That's not what the game does. The dog is just there so you can say you can pet the dog. It's just there. It follows you, sometimes it doesn't, sometimes you have to press a button to call it, sometimes you have to go back and hug it. It is just a chore and there is no real connection happening here. But the best example of this missed opportunity is the combat I think. After the first chapter, the dog can fight alongside you. But it's not really fighting with you. You do your things, it does its things, and that's it. There is no collaboration. No mechanic is making you feel a closeness with this creature. It is just there. Anyway, I got a refund after the 2nd chapter. Maybe the game gets wonderful after that, I wouldn't know. And at this point I don't really want to. To me it feels like the devs did not understand what made Gris so special and powerful. And I am sad.

_childDocuments_.review: Gris was a masterpiece and Neva is another, as good or better. Both games follow a similar format - a platformer with the most stripped-down possible user interface, telling a moving story with almost zero text or dialogue. Not a long game - I apparently finished it in seven hours - but stunningly beautiful and with solid gameplay. It didn't seem that short due to all the different environments, a few interesting play dynamics, and a couple of punishing boss fights. Bravo Nomada. Most of the platforming is pretty easy so you can admire the beautiful art direction while you jump around, unlike some other games (I'm looking at you, Cuphead) where you have no time whatsoever to admire the art unless you want to die (again). Anyway, solid recommend, 10/10, paid full price on release, no regrets.

_childDocuments_.review: I should start by acknowledging my biases. Gris is one of my absolute alltime favourite games. I played at the absolute perfect time in my life to let it impact me, and still do regularly. So when Nomada announced this game, my expectations were already incredibly high and my hype was unmatched. I played this game in a single four hour sitting today, and I absolutely adored it. I cried several times, including on the title screen and pause screen somehow? This is of course where my nostalgia comes in, because feeling nostalgic for Gris was the biggest reason for that I think. That being said, this game improves on Gris in a number of ways. The addition of combat makes it feel less like a walking sim, which I never minded, but I know some did. This also means we get Berlinist combat music, which is just as incredible as the rest of this beautiful masterpiece of a soundtrack, which is to be expected from Berlinist of course.All this is to say, if you enjoyed Gris, you will enjoy Neva. I highly recommend this for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva is a cute little game that falls more on the artistic side but its gameplay doesn't lack depth, it's fun, a little maybe too short but it has nice things to offer - some interesting use of game mechanics, beautiful music on its background; you can finish it in a few hours and it is a really beautiful journey. It adds combat in it; it's weird if you think about it, an art game with a poetic tale using aggressive slashing? How does that work? But it works pretty nicely to the point it even becomes iconic.Its different than Gris and way more aggressive, while the other game uses grief in a poetical sense almost as a self-induced hikikomori dream, in NEVA you're thrashing your way in a quest that feels like a challenging rush, with some kind of urgency. And it remined me of Ghibli's Princess Mononoke because of the white wolves and also of the "eco-goth" vibes which really bring the artistry on front on this game through environments and color and it's definitely a step forward from its predecessor game in terms of arts quality: the world of "Neva" feels alive and has tridimensionality in is two-dimensional world even tough its art style is portrayed by an overlay of 2D art assets. Knowing this sometimes "broke" the wall between me and the piece of fiction looking at the technicality behind it all but I still found myself truly immersed at least at the chapters towards the game. And I found myself smiling at the screen several times. There are different style in both games but even then Neva reminded me of some scene in Gris even though those memories were drifting years apart in my mind, separated by countless other games; and it felt nostalgic somehow playing this.I did love the themes of nature in combination with its life cycle, and it does feel like something original in combination with something we already know. It is a beautiful, interesting often heart-breaking tale carefully crafted in an art game.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: After the game Gris, which I LOVED, I have to say that I loved Neva even more. Visually stunning accompanied with very beautiful and emotional music, the gameplay feels smooth, and Neva just sucks you in into it's beautiful world. Can't recommend this game enough to casual players, who just want to lay back and go on a little journey!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful both in visuals and narrative, and each chapter tugs at your heart in different ways. I only wish it was a longer, because when the gameplay really clicks and goes into flow, it is a magnificent experience. The music really elevates this game, making those triumphant moments soar and those sad moments devastate. A masterpiece on many levels. Don't forget to pet your magic deer puppy. She needs the pets.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; It's okay, Gris was better. Some things worked out, while some didn't. If you liked Gris, you will enjoy Neva. Looking forward to the next Nomada Studio game.After Gris, my expectations were high. What I can say that Neva definitely delivered was beautiful art and music. The gameplay didn't change that much since Gris and it's okay. The story was touching, but I'm not sure if I understood it completely. Puzzles were sometimes very interesting (especially in the Winter part) but often the case, they were just plain and simple (Summer, first parts of Autumn). These arguments are enough for me to recommend this to people who liked Gris. It's good enough to be enjoyable. BUT, the shortcomings are numerous.First of all: although the art was beautiful, it wasn't used to it full potential, especially in the Autumn Chapter. It was mostly overly dark and boring. I understand that it was a compromise between beautiful art in the beginning of the game and dark side of the story, so the art had to be adjusted accordingly when the story advanced. The fights were frustrating. The final boss was much easier to beat than normal fights with group of enemies (especially with the flying enemies). The idea that the HP of the enemies is not visible is absurd to me. I felt like I was hitting a wall sometimes. Especially when the fight was dragged out, it felt just boring and discouraging when I died for the 5th time and I still don't know how much hp the enemies had left. The fight mechanics were just too simple in my opinion. I hope that it was experimenting on the side of Nomada Studio and in the future they get rid of it, or they develop something better.Next, I don't understand why there was introduced the mechanic of riding on Neva, if it was not possible to use it in 90% of the chapter. It made no sense to me. If it was introduced, then the puzzle should have been adjusted to utilize this skill in any way. Lastly - minimalistic style of the characters. When we compare the faces of gris and the main character here, there is an absurd difference in the beauty. It was a big bummer. I loved how in Gris there were closeups on the main character and we could admire her beauty. In Neva it is completely opposite - the face is compromised of 5 strokes with minimal details. The same with Neva (dog). I didn't like the minimalistic art in these cases.I wrote up that much critique is because I had high expectations of this game after completing Gris. In most of the aspects Neva delivered, but the truth is there were numerous places, where the game could be better. Nevertheless, I am looking forward to the next Nomada Studio game
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I can't give this game a thumbs down as there's too much beauty in it and I want to support the great dev team, but I really REALLY HATED THE COMBAT. Even on the easier setting, it took me out of the experience every time. I wish I could've just turned it off. If they make another in this series (and I really hope they do!) I hope they go back to the non-combat format (or at least have an option to turn it off completely).I also would love more puzzles and for them to maybe be slightly more challenging, but that's not as important. The most important aspect of these games for me is having beautiful worlds to explore, and they did amazingly on that front! I would say the worlds in Neva are even more beautiful and epic than those of Gris. They made me feel things! I just wish I could've explored them without having to pause and mash buttons every few minutes!

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who picked up GRIS for nearly nothing, and dropped it for not catching my attention fast enough, I nearly did not begin my journey with Nomada Studio. One night, I decided to give GRIS a go, and finished it in one sitting. One of the most beautiful, artful games I have ever played and likely ever will play. Pensive, gorgeous and with an incredible soundtrack, I loved every minute of the short but sweet platformer.NEVA took what worked with GRIS, and elevated it beyond what I thought possible. I bought it day 1, because I knew that I would be in for something special no matter how long the game was. The artstyle was changed, but made more beautiful, there was actual combat in between and against the beautiful vistas, the platforming was just as interesting, although having lost the steampunk aesthetic, could not be as visually stunning. And finally, I was accompanied by a beautiful and powerful animal that grew alongside me and eventually could help me with platforming and combat, tying all the aspects of the gameplay together. Short and sweet, just like its predecessor, Nomada have made a wonderful game that is well worth the relatively cheap asking price and perfect to curl up on the couch and bask in the environment and soundscape. 7.5/10 - short, sweet, beautiful and well worth the price

_childDocuments_.review: I am so conflicted, to be honest the only reason i choose to recommend it is because of the art & sound design.[Do not take note of playtime - i've left the game idle far too many times - it totals around 4 hours]So let's talk about the good:- Art is amazing and that's not a surprise, but Gris had somehow much more impactful design. This one is a bit flat. - Music is great as well.- The platforming is actually really fun for the most part and I personally think the game didn't need combat.The bad:- The combat is really annoying - yes, when you learn the move sets of the enemies everything is easier but the hitboxes are imo terrible - you never know when you're touching an enemy if you're gonna take damage or not. That oftentimes feels really bad, especially when you have combat with multiple enemies/moving platforms which is often the case. I quit the game many times out of rage from fights such as these.I think Nomada should stick to platforming as they are pretty good at it and skip combat. There are some amazing sequences in a few mirrored areas that prove that this is where Nomada shines (besides art & music).Story wise I feel conflicted as well - I did not experience as much emotions as with Gris, but even previous title aside, I didn't get a satisfying enough resolution or justification on why things were happening.Overall I think Neva is still worth experiencing but for me it's a step down from their previous title. The puzzles aren't as difficult as Gris, but that may be because I knew what to look for because of Gris.  The bit with the mirrors was epic....great job on that!  Super fun to try to figure it out, and once I figured out WHAT I needed to do I was still VERY challenged by trying to actually do it.  I LOVE everything you do, Nomada.  I'll always see your name and buy that game, forever and ever.  Devolver...you are so diverse and when I see you've made a game, I'm there for it too.  Thank you for sharing your gifts with me. _childDocuments_.review: Neva is a beautiful, short, 2D puzzle adventure, much like Nomada studio's debut game, Gris. The art style, while different from the distinctive staining water colors of Gris, are breathtaking nevertheless.The sedate beauty of the scenes, along with the magical background score sometimes lulls you into a numb navigation of the game world, but then there are moments where it jolts you and demands attention. Unlike the solitary experience of Gris, Neva introduces the titular companion creature which makes the game experience fresh, dynamic and serves as the hook that makes you invested in the events of the game all the more. By choosing a more well trodden nature/corruption theme, I feel Nomada may have played it safe. The more abstract and personal journey of Gris felt a lot more bold and rewarding. Even the game play elements, especially in some sections made me feel I was playing Gris all over again, which is not necessarily a bad thing! Those subjective observations aside, Neva is a great followup by Nomada and I look forward to more of their remarkable artistic expression along with their brilliant musical collaboration with Berlinist.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Much like Nomada's previous game, GRIS, this is a beautiful piece of art that, in my personal opinion, everybody should experience at least once (unless you can't stomach harm to animals - in which case, stay far away). Featuring striking environmental design, emotional musical accompaniment, pulse-pounding combat encounters, and a gut-wrenching visual narrative, Neva will leave you absolutely breathless. The option of either Adventure Mode (where combat has risk of death and enemies have additional health) or Story Mode (squishier enemy encounters with no deaths) allows the game to remain just as accessible as GRIS for players looking only to enjoy the overall gameplay and story, while offering a new, more difficult experience in Adventure Mode for those seeking challenge.Character movement is fluid and mostly intuitive, at first building off of basic, familiar mechanics from GRIS, then progressively adding fresh ideas to the mix of abilities which differentiate Neva from its predecessor. Combat is mostly simple, but enemy encounters and boss fights are varied enough along the way that it never feels tiresome or repetitive. My only nitpick with the controls comes from a few sections late in the game where the platforming difficulty curve felt like it peaked a little too high for a casual experience in Story Mode.Chapter selection is unlocked after finishing the game on either mode and you can go back to find all of the hidden secrets in each chapter without having to fully replay. This makes getting all achievements a bit easier for those who seek completion.The story and overall presentation borrow familiar aesthetics from GRIS, Journey, and the Studio Ghibli film Princess Mononoke (which is no surprise, as GRIS featured a nod to the same movie), while taking some uniquely dark twists along the way to set Neva apart. As mentioned at the beginning of the review, this is not a game for anybody who has difficulty seeing animals die or be in perilous situations, as the core gameplay and story often lean heavily on the struggles to be overcome by your furry companion. If you have the stomach for it though, Neva offers an intensely emotional journey which will not be soon forgotten. Much of the success of that narrative comes from the impeccable level design, built specifically for environmental storytelling, and another brilliant soundtrack from Berlinist that can tear at the heartstrings all on its own.Pros:+ Satisfying gameplay mechanics and progression+ Memorable and emotional story+ Beautiful art design and visuals+ Outstanding soundtrackCons:- Significant content warning for animal death, harm, and distress- Some platforming sections which could prove frustrating to casual playersScore:9/10 - Highly recommended
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

I did not relate with the characters or story much. There are higher stakes and animal themes which I know some get more emotional over than others. Not a flash in the pan like Gris, but I am eager for more of this quality over length to see what games are capable of.

_childDocuments_.review: At about five hours it is a bit short, but it's also one of the few such games I actually feel like I may want to replay, so there's that. It does manage to avoid being repetitive, as it introduces new enemies (and new abilities as Neva grows up) as well as new environments.Art style is similar to GRIS but it doesn't seem to be a sequel as such. It's a lot less abstract and it's a lot clearer what the heck is happening. Music is also pretty great.There is combat that can be fairly challenging if you're playing it on Adventure mode, but also fun once you get the hang of it. There is also Story difficulty that does not track health/hitpoints, making it a lot less frustrating if you don't really care about combat as such.Platforming for the main path isn't particularly challenging. Reaching some of the collectibles can be a bit difficult. But the difficult ones are generally puzzles that require some thought and attention, rather than hardcore platforming skills.In some contexts the Y button does more than just interact with Neva. It's easy to miss some of the achievements on the first run if you're not looking out for that. But you can also go back to specific parts of specific chapters so you don't have to replay the entire game if you just want to 100% the achievements.Expect cuteness. Bring tissues.

_childDocuments_.review: A total evolution on what made Gris an excellent game. Amazing visuals, audio, music and storytelling. Everything is told visually and lets the player come to their own conclusions and interpretations, even though there is a very solid and clear message told by the symbolism and subtext of the game. _childDocuments_.review: Having been mesmerised by Gris—with its beautiful watercolour aesthetics and poignant story of grief—I had high expectations going into Neva, and I’m thrilled to say that it didn’t disappoint! The developers of Gris have once again captured magic, but in a refreshingly different way.Right from the start, I was enchanted by the shift in the art style. While Gris flowed with smooth watercolours, Neva opts for something more textured—repeating small blotches, almost like a brush's distinct impression scattered across a canvas. It’s an interesting evolution, still breathtaking but in a more tactile, raw manner. The difference feels deliberate, bringing both depth and a refreshing change, while remaining visually accessible for any viewer to easily perceive and appreciate.The music, another stronghold of Gris, makes a powerful return but with a new flair. Given the addition of combat in Neva, the score rises to the occasion. It swells during intense moments, giving the fights a heroic and inspiring edge, yet it never overshadows the beautiful art. Instead, it perfectly complements it, enhancing the emotional depth and atmosphere while allowing the visuals to shine. The combat itself is simple, which I appreciated, as it allowed the core elements—art and music—to remain in focus, reinforcing the game's identity as a work of art in motion.If I had one wish, it would be for a photography mode! There are so many stunning frames throughout the game, and I found myself yearning for a way to capture them. Whether it's a shot with Alba or Neva (or both or neither), having that extra layer of interaction would have been delightful!I have to say—calling for Neva never got old! I found myself petting and interacting with Neva often :')  (It added a personal touch to the game.) To summarise, Neva beautifully blends evolving art, enchanting music, and engaging combat to create a journey that feels both familiar and fresh. It's a game that, much like Gris, leaves the player with something to think about—though perhaps not to the same degree of impact. However, sometimes parental love doesn’t need to be as profound and complex as grief to resonate deeply.

_childDocuments_.review: Save the doggo, save the world.From the same developer that created GRIS, Neva brings a lot of what made GRIS great, and adds a combat system to the mix.  The combat is overall fairly solid, but I will say that players who are a bit more on the casual side may have more trouble with this game compared to GRIS.  There is a Story/Casual mode available to make it easier, but I don't have experience in what is actually easier.  I believe it said there are no deaths in that mode at least, which should help some casual players out a lot.Neva is quite appealing visually, and there are definitely a few in game scenes that are great to look at, as well as cutscenes that are enjoyable to watch.  Some puzzles can be a bit tricky, but overall I didn't have too much trouble with them.  The combat is solid, but like I said earlier, could be a bit difficult for some casual gamers.  The sounds in the game are nice, and both main characters are well done.  Definitely a fun experience, and I'll soon be getting the last few achievements I missed to fully complete the game.Both Neva and Gris are definitely worth playing, just know that Neva has more actual combat.  My personal take is that GRIS is a bit better overall, and I think I really enjoyed the color coded areas of GRIS a bit more too.  I did find the combat decent overall, but not enough to where it overtakes the other parts of the game that GRIS did a little better.  I believe they are similar game length as well, and visually you can see a lot of similarities between the two when it comes to the structures and just overall feel.I definitely recommend Neva, and also GRIS, if you haven't played that game either.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing Neva felt like playing Princess Mononoke The Game. The animations were beautiful and music was emotive.But despite the short length and generally enjoying my time with it, I definitely felt like I had to push through to finish the game.Without spoiling anything, the abstract nature of the story didn't grab me and I didn't quite understand the point of it. It was trying to say... something? I understood the metaphors but didn't find it compelling. There were large swaths of the game where I was simply just holding down the directional button/stick to go in one direction - it's almost like I was being forced to "see how beautiful everything is!" The platforming and combat was pretty basic and didn't really evolve, and the puzzles were alright.I have mixed feelings about my experience with Neva, but still positive. I do recommend it because I think it's important to support studios that clearly pour a lot of love and passion into their games.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game, but would struggle to recommend it given it's short length and overall lack of depth. This isn't a walking simulator by any means, but aside from stylistically exceptional visuals, all other aspects of the gameplay are weak to mid at best. There are some interesting mechanics, but the game is just too short to ever really fully explore or appreciate them. Even the stunning artwork seems to stumble in places with some assets that (in my opinion at least), seem jarring and out of place. I see little replay value in the game either as other than "find the secret flowers", there isn't anything to do. [1]Sound and music is on point for the themes and the characters, Neva especially, are adorable (disclosure, I love dogs so this was an easy sell). Clearly much of this being inspired by Princess Mononoke.Would I pay £16.99 for the game? No, there are far more engaging and long lasting indie titles available on Steam that offer much better value. Would I pay maybe £8.99 for the game. Yes I probably would, just to experience the visuals. At full price however, I'd say give it a miss.I will now however, go and give my 11yo Samoyed a long hug as the themes of loss in this game has reminded me how precious she is and how little time we may have left![1] I'd love btw, for someone to correct me if I'm wrong on this, but I didn't see anything other than linear progression in the story.

_childDocuments_.review: from the creators  of gris, neva is a beautiful game telling the story of a young woman and her wolf/deer? ( seriously it has horns ) as they travel through the seasons of a blighted and dying land.stunning visuals, liquid smooth animations, emotionally epic music, satisfying platforming and combat all combine to create a real emotional gem of a game.and yes you can pet neva. the wolf with horns.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I would recommend this game, but for those wondering how it compares to Gris, personally I would say that Gris was the superior game. Gris and Neva share some obvious design elements, and both games are pretty and feature some fun and interesting platforming, but I think Gris was stronger narratively, as well as more interesting musically and artistically. One big and obvious difference between the games is that Neva features combat, and this, as well as more precise and difficult platforming, makes the game feel more punishing, while I found Gris to be a more relaxing experience. All of this brought me back to Gris several times, whereas I don't think I will be replaying Neva. Of course, your experience may very well differ if the themes of Neva resonate with you more strongly, or if combat and more challenging platforming are right up your alley. If you found Gris challenging enough, or are looking for a more laid-back experience, you might want to try the game on story mode, or otherwise give it a miss entirely.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m only in the fall chapters and I’m already in love with this game. A worthy successor to Gris, with the same kind of gorgeous animation in a very different setting and with some snazzy new combat mechanisms to boot. And, most importantly, you CAN pet the dog!! Neva is adorable and continues to grow fiercer as you progress through the seasons. The gameplay is smooth and satisfying, and traversal is quick with both a roll and a jump/dash, though I never want to move too quickly through the beautiful landscapes. Overall, this gives me major Ghibli vibes and especially Princess Mononoke…it can’t be a coincidence that the main animals I’ve seen so far are wolves, a deer, and boars, all of the giant variety.Edit after I've now finished the game: this was truly beautiful and heartbreaking in the best way. Journey before destination....the story and the setting were both beyond stunning, and I'm so glad I played this! _childDocuments_.review: I do not recommend this game, but it is only after passing the first few levels that the disappointing features become apparent. This is a game in which a protagonist and her pet wolf maneuver through obstacles.  Similar themes are found in the Japanese movie, Princess Mononoke. The graphics are beautiful. I have not encountered any puzzles, despite the Puzzles tag. It's mostly action-adventure/physics/hand-eye coordination. Unfortunately, the keyboard controls (as shown in the game settings) do not advance the character to the degree necessary to succeed, especially in the harder version. Had to switch to the easier version. This offers fewer features to replace the glowing fountains of life, so there's a lot of wasted space. Additionally, the character mysteriously cannot leap to reach a glowing hibiscus/lily flower - but she can leap exactly the same distance to traverse the level. The control triggers and responses seem arbitrary. The fight scenes do not produce better results from planning attacks vs simply button-mashing and there's no real satisfaction. I could not get a refund because level one is very easy and it was only after awhile that I noticed the problems in this game. So, I'm playing it through, but I would not purchase it again.

_childDocuments_.review: As a successor to GRIS, Neva has a lot to live up to. I believe that Nomada Studio delivers. I appreciate that some reviews don't feel that Neva has the depth GRIS does, and I'm not one to compare two mediums, but I have to state my disagreement outright. There's a difference in approach with each game. For one, grief is a universally-felt emotion. It's inescapable. Anyone who played GRIS will find an easy self-insert with the player character. However, many of us can only imagine what it's like to claw and scream and beg your way forward in a world that isn't built for you anymore.-No spoilers, but some social commentary that might spoil the theme for the smartypantses in the room-That's where Neva absolutely shocked me. I was elated to see a black woman as our protagonist, especially in an adventure series. It wasn't until the end of the game that I realized how absolutely necessary it was that the protagonist be a black woman. Nomada Studio has a clear point they want to make. Sure, we can relate what happens in the game to climate change and greed and colonialism, but it's much closer to home than any of those themes.I adore this game. GRIS struck me in the gut. But Neva gently took my hand and flipped me upside-down.Aside from the theme, the combat does feel unpolished. I don't care too much because I'm not invested in this as a combat game, but if you care, that's between you and your god. Additionally, Neva's progression feels well-engineered, but I wish some of the elements (eg, achievements and collectibles) helped with the world-building.In short, Neva is gorgeous. If you want depth, it's staring you in the face. You may have to go outside of yourself for this one. It's a doozy.11/10 I would kill God and punch the sun for the goodest doggo.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a neutral option because I don't think Neva is bad, but it could've been a lot better. It didn't do well enough to earn a thumbs up from me, but it doesn't warrant a thumbs down either. I eventually settled on a thumbs down by the logic that it's currently 'very positive' on the steam store, and I think it should be a bit lower than that.The main problem I had is that it was too similar to Gris visually - a woman with hair that doesn't go past her shoulders and flowy clothes walks left-to-right a lot through a watercolour-y land with strong colours and symmetrical architecture with a lot of arches and towers. She collects white dots to activate big floating squares, and is attacked by a black, amorphous monster that changes shape fluidly and screeches. Personally, I just found it really hard to get immersed because I was so often being reminded of Gris and couldn't stop comparing them while I was trying to enjoy the game.Later areas innovated more (I loveddd ), but I wish the game pushed itself to be more different in aesthetics and music. Especially since the visuals are simplified down (understandably, considering the more detailed world of Neva), it sometimes feels like a cheap copy of Gris' design. That's not to say it's bad, it's just too similar to something better.Speaking of different, Nomada studios did an excellent job of adding combat - movement is fluid and easy to control, and the attacks feel intuitive and seamless. Getting Neva to . I have no complaints about that aspect of the game, but the non-combat parts can drag a bit. It gets more fun when movement goes in other directions , but Neva has quite a few sections that are simply walking/dashing along long stretches of perfectly horizontal terrain. While Gris was slow and meditative, Neva verges on slow and repetitive. TL;DR: Good game, but probably a lot better if you haven't played Gris first.Also I am a bit biased tbf because I'm neutral about dogs. It would've needed to do more to get me emotionally invested in Neva - at the end

_childDocuments_.review: If it would be possible to give a neutral review I would. The new protagonist is essentially a reskinned Gris, now a Black female samurai. She looks, runs, and jumps almost identically. It's the same game with a new coat of paint. They haven't even tried to create something new.Gris sold well, received critical acclaim, and won awards. Yet, the developers inexplicably decided to address criticisms by adding combat, weapons, and death. These additions might be beneficial in other circumstances, but they already had a masterpiece with global recognition. They've tried to fix what wasn't broken.Gris took place within the subconscious of a young woman grieving the loss of her mother, which explained why she was the only human present. Neva, however, is set in the physical world. WHY is the protagonist alone? Where is everyone?Why am I forced to babysit this creature the entire game? I feel nothing towards it. With the statue mother in Gris, the player's connection developed gradually. Through imagery, we understood her importance, her suffering, and the reciprocal nature of our relationship. The theme was developed, allowing us to empathize—that's how it works. Here, it's just, "Here's your furry Pokémon, now babysit it." I don't want to! Seriously... I don't want to do this. I don't want to babysit a kid. I don't care about him; let him go grow a tree out of his head in the forest. I'm a Black feminist samurai on my way to African Japan; leave me alone!The monster, the black one with the white mask, is ripped straight from "Spirited Away." If you haven't seen it, watch it.The forest being infected with black ink blots is stolen from "Princess Mononoke." Again, just straight-up plagiarism.Regarding the visuals: The technical level is similar to Gris, but that game's surreal world masked its limitations.  The game is way too short, it will take you about 4-5 hours to complete it, hence I cannot recommend it at full price. It costs 76 rmb (10.70 USD)  in China region. I would say something in 45-50 rmb (6-7 USD) price range would be fair. Hence, wait for discount if you want to get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game on its own, but compared to Gris does feel inferior in pretty much every way. I might change this to a positive review once I've read other people's theories regarding the story and ending. Right now, the story as I interpret it, falls flat. It just feels like a generic nature good vs outside forces (dark) = bad. I couldn't really detect anything deeper in it. The music in this game is also quite forgettable (compared to Gris), which I believe to be because Gris intertwined gameplay and music, making the music feel part of the world. Here's it's mostly just background noise. I also think Gris did a better job in the art department. Blending abstract and organic looked wonderful in that game. And it worked because Gris was all about emotion, which is both raw (organic) and human (abstract). In Neva organic and ''human'' / abstract are clearly seperated, making it all feel a bit cold. As if anything other than naturalistic is not good, to be avoided. Again, this view of mine might change once I've read more theories regarding the story and ending. I understand that Gris set the bar pretty high, so this might just come across as rambling, but these are just my two cents.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: GRIS is my most favourite game ever. No other game has left a mark on me like GRIS. It's a masterpiece. I was expecting either an equal or elevated experience in Neva and I have never been more disappointed in a sequel in any form of media. Okay, maybe Boruto is a worse sequel but I digress.For me, Neva is a wholesale downgrade from GRIS. The platforming, puzzling and narrative lack any depth. The whole game has nothing to say. Its generic and unoriginal, it feels uninspired. While the combat can be fun and there were some highs, the combat really feels like a distraction from the lackluster story and platforming. I can't imagine what people who played the narrative focused version went through; without the combat there is barely a game. Again, only in comparison to GRIS. The mirror level was the only spark of GRIS-esque brilliance, but was so short lived, and still falls short without a story to ground it.And on the note of the story, the ending would be clever if what came before was interesting in any way. The whole time I wondered why Neva never showed any pain, regret, anger or frustration for losing her mother. It makes more sense why it was such a empty revenge story, because it never was one in the first place. Regardless, the only progression in Neva is her size and abilites. Then there's the main character , she doesn't really go through any narrative journey. She's there, she calls for Neva, she fights and then rinse repeat. There is no real masterful subtlety in this game, there's no real reason to connect with the characters and there's no reason to replay this game, especially after that ending.Sigh, if this was a first game from a studio I would say the game is fine, nothing to write home about but fine. Very pretty but fine. I did have fun, sweaty moments with the combat and some puzzles but the journey to those moments was so empty. Unbelievably empty or to be fair unbelievably empty in comparison to GRIS. GRIS was brilliant from head to toe and it arguably has one of the most memorable indie soundtracks out there. Neva's soundtrack, like it's story, like it's platforming will be memorable only in that it is a reminder of my disappointment. This whole game is memorable in a way it neva intended to be, and that's why I have to dub it the Joker 2 of gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, i was expecting something more. Game is okayish with flavour of "gris touch", but i dont feel that emotion this game is providing me.Graphics are okay but too plain with some post processing effects to cover it up. U cant compare it to Gris, its different game, but its quite similar in many ways, and this is the main reason why i did a refund. Its not near good in terms of execution and pet animation is trash.

_childDocuments_.review: Been a while since a game has so thoroughly disappointed me. The combat adds nothing to the game in my opinion. A handicapped gamer with a neuromuscular disorder, there are simply points where I cannot progress, even on story mode. Take a glance at other recent games like Crypt Custodian in the indie realm for an example of how to do accessibility right with options to make timed events easier. I'm not opposed to a difficult game, but dying repeatedly during a chase/escape sequence where the timing is way too tight just isn't fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the art of the game, but it does look stolen from princess Monoke and Spirited away. The wolves and deer are far too similar to the ones in princess Monoke, as are the corrupted boars, also the monsters literally look like no face from spirited away. The game was really short, I finished it in only three hours and that was with stopping to eat. It felt like it was getting going and then it just ended. The ending also felt dumb to me, like wah? If I could, I would give it a neutral review as it wasn't amazing, but it wasn't bad either. I just do not really approve of the blatant copying of Ghibli characters and how unfinished the game felt. Other than that, the game play was fun.

_childDocuments_.review: 5.4/10 - Game is way too short and easyI want to like this game and recommend it, but I just can't. I played this on stream and was excited to try it out because the art style looked unique and the combat looked cool.  Unfortunately, while this game can be fun and is definitely beautiful to look at, it's too easy and the little bit of the story that's there is not that interesting. Combat is a cake walk once you get the hang of it, puzzles are a breeze to figure out, and oh yeah, did I mention this game is painfully short?  I beat it in about 4 hours and while I liked aspects of this game, I don't think it's worth the money, even though it's on the cheaper side.  If it gets a really steep sale and you want a casual game that's pretty to look at, give it a shot.  Other than that, I'd say skip it.

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to Gris, Neva is an absolute disappointment.First of all, graphics/art. Gris has brilliant architecture design, vivid and diverse color use, and very memorable character design (e.g. the cute little creatures in the forest which u need to feed them apples). I feel NONE of these in Neva, only tons of CHEAP CHEAP color blocks in the foreground and background.Secondly, combat. Why the hell did u guys add combat system??? If someone would like to combat in a dark nature setting, he would simply buy Ori. Gris has no combat, which is great, because it makes the players pay more attention to the scene, the story and music, etc.I waited SO long for another mind blowing piece of art like Gris, but sadly, WASTED
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I adored Gris for all the reasons everyone else does, but I never emotionally connected with that game. It's themes were a bit too abstract.From beginning to end, I was far more emotionally invested in Neva.  I recently lost a cat of ten years to cancer. I still love him. I still miss him. I had raised him from one week old. Playing Neva brought that loss back to the surface. The grief is fresh again, but I think I'm in a better place with it. It's a beautiful game about the cycle of life and death. There is hope on the other side of loss.Rest well, Phineas
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely gorgeous game. Loved the tension in the combat and the beautiful atmosphere. Even at the more challenging segments, things felt super chill. The puzzles aren't insanely difficult just to be difficult. The leveling up aspect is pretty unique to me, but I have never played GRIS and will be doing so after this stunning introduction to Nomada Studio.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This takes its place among my top three games of all time. I have cried again and again playing this game, and I can honestly say that it is a piece of art which has truly changed my outlook on family and motherhood. I do not say this lightly, of course. I would like to keep this review more about Neva, but I will say that I do love Neva far more than GRIS. While GRIS is beautiful, and its exploration of grief is enrapturing, it pales in comparison to the sheer weight of emotional impact (at least for me). I see myself playing this game every so often just to get a good cry in. I counted how many times: 12, four of which were ugly cries. Keep in mind Neva is not a long game either - I cried approximately once every 15 minutes. I encourage anyone who loves GRIS to play this game, and for those who haven't played either, I'd say to give it a shot anyway. Any acclaim I can give this game would simply not be adequate.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Besides the goods everyone already mentioned, i wish there was Mouse support for people who are terrible with controllers. I only wished to be able to aim/attack with my mouse with + WASD controls. You simply can't bind actions on Mouse buttons.I still managed to beat the game, with some frustration, especially at a certain later part of the game. You can choose to play on "Story Mode" where you apparently can't die. Besides my frustrations, combat was actually decent.There was no way i would miss a game developed by makers of GRIS so you should also check it out if you've liked GRIS.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, with a burning passion. I don't think it has quite the same artistry that Gris does as the story in Neva is a bit more... Up and front. But if you enjoyed the water color style of Gris, this game does not fail to deliver on that front. And in some cases, it is so much better. Several times I found myself blown away by visuals. I would absolutely recommend this game. Especially if you're a pet owner.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva is an absolute masterpiece! From the very first moments, I was captivated by its breathtaking art style and deeply emotional narrative. The game masterfully weaves a story of loss, growth, and love, all while immersing you in a beautifully crafted world that feels alive and vibrant.The gameplay is smooth and engaging, perfectly complementing the storytelling. I loved how the puzzles and challenges were not only fun but also tied seamlessly into the emotional beats of the game. Every moment felt purposeful, and the connection between the protagonist and their companion was genuinely moving.Neva isn’t just a game—it’s an experience. It left me reflecting on its themes long after the credits rolled. If you’re looking for a game that combines stunning visuals, heartfelt storytelling, and meaningful gameplay, Neva is a must-play! Highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys indie gems that truly stand out.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Good game as a standalone title. Overall, I'd say it's worse compared to Gris though.The art and visuals in some levels have improved in Neva, though Neva also has a lot of levels with darker themes which are not as engaging to play through at all, both in terms of visuals and music. Even though there's some beautiful songs, overall the music is a slight downgrade to Gris imo. One aspect where they fumbled the bag compared to Gris is the story though: While Gris had a creative and rather innovative approach to the story and theme,

_childDocuments_.review: I will proudly say this is the most beautiful game I have ever played. The cinematics are breathtaking, and I particularly enjoy the shift of camera focus throughout it. The soundtrack in this game is so moving. It tells the story for you, and the score perfectly captures the emotion of what's at hand. These were the biggest reasons I decided to download it, and I can happily say I'm incredibly glad I did. From the story, to the environment, to the SOUNDTRACK, it's absolutely amazing and this will be a game I will encourage everyone to play. It's a perfect game to show that you don't need dialogue to tell a great story. If you were hesitant about whether or not you should play it, this is your sign that you absolutely should.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva carries the visual polish and sonic mastery from Gris with a casual combat system creating a little more variety. Though neither go out of their way to surprise, and can at times feel a little uninspired and repetitve, Neva is still at its core a sweet experience meditating on the cycle of loss and grief.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I streamed this game for Extra Life just a couple days after it was released. It immediately drew me in with its gorgeous art style and music, punched me in the feels, and then pulled me along to find out what happened next! The environment is full of things to discover, intuiting how to navigate the terrain and puzzles with minimal UI to distract you, and leaving you wondering when the next conflict will jump at you. I also recommend acquiring the extra items like the art book if the visuals are what appeal to you most--there are full pages of nothing but plant designs! Half of my Steam Awards nominations are unapologetically for Neva.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I knew the games of this studio thanks to Gris, at the time, made me enjoy it beyond what I would expect from a platformer. Of course, as soon as I heard about the upcoming release of Neva, contrary to what I usually do, I pre-sold the game. I was not disappointed, the game is that reset of calm that we all need, it has the necessary action, without reaching the level of frenzy. The art is a visual ride from start to finish. And also the game has a message without falling into the fanaticism of the wrongly called `woke` movement.It is impossible to play it and not feel in the world of Ghibli with Princess Mononoke. Buy the game, whether it is on discount or not, it is worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva is a true testament to how video games can transcend entertainment to become pure art. Visually, Neva is a living painting. It’s impossible not to stop and admire the sheer beauty of its hand-drawn animations and vast color palette, which rival even the most celebrated animated works. The environments feel alive and layered, drawing comparisons to the works of Miyazaki. The soundtrack by Berlinist wraps it all together, evoking melancholy and hope in equal measure, a perfect complement to the game’s stunning visuals.

_childDocuments_.review: Very pretty visuals and a touching story ultimately didn't quite surpass the mechanical issues with this game. Platforming, although functional, never really as fluid or as weighty as I would have wished. Combat suffers from similar issues, with the core loop never really clicking in the way I wish it would. _childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely gorgeous game, the art is hauntingly beautiful and music that matches perfectly. I cannot stress enough how visually stunning every level is, with colours that follow your journey and evolve as you progress. Plus a lovely story with combat and platforming that feels fluid and not too difficult (though there is a "story mode" which removes lives if that's not your cup of tea). With me savouring a lot of the landscapes, I finished the game in about 4.5 hours, with 100% in about 6 since you can skip to the chapters with collectables you missed. Maybe a bit short for the price tag, but the incredible experience more than makes up for it in my opinion. Wonderful game and definitely one I'll be revisiting. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful, sad and hopeful – all at the same time and all without a single word. Amazing art direction, very tastefully emotional soundtrack. Short yes, comparatively light on gameplay, yes but Neva aptly demonstrates that a game can be so much more that just stats and intricate mechanics. I enjoyed every moment of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: A Masterpiece of Emotion and AtmospherePlaying Neva felt like rediscovering the magic I experienced when I first played Hollow Knight. This game is a heartfelt journey, beautifully crafted in every aspect.First, let’s talk about the art style. It’s simply breathtaking. Every frame feels like a painting, blending delicate details with vibrant colors. The world feels alive, with stunningly designed environments that seamlessly shift between awe-inspiring beauty and haunting desolation.The music deserves special praise as well. It's not just a soundtrack; it’s an emotional compass, guiding you through the highs and lows of the story. The way it adapts to your actions and the unfolding narrative creates a deeply immersive experience.The controls are incredibly responsive, making every movement feel intuitive and precise. Whether you're navigating intricate landscapes or engaging in combat, the gameplay flows effortlessly. Speaking of combat, while it isn’t overly challenging, it’s undeniably fun. The straightforward mechanics make battles enjoyable and accessible, adding to the game’s overall charm without detracting from its emotional depth.But what truly sets Neva apart is how it makes you feel. It captures that rare magic of a game that’s not just a series of levels but an emotional experience. It’s a game that will linger in your mind long after the credits roll, much like Hollow Knight did for me.TLDR: If you’re looking for a game that blends stunning visuals, evocative music, tight gameplay, and engaging combat into an unforgettable experience, Neva is a must-play.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I've adopted Neva since the day the first trailer came out, which I cried every time I watched it. Now that I've gotten to play it, it's so worth the wait and this will have a big place in my heart. I love wolves, I love nature spirits - I love fighting against corruption upon mother nature (love their concept). This game is so breathtaking, the story is beautifully told, and it's heartbreaking at times. I hope to see more, if not more of Neva somehow but different story, same universe - maybe.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva is definitely a step in the right direction for Nomada Studio.While Gris was an impressive audiovisual experience, its gameplay mechanics were quite barebones. Neva takes the core mechanics of Gris and improves on them by adding combat and interactions with the animal companion. This results in a more challenging gameplay experience, which experienced players should find more appealing. On the other hand, there is also a story mode suited for more casual gamers that just want to enjoy the beauty of the game without the extra challenge.Speaking of beauty, the art style of Neva is as breathtaking as that of Gris. The ambiance of the game is a lot darker compared to Gris, but there are also some impressively colorful scenes projecting hope and the feeling of renewal. One obvious influence when it comes to the art style is Studio Ghibli. One can see Hayao Miyazaki's influence when it comes to both the enemies and the animals.A review of a Nomada Studio game wouldn't be complete without mentioning the music of Berlinist and the way it blends with the art style to guide the flow of the story. Every note enhances the experience, be it a calm moment enjoying the ambience or the heat of battle.I must admit I was worried whether Nomada Studio would be capable of repeating the success of Gris. But the creators of Gris proved they can not only replicate the brilliance of their previous game but even improve on it.
