The way the game intertwines its themes of growth, loss, and survival with beautifully crafted puzzles and combat is masterful. The emotional weight is undeniable, making this journey one that lingers long after completion. With minimal UI and a haunting soundtrack, [/i] Neva [/i] is a perfect blend of art and emotion, proving once again that Nomada Studio knows how to craft experiences that move the soul.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Gris, but more for the music and artstyle, the gameplay itself was a bit less interesting and didn't give you a lot of agency. Neva, however, fixed that completely.Still gorgeous music and visuals, with an engaging story that you felt the weight of the whole time, but also the gameplay is great! Because I felt like I was in control in combat and that I could lose I felt desperate and satisfied with what I accomplished.The gameplay grows as the game goes on and it further pushes the relationship between you and your buddy.The different levels have such unique gimmicks and tones as well.Truly lovely, maybe even my game of the year.I'm going to go cry now <3
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: A bit underwhelming compare to Gris, I strongly suggest story mode for difficulty to not break your immersion from a bit clunky combat system. Stunning as expected, it is a short title, if you preferred waiting for a sale you may but I opted to pay full price for what I think are rare gems that need our full support.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: The art style is obviously beautiful and haunting, music beautiful, gameplay is fun and challenging at times; the world is simply a pleasure to be in, even though it's a fairly linear game. For me, the story wasn't able to hit the emotional heights that Gris was, and I found I was able to predict some of the beats and the ending, once it became clear what they were going for (possibly because I've played Gris a few times). But I don't really see these as drawbacks or negative aspects, as the game as a whole is good, and it is it's own story, it's own game. I also liked some of the innovations in the platforming a lot, really cool stuff. And vibey as heck! Would definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I usually do not write reviews.However, I hear some people say the game is too short, or that it is not "action" enough, or it does not have enough tough platforming challenges.Not every game needs to fit into the same mold. Neva is a beautiful work of art and an emotional journey, like other games before it (Gris from the same developers, Journey, to name just two examples.) If you like games where an emotional core, beautiful music and stunning visuals come together, you will like this one.Some experiences are just meant to be played and enjoyed. I enjoyed this, I did not mind the price at all and have bought the artbook and soundtrack DLC to further support the creation of emotional pieces like this one.Oh and I also took 414 screenshots while just running around the beautiful areas. I am sorted on wallpapers for the foreseeable future.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful story that i liked. Some combat puzzles were a bit frustrating but the game is worth it in my opinion.Those who compare it to Gris.. Can you really? Why? Is this game not gonna be its own thing? Why compare them. Different games. Gameplay will be different and i did like it. The puzzles were fun and the cute interactions with the wolf itself is adorable.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva presents a visually striking experience; however, it ultimately falls short of the emotional depth established by Gris. While the game features elements of combat and platforming, there are moments that lack engaging content, which can make the experience feel like just a "walking simulator".Although the art direction is undoubtedly the standout aspect offering a mix of breathtaking landscapes and some way less successful surreal elements, this visual appeal may not be enough to sustain  interest. Even the charming presence of the wolf cub fails to fully captivate. On a positive note, the game is short !
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Another good game by people who actually take the time to make a polished product. Beautiful art and music, and a simple but still fun combat system. Enjoyable platforming mechanics that work well in and out of combat.A very emotionally heavy game, but I didn't find it to be as moving as their previous game (Gris). Not to say that it doesn't do a very good job at what it sets out to do, but that I personally was less interested in the subject matter.Overall, go play this game. 9/10. Seems to be around 6-7 hours for 100% casual completion.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: i have been excited for this game since i heard about it, as Gris was a fantastic gorgeous game. Neva is everything i expected and wanted-- art and animation is just as stellar, and the gameplay is done well with simple but satisfying combat and exploration. it has enough challenge (for me, a pretty average gamer) that i felt like i was doing something impactful while playing through the narrative, and it all felt very satisfying to play the combat. the game is not super long but it is a great experience-- stunning, well written, and well done simply gameplay that had me happy with it overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This game was well worth the wait. The visuals are stunning and the story is incredibly captivating. To anyone who hasn't yet played and is reading through the reviews: Make sure to have a tissue box nearby, trust me. At the point of me writing this I haven't yet completed the game but I've already cried several times. The musical scored will make sure you *feel* the scenes.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Stunning game and an wonderful experience. It was a good step forward after Gris, which was already great but this game was even better.The music, artwork and environment were all amazing, and the story was really beautifull. I can´t recommend this game enough if you want to have a delightful and relaxing experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: It's a beautiful story with soothing sountrack. Graphics are amazing, movement is fluid for the most part and there is a combat system - which is fine. The game overall looks amazing, sounds great and  tells a very nice story - but plays just alright.  I would still recommend to experience it for yourself tho.I wouldn't necessarly compare it to Gris too much - they have some similarities (mostly in animations, basic movement and level designs) but play and feel completely differently.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: My expectations were very high, and yet i was surprised. Just like GRIS, the artworks and the soundtracks are ASTONISHING. The gameplay is very intriguing and quite challenging. Puzzle solving is less present but still entertaining. The only "downside" is the longevity, as it takes only about 4hs, but again, a well deserved 11/10
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I 100% this game on an LCD Steam Deck. It runs at an easy 60fps, and doesn't really work the fan. There was a weird audio glitch at launch, but it has been patched out. This is one of my favorite games. It's not long, but definitely worth playing. Nomada Studio did a great job on the art and story telling, just like they did with Gris. Berlinist made an amazing soundtrack. The puzzles and combat are not overly difficult, but are definitely fun, and the controls are simple and work reasonably well. Overall, I highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I am sorry i just cannot recommand this game.It's pretty, but the gameplay is way too bland. Other than that, the game responsiveness is good.There are games less expensive out there with more content and depth.Don't get me wrong this type of simplistic gameplay might be the direction the devs went on, and it might suit some players.And no offence to the developers, you might consider adding a bit more content and i am sure the game will be great!I am just saying that the market is overwhelmed with games like this one,  they are less expensive with more content, not necessarily harder or more complicated. Adding customised weapons (bow, spear, etc), pet attacks, cosmetics, the list goes on, if you're not going for specific difficulty but for the fun then balance isn't really your main concern, just add anything that comes to your mind.I will keep the game on Wishlist in case the situation changes.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the game, it retains the style and elegance Nomada Studio showed with Gris. The game is short, maybe too short, but it does not lack amazing art or screens that can make the player emotional without talking. The music is also amazing. The gameplay is easy and has few actions the player can do, but they are well-tuned and perfectly used to make the game feel always different and fresh for all the 3 hours the game lasts. Tbh, this game did not move me as Gris did, probably because I already knew the Studio style, maybe because it is less personal than Gris. But it was amazing seeing how similar emotions changed in "weight and meaning" while feeling them together as Neva and the Protagonist. Give it a try, there is talent in this game, in Gris and in Nomada Studio.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva is obviously a gorgeous visual treat but it's also just challenging enough to keep you invested in the gameplay as well as the emotionally story. There is an instant fluidity to the movement of the protagonist, with double-jump and air-dash available from the start. Something I'm not used to in most games that fit this genre but it all felt so organic that once you pick up the controller you know instantly how to play. That's a testament to good game development. Short and to the point, the game leaves an impression on those willing to invest the time into it. It's well worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I just started playing, and I want to play it so much more but also to slow down and take as much time with it as I can. Every frame so far seems like an art piece. I just keep taking screenshots. The music is beautiful. The controls feel fluent, the 'combat' is forgiving but interesting enough so far. Will update more soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the best game I play. When I finished the game, I was feeling it was the final boss of video games. I also played Gris and I loved it. Neva is like Gris but everything is better, starting with the gameplay (I had a lot of fun) (Boss fights are amazing).Obviously Neva is Beautiful. the story is great and I sometimes just stoped playing to enjoy the view and the music.I don't want to say too much, just:PLAY NEVA!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Another beautiful game from Nevada Studios. Visuals and music again are beyond beautiful. Atmospheric and heart touching. I enjoyed the combat, felt a bit awkward in the beginning, but you get the hang of it, and even the combats are so visually pleasing.I agree that it cannot compete with GRIS, the story arc did not feel as round as with their first game.But it in itself is still a very wonderful experience that I greatly appreciated. (Also 10/10 for being able to pet Neva. It matters <3)
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Like GRIS from the same developer, Neva is another great experience.It's rich in aesthetics. Controls are tight. Nothing lingers on for too long. Music is brilliant. Sound design is brilliant. It's short but the time you spend with it is quality through and through. Perhaps a bit too artsy for some but for me it's perfect. It hit some really good emotional points with me as an avid dog lover. It didn't hit quite as hard as GRIS, thank god, but it's great nonetheless. It feels like a passion project. As with GRIS, I'll be recommending this game to anyone I know.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing so far.If You are looking for a game like Ori then this might be for you, its got the story telling and art style of GRIS.With the platforming of a side scrolling like Ori, and the bad guys and attacks from a game called Heart of Darkness + pet dog.It feels like mash up of 3 amazing games and I love it.The game is Cute and sweet yest dark and spooky.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This game is such a unique experience - it feels like watching a beautiful movie while having all the fun of a video game. The wolf mechanics are so cute, the visuals astonishing and music beautifully ties it all together. Definitely matches the expectations after playing Gris, and goes way beyond that.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Nomada and Berlinist hit it again. I've been a big fan of the OST in Gris and have been excited for this game when it was announced. This game feels like a true PVE Metroidvania but with all the eye candy of Gris. The splotches of paint and just the environmental design is just chef's kiss. My only complaint is that some parts of the level gets covered by the foreground so first time navigating was confusing and on higher brightness settings your screen may be too bright to tell which is a proper platform.Also you can pet that dawg. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva has the emotional and artistic weight of GRIS but with the addition of extremely satisfying combat and an animal companion that propel the story forward. This game is a masterclass of "show, don't tell," with essentially no dialogue and very minimal tutorial text (basically just telling you what a button does when you can use it for the first time). There is a sentimental and thought-provoking conclusion after about 4-5 hours of gameplay. Encourage your friends to buy this game (or buy it for them) and have a nice heartfelt talk about the meaning of life when you're done.I found the difficulty level of "adventure" mode to be in just the right sweet spot: not ridiculously challenging but not a pushover either; you aren't set back too hard for "failing" a particular fight or environmental hazard, but you do need to restart that screen until you get it right. There is also a "story" mode that allows you to play the game without deaths and with "slightly easier challenges." I haven't tried it, but I'm glad the option exists for people who want to use it.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I have just started to play it but i already love the connection with your companion and ambience of the world you explore through it. Seeing Neva go through any and separate me hurts not just the character but me as well, connecting me more to the whole story and me making it through this journey , for Neva.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I'll finish my review when I finish the game, but I feel like the story, arts and music of opening sequence is enough to buy it.1) I cried during the intro sequence, not for sake of cheap string-tugging, but for the sake of my own life experiences.2) I made many platforming mistakes. They did not punish me, many times. In fact, they allowed me to continue on.I suspect these themes will continue throughout my playthrough. Will update when i finish the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I've had this game on wishlist since the announcement, and I couldn't be happier with the release.This game is beautiful. In all aspects. Beautiful visuals, characters, scenarios, fluid gameplay, freaking amazing OST and most importantly, a spectacular storytelling. I was so hooked that I played this in a row (since is not a very long game either).Although it's approach being very similar to Gris when it comes to the gameplay and some parts of the scenary, adding combat was such a great choice. The bosses wasn't particularly hard, but I did struggled in some fights so I guess this was good :D*spoilers*I wasn't expecting that sort of "loop" by the end of the game, and I was so devasted by what you guys did to Neva, my therapist is going to listen to all my complaints because of you all. Jokes aside, I can't wait to see whats the next project is going to look like since you guys delivered once more.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: For two thirds of the game I was mad at it for not being 'Gris'. I was nitpicking, and ready to fault it, frustrated, fed up and then, then the final third was a tumult of joy, terror, grief, fear, anger and finally pulled my heart out. I have never sobbed and screamed 'no!' at a game before, but I have now. I don't know what to say, really. The journey is worth it, even if it hurts. Neva is forever.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: nomada studio did it again, they made me cry during the first thirty seconds of a game! this story is so lovely and emotional and neva exceeded my expectations. everything about it is just as magical as gris, but with new game mechanics, the cutest animal companion you could ask for, and a hauntingly beautiful world that you can get lost in. neva is just as much a masterpiece as gris and i cannot recommend it enough!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't think it was possible for things to get so much more intense from Gris. All the colors are more vibrant, the set pieces are incredible, and the music by Berlinist is just on a different level. It's like everything I liked about Gris was cranked up even further, and then they added a "pet the dog" button. Add sex to the next one
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva is undeniably gorgeous, dripping with iconic Nomada style. The game opens strong and does a fantastic job of getting you invested in the relationship between Neva and Alba. The soundtrack is of the quality you'd expect from Berlinist, but generally more subtle and less moving than Gris', with a few notable exceptions.The gameplay is similar to Gris in many regards, with the addition of some extremely basic hack-n-slash combat which feels like a response to critics of Gris' gameplay. It's... Fine. The swordplay is serviceable, but not especially weighty or satisfying. The special attack does deepen the combat ever so slightly, but ultimately the combat detracts from the Nomada experience more than it enhances. Rather than being fully engrossed in the audiovisual experience, you need to stay vigilant for ambushes and combat encounters which can break your momentum and break your immersion through video-gamey frustration. A "story mode" option exists, which makes you unkillable and slightly eases combat encounters. If I ever revisit Neva, that's likely what I'll be using. The watercolor aesthetic of Neva is at times quite similar to Gris, but also much darker and even a bit grotesque, in a Studio Ghibli sort of way. I appreciated that, while the game clearly shared a lot of Gris DNA, Nomada gave Neva its own distinctive flair. Gris was a phenomenal debut outing, and left Nomada with a very tough act to follow. They didn't quite capture that lightning a second time, but there's no shame in that. I respect their ambitions, even if I don't always like the changes, and the end result is a fantastic game that's well worth the price of admission.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a sequel to Gris in any way, but it is done by the same team and feels similar. I am thrilled! Berlinist's music is excellent again, the art style is fabulous. The game is great. Update: now that I am a few hours in, I am still very much enjoying the game. I have flipped it to "Story mode", which I would suggest that people who enjoyed Gris try.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Is it foxdeer or deerfox?Comparable to Gris, just as beautiful.If you played Gris, don't expect Neva being anything more than Gris with an imaginary mammal friend and some combat.You might like Neva more, you might like Gris more, but in the end it's enjoyable and 100% worth the time.It's more of the same which is good if you come with this expectation i mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Objectively, Neva is just as good as GRIS if not better. Visuals are still incredibly beautiful and striking. The animations are super detailed and smooth. The OST is S-Tier here too. Gameplay wise Neva is more varied than GRIS and the addition of combat which is simple but effective will allow for some epic moments with the soundtrack.However the story falls short to me, here we have a nice story about the Cycle of life which compared to GRIS's metaphor of grief, did not hit me emotionally as hard as GRIS did. I still really enjoyed the game. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is the first time a game has ever made me cry within the first five minutes of starting it up.I was excited to play this after GRIS, and it does not disappoint so far. The environments and lighting are stunning, along with beautiful music to go with it. It's been satisfying so far to be able to play with the wolf companion, and it's a more involved experience than I was expecting and very happy with. Neva is legitimately helpful during combat, but not to the point you don't feel a challenge, and it's very adorable watching them interact with the environment.My only thing I find a slight negative is the combat at times; I'm not sure if it is just me but I do find that the character is not quite as responsive to the specific actions I'm looking for her to do, and the dodge mechanic can be a tad finicky (sometimes the harmful element still registers during a dodge, sometimes it doesn't) but none of this detracts too much from the overall game play; just something to potentially be aware of. The game is very forgiving in the event you do die.Oh, and you can pet Neva whenever you want ♡

_childDocuments_.review: If you´re searching for a beautiful game full of art, meaning, and emotion, then you found it. It's a solid 9.5/10 for me solely because I wish it would´ve been longer. Games like these make me wish I had the ability to just delete my memory and play it over and over for the first time again.The designs of the characters and the background are so painfully beautiful that I couldn´t help myself making a dozen screenshots. By the end of the game, you´ll be balling your eyes out. And don´t judge a book by its cover ... these fights ... daammmnn. Such a nice balance between challenging and improving your character's skills with Neva to the mechanical changes in the fights which always made it exciting again and not at all repetitive. As for the 19,99€ the game costs ... I would've even paid double for it. I do understand that it might be not it for some people considering the fact that the base game isn´t longer than 5-6 hours but there is so much work and love behind this game that I didn´t even bat an eye when I bought it. I can 100% say that it's been absolutely worth every cent. Ever since Gris came out in 2018 my view on video games has been permanently altered. The pure emotions and art mixed up in a game were simply breathtaking. So when Neva was announced back in 2023 I was so excited to see what Nomada Studios has come up with. My only expectations of this game were beautiful art and that it would leave me in shambles. Neva did exactly that. When I opened the game title itself I was greeted yet again with the amazing soundtrack made by Berlinist. So happy that they were back on board again. The animations have improved so much as well! Gris already looked amazing but they really stepped up with Neva in terms of the animation. I could never put into words how much the games of Nomada Studios mean to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Global grade (final impression, not section average) : ★★★★★★★★★☆Neva succeeds at everything Gris was already succeeding. There is a clear change of tone, mainly in the story and the conveyed message, but other than that it shares the same traits: beautiful, an interstellar sound design, a simple and efficient gameplay. The game is pretty short, count 3-4h for main story. I didn’t do the 100%, but I assume it should require around 5-6h to achieve. I recommend the game without hesitation.At first I thought the gameplay would be the weak point of the game because the beginning of the game is… kinda dull, you don’t have much to do. But as the menace ramp up, so does the complexity of the game, both in difficulty and richness of the gameplay. You have a pretty simple move set, but the game does shine in how you progress in the environment. It does not revolutionize anything but work darn well to deliver a smooth experience, with a well balanced difficulty (the game is easy by my standards), with some slightly harder moments and a death with virtually no progression penality. For casual gamers, Neva constitutes a perfect blend. For more seasoned players, it will be a story game but interesting to play nevertheless. Also, a quite nice perk: you can pet the doggo, at will. Pet the doggo. Pet it more.The strongest point of Neva, the game is just, well, subjectively I suppose, B-E-A-U-T-I-F-U-L. The animation is quite good overall, but the real deal is the environment composition of Neva. Every landscape is gorgeous, multi-layered, and often evolves with your progression. And the best about it is that the environment has such consistency you can sometimes hardly delimit what constitutes pure decoration and elements you can interact with, without really confusing the player more than a couple seconds. The game features several moments of pure “Oh wow” sceneries. And a fair part of what does not constitute “Oh wow” sceneries, constitutes instead some “Oh ♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥” epic moments, adding to the immersion of the intense parts of the game.Neva is some 2D gourmet stuff. Assuming you like its artistic style, as usual with those kind of games with a strong visual identity.See what I said on graphics? Well transpose that to sound design. Enough said.Neva has no character development as there is no dialog.Let’s be honest, Neva story is similar to Ori and Gris: post-it sized and made primarily for feelings, not for lore. It constitutes the still reasonably okay weak point of Neva because with the addition of minimalism comes, unlike Gris, a pretty dull and Manichean message with the subtlety of a bull in a china shop. But while it is not exactly the memorable part of the game, it does the job, especially at filling you with emotions.Bugs: None encountered on Day 1 on my side (the game did required for me to enable steam input), it should be noted however that some players seems to be experiencing difficulties with controller support at the first release version. But I trust the devs to address that. In case of doubt consult the discussions.

_childDocuments_.review:
Neva is an emotionally-charged action adventure from the visionary team behind the critically acclaimed GRIS.

Neva chronicles the story of Alba, a young woman bound to a curious wolf cub following a traumatic encounter with dark forces. Together they embark on a perilous journey through a once-beautiful world as it slowly decays around them.

Over time, their relationship will evolve as they learn to work together, helping one another to brave increasingly dangerous situations. The wolf will grow from a rebellious cub to an imposing adult seeking to forge his own identity, testing Alba's love and their commitment to one another.

As the cursed world threatens to overwhelm them, Alba and her courageous companion will do whatever it takes to survive and make a new home, together.

_childDocuments_.review: I got on the hype train for the global release of this game.Issues to be aware of prior to playing this game1. You will need to change MANY settings during prime times just to play the game2. Even then you will still suffer lag - I personally was lagging so frequently that it was impossible for me to do any jump quests/puzzles which I usually loved doing in other MMORPG's3. The combat is good BUT the time you need to waste on upgrading not only your gear but also your abilities both actives and passives makes this whole thing a massive grind at the end game4. the dungeons are amazing but once you get enough gear score they become a walk in the park whereby parties can literally skip the mechanics and do some dungeons with zero tanks.5. The PVP is highly unbalanced with the meta currently heavily favouring dagger/xbow6. The UI interface is clunky and badly designed, a great deal of scrolling and clicking into windows required7. The cut scenes are dubbed and have not been redone for the GLOBAL release8. Changing classes is a nightmare (I levelled up 3 characters instead)9. The whole thing just feels like a GRIND, if i'm going to sink potentially hundrend more 10. No dedicated AUS servers likely causing the terrible game lagIf you are happy to take all these on board here are the positives1. Beautiful game2. Boss fights and content is quite fun3. Cut scenes are great to watch - even with the dubbing4. One of the best MMORPG intros to any game i've ever played with the ability to skip most content if that is not for you.5. This is an already established game from Korea with backing of AMAZON so the game is going to continue with updates and events (paid) which is highly unlikely to flop if they can fix the other issues mentioned.6. The music scores are FANTASTIC except for some areas where you want to murder the producer for even putting it into the game ( you will know when you hear the music score. It's terrible)These are obviously one persons opinion so take this with a grain of salt and do your own research if you are unsure or disagree with what I have said.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great and most complaints come from people feeling entitled. The game has a lot of PvE content that you can enjoy, which you can clear pretty much with starter gear if you wanted to because all bosses have mechanics that you can almost all block making it so taking damage is almost optional. The world is absolutely stunning, the areas and dungeons are unique, and the fact there are no loading screens even on my laptop surprises me every time I play. The PvP currently feels pay to win, I agree with that. But you don't have to do the PvP events yet, that is a choice. There are so many other things you could also be doing at the same time that if you go to a PvP event and complain it is really on you (Ignoring the fact that you get awarded for simply participating anyway).Besides that the "P2W" elements are more like "pay to skip the line" elements. The thing that people complain about most are traits, which one can eventually get through farming, while the people who bought their way to have the best gear really don't have anything to do anymore; 90% of what makes an MMO great is the farming after all. Even then, you can earn the battlepass, cosmetics, or even weapon traits if you want to, for free simply by playing. If you get drops that you don't need you can sell them on the market and make some decent money from farming that way. This is in turn ofcourse another way that F2P players will be able to catch up, as I personally have been able to buy traits for my weapons already from selling other items as well. Another complaint I have seen was about the fact that there is no direct trading, but in my opinion that is a good thing. They have been pretty fast at handling bots as well, but the direct trading helps with RMT which has no place in a game like this. I personally think the auction house is great for this, especially combined with the tax system which makes bot farming even less lucrative. It's healthier for the game this way. I will admit though, there are A LOT of systems and currencies to learn about, and the game can be punishing for spending some currencies the wrong way. At the same time it is part of what makes the game so great for me, as I love learning about all the systems and min-maxing my profits.

_childDocuments_.review: At its core, the game presents itself as a free-to-play experience with PvP elements, but it ultimately hides its lack of substance behind charming graphics. While the combat system is enjoyable, it remains simplistic, relying primarily on gear upgrades rather than complex mechanics or player skill. Exploration, despite the game's beautiful landscapes, feels lackluster; there are few rewards like hidden chests or engaging discoveries to encourage adventuring.The interface is cluttered with numerous menus, many of which are poorly explained. Housing feels like an afterthought, you receive a room but have no meaningful interaction with it. There’s also a room for adventurers, but its only purpose is to send them on missions to collect resources, making it a missed opportunity for deeper, engaging content.Another major drawback is the time-gated events. Missing an event forces you to wait three hours for the next one, and since some of these events are linked to quest progression, it feels like a mechanism designed to keep players logged in, disregarding their time outside the game.In short, the game feels like a hollow experience, a visually appealing surface with no real depth or structure underneath.

_childDocuments_.review: This is another PVP game that is so mechanically flawed in balance that unless you have the money to waste to join one of the top guilds.  There's no reason to play.  They allowed top geared players to sit and farm all of the "peaceful bosses" by utilizing a flawed mechanic in the game.  With the limit to dungeon runs both co-op and abyssal, no new player will ever be able to compete without spending money.  Furthermore nearly every server is controlled by guilds that when someone was near their level competition wise, they just allied.  Game has already lost 200k average players since it's release.  Unless you have money or enjoy watching 200 people spam abilities at you while you try to see what the pvp is about.  Don't waste your time on this game.  Needed a mechanic in place immediately that moved mega guilds to the same server so that they could compete with each other while other people could enjoy the game.  Probably see the game down to less than 3 N/A East servers within 3 months.

_childDocuments_.review: From the perspective of a free game to play by yourself or with a small group, its an almost okay grindfest.Unless you have 70 people in your main guild, with three more full 70-man guilds publicly labeled as your 2nd, 3rd and 4th guilds, all under that same banner, then you cannot truly play the endgame. I'm sorry, you can either join the zerg or choose another game.You wouldn't believe the grind. All skills have cooldowns and your autoattacks are pathetic. You are not going to be able to learn what you need to learn to play the endgame without researching online on your own. Its convoluted and CC-centric. Prepare to be stunned for the whole fight with no diminishing returns.The great voice-actors can only do so much to smooth down the cruddy translation and shallow stories. Its unremarkable in every way, aside from looking and sounding pretty. The movement and combat systems are anything but fluid, its jerky and cancels your abilities often.tl;dr: its okay until max level then uninstall.

_childDocuments_.review: Its meh. The main story line is a typical MMO type 'go to this npc to talk about total rot', then that useless mind numbing npc sends you to talk to his brother npc, who is just as boring, to 'talk about nothing', and you get some bread crumb reward... And it is generally rinse and repeat. Yawn. Look, i've got over 100 hours down, and its been okish. However ive now got to end game purple gear and the grind is INSANE!! They have made it achievable IF you want to grind for gear with one of the worst RNG formulas ive ever seen. This draws you to the store, which is why the whole game has been designed the way it has, for you to open your wallet as the grind has you pulling your hair out and making you feel like you want to jump off a bridge, just to stop the pain. Im FTP and will never put a $$ into a game like this that has obviously put up a MASSIVE PTW wall to take away the pain. So lets say you did open your wallet and threw $1000 at it, and i reckon even that amount wouldn't get you the exact gear you wanted with desired traits, what then? Great you have some of the best gear, your character is OP, however what do you do then? Go grind more dungeons for gear you no longer really need? Don't be stupid, these games are about the journey, not the end. You get the end and then what? More boring, tedious and repetitive game play? How boring. If you have the $$ then go for it. If you don't be prepared for a MASSIVE mind numbing grind that could bore an arse hole into a wooden rocking horse. I'm at end game and im just not going to grind for 100's of hours to get possible gear and trait drops, ive got much better things to do and play. Way to money hungry devs im afraid. AND the movement is appalling. The amount of times ive been running along and have gone to simply jump off the edge of a hill, wall, you name it, and it pulls me back. Then it freezes you in mid air, then your 10 metres away from where you were to start, or you fallen to your death. The rubber banding is enough for an uninstall, worst ive ever seen. And the jumping and climbing, wow!! IT IS SO BAD AND CLUNKY! Enough to want to make you want to smash your monitor, yet again, some of the worst jump mechanics ive ever seen. _childDocuments_.review: This game got me back into runescape. lvl 1-50 is a very short, boring journey with uninteresting characters aside from a bard you run into later in the story. The game focuses more on late game pvpve, and while the world bosses are fun, movement and combat both feel extremely clunky. The p2w is pretty bad, shoving a battlepass and leveling pass down players throats which is nearly required to be competitive in end game pvp. I also dislike the auction house system which allows players to buy items using a currency that is a MTX, but also allows players to sell earnable in-game rewards for the same currency. I feel like being able to swipe your card and have an advantage takes the rewarding feeling of getting better gear away from everyone. It creates an environment where players who buy their gear are only satisfied by winning in pvp, and players who grind it out feel like they wasted hours of grinding a boss that they could've just skipped if they had a few extra bucks to spend just to be competitive.Another Odd system they have in place limits the amount of dungeons you can do per-day. I don't find myself being affected by it all that much as someone who doesn't run dungeons a lot, however a LARGE part of getting better gear is through dungeon rewards. Having a limit on how much content a player is allowed to experience in a day is insulting. servers shutting down for 7+ hours unannounced multiple times a week is insulting. telling me to pay my way through pvp is insulting. giving me a half baked combat system is insulting. this game is waste of time. Im gonna go play osrs

_childDocuments_.review: Pay to win - YesPay to win currency is something you can grind in game to buy the same advantages as any P2W player. I will not sit here and tell you that you can keep up with them unless you have insane RNG luck. That said, after 300 hours I have not felt a huge gap in power outside of for a few days maybe. If you strategically grind your endgame content it is possible to achieve plenty of power with out paying anything. The game gives you incentive to keep grinding even at power cap to prepare for future patches because of the system of Lucent/pay to win. You can save up lucent for future patches to further avoid the want to pay to win and be prepared to trait or even purchase future gear using nothing but currency earned by the same thing on in the in game auction house. Overall, this game runs fairly smooth. The scale of players at events and PVP has not slowed down since early access and I still find myself logging into TnL everyday a month later. This game puts emphasis on guilds in a way that ads a lot of competitive nature and character to this games make up. This game does not over saturate you with daily quests, but does have a lot of repeatable daily content to grind at level cap but gives you lots of option on how you want to grind/where you want to grind. As a veteran MMO player have been surprised by TnL and look forward to seeing what the future chapters of this game hold.

_childDocuments_.review: Completely disappointed with this game. I wanted to try it out because I heard it was going to be called Lineage 3 and then changed the name, which now I'm happy to hear since this is an insult to Lineage 2.You don't level up your character through farming and killing mobs, they give close to 0 experience and adena. The game is designed for you to get max level by just completing the main story line and a few secondary quests.All the quest dialogues are bugged and will repeat twice and even thrice. The NPC throws 2 sentences, you click next and it gives you the exact 2 sentences again so you have to click next over and over, and this happens constantly.The combat system is horrible and frustrating. Targetting a mob will instantly attack it, so you cannot have it selected just to get its info if you're inside attack range or you will attack it, you either have to get far or target it and instantly cancel attack with [x].When you target a mob and use a skill or the attack command, your character won't run to that mob if you're out of range for your attack or skill like in Lineage 2, the game will simply spam a "out of range" message on screen.It is impossible to select a mob when there is literally 1 player in front of the mob, no matter where you click (the mob itself, the name) if there's a player in front of it you won't be able to select it unless it's a tall mob.This game has skills that you have to activate twice, the first one give you an arrow so that you can aim it, and the second use will activate it (just like League of Legends without quick cast). These skills won't get activated most of the time if you click them with mouse instead of with numerical keys, I have to constantly spam them 3 to 5 times for my character to use that skill.Movement in the game is horrible and frustrating. You cannot jump and advance a little, for you to move while jumping you have to press a directional key or be in movement while pressing [space] which translates into jumping at maximum horizontal velocity. This is a problem for precise jumps where you don't want to go too far and miss the landing.Moving your character with mouse is possible until it isn't. On open space it works, but as soon as there is something behind your camera position (like inside a small cave, a house, a tent, etc) the game will think you're clicking that surface that's behind your camera. Even Lineage 2 didn't have this issue, a 20 years old game.Hooks won't work many times even if you're looking at it and you're in range, because if you have something else targetted, the game will think you want to talk to that target instead of using the hook. The funny thing is that, you can have something targetted and will not be displayed on screen (Like a mining or gathering point you already used and disappears).Crafting in this game is between non existent and a joke. There's 1 single material for each gear category, and everything requires the same amount of material. The joke part is that, if you are looking to craft X weapon because you want that weapon, first you need that weapon as ingredient. Isn't it wonderful?And then you search info on how to do it and realise that crafting C-grade has been disabled in the global release.No variety in gear, it's the same 6 or 7 stats all over again and again with no set bonus until B-grade which is the highest grade in the game. There are 2 set bonuses for tanks, and both have the same set bonuses.No variety in skills, it's the same 6 to 12 skills for every class, you will be seeing the same visual effects and animations constantly.Chat system is horrible and frustrating. You can't change from global chat to party or clan chat with a single click, you have to open chat, click a drop down menu, select the chat you want and then you're in that chat.The game gives the ability to morph into 3 animals for movement, this is just bad game mechanic in my opinion. If you want to run faster you get a mount or buff your self with a sprint ability if your class has one, that's how MMOs use to work. The animal for swimming is just there so that devs don't have to animate a human swimming. Also, there's no diving in the game, unlike Lineage 2 which had diving as a good part of their game.There are no races in the game, this is most likely DEI doing their typical discriminative work. No dwarves, no elves, no dark elves, no orcs, etc. no variety.Character design system is limited at best, this is again DEI doing their discriminative work. First we have the "Type A and Type B" bodies where the silhouettes are of a male and a female bodies. Then you start tweaking the face, upper body, lower body and see a lot of sliders you can play with, but at the end you realise there are no bust or buttocks sliders, because men or women with larger or smaller chest don't exist.PvP has no PvP system. There is no flagging and there is no PK system, you can camp and kill low level characters over and over to get some PvP coins and there won't be a issue.The hand-holding in this game is ridiculous, it treats the players as if they were ********. You can skip every single quest dialogue and every single cut scene and you will complete every quest because the game tells you where's everything you need for the quest. It won't encourage the player to read, investigate or explore.The game calls their translation as "localisation", another DEI thing, and is full of mistakes, misspellings and random symbols because they were more worried adding their agenda rather than having misspellings everywhere.Clipping bugs were you're stuck and can't move are normal in the game. You can get out of most of them by morphing, but that's not a fix.Mob path tracing is sometimes really bad, they take the longest patch to reach you.Mob spells hit you even if you're outside the visual area in the ground, and bosses attacks that are an area in the ground will hit you if you're flying.Boss damage is not consistent, I faced the same Boss with lower level and gear, and higher level and gear and took more damage in the later situation.There is no trading and the market system is almost pointless because you cannot sell your gear there. You need to have a "great success" on your gear to be able to sell it, and if you upgrade that gear (Adding best abilities,enchanting it, etc) it will lose his "great success" status and you won't be able to sell it.Also, no C-grade gear in the market since you cannot craft them.NPCs are just fillers, there's a bunch of named NPCs for the main quest line and a couple of secondary quests, and everything else is "child", "resident", "merchant", and so on. 0 work done for inmersiveness.Buff system is a mess, buffs and debuffs are mixed in the same row.Parties have no loot system.The game will only let you create a maximum of 2 characters, this is worse than some Gameboy advance or Playstation 1 games.The "no loading screens" is a lie. You will feel the world loading when your PC freezes, so that frozen frame is your new loading screen in this game.In summary, this game is worse than Lineage 2, a 20 years old game, in every single aspect of the game. Character creation, leveling system, raid boss system, gear, gear enchanting system, trading, economy, chat system, movement and actions, responsiveness, bugs, fishing, killing mob trains, crafting system, class and subclass system, quest system, NPCs, party system and other multiple things that I don't remember right now.A disappointment/10, they just needed to make a new Lineage 2 and people would go crazy since MMO fans are desperate for a good MMO, but they had to involve DEI and make a yet another generic cash grabbing, 0 effort MMO.And by the way, when you pay real money for in-game coins called Lucent, and use those coins in the market, the market has 20% or higher in-game tax, so the game is literally stealing real money from players that pay real money for in-game coins.

_childDocuments_.review: ProsGorgeous VisualsThe game features a beautifully designed world filled with fantastical landscapes and creatures. The stunning environments is easily one of the highlights​Flexible Combat SystemPlayers can switch between two weapons mid-combat, allowing for more dynamic playstyles. This flexibility provides a sense of freedom compared to the more rigid class systems in other MMOsEngaging Boss FightsA lot of the boss fights are very focus intensive when it comes to unique skills or patterns that you will have to learn in order to successfully complete raids/dungeons. Paying attention to what the boss might say or how they move will determine is you complete it.Progression VarietyI appreciate the variety of progression systems, including skill books, stat boosts, and crafting. This allows for multiple ways to improve characters, keeping the game interesting for those who enjoy customization​Exploration and Morphing AbilitiesThe ability to transform into animals for faster travel and vertical exploration adds a unique layer to traversing the world, making exploration more funConsRepetitive CombatWhile some elements of combat are dynamic, many players might find the overall experience repetitive, especially with basic enemies. Auto-attacks and cooldown-based abilities can feel passive (however this is quite typical in most mmos)Grind-Heavy ProgressionMany players feel that progression becomes grindy after a while. This can slow down gameplay and frustrate those who prefer faster progression​(again, very typical for any mmo)Technical IssuesEarly technical problems, like server instability and balancing issues, have impacted the player experience. Although patches have improved some aspects, these problems still persist for some​ (considering its still very early into its life span, i'm sure these issues will be fixed over some time)Repetitive QuestsAnother common issue with any mmo that this game shares with others is repetitive quests, killing the same mobs or running the same dungeons can get kinda mind numbing.All in all this game is easily an 8/10 for me. _childDocuments_.review: I have played the game quite alot in the Beta, so dont mind my playtime.The game is a really great MMORPG. It doesnt "reinvent" the formula or anything, but what is there, is really solid & sometimes suprises.My personal positive points:- Probably the most fleshed out Tripple-A MMORPG we've had in years- Detailed World, Main Quest, Side quests, Animations & Sound design- Most of the game is voice acted, even the sometimes smaller side stories- Very fun world traversal because of the Morph-system and Grappling-hook- The combat is much better than it was before, and actually feels very solid now- Collectibes (And optional side stories) scattered across the world - Visual progression is great, and you dont need to pay for good looking armor sets!- The cutscenes and story sometimes surprise and actually hold some weight- Group content is very fun- Open world PVP is also very fun- Enough PVE content to keep PVE-only players busy for quite a while, although the focus is on PVP- Good (clean) UI and Great UI customization- Breathtaking graphics (probably the best in any MMORPG so far)- Great Performance even in larger scale battles- for a F2P game, the monetization is not the worst I've seen.My personal negative points:- The early access packs are not worh it, and (for me) seem bad value- The game does have P2W, although is not as bad as many make it out to be- It doesnt do many "new" things, it just refines old formulas.- Its a korean MMORPG, and its clearly visible when playing the game (for some that is a big negative aspect)- The translations are sometimes a bit wonky and don't always match the subtitlesThis is just my view on it as a casual MMORPG player.(review to be updated later)

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most directly p2w-MMOs ever to be released. Being powerful early on grants you acccess to more and more systems to exponentially extend your lead (especially considering the time-gated gearing systems, which you can only avoid by directly buying ingame currency for money and using the auction house - it will cost you hundreds of euros to be competitive and this will get much worse once arch-bosses are released). PVP impacts all aspects of the game and is obviously dominated by whale-alliances who can literally lock entire servers out of content.The next issue is the netcode/servers. Since launch, there have been ongoing frequent desyncs (teleporting players, positional rollbacks, party-members either not being displayed on the minimap or in the wrong location, skill charge lags, etc.), and the party-system keeps breaking ever so often (which can be great fun mid-dungeon or in pvp arena combat).That said, while the game hiding beneath this hilarious type of monetisation is pretty fun compared to your typical f2p mmo, there is very little actually engaging pve content, and pvp is not exactly well balanced to say the least (even ignoring the p2w aspects).Fun for a few weeks, but it won't take too long for a huge part of the playerbase to vanish.

_childDocuments_.review: First off I want to start with one fact, this game is not as P2W as many claim it to be, especially because often times there are simply NO items to buy on the AH, most guilds prefer to auction them internally in the guild. By the time people start whacking them on the public AH, it won't matter if you get it, people who are much better players than you already have the better items anyway.Yes you can buy items to get your traits faster, but let's be honest, if you suck you will suck even with traits. Great players know how to earn their lucent and don't mind swiping a bit for some faster trait progression. But WoW is similar, or even worse, you can pay to get raid/PVP carried with gold which you get via token, soo.... it's worse :DAnother thing is that even if you have T2 weapons and BiS items with traits etc. it still does not make you a god, not even close. The classes and specializations work in a Rock Paper Scissors way, so there's always a build that will wreck you, especially if they are a better player mechanically and know their rotation better. Battle pass and Leveling pass items you get from it are laughable to be honest, it doesn't really boost you by much...Some classes are definitely better than others (GS/dagger, probably the overall winner for most people) and there are some dubious choices which are simply not good enough. Hopefully in the future the dev team will introduce more benefits for various choices which will make them more viable.Leveling and story is pretty decent, the early progression feels nice. Leveling also gives you enough materials to upgrade most of your gear to at least L9 blue, same with skills, they are easy to get to at least blue, and most crucial ones to at least L1 of purple.The graphics are very nice, maybe not the best ever, but very good in my opinion. Same goes for sound.The content is quite nice and while there is a lot of content for large scale PVP, there is also content for loners, where you can always just go and do some dungeons via dungeon finder, or just go kill some stragglers in a PVP event (usually not the boss fights, but the collect X events). Overall material farming feels nice, but I would like a bit more variety on what you can do to get materials. Guild chest IMO needs a boost :)The problem for many people is the combat, and while it's much better than what it was when beta came out, it's still not perfect. But I have faith the combat will only get better with new additions and polish. I have experienced some issues with a couple of skills where sometimes they keep channeling but nothing happens (no stun, sleep, silence etc.) and sometimes it works like a charm, maybe just a lag issue. Also I really like the block feature which is not just a block (Q) but there are different versions which give you some bonuses after you block.Once the game launches as F2P, it's definitely worth checking it out. Hopefully Amazon can fix the servers, improve the netcode as it's painful to play from Australia on US... so every little bit of optimization helps. Or maybe just open OCE servers? :P

Largescale is like every other large scale mmo about shotcalling, numbers on members and some coordination. If youre seeking for class complexity this is the wrong game for you.-Graphics: very good to be fair-Community: depends, my server was partially extremely toxic enviroment between top guilds and between top guilds and the rest of the server. I personally dont have a problem with toxicity and was bm'ing aswell sometimes but if you're sensitive it may be not for you. so yes I was part of the problem but its an asian pvp mmo so its nothing new.-Daily loop: absolute cancer in my eyes and I am sorry for these words but I cant find any other for that. If you played lost ark its basically the same. everything is timegated but on top of that you are forced to do the daily stuff otherwise you will be capped on ressources after a few days. Not for me. Another comparison if you played BDO: its like agris fever which will fill up daily up to a maximum but in TnL you dont have 1 system like that, no you have 2 of them plus one ressource that stacks up when you use one of the other ones. Wasnt for me, i stopped doing daily ♥♥♥♥ after getting my build ready. this plus the other activities that will come across for you when youre joining a competitive pvp guild (conflict bosses, pvp events, rift/boonstone wars) it just felt like a 2nd job and if you really want to min max everything and getting to a high rank in the ranking system you basically have to be unemployed)-Monetization: In short: LOL. Full: I dont recommend swiping at all, their prices are predatory for the amount of worth you get out of it. thats why they immediately banned RMT with draconic punishment (they basically took away the lucent you bought illegally and force you to buy the amount youre in negative to use the auction house again). Which is fine but they should ask themselves why ppl instantly started RMT that much, because its completly not reasonable. Its like buying currency on a mobile game, it just feels off and you feel robbed. I didnt RMT personally but still have the opinion that they shouldnt be surprised that this would happen.-Misc: There are techniques and hidden knowledge for the systems in the game that are recommended to know in my opinion. When EA started it forced many players (me included) to restart on a fresh character because it just wasnt worth to continue on the first one. So I strongly recommend to do your research because the game is very punishing when doing mistakes.My conclusion is that it was somewhat fun for nearly 300 hours now but uninstalling was followed by a big relief. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If you live in Australia don't even bother with this game.Pros:Fun, engaging game play.amazing guild vs guild combat.large open world dungeons and instead of daily's there is a cool contract system with weekly harder contracts for group-based game play rewarding you with a chance of higher tier gear.the game has enormous potential,it also doesn't punish you with death tax or removal of xp on death, nor do you drop gear on death or have to repair.The developers have done a lot to remove the menial frustrations of standard MMO's which work well for it...However, in doing so they have created so many other frustrating problems which seem to be at an engineering level and are made worse with latency.... So bad that if you live in Australia.... don't even bother playing.Cons:If you Live in Australia... save yourself a potential brain bleed and give this one a miss...A lot of the game mechanics revolving around jumping or dodging or blocking will frustrate the life out of you to the point you will break some devices on your desk... PvP would be incredibly fun... if you dint have 240ms latency...Click targeting is poor and problematic... this wouldn't seem like a big problem.... until you enter large scale combat... so you resort to tab targeting... the only problem is the tab targeting seems to have a range... and it’s not that far... so usually healers in a pvp environment are too far out to tab target.RNG in this game seems to be very unfavourable... in almost a month of playing from early access i have had 3 usable purples drop for me.... the rest has been for completely different class where i have had to butcher the items to sell on the AH to purchase the gear my build needs...Numerous bugs... so much I can’t mention but one of the worst which impedes game play is the charging bug... you will have some abilities which require charging.... sometimes these get stuck at full charge but won’t let you to actually cast the ability...Mobility abilities are Janky AF.... you might want to dash off a ledge to get away from a pvp encounter or to get into one.... NOPE!! you will get stuck on the ledge but then rubber band off it and fall to your death.or your rush/dash abilities will get stuck on environmental objects like small rocks or planks and stop your dash / skill right on the spot. you also cannot dash over ANY small gaps or off any type of ledge.Dash ability issues with cursor aiming and environmental objects... if you are aiming your dash forward but your courser just so happens to be on a tree limb behind your character... your character with dash backwardsThere are so many more I could just keep going....Wrapping up!!!Dev still has a long way to go with numerous mind-numbing bugs.Potentially really fun game but ruined if you don't have sub 100ms internet

_childDocuments_.review: Throne and Liberty struggles with clunky mechanics, unoriginal content, and lackluster design. Its gameplay is filled with uninspired features borrowed from other MMORPGs like Guild Wars and Black Desert, but with low-quality execution. The combat feels slow and repetitive, and character transformations (like morphing into animals to swim or jump) come across as gimmicky. The visuals, marred by static and purple-heavy UI, lack uniqueness, feeling like assets were hastily sourced from Unreal Engine's marketplace. Players note constant crashes, uninspiring storylines, and a grind-focused progression. Despite claims of high player numbers, it feels like a small, bot-ridden community with a lack of genuine engagement.

_childDocuments_.review: This free-to-play game is surprisingly worth sinking 30+ hours into. It’s technically impressive—no matter how many characters or mobs are on screen, there’s no slowdown, crashing, or lag, even at launch.The game leans heavily toward solo play, with most quests taking you into individual instances. While the overall difficulty tends to be on the easier side, there are still some decent challenges (like secret dungeon bosses) if you're looking for something tougher. There’s a lot to explore and master, from upgrades and quest chains to figuring out lithographs and other mechanics, which can keep you occupied just getting the hang of things.The gear system feels a bit simplified—there aren’t as many options for customizing armor and weapons as I'd like. That said, it makes it easy to dive right in without worrying about min-maxing, which is a nice change of pace. Plus, while there are plenty of microtransactions available, none of the essentials are locked behind a paywall. Inventory space, stat resets, and other basics are all free or tied to in-game currency, not real cash.You’ll likely hit max level around the 25-hour mark, but there’s still more to do, especially if you enjoy PvP. I’ll probably stick around for a bit, casually exploring until another game I’m waiting on releases, but for what it is, this is a solid 30-hour diversion.Edited to add: good luck getting a character name though---they're global, and rumored to not release even when a character is deleted. I went through 30+ iterations first (I suppose I'm just not that creative, but I really tried hard not to add numbers to my username).

No classes, you choose some weaps and GO! Awesome but they're also levelled with books as are the related skills attached to said weapons. Fancy changing up your playstyle and using some new weapons? Nope. Enjoy level 1 everything skills and passives. There are a few heavily limited ways to switch (conveniently less limited by the injection of cold, hard cash).Weapon Mastery seemed a fun idea at first too. Use a weapon more and you get extra bonus passives that make you more shiny in combat. Love it! Except they changed it so only weird daily contract things give you weapon xp and it's a whole extra (and heavily limited) grind. Which you can of course, avoid (some of) with the injection of cold, hard cash.We've not even started on the true corporate idiocy yet though. Enter: Limited points to run dungeons, limited contracts for the Weapon Mastery points, Open world dungeons (awesome idea, love it again!) with limited points for rewards after which you're just there and all the mobs forget they have loot tables, 5000 currencies, all of which designed to obfuscate progression to the point you don't even know what any of them do, you just facetank the grind and hope blue is better than green when it comes to some potential maybe upgrade in the future. Also, don't forget to pay for the premium levelling pass on top of the premium battle pass for maximum rewards :DAlsoalso, there's PVP. Not my thing but okay. _childDocuments_.review: Its pretty much on par with Elder Scrolls Online and it feels like what ArcheAge should have been like. It does give you quick explanations of how menus and mechanics work, but it may be worth doing additional research as some of it can be complicated and there are a lot of min/max tips to consider. As a new player, its worth slowing down and completing as much as possible for every given area, as well as collecting equipment pieces for your lithograph (which consumes the equipment for rewards). Also, while there is no inherent class system, the game does have weapon based skills and mastery passives that require you to use skill books and earning exp to level them up. So when you pick a combination of 2 weapons, you should stick with those weapons until that "class" is fully mastered before trying to get into anything else, so that you stay levelled alongside whatever area you are in. At the beginning of the game you'll get a bunch of starter weapons to try out on dummies. I picked Staff and Daggers, which is designated as a "Spellblade" and I do recommend it.I can't speak on endgame P2W yet but it really doesn't seem like this game will be that P2W. As long as you slow down and play at your own pace, it's not bad at all. It's not a race.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried it because I've been on a 10+ year search/wait for an MMO to release that isn't pure unrefined steaming garbage. I have thousands of hours in GW2, GW1, Runescape back in the day, New World and it's early beta, Elder scrolls online, DCUO, SWTOR, the list goes on, if this game is meant for anyone, it is meant for losers like me. That being said, my god I could not maintain interest in the game for long enough to even get passed the tutorial. The combat is just so astoundingly clunky and has no feedback or weight to it. I consciously am aware what my skills and attacks did, because I read them, but it didn't look like I was doing anything, and it felt like I was just pressing buttons and not experiencing combat in a game. The fact that you select the hotbar, even if you switch out a weapon, and you keep the same hotbar skills even when switching between 2 active weapons, is entirely redundant, GW2 did weapon based skills and hotbards much better and understood that you switch weapons, your skills should also change, there you got specific skills for the weapon you had equipped, you switch to your other weapon, now you have a new hotbar and new skills, you get 2 full hotbars of skills with 2 separate hotbars, this game you get one hotbar, all the same skills no matter what weapons you switch to or equip, even if you fully change weapons and no longer even have access to the skills anymore you have to manually change the entire hotbar skills. I could get past the hotbar issues, if the combat felt in any way satisfying, but it just isn't, and while I generally don't care about graphics, especially in MMOs, this game looks like it is trying desperately to be new gen while failing and looking like a 2010s uncanny valley attempt at realistic hair/skin on characters, as well as the environment looks very clearly to be flat textures and assets with no real texture or depth to them. All in all, I didn't play nearly enough to give a full review of the game, but the fact is I love MMOs, and even for crap like New World I invested hundreds of hours into it and level capped, this game I couldn't get past the tutorial...

WASD movement while having to manage 10 skills and a few other utility buttons like dodge and potions is too much. Moving your mouse the slightest will rotate your camera instead of moving.3. Often your trigger will be at the ceiling making your character move in unexpected directions.4. No path finding included.  It is not possible to:1. hide HUD elements. You are only able to move some elements behind the mini map.2. resize separate HUD elements.3. set which HUD element should be in front.4. move HUD elements even party outside of the window. _childDocuments_.review: Invested around 400 hours since release and it starts to feel pretty dull to me. I don't care too much about repetitiveness in MMO's cause they all have that sort of grind to them after all. But there are some mandatory issues with the crafting side of things, how abysmally low droprates are, how slow progess can be as a F2P-Player and that many mechanics are build to create "fear of missing out" so you end up spending money. I had high hopes for this game when it released but the more i see/play the more cracks and flaws shine through. I feel burned out at this Point even tho i was part in a Top 3 Guild on Server destruction.Biggest red flags:- If you are not in a top Guild you basically skip half of the games Content because you get outnumbered or just dont have the Chance to Play for any Guild vs Guild Content. But thats literally what 99 % of this game is About: PvP- Crafting System? What Crafting System? You literally throw the same gear together to unlock traits. Some traits right now cost around 300-400 lucent (ingame currency) for any Epic gear to boost your Tiers. So in order to uprade an Epic item you either need a lot of dropluck or around 3000-6000 lucent depending on the item. Good luck "farming" them. Everything is timegated and rarer loot is only achieved in (open world) Dungeons for which you Need Tokens to enter. Items, once you have touched them, are basically completely useless. You can throw them on other gear to transer the EXP and some Blessing for the traits and that's About it. You won't be able to sell it or get any resources back. A complete moneysink made to vanish the lucents you spent into oblivion.- The game is GIGA-punishing: The game leaves no experimental freedom in so many areas. You essentially set yourself behind in multiple ways if you do not know how it's done the right way.=> You skipped upgrading / full traiting your blue gear and went right with epic gear like any logic human being would do? Too bad, you coulda saved so many Growthstones and other resources so you essentially just set yourself behind for days (if not even weeks) to get these resources again cause you didn't know better. => You wanted to swap your Weapon cause you didn't enjoy your current setup? Aww, lets level that Weapon mastery right from the start again. If you are lucky you still have some of your precious Skill-Swap books. And if not: Just start a new Character cause thats way more efficient than rebuilding your character.I can assure you that MOST of the playerbase did the 2 above mentioned mistakes unless you played in Korea before or you studied this game way before it came out. Games should leave room for improvement and freedom to explore or expiriment with the options and skills. This wiggleroom is not available in TnL and if you don't do stuff the correct way right from the start you are screwed,- PvP: Right now theres exactly one META - stack Melee Evasion when you are ranged DPS and the other side stacks Hit Chance when you are tank / melee. This Right here is the most FRUSTRATING calculation i have ever seen in a game. If you happen to come across someone that has substantially more Evasion Chance than you got Hit Chance you basically miss 75 % of your attacks. That does NOT only include Auto attacks but also EVERY. SINGLE. SKILL. You love a guy being prone on the Ground cause you finally managed to hit them with CC, Pop your Guillotine blade that charged for 2 seconds, you smile cause it's almost fully charged just to realize: MISS - never have i seen a more infuriating hit calculation than in TnL.- Loot Distribution in this game is HORRENDOUS. The game should be played in guilds cause it has a lot of Benefits besides the social part. You can do contracts for Reputation, you can do Guild bosses for loot, you can buy stuff at Guild Merchants that offer some daily resources. The game is not meant to be played as a single Player or purely for PvE. The biggest issue with guilds tho is that NCsoft aswell as Amazon completely shifted the responsibility to distribute loot into the Players Hands. Guild Leaders can decide whether loot you drop goes directly into the guildstash, you can Claim them for 5 minutes after dropping or every Player gets their loot direcly. More serious Guilds that have the slightest of ambitions tho will distribute items to Players that can make use of the item most of the time. You basically share loot with thousands of Players cause there is no "own" loot besides the dungeonchests you can Claim three times a day.- Pay2Win / Pay2Progress: Essentially the same Thing but People will say that you COULD POTENTIALLY achieve something a swiper does so its "not that bad" Right? But where do you draw the line if Pay2Progress = Pay2Win or not? Someone straight up outgearing you at a certain Point cause he Paid Money and you refused to is still Pay2Win. If you have 2 equally skilled Players the one swiping will still win most likely. This won't have the biggest Impact if we talk Large Scale PvP but it does have Impact in Arena or even Guild vs Guild.TL;DRIf you can deal with being behind in Progress constantly without investing money, you just want to Play a Beautiful game casually when you got some spare time or you give a ♥♥♥♥ About Money and swipe: This game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're not an avid fan of MMO RPGs, Throne and Liberty is a title you can comfortably pass by. While its open world and traveling mechanics might initially capture your attention, the game falls short in almost every other aspect, resulting in a deeply unsatisfying experience.To begin with, traveling through the world of Throne and Liberty feels surprisingly pleasant. The seamless transitions between different terrains and the fluid movement mechanics provide a brief respite from the otherwise lackluster gameplay. However, the travel experience is marred by a few bugs—though these glitches are far from the game’s biggest issue. If the only thing you plan to do in Throne and Liberty is move from place to place, you may find some solace in the exploration. Unfortunately, that’s where the enjoyment ends.One of the most glaring issues is the combat system. From the very start, you’re inundated with a large array of abilities, many of which are unlocked within the first hour of gameplay. Instead of offering a gradual, satisfying progression, the game overwhelms the player with an excessive amount of skills. Combat devolves into little more than random button-mashing, where memorizing your abilities is secondary to simply spamming the keyboard. This chaotic system strips the game of any sense of accomplishment or tactical depth, leaving combat feeling shallow and unengaging.Another major flaw is the game's UI. While it’s common for some MMORPGs—especially those from Asia—to feature dense, information-heavy interfaces, Throne and Liberty takes this to an extreme. The interface is cluttered with an overwhelming number of buttons and dialog options, making the navigation of menus and interactions with NPCs feel unnecessarily complicated. For a game that’s supposed to immerse the player in its world, this bloated UI serves only to frustrate and disconnect.Perhaps the most crucial disappointment, especially for long-time MMO players like myself, is the complete lack of support for MMO mice. Many players, myself included, rely on specialized hardware for seamless gameplay in these types of games. However, Throne and Liberty does not support these inputs, rendering my MMO mouse utterly useless. The game also lacks proper integration for foreign keyboards, particularly those using characters slavic keyboard etc.. These oversights are inexcusable for a game released in a global market.Interaction with the world is another area where the game falters. Whether you’re attempting to position yourself for combat or interact with the environment, the mechanics feel imprecise and clunky. You may find yourself standing directly next to an enemy, yet your character refuses to attack unless you’re positioned perfectly inside the hitbox. Interacting with objects often feels similarly flawed; the game prompts you to press the 'F' key, but it frequently fails to register, leaving you to fumble around trying to reload the interaction prompt. These moments of frustration occur far too often and detract from the overall immersion.For those deeply embedded in the MMO RPG genre, Throne and Liberty may be worth a try, if only because it's free-to-play, features attractive graphics, and offers a somewhat enjoyable travel experience. However, these fleeting positives are overshadowed by clunky combat, an overly complicated UI, and glaring technical limitations. If you're not a die-hard MMO RPG fan, do yourself a favor and give this game a wide berth.
