_childDocuments_.review: Throne and Liberty isn’t a bad game per se, but Amazon Game Studios has once again demonstrated their incompetence in managing an MMO, as they have with every other title they’ve published.The game is definitely p2w, but it's a pretty managable and non predatory aspect and it's possible to be on par with whales just by playing. The real issue is that the game is plagued by guilds, mostly Russian, that abuse scripts and exploits without facing any consequences. The Siege event, the most important in the game, further highlighted this issue, turning into a complete clown fiesta where the winner was whoever could exploit the most. Amazon not only wont punish the offenders but even promoted the exploit on Twitter, stating it wouldn’t be fixed in time and advising players to simply ‘be on the lookout and defend against it.’Throne and Liberty has its qualities and is a decent MMO, but its severe flaws and poor management make it hard to consider it a truly enjoyable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Tldr: Good if you're a whale and like to join a circle jerk group of whales. Bad if you're a pleb.Good as an mmo to play for maybe a couple of months. If you care about progression at a fast pace, you would need to spend. Min maxing a gear at end game is very costly.Good luck offering to lady luck to even get the gear you wanted, much less the traits...The way the guild system works is very bad because the whales make their own guild and basically gate keep every other guilds from progressing.Biggest example is how the nodes work. Only sweaty guilds with P2W players at their bulk can capture those. Once they have them, they get resources BY THE HOUR!!A regular guild can only get resources from their guild members by donation. That is if the members even remember to donate such resources.I was once in the top 2 guild of my server and the amount of stocked resources is just disgusting as they are getting them per hour on top of guild member donations.Lets not forget alliances. The top 1-3 guilds are all allied. Meaning every conflict zone boss events are held by them. I would know, I was in the top 2 guild.Every time I join such events, I only see a sea of green (alliance) on my screen. You rarely see anyone competing with them.Last but not the least, the drops from bosses cannot be sold on the auction house (which uses real money btw). You would need to "extract" the trait which uses trait extraction stone. Something that is very hard to come by.Only drops from guild raids can be sold outright.The bad thing about this is the guild reserves the right to withhold the item even though it was dropped to you so you better be chummy with the guild execs or you will never see any items given to you.Overall a good mmo, ruined by bad guild and auction house system.I can get by the RNG drops, since that is an mmo thing since forever, but the way it is built around guilds and players who pay for it just aint it...At this point, it basically mirrors real life where rich people have all the resources while us plebs go after the scraps.I play games for the fantasy. This aint it. So while I was an active member of a top guild, I decided to quit before I'm told to spend more money in this social experiment of a game....

_childDocuments_.review: If you don't wish to read a thorough analysis: Pointless, a waste of time and a money grabber masked as a game.If you have time to read a thorough analysis:I have been playing mmorpgs for more than 15 years at this point. I have tried almost every mmorpg out there. Throne and Liberty is nothing more than a money grabber that tried to follow a mmorpg formula. Unfortunately it fails miserably on every single level. It's a game without soul, without an essence. By february next year, probably will plummet to 10k players.The pros:- Visually good game.- Decent optimization when not in mass pvp, with minimal loading times.- Good soundtrack.The bad:- Classless system- 2 weapons to swap. What is this?- PVE and PVP builds. Why? Just to make more money.- Only human race- Auction House with real money currency- Not a social game. You will do dungeons with people and never see them again in your life since its a cross server and cross platform game.- You will not make friends.- No 1v1 arena- No damage log- Broken classes- Community is awful. You either have dead guilds or toxic sweaty antisocial people. Nothing in between. The awful:- PVP is utterly garbage and pointless. Its a fake system with special zones that you can pvp during night, and if you die you cannot get back in. Mass PVP is a zerg fest with 10 fps. No open world pvp, no karma system, no flagging system, no PK system. - Game has become a chore and takes more time than my real life daily chores.- So many activities to do daily, and if you dont you just fall behind.- Huge amount of currencies like a typical money grabber mobile game.- No trading. If you want to start a new char forget it. Unless you no life it, you cant give it your own gear.- It's not a solo game, you need a guild to progress since the best gear is behind raid bosses that you do with your guild.- Guild leaders have too much power. They can scam gear worth thousands of dollars and just leave the server.- Loot system is horrendous.- Gear system is so bad. If you no life it's relatively easy to get full build. Anything other than that you will be less than mediocre.- Each gear has 3 traits. You will need thousands of dollars to get full build traits.- Game moves extremely fast. I almost no lifed since release and on march my gear will become obsolete since T2 will be released. F*** THAT! Who releases completely new set of gear in less than 6 months??- They will keep adding new equipment types so they can milk more money.- 3500 gear score today with on the high end. After 3 months it will become the norm. This pacing is not normal.- Gear score is useless, i have seen 3500 GS people that do no damage.It's a fake mmorpg that has only 1 purpose, to extract as much money from the hamsters in the wheel. No sense of community, no sense of achievement and a game that is moving so fast because even the devs know that this time next year they will have less than 1/5 of todays population running around.300 hours could have been better spent. Never touching an AGS game every again. 3rd strike was the last.

_childDocuments_.review: DO NOT LOOK AT NEGATIVE REVIEWS. A lot of these reviews are coming from people who cant run it for some reason or from people in the EU angry they bought early access. So this game grew on me quite a bit. I had played the korean version on launch and I can honestly say they have made VAST improvements. So much so that the game actually feels genuinely good to play. If you are in the US and wondering if you should try this game I definitely recommend. Servers in EU i guess have been not so great but I have had no terrible glaring issues other than the occasional crash ( mostly from me overclocking and trying to find stability). When it comes to the overall amount of stuff to do I think that it was well worth the money I paid (30$) and at launch at that. There are some systems that need some love such as the life skills and such but its not that they arent fun or engaging its just there needs to be more to them I think specifically cooking is a bit lifeless as you just buy ingredients from npcs and right now apparently some mobs are not dropping ingredients they are supposed to. I found fishing the most fun so far as a life skill. YOU CAN SEE THE FISH COME TO YOUR LINE. The progression system is quite nice with all your old gear feeding into the next tier of gear up so on and so forth and it is quite constant like im upgrading constantly at least during leveling. I would say the game does not start until end game but I currently have taken my time and am only at level 30 and have had a very enjoyable time. Skills are nice and generally depending on what weapons you use depends your playstyle and role. I play a paladin like character who is tanky and also heals. There are a lot of builds out there but I have found myself actually kind of going with the flow and doing my own thing. Its interesting and new and the devs are fully behind the game. There was a issue on launch with a side quest and by the next morning it was fixed already. Even though there have been disconnects sometimes I have played quite constant they even sent out a big chunk of currency for players as a thank you and a sorry. Compared to other launches at least US wise this game has had an amazing launch.

_childDocuments_.review: I keep trying it because it looks stunning. Truly stunning. The game slaps you with amazing visuals right off the bat and beautiful looking models. The world seems vibrant and lively!But....I just keep getting bored. The story does not make me want to keep going and I read through + watched quests, cutscenes and more when I played WoW and currently FFXIV. It's painfully generic and the dialogue is uninspired typical predictable stuff. It tries to make up for its dry writing with some fancy dynamic camera moves and character animation but it all just ends up being really corny and overdone in contrast to what it's all paired with. The combat is nothing to gag over. The skills you have at your fingertips are based on your primary and secondary weapon of choice much like ESO which isn't something I dislike, it is very nice to have that flexibility. However the feeling of both tab-target and 'action' playstyles left much to be desired. The tab targeting feels clunky and only serves to hold back its action potential. It feels like they designed it with an action style (like Black Desert) in mind but made the odd decision to give us the classic tab-targeting option. These are both extremely different ways to not only play a game, but how pve/pvp fights are designed around. At the end, you end up with a hybrid that does neither especially well.The unique 'gimmick' Throne and Liberty seems to bring to the table are the morphs you can use, turning you into different creatures to run, fly and swim - but really that's all it is. It's transportation, like getting mounts in any other MMO. It doesn't play a role beyond that and is disappointing considering it is the only arguably original thing it does. Overall, it's free so give it a try. It is absolutely beautiful and the artists really knocked it out of the park. However, don't expect anything beyond a free MMO that feels ultimately like it looked for inspiration from GW2, FFXIV, WoW and ESO while being unfortunately confused as to what it wants to be at the end of it all. I was hopeful, but I think I'm done logging on for the time being.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall the game is enjoyable until you attempt to gear for end game content.  Dungeons can only be ran three times per day with your allotted daily tokens, so getting equipment there is extremely slow.  World bosses spawn in either PVP mode or PVE mode.  PVP mode is just mass zerg fights between the top pay to win guilds on the server.  The PVP mode is the most effective way to get gear though, as your guild has the option to assign the gear to whoever they deem worthy to get it.  PVE mode has a small chance to drop one epic piece of gear, which is currently assigned to the highest DPS roles that participated. This means if your a tank or healer you have zero priority for gear from world bosses. On PVE bosses, they sometimes spawn in conflict zones which get griefed by the pay to win guilds, who activate an ability that forces the zone into a PVP area.  Once this happens they basically gatekeep the instance entrances and only allow their alliance members to enter.  Finally, if you are not wanting to spend a bunch of money on the game you are always going to be at a massive disadvantage to the people that spend thousands maxing out their epic gear.Overall I would not recommend this game to anyone I play with having experienced the massive pay to win aspect of the end game.

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed the game, but the uncertainty of whether most players are going to drop it and it becomes another whale x sweaty hogged game is still around and after doing a few instanced dungeons (the ones required for epic gear), it just seems so likely. Not because they're difficult, but because players just follow some linear guidebook that's absolutely not required for clearing it and have inflexible (and often extreme) raid requirements.I went in with just the gear i got from the story (blue + 1 purple armour, 1 blue/green weapon each) and we cleared it after 2 tries. Most people i encounter are able to get the mechanics after 1 attempt, since there's usually only 2 wipe mechanics for the current dungeons. There is no dps check, only a consistency one. As long as the players "play properly" you're bound to clear the instanced dungeons.The fact that you're not required to play at all for a while, but are still able to keep up speaks for itself though. One of the main ways to attain materials required to convert gear into items (optional min-max trait enhancements and crafting templates) to sell at the auction house for Lucent is available from early on and will stack up for 5 days, allowing you to run through them in one day of a week. Same holds true for for instanced dungeon tokens.The only "disadvantage" from not logging on daily is missing out on your chance to get  your <1% chance of World Boss loot as well as side content such as the Amitoi house and guild donations. Latter makes up a insignificant portion to anything you gain.Imho nothing is particularly gated behind some mile-high mountain, even if you just play how you want. It's very lined up for players to be at somewhat parity and took inspiration from other MMOs i know of like Lotro, BDO, New World, FFXIV and Lost Ark. If i placed it between FFXIV and Lost Ark, i'd say it's closer to FFXIV.That said all of this is how it is until now. Things that seem worrying are the oncoming grindiness of purple gear progression and crafting things like Epic gear Lithographs, which require you to farm 1250 of a world-farmed resource. I don't think i even have that much.Story is... alright, but nothing amazing. Thankfully you only have to do it once, and even then are able to skip through most cutscenes and dialogues.If i had to describe it briefly it would be mostly "well-rounded" or "planned out" with some intentionally built in exceptions, that act as whalebait such as titles and being able to make it rain (every 12 hours). So far the content limit-cap seems slower than the average (non-hardcore) player progression allowing for everyone to reach "the end" eventually. I can't look into the devs minds nor know what's in store for future content, maybe they blew all their effort with what we got so far, maybe it'll continue being great.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write reviews often, but I felt like I need to here. Strap in.Throne and Liberty, in my opinion, is the WoW 2 that people want. Before everyone freaks, hear me out. One of the best things about vanilla WoW is the sense of adventure and doing things together. The sense of needing to be a part of guilds and communities to do things. Not FLYING everywhere so you have to explore and get that sense of others doing the same things you are. Yes, the gliding is there, but I do think it's a nice middle ground where it allows you to get places faster, but also creates nice verticality in the game as well. There are a few other things in the game that remind me of vanilla WoW, some good, some bad. Gathering nodes are fought over instead of everyone being able to gather them individually. I feel like this makes sense in a PvP/conflict type of MMO. We aren't group hugging here outside of our own guild. Also, the story feels more like individual instanced stories as opposed to a full overarching story. There is connections between them, but as of where i've gotten (chapter 5ish), it definitely feels more instanced. This all isn't even considering how GORGEOUS this game is. Some of the best parts of WoW is that there's no loading screens and you can just walk from A to B with no interruptions. It FELT like an open world. THIS IS an open world. Even the teleporting doesn't use loading screens! It's the closest we've ever gotten to the most pure sense of discovery and awe that we had when we first played Vanilla all those years ago. That isn't to say there's flaws with the game. Some of the mechanics and movements can feel a little clunky. There are some slight P2W features, but they are very minimal compared to other games. Most of it revolved around end game progression with traits and MAXIMIZING your character. The benefits you're getting from this though (from my research) are pretty minimal; maybe 3-5% increases. There are currently some bugs, but they're getting patched REGULARLY (This is a whole different conversation I have where people want games to be fixed and free of bugs, but then they also complain when there's maintenance). The problem is that flaws exist in EVERYTHING. Vanilla WoW, no matter how much we loved it, had plenty of flaws; they were just DIFFERENT flaws. Terrible class balance as well as slow and tedious progression to name a few. That doesn't mean you can't enjoy the game for what it is.The biggest problem is our own mindsets. We're so worried about rushing to endgame and maxing everything out that we can't see the thing right in front of us that we've wanted for all these years. All we care about is the gear grind and the top of the top, even though most of us won't even get anywhere near it. We look up guides for gearing, boss fights, etc. We put everything on easy mode even though most of us came from the time period of The Lion King on SNES, progressively harder game modes like in Devil May Cry, and more recently, harder souls type games. Why blow through everything when we're all going to reach the end anyways? I'm enjoying the world for what it is: an expansive, beautiful, and creative experience that recreates those nostalgic feelings we had for Vanilla WoW when we were kids. Take your time fighting those crabs, wasps, goblins, and spiders. Enjoy the sense of adventure while you have it. Don't ruin the chance to enjoy one of the better new MMOs to come out and that will come out for quite a while. Take in the scenery, the models of the enemies, and the skills your casting. Stop blasting through content like you're a streamer doing a sponsored game. Don't let some slight P2W features blind you from the rest of the game. At the end of the day, if I'm enjoying the game, i'll gladly pay for the battlepass and leveling pass and treat it like a subscription to the game. I've paid for subs for WoW and FFXIV, and i'll pay it for this game if I enjoy it enough to keep playing. We'll all reach the finish line eventually, but I for one want to enjoy the journey and not just reach the destination.

_childDocuments_.review: Throne and Liberty is a breathtaking game that truly delivers on visuals. The graphics are gorgeous, and the immersion is enhanced by the sheer number of players online at the same time. It feels like a classic MMO, with solid gameplay and a lot of farming. A huge plus is that it doesn't seem to be Pay-to-Win—only cosmetic items are paid, and you can grind to earn premium currency, which is great.Edit: The game Auction House is pretty much mandatory, to keep up in pvp please insert Credit Card :)However, there's one major issue: the game is clearly optimized for Nvidia cards. Owning a RX 7600, I can say that while it’s not top-tier, it's still modern and comparable to an RTX 4060. Unfortunately, it struggles with Throne and Liberty. Nvidia users have access to DLSS 3 and Frame Generation, which are essential in crowded player zones or during PvP. On the AMD side, there’s only FSR 2.0, and it doesn't work well. If you don’t have a high-end AMD card, you're in for a rough experience.Another thing to note: go for a powerful CPU, ideally an X3D model, because the game is very demanding. And aim for at least 32 GB of RAM, or you’ll face performance issues.In summary, a great game, but non-Nvidia optimization is disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: My oh my, i was honestly not expecting this game at all and didn't think much about it.But other than the shaky start of its launch with the servers actually filling up unexpectedly, after all that ruckus i finally managed to try the game, and what can i say, First of all it is a beautiful game and i love how it looks, the combat is nothing like i've ever played with before and takes getting used to but its very smooth and engaging, unlike mmo games, the story telling is reminiscent of baldurs gate and is very engaging.I didnt expect to be hooked to this game but here i am, i see myself playing this for quite some time and perhaps supporting it. I haven't played that far out yet to fully judge it but i only see good things ahead and can absolutely recommend it.Combat at the beginning is rather easy and allows you to get used to the unique controls or change it to your liking before proceeding to the harder content.They're not overwhelming you with content and instead slowly releasing content so that each individual players get time to progress.I haven't participated in PvP content yet and don't plan to yet that hasn't been a problem because PvP content is optional, i saw reviews of people getting jumped by PvP players and complaining but i believe that that's on them for jumping into an open world conflict area of not paying attention to the warnings and details on their map. These zones are avoidable.At the beginning of the game you get a weapon selection and it might make it seem that you can freely swap classes but this is not correct, upgrading skills takes upgrade materials and weapon mastery progresses painstakingly slow, and its important to specialize in a class or weapon combination.Upgrade materials are provided as you continue with the main quest and sidequest, these however require more effort to find as you finish the main story, for now the story ends at chapter 10 but we have to consider that the whole map isn't yet open from the time i made this review.Micro transactions are i gotta say, cheaper compared to other MMO's i've played so far mainly, BDO, POE, Blessed unleashed, Lost ark, and new world. But its still quite a sum, they are however mainly cosmetic items and a battle-pass. But what game doesn't have a battle-pass these days.It is however a grinding game and your efforts are rewarded properly. Some people tend to farm at the wrong places then complain that drop rates are too low. If you really want to have fun with the game i recommend reaching at-least level 20 and experiencing the first dungeon as it shows how valuable the dodge/guard and weapon specializations are and even trash mobs get their own unique wipe/huge damage mechanic as you progress you harder endgame content.

_childDocuments_.review: --Open 5 measly servers with stupidly low population caps.--Lock all servers because there were too many players you somehow didn't anticipate, YET AGAIN.--Open 100 new servers so that in a few weeks the game is ultra dead and you need to merge 100 servers.--Can't keep servers stable in the first place, so players get disconnected for trying to make a character. oh! and a 60gb download despite a pre-install? ok. EDIT- POST LAUNCH: -the story is almost there. it has really good ideas/concepts but really lame narrative execution. the visuals and soundtrack are wonderful, but the actual writing is a pitfall. There are plenty of moment where the game is telling me things, instead of showing me, as well as genuinely lame as adjectives being used. for instance, for the carmine forests, a place with they describe it as "a place of green turned darker red," which idk it is oddly vexing that these descriptions are so lack luster. or a girl who has gotten abducted, you find  oh yeah, the bad guys left a list called "abduction list," outright. like please, that is so epically lame. lmfao. the game is full of it. There's a whole cutscene dedicated to a guy saying he knew the old wizard that saved you, and then he leaves instead of talking despite the fact that you helped his troops and stuff. no exposition, just guys being mysterious in the most unmysterious way possible. it's so forced and contrived. Generally the dialogue is lame too, and feels same-samey with every character.  the combat is clunky on M+KB also. Probably better played on controller but like..come on? I think the combat is fun, if not a bit dry after awhile. I think the game is beautiful, however, and the world is almost interesting enough for me to get into, but after the tutorial intro, it falls off. also, it feels like it shoved every popular fantasy thing, from every genre, into one game--such as the Witcher 3 style art cutscenes that feel like a ripoff, and some of the creatures being pulled from other franchises and not altered in any interesting way. there are also dialogue bugs, the ability to add friends is broken lmfao, group finding is awful, the character creator seemed less impressive than ff14 in a lot of regards, healers do not get kill credit and also means they do not get drops as often, there are a lot of bots already running around, etc.I just can't recommend it in the state it's in.

_childDocuments_.review: The TL;DR Version:After spending 100 hours in the game, I'm still having a lot of fun with the gameplay and gameplay loop. Timegated content really sucks though and getting refreshes once a day for 3 dungeon runs and 10 contracts feels awful. Basically makes world and guild bossing required for any kind of power spike. If you are looking for a genuine MMO experience this game delivers. If you are looking to casual game don't expect to be max power any time soon.I still recommend because the gameplay is fun and the guild features are cool.Good:1. Even with the battle and leveling pass (which I think are absolutely required to feel powerful), it's far far cheaper than any AAA game on the market.2. The Gameplay loop at all stages of the game is pretty fun.3. The pay to win items in the NA version are locked behind lithographs which will discourage P2W players as each item takes materials to convert the lithograph into the actual item (generally > 12 hours of farming for 1 item or several weeks of daily buys at shops)4. Guild content is great and free5. The game felt really rewarding as I went along.6. Every pay to win item is a lot easier to get as a guild who does raid bosses (like most mmos)Bad:1. Co-op timegated dungeons (900 coins a day when end game dungeons consume 300 coins a run with no way to recharge the coins except waiting a day)2. Limited number of contracts to do a day (10). If you were needlessly doing contracts during the campaign, you weren't really doing it right.3. A lot of time-gating on farming materials for upgrades4. Special ability of #1 guild turns any zone (even peaceful boss coop raids) into pvp and it sucks5. Best items at the auction house are tough to grind for. I got two drops and imprinted them to lithographs and still can't afford most items (ridiculous)6. I never have enough Sollant (think generic gold)7. Leveling alternate skills feels absolutely awful because each skillbook takes 5 parchment and its a random drop you can't get anywhere at a shop.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - I will continue playing, but as is, I can't get into it hardcore like other MMOs. Being free, I would definitely say TRY IT and see if you like it or not. It is decent, just nothing amazing  To get a simple idea, it is like New World game play within Chrono Trigger / GW like world (early view). See you in game! ...maybe? lolDecent game, a bit "dialogue-y (verbose if you rather)" at the beginning where they force you to press "F" in the beginning to continue with the dialogue. Couldn't play long since it kicks me out for "anti-cheat" for no reason. I had some web browsers open in the background, reading manga between fights for fun, guess this easy anti-cheat is sensitive more so then other games? I've done this with almost every game I play online but this is the only one with the issue. When you get kicked you may or may not be able to just log back in (pending what? some type of queue? no idea). This makes it a bit concerning since it can kick you out mid fight, happened to me. Regarding game play, the combat is okay, nothing amazing so far. It feels like a sub-par GW2 design. When you newly equip weapons, it forces you to open skill window and "map" what skills you want on your tray. You can hotbar more then one so this is just annoying in the beginning but long term shouldn't be an issue. Plus, this is because you will gain more skills s you level. Would have been nice if you only have a few skills, in the beginning, it pre-selects the few on to your tray. Graphic/atmosphere is decent, a cross between GW and Black desert. The "mood" reminds me of Chrono Trigger. Music, no idea, I have it off since I have hearing issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Throne and Liberty seemed promising at first, but it's falling short (go figure w/ Amazon + Korean MMO roots). The PVP is dominated by zergs, making it difficult for the average player to enjoy, especially when the game goes free-to-play and more players join (more bots/multiboxer). There's also a lack of engaging endgame content with limited dungeon clears (3 per day), forcing players to either wait for RNG or pay to progress. This pay-to-win mechanic is a huge turn-off, discouraging casual players and creating an unfair playing field for PVP. Would not recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Good looking lag fest with many bugs. Week 1 you would get often Disconnects, especially day -5(pre-buy) to the first few days. Week 3 we started having Party Disbanding often ,  almost always happens when you are near the end of the dungeon(30-40minutes spent if you are with random people). Week 4 bosses don't fight back, many bugs, desync. You fly on the ground and cant move anywhere, you transform (morph) into a bird just to die from fall dmg 1 meter after you transformed. Mass disconnects during boss fights since its a lag fest. The game recommends me HIGH settings , I have everything on low and I see less Frames per second than if i was scrolling through a power point presentation.And lets not forget that we receive half the rewards that Korea receives for Halloween event. I thought BDO was bad during node wars . . . now I am considering going back to the desert. Just skip this MMO.Edit1 (same day): Also it is entirely group based. If you dont have time and want to log in for a few minutes or grind for gear you have nothing to do except some 5minute daily for materials(not gear). When you hit level 50 your day starts to be - Contracts(those fast dailies)-> Co Op dungeons x3 (because you are allowed to do 3 per day but can stack if you missed a few times until 15?) -> Open World Dungeons (group based). AND it is really beneficial to have an active big guild so you have to do Guild events and Guild bosses (all group based). Many of the stuff is TIME gated so you can't log in whenever you like and do those group contents. It is a lot of constriction on you. First you have to pray to the server for stability, then log in in the proper time and then find a group that knows what it is doing. I know I mentioned BDO before, BDO does the opposite mistake - it makes almost everything solo but I think I prefer login in and playing on my terms than be pressured.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics: 8/10Gameplay: 7.5/10Music: 8/10Content: ?/10Stability: 5/10P2W: 0/10Let's start with the most glaring issues:I originally started playing this game because many people online said it was very light on p2w and that "you can only buy the base items for $$" but this is a lie. While yes, you cannot buy upgraded items on the auction house (which exclusively utilizes the cash shop currency), and you have to farm up the materials to upgrade the levels of the item, this is absolutely not the biggest issue as this easily just happens over time. Upgrading every item to level 9 (max level) isn't what will set you apart.Items come with main stats, substats and unlockable traits and this is where it gets dicey.Traits are what make or break your build and your competitive viability. In order to unlock new traits you can either use a special currency which you can't directly purchase with $$ (other than season pass) but you can also extract traits from items and sell them on the auction house.This means that for $$ you can buy the base BiS (best in slot) item and all its traits as well as fully upgrade these traits as soon as you unlock the auction house (level 40).Traits are by far the most important aspect of your character's strength and vastly outshines anything else.Resulting in some of the most overtly p2w I have ever seen in a game. Some of these best in slot items cost up to $500 to fully trait, and due to the mechanic on how content is unlocked over time for everyone on the server, we don't even have the most rare items yet. On korean servers, these base items (without any traits) alone sell for over $1000.Can you attain these without paying? Well... yes kind of.Since everyone can extract traits, you can too. If you run a dungeon (you can only receive 3 item drops per day) you can get lucky and get a good item with a good trait, extract it and sell it on the auction house.For some of the BiS items, you would need to get the most expensive item with the most expensive trait from a dungeon for up to 10 times. Just for the base.Well yes and no. Multiple aspects of the game incentivise PvP to an absurd degree. There are world bosses that spawn as "Conflict" or "Peace" bosses. Conflict are PvP, Peace are PvE.This results in the strongest 3-4 guilds building an alliance and locking down every single Conflict boss.Since field bosses only drop 1-2 items and every other spawn is a "Conflict" spawn, this means that every other item drop is guaranteed to belong to the strongest alliance.This also applies to open world dungeons as these have some of the most valuable field boss drops.In addition to this, open world dungeons become "Conflict" zones at ingame night-time. In addition to even that, the #1 open world kills ranked player receives a skill that forcibly induces ingame night-time.In addition to this, one of the open world dungeons drops chests at night which when opened reward you with another chance to receive loot drops from dungeons, as well as coins that can be exchanged for gear.It took about 3 weeks for the top 4 guilds to entirely kill the server. In those 3 weeks they have managed to get so far ahead of everyone else in terms of gear, that there is no feasible way to ever contest them.Night time belongs to them, conflict bosses belong to them. Even non-conflict bosses in open world dungeons belong to them because they just make it night and kill everyone so they cannot come back.In addition to that there are siege wars in which guilds can claim ownership of certain nodes (similar to black desert online). These guilds then receive a share of the auction house tax (cash shop currency) putting them even further ahead.Since alliances can be up to 4 guilds and the top 4 guilds are likely in an alliance already, the ownership just rotates between these 4 and all 4 fight and defend the ownership against anyone else.Again, the server belongs to them. Your money belongs to them. The auction house belongs to them. You either join them, or you eventually quit the game.This wouldn't be nearly as much of an issue if you could grind your way out of it like in black desert (for example) but every grind is time-gated and you can only do so much per day before you don't get any more rewards.This also wouldn't be nearly as much of an issue if alliances were smaller. Or if you could accidentally attack alliance members. As it is, if you try to compete with the top 4, you are a shrimp trying to fight an onslaught of 80+ fully BiS geared players. It's not open world PvP. It's an execution.Combat itself is fun, rotations are neat but because the game is tab-target and essentially nothing is a skillshot, pvp is just a matter of trying to predictively block incoming stuns until you run out of stamina and considering the current meta where only longbow can detect invisibility and greatsword has 3 separate stuns/roots with a prone (you cannot get ouf prone. think of it as a hard stun against which everything that removes stuns does nothing) and this prone duration is increased everytime a greatsword (and only a greatsword) achieves a heavy attack (similar to crit but not really) you will mostly be stalling for time if a group of greatsword users charge you.PvE would be fun if there was more content, especially challenging content.I'm 255 hours in and there isn't a single boss where I don't skip essentially all mechanics. It's funny the first few times when it happens but it gets old very quick.There is also a TON of jank when it comes to movement as well as server stability issues. I could and would overlook them if the p2w wasn't as blatant.tl;dr:a potentially good game that is entirely destroyed by greed.Just another microtransaction p2w mmorpg. Much more p2w than black desert. Basically as p2w as any competitive gacha mobile game

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer : didn't play F2P and barely touched PvPWhat's good/okay :+ From a visual and performance standpoint, the game is good (except for some specific situations)+ The gameplay feels great, I play it the classic way aka tab-targetting and I like the fact it's the default option, I missed playing MMOs like that+ Servers MOSTLY run smoothly+ Even though gimmicky, I like the transformation system+ Codex has good content for completionists+ Boss fights are okay, their strats are usually pretty simple, difficulty comes from the playerbase unwilling to listen and learn the bosses' mechanicsWhat's not :- Art direction is super generic, there are a few things I like (most armor sets, creatures like Gigantrite, some leveling areas) but otherwise it's really uninspired- In concert with my previous point, the lore and world building is boring as ♥♥♥♥- Only 1 playable race (humans) even though we can see dwarves in-game and it's possible to have characters with pointy ears- No side activities besides fishing (no housing for example)- Crafting is boring and its only purpose is maxxing your gear- During world bosses and public events, since the game is so adamant in showing as much players as possible at the same time, performance can drop DRASTICALLY (I can go from 60 fps to 10 fps)- The drop system on world bosses seems to heavily benefit DPS classes (personal feeling as a tank/healer)- A lot of FOMO based content- Gameplay loop gets boring really fast and PvE content is a bit lacking at the moment, they really need to add side content otherwise all casual players unable to keep up with the PvP whales are going to leave and the game will die- Barely played PvP, but judging by the leaderboard on my server, some classes are clearly way more viable than others (Liberator, Ravager, Scorpion and Crusader)- No transmog, dye system only for paid outfits (which so far, have been more "modern" than the base game armors and not very good looking)- The community is icky (at least the french one)What's utter ♥♥♥♥ :x Auction House works with real money. You can earn said money (Lumens) by selling stuff you might loot or craft (when you craft an item there is a 20% chance it becomes sellable. Yes, you have to get a "Great Success" on your crafted item in order to be able to sell it) in the AH once you get lvl 40. Or you can just swipe your card and get them. From my experience, I spent something between 150-200€ into the game, and managed to make roughly 100€ of Lumens via the Auction House. If you're lucky and like grinding A LOT, you MIGHT be able to stay entirely F2P. Nonetheless, the principle of having an AH working with a currency tied to real money ONLY is a disgrace to MMOs and gaming in generalTL;DR : Throne can be a decent entry point in the MMO genre if you're looking for a visually appealing game that is free, but content, lore and gameplay wise, I think all tab-targetting MMOs already existing do it better, especially the subscription-based ones like FFXIV.

_childDocuments_.review: Part 1:Another game that will live, and die, because of it's PVP-centric approach.PVP has ZERO place in a PVE setting. You want PVP? Go all in 100% all in PVP.Part 2:This game is pay to win. You can buy Lucent to purchase gear on their auction house.Some people may be like "Oh... but...this." or "Oh... but...that." Don't listen to them.This is a PVP-centric game, you're giving your players the ability to use their real life money to purchase the highest tier of gear, or even BiS. This gives them an edge over everyone else who might have to go through the normal slog to grind for gear. Further this allows those same players to outperform and continue to get better gear, not only for themselves, but also for their friends or guildmates. This is unacceptable at any point.Part 3:This game will die because NCSOFT hasn't figured out that you can't use PVE to prop up PVP, especially when there is no incentive in which to do so. Dynamic Events will grow old, Dungeon content will become stale, players will not keep grinding the same thing over and over again, especially if less than 5% of your population has centralized all power, and the only incentive to remain is to PVP against a guild that will by that point have accumulated the most skilled and active players, to remain at the top.You'd think all the years of development on Lineage 1, 2, and Guild Wars 2 would've taught them something by now... _childDocuments_.review: Let's get straight to the point:I'm not a fan of Tab Target based MMO's (I prefer things like ESO, TERA, BDO, etc.), but I did enjoy this games combat. It doesn't do anything new, it just feels and performs very well. The grappling's pretty neat.The graphics and performance are great and should set the standard for MMO's. This is just Unreal Engine 4. The idea of future MMO's using Unreal Engine 5 have me drooling. DLSS 3/Frame Generation in an MMO? That's nice. On that note, I do have a 4080, so others performance may differ.Did I mention there's no loading screens? Correct, there's no loading screens. No loading screens when porting to the literal complete opposite side of the map. No loading screens when porting into an instance. Literally none. That blew my mind.Character customization is pretty good, but the big feature I enjoy that I hope more MMO's do is the ability to upload a photo of yourself and have the game change the characters face to match the person in the photo. There's no transmog system, as the current outfit system wants you to buy the cosmetics from the IRL shop.The blend between sea, land and air mounts (you are the mount, btw) is nice and fluid, and it's awkward going back to other MMO's, jumping off something and not being able to transform into my flying mount, and instead just fall to my death.Upgrading gear is incredibly simplified. Want to upgrade a blue piece of equipment? Have the blue upgrade book. Is it a higher level piece of blue gear? Just have more books. You don't need 10242 different upgrade materials, just the same thing and more of it.The ability to transfer XP from a lower tier piece of equipment to a higher tier piece of equipment is very nice but you'll realize that late game, this feature is pretty much useless and unused. The tiers of equipment are Grey, Green, Blue, Purple. Purple being the best. I pretty much skipped blue tier equipment and went from Green straight to Purple because World Bosses can drop Purple gear and you get Purple gear from dungeons.Crafting is cool at first until you realize it's basically useless late game. Grey items can be bought, green items can be crafted in the traditional way. But Blue and Purple items require a Lithograph piece of that specific gear. How do you get this Lithograph piece to craft the item you want? Simple! You have to obtain that item! But wait, I know what you're asking, that doesn't make any sense! In order for me to craft the piece of equipment I want in order to become stronger, I have to already obtain it from an alternate means, use an item to turn it into a Lithograph, and then craft it again? Correct! In other words, crafting Blue and Purple pieces is absolutely useless. What you want to do is farm Purple pieces in dungeons (you don't even need to obtain any blue gear, you can skip it entirely and use the blue gear the game rewards you with for completing challenges!) and World Bosses and hope RNG gives you the trait you want. If it doesn't, no worries, you can spend IRL money to buy traits from players off the market from the Lithographs they created. You honestly don't even need to craft Purple gear either. Honestly, you don't really need to craft anything because the game naturally provides you with gear as you go through the story and complete different challenges. Then you just grind dungeons, world bosses and raids to get the purple gear and wa-la, all done. Why does this game have crafting again?Oh yeah, food. Food is useful, so that's at least a worth while crafting spec to work on.The auction house uses IRL currency only. Your in game gold will pile up fast as you begin to realize that it's literally useless, as all the useful things in the game all have separate currencies. Gold is pretty much your fast travel currency and daily currency so you can buy a grey quality item real quick to destroy it for your daily battle pass challenge (if you have it). The top half of the map doesn't exist and the story stops very abruptly at Chapter 10. Correct, when you open your map and see how big and great it looks (which looks strikingly similar to Elden Rings map), you'll think, "Wow! Can't wait to explore all that!", and then you realize the entire top portion of the map, which is 50% of the map, isn't playable and your journey ends quickly very abruptly. The game focuses on group content/guilds. You can do a lot by yourself, like clearing the story, doing the dungs for the purple gear, praying RNG drops you good stuff when a World Boss is defeated, etc. But certain content requires guilds and the end game is focused on Guilds. That and PvP. The PvE serves the purpose of feeding into the PvP. But the game is still enjoyable for PvE casuals.Speaking of casuals, this game is filled with casuals. If you've played an MMO where dungeon/raid bosses have numerous/complex mechanics, you'll jump into this and realize that each boss only has about 2 actual mechanics, and are incredibly easy to deal with. This leads me to believe that a majority of the player base are first time MMO players or just casuals because if you do dungeons with them, you will prog for 2hrs straight as they try and grasp their head around the concept of "kite clockwise around boss", or "stack on marked person". If you're inside of a circle and I tell you to move clockwise, you would move your character left. I had someone who kept wiping group tell me clockwise was moving right, not left. Huh?! "Hey, when you have this obvious red orb over your head, make sure to move out of group so the giant AOE it spawns under your feet doesn't eat all of us". -Proceeds to drop it on entire group-Obtaining the gear is very easy because the game wants you to do late game quickly and feed into the system of Lithographs, perfect traiting and IRL money. You don't need to spend IRL money though. You can obtain gear and items people want from farming the content, sell it on the market for the IRL currency, and wa-la, you've now become an entrepreneur without spending a dime. And the whales get to have fun because they don't need to spend time farming at all, they can just get it instantly with cold hard cash.PvP is pretty fun, and the competitive PvP is in the Arena's with things like 3v3's. PvP in open world with zergs is just like how it is with literally any other MMO. The larger group always wins unless they're apes and the smaller group is communicating and hard focusing proper targets. This is assuming all gear level is the same.Overall, the game is pretty descent. There's things to like and things not to like. The crafting and sense of progression from working your way up through the gear quality and levels and such is what killed the game for me, because it's pretty much nonexistent. Top that with the fact that you will lose your brain cells progging something for 2hrs that should be done in 30mins. The game died quickly for me, but that doesn't mean I still can't recommend it to others since it does do some stuff good and was enjoyable while it lasted. The first major update came out the other day and addressed quite a few things, one of them being able to do random queue's instead of only specific queue's, so if the devs continue to update their game with nice QoL stuff like that, I might return. We'll see.Anyways, I'd recommend giving it a try, you'll at least get your moneys worth out of it.Oh wait, it's free.

Felt a little like diablo to me - not a bad thing but just not for me. This is a solid free to play MMO that I'm sure a lot of people will get into. I think you'll see a lot of content come out for it and i genuinely believe there will be a strong international following for the game. If you're reading this review, you should consider the source. I know I often forget that game reviews on steam come from a wide audience of players around the world. It's only natural that these reviews are influenced by popular opinions within that player's respective culture so take my review for what it is - I'm an old 40-something american gamer that generally enjoys light quirky games with little to no story and mindless fps's. TLDR; Throne and Liberty isn't for me, but I know a great game when I see one. This one will be a wild ride for sure with content and updates over time. Ignore the reviews, play it, and see where the devs take this!

_childDocuments_.review: As of right now there is no way to switch servers for free now. Once you create a character on a server you are stuck on that server unless you want to pay $20.00 USD for the Lucent needed to buy a server change ticket from their shop or use your 2/2 character slot to make a new character. They don't allow for direct payment for it which would be around $13.326 USD for 750 Lucent (based on the larger package for $19.99). You have to buy the $19.99 package of x1125 Lucent. Next lowest package is $9.99 for x500 Lucent..  Otherwise you can grind and sell some items on their auction house which gives you Lucent but is a very slow process.No spoilers here.Story is good but extremely short. Story kept me going and wishing there was moreLike most MMO's. you will be visiting the same areas over and over. Fight mechanics are decent. You can switch between classic and Crosshair mode.Downside to this is most of the time you will switch to Classic (cursor) to select items in the world since half of them bug out unless you get on top of them, i.e. npc's, quest items. The classes are what you would expect of any mmo bu they bring in a primary and secondary equip like some other games already out but let you choose all the spells on your main bar from both equipped weapons sets. IMO-downside is that a lot of MMO's are stepping away from your nastolgic classes of being what they are. I.E. Tanks are tanks, healers are healers, DPS is DPS. The developers have decided to go with anyone can do anything just by changing weapons. Personally this is off-putting to me. Consider me nostalgic for older games role(s) PvP can be a lot of fun. For some I could see that it puts them off the game. Known already several just to leave because of PvP. Just so you are aware, PvP is based mainly on open world content. The area(s) switch between peace and conflict on a schedule. So if you are looking for a game to play through but only have a bit of time to play, this game most likely will not be for you.  World Boss drops are needed to progress and more than half the time world bosses are in conflict state for the area.  As of right now there is good lead to those willing to pay. Between the Battle Pass, Premium Leveling Pass and Transformations for Land/Flying/Aquatic mounts with the in-game store (will level speed the more you have). The items given between the two passes will allow you to upgrade and obtain mid-end game gear with just putting in your card info.   Battle pass gives you the ability to improve armor fasterAll end game gear is obtainable for class metas within the world. For most of it you will have to farm world bosses 40x times to get one of the pieces. You can farm and sell on the Auction house (select items) to get store currency "Lucent". For most that will be a bit of a grind as well. That Lucent will allow you to buy anything on the in-game store. (don't say I didn't warn you it is a grind)IMO - These are the worst mechanic(s) in the game. One of the more simplified profession and crafting experience I have played in a while  You have three Professions in total. (The best of the three) point, click and reel in.  (without spoiling the game) Levels as you progress in game.   ( I left this for last due to my annoyance with this one system)So cooking is a click recipe and done. The part that truly gets to me is you can tell this one profession was rushed. One of the main ingredients you need to progress this skill is Salt. Salt has to be Farmed from crabs/lobsters. Even though you are right by the ocean (i.e a bucket and a fire would do just fine) you instead spend hours farming salt which have a very low drop right on the tables.) Guild is a guild. Members, ranks, guild quests. Instanced guild house in one of the cities.Allies/Enemies For more information I would advise the wiki. All in all the game is enjoyable to me through the story. The grind was not worth it to me personally but I decided to give it a fair chance. The game itself is beautiful but something I most likely will not return to unless I see a lot of changes in the community updates.  If the developers come through and add a lot of different professions and mechanics that were a little more realistic then I might change my mind,.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I've now played the game for around 400+ hours so you don't have to and can objectively say that it doesn’t work as an MMORPG and won’t sustain itself in the long term, not surprised it died in Korea. The game is fun for a few hours, but you quickly reach a point where it devolves into pure grind/second job, and the daily, repetitive, limited task rotation feels more like work than enjoyment.But first things first. There is a main story and quests, which are fairly good, sometimes including puzzles, and they provide a good introduction to the game. You also get showered with all sorts of items and resources for crafting and upgrading, giving you a constant sense of progression. This phase of the game is quite enjoyable. However, as soon as you reach level 50 and enter the endgame, the game reveals its true face: monotonous mechanics and a repetitive task rotation, bound to various currencies that constantly limit and restrict you.The open-world dungeons and PvE content differ at best only visually; content-wise, it’s the same mechanics—usually a series of arena fights against bosses. The group dungeons are also extremely small and simple, usually consisting of a few rooms with a final boss whose mechanics are easy to learn. It doesn’t really matter whether you’re fighting an open-world boss, doing a dungeon with a group, completing resistance contracts, or soloing bosses. Everything feels the same, is quickly done, offers little depth, and serves merely to add some visual flair to the gambling aspect, repeated as often as possible to keep dopamine levels high. Nothing has real depth; everything is highly repetitive because it doesn’t matter why or how you kill a boss or complete a mission. The only thing that matters is the anticipation at the end to see if you get the desired item or not. It’s pure gambling mechanics, like at a slot machine—nothing more, nothing less.And of course, you never get what you want. When a world boss is killed by 150 people but only drops 6 items, with 5 of them always being resources and the last one going not only to just 1 in 150 players but also with a 1 in 15 chance of being the wrong item, you can calculate how long you’ll be killing bosses. That the bosses only appear every few hours and all at the SAME time, so you can only do one boss, I’ll just mention briefly in the context of probability and time factors. For comparison, I’ve been playing for a month now, every day, for over 400 hours. I’ve participated in every guild “raid,” done open-world bosses daily, and at least 3 dungeon runs a day, and I’ve never dropped anything relevant to my meta gear. Not a single usable item for me. You also can’t really play freely; you’re constantly restricted by this time system, the currencies, and limitations. If you can’t kill a world boss at exactly 8 PM to take advantage of your 0.0001% drop chance, you’re just out of luck and can try again the next day.Every day, you grind through the same boring stuff and even feel pressured because if you don’t play for a few days, the currencies you need for dungeons only accumulate up to a certain point and then expire. This creates pressure that needs to be dealt with. Guild tasks, raids, and bosses are the exact same as solo tasks or open-world bosses. Nothing really stands out or provides a challenge. You only occasionally fail a group dungeon due to a lack of communication from teammates. Everything is tied to endless grinding: resources for crafting, items for the lithography book, and whenever you manage to gather something, you realize it’s just a fraction of what you need to, I don’t know, craft armor—only to have luck spoil it because the crafted item doesn’t have the trait you need. Sure, you can change that, but that, too, is tied to endless grinding. I can’t fully describe how deviously long-winded and boring this system is. I hate to say it, but you’d have to be an idiot not to see it—or to see it and still keep playing the game because I wonder where the gameplay or fun is supposed to be here if you aren’t addicted to gambling and can’t stop.The game is heavily pay-to-win oriented. PvP fans might want to give it a try, but they should know that without spending real money, progress is minimal. In open PvP, like with conflict bosses, a solo player stands no chance, so joining a guild is almost mandatory. In arena PvP, it’s nearly impossible to get by without real money since gearing up is essential to remain competitive. While you can earn in-game currency (which can also be purchased with real money), it takes forever—and I mean forever—and still isn’t enough to make a significant impact. Don’t even try to play as a healer in the arena.The PvE content feels like pure busywork, grinding PvP gear that you eventually end up buying or upgrading out of frustration because it takes way too long, is the same boring routine, or you just never get anything useful. In the end, everything boils down to repetitive grinding to slowly—very slowly—get stronger. This monotony makes the game unfortunately very boring and frustrating in the long run, especially since it’s the same thing over and over again. The world is small, the dungeons are irrelevant, there are no raids, boss mechanics aren’t really challenging, the PvE content feels like work, and you can tell that the whole game is just about keeping players hooked—to make them addicted and then get their money.Speaking of raids. There are raids, but they look exactly like an open-world boss, except that you can exclusively fight this boss as a guild in an arena. But there’s no lead-up to the fight, no old castle, no ship, no enchanted forest—nothing. You just enter a portal and are immediately in front of the boss. Then you fight for 5 minutes, the gambling factor kicks in, because this time you’ll definitely get something, right? Nope, nothing again; quickly move to the next open-world boss. The same clicks as always, nothing dropped again; off to the open-world dungeon. The same mobs, killed the same way, and after 3 hours, still nothing. And that’s the whole day, until your currencies run out and you’re more inclined to buy what you need because you can’t handle the frustration anymore. I really can’t put into words how vile this game is.Also there is no crafting system and all the material farm is timegated aswell , you need rain in-game to get apple's to craft PvP food which is on an hourly schedule , whoever designed this is a nut case.If you managed to read this far I just want to enforce how pay 2 win this game is one last time and being in a top guild won't help you either because you have to roll against dozens of people and all the builds are mostly shared atleast a few items , I managed to get one talus staff across 400 hours from my guild and that was it , while having top DKP to boot, items just don't drop and when they do it's a bidding war with the clannies and you wait months for 1 item.Save your money and your time and invest it in anything but this game , literally anything but this game , it's a sad time when MMORPG's have moved to a full p2w mechanics and super scarce drops , this game is worst then Lost ark and that's saying A LOT.I just finished my 100% Steam achievements, as there’s not much left to do, and then I’m uninstalling this garbage. Absolutely no recommendation from me, and I’m not saying this out of frustration but from an objective realization that has matured over 400 hours of game time.God bless if you managed to read this far.

_childDocuments_.review: The single player story feels condensed at best.  They introduce characters/storylines that you are supposed to care about, then you kill them off two missions later.  Powerful demon who has been around for centuries?  I killed him off the same mission I learned about him... Other powerful demon?  Only a mission or two more.  The big bad?  A mission or two after I met him.  So I definitely wouldn't recommend the game for the story.Gameplay is fine, except you are limited to two characters, it is a pain to switch weapons if you change your mind, and a bunch of stuff (e.g. the battlepass) is CHARACTER and not account bound.  Once you finish the story it becomes about a ridiculous grind, and you can screw yourself over if you don't know various tricks (e.g. don't immediately transfer your blue weapon into a purple weapon, apparently is better to wait to save growthstones) or make poor choices.The morphing doesn't really add anything, it is just the equivalent of sprint.  The glide morph is incredibly frustrating.  You can only glide and not fly, you go less distance if you can altitude, you will unmorph if you hit a branch or other minor obstacle, and you will randomly nosedive into the ground.  It just feels bad in every respect.PvP is a stunlock zergfest.  I didn't sense any real opportunity for strategy or even real combat.  Maybe is better if you focus solely on PvP with your build, e.g. choosing the correct weapons and the correct skills at creation, but that requires foreknowledge.  If you just try to play the game good luck, it won't be fun.Definitely feels like there are meta 'correct' choices for weapons and skills for various activities.  Want to compete in world events and PvP?  Good luck...Maybe I have been out of MMOs for too long, but the dungeons are just tedious rather than challenging.  Numerous instant kill 'mechanics' that you need to be aware of in advance to create faux challenge.  Doing the same thing every two minutes to avoid instant death is not a fun or challenging boss, it's just annoying especially if you dare play with a PUG.  Various gacha/mobile style time gates.  You can't run as many dungeons as you want, only X number, you can't do as many contracts as you want, just X number, you only get X abyssal coins, you only can by X eggs/honeys, etc.The store is ridiculously overpriced.  And a real money auction house is obnoxious.  I don't know what is more ridiculous, that I sold a world boss drop for the equivalent of $100, or that they 'taxed' the equivalent of $20 of a currency that you have to buy from them.  This might tie into other mechanics, but will only reward the top whale/zerg guilds if it does.  It feels like a game that will quickly become about the whales/sweats (or whatever the term is) dominating everything, and everyone else just being there to provide them with fodder.

_childDocuments_.review: Captivating universe: The game has a rich and well-constructed world that makes you want to immerse yourself in it.Class and combat system: True to NCSoft's tradition, the classes are well-designed, and the combat is dynamic and enjoyable.Graphics and animations: The system of transformation into land, flying, or aquatic creatures is visually appealing, even if it lacks gameplay depth.Interesting dynamic events: The game's dynamic events are entertaining and add a touch of fun to the gameplay. However, it would have been interesting to see more of them and in a more diversified way, similar to Guild Wars 2, where events can occur spontaneously and truly influence the game world without being tied to a timer or a planned activation.Abusive and unshared Battle Pass: The Battle Pass system in this game reaches absurd heights. Not only is it not shared across the account, but it is linked to a single character. In other words, if you have two characters, you will need to pay for the Battle Pass twice to fully enjoy it on both. This is purely scandalous! Such a lack of consideration for players is unacceptable. At a minimum, the Battle Pass should be accessible to all characters on the account, with perhaps specific tiers for a unique character. But asking to pay again for each character borders on the ridiculous; it’s a true disguised scam.Camera and controls optimized for controllers: The gaming experience is much less enjoyable for players using a keyboard and mouse, clearly favoring controller users.Unbalanced loot system: DPS classes are favored to the detriment of healers and tanks, making it more difficult for the latter to obtain quality items.Evolution cost: Upgrading weapons and equipment is extremely expensive, requiring either long hours of gameplay or a significant investment in real money.Frustrating economic system: The need to use currency purchased with real money to sell certain items makes the experience unfair for less fortunate players or those with less time and more pay to win, because the best item are in the auctionhouse ! Only 20% to craft one item purchaseable with epic resource already hard to get ! These items are worth between 5000 and +9000 lucents either 90-120$ !!!F2P guilds vs Credit card guilds = Credit card guilds win, and it's final !!! In addition, the Koreans have installed themselves on all Western servers and have taken over the businesses. Prices will increase.Transformations with no gameplay impact: Although visually appealing, transformations into creatures provide no real advantage or game mechanics. It would be better to leave the character in human form during a sprint, add a free grappling hook system like in The First Descendant, etc.Aggro balancing issue: Ranged classes have an unfair advantage in drawing enemy aggro compared to melee classes.

Combat is fun, and the dual weapon system defining your role, as opposed to choosing a class, is cool system that combined elements from games like FF14, GW2, Albion, ArcheAge, etc. Sure there will be  some combos that will more meta than others, but if you're not a sweaty player, you can get a lot of fun out of this game. My hardcore MMO days are over, I'm just a casual now, and I think with that mindset I can have a lot of fun in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: While not a totally awful game, I don't personally find myself enjoying it after about 7 hours. You could make the argument that "7 hours isn't long enough to judge an MMO, it gets better" and you could be right - however I'm of the mindset that a game should be enjoyable out of the gate, not 10's or 100's of hours later, and 7 hours was plenty of time to realize it's not for me. The game is alright, but "just alright" isn't enough for me to wanna invest my time in a massive MMO like this. There is some good here - the visuals are nice, the english voice acting is localized better than most non-english MMO's, you can tell there was time and money put into making the game look pretty good, animations are fluid. The Morph system is a unique way to handle traversal and feels cool. Though, many of  the other systems ended up feeling like a toss-up between alright, serviceable, or below average - the most major of which are the combat, crafting systems, cash shop, and the (at times) generic-feeling game design.The hybrid combat has its moments, but there are games that do tab targeting better (WoW, FFXIV) , and there are games that do action combat better (New World, BDO). I also see the usual trappings of other Korean MMOs, like chance based upgrade/crafting systems (think similar systems found in BDO or Lost Ark), P2W Elements (Battlepass, separate premium level up tracks, and store purchases that translate directly to power via market purchases, as well as other systems that can be accelerated or bypassed with money), among other tropes of the MMO genre in general, leading the game to feel formulaic and grindy in a way that feels unfun to me. All I would say is know what you're getting into, check gameplay online; see if it's for you. At the end of the day it's free - you can always give it a shot yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is full of bugs, quite broken, even Warzone didn’t have this many bugs. It’s also not optimized at all. I reported more than 10 critical errors in the last 2 weeks (some of them occurred while doing 2 star dungeons).It’s not pay-to-win, don’t get confused. At most, you can invest money to speed up progress, but everything is obtainable in-game, and everyone has to grind and complete the content, even those who buy the in-game currency. There is no direct transactions between players to prevent p2w. This is the way for all the companies now, and it won't change soon or never, it doesn't exist a modern f2p mmo without boosts.On the other hand, the mechanics for acquiring items, leveling them up, and buying traits in the shop are quite frustrating, confusing, and poorly explained at the beginning. It’s a system where, if you make mistakes early on, you lose a lot of time and money if you’ve invested any. It doesn't allow you go back, if you do mistakes, you have to work A LOT on your gear.Dungeons currency, time, and contract limitations make the game extremely monotonous—you have to do the same thing every day, and if you skip a day, you lose progress. It's not for casuals, it's a PVP game. You need to progress as fast as you can.There aren’t many world raid bosses. The ones that exist are very easy to kill. The drop rate is low.There’s no PvP for all levels, which is the most bizarre thing, considering this is a game focused on PvP. To enjoy PvP, you need to be very well-equipped. Your character can only withstand 2 hits if you try to engage in PvP in any area or event. I remember in Lineage 2, PvP was enjoyable at all levels, anywhere, at any time. The fights took seconds or even minutes. And if you didn’t want to engage in PvP, there was plenty of PvE content, and this content wasn’t necessarily super repetitive, time-restricted, party-dependent, or reliant on the party playing well, avoiding issues, not disconnecting, understanding mechanics, etc. It’s not well-designed.Everything is designed to make money and show good metrics in Amazon’s reports while they can.I highly doubt they’ll do anything to change this. In Korea, this game has already been dead for a while.

So everything is doable which is a good thing.- There are only three very major flaws about this game; 1. Very CPU intensive game. You'll need a good CPU otherwise fps will drop very much in crowded areas. Even so it drops to 40-50'ish, so you better prepare yourself.2. Very toxic people in this game. You might be called names while learning boss mechanics, so gear up and don't let yourself down, fight back.3. Hard to get into Co-Op dungeon parties, just because back to number 2. _childDocuments_.review: Throne and Liberty is a breath of fresh air in the MMO genre, and I’ve been thoroughly impressed by what it offers. From the moment you step into its world, the graphics take your breath away—stunning landscapes, detailed character models, and immersive environments make every location feel vibrant and alive. It’s more than just an A-to-B MMO grind; the game world is dynamic and genuinely invites exploration.One of the standout features is the guild system, which is extremely well-designed. Not only does it encourage cooperation among players, but it also provides a sense of purpose and progression for guilds through large-scale PvP and guild-wide objectives. The sense of community and teamwork is front and center, which is a crucial element for a game like this.The quests are varied and engaging, with some interesting narratives and mechanics that keep things fresh. But what truly sets Throne and Liberty apart is its open-world events. These events aren’t just there to fill space—they’re massive, challenging, and rewarding, with unpredictable elements that keep you on your toes. It really adds to the excitement when you’re not sure what’s coming next, and it feels like you’re part of a living, breathing world.As for the negative reviews? Frankly, I don’t get them. A lot of people are upset about server issues on the first day—but come on, this happens with almost every major online release. Of course there were server hiccups! Tons of people were trying to log in at once because so many were eager to play. To give the game poor reviews for something so trivial is frustrating, and honestly, it’s the kind of toxic attitude that discourages developers from even making MMOs these days.Games like Throne and Liberty are rare gems, and we should be celebrating them for their innovation and ambition, not dragging them down for something as temporary as launch-day server congestion. It’s time the MMO community took a step back and appreciated what we have, rather than nitpicking over small issues. Throne and Liberty is a fantastic experience that reminds us of what MMOs can be when done right.

_childDocuments_.review: My opinion after just 3 hours in early access, so this is FWIW:  If you like Black Desert, you'll like this game.  It's basically the same except that the TL combat mechanics are not as good. You have the same silly floaty friend following you around (except this one is a rag doll that might appeal to an 8-year-old player). The same look/feel. The same terrible voice acting. Very similar quests. Similar depth in skills, armor, weapons, and crafting (great if you like that depth). Same sort of narrative that's only there to push you along as you grind. I was able to play for a bit today without constant server disconnects, so that's good. It's my intention to keep playing in the hopes that the PvP game and guild features make this worth it. If so, I will amend this review. But, the easy way to know if you want to play this early on is: Do you want to play Black Desert again?

_childDocuments_.review: Boring, no wonder it failed in koreaThe game starts off fun and fresh, and the progression isn't too bad. But once you hit level 50 and finish the main quest line, the game becomes plain boring.After reaching level 50, you can do 3 dungeon runs, which take around 10 to 15 minutes each.You complete your daily 10 contracts and Mystic Globe keys, which take 10 to 20 minutes. Then you farm mobs for Abyssal currency (but once that's gone, you won’t get any more drops).Optionally, you can participate in event boss fights every 2 to 3 hours, which take less than 3 minutes to complete, fighting with 100 other people over maybe 2 good loot items. Or, you could do region events, which don't drop anything special at all.There's some PvP content, but it's mostly dominated by meta builds or gatekept by bigger guilds, with no rewards unless a boss is in conflict.Life skills? There really aren't any, aside from cooking and fishing. (what level super easy)You might think you can make money with with food (Lucent) , but no, not really, since there's less than a 10% chance of creating something sellable.Even breaking down gear to sell on the AH is time-gated by weekly items you have to buy.so not your level 50 and you spent 2h a day to do your MMO job because it feels like a job now. then log off and maby log back in quick for a boss then log off again.BECAUSE THE IS NOTHING TO GO FOR
