_childDocuments_.review: This game should come with a massive legal disclaimer that all your favorite streamers are being sponsored to play this game, and they are swiping upwards of $5k (likely as part of their contracts to get to show you the end game on there Giga expensive PC's). So, first and foremost, the game play you've seen in these sponsored streams are HIGHLY un reflective of the experience you're going to have (notwithstanding the praise streamers are paid to regurgitate). It's also critical to note the following before you actually begin criticizing this game on other merits: - This game is designed around larger scale pvp content, and therefore it necessarily precludes skill expression - that's just how game design works; you cant have everything all at once. Okay, so now with the premise that this game is designed around large scale PvP lets examine why that's problematic given the rest of the game:1. Always remember: even if you can withstand all of the below issues and manage to reach end game, if you don't have a PC that costs around $3-5k, you cant reasonably enjoy large scale PvP content. (unless you some how enjoy playing a game with settings so low that you might aswell be playing roblox). 2. Gate kept Content: Almost ALL forms of content are gate kept either by 1) Time, 2)Other players or 3) Your ability to swipe. (Even co-op dungeons can only be ran a number of times per day before you're unable to receive any loot/rewards)3. Gear Progression: Slow and, very importantly, BORING. Want to craft gear? Too bad, need materials from gate kept content. 4. PvP: A pvp game where you can only PvP 10% of the time (i.e when the game clock goes to night time which is for 30 minutes every X hours). When you do find the 30 minutes to PvP - you are just getting 1 shot by giga geared players.5. Open World PvP (night time open dungeons and world bosses): Gatekept by uber geared players who will 1 shot you and massive guilds who will 1 shot you before you can get within 200meters of the boss, respectively. 6. The resolution to the above?: Mindless day time PvE grind (remember we installed this game to pvp righht?) OR just swipe so you can buy gear and not get 1 shot, so that you can still mindlessly PvE grind but atleast you'll be the one 1 shotting undergeared players now.7. Clunky combat, clunky movement, uninspiring weapon skills: Cheap combat, no real skill expression, bad small scale balancing. 8. So, you finally managed to swipe, and you went through the hell of boot licking either the game developers with your wallet and/or some skinny nerd guild leader so you can finally participate in end game content. Welp, go back to number 1. Cheap mobile game, developer company is injecting large amounts of cash to streamers so that they can hype this game whilst lying through their teeth. Combat is elementary, no skill expression. Content is gate kept, and or otherwise extremely boring. Requires giga op PC to enjoy said gated content. This game is a lose-lose situation. Quite literally, as another reviewer put it, a "waste of time".

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the deluge of negativity around the P2W system, which having only played PVE, I haven't seen yet, this game is a lot of fun with a rewarding progression system for the early part of the game. The classless system is engaging because you can truly build out a character however you want and it gives more incentive to grind out various weapon skills and create a character that can handle any situation. The visuals are quite good for an MMO, with great optimization for anyone running a decently good rig. DLSS of course helps, but that doesn't stop the game from running smoothly, with little lag or server issues either. The art design is a feast as well. The various creatures, bosses, world events and enviroments all look amazing from a design perspective. It is a good blend of western and eastern sensibilites. The community has been positive so far, before the launch of the F2P model. Here's to hoping that it stays that way for the duration of the title. For anyone that is still reading, do not be discouraged by all of the negativity. The gaming community, especially for MMO's always seems to be increasingly toxic, wanting to compare everything to a game that they played 10 years ago, instead of assuming positive intent and embracing change and new ways of interweaving old mechanics with new.

_childDocuments_.review: A Solid Leveling Experience, With Room to Grow in EndgameAfter playing for several months on the KR servers, I'll keep it brief: Throne and Liberty offers an excellent leveling experience, though the late-game content feels a bit shallow. However, I have hope that future updates will address this gap and bring more depth to the endgame. Overall, I'd recommend giving it a try.Now, let’s talk about concerns around monetization:It's not pay-to-win. Traditionally, pay-to-win (P2W) meant gaining an exclusive or early power advantage by spending money. That’s not the case here. Best-in-slot gear is available to all players, regardless of spending. Yes, you can spend large amounts of money to buy gear, but you can also earn premium currency in-game to acquire those same items without paying. And just having the best gear won’t guarantee success—you’ll still need to build a viable strategy and execute it well.

You get the max level so fast and then you hit a brick wall and by brick wall i mean pay wall. _childDocuments_.review: Best MMO RPG I have played in a while.The in-game systems have a good amount of depth and are not shallow.Amazing skill customization system that lets you make different variations of the same skill, offering a lot of different ways to build your abilities based on content and situation.The game has a good endgame loop; you'll never log in and not know what to do.Crazy good optimization allows hundreds of players to be in the same spot fighting with little issue, though it still requires fairly recent hardware, so be careful.Combat is basically the same old tab targeting we all know. Whether you like it or not will depend on you. As a tab targeting system, the combat is 9/10. It has a few small quirks, but overall it’s very well made and is one of the best tab-targeting systems currently available in MMORPGs.Best-feeling massive PVP fights since the Lineage 2 days. The game has a big focus on PVP and Guilds/Alliances. If you don't like group play, you can still get a good amount of solo/party content, but it won’t feel like a complete experience.The biggest negatives are the mid-story and fast leveling (for me).Regarding pay to win: This game is most definitely pay to win. But in my eyes, it’s one of the best P2W systems I have seen in an MMO so far. People tend to ignore the fact that all MMORPGs since the start were P2W. You were always able to buy in-game currency from the black market for real money and literally pay to progress. Sure, it was against the terms of service, and people usually didn’t see it advertised publicly, but it was always there, and some shady guy was getting the money.In contrast, Throne and Liberty has the whole game designed around P2W, with an in-game shop and premium currency that you can buy for real money. At first, it looks bad, but when you look closely, you will see many in-game blocks specifically designed to prevent P2W players from progressing too fast. Instead, it gives players with less time to play the game a chance to compensate with their money, but just in regulated amounts. Nothing is simply "pay and forget about it" – you still need to grind and actually play the game.Also, the best premium currency idea is the auction house based solely on premium currency. Every purchase of Lucent (so-called "whales" or anyone else) is not only for them. This person goes to the auction house and buys items for themselves. What items? Items other players grinded for, which free-to-play players are selling. So the Lucent this person buys for real money is distributed to the whole community sooner or later, in a slightly reduced amount. This player who is buying cannot get anything that hasn’t already been dropped by someone in the game. They gain no huge advantage over others, as most players use the best gear they need themselves first and only sell extra drops or items they don’t need.Sure, this system is not perfect, but as a whole, combined with in-game limitations, such as server milestones for new dungeons and events, it makes the balance of power fairly equal.To simplify, it works like this:You play for free, you spend more time playing.You play and spend small amounts of money (equal to subscriptions other MMOs have), and you grind a little less.If you spend big amounts, you can play less, but if you still want to play a lot, you’ll simply hit walls of progression constantly, making it boring for you, as all you did was get to the progression block slightly earlier than free-to-play players.My recommendation is to play for free and take your time to get to know the game. Reach level 50 to experience the peak of combat performance. After a week or two, you will need to decide if you want to play more seriously. While not mandatory, it will be more convenient to spend small amounts of money each month (equal to comparable subscriptions in other MMORPGs). If you don’t feel serious about the game, just don’t spend anything and play for free. You won’t be missing out on much fun, as most content will eventually be accessible when your gear is better. Always try to join a guild and make some friends – it will make the content more enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I want to address the hottest topic: The P2W topicPeople need to chill about this whole thing, while you can pay to get gear and to get the right traits for your gear you have to consider that the word "win" is so out of place. Early on the auction is empty and good items will be kept and used, not sold. Once they start to get sold they'll be so overpriced that no sane person is going to pay money for just a fraction of the progress you need. So, you can technically pay to buy gear (and traits for gear) off the auction but it'd be insane early on. The game rewards your consistency more than anything else. Login everyday, complete your contracts, complete your dungeon runs, use the abyss tokens and you'll be competitive in any pvp scenario... pvp itself is not even all about gear, there's actual skill applied and smashing buttons randomly won't do it.If you DO NOT spend money in this game you're not cut off, people forget that mmos are all about knowledge, The very top leaderboard players in the KR version are F2P. I also have been playing quite a while in the KR version and the past betas too, this 4 days of EA I managed to grind enough and sell items for a total worth of 60€ of lucent, so, go watch game guides and figure out how the economy works and you'll be just as successful as anybody else.You normally have 2 kinds of players: you have the ones down to pour 12 hours a day and the softcore players coming back home over the evenings to play some, skipping days at times.This game is a bit more on the softcore side, many things are time-gated, you get to run 3 dungeons a day, consume 5k abyssal tokens a day, complete 10 contracts a day... Once you're done with these there's not much else to do really (progression-wise), those who have more time will pour time in arena 3v3, open pvp, or make an alt character they can use to feed stuff into the market and make extra lucent (since lucent are account-wide).Also don't forget the game revolves a lot around guilds, most of the times people will be busy with guild content which include territory sieges, world boss contests, guild dungeons, and also some small-scale guild content...My 300h are not effective ones, consider lots of idle time or me leaving the pc on when out of home or sleeping. However, good chunk in game clearly. I'm currently sitting on 3'000+ gear score and I know some people (f2p as I am) being 3100, 3200... Consider the cap is about 3400. I'd say "probably a bit", but overall not as most may think. When I face someone being 3.3k / 3.4k gearscore (which I'll refer to as "GS" from now on) is likely the dude is a few hundreds $ deep by now. And being 3.3 / 3.4 GS, makes quite the difference in PvP but we're talking about 1v1 or 1v2 scenarios. The game revolves a lot around groups. You could be 3.4k GS but you ain't going to 1v3 against a squad of 2.9k GS unless huge mistakes come in play.We're almost 3 weeks in since the release and is pretty much impossible to be 3.4k GS as  F2P right now, being 3.1/3.2 GS is the peak of what you could expect from a f2p player, I (as 3k GS) could be 3.1ish or a bit more but i made some mistakes in my build and I'm in the process of fixing it so I'm playing catch-up. I must say that mechanical knowledge pays off a lot, I've been facing 3.3k+ opponents and won those fights (not all of 'em clearly) but it comes down to what class your opponent is and how good of a PvP player he is.Those who pay, spend money on traiting up certain pieces (accessories mostly) and I've been tempted to throw a 100$ to get 6k lucent to trait up a bit more but after doing some math I decided not to because 100$ is not going to change anything of substance. You need a few hundreds to properly trait up, that's if you have already the base item and you only need traits. If you need the base item you're going to spend a lot more. Sorry but I ain't spending that much in a videogame when I can just be a bit patient and keep up the grind. Those who pay will be capped and will be caught up eventually. As a F2P I'm still competitive by the way, me being 3.0k GS still shows great results so far, I do however feel it when I face a 3.3k+ player.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is very fun, the dungeons are great, and the combat style is neat. However, what really detracts from the game is the semi-forced PvP. You can say there are scheduled peace activities, but let’s be honest: the top guild on each server can dominate everything and earn double the rewards, further outpacing the entire server. These same guilds often form alliances with other strong guilds, and all the spenders come together to control every conflict event. If you’re not in one of these top guilds, forget about joining—if your gear score isn’t around 3k, you won’t be accepted. Overall, the PvE content is great; I would gladly pay a subscription for the game if it focused solely on PvE with optional PvP.The Good:Public dungeons are fun, and there are always groups available for them. However, the need for tokens to access the drops diminishes the experience. With a limited number of contract tokens each day, much of the appeal is lost.Co-op dungeons are enjoyable as well; the boss designs are great, and the mechanics aren’t very difficult. However, the experience suffers again due to the token limit—you can only complete three per day at most.The Bad:The drop rate in co-op dungeons is not friendly unless you have the luck perk or choose to spend money. I’m not opposed to low RNG, but without a pity system, it feels pointless to play this game beyond finishing the story content.Overall, for the first 30 hours, you will have fun, be confused about what to do, and be amazed at the size of the world and the variety of monsters. However, the game quickly changes at level 50; it starts to feel like a job. Each day, you have to spend all your resistance contracts, use all your abyss tokens, run your three dungeons, check the schedule for peace events, find one you want to do, complete it, and log off until the next day or the next event starts. And don’t forget: if it’s a PvP event, you might be executed before you can even see the boss or complete a task.As a final straw, if you join a guild, any drops you get go to the guild for distribution unless you claim them first. If you receive something you could sell for a lot of lucent on the auction house, it could be quickly taken, and there’s nothing you can do about it because the game is designed that way. There have already been several instances of this happening, and it is not a punishable offense.As I write this, part of me wants to recommend the game based on the PvE, but due to the constraints that the in-game systems impose, I doubt it’s worth the 30-50 hours. However, it is a free game, so at least you only lose time playing it and not money. Why listen to someone review a game when you can try it out and find out for yourself?

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is very enjoyable. It has good content, and it looks nice. It's a very decent MMO if you're looking for something new to play. However, verticality and vertical movement in this game basically destroys all of that for me. The game introduces flight/glide mechanics as well as a piton system for grappling up sheer vertical faces. It's a non-inconsequential of several quests and boss fights in the game. I suspect it's a component of whatever anti-cheese system the game is running on its servers to prevent people from exploiting terrain features or boundaries, but every aspect of vertical movement is such a pain in the ass that it actively degrades every other aspect of the game for me. For example, simply falling off a small ledge in the course of running around on the map rubber-bands you back to above the ledge... then back down it. Then back up it again, until the anti-cheese system determines that you weren't trying to cheese something and it rubber-bands you to your intended place and where you should be. It's amplified and worse when you're attempting to traverse cliff faces or time-trial quests that incorporate flight, and even moreso when you're involved in a bossfight and trying to stay alive while also combating the clunky verticality mechanics. That's my ultimate rub with the game: the vertical movement processing is something you actively have to fight against, and it does not help you. Movement controls are a basic core function of any video game, and considering this is an MMO, they should be helping you and not hindering your progress or ability to play the game.I hope they fix this problem, because otherwise the game is fairly enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: From my experience, Throne and Liberty falls flat on numerous fronts, making it a frustrating game to engage with. The PvP system is particularly disappointing, with horrible targeting mechanics and a heavy reliance on pay-to-win elements. It’s 100% P2W, meaning players with deep pockets can easily dominate the gameplay while those who don’t pay are left struggling. This unfair balance makes PvP feel less about skill and more about spending money.The guild system adds another layer of annoyance. It’s excessively grindy and competitive, with players at risk of being kicked if they’re inactive for just 48 hours. This creates unnecessary pressure and discourages casual play, making the game feel like a second job rather than a source of enjoyment.Additionally, the community and social experience are lacking, which hampers player interaction. The PvE content is bland and repetitive, offering little in terms of excitement or engagement. Coupled with the rampant presence of bots, the game feels less authentic and more like a cash grab. Overall, Throne and Liberty leaves much to be desired and fails to deliver a satisfying MMORPG experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Throne and Liberty is a mixed bag for MMO fans, but it does have its charm. NCSoft went all out on the visuals, and it shows – the world is gorgeous and packed with things to do. One cool aspect is how they handle events; every few hours, dynamic quests pop up all over, so there’s always something happening. From world bosses to massive group activities, it’s pretty easy to find people to team up with if you like the social side of MMOs.The combat’s a mix of old and new. You get classic tab-targeting, but there’s also a neat system where you can time defensive moves to block or counter, adding a bit of skill to keep things fresh. It’s a solid blend for both PvE and PvP.Progression has a bit of a grind, but here’s the catch: you can spend premium currency (Lucent) to speed things up. While you’re not forced to pay to win, some might call it “pay-to-skip,” since throwing money at it can get you resources faster. This won’t make you OP right away, but it does give paying players a bit of a shortcut.Story-wise, it’s your usual “hero vs. evil” setup, but the voice acting and cutscenes are surprisingly good. If you’re looking for something that blends solid graphics, a social vibe, and decent PvE/PvP, Throne and Liberty is worth a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: After 100 hours this is my take:Its free. Even so, I spent $$ on the Battle Pass and Premium upgrades. After I got to max level (50) I created another character and discovered that these upgrades are really really important. At level 30 my primary character had a GS of 1600 but my level 27 only has about 1200. This is because the alt character doesnt have access to the upgrade mats that my primary character had. Inventory is not shared between characters. You are limited to 2 characters, cant even buy more character slots.Cosmetics are kinda pointless IMHO unless you like to look at yourself a lot. Because your in 3rd person you dont really see the details of anyones armor/weapons. My staff has a headless naked female sculpture at its head... but no one will ever see that. While this is all subjective, the starting gear looks on par with late game gear. Nothing really says... hey look at my achievement as represented by this awesome armor or weapon.My primary character is GS 2313. A lot of the stuff I need to upgrade is locked behind server wide achievements that are further time locked. Originally I thought this game was going to be like Lineage 2 where guilds owned castles and defended them... but so far, i see no evidence of this even though the trailer seemed to indicate that was a thing. Guilds can own (control) Riftstones but its all really kind of pointless. The open world bosses are half the time co-op, and the other half open pvp... and its pure chaos. There is a floating whale that appears every now and then and provides a server wide buff. Its fun to get on it and ride it to the point where it dives back into the sea. The thing is, its a very pretty game. Korean games generally are... but the end-game is basically dead. Its a fun journey getting there and I should make sure im clear about that. Unfortunately im writing this end-game so im writing this with a fair amount of end-game bias. Franky Black Desert Online and ArchAge are/were better. you could build and pilot ships in both, not in this game. You had your own property in both and can grow crops, not in this game. Im giving this a thumbs up because it held me for 100+ hours. If you dont care about end game, or at least care about it less than the journey to get there, then this is a thumbs up. _childDocuments_.review: after launch: Due to the toxicity of the player base, I will be completely and utterly avoiding this.----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------pre-release early review before the launch:It's clear NCSoft and Amazon did some homework and it's nice to see. As a long time MMORPG veteran, I'm glad to see it. Again, I wish steam would have a "meh" / "neutral" review instead of yes/no system.  As, this game is worth looking into and playing at the free to play price point, for now. throne and liberty is a really weird game.  I'm unsure if i like it as Its like...a mix of tab targeting and action combat?? It feels weird and reminds me of a crappier archeage.  Takes some time getting used to.  The character creator is decent and the fact that the classes are tied to the weapons like new world is pretty neat.  Speaking of, this game also kinda reminds me of New World in some aspects.  For instance the book collectibles are pretty much like that of New World. At least in this game, you can swim.  So...there's that, i guess?If you can wait, i suggest waiting until throne and liberty launches on October 1st and trying it out when it releases as a free to play game instead of buying into it to try it out. At least it gets you to try to engage with the story.I really wish the "action combat" was actually action combat instead of tab target [in this case, click target] and just using abilities and having to move out of the way for aoes like every other bog standard tab target mmorpg out there. _childDocuments_.review: I would not recommend. The positive thing I can say is that it has some good MMO game play. The leveling and itemization system is definitely unique. And there is some interesting end game PvP, Guild Raids, and Bosses.Now the reason I do not recommend.-BugsSome quests are not complete where a specific creature is needed. You can kill Sea Crabs all day and all night and never get the drop needed to complete a gathering questSome items required for crafting and gear itemization are missing from the game. There is no way to run as a crafter type because the required items are just not in the game. Blue Ink, I am looking at you. Apparently the player base wants to re direct you to speed running dungeons to get drops, that have a limited chance to get the item you need, and even more limited chance to get a trait you want.-Timegates and Loot DropsDungeon loot can only be obtained by spending coins. These special coins are limited daily so you can only really run those a couple times per day. And they are fast, like :15 - :20 minute experiences if you want to clear them. If you speed run some of them can be done in five minutes.Loot in this game is completely non existent. Playing this amount of time and I have gotten like seven open world drops. It is all useless gear that goes into this lithograph that supoosively gets you better gear. But the big catch is, the gear there can all be crafted, if there was blue ink.-ChildishThere are stuffed animals that you collectThere are dashing, gliding, and swimming morphs that you collectYou swim as an otter, you dash as a wolf. There is not going to be any such thing as a mount ever in this game because the bright minds who developed this product think they solved that problem with the morphs. Sorry, but I think it kind of missed the mark there.-AmitoiSo to be successful crafting you need these stuffed animals. There is just a bunch of running and collecting quests from one side of a zone to the other side of the zone. And multiple clicks at the same object. Like click the stuffed animal. Turn around and click the scroll. Then turn around click the stuffed animal. Then travel to the exact opposite end of the zone to click on a rock. And then travel all the way back across the zone to click on the stuffed animal again.Then go all the way back to the main starter town to go visit some ol maid seamstress, who by the way looks to be 12 years old, to talk with her to restore your Amitol.So these are able to go out on gathering quests and collect materials. But then, crafting is just broken and non existent as you collect all these materials that cannot be used. you pretty much just make food and that is it.-Pay WallEverything in this game is put behind a pay wall. You will need to swipe your credit card to even have any advancement to end game and experience end game content in your guild. Some guilds even require upon membership for you to swipe and purchase items for real money.Which leads to the Bots. With the real life money mechanics, and the requirement to swipe your card to advance, has lead to a large body of exploiters who are farming this games using scripts and bots for the sole purpose of making money off of you.

_childDocuments_.review: A Fresh Take on the MMORPG GenreI've been playing Throne and Liberty for a while now, and I must say, I'm really impressed. It's not often an MMORPG manages to balance a beautiful open world, engaging combat, and deep progression, but this game truly delivers on all fronts.Graphics and EnvironmentsThe world is incredibly beautiful with stunning landscapes and details. Whether you're exploring ancient ruins, vast forests, or snow-capped mountains, it feels like every area is alive and carefully crafted. The graphics engine does a great job of creating an atmospheric experience.Combat SystemThe combat is smooth and responsive, with a good mix of action and strategy. Each class feels like it has its own identity, and finding the right combination of skills and gear for your playstyle gives a real sense of progression. Boss fights and world events are also thrilling and challenging.Community and Social GameplayOne of the game's strongest points is how it encourages cooperation. The guild system and the opportunities to collaborate with other players in both PvP and PvE events are well-designed. It feels like the community is central here, and that adds to the dynamic, living world.Exploration and FreedomThe ability to shapeshift into different animals to explore the world is a really fun and unique feature. It gives you a sense of freedom and access to areas that would otherwise be hard to reach.ConclusionIf you're looking for an MMORPG with depth, stunning visuals, and a dynamic world that evolves with your gameplay, I highly recommend Throne and Liberty. It definitely has the potential to become a favorite for both veterans and newcomers to the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Technically a fine game. Smooth graphics and transitions, etc. Some interesting game mechanics. Unfortunately that is not enough the negate all the negatives. Pure P2win. Grindy as hell. Uninspired environment, cookie-cutter fantasy setting with bland story. RNG. You get locked into a "class" (weapon combination) early on, changing is possible but painful, and you get only two characters. Strange loot distribution based on dps (goodbye, tanks, healers and support). No trading apart from AH. No gifting items to friends. Not just the common "character-bound" limitations, but literally *nothing* can be passed on to friends.Everything in the game is geared towards PvP (even in non-PvP zones you're still competing: having to run to a resource to harvest before someone else gets there, events that are competitions, etc) and funneling you to the cash shops. Early on you get "trained" to accept that shop items are required for normal play. At first that's the "gold" shop, which is easy enough to earn. Soon enough though, you end up in the cash shop. Even without guild vs guild fights, the guilds are still in competition, based for a large part based on PvP activities.Then there all the usual practices to trigger you. Someone in the zone you are in loots a purple item? It gets flashed on your screen, trying to trigger a bit of fomo to send you to the shop. It gets real old, real fast.Then there's the fact that some activities, both open world and dungeons, are time-gated. If you log on when an event has just been completed, you'll have to come back the next day. In short: it wants your time *and* your money, and doesn't deliver anything worth all that.The best thing about it? It's free, so you can go make up your own mind.

_childDocuments_.review: Bots are multiplying faster than bunnies at a carrot buffet, with over 100 bots per zone zooming around like they're in a shopping spree from hell, snatching up everything from new players. At this rate, the bots are gonna hit endgame zones before you even figure out how to dodge-roll. And what's Amazon doing about it? NOTHING. They're sitting back, sipping their coffee, probably thinking, “Eh, we'll let the economy collapse like it's no big deal.” Why fix it when you can just let the players suffer while rolling in their cash, right? Hiring GMs takes time, effort, and worst of all, MONEY—and these companies are tighter than a locked vault in a bank heist. By 2025, we won't even have an economy; we’ll have Monopoly money and a ghost town for a playerbase.The Auction House? Oh, yeah, it's great—if you love throwing your hard-earned cash into the digital firepit. Welcome to "Lucent," the currency that might as well be called "Pay-to-Win Tokens." Wallet Warriors are out here dominating both PVE and PVP, flexing so hard they'll kick you from dungeons because you haven't hit max gear score in your 10 hours of gameplay. Sorry, there's just no room for you peasants. We’re looking at Lost Ark 2.0 here, but with more credit card swipes and fewer chances for anyone who doesn't have a black card.PVP? HA! Don’t even dream about it unless your wallet's so fat it needs its own seat on the plane. BIS (Best in Slot) gear? Yeah, you can buy that straight from the Auction House and get tricked out in five minutes, while the rest of us are grinding our souls away for 100+ hours just to get a pair of boots. The top guild? Oh, it’s just the one with the highest credit limit, obviously. Dungeons and events? Forget about 'em unless you're part of the Whaley McWhaleface squad.PVE isn’t much better. Sure, you might get a little farther, but don't be surprised when you get kicked from the endgame boss fight to make room for someone's cousin who’s rocking half your gear score. It’s basically a revolving door of favoritism, where your gear score’s just a suggestion and their friends list is the real priority.And the targeting system? It’s like trying to hit a bullseye while wearing a blindfold and spinning in circles. The default settings? Oh boy, they're like someone handed a toddler a keyboard and said, “Design a game!” Sure, you’ve got a million settings to choose from, but none of them actually help. You’ll need a whole YouTube degree just to figure out how to aim at the thing you’re trying to kill. It's that bad. It's like the targeting system is actively trying to make you miss.

You're constantly building up your character, exploring and having a good time.When you hit the end game, however - it becomes a chore. Systems on top of systems, currencies gallore, Lots of dull grinds, limited content, upgrade failures, impossible drop-rates. Combine this with the fact that there is a real-money auction house that whales are happy to utilise, you'll soon find yourself feeling the shine wear off this game. It's certainly possible to sell items and mats on the real money auction house - an argument that people do make - but ultimately, you end up depriving yourself of mats and resources that you'll need yourself later. I can recommend this game if you're the sort of person who loves a grind, loves a routine and has plenty of time to spend farming mats -- or if you've got a lot of disposable income. But for everyone else, It's not the MMO that you're looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: Got to max level, hunted some BIS gear, 100%'d every zone and side story.Simply speaking, if you're someone who likes to sit down and grind out character/gear progression, this game isn't for you. It has daily lockouts on loot chances to push people towards buying premium currency to buy gear with on the Auction House.Once you complete the main story and start to do end game world bosses, dungeons, and world dungeons; you'll soon start to see certain issues arise. Character and gear progression is time gated by resources that refresh daily (ala genshin impact), instead of time played. You get 900 of a currency a day, and 300 of said currency is used to open the chest at the end of an endgame dungeon for a chance at loot. Then, your other chances are farming openworld dungeons loaded with full parties of players all fighting over the same mobs, or world bosses that spawn every few hours and drop one piece of gear that you have to roll against hundreds of other players to obtain.There is a pity system with loot, to obtain a purple main-hand and off-hand and unlock all traits for them both you need to complete every dungeon 30 times. Depending on if you have a dedicated group to play with or using party finder, this can take anywhere from 45-90+ hours. Not too bad, but it'll probably take much longer to max out your weapons once you get them.Why are dungeons designed on a daily lockout basis? To drive people to the auction house. Why are they trying to drive people to the auction house? Because the only way to purchase things on the auction house is with premium currency, which costs real money. You know, the thing that almost killed Diablo 3 in the first week but with an extra step :)What could have been a cool game to grind out and max in, is just another cashgrab that tries to annoy the player with lockouts into spending real money.Dishonest pile of garbage. F2P MMOs have been dead since the early 2000s and this doesn't do them any justice for anyone who grew up during the golden age.

_childDocuments_.review: Story: 9/10Get ready to dive into a world that’s as immersive as your favorite book! The story is absolutely captivating, and I’m still savoring every twist and turn, even with the side quests. Sure, not every side story is a masterpiece, but they’re consistently enjoyable, adding depth to the overall experience. While it might not redefine storytelling, the writing is solid, and the voice acting is a delight, keeping the pace brisk and exciting. You’ll find yourself hooked, eagerly wanting to see what happens next!PvP: 8/10Prepare for some exhilarating battles! While my guild is a bit on the quieter side (averaging about 10 players), we’ve had a blast with small-scale PvP. Picture this: we coordinated a surprise attack on a zerg in a PvP boss zone—talk about a thrill!BUT If you’ve got a lively guild, this score jumps to a solid 10, making every skirmish even more fun! Come here to make friends. be weary of the ones who complain a sour apple can rot the whole mindset.PvE: 8/10The dungeons are a sight to behold! While some are time-gated (which can be a tad frustrating), they’re beautifully designed and packed with engaging mechanics. It’s all about keeping your eyes peeled and mastering the fun—sometimes, a little chaos is part of the charm! Overall, the PvE experience is great, just wish I could dive in whenever I wanted.Pay-to-Win Aspects:Don’t worry about breaking the bank! Unless you’re itching to throw thousands at the game, stick to the battle pass and the story mode—you’ll snag the gear you need without spending a fortune. I only grabbed the early access pack, and as a free-to-play player, I’ve been having an absolute blast. You really don’t need to buy upgrade materials unless you want a fast track to endgame, which everyone will hit in about a week anyway, regardless of your spending habits. They've struck a great balance—keeping things accessible while making it tempting to splurge.In short,Throne and liberty (early access)] has bee a delightful journey filled with engaging stories, thrilling battles, and a fantastic community waiting to be explored. Whether you’re a casual player or a hardcore enthusiast, there’s plenty to enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: Bear with me, this will likely be a very long write up, but if you're looking for an unbiased, no bullcrap review, you've found it.I'll start with the positive. Combat is pretty cool and engaging, but nothing unique and special. It's just alright. There are both pros and cons, and I'll touch up on this below.That's it for the positives. Let's start with the extensive list of negatives. Combat itself is alright, but it is flawed because of controls and its functions, as well as external factors that will be mentioned below. While it does somewhat feels smooth and fluid, it falls flat and reminds you of how bad it really is. It is clunky and options that should've been on by default must be manually activated, which still don't really fix the fundamental "clunkiness". The movement of the game is slightly awkward to the point that combat is heavily affected by it, not allowing you to perform as perfectly as you can during fights like many other MMOs. The movement animations themselves aren't the problem, but rather the mechanics involved behind the movement. The world is so clunky as a whole, that simply jumping over a rock will cause you to magically teleport all over the place. This is even more evident when using the terribly designed morph/glide travel options, when attempting to glide to a puzzle and your character somehow gets stuck teleporting in air upon reaching the rock. It's clear the character has a sort of ifCollision>isStuck>UnstuckTeleport type of function, even though you're not actually ever stuck. It is a fundamental function that should be completely overhauled or scrapped. There's nothing positive to say about this. This is the equivalent of a Ground/Flying Mount, except there's nothing there but constant annoyance over the "clunkiness" of forms. In a world as large as this, it is extremely slow and extremely aggravating when trying to navigate the terrain. Another way to navigate the terrain are via grappling hooks, which are mixed with the movement/collision system and just as flawed. In return, you get a ridiculously annoying blend of features that you must contend with, if you want to play the game as a whole. You might then ask a simple question: "How can we make it faster?". It is Free-To-Play, so there's really one way to make money, at least for these modern gaming developers. Much like Lost Ark, and others, you are able to buy real money currency, which then translates into buying upgrades and items themselves. If you take Lost Ark, as an example, even though it is P2W, it doesn't really matter as much because the game is focused entirely on PvE, and one shot mechanics render gear useless, so to speak.Unfortunately, this is not the case here. This game has a heavy focus on Guild PvP content, which means if you swipe your card, you can get the best gear available and upgrade everything to max in minutes. But wait, there's more! How can we make travel mode faster? You guessed it right. To get more speed, you simply need more "forms", and there are premium and FOMO forms for sale that if you miss, you likely may not be able to max out the speed. In turn, that means not only does the enemy player that swiped has an advantage over you gear-wise, but also passive speed. There's really no point in doing PvP when it's like this, which brings us to the next point. If you're looking for an MMO with both PvE and PvP, this is not the game for you. While the game does have PvE content, aside from the obvious leveling experience, the endgame is extremely empty in every way. You are currency-locked to get rewards from dungeons to only a certain amount per day, and since this is a korean MMO, you have to grind a  amount of materials to craft your upgrades.This is essentially your daily PvE routine. Complete your daily contracts, do your 3 daily dungeons, and that's it. You could do world bosses and events, but these are locked behind schedules and don't actually help you as much in farming. Let's take it a step further. Let's say you don't PvP ever, and you got everything you need from the dungeons, and you're fully upgraded.Now what? Nothing. You're done, there's nothing else to do. There's a "Tower" PvE challenge content like Lost Ark, but once you get the rewards, there's no reason to do it again. Every weapon type has a mastery system with perks. It takes a colossal amount of time to level, and I truly mean a colossal amount of time. This essentially means that if you choose a set of weapons, then later on decide that you want to change, you're now way behind, because you have to start from the beginning. It also means you're going to have to grind a hell of a lot to catch up, or open your wallet. This applies to equippable items, and travel forms. This is yet another "large" game released with barely anything content-wise, which includes items. Each weapon has a skill tree, but there's barely any weapon types. There's also not a lot of travel form "morphs", especially depending which form. For an MMO, this simply doesn't make any sense. If MMO means regular, engaging content, then no content essentially means dead game. I don't understand how these developers continue to make the same mistake, unless they don't really care about any of this, aside from the potential profit on an empty game disguised as large simply due to the scale. The game itself is not difficult, and once you figure out how to bypass the overall "clunkiness", you're able to have some sort of fun, until you do content with other people. Much like Lost Ark, there is a skill ceiling in dungeons, and if you're not on top of it, you will cause the group to wipe, potentially causing players to rage quit. Unfortunately, as simple as some mechanics are, such as just press Q to defend when boss counter icon pops up, perfect or not, some people are unable to do this. Essentially, this means that you are forced to join a guild, and play with people that you may or may not particularly enjoy. That's not to say you can't achieve your goals solo, but it will take way longer due to randoms not doing mechanics.The problem with difficulties such as these in an MMORPG, is that you completely alienate a majority of your players. What happens if there's no content for your non-sweaty players? They'll simply leave, and spend their money and time elsewhere, case in point, Lost Ark.The reason World of Warcraft, as an example, is still one of the best MMOs out there that cannot seem to be "dethroned" is simply because there's no real difficulty for you get started, and you're not completely penalized by screwing up once, not counting the higher endgame difficulties that only a small percentage even bother with. This creates an environment where any players can play and progress without anything limiting or restricting them, like Lost Ark and this game.I do not recommend this game, whether you're solo, in a guild, or with friends. It is not made with longevity in mind, and will very likely have the same fate as New World. It's only a matter of time.It is a very flawed MMORPG, lacking the most basic MMO features, such as ability to transmog your gear. It doesn't matter if it comes later, it's the fact it wasn't included in the first place. This doesn't look good for developers, as it shows they're unable to do the proper research into what works, what doesn't, what should be included, what shouldn't, in order to create a gaming environment that keeps the only currency they need in order to survive. PEOPLE.One could hope that future developers would understand the simple fact that PvP only games die by the thousands, for one tiny reason. If you don't have people, you don't have a game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is the classical Korean RNG based game: the goal is to farm and raise the combat power.Content wise there are instances, group content, pvp content, pve, bosses, many (redundant) other mechanics... there is "a lot" to do, but you must follow strict rules and timings. Many almost all the PvP is instanced or scheduled and limited to fixed areas.Player trading is strictly moderated (devs say they do this cause of goldseller, meh...), in the auction you can trade a limited assortment of objects with a currency that you can buy in the shop for real cash. You can't even trade your crafted items (unless you "crit" them) or loot.All other mechanics are really the condensed concepts of themeparked game with an overly complex combat system with dozens of different undocumented and somethimes mysterious parameters.The only things that limits the grind are the time and quantity limited amount of items that enable for part of the game content (scrolls/points for contracts, points to drop from certain areas, points to unlock chests...)Overall i find it a very repetitive product, that requires an everyday effort (cause activity points recharge daily basis and there is a cap for the amount you can stack). Some may love it, but I think that the majority of westerner users will leave in a couple of months. If you want to raid bosses for a (small) chance of higher level drop, you must enter in a guild, learn to play and tryhard gearing accordingly to standard optimal builds until the next expansion that will of course change the meta and force you to start all over again.I already feel a bit tired, now that I understand the endgame and I'm not sure I want to repeat the same instances with ridiculously low drop rates, so I'm just casually playing.The pros? Well... it's free.Technically the game is fine, some areas are very well made (like the initial town) but others are really boring and less insipred consisting in just fields full of packed mobs with fast respawn rate. Textures and models also are not consistent in quality.The engine (UE4) works fine but you'll need a powerful CPU to manage large crows of players. My Ryzen 5900X limits the GPU to 60-70% in cities with many players. Maybe a series 7xxx or 9xxx X3D can behave better, not sure.A final suggestion: if you are not an hardcore player, DO NOT RUSH the game. Take your time, follow the story, do the side quests and watch the cinematics. The lore is not that bad and you can enjoy at least 30-40 hours of decent gaming before entering the demonic endgame loop.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has way too many issues which if they do no fix will eventually make me uninstall. I am not a hardcore player but I have reached PVE endgame(Very easy to get to) and have played enough to leave a review.Lets start with the negatives:-CONSTANT BUGS/GAMEBREAKING GLITCHES : Yes, this game has hundreds if not thousands of glitches. The most frustrating of them being boss mechanics not working as intended and basically being rng if it works or not. Another really annoying glitch is being completely stuck in a specific part of a mountain or stairs which causes a rubber band glitch. Furthermore transforming into the flying mount is so inconsistent which can lead you to just die of fall damage.-DUNGEON BOSS PREPARATION:For some reason the devs did not think to teleport everyone to the boss area when one player reaches it. This makes it so that even if a player is ready but is 2 cm away from the arena then guess what, that player IS BLOCKED FROM ENTERING and wont get any loot if the party beats the boss without them. Its such a terrible system and i do not know why the devs simply cannot follow what other mmos did??-OPEN WORLD DROP RATES:Oh my goodness this just makes grinding open world mobs miserable. Somehow a dev thought it was a brilliant idea for all monsters to have a 30% chance to drop NOTHING. This makes it frustrating to even get a common piece of equipment. (Also note this is not an official percentage as the devs hide percentages of all drop rates in the game, it genuinely just feels that way)-ALL DUNGEON DROPS ARE UNTRADABLE:Speaks for itself, this game acts like it encourages SSF but in reality there is an option to dismantle the gear from dungeon and craft it again to have a 20% CHANCE to be able to sell it on marketplace. HUH????-UNBALANCED PVP(I COULD BE VERY WRONG HERE):I do not know much about pvp but i saw some pvpers(one of them being a warrior and the other a paladin) battling in an arena and i kid you not they have been fighting for 15 MINUTES with one of them still having full mana and both of them basically at full health. Again i am not exaggerating.-TERRIBLE OPTIMIZATION:This game takes up almost all of your RAM if you have 16GB or less which at times causes severe lag spikes and fps drops. There might be some config file i can change to fix this, but for now i will still leave this here.-NOT ALT-FRIENDLY:Literally nothing is shared between characters. The storage is only per character. Mats are also per character. Gold is the only thing that can be sent in mail. If you make a second character its as if you are making a brand new account. if you have read this far Congrats! Now is the time for the positives.-GOOD VISUALS:I have to admit the visuals of this game are pretty nice, not quite as good as bdo however the visuals are definitely up there.-MOUNT SYSTEM:I find it pretty cool and satisfying that you start off from the very beginning with land mount, flying mount and water mount. (Note the flying mount is more like a gliding mount though)-LEVELING:Some might disagree that its good and thats okay, but to finish the Main story it legitimately takes around 6-7 hours if you speedrun it. I am a big fan of this as casual players no longer need to wait months to reach endgame like other mmos. At the moment the endgame of this game is lackluster but it is a new mmo so it gets the pass.-GEAR PROGRESSION:Although I have spoken about the dungeon drop problem, the gear progression is quite nice. You can level up your lower rarity gear(which uses easier to get materials) to then transfer your enhancement level to a higher rarity gear without using the harder to get materials. Example: Transferring a +9 blue gear into a purple to make it + 6-SKILL ANIMATIONS:The skill animations of this game are very satisfying and flashy and feels like there is power to them. This makes pvp combat actually fun regardless of what i said about pvp. If you like BDO combat then you will also like this combat.-NUMEROUS PLAYSTYLES:Similar to GW2 where you can have different skills depending on what weapons you have on. This makes it so there is a lot of variety in builds. Want to tank and heal at the same time? You can do it. Want to be a hybrid healer and burst dps? You can also do that. Want to go all in and do massive burst damage? You got it. -FREE TO PLAY:With this game being free to play I would say that it is actually worth atleast giving it a shot if you are curious, however note that because of this it is p2w.TLDR: The game suffers from hundreds of glitches(Many gamebreaking), terrible drop rates, untradeable dungeon drops and potentially unbalanced pvp. If you do not mind these and do not care about making more than 1 character,  then you will be rewarded with a smooth and fast leveling process, satisfying skills/visuals, great build variety and good ssf gear progression.Final Rating: 6/10 when compared to other mmos. Close to no originality

_childDocuments_.review: This review is coming from a casual long-time MMO player through the years. I do buy the battle passes and once in awhile will spend a little bit on the auction house, but have only spent maybe $60-80 so far on this game, beyond that you are just blowing your money and bypassing content. Overall so far this is the best non-WoW MMORPG I've played since Rift and Aion back in 2011/2012. Graphics are gorgeous and the best I have seen in an MMO. The PvE events/dungeons (~15 of them)/open-world dungeons (5 currently) are all a lot of fun, most trash monsters aren't too difficult but the bosses can have a lot of one-shot mechanics. If you like doing dungeon after dungeon and doing open world dungeon grind groups then this could be the game for you with it's continuously small but consistent long term character progression. The game actually is engaging as a community/socially, something I haven't seen in MMOs in a long time. Not everything is perfect though. The PvP is not very balanced at all since there is no specific PvP gear in the game, and there are LOTS of minor equipment and skill upgrades (long term character progression) in the game, so a fresh 50 is straight up fresh meat compared to someone that has been living on the game since launch. As a fairly fresh 50 the large scale PvP sieges and events hasn't been my thing since I typically just die so quick, but I'm also not a PvP focused player generally. There are some bugs here and there in the game, and the combat could be made a little more fluid, but it is still better than 90% of the MMOs I have played. The combat abilities do mostly at least feel impactful though. The community can be a bit toxic at times especially to newer players in dungeon/raid groups, reminds me of old PvP realms on WoW back in its heyday.. but hey at least this game does emphasize community and being social. Right now the monthly battle passes are cheap ($10), and the game doesn't have too much pay-to-win unless you are willing to spend hundreds or even thousands of dollars on a character, which realistically very very few players would be willing to do that. Paid currency is also obtainable through selling items on the auction house, so in the end it is no different than the WoW token system as far as pay-to-win goes. Hopefully NCSoft and Amazon Games can keep the content updates and game improvements coming on this game.. if so it will definitely have a successful life as it has the most potential of any new MMOs I've played in the last 15 years.

_childDocuments_.review: As a veteran MMO gamer, I found several issues with this game after achieving level 20 and 8 hours of gameplay.Story: While the opening video is well-animated, the lore is minimal, making it hard to get invested. Town names like "Moontown" or "Crescent Town" (even the voice acting could not save the fact it was confusing at best) feel generic and uninspired, reminiscent of "Wizards 101." The overall narrative seems dumbed down.Controls: I tested both keyboard/mouse and controller setups. The controls felt clunky, especially when switching between weapon styles. Targeting was frustrating, with frequent lock-on issues. The controller was slightly better, but the grappling mechanic was still unreliable.Game Play and Events: The open world PvE events, similar to those in RIFT and other MMOs, provide some nostalgia. However, high-level players often dominate these events, making it difficult for lower-level players to compete. Moderation is key—no event should be monopolized by the same group. Gear primarily comes from crafting, so drops aren't a major concern.Dungeons: Seem to be the main source of drop income forced to party up queues can take a while before you can actually get in based on your class there are a lot of Tanks and Healers or there are too many DPS. It feels as though T&L should have taken notes from FFXIV and had the first dungeon with NPC's but you dont even get to your first dungeon till level 20.Character Creation: The character creation system is impressive, though the feature to import character images is currently broken I could not get it to work at all either from QR code or import from my files.Micro-Transactions: I dont like the idea to pay to win in an MMO the idea is to enjoy the journey but because guilds will need to hold territory in the game you need people that can play fast and quick but not good. I never liked micro-transactions I think companies are getting too greedy. _childDocuments_.review: I cannot express how insulting this point system in ''Arena'' is to anyone who takes gaming even remotely seriously. The very essence of competition is completely annihilated by a mechanic that rewards players regardless of their performance. In what universe does it make sense for someone who spends an entire match getting obliterated to still have a shot at winning? This isn't a battle arena—this is a glorified participation trophy simulator.The whole idea of "even if you die all the time, you have a chance to win" is stupid beyond belief. It undermines every shred of skill, strategy, or effort put into the game. Why bother improving? Why bother learning the mechanics? Just run around, die, and somehow, you might still end up on top. It's a slap in the face to players who actually put in the time and energy to master the game.This system doesn't promote fair play or competitiveness—it encourages laziness and luck. It reduces every match into a chaotic circus where outcomes feel random and undeserved. If the developers wanted to make a casual, consequence-free experience, they should’ve created a sandbox, not a mmorpg.To say this point system is a failure would be an understatement. It’s a complete mockery of the idea of skill-based gaming. If the goal was to frustrate and alienate players who value competence and growth, then congratulations—it’s working brilliantly. Fix it. Immediately. Or risk losing the respect of everyone who values a fair fight.

_childDocuments_.review: Its the early stages but the game is alright. I will say it is a big focus on large scale PVP with a consistent rotation of said events. Almost every hour you have a Guild PVP event, Open Conflict boss, or it just happens to be night so you raid a dungeon along with territory control being GvG in Rifts/Boonstones or AvAvA in something like a castle siege. The PVE in the game is pretty okay, There are Peace bosses and activities for those looking just to outscore others. There are dungeons to run to that are also good. At level 50, you will get enough chances to run 3 a day to pull loot. Note that I didn't say 3 runs, as you only pay to open the chest at the end. And the dungeons are actually pretty good, each having good mechanics and are a decent challenge to learn.Alright the elephant in the room... Lucent and non-large scale pvp. Lets start with non-large scale PVP. Currently the game does offer 3v3 arena match making and Dominion events. 3v3 is what you expect, but there isn't any gear balancing so you can get on a team with green gear vs full decked purple gear. Dominion events are effectively large scale PVP events with random teams, but since there isn't good routes of communication between the field of random players this often results in one team snowballing and the other teams struggling to play objective as there is no effective rally tools. I personally would enjoy the game trying to add some small gang content such as a PVP dungeon where you can only know your party while all other players are anonymous. This would give smaller guilds or off hours groups a competitive feel.Lastly... Lucent. This is the currency you pay for and its used also in the Auction House. Lets start with what Lucent buys directly. From there you are looking at the Battlepass (effectively $10 per month), Leveling pass (effectively $10 per character), and cosmetics. The battlepass and leveling pass do give you a jump start of materials, however most of these can be grinded out in the world rather easily. The main thing in the BP is the skins and morphs to give more cosmetics to choose from.And now the hot button; Lucent and the AH. Technically this is the "Pay 2 Win" claim most people are going to make. And in the purest sense of it. Your mainly going to be use the AH to buy and sell either weapon traits or if your lucky trade gear. Currently the prices of items are out of this world where a Chernobog SnS is costing 14k lucent, which is about $250 in straight lucent packs and competitive gear to that can be earned in dungeons at a reasonable rate. Most traits are more reasonable being sub 500 Lucent or less than $10. But in the end if you swipe for these your just rushing to the finish line and giving yourself less room to grow.For perspective on current power of players, its about 2300 to 2500. This can be obtained with blue gear if you work on getting your traits together.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot honestly recommend this game.It's incredibly generic - everything from the graphics, the storyline, the music, right down to the game mechanics all feel like poorer iterations of things that other MMOs do far better. Even the morph system (when you sprint you turn into a mammal, when you swim you turn into an water-based creature, when you leap from a tall place you turn into a bird) as a unique selling point feels completely half-cooked.The crafting system is incredibly basic. The cooking vibe feels like a direct rip-off from the Monster Hunter games. Even your magical little companions, Amitoi, are a rip off of the Palicos from the MH games.The biggest issue for me though is the loot system is designed in such a way that the strongest keep getting stronger so if you're late to the game you're going to have to spend real-time cash in order to drag yourself out of the doldrums. Which is likely part of the plan from the devs.The journey to 50 is "ok" but after that it really struggles because your progress absolutely falls off a cliff - you can't do enough damage to bosses to reach the contribution required for the good drops so those that are already strong keep getting the good gear to sell or to transform into beneficial traits. You'll get completely wiped on PvP events for the same reason.My one line summary would be; it feels like a jumped up mobile game.

_childDocuments_.review: Disadvantages:The gear itself offers very little variety. There are only four rarity levels: Gray (trash), Green (common), Blue (less common), and Purple (rarest). However, until you reach level 50, you’ll mainly be using Blue gear, and even then only minimally, as Blue and Purple items are not easy to craft. You need to get them from dungeons or through the lithography book (a fusion mechanic involving other items).Level progression from 1 to 50 takes around 30 hours, which I find too fast. In some parts, you can progress from level 45 to 50 very quickly through story quests.60% of the world map is not yet accessible, which is, in my opinion, the game's biggest drawback.After roughly 30 hours of gameplay, you move very quickly into the late game, which involves increasingly difficult dungeons, guild battles, and events with friendly fire, among other things.My feelings are mixed. Honestly, if it weren't for a friend of mine, I probably wouldn’t have ended up playing this game. The game feels a bit cheesy, especially due to the strange schizoid companion creatures called "Amitois." Personally, I miss the presence of other races. Just humans? Sorry. As a result, I would rate the game 4/5 stars, at most.Advantages:The game is free to play.Many mechanics have been optimized. Compared to other MMOs, you can really feel that the "pain" points from other MMOs have been learned from and improved upon.The game offers a unique opportunity to try out all classes on one character, thanks to the weapon types, and to further develop them. At the same time, you're primarily limited to two classes.The graphics are, to my knowledge, the best in MMOs currently.The music is very well done and orchestral. Music enthusiasts are sure to get a catchy tune stuck in their heads.There is no gear-level requirement. If you have the armor, you can equip it even at level 1.Disadvantages:The gear itself offers very little variety. There are only four rarity levels: Gray (trash), Green (common), Blue (less common), and Purple (rarest). However, until you reach level 50, you’ll mainly be using Blue gear, and even then only minimally, as Blue and Purple items are not easy to craft. You need to get them from dungeons or through the lithography book (a fusion mechanic involving other items).Level progression from 1 to 50 takes around 30 hours, which I find too fast. In some parts, you can progress from level 45 to 50 very quickly through story quests.60% of the world map is not yet accessible, which is, in my opinion, the game's biggest drawback.After roughly 30 hours of gameplay, you move very quickly into the late game, which involves increasingly difficult dungeons, guild battles, and events with friendly fire, among other things.Overall:If you're into boss fights, dungeons, or massive guild battles—especially Guild Bosses and their reward gear, which you can only defeat and challenge with a guild—this game will definitely fulfill your wishes. According to rumors, there’s even a battle with 1,800 players simultaneously on a server, which the gaming industry hasn’t seen before.My feelings are mixed. Honestly, if it weren't for a friend of mine, I probably wouldn’t have ended up playing this game. The game feels a bit cheesy, especially due to the strange schizoid companion creatures called "Amitois." Personally, I miss the presence of other races. Just humans? Sorry. As a result, I would rate the game 4/5 stars, at most.Therefore, I give it a critical 3.5-4/5 stars. There’s still a lot of room for improvement, but for what you get for free, it's definitely worth checking out for fans of this game genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Feel like I've given the game enough playtime to give a decent review, so here goes. Like any game it comes with the Pros and Cons. Warning, this is long, read at your own risk! Open World and MusicOn the level of gorgeous. Both from the textures and detail to the lovely soundtrack.Character CreationTop notch, but not quite BDO level creation. Excellent quality with a lot of options and colors. Still can't mess with hair though.Mainstory and Voice-oversThese are actually very good for an English translation of a Korean game, I was surprised. However, there can still be scene stuttering and skips, so this part needs a bit of optimization work.   PvE vs PvPIf you don't want to run into PvP at all, then you'd better look for another MMO. There is really no avoiding it in this game and you will run either PvP based events/bosses/dungeons in the open world. While you aren't forced to participate, you will most likely just walk right into something PvP oriented unintentionally. That being said, both the PvE and PvP are actually decent fun in the game.   CombatComing from a keyboard, the combat is actually fun and very in-depth, but it can be a bit confusing at first as there are so many options to build your character along the multiple choices in gear. (and yes, it's a grind) Think almost like at a GW2 level, but with stat building in the mix. But while there are options for both action and tab target combat, my experience with the action version has been less then decent and it is not on the same level as Black Desert or (rip) Tera. It's better to stick to the tab targeting while adjusting the in game settings for a better combat experience. Gear and LevelingThis could use some more work. The current gear pace cannot keep up with the leveling pace. You will probably find yourself stuck in mostly green gear until the lv50 cap just from doing the main storyline alone and find yourself heading straight into purple gear bypassing the blue gear entirely, making crafting anything a bit useless beyond the first grade. Currently the best purple gear (endgame atm) just drops from bosses and dungeons. Piece of advice, pay attention to the NPC tutorials and what the text says in the enhancement system! Crafting Also needs some more work. Besides the being a bit useless for the gear, it is also lacking in other areas. Certain mats are a grindfest to get and your Amitoi's (little yarn doll minions) can only bring back so many resources at once. This kind of puts you in a grid lock, so crafters be warned. Dungeons and BossesThese have actual tough and you-need-to-learn-mechanics-or-you-may-die deal. It's about near, but not quite, the later level FF14 dungeons/GW2 strikes level, but as of this review, the game doesn't have anything with raids for anything seriously hardcore yet. You will have party wipes. In other words they are fun and frustrating, so this part they have down pretty well. However, they are not level locked, so getting higher level help is an option as players will go back to these later to finish their codex. But do not think being carried will help later. Most of the dungeons are max level, you will need to learn s*it. World bosses are almost the same deal, but easier as the die-you-will-spawn-right-back-by-the-boss is a thing here. MovementIt sucks, period. While the standard flat-surface movement is good, when it comes to the parkour movement, its bad. Your character will be more often then not be jerked, jutted, killed and what will feel like rubber-banding (no its not your PC) all the way down the cliffs to the grapple chains. Those are a cool feature though.Computer PerformanceThe game is a CPU eater. I do expect to see some optimization down the road. While you can run this fine on big rigs it's best to follow the basic practice of adjusting the game's power flow to other cores and leave the main core free for the CPU power flow only (believe it or not most average gamers won't know about this) otherwise you are in for a lag fest and an overheated PC if you are running older tech. While you can run this with a lower gen i5 processor, it's not recommended for PC life.   Is it Pay to Win?I have not seen anything in the Cash Shop that gives anyone a stupid OP advantage yet, however, this is a Korean game, so I do not expect it to hold up on a no P2W status for very long or they add P2W items in the foreseeable future. The only thing I see that could be deemed P2W is the Auction House as you need do buy currency to purchase anything in there.  All-in-all, Throne and Liberty can hold your attention for a good while without having to just drop it on the fly, so here's hoping NCsoft does not screw this one up.

detailed_description: DRAGON QUEST BUILDERS + DRAGON QUEST BUILDERS ２ Bundle The block-building RPGs “DRAGON QUEST BUILDERS” and “DRAGON QUEST BUILDERS 2” are now available together as a bundle! ■Bundle Contents DRAGON QUEST BUILDERS (main game) DRAGON QUEST BUILDERS 2 (main game) About the Game The first title in the BUILDERS series, DRAGON QUEST BUILDERS, is bringing its handy crafting features to Steam! Gather, craft and build to defeat defeat the evil Dragonlord and restore Alefgard to it's former glory! In a world made out of blocks, everything that you see can be materials used to create! Farm ingredients, craft various items and build your base to unite the people roaming the ruins. From buildings to entire towns, you have the freedom to make your village your very own. ■ Story BUILDERS is set in the realm of Alefgard, the setting for the first ever DRAGON QUEST game. The world of Alefgard has been plunged into darkness, its light stolen by the evil Dragonlord, and this story begins with the appearance of a young hero with a mysterious ability to build things... And so the stage is set for an epic tale in which the dark world of Alefgard is returned to life with the power of creation! ■ The first DRAGON QUEST BUILDERS title, helpful crafting features include:  Place blocks remotely, or destroy blocks with ease, with just a single click of the mouse!  Now Includes a helpful Undo feature, which allows you to put things back to how they were before!  Now Featuring Big Bash, a useful feature introduced in DRAGON QUEST BUILDERS 2 that allows you to break all objects in a particular area in one go!  Terra Incognita, BUILDERS’ free build stage, the stackable block height is doubled!  Includes fun side content, like collecting figurines of NPCs and monsters, or gathering pixels and exchanging them for a variety of handy items!  Use Build Cards to share buildings with other players and bring their buildings to life on your island! ■ Includes all DLC from previous versions of DRAGON QUEST BUILDERS! The Steam version of DRAGON QUEST BUILDERS includes all of the DLC from past versions including the free build mode, Terra Incognita: Magic Carpet, Boss Monster Model Set, Astronomy Set and Pixel Ring.
