Though we'll wait to see if anything like the infamous 'microscope' puzzle from the first game makes an appearance...So, again, I personally recommend this myself; I honestly played it for the first hour and had no idea it'd even been that long, so that's how much I was sucked in.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I'm running this on a 64-bit Windows 10, GeForce GTX 1060, i5-7500 3.4GHz, 16GB RAM, installed on a 250GB SSD, which is actually below the minimum specs in some areas, and then through the official Oculus Link cable to my Quest 2, and it runs more than well enough with all the in-game settings on full for me to enjoy it. I can imagine it must be much better running on a native PCVR headset and will also be better on Quest 3 native too (which is also going to get a proper update to take advantage of the extra power over Quest 2 there soon). The visuals, audio, and general atmosphere and stuff are all great imo, and no real bugs I've noticed. Other than a bit of fiddling with the hand interaction at times, none of which is a major issue, it's pretty great for what it is imo. Only thing I wish they'd add is an option to have the map and torch physically down by your sides so you just grab them directly with the grip buttons to use them like anything else in the game, which would leave the index fingers free for general pointing and stop me pressing the wrong buttons constantly when I just want to use the torch or map. Just a quality of life improvement I'd like to see there really.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore my play time -- I've completed this on PSVR2 -- it'll take about 7 hours to beat the game.  This is a pure and joyous reinvention and remaster of the original.  The 3D tech to make the ghosts come to life is phenomenal, and the puzzles are downright divine.  There weren't very many logical puzzle leaps, but it will challenge your skills.  One asked that you know chess, another some knowledge of advanced mathematics.  You can always work your way through them, even when it requires brute force, but each is fun and engaging.  Highly recommend this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: This game  was a great remake of the original 7th game.This  developer has updated the classic puzzle game into a modern masterpiece.  The original game  had great puzzles it was marred by  technical limitations (Lots of the plot was actually cut due to "Technical Limitations".)  While the original story was a confusing mess, the updated game manages to recreate the great atmosphere, have a ton of great lore fitting puzzles and tell a coherent story.  All of the guests feel more fleshed out and their motives are more clear.This is one of the best VR experience that I have played, Staufs Mansion is fully intractable, creepy and fun to explore.  It was a shame that there was no Flat Version, this  would have  been a best seller and reached more fans. Hopefully Vertigo Games keeps making VR games.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: This might very well be the best VR puzzler you can get your hands on.At its core, The 7th Guest VR is a very typical puzzle game. Puzzle design is for the most part logic based and always solid but by no means very innovative.The real star of The 7th Guest is its presentation. Visuals, music and general ambience are all top-notch and in part even groundbreaking. The use of volumetric video clips is outright impressive and serves as a testament to the power of the VR medium.For every friend of the occasional VR puzzler, I highly recommend giving this one a try. If you don't like puzzle games, this one will probably not change your mind, but it's still worth experiencing for its presentation alone.For a more in-depth video review see:
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Great atmosphere & revival of a classic. It strikes an interesting balance of the old-school feel of 90s FMV games and modern VR.The volumetric recordings feel like actual "video" that you can look at from all perspectives, if that makes any sense - they provide a noticeably different type of experience from flat videos and regular 3d animations. Really cool.Interaction with objects and puzzles is a bit clunky at times, and overall there is some jank, but considering the comparatively small and large ambition team behind it, this is nothing that spoils the experience as a whole.The puzzles are, for me, a good balance of being casual enough to solve without hints, while still giving you a sense of having figured out a clever solution, with only one puzzle being a bit tedious.Overall, well worth the price and a reasonably unique and pretty fun experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a fan of the 7th Guest since the 90s. Being able to actually walk through Stauf's mansion is a dream come true to me. The detail, the atmosphere, the cut-scenes, the music (bringing back some of the classics and it's own original score), and the puzzles. Absolutely breathtaking! To be clear, this is a complete remake of the first game. All of the puzzles are different (for the most part). The cut-scenes are done very well here! They are actual full-motion 3D scans of real actors and it just works fantastically. As a VR veteran, it has been a while since I lost myself in VR, and this game did just that. I lost all sense of reality and actually felt as if I was inside the mansion, solving puzzles, and getting to know each character and their fates.If you are a fan of puzzles games, get this! You will not regret it! As a fan of the 7th Guest series, this DEFINITELY did not disappoint! Here's to 11th Hour VR remake!
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant game, ruined by the horrendous inability for hand functions to properly work. I can't tell you how many times I've tried to open a cabinet door only for me to grip the wrong area, or once I grip it and begin the motion to swing it open for my "hand" to decide to let go of the knob/handle. I am currently trying to grab "coffins" for a certain puzzle and my hand highlights 1 and when I grab it I select a completely different one. I am getting beyond frustrated with just having simple VR designs not function properly and I will adjust my review when they fix it. Until then, this is a headache waiting for most VR enthusiasts.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Wow this game.  Some background:   I’ve done lot of VR.  VR reminds me of the wonder I had as a 14 year old getting my 386 PC and playing doom and syndicate and many other titles.  It allowed me to dial local  billboards (early micro internet) and take my pc to a mate’s house for a LAN party.The 7th guest and Phantasmagoria blew my mind because puzzles made you earn story progress and I loved horror so the darkness was enthralling.Now it’s 2023 and now Vertigo gives me this glorious experience in VR?  Pinch me.  And it delivers.Pros: almost everythingCons: some janky controls sometimes grabbing or maneuvering things but it’s a small thing9.5 out of 10Thanks Vertigo, please take this review as inspiration for more (and scarier) titles like this. Many thanks.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the original 7th Guest back in the day, but was never able to finish it.  This has been a great re-envisioning of the game.  Puzzles aren't quite as difficult as I remember from the first game (could just be me though), but they're well made and fun.  Game took me just under 8 hours to play, but it felt like a good length for the game.I hope this does well enough for them to want to make the 11th Hour in VR.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: You can view my review & gameplay here: This is a very good classic puzzle adventure game remade for VR and modern audiences. The good news is that there are high production values here and there is a huge variety of puzzles with a huge spooky mansion to explore. The bad news is that the puzzles are not very challenging and the story / acting is a bit campy.  I would say the game is perfect for puzzle beginners as it's impossible to be stuck in this game. There are two hints for each puzzle and there's also a coin auto-solve (you find coins everywhere and can use them to auto-solve a puzzle for you). I would recommend against using these coins as all the puzzles are pretty straight-forward. All but one of the puzzles are fully self-contained (you can solve puzzle in the same room). Each room has about 2-3 puzzles. As soon as you solve one room, another one automatically unlocks. Game auto-saves after every solution or event.The story does start out a bit confusing, because there are so many characters and you're not really sure why you are there. However, by the mid-point of the game, the story does start to come together. The 3D holographic models gives the game a bit of an extra spooky feel to it. The problem is that almost the entire story and the acting are pretty cheesy / theatrical. So it's not as scary as it might have otherwise been due to this. The atmosphere and the musical soundtrack are excellent though. There's a lot of attention to detail in the mansion itself and it's fun to explore it.Game is running on the Unreal Engine. On my RTX 3080, I was getting a steady 90 fps (or 72 fps on Quest 3) on high graphical settings with super-sampling set at 110%. I did not experience any major issues or bugs. However, some VR interactions were clumsy, such as having to play the piano keys. My screen also went black anytime I hit a boundary which happened a bit too much. You do have full locomotion or teleportation available, along with smooth or snap turning. You can choose dominant hand. You can play seated or standing.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice game.I nearly didn't buy it because I can't stand horror games and much less in VR but it's mostly a mystery game with no jump scares.Puzzles are fine, not too easy, neither too difficult. Puzzles are are contained in each room so no need to keep track of objects o clues hidden in different places.I bought it with a 40% discount (18€) and took me around 6 hours to play it.It didn't play the original game but this one, in VR it's worth it
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Bought for the price of a movie and enjoyed on a Quest 2 VR headset.Initially was quite stuttery and jumpy, played through Virtual Desktop as AirLink crapped out on me for some reason, many months ago and despite several updates and attempts to get it reworking it never works - everything else (Virtual Desktop/SteamLink) does - so well done Meta, keep up the great work! Anyway, switched over to SteamLink which opened up flawless game play, so that is what I would recommend to play this.I've been into VR for years, since Google Cardboard and Oculus DK2 etc. I've played most of the relevant VR content out there, and this is a top notch experience that I really enjoyed and got fully immersed with.The detail is the mansion is amazing, each room is full of detail to explore and take in, and the volumetric acting is absolutely gorgeous, the acting itself is brilliant, the sound and atmosphere is perfect, I absolutely loved it and wish there were more games that took this formula.Despite what others have said, some of the puzzles are challenging, others are fairly straight forward, but I ended up with plenty of "pass" coins left over at the end so could have made it easier if I so wanted. Yes it is very easy if you find the coins and just want to "pass" all of the challenges, but where is the fun in that! Ultimately, it is as difficult or as easy as you want your play through to be and if i wanted to go back and be a completionist, I think there would be a few more hours in there for me yet.A lot of people complain about the Steam rating system only having "Recommend" or "Not recommend", if there was an option for me I would go for "Strongly Recommended", this is what VR should be about and I wish they would make more games like it!
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful adaptation of The 7th Guest.  Loved being there in VR.   Challenging but not horribly difficult puzzles and games.  The characters are wonderful, true to shady, oily character leading to the evil character at the top!  Loads of fun.   Took me about five hours off and on to complete.  Realy puzzlers? :) will probably finish in less time.  Recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Yes definitely recommend this game! Sadly I already finished it. I never managed to figure out how to use the Stauff coins though. It felt like my board didn't want to use the help/ progression part, but that might be on my end. I only struggled with the piano puzzle. Every other puzzle was not too easy, but also not too hard to solve. It was the good mix of puzzles.Lots of fun, lots of nostalgia. Thank you so much for remaking this. The acting/ voice acting and everything brought me back to 30 years ago. Stepping in the hallway for the first time made me emotional being hit by the nostalgia bat.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: Check your height settings. The floor was off, which seemed to be the major cause of motion sickness. Have been able to play a couple of rooms without issue. MUCH betterI love the puzzles and being back in the world but I am having a VERY hard time with motion sickness in a way I don't in other games. It seems very shaky to me somehow, and I can't play for more than 5 minutes without a break.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: This is more like a mid review. Not bad, not great either. First up, the graphics and specially the way human actors are made in 3D is excellent, it is obvious they spent effort to make the game look and feel great.However, majority of the puzzles are too simple, there are hardly any interesting ones. Either they are those boring ones like pressing buttons to make a pattern which pretty much can be solved by trial and error, or they are pretty easy to figure out, just annoying to implement. Some of the puzzles I have no idea how I solved them exactly or they seemed bugged. Overall, very "light" puzzle game, not for me who is pretty hardcore in this genre. Next I think I will try out Raven remake to experience actual challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original 7th Guest way back in the 90s when Full Motion Video games were kind of the rage, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ was it the most punishing puzzle game on the PC ever to exist at the time. I still loved everything about it, and played it a few times to really get as much as I could out of it.Fast forward to now and Vertigo Games probably made the best love-letter to The 7th Guest possible, while also again trying to push the limit of media technology and show what a platform is capable of. The OG 7th Guest came on a few CDs and had really demanding CDROM specs in order to even get it to play well enough to enjoy. This one requires a little bit of a good PC and headset to get the best graphical fidelity out of, but even with reduced settings I still think Vertigo Games knocked it out of the park.Tonally the acting and video graphics absolutely matched the vibe of what a modern take on T7G would look an feel like. The design of the house and the game mechanisms within are also extremely appropriate. The team really did the best job they could and you can tell they respected the source material a lot.My only complaints are that some of the puzzles are too easy, and sometimes you have to force your character to clip into the environment to operate the puzzles--especially if you're playing seated. I think they wanted a wide range of appeal and to also appease fans of the original game, so in that regard it's a success. There's no reason not to play it. I hope they're selling lots of copies because this should be a title that helps sell VR and especially PCVR.This is one of the best VR games I have played in 2024 (even if it came out in 2023.) I hope they also work on a modern remake of The 11th Hour, because I never really got to experience that game and I've always heard the story was a little weird.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best VR puzzle games available. Took me about 6 hours to finish and is a very pure puzzler with lots of rooms with puzzles that require using your hands to move and manipulate things in the game. Some of the hand interactions were a little Janky but not enough to ruin the game and after finishing it I highly recommend any Puzzle fan to pick it up.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: It was a great experience!  I loved the ghostly characters acting out scenes and the creepy environment was awesome.  Puzzles weren't all easy but I didn't run into any issues where I wanted to hit my head off a wall due to frustration.  I felt the graphics were done beautifully and there was plenty of lore laying around to add to the overall story.  Honestly though, Vertigo Games are one of my go to developers as I feel they put work into their games and there not overpriced tech demos.  All that said, puzzle games are my favorite for VR as they seem to utilize more VR mechanics than the other genres which adds to the immersion.  So if your a puzzle goer and/or just looking for something other than the hundreds of VR FPS or Adult games currently blowing up Steam give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: You know those VR escape room games and how there aren't enough good ones? Okay, so imagine that, but instead of escaping you're learning about a story that is portrayed by the literal ghosts of the past all with the quality and polish of Arizona Sunshine. That's this game.The original  was a point and click puzzle game made back in 1993 made by . Old as heck models, simple design, and intentionally convoluted layout. What it did great was provide a great story, simple yet difficult puzzles, and "spooky" stuffs that somehow makes the player feel unnerved without a single jump scare. There were many issues that original game had, mainly due to the old software and hardware it was made with. The game had a brilliant art direction, while still being goofy and scary at the same time. It's odd playing it now. The uncanny aspects of it feel almost intentional. The  issues was the game ran (and still runs) very slow. Moving around is very time consuming so they had a bunch of goofy shortcuts that teleport you to various places in the house. The other issue is that it's not linear, so it becomes very easy to get lost and having to backtrack . The game still has a lot going for it, even with it's glaring issues. They actually made a sequel called . While I have yet to play that one, it came out a year after so I don't really see much reason to. They also released a remastered  with updates graphics and movies, better audio, a map, cutscene skipping, and a couple more improvements.THIS is not a remaster. This is an entire re-imagining of the game by  (the people who made ) . They recreated the whole game from the ground up for a VR suited experience. Everything from the models, to the puzzles (except for the one chess puzzle, but that was perfect anyhow). This game beautifully captured the original heart and soul of the game and let that guide their every action in this new game. I was impressed with literally every puzzle. Not one felt convoluted or out of place. One of the biggest issues a lot of VR games have is that they are easily translatable into a desktop format. But NOT this game. Remember that one puzzle from Alyx with that pipe wheel? That's this ENTIRE game. I literally struggled trying to think of how to make like 80% of the puzzles into a desktop version. So many of them require the ability to look around it and using your hands. Sure some of them could be, but it would end up being easier. The challenge is what makes this so enjoyable.The game isn't like super duper epic models, but that's intentional. It has a great style, one you can see from this studio, but man did they outdo themselves on this one. There is so much detail in every nook and cranny, and looking gives you a bit of a reward taboot. On top of the visuals being stellar, the audio was mouth watering. This game has NO jumpscares, but I kept turning around and looking behind me cause of the noises and sounds. And as for the ghosts, they didn't do a typical modeling and rigging, nor a video screen, they had real life actors be recorded by volumetric cameras so their expressions and movements feel sooooo lifelike, And for the acting itself, WOW did they do a great job! Especially near the end. Everyone had become one with their character and played them perfectly. I hope they go further in their acting careers.The game is now linear, now pointing you in the next direction making the story so much more understandable. The way they implemented the old map system was genius, on top of the ability to use the lantern to find secrets and see into the past. It didn't feel like it held your hand, which is what made the original game so good. You had to figure out both the solution, AND the puzzles themselves. They combined the aspect of exploration and puzzle solving brilliantly. The last few puzzles were a lot of fun. Felt so dang satisfying figuring them all out.If you have a headset, I highly recommend you give this a play through. It's a lot of love and stands out among the usual VR puzzles we see. And it dosen't matter what you play with too! The controls are simple and translatable to all devices, even those Vive wands. And heck if you really want you can go into Steam's controller bindings and change it how you see fit. It's a wonderful adventure, even for only a couple of hours.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of variation in puzzles and "some real headscratchers" as Stauf himself described them.The volumetric capture fits suprisingly well with the stylized art direction.There is hints/solutions available if you scavange for the hidden coins.Supports both teleport and smooth locomotion.Encountered very few bugs:I was able to get unstuck by using teleport movement.So far I have not encountered any game-breaking bugs or crashes, and I did not encounter any on the first playtrough.I wish once you complete the game, you could go back to any puzzle you want to replay or be able to re-watch the volumetric captures. But anyhow
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not usually very good at puzzle games but this was an enjoyable 6 hours all the way through without being too difficult. The puzzles are all self contained, so you know everything you need will be right there. This cuts down on useless back tracking, and makes everything more streamlined. It's all so creative and memorable, the actors are fantastic, the lamp was constantly interesting, the paintings are everywhere between hilarious and creepy. I totally recommend The 7th Guest.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: For anyone that isn't in the know, The 7th Guest was originally an old horror/puzzle game from the early 90's, back when survival horror was barely a concept genre wise. Back when titles like Alone in the Dark were still new, innovative and... well... good...The 7th Guest was in that ballpark. At it's core, it's a puzzle game and little more, but with a spooky coat of paint thrown onto it that gave the original a feel and ascetic that made it unique and interesting for the type of game it was. The new VR version of this game isn't much different, and is effectively the same game the original was. But here's the thing: It's everything the original was, but updated for the times!There's plenty of situations where this could be seen as a bad thing, but that's not the case here! The nature of VR as the medium for this version of the game breathes a whole new life into The 7th Guest that probably wouldn't have been possible otherwise, giving a player the ability to actively roam and explore the haunted grounds of Stauf Manor in ways the original couldn't allow! While the overall story from the original is largely unchanged, the means for uncovering that story and the mystery it holds is presented in the venue in entirely new (if familiar if you've played the original) puzzles that help to breath that new life into the old game that I was talking about! After all is said and done, this version of The 7th Guest is way... WAY too cool to not play if you have the ability to do so!Get this one! From the engaging puzzles, spooky vibes, and general camp that still exists from the original game, the VR remake of The 7th Guest will not disappoint!
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know what it is about this game but its sooo uncomfortable to play. I get motion sick so fast, the HMD tracking seems to shake a lot. I'm sure its not me (hell, I'm a dev on one of the most popular VR games so you'd think I'd know!)... and I've definitely seen others complain about this too. I don't think I'll be playing anymore of it, its just not an enjoyable experience despite actually being quite entertaining as a game.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: From the environment-altering lantern to the cheesy but impressive 3D FMV sequences, I adore the presentation of The 7th Guest’s spooky mansion. It’s just the right level of eerie. There are enough unseen noises, ominous shadows, and foreboding music to keep you on edge and give you a few goosebumps, but it never goes as far as to outright scare you. The mansion itself is full of detail and VR is the perfect medium for these spaces. A game like this wouldn’t be the same on flatscreen.Most of the puzzles are soundly constructed, visually appealing, and properly mysterious. No two feel alike. When they’re not offering an interesting mental trial, they’re supplying a tactile sequence. However, some actions such as rotating cranks, precision picking up/putting down, and pushing only one of several densely grouped buttons are still tasks VR can’t quite realistically handle. But outside of those spatially dissonant or meaty-handed moments, I’d reckon that the game does an above-adequate job with its haptics.It should be noted that there are a couple of puzzles that are pulled from the roster of tedious mini-games you’d find in a tactless escape room. The sort you’ve done before at some point and either see as trivial or an instant pace-killer. Thankfully, there’s a healthy number of puzzle-skip coins to help keep things moving (Tip: try to save ten coins in case you ).If you like solving puzzling rooms, have VR, and enjoy a little bit of spookiness in your life, The 7th Guest VR is an on-sale no-brainer, especially if it happens to be around Halloween.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. Clocked it in about 9 hours, but I missed a few collectables and achievementsPros:+Very atmospheric (visually and aurally)+Respects source material+Great texture work with paintings that change before your eyes as you shine your lantern+Creative puzzles that didn't outstay their welcome+3D live cutscenes I have never experienced before. Casually wander around live theatre. Great fun!+Collectibles galore. Can you find them all?Cons:-I missed seeing the original Stauf. He was in the 13th Doll recently, so a shame he couldn't make another appearance.-Didn't particularly like the last puzzle. I did it on my first try, but felt like chance more than skill. The 11th hour final puzzle was awesome I seem to remember-Experienced some minor typical VR jank, e.g feeling like I had to stretch my hands a bit too far on occasion. (I play stationary with a small room)Overall, well worth a play
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Escape room-style puzzle game with a ghost house theme. House looks good, and the game runs well. The lantern is very clever. A highlight is watching the cast act out the story in 3D volumetric videos, calling back to the similarly innovative (for the time) FMV clips in the original. Good variety of puzzles. Not too difficult, the solution to each room's puzzles are contained in the room. If you get stuck there is a hint system.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Really liked it. Nice puzzle variety, looks and sounds good. Spooky but not too scary (I also don't remember any jump scares). Originally bought it to play during Halloween but only finished it now but it would've been a good fit. Never played the original or its sequel but now I'm hoping for a remake of 11th Hour as well.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing VR port. Technically flawless. A throwback to the original, but improved in every way. All-new puzzles that work perfect in VR (I think only the "8 queens" puzzle is from the original, and the hardest).The mansion is breathtaking and the clever lantern mechanic and changing rooms as you solve the puzzles means you get to enjoy the mansion in two ways!Minimum specs are even exaggerated... played absolutely flawlessly on a GTX 1070 and an Oculus CV1 headset.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: It's among the most fun and better realized brain teaser games i tried, both flat and VR.I was attracted to this game in particular for the unique volumetric capture of the actors and was curious of how it would work out in VR. I was not disappointed and gives a very neat and unique style. About the actors and how they present the story, they are theatrical. So if you don't like this kind of recitation, it might bother you. Differently, is good as glimpsed in the trailer and in my opinion fit perfectly the style of the game.The puzzles and brain teasers vary greatly from one other but i enjoyed that the majority of them are about logic, deduction, memory and so on. Never too difficult, but neither too easy.Some of them are classic games but a bit reimagined or simplified, like sudoku or one that require you to know the very basic of chess, but to resolve a puzzle that have little to do with chess.Several of them are fun to the point i would consider doing another run of the game in the future.And probably i'll do it also to revisit the mansion with all of its paintings and portraits in very high definition and with cool effects when you point light at them. A very entertaining thing to do while exploring. In every new room, i spent a good amount of time just snooping around for those paintings.Also i tend to dislike a lot puzzle games where the "puzzle" to solve is finding the right items around the map, fortunally here is not the case, so if you are alike, you'll notice that and enjoy a lot more the game (there are some collectibles but that's for achievements hunting).The story in my opinion is nothing special, or personally it didn't catch me particulary, but as i wrote, in my opinion is very well told with good pace and is not in the way of the main focus of the game.Totally recommend to play.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice puzzles but not very nice VR interaction. Most movements / interactions are janky, not fluid, and interactions are limited basically to the puzzles you have to solve ( you can still grab bottles etc around the house but that's it).Graphically pleasant most of the time, with the nice addition of cool 3d scans of real actors.Some up and downs with framerate / artifacts on Quest 3 with virtual desktop, not sure why, if it's memory leak over time or just some compatibility issue (don't have any problems in any other game, you can check my specs on my profile if you want to know more), but overall everything was fine. Height worked weird for me...sitting or standing, I was either too tall or too short compared to the in-game world. SteamVR gets disabled for some reason (at least with Virtual desktop) so cannot override room scale from there. Nothing game breaking though but will make seeing / grabbing some coins more difficult, in case you are too small compared to the game scale (the ghosts also look weirdly bigger compared to beds and chairs).
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I was enjoy it while i had my Oculus cv1 and i upgrade to index and now i can't play it and keep get a fatal error and even had my friend test it on his and same thing so !WARNING! if you have Index or Quest you have a bigger chance it wont launch. Until they patch it it wont work. Will update when they fix it.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. I highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys quiet, stress-free, exploration-type puzzle games.I was very impressed with the graphics, textures, and imagination behind the puzzles and environments, all of which is on a par with Cyan's VR games (Obduction, Myst, Firmament).Though some of the puzzles may be inspired by those in the original game 7th Guest, they are completely reinvented or new, and very well made. Most of the puzzles are different from each other. Only a very few of the many puzzles are based on a common principle, but they are so different in appearance that I didn't mind.In my opinion the puzzles are just right in terms of difficulty. Not immediately obvious, but also not taking forever to figure out. And more importantly, no busy-work, i.e., no puzzles where it takes forever to solve even when you know how to do it. Once you know the solutions, you go through the puzzles very quickly.The acting is great, theatre-like, and very entertaining. This is the first time I encountered "volumetric capture" in a game, and it blew my mind. The live actors are completely 3D and you can run around them and watch from all directions while they play out their scenes. It was like being on a holodeck in Star Trek, except the characters don't interact with the player.The atmosphere is fantastic, generated by a combination of surroundings, music and noises. Occasionally there's a  which made me jump. Not a  but if you do notice it, the effect is quite powerful. With all that atmosphere, by the time I got to a room with  it took some mustering of courage to even approach.People have complained about the finale, but I thought it was awesome and fun, and I enjoyed walking around and taking it all in.I found only a few minor cons with the game overall. One is that you can't save and later go back to an earlier point in the game. Which would have been fine except there's one rather important place that is easily missed, and later there's no way to return to that place. If you miss it you have to start the game over if you want to see that place. Though according to the Steam forum you can work around that by manually copying the autosave file.The game ran fine, with no glitches, crashes, jitter etc, on my system: Windows 10, SteamVR, Valve Index, RTX2080, i9-8950HK CPU @ 2.90GHz. Except on two occasions, when I had to relaunch the game to continue. Once when the game didn't acknowledge that I had solved a puzzle, and once when the moving parts on a puzzle refused to move. In each case, once I relaunched the game, I got unstuck.That said, these few cons are to me very minor, and I will remember this game as one of the greatest VR experiences of my life.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Great cosy game that is quite unique in the vr genre so far. The story / storytelling could be better, however, while being short, I liked the narration of the toymaker's life story a lot. The atmosphere and puzzles felt like a blend of Syberia, Cluedo and the Haunted Mansion at Disney World. There is some beautiful cello music. Graphics are a tiny bit questified but still looking good. I guess when handled like this everybody (standalone and pc users) can be happy.A few of the beautifully crafted puzzles can get quite challenging. In case you get stuck you can buy hints with coins you find. Shining the magic lantern on stuff lets you see former or different versions of  paintings, flowers etc. which is very fun to try on everything. A good portion of my almost 15 h playtime was admiring every single bit of art.And: For the first time in a vr game in a certain room I could pull a curtain which moved totally impressive like real life!It is definitely one of the best vr games of 2023 and gave me good vibes.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who knows nothing about original 7th Guest game, I came into this one blind and was immediately blown away. Originally having my eye on this since the Meta Game Showcase back in the Summer, I anticipated playing this game for a while and it definitely delivered.The puzzles were challenging and diverse. There probably wasn't a single puzzle I disliked other than the bathroom ones. But luckily, the game provides you with tokens you can use to auto-solve puzzles for you in case they are too hard. But of course, the tokens are hidden so you'll have to find them throughout the rooms. The one thing I do wish was changed is the cost of solving each puzzle. It felt like there was an abundance of tokens, but I'd rather each solve be more expensive so the player has to think harder about whether or not it is worth it to use tokens on certain puzzles. Or, you can be like me (and I assume most people) and solve all the puzzles organically, in which the game allows you to choose either path. Either way, I think the 7th Guest's method of helping players who get suck on puzzles is much better than other games that would instead hold your hand through each step. Though do be prepared to be hit with an insult occasionally for each failed attempt.The biggest positive of the game, in my opinion, must be that each puzzle has to be created and coded independently. You'll come across a puzzle and realize: "wow, the developers programmed the ability to do such and such, only for it to be used in ONE puzzle?" It is the attention to detail and the effort put into each small section of the game that makes this experience so rewarding to play through. Often times, you will see games in which various content uses the same game mechanics recycled, but the 7th Guest is not one of those games and instead takes it to the next level in terms of individuality for each puzzle. This is something many people take for granted, but I do think it should deserve recognition whenever it is present.In terms of replayability, there isn't really much of that. But that's okay. In my opinion, puzzle games like this one, with a linear story, aren't meant to be played more than once. It's the initial experience that matters, and that's what I came here for. Maybe some might think a $30 game isn't worth 5-8 hours of gameplay, and normally I would agree, but this game is an exception in my books.Overall, I highly recommend this game, especially for VR enthusiasts. Lately I have been playing more VR games, and the 7th Guest is a fantastic reminder of why I fell in love with this medium to begin with.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: This succeeds as an incredible showcase for VR, a delightful modern adventure game and as a beautiful, charming tribute to the original. The puzzles fully take advantage of the medium, were exactly tricky enough to be interesting without overstaying their welcome and were well integrated into the environment. Other stuff: I love the just slightly larger than life performances and the updates to the story (the way Eleanor is handled, especially). The "scary but mostly fun and spooky" atmosphere is so rare nowadays, and I love that I have an interactive ghost story that I can also share with my 10 year old daughter. The way the original musical motifs were handled and, as a huge fan of the original, the music chosen for the credits (surprised by how it made me tear up).Unless you actively hate VR, puzzles and spooky stories, play this if you have the chance. Or maybe just give it a try regardless.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the original game and this is a great re-imagining of it.  All the puzzles are really fun to solve except the last one, which is more like snakes and ladders than a puzzle.  The live action video works really well for ghostly figures in VR and the haunted house atmosphere is fantastic with a lot of items that can be interacted with.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original 7th Guest a long time ago, and up front I was afraid this version would not live up to the old game. But I was wrong. It brought back the same atmosphere and exitement, and it being in VR made it so much more immersive. The VR now what I missed then, without knowing it. I enjoyed every minute of it. I hope more of the classics come back in VR. Phantasmagoria for instance.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: While there is a lot of room for improvements on PC VR (many of the textures are relatively low-quality, for example), this title does run reasonably well and overall looks and plays well. The puzzles are fairly difficult and fun, and the atmosphere/vibe is great. Minor quibbles: the motion capture was probably done at 24 or 30 fps. It's OK, but there is a bit of jerkiness about them as it doesn't look like they are playing at a rate that matches the user's chosen refresh. It also have major issues with Wide FOV HMDs, which means Parallel Projections must be used, dramatically reducing performance. If you have invisible objects (reptile-eye-gem at the start, for example) or strange issues with shadows as they move (decking of pier as planks move into place), then you'll need to turn on your Parallel Projections. Would have been great if the title hadn't needed that. On the other hand, it uses normal AA rather than TAA, which is a huge plus for this title. Not using TAA means that details and clarity are great compared with titles using TAA. If they would up the texture resolution for PC this title would look absolutely fantastic.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original 7th Guest with a bunch of friends in a strangers house on Christmas eve in Guatemala on 486 computer using the first CD ROM that I had ever laid eyes on. The experience was magical and even though the puzzles were mind numbing, the experience stuck with me at a level that when I returned to the states a year later, I built a computer and bought a copy of the game right away and then proceeded to hammer my head against my desk for hours while Stauff laughed at me. When I saw that it was being offered as a VR game, I didn't obey my rule of waiting for games to go on sale. I impulse purchased the heck out of it. I am not sorry that I did. Well done Vertigo! You took nearly everything that was fun and memorable about the first game, enhanced the experience, added some fun mechanics, and scaled the puzzles so that you don't want to throw your mouse at the wall while playing! win win win! The only thing that I missed was the spooky factor, which was a little less in this version. All in all though, a phenomenal effort! Easily ranks on my short list of VR games that I actually enjoyed playing. Thanks very much as well for providing options to either teleport or glide. Gliding makes me motion sick something fierce, but I still enjoy playing with it. It was nice to be able to turn it off when I couldn't handle it anymore, but it still gave me the chance to play with the mechanics a bit.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely terrific VR game! If you played the original point and click game, you're going to love this, it has new puzzles and was really built up from the ground for VR. It's not a remaster, it's a complete remake, a new interpretation of the game for a new generation using new tech. And if you haven't played the original - welcome to the Stauf mansion of the 21st century! I know you're going to love it here...  :) The game is gorgeous, it has some original mechanics (I'm looking at you, spirit lamp), and the combination of Full Motion Videos in VR is brilliant!The puzzles are well balanced, fun, and rewarding when you solve them on your own. And if you're stuck, there is a built in hint system. Plus the maintained the original atmosphere. A creepy old mansion, but no stupid jump scares. The scares come from the general feeling it gives you and the story as it unfolds. I definitely recommend this one!
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: This is a charming puzzle game with a light horror atmosphere.  It most reminds me of theme park experiences, and that's about the level you can expect regarding the acting.  However, I think the exaggerated and cheesy acting is appropriate for the game.  I haven't personally played the original, but from what I've heard from others who have, this game is considerably toned down regarding how gruesome it can get.  It's basically Haunted Mansion on PS2, but instead of lots of arcade style shooting mixed in with puzzles, this is all puzzles.If you're familiar with escape room style puzzles, you shouldn't have any issues with this game.  The difficulty is on the easier side, I'd say.  Nothing you need to take notes over (a concession for the VR, likely).  Nonetheless, it is fun to solve the puzzles, and you can essentially pick your difficulty: No hints, a riddle that can point you in the right direction, instructions on how to solve the puzzle, and outright solving it for you.That last point is important, as the game is unfortunately a little buggy.  I had a case where a door would not open, and I could not access a puzzle piece, so I had to do an auto-solve, robbing myself of the achievement for not using it, but I would just play it again if I really cared about the achievements.  Another criticism I can levy at it is that certain areas of the game look very poor graphically, specifically outside the windows of the mansion, and the model used for Stauf in certain areas.  Everything else looks up to par with great lighting (that sometimes is pointing to a hint).It is a relatively short game; if you're an experienced puzzle solver, you could probably beat it in about 6 hours.  If you're a miser like me, wait for it to go on sale; it happens regularly enough.  I managed to get it for just under $17 from Gamers Gate.  As I write this review, it is on sale from Humble Bundle for just under $20, though you can get it for that price on steam directly occasionally.  For that price, I can heartily recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the whole game until the end.  You spend the whole game using your brain and skill to solve puzzles and then the very last activity is some non-puzzle RNG nonsense.  I gave up on it, just watched the end on youtube to get my closure to move on.  End totally soured the game for me.  Changing the entire gameplay for the final battle is a game design sin, i hate all games that do this.  No idea if this was how the OG version ended or if this is something new but its not my jam.Played on a Pimax 8kx, 3080 gpu, all settings high except shadows were on low.  Performed fine, controls and tracking are fine little hiccups here and there.  Fun story, graphics were a good quality level , good exploration and collecting activities.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool re imagining of a classic. It did a great job at capturing the feel of old school puzzle/horror, while at the same time implementing some very unique modern mechanics. I have a feeling some of the elements of this game will be used in many vr games to come. Easily of one the best vr puzzle games available at the moment. Solid 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I never played the original game nor any of the remakes until this one.  The quality is very good, along with the performances of the actors/actresses.  I was worried about jump scares or having to "Run away" from danger since I have very bad motion sickness, thankfully this game didn't have that, although it did have one or two jump scares (intended and not intended).  The only problem I had was when the puzzles sat on tables or flat surfaces and if I physically moved the visuals would bob up and down several times. This also would happen on stairs or steps.  I would have to step back or quickly teleport elsewhere , but it would start triggering my motion sickness and soon after I'll have to take a break or stop altogether. I know this is the collision objects and trying to put me back into a location, so it's not a bug, I've experience this in other VR Puzzles game. other than that one small thing, it was fun. The puzzles weren't too easy nor too hard, the story was easy to follow, and overall an enjoyable experience.  I would play again.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I love that this is the first and only VR FMV game. Don't know how they converted 3D captures to polygonal models, it's rather rough mesh-wise but decent texture-wise, and it is an interesting look.The flashlight mechanic is fun and the house is handsomely rendered.Changes to the narrative make it a lot more coherent, less stupid and outlandish, and the puzzles are generally more sensible.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: BUY THIS GAME.For something over 30 years old, the story still remains iconic, the house is still haunting (as well as haunted) and I still never got to try the soup. I didn't have to solve the ultra-hard "try to get the game to start" puzzle of the original DOS version. (Bonus points if you remember that one...)Okay, let's be honest, I'll get the critical stuff out of the way. I was a little disappointed that Hirschboeck didn't reprise the role of Stauf for this game, and there are some times where maneuvering around is a little tricky when an interactable element should be reached.That said, the positives far outweigh the negatives. Bringing T7G to VR was a genius move. The mo-capped actors don't need to overact so much now that the resolution is better, and there are haunting phrases and melodies that bring to mind the vintage T7G game that popularized the optical drive in the 90's and made it a staple of computers and gaming consoles. Not surprising, since Matthew Costello, the original writer of T7G, takes up the task to update the masterpiece. And he does it well...while there are changes, it doesn't disrupt the continuity with games like 11th Hour and 13th Doll.New elements add to the gameplay. The puzzles can be vicious, but persistence pays off, and are still challenging for puzzle masters. The new Henry Stauf (Carl Wharton) brings his own dark magic to the game, being more of a horrendously evil version of Dr. Strange.In terms of the VR experience, they actually put in a full suite of control options, including being able to enable different movement modes and vignetting to reduce motion sickness. As a veteran VR player I didn't need the vignetting so much. There were one or two places where I got physically stuck, but teleport move was a great help.If this is the quality we can expect, let's see Tad finish his adventure in a VR version of 13th Doll, and experience the final battle with Stauf in a VR version of 11th Hour.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: For some reason the game gives me an old-style Disney movie vibe (when Disney was still good), and I see that as a good trhing. The mix of a CGI environment and real actors works fantastic. If you love solving puzzles where you have to figure out how they work before you can even begin solving them, this is absolutely a must-have. I did have some motion-bugs where I would suddenly turn 180° or make a jump sideways, but it wasn't that big of a problem. More games like this please!
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I can confidently say it’s a brilliant remake of the classic game. The eerie atmosphere and cleverly designed puzzles kept me engaged throughout. The use of volumetric video for characters enhances the narrative as past scenes unfold while solving challenges. Overall, this immersive adventure pays homage to its predecessor while offering a fresh experience. Completing all achievements was satisfying, making it a must-play for fans of narrative-driven puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty well put together game as far as VR titles go. The puzzles are satisfying to solve, and the environment is great for people who love spooky and unsettling without jump scare horror. The volumetric video capture scenes are really cool and do a good job of selling the narrative.Sometimes the physics are bit wonky or stiff and you have to try a few times to grab something, and if youre playing in standing-room only mode some times you might have to move yourself in-game close to a table and then walk forward irl to actually look down at something.All in all definitely worth the price if you like puzzles and murder mysteries.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful exploration experience!By the time I had taken notice of the original 7th Guest, hardware incompatibilities had made it unplayable. Stepping into the mansion now in VR feels like a present I've been waiting decades to open.Puzzles are engaging, graphical tricks are used to great effect, and the use of live actors proves as excellent a choice as it was in the 90's to convey the game's mystery.Especially welcome is the familiar melody of "The Game" :)
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty great puzzle VR game just in time for Halloween. They’ve very faithfully recreated the game, even using volumetric FMVs instead of trying to recreate the feel of live actors with 3D models. The puzzle are clever and utilized VR very well, making them intuitive to solve. VR really is the best way to give new life to point and click adventure style games and I’m hoping we see others, like say Scratches, remade to take advantage of what VR offers the genre or Brad new VR point and click style games.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Since playing the original 7th Guest back on DOS, and TBH, I did not really care much for the 11th Hour, but I have always wanted to see what Stauf's house would be like IRL.  Well, VR has gotten me pretty close to that experience.  This game has a feel, style, and gameplay very close to the original 7th Guest.  It is awesome being able to explore Stauf's house and it still has that creepy atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Fun game until the end, when it is terrible. Very low replay value.This is relatively fun right until the end. Without giving spoilers: The whole game is based on your ability to figure out puzzles and think creatively in the atmosphere of the world. They fixed the problem of "where the hell do I stand to trigger the cut scene" and the visuals are pretty.  The story is fun and the puzzles are challenging but not impossible. The only one I needed to self-solve was one where I couldn't physically FIND IT (no hints that the damn quilt on the dresser WAS the puzzle and not just decoration) and I decided to self-solve the tea party puzzle because it just looked tedious. The ending, though... that was bad. You're playing a two-player game against an opponent who always knows and runs the best possible moves, the rules and actions and strategy are not well explained, and you rely on DICE ROLLS for luck. Luck is the biggest driver of the end, and you need both luck and skill to win the last puzzle. That's fine on a desktop with comfortable seating and controls, but in VR it's just tiring and the controls for a board game are hardly as good as a desktop's point-and-click.  After a while, I gave up and had no desire to play it again (thus no desire to re-play the game.)
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love how this game looks! The atmosphere is wonderful and very well done, I definitely spent quite a while looking around and admiring paintings and other stuff :). I never had the chance to play the original game but my viewers who were checking this out with me told me they absolutely love this has been brought back! The puzzles are definitely challenging as the description mentions.The price for this title is really good as well. I cannot wait to unlock more rooms and continue the story!I have the Oculus Quest 1 and it works great.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I’m playing PCVR using Quest 2 and Virtual Desktop. I run AAA titles without any problems.The 7th Guest is a haunted house where every room is a puzzle room. The graphics are great and the the puzzles are very logical and can be solved pretty readily. It started out fun and had a lot to offer.Unfortunately, The 7th Guest follows the typical VR modus operandi: release a game before it’s ready, wait for the customer to be your quality tester, and then release a patch. It’s too bad because this could have been a great game. It just has too many bugs. The collision boxes are huge. It stutters and lags where the worst VR game doesn’t. I’m about half way through and it’s just getting frustrating- the fun is quickly channeling out. I recommend the game but at $32 it’s an insult.Update: Downgrading to "do not recommend." After reaching the attic and the last parts of the game it became unplayable. Constant "out of bounds," freezing, stuttering, losing hand tracking- I gave up and won't be able to finish this game. Ran all the diagnostics and overlays, pc is tight, no problems with any other game. I won't buy anything from this company going forward.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Never heard of this franchise before so I had no idea what to expect. It's a good puzzle mystery. Works well in VR. Haven't experienced any bugs or glitches. I've really got no complaints. Works great on Virtual Desktop. VR needs more quality games. The main complaint I hear from people is that they don't think a puzzle game is worth 30 dollars. Pretty sure this would be a lot of buyers if it went on sale. I personally don't have a problem paying 30 dollars to support VR developers, especially if the game is quality. Plus it's got achievements, which is more than a lot of VR games can say.UPDATE: So after playing a lot more, I can see a few things that need to be patched. I keep getting the same exact "Stauf Chronicle" thing over and over and I know that there are supposed to be more than just the same one laying everywhere because there is an achievement to collect them all. The game is extremely basic and short. The entire environment feels dead. You can interact with stuff in the sense that you can pick things up or throw them but that is the extent of how interactive things in the environment are. If you throw a glass bottle, it doesn't break. Swinging a cleaver at a piece of meat doesn't feel fulfilling because nothing happens. It just all feels lifeless. So they really aren't playing into the VR aspect that well. It's a good game for what it is but might be a little overpriced. Plus the rooms always have this weird mist overlay before you complete a room and honestly, it just makes the lenses look fogged up and very bad on my brand new Quest 3. Windows have handles on them to open them but you can't open any of them. The outside textures of the house, looking outside from in, look ugly and warped. Not sure if that is a stylistic choice but.... it's ugly.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Man alive, this is a fantastic retelling of the 7th Guest. All the characters are there, played by new actors. I am grieved that Robert Hirschboeck didn't reprise his role as Henry Stauf; no one else could do  quite like him. But it would be impossible to get the original cast to re-act the scenes given the thirty-year timegap; Debra who played Martine Burden wouldn't be as seductive as she was three decades ago.What is cool is that all of the scenes are played out by actual actors just like the original, shot with volumetric video, not 3D rigs; it's like walking on a holodeck and seeing a recorded video shot from every angle.A little artistic license was taken but the story seems consistent with the canon, with Stauf's past and his relation to the seven guests expanded upon) and a lot more ordered (not fragmented and randomized as in the original).So far, there are several nods to the original. The chessboard puzzle in the game room is instantly recognizable (if you played the original) but also requires a short scavenger hunt to complete, making the whole room akin to an escape room. In the dining room, you get to see something familiar when you solve its puzzle. The Stauf Mansion is a bit different from the Nunan Estate the original was modeled after, and the layout is more consistent with the exterior, but it's easily recognizable both in and out. And you may recognize the music if you listen carefully; it's a different arrangement but early on you can hear bits of the original melody ( is the most obvious).Let's talk spookiness... Though it takes place in what is effectively a haunted house, much if not all of the creepy factor is atmospheric; I've finished and seen zero jumpscares. You may feel some trepidation in your first playthrough (I did, but I feel that way about all 3D games) but there's nothing dangerous. In my opinion, the  was  far creepier ().In short, I found this to be a great successor to the original 7th Guest, with the same story spiritually and a familiar feel throughout, with some new elements to deepen the experience. If you're a fan of The 7th Guest, and you have an Oculus Rift S or Steam VR headset, you should take the time to find out what's inside, away from all the wind and rain.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: The standout feature of The 7th Guest VR is its ability to breathe new life into a classic. While remaining faithful to the original, the adaptation leverages VR technology to create a nostalgic and fresh experience. The puzzles, the storytelling, and the atmosphere are all heightened in VR, providing players with a truly memorable and captivating journey.But even if you've never played the game.. If you like horror or adventure games you will find lots to enjoy here. With its hauntingly beautiful visuals, atmospheric audio, and seamless gameplay, The 7th Guest VR stands as a testament to the potential of bringing classic games into the VR era. For fans of the original and newcomers looking for a compelling and nostalgic adventure, The 7th Guest VR is a must-play. Prepare to be transported to a world where the puzzles are intricate, the mysteries are captivating, and the nostalgia is ever-present.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original this gives me goosebumps with nostalgia when i play the music, and the theme makes me think way back when i played the first one, the graphics and the gritty dark feel is just right, not too much not too little the graphics are beautiful, and the vr controls are very good, i am playing on the quest 2, absolutely love it 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: It sucks that I can't recommend this game. Since the non-vr game came out, I've wanted to play the game, but never could get it to run. I eventually got the VR game and then it needed DX12. Fine, I'm on Linux on my gaming workstation now and I have it (the VR version nonetheless) running. None of that factors into the negative review; it's just to explain how much I REALLY wanted to recommend this. I remember, many years ago a picture I saw on a SNES CD-Rom in-store box-display for marketing back in Electronics Boutique that included just the face of Cosmic Osmo and the scene etched in everyone's mind of The 7th Guest's foyer with the iconic staircase.Fast-forward to today and there's a VR version. Naturally, I was all "shut up and take my money!". They've obviously tried to leverage the VR technology to increase immersion of the player through more direct interaction (picking up objects, sliding things, pushing open doors, etc.) But it really doesn't translate to an amazing experience, it's more of a "oh that's cool" kind of thing. The graphics aren't bad, but it would have been SO much better if the game's textures an polygonal count for the models (plates, chairs, boats, docks, etc.) were much higher. Again, this furthers the ho-hum kind of feeling. There's also heavy latency. It could be because I'm gaming on Linux and using Proton, but I don't think that's it. Other games run just fine that have much higher graphical fidelity. It's not horrible, but it's definitely enough to bring on some simulator sickness since it's in VR. Where the negative review comes in, is when you look at the first real puzzle.. This is where the ♥♥♥♥-show starts. The stupid dining room puzzle.There's a sphere in the center of the dinning room table with a circular bar around the base of the sphere that you grip and can rotate (and the implementation of the gripping of the circular bar at the base of the sphere to turn the thing is just absolutely horrendous) the entire sphere. The sphere has columns all the way around it with 5 buttons. You're supposed to tap the buttons but they're supposed to be done in a certain way. Imagine a little game's rules (similar to rock, paper, scissors) in where A goes to B, B goes to C, C goes to D. At least that's the way the hidden clue indicates, which completely misleads you into thinking you have less options available than you actually do. In any case, you have 4 symbols that you have to select by tapping the buttons along the surface of the sphere, and those buttons (each with a symbol on them) must be all in a contiguous line, it can be a cross, a Tetris-like "L", 7", "T", etc. and you can only have 1 of each of the 4 symbols in each 4-button selection you make. Where it gets to be obnoxious is when you know this and finally understand how the damn puzzle is supposed to work, yet every single attempt you try, you wind up coming to the last or 2nd to last 4-button selection and not being able to make a contiguous line of 4-buttons (i.e. there's a space to get to one of them). So you reset, and you try it again, and you reset and try again... over and over and over again. All the while, you're trying to grip the damn circular bar and can only rotate the sphere less than an inch because the game has no ability to determine side-to-side hand-motion (in real life) as meant to be implied as tracking around the curve of the bar, so you nearly immediately lose your grip on the bar and have to keep re-gripping the damn thing. It's a puzzle that is absolute garbage for VR and I, for the life of me, cannot understand why QA didn't pick up on that and opted to include it. My hopes aren't very high for the remainder of the game. I'm going to... I'm maybe... I'm probably... maybe... I dunno... play it to finish it, but it's not a great experience so far for what should be an awesome experience (who wouldn't want to explore a dusty old mansion with secrets?).
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: VR ONLY!!!!!!The puzzles - for the most part - are challenging but not impossible. I wish there was a little more description on some of them rather than simple trial and error guesswork; I like knowing the rules of the puzzle rather than having to guess what certain icons/numbers are supposed to be. Overall, this is a solid game, and if you enjoy VR and puzzlers, you should love this one! Also, it's family friendly too - except for one particular painting, that has a "slip". But you won't notice it unless you're looking for it. Oopsies!This is a solid 8/10. The puzzles bring it down just a smidge (for reasons mentioned) and it feels too short. Reviews said this was a 8-10 hour game, and I got it done in 5, so your mileage may vary.I'd pick it up, especially if it's on sale!
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I was really looking forward to this game because it is one of those rare games where it isn't all about running around shooting your enemies . But I was disappointed.  Yes, some of the puzzles are fun to play.  But others made no sense  what so ever. I used a lot of hints and skipped some, even with using a walk through. I did like the story line and the graphics were decent. I would rate this game 4 stars.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I HATE puzzle games. Despise them in fact but this games atmosphere + challenging but understandable puzzles really kept me gripped. The acting is decent and funny enough to keep you watching too. Solid 8/10 I would say 9/10 but you'll see why below.The only thing that was absolute horrendous was the ending.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are generally head-scratchingly hard and tedious. Top marks for visuals, it's certainly impressive in that department. I think the issue is VR. If I were just moving my mouse and keyboard then fiddling with something for multiple minutes would be less tiresome. I normally enjoy puzzle games, but almost every puzzle I came across (not all) was difficult. I probably gave up on each sooner than I would have done had it been a flat screen game. So, for this reason I'm giving it a thumbs down. I just didn't enjoy it, even though I appreciate what they've tried to do here, and can see a lot of favourable reviews.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is pretty great. Awesome improvement and a satisfying trip down memory lane for those of us who played the original. But if you are using a Meta Quest 2 headset, stay away. I could never get the game audio to come through the headset no matter what I tried; just the PC speakers. Eventually after trying everything I could find in support forums and think of on my own, I can't even get the game to launch anymore. And of course since I played it more than 2 hrs, Steam will not refund me...figures.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I mean, it's cool and the puzzles seem decent, but they just took too many liberties. Yeah, people would have complained if it was just a remake, but that's kind of what most of us wanted, I think.It's not the same house. Some of the rooms are similar, but the layout is largely different, especially upstairs. I really wanted to just have the original house in VR.The puzzles are entirely new, which I'm definitely fine with (especially the laboratory "puzzle", good riddance!).My ideal version of this would have been same house and layout with new puzzles. Optionally maybe a NG+ option for the original puzzles.It's good if you're coming to it fresh. If they didn't call it the 7th guest, I'd recommend it. But it just isn't what I wanted. I know, I'm unreasonable, but these reviews are subjective and aggregated, so don't hate on me for being a grumpy old man.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: For those who haven't played the original 7th Guest: This is a vr puzzle game with a spooky story that unfolds as you explore a creepy mansion.If you are familiar with the original game; what you need to know is that this is a retelling of the original story told through similar means. The puzzles are different, and the way the story is told has differences. But the live action actors over-performing the characters is intact. The puzzles are completely different, and much more forgiving. I had just enough patience to solve every puzzle without needing a hint. The layout of the house is not a perfect recreation, but is similar enough that it feels familiar. Generally speaking, whether you will like this remake or not is up to you. If you thought the original was a work of art that should be preserved, this isn't that. If you're someone who thought the original was an overly punishing and player-unfriendly, then I think you will be pleasantly surprised with what they came up with.It's worth noting that unlike the original, this is not a very scary game. There's some creepy things about the house, but it doesn't go out of it's way to scare you in between puzzles. Gone are the random haunted paintings that reach out to grab you, and the creepy ghost women beckoning you into the darkness. So, if horror games aren't your thing, you can probably make it through the game without any trouble. It's about as scary as Disney's Haunted Mansion ride.Of note, I was impressed with the mechanic of the lantern, which can reveal clues, and highlight points of interest. Also, the lantern always reveals what the mansion looked like before it was a decrepit mess. It's a neat visual trick that I liked.I was also impressed with how they handled the characters. Mirroring the original, all the cutscenes are performed by live-action actors, who appear to have had their performances not just motion captured, but photo scanned(?) into the game. The implementation isn't perfect, but it's neat being able to see a live action performance, and actually walk around it and see it from different angles. It captures the feeling of the original cutscenes while honoring the new technology that we are playing the game through, now.All in all, a good effort. I enjoyed my time with it. And it felt good to play a version of the game that didn't make me pull my hair out.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Crashes when attempting to load while using Oculus Quest 2 over Virtual Desktop, ALVR, or the Official Air Link option.I don't want to use the quest specific version as I want to play with my family in full resolution.I cannot recommend this at this time for quest users. Willing to change review when issue has been patched.edit: i have tried the suggested fix for virtual desktop to no avail. issue persists after upgrading to Oculus Quest 3, as well as using a quest-link cable, as well as steam link. it's possible that the fact that i'm using the Quest Pro Controllers is throwing an error but i haven't checked due to that being unlikely.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down, one of the best games of its kind I’ve ever played. Somewhere between an escape room and a point-and-click, it offers an immersive experience beyond measure, with carefully crafted graphics, engaging acting, and incredibly believable characters; just what you’d expect in a classic manor-thriller. The setting and atmosphere are simply perfect, and the story is original, occasionally moving, and well-structured. I couldn’t ask for more.In case anyone’s wondering, the game has no jumpscares, although there were a couple of moments where I had the uncontrollable urge to take off my headset (spiders, anyone? And yes, you actually have to interact with them… and I’m arachnophobic!)It’s a real shame it’s already over, I could have played for many hours more. I wish there were more games like this. I don’t think I ever needed any hints, which means the puzzles were never frustrating, though they weren’t super easy either. (For some calculation-based puzzles, like filling chessboards or predicting the opponent’s moves, I relied on my calculator-minded partner, as I’m hopelessly bad at this!)Highly recommended, a feast for the eyes and ears. There are some lag issues when opening doors, which can cause motion sickness over time (we took turns playing in half-hour sessions to avoid feeling unwell), but it’s probably more due to our hardware than the game itself (we’re playing on Steam with Oculus Link on an older Oculus Quest).On a bitter note, so sad to see that no translator was mentioned in the credits, Localsoft being the only one displayed. Support your translators, they're incredibly valuable! Show them the due respect! #TranslatorsInTheCreditsDid I mention it was amazing? BUY IT!
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Very well done, as a casual puzzle game. Don't expect a great challenge, but the ambiance is great and it works really well as a VR game. What surprised me the most was that I really liked the performance of the characters in the visions. I expected it to be pretty cringe bur it was surprisingly good and fit the settings very well. + Story and characters are interesting and well made.+ Looks great and runs great on my Quest 2.+ The settings with rooms to solve makes for perfect stopping points to avoid VR fatigue.- Controlling items in the world can sometimes be a bit fiddly and annoying with the Quest 2 controllers.- The puzzles are mostly very simple.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great as a VR puzzle game, and the live action actors look amazing. However, it lacks the horror elements that the original had. That is to say, the original was darker, scarier and more unsettling in a way that this one isn't. Its unfortunate the original's score was not used more.What this game does improve on is its puzzles that are much more creative and thematic to the characters, as well as having a story that is linear and understandable unlike the original which was difficult to piece together.Worth it for any fan of the original, and anyone who enjoys a good VR experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: This game oozes atmosphere and the puzzles are pretty fun if only mildly challenging. The VR interactivity is pretty high and a good amount of interaction is present. It's a bit cheesy in it's "Horror" but at least it doesn't have any cheap jump scares and only tries to be creepy through the atmosphere rather than scary. The game also runs and looks great considering they co-developed it for standalone too. This is an easy recommend for me, though considering how short it is I'd wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I think it's a very interesting and different game well worth it for under $20 if you are under the age of 18. Over 18 I wouldn't pay more then $10 unless your really bored. It's different which makes it interesting, there is lots of content. But it's more interesting I found for kids.Love the lantern idea, solving rooms like Talo's Principal (Favorite Game Ever). It adds a little backstory.No noticeable bugs for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Was a lot of fun! The 3D video of the cast really made the game. I've beat 7th Guest 1 and 2 several times and the casting is really what makes the game shine. I wish other VR games would have live actors in them as well.I miss the original Stauf.
