_childDocuments_.review: It`s clear that cheap games based on a movie license cannot be taken seriously, they are usually made as if just for show,For "Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles" this is also relevant, but only partly, Firstly, it is curious how quickly they began to develop the universe of the new film (in the summer, a good series was also released), and, naturally, the main pillar is the cel-shaded visuals copied from Spider-Verse cartoon,But TMNTU also stands out for its fairly good, smooth combat mechanic, a fairly diverse number of techniques, combinations, rolls that you want to repeat over and over again, "AHEARTFULOFGAMES" was hired for the development, responsible for a tiny indie beatemup, and apparently they approached the matter with all their heart, if you play some old projects about the carriers of the shells of the 2000s or even 2010s - all the mechanics there were much more crooked than in "Mutants Unleashed", believe me,Also here Arenas and transitions between them use platforming, but it's too little to make a revolution in the genre, and somewhere it's inconvenient because of the fixed camera, if you're hoping for a full-fledged level like Tony Hawk with sliding along the railings, then, alas, all the maps are small boxes, and btw with a lot of backtracking, but this isn`t particularly noticeable, since the beginning and end of the map often change places,In short, my main thought about the game is that the combat system is literally constricted here, the target audience for the publisher is children, so they left no chance to reveal the potential, the enemies are too easy, so much so that you will get rank S in 99.9% of cases, without even having time to warm up your fingers, there is, of course, a small progressionespecially when mobs that shoot lasers appear, but you are unlikely to endure 5 tedious hours for the sake of a little difficulty at the end. Even with the bosses, things are uneven, the first one is very difficult, and the last one is click-killing in a minute, in terms of mechanics it's standard dodges from circular damage and a lot of hp, nothing special,And in short.. there's another fundamental problem: someone came up with the idea to stretch such a simple game, putting it in the shell of some Japan-RPG.. Like time after time we have to start missions from our sewer hub, or before the task go to the gym or office.. like a place where our friends are waiting for us, which opens up a new level of upgrades for one of the turtles just for dialogues, like in a visual novel ) And here there is also a day and night system and restrictions on completion by days. There are a couple more things like in the arcade you can take a modifier for 1 run to increase damage or for additional life (when you die, you return to the map), you can go through optional missions to find infected enemies.. which then for some reason will open up infected everywhere. There is also a pizzeria, where several unsuccessful platform levels for speed are available, and at home there are dojo challenges.. damn, there is also a smartphone there, you can read notes with it and scan the area for some goodies that are not used anywhere, as well as coins and cassettes, found on the main levels - In general, all this is so unnecessary, it kills the pace of the fighting game if anyone forgot..These cutscenes-dialogues about nothing with anthropomorphic animals from films begin to seem endless, fortunately they add the ability to skip them, but even so, the soul is exhausted by the minute-long loading between 3-minute levels. The content of the story also doesn`t affect the films, there everything is at the level of experiences of secondary characters like Bebop and Rocksteady disappointed in people, became bad, but we convinced them and "changed their shoes".. well, and some villain scientist spreads a virus at the end.. and I won't remind you about cheap animations, everything is clear here,And with aaall this, the game is not without the usual bugs, the most critical - because of which I cannot recommend the Cooperative game mode for 2 players (for which the camera is not adapted) - this is if you cross the checkpoint script before your friend, then you will immediately be separated by an invisible wall, because of which you will have to go back in order to then go forward together, and the passage back will again be frozen by the "wall" - who did this for what reason..🏆 In general, if you are a fan of Turtles and have a huge supply of patience, then it is definitely worth a try, after all, this is Beat ’em up an outdated genre, usually offer nothing but a dull slaughters, and mechanically it`s done cool, you won’t want to let go of the joystick buttons once you start (of course, it’s better play with it).

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really interesting. The gameplay is nothing special. It's solid and has some nice aspects. The only legit issue with it is the game is not just difficult and even as a kid I don't think I'd ever struggle with it. Where the games shines is literally everywhere else. It stays true to the film and you really feel like youre in that world. Same VAs, for the most part, the animation is properly realized, the story makes sense within the world of the movie, and it has a shocking amount of side content and content in general for that matter. The game is over 10 hours long with a lot of cutscenes and majority are fully voice acted. The surprising thing is it has this persona inspired hub system. So inbetween the main missions, that're classic beat'em up style, you have the turtles home in the sewer. Where you can talk to everyone, upgrade the turtles, do extra content on their phone or computer, and theres areas you can go to from the map that're also in that persona style where there's side stuff to do. The main use for them is to interact with people and each turtle as a quest line through a specific person. Every time you do one the turtle's upgrade path is leveled up. There's not a ton of depth to these persona inspired moments but it's still a cool addition and lets you live in that world more and not just feel like you're mindlessesly doing fights over and over. I think that adds a lot to a game like this where most people are coming for the TMNT world not just a beat'em up expierence. Overall this game is impressive and isn't just another run of the mill beat'em up. Hopefully they can build on the ideas from it and make a even better version along side the sequel to the movie.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had my eye on this one for a while. I love the art style. Feels just like the recent movie. Initially I was worried about how this game would be to play but happy to say it's pretty fun and very different from any previous TMNT game. While there is a fun beatemup at it's core there is also a whole social mechanic built in similar to the person's games where you can choose how to spend your free time and build relationships with various characters to level specific skills.  This is actually really nice as it explores the different turtles personalities and relationships in a way you haven't seen in other games. My kids love the crazy smashing and bashing of the fighting but they also like walking around talking to the NPC characters. Also the dialogue and interactions are really lovely. Each of the turtles is generally being really considerate and caring towards the other characters and this is something i want them to see. These cartoon characters they love being kind to others.Each of the characters has their own movesets you can upgrade and unlock.  Each of them feel different enough to play giving you a reason to want to spend the time mastering each. It's a quirky off the wall turtles game with a surprising amount of stuff to do and unlock that allows you to spend time not only leveling characters to earn new ways to beat up mutants.....or newbies ....as well as letting you explore the TMNT world and characters in a new way. Definitely a fun game. Not super difficult but also difficult enough for the more casual gamer. Some enemies in particular are very annoying (flying creatures.... who ever likes flying creatures in games)The price is gonna put alot of people off sadly. I think this should have launched at half the price to get people interested but that's just how things seem to be priced these days. Stuff is expensive. People's time is expensive. Overall good light hearted fun.Performance wise it runs great on both Steam Deck and PC with locked 60fps on deck at max setitngs. You can drop settings down and lock to 45 for really reduced power draw and extended battery playtime.Also the classic skins are just so good. Switched to them instantly and haven't gone back to the defaults..My biggest gripe is the camera system. It is actually beyond awful. Often you mess up platforming jumps because the camrea is stupid. Or combat becomes confusing and needlessly frustrating because of the camera. I really wish they had hired someone with a decent level of experience to deal with the camera in this game is it will make alot of people quit the game and refund. The way they have it currently is just unacceptable. TLDR: Recommend if you are a turtles fan and enjoyed the recent movie / Mutant Mayhem cartoons. Great fun to play coop with the kids and want to kick back and chill with the turtles in a much slower paced adventure that is as much about socialising as it is about punching mutants in the face.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished my first of at least 4 playthroughs, and I'm ready to speak my peace.The game is split between two areas of play. Traditional action sections, and social links building. Talking to NPCs will open up new skills and resources the turtles can use in the combat sections, and I firmly believe that this is the one incarnation of the turtles where these two things could be combined in an organic way.I am a gameplay first, and story second style of player, and I genuinely enjoyed my time with the game, and as mentioned above, am planning multiple more runs. If you don't want to engage with the more verbose aspects of the game you can easily just do the minimum to upgrade your preferred Turtle and run just the main story. Since the game doesn't have traditional RPG elements like stat raising, you will never be underpowered by just running campaign missions.The combat is very engaging, and I feel with a bit of tweaking, could easily stand up as one of the best 3D action games the turtles have ever had. Moves are varied, options are plentiful, and each Turtle has distinct playstyles that will absolutely encourage you to pick your favorite and stick with them as your main choice. After the first missions you can select any Turtle for any mission, so you will never be forced into using a character you haven't invested any upgrades into.The game does feature a new game plus option, and while claiming it is more difficult, I can't speak on that seeing as of where I am now, the difficulty does feel about the same. That being said, the games difficulty does start pretty tame, but by the end of your 10ish hours in the story, you will be definitely experience some fights that will require more careful and calculated play to keep from dying.There is plenty of side content to chew on in the form of optional platforming and combat challenges, but a dedicated survival mode or arcade mode would have pushed this game just that much further into being a game that any action player or TMNT fan would get enjoyment from. As it stands now though, there will be a lot of cutscene skipping required to get back into the fights. I am really hoping that the post launch content in the season pass will rectify this issue.I don't by any means feel that this is a perfect game, but I do absolutely feel my money was well spent picking this game up.

_childDocuments_.review: This game offers impeccable hack and slash gameplay that will delight fans of the genre. The combat is fluid and satisfying, with an excellent variety of moves and combinations that capture the essence of the genre.As for the graphics, the game dares with a vibrant and bold visual style, which fits the aesthetics of the latest movie of the turtles wonderfully and I personally love it.Performance is another strong point to highlight. I tested the game on both an old PC and the Steam Deck, and in both cases it maintained a constant 60 FPS frame-rate per second, ensuring a smooth gaming experience.What really adds depth to this adventure is the inclusion of social bonding mechanics and deadline-driven quests, in true Persona saga style. This adds a strategic layer to the game, as you'll not only have to worry about defeating enemies, but also managing time and deepening relationships between characters to unlock upgrades.After almost 8 hours of gameplay, I haven't encountered any bugs or glitches, which shows a very careful polishing job by the developers. Finally, the only negative point in my opinion, in some isolated cases the fixed camera can play a trick, preventing the view of some important elements on screen.

_childDocuments_.review: Taking place months after the events of the movie, the game will feature unique visuals inspired by the film's bold, painterly art style. Combining energetic ninja teamwork gameplay with a humorous narrative, players will take control of the Turtles as they interact with a host of memorable characters from the franchise and fight to save this stylized take on New York City from a new mutant threat.

name: Quantum: Recharged
detailed_description: Over 40 years since its arcade debut, Quantum: Recharged warps the classic arcade title with modern flourishes that have become a staple among the Recharged series. Defeat waves of enemies using your ship to circle around them and create a punishing deadzone. By removing the traditional ability to shoot enemies, this title challenges players to avoid taking damage and progress through increasingly difficult levels. This Recharged release expands on the classic gameplay with a wider variety of deadly enemies and some new moves to even the odds. Accelerate to make some distance between you and a stalking Neutron and use your dodge to avoid the Quarks’ deadly laser attacks. With two modes of play, you can chase for high scores in both the endless arcade mode or 25 curated levels designed to push your reflexes to the limits. And, of course, it wouldn’t be a Recharged title without some new beats from Megan McDuffee. Hear the music build in real time as your combo multiplier grows higher and higher. Try not to get hit! Features Arcade Mode: Survive as long as you can against progressively dangerous enemies until you’re out of lives. Challenge Mode: 25 hand-crafted levels with unique challenges such as defeating a certain number of enemies within a period of time, each designed to make you think of new strategies to conquer them. Power Ups: Unlimited dodges, freezing enemies, and the critical extra life will spawn to help you turn the tables on your enemies. Local Co-op: Cover more ground with a friend across all modes of play to strategically clear out enemies in tandem. Note: At least one controller required for local co-op Leaderboards: Compete in global leaderboards in arcade and challenge modes

_childDocuments_.review:
Quantum: Recharged reimagines the classic 40 years since its arcade debut, featuring modern flourishes that have become a staple in the Recharged series. 

In Quantum: Recharged, players must defeat waves of enemies by encircling and entrapping groups of foes with their ship to create punishing dead zones that destroy them. With no on-board guns, lasers or missiles to shoot enemies down, Quantum: Recharged challenges players to avoid taking damage and progress through increasingly difficult levels by mastering their ship's maneuverability.

A fusion of frenetic gameplay and quick-thinking problem-solving, Quantum: Recharged is a visual cosmic wonder complemented by an energetic original soundtrack from award-winning composer Megan McDuffie, featuring soaring melodies and infectious beats.

name: Obsidian
detailed_description: Welcome to Obƨidian… Your Rules Do Not Apply Here! You arrive, a stranger in a strange land. Confused, disoriented, you make your way through the twisted and surreal world in search of your partner, Max. All you carry with you is the knowledge you’ve grown to accept as the truth. However, you are about to discover that what the truth is depends on what world you are in. And in this world, things do not necessarily work the way they are supposed to. In this world, the characters do not exactly do what you expect them to do. In this world, the laws of physics have somehow become contorted; what is up and what is down is merely a matter of opinion. Here, after every perplexing puzzle you solve, another lurks around the corner. And, as you unravel each elusive mystery, untangle each riddle, an even bigger enigma begins to unfold. The question is, will you put together all the pieces of the puzzle and make the right choice, when the time comes… Features: Compelling story driven by fantastically unusual and surreal 3D environments and characters. Five CD-ROM’s worth of absorbing exploration take you through four dream realms. Challenging puzzles that become your world, as your world becomes a puzzle. Original musical score by Thomas Dolby. “We hope you have as many sleepless nights playing Obƨidian, as we had making it.” — Adam Wolff, Howard Cushnir, Matthew Fassberg and Scott Kim – Obƨidian Game Designers

_childDocuments_.review: You, as biochemical engineer Lilah Kerlin, and your partner Max Powers, an environmental engineer, have created the Ceres Project -- an orbiting satellite that releases nanobots into the atmosphere designed to restore the ozone layer and eliminate atmospheric pollution, which has reached a crisis point in the year 2066. After successfully engineering and launching Ceres, the project is left to operate under its own control. With the job complete Lilah and Max decide to go on a long overdue vacation. However, while vacationing they discover a strange black, crystalline growth that is becoming larger every day ? and somehow it seems to be eerily linked to the Ceres Project. [AdventureGamers.com]

name: Mouthwashing
detailed_description: More from CR Channel About the Game Mouthwashing is a first-person horror game following the dying crew of a shipwrecked space freighter. Who could have known what good ol’ Captain Curly was capable of? Guess he thought his crew dying alongside him was only right. But some men can’t even kill themselves properly. Maimed, limbless and unable to speak, but alive, Curly is now at the mercy of the crew he has doomed to a slow death. Descend into Madness Follow the lives of the crew as they weather starvation, isolation, and each other. People were never your strong suit anyway. Zero Chance of Rescue The ship will run out of power within six months. Food rations long before that. Immersive Storytelling Pay attention to your surroundings. Psychological Scares Your eyes are lying. Unforgiving Narrative Hope to die, or for goodness sake, pray that everyone else did.

_childDocuments_.review: I like horror as a genre, but personally prefer psychological/creepy elements in horror rather than just gore and jump scares. There are a few jump scares, but not many, which in my view is a plus. This is a great game. They did an amazing job telling a story that is best told using video games as a medium.

_childDocuments_.review: Played this on call with my friends. It put my best friend off of her dinner, another one almost needed to turn away all completely at some point. But this entire experience was far too captivating to peel away from. Genuinely a hauntingly well written narrative with VERY fun visuals and layers, and layesr, on LAYERS of symbolism and intense visuals that do not hold back. It's refreshing to see something so visceral and something with genuine teeth.It hurt. This game hurt a lot; and I think it's actually a very important game (for anyone with a strong enough stomach to handle it). This will be a game I will hold a place in my heart for a VERY long time.It's best to go in knowing as little as humanly possible; nothing if you can manage. Even knowing content warnings feels almost unadvised-- But this game is tackling extremely delicate subject matter in the most bold fashion that holds no punches. Making you QUICKLY love and hate what you see. But loving and hating feels so good. It NEEDS you to feel this love and hatred. And you will whether or not you want to. I liked this game very much, I hope anyone and everyone who can play it, can.

_childDocuments_.review: Really good 2-ish hour exploration of guilt. The story here is actually pretty straightforward and not as abstract as How Fish is Made and it's nice to see them pull this style of storytelling off just as well. Definitely some good writing and visual storytelling at work here, well worth the asking price. It's also pretty clear at least some part of the dev team are pretty big Eva fans and that's nothing but a plus in my book.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna talk about the story in broad strokes, so please be wary of spoilers. I also feel kinda bad about giving this a thumbs down, but this is a subjective review, so doing a "Thumbs Up" and then stating "I don't actually recommend playing this" would be kinda silly. So there.This game just didn't land with me at all. Initially, I was thinking this might be a "Passion of Christ" kinda deal: Curly, giving up his body and all of his (and everyone else's!) future to remind the other crew members (who all, in some way, are somewhat bad at that "being a person" thing) of the beauty of life, so that they may face death with newfound fortitude, the joke here being that he was the one that doomed them in the first place. I think the notion of such a presumptuous, useless sacrifice is quite entertaining!But, turns out, it's more of a "Huis Clos" kinda thing, in particular, that one line, you know the one: "L'enfer, c'est les autres", but not in a "Personal identity is always assailed through the eyes of other people" way, but in the more popular "People just kinda suck" way.Everyone is horrible, but even so, I don't understand why the characters in this story act the way they do; its themes lean heavily into anxiety about the future and general existential malcontent, and it's made clear that all of the characters feel this in some way or another, but I don't think the events preceding the collision justify it in any way; the cause is entirely disproportionate to the effect, unless I missed something and/or am  just really stupid.It also felt to me like the game's indulging itself in lavish visual metaphors a bit too much towards the end. I did appreciate the "Miracle of Life" kinda thing. Big fan of those. Big fan of the soundscape, too! I highly suggest using headphones, should you decide to play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This was definitely a strange game. This is a slow burn, story driven, sci-fi horror. I never found myself bored. Plays with the fear of isolation and madness. The characters do not speak, you have to read the dialogue but I actually really enjoyed that as it made me feel more immersed in the story. The story goes back and forth between two characters as well as two time lines. I won't spoil anymore from there. I think it's worth the 4.6 hours it took me to complete. I especially recommend this for sci-fi horror fans and artsy horror fans. The end got a little over the top strange but when thinking about it further, it fits. No real combat, more of a puzzle/ exploration game. If done right, this could make a pretty scary movie!

_childDocuments_.review: This is an edited Review, I'll leave the original version of it below, because my criticism of the game still apply.   Mouthwashing is a great game, that takes the perfect amount of time to tell the story it wants to. I'm sure all positive things I could say have already been said in other reviews, so I'll only get into why my review changed from a negative to a positive review. Originally I was unable to finish the game due to reasons explained below. I emailed the developers and they got back to me in a matter of hours, letting me know how to skip the section, while this is great, it shouldn't have taken me an email to finish the game. I'm worried that the inaccessibility of that information combined with the inaccessibility of section will lead to some people just not finishing the game and leaving with a bad impression of an otherwise amazing game. Having played both how fish is made and  mouthwashing I'm looking forward to what the team does next!Original Review: For the most part I very much enjoyed the first 2 hours of the game, but the Graveyard section honestly ruined the experience for me. It's a total genre shift and will make it impossible for people, who don't have quick reflexes or are used to shooters, to finish the game.It's a skillset that isn't needed for the first hours and it's honestly a shame that i won't be able to see the end of the story myself. The fact that you can't pause and have to replay 5 minutes, if you quit out of the section don't help. Getting killed in the middle of adjusting my settings in hopes of maybe having a chance isn't fun. And if I have to replay 5 minutes every time I want to give it another try, I probably won't give it another try again. I would give the game another shot and change my review if there is some patch to the game that helps with that section, but until then the end of the game is inaccessible for me and I would've preferred to know about that aspect of it before hitting the 2 hour mark.

_childDocuments_.review: Get ready to see the best of yourself in others, and the worst of others in yourself. Ask yourself if anyone truly makes wrong choices, then challenge your answer. The intersection of means to an end and the end to the means is wrought with visceral, intimate truths about yourself and the people around you, leaving you only to wonder which matters more, and which is worse.Some games feel like a movie, but this one felt like a novella - short enough to fit in your head all at once; dense enough to lurk in the back of your mind for a long, long time. If you like your equations cold, you're in for a treat.

_childDocuments_.review: "Psychological horror" may be one of the most misapplied terms on Steam, if not in media in general. It does not mean horror with crazy people in it, or horror featuring characters having thoughts. It does not mean surreal horror. It does not mean subtle horror. It is not just a fancier word for horror in general. "Poppy Playtime" is not psychological horror. "Dead by Daylight" is not psychological horror. was still there obviously being disheartened when i saw it wasnt, so heres my second attempt, if it sucks blame steams Hud and whatever transpired on the minimize.----------------This games like a old psychoedelic movie, the scenes, and the story, and how its broken up, it all feeds into a feeling of being on the edge of a abyss, looking down into everlasting nothingness, and i personally loved _childDocuments_.review: Lukewarm recommendation - a story of 5 people  in space without a toilet or shower from a team that made a game about a fish flopping around.I appreciate it more for what it tries to do than for what it is. If I should compare it to something it is a home grown version of Layers of Fear, but fortunately better in most aspects.I do have reservations - the game is too on the nose with the story and it overexplains everything. It should say less - I would much more prefer if it went full Lynch and you'd need to put some effort into thinking about it. The story feels like it needs a bit more mystery.The game feels like it is a bit padded for time - walking forward in long non linear areas works thematically in some parts but kills pacing and it's not particularly engaging. At the same time these are the places filled with the surreal things which I liked.There are few 'minigames' that you might have seen elsewhere which brings the common problem - running from the scary monster gets boring, if you have to do it repeatedly. At that point it breaks the flow. I think the game strikes a decent balance in this but it still feels out of place at times.I would also like if the game leaned more into the  and how that changes the dynamic of the group. The problem is that most of the plot could exist even if . Nothing would meaningfully change - that probably was the aspect that needed a bit more focus.In any case - interesting experience with some good ideas and a promise of potential future games.

_childDocuments_.review: Full gameplay: How Fish is Made is one of the best games of all time, so Mouthwashing is kind of an instant "I'm going to play this," title.  I was lucky enough to get a free key through LV1 Gaming since I'm a volunteer writer over there.  Pretty sweet.I could take the easy way out and use the same review I used over there, but naaaaaah.  I'm going to do a new one, just for you fine folks here on Steam.The story is pretty good, told through the eyes of various crew members.  Some flashback bits, and some weird stuff spread around in it.  I really want to compare it to Event Horizon, but it isn't really a just comparison.  I guess it's because there are some creepy horror vibes at certain parts of the game that definitely bring it to mind.. But it's not quite that kind of horror.  It's more psychological horror than space horror I guess you could say.My only major complaint with the story is that there's not really enough put into the interaction and backstory of the crew.  It feels like there is so much more to unlock, but we have such a little amount of interaction with them due to the game's constant desire to push you forward in the narrative.  It makes the story feel just a little shallow at times.Gameplay wise, it's essentially a slightly spooky Walking Simulator.  And that's fine.  There is a continual sense of creepy dread that I think does a great job for the atmosphere of the game.  There's no combat, so it's actually kind of a chill vibe even.  There are a few areas of the game where you have an actual feeling of impending danger, which might even be kind of real danger.  But there aren't a huge amount of those moments.Graphically it's a low-poly horror game.  But, despite the low poly nature of it - we get a ton of detail in all of the different areas of the ship.  The game certainly feels kind of unique this way.It's not super long, you can probably finish it in 2 hours or less.  And that's fine.  A good story you can sit through in one sitting is hard to come by.  Definitely recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I find myself in the rare position of wanting to review a game positively, but also being aware that to be too specific about my reasons for the positive response would spoil some of what I think is wonderful about the game. I love when I discover a game that impresses me so much that I'm not sure how to review it and also preserve its specific magic.What you have here is an extremely dark, extremely horror-saturated narrative, tightly edited and brilliantly constructed, presented out of chronological order to the events, but in such a way that the story builds beautifully based on what's revealed to you as you play. There are things that were said and done by characters in my first playthrough that I entirely missed the significance of because I had no context for them yet, and which retroactively gained terrible importance. The cast is small - five characters altogether - and so is the setting, but the amount of story conveyed is enormous in light of how tightly scripted it is. A friend of mine watched me stream this on discord and said he was riveted the whole way through, and we talked about the story and characters for an hour the next day. That's really something.Not everyone will like this. You could even arguably consider it a walking simulator, though you interact with the world. But if you're the sort of person who likes to think about characters, their motives, and the messiness of human relationships, particularly under the umbrella of horror, then this is a solid pick for you. It's smart about how it handles its horrors -- one sequence in particular will remain memorable for me, where a piece of proxy media subs in for things that would have been far less impactful if they'd been rendered fully in the game.I really can't wait to see what this studio comes up with next. They have a unique flavor, and I really like it.

_childDocuments_.review: The first half of this game had me hooked. I'm not usually a fan of non-linear storytelling, but I was willing to go along with the story it was trying to tell, and I was decently invested. The worldbuilding was great, the characters were solid, the gameplay was simple yet interactive enough to justify this sort of medium. I was really looking forward to seeing it through.Unfortunately, the second half brought the entire experience crashing down for me.Mouthwashing tells a decent chunk of its story through subtle implications and context clues, meaning you aren't directly told a lot of what happens or has already happened, and need to piece it together yourself. Now, there's nothing wrong with this kind of storytelling, and it can be done well; but when you get to the point where every other section is some kind of trippy nightmare sequence that feels like it was just done as an excuse to throw in some shocking horror visuals, it can become nearly impossible to glean what's actually part of the story and what's just there to scare or disturb you.Speaking of gameplay, just about every part of Mouthwashing that had some kind of "fail condition" was one I thoroughly disliked:Every single one of the above sequences was either boring, confusing, frustrating, or some combination of all three. I understand that gameplay isn't Mouthwashing's strong suit, or even its focus really, but no amount of brilliant storytelling or believable characters can make up for the game being borderline unenjoyable when these elements aren't there to support it.To top it all off, by the time I had finished playing, my playtime clocked in at just over two hours; the standard maximum amount before a Steam game can typically no longer be refunded. Now while I did manage to acquire said refund, and while I fully acknowledge the amount of work and detail that went into so many elements here, I can't help but feel as though nearly half the time I spent "playing" was just padding via nightmare sequences, and those could have easily been trimmed or cut to provide something much more to-the-point and enjoyable. But still... $13 for a flawed two hour experience just doesn't sit right with me.I want to close this review by reiterating that I'm not actively trying to take up some contrarian stance given that Mouthwashing currently has a 96% rating on Steam. I was decently excited going into this, and I did genuinely want to walk away from this feeling satisfied by the experience. I feel like if a few elements were tweaked and adjusted - and there was a bit more content to justify the pricetag - then I'd be able to recommend this to other fans of the genre; but in its current state, I just can't bring myself to do that.

_childDocuments_.review: Mouthwashing is a surrealist retro horror descent into madness developed by Wrong Organ, whose previous game How Fish Are Made I had played August of 2023. In fact, that free DLC tie-in they had for it was how I first heard about this game considering they revealed it there first. I had wishlisted it due to the interesting vibes and had watched its development over the course of a year, though I haven’t really delved much into it. I saw some extra trailers from indie horror gaming shows but I didn’t really pay full attention to it until my buddy Wrathne had bought it for me on a whim to make me stream it for her after beating Buffy the Vampire Slayer on Xbox. Play it I did, and over the course of the morning I’ll just be straight up and say that I played one of the most surreal and greatest tier retro horror games that I’ve ever seen in my life (on par with my fandom of The Heilwald Loophole). Going to say it right now, if you’re into these type of games then YOU NEED to play it end of story. Speaking of story… (For my feelings on the plot, though please play the game first)The gameplay for the most part is rather simplistic, you could say it’s a walking-story sim; traveling around the main rooms in the Tulpar while talking to one of four other ship inhabitants, perhaps engaging in some cooking depending on the sequence or solving puzzles using a Blacklight flashlight (which you can bypass for achievements by putting in the code itself through guides). There’s a section later in the game where you’re slowly walking over metal grates while attempting to avoid an invisible ghost horse that you can only see with the Blacklight that’s pretty tense but can also potentially feel a bit frustrating depending on the person. There is a boss fight later in the game which involves shooting someone three times that’s ACTUALLY really intense due to the randomness of the enemy which was solid; however this is more of an atmospheric horror game where you let it take you where it needs you to go, though if you want to speedrun or noclip through the game there is an attached Developer Console mode (needed for an achievement) by pressing the Squigly key on the keyboard. Getting into the graphics and atmosphere, let me say that the game certainly holds those Playstation-styled crunchy graphics. However, this game is a lot more detailed than the usual style of graphics that games like this hold onto with it’s expansively detailed environments that actually has you able to read texts like post it-notes, or individual moles on someone’s face or neck folds (like Swansea). The level of detail is immaculate and the character design is amazing; some notes I’m going to throw out there is that Anya looks like Shelly Duval which I think is purposeful because it captures that level of anguish that she had playing her role in Kubrick’s The Shining. Curly is going to be the most recognizable character in the game due to being covered head to toe in bandages and managing to hit this ground between creepy and sympathetic. The environments in the game look retro-like but almost unique, like you’re at home but also you’re not. The game only gets more twisted with its freaky designs the more and more you go down the rabbit hole, and really encapsulates the themes of corporate hellhole that not a lot of games can manage on their own. This title pulls it off spectacularly, and there wasn’t really a moment where I couldn’t say I sat back and thought “Wow, this is freaky as hell” or “This looks amazing”. Some of my favorite examples include watching the reflections of a TV program come off of the floor in the middle of a dark room and actually keeping up with what was being played, while another one much later in the story has a man strapped to a table and having to feed him while watching the cameras, and the detail of watching the meat go through the entire body into the stomach was one to behold. Walking through dark hallways and having eyeballs pop out and stare at you from them  is one to behold and that’s only three things I brought up. The game felt spectacular for its atmosphere and I would literally promote the game just off of that, between its horrifying visuals yet excellent use of color schemes and imagery.The sound design is an excellent one too, starting off with the actual noises in the game. The clicking of the text prompts as I go through them, the fleshy noises as you open Curly’s mouth, shooting off a revolver to have a brief ringing sound, the slamming of feet on metal grates; all of these work well efficiently though if I were to honestly give a real moment of squick (in a good way) for horror then I would say it’s this: Curly’s screams throughout the game, while not really loud, really made me uncomfortable and anxious for the guy. As for the voice acting, there’s only one real bit of voice acting that I remember and that would be the Pollie mascot towards the end of the game, which is strange considering the rest of the voice cast don’t really have an actual voice. However, I guess it’s on point considering these five people probably feel like throwaway workers, with the themes of corporate propaganda being so overbearing that it would make sense that only The Pony Express would have an actual voice behind it. Finally, the music: while I don’t specifically remember any tracks as I was so engrossed in this game’s atmosphere and lore, but Martin Halldin did a fantastic job creating this somber mood with atmospheric tracks or unsettling alarms and nightmare fuel, though there are a couple of upbeat ones that represent more corporate commercialism through advertisements. Either way, they all bookend their accompanied moments extremely well, so yeah the sound design is solid. Like I said earlier, Mouthwashing was a surreal experience and one that I don’t feel should be missed out on by vidya gamers who are into retro-styled graphics and straight up horror. Most horror games don’t really scare me (especially of the retro variety) due to me being desensitized in general to horror as well as games sometimes just not really hitting the marks they should. I wasn’t overall screaming playing this game, but it certainly hit their marks when it comes to creepy tension, jaw dropping revelations and themes I’m still trying to decipher while writing up this review. Play the game, buy it by any means though I can understand if 12.99 for the price is a BIT much for two to three hours so maybe wait for a sale? I don’t know though, I’m not going to understate how much of an experience this game is; this game is certainly Halloween worthy whether you’re continuing the celebration or if you’re going to save it for a different time. As for Wrong Organ, it’ll probably be a long time until they come out with their next game but after playing How Fish Are Made (which was a solid game in its own right) to playing THIS? This was several leagues above and you could tell that these guys were cooking, so I’m REALLY looking forward to whatever Wrong Organ is going to shape up next. You will just NOT BE able to think about anything else until you finish it and know how it all ends. And sometimes even be surprised afterwards while reading explanations as some elements aren't bluntly talked about.Been a while since a game actually grabbed me by the neck from beginning to end, fully recommended, have fun and theorize along the way! :)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm blown away. _childDocuments_.review: Saw a couple of videos online and being into horror and sci-fi as a genre - in both movies and games - I thought I'd give it a go. I am beyond impressed: the story and mechanics of the game, while not flashy (certainly the point) do so much to immerse you in the story. I've found myself at many turns questioning whether a sequence was real or just deep-space madness. And the concept of having a player character act as an unreliable narration is one which ought to be explored further, beyond games like Silent Hill 2 which did it way-back-when. I have loved piecing together what I could from the game and am very much looking forward to the end, which I am soon approaching.TL;DR: I you're under the impression that the quality of this game is over-exaggerated by internet hype, please: give it a go, then come back to me.One of my favourite games for sure.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tragedy. It isn't really a game, it's a walking simulator/movie, and is a very intense character piece about a small group of people in a bad situation. The story is told in a non-chronological order, The story is interesting, though it feels like the end was a little bit belabored and lingered too long. The game also has a few brief gameplay segments, but they are the worst part of the game overall.It is hard to say too much about the game, as it is one of those stories where you are unveiling layers of what is going on as you are playing through, and trying to guess what is really going on, or what will be going on. You know at least one of the characters is psychotic, and as a result, you can’t trust what you’re seeing on screen is an accurate representation of reality.Overall, I’d say it is a well-told story, but it suffers a bit from some pacing issues in a few points, and once you figure out what the twist is, it can feel a bit like it is belaboring things a bit much.Be aware that it is an indie project (with very limited voice lines – it is almost exclusively text) and that it is designed to look like a PS1 era game. It is also about 2.5 hours long, so don’t expect a very long experience – but it is the correct length for what it is.If you like tragedies (with a tinge of horror) and like narrative storytelling, this could be the product for you.If you are looking for an actual GAME, you will be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: My biggest regret with Mouthwashing is that I almost picked it up on launch day, but decided to hold off for the sake of my backlog. What a mistake -- Mouthwashing is one of those rare games that feels tailor-made to my tastes.At no point during my 2 hour playthrough of Mouthwashing did I even consider taking a break. I was hooked from the start. The use of non-linear story telling and multiple perspectives was an excellent choice for building up the mystery and intrigue as you learn the tragedy that lead to the Tulpar's crash. The style of storytelling coupled with a tight narrative creates an impressively cinematic feel to Mouthwashing. The characters are expertly written, each being believable and having a an important part to play in Mouthwashing's exploration of the human condition. The little slice of capitalist dystopia the game presents is spot on. The surreal and unsettling visuals and shifting of your environment brought the characters' mental states to life impressively. The music was excellent both at creating tension in the more hectic moments and a feeling of uneasy calm in the more introspective moments. There is a constant sense of dread, with outright "scary" moments used sparingly -- which is exactly what I love in a horror title.That said, there area  couple of small things that kept the game from from getting absolutely full marks in my books.  As well written as the characters are, there are a couple that could have done with slightly more backstory to really solidify my attachment to them. The more "game-y" sections weren't my favorite. I'm not into stealth and chase-based gameplay. That said, they totaled just a few minutes of the runtime, did serve to add some tension, and were easy enough to not be frustrating. So, just a small ding from me. There were also a couple of grating sound effects here and there. Not a big deal, but noticeable when the rest of the game is so well made. Again, all of those issues are quite minor in the face of how Mouthwashing succeeds. It's easily one of the best games of the year and worth checking out for any and all horror fans.

_childDocuments_.review: Mouthwashing is an exceptional psychological horror game that lingers in your mind long after the credits roll. Despite some personal caveats, it delivers a masterclass in atmosphere, storytelling, and character complexity, making it a must-play for fans of the genre.The game's ability to make you feel uneasy when it wants to is unmatched. Every moment seems crafted to keep you on edge, with unease building gradually and effectively.Sound plays a pivotal role in the experience, seamlessly enhancing tension. The audio perfectly complements the visual horror.While there are moments where it might feel heavy-handed, the narrative is thought-provoking and rich with psychological depth. It’s the kind of story that stays with you, inviting reflection long after you’ve finished playing.The retro aesthetics amplify the game’s unsettling tone. The pixelated gore and eerie lighting work hand-in-hand to make the horrifying imagery even more impactful.If you enjoy exploring the intricacies of the human psyche and its flaws, Mouthwashing is an absolute treat. The characters feel like case studies of broken humanity, making the story as haunting as it is fascinating.There’s a segment near the finale where you’ll find yourself wandering through an excessive number of halls. These scenes could have been trimmed without losing any narrative or emotional weight, making the ending feel more concise and impactful.The game transitions from a standard psychological thriller with exploration and puzzles into a string of "gamey" sequences that feel disconnected from the main story. This jarring shift, particularly near the end, left me wishing for a smoother progression.The mini-game-like sections lack meaningful consequences. Failing simply means retrying, which shifts the mood from tension to frustration. These segments could have benefited from penalties or narrative implications to keep the player immersed.By the final act, the game begins to hammer home its themes in a way that feels unnecessary. The earlier sections already establish the message powerfully; the prolonged reinforcement dilutes its impact.Despite its flaws, Mouthwashing is a masterpiece. The shortcomings—mostly confined to the final act—don’t overshadow the brilliance of the overall experience. If anything, they make the game more memorable in an ironic way, leaving both positive and constructive impressions.Would I play it again? Probably not. However, as an aspiring game developer, Mouthwashing taught me invaluable lessons about pacing, thematic delivery, and how to balance gameplay with narrative. It’s an unforgettable experience that I highly recommend to anyone who appreciates psychological horror.

_childDocuments_.review: Mouthwashing, developed by Wrong Organ, is a chilling experience which I am immensely glad to have experienced. It’s a brief run, lasting only 3-4 hours, but… wow. This game delivers a genuinely awe-inspiring narrative in that time. All along the way, it inspired such insane dread within me.Mouthwashing is more–or-less a visual novel with point-and-click elements. It’s psychedelic, it’s gory, it’s incredibly inspired, and it features multiple stealth sections. (Grooooaaaaaan.) The whole trek stars five characters – Jimmy, Curly, Anya, Swansea, and Daisuke – and all of them are superbly developed. The story follows a bottle plot, with all of them being stuck within the rapidly deteriorating spaceship Tulpar after a shipwreck.The story therein is a deep, grotesque meditation on sexual assault and economic desperation under capitalism. And Jimmy, the main character, is detestable. The narrative unfolds as he gradually loses his sanity amidst dwindling resources (besides mouthwash, of course). Now, let’s be clear: Jimmy is a rapist; he’s a killer; he’s a liar. But I am still incredibly impressed with how this game portrays sexual assault, its aftermath, and how perpetrators think. Play this game for the plot; it’s worth it. Every character is superbly (but briefly) written.Also, the visual direction in this game is top-notch. It’s a PSX-style art direction here, and I quite enjoy it. The shading is perfect; the characters are intelligible and well-designed; cutscenes and directorial matters are handled quite well; and the environments are absolutely chilling. I have no complaints. The audio direction, too, is good; however, I do not think it is anything game-changing.I attempted to get all the achievements for this game, but a few of them were either bugged / annoying to hunt. For the foreseeable future, I do not plan to 100% this game. But I got close! The achievements all quite silly.As for negatives, the movement can be annoyingly slow sometimes; some plot beats tarry on a bit more than necessary; and some writing is so subtle that I missed it my first time through. This last criticism is not necessarily considerable, as I am unsure whether that’s the game’s fault or mine. In any case, all of these criticisms are very minor.Go play this game. Now. It’s great. It’s memorable. It’s short! 8.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Mouthwashing is the freakiest indie title released all year.  The game really knows how to throw you into a tail spin and apply horror-game pressure simultaneously.  Sequences of repeating corridors, rusty pipes haphazardly clumping together, fleshy horse monsters, and mushy, spaghettified textures are in abundance.  All while juggling a psychological lost-in-space horror setting.  Well-groomed character writing and dialogue form a compelling, yet crooked story of downward spiral madness, betrayal, and jealousy between the crew.  These twisted elements all come together as robustly as a game like this can.  Mouthwashing's brevity does work against it though, it could've benefited greatly from being a bit longer.  Point-of-view transitions can feel a bit heavy-handed at times too.  There are opportunities for the player to establish deeper connections with these characters, but instead transition prematurely to the next scene.  Shifting tone on a dime is pretty difficult to pull off; Mouthwashing doesn't always stick the landings here unfortunately. Yeah this game is a banger, I was floored.  I highly recommend.  8.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: (Spoilers ahead)I'm not really a big fan of horror games. I'm technically a scaredy cat when it comes to them. However, something about this really pulled me in. I've done a project on psychological horror before, and this game beautifully captures the psychological aspect when it comes to this genre as opposed to other so-called "psychological horror games". As much as I despise Jimmy, I must admit that he is a very well written antagonist in the story. After analysing, you can clearly tell that Jimmy was sick and tired of constantly being in Curly's shadow, and after everyone got fired before the crash, Jimmy didn't want it to end with Curly being "above" him. You can clearly see how much he hated, how inferior he felt to Curly. He's a man who is on the run from his problems constantly, refusing to acknowledge the things he did wrong. This is also why he shot himself in the end. He didn't want to carry that burden, knowing this horror was going to follow him to the end of his life. With Curly being the Captain, the term "The Captain goes down with his ship" is brought to light extraordinarily in this game. With him being the only one alive, that is. What is also interesting to me is how everyone, except Anya, always lost an eye after their death. Curly and Swansea having lost their eyes shows how both of them didn't see eye to eye when it came to Jimmy. Daisuke was simply too naive to notice Jimmy's true nature. Except for Anya. With her having gone through the sexual abuse (which we can tell through her mentioning the locks), she knows exactly what kind of man Jimmy is. How ruthless and selfish and downright heartless he is, how he's willing to do such horrible things just to get what he wants. Just to be seen as the "Leader". Honestly, I never thought I'd be interested in horror games, since I really don't like playing them and can only watch them. But this? Apart from the "acquire the mouthwash from the cargo" part (scared the absolute hell out of me), I genuinely loved this game above all else. I could talk about it for hours simply analysing each small part which I've noticed whilst playing the game. It's short, around 2 hours of playtime required, yet the story has been captured wonderfully from the dev team. It'd be nice if there were a dlc where we get to know more about the characters, or you name it, etc. 100/10 I recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: I completed Mouthwashing in around 1.5 hours. Half of that time was spent walking about the nightmare second half -- clicking on whatever the game told me to click on, speaking to whoever the game told me to speak to, and fumbling around with the game's final 4 puzzle sequences. It was not very enjoyable. The first 45 minutes were better, as that is where the tension was built, was the payoff (i.e., the story revelations) were not worth it. After I finished the game, I was ready to just move on but forgot how much I paid for it -- $12. The only reason I'm leaving this review is because I don't think the game was worth such a price at only 1.5 hours of playtime.I had no expectations going into this game as this just popped up in my feed with an Overwhelmingly Positive and a Psychological Horror tag. I was really excited to play it. The first 45 minutes were phenomenal. The sound design, the eeriness of the situation, the mystery. It was all great. Then it stopped being fun or scary, the mystery only increased but the answers were not satisfying, and 45 minutes in I had pretty much squeezed out all of the "story" the game was willing to provide. The game presents it in a non-linear fashion, which is perfectly fine, but the story that is presented feels almost like a concept film dragged out to paper-thin levels. I thought I had missed something, but no, the story is exactly what is presented:When I lay it out like this it especially does not feel like that compelling of a narrative to tell. There are so many elements in the game that detract from this primary plot point and end up feeling like loose ends because they do not contribute to this in any way:The worse one has to be  I just didn't feel much emotion from the way the story was presented. The game itself has its fearful moments and there is a lot of tension, but after a certain point you realize that nothing is going to happen, that there are no more twists, the scares just stop working, and I really just wanted the game to end, but then it continues another 45 minutes of various puzzles. I don't dislike this game because it is an indie game with a story focus. I think this game uses the video game medium of storytelling well, it puts you in the POV of Jimmy and the way things go down I don't think could have been told many other ways. I dislike this game because the story was ultimately not worth all of that build-up, and the game part of it was not very fun.Other narrative-driven, gameplay light psychological horror games I think are good and have stuck on my mind:- What Remains of Edith Finch- SOMA- Slay the Princess- FAITH- OmoriI would not put Mouthwashing up there, which is a shame because I think if the story was good, the presentation could easily pull it up there.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr = Its a GREAT short horror narrative but its completely lacking in any real gameplay or difficultyI really dont know how to feel about this game. I'm not gonna lavish praise upon it like everyone else is though. I will say the writing is hauntingly good, the narrative is interesting and the story stays with you but thats about it. There's no real gameplay here, it boils down to a walking simulator in a very interesting setting that occasionally peppers in very small, sometimes frustrating and honestly mostly out of place minigames that don't always fit in the story and could largely be removed entirely and very little would change. Worse yet the game constantly teases you with really intriguing and interesting scenarios that you want to see play out and then... nothing, game cuts out in an intentionally glitchy way and you're on to the next scene. Which is usually the aftermath of a scene you saw play out 3 weird glitchy jump cuts prior. The game uses the same kind of narrative structure as Pulp Fiction where you jump back and forth in time, seeing from different viewpoints but like i said it cuts right when the good stuff starts.It would be like if Pulp Fiction was recut so that the second any violence or action happens the scene cuts to another scene and then back to show the aftermath later. Its honestly pretty frustrating and I feel hella blue balled about it.Honestly though my biggest problem with this game is theres just not enough of it. Its too short, it cuts out before you can ever really explore or discover anything, and worst of all its only real "gameplay" is frustrating out of place minigames that don't move the story forward or expand upon anything other than the relevance of the imagery and themes.I really really wish the game had taken a few more years and actually become a game. Spread the story out a bit and allow me to explore the world and setting you've created cause its honestly really interesting. And for the love of god STOP CUTTING OUT RIGHT AT THE GOOD BITS.I want to see the moment it happensI want to see the pills get swallowed, the cake get cutI want to see the meaty globule reach the end of the intestinal tractI WANT TO FINISH THE F***ING CHASE!So yes I recommend it, but go into it like you're about to watch a great horror movie except the director is a cabbage who pans the camera away anytime anything interesting happens. Dont expect any fun or interesting gameplay either. Its a straight shot through the narrative with no deviation or distraction. Bloody great horror story though.

_childDocuments_.review: You have 5 not super sane people stuck in a space freighter together for over a year of travel together working for a company called the Pony Express, when all other companies have moved away from manned space freighters. What could possibly go wrong? A whole lot apparently.Mouthwashing explores the depravity of humans who are stranded together and what they will do when ♥♥♥♥ hits the fan. It's not a particular scary game in the traditional jumpscare or something going thump in the dark sense of horror, it's the type of horror to claw away at your mind because it makes you wonder what other people would do in that situation. I honestly cannot stop thinking about the game hahah. Also, I love the non-linear story and the direct parallels the game draws between characters.This game is something everyone should experience for themselves if they are able to, not just read up on the story or watch play-throughs.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: This was an entertaining game to pass the time today!! I'm a fan of psychological horror, so this was very up my alley. I liked the way the screens would melt away and glitch out when turning to another scene! There were a few mechanics I found very nifty, and I appreciate the homage to the golden era of horror/video games.There wasn't an excessive overuse of jumpscares, and the times they were present were effective. I did have a small problem where it seemed like my computer mouse would suddenly lag, and I had to minimize the game and reopen it to ensure that the mouse would move at its correct pace, though I'm not sure if it's a fault within the game or on my end.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: Mouthwashing puts several very creative spins on the 'layers of fear'-esque linear horror experience.Despite being set in a space ship, the dark plot stays grounded at first and then spirals into madness in the later part of the game.What it lacks in high quality assets it makes up for with unique mechanics and set-pieces, as well as great (also disgusting and horrifying) sound design.The characters in the story are well designed and there are some good twists and turns. I can't say the 'message', so to speak or the ending left me fully convinced or baffled, but it was very interesting nonetheless.Either way the game is great at setting the atmosphere, with a clear mountain of game design knowledge on the part of the devs and it's full of unique surprises. Definitely recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: best 12 dollars ive ever spent ever, i think. i cant even describe in perfect words how much i enjoyed every second and every frame of this game. the whole mouthwash thing is an interesting metaphor that i never really thought of until playing this game. forgetting or "fixing" 99.99% of all your problems, until that 0.01 you left or somehow missed will eventually come back to haunt you. forcing you to actually face the consequences and "TAKE RESPONSIBILITY." of course there's other themes and hidden meanings other than just mouthwash, but it's definitely something that you're constantly reminded of.i wish i had better ways to word out my thoughts, or how to express how great this game is. but its 3 in the morning and i am still thinking about the crazy scares and the insane wtf moments i had to face. anyway, this game is hella ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good, and im in love with how the storys written. i would give all my money to the devs if i couldtldr: this game gud, and i love anya and daisuke with all my heart.

_childDocuments_.review: Sci-fi ship crew crashes into space debris and struggles to survive while living off mouthwash and vending machine slop. I genuinely think it's only this long to avoid Steam's 2 hours playtime limit for easy refunds (which is a shame that devs have to consider that when making shorter games). The three typical 'horror game' segments dragged on, and the story jumping around the timeline got was frustrating until I got used to it.£11 is a steep asking price for <2 hours of playtime, but it's really good. It's a story game so I can't exactly explain why, but I'd recommend if you have interest in these sorts of games.

_childDocuments_.review: What a special game.Playing SH2 Remake (the remake of already one of my favourite games of all time) and this back to back was incredible, a really amazing experience.I played this game all in one sitting this morning and it really surprised me. I managed to stay blind going into it and chose not to watch any YouTubers play it so I could experience it fresh for myself and I’m really glad I did.Mouthwashing is an incredibly powerful and heartbreaking game following the crew of the Tulpar freighter and the events before, and after a crash leaving them stranded. All five crew members are incredibly interesting in their own rights, with Curly being my favourite of them all. Following Curly, Daisuke and Anya are my next favourites of the crew- as even though Jimmy and Swansea are incredibly interesting and compelling characters, I don’t like them both as much as I do the rest of the crew.The editing, artstyle and story of the game all very much appeal to me as they’re all done in ways I absolutely love. The editing and non-linear storytelling is incredibly effective at having you piece together the events on the Tulpar while the artstyle really brings together the horror and unsettling nature of the events while still being able to craft beautiful moments and unique scenes that really really stick with me after playing it. The soundtrack is incredibly impactful and especially the Main Theme and final credits theme.Both the main menu of the game and credit roll are some of my favourites in games as the credit roll is done in an incredibly unique way that I’ve only really seen in episode 15 of Re:Zero, and the menu provides a beautiful yet unsettling image of Curly in the hospital bed with the sun on the screen behind him while the main theme plays- it’s one of those menus that really hits hard, much like Outer Wilds in particular.Honestly I’d give this game a 10/10, it’s currently in my top 20 of all time and I can see it going up the rankings for my favourite games of all time. It’s one of those experiences that is much like Outer Wilds in that it feels like you’ll never experience the same thing again, but this definitely has more replay ability after the credits roll and you fully understand how the narrative unfolds.I will definitely be going back and 100%-ing this game. I can't recommend it enough

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly creative in the way of telling a depressingly tragic story, teaching you to make the best of the hands you're dealt with in life.Take responsibility.The surreal horror segments especially (but level design in general) are delivered through intense sound design - something a lot of games like to neglect, giving it it's effectiveness.Everything is placed with care for a reason and a lot of small dialogue pieces (or even just the way people are positioned) hint at the greater picture, that you only fully understand once you put all the pieces together.Oh, Curly...

_childDocuments_.review: This is perhaps my GOTY. _childDocuments_.review: I am the kind of person who avoids horror games like the plague. Don't get me wrong, I love the horror genre and all the avenues for storytelling that it opens up. If I hear that a horror game has a good enough story, I'll watch someone else play it or watch an analysis video. I just don't like living through it. I don't like walking through dark suspenseful hallways, I don't like feeling like I'm being chased, Mouthwashing is worth being afraid. The story, the atmosphere, the constant  in your stomach are all worth experiencing for yourself. And don't just watch someone else do it, play it yourself. You need to feel the effort put into every action, and know that everything was a choice, everything was on purpose. Look down at every door handle and open every door. Shine your light at the paper, manually punch in every code.   This is quite possibly the worst I've ever felt playing a video game, yet I didn't regret a single second I spent playing it.If this is your first time playing, have fun! I hope this hurts.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: Mouthwashing is a game you go into knowing it's not going to have a happy ending. You're not here to try to change the outcome, but to try to understand the tragedy that's delivered. You won't complete the game and think, "Man, I loved this game." - Instead you'll feel a sense of dread and defeat knowing you were just as hopeless as the crew was. I wouldn't recommend this game to anyone who can't handle strong emotions of doom, but I would recommend this story as a journey for those looking for something a little different. In the end, I loved this game for what emotions it conveyed in me, through the little time I got to have with Anya, Curly and Daisuke.Also, don't drink Mouthwash.

_childDocuments_.review: Effective and stylish horror. Mouthwashing hits all the horror high-notes: an oppressive foreboding, characters grappling with their despair, jump scares and shocks, body horror plus other gore and grotesquerie. And it does so as a snappy pace while telling an interesting story. Maybe a scene or two that seemed closer to "cheap-trick" rather than truly horrific but the pace is a saving grace here. And I suspect that if you removed some or all of these scenes you'd dilute the surrealism that is key to the uniqueness of Mouthwashing's setting and mechanics.Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: This game tackles the most serious topics. It made me uncomfortable, but in a way that made me aware of the situation. The foreshadowing throughout the game is amazing. You can slowly put together the story before it is verbally said and done in front of you. The horror aspect takes on the analogy of horror while also thrown in the narrative side. There isn't much said about the story, although there is a lot of reading, but the simple story we get tells us a lot about the characters. The Characters are written so simply; the confident leader, the shy smartie, the comedic nerd, the grumpy old man and the narcissistic manipulator; you learn to love the characters you hated, and hate the characters that seemed innocent. You can finish this game in one sitting, but this type of game is where you can play multiple times and still find still find new foreshadowing moments. Although the game is a horror game, it works on more making you uncomfortable than cheap jump scares.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: Much like Signalis, Mouthwashing took my feelings about life, employment, existence, space travel and condensed them into a consice, efficiently and brilliantly written horror story. Every chapter ratcheted up the tension appropriately, and never played it's hand too early - and the hits are hard. You grow to like the crew of the Tulpar, and feel for them over the course of the four hour story. The game is great at putting you in the player characters headspace and the feelings only compound as you learn more and more about what happened. My emotions flared at the wrong characters, biases began to form, and I realize by the end that I was ending up just like them; Feeding into the anger and resentment built up over months of survival... our resources, patience, and sanity dwindling as we sit stuck, endlessly staring at minty fresh oblivion. Their losses were MY losses. I felt for each and every crew member...well, almost all of them.I laughed and I cried and I joked and I feared for my life. What a fantastic game. I'm going to be up thinking about this one for weeks.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: I played this on Halloween, and having ruminated on it for a couple weeks, here are my thoughts: Aesthetically, the game is a vibe. It's a great looking and sounding game. Story-wise, it's a mind♥♥♥♥. You're piecing together a mishmash of story and plotlines jumping back and forth through time. Things slowly start to make sense before you're thrown into the deep end again - however, this is not a negative. The game keeps you on the back foot as you slowly work your way into the conclusion. *** I will note, I did look up a plot summary at the end, just to make sure I hadn't missed anything I really, really enjoyed this game. It's one of those games I wouldn't mind experiencing again for the first time. If the dev releases more games, I'll be on the lookout.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: Mouthwashing is a game that will stick with you long after the end credits roll. This game WILL make you feel uncomfortable and upset, and deals with serious topics that may be triggering to some.The game makes up for its short run-time with impact and memorability. In typical narrative-driven horror fashion, the gameplay mostly consists of walking around and talking to the other characters, but this gets broken up fairly often with unique gameplay segments here and there. If you're looking for an indie horror game with a captivating story to tell that's presented in a unique way and can be finished in the span of an afternoon, this is it. The charming graphics are a bonus too; they aren't just memorable, they add to the delivery of the story by creating a real sense of unease with the use of freaky-looking glitch effects and a dithering overlay that can make you feel dizzy at times. The time-skips in the story add to that element of disorientation without making the story too hard to follow.I was personally really impressed with how realistically and tactfully they handled one of the more sensitive themes in Mouthwashing. An aspect of this theme that I'd never seen explored in games before was brought up throughout the story that really makes you think, and adds a lot of realism to the story.With the interesting characters and the amount of metaphors and striking imagery in this game, it's no surprise why so many artists and creatives online have made fan content of this game. It rightfully deserves the community it's built up so far, as Wrong Organ truly has something special here.

_childDocuments_.review: You see here, what we have here is a honest to god walking simulator. It's not really a game as much as an experience and it is worthwhile. This isn't a comprehensive review because the game should be experienced rather than told. Going back (Because you will be doing that for the rest of the game) you will find a host of characters with side stories, all of which play a role to the direction of it's ending. Each character you interact with (There are only 5 - Curly, Jimmy, Anya, Swansea and Daisuke) Each of them are your RESPONSIBILITY as you are captain of the ship when you begin the game. You roam and flounder around this heap of metal floating through space with only MOUTHWASH to keep you and your crew mates sane. Clearly it isn't doing the job as many of your mates are succumbing to madness, but you? No, you're level-headed and under control. You take RESPONSIBILITY for your actions and don't get buried under the monotony of holding them all together. Curly - Boy this guy's ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Like really ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Super ♥♥♥♥♥♥. There isn't anything you can do for him and that's because you're a prick. Although he's reasonable, he's also at blame for the events that occur on the ship. There are moments of clarity for him in the story as he illuminates things for the player through conversations with other characters, namely Anya. Besides that he's ♥♥♥♥♥♥ lolololol.Swansea - He's what I picture when you put someone in the shoes of being controlled by external factors, namely in American society as this is the closest thing I can relate it to. He's quite the character as he puts up a solid front for the rest of the crew, even sarcastically emboldening YOU, captain. It's clear he has a drinking problem as he breaks his vow for MOUTHWASH. Revelations with him are fairly straight-forward and require not a lot of thinking in my fair opinion. You probably know a Swansea or two. Anya - Soft and gentle but also much like Swansea, controlled by external factors. While she had a much deeper connection to Curly and Jimmy it is clear that she is a mishmash of emotions. In reality though, how can you blame her? She's consistently pushed aside and shirks her duties when possible. I think out of the few characters they made I'd like to believe this one had some serious decisions to make and is the focus of the *why* much of this happens. No blame on her though, I'd probably do the same though in not so many steps.Daisuke - The child-man. That's pretty mean, he's actually the comedy and tension relief. His personality is so easy going and clay-like. He's much like Swansea in so far as you could probably find someone you know who fits his description. While he is an underling/shadowing Swansea for his job, he is also considered stupid and rather small compared to the rest of the cast. There are nods to him through out and he even helps Jimmy out in particular situations. He also gives into MOUTHWASH and even helps you with Swansea later in the game. Poor kid. Poor Poor Daisuke. Jimmy - Ah yes. Finally. The protagonist of the game. You could also use hero or captain if you wanted though I imagine sadistic villain and psychopath could also cover it. Much of what goes on is interpreted by him as you take command of the ship and name yourself captain. He does a lot of ♥♥♥♥ that kicks much of this game off and is one of the sole driving factors if not the only factor that forces change on the ship. Many of the characters which were mentioned prior are just ripples in his MOUTHWASH. He is emblematic of what a person is following his internal factors to a T, impulsive, arrogant, deceitful, lazy, the list goes on.
