name: Expeditions: A MudRunner Game
detailed_description: Editions Expeditions: A MudRunner Game - Year 1 Edition You will receive the following content when the game launches: • The base game • The Year 1 Content Pass • The Cotco Canyon truck Expeditions: A MudRunner Game - Supreme Edition You will receive the following content when the game launches: • The base game • The Year 1 Content Pass • The Cotco Canyon truck • The Pioneer Pack, including an alternate version of 4 different trucks About the Game From Arizona to the Carpathians, chart through expansive open worlds in search of hidden treasures and forgotten ruins. Expeditions: A MudRunner Game is a groundbreaking off-road simulation crafted by Saber Interactive, creators of the critically acclaimed SnowRunner. Lead research missions as you drive a variety of all-terrain vehicles, using high-tech tools and managing your camp and crew to ensure your success in the wild. Embark on ever-rewarding scientific expeditions as you adapt to nature's challenges. Unravel the mysteries of uncharted lands, whether you're alone behind the wheel of your vehicle, or with fellow travelers in the online co-op mode for up to 4 players. Expeditions: A MudRunner Game builds on the legacy of Saber Interactive’s off-road simulations with its advanced physics-based gameplay systems, perfectly encapsulating the feel of driving through the wilderness. Whether you’re a long-time player of MudRunner games or a newcomer, you are in for a thrilling scientific adventure. Success depends on preparation. Plan your missions carefully and hire a team of Specialists to improve your skills in the field. With the drone and metal detector, scout your itinerary and locate points of interest. Invest the profits from each expedition to expand your home bases by building support structures to gain useful supplies and summon new vehicles. Equip your vehicles with state-of-the-art technologies and cutting-edge gadgets to ensure success in the wild. Use the winch and portable anchors to perform intricate maneuvers, and traverse treacherous rivers with the echo sounder. Choose strategically, as the tools at your disposal can make or break an expedition. Winch: Get your vehicle unstuck from the mud or rappel down steep cliffs Jackscrew: Turn your vehicle back on its wheels after accidental flips Echo sounder: Avoid sinking by probing the depth of the water around your vehicle And much more… Customize your vehicles in the garage, choosing between nimbler scout vehicles, off-road machines or large trucks. Tailor your approach for light and fast exploration or slower, equipment-heavy trucking. Successful expeditions allow you to invest in new accessories, such as storage extensions, spare parts, and measuring tools. From arid deserts to rugged forests and steep mountains, explore vast, uncharted lands brimming with hidden wonders and forgotten ruins. Archaeological sites, dinosaur fossils and natural curiosities can be found in numbers across Arizona and the Carpathians, and each discovery can be the key to groundbreaking scientific breakthroughs.

_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played and enjoyed the originals, you'll be more than happy with this Remastered collection. It's the same old games you know and love, just with: a new lick of paint, achievements, and bonus levels included. Also regardless of whether you prefer the old graphics or new, this collection even allows you to swap between the Remastered graphics and the original textures on the fly! This can actually be really useful for navigating levels & finding hidden items, since the brightness differs in some areas between original & remastered graphics.To help newer players, there's also an option to enable "modern controls", allowing you to ditch the old tank style control scheme for something that you  find more intuitive. That said, even the new controls aren't perfectly smooth, and new players will probably still struggle to enjoy these old classics. The original Tomb Raiders were always hard, even by old game standards. And despite a few small quality of life features, like adding action prompts for switches/ pickups, and dropping the limited "save crystals" mechanic in Tomb Raider 3 (instead allowing unlimited saves, and keeping the crystals as optional collectables)... these games are still fiendish.These games are very much of their time, and that's something you have to accept to be able to enjoy them. All the same, I'm definitely onboard with this remaster. The only other criticisms I have:
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: If you missed Lara's adventures in the 90s or weren't even born yet to enjoy the hype surrounding the original games, you can now catch up without having to buy a PS1 from the nearest retro shop. The first three parts of the legendary trilogy shine in new splendour, and finally more than 20 years after its release I was able to finish the third part for the first time ever! Thanks to the updated controls and the tons of achievements, it's also worth playing through several times, and even the DLCs have been included. Small, decent changes (health bars for boss fights, camera lock-on and the smooth switching back and forth between the original, old version and the remastered one) are excellently implemented. You can feel in every corner that the developers put all their heart and soul into this remaster. It has to be said that quite a few achievements require an enormous amount of insider knowledge about the original trilogy and therefore greatly increase the replay value as well as the one or other ‘try-and-error moment’. What I particularly love is that this remaster remains true to its roots, there is no autosave and your frustration tolerance is put to the test time and time again, just like back then. I can hardly wait until "The Last Revelation" and "Chronicles" will get their remaster,too - at least I really hope so!
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: Historians will one day look back on my life and refer to this as "The Incident". Playing the classic Tomb Raider games for the first time has started me down the path of insanity, I have played for 29 hours and only beaten the first one, am I enjoying it? Absolutely! It's fun to not have your hand held through puzzles and it feels so satisfying when you actually solve it
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: Review for Tomb Raider 1:----------------------------I remember playing the original game on my first self-built PC (486 CPU @100MHz and 16MB RAM), so this remaster was an amazing nostalgic trip for me. The modern controls didn't work for me, but I got used to the tank controls somewhere in the second level. The camera can be extremely frustrating as soon as you're close to a wall, but the level design is brilliant and even today a blast to explore. Only exception for me is the mine level, which has too much needless backtracking and instant-death traps. Also my compliments to the devs for the excellent remaster. It runs and plays great on the Steam Deck.

Think of the games as slow paced methodical puzzle platformers in a style similar to 2d Prince of Persia rather than an action platformer like Mario, this is a much more deliberate style of platforming, with deeper puzzles

Never played the originals besides a few minutes over at my cousins as a kid growing up. Already getting nostalgia of childhood type games and loving every minute of it. _childDocuments_.review: Now this is iconic and the only true Lara. Glad that this triangular sex-symbol of my generation is back in 2024. Tomb Raider II was one of my first games. Played all of them dozens of times. Last time replayed them few years ago. Unfortunately Remaster is full of hits and misses, but overal I'd call it acceptable. Lets's start with the brief overview.What's good?- It absolutely the same game from Core Design. Literally.- Lara looks really good.- Both airbags are at place.- Iconic dual-pistol are at place as well.- You can make a handstand and lock Winstone inside the fridge as before.- You can switch between OG and Remastered visuals with F1 any time.- All 3 games with their add-ons in one place.- Photo mode.- Tons of achievements.- New game+What's bad?- It was handled by Crystal Dynamics.- Lighting. It's a joke.- Random fps drops at certain levels.- A lot of visual bugs and glitching textures. A lot.- Minor censorship and virtue signalling.- Very lazy retexturing in lots of locations, mostly in add-ons.What's controversial?- Modern controls.- Visuals. They are good until they aren't.Ok. Now let's discuss some points that need explanations, excluding obvious ones. My biggest claim here is the lighting. While it's not terrible on it's own, but compared to OG it's totally screwed up. Remember GTA Trilogy [vomits] The Definitive edition? Everything was too damn dark there. TR has the opposite problem - everything is too damn bright here. Everything. TR was rather grim game with lot's of dark rooms and dim light. Here, no matter where you are, in caves, dungeons or sewers, etc - everything is brigh as in some ballroom. You can easily see it when you switch between OG and Remastered visuals. Also, this made flares totally useless. It was a common thing in OG to use one here of there even if you are a veteran of TR series. Here? - chances are that you won't burn even a single one. Now about visuals. Just as I said above. For the most part they look good... untill you encounter the situation where they cause troubles. It is not uncommon issue here when items just blend in with the terrain. Yeah, imagine this paradox, everything is bright, but it is still possbile to miss stuff. I replayed OG TRs dozens of times, remember locations literally of every key, medkit and ammo clip and these new visuals managed to confuse me. There were situations when I enter the room and was like: 'strange, a key/switch was supposed to be here, wher... ah here it it.' Obviously, Crystal Dynamics didn't play their own Remaster enough. I assume they noticed this issue too late, and instead of fixing it, they just added so called 'crutch'. Now everytime to come close to any point of interaction (medkit, switch, movable box), you get big ""!"" on your screen, lol. Absolutely ridiculous but this is how it is. Also, some locations are just not good. Floating islands in TR2, for example, in remaster are just meh. Totally lack any taste and style compared to OG.Technical condition? Overall - good. But at some levels, for example at Opera (yeah, I started with TR2) I had random fps drops to 20. At certain levels, if you start running into closed doors, it may drop fps so hard, that game will freeze for a second or too. Also, flipping or missing textures here or there. 2 at the Deck, 1 at Catacombs, a lot of Xian Temple and so on. It's funny, because you can switch back to OG and see that texture is there, then you switch to Remastered - invisible wall, haha. As to controls, there are classic (tank controls) and modern ones. I play with old ones and they work perfectly. I do not bother with new ones, but I heard that they have some issues. I can't help you with new ones, but if what, just remember that the game was created with tank controls in mind, so don't be afraid to switch back to classic ones.I mentioned achievs as an advantage not because it is something great on it's own, but because here they will really stimulate you to replay the game differently and choose various interesting options. Keep in mind, gameplaywise nothing new was added. It just proves one more what a titanic work was done by Core Design decades ago, if after so many years you can squeeze so much content out of it.In the end - I still strongly recommend the game. Well, mostly because it is still THAT game. It seems like Crystal Dynamics are just intentionally rage baiting us by doubtful statements and by doing/undoing censorship just to sabotage their own game. If they condemn something in these games, obviously, they hate OG TR and OG Lara. Don't give them such joy.

As a veteran TR player i prefer the classic setup, but it would be great the dev team fand a way to fix modern inputs, which would provide a fresh and new perspective of the classic.

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond 60fps and some high-poly models, what have Aspyr actually done to improve this game? Let's take a look:The 'modern control' system that has been added for the remaster is fundamentally not fit for purpose. It removes or obscures certain functions that are essential to navigating the grid-based world as it was designed back in 1996, such as being able to easily step and turn in order to position yourself. Some portions of the game are literally impossible to complete with this control scheme. The free camera for this system is also broken - in some contexts the camera will snap wildly about, and given that movement is camera-relative when swimming, for instance, once again the game becomes impossible to play using this new scheme.The 'start' button on your controller doesn't take you to the pause menu, it changes the graphics from new to old. On the PS4 controller I use, the 'Share' button - the one no-one ever uses - is the pause button. So if you're in a pinch and need to use an item or change weapons quickly, you might find yourself switching back to 20fps PS1 graphics while you get attacked. These buttons are the *only* controls in the game that can't be reconfigured.The original game has a checkpoint save system by way of 'save crystals' dotted around the levels. These have been removed and replaced with the option to save any time, but there is no longer any reminder to save and no autosave feature whatsoever. So if you forget to save and die you could end up reloading in a different level. And finally, the new item models have been resized to be more realistic - meaning that the keys that used to be easy to spot are now tiny and often the same colour as the texture they're sitting on. On one occasion I only found a key by accident because I happened to change the graphics mode and suddenly a large visible key popped up in front of me. On more than one occasion I had to resort to a walkthrough because I kept walking past a near-invisible keySo...beyond the frame rate and some of the artwork, literally every change made to this game actively makes the game worse? I initially wrote this review as a warning to new players about the fundamental clunkiness of the original game, but as I continued playing, the more important issue turned out to be that this is an unbelievably low-effort release that somehow makes an insanely clunky third-person platformer *less-playable*. I strongly suspect the game wasn't playtested, or the testers were ignored as I cannot imagine a scenario in which a human with a brain didn't flag the new control scheme and the key models and the lack of level-start auto-saves as being inherently terrible ideas. I don't know why they wouldn't fix the misaligned textures of the original unless they simply palette-swapped every texture in the game and didn't bother to check beyond that. I also noticed that the glittering effect for Midas' hand turning Lara to gold had been removed, but when turning the bars to gold it remains - the only instance of an old PS1 effect in the new remaster. So development seems to have been at the very best, rushed by the publisher, and at worst actively lax with a 'we'll fix it if enough people pay for it' mantra. I strongly suspect the original graphics mode is one button-press away as a crutch to compensate for the issue of model invisibility. The fact that tank controls are default feels like a subtle acknowledgement.You can and should ignore the new controls. But you can't ignore the other changes, only deal with them. I played these when I was a kid and while I had my progress set back because of checkpoint saves, I never had my progress set back because I was too focused on playing the game, and I was never sent back to the level before I died. I never wasted my time searching for keys that were right in front of me. I never drowned because the camera wouldn't respond to my inputs.I cannot think of a bigger indictment of the industry than the fact that an ugly, janky fledgling platformer for the PS1 came out more functional on day-one of release than its 'remaster' did 28 years later. What a bad joke.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: Tomb Raider II was my first 3D game and will always be my favorite. I was waiting for this remaster for a long time and was not disappointed. Usually, when I return to an old game after a few years, graphics looks outdated, because it looked "state of the art" in my memories. However, this was not the case. Thanks to graphic overhaul, it looks exactly how I remember it and moreover, the new Game+ mode made the game as difficult as I remember it from my first play-through... ...just amazing! Thanks to the new photo-mode I could finally explore some inaccessible areas.Yes, textures could be better (visible AI artifacts, no bump mapping etc.) but frame-rate and lighting system is pretty fine (considering how the original TR engine worked) and real-time switching between an original and new graphics is fantastic.Definitely recommend this game to any fan of the originals. It is more than a quality nostalgia trip.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: Sure, we could keep modding and patching the first 3 Tomb Raider games to death and the fans kinda have over the years.But with this version? it brings the games up to a more modern compatibility standard with most machinesmostly improves on the textures, models and lighting, gives you a retro to modern toggle, adds over 260 achievements which are nods to all sorts of trivia and glitches in the trio of games Does all of this while also not losing the soul of the first 3 games that made Lara Croft a videogaming iconIt experiments too with new small things like boss health bars and a photo mode, but it's all harmless stuff which respects the source material. Allow some modding and this is basically the definitive way to play the first 3 Tomb Raiders for generations to come, with the same kind of flair and attention to detail as those updates to quake 1 and 2.The only big letdown I noticed is the updated somehow even inferior at times water textures and the cutscenes just look like sloppy AI upscaled versions of the originals.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: I have always preferred the LAU trilogy over the classics, as they were what I grew up with, but playing the remasters has been an extremely fun experience so far. The new visuals are stunning, and I like the modern controls, although the camera is very buggy at times. As someone with little experience playing the classics apart from TRLE levels, I am happy that the remasters have breathed new life into them, and I am thoroughly enjoying playing TR1-3 properly for the first time.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: This set of remasters is simply stunning. The first 3 games are given a visual overhaul, along with their expansion packs. They have added modern controls, which i dislike, as i  can run the tank controls all day long, and the ability to change to the original graphics. The attention to details is simply stunning, and leaves you with greatly enhanced environments. A greatly enhanced model of Lara Croft much akin the box art in the original games, and advertisements for the games, and pistols are also modeled after such box art. I am currently on the Opera House level of Tomb Raider two, and thus far it has been amazing to see the transformation that has taken place. Weather traipsing about the Croft Manor,  or tackling daunting puzzles, visuals are a pure delight. there are now 3D pickups so items like Medipacks, Ammunition, and secrets, have more reality to them. This remastered collection is definitely worth 30 dollars, and worth picking up. There has been a lot of care and dedication to this collection, and those who would not like it would be those who cannot get used to the controls. Either the modern style, and or original, and or those who expect more out of this collection that what it is. A faithful reproduction of original classics, slightly revamped and modernized, with support for 4K UHD 60 frames a second
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: I have never had the chance to play The Lost Artefact DLC for Tomb Raider 3. I would have paid $30 for this experience alone... I am blown away. Thank you so much for making this remastered collection. To all of those people who gave this game a negative review because you didn't like an optional control scheme, do us all a favour, and stop reviewing games. That is a petty reason to label a game as bad. Thanks!
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a pointless Trigger Warning and they censored breasts, but not the micro P E N I S E S in the Colosseum. If nudity is evil, it should be completely censored. You don't get to pick and choose.With mods, this is the best way to play these games. Not only did they NOT make Lara ugly. They made her HOTTER than she was back in 1996. Controls are better, but still frustrating because of the engine it was made in at the time. It's honestly impressive. I was waiting to see this game be completely ruined, either by hijacking the game to push a political message ( whoops, they couldn't help but censor women while keeping the micro P E N I S E S), they didn't make Lara ugly. Or release the game in a broken state. This remaster is surprisingly good. Just need mods to revert the censorship and allow you to play the whole trilogy in the wet suit. That would be awesome.

_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't expected that old TR suck me in again SO MUCH. With improved graphics it turns out that game is not only playable but actually still good! It has some obscurities in terms of enemies: there are too many of them and their placement is sometimes weird (when they are waiting for you in tight, unusual places). Human enemies are even worse: their stupidity and lethality still hurts, too. But Tomb Raider is a game of discovery, exploration and solving puzzles. And it easily exceeds in these 3 aspects many other games, even modern AAA ones. Play with modern controls, although some patience and time are needed to learn the game with these. But it's worth it.PROS:- beautiful graphics, colours, lighting- exploration , puzzles, mysteries!- watching how Lara moves and explores is still satisfying!- option of switching graphics in any time- feeling of nostalgia is so strong!- modern controls with free cameraCONS:- it needs time to get used to TR again; some players may hit the wall- combat is still flawed and sometimes there is too much of it- occasional problems with camera- modern controls are good but flawed and patch would be welcome- no graphic options (ray tracing? different filters?), no gameplay options- swamps could look better (but it's a nitpick).Remaster has its flaws but at the same time it's faithful to the original which was, and is again great game! Hopefully success of this TR bring us more remasters and show Crystal Dynamics what real TR were about and what is truly important in Lara's adventures! Highly recommended

_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant graphical update to what are, in my opinion, the best Tomb Raider games. There's been no real changes to the gameplay, asides from a few quality-of-life improvements and the odd game-breaking bug fixed (most of the other bugs have been left in, with a few achievements for finding them!), and the graphical improvements can be turned off with the F1 key - which is oddly not shown in the controls, nor is F3 for Photo Mode - making this the best way to enjoy classic Tomb Raider on modern systems.For half the price of most games, you get three full games and their expansions, giving the average gamer around 50 hours of playtime, making this an absolute bargain! It is also a fascinating insight into early mass-market 3D adventure games, and the gameplay still holds up to modern standards. For those complaining about the lack of a rewind function, just do what I do, and have done since the original releases in the 1990s, which is spam F5 to quicksave and F9 to quickload. There's no limit to how many times you can save, and you can have multiple slots as well. Plus, Stella's Tomb Raider site has save files and walkthroughs in case you really get stuck.It would also be nice to have a level select function once you have completed the game, though you can just download save files, use the level skip cheat, or create a new save in a different slot at the start of each level.Update 7th March - I have found a few issues with Tomb Raider III, including a wall that you can swim through in the Nevada level (this wall isn't present in the old graphics), as well as sounds for boulders and spike walls becoming very high pitched and quiet after the first India level. There is also an overall issue with the increased draw distance making it possible to occasionally see behind the scenery, though this is only a very minor issue.Hopefully, these are things that the developer will patch out, as they do seem to be working on a big patch at the moment.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: To anyone complaining about the controls or anyone who is curious about the bad reviews concerning that:i played the originals in the 90s on a computer and let me tell you something, if you play this remake on a pc with no controller, it is going to feel exactly the same as it did 20 years ago. there is nothing ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up or clunky. i was confused at first while using a controller because the joystick that controls the camera feels absolutely of if you try to navigate the camery free while lara is bound to be controlled in a more step after step motion rather than flowing through the obstacles like altair. so, if you dont use modern controllers, you realize that this remake is one of the best available. because its a reMAKE not a reBOOT. dont get me startet on the graphics, the way they added 3d models and made them look like their old 2d counterparts is GENIUS, i never adored ladders that much in my life. 11/10.

_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: There are many ways of alienating an existing player base with a remake or remaster, but this collection managed to do several of them: insulting players and the original developers as "inexcusable" racists in a trigger warning (first thing you see when starting the game), removing content that was in the originals to begin with, censoring and changing the games further post-release. This release angered a lot of people, unnecessarily, but at least Saber/Aspyr reversed, with the third patch, some of the censorship which was added post release.This whole affair left players with a very bad taste in their mouth, but it speaks well of the publisher if they listened to complaints and corrected course.So, how good is this collection of classic Lara Croft games? Mildly disappointing. This release is indeed faithful to the original experience, at least in terms of gameplay. A couple of changes I'm not a fan of: health bar in bosses, and action object indicators which make the puzzles easier but these can, at least, be switched off in the options. Not the bosses bars, though.I'd have preferred to see more graphical options to better exploit the capabilities of your card, because what's in the package is the bare minimum. No configurable antialiasing, or filters of any kind. Look for anything like video options in the settings menu, and you'll find nothing. Textures and models are kind of bland and they don't improve that much the visual appearance of the originals, save for being high res. Neither do they keep a close resemblance to the old textures in the aesthetic level. The games feature a different visual style than they used to have, but I can't really say that the change is for the better; some of the atmosphere has been lost in the translation. Many players seem to switch to the original textures for this reason, which is an option included in the game. But playing with pixelated graphics kind of defeats the purpose of buying this collection... not to mention that the classic texture mode, for some reason, limits your display to 30 FPS. And they actually feel like less.Its hard for me to recommend "Tomb Raider remastered". I feel that it doesn't improve on the originals, but neither is faithful enough to them in certain cosmetic and UI elements... it is more of a middle of the road compromise which will satisfy nobody, not the purists, not the people expecting a modernized version. And a couple of elements still remain censored despite initial claims on the contrary. Overall, this is a far too lazy and low budget effort to earn a recommendation from me. My advice is to skip it and keep playing the originals instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: Solid remasters that improve the graphics plenty and stay faithful to the original games in terms of levels, no unnecessary changes etc.However, be prepared to play with the old "tank" controls if you want to avoid frustration. Movement behaves differently depending on whether or not you have your guns out too which takes some getting used to. Modern controls also has some of the original move set completely disabled which can make various platforming more difficult.

_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of good stuff here, but the AI-upscaled textures just don't work at all. If you're someone who has dabbled in AI image upscaling (ESRGAN etc.) yourself, you'll absolutely be able to spot the tell-tale artifacts. The new textures also tile very poorly which feels careless. These textures about on par with what you'd see in something like Morrowind Enhanced Textures (which AI upscales Morrowind's textures) which is neat... for a free mod made by amateurs. (And the textures in that mod do tile properly, mind you.) For a £20 professional remaster I'd expect something more carefully done. The redone models here are pretty good, so clearly Aspyr does have some artists working at the company.Also it would be excellent if the classic models and textures could be combined with the high-frame rates and new lighting.The total lack of graphics settings is also crazy.Edited:I can only assume the Jester ratings are from people who are easily pleased? If you can't see the upscaling artifacts I envy how carefree your life must be (or feel bad for your untreated cataracts) but they are not subtle. There's a lot of promise here - I'm fond of the geometry changes and new character models - but it's clear Eidos/Squenix forced the small dev team to cut corners to get a minimum acceptable product out for Feb 14.Hell, even the map geometry changes get much sparser after TR1. Lara's Manor in TR1 got 3D windows, but they disappear going into 2 and 3; and the doors inside the house become an inconsistent mix of new models and old flat surfaces. Just a microcosm of what feels very much like a product that was shipped 2/3 of the way through development. Especially given I haven't even mentioned the bugs, like painting textures appearing in water where they shouldn't, or baffling decisions like nearly-invisible keys, that give off the strong impression that QA testing wasn't a priority.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who played these games when they came out, this is fantastic! If you're nostalgic for the 90's era PS1 Tomb Raider games then this will be an 11/10. If you're coming from the newest trilogy and have not experienced these I think you'll really love discovering what made Tomb Raider so popular to begin with. The little quality of life improvements are great and I'm really enjoying them. Please make a Last Revelation and Chronicles Remaster!
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: These remasters are a labour of love. If you've played the trilogy before and are an old fan, you will love this.Use the classic/tank controls (I haven't bothered trying the modern controls). Tomb Raider requires precise platforming skills; the controls can be a little frustrating for new players but it pays off to learn and master them.Be prepared to explore, solve puzzles and shoot enemies. Most of the time the games won't tell you what you need to do to progress. You will have to try, fail and try again. Some parts can be difficult but it feels very rewarding when you conquer a level or when you discover every secret and pickup in a tomb.Tomb Raider is an iconic video game franchise and these 3 games are the reason why.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying that this remaster was very well made. The rendered layouts of the worlds are beautiful, from each minute detail to the most elaborate of designs the worlds are absolutely stunning to view. From the lush vegetation to the awesome stone reliefs of the architectural structures it's truly amazing. The iconic musical scores were truly beautiful as i remembered it being aswell. As a veteran gamer, Me and my son played all Tomb Raider games on the first Playstation console, Tomb Raider 1-5. At the time I was a younger man and my son was about 2, our first exposure to Lara Croft was Tomb Raider 2, my most favorite of the initial games. We mastered all games with 100% completion and all secrets found. Of course he also finished the remake, Legend, Anniversary and Underworld. I finished Tomb Raider 2013, and Rise of The Tomb Raider, also almost Finished Shadow of the Tomb Raider. Playing this again bought a tear to my eyes as it took me back to simpler times, when gaming was a family event and all the fond memories that I have of my son and my wife at the time just came flooding back again. I definitely appreciate Aspyr for preserving the Lara Croft that we always remembered and loved. The camera panning is as crazy as I remembered it being lol!
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: Great remaster, a lot of care went to it. Even if crystal are negligent it seems Aspyr cared. _childDocuments_.review: The game, despite the nostalgic atmosphere, has one of the worst "Modern Controls", and the lack of any graphic settings, there is not even the ability to change the brightness or disable / disable vertical sync, a plus for the developers that they left the original controls, but it would be nice if, in addition to subtle graphical changes, they put more attention to this release, especially in the context of the already discussed controls, which here by one of the worst camerawork spoils completely any enjoyment of the game
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: For fans of the original Tomb Raider trilogy, this remaster is good. It gives you that nostalgic feeling from your first play through, which was for some of  us 26 years ago (holy sh*t). Alone for that, it is worth the price.Objectively, the graphics are like a 1000% improvement from the original, but nowhere near a modern game. The controls are exactly like you remember them, which is a good thing in my opinion. However, if you have not played the original trilogy, the controls will be a pain in the a**, since 90s gaming was not even remotely as convenient as it is today. Likewise, the sounds are basically the same as in the original, which heavily contributes to that nostalgic feeling. From nowadays perspective, the sound simply s***s. Therefore, this game will be great for 35+ gamers who played the original. For new players, it may be not worth it. All in all, a fun remaster. I would give it a B on A to F scale. The only true point of criticism for me is that they did not remake the cut scences. There are not that many, this should have been possible for a 30€ game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: If you played it in the mid of 1990, you will get flask backs. Control is totally different to what is today's standard. It takes some use to it. The remastered graphic is very nice done, but some ways are even harder to spot. Definitely the money worth. Would recommend it if you know Tomb Raider, or are interested what it was in the 90. Enjoy
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: Reviewing this game seems pretty simple to me.  It is the first three games with a fresh paint of graphics applied to the original control scheme.  To this end, if you loved those first three games and don't mind the controls are not very easy to get used to, this is the game for you.  Personally, I was really hoping they would update it to the scheme used in the newer games or even the games Underworld or Legacy.Visually speaking it is a very nice step up and as a showcase of how graphics have evolved, it has a neat option to switch from old-school to modern(ish) visuals.  I can't speak on the audio given my hearing impairment.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: It is very fun to have The Original Lara Croft back in action with her iconic dual pistols, beauty and desire for adventuringnot to be some hero or finish her dads work, but simply because as she says herself "I only play for sport."There are some rough spots however. The new controls that are available for the game I found to be very strange to play with so I chose to play withthe original tank controls.There is not a graphics options tab in this game, and while it isn't really a big deal since it doesn't really need it, it still would have been nice.Sometimes the remastered graphics have a tendency to have places be a bit too dark, so you have to switch to the old graphics to get a better view of the environment, keys on the floor are sometimes a bit too difficult to spot with the remastered graphics as well.Outside of this however I am incredibly happy with how this remaster turned out. Lara's model in my opinion looks a lot like she did in the FMVs of the original games and graphically reminds me a lot of Angel of Darkness. It is very charming and cartoony which I think is a fitting style and I would love to see more Tomb Raider games with this art style.I also love some of the Quality of Life improvements like the "walk to action" option.Overall I'm very happy with this Remaster. It is not perfect but the issues I have are very smalland can hopefully be fixed in a patch.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: If you're not pulled in by nostalgia alone, you'll also find plenty of huge locales to explore, tricky platform sequences and beautiful updated graphics. Combat is a little bit tedious at times (especially in Tomb Raider 2) and by the last level puzzles can feel a bit repetitives, but nothing beats the joy of raiding a tomb with the great adventurer Lara Croft herself and relaxing in her humble abode with the last mystical trinket she snatched from ancient temples and gorgeus ruins.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: This is so amazing! Last time I played these games I was, I think, just 2, and now, 20 years later, being able to jiggle with Lara around good ol' locations and 'dying/falling' places with revamped looks is just priceless. Just glittering, might I say?!I don't want to criticise the new games too much, as they are still not bad, but this is the real Lara, not that. Thank you to Saber Interactive and Aspyr Media. I hope the Embracer Group will follow their good gut and EMBRACE the Classic Lara, and not undermine her like Crystal Dynamics did.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the greatest remasters for one of the greatest video game trilogies ever made. I hope they continue updating and improving the modernized controls. _childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say?!It's pure nostalgia!I love how much love the developers put into this remaster.Of course there are some textures that look a bit strange, but in the end it's a visual masterpiece when you look at the original classic parts. Experience Lara like never before!Because the graphics scheme changes between classic and new on demand, you quickly get an impression of what the developers have achieved there and how much attention and love to detail there is in everything.I also understand that the classic tank controls seem more alien to some people because many people didn't grow up with them.I also understand the problem with the modern controls, as they don't seem to be fully developed.But seriously, people: The game was originally from 1996 +, the action-adventure genre was not yet defined for 3D games at that time.This means that everyone initially developed on their own until it became clear what customers/players preferred.So this game is a remaster. The core of a remaster is to adapt the graphics to modern ones and, if necessary, fix bugs.In my opinion, the developers have more than succeeded. It feels like it used to, only now it's very pretty. I found myself thinking that from today's perspective I don't think the classic graphics are that great anymore, since I can now play an alternative.I really wish that they also do TR4 and TR5 and, for that matter, AoD too. Please make this possible so that I can enjoy all the classic parts as much as I can today with the remasterd!For the classic games 1-3 you also get the respective DLC´s for your money.So big booty for “little” money!A clear purchase recommendation from me if you just want to experience the classic games of your childhood in a new style.Stay away if you're just too modern and too stupid to deal with tanky or bad modern controls. It's better not to do it then, because you probably won't learn that in the future either :DIt's a 90's game, what do you expect :PDisclamer: My englisch is not the yellow from the egg but you will understand :PPPP
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: It's not without it's problems... but it IS the definitive way to play these games.Full support of modern controller standards. Good compatibility with a wide number of systems. Beautiful without sacrificing the aesthetics of the original games. And it has options for people who struggle to adapt to the classic "tank" controls.That doesn't mean it's a collection without problems. At the time of this review the first (possibly only) big patch is yet to be released, and there are plenty of minor issues in the game because of that, from audio issues to missing or wrong textures to issues with the "modern" control option provided. So far, in the time I've spent in the game, though, none of these have been game breaking.HIGHLY recommend if you're a long-time fan of the series and looking to either re-experience the originals or play them for the first time. The loss of the distance fog in every level ALONE is worth the entrance price.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty much everything I would want from a remaster. The same great games but better looking.Was clearly worked on by a team passionate about the trilogy.Even runs at 4k 60FPS on the deck.I recommend sticking with the original controls as the games were designed around them. Using dpad or keyboard is the way to play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, just wow, it's so beautiful! Completed every level and this is my revised review upon full completion. As a fan of the original trilogy this is amazing. Beautiful graphics, old school controls, and original soundtrack. Also I really appreciate the new ability to play with any costume you want on any level you want (once you complete a game). This is a dream come true feature. I always wanted to use Lara's catsuit in my favorite level, Area 51.Minor beefs:-1. Modern control setting is off by default but the day one version didn't let me side or back jump in the classic Lara style. So I switched back to Tank controls. The revised version may be better but I haven't tried.2. As expected they didn't really remaster the FMV cinematics. Yes they are slightly better, since the originals (when played on a modern PC LCD) looked weird as they were designed for CRT. So now they look proper on LCD but aren't a bump up in graphics. So you go from beautiful in game graphics to the old school FMVs & it sort of ruins immersion. But I'd rather have them than lose them.3. I keep accidentally hitting Start to pause but now which causes me to switch to old school graphics. Now I know that was an advertised feature & I understand why this may be cool for some but I'm here to play remastered graphics all the way through. Instead I get that beer goggles effect in a bar with a charming lady becoming an oaf after a sober morning each time I accidentally (out of reflex) try to pause. Maybe provide a way to turn that feature off or do what PS4 would do for re-released PS2 games and make the touch pad on PS controllers into the new Start / Pause button.It may seem like I typed more negatives than positives but it's just because the positives left me speechless, but I highly recommend this game if you can handle old school Tank controls and the charm of exploration with it's occasions of frustrations. If it gets really difficult for the new generation Google Stella's Tomb Raider guides or YouTube walkthroughs for guidance.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a good remaster for people who have played the game before. Also very fair pricing. However the controls are so hard to get used to if you never played the originals. Modern Controls is a cool feature but broken. There are some mechanics that are disabled all together when using the new updated controls. The camera when in tight spaces breaks, it's impossible to look anywhere. It takes a while to get used to the original tank controls but in my opinion this is still the way to play this game. You aren't as snappy and mobile but you feel more precise and in control of the character.Then for a new remaster the lack of features is strange. There is no menu to change resolution/graphics, etc. Auto-saves could have been implemented in between levels or in certain parts of a level aka checkpoints.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: Exactly what you should expect from a remaster, definite buy for new fans who want to experience the old games and for older fans who want to re-experience the best games of the franchise, I tried using the modern controls but honestly I think the classic tank controls are the way to go, for people who haven't used old school tank controls it'll be jarring at first but you'll get the hang of it soon enough, overall highly recommend picking this up
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: I can't get over how essential this remaster is - Aspyr have done some incredible work making these 30(?!) year old games feel fresh and look great.Some aspects of tomb raider's design still feels a bit jank, but at its best, the levels are these incredible rube goldberg machines and puzzle boxes. Adding in the option to play without tank controls feels great! There's some clunk with being unable to back-step without pulling your guns out, but, 99% of the time, it's a huge boon.There's at least 70 hours of content here?! at this price point, that's crazy good value.I genuinely believe Aspyr have what it takes to make Angel of Darkness good.This is strongly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying I've loved Tomb Raider since my then-wife bought me a copy in 1996 for the PS1. I've played through TR1 literally dozens of times over the years, it's one of my favorite games of all-time. TR2 and TR3 I've completed previously on PS1 and I've enjoyed both. I've owned every PS1 game, AoD on PS2, I have every game in the series, both from Core & Crystal Dynamics days on my Steam account. This is easily the best looking version of the original TR1-TR3. But it's far from ideal. I've not even gotten to TR2 or TR3 yet. These are my thoughts as I get frustrated with my initial playthrough of TR1.Issues:1. Lack of sidestep buttons. They've replaced it with JUST the walk button, which makes both walking and sidestepping significantly more frustrating than it ever was in the original. Seriously. We have more than enough buttons, give us back dedicated sidestepping.2. No quick save/quick load buttons. Come on guys. This is PC in 2024. It's BEYOND PATHETIC to not have an option for a quick save & quick load.3. They're false advertising. These are NOT the originals with prettier graphics. The New Game + in the originals granted you unlimited ammo. These morons have decided to not only ditch that, but to increase the enemy health as well. Seriously. Someone should have slapped the idiot that recommended that asinine option.Having only recently played through both the original PS1 version AND the Steam version of TR1 (patched to the gold version), this version IS more attractive. But it plays horribly by comparison thanks to the poor decision to leave out the sidestep buttons and to change NG+ from a reward to a punishment. If they wanted a hard mode they should've added it and left NG+ alone, or at least made a NG++ mode.This is NOT a horrible package. But it is an inferior one in the most important ways (gameplay/controls) compared to the originals. If they'd fix the control options & NG+, the game would be a near perfect package.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are willing to play with keyboard and tank controls, this is actually a fine remaster but if you are playing with a controller, DO NOT bother! Both schemes, tank and modern controls are broken with a controller.For the audacity of putting out such a shoddy control scheme I wasn't recommending this at first. Controller will give you a bad time and put you in a bad mood.Texture work is pretty terrible in some places, seams everywhere, textures are not tiling. It looks like patchwork and very jarring. Overall though, it does a good job 80% of the time. There are some pros and cons to everything:- Textures, look nice but often don't tile and look more like a bad Minecraft HD mod- Lighting is great but can change the atmosphere drastically. You never get the feeling of being underground as there are holes everywhere to get light in.If you are willing to put up with that, there's no better way to play TR1-3 other than the open source engines.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very lovingly made revamp of the Tomb Raider franchise's golden years. _childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, remaster or not, these are just really fun classic titles so that alone is enough for me to recommend these games. The visual upgrade this remaster provides elevates them to a whole 'nother level though. I particularly love how many stages have new ceiling openings that provide nice natural atmospheric lighting. The model and texture work is great as well, most notably the added foliage in certain environments and Lara herself. She looks just like how she does in the classic in-game FMVs but even better. The coolest part of all is that at any point in the game (aside from like loading screens) you can press a button and instantly switch between the Classic and Remastered graphics.Not that it bothers me too much personally but the new "Modern Controls" don't seem to be that great to use. Honestly, I feel that was always going to be a given though because the original games are entirely built around Lara's "Tank Controls" and how those controls work with the geometry of the game space. Also, the lack of a level select feature is a bit baffling though I guess it isn't a huge issue at the moment for me given that you can just create new saves at any point in the game.Aspyr has been releasing various patches over the past couple of months that have fixed or tweaked various visuals and even added new features such as an unlockable outfit selector. So despite some problems I have with this game, I can still very much recommend it because it does seem that Aspyr is putting in the effort to go back and get things juuust right. I hope in the upcoming months this collection will continue to receive various improvements and features alongside Tomb Raider IV-VI Remastered when that releases. I can't overstate just how nice it is to have these games on modern platforms and presented in such a way that feels so faithful to the original visual style of the franchise.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: This is the definitive version of classic Tomb Raider! A lot of love, care and attention to detail has been given to these 3 amazing games which stand the test of time impeccably. There's nothing like them and hasn't been since. Besides the gorgeous and faithful graphical overhaul they added 2 great Qol options for new players. The interaction indicator which takes out the guesswork on certain mechanics and the photo mode which serves as a "scanner" for the level for when you get stuck and don't really know what to do next. Of course their use is completely optional. No comment on the "modern" controls option. I'll argue these games didn't even need the optionIf you're a fan of the original games you should absolutely buy this! If you're new to classic TR then also go for it and find out why we fell in love with them in the late 90s. I really hope they do Last Revelation/Chronicles next so we can have the complete classic Core Design saga.

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up on the original three Tomb Raider Titles and I loved them to death... But eventually my Playstation died and and there weren't new systems being made anymore and in fact I upgraded to the Playstation 2. Which wasn't bad but eventually the Playstation 2 went the way of it's original system save? I've also bought the X-Box and Gamecube too! But one day? I looked at ALL my consoles and figured out HOW MUCH CASH I BLEW on all of them. EXPENSIVE and I can't afford this type of expense anymore but PC? Yes the system is generally twice as expensive to start with but perk? You buy a new PC when you old one dies? You simply transfer all your old games to the new PC. PC towers also have their own set of headaches but? Their flexibility makes them worth it. But Tomb Raider was one of the few Playstation games I couldn't emulate successfully on the PC no matter what emulator I used. Something game breaking always glitched IF the game would run at all.So I was actually excited to buy this remastered version and better yet? Seems to be running flawlessly. It's almost actually painful to watch the original graphics on a Hi-Def TV! LOL. More importantly? The gameplay itself hasn't been touched and the camera going wonky occasionally in Tomb Raider? Remember this was one of the FIRST EARLY games to play in third person as the vast majority of the time? Camera works just fine.I loved the first Tomb Raider, the second one was kind of hum ho and the final third one? WAS THE BEST easily! These classic games are easily worth $10 a pop, granted a lot of people whom never played the original Tomb Raider? Going to HATE the controls but the game was actually DESIGNED around them too. Some jumps HAVE TO BE MADE PERFECT or YOU WILL DIE. A standing jump and a running jump definitely define how far you CAN jump and it takes Lara exactly of square to hit running speed and also when you pull back? She hops EXACTLY one square back so you can get the perfect running space needed.Well enough going down memory lane, there's a REASON Tomb Raider was so good back in it's day and with the graphics touch up to roughly today's standards? It's not an eye sore either. But if you are into games where you need instant gratification? Avoid this game like the plague. This game is about exploring and figuring out how to get from point a to b with a decent story tied to it. The creatures are more jump scares than anything else as it usually is the levels themselves that are the MOST dangerous to you. Granted, definitely don't try wrestling with a bear either! LOL. Don't know why but ALL animals hate Lara and all the people she meets? Want her dead too! But great game just the same.

_childDocuments_.review: This is what Embracer Group's IP buying spree has got you - closing established studios halfway through projects, and bare bones rehashing of established IP so they can get money for old rope. Barely qualifies as a remaster - it's nothing in the league of Mass Effect Legendary, where you had graphical and gameplay changes (at least in ME1), or Halo, where the older games were pretty advanced for their time but still got updates in graphics, audio and gameplay. No, if there's any games that needed gameplay changes, it's the ones that are 28 years old - and these didn't get it.They aren't bad games - they are some of my favourites. But as a remaster? For $30? This is very basic stuff, with very basic improvements. Graphically they've slapped some new textures over it, brought in new models, and now their mouths move to speech, etc. There's new lighting, but it's pretty hit and miss. "Lovingly restored" is a stretch when most of the textures could have been bought on the Substance store. There's no depth to them. They look *better* but I would never go so far as to say *good*. But I can't hear any improvement in audio, which is disappointing - it lacks any kind of depth, when the vast improvements in audio tech in the last couple of decades could have done wonders. It's still like we're stuck listening to static CD tracks like the original Playstation versions.The gameplay improvement they did implement - modern controls - really struggles to work in the old environment - the one that hasn't changed to any appreciable degree. These games are on an obvious grid system that works with tank controls but not modern controls, which give you more freedom but at a cost. Modern controls interfere with shooting, the camera regularly gets blocked by and/or clips into walls, and they're woefully inaccurate because of this - they interfere with jumping, they interfere with the cutscenes (which aren't cutscenes, gameplay carries on while the camera is struggling with this). Your gameplay will be very classic and very *90s* because they didn't change a damn thing. No other observable gameplay changes.And no UI changes. Not even that. You don't even deserve that for your $30.And there are still bugs - controller freezes are my main issue, but then you have stuff like the camera clipping through the walls or the character in confined spaces, etc. Stuff that would have been fixed in a "lovingly restored" version of these games - but isn't here.To call this "lovingly restored" is an outright lie - it's received the most basic mods to be able to call it a remaster. Do you like Tomb Raider? Love the originals? This is for you. You'd probably find this forgivable. But is this an acceptable way to ask for $10 per game? No. The starting price for this should have been much lower, because then it'd reflect the amount of effort that's gone into it.There's no on the fence here. I like Tomb Raider but this is so low effort I can't even think about recommending it at any price.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: Yes I do have more than 5 minutes of playtime… but Steam does not recognise offline playtime. I've played it for about 5 hours on the Steam Deck while on the go.I'm a big Tomb Raider fan myself, and I think this is the definitive way to play the game.I started with Shadow of the Tomb Raider, and worked myself backwards until the first Tomb Raider game from 1996, but I couldn't really get into it. I stopped playing after 4 hours feeling frustrated by the controls, and I barely made it through the first level and got stuck in the second.The first, second and third Tomb Raiders used exclusively Tank Controls. In case you don't know, Tank controls means that the player character moves into the direction they are looking, as opposed to the control scheme used in virtually all games today, where the character moves where the camera is looking. Tank controls have a big problem, they are very unintuitive. The remaster solves this problem by giving you modern controls with the option to move the camera and an updated control scheme. This has allowed me to finally get into the game, I'm already in the third level and i'm no longer feeling like fighting against my own brain constantly. Playing has turned from a chore into being enjoyable.The game includes an option to toggle between the old and new look on the fly, I just love this feature. It highlights how much the graphics have improved. And while there are some areas, particularly caves and the first level, that only feel like a slight improvement, many areas have become significantly more beautiful, especially Lara's house in the tutorial and outdoor areas featuring plants. The textures are no longer a blurry, pixelated mess. 2D 'sprites' (a rotating texture that was meant to give the illusion of a 3D object. A common technique in old games) have been replaced with actual highly detailed models. Lara herself has perhaps been given the biggest graphics overhaul, previously she looked kinda like a doll. Water, and other visual effects have also been significantly improved, they added small details to some scenes like snow falling in from a gap in the ceiling, or fireflies, and so on. The improvements are too numerous here to list them all. Go watch a review on youtube like Digital Foundry's if you wanna see everything that changed in detail.The game also features numerous other improvements, like almost 300 achievements. Higher framerates. Steam cloud support, and controller support. These, although often taken for granted, make the game much more playable and enjoyable in my opinion.You might've noticed that the game has a verified rating for the Deck. Is it warranted? Absolutely! The original games were barely playable on deck, and had issues such as no controller support, cutscenes were messed up, inaccurate colors, and the third game had no sound at all. So far my experience has been butter smooth, and while this PC port has issues on desktop with stuttering, it runs absolutely fine on the Deck, out of the box. It makes it the best way to enjoy this trilogy.While the modern controls made the game playable for me, they are by no means perfect. My biggest issue is that the camera completely crap the bed once you get anywhere near a wall, which is… pretty often considering Lara likes to explore caves. This is really annoying and hopefully the devs will improve this soon. Also there is no dedicated button for stepping backwards (or sideways) any more, in the modern controls. There are workarounds, for example, backstepping still works when Pistols are equipped. Or my personal favorite, dangling from the ledge I want to jump across, then vaulting back up, and doing a roll will do exactly the same as 1 step back. But the fact that the devs just neglected to include this important function for a platforming game is honestly baffling.I don't know what the devs were thinking about remastering the whole game but leaving the crappy original cutscenes in. Much of the games' story is told via these, and they look just as bad as in the 1996 version. Maybe a little sharper. But this is unacceptable considering the phenomenal work they did with the rest of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that the embargo is over, I can finally review this remaster!Although I am far from finished due to work, I did play the original ones, including Unfinished Business, so I am here to comment on what the remake has brought us.Other than enhanced HD textures and remade models (Lara looks amazing!), the CGI cinematics are upscalled, and the sound has been enhanced as well (both music, SFX and dialogues). The items are now 3D instead of 2D textures, we have achievements (some are funny, some are easter eggs that people who played the originals will understand - like getting  Large Medkit through the corner glitch).The tank controls remain as an option, thankfully, because the modern controls are buggy (Lara doesn't backflip, for example). The classic visuals are also an option, if you press F3 you can switch between them and the modern visuals. The essence of the classic Tomb Raider games is fully here, it's like reliving memories but with higher quality!I experienced a few texture bugs (especially places with the ceiling missing), and had friends that experienced progression bugs too, which I hope they get fixed now during launch.Overall, it's an amazing remastered trilogy that comes with the add-on levels! My favorite of these three will always be Tomb Raider II, of course!Special thanks to Crystal Dynamics for the early access and free key! Thank you for this oportunity to try out the game so we could report the bugs to be fixed!

_childDocuments_.review: After 5 months, is it worth the wait?Uh...maybe? It's hard to say exactly.For 30€ it's pretty decent as a package. I've not played too far into 1 or 3 but I got some decent understanding.- FMVs look AI-upscaled. Cutscenes use the same animations (including head bops) but include (somewhat jarring) lip sync and eye movement.- You can play Lara's Home in all 3 games, you also have access directly to the expansions through the Game option.- You really can toggle the graphics with the push of a button (Start on gamepad, F1 on keyboard) anytime but the originals run seemingly at half the framerate.- I discovered Photo Mode (L3+R3 on gamepad, F3 on keyboard). This could be a fixed input listed in the bindings.- Inventory screens don't have the backgrounds seen in Classic graphics. It's a bit weird.- Speech triggers (at least in Lara's Home in TR2) repeat immediately afterwards.- I first played using a 1920 x 1080 monitor, then a TV where the only 4:3 (1600 x 1200) resolution fit the whole screen. The game's UI doesn't take resolution into account so I can't see all stats (they go beyond the TV borders).- I saw at least one bottom tile turned wrong in the first pool of Offshore Rig. Very minor thing but once you see it...you know.- You can only choose one language to use for everything, you can't mix e.g. English UI and subs with Japanese dubs. Though this would require all 3 games to have their own language settings.I played with a gamepad. Works fine...for the most part.- Lara feels about as responsive as she used to be. Which is good. About the only thing that I've noticed is that her aim at spiders is worse. It takes much longer to gun one down and I can't get used to it.- Turns out that in TR2 at least you can light a flare by pressing Inventory+R1, same combination also tosses it. Problem is, this wasn't listed anywhere. All combinations in fact should be listed in the bindings.- There is no button assignment for sidestepping. You can only sidestep by holding Walk while not moving. There should be buttons for this in at least 1 and 2 since sprinting and crouching are not present.- I had given the modern controls a shot; I don't like them a whole lot. I can't really turn in place to get right under a ledge (unless there's a slide or drop). The camera is also about as bad as people have pointed it out to be. For me it constantly got stuck in Lara's head or something, especially in a tight space.- This plays *very well* on the Steam Deck. The UI still fits a 16:10 display so no stats go over the sides. If only the d-pad was comfortable with 8-way movement, it would be perfect...I played in Finnish. A few things stuck out to me.- In the agreement prompt it says "Hyväksyä" (lit. "to accept") instead of "Hyväksy" (lit. "do accept").- Grenades are referred to as "Granaatit" even though "granaatti" means "garnet". It's "Kranaatit".- Achievements (at least those I've seen in TR2) are ordered wrong. The icons are correct but not the names nor descriptions (they seem to be off by one achievement). It bothers me a lot, hopefully fixed at some point.Tldr; if you like classic TR or want to try them (and don't mind a bit of tank controls), then yes.This review may see changes if issues are addressed or progress is made.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the original tank controls, but one thing missing in Tomb Raider 2 (the one I mainly played back in the day and still do on my PS3) is how you had two buttons for precise walking: R1 would allow you to walk forward/backward and use the left and right directions to rotate and walk, and R2 would allow you to either walk forward/backward or strafe left/right.What they've done here in this remaster is put those functions in a single button, namely R1: to walk and rotate, you must first take a step forward, and then start turning. If you simply press left while holding R1, you will start strafing, as if you were holding R2 back in the PS1.This is counter to my muscle memory from the PS1, where I could both walk forward and rotate while still holding R1. In this new version, I must let go of R1 if I want to rotate in place, which is weird and confusing, and creates the risk of Lara starting to run forward if I'm using the analog stick instead of the d-pad.Another thing that is missing is the ability to use PlayStation button icons. Frankly, it is unacceptable for games to be releasing in 2024 without this option.I wish the developers would fix these issues before my refund window closes, because I really want to play these games.In most other regards, this is a beautiful port.

_childDocuments_.review: Reviewed on Steam DeckI love this remaster but it’s not without its faults. But before I discuss the remaster, a few words about the individual games.The first game is the best. Hands down. Tomb Raider 2 is the worst game in the trilogy. The franchise works best when Lara is raiding tombs not Opera Houses or other modern structures. The game's internal logic fails when you start wondering why a modern day opera house is filled with the same kind of puzzles/traps you would traditionally find in an ancient tomb. Combat is over emphasized in the first sequel with the vast majority of the game’s enemies being gun totting muscle men rather animals that the player encounters in the original. Often you find yourself facing off against a thug in a claustrophobic corridor, staring one another in the eye as you blast away at each other until one of you drops. You can’t dodge, take cover, or evade, the confines of the modern architecture and rudimentary comtrol scheme doesn’t allow for that. Tomb Raider 3 unfortunately repeats many of the mistakes of the second game.There is far too much gun combat with many of the levels taking place in urban locations which makes no sense given the gameplay requirements and basic premise of the franchise. For instance, pulling a lever in one area to open a door in another makes perfect sense in an ancient tomb designed to protect the secrets inside, but makes no sense on a London rooftop.I would have had no problem with the game's designers including the urban settings if they had been in moderation and had created the appropriate gameplay to suit.Another problem I have noticed with this game is the occasional nonsensical puzzle element. I can't help wondering if these were included as a cynical way of selling strategy guides back in the day.The story is also worse this time around feeling a little disjoined from the whole. The series felt like it was running out of steam at this point with the developers just phoning it in while anticipating their bonuses. While the graphics, sounds, and animations were improved for the time, the same basic gameplay problems persist, namely the inane fixed camera that tends to show repeated close ups of Lara's backside rather than the ledge you are trying to jump to. I don’t blame the original develops though. The publisher refused to allow them the time between releases to innovate and seriously improve things. And then, ironically when they did give added time to the devs it was the wrong team (Angel of Darkness) who had no idea how to make a Tomb Raider game or what the franchise was actually about. Now, back to the remastered efforts. I’m very pleased with the graphical presentation but I will say that some areas are now way too dark and items don’t always appear visible. And that’s following a series of patches from the developers. This leads to frustration because often the player will overlook a key or wall lock because the assets no longer stand out in the environment as they did in the original versions. I think it would have been a welcome edition to the collection if the developers had included a torch (without a stupid 30 seconds health bar) as an optional toggle option in the settings menu. Also, how great would it have been if the remaster had implemented ray traced visuals?Finally, the controls suck. I get it; the grid based design limits what the devs could do to compensate but why can’t I hold the walk button, for example, to sidestep or backstep? Why couldn’t quicksave and menu items be mapped to the d-pad (or track pads in the Steam Deck version) and why can the camera move with the enemy when locked onto them? If an enemy moves out of Lara’s field of view the camera breaks lock. Why not include an option for the camera to track with the locked enemy in the controller options menu? Why can’t I hold the jump and walk buttons to side jump during combat when using modern controls? As it stands, players are stuck between a rock and a hard place. Tank controls give better precision, but modern controls aid basic navigation. With a bit more thought and work a better compromise between the two could be found. The game also lacks any kind of in-game manual. You will find yourself googling to find out how to accomplish simple gameplay mechanics. Some achievements are also broken. I sent an email to the developers but have yet to hear back from them. Despite these grips I do love the collection, I am a huge Tomb Raider fan, and would absolutely recommend the collection to fans of the original games although I’m not sure how much they will appeal to a ‘modern’ audience. I hope the devs don’t bother to release another trilogy featuring Tomb Raider 4-6 — those games suck!I would, however, welcome a remaster of the first Crystal Dynamics trilogy (Legend/Anniversary/Underworld) however! 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I played every classic Tomb Raider when they were originally released, so I'm a certified "oldie" (not really, I'm only 35 as of this review, but I suppose that's old to some), and veteran of the franchise. These games were a big part of my childhood and hold many dear memories. These Remasters are, to me, nearly perfect. They're still the same games I adore, but much better looking and with some added surprises, such as New Game+ after beating each Tomb Raider, which is essentially a hard mode that didn't exist in the original releases.If you are new to Classic TR, expect exploration, puzzles and platforming/climbing with no hand holding at all. When I was a kid I had a lot of patience and time to bang my head against the walls to find the way to eventually progress, but these games are obtuse at times. TR3 can be particularly frustrating, the London levels are a nightmare when going in blind, ask child me. So don't be afraid to look up a guide from time to time if you get too stuck. Definitely start with 1 and end with 3. The difficulty gradually goes up. The first level of TR2 alone, coming from beating TR1, will show you the developers were expecting players to know their stuff already.Really, the absolute only complain I have is the difference in lighting in a significant amount of areas when switching between Classic and Remastered graphics (which you can do on the fly at any moment, an incredibly neat feature). But I do appreciate it in cases where, particularly in TR3, it's much easier to see items with the new graphics.There are of course a lot of places where the different Remastered lighting does feel better and is an improvement, but some areas which should be darker, aren't, and some which should not be so dark, are. There are also some details lost with the Remastered graphics, such as a few areas that are supposed to have flickering lights not being displayed in Remastered graphics, or the golden glowing skeletons in the TR2 Golden Mask expansion not being glowy at all. Those maybe can be addressed in any future patches, if any more are planned.A common complaint I've seen is no level select, which at least the PS1 versions had. I don't particularly mind that much. I just use separate save slots at the start of each level, just in case. I recommend you do that too.Anyway, I mentioned the Golden Mask earlier. Like many TR veterans, I never played the expansions until now. They aren't bad, but the best is definitely the TR3 Lost Artifact expansion. Very good levels, gorgeous looking too, with awesome secret areas. If you've played these games before but not the expansions, this might be a reason to get this.If you care about achievements and completionism, you'll definitely have to sink a lot of time on getting 100% (ask me how I know). There are 269 of them across all 3 games and the 3 expansions. Some achievements are interesting in the sense they highlighted things I didn't know about the games despite all the times I played through them over the years, or I heard about but never tried, such as using a bug to reach an unreachable item. Some are challenges, like letting all creatures in the Colosseum live, or crossing the swamp in the Crash Site level in less than 20 seconds. Even silly things such as letting a block fall on your head. There are others which are just the standard "collect everything" and the like, though, and some span an entire game from start to finish.But yeah. I'm happy with how this was handled. Still the same games I always enjoyed, but better.
