_childDocuments_.review: A lovingly and faithfully crafted remaster of the original three Tomb Raider titles. I appreciate so much of the work done to refresh the look of the old game while still keeping the art direction mostly in line with the original games while adding in a couple of quality of life features.The collection is great as it is, but I do not believe it is perfect. There are a few missed opportunities to add or improve features that would have made playing through the games again much more enjoyable.If this game is going to receive further patches, then my hopes and wishes would be:- Unlockable by completing each game/expansion at least once so you can revisit your favourite levels without having to play through each game all over again. Would be really useful for getting some of those peskier achievements too! (Perhaps add a cheat code to unlock all levels if you don't want to play through the games again to unlock the Level Selections.)- Unlock costumes as you play through each game so you can use them whenever you want in any game. Perhaps add in the Gold Lara and Clone Lara as fun outfits from TR1 too! Modding can already do this now, but it would be nice to have an official toggle in-game like how you can switch outfits in Photo Mode.- Probably the least likely improvement to impliment, but if it does happen; it would feel more inline with the new remastered graphics if in-game cutscenes were reanimated, just like how characters already have new facial animations during in-game cutscenes with remaster graphics on. So why not give them new animations for the rest of their bodies with those faces that still fit with the existing cutscene audio (and keep the old animations when the old graphics are turned on!) As for FMVs, I get that they'd be too time-consuming to redo from scratch, so until the source files for them can be found in order to re-export higher quality videos, then I am okay with the current up-scaled FMVs.Despite my minor disappointments with some missing features, I am enjoying the remasters. It is an improved collection that I've dreamed of seeing happen because the old Tomb Raider games desperately needed them, and to get one made with love and care by true fans is the best thing to have happened to Tomb Raider in a long time. I absolutely can recommend this game to anyone who wishes to try them, and to fellow fans of Tomb Raider.I give this game a strong 8/10!
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: Perfection for $30. TR 1-3 remastered was almost pristine upon release. However, the camera was a nightmare. They have clearly patched the issue up nicely and silently today. The game is nostalgia heaven, giving players the option to alternate between old and new graphics on a whim. Updated controls are butter smooth. Regular movement is all we ever wanted for the game. Even retro controls seem optimized.  My overall opinion is that the game is gorgeous. Even the retro graphics. Combat has not been updated. Its true to the original and lack luster. However, TR was never known for combat. It's really just decoration for the exploration. The exploration and thought provoking aspects are top tier. Lara Croft is one of my favorite villians. This is the remaster she deserves. Also, including all DLC for each game is worth way more than the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're new, know that these are precision platformers like the first Prince of Persia, with a moveset tied to the blocked out architecture. This might feel slow and awkward at first, but once you know the rules it's very reliable and more tactile than jump-floating and snapping to ledges. You'll never slip to a QTE here.This is, however, a bad version for the original PC look so get the actual originals and run them through fan projects for that. A little ironic when people behind those projects led this one. There are no settings, not even resolution -  never seen that before. You can use Reshade though to tweak brightness and add FXAA. I also use it to tone down the yellow tint.Plenty of mods already, mostly visual replacers or joke mods but more advanced stuff seems to be possible with dll-hacks and remodels. Hopefully there can be a first-person view - the one in OpenLara is very cool and a new way to play.TR1 is obviously the most classic, but TR2 is probably my favourite - perfect balance, great locations and fun secrets. TR3, again has great locations, including Aldwych that is so cumbersome. Despite having finished that level several times I can never remember how, always ending up a rat in a maze so that Lud's Gate seems really easy afterwards. Secrets are really hard in TR3 and it can feel like being punished to go after them, but this does add replayability. TR3 also has many absolute peak Tomb Raider levels in it so you have to forgive it.This is very close to the definitive edition, just needs extensive options menus and fixing of the remaining visual downgrades - far less after the first patch but some persist, like no underwater splash for waterfalls - a small thing but you can't discount details like that in games with so much water.As far as remasters go, this is still an excellent effort.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: The camera is absolutely terrible. In tight spaces it will suddenly rotate when you get too close to a wall, which also rotates the direction of your movement input. To make it work i have to jump and then press the interaction button, but then, it makes vaulting over minor obstacles with a better precision just not a thing.When attached to the edge of a wall i cannot drop from it, i can go up, but if i need to drop, i need to go up and then drop from the edge.The modern controls in Keyboard and mouse need to be looked at.PS: in tank controls the interaction button works fine.Will give a thumbs up when the issues are resolved.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, no, I don't know.I love TR, Lara was always my idol from that moment I saw my father play the first TR, from that day I was a fan of the franchise and of her (until the new "Lara" came out). I was really looking forward to this remaster and the comments can't stop talking about how good it is, so I gave it the opportunity to relive the nostalgia but with better graphics. Lara looks beautiful and it shows that a lot of care and detail was given to her, but the rest.... the rest is very bad and made with AI and it shows, the videos have noise, the first video that welcomes you to the game has noise and one of the characters loses his eyes and his face mutates, BUT WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥, no one saw and fixed that? It's the damn first video. Thne I find myself constantly switching (f1) between old and new graphics, the new ones are extremely dark and there are parts where it is impossible to see anything, there are levels that are only playable with the old graphics that are brighter. The best controls are the tank ones and that is saying a lot, although the game was created for those controls and not for the modern ones, they could have taken the trouble to at least make them useful for the game, you are not going to have a good experience if you play with modern controls and tank controls are quite uncomfortable nowadays so you need to adapt.It's difficult, it should be neutral, not yes or no. _childDocuments_.review: I played the original games to death. Even if you loved the originals, I'd recommend you stay away here. I refunded after 10 minutes. The new graphics engine with the "modern" graphics is too dark to be playable. I think the devs knew this and that's why start on your controller switches graphic modes rather than goes into what passes for a "menu" here. You need to switch to the classic mode to be able to see secrets and pickups.I was sick of having to switch constantly between graphics modes to be able to see pickups and switches. Switching into original graphics mode is a nice bit of nostalgia for all of 30 seconds then is unbareable, because the difference in frame rates between the modes is jarring. If you're thinking "why not switch around some graphics options to improve frame rate or brightness"? Well, there isn't one. I don't mean there's a limited graphics option menu, there's literally ISN'T one. You can't change a single setting. Hell, I couldn't even work out how to QUIT the game and had to three-finger salute it to get out of it.I don't recommend this. It's a half-assed "update" where the graphical updates make the game unplayable. Glad I can get my money back.

_childDocuments_.review: They've done it. They've absolutely nailed it.As someone who was highly worried about preservation of the original games' vibe, I couldn't be happier with the end result. The lighting has been updated beautifully, the controls and physics are identical to the original games but you can now look around with the mouse / right thumbstick while running around, a perfect upgrade.The remaster so far has absolutely blown away my expectations. _childDocuments_.review: It's not good. I got this because it said that they had updated the controls and graphics to be playable. You can choose between the old tank controls or the updated controls, and also the old or new graphics. The updated controls are not updated enough, and it's still basically unplayable. When you are walking around the camera will randomly change directions like old Resident Evil hallways. That is a big problem when you're trying to walk or jump anywhere, especially using analogue sticks. You have no chance of being able to jump from one platform to another with the way the camera and walking direction randomly changes for no reason. You'll think you're going straight, and then all of a sudden you'll be going backwards or sideways, or the camera will just be looking at the ceiling so you can't see anything that you're doing. You'll just constantly fall off everything. Lara also randomly doesn't jump 50% of the time, so you'll push to jump and just walk off a ledge for no reason. You still can't aim. It has to lock on, but sometimes just doesn't. When you're trying to shoot an enemy you just have to run straight at it and hope it shoots it. A lot of the time you'll randomly be shooting the wall or floor as you can't aim. The new graphics are way too dark and you can't change anything as there's no settings, so I've had to keep changing from old to new just to try and see what's happening. There's no way to enjoy playing it. I've stopped playing as it's just awful, and would get my money back if I could.

_childDocuments_.review: Played only a bit of this, and from what I can tell, it's the perfect remaster - if you're fine with the original tank controls. I am. They're what I'm here for. With the modern controls, it's hard or impossible to pull some maneuvers necessary for smooth play. That's definitely gonna be a pain point for people not willing to use the tank controls.There's also no clear tutorialisation for the modern controls, so it's a bit of a trial and error thing to figure them out. Conversely, they make some parts of the game too fluid and easy - but there's really no way around that. For now, I recommend the original controls.The graphical part is great - it's not up to modern standards, but it's up to the standards of my brain remembering what the old games looked and felt like. Probably one of my favorite graphical remasters of an older game, ever. The ability to dynamically swap to the old graphics is a huge, huge plus. There are a few spots where the new lighting is a bit less clear on what to interact with or where to go, so it's appreciated from that POV too.Also, it's probably too faithful to the originals to keep the jumping as unresponsive as it always was, even on the modern controls.So, realistically, fixing the modern control issues would bump this from a 9/10 to a 10/10. Still the best Tomb Raiders ever, especially 2. If you're here for nostalgia, you can't go wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: So... It's awesome. I bought this thinking I would just play a few hours of Tomb Raider I for the nostalgia and to see what the "Remastered" was all about, and... 85 hours later it was so much fun I played all the content.I have previously played all Tomb Raider games so I have some good context to compare these games to the original, and it's a very nice fresh coat of paint on some old games, but unlike painting an old car, this paint actually adds some performance to the engine.Really the main new feature in terms of gameplay is the "modern" control scheme. This is great. It makes these games so much more playable than the classic "tank" controls. It really makes Lara much more responsive. I could not go back to the tank controls at this point.There is, however, one problem with the modern controls.... And that is the games sometimes requires the tank controls, so sometimes you have to switch to them and this is annoying. Basically there are  situations where to make a jump Lara needs to walk up to an edge, take a step back, and then she will be perfectly lined up for a running jump. It is very difficult to line these  jumps up with modern controls. There is also situations in Tomb Raider III where crawling will get Lara stuck and you have to switch to tank controls to get her unstuck. This should have been solved by putting tank controls on the d-pad (at least turning like a tank and moving forward an backward, you don't really ever need to side step).There were some issues with the new graphics though, for example there is this level in Tomb Raider I called The Cistern and I was wandering around for an hour without a clue as to where to go... And I switched to the classic graphics and then I saw it, some key sitting on the  ground that was basically impossible to see with the modern graphics, but very visible with the classic graphics. Maybe they fixed that in one of the patches, but I did find myself switching between graphics modes a lot just to make sure I didn't miss something (it's easy to switch graphics modes, it's a single button press).I guess that's my review of the "remastered" content, so I want to talk about the games for a bit. Tomb Raider I and II are great, I didn't have much trouble getting through them, but Tomb Raider III... I did not remember it being this hard. The intro levels were fairly straight forward but once I got past them I was constantly looking things up in guides. For people new to these games.... Know this.... These are old games. They are not the fast paced action with forgiving controls, there are very timed and precise. They take patience.Finally, I just want to say, I hope they bring in The Last Revelation and Chronicles as DLC, or otherwise release them with the new remastering. They are all basically the same engine and could all use this treatment.

Just a brush up to run, cheap price, and let the fans make what they want. You might suggest this to a younger generation who loves Fromsoft type agony but even they might roll their eyes at the last boss which turned out to be the camera all along. I can't really recommend this despite the feelings of nostalgia. I've moved on and replaying it just makes me remember why I put it down all those years ago. _childDocuments_.review: If you like the originals, you'll like this. If you're new, you might not like it. I'd discourage everyone away from "modern" controls as the game was not designed like a modern game so playing with those controls causes tons of additional issues that weren't real issues in the original controls. "The camera!" is a common one I see when people play with it. The tank controls allow you to do your movements without being able to see, and the camera never gets so out of whack because it's movement is much more restricted in the original controls. Especially vertically. Play as it was intended. With a d-pad or keyboard, and tank controls. It'll take you getting used to either if you're new and you may as well go with the one that the game accounted for in it's entire design. The remaster includes the expansions, makes playing the classics on PC a lot easier, with a face lift (and I guess with a new control scheme if you so choose to torment yourself). The only criticisms I have thus far- FMVs were not made new. I'm sure the budget of this was low, but it would've been cool to be able to have new FMVs for the cutscenes to switch back and forth as well. It would've just made the package feel more whole. - No ability to disable the boss health bars on modern graphics, I don't like it personally. It takes away the pressure and stress of boss fights to have the health bar visible. - NG+ is treated as a hard mode, and it should be more customizable. Save crystals return there, but I think it would be nice if you could choose to start the game with save crystals if you want to play that way. Similarly be able to choose the harder mode from the start instead of it being restricted to NG+. More flexibility would be nice.And some glitches. Oh, and there are some lighting issues. I'm not really in the camp of disliking the lighting being more dark in *some* areas. However, there are certain onese where it's absurd. The area in Egypt where there are black panthers for example, in the first game. The two tunnels that panthers come out of are pitch black. You cannot see at all. It is ridiculous. I get that lighting works as a source in the updated graphics, but you should cheat it when the alternative is literally a pitch black void. Even in real life if we had to walk down a pitch black void our eyes would adjust somewhat. Either toss a fake crack in the wall to push light in a bit, or just cheat and make it lighter anyway. It's just bad. I like the lighting in most other areas even ones I've seen people complain about.That said, more settings would be nice. Like lighting. I wouldn't really adjust it I don't think, but I know a lot would like the ability and it would be nice if possible to add such things. The music is insanely good. I'm honestly surprised, because people don't usually bring Tomb Raider up in best OSTs but I'm getting to the point where it may be one of my favorites. I'm overall just happy to have the real Lara Croft back. I miss puzzles, exploration, and platforming that required thought and effort and not just holding one button down as you essentially watch a cutscene of climbing animations during a set piece (if that). Traversal is a trend in gaming that needs to go away. Far far far away. It is boring. Nailing a platforming section in classic Tomb Raider is so rewarding. Not a lot of modern games make you work for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming back to this some 25 years after I first played it, I was worried I would get a bit of a nostalgia kick and then quickly put the game down again. Couldn't have been more wrong. This collection really stands the test of time and there's so much gameplay here that makes me think 'I wish they did more of this nowadays'. The controls take a minute to get your head around, and although clunky by modern standards, once you get used to them they have a satisfying internal consistency. Great atmosphere, satisfying puzzles that don't hold your hand, and some sudden transitions between exploration and action that always keeps you on your toes. A whole lot of great game for the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Plays just like the original games, also with updated modern controls too (which still aren’t as good as the original tank controls if you're using a controller because of how traversing the world works in these older games). If you’re a 90’s kid like me, you will be right at home jumping back into these, they are especially good with MKB(using modern controls) because of the non-analog stick era from which these come, movement was controlled with just a d-pad and that translates perfectly to WASD directional keys.For newer players, you might also enjoy these if you’re willing to put in a few hours getting used to the controls. All your knowledge of playing 3rd person games will not be enough to acclimate you instantly like it might for a modern title like God of War or Uncharted, these games are just different. The movement and combat mechanics might seem unintuitive at first but if you play long enough, it will start to click and you will actually find it very rewarding in the end.The graphics look really nice with beautiful baked lighting, reworked textures, and a new Lara Croft model that looks exactly how she was portrayed in marketing materials and FMV prerendered videos from these games. Her in-game character model never quite matched though, but now it’s a dead ringer, you can tell that the team who worked on this remaster are fans of the original games and have love and respect for what they made here. I have no problem spending $30 to support this, I want to see more old games getting this treatment (Legacy of Kain, anyone?)  I mean the true classics that are due for being remastered (not 5-10 year old games like TLOUP1), I’m honestly surprised Crystal Dynamics went for this, maybe Embracer forced them to do it? Either way, thank goodness for companies like Aspyr, Nightdive, Limited Run, etc. Y’all are out here doing some amazing work reviving these older titles.Also, supposedly people are upset about Epic Games Store getting a better/newer build of this game at launch? This version seems fine to me but I’m only playing through the first game, maybe the issue lies in part 2/3? 🤷🏻‍♂️

_childDocuments_.review: Playing TR1 for the first time, wasn't even born when this came out. Graphics are great considering what this is, a faithful remaster of the original games. This game has a steep learning curve, but really does get fun once you figure it out. Here's a few tips I think new players could use:1. You're going to die a lot, especially early on. Save early and often, and use multiple save slots. When I enter a new level, I save the game to two separate slots in case I overwrite one.2. Use camera mode. The new camera mode is your friend, it allows you to move and position the camera so that you might see things you otherwise might miss.3. Keep a guide handy. I've been using Stella's guide as it feels a bit more "old school" and fits the vibe of the game. It's fun to solve puzzles on your own, but if you find yourself getting stuck it's well worth a peek.4. THERE IS A WALK BUTTON HOW DID I NOT KNOW THERE'S A WALK BUTTON. When you walk, Lara will not walk off the edge of ledges. I am embarrassed by how far into the game I was before I learned this.A couple gripes:* The "classic" graphics only run at 30fps. Why?* The remastered video cutscenes are all AI upscales, and they look as ugly as that sounds. I hope they can improve this in the future

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish I didn't have to give it a negative review.However, after carefully considering everything that I have encountered in the first game... yeah. This review is for the first game. But pretty much if it's like this in the second and third you can probably draw up instant conclusions: So let me say this for the public record: Aspyr & Crystal Dynamics have done a fantastic job at recreating the game with stunning modern visuals. Holy crap it's amazing.When it comes to the GAMEPLAY portion however that's when you see the split First off let's talk about the controls. Tank controls? It is as faithful as it is on launch day back in 1996. However, what the game heavily promotes is not just the updated visuals, health bars for bosses, photo mode, but also MODERN controls. Meaning it will play like a platform title from the PS2 days.Here's the problem: The game was never ever designed with modern controls in mind due to the grid system and heavy reliance on Lara's acrobatic abilities. Hell, the tutorial talks about the tank controls, and not the modern controls. That's a "For you to find out" which is silly. No lock on system that let's you tap a button to auto lock, and oh my god the camera. THE CAMERAOn tank controls. The camera is as friendly as it was back in 1996. On modern? The camera is basically Ivan Drago out to murder you and make you sick or annoyed or both! It does not like tight corridors, tight corners, tight anything it will disown you, your ancestors, and your sanity. Also for the sheer fact that there are a bunch of guides and videos on the topic. You know the developers just slapdash this into reality and said: "Okay done" noooo. You need to QA this ♥♥♥♥. You need to make the controls more intuitive rather than frustrating at times. Also finally the save system. For whatever reason. The game does not introduce the save crystals on the FIRST go around. Yup, the classic save system is behind NG+. So what about it? well, remember when I said it's a faithful visual upgrade? Try remembering where you need to go after a while. Or better yet, try remembering to save at the right time. There is no quick save system. Period. No, I don't want to hear F5 & F9. That's a QUICKER ACCESS. Not a "Quicksaving..." on the top right or left corner like a Bethesda game or any game that has a quicksaving system. That ain't it. Because what was special about the save crystals is how not only does it balance your logical thinking of: "Do  I need to save here specifically or can I risk it and see what happens" because after you use the crystals it disappears. That is a way better save system because at least you know it's constantly there. If they would've just add a better quicksave system then this wouldn't be such a sore topic (along with the camera and modern controls)As i said. It's a faithful remaster down to the last pixel. But my god, they really and i mean REALLY screwed up with catering to the modern gaming audience because... yikes.

_childDocuments_.review: The first three Tomb Raider games were some of the first games I bought with my own money back in the late 90s, and to this day they remain some of my favorites. All the globetrotting, death traps and monsters... as much I appreciate the newer Tomb Raider iterations, the classics are still in many aspects unmatched today. Luckily these games have received now the remasters they deserve - throughout all three games it's obvious that they were updated with love and care, and the first patch that just dropped brought further improvements and polishing.If you are new to these games, I highly suggest taking the time to learn and master the tank controls. The games where built around these, and the level design shows. It also gives a whole new level of tension and deliberation to climbing and platforming sequences. Also worth mentioning is that the tutorials in Lara's mansion only teach you the tank controls, so for the more intricate details of the modern controls you must rely on experimenting or the internet.All in all two thumbs up for this great collection. Hopefully remastered versions of at least TR4 & TR5 will follow.

_childDocuments_.review: The gold standard for older games that receive the remaster treatment. Reasonably priced, support for modern controllers, modern resolutions and frame rates, and at the press of a button you can go back to the older visuals. I loved getting all of the achievements and playing these titles without having to mess with mods and Windows Compatibility mode, which was needed for the original Windows titles. On release there were a few visual bugs, along with other bugs that made some achievements unobtainable. Thankfully these have been patched but I wish the game was released bug free.Bravo to the development team. It was obvious they are huge fans of the games and did everything they could to make them shine. Thank you for also not censoring the games. I thought that the TR3 South Pacific native tribesman enemies would be the first thing that would be Thanos-snapped away, but thankfully they are still there in all of their cannibal glory. Dr. Willard also still drops the R word in a cutscene which was pretty based. Please do TR4 and TR5 next! Include Angel of DANKness as well, but that would need a disclaimer upon launch telling people the game was never finished and stinks. Would also love to have this team remaster Indiana Jones and the Infernal Machine.

_childDocuments_.review: I've wanted remasters for these game for a long time, and these are pretty much everything I wanted from them: modern controls, revamped graphics and controller support. I know it's not asking much, but it's all there and I love it. This isn't to say this remaster is without its flaws, but I love it nonetheless.Getting into specifics about its issues though: the modern camera gets impossibles at times. It really struggles in tight spaces and will make you miss jumps quite a few times. You've got unlimited saves to keep retrying these jumps, and sometimes it helps when yoy toggle old graphics on, but it's still frustrating.  Another thing lacking with modern controls is the option do side steps, and specially back steps, for which I've had to turn tanks controls on a couple of times, because they're needed to drop into ledges. The annoying thing here is that they could very simply be assigned to the d-pad, but aren't.I would also love it if they added a quick save and quick load button, and maybe some quick healing and weapong switching.But as I said, I love what we got already. I've played this games a lot as a kid but never finished one. As an adult I got the classic versions on steam years ago, but never got too far on any of them because of how dated they are. Now, after 20 hours, I've finally beaten the first tomb raider. It was rough, and I had to consult playthroughs a couple of times, but it still left me wanting for more. The level design is what set these games apart and makes them stand the test of time, even if sometimes it is a little outdated. Exploring these levels is a magical thing because they are gorgeous, even with the old graphics, and they brimming with secrets that are joy to discover. The only downside to these secrets is they almost never have interesting rewards, just health packs and ammo.I thought the modern triology was ok, but they don't quite capture the same feeling of exploration that the older games have. And the enemies you face are also very 90s rad video game like. Just in the first game you fight a t-rex, alien mummies, and a skater boy with uzis.Anyways, I'm just rambling at this point, but that's a testament to how much I love this, that I just want to talking about it. If you're an old fan, I'm pretty sure you'll like this remaster. If you're new to these games, I'd say give them a go If you like challenging, sometimes frustrating old games

_childDocuments_.review: A resourcepack not a remaster. Useful if you gave up 28 years ago as it gives you and the series a second chance. Optional if you remember the games as you will notice little to no fixes in return for plenty of new issues. Yeah it looks HD but that's that... Rendering issues in multiple levels. Wrong textures. Missing objects and textures. Localization feeling AI generated. Controls not fully responding. Lags which cancel keyboard commands (could possibly fail achievements when occuring). Some pickups are not visible which cost me unnecessary time. Voice lines are trimmed. Music cuts off in the menu (really? whose idea was it?). Immersion drops in places which try to be epic but sacrifice the original mood. Some patches were not included even though their authors were on the team. Finally, what I absolutely can't forgive is the "vanilla" renderer does the game dirty as it displays it WORSE than it used to be, so new players will see the OG game in bad light while overrating the remaster instead - it's either an oversight or a sabotage, so it better be fixed regardless. In short: I need names and addresses of those responsible for why this project was so awfully hindered, so I can get those invisible harpoons and stick them in the appropriate Mesh#0. If the fans ever get the tools used here, they will do a better job. Until then, I'm still waiting for the actual remaster and recommend you not to play this attempt unless it's repaired and stops feeling like a beta-sweet symphony.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I wasn't expecting much from this remaster, and after playing it, I have to say, it's a bit of a mixed bag.I still wanted to support this work, because the original Tomb Raider games, as well as Lara's character in them, are still the best; far better than the reboots developed by Crystal Dynamics.For the fans of the original games, I would say that it's worth buying.You can seamlessly switch between the 3 games from the main menu. And during gameplay, you can switch on the fly between the original and the remastered graphics, by pressing F1; you can also switch between the modern and tank (classic) controls while playing as well, from the game's menu.One downside is that there are absolutely no graphics options; you can play the game in borderless fullscreen, or switch to windowed mode by pressing ALT+Enter.From what I have played so far, everything from the originals is in there; the content and the level layouts have not been changed.So, how do the remasters measure up?The remastered FMVs are not that great; they are too blurry, and some of them are way too dark, to the point where you cannot really see much of anything. Modders have actually done better jobs at upscaling the original ones.The new visuals are pretty nice, though they are nothing special; there are new textures, new models, new foliage, new lightning, and the old environmental sprites have been replaced by 3D models. Some level art has been slightly changed, but not by much and the layout of the levels has been preserved (for example, in some cases you'll see an open ceiling with light coming through instead of a closed one).Graphic mods for the original games will net you similar or better results (they also update models, textures, foliage, etc). In addition, if you use an RTX remix mod as well (only if you have a supported Nvidia GPU), you will also get superior lightning, which can result in a vastly improved visual experience.I expected the modern controls to be fairly bad, but I did not expect them to be abysmal. They don't work well at all with the game's grid based system. You cannot jump back by tapping backwards; you cannot do a back flip; this makes larger jumps, which are very easy using the classic controls, a complete pain to pull off. Positioning Lara in front of objects is also a pain, because she automatically turns to her side when she reaches a wall.She also has a habit of getting stuck in environments after interacting with objects, like levers; nothing worked to get her unstuck, except switching the control scheme to tank controls.There are many other gripes I've had with the modern controls, including wonky underwater handling, but those above are the bigger ones.Thankfully, all is right in the world when you're using the original (tank) controls, and Lara controls like a dream.What about the actual games?The best one in this collection, and in the whole series, including both reboots done by Crystal Dynamics, is still Tomb Raider 1.TR1 was a perfect storm of engaging gameplay, foreboding atmosphere, great exploration, good pacing, and an interesting story.It perfectly captured the soul of the Tomb Raider - delving into the unknown, discovering lost artifacts, and traces of bygone civilizations. Something that unfortunately has been diluted quite a bit in the rest of the games.It had great locales and diverse levels, like Peru, Greece, Egypt, and the level design was extremely strong, and consistent throughout the game, both thematically, and from a quality standpoint. There was a strong emphasis on exploration and puzzle solving with the occasional combat sequence, and it all felt great.The Unfinished Business levels pack didn't really have a story, were quite a bit more difficult, but were enjoyable nonetheless.TR2 started out pretty strong with the Great Wall level, displaying all of the strengths of a Tomb Raider game, but it slowly started to fall flat on its face. They added way too many human enemies (and combat encounters in general), all veritable health sponges. While in the 1st game, there were only a few human enemies, in the 2nd one there are tons. And with their poor AI, rudimentary hitscan damage, and blatant spawning in front or behind you, killing them is the same bland chore every time.This is something that the devs themselves acknowledged and rectified to varying degrees in 3 and 4.Because of this forced shift towards an action game (and not a particularly good one at that), TR2 suffered greatly in terms of the atmosphere, mystery, pacing, exploration, puzzle solving.The story was somewhat interesting and while it did have some great levels earlier on, the level design was nowhere near as good or as interesting as it was in the 1st game. Later levels were excruciatingly dull and dragged on for way longer than they needed (like the sunken ship).It is not a bad game, and it has its enjoyable moments, despite some of its dull and tedious parts, but it never managed to reach the heights of TR1.The Golden Mask bonus levels, were kind of a pain. They were riddled with annoying invisible enemies, poor exploration and puzzles, and ultimately unrewarding.When the team started TR3, they were already suffering from considerable burnout, and it showed. This one is among the weakest in the series, with a pretty forgettable story. It has less tedious and poorly designed action than TR2, but the level design and pacing are all over the place.It started out pretty strong, with the India levels, but it slowly and steadily declined from there. The South Pacific levels were decent, while the London ones were simply abysmal (the only redeeming part about them is you had the option to skip large parts of some of those levels), and the rest, somewhere in-between.Fortunately, TR4 was a return to form of sorts, but that is a story for another day.

_childDocuments_.review: My younger sis is actually named Lara after the protagonist because my whole family enjoyed the games so much. I've just played the first 3 levels with my older bro (who's a super fan and a pro at this game) and all 3 of us are very happy with the remaster. And I look forward to exploiting my older brother's nostalgia and memory for 100% achievements! :) Things I Like: +++ GRAPHICAL IMPROVEMENT: The remastered graphics look so good. My brother, who said he's only going to use classic, was blown away by it and has been using them too. I still turn back to PS1 graphics on the fly just to relive those days and check out each room in a new view. It's superb and funny to remember how the PS1 looked. +++ ON THE FLY: It's literally press one key or press START on a playstation controller to change between the graphics. It's as fantastic and eye-opening as when Halo did it. Here you can even do it in the main menu, loading screens and cutscenes! +++ CLASSICS: They really didn't change much at all. My brother blitzed the first level like the good old days. Knew where all the enemies where, collected all the secrets and performed some stunts they don't tell you about as memory served. I was super impressed! And it still has that spooky feeling while playing. It's such a  special feeling and they have maintained it flawlessly.  ++ 3 EXTRA LEVELS: If all 3 games wasn't enough, they have 1 extra level per game that not everyone got to play. You can start them whenever you want on the main menu. We didn't get to play these levels back in the day and my brother is super excited to conquer them.  + CONTROLS: They give you the choice between the classic "Tank" controls (using 4 directional movement) or "Modern" using free movement/the analogue stick. Beware though, every other button is very different and you still need to hold to grab ledges! My brother says TR1 has a move it didn't have back in the day, so I suppose they just created 2 solid movesets with everything included instead of including the quirks of each game. + ACHIEVEMENTS: I usually don't care for them, I did my part of platinum trophy hunting on PS3/PS4 and it's thankless, but it's cool to have stuff to do in a game as old as this. And there's a ton: 269 achievements across the 3 games! + STICKING OLD MEN IN FREEZERS: Put that old King Charles mf on ice babyyyy!Things I Dislike: - MUSIC: These games have good tunes for both tense and relaxing moments, so I thought for a remaster, they would at least make the music continuous but instead they didn't touch this area at all for the remaster and left it so a track triggers when you first enter a specific area and just ends, leaving you to play in the quiet. We've resorted to opening up a playlist in the background while we play.  - CONTROLS: Modern controls could've been improved, they're awful. There's not enough control on the camera. In fact, it fights against the scripted static camera angles and you will get all turned around. The all-in-one button for equipping gun/locking onto nearest enemy is annoying and not modern at all. When an enemy dies, you'll stay locked on forever if you keep shooting, so encounters with multiple enemies are a bit awkward feeling. Traversal is messed up because you cant hop backwards for run and jump moments, you just have to gun it or slowly turn all the way around while walking. I haven't figured out a way to safely lower myself off a ledge either. And the same button for walking is also for swan-diving so I often find myself smashing head-first into a wall when I want to walk to a ledge and jump from it. And you also don't auto-grab far ledges. How many modern games restrict you that much? Zero! Not even the MODERN Tomb Raider games! - GRAPHICS OPTIONS: There aren't any. Seriously, no changing resolution in-game or anything like that. It's just stock.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've never played the original Tomb Raider series this is actually a really nice way to handle remasters. Being able to toggle between newer graphics and older style is wonderful. The games are solid and do stand up even today. There's a lot of puzzles, careful platforming, and combat that made the game such a success first time around. Unfortunately, there are two big issues that just don't work well and they revolve around the controls.Way back when, at a time when I played the original Tomb Raider on the Sega Saturn there were dedicated sidestep buttons. That meant I could complete the first two levels in 15 minutes flat (collecting all the pick ups and all secrets). Now I was prepared for a learning curve, but the lack of dedicated sidestep buttons is unacceptable and makes Lara harder to control when walking or trying to be careful. Now this is talking about when utilising an Xbox controller. Now the second issue is when it comes to the keyboard controls. The remaster doesn't treat the systems as different. When playing the GOG versions of the original games - well, it is a far easier customisation of the control system. There isn't an excuse for how bad the control system is. That makes it difficult in deciding if I would recommend this remaster. If you care about more modern looking graphics, then yeah. If you don't want to have to fiddle with Dosbox, then probably also yeah. Over £20 for a slightly prettier looking, but harder to control version? I wish I hadn't spent that...these same games cost me £6.99 on GOG and it's the originals. They work just as well and control much better. I just don't think that it's worth the cost. Most of this remaster work was done for earlier android versions of the games (which I have, but don't appear to be available on Play Store any more), so the cost is just too high to be worth the value that you're getting.To be clear - if you want the graphics and will put up with a poor control system - get this. Tomb Raider (and II and III) are good games. I just feel like there isn't enough done well with this to justify purchasing this over the original versions over on GOG.[EDIT/UPDATE] I've now tried to use a different style of controller. I have USB Playstation 1 and Sega Saturn controllers. Unfortunately, Aspyr have not anticipated that people might use anything other than an XBOX controller and as a result doesn't allow for remapping of their controls with any form of controller. This now places it in the hard - do not recommend category. If someone wanted to use a PS1 style, or Sega Saturn style controller to get a real taste of what the game would've been like way back when - well that's not possible. Basically, lazy coding, and development. I dread to think how this will play on my steamdeck, when the non-xbox controllers don't have decent control system customizations.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great. It looks a lot better and I haven't been able to stop playing it. I've seen a lot of people on here complaining about the modern controls and after almost fully completing the first game what I can say about the modern controls is that they do make the game way more playable. The issue isn't necessarily with the modern controls but with the camera in some (few) tight spots where when you need to make a jump but the camera is up against a wall in a small area it will sometimes start conflicting and going crazy and make it really hard to make precise jumps and that does get pretty frustrating. But others have been complaining about modern controls lacking features the original tank controls had. That's not true and these people just couldn't be bothered to look it up before taking to steam reviews to trash the game. You CAN climb out of water with modern controls using right trigger and you CAN side and back jump with modern controls you just have to have your guns out. All the modern controls do is make the game play more like the more modern LAU Trilogy games and would be perfect if the camera was a little bit better. It needs to be fixed but it doesn't happen often enough to break the game for me. Played almost all the way through 1 so far with modern controls and I could never go back to the old tank controls.

_childDocuments_.review: Although this package should be a welcome remaster package, the price tag for such a poor work which includes trick advertising regarding "modern' controls, cannot be justified. The graphics look very good and make playing the games much better than the originals. From visual perspective, there is nothing to complain about, it looks great. But the old frustrating gameplay mechanics have not been fixed (it is indeed hard to fix this with a simple remaster). And the fact that they included "modern" controls to this package is what attracted me to buying the package at the huge price it was sold at (25-30 euros). But these modern controls, although they do work, do not work together with the whole interface and level designs which have remained the exact same as the old games. It becomes even more frustrating, because they do not match together and make playing the games even harder and even impossible to surpass some parts of the levels. For this alone, I do not recommend buying the package, only if it's price lowers itself to 5-10 euros.

_childDocuments_.review: Remaster Review:An admirable take on the Tomb Raider Classic trilogy and it is truly lovingly restored but don't expect it to be much innovated upon.The new graphical vision for the games is beautiful and there is too much work put into the models and environments to reimagine what the original developers had in mind making the originals, I am in love with this collection but:- I experienced some graphical bugs in modern graphics mode.- I noticed that when switching to the classic graphic mode the frame rate decreases to 30fps and the graphics are not as good as the PC version of the older games.- The new controls offer players old and new a new way to interact with Lara, the tank control oriented environments make it somewhat difficult to operate.- The lack of autosave is unfamiliar with newer gamers.Although with the amazing preservation that this remaster offers, it doesn't completely entice new players to try the classics because of the lack of new quality of life features.This is a remaster from the fans of Tomb Raider to the fans of Tomb Raider and it shows!Game rankings (Most to least favourite):1. Tomb Raider 2. Tomb Raider III3. Tomb Raider II

_childDocuments_.review: Have always been a fan of the original Tomb Raiders,                              and these remasters have not disappointed.The modern enhancements breathe a unique personality to the worlds; examples being the windowed ceilings, a sky (Tomb Raider I), and alternate lighting directions compared to their originals.The expansions also being an appreciated inclusion. _childDocuments_.review: Edit #5: I guess I really love this game...So I'm switching the review rating...Beware that every patch will probably break stuff and make the game worseEdit #4: Another patch, and the game gets worse...I wish they'd just make every new change optional. Bug fixes is fine, stuff that fundamentally changes how the game controls or looks is not. Lara's braid is on screen at all times, and now it looks worse than it did at launch. because they couldn't implement a simple filter in the modern graphics to minimize torsion (though, depending on the code base, this may be easier said than done), so they had to hack the model so that each "ball" in her braid coincides with each joint.Anyway, I cannot recommend this game until it stabilizes, and all major visual/gameplay changes become optional.Edit #3: I still love this game so much I can't give it a bad review.Edit #2: After playing through all of TR3, and half of TR2, the new patch changed the game significantly. Although there were plenty of nice changes (visual, mostly), a variety of new bugs were introduced, and there were a lot of changes to the gameplay that make this product significantly different from the one I purchased. These include: changes to the combat system (lara turns automatically now), changes to the jumps (less precision, more coyote time) and changes to the UI (the new hand icon is difficult to see, and paradoxically also more distracting). Until these changes can be toggled in the options or we can easily acces the previous version of the game (using the steam betas functionality, for instance), my review will be negative. I don't think a game should be patched to become a significantly worse and less fun experience than the product I paid for (even if overall the game is still pretty good). As it stands, I don't even have much reason to recommend it over the originals, as the new feature (modern controls) has been severely worsened.Edit: MY GOD WHAT A BREATH OF FRESH AIR THIS IS, PLAYING WITH THE NEW CONTROLS and new visuals.Some dubious textures aside, this is the most fun I've had with Tomb Raider since playing the first one.Feels almost like PS2 Angel of Darkness, if that game only had good bits. Even the rig+sunken ship levels aren't terrible anymore! And TR3 is now good, as opposed to bad!(Original review (at 2 hours played) follows)As someone who spent countless hours playing the originals (on PC and PS1), I can't recommend this one enough! The old games are here, they look almost exactly as they did on PC, but are a lot easier to setup. The remastered assets look really good (apart from the upscaled FMVs: but you can switch to the original with the press of a button), and even though I prefer the FMV lara, the new models look really really good.I've played the originals so much that I've been playing the new ones with the "modern" controls and I'm really enjoying them. Sure, there's some awkwardness (swimming in tight corners takes some getting used to - why don't we have a "swim up" or "swim down" button?! - , and dropping from a ledge is complicated), but it's a wonderful new way to experience these classics.The one thing missing compared to the old ones is that you can no longer move and look around in the same way you could on the PS1 with dual analog sticks. (You can still move and look around, it just works differently)The triangle rasterization is not watertight, which means that you can see a few pixels (sometimes very bright!!) between the triangles.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: After the first couple of patches I feel like I can recommend the game. Overall it's a pretty simple repackaging of these three classics, nothing ground breaking. The visuals are nice and crisp (for a remaster) and the modern controls are definitely much better now (played all three games with them). Lots of basic elements that you'd have expected from this are still not there, like autosaves, level select, the ability to simply hop backwards for a run up on modern controls or other touches that would have made this feel more modern (maybe allowing sprinting on all games? Better enemy locking in combat?).And I was sad to see that the character animations are exactly the same despite the higher polygon models, which makes them look very weird, especially in cutscenes. They definitely could have added more detail to them. But overall a fun trip down memory lane. Could have been much better, but not the worst remaster out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Ingame graphics have been upgraded perfectly.The original gameplay has been preserved.FMV's are lazily implimated with AI upscale.Modern controls are awful and will turn away new players. Almost a perfect Remaster. It does exactly what I would want from a Remaster, updating the visuals without changing the gameplay. The ingame visuals are perfectly done. All textures have been improved, the lighting is beautiful and original Lara looks superb. You can even switch between the old and new visuals on the fly with the push of a button/key. Just Like in the Command & Conquer RemasterThey've even took some liberty's and changed some of the levels so the lighting improvements make more sense. None of these changes effect gameplay or the layout of the levels and are expertly implementedThe gameplay hasn't been changed much, which is a good thing as it preserves the original feel of the game. However in Tomb Raider 1, Lara now has the ability to jump and flip midair, which was an ability that she got in Tomb Raider 2. It doesn't really change much drastically but it does allow at least one secret area to be reached more easily.There's also a new Photo mode which I've had tons of fun using. You can select some preset facial expressions and pose's as well as reposition the camera around lara in anyway you choose. It's really neat.The FMV's haven't been touched at all, the devs just copy and pasted in the originals and AI upscaled them. I personally would have appreciated a remake of these FMVs to match the quality of the rest of the game. The subtitles in these sequences look like a mess due to the aforementioned AI upscaling. Just completely lazy.The new "Mordern Controls" are dreadful, this remaster would have been better of without them, and since they're the default control scheme, people who are new to these games are gonna have a frustrating experience. Not only does the button layout make no sense; It doesn't feel natural & Lara loses a few critical move sets because they aren't included in these controls. My recommendation is to They maybe chunky and dated, but at least they work with the design of the game and not against it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the EXACT SAME game, another low effort remaster. The fact that they keep the gameplay the same is understandable, it a classic.However the fact that they keep the same menu, the same animation, the same environment is not.They could add more details, like gravel on the ground, overgrown plants on the wall, some smoke effect on the gun after shooting. They could at least remaster the cinematic (they are the same, in all of their 144p glory). I'm pretty sure this remaster could run flawlessly on a PS2. _childDocuments_.review: I never thought I see the day where we get this remastered trilogy considering Anniversary is somehow the worst selling game in the series, but I am glad I am wrong. This is a great remaster it has it's problems, but this is definitely the best way to play the first 3 games (I like to consider Anniversary as it's own thing).First of graphically this game looks really good it has a ps2 like charm to it in a lot of ways and the in game ways they made the levels brighter is really nice (cave roof being destroyed, chandelier lights being brighter etc.), but if you are not satisfied with the new graphics you can change them with one button, like how Halo the master chief collection did.Secondly there are now 2 control schemes, classic controls and modern controls. Classic controls are your regular tank controls and as far as I know they were mostly unchanged (you can do mid-air rolls in TR1 as well, running rolls are now done with rolls instead of pressing jump etc.), but at the same time there are new moves that the game doesn't mention more on that later.Modern controls is the brand new control scheme added to the game. A lot of people say that they are terrible and you are better off mastering the tank controls, but after doing a lot research and experimenting I strongly disagree. While unfortunately they aren't the definitive control scheme, because of it's flaws it makes the game much more easier. Vehicle sections feel like normal vehicle sections instead of elaborate puzzle sections, where you had to make sure your vehicle faces the right angle during ramps. And combat I think is a lot better, also instead of just spamming backflips and sideflips, you can now run circles around enemies, on top of doing your regular jumps and flips. The problems start when you are doing regular platforming, and they definitely need to patch things up as soon as possible. First of you can only do back/side flips and back/side steps, while your weapons are out, which makes you rethink a lot of platforming sections (thankfully you can still do a backflips from slopes so it's not like the game soft locks you). Secondly the camera, is easily the biggest enemy in the game, while you are using the modern controls, it constantly disorients you, a lot of times where you are not seeing anything it needs to be fixed ASAP. Thankfully you can reset the camera using the view button or by pressing the walk button and walking a bit, but those are sadly bandaid solutions.Also like I mentioned previously there are brand new moves added to this remastered trilogy, some from later games and others are brand new moves, the problem is Aspyr haven't created at least an instruction manual that describes said moves. At best there is an  overview of the modern controls on their support page, but it's super barebones.To the point I decided to make a manual myself (shameless plug):Overall, while it's not a perfect remaster it's still puts a lot of other remasters to shame (GTA "definitive" edition anyone), I definitely believe they gonna iron out this trilogies problems and we are definitely getting 4 and 5 remastered at the very least.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a true remaster. Not a remake but a remaster. These are the same three old games from the PS 1 era including the add ons (1 per game) with some quality of life changes that are purely optional so even the purists can enjoy TR 1-3 again without emulation etc.This means, there is nothing changed in the level layouts, hitboxes or all the wonkiness that may come with a game from that era. It's Tomb Raider like it's been 1996 - 1998. Even some famous bugs / glitches are here for you to exploit.That said you can switch from 1996 graphics to remaster graphics with the push of a button. Even in cut scenes. To be fair the remaster graphics are actually nothing to write home about. I think even TR Anniversary looks better but this is due to the fact that they preserved the "blocky" grid layout from the original games. The famous PS 1 warping and "see through" graphic bugs are mostly erased. (They weren't that present on DOS anyway)There is a New Game + mode which is a real challenge.250+ achievements that are actually fun and challenging if this is your kind of thing.I think this is the best remaster the first 3 games could ever get. If you like to take a nostalgia trip or want to experience the games in a better graphical style again, this is it.

_childDocuments_.review: (TLDR close to end)Just finished Tomb Raider I on this remaster and played through Lara's Home on TR2, so yes I still haven't played TR2 and TR3 on this remaster.But as a player of the original games back in the day, I can tell what this is. It's very faithful to the originals, making it a preservation dream, since now it now features crisp textures, improved lighting and resolutions and framerates as far as you can imagine.True to the originals, this is about the level design and traversing through the levels with a mix of jumping/navigation skills and spacial awareness, occasionally with some enemies along the way.I played with the original tank controls from the original 90's releases. Nowadays, they feel completely backwards, but the truth is all the games were originally designed with that in mind - you cannot really enjoy these without taking into account the time period.That said, of course it's sad the modern controls are giving many people grief from what I can see online, but I really don't see a way they could have made it better. These games originally are like a 3D version of the original Prince of Persia in DOS - the controls are tightly knit into the "grid" design of the game and if you just put the modern fine-tuned and very flexible 3D controls into it, all the level design just feels boring. Also, this is a time where the production values are nowhere near what we see nowadays. The game is so quiet and the cutscenes so non-detailed (compared to what we see usually today) it's so interesting how much stuff a player made in their own mind to fill all that whilst playing.With all these honest "cons" for it, I cannot but feel reunited with the feeling of true exploration and being immersed in these locales, just as I did originally. Usually it's very quiet and you are focused on the minute actions you need to do the platforming and being quick on the reactions when enemies pop-up. And if, like originally, you let your mind fill the "make belief" on locations you are on - the ancient Greece one tickled my fancy - it's no wonder you can understand the allure of the original games.It can also be an exercise in delving through the history of gaming, and I wholeheartedly encourage people to find and watch the many documentaries about the original franchise on YT and the likes, and then play the actual thing presented here with modern accouterments. Just going from TR1 to TR2 and then TR3, the jumps in features are obvious and very interesting in what games can make available to players.So, TLDR: --------------if you are far removed from this era, I fear it's going to be hard to get into the mindspace of the level design for these games, no matter how nice the graphics and performance are improved - since they are very tied to the original tank controls. If you are an existing fan or if you've lived through the era and never played the originals, this is the perfect release for an historical expedition. BTW as an experienced player (this is like my 4th TR2 playthrough, I think) this is now  my favourite podcast gamePS: I hope that people buying this signals and enables a new modern entry in the series. The "newer" Tomb Raider trilogy (started in 2013) is impressive and imho totally deserves continuation. And amidst the Embracer group woes, I truly fear the franchise is in series risk of being lost, never for the likes of an intrepid adventurer such as Lara to unearth it ever again :(

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I don't even want to give this a NEGATIVE review, it's more a 'mediocre' one but the game has so many positive ones anyway this is going to have to be negative by default, if only to balance it out.The two biggest issues are that achievements don't trigger and the camera is a mess.Check the Steam discussion pages, there's tons of people talking about how many achievements there are that simply don't pop, and I've had it first hand where they simply fail to activate despite doing everything you need to for them.And the second, and in my opinion far worse issue, is the CAMERA.The camera is a complete joke. It drunkenly swings around behind you, gets stuck on level geometry, twitches and stutters between different angles, and changes your controls when it does so (IE: if you're walking forwards and the camera lurches around 180 degrees, you're now walking backwards but are still pushing 'forwards', so if you suddenly press the 'backwards' control, you'll start moving in the opposite direction, going 'forwards'). It's incredibly disorienting and leads to a lot of unfair deaths, when the camera lurches the wrong way and suddenly you walk off a ledge you were going out of your way to avoid.Like I said, I don't want this review to be NEGATIVE because there is a lot of good in the game, but these issues are incredibly obvious, so obvious I'm stunned the game was released with them still baked in. The fact that nobody's done ANYTHING about the camera is honestly shocking, and might force me to demand a refund if it keeps on being as much of an issue as it is. Bear in mind that at the time of writing, I've only played for 3 hours and haven't finished the first chapter of the game yet... mostly because it's too frustrating to play, and I'm barely that far into the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I must start off this review by saying the only original tomb raider game I had ever attempted before this was the OG TR 2, which I had a bad time with. However, after switching back and forth between classic graphics and remastered while playing, I think I can safely say that the remaster is absolutely beautiful. I love the way it upped the environments and backgrounds, Lara's model herself is also perfect and I loved all of her outfits. I started playing with modern controls, but they were not my favorite so I learned tank and had a much better time. Modern is fine, and I'm not sure if it's been patched so it might be outdated for me to say but the combat was not so good with modern controls. I will also give my reviews on each individual game, since this was my first time playing through any of the originals. Tomb Raider I- this was my favorite out of the three. The level design was fantastic, especially near the end I loved the way everything looked. The enemy design was very good, the dialogue was entertaining despite being dated, and I loved Lara and her personality. The story was my favorite out of the three as well, fairly simple but that's what I loved about it. Tomb Raider II- I see a lot of people talk about how much they love Tomb Raider II and I'm sad to say it did not live up to the hype for me. The story was fine, but I didn't enjoy a lot of the level design and often found myself confused and needing to resort to walkthroughs. My lack of enjoyment could have been due to how much difficulty I had trying to play the not-remastered version of this game, but there wasn't much difference between them (since I played with tank controls). Tomb Raider III- I was equally amazed to see a lot of people don't like TR III. I really enjoyed the first half (I played Nevada, then London, then Pacific), but the quality definitely did drop off after most of London. I did not enjoy Antarctica, but the final boss was pretty good. The first half though, was great and the opening levels especially I thought were gorgeous. But yeah the story is wacky and has way too much going on, and I agree that the game is too long. Overall I had a good time with the remaster!!! Definitely recommend!!

_childDocuments_.review: I am 24 years old.My ex-husband and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak girl I was behaving like.Today, I am close friends with the father of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The man I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: Temper expectations on this one.While the nostalgia hit is strong, especially when the old TRI theme starts on the menu screen, the wistful memories of halcyon days soon give way to the reality of time.The game looks nice...for the most part.  The new art style is pleasing to the eye without being so slick as to distract from the unchanged level-design. You can hit start (or whatever the kids are calling it these days) to instantly switch to the old graphics and see just how far we've come.Unfortunately, nothing has been done to the cut-scenes, other than a slight uplift to the resolution (and I mean *slight*).  It's jarring when the in-game visuals look somewhat polished, but the FMV would've looked outdated a quarter of a century ago.Worse still are the controls.  You can choose between Tank and Modern, but neither feels particularly good. "Modern" provides twin-stick movement and maps shooting to the triggers, but it feels awkward: too smooth to match the grid-based level design; too flimsy to give a truly modern feel, especially when it comes to combat.  With no such thing as free-aim on a 1996 controller, there was a generous lock-on to make combat playable, which has been carried through to the tank controls here. With modern, however, the lock-on and free camera seem to be constantly at odds, with the lock-on being dropped whenever an enemy goes out of frame or you want to see where you're going.As such, I found the Tank controls preferable because, although the set-up is archaic, it better fits the level layout and enemy mechanics.  The modern set-up is more of a problem for TRI than II & III, but it doesn't feel great in any of them.The thing is, none of this would be so bad if all you're after is a somewhat modernised nostalgia trip.  The up-scaled graphics are nice to see and everything runs smoothly enough.  Where I struggle to recommend this package is in the price.  With the industry standard now nearing the £70 mark (unless you want the *whole* game), £25 for a remastered trilogy might not seem so bad, but this collection is over 25 years old, with the originals still available to purchase, often for less than £1 each.  With tighter controls, more care to the presentation and some re-tuning to the combat, then this might have been a better deal, but as is, I don't feel like enough effort has been put in to justify choosing this package over the 3 much cheaper stand-alone titles.(personally, I'd have preferred a full, Anniversary-style remake of 2 - *that* I'd have paid full whack for!)

The gameplay is smooth but classic mode has some frame skip issues, it just looks a little choppy.  There's a setting you can fix it with in Nvidia control panel and with it enabled it looks a lot better.  The older style controls are sometimes frustrating, especially when you're trying to align Lara precisely.  The camera gets stuck and I find switching back and forth between classic and remastered visual mode unsticks it.  Hopefully we get a patch addressing some of these things.  Otherwise its been an amazing remaster and so much fun re-experiencing these classics.Update: I finally figured out how the controls work lol.  Its much easier to position with tank controls and theres a grid system to map how how far each type of jump goes.  The biggest thing was learning to hold the action button until she pulls herself up.  I thought you tapped it and was so frustrated when she never stuck a grab. _childDocuments_.review: All three versions of tomb raider, core/edios, crystal dynamics, and square enix, have their distinctions, and are all vastly different experiences unto themselves. Younger gamers, aka “modern gamers” may in fact hate this release, as even with its fresh repaint, it’s just the original pc/psx releases that look a helluva lot better; all the wonk included. I’m old. I played these games at release back in the 90’s. For me and folks my age they hold a lot of atmosphere and weight and emotion for us. But they aren’t the products of the modern game industry with 1000’s of devs all working on them, the original game was made by 10 people. And while the product of that was amazing in the 90’s, it shows today. TR1 is old. It feels old. Painting it doesn’t change that. TR2 is still wonderful, but also still old. (Full disclosure: I have launched TR3 yet)If you want to play some psx era video games with 100% accurate controls, this is a great way to do it. But if you want a better experience, I’d send you towards “tomb raider anniversary” as it’s a remake of the original, that’s better all around.I like that this version allows for instantaneously switching between the new skins and original. It allows you to see how much work they put into it. Some areas look completely different. The “modern controls” seem to completely break the game tho. They don’t work at all with the math of the level design, nor the basic functionality of the game. Just keep it on tank controls and lean how to play it. Music is still fantastic.Random old guy thoughts follow:There is a major difference between the Core/Eidos Lara and the modern Square enix Lara.  The 90’s Lara is female James Bond. She’s heartless, brutal, and not afraid to merc anyone or anything. You get this told to you via very short, disjointed cutscenes. 99% of these games are mazes and puzzles. No awesome cinematic angles, no emotional damage, no epic story. Just puzzle, shoot occasionally, maze, repeat. These are games as they used to be. For better or worse. Don’t get me wrong, I absolutely LOVE the square Enix boot of Lara. Some of the best games I’ve ever played. But I do miss her Bond persona a lot. I’d like them to split that universe into like the 616 and ultimate universe from back in the day. Give us a modern version of the original Lara , including her questionable choices.

_childDocuments_.review: If you have problems or the controls feel bad -> Try to play it orgininal style!I suggest to use a pc-keyboard like the game was made for (bluetooth keyboard for TV etc.)Switch to "tankcontrol" in the settings, -------------------------------------------------------------------> Then map the keys to the classic button layout: arrow keys (yes, THE arrow keys) = movementalt = jump space = draw weaponctrl = grab (ctrl-button on the left side of keyboard)shift = walk (shift button on the left side of keyboard)Numpad 0 = look around-other (not changeable)Esc = inventoryF1 = toggle classic graphicsF5 = save-listF9 = load-list-Then watch some youtube videos to learn the style of moving and pacing of the game.Take your time in the tutorial mansion level.Just know that it is more a puzzle and hard "climbing" game and you wil have a good time, playing a historic dos game! And save as often as you can!
