_childDocuments_.review: is a cleverly written, engaging, dare I say fang-tastic visual novel about helping vampires overcome their emotional hang-ups. The approach is humorous and witty, blending real life cognitive therapy elements into the narrative. It does not shy away from real life sensitive issues but treats them with respect and a touch of dark humour. You play as Sam, a cowboy from the Wild West. Sam himself is a vampire, but tired of the blood-thirsty existence that comes with being an immortal dead and he  a more positive way to live his life and travels to Germany where he meets the ancient vampire named Andromachos or Andy for short. Andy takes on Sam as a therapist-in-training. So your clients are obviously vampires. You meet many interesting and unique characters, well fleshed out and written who go through their own personal arcs as they proceed through therapy. The cast of characters range from historical figures to modern day streamers. The game at times is quite humorous and does not shy away from sexual humour and playful dark banter. One part I had a good laugh at is how Andy described Marcus Aurelius (the Roman Emperor), as Marky.  The roasts in this game are epic…”If I cannot consume high-quality blood, I might as well drink blood from Florida”. Settings include screen mode, resolution options, graphic options, text options and audio controls.* In order to save you have to hit ESC and then save.  However there is a way to view a history log,  press L to see the dialogue in text form. As you play the game you will be presented with choices like most visual novels. However this one mixes the fun of vampires and actual well-researched classic cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) elements into the gameplay. As a therapist-in-training you will talk with people, construct a treatment plan and evaluate their progress. There are four main clients you will interact with. Dr. Drayne, Isabella d’Este, Edmund and Meddy. As you treat and talk to them you will uncover cognitive distortions (they appear as choices on the bottom of the screen) that become choices you can make to move the story forward in the right direction. There are no real wrong answers as Andy will cut in if you chose wrong and urge you to try again. There are some mini games. One is drinking blood (just match your cursor or “fangs” over the vein in the person's neck and a meditation mini-game. They are included to mix things up and while the vein mini-game is fun I really did not enjoy the meditation game, I found the floating text to be not as responsive as I would have liked.All the characters in the novel are not only voiced but voiced by some really great talent. Talent that makes the vampires . It is also developed by a talented voice actor,  who is known for his roles in the super popular game Hades (he voices Ares, Dionysus and Theseus). Amongst other greats such as Kit Chen, Kylie Clark, Sarah Grayson, Francesca Meaux and Matthew Mercer. Visually the game is great to look at. Unique characters with all their own styles. Hand drawn and vibrant. I need to shout out the artists that contributed; Ruth Bosch, Kim Schumacher, Sibylle Hell, Barbara Langa & Darcy Grimm. One of the things I love the most in visual novel games is CG’s (computer graphics) or as I call them  artworks. Sadly this game does not have any which is such a shame. The artwork is so well crafted that I would have loved to see some special arts of the main characters.  This game despite being highly unique and full of dark humour is really one that leaves you thinking. The concepts of cognitive behavioural therapy can benefit us all. We all are inclined to indulge in one or more of the cognitive distortions presented.  It is a novel that makes you think, feel and realize maybe we are too harsh on ourselves at times, harsh on others or our view on the world as a whole. Keep in mind this game is not influenced by the choices you make and you, realistically, can not fail which could be seen as a negative if the game was going for more of a darker twist. If you ended up not bettering a client but the opposite. But that would change the dynamic of the story and I think the whole point of this game is to teach, enlighten and entertain while keeping it overall in a positive place. I will be honest, those looking to just be purely entertained will not find this game engaging. It is a game that takes the therapist aspect more seriously than maybe it should, especially in the second half of the game where the concepts of CBT get more complex. Each client has 3 sessions each, so before each section more concepts are added, honestly making the game at times feel more like studying by having to keep referencing the in-game journal, than fun. So this game will be for some and not so much for others. I enjoyed my time with the novel. I do wish there was a bit more choice & consequence and maybe pulling back on the clinical terms and elements. 🩸

_childDocuments_.review: Played this game with my husband for a date night, and it honestly has been surprisingly great for our relationship? We originally picked it up just because it seemed silly, but it actually describes CBT concepts really well and in a way that is easy to follow. Both of us were able to recognize what cognitive distortions we tend to use in our day-to-day by which ones we struggled to recognize in game. He struggled with emotional reasoning and personalization, while I struggled with black-and-white thinking and discounting the positive.This led to an actually deep and meaningful conversations on areas we could grow and how these distortions affect our relationship?????Came for Vampires. Stayed for the Therapy.

And dang if it didn't get me to reflect on the things I'm doing and thinking in my own life. If you love vampires and you've ever thought "I could fix them", this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: As an Licensed Professional Counselor, this game is an amazing guide to Cognitive Behavior Therapy (CBT) and other common orientations that are used in helping to stop the distortions that we have. This game teaches the CBT model and other therapeutic lessons in a sensitive but creatively engaging way, and of course all while being a lovable cowboy vampire! Can't recommend this game enough, I have had clients play it in between sessions.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: As a counselor this is an interesting game. The story telling is fun and the use of CBT principles is really interesting. I think if you are a geek therapist and you work from a CBT lens, this would be a great game to do with your client in session or give as a way to practice identifying cognitive distortions between sessions as they work on building insight into their own behavior. You can tell they consulted with a counselor when making this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: So I actually work as a therapist, having obtained my license less than a year ago, they state in the game that this was made alongside licensed therapists and that tracks. In fact, this was actually a nice refresher of some concepts to the point that I actively think playing this game could be beneficial to new clinicians. It  also has great voice actors and art so you know its a great ride.The core game play comes in the form of challenging cognitive distortions, but the joy of it comes from the stories being told, watching your clients learn and grow into the version of themselves they wanted to be. Just as much as the main character learns to find the joy in hearing those stories and playing his bit part in their happier ending, I also recognized myself in that journey. I should hope that therapists the world over learn to find their joy in the work in the same manner, and can only recommend that if you enjoy stories and want to learn a bit all the while then pick it up. You may just learn a thing or two about yourself while you play.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: My background going into this is an intro level familiarity with VNs and a Bachelors in science of Psychology.Vampire therapist is a well written, excellently voice acted and highly compelling visual novel that tackles the idea of immoral beings struggling with centuries of emotional damage. It features an amazing cast and no one if phoning it in, for the dialog along VT is worth a play.Now as a psychologist I often find myself curious how well a game about psychology actually represents it and I'm happy to report I feel VT actually does a very good job.Now in session you probably would overtly state what sort of logical fallacy the patient was making but the empathy and earnest desire to help people, without judgment or condemnation, is the goal of any good counselor. Additionally, I appreciate them taking the time to point out that you shouldn't casually psychoanalyze your friends outside of session. Too often these days I see psychology applied to social and business stations to exploit people. Examples being so called “subtle manipulation” to get what you want out of people or “loot box” mechanics. Thus, touching on the ethical aspects of psychology and it's application are nice to see in a game focused on it.The only thing I'd say they got wrong was a bit of history on the nature of introspection. At one point it's said that “people haven't really been thinking about how they think very long” or something to that effect. The truth is, the Greeks often used self reflection and introspection in their phylsopy, in fact the Greeks went as far as to theorize that there were chemicals within our bodies that helped to regulate our moods. Fun fact: That's where the world melancholy comes from! As an aside, I don't normally reply to other reviews but I wanted to say that in my Psychology studies here in America, it was in fact greatly encouraged that you undergo therapy your self at least a few times, to understand what it's like to be on the other side of the equation, so that you can have genuine sympathy and understanding for what the patient is feeling or experiencing. On a more personal note, I would be somewhat skeptical of any counselor who has never known what it's like to be a client.Over all I'd give Vampire therapist an A+ as a game about psychology, it borderlines on being a teaching tool but doesn't loose track of the story or come off as “textbooky.”If you like sexy vampires, psychology and/or VNs with great VO work, this is a def pick up for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: It's is what it says: Vampire therapy, but i do wish there was a little more to do outside of the therapy...? I like Sam as a character and hopefully there's more story content for him. It plays like Ace Attorney, you pick up CBT terms and apply them where you need to in sessions - not particularly hard, and the clients you meet are usually fun to interact with. Another thing to note is that there is no fail state, if you use the wrong term the game tells you "thats wrong".Huge plus is that the entire thing is voice acted.My minor nitpick being that in the very first hour of gameplay two characters hit on you and you deny them four times in a row before being forced by the game to go along with their advances into a mini game- it felt like a weird choice given how the rest of the game works. Personally it did not bother me but I can imagine there might be someone put off by that game design decision.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: Once I saw the name of the game and that the main character is a vampire cowboy, I knew I'd have to play it. Vampire Therapist is a generally charming game. I enjoyed the core gameplay and voice-acting, and I'd recommend it with some reservations (particularly one huge one at the end).I do wish that Sam's cowboy terms for cognitive distortions hadn't been immediately discarded. His examples are fun and evocative, and using terms like "High Noon Mind" and "Saloon Thinking" got me re-examining CBT concepts I'd long since internalized and otherwise tend to mentally gloss over in text. In comparison, "Nosferatu Thinking" is... cute? It's a joke but not a very evocative term, and for the first few sessions in the game I had to keep stopping to remember what it was supposed to mean.I  the blood-drinking mini-game though, and I wish it had been left out entirely. The teeth never actually line up with the vein you're supposed to bite, and I was never really sure why I succeeded sometimes and failed others. Overall, the experience is just irritating. In comparison, though the meditation mini-game is counterintuitive enough that I got stuck there for a while when it first appeared, I could consistently get through it easily enough after figuring out what it wanted me to do.You can also watch old black-and-white movies in Sam's coffin, for some reason. I really have nothing to say about the coffin TV besides that I'm confused about why it exists.The main reservation I have about the game is also the one part I'm genuinely angry about. The game provides some content warnings at the start, but it doesn't forewarn you then or at the time when it occurs that the last bit of gameplay is stopping a character's suicide attempt. There's also no way to prevent or skip over that section of the game. A game built in consultation with therapists and focused on mental health should know better than to spring that on players, and there's really no excuse for that massive oversight. There isn't even the token inclusion of a suicide hotline in the credits like most modern games that include onscreen attempts. This alone makes me wish there was a "maybe" review option instead of just "yes" or "no."As is, though I'd recommend the game in general, I absolutely would not do that without also spoiling that portion.

_childDocuments_.review: Lundy Bancroft is a counsellor who specialises in abusers, and a very good author. He warns that abusers and predators who receive generalized therapy can become more dangerous, and their therapy can 'inoculate' them against more specialized therapy later on.Vampire Therapist is unintentionally extremely good at portraying this, in its accurate and thorough portrayal of talk therapy. Its writing is well researched, it shows the severe holes in the practice between the lines, but avoids addressing this problem directly. I highly recommend this game, but I cannot do it in good conscience without a warning of what this game is avoiding.This kind of therapy is very good for identifying negative thought patterns, and for building an internal sense of self esteem.  It is very good for working with patients as they are, in a non-judgemental fashion. Because of this it often can't, or won't, present positive values to patients or teach them replacement skillsets or social expectations. So instead of making predators and abusers less of that, therapy can make them far more effective in their behaviours because they can use what they've learned in therapy as a weapon, and because it teaches them how to feel far more confident and unashamed in their antisocial behaviours without actually preventing those behaviours. Doing my best to not use spoilers, because I do recommend this game, I will limit myself to saying that the game has at least two storylines which show a heavy emphasis on the patient's emotional wellbeing with near total disregard to how dangerous they are to the people around them, and in one case a patient is celebrated for becoming more predatory in self-acceptance. This is not weak writing, but an accurate representation of this treatment in practice, and why getting the right *kind* of help is as important as getting help at all.Play Vampire Therapist, but keep this question in mind; "Does helping this patient hurt other people?"

_childDocuments_.review: At the end of my session with my Vampire Therapist, I would say I felt better overall (hence the brilliant blue thumb of approval), but unable to achieve full mindfulness.- Excellent VO performances. The voice talent carry this game.- Authentic characters expressed through natural writing.- Learn techniques to identify your own thought patterns!- Shoddy mini-games. Biting game feels like filler. Meditation game has bad conveyance (what am I supposed to do?).- The game is wrong about the "correct" Cognitive Distortion sometimes.- The above point is not my Cognitive Distortion either. Yes, I need therapy, but not over this! Let's talk about YOUR mother instead and see how you like it!!- Polish issues: Animation jitters. Script and VOs sometimes out of sync. Some outtakes still present in the wrong distortion choices. - The writing hiccups when transitioning to the spot the distortion sections (Lots of "That's neat, but let's continue . . ." kind of breaks)- Dialogue dips deeply into sappy, saccharine speeches - Summarily distracting (a lot alike abrupt alliteration). - They run the "Americans can't handle sex" joke into the ground. Firstly, this game taught me that's an Over-generalization. Secondly, as a citizen of Californication and a weeb with a Hidive subscription, this joke fell particularly flat.- Theater fans who enjoy passionate performances.- Fans of stories featuring characters with strong personalities, alien perspectives and intriguing histories.- Anyone who wants to dive into the thought patterns of ancient predators who could  while away their immortality writing Hallmark greeting cards and fortune cookie affirmations.Again, I want to stress that I liked this game, but I found myself constantly distracted. Sometimes those distractions came from without, via polish quirks and gameplay gaffs. Sometimes from within, via my fixation on writing that would cause my teeth to ache due to its sugary overtones. Perhaps a less curmudgeon-y, less finicky gamer would sink into this game's euphoric dialogues without feeling the sharp bite of dissonance prick them out of the moment. If you're a cynical bastard like I am (Labeling, I know), or can't switch off the part of your brain that's always spotting bloopers and ruining the movie for you and your couch buddies (and you're not in my "Recommend To" category), this might be a pass for you. Anyone else still reading this will likely enjoy their exceptionally voiced therapy sessions (hopefully subsidized with one of those schmancy non-American health plans).Now on the other hand, if you're all about those cynical bastard takes, or find something about my review style that speaks to you,

_childDocuments_.review: This is a highly intelligent game.  Not in the sense that it is pretentious.  A few of the characters you meet in the game ARE pretentious.But your main character is just a down to earth cowboy vampire who happens to be good at being a therapist to the undead.I found this game to be mentally stimulating, and even challenging.  Now this game is unpunishing - if you make a wrong decision, you don't get a game over, or a strike against you.  You simply try again, until you get the right answer.  But, you WANT to get the right answer the first time.  See, this game introduces very complex abstract concepts, and allows you to apply them to these troubled vampires, as they open up to you about their problems.  The goal is to get them to see past their own cognitive dissonance, and to see the truth of the situation they are in.  The truth of the matter is, their un-life isn't as bad as they make it out to be, and they are unnecessarily adding a lot of stress to themselves by holding themselves to unrealistic standards.I've only played this game for 3.7 hours at time of writing, but I myself am already learning a lot, about cognitive distortions, and, more importantly, about myself.  For I myself tend to view the world in very black and white terms, and that is a cognitive distortion that this game has helped me realize about myself.  For $15.00, that's a hell of a bargain.But the benefits of this game do not stop there.  This is, truly, a very gripping game.  It is more like a visual novel, with prompting similar at times to Phoenix Wright (when the court demands that you give the correct answer), but I truly felt that each vampire I interviewed, very much felt like a boss battle.  A fight.  Not in the sense that you are going against them, per se, but rather their distorted view of reality.  And it is exhausting.  I felt after each interview, I myself in the real world needed a break.  That is how deep each conversation gets.  It's almost emotionally draining, to talk to these vampires, because their personalities can be very abrasive, and the voice acting is so good and convincing, that this really does feel like having a difficult conversation with a patient, or a friend.  With the hardship of talking to these people, comes the very real reward that one feels when one successfully convinces a vampire that perhaps their view of reality is a little too extreme, and they should re-assess in order to fit in accordance to reality, not in spite of it.Yes, this game is very, VERY rewarding....as mentioned before, the voice acting is entirely on-point.  The art style is endearing, and the character designs are unique and vibrant, to match the characters' eccentric natures.  At no point did I feel bored.  These vampires keep you on your toes.  Buy this game.  Do yourself a favor, and get it.  When you talk to these vampires, you may just learn a little bit about yourself, as I have.

_childDocuments_.review: Vampire Therapist follows a cowboy vampire named Sam who has been alive for over 200 years. He has done some terrible things in his past, but after spending 90 years wandering the wilderness finding himself and coming to some realizations, he had the urge to help his fellow vampires. After learning how to use the internet just enough to email people, he came into contact with a 3,000 year old vampire known as Andromachos. Andromachos invites Sam to his club in Europe and, after proving himself to his employees, is able to meet Andromachos himself. It turns out the revelations Sam had were cognitive distortions he was able to figure out entirely by himself, which Andromachos was pretty impressed by. He teaches Sam the correct terms (rip Sam’s original names for them), tests him, and tells him that he will take Sam under his wing if Sam agrees to receive therapy as well. Much to Sam’s surprise, Sam will also have four vampire clients of his own, one per week with them returning every month.Thus, starts the game’s narrative loop. Sam will have a therapy session with Andromachos, where you get to hear his struggles and backstory, and learn more cognitive distortions to use. Then you’ll have sessions with your four clients as their therapist. You’ll get some basic information on them and what they’re coming in for, but it soon becomes apparent that there’s more to it. Despite being vampires who died in different time periods, they are actually pretty relatable with the problems they end up having. There’s Dr. Drayne a researcher struggling with addiction, a previously powerful matriarch named Isabella d’Este who feels her life/unlife was meaningless, Edmund Kean a Shakespearean actor who wants to return to the stage but has anger at the mere thought of getting criticized, and Meddy who is basically a vampire influencer who is struggling with the increasing demands of her followers. These guys are all pretty unique and interesting to talk to and learn about. There’s also some side characters you’ll interact with as well, with Crimson being the one you learn about the most.Gameplay is pretty simple here. Aside from the occasional dialogue choice, you’ll be tasked with identifying the cognitive distortion your client is exhibiting using the five that’s listed (which, once you learn more than five, are ones you end up picking yourself before the session). Don’t worry, there’s no fail state here so if you pick wrong you just get a hint on what the answer is and asked to pick again until you get it right. There’s also two minigames, which I found pretty okay. The first has you line up an icon of fangs to a human’s veins to drink blood (though it does get a bit harder with those that wear collars) and another where you meditate by breathing in and out and hovering your cursor over the words. I didn’t mind the inclusion of these minigames, but they are a bit annoying when you’re replaying to get missing achievements.Sam also has a journal where he puts all the cognitive distortion definitions in his own writing style, with cowboy-centry examples, session summaries for his clients, and journal entries for what he did during the time skips.No game is perfect and Vampire Therapist is no exception. Some of these are personal annoyances and some of these aren’t and I’ll just list them out:I was not expecting this to be fully voiced. All the voice actors did a wonderful job and really brought the characters to life. Each voice actor fit their character really well and I especially loved Meddy’s and Sam’s voice actors and the direction they were given. The music is also pretty good, giving it that club feel while also it perfectly balancing between being good background music and being too annoying to listen to constantly.Vampire Therapist definitely met my expectations that I developed after playing the demo. There are some aspects that I got annoyed by, but this is a great, solid, game that I’m so glad I played. Vampire Therapist managed to implement the real concepts of cognitive distortions in a way that was fun to learn and use. The writing style is great, and adding the wonderful voice acting brings more life to all the characters, and all the characters were all written very well. The game does a great job in bringing us along on their therapy journey, giving us their backstories naturally, and shows how each of them change over time. I honestly could not bring myself to end a play session until I did everyone’s session for that “month” and could barely stay away from the game for long. Not to mention that you play as a cowboy vampire!I’d say if you’re interested in playing a visual novel where you’re a therapist, uses real cognitive behavioral therapy concepts, and fine with it only focusing on the therapy; you’ll most likely like Vampire Therapist. The game is actually priced perfectly and is worth playing if you’re interested in what this game is offering. Though, you might get disappointing if you’re expecting to get scenes that aren’t focused on being a therapist and you’ll of course not like Vampire Therapist if you’re not at all interested in the premise.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing Vampire Therapist has opened my eyes to an entirely unexpected gaming experience. What truly captivates me is how it masterfully weaves legitimate therapeutic techniques and psychological terminology into a narrative centered around vampires. The game delves deep into their struggles with loss, emotional trauma, and the fascinating tension between morality and immortality that develops as these beings age through centuries.What sets this game apart is its refreshing take on vampire mythology. The characters are wonderfully crafted, balancing profound depth with moments of genuine humor that catch you off guard in the best possible way. I particularly appreciate how the game challenges traditional vampire tropes, presenting these immortal beings through various lenses and showing them grappling with challenges that feel surprisingly – almost uncomfortably – human.For anyone seeking an unconventional vampire story, this game delivers something special. _childDocuments_.review: Two sessions in and I can safely say I wish this had come out sooner, as it'd have made my studying for Psych back in college much easier if I could de-stress like this. It's by far not meant to be used to treat yourself, but it provides an external lens that might just highlight a couple things in you.It's ultimately your average VN affair, but the approach of being a therapist gives it a 'pleasant' hook: the draw of helping others. I've had a few moments just among the first two clients where I had to pause and go 'Holy hell I've said about that much myself' and then found myself wanting to help them out even more. Like I said, this won't fix you, but at the very least it may help you identify a few things to speak about with a proper professional, or at the very least try to adjust yourself in the interim.Besides all of that, the art has been quite nice. It's easy to get a vibe for your clients just off of their portraits, and the character designs have been rather fun. Sam's just an overall enjoyable MC, and Andy is  as your guide. Voice acting is quality as well. Overall for a 15 dollar price tag this is a steal in my limited VN experience, especially considering the baseline exposure to basic psychotherapy.EDIT: One visit each with 4 different clients and my opinion remains the same. There are some startlingly relatable scenarios in play for centuries-old bone bags. And it's not all sunshine and rainbows either, which I enjoy. I expected the pushback, and it was realistic. _childDocuments_.review: Having just finished the game, I’m updating my review. This game is everything I didn’t know I needed. I adore the characters so freaking much and the ending, without giving too much away, left me fighting off a case of the sniffles. Despite being a fairly short game, 12 hours give or take, I quickly grew attached to the characters because they were all very well written and the conversations felt realistic and organic, a thing which is kind of lacking nowadays. The music and sound were very well done, and while I hate the term ‘cozy’ in relation to a game, the setting for this was. It was relaxing, and I often found myself playing later in the evening when I wanted to wind down. I also enjoyed that the game caused me to take a look at myself as well; I even ended up mentioning the game to my therapist, and we had a few chats based on this game made me think about. However, that isn’t to say it’s ALL good. The game is, as I said, fairly short. Because of this, things happen quickly. There’s a lot of ‘behind the scenes’ relationship building between everyone that would have been nice to see firsthand. Stretching things out a bit would have also helped with the distortion concepts. Some of them were quite complex and hard to grasp, even with Andromachos’s examples. In the late game, I noticed quite a few spelling and grammar mistakes, small things like a missing comma or switched letters. There also doesn’t seem to be any replay ability to this and there is no real way to ‘lose’ or fail. Everyone gets their happy (mostly) ending. Now I could be wrong about that, but that’s how it appears. Lastly, the neck biting mini game. I’ll be honest. I hate it with a passion. I’m color blind and couldn’t really see the veins from the skin, let alone the two different veins, a fact which was made ever harder by the speed of the teeth. Maybe a progress bar with a little green ‘click when the slider is in here’ spot would have been better. Over all this game is amazing, and that teaser at the end, for a part two was just cruel because I WANT to get to know these characters better, want to spend time with them and I want to talk to them and hang out in the games world.

_childDocuments_.review: I almost never leave reviews but felt somewhat obligated to write this one. Despite the fact that I thoroughly enjoyed this game and am giving it a thumbs up, I am only really leaving this review to say that it absolutely will NOT appeal to everyone, and there are some things that should be made 100% clear to you before you decide to buy it.Most importantly, this is probably the most on rails visual novel I have ever played. You are moving from point A to B in the story no matter what happens, with no input on the proceedings whatsoever. Not only that, there are no fail states either; you cannot lose at Vampire Therapist and you are not punished for wrong answers in therapy sessions (you are rewarded for repeated successes with achievements though, for what it's worth.) I saw a negative review that summed this issue up quite well by calling it a quiz edutainment game more than anything else. It's not that the game doesn't have more to offer than that in terms of character or narrative, but that is absolutely the core gameplay loop of Vampire Therapist and needless to say this all ends up hurting replayability.Another small issue with the game that ties back to my first point is that because the game is so incredibly on rails your playtime is going to depend almost entirely on your reading speed. This is not necessarily a bad thing, but I think most people who play this kind of game can generally read at a fairly decent pace so you might not end up taking very long to complete all of the content. You can see this in some of the positive steam reviews for the game with some people having evidently completed it in four hours or less. This is most apparent with the two free DLCs, which despite being said to take approximately 30 minutes each are not very difficult to read through in five to ten.Lastly, in my very subjective opinion, the humor is also somewhat hit and miss. It is absolutely capable of being a very funny game, but that is not a rule. Most egregious in my opinion are a few jokes that end up dating the game, usually bits that refer to some kind of specific event from recent years in our time period. The game is small enough in scope that I imagine not many people will be playing it ten years from now, but if someone does something like that will absolutely feel very dated. Again, this is the most subjective part of the review by far, though. I probably made the game sound pretty bad with these three points, so let me be clear in saying that I still very much enjoyed it. It is well written, usually funny, has a cast of interesting characters who all have enjoyable, complex personalities, and probably most importantly clearly has a lot of love put into it. Even though there are certainly elements that I did not entirely appreciate, that is not to say that there is nothing good about Vampire Therapist.If all of the negatives that I listed out do not sound objectionably bad to you, I would recommend giving this a try.

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting something more lighthearted and comical when I picked up this game, something along the lines of "Analyze this". I suppose that is what sprung to my mind when I read the title "Vampire Therapist". Though it does contain elements of lightheartedness and humor, this game deals with some heavier stuff than that. Not being what I expected does not equate to being bad though, so I recommend giving this game a try.Going a little further into details:You play as Samuel, a 200ish year old American cowboy vampire, who has had a revelation after spending 90 years wandering in the wilderness. He wants to help other vampires deal with the negative thinking (i.e. cognitive distortions) that keeps them from achieving personal growth, in other words he wants to become a therapist. For this, he travels to Leipzig, Germany, to meet Andromechos, an ancient several thousand year old Vampire, who becomes his mentor. While Adromechos takes Samuel into therapy, to help him deal with his own congnitive distortions, Samuel takes on 4 clients. A scientist, who has an addiction problem. A rennaisance noblewoman, who believes her existence has lost its meaning. An actor, who feels unappreciated by his critics and audience, and an internet celebrity, who feels stressed out by the demands of her followers. All of them also vampires.Through a series of sessions, you attempt to identify your own and your clients cognitive distortions, by clicking the correct option, with Adromechos offering advice when you get it wrong. As the game progresses, the difficulty increases, as more distortions are introduced and explained to you, and you must select which to focus on prior to each session. Other than some very simple gameified neck biting, and mildly entertaining cutscenes, that is pretty much it.I found it somewhat entertaining and challenging, and recommend giving it a try. The neck biting felt like an unnecessary and somewhat pointless hurdle between sessions to me, and unless you are a perfectionist and/or achievement hunter, I don't think this game offers much replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes a game comes around with a concept so seemingly tailor-made for your artistic sensibilities that it seems too good to be true. Speaking of the characters, I was instantly invested in their stories and wellbeing. I was literally clapping and cheering at certain points! It's definitely more of a reading experience than a gameplay experience, but the gameplay does a good job of enhancing the story by making the player think carefully about what the characters are saying, even if making an incorrect choice doesn't result in penalty most of the time. I'm not usually one to take notes for games, but I found myself naturally jotting down which cognitive distortions the clients used most often, or thoughts about what might be causing a certain reaction. This is the kind of game that makes me want to write something about it, and that's the highest praise I can give.

_childDocuments_.review: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a psycho-social intervention that aims to reduce symptoms of various mental health conditions, primarily depression and anxiety disorders. Cognitive behavioral therapy focuses on challenging and changing cognitive distortions (such as thoughts, beliefs, and attitudes) and their associated behaviors to improve emotional regulation and develop personal coping strategies that target solving current problems. Though it was originally designed to treat depression, its uses have been expanded to include many issues and the treatment of many mental health and other conditions, including anxiety, substance use disorders, marital problems, ADHD, and eating disorders. CBT includes a number of cognitive or behavioral psychotherapies that treat defined psychopathologies using evidence-based techniques and strategies.

_childDocuments_.review: I was utterly let down by this game.  What first seemed to be a uniquely creative experience quickly devolved into a soap-box piece.  I love vampires, and I love the concepts of cognitive based therapy.  How could this go wrong?  The voice acting was also charming in the game.   So how could it go wrong?  It becomes a long winded diatribe against a certain portion of society, and that takes away from the story of "Vampire Therapy" to the point my immersion and humor was ruined!  When I realized I was just hearing someone's personal ideological rant from each character, rather than a story born of unique characters, I had to put it aside for wasting my time.The first instance was this long winded exchange that the great flood is a myth.  (It had no context to any of the characters either, as in, there was no character traumatized by the flood.)  It was out of place with the context of the discussion and odd.  Archaeology shows us sediment layers and fossil groups that prove Earth endured a major flood event, its why there is a great flood story in almost every culture's religion and records.  Whether you are Atheist, Agnostic, Muslim or Christian, science has shown us for a long time now that there was a great flood in Earth's history...  So while I would've accepted this rant if one of the characters was traumatized by the flood, it was entirely out of context and also ignorant of science.  Why are these age old vampires in the game not aware of that, and why the long winded rant against it out of sync with any subject matter the characters were engaged in?  I shrugged it off and played on. Then from that point, it only became more and more clear....   Jokes about Jesus and anal sex.  Jokes about farting in a chair that Jesus made.  Amongst other out of context, endless diatribes.  But it wasn't like it was just coming from one character who had an issue with Christianity or Jesus, it was coming from several characters, none of whom had an issue with Jesus!  So...  wtf?  Okay, well, traditionally speaking the very origin stories of vampires were that they hung out in catacombs and protected churches in exchange for protection during the day when they slept.  Then we have Dracula, an orthodox turned catholic crusader who repelled the Ottoman invasion.  So...  it wasn't humor or therapy that this endless exchanges were coming from, and it was odd that the game moved from the delicious concepts of Vampire Therapy to this anti-Jesus tirade.  And then, suddenly, came the tirade against the United States' personal liberty and the competition of Capitalism.  Again, this was not born out of what happened to one of the characters for the sake of therapy - it had nothing to do with the poor choices one of the characters made, yet it was inserted and then after sitting through it, there was one loose statement trying to tie it in to the trauma of the characters and I'm sorry, it fails!  It is obvious that "Vampire Therapy" was being loosely and illogically used as an excuse to force-fit ideological rants (not thoughtful discussions) into the game.  I wonder if the person who wrote this experienced the mass starvation tied to the history of nations run by communist dictatorships.  So, yeah, the game started off charming, but quickly devolved into an anti-Jesus Christ, pro-communist rant that Did. Not. Stop.  When you hear the same words and the same lines come out of several characters, those aren't genuine characters, that's bad writing.  And when you realize you're just reading someone's ignorant first year college essay instead of playing an entertaining game with genuine characters, I check out.  I uninstalled this garbage and deleted it from my library.  People who want to create 'games' only to self insert their rabid rants need to advertise correctly that the game is about that rather than try to sell it as "humorous and thoughtful discourse."

_childDocuments_.review: I don't remember when I added this game to my wishlist but I got it for my birthday and I was super excited to play it. I've always been a psychology/therapy enthusiast. Finding out there was a somewhat accurate game about being a therapist to vampires was like a dream I didn’t know I wanted to have.The game uses real therapy concepts like cognitive behavior therapy, vetted by licensed professionals. So you know that what our characters are saying (at least the technical stuff) is real! It's like Therapist Simulator- Vampire Edition. I'd totally buy that one too. Besides therapy aspects, the game also has a lot of comedic elements. It's considered dark humor, but to me its just humor really. With that same comedic lens, it looks at some alternate historic depictions - could be characters and event or both and also the depiction of vampires.  It's a vampire game after all. But remember this, even vampires need consent! They can also learn too! I love that this is one of the things mentioned in this game since it has been historically depicted that vampires don't care. This gives vampires a little bit more humanity and respect towards others.  While still in the subject of how the game plays, even if it is a visual novel- it has mini-games! You can see how beautifully I mess up these games in my video. In clearer terms, I suck- pun intended. The game also features a stellar cast of voice actors you may even recognize some! During game play, I kept thinking, I know that voice. Once the credit rolled and I saw "Matthew Mercer" I screamed "I knew it!!"  at my monitor. It was very awesome to hear some actors I've heard in other games before. _childDocuments_.review: I bloody love this game, pun intended obviously. I'm a glutton for stories, I read books in one sitting because unless I'm forced to forget about it, my brain wants to know the whole story! It can very much be appreciated in more bite-sized chunks of time, though. As I was watching the end credits, it hit me : it feels like an indie game from 10-15 years ago. But not a game from then played today, it's not a qualitycomparison at all, it *feels* the same way. The love, the research put in it and yeah, the overall vibes! made me feel like back when I was discovering those fantastic games made on RPGmaker, like To The Moon. It doesn't feel like a superproduction, but you can feel the humanbehind it and THAT is why I love it so much. Andy the vampire daddy lured me in, for I am weak, but it's the entire game that has entrapped me. _childDocuments_.review: A deeply analytical game on what it's like to be a vampire and the mental health problems that could come with it. The characters are well fleshed out and all highly unique. The game also taught me quite a bit about psychology as an academic subject. My only real complaint about the game is a weakness of the visual novel genre. Sometimes the game is looking for a specific cognitive distortion and I don't agree with the answer the game says is right. I think it might be because certain statements have more than one cognitive distortion, but for the sake of gameplay and the visual novel genre only one can be right. _childDocuments_.review: This visual novel seems to be very linear, but it proved to be an excellent educational experience into exploring various cognitive distortions, with examples that were framed in a compelling narrative that made me tear up several times. _childDocuments_.review: As someone who is a fan of vampires, story driven games and the practice of psychology, this game ticks so many boxes for me. _childDocuments_.review: So for reference I have beaten the entire game (7.3 hours), and am a therapist in real life myself, a Cognitive-Behavioral Therapist as well, like the game seems to base itself on. As such I am extremely biased so keep that in mind.This game is so good, so amazing, as both a teaching tool and as a shockingly realistic portrayal of what effective CBT therapy is, that I am heavily considering assigning it as homework to clients as a teaching tool (and will be requesting my own personal therapist, an older gentleman, play himself to potentially pass it along to -his- clients as well). The characters are genuine and sincere (and oftentimes annoying as hell, as humans tend to be), the voice acting is top notch (either A+ tier impressionists or they found genuinely skilled voice actors from all parts of the world), the writing is funny and insightful, and the insight and genuine mastery of psychological principals are humbling. -I- learned things, and at a minimum, even as a therapist explicitly trained in these things, it was an excellent review.I'm not sure if it will be for everyone, but it is clearly made with such love and care and passion, clearly with the intention to do good in the world rather than to make a million dollars, that it is breathtaking. I feel like it's one of those games that I will think about for years. Especially that final part, which without giving too many spoilers, really highlights the "unique to therapists" problem of thinking we already know enough that we can't fall into the same traps that our clients fall into, and thus how important it is for even therapists to have therapists. Truly beautiful.This is a game filled with love, and compassion, and acceptance, and healing, and growth. It reminds us that the most frustrating, upsetting, annoying, hurtful, and even "evil" people in this world are in the end deeply human, and flawed, and oftentimes hurting. It's also charming as hell, as only an "awww shucks" cowboy can be. Beyond excellent, 10/10, "literally recommended this to my mom who doesn't even play videogames" seal of quality.Edit note: So a few of the negative reviews have pointed out being "railroaded" into choices, particularly in regards to the activities your character participates in. While these are true statements I want to point out this is a visual novel and not an RPG, you are not "playing a character", you are following along with what the main character, a 200 year old cowboy vampire who may have tastes, morals, and desires different from you, would do. So if he makes a choice you yourself don't like or wouldn't want to do, that's perfectly valid, but to that end I ask people to keep in mind that he is acting according to what -he- would do. I would also state that there is (in my opinion) nothing explicit that he ever does/"you" have to do, so if that is a barrier for you/causes you discomfort, I would also state that exploring difficult people and concepts and alternative viewpoints from a wide variety of people is indeed the point. I would state wholeheartedly that what the game has to offer/teach is worth the discomfort it may inspire in some people.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game that's helped me look inward! The different characters are fun to interact with, and the writing's got a great range of light-hearted humor with its more serious/dramatic moments. The mini-games take some getting used to, but they're nice breathers from the rest of the visual novel elements.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely delightful game - although if I'm being honest there isn't much 'game' there per se, it plays a lot more like a Visual Novel where guessing the correct cognitive distortion grants you more dialogue.That being said, what Vampire Therapist does well, it does VERY well: the characters are very compellingly portrayed, both in their gorgeous visual art and top-notch voice acting that helps bring them to (un)life. While charming and funny, often using light-hearted jabs at various national and historical stereotypes (because remember, vampires are immortal), the game does also have its more serious moments that stop that the characters from being complete caricatures - after all, it's hard to give a character therapy if their trauma doesn't feel real. Ironically, the more vampiric the characters act, the more they reveal that they are actually very human, which I suppose is the point.From a technical standpoint the game is a little bit buggy, although not in a way that stopped me from enjoying the experience: the curtain transitions are VERY choppy, and I noticed that sometimes when I saved while on the screen in which you choose cognitive distortions for your next session, loading back into that save would result in a placeholder menu with no patient data loaded in, plus some other minor things like loading when an image was being displayed might show the wrong image. However, these were very minor gripes thanks to the game's autosave (or checkpoint) system; the actual dialogue, character images and voice acting all played as they should.Wait... SHOULD?!
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for this game since I found out about it! Very fun and actually something for the brain :) While you try to help other vampires through their crisis you learn a lot about psychological phenomena and about yourself (as Sam). What I didn't anticipate was tearing up a few times already because of some devastating fates.I cannot wait to see how the stories of my lovely clients continue and what lovely Andy has in store for Sam too!10/10 would recommend :)P.S. Astarion would be a perfect patient for Sam.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: this game was certainly what i expected. for one, i thought i'd be playing a plain old vampire, but it turns out i'm a COWBOY vampy. Wthis game has immaculate vibes, captivating character designs and engrossing stories. through providing therapy to other vamps, i learned a good deal of these cognitive distortions and how they can cloud our minds and trouble us. this game is insightful, funny and, well, vamps are sexy. not to mention the superb voice acting. 100% recommended
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: This game has helped me identify my own cognitive distortions. Although I haven't completed it yet, it has genuinely assisted me in processing many of my personal issues with friends and family. Thank you. I highly recommend this if you have any mental health issues or just want to be able to feel more empathetic to those around you. I've had so many moments where I sat back in my chair and rethought so many situations I've personally been in. Genuinely, I think this game has changed me for the better, and I'm so happy for it. Thank you, so, so much, developers. This game has impacted me in ways I never thought possible.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: I friend gifted me this game wanting to see me play it and oh man, it was so much fun! Me and my chat were having a great time with all of the humor and funny moments and that was just 3 hours in. Told my friends about this game and they love the concept too. If you like psychology and silly (maybe a little kinky) humor, this game is for you. 10/10!
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: this game is so so fun and amazing, the characters are fun, great, 3 dimensional, and really neat. the art, the sound, the music, everything is amazing. i think the only complaint I have, which isn't super bad, was that It had a tendency to crash on me very often, so I learned to save very frequently. however it did break from my immersion a little. the crashes were random and happened pretty often, so it was hard to know when they would happen. i really hope there will be more bug/performance fixes soon and maybe adding a couple more tutorials, especially on the meditation mini game. other than it is an amazing game and i hope to see vampire therapist 2!!
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: I just finish the game! And hell I love it from the beginning to the end! It become one of my favorite visual novels that is for sure. As a therapist it was amazing see my work space portrait in such amazing and beautiful game. The voice acting was impressive, as the art and the history! I must congrats to everyone who is working on the project!I am eager to see more, and I hope there is a second series or a dlc! I would love to see more therapy sessions and have been thinking how an therapy session with historical figures that I like would be; like Achilles, Odyseus, Circe or even Medeia!!! huahaua Don't hurt to dream :v I am surely gonna play this game more than once and recomend to everyone!Thanks for all the time and effort everyone who worked put on this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: Played the first couple hours together with my roommate, have to say this is genuinely one of the most fun games either of us have played in a while! Super interesting concept, great voice acting, love all the little moments of levity (horse neighing sound effects? Blood-drinking minigames? Incredible) Really great balance in terms of difficulty for selecting each distortion - prompted some really fun discussions between us! I think it'd be fun to play alone, but it works really well to play as a duo and switch off with someone you're comfortable/close with. Maybe the first time I've seen a really accurate depiction of what it's like to be in a therapy session - there is joy and lightness and pain and sadness and sometimes, yes, you do have to explain to your therapist the difference between RPG and FPS games. Such is life.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: In the midst of the ever ongoing vampire craze, this is a pretty unique take on the creatures of the night and their surprisingly ordinary problems. If you love narrative games with a bit of a twist on the age-old formula, gorgeous character artwork and a generous helping of (sometimes cringey but good-natured) humour, this will be right up your alley. I didn't expect the game to remain so genuine throughout, considering you meet some whacky characters right out the bat (ha!). It manages to get a couple of complex concepts across while still being entertaining. Every patient has their personal history to explore and figure out a way to live with that in modern times with all its trials and tribulations. The results are funny yet heartfelt and emphasize compassion as a core message - I can honestly say it was a refreshing and enjoyable ride. Last but not least, always a joy to see some more games toeing the line between serious game and a fun time, as well as being produced in Germany. :) Doubly so as it is very queer-friendly. Diversity win!
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: Vampire Therapist is an excellent game that feels like the start of something big and I'd recommend it to all fans of visual novels who like games that push the VN formula a little further. The characters in it are all charming in their own ways, all fully voice-acted and are certain to make you laugh one minute, while feeling genuinely for them the next. You will also learn a lot about therapy and about yourself while playing without even realising it's happening. Also, there are cowboys AND vampires, so that's pretty ideal!My only question now is when's the sequel happening?
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: I delight in playing Vampire Therapist almost as much as it delights in poking fun at Americans' discomfort around foreign languages and intimate matters. This game's writing is sharp, its voice acting on point, and its message genuinely heartfelt and helpful. The occasional typo and the audio being cut short in one or two spots are my only real complaints. Even if this game pokes at some sore points and highlights harmful patterns in my own thinking, I'm happy I found it and will recommend it to everyone I can.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing and actually super educational with regards to emotional intelligence. I also really appreciate the writing. I appreciate the twists and turns the dialogue takes in each session even if the game (from what I've played so far, is mostly pretty linear in the beginning and middle. I haven't gotten to any of the endings yet though. Overall I'm really happy with this game. If I were rating I'd give it a 4.5/5That said, I have a few recommendations for the dev/s: -Please allow us to access the journal when we are choosing which distortions the client might exhibit before the session. It will help us to better deliberate on which distortions we should pick.-Add an auto advance button for dialogue.-add a message log for past message.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: If you like sexy vampires, clever banter, and improved mental health, this is the game for you.You play as Sam Walls, a 200-year-old cowboy vampire, who seeks out Andromachos, a powerful ancient vampire (and goth club owner), for advice on helping other vampires overcome harmful patterns of thinking. As you conduct frank and funny therapy sessions with some delightfully messy vampire patients, you learn to identify real concepts from behavioral psychology. Superbly voice acted and wittily written, Vampire Therapist just sticks with you, in the best possible way. I catch myself watching my own words and thought patterns even after I've put the game down. I also look at people's juicy arteries differently. (Props to the neck biting mini game!)I played an early version of the build and busted a gut laughing out loud. Now I've started over, playing the game in its full campy, sexy glory, and I can't get over its utter charm and originality. Full disclosure: I know the creator!
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so good I'm writing my first Steam review!- Excellent writing- Beautiful art- Witty voice acting- Tight, elegant game loop centred around narrative choices- Just the right pinch of tiny mini-games every now and then- Actual deeper thoughts that make me question my own thinking.Go play it! It's definitely worth the 15 bucks!
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: Adoring it so far - it's clever, funny, sly. Characterisations are great for a text-based game. I've already laughed out loud twice, and that's rare. The 'therapy' part seems completely legit, and very well presented. I'm guessing Andromachos is a reference to the fact that Man's greatest enemy is himself (a pretty good working slogan for therapy). That's typical of the clever details in this game, though you don't need to be aware of them to have fun with the process. Also, I'd never bitten anyone before. So there's that.

_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: Love the story, the voice acting is superb. Usually I'd skip voiced dialogue after a bit but for this I am hooked. I love the therapy concept and you can tell that this is a labour of love for the developer. This is a really unique experience, has super memorable characters and is one to talk about I think.I played the demo and loved it, and I can't even speed run the bits I already played because I like the characters so much. :D
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: I have a rule against day one purchases, but this is absolutely broke that rule with the writing, voice acting, and comedy gold! It's probably the only game that could say "CBT" as both Cognitive Behavioral Therapy & ♥♥♥♥ and Ball Torture in the same breathe and still make complete thematic sense. And the amount of jabs towards American Puritanism is so utterly wonderful and refreshing to see.         Absolutely 10/10. It's not hyperbole to say this might be 2024's best visual novel as this Berlin dev team came out of no-where and knocked it out of the park!  (On a serious note, while this absolutely isn't a replacement for therapy, these cognitive distortions are presented so accurately that I wouldn't be surprised if a few therapists use this as supplementary material.)

_childDocuments_.review: Guide vampires through centuries of emotional baggage, decades of delusions and the odd bout of self-loathing with real cognitive behavioral therapy concepts and become a Vampire Therapist! Even vampires need a shoulder to cry on when a neck to bite just won’t do.

About the Game Visions of Mana is a brand new title in this series revolving around the sacred sword and mana. The protagonist Val and his childhood friend Hinna, the newly appointed Alm of Fire, set off on a journey to the Mana Tree. This game’s iconic vibrant and vast semi-open field contains adorable yet ferocious monsters, allowing you to enjoy swift three-dimensional battles using the power of the Elementals. Through adventures with friends met along the way, they start to see the truth about the world. Must we accept our fates? A new “Mana” tale begins here as a classic fantasy series returns to its roots. ▸Bold graphics full of characteristic “Mana” flair The characters journey across a vibrant world alive with spirits. ▸Exploring the world Explore the vast, semi-open world that stretches as far as the eye can see. Traverse the environment quickly and safely with new companions, the “Pikuls'. ▸Harness the power of the Elementals In this game, you will fight enemies using weapons that house the power of the Elementals. Change between different classes and characters to suit your playstyle and enjoy combat that has evolved both three-dimensionally and strategically. ▸ Breathtaking and immersive soundtrack Around 100 background music tracks by a talented team of creators who have worked on countless tracks throughout the series. The music in field areas feature interactive music, heightening the mood for adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like sitting in front of the SNES playing Mana in the 90s. The music. The colorful intro. The characters. Everything about it, is pure Mana. Child-like wonder and the power of friendship. I hope they port the other Mana games over to Steam. These games are instant buys. There was one summer where every day, I'd ride my bike down to a friends house to play Secret of Mana with him. Furiously pedaling, hoping against hope that he didn't progress the story any since the previous night. This game takes me back to that time. Where are you now friend? We have a new Mana Tree to save.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: After a long wait, the new installment of the Mana series is here. I enjoyed the combat and personally feel it is the most distinctive feature of Visions of Mana. It’s fast-paced and has a ton of depth with the class systems. I spent a lot of time experimenting with different classes yet somehow they all managed to synergize with your team in meaningful ways, making it hard for me to just stick with one class. There are a lot of fun minigames that test your knowledge of the game's mechanics, which is a nice incentive to learn and make full use of the little advantages some elements and classes have instead of just over-leveling one.The story is pretty simple in the early acts but does an excellent job of establishing the cast of charming characters and likable protagonists, but I do feel the later stages suffer from pacing issues and repetitive content. Despite this, the overall experience and narrative thus far remain emotionally satisfying. The game's vibrant high fantasy art style is beautiful to immerse yourself in, though I noticed some occasional visual bugs and framerate drops when a lot of effects appear on screen.There isn't much else to say, it's an amazing return for the series with innovative mechanics, extremely rewarding combat, and adorable characters that make it a strong contender for fans and newcomers alike. Despite consecutive mediocre and disappointing releases the past year, Square Enix finally delivered!
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: It's a damn shame the studio already got shut down. NetEase is a very scummy company, but we pretty much all know this by now. As counter-intuitive as it may sound, giving this game the positive press it deserves will probably convince Square to rehire the devs as a new studio, since it's clear NetEase is washing their hands of this game.This is a great game, it feels exactly like Trials of Mana (3D), in all of the good ways that make me love that game. I hope the developers get re-hired by Xeen or another Square adjacent studio to keep at it. This game still has minor performance issues, but there's still a chance someone else will patch the game because it's UE5. Geometry pop-in is pretty bad, although Trials had the same issue, and someone made a basic mod to fix that.Game is still kinda easy, again, just like Trials of Mana, but that's also likely to be fixed by mods, again, just like Trials. Although Trials got an update adding some nicely brutal NG+ difficulties.I will say, if you enjoy this game, give Falcom's Ys series a look (specifically the Team-Based games), or Ni No Kuni 2, those games don't get enough attention, and have a very similar game feel and aesthetic.EDIT: I had an internet outage for multiple days, long story, but this game kept me company, Steam didn't record the time because of the outage. and I have one more thing to say about it.The level curve is much better balanced than Trials, unlike Trials, overlevelling is incredibly hard to do unintentionally, which is great because I ended up overlevelling and steamrolling the endgame of Trials trying to get ??? seeds early, before I realized that the game has a failsafe to get every 3rd class item through the ??? seeds assured via chests, which I'm fairly sure wasn't a thing in Trials' 2D version..In this game, the level requirements increase just enough to deter grinding without making it impossible to get an extra level or two, which is the sweet spot for experience curves. That being said, without grinding, the encounters are still very manageable even underlevelled, and gear matters more than level, and you get enough lucre to buy basic gear. Unlike Trials, you're not encouraged to get a huge stack of money before you're supposed to for a cheevo and never have to grind money ever again.EDIT EDIT: Basically just thought about this while checking in with the current reviews, I don't really agree with the complaints about lack of advancement, in terms of skills, there's still a lot of thresholds of growth for each class. Every class is actually multi-tiered, and you learn both universal skills and passives. There's no visual progression between classes' skill tiers, however I think earning new skills through earning new classes or gaining the items to unlock new tiers, still adds a satisfying sense of progression.I mean, sure, there's not anything with as big of an impact as class changing in Trials/SD3 Remake, but there is SOME depth to be had. However, I'm willing to point out that a fair amount of the complaints people seem to have with exploration are also problems I personally have with Trials that weren't addressed here, I just considered them minor to what was done right in both games.People seem to be quickly jumping to say this game is worse than Trials Remake, as if Trials Remake was some sort of respected ARPG classic, when Trials itself was actually pretty divisive on launch and really didn't do well critically. Original Trials fans were extremely split on it's changes, it was considered slop on release by more hardcore ARPG fans, and only got it's reputation over time thanks to people like Vinesauce who loved Trials, rightfully so, I think it's a fantastic lovingly-made and well-executed remake of a classic. I do think journos are overcompensating for their cold reception towards Trials Remake, but there are a lot of genuine improvements over Trials Remake.I personally struggle to find an area this game regressed in, other than that there's not much meaningful permanent gameplay choices regarding character builds. This game is almost too respec friendly to the point where building feels pointless. But also Trials had the exact opposite problem where it's extremely hard to actually reverse class choice to the point where it doesn't feel like a legitimate option.But, and this is a very big but, I would argue, being too respec friendly is a much better problem to have, than being overly restrictive. Overly restrictive progression has the problem of inducing choice paralysis, and encouraging restarts from people who think they botched their progression. I think my many abandoned XCOM files showcase what perfectionism in RPG progression can do to people. However, a balance is ideal, at the end of the day, but I'd err on the side of free-form character development.

_childDocuments_.review: At first I played the demo. I thought it was stale, boring and slow, but since I played other mana games growing up and Trials of Mana, I preordered the deluxe edition from sheer nostalgia and because I'm a sucker for JRPGs. I looked at the posts about the criticisms  of the game and also thought some of them were fair reason why they dont like the game or dont want to buy it. I was regretting the preorder and wanted to cancel it because of my first statement, but after playing about 18 hrs, I'm enjoying it. The maps are huge, the combat seems a lot better and more optimized than the demo and the world is beautiful, that I started enjoying the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Will update the review when I complete the game but here are my thoughts as a big mana fan so far.This game really makes me happy, it makes me smile, it feels like a 90s SNES arpg brought to life in a 2024 arpg presentation. My biggest issue is the price point so far, the game is really Double A which I love but it is prices like a Triple A title which might make some people disappointed. It's a really cozy, really fun game that doesn't need itself to be a crazy action game or another soulslike. Another aspect is how kid friendly the game is, I grew up on the mana titles and they were kid friendly enough while still keeping some really tragic stories and this tradition seems to continuing to this day, in fact even though it's a big 3D game now the controls feel really good and I can definitely see myself giving this to my kids, this is the kind of games nostalgia is born from.Now the bad news, the studio that made this game has been shut down the day of the games release. It's a really tragic tale, one of money. We probably don't know all the details yet, but so far it seems that china was investing a lot of money into japanese games, one of the result of this investment was Visions of Mana and its studio. Now that Black Myth Wukong is a major success, chinese companies have pulled fundings from japanese games and will invest more in domestic entertainment.This might be the last mana game but I really think they went out with a bang, with a game that has more soul and passion than any Triple A you will find recently.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I had waited to buy this game. It says Square Enix on steam for the publisher and dev but this game was actually handled by NetEase with their developpers Ouka Studios. A single day after launching the game, NetEase fired most of the dev team and basically plan to shut Ouka Studios down. This is not a practice I want to reward and I wish I learned about it before getting past the refund window.This game is not bad, there's a fun combat system and the story is ok albeit a bit weird with how everyone  On hard mode it hasn't actually been challenging so far which is a bit disappointing, but what really gets to me is that every zone and town is a collectathon hellscape. They went so heavy with it that the illusion of exploration is gone for me, you just see these shiny things littering the whole place and you've got to go pick them up because a lot of them are important. This turns a small zone that would've taken you 5 minutes to get through with a couple short fights into a half hour of going into every corner of the map systematically.TLDR: Combat is fun, story is a bit weird, zones are collectathon hellscapes, hard mode isn't really hard so far, and the real NetEase are scum and killed the dev studio a day after launch.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: It's been forever since I played an expansive RPG like that I genuinely love in every aspect. The characters are charming (even the main protagonist with a sword and anime hair, which I never ever like usually), the story so far has some interesting twists and turns that I genuinely did not see coming, the combat is extremely fun and the class customisation is actually quite deep thanks to how varied each character's classes are and the ability system. I can't get enough of it and I highly recommend it.(Warning, the demo is objectively more boring than the full game in part because the team they give you has less customisation than you would have at that point in the game and the areas in the demo are some of the least interesting ones in the game, there's way better areas before and after the demo which is an unfortunate coincidence)

_childDocuments_.review: OMG!  This is by far the finest attempt out of literally hundreds I've tried to play to recreate what made Squaresoft games amazing back in the 90s.  I can completely understand why anyone under 40 feels this game is undercooked and tedious.  This game isn't for you kids.  Its for old grumpy dudes like me who used to level up their Final Fantasy 3 party while on the phone with their high school girlfriend.  Nothing I have played in the past 20 years has felt to me this much like a real 90s game.But in the modern context, it is very nice to see a Japanese Action RPG that doesn't live and die based on whether Team Ninja or Tose felt like trying this time or not.  Ouka is bargain basement company that spanked a homerun on this one as far as I'm concerned.  The scenery is wonderful.  The action is sufficient and fun without being overly stressful.  It actually brings to mind the early "Tales of" games more than anything else.
