_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game, fun game-play (even if a little simplistic), fun characters mostly.That's the only positives I have for this game. Now onto the negatives (minor spoilers at best):* Controls fight you tooth and nail to listen to you when you want to use items in battle. I've twice had issues where I cannot use items at all during the fight (bug), leading to frustrating restarts. You also have to standing perfectly still to use items in battle or else your character just stands there like an idiot. I even had a few instances where it bugged out completely and I couldn't even attack (different bug) - had to restart.* There are no auto-saves at all, so if you fail due to you know, bugs like not being able to use items in game, you damn well better have saved recently else you gotta do a bit of it over again (it does auto-save whenever you enter an area but that's it).* AI seems brain-dead STUPID when it comes to flying enemies. On several occasions, I am wondering why I am struggling against enemies I am 15 levels stronger than and its because I find my AI companions just running back and forth not doing a damn thing (everything set to be offensive battle strat).* Half the characters are pretty good, and the other half I cannot stand. Alm of Wind and Darkness can go jump off a cliff as I cannot stand them.* Exploration is nigh-meaningless as everything except the lil cactus dudes is highlighted on the map for you. This would have been nice as an end-game feature, instead of given to you immediately.* Playing on normal difficulty, the difficulty spikes are all around.* Status effects. They are all extremely debilitating and if all 3 of you get hit by something, you just gotta stand there and die. I remember some tutorial saying spam buttons to get out but it's never worked for me.* Speaking of tutorials, it throws so many at you towards the start of the game its annoying. Another tutorial says to double tap left bumper to auto-run to your next destination - that never worked for me either lol.* Collecting chests or talking to anyone is very *precise*. You basically have to stop in front of it in order to perform the action, cant just run up and press it like pretty much any other game.* Invisible walls galore. If you ain't on the path, it blocks you basically. See something that looks like you can jump on? Nope, invisible wall.* Your dog companion (to travel faster) is pretty useless. A lot of actions will kick you off him, he throws you off whenever he touched any water (even puddles) but other times he can roam water just fine. There's no consistency.* Unless you're constantly boosting, grinding seems pretty weak so you're just progressing the story - feels like a 'fake' RPG in that sense. It does get better, especially if you do all the side content.* You're extremely weak up until you get your 3rd main character to help in battles. The first boss in the game took me like 10 minutes because I did no damage. Then you go insane damage.* Story is rather predictable - it has one twist that is easily seen coming somewhat early on and the rest of the story is pretty mid. Due to the numerous frustrating issues I was having with the game, I fully tapped out of the story By Chapter 6 and after witnessing my allies doing nothing against a flying enemy *again*, I had enough and uninstalled - I wanted to finish the game but that was the final straw for me.* Several story elements make no damn sense except to progress the plot (bad guy gets away? When you're in a cave? and he can barely run? Your bird companion doesn't want to move a rock and go to the area behind it but after you move it, all good it will go with you!??? etc)* Had 2 crashes, which wouldn't be so bad if the game auto saved more often.Overall, the game is quite fun and nice to look at, but has a lot of frustrating mechanics and bugs that irritated me to death to where I cannot stomach finishing it anymore. I do not recall Trials of Mana being like this, so play that instead.

Besides that, you can find a character or team that represents YOU well. Not having multiplayer mode is a CRIME, but I guess there are game-pausing features that they'd need to figure out3 chars max, no need for dedicated healer since you can spam up to 9x healing (small to large) and 9 revive items per battle. Support role is great to have. Magic skills are limited, mostly to cause effects or change elements of your melee attacks. Melee skills are limited. If you push it, you can make a ranged/support character melee, but there are only 2-3 most viable combos (by far) that make sense to spam. - Val: main boi, required for his buffs if you spam melee and/or need elemental shield. Slower melee and can be annoying; extremely limited offense magic blasts. Best elements: Wind (BIG buffs), Light (tank and low taunt)- Careena: tsundere, flexible buff/debuffer, fills supporter slot for ANY team. Workable melee with fire element. Best elements: idk any would be good, Fire for main melee if you like.- Morley: deep voice nyan, CRIT boiiiiiiii. Best elements: Moon for 70% crit chance, grab other effects for debuff on crit; other elements are gimmicks.- Palmena: HOT ice queen, an actual queen, squishy (HP and thighs), offense-wise is purely magic skills, limited melee but cool basic combos later on (still weak combos though). Best elements: Earth according to guides, maxes her magic stat and provides dmg reduction, Water for thighs and cast speed- Julei: sarcastic shouta old hermit, dedicated healer and supporter. I don't play him cuz defensively it's cheese and excessive. Anyone can cast heal and regen, especially regen and that's enough. Great/excessive pick for support slot. Best elements: Wood (team wise revive; useful if both the other 2 chars died lmao), Light (heal, class, self revive to prevent game over, revive everyone once per battle so that's twice the out-of-jail cards(?))Classes are tied to elements. 8 classes for each of the 5 characters = 40 classes. But the downside is you can only pick 3 out of 5 characters at any time. I just wish they made 2 support slots. It is what it is. Each element has an inclination towards a role regardless of who you play.- Moon: crit, time-control (coolest effect honestly), supporting effects, maybe some HP drains I can't remember- Fire: burn, ATK boost- Water/Ice: freeze (strong), MATK boost, some cleanse, HP regen (very nice)- Wind: main char's best class, unlocked early on, due to elemental imbue and later on teamwide elemental shields/imbues and buffs upon them. Other chars get some regens and mostly aoe buffs and debuffs- Earth: somehow the magic caster's best class, can petrify maybe. Others can raise DEF- Wood: poison and summon oriented. Summons are almost one-off attacks with a variety of elements. Chars can get revive and maybe cleanse skills- Light: healing and MDEF boosts, tanking and support options, dmg spreading ultimate- Dark: silence, grouping ultimate, stat boosts on low HP, enemy buff dispels, self cleanseElemental debuffs can be applied at a 80% bonus rate, so very easy to use later on. Stat debuffs benefit the whole team (for 3 members so not that much). Stat buffs are better against single bosses, some broken dmg-immune ones don't last longs, elemental shields and imbues last long; disappear on death.Class Passives don't stay with you if you change to another class, at least until endgame as far as I know (it's an incentive to stay with a class) Class Active skills you can retain when mix and match, which I thought was the BEST regarding customization. AI teammates (and you) and hold up to 8 active skills in battle if I remember correctly; so set up wisely. The active character can also bind up to 4 skills to hotkeys; these won't be auto-cast by AI.are just stat sticks. You can change the weapon skin as long as the desired weapon isn't sold.provide options to use active skills from any classes and any character, which is nice. The downside of using other classes's skills is you are not benefiting from whatever passives that indirectly boost those skills.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a truly astonishing example of just how a bad story can ruin a beautiful and fun game.Before we begin, I am an English teacher. I completely respect that lots of people enjoy stories at face value, without intentionally considering the story's themes. If you are one of those people who will see the story as something that can ultimately be skipped in service of gameplay, my review will not be applicable to your experience.That said, I'm truly curious if the cultural divide between the United States and Japan is so deep that we don't even seek the same fundamental morals in our themes. I don't understand how someone could even successfully write this story unless their entire personality is the consequence of decades of generational trauma.This game's world is one in which the inhabitants enjoy the protection of magical forces from the Tree of Mana, but in order to do so, must make human sacrifices to that tree. The story begins with a woman being chosen as the sacrifice of her village--a woman who is not even a native of that village, who never had to be there, and who therefore owes them nothing twice over. She seems ultimately willing to do so. It is her lover who refuses to let her go, ultimately damning their entire village to destruction.So we've done two pretty disgusting things right off the freaking bat, here. Number one, we've effectively established the planet itself as the villain. The tone is clear. The monsters it summons to try and stop the pair are clear. The transformation of the girl into stone just as they are about to escape is about as clear of a "screw you" from the planet as anything can be. But, somehow, the Earth itself is not the villain. No, it's the people who would criticize those who blindly sacrifice one another for the planet. Those are the villains.And then there's problem number two. Do you know what this woman did the whole time her boyfriend was refusing to let her change her mind and help her people? She was damn-near bent over backwards so that her breasts could be the focal point of every scene as she blandly "ummed" and "uhhed" instead of taking any control of her situation.So the first woman the story introduces is freakin fridged by this world's god, and not even to inspire a hero to kill him as the villian, but instead as a gesture to ensure no one else rises up against this tradition of ritualistic suicide.Like, I'm sure this game is a real banger. Its so pretty, and it looks like the kind of game that would really restore my childhood RPG feels. But I'm not a child. I can read.Tl;dr It isn't "Dark." It's bleak, hopeless, and thematically toxic.Edit: I looked up the remainder of the plot and willingly spoiled it for myself to see if it was going to redeem itself. In my eyes, it doesn't. But I'd hate for any of you to mistake my review as a review of the first 40 minutes. I already told you I adored the gameplay, but the story was really ruining it for me. So, I spoiled the story to see if I could make it through. I cannot.Those of you who are criticizing me for making a judgement too soon, if I had in fact only played the first 40 minutes and made no other research on my own, you'd be entirely valid in your opinions. Likewise, I empathize with your frustration. You are not wrong to have felt this way about my review.However, I am also not wrong to be repulsed by the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Review: Visions of ManaRating: 8/10Visions of Mana is a captivating entry in the action RPG genre that expertly combines a beautiful, hand-painted art style with an immersive fantasy world. The game’s storyline dives into a rich lore of mystical creatures, elemental spirits, and ancient conflicts, making each quest feel like a step deeper into an enchanting saga.One of the strongest aspects of Visions of Mana is its world-building. The environments are meticulously crafted, from lush, sprawling forests to haunting ruins, each locale packed with details that make exploration a pleasure. The dynamic weather and day-night cycles also enhance the immersion, adding atmosphere to each environment and influencing gameplay in subtle ways.Combat in Visions of Mana is fluid and satisfying, balancing fast-paced action with strategic elements. The ability to summon elemental spirits offers a unique twist, allowing players to adapt their style on the fly and exploit enemy weaknesses. It’s rewarding and keeps battles fresh, though the game could benefit from slightly more diverse enemy types.Character progression is well-paced, with a customizable skill tree that lets players shape their character’s abilities to fit different playstyles. However, some players may find the grind for resources a bit repetitive, especially when it comes to crafting powerful gear.While the main storyline is compelling, the side quests are hit-or-miss. Some offer intriguing lore or unique challenges, while others feel like standard fetch quests. That said, the game's charm and emotional resonance shine through, particularly in key narrative moments and character interactions.Overall, Visions of Mana is a beautiful, engaging RPG that may not be perfect but still offers an enjoyable and memorable journey through a lush, magical world. Fans of fantasy and adventure will find plenty to love, and it’s an easy recommendation for anyone looking for a deep, atmospheric RPG experience.If you’re a fan of world-building, elemental magic, and heartfelt storytelling, Visions of Mana is well worth the adventure!

I feels like two different people wrote the script and didn't talk to each other: there's the heroes' plot and the main villain plot, and they don't really interact, so you're left with a bunch of half-explored strands that never really amount to anything. The side quests are nothing more than an afterthought, boring and unrewarding. You'll quickly learn to ignore them.Again, the game is fine. I played though the story once and I had a good time. But I don't think I'll touch this ever again.Play if you're a Mana fan. If not, play Trial of Mana, become a Mana fan, and maybe come back here if you want more.

_childDocuments_.review: As a longtime enjoyer of the Mana series going back to Secret of Mana I was really hyped for this game. That was probably my first mistake. This game has a lot of potential that I feel wasn't realized with that I've experienced so far. At this point I have completed my first playthrough of the main story on 'Hard' difficulty and unless the extra chapter has a lot of content to make up for all the hanging plot threads I can't recommend this game despite its pretty good combat. For those that played the remake Trials of Mana the combat system is almost identical with just the addition of elemental vessels/breaks which range from useful to overpowered depending on the enemies. The remake of a number of classic bosses in the new style was interesting at first but felt like they didn't make use of the fracturing weakspot mechanic or otherwise have reactive boss mechanics like they tease in the prologue.If you are looking for difficulty, as far as I can tell hard mode just makes things more bullet spongy, and with the exception of 2 minor bosses I didn't wipe a single time. I'm not a particularly good player and I didn't take the time to farm or optimize my builds/items/comp so I can't rate this game highly for challenge.What really killed the game for me in the end was the story however. While at first I thought they were going for a darker tone with the sacrifice of the souls to the Mana Tree it rapidly became clear that the story was focused almost entirely on juxtaposed love stories. Now this could have been done well if you made the 'villain's story a bit more deep to flesh out how he became the villain rather than treating the character as a one-dimensional plot device. The number of inexplicable power-ups that in the setting make 0 sense for the main enemy of this game is incredible. Some may say that its just the power of emotions taken to an extreme but when you are playing through it in-game it feels very contrived. Frankly speaking the game lacks any example of a good evil character or even a joke evil character that both of the previous games that I played had. It feels like at several points in the game that there might be the existence of a 'hand behind the curtain' type of enemy that engineered some of the tragedies that occurred within the world (like with Etaern) or even what appears to be the corruption of the main enemy however nothing actually comes of this and I'm left scratching my head and guessing I just read too much into things.In any case I feel like I'm rambling so the TLDR is:Decent combat/art/worldGood performanceWeak writingTerrible antagonistLess boss/enemy varietyMore chore content familiar to other open world style games.Low baseline challenge (extreme mode not tested yet)Again really wanted to like this game more but left feeling unsatisfied in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Visions of Mana is mid-tier ARPG comfort food. These types of games are great to boot up at the end of a long day, knowing that you won't have to put much thought into it. There are a lot of things to like about Visions of Mana. The crisp UI and gorgeous general art direction are the two things that stick out the most to me. Everything from the party interface to the crisp damage numbers looks absolutely amazing in Vision of Mana. The sound design is also absolutely fantastic. However... the character design, particularly Val's character design, is extremely odd. Look... I usually stay away from commenting on these types of things in game reviews, BUT Val is a VERY androgynous looking protagonist. We're all mostly used to this when it comes to Japanese ARPG's. They have a tendency to make their main male characters have feminine features, but Val's design really takes the cake. Everything from his Reba McEntire hair style, to the mid drift armor sets are all...uh... very interesting design choices to say the least. Why Japanese JRPG artists seemingly make all of their protagonist look like Caucasian cross dressers, I'll never know. The main reason I comment on this in general is because I really do feel like this game would sell better if the male protagonist lead didn't look like American factory women during WW2. While Val's character design doesn't ruin the game, it is absolutely a constant distraction for me. It's hard to get excited about a new class knowing that Val will almost certainty put on his best Mid-drift, chain skirt combo. Having relatable characters goes along ways, especially with mid-tier RPG's that aren't making up the difference elsewhere. The combat also is not perfect. There are definitely some things to like here, particularly the boss fights, but overall the combat feels floaty, no weight, and has some pretty extreme balance issues. I have about half the classes unlocked at this point, and the shield/spear classes for Val are EXTREMELY under-powered. There's virtually no point in using these classes when the claymore does about x3 the damage. The combo's, class builds, and ability seeds are also extremely lack luster. Besides Val's weapon enhancements, and healing spells, there really no reason to use any other ability. Fireball does about as much damage as half a single weapon swing, regardless of your stats. They only give you 2 ability seed slots (atleast so far), and it's pretty much ALWAYS better to simply use stat increase ability seeds rather than seeds that give you actual new abilities. The spells in this game are very underrepresented, don't do enough damage, and is basically far inferior to simple meele attacks in just about every scenario. It's weird to have a game called Visions of Mana, and then proceed to make magic EXTREMELY underwhelming. All in all, this is most definitely a skipable game. You won't miss much by NOT playing Visions of Mana. You have seen all of these systems done better in other JRPG/ARPG's. However, if you like a change of pace from difficult games, and you're looking for something mid-tier, but enjoyable to put on at the end of the day, Visions of Mana can fill that void.

_childDocuments_.review: There are three sections:Gameplay... Story... and Art.Gameplay:It's like Trials of Mana but weaker and glitchier. The class system is kinda bad, and while there are definitely some neat ideas, so much is kinda messed up by things. Sure, there's more variety, but the variety is also redundant, as every spell is learned by every class for a specific character, but classes are tied to elemental vessels, which only one character can equip at a time. As a result, it means having any character as a class will necessarily prevent other characters from picking certain classes. There are 8 elemental vessels and 3 party members used at any given battle, so it isn't always a problem but is very annoying.Then there's the glitches and UI issues.... dear Lord the glitches. Just FYI, this is only a spoonful of the bucket of these issues. First, and perhaps most egregious there's the Class Strikes issue. Remember jumping up and coming down with a giant magic circle as Duran in Trials of Mana? Yeah, throughout the main storyline of Visions of Mana, these attacks were used 0 times. This is because, for whatever dumb reason, this game refuses to accept controller inputs for Class Strikes. I even tried switching to a separate button, only to discover it limited what buttons could be slotted to that action to only the shoulder buttons, thus being a dumb UI problem, and switching still didn't fix it, but it did prove that the button wasn't broken and was entirely the fault of the game. However, after completing the entire game, I tried using my Keyboard, which worked. This is a basic quality control issue and there's no excuse. Movement works differently in town, the ability to swap party members doesn't exist in town, and for no good reason. This became an especially big pain in my rear in the optional pillar fights, of which a couple are in towns, thus preventing me from rearranging my party for the fights and forcing me to fast travel just to change my party, which leads us to fast travel. It was seriously easier to move about in Trials of Mana because I wouldn't be forced to go from fast travel to fast travel to fly to fast travel, which happened sometimes in Trials of Mana because fast travel has a limit by landmass. This, combined with load times and unecessarily long transitions just wasted time.Story:I don't spoil it unless it sucks. You are being warned that this indeed sucks, and this is where I go from thumbs up to thumbs down. I could forgive the glitches, not this. This game handles the serious topic of human sacrifice in a way that insults my intelligence. At first I was worried it would be crap, then felt relieved by some early turns, only to find out it was really the worst type of crap. There are significant plot holes created by later plot reveals, one significant one being that the reasoning for the prologue events are completely called into question in a functional sense, as the later reveals only complicate the issues. Then, there's the problems that both of the villains are right in their own ways. The first is just completely correct, and that's all there is to it, even if he was tricked by the villain and upset the protag with his actions. The second, and main major villain, is correct in the fact that his motivation doesn't make sense considering he already knew better from personal experience considering who his companions were in the past. His story only makes sense of the Goddess of Mana ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up. How is the Goddess of Mana not able to just finger snap undo the problem that made him use the Sword of Mana for evil? She literally pulled the same thing for the ending of one of the party members of Trials of Mana, and that was when mana was waning in the world, so it's bullcrap reasoning to assume she can't do the same in this game. This is made even more worse by the ending resolution, which depending on what you believe the MC did with that power in the final scene, either way it's bad. If he used it for a rez, then he was the only person who got a happy ending of all the others who suffered leading up to this moment, and if he did not, then he basically was cheating on his true love for his entire lifetime, having sex with his wife while dreaming of a girl in his past. The general belief from a major fan wiki is that he took the latter option. Look, just seriously, did the devs forget that Heath happened in Trials of Mana? Did they simply forget that Charlotte's story resolution could be used as a simple solution to everything? Just putting that out there. Either the Mana Goddess and multiple other characters have a few extra chromosomes, or the writers do, because this issues of this story can only be explained by stupidity.I get the feeling that there were competing ideas on how to write the story, and then the writers threw their hands up in frustration and all wrote competing lore with nobody doublechecking them. Art:The style worked before in Trials of Mana remake, but it did two things differently from Visions of Mana. First, Visions changed them to be realistically proportioned, which ruins the cartoonishess of the absurd designs. Remember the weird outfits, especially Angela's from Trials? Well, with realistic proportions, they look terrible. But then there's the second problem, which is so much worse, and that is how overly intricate they are, and not in a good way. Like, people made jokes about the belts on characters in PS2 RPGs, and I laughed at them for being overdramatic, but Visions of Mana is in full on WTF territory with outfits having random hanging bits in the dumbest places, random bracelets and bands on limbs in weird places, tassels that serve no purpose, extra layers of textures and redundant detailing, and so many more terrible ideas that they are kinda disgusting, because my brain immediately asks "why the heck would design something this terrible" and realize I am talking about Square devs. And yet, all the NPCs and their simple clothing actually looks nice in comparison, even having tons of variety, it proves that they can design well, but simply didn't for the main party. About half of the class costumes in Visions of Mana are just plain awful, and not in the simple dreamworld way that classic Mana games have.Then there's one last issue that is both an Arts issue and a Glitches/UI issue. First is how much this game drained my PC's specs. Like, I'm using a 3060, and it's consistently at or near 100% of usage when this game is playing. And that is atop it using the majority of my regular RAM. This game is not optimized, and this could be for several possible reasons, but it looks terrible at low resolution and makes my computer fans roar at high resolution. There are also glitches with it detecting my display, which resulted in me having to turn off the program several times the first time I played just to make it work. This game is built using both the Critech and Unreal engines, and I don't see why both could be necessary for it, although this one could be a misunderstanding on my part. Either way, this is too much.Still a thumbs up? No. There were too many basic mess ups in this game which should not have been mistakes. If you haven't played Trials of Mana, go play Trials of Mana, but avoid Visions. I don't expect them to make a patch that fixes it.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't.  I wish I could.  But I can't.While the class system is decently intriguing and the battle is decently enjoyable, it's just not enough of a game. It makes the world mean less when you're just led by the nose and there's hardly much else around except for optional side questing which isn't that interesting.Also, it's unfortunate.  The game wants to tell what feels like an interesting story.  But the way it tells it is disjointed and not intuitive.  You don't get enough to "feel" for each character, so when events happen concerning them, it's a popcorn fart, bereft of the emotional impact that they clearly wanted to do. But that's not the worst of it.  It's horrifically buggy.  In the very first sequence of the game, you can literally clip into the one of the buildings (out of bounds) with zero effort.  This happened on at least three occasions that I counted.The point where I quit and refused to continue: the Gamurda Mines.  The golem you control - framerate completely tanks from over 90fps down to 1 (literally) when you do the Stomp.  That's just plain unoptimized.Then, I encountered a game-breaking bug.I grabbed this photo from a walkthrough.  This statue has to be pushed into the tower to proceed.  When I went back there after the notification to do so, the statue simply isn't there.  I even rolled back to the autosave which was a ways back, still not there.This is a very tedious dungeon and an inexcusable bug.  I flat out refuse to do the dungeon all over again.

_childDocuments_.review: Visions of Mana is the first sequel in over a decade to the mana series. The old guard creators of the series came out to do this game. If you love Secret of Mana, Trials of Mana and Legends of Mana you will love this game. 1. The combat is good and you can expand and learn more combos and spells through Elemental Vessels. 2. The characters are endearing and surprisingly deep for a mana game. I will remember all of them and all of them learn a lot and develop their views. Julie is the best though!3. Class/ability options are REALLY good. You use seeds to customize your class and there are a ton of them. Seeds can change how a character is played a lot. 4. Side quest actually reward well. You get good chunks of money as well as ability elixirs, large quantities of buff and heal items.5. The scenery is gorgeous. Enchanting, majestic and epic in a whimsical fairy tale way. Something we lack in games now. Saturated colors with LARGE zones. 6. English Voice Acting is ok, better than Trials, most of the characters sound similar to their Japanese counterparts, NPCs suck though. Careena's voice is a bit off for the setting. But the Japanese is recommended, they sound more personable.  7. No woke agenda or DEI consulting group, no tentacles of Blackrock or Vangard. This is VERY apparent as males and females look traditionally pleasing and what would be expected of their sex and there is NO PRONOUNS. No self inserts, no "THE MESSAGE", no political statements, NADA. This is a classic JRPG from Japan. It's a Mana game. 8. Story. The story is the classic hero saves the world trope of most JRPG, and that's not a bad thing. The difference here is that the characters are deeper than all the other Mana games and there is more character development and morals learned. There a bit more complex to. I'm not saying it's Game of Thrones, but it is not shallow and has meaningful things to say about love, friendship, loss, hope, all things we are told is bad or unworthy in our modern day that I am glad to see again. 9. Game has New Game Plus!!!10. Finally, what I consider it's weak points. I wish the game was a bit longer, I had so much fun with it. I also wish the game was multiplayer, locally or online, as Secret of Mana, Trials of Mana (in the form of Seiken Densetsu 3) and Legends of Mana all had multiplayer. Visions of Mana not having multiplayer made me sad.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - This is a pretty game that had its narrative hooks in me before I left the starting village, but that's because I loved Trials of Mana on SNES emulators as a kid, loved Trials of Mana as a remake, and am enjoying similar gameplay, better tuned, and with 3 hours on my save, the beginnings of a variation on a classic Final Fantasy theme that was entirely unexpected, but not at all unwelcome.40 hours in: yeah, this is a great game and takes up the mantle of Mana well. I've been a Square fangirl since the beginning, and the only thing that keeps this from fully inheriting the spirit of the SNES Secret of Mana and Trials of Mana is the lack of local multiplayer. It manages to feel like a larger world than Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom despite reasonable zone boundaries to demarcate territory. Exploring the world feels fun. There's tangible rewards for every elemental you acquire on your journey, even if you like none of the classes associated with it. There's a fluid class system! No more planning runs for which abilities you want to have available at endgame! It's got a weird plot that nonetheless hangs together well, with surprises that feel natural! The localization is quite good! I couldn't be happier with the game.--I was really excited to see that this had launched, but my excitement turned to sorrow the moment the game installed. It does not run on my PC at all, even slightly. Final Fantasy 16 (DEMO) runs without a problem and yet this can't load the game engine without getting an Unreal fatal error. I really want to enjoy this game, but that's simply not possible on PC at this time because it is too unstable. Maybe despite destroying the creative team that built the game, they'll still do a stability patch?I was really hype for this new entry in the Mana series because it looked like they'd taken innovations made in modernizing Seiken Densetsu 3 into Trials of Mana and gone even further, but I have no idea, because the furthest I ever got was the second spat of dialogue between the two opening characters before the game crashed again.---EDIT: Apparently my CPU, a 14th-gen Intel i7, is trash, and I needed to tune it down four notches to make it run normally. So, uh, dunno why this game is so finicky when the FF16 demo worked just fine, but this ultimately an issue with my rig and not the game.--EDIT 2: The demo ran fine, so I repurchased the full game.The full game corrupted the demo so that it stopped running fine. WTF.-- EDIT 3: The fault here lies with the BIOS on my motherboard being needlessly obtuse to update that I missed an update from a couple weeks ago that seems to have smoothed out issues with the 14th gen Intel CPUs, so  it did ultimately run and I did ultimately purchase it again because I love this franchise.I will say that this game has the unique distinction of standing alongside Lightning Returns as "PC Games That Wouldn't Run Because My BIOS Wasn't Up To Date," which is a little weird 'cause it was just the two and not Destiny 2 or Warframe or FFXIV or FFXVI (demo) or FFIV The After Years, and I think is evocative of the type of trouble a user might run into if they aren't rigorous about keeping their hardware-to-software communication (drivers) up to date. Maybe I'm alone in this, but I would have honestly taken a minor downgrade on the graphics to be able to play this on my Switch. I haven't seen anything so far that seems different enough from the Seiken Densetsu 3 / Trials of Mana remake to warrant the decision, but it's still early, maybe there's something that might blow me away later.--Edit 4 for clarity and tl;dr

If you get this game, don't start on hard mode unless you really like those kind of challenge.There is a mechanic you unlock post game which I think should have been available somewhere mid game. I won't talk about it here but I do think it would have made the game way, way more enjoyable.I would point out some stuff I didn't like but it has been a while since I lasted played. _childDocuments_.review: A delightful and charming action rpg that throws back to simpler times in basically all respects, this feels like a SNES game with modern production values in terms of overall tone. And those production values are put to excellent use with a vivid colour palette and very eye-catching scenery.The combat is fairly straightforward but it mixes itself up with enough frequency to stave off repetition and it actually bothered to include elemental weaknesses so there's value to the party composition/skill selection aspect of the game, I say, as I violently side-eye final fantasy sixteen. Plot's a little head-empty, true to its SNES roots its also a largely what-you-see-is-what-you-get kinda deal but the characters are likeable enough in their own way to keep things chugging along.It's nice comfort food for fans of this style of game, I don't think it'll light anyone's world on fire necessarily but it's pleasant to play and look at and the simplicity of it has a charm of its own. Anyone who complains that they "don't make them like they used to" should play Visions of Mana, because it turns out they do make them like they used to.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I'll keep this fairly spoiler free.   Story plays things incredibly safe, E for everyone and every time it seems like it's going to be more mature it takes a sharp turn to get back on optimistic avenue.   Combat is frankly overly simple and takes about 20hrs to feel decent due to how heavily locked out you are from unlocks for most of the game.   Really wish the game unlocked gameplay mechanics at a faster pace because it felt really good in the post game(of which that took like 2hrs to finish) and the story would be sooo much nicer if it wasnt made to be so light and fluffy at every turn.   5/10 - Final Fantasy for people who never want to question the powers that be or experience bad things in the world.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure if this is my new favorite Of Mana game, but it's definitely close.My only downsides are:- Too many side quests (I felt pressured to do as many as possible but many were just boring busywork)- Not enough detail in facial animations for key characters- Maybe too easy when you find out a broken build (Morley with Moon Vessel and Crit % + Crit Damage buffs)But overall I thought the story, characters and world were really enjoyable. It was also a little longer than I expected, but at least it didn't try to be a 60-80 hour RPG.Easily the best combat in any Mana game so far too. I was really impressed with both how traversal felt as well as how well-built the combat mechanics/controls were.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: A good game, but with some flaws, specially for the players like me, who didn't like the "anime clichés" (my point of view only)Pros:- good action rpg- nice visuals- good performance- good length (30-50 hours, without NG+)- NG+- Somme bonus fights, with more difficulty than the main quest fightsCons:- mediocre sides quests- a lot of JRPGs clichés (edgy boy, sexy innocent lady, perfect and noble knight, cat people (beurk), etc.)
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game completely. First of all, I have to say that it is the only game that gives me peace while playing. The game never creates stress on the player even if you fight with huge bosses, on the contrary, it calms and makes you feel good. You should definitely try Visions of Mana! It has already become my favorite Mana series. The graphics of the game are very high quality. The environments in the game are magnificently designed. The characters were already extraordinary. Get this magnificent game and play it!The only negative thing I can say about Visions of Mana is that the storytelling can sometimes be too long, boring, and distracting for the player..Cheers!
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Its really good to have a  Mana game to dip into again, as and when i feel like it.  This is not amazing, there's nothing new or unique to make this game stand out over all other games in the genre.  It does what is says on the tin and that's enough for me.  If you love the Mana universe, you'll love this game.  That is all...
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a bit of middle ground. If you are looking for a good jrpg to sit down and play through, enjoy some light hearted moments some silly moments Its good, but it misses a lot of the marks towards the late game and even in the post game.The overall Story is good, its not great or amazing. Power of friendship and love win and the people that believe in us is pretty much the sum of it i feel. I might have missed the mark but that was just how i felt. Spoiler :. As i said the mid game misses a few marks even to the end game with gear, I felt the gear could have used some work cause i remember in the first Secret of Mana you would get weapons that were effective against certain enemy types do more damage but that is replaced by passive skills. I got a hammer weapon for one of the characters called "Thor's Hammer" and just boosted the phy and magic attack was kinda of hoping maybe like 5% chance to cast lvl 1 wind magic, or perma thunder sword enchant, even would have been nice to have more gear slots that could do things the abilty seeds could do. Poison Res bangle, 10% to reflect status ailments rings. Just have weapon and body armor that is your choices. The game does let you glamour your weapons but that is it. At post game when you unlock your full plot and can customize your classes a bit more was hoping you would be able to change out apperances on the class armor but no you cannot if you like one of the 8 elemental choices looks your locked into that weapon and passives no customization save for what abilites or moves you can do.Speaking of classes the way you obtain the items for job changes is...really weak its not as epic i expected it. Such key items that people talk about are pretty much common house hold items lol. Took me about 90 hours to complete the game lot of that was just going back and forth for side quests and just taking my time running through things. Never did grind mobs and even with that I was always 10+ levels ahead of bosses even in post game I was higher levels than the super bosses and had no problem beating them on Hard difficult. Final Verdict from an nobody: 7/10The music is pretty good at times, the story is alright its nothing amazing. Gameplay is fun combat is fun at the start but wish the characters had more unique move sets or more options to learn weapon combos vs abilities. Itemization just wish it was a bit more complex vs bigger numbers. Game is good for someone that likes to take their time through games and explore cause lot of good visuals. But id wait till it goes on sale maybe or see if you can get it on game pass xD.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Games like this are why Steam needs to have a 1-10 rating system instead of a simple thumbs up or thumbs down.  On a scale of 1-10 I would give this game a solid meh.  5/10 or maybe 6/10.  Not quite worthy of a thumbs up or a thumbs down.Maybe it gets better later but at this point I think I am about halfway through the game and the combat is very simple and rather dull.  The story is also simple, dull, and completely unoriginal.  I just passed what I am sure was meant to be a major story milestone and I honestly do not care one bit about what is going on.  I kind of feel like this game is aimed at young kids more than anything.On the plus side the voice acting is decent and the art style is gorgeous.  And something this game has that you don't see in games very often anymore, some very attractive looking female companions.At this point I am not sure if I will keep playing long enough to finish it but if I do I may update my review.  That or I may set it aside and try it again later.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Play as Morley, use daggers, hold triangle. The combat is very basic, and could have used more depth. Could have done with a longer story, and more of a post game. Even on the hardest difficulty, was a little too easy. I absolutely love the various references to other Mana games. While it may not the best game in the Mana series, but definitely well above average at a 7.5/10. Worth buying, maybe wait for a discount if you are on the fence.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely the prettiest of the Japan/China RPG trash factory collaborations that SE has extracted from the overworked teams.Like Trials of Mana, switch to JP voices and English subtitles. Im sorry Stephen Fu, you cant come back from Kevin, I cant unhear it. Class system is pretty neat. Abilities learned from other trees can be used on other classes but not the passive bonuses which can feel entirely useless no matter how thematic they are to the class. Once you find a crit/damage bonus passive in a class you'll honestly never switch that character out of it. (Catboy+Luna)Combat, including the story bosses are laughably easy once you get a decent party build going. The real challenges are the Nemesis monsters that can turn the tide on you really fast and just one shot a character. I would say the Greater Elemental Aeries are the real challenges but they are just fighting a timer and are more puzzle fights and frustrating than actual combat mechanics. The story is surprisingly good. Fighting a flawed tradition and forging your own fate and taking responsibility for yourself and such. I can safely say if you want to play a modern Mana game this is the one to jump straight to. It has some of the most polish of SE's non Final Fantasy nostalgia games.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: It ain't an award winning game. The story felt bland and badly written for about 1/3 of the story, didn't enjoy it at first, but it was good enough that the gameplay kept me going. After that it picked up and became a fun experience. Still they do nothing new, not the most well written, but it scratches a JRPG pretty well and loved exploring, the fights and the characters once they became more fleshed out. See this game as you would a fable/fairytale, if like me, story is an important part of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy addition to the Mana series.  Has some of the same rough edges as Trials of Mana and alike, but art direction is absolutely stunning.  Story and growth systems are kept pretty faithful to how the series operates.   I think Square has proven they can still make a Mana game that feels like a Mana game.   While that does mean some design decisions feel stuck in the past, what does work, works really well.  Hope in the next one they take more risks as i'm excited to see this series reach more people.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty good. Looks great, and is generally fun to play. But it's not the deepest experience, and doesn't really offer anything that hasn't already been done better elsewhere/by other arpgs. In fact, the main takeaway I had from the game was that it just made me want to play Tales of Arise again.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me feel things that I haven't felt since my SNES days as a child. That magical and elusive "awe" factor that seems to dissipate the older one becomes, but we never stop yearning to feel again. Visions of Mana is a very colorful, fun, charming game with a...serviceable story that hearkens back to the olden days of action RPG's, and I loved most of my 56 hours with it. With a few exceptions.First, side quests in this game are some of the the most lazy, tedious, copy/paste pile of mi krop that I have ever experienced in gaming, and I regret spending the time it took to do them all. I kept expecting better rewards, only to realize that most quests only reward you with money (I had way too much throughout most of my journey), or a few weapons that your companions/classes may or may not use, depending how you build your party. There were a few stat upgrades in there, but that hardly made it worth it. Some of you may be ok with redundancy, but for those of you who value your time, I'd advise to skip. Second, Careena is one of the most annoying characters I have ever tolerated in a game, and her fake southern accent made my soul cringe any time she opened her face hole to project noise. Such an odd, obnoxious choice. Especially given that nobody else in her village talked in that god awful atrocious accent. The rest of the game, though...*chef's kiss*. I felt like I was 10 again, locked inside my room on a rainy day, playing my Super Nintendo. It really saddens me that this studio got shut down after release, and I really hope they get picked back up and get another chance to make another Mana game. They deserve it. Just...please, for the love of the Mana Goddess, chill with the butthole side quests next time around, yeah? Quality over quantity, as they say.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say I absolutely love the game. I played Secret of Mana back in the day on my SNES and this is such a fun reminder to the series. I haven't finished it completely as of now, but I will. Playing and having fun with an intriguing story, plenty of side quests to explore the world, cut scenes when necessary, and none more than 20 minutes. The mechanics are good, lots of ways to adjust the build of each character and adjust your team without being too overwhelming. This is a great game all around, and look forward to going back into the Mana Series.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I love watching my party die and not heal each other on hard mode, whilst getting one shotted by nemesis that aren't too far from my level. Good game.OK salt aside, the game isn't actually too bad on difficulty, I would say if you are starting on hard, expect the bosses to have a ton of health, it did take me some time to get through them. It's not exactly hard to play as the mechanics are pretty forgiving, for the player at least, not the ai. The ai does struggle at holding their own in combat, from not keeping themselves safe to not casting magic and a party member that needs healing, or at least, taking a long time to do so. I wonder to myself if telling them to use items may alleviate this issue, since it doesn't involve casting times, giving the ai time to heal without putting themselves in harms way.It also has a class system, similar to Trials, which characters in the party get to keep the spells and weapon combos of, however, the main thing to consider with these classes now are stats, passives and weapon type. Find out your playstyle regarding these, experiment with different characters, you may find yourself enjoying some more than others.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who really loved Trials of Mana I have to say this game is a letdown. I haven't completed the main story yet, but I have experience a good amount of the combat. So far I really notice a lack of polish the previous game had, as combat can be really inconsistent. Some enemies you can stun-lock into oblivion, others don't get stunned at all and give no real tell for their hp chunk attacks unlike past iterations. The combat is not difficult per say, just inconsistent in a bad way. Maybe I've just outgrown the target audience.TLDR: Don't pay full price or buy Trials of Mana.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Nice call backs to older WoM games like Secret, Trials, Dawn, and Legend. It feels more like an open world in many cases, and its clear FFXIV was an inspiration. The story is original and delves into sacrifice and "the greater good" (cue "Hot Fuzz" meme). The dungeons are really interesting, and the addition of the Elemental Vessels to help you traverse them makes the platforming different from other Mana games, too. A lot of the boss designs are taken directly from other World of Mana games. Sometimes, you're looking for more original boss designs, but the fights themselves can be pretty original. I hope future World of Mana games will incorporate more original boss designs, but I can understand why they did. You might be fighting the same monster from "Trials of Mana" but it is nowhere near the same fight.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: so far Visions of Mana represents a significant evolution in the action JRPG genre, offering a unique blend of engaging combat and rich exploration.  Combat may initially seem slow and clunky, it provides players with an extensive array of options to master . This depth not only enhances game-play but also fosters a more immersive experience reminiscent of classic titles such as Dragon Quest.Moreover, the game’s story is compelling, particularly through the development of its protagonists Val and Hinna. Their relationship is a little cringey but it ultimately pans out to be interesting enough to keep you engaged .I am not that far in but so far I really must recommend it to new and olf fans of Classic JRPGS

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, three dimenisonal world that evokes the lush fairy tale environments that have come to be the signature style of the Mana series. The familiar class and elemental system is balance by novel combat and point-allocation systems. There are some compelling twists in the plot for this game, making it somewhat heavier of an entry, but it still retains every ounce of fairy tale whimsy and levity that Mana titles usually deliver in spades. Worth the time and price.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy addition to the Mana series despite the lack of charm found in prior installments. I'll keep this short and to the point, everything except for the story in this game is solid. "bUT thE SToreEe iS eVEreEeEeThING wITh JRPGs" No, not with this one. Not when the story is a flagrant ripoff of Tales of Symphonia. _childDocuments_.review: Pretty decent RPG, Although it has some flaws.The world itself is ridiculously beautiful, Some area's might be the best looking i've ever seen in gaming. Exploring the maps is pretty fun. The combat is fun, however most of the game is ridiculously easy which takes a bit of the fun out of it. I think the story is decent, however it's nothing groundbreaking and you won't be blown away. And the side-quests are super boring, you won't really miss out by not doing them.If you are purely looking for a rpg with a good and deep story, i would skip this game, however if your simply looking for a chill time, a decent fairytale, with a good looking world, it's worth checking it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: The demo really doesn't do any justice to this game and almost made me refrain from buying it, because this is without a doubt the best Mana game ever made.What i love about this game:- A lighthearted RPG, a breath of fresh air.- Characters you care for and well developped through story and side quests.- The graphics: Damn they're gorgeous, the art team did an incredible job there also i highly suggest using HDR if you can (use Windows auto HDR or even better: Special K's HDR feature)- The combat has a very good feeling and offers quite a range of styles to play with.- The world: All I can say is that Ouka has real and talented artists and derserve praise for crafting such a beautiful world, and cities.- The exploration: It's got a bit of Xenoblade DNA there with many exploration rewards in a gorgeous world, sign me up!What let me down a bit:- The music: while Kikuta, Sekito and Yamazaki compositions are quite enjoyable and fit well the universe, they're not unforgettable (like the Secret of Mana theme for instance).- The story: it's predictable and nothing groundbreaking but it's enjoyable and well written.- The PC port: While it's running ok, more settings would've been welcome, also Unreal Engine isn't known for being the most optimised engine... i recommend using Kaldaien's SpecialK to fix some stuff and get HDR.Overall it's a great game, one of the best Square Enix made lately and as always with great SE games, it's been outsourced! (RIP Ouka btw).
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Took my sweet time since owning the game from day 1 but after beating it today, i have to say that VoM is a strong JRPG and one of the best for 2024. Eveything clicked, from the graphics, combat, music, characters (Careena, my beloved:3) and story (not anything groundbreaking, but enjoyable nevertheless).Major negative was the dumb AI. It was the main reason that i was forced playing the final parts of the game from Hard at Normal difficulty, since the rest of my party were doing random stuff. It was really irritating watching them eat whole AoEs without doing anything, for example.So yeah, it was a memorable journey and i hope for more Mana games in the future, even if things look grim right now, since the development studio is no more.

_childDocuments_.review: So this is my first time leaving a review for any game, and as a huge fan of the mana series I am going to be pretty biased. So bear with me.Visions of Mana is a great game for fans like myself and people new to the series. Each mana game is self contained and so you don't need to play any of the other games to enjoy the story. The plot starts off with your protagonist setting of on a pilgrimage to escort a group of people known as Alms to go to the Mana Tree. As you might guess from the plot the game is linear, but that doesn't mean you won't do any exploring. Each area you come across is quite huge and filled with things to collect, treasures to find, optional challanges to take on, monsters and Nemesis (optional tougher monsters) to battle. Also from the get go you can double jump and air dash! The gameplay itself kinda reminds me of Kingdom Hearts, where there are some lite platforming elements and a lot of focus on fun combat. Even the Protagonist Val is so bright and cheerful like Sora.Now my only complaint about this game is for some reason the developers seem to think that players cannot  find their way out of a paper bag. So what do I mean by that? So the game will give you a map of the area... ok, that actually is helpful. You also get a mini map that you can turn on/off in settings...  ok cool, I know some people like the mini maps but I'll turn mine off. Then the game lets you know that you can summon a trail of light that will show you where to go... I mean I'll never use that but it's nice to know that it's there. Finally there is a star that is on your screen AT ALL TIMES that shows you where you have to go. Really guys? I've learned to ignore the star, but it would have been so much nicer to just be able to disable it in settings. This might be the first time I've consider making or finding a mod to add to the game to make that annoying star go away. It's not like the star was necessary in the first place because if you do try to go somewhere you are not suppose to you'll get a cutscene of the characters telling each other that that's the wrong way. Sorry rant over.That being said I still recommend this game to anyone who likes the mana games or just enjoys some fun action rpgs.

_childDocuments_.review: kareena is so funny i wish southern accents were realreally fun game, pretty landscapes,a story that, while mostly predictable, still had quite a few surprises, definitely a game for people that like to tinker with teambuildingmain downsides are the sidequests being mostly boring fetch quests and only being able to track one at a time, and fast travelling around the world being kind of limited

_childDocuments_.review: Spoilerfree review about what I liked and disliked as a long-time Seiken Densetsu (they're all great!) player.Before talking about the game I just wanted to briefly mention that I buy way too many games but I rarely buy AAA games or anything like that and I almost never buy games before release - this game was an exception in all of those ways.Starting the game felt a little bit like a way too long introduction. Chapter 1 took me around 12 hours (being the completionist that I am) while chapter 2 was down to 4 hours and chapter 3 was even shorter. The story didn't really catch me at first but after 22 hours I can safely say that it has a lot of that old "Mana" feeling while slowly introducing some unusual topics for such a game. So it seems that it gets better and better, I like how the story continues to evolve and how I actually care for the characters a little. I wann see what's next!Graphically the game is okay - while not top-notch, the art style will surely make it a classic that can be played after a decade or so. Not sure about replayability so far though. The combat is nice an satisfying and special and ultimate attacks look super cool. Changing your elemental vessel looks like Sailormoon transforming - super cool! I love it!However, I feel like the went a little overboard with the game mechanics. You can buy and sell weapons and armor - okay. Weapons are only valid per character and per that character's class. Then you can spend some points in the elemental plot which is kind of a tech tree. You can further exchange seeds, grizzly sirup and niccolo coins for more specialization. With sirup you can buy e.g. special potions that permanently upgrade your stats. Per character you can use two seeds to increase stats or learn special attacks while they're equipped. And I have so many of those seeds that I will probably never use 80% of them. Ever. Then you have you standard attack, special attacks, and elemental vessel attack and some kind of ultimate the charges up over time. But the problem is that you can just mostly ignore all of that. And I'm pretty sure I still missed something obvious. Honestly - why? Why have so much stuff and so many options? I feel so stressed that I mostly don't care about the options as it doesn't really feel like it has any impact anyway. But maybe I need more hours in this game to be the judge of that.Some final notes about performance and the Steam Deck. It plays great and it is my preferred way to play although the font is a little bit hard to read. Performance is mostly good but with a lot of foliage or water you can get insane frame drops. Cut scenes a limited to 30 fps for whatever reason. Eh.All of that being said - so far I'm super happy that I bought this and I have been playing since launch. Which - normally - I never do. It feels very much like the old parts of the series in a way while being still fresh enough to be it's own thing. So, should you buy this? If you're a fan of Secret of Mana you will probably like this as well. So go for it! And I really hope we get another one of these!

_childDocuments_.review: I took a little time after I finished the game to write this because I wanted to get my thoughts in order.  I think this is one of the better Mana games, the story is interesting and has a lot of call back to previous entries.  It had some interesting ideas that were not fleshed out.  One of the best mechanics does not unlock until the post game.  Which really only consisted of a couple of re-fights and a new boss.  I would really recommend playing this if it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolute blast of a game. If you're a fan of the Mana series this is a modern game with all of the QOL you might hope for. The combat being an rpg can reach a point where it feels trivial, but as you reach the final bosses it scales up in a way that manages to be interesting. The harder difficulties also have the "benefit" of making sure death is only a hit or two away.If you like Action RPGs this is a solid pick, and one to remember fondly.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Visions of Mana delivers a mixed experience, but there are several highlights worth noting. The story, while predictable, offers simple and enjoyable moments that don’t push boundaries but still manage to engage. It’s not groundbreaking by any means—just solid enough to keep the adventure going.The combat system, while fun, isn’t anything extraordinary. It’s serviceable and has a nice flow, but ultimately it doesn’t stand out compared to other RPGs in the genre. However, the game truly shines in its visuals. The watercolor-style graphics are breathtaking, evoking the feeling of stepping into a painting. This artistic direction is one of the strongest aspects of the game, and it left a lasting impression.Unfortunately, the same can’t be said about the music. It’s fairly unremarkable, with no memorable tracks that stick with you after playing. The score does its job, but it fades into the background without making a notable impact.One of the standout features is the Job system, which adds a layer of depth to gameplay. I do wish that all of it was accessible in the first playthrough, but it remains a fun mechanic to explore.Finally, I appreciate that Visions of Mana chose to steer clear of political messaging. Sometimes, a straightforward game is all that’s needed, and for that reason, I’d recommend this game to anyone looking for an enjoyable experience without distractions.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful game! As someone who was formed by and had Secret of Mana imprinted on himself, i really really looked forward to this game and after beating it, i can say that its very solid and worth the money.In the/a next game, the facial expressions could be a notch better and maybe more freedom again in picking every weapon like in SoM back in the day. I really love the (midair) combat and movement and lovely visuals.I hope this game finds its way under many christmas trees of both young and old gamers this year.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adore this game. Truly a quintessential Mana series game that I'm sure will stand the test of time. Here are some cons. There are some aspects of the game which felt dated to me: fixed save points and fetch/kill x number of monsters quests can really be left in the past, if you ask me. I think the character sprites could have been a bit more expressive in their facial features. I wish the game had some of the more complex systems of Legend of Mana (my favorite entry of the series) like crafting, golem building, and pet raising. New class unlocks could be disappointing if they didn't fit your playstyle: if you do sidequests between main events you can spend a long time waiting for the next power up only to find it just isn't what you're looking for. The main antagonist was a disappointment.. ... but he IS a good foil...The pros include everything else. The game is shockingly pretty, the music was great, the story was excellent (although it had me worried for a while, I think that in the end the developed themes hold up.), the combat felt fun and fluid (if a bit hectic at times), the class system was fun to engage with, the ability seed system was fun to engage with, the strategies for allies actually impacted how they played and (at least on hard) I did have to change my strategies to adapt to particular fights or regions, and the characters were fun and memorable even extending to many of the NPCs (like Fiona, who had an interesting type of quest). The villain was disappointing but thematically makes sense... . I actually loved the clear impact Legend of Mana had on the lore of this world and the many recurring characters from that game, since it was (and still is) my favorite.Long story short, I highly recommend it. I didn't love back tracking to fight level 12 monsters when I was at like 34 to fulfill some guy's need for quills... but on the whole the game was a solid experience and one that I'm sure I'll come back to in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Quick and simple review.It's a good JRPG worth your time. If you've never played a Mana game, it's not going to blow your mind, but it's fun and worth a shot. If you have played Mana games, then this game will hit you right in the nostalgia bone. It very much feels like a Mana game akin to Secret of Mana, or Trials of Mana. Fan of either or both of those games? Then this one is a must play.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Always been a fan of this franchise and I find the darker toned story a great change.  And I think the battle system has been refined to an absolutely wonderful degree.  The way the class system works is a lot better than the permanent commitments you make in older games.  You can freely swap between all the classes you know and skills you learn in one class can be used in any other class, which feels a lot like the job class system for Final Fantasy Tactics.  I will say a super awesome component of this system is locked to post game, which is unfortunate, because it really opens up what you can do, and would have been way cooler to do this in pre-post-game.Just to touch on the art style and music for a second; it's exactly what I imagined a 3d version of Secret of Mana would be.  That and I'm just a sucker for a flock of flamingos flying around a giant tree.  It just needed some whale noises to absolutely crush the nostalgia.There are some nitpicks I have though.   And I think the best way to describe it is poor illustration.  Example:  Just foiled the bad guy's plan.  He's standing not far from you.  After giving his "I'll get you next time" speech, he just casually turns around and walks away.  The main character then proclaims, "No, he got away!"... What?  No.  He's literally like 10 feet away from you and isn't even running.  You could easily catch him. There's a handful of other examples, and I feel like there could have been something done to better illustrate events as they happen.Most side quests are just "collect X monster parts" which does feel a little lazy.  What's worse, is you could have fought those monsters, bu those parts will not drop unless you have accepted the quest.  And that sucks.    I only recommend doing the side quests you are actually interested in getting the rewards for and ignore the rest.I'm a bit of a completionist, so I did endeavor to do everything.  And no kidding, some of the Greater Elemental Aeries affected my overall enjoyment of the game.  Like whoever put some of these together needs a swift one to the jaw.  It really sucks that I had such a blast the majority of the time just to stumble at the VERY end.  When it comes to post game content, I absolutely recommend messing around with the battle mechanics you unlock and doing the optional chapter and bosses.  But stay away from the Greater Aeries.But aside from the mostly boring side quests and the Greater Aeries, I am incredibly happy with the overall game.  This is the best the storied franchise has to offer and I just wish it had multiplayer like back in the SNES days.  Modders should get on that.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Several times I stopped to play the game just to go, "ya know what? this is pretty good". It's not perfect, but it could easily hit the middle of your GOTY list just for being such a solid entry. Here are some key takeaways:Definitely worth a check if you have the time and you are invested in the series. Just a solid game.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: A solid entry in the Mana series. That is, until the game starts throwing dozens of pointless side quest at you that egregiously waste your time (eff you chapter 7). If you want to enjoy all the good aspects do yourself a favor and skip 90 percent of non-mandatory quests. Usually after completing one of these quests Val will say "That was a great new experience." _childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute gem. It was my first time diving into the series since I’m all about action-packed combat, and wow, it didn’t disappoint. The story is so rich and deep, and there’s a beautiful narrative driving it forward that really pulls you in. Games like this are rare and deserve to be appreciated. Honestly, I’m straight-up jealous of anyone who gets to experience it for the first time. You're in for a wild ride!
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Visions Of Mana is a great JRPG with a beautifully designed world, fun characters and well executed Battle System. It has it's issues with basic side quests, some info-dumping in the latter stages and lip-syncing not being great for the English dub, but overall it's a fantastic entry into the Mana Series.The overall story for Visions Of Mana sees you play as Soul Guard Val, tasked with keeping the Alm Of Fire, Hinna, safe on her journey to the Mana Tree. There the alms sacrifice their souls in order to prevent the world from falling into destruction.You'll meet other characters along the way, some with stories that will pull on your heartstrings and others which will have you looking forward to skipping their cutscenes.There are a lot of cutscenes in Visions Of Mana! In fact, if you don't bother doing side quests, you'll find yourself in a cutscene simulator for many of the chapters, with the occasional boss battle to break it up.The battle system is what makes Visions Of Mana great! There are some amazing boss battles in this game with stunning effects and atmospheres. And you'll have plenty of fun tinkering with your class setups and abilities to take down the toughest end-game bosses.You have a party of three characters in battle, choosing from a possible 5. Each character can morph into another class using Elemental Vessels, giving them new abilities and battle effects.It would be nice if there was a lock-on feature similar to Kingdom Hearts to stop enemies from getting away (especially flying ones!). Definitely a fun game and worth playing if you're a JRPG fan! The music is gorgeous too and can't wait for the OST to be fully released.Check out our full review here:
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly.... I literally have nothing bad to say about this game.....But then I also have nothing good to say about this game either...I played legends of mana and trials of mana before so this is like my third entry to the game.The game itself is quite fun and light and everything what mana series usually has been. Therein lies the problem. Nothing is new for me. Just another mana game with better graphics and environment.That is about it.So I have nothing bad to say about this game. It fulfilled every perspective I had hoped for with no new thing at all for me at least. Story wise is good, light, heavy and fun. The combat I never felt clunky nor bad at all it is responsive enough for me.No bug at all mostly. Except in some places the placeholder and loading border might glitch and fall through the ground. That is just me being thorough with every corner of the map and only happened once so it is ok.All and all the classes system is somewhat unique and varied a bit form previous mana series. But then it is still not game breaking feature. So OVERALL Rating 7.5/10. That just being me trying to be as generous as possible. Some omph factor is missing to make it 9/10 or 10/10.  I dunno which factor either. Cannot pin point the missing part.It is still an enjoyable journey thru and thru. I would still recommend it. PS...>>> I prefer trials of mana over this for some reason I can't describe although this game has better aspect on world exploration, combat, graphics, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I recommend buying this. I watched noisy pixel's review and knew about the slow start.  I kept playing and despite not having collected the whole team yet I'm pretty happy with my purchase. Random thoughts:Q: If a people had to sacrifice themselves through ritual suicide for the sake of the village, what kind of story would they write?  What if they didn't have  a clear understanding of religion and the thought process behind a pilgrimage:A: This one. Comments while I was playing this game:  "Oh look, those animals are soo cute."  "No honey, those are monsters and I have to kill them.  See that cute dressed up cat, also a monster, same with that cute bucktooth rabbit.  Now let me get back to my game, I have to ensure the safety of the heroine to make sure she dies properly." "What kind of game is this?!?"

_childDocuments_.review: I can remember when Secret of Mana came out when I was a kid and this game gives me a nostalgic feeling that takes me back to that time. The game is beautiful and the combat structure with classes and various abilities add a lot of variety to the game. I haven't enjoyed a game this much is a while, it's lighthearted and fun.
