_childDocuments_.review: Great game, good visuals, good gameplay, story is nice but simple. Battle system is very simplistic in the early parts of the game but picks up once you unlock more classes.I only have one gripe: The game takes to long to open up:Once you unlock more classes the game gets way better and more fun to tinker around with builds.Also than the story picks up and has some twists.I just don't get japanese game design to limit the early game so much: only some classes unlocked, no access to all talents, no access to all characters etc. They should make everything available within 5 hours imho.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: As an adult with little time for games I find it hard to get hooked into one game for long. I don't know what it is about the Mana series of games but Trials of Mana and Visions of Mana both had my attention from start to finish. And are two of the four games I have gladly wanted to 100% all the achievements so far. I just got to the credits screen on hard and I know there's a post game to still go. Then a harder difficulty and character build changes for a new game plus. I can't wait to play it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Give this game some time to warm up. At first it seems like a generic vanilla JRPG that throws some nostalgia rabites at you from time to time, but as the story progresses and the magic of mana slowing starts to build up again, blooming dancing flowers in the sunlight, glistening water and a magical realm that gently guides you on a phantastic quest with wacky and amazing characters alike, that never gets boring are suddenly back. You really start to see a Secret of Mana 2.0 in this thing. Seiken Densetsu 3 and 4 certainly did not scratch that itch in me the way 5 does. This is truly an amazing game. If you feel a great love for Secret of Mana in your heart, this is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Game runs well, but my goodness does it drag along in the final act. This game needed to be like 5-7 hours shorter and it needed a tighter narrative towards the end. In the end it dragged on and on for me, but of course your mileage will vary. Enjoyed the game, but it started out as a 8.5 for me and later turned into a fun 7. If you like JRPG's pick it up on decent hardware, its worth. Also could be a fantastic game to pick up on a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Totally feels like a Mana game. Unbelievable beautiful art design and asthetic choice. Even the landscapes seemed to be done by people who know how lines and silhouettes are used to frame it perfectly. Example: Just stand in the first village and look to the volcano. All surroundings and lines are moving towards the volcano to make it the center of attention. All in all a lot of love went into animations and character expressions, with only here and there with some floatyness and wooden faces. The music really uses all the elements and orchestrations of the older games: high stacked woodwinds, gamelan bells and even one track with the Densetsu 2 and 3 drumming. Thats the only thing it could have more of. But the metal/rock tracks were also nice but not quite as iconic. All in all the game valued my time, teleportation system was very good, only the way quests needed teleporting back and forth was a nuissance and one of my biggest gripes.The cons are that here and there it has technical difficulties: Stuck characters, screenfreezes, but it does autosave regulary , so it is not as big of an issue. Maybe had to restart the game 2-3 times for my whole playthrough. Endgame Sidequesting is tedious checklisting, but i know there are people enjoying theese. And you can grind a lot for Postgame content , if you like to do so. Normal mode was pretty easy and a bit unbalanced (although, in a funny, positive way) , but picking fights with enemies 20 levels above the party were very fun and rewarding. Also me doing the postgame bosses underlevelt and realising that the last elemental plot upgrades make your classes 10x stronger...Other than that i enjoyed my time a lot with this game and hope it sells a lot more , because the series deserves more , and more refined entries.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I have not been excited for a JRPG for a long time until now. This game is a delight!The combat is really nice and safisfying with flashy cool moves that the characters do. You can choose between 5 characters to play with 3 in your party to fight. The combat is easy to pick up and flows well.The music is completely and utterly beautiful which you would expect from an SE published game. The music goes well with your surroundings and different areas. I found myself just sitting there enjoying the music whilst playing a lot!This is a good classic Mana game and I would definitely recommend this to Mana fans thinking of trying this game. It is a little child-like but the Mana games are like that generally.The story is great and as a typical Mana game story is meant to be. I would say the story is 25-40 hours long depending on how you play and if you want to do all the achievements like I did, that took me 71 hours!10/10 ♥♥♥
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: A great game in the Mana series.  I can describe it as a mix between the Zelda games, the Mana series (obviously) and the first Spyro the dragon. The graphics are beautiful and you feel the characters as well as the monsters are true to the styles and look from the series. On the negative side I can say that the English translation sometimes seems a bit off. Like there are words that has deliberately been chosen because they are older or far less in use today. There are many attack, abilities and elemental combos. To a point where it actually might be a bit confusing. I’m sure you can excel in the game by knowing exactly what ability to use against each different monster and what tactic to apply for every boss. But the fact of the matter is, that luckily it’s not necessary, in order to go through on normal difficulty. The world is semi open and it can at times be difficult to see what is meant to be traversed and what is merely background art.You can quite easily travel the maps on the smaller scale. None of the houses are explorable and it’s sad that they cannot be entered like they could in the previous games.Another thing I would like to see was that you could use whatever weapon the character can hold, in whatever elemental combo you’d like. Also the game has made a great deal out of you being able to take the look from one weapon and apply it to a similar weapon. But ONLY if you carry that weapon with you forever, if you sell it. You can no longer have that appearance. Also you cannot sell the starter weapon, you will have to carry that with you forever, which is adding to menu clutter, for which there is a lot. You can’t have more of the same weapon or amor in the backpack so if you just bought one from a vendor, only to find it in a chest, you will either, have to throw away the item from the chest, or leave it. Then go back to a town and sell the item on you, only to return to the chest and then claim the item once again.There are areas, usually ruins that has high level monster. DO by all means watch out for them or you will be killed in an attempt to take them down.I’m using a PS% joypad to play the game but the game will only show an XBOX joypad guide.Possible spoilers:There are MANY references to the former games. Like when you see a cutscene of Val (who in general looks a lot like Randi from Secret of Mana), at an inn, and there are 3 beds next to each other.A green outfit for Careena bears a striking resemblance to Riesz from Seiken Densetsu 3 (or Trials of Mana)A place called Luka Ruins (Secret of mana) and so on
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Looks gorgeous on the Steam Deck OLED. Text is indeed quite small in areas. I did have a couple issues with “fatal error” screens on the initial startup, but after switching to desktop mode on my Deck, starting the game there, and then heading back to gaming mode for a restart, things were fine. I’ve barely gotten started, but the story has me hooked so far. Really compelling from the jump. The art direction is stunning. I feel like I’m in a living storybook.  Gameplay feels smooth and fun. Only critique so far is that there is a lot of “stop and go” with the cutscenes so far (seems every time I complete any minor task, I’m pausing for a cutscene), but maybe this is just an issue with the beginning of the game. (Some people may like all of the cutscenes; for me, it breaks the immersion). That said, is my first Mana game, and it’s already making me eager to dive into Trials of Mana after I finish Visions!
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time fan of the Mana series I had alot of fun playing this new installment. Visions of Mana presents you with stunning visuals,  combined with a soundtrack that will be somewhat familiar to veterans of the series. The story is lighthearted and engaging enough to the end, and with an additional post game chapter and new game+ allows for replayability. The difficulty isnt particularly tough, though there is an unlockable expert difficulty for more of a challenge. Overall a solid addition inline with the secret of mana remake and trials of mana remake. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I am really conflicted about this. If you're a fan of the Mana series I'd recommend this. It's got all you'd expect: The Mana Tree, the Sword of Mana, the Elementals, Flammie. If you're new to the series then it's hard to recommend as this is a largely forgettable experience.This was the best thing about the game. The world is vibrant and colourful and continues the charm of the Mana series art style since the Secret of Mana remake. Seeing the Mana Tree made me feel giddy and this was the best realisation of Hiroo Isono's original inspiring artwork. My only criticism of the graphics is that the characters are mostly expressionless except for their eyebrows.Visions of Mana does not respect your time. With huge open world spaces the game is mostly empty. In the cities you are constantly running back and forth in wide open areas with no NPCs moving around, they're all just static. With a few exceptions you're also unable to enter buildings so it feels even more lifeless. The UI is clunky and you keep needing to skip through pointless cinematics or jumping between menus when you try and do something. New Game+ is also completely pointless. I played on Hard for the majority of the game and only did a little bit of grinding to get my level up. Unfortunately the combat isn't rewarding and just turned into some button mashing. It's either frantic or boring. It's either too easy or frustrating. Your AI controlled companions have a habit of not making themselves useful regardless of which Strategy option you give them. After every combat you need to wait 5 seconds for the XP screen to go away before you can interact with anything. This becomes annoying very quickly and again goes back to the game not respecting your time.No spoilers - the story is one of the weaker elements of the game. Like many have said before, it's as if everyone's in a cult. Coupled with the soap opera quality dialogue it's again very forgettable. While the Mana series typically has a fairy tale like quality to its story, the narrative in Visions of Mana feels flat and uninspired.This is what disappointed me the most. My favourite game of all time is Secret of Mana and the OST had some crackers and were one of the amazing things about the original game. If you're unfamiliar look up any of these: Into the Thick of It, Mystic Invasion, The Dark Star, Prophecy, Whisper and Mantra, A Bell Is Tolling, A Wish..., Fear of the Heavens, Still of the Night, Leave Time for Love, Meridian Dance.Visions of Mana has nothing that comes to close to anything that Secret of Mana had. Weirdly, even with BGM on 10 and SFX and Dialogue on 3 the BGM still feels as if it's muted. I was really excited knowing that Hiroki Kikuta was coming back but unfortunately it seems they took "background music" literally as none of the tracks are memorable.I paid good money for the game so I decided to 100% it but I can't see myself spending more time into it. I would love another Mana game but instead of an empty open world, give me a refined linear one. Visions of Mana tries to do a lot of things, instead of doing a great job of anything, it instead has done a mediocre job of everything.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game and easy to 100% my only problem with the game is that some areas have low resolution images/quality like how it was in the FF7 Remake with the door and background. It's not something that would deter me from recommending the game to anyone, although it is always something of an annoyance to see. The game was very fun none the less and I very much enjoyed the journey of the game
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: The characters feels like they are too forced when talking, the voice actors are terrible and the facial animations and lipsync are low budget or the designers are lazy. If they were made a game with only text would be far better. The OST is poor, no variety at all and not engaging to what we are used to see from SE. The true potential of the combat system is unlocked after complete the game and there is nothing to motivate you to play game +. The story is just normal.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: For what it is, Visions of Mana is pretty fun. The combat is engaging enough, and the visuals and music are all good. There's a lack of polish that becomes more apparent as you continue to play, and it feels like there's a lack of optimization as well. The difficulty curve is like a cliff that you start at the top of, with only a handful of exceptions, and there's about a trillion sidequests that have very little worthwhile reward. There's also more than a few bugs. The maps frequently show misplaced quest and sidequest markers, inputs occasionally fail to register for no apparent reason, and more than once during my playthrough I was just completely unable to jump or dash in a non-town area. If you're really interested in playing, and plan on doing all the content, it's probably worth the price, but otherwise I would suggest waiting for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Had alot of fun with this one. Story-wise, it's very SNES story telling JRPG. However, The class system was cool, the boss battles are visually stunning, the elemental effects are unexpectedly detailed and stunning and very fast paced, but can be adjusted accordingly as the game progresses: fast, slow, magic, it can be adjusted.The thing I loved the most about the game though is that fighting in this game has alot of finer details that made me want to keep fighting and enjoying all the details that were added. some monsters don't like certain elementa and react accordingly, alot of regular mobs and especially bosses have weaknesses and emote in incredible detail during attacks and give the chance to critical strike them if you know what you're doing. While the game's fighting can get repetitive, the amount of time I spent experimenting with new elements and combos kept me going and trying them out on new and old monsters. IT was a fun experience and I certainly loved toying around with this was fun as the story went alng. I recommend this for people that are a fan of RPGS and want to try a game with an elemental system that's fun to toy around with while watching all the cool special effects on play.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: This game is by no means perfect, but it's a very fun experience with a lot of cool ideas and a surprisingly good story for a mana game. I'm mostly writing this to support the devs in any way I can because I love this series no matter how much Square tries to ignore it and screw it over. If you think you might like it, don't hesitate to try it out. And pro tip, Divine Fist Careena is super broken, would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: The game is beautiful, unfortunately doesn't support 32:9 I have to mod it to get support for it.  Outside of that, this games art style, character designs, landscapes are beautiful.  The story is straight forward but good, the gameplay is the best part of the game, I'm not far enough in to really comment on it in great detail but I have 3 vessels and moved to the next continent and the fighting system is quick, polished and fun.  Its really unfortunate to hear what has happened to the studio but this game is a gem of an action RPG, I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: My personal first entry into this franchise and I'm loving it. Top two biggest draws, for me: 1) Art style is gorgeous; 2) Class system and fantasy appears, from what little exposure I've gotten so far, to be top notch. Cannot wait to delve deeper, but I'm also pacing myself knowing it's a finite game.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Did almost everything in the game, I think if I 100%'d it would have added maybe 5ish hoursIt is a 7/10 JRPG and I mean it in the best way, a modern JRPG that felt like I was playing a classic, while the story was a bit hit or miss, mostly kind of boring but with a few moments that hit, where the game really shines is the visuals, combat, and build customization/job system.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Good RPG. Enjoyable characters. My only two problems are that the English voice actors don't do it for me(and it comes with Japanese voice as an option, so it's a non-issue) and the Dark Souls 3 targeting system. You know, when you're facing an enemy within attacking range, but when you take action the target switches to some enemy offscreen and out of range.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a few design decisions away from going from average to great.Good:+ Aesthetically Pleasing+ Exploration is encouraged (treasures and gatherables)+ Able to change classes/elements on the fly+ Combat is mechanically simple and funBad:- Lot of backtracking (new abilities, story reasons, sidequests)- Sidequests are poorly implemented. Lots of sidequests just give gold for reward and are usually fetch quests. Later on, some sidequests also unlock earlier than they should (level wise)- Character designs are a downgrade from Trials. Careena is too short. Morley is too furry. Lyza and Hinna, with arguably the best designs in the game are not playable- Ending (and lack of alternative/true ending) leaves a poor tasteRating:3/5 Dial soap bars
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Better than Genshin Impact.  Market nowadays revolve f2p mobile game and marketing so this game is very underrated.  It doesn't help that Demo let you access only early game part which isn't fun yet.  The game become better as progress will let you unlock skills and tactics just like any classic J-RPG.Best of the Mana series so far. The class system give it nice replayable value too.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Y'all ever experience  that you just can't put down, even though you know you should go to bed -- doesn't matter the genre, we all have at least one we're thinking of now -- but y'all ever stay up way too late reading that book? Get attached to the characters? Y'ever fall asleep on top of that book and wake up with creases on your face from the pages?"Visions" is that book for me, and I don't regret any game-play, lost sleep, or key imprints on my face, it's been worth it all to experience this story.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Being a mana fan, I think this is a good direction to revive the mana series.  Many things were modeled off Trials remake since that one was well received.  I would say in general Visions had deeper class system, much greater combat customization, and a longer story.However, some parts of the story make little sense.  And for combat, while is mostly an improvement from Trials, some controls and mechanics are still lacking, including ease of switching characters (characters don't register right after revived), ring command being ignored, etc.Overall, I think it's still a great game and I had a blast playing through the entire thing.  It's not perfect, but it's a good enough game that can represent the new direction of mana series and should be able to appeal to a greater audience.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most delightful games of the year and it's a shame that the developers were closed down days after the game's release. This is a Mana game for anyone who stayed up until 3am chomping on pizza and gurgling Mountain Dew in the 90's playing Secret of Mana on SNES. The story is lighthearted to start, but the weight of what the cast is actually doing comes into light as the story progresses and it really grabs you. Me, at least. They've perfectly nailed the updated look and feel and the traversal alone is as addicting as the combat. The game may be slow to start, but stick with it and the drip feed of features and traversal, majesty and combat variety, along with a maturing story along with the character arcs really meshes well into something special. It could use some QOL improvements like to the fast travel system, sure, but the scenery is so beautiful, the music entrancing enough to get stuck in your head, and the combat so punchy, fast and fun that I don't care. Everyone has their preference, but the reviewers who ragged on this game are not who it's for. It's for the folks who would rent Dragon Quest (Warrior) from their local video store every weekend until they beat it. The ones who would go over to their friends' house to co-op Secret of Mana and do just one more town or dungeon. This is a Mana game, and they nailed it. Really a shame it won't hit the levels it should because it really deserves it.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Underrated JRPG being overshadowed by the big titles. If you're a fan of classic JRPGs, or just good games in general try the game out. The world is very vibrant and colorful, and the combat is good with an actual job system. It's also a great game to wind down with after a stressful day, it's quite cozy.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I have not played the earlier version of this game, but this game is very good in its telling.  Has very good story with interactions for all characters which brings the game to life.  As I have not yet finished the game I cannot give a full review, but this game is very very cute and something worth giving a try if you like RPGs.  Combat system is very good with having a minimal level of difficulty, but you are able to persevere.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first Mana game and I've only played until chapter 3 so far but I'm planning to play until the end of the story. The prologue pretty much sets the tone for the rest of the game. There is a dark tone lying underneath the happy-go-lucky vibes of the game. But other than that, it's typical JRPG stuff with decent voice acting for the Japanese version. The graphics and environment are breathtaking, and sometimes I would just stop for a few minutes just to admire the creative details of each location. The color palette reminds me of Genshin in a lot of ways.The action combat is good enough, but I wish it was more similar to Tales of Arise where your characters can follow up attacks seamlessly rather than just button mashing all the skills that you can throw at the enemy.  There doesn't seem to be any i-frames for dodging too, it's just a dash to distance yourself from the enemy.As you progress through the story, you get to unlock more abilities and get tons of classes to choose for each character as well. Hard mode can definitely be adjusted a little bit. It was rough starting the game on hard mode as the enemies just seem like HP sponge, but it starts to get a bit easier once you get more party members and unlock more things. The equipment system isn't really interesting, you just get increased stats and throw away the lower level gear. It seems like they've put most of their effort into the classes, the passives and the abilities.Another interesting design choice is that they show you all the unlockable chests on the map, so you don't have to look at every nook and corner, helping you save up time. This might not be to everyone's taste, but it's good for casual players that just want to get to the story rather than waste too much time exploring and trying to find every single treasure on the map.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most lovely, enjoyable RPGs I've played in ages.  There are a few performance hiccups and bugs here and there, but none are enough to mar the experience.  It has a solid class system, though it takes some time for the character customization to really open up.  The combat is enjoyable, with Hard mode being a fair challenge.  The story is bittersweet, and ultimately hopeful, and is wonderfully told, though the characters' facial acting leaves something to be desired.  Much storytelling is done through the countless NPCs, so be sure to talk to them for a fuller picture of the world.As a Mana fan, it's a 9/10. Visions will probably go down as one of my favorite RPGs of the generation, and is a model of what team-based action RPGs should be.  Here's praying it is expanded and improved upon in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: "Vision of Mana" is an outstanding RPG that masterfully crafts a deeply immersive and atmospheric game world. From the very first moments, you’re drawn into its meticulously designed environments that feel alive and full of detail. The developers have done an exceptional job in creating a world that is not only visually appealing but also consistent in its tone and mood, which enhances the sense of immersion.The story is another highlight of the game. It unfolds gradually, allowing players to become fully invested in the characters and the world around them. The narrative is rich with unexpected plot twists that keep you constantly on your toes, making you eager to see what comes next. Every twist adds a new layer of complexity, ensuring that the story never feels predictable.One of the game's strongest features is its fluid controls. Movement and combat are intuitive and responsive, making exploration and battles feel smooth and enjoyable. The combat system is dynamic, offering a satisfying blend of strategy and action.The side quests in "Vision of Mana" are far from filler content. Each one is carefully crafted, with interesting characters and stories that add depth to the game world. They offer meaningful rewards and further enrich the overall experience, making the world feel even more alive. All of these elements come together to create a game that is truly captivating from start to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first Mana game. Despite its flaws, it has an endearing charm to it.Not anything groundbreaking, but for what it is, it is a good game for me. I enjoyed it through and through.8/10It's a shame that the studio responsible for this was shut down even just after the game's release. This was a good game, but unfortunately, the timing of Visions of Mana's release, plus the kinda niche-like appeal of this game via its marketing, didn't quite catch on to the general audience, but I'm sure games like these will live on well into the future, making it a hidden gem.I'm glad I got to experience the story of Val, Hinna, and the Alms. Careena is a force to be reckoned with. Her Southern accent grows on you as you go along the journey. Trust me. She's a treat!
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: A modern classic from the jump. Even if you didn't grow up on the Mana series, there is a familiarity to modern open world games ala Genshin and Kingdom Hearts that makes this an easy pick up. The amount of love and care put into the game shines from every corner. From the characters, the world and music it all has a warm JRPG hug feeling that reminds me of the earlier days of gaming with wonder and whimsey. I hope this game gets the recognition it deserves.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: After 40 hours I've completed the game and its post game but not 100%. With all this time invested into the game I definitely say give it a try if you like action combat (vaguely like genshin impact as a quick reference). Long and short is the game can be a bit woobly with the story and exploration but makes up for it with great character interactions and combat.So time for The Good! The combat feels great, I love most of the weapon types, classes, spells, and elemental vessels in combat. It feels like there are a lot of ways to approach fights and feel valid (on normal difficulty at least)! The bosses are exciting and the Mana series iconography is here in full force. Personally I got a giggle from the nemesis monsters, powered up versions of normal enemies. It made me think of when that was done in mainline Final Fantasy. Being able to put cosmetic glamours over your weapons is great too, I wish it was as plentiful with the class outfits but maybe in an update? When it comes to the story I enjoyed it a lot. It was overall a sweet adventure, but not perfect. Still the characters are great in this game they all feel lively and full of personality, the way they all bounce off each other can be hilarious. It does really feel like there was love put into this game by the people who made it.These are things I felt mixed. Exploration is a lot of fun, the maps are wonderfully designed! I love running around the world but it felt lacking in particular aspects. Some collectibles just take up space until late game (grizzly syrups) or they stop feeling good to collect (gold clovers). That and a lot of the elemental vessels are under utilized or just not very exciting to use in field exploration. Then the story itself. So the story is about a merry band going on a trip around the world. Why? Because they need to sacrifice themselves to preserve the world. The tone can be a bit off putting at first because no one really seems bothered by it, but I can say it 100% gets better later on as more plots points illuminate the world.Finally the things I disliked. I can't honestly thing of anything major I hated! There are a lot of little cuts that keep this game from being a 10/10 experience though. There is a delay when using items in combat, the npc allies can be dumb as bricks sometimes, fast travel being locked to continents, the cutscenes playing every time you hop on your boat or flying mount. There is the poor organization of seeds making it a pain to try and load out my characters. It bugs how side quests are bland stock MMO 'kill five X' kind of running around and most of them have lame rewards. Not to mention every few plot points the towns will trickle feed more tedious side quests. There was a kind of puzzle boss in the game where the camera broke for me and I couldn't see the answers I was picking! I think you get the idea, there are a thousand little cuts in this game that sucked.Overall though I loved playing this game, it was nice to run around and beat up monsters. The characters were a treat and the world is such a nice colorful place.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: If you crave the typical jrpg experience this game gives it to you.While not without minor issues I really enjoyed the game so much so that at times I couldn't stop playing, which is always a great sign.The story is what you would expect from a jrpg and it did not disappoint.The combat is a bit stiff at first but after you get into it and unlock some stuff it's really nice.The best feature of this game by far is the class system it had me mix and match different classes though I almost always had the 3 characters I liked the most as my team.(Ability-Seeds = equip able abilities and stat modifiers such as spells, atk up or crit rate up)Where I would have wished more organization is the U.I. for the most part it is fine but trying to change ability seeds for a character can be a real bother, finding them checking if another character already has them equipped etc.For some challenges you have to switch characters and so also switch ability seeds so you had to sit there for 10 minutes searching for and equipping them. This also made me even less inclined to change the 3 characters I set for my team the whole time because every time you switch you have some ability seeds that you always need to change.To the next point most ability seeds feel utterly useless. While some spell ability seeds are nice to have in the beginning, I quickly found myself just equipping stat increases because everything else was really underwhelming. Most challenges gave Abilities seeds that where in some way conditional so I never really used them.I would have liked to have a cleaner and better way to track side quests as well. Having only one side quest icon shown on the map can be annoying. I would have also liked some kind of tree view with a grouping from where these side quests are from or some other kind of grouping. Because it is extremely easy in the later stages of the game to lose track of where these side quests are even meant to take place.In the end these are, for me at least, mostly minor issues with the game that would have made it more convenient but the core gameplay is still really good I would recommend everyone that likes jrpgs to try this game out.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game and the definitive "Mana" series experience.What I like:* Art style, especially the environment of 35+ unique maps which are breath-taking beautiful* Even though this is a linear game, some maps are open enough to feel like open world exploration* Combat, at least specific classes, are fluid. Abilities are fun to use, also have "caster" classes* Optional challenges with good rewards that scales with your level (so you can grind to cheese them)* Somewhat traditional JRPG story, which I liked and all party members have decent character developments* Character (power) customization offers many optionsWhat I don't like:* character (appearance) design. Let's just say it's trying to be faithful to the mana series original 2D sprite and the result is an aquired taste* clunky fast travel - you are only free to travel within the same map. Traveling to a different map requires an additional action + loading screen. Traveling to a different continent requires even more loading screens and a partially unskippable cutscene* there are some amazing character power growth and customization options that are only available in post game, which is not very long -> should have been there earlier so I can have more time to play with them* a minor combat bug where the character I control cannot use items - selecting item has no effect, usually happens after my main died and I was forcefully switched to another characterOverall, these cons are not enough to hamper my enjoyment of the game and I would give it 7/10 (would have been a 9/10 if it has Tales of Arise's style of characters)
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best looking JRPGs out there. I enjoy the characters, the story, the worldbuilding, its encyclopedia and I recommend using the No Transparency Camera Mod (when you unlock Palamena you'll know why). A game made with passion by talented developers that deserve more praise that I can lay down in these few sentences. I was sad to find out that Ouka Studios was closed by NetEase, but maybe this is not the end of the Mana series as we know it and I hope that the hardworking people that made this amazing game will become part of a new studio that will gift us an even better game than Visions of Mana. In the end I want to say that this is definetly my 2024 Game of the Year, and the year is not even over yet as of this review's date.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: - Everything has beautiful art and is wonderfully animated.- The environments are visually stunning and have a unique feel in each zone.- Combat is fast paced, but gives you the option to pause to case spells, use items, or even program the behavior of your companions.- There are a ton of classes to choose from for each character, and you can customize your abilities further using seeds.- There are also four difficulty settings, normal being approachable and fun.Long story short, you get to play how you want, the way you want, any enjoy a well written story with tons of nods to the classic games in the Mana franchise. I love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, but unfortunately, it falls short in several areas. The story feels lackluster and contrived, with an "idiot plot" where the villains are actually in the right, and the character growth is superficial at best.While the gameplay is enjoyable at times, the quasi-open world feels empty and lifeless, filled with tedious busywork and repetitive side quests that amount to little more than "kill that" or fetch quests.As a longtime fan of the Mana series, it pains me to say that Visions of Mana misses the mark. If you're looking for a great Mana game, I'd recommend checking out Trials of Mana instead - while it may be a bit older, it's a fantastic remake of a classic game that never made it to the West.If you're still curious about Visions of Mana, I'd suggest waiting for a significant discount before picking it up.It's also worth noting that the studio behind the game was shut down immediately after release, before sales numbers were even collected. This seems highly suspicious and suggests that the company may have planned to end the studio from the start.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cosy little JRPG with and interesting story, likeable characters and a servicable combat system.The game gives you ample opportinities to customize your playstyle.It's no "Tales" game, but it had the potential to eventually get there.Sadly, now it will never get there, as the studio was closed before the game even released.My 2 main gripes with the game:1. You can't switch party members in combat, so 2 characters are completely wasted2. The AI is as dumb as a box of rocks, and there's no solution to improve it
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Combat can be enjoyable after unlocking a lot of the skills classes, visuals and music are good, although personally i don't like the design of some characters.Customization of the combat is very good, every characters has 8 classes, so between classes skills, passives and the ones we find in exploration or just progression of the game there are alot of options.Unfortunately the story kinda sucks, it starts good and the characters are likeable,  around the 15h i was intrigued by it,  had a lot of potential for a really good story, but it went into generic jrpg tropes, the main villain sucks, is a villain without a good reason, the main theme is not even properly addressed in the final chapters, pacing is terrible, it should be 2 to 3 chapters shorter (last chapter is a boss rush, but the bosses are just early game bosses but stronger)The game had some technical problems later on with frame rate dropping to half in some zones/battles.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: This game is 100% worth playing, especially if you like ARPGs and/or the Mana series and liked the recent remake. I hope the folks who built this get opportunities to follow up and further improve upon their ideas.Positives* Good music that fits the mood and isn't boring. Mana series standard.* All of the bosses were fun, I thought, and the boss rushes you face towards the end are enjoyable too.* The plot, while a bit basic, had a few interesting twists and surprises in it.So-so* Game could be longer. It doesn't outstay its welcome though, so that's good too?* Game is extremely cheery even when bad/sad/horrifying situations happen in the plot. This seems common in Mana series but even more noticeable here. I think other reviews have noted it. Bittersweet isn't a bad combination, it's just the characters cannot possibly be more "sugar sweet" in their presentation/niceness and it's kind of jarring when combined with a deeper plot.* Other than the Frozen status effect on a certain enemy or two mucking things up, it's possible to get some really broken builds with very high DPS, instant kills, and elemental vessels usage that make the combat a cakewalk towards the end of the game. I can bet what speedrunner builds will look like already. You can opt out of this though if you want more of a challenge.Negatives* Side quests were mostly boring and would have been better off with at least half of them cut. There's a few nice ones mixed in but there's basically two categories: fetch quests (sometimes chained back-to-back) and defeat a group of enemies. If the fetch quest chain is long, sometimes the reward is worthwhile, but not always. When the group of enemies includes a nemesis, it's fun and worthwhile and usually the reward is decent. But the rest were completely boring padding. Defeat N of an enemy type is especially bothersome since you have to wander the area for specific enemy groups. Certain areas are cool the first time, and annoying to navigate a second or third time just to kill a few monsters for a side quest.*  seems they adjusted this with a patch. Null Freeze probably still best status effect defense other than null silence on casters, but not as required.* The timed aerie challenges were interesting but I thought the multi-wave 20sec ones were a bit too tight for my liking. You need very specific builds to DPS sufficiently and sometimes you have to retry multiple times anyway because of derpy allies, such as knocking away one enemy in the wave to the opposite side of the arena.* While I didn't encounter any major glitches, there were two notable oddities: 1) autosave doesn't happen frequently enough to avoid losing progress on the one crash/fatal error I saw during gameplay or getting surprise KOed by an enemy with a stunlock once or twice. 2) requesting item uses is strange; it's sometimes looks like it queues the request and your ally (or your own character) doesn't use the item until you repeatedly issue the command. In tougher/more hectic fights this was annoying, but there were only a few of these in the game, mostly optional battles.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: a GLORIOUS return for the mana series!This game does so much right, beautiful visuals, great music and fun combat! Shorter than most JRPGs with TONS of side quests. Visions of mana constantly stunned me with its twisting story beats mixed with peaceful and fun momentsI do have a few complaints, the ending was kind of a flop, it just kind of fizzled around the 2/3rds mark and never really recovered, i felt like i had seen everything and while it was pretty to look at i had already seen it before. the english dub lip syncing kinda sucked too and Careena has a funny accent for some reason. Not a perfect game, but id give it like a 7/10! well done! I really hope we see more mana games!
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty near exactly what I was wanting from a new Mana game.  Side quests could use some work and the combat could get some more depth, it's a good start to a return.  Rather a shame that NetEase shut down Ouka, I'd have loved to see what they would have done if they got a couple more games under their belt.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: really enjoying the game. the graphics are bright and the story so far is very classic rpg, which im into.great sound and music, voice acting is peppy and not a fan other southern accent on one of your main chars....but it not horrible. odd no one else in her village has one though. anyhow. if you like the setting of mana games in the past its worth playing this.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really very good. You get precisely what you see. A fantasy adventure that resembles a fairy tale, complete with lovely artwork and amazing soundtrack.Although the cast of characters isn't my favorite from the MANA series, the story is intriguing, and it looks, sounds, and plays fantastically. You essentially control the pace of the game, so if you're not into exploring the large maps with lots of minor things to find, you can just go straight to the main story. The combat begins really basic and gradually expands with more and more features.It's a shame that the studio was shut down right after the release of this great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. Im an avid JRPG players and this game is visually beautiful and the combat is alot of fun and its definitely not hard to understand. Mos JRPG's you have to spend time upgrading weapons to make them stronger however in this game you just get better weapons and equip them as you progress without the headache of having to upgrade things. Same goes for the armor. Highly Recommend this
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Very much enjoying Visions of Mana it's initial beauty grabs you and pulls you into it's world full of rich characters and settings to explore. I enjoy the combat it's familiar territory for the series with it's action combat and ring system with a few great additions. I'm giving Visions of Mana two thumbs up cheers!
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent return and improvement on things previous games in the series did. One of the most beautiful games I've ever played, and overall a game that RPG fans should play! Don't let the demo shape your opinion on this one. I hated the demo and then when I decided to just give it a shot anyway I was pleasantly surprised with how much better the pacing and overall gameplay felt rather than throwing you into a bad spot and having you be flooded with tutorials. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Gonna start this up by saying this is a great game, there's a few minor problems i have and some suggestions that could have made it better but overall i enjoyed my time playing. The Controls are responsive, the gameplay feels great, the story is a little generic but told very well, if you're into action rpgs from the ps2/ps3 era, you can buy this game no questions asked and have a blast. It's a shame the studio behind this game is basically done for give they delivered what i would consider one of the better games that came out this year.Now to go a bit more indepth. First the Visuals:Most of this game looks fantastic, its a gorgous stylized artstyle that will hold up for times to come, however i do feel they could have done a bit better on the actual character models. You notice some texture smudge when they close their eyes and they don't really emote too well so i think this part could have used a bit more love for the final product. There is also some parts like geopgrahpy just kinda floating in midair if you look closely and the lava texture in the volcano looks like it could have come from an actual ps2 game if you look at it upclose, but those things aren't too obvious if you don't specifically look for it.Gameplaywise i think this is a very solid action game and natural progression of the mana series, you have your basic attacks, heavy attacks, can cast spells and like in trials of mana remake you can use a supermove once your special bar is filled. Every character has 3 weapon types and with gains a new class you can freely switch to when you gain a new Elemental Vessel, so 8 classes per character. These are not balanced all that equally, since some classes get better benefits then others but each elemental vessel also gives you a coresponding special move to use, like the wind vessel letting you throw boomerangs that throw targets in the air, the moon vessel creating a bubble which slows enemies and the fire vessel giving you a homing uppercut which sort of works like a stinger and instantly refills if you kill an enemy with it, just to name a few. Personally i think the game would've been even better if they would A. let everyone use the same vessel if you want, therefore not limiting your teams class combinations so much, and B. if they had let you actively switch between classes in combat, sorta like style switching in devil may cry. Maybe limiting it to 3 or 4 classes you can switch between during combat and not all 8 since that might be a bit much but it would have definetly elevated the gameplay even further in my opinion.The Story as mentioned before is somewhat generic fantasy, tho i definetly wouldn't say it's bad. It is told very well with good pacing, great writing and satisfying story moments. You do get some clichees like "the evil politician character who wants to seize power" but those do not detract from the overall story/storytelling. In fact i welcome this storytelling over the endless amount games nowadays that try and shove political messages down your throat.I do have some other minor issues like for example:-Sidequests requiring you to collect an item by defeating a  monster, but said item only dropping after you accept the sidequests, so there's some unneccesarry backtracking which inflates gameplay time if you're going for side quests. But given these items are guaranteed drops once you do accept the sidequest its not all that awful. I just think this could have been handled better by letting these items drop at random from the start and having them otherwise be used to craft/trade for ability seeds. Eitherway you don't have to the sidequests but some of them do give great rewards so you shouldn't entirely skip on them either.-Leveling i think could have been made a bit more meaningful other then stat increase, by maybe having milestones every 10 levels or some that unlock more elemental plot or ability seed slots instead of those being relegated to items.-This is more of a suggestion but if this game had come with multiplayer similar to older games like Secret of Mana and Seiken Densetsu 3 this could have easily become a must buy in my opinion, especially with online multiplayer, since i think we rarely get any story based rpgs with pve multiplayer. It's either full on focus on multiplayer with next to no Story or Story focused but singleplayer only.TL;DR, This game is a very solid 8/10, very reminiscent of older Square Titles with a (mostly) beautiful asethetic and somewhat modernized take on the Mana-Series Gameplay. I very much recommend it, Especially if you can grab it on sale but even if not i't worth it, given i've put almost 40 Hours into this game at this point and havent even done all the postgame stuff yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nostalgic game that hits a bunch of Secret of Mana staples in a pleasant low-impact way.It may not be worth full price, and Trails of Mana is likely the better introductory game into the series (also available on steam), but it's a solid "Good enough" game made by people who clearly cared about the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks great, but the gameplay is stale, the story isn't very interesting, and there's zero incentive to explore the world.It seems like most of the budget went into the world art, but despite that, the world feels incredibly empty. It's as if they made an open-world game just for the sake of calling it open-world.I'm surprised most people gave this game a positive review. It feels like they completed the world first and then rushed to develop everything else around it just to finish and ship it out.I forced myself to keep playing, but it doesn't get any better. When I checked the story-related achievements, I noticed that only 3.3% of players have unlocked one that you earn about a fifth of the way through. And I'm not even that far into the game yet. Considering the game is about 29 hours long, this suggests that people either bought it just for the name or stopped playing altogether after an hour or two.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: This is a solid game, with lots of nostalgia since The Secret of Mana was one of my favorite game when I was a kid. Fun combat, great graphics, cute and cozy aesthetic. However, I just learned that the studio that produced this game just got shut down. Skill-Up talks about it in this weeks roundup of gaming new. This is heartbreaking....
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I love the class system in this game. Like a lot. It is so much fun unlocking the classes and trying them out.But the progression system in unlocking different aspects of the class do not flow well with the overarching progression of the game.it is so strange to me that for most the game, you will have few classes, but then suddenly unlock all the rest at one point.Or even more strange is that you will beat the game at only unlocking 3/4 of each class's strength.Something really cool does happen when you max out a class, but you can't even do that until you beat the game. So what little content is left to do with that really cool mechanic. Also, I beat the entire game playing nightblade and spamming special attack.The combat really isn't deep.The story is basic at best.But for a game, I did have a good time
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: It's ok. I'm not sure who it's for though... The writing is childish (and excruciatingly bad), and the setting and characters are cute, but it seems like the many of the outfits are geared towards adults. The topic is also very dark, but played off as light.... making it even more dark. The story seems to be the main focus. There are TONS of long cut scenes. You'd think they'd make the writing better if that's most of what you're getting.Another complaint is the exploration... which they spoiled with thousands of little pick-ups all over the place that become the focus of your attention rather than the beautiful setting. They don't actually contain anything that valuable, just items and bits of money that you kinda actually need, so you have to make it a point to get them.So far, I want to burn the Mana Tree to the ground and dance on the ashes. Am I supposed to feel that way?! Who made the Mana Tree the villain in this series?Anyway, the nostalgia play is good. The music quotes a lot of famous game music from the Secret of Mana era, so maybe that's the audience? Anyway, it checks enough boxes to get a thumbs-up, but buy it on sale. ...and leave your sanity at the door or you will want to punch everyone in the entire story.Music, amazing.Battle, excellent.Exploration, good.Story, grade school.Writing, kindergarten.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy the visuals and art direction of this mana entry. The action combat is definitely serviceable, and I have not had any issues with performance during my playthrough. I have enjoyed all the characters so far (I'm missing one, I believe), and I think they all play sufficiently different. Overall, I think this is a great title, and I'm saddened by the closure of Ouka Studios following the release of this game. I can tell that a lot of passion and talent went into creating it.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Im really enjoying this game, after 10 hours I can safely say this is really comfort food for people that loves JRPGs! The visuals are among the best I have seen, the developers pushed Unreal engine 4 to its utmost limit!The pacing is good, solid plot with convicing characthers motives and beliefs. Soundtrack is lovely and relaxing. The gameplay is fantastics and Im sure it will only get better from where I am. Would rate it 9/10 for now!
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: It is exactly what I like in a game. Lots of areas to explore. Different maps and terrains. Good graphics. Full voices - not just talking for one sentence and you have to read later. Interesting battle system which is hack and slash so it doesn't get boring. I absolutely love it and it reignited by love for Squaresoft games back when I was a teenager.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the plot of this game up until the end of chapter 5. They were doing a lot with the premise of a society which has ritualistic martyrs. But, at that point they change the plot to be a much more generic fantasy story and barely touch on the interesting premise after that. You spend most of your time fighting elemental bosses and a big bad who has only one personality trait by the end. There were a few more interesting villains earlier in the game that I wish had become the final boss instead. I'm just a bit disappointed that it didn't live up to my expectations, but it's still a very nice fantasy story. The highlight is that the playable characters remain excellent throughout. Even with the story becoming a bit rote I still enjoyed spending time with them. Part of this is due to extremely strong voice acting and excellent facial animations. You can really tell the difference when you do a side quest and it's not voice acted any longer. The music and sound is also good. The graphics are beautiful and each area is a distinct riff on the elemental which governs it - such creativity put into this idea!The areas you explore are a bit too large for my liking but they do give you a lot to do, from treasure chests to sparkling items to pick up off the ground, to a new type of currency. There are also side quests. Lots of fluff to extend the playtime. I don't love that concept but it's also not required to participate in all the side stuff, you can just barrel down towards the main plot and just turn down the difficulty or use a lot of XP increasing items.The combat is a bit too button mashy for my liking and it only gets more so as the game goes along. There is some strategy with dodging and elemental weaknesses but overall it wore out its welcome by the end of the game. There's a post game chapter where you can fight even more and I decided not to do that.So come for the plot, characters and the beautiful scenery. The second half isn't as strong as the first but it's still well worth your time regardless.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: While it's too early in the game for me to comment on the story, I just wanted to say that the game has been charming and delightful so far. The world is colorful and vibrant, and it reminds me a lot of Xenoblade's worlds (not quite as sprawling, but great to explore). The gameplay is highly reminiscent of Trials of Mana, or what I figure is probably standard ARPG fare these days, but it's fun and easy to get into - I've been playing on Hard and it's been a decent challenge. I'm enjoying what I've experienced of the class-based system, and am excited to see more of what it unlocks. The game has clearly been inspired by earlier titles in the series, and has had enjoyable references and nods to the previous games.Honestly, at this point I can't see the game severely disappointing me or changing my overall opinion, so I wanted to drop this preliminary thumbs up because I think it's shaping up to be a great entry in the Mana series (which has been getting quite the revival between Trials and this title).
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Exactly what we needed.  Beautiful looking, great story, nastalgic, easy to control, great upgrades. In a mess of AAA games and soulslike types, this is like a breath of fresh air for a gamer like me. Reminds me of a time of playing Secret of Mana on my Nintendo, staying up late taking with the g'f on the phone while wishing I didnt have school the next day. The music is very reminse of old school RPG games, same as the story. It is a bit early to make a review but I am really enjoying it. As far as the bad, well no real bad for me as it has been everything I expected, but The price is steep, some may not like the cartoon graphics, or simple nature of some quests. But again for me this is exactly what I have been waiting for. A great old school RPG that is new lol.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Between this and the Trials of Mana remake, people really need to pay more attention to this series.Visions of Mana is exactly what I was hoping for with a new entry, still being a somewhat simple action RPG but building out the zone exploration and job system.I highly recommend this game, certainly one of my favorites of this year, so far. This is what a AA game looks like, games like this need to be the future of videogames.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I know I probably still have like 30 hours to go, but so far so good! Gameplay is simple but sweet, eventually getting more options for how to attack and what kind of magic and specials to throw at enemies. Feels like a natural upgrade from Trials of Mana. The "open-world" is big enough to be interesting and small enough to not be overwhelming. The story and characters are your standard JRPG affair, but they're more on the simpler side. I may not be binging this game as much as other games I would be more excited about, but I'm having fun and I'm sure it'll be a nice pick up and play game for the next month or so. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Not much to say, other than... if you grew up with the JRPGs of old, this game will scratch that itch. If you were a fan of Mana from the start, you will be delighted. The story is pretty great. The game excels at providing you interesting options (8 classes per character? Yes, please.) I would say, it's not a game for the modern gamer. Now that I'm old, I can see what my nieces and nephews and kids like to play, and it's probably not their speed.But if you're in the mood for some nostalgia and the way games used to be, this is right up your alley, especially if you enjoyed Trials of Mana (which was a remake of Seiken Densetsu 3, albeit modernized). For a new Mana game, this is exactly what was needed, not the detours that were made along the way, even though they had their charm and merit in their own right.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Can't compare to the older mana game since I didn't play them, but this one is pretty decent.      A bit overpriced though...or maybe not and I just need to get used to the high game prices nowadays?        From a high level point of view, the plot is charmingly simple yet not entirely devoid of complexity. The combat is fun enough, if maybe a bit too easy to exploit, but some of the bosses/mini-bosses are pretty good.        The open-world exploration is...ok. A bit too checklist-like, and a bit too many invisible walls, but entertaining enough.        PC version is adequate, even if square enix, as usual, is apparently unsable to understand 30fps is not standard for PC during cutscenes or random things like that. But minor grips overall, nothing too serious.       Overall, I would give it 7/10 for now. Depending on where the story go and if it becomes a bit more than just what it has been so far, maybe 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: About time that they released an other Mana game! A lot of customization to your characters with classes which gives replay value, Great world building with semi-open world maps that have enough content in them. The maps are stunning to look at with a lot of detail and much bigger then in the previous Mana games. The main story game is a solid 30 to 35 hours long with extra content afterwards. I hope I don't have to wait an other 15 years for an other great Mana game. Very good game! 9 / 10
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Got to the final boss and had to stop. This game does a poor job with leveling. Enemies give pitiful experience and you waste all your cookies on weak enemies are few and far between the first 70% of the game. then you barely have any to use to catch up and you end up being 7-10 levels under the final boss. the last 10% of the game, the levels jump by 10 levels out of nowhere without warning. Even if you save your cookies to use on bosses, you'll still be under leveled until the last 30% of the game. All this is on Easy mode by the way. It's a great game, don't get me wrong. The story is phenomenal and made me tear up with every chapter. But the leveling and exp distribution being not so good with common enemies kind of makes it hard at the end. what doesn't help is the game only allows you 9 of an item per fight. If you want to enjoy the game and story, i suggest looking up guides and min maxing everyone. Because regular weapon attacks never peaked past 50 damage for me. Each element resists another, is immune to one and strong against one. The final boss will switch through all elements. but weak weapon attacks and poor exp system makes this game not as good as it could be.My final score:Story: 10/10Gameplay: 7/10Characters: 9/10Overall: 8/10Great game, suffers from poor exp distribution and random level jump at the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a love-letter to fans of the Mana series and it's a travesty Netease fired the entire studio before they had a chance to see the reception the game would receive. The combat system is extremely similar to trials of mana, while the colorschemes and designs are very much secret of mana, with character designs right out of legend of mana. There are also a lot of great references for fans of the series. Like the Luka temple, the Primm boat, and the Jacque seed. The game is very open world, lots to explore, and the combat system is very fluid. There's also easier difficulty settings for people who want a more leisurely gameplay experience.  In all I would highly recommend it if you're a fan of the series and want something to tickle those nostalgia dopamine receptors.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was hesitant to buy this because, with exceptions, I'm usually not that into JRPGs. Usually due to disliking the character designs and voice acting/scripts. To be blunt, I often find them cringey. But I decided to look past those things after giving the demo a try.It turned out to be a good choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic entry into the Mana franchise, To me it feels like some of the voice acting doesnt match the characters but all the other elements are there. The world is broken up kind of like Final Fantasy 12's where each area is very large and has a number of items you can collect in each, different collectable currency, Mana totems to activate and so on. The music feels very "Mana" But not quite as intense of whimsical as Secret of Mana. Combat is fun and reminds me of Kingdom hearts. Per the mana standard you get three characters active in combat but now you get a total of 5 characters to rotate and choose from, With certain items you get to unlock classes for each character that can be swapped when not in combat, each class has a variety of skills unique to each character. You can also customize your characters with 'Seed' items that let a character learn skills of monsters, boost stats and learn class skills that may not be normally available to them. I havent enjoyed a mana series game since the GBA and even then it was lacking. This feels like a solid mana entry.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: As others have stated, this game is stunningly beautiful and draws me back to those early JRPGs. Exploration is so much fun and the combat is quick and really fun as you start to unlock different classes. The story is compelling and will play at your heart strings. Highly recommended for anyway who grew up playing classic JRPGs
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Visions of mana is my first outing in a Mana game. A nice looking JRPG, no technical issues, solid 60fps in 4k, lots of varied enemies with a nice difficulty curve. Although the enemies do like to hit you with control debuffs a lot, they can be negated with proper planning. It has shades of Final fantasy but also reminds me of tales of arise too. Now I'm going to have to get into the other titles, I rate this 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I am one of the lucky people who was already alive when the legendary "Secret of Mana" was released in 1993. Until this day, it is one of my favorite games ever. The difficulty was fairly easy, the story imaginative and the soundtrack was simply fantastic, even on 16 Bit.Needless to say, I was thrilled when I heard of Visions of Mana and bought it shortly after release.And I am stunned. The designs are beautiful, the soundtrack has motifs from Secret and Trials of Mana in an entirely new arrangement and creates a stunning atmosphere. The main characters are loosely resemblant to those of Secret of Mana (or Trials, as you can see on some of the DLC-outfits).I have no idea how far I progressed in the story yet. I completed chapter 3 and I guess there is a bunch of story (and backtracking) in front of me. It has been a long time since a game captivated me for such a long time in a row - 14 hours in 2 days now. I hope my wife and children are doing okay, but I guess they'll be fine.Of course the characters and story do have some flaws. The end of chapter 3 was predictable (no spoilers here), the characters are mainly likeable due to their resemblance to beloved known chars. Well, except for Carina - she is simply amazing and I love her attitude.The story doesn't offer too much new stuff yet and although it is no another "Secret of Mana", is keeps continuity in core elements and references.The german text translation has some really imaginative structures. I just wish they had kept the names of the elemental spirits. It is a bit tough to hear the name "Lunar" (english voicing) and read "Selene".The voice acting adds a nice flair to the scenery - and there are incredibly many voice lines.But what makes this game so special - apart from the nostalgia and the music - is the amazing scenery. I have spent hours just walking, fighting and riding through the different setting, trying to explore every last bit of the map and find all the secrets. The graphics are amazing and although it is not really an open world, it sure feels like it. To me, Visions of Mana is definetly a worthy successor to Secret of Mana yet. I might update this after completing the game, depending on where the story goes. However, if you look for a challenging game with an intruiging, extraordinary storyline, you might want to look somewhere else. This is a cosy game with a couple of challenges and a whole lot of atmosphere. And I love every panoramic shot when entering a new area.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing art style, a decent combat system and a worthwhile story. Together with the other RPG elements, and the nice UX/UI, make this more than worth the 60€ asking price.Also none of this "It'll take 10 hours to get good" modern RPG stuff, this is just fun from the beginning.Shame though what happened to the development team, guess that's what happens when your part of NetEase. (Square Enix only contracted this game out to them)
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: After playing this, I realize why Square tried to experiment with the Mana series before giving up and leaving it in the past.There's a lot I like about , but I also hate just as much as I like about it.The game has so many cutscenes. It rivals  for how much dialog there is in this game where you just watch the characters talk to each other, walk a bit, watch another cutscene, and repeat.The game has a lot of exploration and combat, but also a ton of plot and story. Much more story than I expected, and maybe more than the game really benefits from.All of the characters and dialog are hopelessly adorable and engaging. Because of its lighter tone and naive positivity, I don't mind sitting through the cutscenes. For some reason, I really like them all.There are also hints of more going on beneath the surface of the "human sacrifice" angle of the quest of the Alms.The combat is the worst aspect of the game, because it brings forward the Mana series's worst aspects.Most encounters are ridiculously easy, because you'll just be stunlocking every enemey to death. Many enemies will never get an attack off at all, as your three party members will keep a group of 4-6 enemies permanently stunlocked.Except for when an elite enemy is immune to stunlock and it kills your two AI companions in seconds. Reviving them is pointless, since they'll die again in a few more seconds.Some enemy attacks or status effects are effectively one-hit kills, since they stunlock you.Just like , this game boils down to stunlock or be stunlocked. This is either very boring or very frustrating.Visual clarity is also abysmal. It's hard to tell where enemies are, what direction you're attacking in, whether enemies are attacking or not. The screen is full of particle effects that make it impossible to tell what's happening.I hate to say it, but the slower, stamina-based combat of  is badly needed here to add some strategy. Take they took out strategy from this game but carried forward the "stunlock or be stunlocked" aspect is disappointing.Normal mode is way too easy for most of the game. Hard is way too easy, since most enemies never get an attack off before dying.However, with some enemy attacks (especially the elite ones), the game becomes frustratingly difficult. In this situation, healing is useless since characters die so quickly.There's nothing between these two extremes. The game is badly balanced.Thankfully, you can ignore all of this and just play on Story or Easy mode. I'm trying to stick it out in Normal, but it may not be worth the boredom or aggravation.While the areas are large and beautiful, there's just not much worth exploring. Hundreds of chests offer minor loot, enemies are around every turn to ignore or stunlock, Grizzly Syrup is everywhere.The art direction and level design are great with good variety in biomes and area traversal. Running around the world feels fun and rewarding for its own sake.After about 8 hours, I feel like I'm losing motivation, and I'm not alone here. Only 10-15% of players are getting some easy automatic achievements, like completing Chapter 1.The game is a big Mana series game, for sure. It has a lot of  and . What it's missing, though, is some sort of experimentation like  or just taking the franchise in a new direction. is a great SNES game that doesn't hold up at all.  is a great update to a great SNES game that is too simplistic compared to modern games but still fun and well done. is just a bigger version of those games, without justifying its length or size, and not bringing enough new ideas to the series.Alright, Square Enix, give us the rest of the games on Steam.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: It takes a little getting used to the controls so the Demo does a poor job of introducing you to the game but playing from the start it feels really good and you can sense the "collect all the shinnies" put in the game. I love Mana games and I love this game so far. Some interesting tropes being explored but we'll see where they go with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: pretty good so far. some of the English voice acting for the non - main characters is strange, and the story is a bit weird as well. I was not very surprised to hear there were mistranslations.the combat takes 4 or 5 hours to really come into form, the complexity seems to come from multitasking with your party. the story is serviceable enough up to where i'm at, mostly as a conveyor belt to take you from location to location. i'm having more fun using the EXP items and fighting high level enemies, doing the side stuff, etc. pretty relaxing game. Unfortunately not very tough, even on Hard. Maybe it'll pick up in postgame or something.
