_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game and beat the final boss within three days, replaying levels over a few times in order to obtain the currency for upgrading characters. It took me about 30 hours. It takes a special game to get me hooked like this.This game has a lot of style. It's something I value a lot. I really appreciate how beautiful the environments and people look, you can tell a lot of love and effort went into this game. The stages are all typical scenes from a pre modern Japanese setting but they feel very lively and pretty. The monster variety is also a shining point. At least one new monster appears every level. All the bosses are also unique.Some people have criticized the base repair mechanic, where you can obtain various extras between stages by running around assigning villagers to fix things in the village. Some reviewers said it was boring and would have simply preferred menus to save time. I found it was a good way to experience the village in its purified state, now that it is no longer defiled. Little things like this really allow you to appreciate the art and feel that went into the game.The combat is also cool. Nothing super complicated, but there is a parry, a dodge, and so forth. Every class feels very unique and every one has a reason to be included and taken along. Except maybe the priest. Figuring where to place everyone before a fight is a lot of fun. The only thing I can fault this game with is having the final level before the boss be a boss rush. So disappointing. They had a great opportunity to make a final level in an ascending mountain shrine area and instead they passed out on it for fighting the same bosses you fought before, which is something you could already choose to do by yourself to accumulate more currency or talismans anyways. So disappointing. Still, it hardly takes away from what is a really amazing game. It really does a great job of making a convincing and colorful world you wish you could step into and explore. It also always keeps you wanting to play more to accumulate more crystals and see what the next stage looks like. Really reccommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess

_childDocuments_.review: A somewhat slow burner but an interesting blending of different genres with a lot of polish. The game is mostly pretty easy to beat, but completing all the optional challenges adds a decent level of challenge and strategy to most missions, so that's not much of an issue. Almost every stage has something unique going on to twist the game's core formula in some way, keeping the game fresh throughout. Boss fights are a bit worse than regular stages, but beating them in the challenge times still requires smart use of both your villagers and your own player to do. The player character's moveset is a bit limited for the first half of the game but after a certain point your options expand massively and the game improves a lot.It's definitely not perfect, but for a first try at a very weird idea this is executed extremely well and is more than worth the price of admission.
_childDocuments_.name: Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess

_childDocuments_.review: Bravo to CAPCOM for this original idea! The game brilliantly combines tower defense elements with hack and slash mechanics. While the gameplay and mechanics are simple, they remain engaging as the game becomes progressively more challenging with each stage. It's been a long time since I purchased an AAA game at full price, but this one is truly worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess

_childDocuments_.review: Major PS2 era vibes with this one, back when AAA was experimenting with gameplay instead of just making mildly interactive movies. On the same note this game is very clearly a first take on something new, so there's some things that work and others not so much.It never really ends up being much of a tower defense since the mobs will stop and fight any defenders they encounter, so instead of exploiting good positions it's much better to bunch up everyone in the same spot to maximize DPS. This turns into more of an RTS things during boss fights since you're going after a boss that doesn't move along a predetermined path, but once again you're not going to need anything more fancy than the all attack and all defend commands. The hack and slash action is a bit basic, but there also isn't really anything wrong with it.Playing the game has really nice pacing. The village cleansing missions alternate between preparation and combat, with neither one ever going on way too long at a time since you can fast-forward the preparation if you have nothing to do. Then you also alternate between rebuilding villages and doing missions, which in turn alternate between village cleansing and boss battles.My main gripe with the game is that it's way too easy and no sign of there being any difficulty options. There are optional challenges, some of which are actually challenging, but those just give you some extra rewards that you absolutely don't need if you can beat the challenges. Would have loved to see some kind of opt-in modifier system to make it harder in exchange for more upgrade mats, since right now you end up dumping them all in as few villager types as possible (just max upgrade woodcutter and archer will most likely carry your through the whole game).7/10, would buy again and would buy a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess

_childDocuments_.review: Cool little game with unique monster design.Has a lot of tedious moments that could have been fixed by an optional gameplay option.A menu based fix menu in towns would have been also nice, because running through towns several time to finish and then go to fix another station was quite annoying since the running can feel slow.
_childDocuments_.name: Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess

_childDocuments_.review: This game is probably going to be my GOTY. Extremely soulful, it feels like a game that would have come out on the PS2 in all the best ways.Anyone complaining about "tedium" can't appreciate the slower moments in gaming. Seeing the villages you've helped save, coupled by all the unique animations and visuals is an absolute treat. Accompanied by the phenomenal OST as well, it makes the time between levels feel really peaceful. My only real complaint is that it takes about 4 levels for the games difficulty to ramp up, since that's when it introduces multiple paths the enemy can come from.
_childDocuments_.name: Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess

_childDocuments_.review: Easily a strong contender for my GOTY this year. I love Tower Defense games, and felt the themes of this game seemed interesting when I had seen it in trailers. However, I was on the fence about buying it out of concern for how long it would be, and how fun it would be. That was until Capcom released a demo and announced collaboration costumes with Ōkami, one of my all-time favorites. If you take nothing else from this review, give the demo a try, because it will really push you off the fence one way or another. In my case, trying the demo out was all that I needed to convince me that the game would be fun, so I ended up buying it at launch, and I'm glad I did. That other concern about the game's length went away when I realised there's a bit of replayability here too. To give you a better idea, I am currently working on getting all achievements and I'm not that far off. I am just over 40 hours in, and still have at least a few more hours to go until I've done that, so while you might be able to beat the game in a weekend if you tried hard enough, you won't be able to do everything.Gameplay time aside, there is just so much creativity on display here that it took me off guard. On top of boatloads of charm throughout the game, every stage has it's own unique gameplay gimmick that sets the stage apart from the others. Whenever I thought I had seen everything, it would always introduce something new. I also like that from the way the stage select in this game is set up, you can see that the characters have really been going on a journey. You'll see other reviews say this feels like a PS2 game or how game companies don't make games like this anymore, and that's completely true, but the reason that is the case is because these types of games will never be massively profitable in this day and age. Capcom really deserves huge praise for taking risks and investing in new IPs like Kunitsu-Gami that are very obviously never going to be the most popular games on the planet no matter how good of a reception they get, but they still make them anyway because it's what developers at their studios want to create, and it's what we want to see.
_childDocuments_.name: Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put, it's an amazing game, probably one of the best releases of 2024. The gameplay feels like a decent PS2/ Dreamcast/ Classic Xbox game - which means a lot because that was the last era of really groundbreaking great titles - as the game itself mixes hack'n slash with tower defense elements. The highlight is the traditional Japanese aesthetics, perfectly done Ukiyo-e inspired art style packed with a superb soundtrack and awesome sound effects. The controls are very responsive, the AI is pretty smart - with a few abnormal behaviors here and there but nothing such as game breaking situations - and the main character movesets are just fantastic. I was very interested in this game since I saw a gameplay on Youtube and felt in love it since I started playing. Some people are complaining about the tower defense level designs but truth is that the game is more hack'n slash than tower defense, so if you're looking for a more tactical/ strategic than action title, this game might not be for you. If you're the kind of person that likes very Japanese games like Okami or Ganbare Goemon with lots of action and great fighting moves, you're gonna be hooked.
_childDocuments_.name: Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only a few hours in but I absolutely love the art and music, especially with the added Okami BGM and appearances! So much nostalgia :)The challenges revealed after clearing a stage make it worth going back once you've gotten a little stronger to try to beat them, too. _childDocuments_.review: Very interesting, unique game, and really a joy to play.Edit: Since the main complaint right now is stability, the only "crash" I have had was the first time I started the game, but I'm pretty that wasn't on the game's side, but was because I had another game running simultaneously.  Game runs great and stable in the 2 hours I've played it so far.The tower defense portions provide a decent challenge without being overwhelming.  The way the game guides you through itself makes it feel quite accessible, as well.  Boss fights feel good, with a mix of reactive strategy and a little more pure combat.The fact that you are encouraged to play through stages multiple times by the tasks gives you a lot of freedom to play how you want -- do you want to speed through the game, or do you want to take your time and collect every power-up?Base management aspects are simple, but work well in the context of the game.  I like that it begins getting into some light time management stuff to work on repairs between stages, but nothing ever feels truly punishing for making a mistake in planning.The game is weird and colorful and bright and fun in a way that reminds me of Katamari back in the day.  The design is beautiful and interesting, with the interface managing to strike a pretty good, if not quite perfect, balance between aesthetics and usability.  The character and monster designs fit the world and the story well.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Kunitsu-gami and I'm quite happy to see Capcom put out something so fresh. I loved the tower defense sections of the game, it was by and far the best part and while they weren't perfect (overly simple strategy being the worst) they were at least engaging. The worst parts were the boss fights, the game definitely wasn't designed to be that type of game and controlling units during this was especially painful. So seeing a boss rush, followed by one final boss with mechanics that clash with the tower defense portion of the game was just frustrating and not very good. Overall though, fun game that was definitely worth the time but needed a bit longer to bake in the oven to be a real masterpiece.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Below is a MAJOR issue I have with the game, but after clearing it, the game is slowly earning my favor again. I will update this review accordingly in the future.This game basically lies about what it is. Anyone who's played the demo, the start of the game is rather familiar, an ARPG combined with a Tower Defense game. I LOVE Tower Defense, and it's extremely hard to find any good ones nowadays that are some P2W phone game. So, playing the demo I was hooked.First few levels are the same as the demo, rather fun, but with the complete game you get a few more bonus activities to get upgrades and what not. A few boss fights too are rather interesting, the demo boss returns, as well as a new, flying creature that relies on archers. However, the 3rd Boss you encounter goes against everything you've learned this far, and is one of the worst pieces of ♥♥♥♥ in gaming.The fight revolves around a new mechanic, Darkness, introduced in a previous level; your units cannot see enemies unless they are in light, rather simple. The boss, however, is borderline invincible unless your units light up all torches around the arena. So, you have to go around and send your units away from protecting the Goddess during the fight, rather straight forward. The problem then stems from RNG. The boss is a giant centipede, and has ZERO predictability. Sometimes he targets the player, sometimes he targets the Goddess. Then, when in his vulnerable state, he can, thanks to RNG, effectively make himself invincible by scaling the walls and ceiling, making it so the player cannot deal any damage to him. Units will also just, not attack him at random intervals. Then, he summons minions that do absurdly high amounts of damage to the Goddess, and summon roughly 20-30 of these enemies per cycle. Oh, and the units just won't hit these either sometimes. So, you have to basically babysit the entire map and micromanage just about everything, which might not matter at all in the long run because RNG decided the boss will take down the goddess' HP by 90% in a single attack because ♥♥♥♥ the player's time. Now, I can imagine all the "git gud" and "bad at game" comments. I have thousands of hours in Monster Hunter across 10+ years of games, so I can fight big monsters against greater odds. But how can a company like Capcom, known for produce numerous IPs with crazy boss fights, Resident Evil, Monster Hunter, Okami, hell, ExoPrimal even, ♥♥♥♥ up THIS badly on a fight. It feels genuinely unfinished, unpolished, untested, whatever word you want to describe it, and is a genuine disappointment. The demo feels more polished than the full game.

_childDocuments_.review: it's so goodit's occult japanese demon ♥♥♥♥ + strategy + action. the strategy + action become more involved and engaging as the game progresses. it's a very pleasant game too. when you're not fighting jp demons you're restoring the natural world of this idyllic mountainside civilization accompanied by beautiful piano music. it's rare to see capcom produce something of this scope outside of their core franchises, so some initial trepidation that this is outside their norm might be warranted. but the game is truly great and leans on capcom's mastery of action games to create a diverse enemy roster that responds sensibly to your character's moves and, when enemy types are banded together, takes smart prioritization to defeat while accomplishing bonus objectives in its later stages. these moments are the best parts of the game.the automated player units have a good degree of diversity in their mechanical usage and are very charming in their own right. in every way this game is exceptionally well made.

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like a game that wanted to be made, rather than one that was decided to be made because it'd make a lot of money, though I don't know for sure of course. It's got a sort of "old"(?) feel to it, if that makes sense, it can feel a little nostalgic at times, but it's very much a modern title and it's quite good. The level selection screen kinda threw me off, for example, in a good way.The actual gameplay will feel a little similar if you've ever played Pikmin, funnily enough. The camera angle is the same and the gameplay loop revolves around you ordering around units and making the most of your time. Dandori and all that.The game is artistic and once you get used to the style, it's really cool and well done. I believe you and your allies use something called "Kagura"? Which, when I heard of it, reminded me of Demon Slayer's Hinokami Kagura, which is apparently "Dance of the Fire God". Basically... fighting demons with dancing and good vibes, and it rocks.There's some sort of theme going on with dancing and colors. The stronger your units get, the more their masks get colored in, and some of the enemies have stronger variants that seem to be painted on. Some demons will also sort of dance to empower themselves. It's really cool. There's not a whole lot of dialogue, but the feel of the game, and, while I'm not done with it, the story so far seems pretty good.All in all, it surprised me quite a bit, and I'm glad I tried it out. It's really good.

Its unique blend of gameplay mechanics, stunning visuals, and engaging combat make it a must-play for fans of the genre. While it may not be perfect, it's a highly recommended experience that offers something truly special. Rating: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended with a large caveat. A very fun and simple game, enough mechanics to keep you engaged with a fair amount of downtime between missions to vibe in the areas you've saved and get some upgrades. The missions manage to hit a nice balance of being busy and stressful enough to feel engaging without ever feeling unfair or too hard, and the progression and upgrades on top of later missions introducing more gimmicks keeps things fresh.HOWEVER: This game has been extremely crash prone for me. It already tends to push my PC decently, and I'm running a pretty modern gig, but on top of that the game crashes wayyyyy too much. It seems to happen the most outside of the actual missions and boss fights, thankfully, but I've even had a few during those which just really sours me. I can't look at the 3D models, and even reading the info on different characters and enemies that you unlock from restoring towns has a high probability of crashing my game. That in particular seems to be a common problem, but it seems like the general crashing is hit and miss between different people, so be aware that the game may work just fine for you, or it may not.Very sad about this because at the time this dropped I was actually in the middle of a hyper fixation on third person RTS games, namely Sacrifice and a bit of Brutal Legend, so this slotted in to that fixation very nicely, but I basically have to dedicate half my playtime to rebooting the game, waiting for the horrid crash logger to show up so I can force quit it, otherwise it takes like 5 minutes to make the log, not even report it, and then restart and re-do whatever I last did. The autosave is nice enough to catch village restoration progress whenever I return to the level select but I've still had to re-do more than I'd like. If the idea of that doesn't bother you or you think it's worth checking if the game runs well on your PC, get it and see if it implodes within the 2 hour refund window. All that aside I highly suggest this game for the same reasons I'm sure everyone else has shared, it's extremely cool to see more "experimental" and unique games like this from a AAA studio like Capcom, and I hope to see more from them, preferably minus Denuvo and less crash prone.

_childDocuments_.review: Truly UNIQUE game and a concise mix of genres: tower defense, real-time strategy, hack and slash and a little bit of high-pressure, time constrained farming sim with a few RPG elements. As it is standard with Capcom games, there is a lot of replayability as well.It is amazing to see such bold creativity in this industry nowadays and Capcom deserves all our recognition for that!The art style and the bizarre japanese inspirations are the icing on the cake. It starts with all the spirit mythology in the inumerous monsters you fight, but it also incorporates a lot of the distinguished niponic humour as well: it is crazy to see the villagers literally dancing after every wave and in front of the portals and the different high-resolution traditional japanese sweets that you can collect!As it is classical in Capcom games, you can collect all the models of characters and enemies (even japanese sweets!) and visualize them in 3D. However, this time they went beyond and introduced the Ema Plaques, which not only provide a nice gallery in the village for them, but each plaque has a lore to read! They most likely took inspiration from FromSoftware games here, since the story of Kunitsu-Gami barely have any dialogue, but at the same time the lore is so enriched with japanese folklore!Only a few complaints from my side:- Musubi upgrades reespec should be way quicker than it is right now... I don't want to see the villagers animations every time I attempt to max out their upgrades: it should be a single button to level a given skill if you have enough Musubi for that- Village classes should be a bit more balanced and unique, regarding costs and what role they fill that no other classes could. There is a clear advantage on using cheap, ranged classes (e.g., the archer), than expensive melee ones (e.g., the sumo wrestler). Alternatively, there should be clear challenges in which it would be extremely difficulty to apply the same villager composition, which generates an incentive to try new classes- We should not need to return to the village to collect crystals and rations after every mission. It is intuitive if you are moving forward with new stages every time, but when you are accomplishing challenges it feels like a quore to load the village map if the village is already completely rebuilt- Some quality-of-life mechanics, such as the "Assembly" command, should be available since the beginning of the game

_childDocuments_.review: Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess is not a game that I could call revolutionary or innovative. It is a very curious mix of hack and slash action game with a tower defense strategy and I haven’t seen it done quite like this before. But definitely not revolutionary. And yet, I can’t help but love this project and wish to see more huge development companies and corporations learn from it. No, not from the mix of genres, but rather from the approach this game takes. You see – this is very much a “AA game”, made by “AAA” standards, which is something you used to see all of the time back in the late 90s-early 00s, but which doesn’t really happen anymore. And playing this game reminded me of how much are we all missing out with the current gaming market trends.But I should explain what this game is and also emphasize that it holds really well on its own, without this “olden days” nostalgic vibes. As mentioned, this is a curious mix of hack and slash and tower defense, where you go through a series of missions, where you have to protect a shrine maiden from waves of attacking demonic creatures. You directly control a ninja-like character who is very good at this task, but can be easily overwhelmed by the amount of said creatures attacking from different directions, hence why you save villagers and assign them to roles using special masks that you unlock as you play. Each mask is a class (or type of a tower, if you will), with its own strengths and weaknesses, some are ranged, some are melee, some are support units or fit even more specialized roles. And each mission is usually divided into the daytime, during which you explore, carve the path for the maiden to walk on, save villagers, gather resources and prepare for the night, during which you focus on directing the units and engaging in combat directly.There’s a big variety in missions, some introduce unique challenges or twist the main rules on their head. Boss fights are treated as a separate type of a mission with their own rules. You also get to rebuild places you had your missions in and upgrade the masks. And each mission has a set of additional tasks and challenges that become visible once you’ve played through the mission once. So the game is very much focused on replaying completed missions with new unlocked masks with the additional motivation to unlock everything.And there’s a lot of surprises too. I won’t elaborate just because I feel like each one of those is an incredibly welcome surprise which evokes that “olden days” feeling that I’ve mentioned, where games just kept on giving you more surprising cool twists without resorting to updates, DLCs or expansions, paid unlocks or “seasons”. And while one can guess where the budget was saved, in comparison with, say, a typical modern Resident Evil release, the game still uses all of the cool technological marvels, has fantastic Japanese folklore-inspired style and storyline and the music is just… Gosh, this is easily the most fresh and daring soundtrack from Capcom in decades. Last time I’ve seen them being so “open-minded” was with Resident Evil 7, but they’re pushing for experimenting even further and I wish they’d done it more often.All that said, this game is far from perfect. There is one particular level that I found extremely frustrating even without doing the challenges. One boss fight was very poorly explained, despite several dedicated tutorial-like phases of the fight. Some of the challenges are just evil in how tough they can be to do. Game is somewhat lacking as both hack and slash and a tower defense title and makes me wish more time was spent to develop both of these halves of the game. Some of the micro-management of abilities and special attacks is very nuanced and frustrating and is mostly unimportant for normal play but becomes a chore when setting up for each mission challenges…Despite all that, though, it’s just so irresistibly charming. I can’t help but admire its simplicity, while fully understanding that it can only be how it is because it was made by a huge studio with the amount of skill, experience and budget not available for most “actual AA” and indie studios. And I don’t remember the last time a release like this even happened. Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess, and I hope I won’t forget the title as I constantly do, isn’t just a welcome callback to a different era of gaming, it’s a very fun game in its own right, with its own voice and its own terrific soundtrack. Thankfully, there is a demo of the game you can try for yourself if you’re still confused about how this even plays, so give that a go. Don’t ignore this title, it’s genuinely cool.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game after reading rave reviews and I'm glad I did. It's a brand new IP from capcom, essentially a tower defense game where you have to protect a maiden from a variety of really creepy looking monsters as she advances across an idyllic Japanese mountain to purify its villages from the corruption that produces said monsters (called Seethe). Along the way, you use her powers to purify certain sections of land, as well as human villagers cocooned by the defilement, which give you crystals that you can spend on powering up each of those villagers into a warrior capable of helping you defend the maiden--which you have to do yourself as well, since you play as genderless masked samurai/ninja type warrior, but since you can't go it alone, you need help. There are 12 different kinds of warriors, ranging from melee axe wielders to marksmen with muskets to priests and sorcerors, and their masks are unlocked by beating certain bosses (Great Seethe) over the course of the game.Very very much worth the buy. The aesthetics might seem strange at first--this is a REALLY japanesey game (to the extent they promoted it with an old-school puppet show, the classic "Bunraku" type that goes all the way back to the late 1600s), so when the characters attack, its like they're dancing, and they also do a little dance whenever you purify the Seethe Gates for the maiden that act as demarcations between sub-stages. But if you can accept that, the game is absolutely beautiful, despite not being a AAA project. There's a surprising amount of variety in tactics and strategy you're not only allowed but encouraged to use, because the game always throws new things at you, whether enemies that make melee warriors irrelevant but are vulnerable to muskets, extremely tanky enemies you need to distract with a tanky unit (a sumo wrestler) so you can attack their vulnerable backs, weapons, barriers, and cannons you need to repair with a carpenter you find who takes time so you can't repair everything, and a variety of upgrades for your soldiers as well as you personally giving everything from special abilities to various kinds of boosts. It's given hours of entertainment so far! The music is pretty good too, mainly Japanese style, as you can expect, but some bosses have nice jazz/funk inspired tracks too.I only have a couple of complaints. First, every stage is also a town you can recover from defilement, and after you beat it you can return to the town to rebuild its structures by assigning villagers to provide you with resources and upgrades to use in future stages. To do this, you have to go into each town from the map screen, and while this is fun at first--it's nice to see the lovely Japanese village, see the paintings and lore statues you can get by unlocking stuff, and even petting the various animals around--it gets repetitive and time-wasting later on. I wish there was a way to both collect resources and direct repairs straight from the map screen instead of having to go through a loading screen and then wander around a town every time. Secondly, the plot is very very thin--there's barely any dialogue aside from some narration from the maiden and the conceit that she herself becomes more corrupted as you use her to purify the corruption. I hope they expand the plot in a second game, but this one was good enough that I really hope there's a second game! :D

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: game is on the good side of mid, worth experiencing, but Capcom could have done betterI will admit this game didn't reach my full hopes, with middling combat being the biggest detractor. I would have thought the studio that makes Devil May Cry could have done better on that front.The strategy element, while the meat of the game, is also mostly just fine. Your unit AI is usually fairly smart, but micromanaging positions can be a huge pain for bosses, as certain AoE attacks mean you need to move everyone at once, and once the attack is done you need to reposition all your ranged units so they don't get hit while your tank is drawing aggro. That said, I sympathize with the fact that a hybrid game is very difficult to design, so I do put up with the jank of adjusting my units.I think where the game actually exceeds expectations, and pushes the review into positive, is the animations. Watching Soh is just amazing, and some of the special attacks make me giddy just watching them. Fans of the judgment cut haven't seen anything yet. The enemy design is also great, with some extremely cool bosses towards the end of the game.If the game is on sale, for the most part it respects your time (it has some quirks with the upgrade system that I hope get patched to be more seamless), so if it looks cool to you it's probably worth getting.

_childDocuments_.review: Why are you reading reviews? This game actually has a demo that is indicative of the final product. Give that a go.But if you don't have the time or don't want to bother: The game is breathtakingly pretty in a way that Capcom seems to be able to reliably deliver. All of the creatures, the people, the environments, they're all well rendered and coherently designed. Seeing them in motion is even more enthralling. Or disgusting. It has a straightforward and entertaining gameplay loop that encourages backtracking without demanding it. You can scour a map of resources in one go; in my experience it's harder to not rescue all possible villagers and cleanse all of the defilement in one go just to make sure you have the biggest possible crew to fight off the horde. You might have to play a map once or twice more to perform the optional objectives, some of which are mutually exclusive, but not often.There certainly isn't much story besides what is already presented, but they still manage to build tension over time with silent characters doing Capcom's trademark over(motion)acted animations. Won't matter. It's pretty enough.I'm honestly amazed Capcom didn't charge higher for this. It looks, plays, and feels like a higher tier title.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game made with love. Not only it's a unique twist to the tower defense genre, it manages to make it unique by merging different aspects of completely separate ideas into one. It shows that CAPCOM or any AAA devs can invest in making games that are unique and can stand on their own among the crowded market of over hyped AAA games. This may not look like a AAA game but its production value and quality is no doubt of AAA level.So what's new about this? I mean there are similar TD games out there where you control hero(es) while set traps, push back enemies and so on.It's the setting. The way you free villagers that you use essentially as mobile "tower" with powers (i.e. role). You have your mobile base (aka the priestess) who needs to be carried to the destination to perform the ritual for freeing given level of any curse. You have special attacks (i.e powers) that can turn the tide of battle when things get dire.All of these are done on the basis of dancing! Yes, the dev who loved the ritualistic dancing of ancient Japan that had spiritual meaning, brought it into this game with a unique twist. The twist is that all your actions, the priestess, and even your villagers perform their tasks while dancing. In a sense the entire game is a portrayal of ritualistic journey. This setting is not only unique but manages to pull you in into a world of ancient myth and horror; simultaneously giving you the purpose and the means to do so.This strange blend of ancient ritual to banish evil presence (exorcism) with action makes one forget that  its a TD game. On one hand you are running to save your priestess from attack, while on the other hand placing your villagers in specific locations to defense crucial choke points. It's strangely fun and intense. Add a really beautiful battle music to that and you get even better experience overall.So in summary what's in it are as follows:+ Amazing graphics. The whole world is made using miniature diorama IRL that were scanned and used for in-game world. This unique method gave the art style a realistic yet fictional diorama-like vibe. Just as the devs intended. It works like a charm. Pleasing to the eyes.+ Amazing setting: a priestess with her savior (Soh) helping villagers to be freed from the curses which was caused inadvertently by the greed of the said people; while killing mythological beasts of weird proportions and looks. + TD mechanics where villagers can be given roles at a cost of crystal orbs that you collect from environmental destruction, purification of entities and killing enemies. Roles can be altered on the go to suit your combat need. You are the guard, soldier, general and strategist, all in one.+ Beautiful and sometimes haunting music. Reminds you that this is a journey of action prefaced by horror. + Quite a few missions to complete. Each can be played again for finishing specific objectives for rewards. Upon freeing some villages, side mission unlocks. These are essentially boss battles that you must do to unlock unique roles for villagers. + Purified villages can be rebuild with people that gives you special rewards.+ Rewards from mission, village rebuild and finishing side objectives earn you special trinkets that you can equip on Soh for passive/active bonuses.+ Soh has  own tech tree of abilities you can invest in. From sword to bow, or magical powers, all at your disposal.A few issues I had with this one:- Some missions are, personally, not my favorite. Or more specifically some objectives associated with those missions. Let's just say I don't like those missions where "you have to do X or else you are..." Some missions can get dicey too but after getting the general pattern of enemies and their path, multiple play of each mission should help one get around those issues. Again not a big issue, albeit a minor one that is negligible.- During intense combat Soh's ability to dodge attacks feels a bit sluggish. Dodging is on its own a type of dance and the full animation can get you out of one situation and place you among another in a tight spot. Just wish there was a quick recovery option available where I could cancel the dodge or just outright come out of the long animation after the dodge.Overall it's a must have for TD fan, but more importantly show CAPCOM that we love this type of game. Game that is made with love and passion. This is not just a game, it's an art project. It's a vision of a person that took place into an art form that we often only see poorly in horror movies. A fantastic hiddgen gem it is.CAPCOM give us Kunitsu-gami 2 please.

_childDocuments_.review: The art and music? Gorgeous. The core gameplay? Stretched thin from covering too many angles. The basebuilding? Tedious. The story? Simple but lovely.I can't believe Capcom of all companies would make something like this. If you love tower defenses, love DMC-style battles and have ever wondered what a combination of the two would look like, and can overlook the pricing-this is the game for you. Special bonus if you love Shinto mythology because this game OOZES it ("kunitsu-gami" itself roughly translate to "deity of the earth", and the enemy types essentially embody kegare-spiritual impurity-gone completely out of control. Like the rotting gods from Princess Mononoke). It's not perfect. The PC runs too slowly and you have to manually collect resources from basebuilding. Playing hide and seek to build everything in time every day is unnecessarily stressful. Certain units and items are blatantly OP. But if you have the time and passion to commit to the gameplay loop,  it's a feast for the eyes and ears to at least go through the core game.

_childDocuments_.review: Such a fantastic gem of a game. A truly unique and creative leap by Capcom. You play as Soh, a righteous retainer of the holy maiden Yoshiro, as you both travel the sacred mountain that's been defiled. You travel from village to village purging them from demons and corruption. Steeped in medieval Japanese lore, tons of unlocks, a surprisingly large reward and skill ceiling, in-game challenges, very good pacing, new game+ with unique add ons, awesome character design...This game just kept surprising me. I'm only half way through and I'm at 20 hours, it's so good. An unexpected but INCREDIBLY well done game. Once you play it, you begin to realize why people are saying this is their game of the year.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game.it truly feels like one of the good, old games we used to get back in the day, it has this nostalgic feeling and game-play that I just love.I strongly recommend anyone to try this game out and just play it, you won't be disappointed. Game-play wise it's an action game combined with a tower defense game.You walk around the map as the main guy, slicing and dicing Yokai while trying to protect the priestess. You have Villagers who you can command and give different roles to like archer, spear-man, etc.During the day you build defenses and collect resources and at night you fight together with the villagers.This will sound stupid but this game just feels like a game.No ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ extras, no busywork, no weird modern influences, it just feels like how a game should feel like.Think SNES to PS2 era.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent action + tower defense-ish games with a surprising amount of content especially if you count getting all the new stuff and new final boss in new game+.The flow of the game is quite simple, accumulate and allocate resources and defenses by day, fight at night. Your villagers will perform their respective roles while the player can micro manage the villagers or just deal with things personally.Though the game isn't particularly difficult, at certain points it does present a challenge, especially if you are going for the bonus objectives. Since meta progression is tied to extra objectives and story progress, if you haven't figured out how to play, you may very well get stuck. Button mashing and poor unit management are costly. Fortunately, it's free to respec.A lot of people have also probably mentioned this, but the "base building" stuff is pretty dull, and needed to be reworked. A small part, but you will notice.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say the game is really fun to play. For everyone that wonders what type of game this is, here is a short summary:The game feels like a Warriors Game, where you fight a horde of monsters with elements of a tower defense game. You can recruit some people and station them around you to protect the priestress at night. At daytime you have to make a clear path for the priestress to walk until you can purify the "exit" (Gate). (Imagine the cargo Mode from Overwatch or similar)The tower defense elements are okay'ish. They don't deal a lot of damage and serve more of a human barricade, until you come to kill all of them. You get the classic "Mash combos" with a light and heavy attack which you can combine, which is way I say it feels more like a Warrior Game.The game itself looks amazing and I really love the art direction. After like 5 hours, you unlock some more things, so don't think that there isn't much to do. I would recommend this game to someone that likes a lot of action with a fair share of strategic Tower Defense.

_childDocuments_.review: Old meets new in  - the latest and greatest in a long line of peculiar Capcom ventures. I can't quite begin to explain what exactly this game is about; it mashes together so many elements, that it almost deserves a new sub-genre of its own. Is it an RTS game? Sort of. Is it a tower defence game? I mean, I guess. Is it a musou-style hack'n'slash? In a way.  strengths lie in its straightforward, unrelenting style based on a few ingenious little ideas and hooks that come together to make the perfect "almost" game. And what do I mean when I say "almost" game? I mean to say that channelling the spirit of a foregone era within the industry has its obvious quirky benefits, but also inherits some of its drawbacks. On one hand, this game has gone full circle in creating an experience that looks and feels twenty years old but strikes fire into our hearts because we had no idea how much we missed it. On the reverse side, we have a game that begins to feel increasingly repetitive when the hollow walls of its interior are broken through. A jack of all trades but a master of none. Novelty wears thin over the nearly two dozen hours I spent with it. But, none of this detracts from a rather brilliant game, more importantly in how it manages to feel truly  in a time where we have an almost endless list of video games. This is 2024's sleeper hit, consider me shocked because I was not expecting it. All that aside, I liked the kagura dancing, it... does something to me.

_childDocuments_.review: Remember the golden age of Capcom when they would make weird off-the-wall amazing yet underrated gems, this is that era of Capcom game design, this game could have been a certified PS2 classic if it was released back then,it's a feature-complete game without current Capcom micros (im looking at you DmC Resi and Dragons dogma).Mix the simple premise of Tower defense and hack-and-slash combat gameplay, with lots of replay-ability and in places a genuinely good challenge, delivered in a stage-based format with replays of levels unlocking new gear and rewards based on the sub-objectives reached in each stage (think 3 staring a level in angry birds lol).All rolled up in a beautiful art style with great sound design and a wonderful soundtrack, seriously listen to the music in the hub worlds and tell me it's not beautiful and relaxing as you set your villager's tasks.The game is reasonably priced for what you get,I think the only shame with the game is its had no marketing so will obviusly fade into obscurity.as a lifelong Capcom fan, it really pleases me to see the current direction the company is going, with the recent re-release of MvC chaos and the MvC collection speeding its way to us just hope they continue to resurrect long lived and loved dormant franchises (DINO ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ CRISIS PLEASE!).

_childDocuments_.review: Overall 7/10. Best selling points are the visual aesthetics and music. Gameplay is only decent. Content is a bit short, would say it's probably better to get it during sale. There should be a demo which you should definitely try it out first. Difficulty is pretty casual, you can always look for strats in guides when you get stuck (which is pretty unlikely), and game has the QoL feature for easy Save&Load.Minor complaints:1. UI can be improved a lot, especially the UI for equipping Mazou statues.2. A bit annoying to assign jobs when bunch of NPCs are clumped together.3. Challenge conditions are not shown before you've beaten a stage at least once. (artificially lengthening gameplay). Also to get all collectibles you need to beat NG+9 (though is not required for 100% achievements)4. Can't change loadout/villager upgrades without returning to base.5. Can't collect crystals/rations without visiting each bases. (Should ease this process starting from NG+ tbh)6. Controller camera speed is too slow, and forced to use acceleration. 7. Player combat feels... slippery? Since the game doesn't have aim assist/lock-on for melee attacks, you have to manually assign attack directions by pressing the movement keys. Yet pressing movement keys while attacking makes you... well... move. So most of the time you will not be able to hit the enemy because you slipped away from their sides. Not a big deal when fighting hordes, but annoying when fighting bosses.8. When assigning tasks for NPCs, the list won't automatically suggest NPCs with closest distance to the task.9. That one challenge that requires killing enemies with thunder is too RNG-based, not a big fan.Major complaints:I'm personally more fond of souls-like combat than RTA tower defense, this game attempted to combine both things and I personally think did not come out well. The tower-defense levels are alright, with mild requirements to one's strategizing and planning. The boss fights however are a bit disappointing. Most of them are designated to be fought alongside NPCs, so you could basically bruteforce through with bunch of high-DPS units and completely miss the bosses' cool designs. I personally would hope for an alternate version of boss fights that are balanced for solo fighting.  I personally think the game shouldn't have let players bring NPCs into the boss fights unless it at least has some gimmicks that requires commanding the units (other than spawning minions).

_childDocuments_.review: + Strong art style with varied locations and some really cool and memorable monsters+ Everything is well-animated - particularly Soh and their dance-like attacks and moves+ Gameplay feels very distinct with a preparation phase, unit tactics and action gameplay+ Stages are well-designed and they mix it up with unique scenarios / mechanics in some of the stages that keeps it fresh+ Lots of units to pick from and upgrade+ Lots of skills to upgrade and different items to try out+ Giving out orders is intuitive and straightforward+ Time-limits apply a healthy amount of pressure between stages+ Difficulty is well-balanced - not super challenging but does force you to mix up units / tactics and to think about your approach+ Bosses are a cool spectacle and are fun to fight- The penultimate stage is just a boss-rush against the same bosses you've previously foughtThis game was a real treat for me as someone who likes Japanese culture and yokai a lot. It's also a really solid game that tries something a bit different to good success. If you interrogate individual elements they won't be the best ever (e.g. there are better pure action games out there), but combined it offers a unique blend that works. The monsters are a lot of fun, there's a lot of types, they're all extremely weird and they introduce them at a good rate - same with the different units you acquire. There's a good level of polish and care to the game in general. Easy to recommend and fun to play something with a clear creative vision that's a bit different.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a challenge to summarize how Kunitsu-Gami plays. The closest comparison I can make is to the "Push the Cart" minigame in Nexus Blitz. This comparison is especially apt, considering  Unlike Nexus Blitz and league in general, instead of unreliable teammates, you have NPC villagers that you can assign roles such as Archer (Ranged DPS), Axeman (Melee DPS), Sumo (Tank), and Shaman (Healer), etc. You free the villagers during the daytime cycle and assign them roles and tasks. During the nighttime cycle, you direct their movement and they fend off hordes of enemies that try to destroy your Cart/Nexus, while you control the player character, Soh, and do the same.It's definitely a niche title but, in my opinion, it's really fun. Especially once you unlock more villager roles and Soh's ability tree—admittedly, I think the latter should become available sooner in the game than it is. It's unfortunate that this game didn't have a wider appeal on release, but I'm glad to see Capcom is still willing to take risks on niche concepts like this. The gameplay is smooth and engaging, and as you progress in the story, the gameplay loop gets mixed up in different ways to keep it fresh. The story isn't groundbreaking, but it's nice; I liked it for what it is and what is had to offer. For those who appreciate art style and art direction, Kunitsu-Gami is absolutely gorgeous.There are some things I think could have been done better. Normally, I prefer when games aren't super hand-holdy but, uniquely in this case, I think a few things could have been explained better. At least in the tutorial menu. I think a dojo in bases where you can try out different abilities and combos would have been nice. I wouldn't go as far as to say "show damage numbers" because I can see how that would clash with the aesthetic.Another thing is crystal collection from bases. You can periodically revisit old bases and collect crystals and rations, which is awesome. This feature will come in clutch at various times during a playthrough. The problem is that I'm pretty sure the game doesn't even tell you about this feature. Additionally, process is rather tedious, as you have to visit each base one by one with a loading screen between every base. A "Collect Crystals and Rations from this Base" option when you hover over a base on the World Map would streamline the process while also making the player aware of the feature. The penultimate mission is a Boss Rush of all the previous boss fights, which is fine. A lot of games do this.  Nonetheless, my criticism of the practice is always the same: either meaningfully innovate on the original boss encounter or just make new bosses. Kunitsu-Gami, like most games, does neither.My last critique is another pet peeve. By the end of the second playthrough (you need two to finish the whole story), you'll still be missing a lot of Mazo Talismans, which are items that grant different passive abilities. Apparently, you need 8 playthroughs to collect them all. The only reason I can't say for certain is that the game doesn't communicate this information to the player at all. So, unless you search for the information independently, you'll finish the game with plenty of empty slots in your Mazo Talisman inventory. Personally, that made me very sad, because complete inventories is how I fill the empty slots in my heart. Making me work extra hard for my Dopamine hit, eh, Capcom.Overall, I'd give Kunitsu-Gami a 9/10. Would play again eight times to collect all Mazo Talismans.

_childDocuments_.review: Kunitsu-Gami is a unique experimental game from Capcom in the vein of the kinds of things they tried out on the Gamecube/PS2 era that combines an action game with tower defense. Overall the game is solid, it understands how to mix things up with the levels and has a pretty reasonable difficulty curve (outside of the 3rd boss, oof). It is not a game where you will be swamped with dialogue, it's very low on it in fact but it does what it's trying to do. It isn't insanely long, my 24 hours includes replaying a little over half the levels to get the bonus objectives done, but it doesn't outstay it's welcome either and has NG+ if you want more.Pros:The game's checkpoints feel really nice, I never hit that point where I had to think "oh god I started all the way back here" after failing something. Being able to freely reassign your upgrade material (Musubi) is really nice, and makes it a lot easier to just use it instead of worrying that you'd rather save it for a new job you haven't unlocked. I don't have a lot of specific points but I liked the overall aesthetic and how everything came together.Nitpicks:If you want to get everything, you are going to have to replay levels, like, every level. All levels have a set of bonus objectives that they won't even tell you when you first play them, which seems bizarre to keep that hidden and while I CAN look it up and try to get them, it's annoying that they don't show them until the first clear.I kind of wish the game defaulted to maxing out your crystals after clearing a stage because them not doing that making replaying certain levels and trying to get the better times on bosses kind of a drag. Crystals are too plentiful for you to run into having less than max going into most missions most of the time which makes the few levels that leave you low annoying to redo. Alternatively not having replays impact your crystal count would work as another solution, that way you can still have the experience of being burned down to none without having to experience it every time you want to do that stage for the side objectives. For an example of why this matters, I was burning turns before the last boss to finish the base building and opted to just nuke the first boss with all woodcutters multiple times because trying to get better times on other bosses where I would actually use other roles would leave me going into the last boss with a crystal deficit. I didn't think this was a problem until after beating the game and realizing it's a decent part of why I didn't try out some of the unit types on bosses or other short missions to get a feel for them.While I like the talisman system, the long list of them to scroll through is a nuisance. There are enough of them that there should really be a table, or let me save load outs so I don't need to go through the huge list every time I want to swap between boss and level gear. I'm glad they have a good variety with varying degrees of usefulness but it's too many for the single list format.Overall I DO like Kunitsu-Gami and think people who are looking for a more unique style game should definitely give it a go, unless needing to replay levels to get everything is something that really annoys you.

_childDocuments_.review: A breath of fresh air in an era full of copy-cats and trend chasing:-[Gameplay]:A neat and unique mix of hack-&-slash, tower defense and RTS, kinda reminds me of creative games of the 90s like Sacrifice, you directly control one character (Soh) and your main goal is to protect from demons (a.k.a Seeth) the priestess until she can reach the last gate in the are and purify it, the villagers you can save/recruit in each level can be assigned roles and ordered to move around, in normal levels they will react automatically to enemies in the radius o their sight and in boss battles you can give them extra commands to attack the boss or retreat, there are also multiple types of structures and objects they can interact with, the night and day cycle also adds a very interesting way to separate the enemy waves and fits with the lore, very neat, even better, every few levels the game will throw a curve ball at you that changes how things work and introduces a temporary new mechanic to spice things up, great design.Also the fact you can refund all upgrades at any time in-between battles without any cost or limitation is a great feature, mixed with the fact that some of the post-battle/boss challenges might require completely different tactics makes experimenting with different skills and unit combinations to beat the challenges a lot of fun. Only criticism I have here is the trinkets menu design is really unnecessarily awkward, it's a long empty list you have to scroll through one by one looking for the trinkets you unlocked, not sure why they designed it that way, it should have been a square grid with a page for each type of trinket, right now the only way to overcome this problem is to go in and mark all the ones you unlocked as "favorites" which is a bit tedious, hope they fix this in an upcoming update, but that's really my only criticism of the game. [Visuals]:The visuals are absolutely phenomenal, it takes well known yokai from Japanese folklore and gives them a psychedelic twist, it's very stylish, unique and colorful with a focus on masks being representative of the different roles your units serve while also serving a ceremonial role in the lore, the kaleidoscopic effects of the magic used in purification are also a sight to behold, all in all a visual treat, but if you are looking for hyper realism and characters where every body hair and eyelash are modeled you won't find this here.[Music/Sound]:The music is very energetic and draws from traditional Japanese music, it also ties with the lore since the act of purification is tied to the priestess and the villagers doing a purification dance, and not only do the characters dance to the beat but the very background itself and the demonic infestation being purified pulses with the beat of the music, you can't help but shake along with the music, as for the sound it's also very well implemented and serves a purpose in locating the infestations to clear during the day and also ambient sounds get more tense and sinister as the time nears sunset and the night looms.[Performance]:Haven't had any issues whether with the demo or the game itself, and the settings for visuals and gameplay are plentiful and in-depth, all in all no problems here for me. IMO this game is going to become a cult-classic, give it a chance if you are looking for something fresh and interesting or you are a fan of tower-defense/hack-&-slash/RTS games.

_childDocuments_.review: Given the fact this game effectively captured my hyperfixation over the weekend enough to complete the ~20-30 hour main story in three days, I can assure you that Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess is a truly beautiful, unique, and fun game. Gorgeous design, excellent music, fluid action, fun strategy, and a simple but affecting story. I do agree with most reviewers that the "base building" aspect of the game is tedious (if charming), but that tedium never put a dent in my enjoyment of the game itself. If the developers are able to tweak the base building to allow some management through menus and collecting of offerings from multiple bases at a time, I feel the tedium would be reduced dramatically. This is a game that is fairly challenging, but the greatest challenge is in mastery of the skills and strategy on offer to complete some truly difficult bonus goals on each mission stage. Replayability is high with many varied ways to approach missions and the various aforementioned bonus goals. I'm very excited for NG+ but will probably hold off until I complete more mission goals. Kunitsu-Gami is absolutely soaked in Japanese cultural appreciation and Shinto-inspired tradition. The level of detail is surreal. It immerses the player beautifully--and I fully recommend folks checkout the "prequel" story Capcom commissioned from a real Bunraku Theater! Vibes, impeccable. I sincerely hope this game does well, because it is clearly a passion-project with lots of thought and love poured into it. The mechanics are sound. The design is thoughtful. The gameplay is fun. Everything coalesced into an incredible experience, and I am certain I will be playing more of this game and spreading the good word of Maiden Yoshiro's purification dance.

_childDocuments_.review: Extreme tastefulness and artistry grace this game as you play the protagonist against supernatural evil.  I wondered if this would just be a mindless gorefest that applied superficial phantasmagoria as its foundation, but fortunately, it is much deeper than that.  Its eery beauty gives me shivers.  This is old school Capcom DNA.   There are definite Shinsekai Into The Depths tones and feels, except that now you are not slowly making yourself through the bottom of the bottom of the ocean alone against a futile, hopeless, inevitable doom of a future, hioping just to survive.  In this title, there is a much stronger sense of mission and heroism.  You are not in this alone, in Kumitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess.  The difficulty level, at least for now, is pleasing.  Some masochists like to get through an extremely difficult game once.  Personally, I would rather play an enjoyable title over and over.  This is just a joy to play and savor.  If you thought Shinsekai Into The Depths looked okay, this looks exponentially more amazing.  Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: 9.5/10. Fresh, bold, and enchanting. Kunitsu-gami is an incredibly fun action-strategy game that screams quality, a work of passion visibly crafted with love. It has firmly cemented a special place in my heart, and is such a breath of fresh air in a crowd of stale, soulless and bland garbage in the video games industry that's constantly trying to get you hooked with dark patterns and hostile practices. I'm not being dramatic; this game respects your time—you can undo any and all upgrades with no penalty, essentially giving you unlimited free respecs.Its core game loop is unique and addictive—a successful blend of 3rd person precision-action combat (Sekiro) and tower defence elements. There are dodge iframes, deflect/parry and counterattack mechanics! Time is constantly advancing in each mission, split into day and night activities:- prepare yourself in the day by gathering resources (currency, healing items, recruiting), repairing structures, placing traps and managing troops. You’re racing against time while Yoshiro (your maiden/priestess) dances towards the end point.- as the sun goes down, the music turns somber and the drums start beating louder. By nightfall, Yoshiro stops moving and the gates of hell open, vomiting Yokai into your world. You fight them off using your combos as well as constantly repositioning your troops and changing their roles depending on where the battle is thickest.Between missions, you get to build up the villages you’ve purified and earn additional rewards for strengthening your character and troops. The ambience and music switches gear to a soft and pleasant one, giving you a relaxing break after a hectic mission where you can take your time to engage with Yokai lore, switch out talismans, look at Emaki scrolls and feed Yoshiro candy.Both its art and music are beautiful and inspired. Of all the games in my library, this game's digital artbook is the only one I took time to look through and it definitely did not disappoint. The environment brings back memories of my time hiking mountains and exploring shrines in Kyoto. Controls are intuitive, smooth, tight and play really well on a controller.If you’re unsure about this game, give the demo a spin—it’s basically a tutorial that introduces you to the core gameplay. Don’t worry if you found it too easy. The game opens up hard and fast after the tutorial with multiple torii gates, forking paths, more elite mobs and minibosses that spawn together and come from every direction.Update: If you’re curious about the amount of content and total playtime, I beat the final boss at around the 20-hour mark. As I was invested in the story and wanted to see the ending, I only focused on the main missions about halfway down the mountain. There’s probably another 5-10 hours more to accomplish every side objective in all villages, and further more in NG+.

name: SONIC X SHADOW GENERATIONS
detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition About the Game SONIC X SHADOW GENERATIONS DIGITAL DELUXE EDITION Purchase the SONIC X SHADOW GENERATIONS Digital Deluxe Edition and receive additional iconic music tracks from previous Sonic and Shadow games, a Terios skin based on Shadow’s original concept, behind-the-scenes art, the Sonic the Hedgehog 3 Movie Pack featuring the voice of Keanu Reeves, and more! It includes: • Base Game • Digital Deluxe Season Pass: o Sonic the Hedgehog 3 Movie Pack (releasing December 12, 2024) o Terios Skin o Extra BGM Pack o Digital Art Book + Soundtrack o Skill Points (Sonic Generations) *If you own the Extra Content Pack, which is included in the Digital Deluxe Edition and Digital Deluxe Upgrade, please install the Extra Content Pack before starting a new game. Please note that parts of the Extra Content Pack may not be validated if installed after a new save has been started. Shadow the Hedgehog is back with Classic and Modern Sonic in SONIC X SHADOW GENERATIONS, an all-new collection featuring two unique experiences! Play as Shadow in a brand-new story campaign featuring never-before-seen abilities that prove why he’s known as the Ultimate Life Form! Speed through iconic stages from Shadow’s history, discover hidden secrets in an expansive hub world, and unlock new powers to take on Black Doom and save the world. SONIC X SHADOW GENERATIONS also includes a complete remaster of the highly acclaimed SONIC GENERATIONS, a time-traveling adventure featuring a greatest-hits collection of 3D and 2D Sonic stages, now with upgraded visuals and new bonus content. The Return of Shadow In this new standalone campaign, Shadow’s nemesis, Black Doom, has reemerged and threatens to take over the world once again. Shadow must journey into his past, confront his painful memories, and unlock new dark powers to save the world. Shadow Evolved Harness Shadow’s new Doom Powers to battle hordes of enemies and tackle platforming challenges like never before. Surf on water, fly over obstacles, and stop time with the return of Chaos Control! A Journey Through Time and Dimensions Relive signature levels from Shadow’s previous adventures and accelerate through mind-bending stages in both 3D and 2D, warped by Black Doom’s influence as Shadow works to piece together the timeline and thwart his evil plans. Explore the New White Space Stretch your legs in an all-new hub world inspired by the open-zone gameplay of Sonic Frontiers. As Shadow gains new powers, he can explore further and uncover the secrets hidden throughout! An Epic Time-Traveling Sonic Adventure Past meets present in SONIC GENERATIONS! When Dr. Eggman teams up with his past self and the mysterious Time Eater to erase their past defeats and rewrite history, they scatter Sonic and his friends across space and time. Now, Modern and Classic Sonic will have to team up to defeat this dastardly trio and restore their timeline to normal! The Best of Both Worlds, Remastered Spin dash through a greatest-hits collection of 3D and 2D versions of iconic stages from past Sonic games, now with updated visuals and reworked cinematics. More Collectibles, Bonus Content, and more! Rescue Chao hiding in every level, rack up the highest pinball score in the Casino Nights Zone, and check out the museum for behind-the-scenes art, music, and more!

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic X Shadow Generations is one of the best gaming experiences in the last few years. Taking the amazing Sonic Generations and remastering it to modern platforms is great, but it's the new title featuring Shadow that really elevates the game to what, in my opinion, can be considered the best Sonic game in the series. With a wonderfully written and preformed story, stellar animation, kickass music and creative level design, this is a statement that the last few years of Sonic haven't been a fluke, Sonic Team are driven by a desire to be seen as a world class developer again, and after the lovely experience that was Frontiers, Shadow Generations builds upon the open zone and action stage gameplay of it's older brother and further refines and developers it, giving us one of the best boost games, and one of the best platformers in recent years.Selection of stages are really good, and every level, regardless of 2D or 3D, is fantastic and use the doom powers and base abilities in cleaver ways. The addition of a online time attack is very much appreciated, and helps add to the game's replayability. Boss designs are really solid too, and carry the flashy action from Frontiers, especially the final boss. The only complain I have is that Shadow Generations isn't longer, but if that's the only complaint, then that's a strong indicator that I simply want more. Sonic and Shadow isn't just back, he's the best he's ever been. If you're a Sonic fan or someone wanting to jump in, this is it. Sonic X Shadow Generations is amazing, and a solid 9/10.(Review based on my PS5 experience, I'll update it after I fully finish the PC version on Steam Deck. Sonic Generations runs at a solid 60fps on Deck.)
_childDocuments_.name: SONIC X SHADOW GENERATIONS

_childDocuments_.review: Original Sonic gens was and still is a fantastic game, and the highest praise I can offer here is it's basically the same game. Still great 3D sonic boost levels, really fun interpretations of 2D sonic, has some minor features/upgrades here and there but nothing groundbreaking but, importantly, nothing gamebreaking (looking at you, colors ultimate).Shadow gens, on the other hand, has got to be one of the most polished and fun 3D sonic games ever. Long and branching levels that aren't just "boost to win", minimal jank, creative and fun powerups, the game has it all. The 3D hub is also surprisingly great, like Sonic Frontiers zones but more condensed and less floating rail spam. The bosses are actually fun and the story doesn't make me want to gouge my eyes out. The only negative is that it's short. There is high replay value, getting better times, getting collectibles, and a good amount of challenges to attempt, but only 4 or so hours if you focus the main content, but it's a damn good time nonetheless.Hope sonic team has finally cracked the code on 3D sonic formula and this can be the standard going forward

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Generations is fantastic, and I believe is worth the price by itself, BUT only if you are a big Sonic fan. If you are just a moderate fan, I still think the whole package with Sonic Gens is totally worth it as well. Since the Sonic portion is just a remaster/port I won't talk much about it. It's still the same great game from years ago, and the added hidden Chao has been a fun addition. I think the cutscene rewrites are fine. Better than the original but nothing mind blowing. However Shadow Gens is great. Easily best performance from current Shadow's VA, the controls are tight, the levels are designed SO well. You can play each like 5 times and take completely different routes each time, and the open world hub is so fun to run around in and explore. It's so nice to have a Sonic game finally take itself more seriously again as well with the story/writing, just like Frontiers. The doom powers are so much fun, although the morph ability does get some getting used to. And naturally, the OST is chock full of bangers left and right. Only major complaint is that a zone that Shadow has never been to is used for one of his main stages. Would have much rather had a level theme from Shadow the Hedgehog instead. Overall though, the stage used is still designed amazingly, and recommend picking this game up, even if you decide to wait for a slight sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Final Review For SHADOW GENERATIONS: Right off the bat the presentation is stunning, every cut scene is so insanely well animated and is so detailed and smooth, such a happy surprise too see things how they should be. The colors, animation, art-style changes and the music is all top notch this time around like ALL of it. There is so much polish in all the animations in Shadow generations, there is so much attention to detail I never thought I'd see in a sonic game again. I cannot stress this enough, THIS GAME LOOKS AMAZING. The cutscenes are absolutely stunning and amazing, I cant put it into words how good they are!The controls/how it plays: Its what you'd expect, its sonic frontiers but smoother and more refined. So its very pleasant to skate around and play with the movement. Its fun and rewarding like before. I can say this game controls great and plays very well. You can customize how it plays like frontiers so you can change what you want which is always a plus. The only control issue I had was the doom powers, they were a bit hard to control, some more than other but overall I have not had any issues so far. Soundtrack: You can already guess lmao, i dont even need to say anythingStory: Im still progressing but I like it so far! A return to previous story parts and is fleshing out the inbetween parts that happened to shadow while sonic was doing his thing in the 2010's...EDIT: I finished the story and It was super fun and exciting, It was so nice seeing some characters back in modern day! I dont wanna spoil anything so PLAY IT. Gameplay: The hub world takes inspiration for Sonic Generations and Sonic Frontiers and combining the two for fun areas so explore with nooks and crannies for goodies along the way. Its fun to explore and fun to move, so its good. The stages are your typical boost formula stages but finally expanded to feel less one lane like some previous titles so there are many ways to go, so its not like your usual song and dance that you are so used too, look around you might find a new path. Theres way more replay-ability due to the level design being improved and greatly expanded. So its like the cyberspace stages in frontiers but a bit longer and better thought out. Gameplay loop is very funLevel design: This is by far the best boost formula levels in the series, I cannot give anymore praise in the quality and replay-ability. They are on par or even surpassing Sonic Unleashes day time stages, THEY ARE THAT GOOD. The improvement from forces to frontiers and now to this, They got it down now. Boss Battles: They are so good, so cinematic and thrilling, super fun to fight them. They are about as good as frontiers boss fights, not as epic but they are still VERY good.Complaints: IT IS TOO SHORT, I WANT MORE and I find the doom powers not super fun to control personally. A cool addition but I didnt enjoy them that much.Conclusion: This  review has gone on long enough so the point is that the game blew my expectations outta da water with its stunning presentation and game-play improvements from sonic frontiers. If you like sonic frontiers and generations you will be very pleased with this game. This is the best sonic gameThis is the right direction.9/10
