_childDocuments_.review: In short: it's peak fictionThe Sonic Generations remake aspect of this package is fairly straight forward and does what it says on the tin: it updates the visual ever so slightly, adds a few bells and whistles such as the drop dash for Classic Sonic; what you'd expect from a remaster. Still a classic 10+ years later and Sega largely left it intact save a few minor story changes.The Shadow side of the package though, is what makes this worth grabbing. If you're like me, you were probably expecting this to play just like Sonic Generations with a Shadow skin and a few new levels. However, it's difficult to convey just how more depth Shadow's unique skill set adds to the experience. If nothing else, it's a testament to how much potential the "Boost formula" has for growth and expansion. These abilities are complimented by some of the best level design Sonic Team has released in recent memory and really invites player creativity; a true playground for player expression. Unexpectedly, the story included in the Shadow side of things is also surprisingly endearing and well written (for what it is) and nails Shadow's character in a way that hasn't been done since Sonic Adventure 2.However, with all the high praise that has been given to the Shadow side of the game, it does create an awkward problem where it makes the Sonic side feel a little dated by comparison, still a great experience though and definitely worth a playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: Though the base game technically has more stages, Shadow's campaign is more than qualified to be considered a full-fledged speed platforming experience with vastly superior level design, visuals, and overall presentation versus Sonic Frontiers. Though it can't compete with the sheer size and scale of Frontiers, it does seem to improve upon the "open zone" design and actually has fully realized levels (finally).It's not as blistering fast as the base game, but it's uniquely "Shadow", offering different kinds of play-styles and tons of ideas that are executed surprisingly well. The story is pretty light (and only fans will really pick up on the tiny details sprinkled about), but it's meaningful for those who have followed Shadow for a long time, waiting for his character to be done right.Honestly an impressive feat from Sonic Team, they nailed it. Fun set-pieces, solid level design all-around, and lots of replayability. Gets me even more hopeful and excited for the direction of future Sonic games. Shadow's campaign really just sweetens the deal of this remaster, which is definitely worth getting if you never got the chance to play the base game. Though if you want a nitpick, it's probably that there are moments where the hub world and 2D levels can feel a bit too cluttered, but maybe that's because I've been looking at the barren emptiness of Frontiers for a while now.

_childDocuments_.review: ✨ 100% Completed! ✨After fully completing both games in Sonic X Shadow Generation, I can honestly say this was an incredible experience from start to finish. Sega has nailed it with this one, striking the perfect balance between the nostalgia of classic Sonic and Shadow games and a fresh, modern take. The gameplay is smooth and fast-paced, the levels are beautifully designed, and every moment is filled with pure adrenaline.The story was engaging, the levels were AMAZING, and the attention to detail is just stellar. With unlockable secrets, fantastic boss fights, and replayability that kept me coming back for more, this game was worth every second spent on that 100% completion.I highly recommend this to any Sonic fan, Shadow fan, or anyone looking for a quality platformer. Sega, if you're reading this—you’re on the right track! Keep it up!

_childDocuments_.review: Like all the other reviews, it looks great but it falls flat in a few areas that just kills me. Firstly, I hate the open world/over world concept (or at least the execution. I found that it was really difficult to find my way around and everything felt really tedious. The extra missions were fine up until I got to the forces and frontiers stages, I'm pretty sure that shadow isn't even in frontiers but I didn't play it. But the frontier stage was god awful, incredibly frustrating and forced me to use the worst ability in the game that controls terribly. The doom morph ability is just bad.How is there not a single stage from the original Shadow game?? That makes no sense, replace the forces or (preferably) frontiers stage with Westopolis or Sky troops, or hell maybe even Eggmans carnival stage, i don't care but just have something. I think the game is fine if you're not an avid fan of Shadow, most people won't care that frontiers has a level in here, most people won't feel like the controls are that bad. _childDocuments_.review: Two games in one!  First Off. You get a brand new shadow campaign which might be the best playing 3D Sonic game to date. It feels like they've finally found a true happy medium between the almost car like controls and spectacle of "Boost" Era games like Unleashed, Colors, and Generations and my prefered more twitchy precise platforming of the adventure games Like Adventure 1, Adventure 2, and Heros.  The levels are gorgeous, of decent length,  sound amazing, and are highly replayable. Its the first time in a very long time I got really into the time attack mode in a sonic game, spent a good hour or two honing the perfect runs on Chaos Island and the like. The open zone here returns from Frontiers but is a lot more compact and frankly more enjoyable because of it. The story is excellent and written by the very talented Ian Flynn who has been spear heading the shockingly plot heavy sonic comics for a while now. Ian is still doing some ground work restablishing Sonics tone after a solid ten years of plot light games just like he was in frontiers. I just wish it was longer. I completed shadows main story in a little under four hours. But if you're not a freak of nature like me who bleeds sonic I'd expect it to be closer to 6.  You also get Generations, which if you're a pc player is not very different from the version that got delisted from steam a couple months ago besides the heavy rewrite of the script and a drop dash. I think its running on a way older version of the engine. The game tabs out and relaunches when you pick it and its missing alot of the graphical options that the shadow campaign has. Biggest bummer is Unlike Shadows campaign sonics is locked to 60 FPS (Sonic games are better at 120FPS once you've had it you cant go back) and no TAA. So youre stuck with old school FXAA. This isn't I guess a mark AGAINST generations as its a 13 year old game at this point but it was pretty hard to come back to after shadows story as it controls alot worse and the side content isn't nearly as fun as shadows.  If you never played either before I would probaly start with sonics story first and then go to shadows.

_childDocuments_.review: This "game" is a glorified 15 dollar DLC that I paid 60 dollars to get 3 day early access just to beat it within 1 day (After my work day too) before it "officially" comes out for everyone else.To get the Sonic Generations side out of the way it is basically the same game. I've played this game probably a dozen times as I got this game on launch in 2011 for the Xbox 360 when I was still a kid and played it for years and years beating my time and scores and getting all the S ranks and beating all the missions. Besides the final boss the game is incredible and will forever have its legacy cemented as a true Sonic anniversary celebration. The only thing that is different besides it running better than before, is that classic Sonic has the drop dash from Sonic Mania. Since that game every iteration of Classic Sonic has had that ability. I love the ability so it's fine by me.Shadow Generations is a good add-on to this game. It took me about 4ish hours to beat so it's about 2/3rds the length of the base game. There's only 6 stages instead of 9 and there's 4 bosses but no rival battles. The stages themselves are extremely good. I had seen that most of the fan base was worried it was going to be "Boost to win" type of gameplay similar to Sonic Forces but thankfully it is not like that. All the stages are pretty lengthy and have a lot of variety in them to play them over and over again much like the base game and THAT, I think, is one of the most important parts of a Sonic game. They really did Kingdom Valley justice and made it a lot of fun for Shadow rather than a slog-fest like the original level and game it came from.The bosses are pretty unique and I like the selection they chose. However, to get to these bosses you have to do all the challenges related to a stage which there are 4 of them. Unlike the base game where you do 1 and get the key you have to collect multiple keys to unlock the boss stage and it definitely feels like a lot of padding to lengthen the time of the add-on and I personally feel it breaks the pacing of the game a bit. With that the game still plays fine and feels great and it generally was a good time.The music is great and the stage selection is pretty good. I did think it was a little weird they used a stage from both Sonic Forces and Sonic Frontiers. I thought they'd put a bit more Shadow stages in there but the stages were really good. They especially did justice to the Sonic Forces stage. I don't remember diddly-♥♥♥♥ from the stage from the original game (And I've played it twice) and I remember at least 3 spots from act 1 alone in this add-on.Which bringing up the acts... The main other weird thing I have to mention is that since this game is still based off of Sonic Generation the acts still kind of function the same. Act 1 is purely 3D with high speed action behind Shadow while Act 2 is pretty much all 2D side-scrolling like Classic Sonic. It makes full use of the camera and will have spots like the 3D style but it's not free motion so you're stuck going one-way. It gives me vibes of the Sonic Generations for 3DS where modern Sonic is still 2D but some sections will kinda, ya know, change the camera a bit. It's nothing bad but just a little weird and it definitely took me about 2 or so levels to notice...All in all the game is good. I don't really care that I spent 60 bux to re-buy Sonic Generations (I already had just the original on my Steam account) for a 3rd time just to play essentially a 15 dollar add on for a nearly 15 year old game that I was able to complete within a weekday. I hope this gets popular enough that Sonic team sees us longing for more Sonic variety and bring back different playable characters and deeper storylines. Deeper than what we've gotten as Sonic Frontiers was definitely a step in the right directions. If you're a long time Sonic fan such as myself you'll enjoy this as much as I did, but if you're strapped for cash then I really don't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: NON SPOILER REVIEW Sonic Generations: This is just a general review of the game, mainly revolving around Shadow Generations. The remaster is worth it alone with Sonic Generations if you've never played that game, it's short and sweet! The presentation is altered in some areas, and there are minor additions but that's it from what I've seen and played. In short, it's a great game for the most part and it's easily one of the best 3D Sonic games at least in my opinion. Shadow Generations:My main hope with this portion of the remaster was that it would adapt some of Frontiers ideas and further polish said ideas and execution when it came to both the boost and Open Zone. While I do enjoy Frontiers, especially after the updates, I still couldn't help but be a bit bummed of how we wouldn't see the progression of this formula for quite a while. The jankyness in some areas and lack of polish really held the game back for me. However, I'm happy to say that this game further validates this new formula. Once again, am I addicted to the gameplay loop of getting collectibles and jumping onto boost stages before I get myself into a boss fight.Shadow controls even better than Sonic did in Frontiers in my opinion. It mainly has to do with the jump being more loose, allowing for the player to make more precise jumps. As well as the jump not killing your speed, two major issues I had with Sonic back in Frontiers despite agreeing that he does control pretty well otherwise. Not only that, but the moveset for Shadow feels a lot more curated and utilized for the game. Of course, Shadow Gens is smaller but still. The abilities and chaos control respectively, opened up a lot of level design potential for both the Open Zone and boost levels. You can see that throughout the entire game, never did it feel gimmicky or anything like that. All of them felt like they elevated the levels even more than they already were. This game challenges you with its timing and reactionary based boost level design. Akin more to Unleashed than Generations when it comes to difficulty, at least from my first playthrough. So, you'll have to use your abilities and moves carefully and efficiently. This is true for both 3D and 2D stages. With 3D stages focusing more on the branching paths and cinematics, while 2D stages focus more on the fast pacing. It made the game that much more engaging along with the creative level design. These new elements makes the boost feel refreshing enough to last the entire game while you get further into the game. This can most definitely be reflected in the challenges, making you get used to these abilities between major bosses and areas. The bosses are well done too, with multiple attack patterns, phases, and very cool cutscenes to go along with them.Speaking of which, the presentation of this game is the best I've seen since Unleashed. The cutscenes are so well done, it makes the adventure feel larger in scale even if the story is simple by nature while still feeling personal and character driven. This along with the cinematic moments in the stages made me enjoy this story. The game just looks great in general, and it sounds great too with the soundtrack with the remixes. The Open Zone is very engaging, especially since these abilities are more utilized for the level design there than abilities Sonic had in base Frontiers. There's also more variety which helps matters more, as it makes traversal between areas diverse, fun, and seem less if you know what you're doing. The platforming is well thought out, the collectibles are easy to spot but are attached to some platform challenges at times demanding your skills, and the different types of challenges can have some difficulty to them. Overall, Shadow Generations is a great game inside of another great game. I do wish a couple of the doom abilities controlled better, and there were some boost challenges that could've been more creative. I also think there are some stages that are better than others. However, all of this being said this was just a solid game throughout. Even at its lowest points, I still had quite a lot of fun. I hope this becomes the standard for 3D Sonic games going forward. I know that I've been comparing it to Frontiers in this review, but that's because it's a point of reference as to how Sonic Team has already improved upon it even if it isn't the same Sonic Team that made Frontiers. I think Sonic Team and SEGA should be proud of themselves with this release. I hope they continue to improve, and I can't wait to see what the future offers. We're really back as a franchise now.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is about the Shadow campaign.It's the best thing to come out of Sonic Team in a long, long time. The very few complaints I can possibly levy against this game are incredibly minor and nitpicky, and do not detract from the overall quality of the product. It seeks to innovate upon tried and true ideas and it does so with incredible flair and panache. It's got wonderful visual and sound work, it's cinematic, it's fast, it's bold, it's something more primal and visceral than Sonic's gameplay. I have never in my life had more fun playing as Shadow the Hedgehog than I have here. The story, while relatively simple and somewhat predictable, is very nice and easy to follow, and doesn't really pull from the gameplay at all.I found some of the new Doom Power mechanics to be kind of questionable, but they are fun twists if nothing else. I also encountered several glitches during my run of the main campaign, this is par for the course for Sonic Team, but I won't deny it did detract from my experience at least a little bit. I wouldn't expect big things from characters that aren't Shadow here either though, this is his story and he's mainly the one carrying it from start to finish. I will say I do love this new version of Black Doom, it's likely we may never see him again after this, and if this is how he is to be remembered, then I can't complain at all.Overall I had a blast with Sonic X Shadow, it's a solid experience well worth your time and money. If you've never liked Shadow the Hedgehog before and want to see what all the fuss is about, give this one a whirl and see what you've been missing. Easily 9/10. Wish there was more of it.

_childDocuments_.review: If you’re a fan of Sonic the Hedgehog and looking for a nostalgic yet fresh experience, Sonic X Shadow Generations could be the game that bridges the best elements of past Sonic titles with new twists. Although it isn’t an official title by Sega, the game brings together beloved Sonic and Shadow gameplay elements with a unique focus on the dynamic between these iconic characters.StorylineThe game’s storyline is relatively straightforward, leaning on the classic Sonic Generations plot, with Sonic and Shadow teaming up to restore time and space to normal. Players travel through time, revisiting different stages and alternate versions of iconic zones from Sonic’s past. Seeing both Sonic and Shadow tackle these familiar stages is a nostalgic experience, especially for fans who grew up with Sonic Adventure 2 or Sonic Heroes.GameplayThe gameplay merges the best of Sonic’s speed with Shadow’s chaos-driven attacks, bringing a fresh take to the classic running and platforming action. Each character comes with distinct abilities: Sonic has his traditional boost and homing attack, while Shadow wields Chaos Control and uses teleportation techniques, which can be a game-changer in various stages. This dual gameplay style creates exciting moments that keep the pace varied and challenging.Levels are vibrant and well-designed, with the 3D graphics doing justice to the original zones, now updated with intricate details and alternate paths to encourage replayability. One downside is that the camera sometimes struggles with the high-speed shifts, but overall, the level design gives players plenty of room to explore both Sonic’s and Shadow’s unique skills.Visuals & AudioGenerations revives familiar tunes and graphics with a modern touch. The graphics are polished, giving beloved stages a fresh look while retaining their classic feel. The soundtrack deserves particular praise, as it brings back remastered versions of iconic tracks like City Escape and Green Hill Zone alongside new renditions for Shadow’s stages.Replay ValueWith collectibles, unlockable character abilities, and online leaderboards, Sonic X Shadow Generations gives fans plenty to strive for beyond the main story. For dedicated fans, replaying levels to achieve faster times and discovering hidden paths for additional rewards is both fun and rewarding.Final VerdictSonic X Shadow Generations is an impressive fusion of nostalgic elements and new gameplay innovations. While it’s not without minor flaws, the collaboration between Sonic and Shadow, combined with the updated level designs and engaging soundtrack, makes this a worthy addition to any Sonic fan’s collection. Whether you’re a veteran or a newcomer, this game’s high-speed action and captivating storyline make it a must-play for platforming fans.Rating: 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I have to leave a good review so SEGA knows they got this one right when they look at their score. I am only going to talk about Shadow Generations in this - Sonic Generations plays like it did a decade ago.Gameplay is crisp for the most part - playing as Shadow just feels GOOD. From the way Chaos Control was implemented (Stopping the stage timer, freezing enemies and obstacles) to the various powers Shadow gets through the game - no two stages ever feel alike, or boring. The game is easy to pick up and play for veterans, and rewarding for newbies who are still learning how Sonic games work. The visuals are stunning - everything is a spectacle, from the Chaos Control intermissions in some stages, to the simple act of chaining homing attacks, foregoing the 'homing missile ball' and instead leaning into Shadow's 'warp', as we saw in the trailer for Shadow the Hedgehog 20 years ago.The OST blew me out of the WATER. From hearing Crush 40 again for the first time in years, to RichardEB featuring in a couple songs, to TEDDYLOID remixing others - it's like Sonic Team woke up and remembered what they were absolutely KILLING IT with in the mid-2000's, and brought in the A-Team to do it again. I am without words.Sound design is spectacular, full of impact, and most notably - if you've got a keen ear, you'll hear old sounds mixed in with the new, /just/ for people like you and I. The rockets from Sonic Adventure 2, in Radical Highway, the goop pipes from Shadow the Hedgehog when you find a Chaos Control 'rail' - the sound team seamlessly incorporated assets from two decades ago into something new, /just/ to dogwhistle to long-time fans, and it is /incredible/. I hope whoever made that decision sees this, as unlikely as it is. Hats off.The stage length is a bit of a hurdle - a lot of the stages feel more like marathons rather than sprints, and that can be frustrating when attempting a 'perfect' run of any stage.The Doom Surf mechanic is disappointing in that you cannot boost while doing it - but feels fine otherwise.Doom MORPH, however, is a classic case of Sonic Team experimenting and just /barely/ missing the mark. It feels a little janky, a bit frustrating, and breaks the rhythm of play very easily - or I just suck at it, I can't tell which. That being said, it's noteworthy to me, so I'm still typing this.Wish there'd been /maybe/ one or two more zones with two acts each - finishing the Shadow side of the game leaves you with a distinct feeling that the game could have gone on a /little/ longer - but you are also getting Sonic Generations with it, so.Overall, fantastic game, 9/10. Not sure the deluxe edition rewards are worth the price - but the base game is worth what you pay and then some.

_childDocuments_.review: i was expecting a bit more from this game than what we have at the moment (actual updated models, textures, visuals and such - mainly thinking something like HE2/Sonic Frontiers assets) but despite that, i really liked it in a way of revisiting the game slightly updated and bundled with what matters the most (Shadow Generations)sure that the changes on existing models and voice acting/dialog changes were unnecessary but outside of that revisiting the game was really fun, and the addition to a new game mode made exploration and treasure hunting a new nostalgia for the oldies of the franchisethe DLCs could have also been way better worked on since the skins dont include Super transformations, or cutscenes which is a bummer, yet its still a nice step for SEGA/Sonic Team to overlook those details and upgrade in their next titlewe all needed this game - its visuals, its difficulty, the little yet big details, the story/plot.. makes this game to good that i cant stop praising it. i personally was expecting it would be a lot more like HE1/Sonic Generations in terms of engine and controls, but it gave a better name to that with HE2 and its power. theres always a lot to do in this game that can make someone busy, specially if youre a thirsty one for S Ranks and Perfect Clears. bringing back old characters from SA2/SH (Adventure Era) and ShTH/06 (Dark Era) was also the greatest decision someone could ever made; proving theres always space for improvement on character design and development despite bosses not being entirely real or (probably) irrelevant to the franchise in generalTerio's DLC was a bit controversial at first but regardless its a great addon to the game that also makes old fanatics to scream of surprise. it was a charismatic move from SEGA/Sonic Team to the people who loved Shadow's earliest designsthis is the way SEGA. this is the game people wanted - not because of the simple parts of the gameplay but for the rich story and challenges we have to face.

I can't ever reccommend sonic games at full price to those who don't already like the series. Now if you're a sonic fan, yes get it. Its short, but tons of replay ability for both Sonic and Shadow. The Sonic portion is virtually unchanged. Some control differences to help it match up with Shadow's part. Shadow Generations is so much fun. Stages arent small bite sizes that feel like they never get started like in forces. _childDocuments_.review: It's... Sonic Generations. Although the game barely feels touched up, (in fact, I ran into more glitches than I ever had with the original) It's still the original game we all know and love. The extra Chao collectibles are cute, but don't really add much besides another thing you have to spend time finding. I personally don't mind the new referential rewrite outside of a few differences, (Amy, why?????) but m main problem is the voice acting. Most of the characters actively sound worse to me, Sonic sounds more deep and grovely and Tails sounds really scratchy. I also just have some bias for the original VAs, which make's Roger's performance sting more.All that aside...You're not here for Sonic. This is a Shadow game that includes a remaster of a 13-year-old game. And boy, does Shadow Generations deliver. It's hard to form a rational, critical statement without gushing. That's how much I loved this game.Some spoilers for gameplay mechanics and levels ahead:Shadow plays about how you'd expect: Like Sonic, but his animations are unique and he has some major differences. Shadow can double jump, his homing attack makes him teleport (which can actually let him move through and past obstacles), and has Chaos Control which is a GAME CHANGER. Not only does it allow you to create new paths, stop alternate paths from closing, etc., but these level time limits felt stricter to me, harder to get S ranks, and Chaos Control STOPS THE TIMER. You can use this feature to help get better ranks, and I love that. I wish I had much to say about the new Doom powers, but I don't. They're fun ways to traverse levels and even fight bosses. They look super cool, though. The levels and bosses are phenomenal and look beautiful. (They even have me enjoying something that;s from Forces!!)My only issues, which are minor, are the challenges and the game length. I did not like the challenges in Sonic Generations. The only upside to them was that outside of the one required challenge for each zone, they're purely optional. I enjoyed the challenges more in Shadow Gens, but they're still challenges. And you HAVE to complete every challenge in the main story to beat the game. This isn't deal-breaking for me, I just didn't love it.My other issue is... The game is sooooo short. We weren't promised otherwise and I didn't expect more, especially due to being a double pack, but I was loving every second of this game and 3 hours is just NOT enough. Here's hoping they can continue this formula and even Make another full Shadow game in the future.I fully recommend this game. I can't recommend it enough. It's an already beloved Sonic game bundled with a masterpiece. If you love Sonic or even a new Sonic fan, this game is absolutely worth your time. Now stop reading this and go play it!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the best Sonic game to release since the original Sonic Generations in 2011. Sonic Generations was already a good game and they didn't change much. If you liked Generations before, you'll like it here. They made some interesting changes to the cutscenes, for better and for worse, but Sonic Gens didn't have much of a story anyway so it doesn't matter much. The new chao rescue is a neat addition, but are a bit tedious to find. The chao can be hidden in some really obscure spots and are easy to miss so you'll have to really stop and look around to find them.Shadow Generations feels like an improvement in every way, building off of the original Sonic Gens formula with the lessons learned from Frontiers. The level design is on par with the Sonic Gens but the controls are so much tighter and more responsive! Shadow's doom powers only enhance the gameplay and add new ways to traverse the levels. Far better than anything like the Wisps from Colors, which were already pretty good. The open zone hub is also fantastic. It's an absolute joy to traverse and I spent hours wandering around trying to collect everything.Basically, everything here is great! If you haven't played Sonic Generations yet, I highly recommend picking this up. If you have played it, it's still worth buying for Shadow Generations alone, even if it's a bit short.

_childDocuments_.review: I beat Shadow Generations in about 4 and a half hours and plan to 100% complete it. I expected the game to be short and don't regret my purchase as a Sonic fan. Sonic Generations is very fun, and I have replayed the modern Sonic levels occasionally over the years before this game was released, but this is a review of the Shadow section of the game. The levels were fun and really shine when you decide to take the side paths and try to get the quickest time possible. Every level regardless of size seems to have multiple paths or challenges to get faster and faster times. Many times the S ranks are unfortunately easy to get, but that did not stop me from playing a single stage for 2 hours to get a better time for the leader board. The levels have a focus on adding abilities and gimmicks, then rewarding you for using those gimmicks and abilities well with better time. Chaos Control is an interesting one, because it also freezes the level timer. Suddenly spending that second to kill enemies might be worth it, and timing it correctly to use shortcuts, or to avoid freezing something you don't want to freeze is important.The hub area between the levels was neat, and reminded me of the open world stuff I liked from Sonic Frontiers. If you liked some of the open world areas from that game, you'll like the hub from this one. The bosses were good, but the second one was a stand out that I immediately decided to replay to S rank it. That boss was amazing to me, and actually had mechanics I felt was worth trying to improve on.The story is good. I really liked seeing Maria and Gerald be actual characters, and was excited whenever a cutscene came up. I do have a minor criticism I wanted to express:     SPOILER:

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Generations is still as good as it was before. Not much had change with it beside some small stuff like collectible chao or drop dash added for both modern and classic Sonic.Shadow Generations is simply amazing. The best 3d level design and overall gameplay. Shadow controls amazing compared to the predecessor, Sonic Frontiers, where I thought Sonic controls were extremely janky. Shadow's Doom powers are great and a better addition than something like the Wisps power ups seen in a few Sonic games. Level choices are good except for the fact that Shadow's own game doesn't get level for some reason.While I did like Chaos Island, it was a strange choice for a stage as it is obviously reused asset and Shadow wasn't even in Sonic Frontiers. Whereas something like Westopolis or Sky Troops would be better fit than Chaos Island. Still, all the levels have multiple paths and agency to make the player actually interact with the stage. Unlike something like Sonic Forces where the game plays itself. With Kingdom Valley being my favorite stage.The overworld is also amazing as I think this overworld is much better than what is seen in Sonic Frontiers. Its smaller than Frontiers' overworld, but is more enjoyable to explore for collectibles than Frontiers. A lot of the challenges are platforming are much more interesting than the ones seen in Frontiers.Music is amazing as always like any other Sonic game. With my favorite being Second phase of the Final Boss theme as it is a All Hail Shadow remix or Chaos Island Act 1.My only problem with the Shadow Generations is that is also short like Sonic Generations. It is a bit longer than Sonic Generations but it is still short overall. I recommend this game for newcomers and old Sonic fans. _childDocuments_.review: Alright, after 100% completing Sonic x Shadow generations, I can finally say that the game, is mid.I will start with the good parts, that being the shadow part of this "bundle".The shadow gameplay is great, although it suffers from the act system where one is 3d and one is 2d for each stage, it is fairly good, even for the 2d one's since you still keep the modern style gameplay and you're not limited to classic sonic.The game doesn't have that many good parts, boss fights are as boring as any normal sonic boss is to fight. You're here for the main stages, the main fun sonic/shadow gameplay, and you get that, for about 30 minutes or less. You have 6 main stages with 2 acts, then after every 2 or so main stage, you'll go on a side quest to do challenges, just like in generations. These are nothing to write home about and they are quite boring. I found them more there just to extend your gameplay, they were not enjoyable to me.You have 4 bosses including the last boss, and again, the bosses felt half-assed with gimmicks that didn't flow well for me, some extra polish would be appreciated.Then we have the story of the game, and the story is quite good. It completely failed to capture me in it though since the game was only like 3 hours long. Oh look, it's Maria, wait how are you here again?It was just extremely weird, and yes I know it's because of the time anomaly, I did pay attention, but nobody is going to get captured and immersed in a game that is 3 hours long, half of that time is you doing challenges, and the others are being in the hubworld, cutscenes and main stages.I'll give shadow gens a 6/10I do think they should've went all in on the shadow stuff and make it full price instead of throwing generations in there because again, it was just too short. The shadow story is good for a sonic game, but with the length just makes it dip a little.Now, onto sonic generationsWhy did we get a drop dash for modern sonic, that we can't turn off?This game was not designed with a drop dash in mind and you can clearly tell if you use it in game, every single time I used it was accidental.It's the same generations, with some really bad camera glitches at times, and you have the addition of chaos here, that you can collect in each stage as a collectable, it was kind of fun finding all of them.I hated doing the challenges just for that 100% but yeah, it's just the same ol' generations that we didn't need a remake of, just there to get this game to a higher price.Worst of all however, this throws mod compatibility out of the window, previous sonic gens mods DO NOT work with this version at the time I am making this review. Modders are actively working on getting things to work, but the hedgemodmanager currently also only supports the shadow version of this "bundle".That means NO PROJECT UNLEASHED levels for this game currentlyI'll give generations an 8/10 compared to the OG version of it, because it feels lazy and no mod compatibility.TL;DRI think the original sonic generations is better than this, and the only reason you would ever buy this version is to get the shadow gameplay that lasts you a maximum of 3 hours of fun, 9 hours for a completionist maybe, with the addition of 11 hours to complete generations as well.I do not hate sonic and I am a long term fan, I was just very disappointed with SEGA's attempt to squeeze out money for something half-assed.Thank you for reading

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Generations portion is a banger. No issues with it so far, runs great and is a blast to play through. The level design is a huge step up from the previous two titles and finally manages to make excellent use of the graphics and physics engine the team has been using since Forces.Edit: After playing and speedrunning more of the Shadow's stages, I really came to appreciate the design of Chaos Control. Activating it pauses the timer as well, encouraging you to go out of your way to fill up the Chaos gauge as many times as possible. You don't always want to immediately use Chaos Control though, sometimes it'll stop objects that will block off your path. Knowing when to use Chaos Control and how to get as many uses out of it as possible is key to getting recordbreaking times in Shadow's stages. It's always fun to use it too, especially with some of the unique boss interactions ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ he's kicking assAs for the Sonic Generations "remaster" portion, it's a mixed bag. I appreciate the improved UI and in-game settings menu as well as custom keybinds, but the game has worse performance and worse loading times than the 2011 version, in fact the performance seems to be worse than the Shadow portion? Presumably thanks to Denuvo. Areas like Rooftop Run's tower climb section (Act 1) stutter a lot.Speaking of Denuvo, playing on a choppy internet connection can cause the game to freeze for a (split) second, a big pace breaker for a Sonic game- wait this is a single player game why is my internet connection causing my game to freeze??? We love DRM softwareLastly, the Drop Dash is a big fumble. I love using it when playing as Classic Sonic, as it neatly ties into his movement as Mania has demonstrated. However, it was implemented as a skill that takes up a slot and 30/100 points. The more annoying part is that, since skills are disabled in missions, you can't use it for the extra side content and I've had a lot of moments where I wanted to drop dash in those.For some forsaken reason however, it is part of Modern Sonic's base kit and cannot be disabled. This led to a number of times where I accidentally drop dashed into a bottomless pit in his stages. It also feels redundant to use here, as the boost button has you covered already and you rarely run out of it, especially when you use any skill that increases the gauge. (its also faster btw)I would (have) recommended getting the original version of Sonic Generations if it wasn't for the fact that it got delisted and locked behind a $60 bundle. While it lacks the UI and settings improvements of the 2024 version, it more than makes up for it with a lack of performance issues and huge modding support behind it.If you haven't played the OG Sonic Generations, I would absolutely recommend buying this game, the price tag is justifiable for the two games you're getting. If you're like me however and have already spent $20 on the original game, you'll have to be willing to spend $50 for essentially just the Shadow portion, in which case I'd recommend waiting for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A spectacular remaster of an absolute timeless classic Sonic game from the Xbox 360 era that also adds a whole, brand-new Shadow campaign with its own levels. The original game getting remastered is amazing as it is, but we are also getting a new story to go along with it akin to that of Super Mario 3D World + Bowser's Fury. It's a remaster and an expansion at the same time, and it doesn't lose it's luster and is just as fun (and sometimes frustrating) as the original. I am serious when I saw this: this is definitely one of the best remasters in recent memory, because it not only keeps most, if not all of the things about the original Sonic Generations that made it such a hit in the first place, but we also get a whole new Shadow Generations and get to experience a story contrasting to that of Sonic's. If Sonic's story is the Saturday morning cartoon, then Shadow's is the gritty OG Teen Titans-esque anime. Getting the original game remastered was fine enough, but the new campaign with Shadow the Hedgehog is truly going above and beyond. Definitely the icing on the cake.An absolute recommend from me. Definitely someone around a 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has 100% both games I'll try to make this relatively quick and concise:SONIC GENERATIONS This is the fan favorite game people know and love from way back when for the most part. As far as additions go, there are the chao hidden in each level which are a fantastic way to further expand replayability (arguably this game's strongest aspect), and the drop dash which... Is a bit of a hit or miss. Don't get me wrong it works great for classic sonic but for modern I found it to be a bit of a nuisance since he wasn't exactly designed with it in mind. Although that might just be due to my old habits from the original version. Either way it's certainly not a deal breaker.The most major difference in this version is the rewriting of the cutscenes which I personally liked but some people admittedly found the writing dissatisfying. With that said, this game is definitely worth the hype gameplay wise, especially if you didn't get to experience it before... And it's not even the main attraction!SHADOW GENERATIONSI really don't have much to say, this is honestly the best sonic game we've ever gotten. The boost format has finally reached it's absolute peak with fast paced, creative level design allowing for a plethora of different routes and skips on both 2d and 3d levels. The new doom mechanics have all been excellent additions to spice things up (yes even the doom morph, it's harder to learn than the rest but mastering it feels extremely rewarding).Even the missions felt amazing to blast through in this one which is a definite plus considering almost all of them are necessary for story completion.Additionally, the open hub world and it's hidden collectibles add some very much appreciated replayability as well as a playground for the players to mess around with, essentially serving as a mini sonic frontiers.Lastly, the story while not exactly genre definiting did what it had to do and more in a spectacular fashion bringing back much needed depth to characters that were stripped of it for over a decade.This package is undoubtedly worth it's surprisingly lower than standard price tag, even more so  if you engage with the post game content.Really the only complaint I have about this game is that it ends and I really hope sega can release some more level packs for both generations games further down the line.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR : Gameplay is good everything you would expect from a generation game. Cutscenes are flashy and great but the story is below average at best. Gameplay is classic generation gameplay with obviously Shadow at the helm. His style of speeding through levels is way flashier and IMO more fun. Each mission is outfitted with some cut scenes in between them. Which for the most part blends seemliness with the gameplay. There are different sonic characters you never got to talk to in sonic generations but they are just as lack luster with dialogue in that game. The music as always is sonic music…IT AMAZING!(Still no spoilers ahead)Okay now that the good is over with here is my biggest problem with the game…THE STORY!What the hell were they thinking with this story?!! In short it is wasted potential for this type of story. It barely expands beyond what we knew about Shadow but where it does expand his story it is just terrible. Emotions are scattered all over the place and Shadow’s motives and thoughts don’t make sense. This is all due to the story being fit into a 3 to 4 hour session! _childDocuments_.review: This truly is Shadow's game. As much as I would've liked an exclusively Shadow game with a longer playtime, I do seriously enjoy this game and it is a must-play for anyone who is a fan of the Sonic series. I'll split the review into two as there are technically two entire games here.[Shadow Generations]First and foremost it has fantastic level design which reminds me of Sonic Adventure 2's designs. Amazingly paced and I was always discovering more hidden routes to find the box keys and to improve my times. I can say with full confidence that I never lost interest in the game and have even 100%'d it because I enjoyed it that much. The game's Doom Sphere 'hard mode' is actually very enjoyable and I attribute that to it actually feeling challenging yet rewarding once you master the movement and the fun ways you can use Chaos Control. The hard mode also doesn't just add unfair obstacles to fake a higher difficulty which I've seen in previous Sonic games so that's always great to see. The stages, like Sonic Generations, are fairly easy to S-Rank but Shadow Generations adds a different layer of difficulty to them as you can choose to forgo access to the Doom Wings in the stages which, in stages that assume you have them, offers a fun challenge to try and S-Rank them using the paths that you would otherwise be flying over completely. The story for the game is fantastic and I love the lore drops in the collectibles. I will not spoil anything here but just know that Ian Flynn and Sonic Team absolutely put their best effort into making a genuinely enjoyable story for Shadow that fans of Sonic can appreciate to its fullest. The controls are extremely intuitive and there is a lot of response in how Shadow moves. He can stop fast, doesn't feel like he's on ice and sliding around, good acceleration, jumping preserves speed by default (iykyk), and lightly tapping my joystick doesn't send him into a wall. I love how aerial boosting feels like a sort of smaller jump that gives you speed. The movement feels very rewarding to learn and there is a lot of room for skill expression and stage knowledge in the game. Boosting also doesn't just feel like a win button because Shadow's stages have a lot of fast-paced platforming and feels like how any Sonic game should feel; fast, intuitive, rewarding to master, and cool. Honestly takes all the best parts of the improved Frontiers movement and none of the bad things! The soundtrack, as standard for Sonic games, is insanely good. Maybe it's nostalgia, maybe it's genuinely just THAT good but I cannot put into words the excitement I felt hearing tracks from Sonic Adventure 2 and Sonic '06 again as I'm going through stages at break-neck speeds. Having Chaos Control right out the gate is an amazing thing and I have always wanted to properly use it in a game (and now I can!) I love how Chaos Control is not merely used as a simple time-stop gimmick but actually allows for some alternative, and sometimes mandatory, faster routes. The challenge stages especially highlight this ultimate power's capabilities in both combat and platforming.TLDR;- Amazing level design- Fantastic story- Best a hedgehog has controlled in 3D- Soundtrack is ALWAYS a banger- CHAOS CONTROL !- Movie Shadow skin incoming :>[Sonic Generations]I can't really say too much more than people have said about it in the past. However, I will say that revisiting this AFTER playing Shadow Generations is a huge shock. You can physically feel the differences in the Hedgehog Engines and they're very annoying to deal with. I had to make my joystick less sensitive because I forgot how floaty Sonic felt and there is skill that takes up a slot on your skill loadout that makes stopping much faster no matter what speed you have and that makes it feel like how it should by default. Shadow definitely spoiled me with the movement and ability to finely control directions. I had also forgotten that, despite separating Sonic Generations into Modern (3D) and Classic Sonic (2D), that a fairly substantial portion of Modern Sonic's stages are also in 2D or 2.5D perspective; some parts allow for side-stepping, some are just 2D. It's very weird honestly and is kind of jarring especially because it can, in some cases, kill all momentum you were carrying over throughout the level which is mildly annoying. It feels like they plucked Modern Sonic and put him in Classic's stage for a moment. The stages are absolutely, insanely easy especially compared to even the easiest of stages from Shadow Generations. I was hoping we could get a slight change to score calculations in the remaster but it doesn't seem to be the case. I will say that I felt kind of baited from the promotional art and even the main menu art featuring the different Chao. I knew we weren't going to be getting a Chao Garden, I swear SEGA refuses to do anything like it anymore, but I was hoping for some sort of interactions at least rather than cameos in cutscenes and them being extra collectibles to a game I thought had enough of them between the music notes and red rings. The soundtrack is good though, same as the original but I wasn't expecting much of a change there.TLDR;- Game is basically the same as the original with slight alterations (mostly just weird obscure things that I think is weird to change)- Controls are a bit floaty sometimes, very obvious after playing Shadow Generations- Soundtrack is a banger, as always !- Extra Chao collectibles are a bit weird but I'm glad to see them again at all- Level design is weaker than Shadow Generations but the levels were made like 11 years ago- Drifting still feels as cool as it did when I was younger[Final Thoughts]Honestly, if you've played Sonic Generations before and done everything there in the past I would say you can probably just play Shadow Generations or revisit Sonic Generations for nostalgia reasons. Personally, I've played the game to death on both PC (though not 100%'d on PC, unlike my Xbox 360) and Xbox and, while I will still be playing through the rest of Sonic Generations, I don't think you're missing out on much if you decide not to (assuming you've played it before)(Obligatory "I received this product as a birthday gift")

_childDocuments_.review: I'll enable comments because I need a laugh and want to see who agrees or has good counter-points for some of what I am going to say here.I wish there was a neutral option here because I don’t think it is a terrible game, I just don’t think it was worth the asking price or the greatest Sonic ever made.  (I'm also going to leave out a lot I want to say not to spoil things.)Shadow is back and has his own campaign.  Yes, we finally get to have something focused on Shadow and he deserves it!The GoodGame looks beautiful!Great performance (then again my computer is a beast.)Rarely had camera issues.  (A common issue plaguing 3D Sonic games.)Radical Highway is back and honestly, one of Shadow’s best levels ever.  It also has quite a few twists in store for us!The music is awesome.  I really loved the music in this game.  But no surprise since most Sonic games have an awesome soundtrack!The BossesI actually really enjoyed the bosses for the most-part.  10/10 would go back and re-fight again!The NeutralLevel designsSome parts of the level design annoyed the heck out of me, however, I do like that they had braching paths throughout the level.  This allows you to find collectibles hidden on different paths and have a slightly different experience in each level if you go back and replay them.  I am a fan of this.Why is it neutral?  Well they give you chaos control and seem to constantly try to stiff arm you into using it.  Many times it isn't necessary, but sometimes it kind of is and it feels too forced.  I understand wanting to stress the new gimmick (a cool one at that) but don't shove it down my throat.  Ironically, I found myself wanting to use Chaos Control at times when they blocked you from being able to use it.  I am probably going to be the odd one out here, but that was MY experience with it.The Over WorldThe over world is cool and there are things to explore, but I prefer the simpler 2D oversold Sonic's campaign gets.  At times getting to certain points can be a tad annoying and it felt like doing the awkward puzzles in frontiers... which I didn't care for.  That being said, it is cool exploring the map and if you are into collecting and finding hidden nuts, bolts, and chests, you have ample opportunity to do so.  It just didn't do it for me.  Collecting the music notes also did not do it for me.  They are even worse in a 3D space.The BadMovementShadow feels slow a lot of the time, unless you are being boosted or grinding.  He just starts off sluggish to me.  But then you get this random burst of speed, as if he has a turbo engine and it just kicked in.  This can throw you off on platforming areas.Slippery ShoesMy experience with inertia is that shadow felt like he had oil on his shoes at times.  If you got that turbo boost of speed, he will just slide.  Not great if you are going for precision platforming.  The game is still playable, but it was something I had a bit of a sore spot for me at a few points in the game.Okay now I am going to talk about some of the changes they made to Sonic's Campaign...  Some of the issues I think were made bigger than they are, and to a degree I think some of the criticism is deserved.Yes some scenes where Amy is all over sonic were changed.  However, there are still scenes where she tries to hug sonic and is clearly showing affection for him.  It isn't like the washed her character completely like they did in Frontiers.The knuckles one where he talks to old school sonic makes no sense with the changes they made.  The dialogue AND the cut scene should have been changed IMO.  That was a stupid oversight on their part.  Speaking of stupid oversight... The scene where Amy is holding cupcakes doesn't even look like she belongs there.  Go back and watch the cut scene.  They did a half-assed job with it. I see people whose normal attire looks waaaay more suggestive than anything they ever made Rouge wear...  It just seems silly to me that we have to cover a little bit of cleavage and her back (which doesn't make sense functionally due to her wings.)People grew up with these characters as they were made.  There are long-term fans that love old school portrayals of these characters.  Of course those folks are going to have issues when these characters are significantly changed.  Especially, in the greater context of what has been happening with games in recent history. _childDocuments_.review: Note: I haven't touched a sonic game in ages, haven't played Frontiers. I've played all other Sonic platformers except the dumbass Apple Arcade one. I really wanted to like this one.I gave into the hype and played this to inject some fresh Sonic Autism into my ADHD veins. And honestly? It's not too bad. I think my only problems are issues with generations in general: The momentum-free speed-setting grind rails, the complete lack of momentum in general in favor of pressing the "reach max speed button" just doesn't feel right. I played and enjoyed Gens when it came out, but the game design is really old at this point, and I wish they'd evolve the movement besides just boost.I feel like 3d Sonic is usually a fairly simple concept, but this time around they've used a lot of the face buttons to give Shadow cool abilities. I'm mixed on how this makes it harder to steer, though. Quick step left and right while boosting is done by sort of clawing your bumper while boosting with right trigger, which doesn't feel good. When turning without quick step, Shadow seems content to do a weird large arc instead of a sudden turn or worse, do a lengthy "hard stop" animation. This lack of fundamental platformer control is reflected in the level design, which features primarily long corridors that don't encourage turning at all, or "open-world" design where it feels more like a chore to get around than anything. There are some moments of platforming freedom, but they're mostly fighting against the "on-rails" philosophy of the Gens game design.As for new moves: Chaos Control would be cool, but the sound design isn't very satisfying. I remember Riders Zero Gravity! They can go hard with sound design if they want to! But instead, it distorts the very excellent music and most of the time I just forgot to use it. Chaos Spear was basically useless, didn't love taking my thumb off the joystick to use it. The wings: Man, I was disappointed. I thought we'd get some new movement options, but all it did was modify my boost arc for one early level, and then they get taken away. Maybe they come back later, I don't know. It really felt like missed opportunities, because these aren't tools that allow you to platform better, they're more like dressed-up quicktime events. This includes the enemy kick button, which is just Laser from Colors but easier, and while it's still as much of a quicktime event as everything else, it does feel really good to use.Overall, to newcomers to the series, it's probably fine. It's got solid setpiece moments and it's a good time generally. Shadow's pretty cool. I only don't recommend it because the controls feel clunky when compared to some of the clunkiest games in the series, the gameplay boils down to "Homing attack at the thing while mashing RT to go fast" and "Forced to do slow platforming with weird, floaty controls". It doesn't really feel like a fast platformer, more like an on-rails reaction simulator that occasionally has platforming. Even the loops (the things that have always been on-rails and are generally exciting in previous entries) feel bad when the camera just zooms out to show them instead of tucking near shadow to give you a sense of speed. If the intended mood is to make the player feel like they're going fast, then you're killing it by stopping to show shadow do a cool move without your input.If you've read this far, thanks. At the risk of being elitist: You should play Sonic Adventure 2 instead. It's a 3d platformer. It actually *controls* like a platformer. It has Shadow. It has a metagame with virtual pets. I straight up went back and played through Hero story to get my Sonic fix after bouncing off this game, and it's still way better than this, sorry. Maybe this one is better if you get super good at tryharding the movement and doing speedrun tricks. All I can say is it's definitely not as fun casually as SA2, and that game is 20 years old.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Generations is basically untouched except for some quality of life improvements and some corny dialogue being replaced. On it's own, it's already a amazing gaming experience even if the story is nothing to write home about. But these mad lads added another amazing game on top of it. Shadow Generations is, to put it lightly, the most fun I've ever had with a 3D Sonic game, and it's one where Sonic isn't even the main character. They have perfected the gameplay this time around from Cyberspace in Sonic Frontiers. It's not too fast, not too slow, it hits the mark perfectly, and is satisfying as all hell. On top of that adds a bunch of cool abilities to make the game that much more fun. Don't even get me started on the boss fights, they absolutely cooked with all of them. The story hits so much harder than Sonic Generations it makes that game look like a Saturday morning cartoon (the final scene is such a gut punch). They don't shy away from their past at all in this game either, Sonic 06 and Shadow The Hedgehog (2005) are on full display here, which makes me very hopeful for the future. I couldn't be anymore happy with how this turned out, the only gripe I could ever have is that it doesn't last forever. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Sonics story is basically exactly like the console generations, and might even just be an updated version of the steam port with a few small tweaks and the addition of Chao collectables in every level, and the controversial censorship. And the reason I say it feels just like the updated steam port, because WHEN YOU SELECT SONIC GENS IN THE MENU, it opens up a whole new window and closes the previous one. Personally I wasn't as upset about this because I never got to play the console version, but for someone who's looking for a full revamp of the original, its kind of the same thing. HOWEVERShadows story is absolutely amazing. I haven't even finished it yet but just with what I've played so far its by far the main game that's actually worth the 50 dollars (60 if your a digital deluxe user.) Sure, they definitely couldave picked better levels to remake for Shadow, but even the remakes of these levels (that ive played so far) Have been absolutely amazing. The music is great, and the new features Shadow unlocks is so refereshing. The 3D experience in white space with Shadow Generations just feels like a nice cup of ice cold water compared to how 2D and restricting Sonic Generations is.So ultimately, yes. get this game. For Shadow <3333. Dont get this game expecting a complete remaster of Sonic Generations, because you might be a bit disappointed, due to the rewrites and censorship (which I will not discuss. thats for you to decide how you feel regarding it.) Nothing feels new and exiting with that game. Shadow Generations is worth every penny though, even if its not the longest game in the world. Thats why I havent beaten it yet, because its so amazing I just wanna savor every last drop of content I get. In my opinion I feel like they shouldave just cut sonics part out entirely, and dedicated all their work to Shadow Gens.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game on the level of OG generations, I did. And I probably plan to just get all achievements cause I might as well did so with OG generations. Needless to say, I guess it passes. But it has flaws. Spoilers below for obvious reasons, although chances are if you're reading them you don't care about being spoiled.SONIC GENERATIONS: A 1 for 1 port with almost the same graphics and some cut scenes changed. Why were they changed? Who knows, SBI detected will probably say something about it, I don't doubt it. I personally always skipped em so meh. Also they added more stuff to  collect, but ultimately it doesn't change gameplay, just another thing needed to complete.I don't need to say more, its the same fun game you loved from before. (or maybe not so much. Not being able to change as many settings + the cut scene changes need to be called out, its as simple as that.)SHADOW GENERATIONS:The gimmicks introduced into shadow's playstyle/character are.. eh. Hit and miss. Some of them feel kinda rushed, truth be told. Doom wing is a good alternative to super shadow and I will likely remember that one (honestly I had more fun with it than I want to admit), but the other ones are easily just weird and forgettable. Doom surf feels way too clunky to enjoy using period and probably should have been binned in place of boosting on water (like sonic generations has). Doom Morph sounds like a cool idea on paper (and works well during the Mephiles fight) but outside of some shining moments, same as surf, too clunky to enjoy using, and on top of that a core mechanic of it (launching yourself directly into the air by being under the morph sphere and releasing the jump button) is poorly explained.Doom blast and Doom spear are pretty nice, I'll be it doom spear is just upgraded chaos spears, and Doom blast is essentially just a means to launch you up into the air when the game wants you to. They're being lumped together because they aren't really stand outs and I probably wouldn't have even noticed if, lets say, doom blast was replaced with a different type of dash ring.Chaos Control is definitely the best of them though, and is a core mechanic you must learn and use well to get the best chance of securing your S ranks.(Also it feels like a nice power mechanic, who doesn't like instantly stopping time as shadow, the guy who's essentially known for Chaos control since SA2?)The levels are mostly good (well, minus Radical highway 1) and I had fun playing them. Same with the bosses. Granted, they are a bit easy, but learning the mechanics and getting the S ranks on them was pretty fun. here's not much more to say, it's not Forces level of level design, the guys for the most part cooked pretty good, with a few burnt ends here and there. (But seriously, why couldn't we play as shadow during the shadow x sonic fight? Missed potential there by just turning that into a cut scene. I'm sure a modder will get on that though.)Edit: 100%ed the game for the most part (still have to do hard shadow bosses but everything else is done), my thoughts generally still hold the same. Radical highway is still.. yeah. Radical highway. Doom morph grew on me but honestly still think its too gimmicky and poorly explained by the game. Overall experience though, buy it if you haven't played sonic generations before, and if you have... wait for a sale tbh, shadow generations is good but the amount of content you get for a casual playthrough is pretty small, so unless you don't mind playing sonic generations again, chances are you're basically going to complete it in a day then probably forget about it.

_childDocuments_.review: PEAAKKK Actual review: A testament to what Modern Sonic should be. The original Sonic Generations already was a collection showing some of Sonic's most iconic stages, with an incredible fast redesign based on modern boost gameplay. Generations was the last good sonic game before the "Dark Age" of sonic games where every one was a disappointment, until Sonic Frontiers came out in 2022. Frontiers had many issues, but it showed that Sega team was finally listening to fans and that a Sonic Renaissance may be finally happening, Sonic X Shadow Generations is the verification of that. Heavily inspired by their work on Frontiers, Shadow's story is fast paced with an interesting, albeit short, story that is well written. The game is incredibly fast that are as long and varied as the Unleashed day stages that inspired the boost formula. While still very linear, every level features multiple paths and shortcuts that heavily affect time. The levels are quick, intuitive, yet encourage replay ability. 6 levels with 2 stages each means a total of 12 stages, 6 less than the base game. This makes sense as generations was developed over 2 and a half years, while Shadow generations likely was done in only a year and a half with a split team. Frontiers released 2022, with a year of planned updates which means Shadow Generations likely started development only last year. The Sonic team did a wonderful job with the time they were given and I believe this game proves that Sonic does still work as a game, it just needs time and creativity to thrive. The game is not perfect, I enjoy the new abilities however the latter stages make less and less use some, while heavily relying on others. SPOILERS (Skip this paragraph to avoid them)         The doom-stingray swimming sections are amazing, they are very fun and a great addition. The second form of travel, which I cannot remember the name of, is less fun. The travelling through sludge form is a good idea, however its use in the Frontiers level is simply frustrating at points. I love Mephilles, but the boss fight is mediocre. I understand why they wanted to base the fight around the doom form, however I would've preferred something else that focused more on a creative reimmagining of that original fight which never got to reach its full potential (sonic 06 was just a mess, but I love the ideas from it). The wings are fun, they are creative, they also are only used on the last 2 stages and can't be used fully in the other stages. I just hope next time they use something like this, it's more consistently available throughout the game. Overall the game is an easy 8.5/10, the Frontiers level brings this down quite a bit as well as some of the design choices around the new abilities. The game is also quite short, I finished it on PS5 in just under 3 hours and am halfway through on steam already with only 1.2 hours played. Besides that, the game is a very fun, quick paced, and exhilarating experience that I hope Sega continues to learn from to improve the next sonic game.

_childDocuments_.review: This will be only for the Shadow Generations portion, as I had already played the older version of Sonic Generations and this is the content I most wanted to play. After many, many years we finally got another Shadow the Hedgehog game, and man was it worth the wait. I know Shadow's original game was mixed. I mostly enjoyed it, but it was filled with flaws, bugs, and nonsensical choices (like giving Shadow guns. I love guns, but it takes away from Shadows character). Here in Shadow Generations, we get the story, graphics, and gameplay that Shadow has always deserved. This has become my new favorite Sonic game, with SA2 and Sonic Heroes trailing right behind it.I really do not want to spoil anything, but the ending to this game made me shed tears. It was masterfully done, and beyond merely being entertaining, it was emotional. Being able to finally see all the proper depth and history of Shadow's character was a delight, in addition to being able to see the tie-ins of the past. For controls, I play exclusively on Steam Deck, and they are tight, and neigh perfect. The default controller scheme for Steam Deck (which I believe is shared with XBox), are extremely comfortable to use. Speaking of Steam Deck, it runs flawlessly. I did not encounter a single bug or glitch in my time playing the game. Furthermore, it looks so amazing on the Deck... the reflections are so smooth and the environments are breathtaking. I've said it before and I will say it again, someone get Gordon Ramsay because this game is cooking! Game length was about the same as it takes to beat Sonic Generations, but it was still too short for how amazing the story, gameplay, and levels were; it only took me four hours and forty minutes to beat the game. The music was also top notch in all areas, though I was greatly disappointing that the version of "Supporting Me" used in the Biolizard fight did not have the lyrics in it.Moving on to things I was not to happy with. Game length, while comparable to Sonic Generations as advertised, was still way too short for just how amazing this story and content is. Short but sweet is the best way to put it. After that, my next issue was progression being locked behind needless boss keys which can only be obtained by completing challenge missions. I like challenge mission, but to make them forced in order to complete the game left a sour taste in my mouth. The reason is mainly because its a forced game mode that some people may not want to do, while also providing artificial padding of the games length. It takes away from what could have been an otherwise extra zone or two that I would have much preferred. Next is the implementation of the advertised soundtrack... most of the music had nothing to do with the game, or Shadow, and the music from the actual game is not in there. What's worse, they lock the music behind software that must be installed to access it, same with the art book. The soundtrack was the only reason I bought the deluxe edition... I would have waited the three days to play. The fact they are saying its the games soundtrack with next to nothing from the game in it, while also making it impossible to play the music on anything other than the software on your computer (or console for console players) is downright offensive, false advertising, and blatantly telling the customer "you may have paid for this, but do not expect to own it). It is very hard to argue against those who have just pirated the music, or will pirate it, because not only do they get to do with it what they want, they also get an overall better experience. Because this does not affect the game itself, I will not let it hurt the games review, but its something to be aware of... they basically mal-advertised, and spat on everyone who paid for the content.Pros:-Story-Gameplay-Replay-ability-Controls -Level Design-Music/Audio/Voice ActingCons:-A Bit Short-Forced Game Modes to ProgressScore:Story: 9.8Music: 9.5Graphics: 9.8Controls: 9Voice Acting: 9Replay-ability:8Overall: 9.2Rank: S

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, after such a long time, we have a new boost game that feels great. This game already is great enough for repackaging Generations, which has been preserved very well, keeping the game mostly intact, with a few quality-of-life improvements, and a rewritten story, which I am mixed on, but appreciate the effort. And shut up about the small edits to Rouge's model and Amy's bio + cutscene animations. Y'all ain't doin' anyone a favor. But the Shadow portion of this is the main "thing" and it is GREAT. It takes the physics from Frontiers and refines them to be their best. The Doom Powers, while still being a gimmick, are very fun to use and flow seamlessly with gameplay, and they only help, especially the Doom Wing. The level design is amazing, feeling fast and lasting the perfect time, around 3-4 minutes. And the story is written very well, and while I won't provide spoilers, it's some of the best in the series. The open world is also great, being inspired by Sonic Frontiers, with tons of collectibles that can be fun to collect. And finally, the game(s) look BEAUTIFUL. While I do believe there is a bit too much of an "aura" around characters in Shadow Generations, It still looks great, making good use of HE2 (Hedgehog Engine 2, the game's graphics engine), having great lighting and beautiful environments. TL;DR, buy the game. It's GOOD.

_childDocuments_.review: Sega has said that this is primarily "Shadow Generations" with a remaster of Sonic Generations included, albeit you can't just buy Shadow Generations... which honestly, probably for the best.Shadow Generations is genuinely super super fun, I loved every bit of it. It was some super tight gameplay that ran amazing and had a great story (for a Sonic game). That said, it feels like most of the content in this game comes from wanting to get S rank on all the stages, as well as collecting all the collectibles (which is tons of cool art, music, and the like). That bonus content is super cool... albeit, I don't think it makes the fact that the base game itself is super short. It's super jarring that it's attached to Sonic Generations, which has a ton of everything (bonus content AND stages + challenge levels to play) and then looking at Shadow Generations, which right when it feels like you're really getting started, it's already ending. There's 1 more level coming presumably sometime in December that's tied into the 3rd Sonic Movie, but even adding that I don't think will fix the problem, just make it sting less.That said, I still think this is absolutely a must buy. While Shadow Generations feels a bit short, it's 100% pure gold and at no point does it feel like the quality isn't there, and it also includes a slightly remastered Sonic Generations with more control options (letting you play either with classic boost controls from Unleashed/OG Generations, play with Frontiers boost controls, or customize how you want with more options). You are losing mod support on PC since (for now) that's only in the original Generations' title, but this is still an amazing title on its own even without mods and that cannot be understated.So yeah, good time.

_childDocuments_.review: The additional content, the Shadow part, was excellent. Great addition to Shadow's story, the levels are tons of fun and there is a lot to do. The bosses are very fun to fight, and I love that Sega FINALLY shows Sonic 06 some love with what they've included. I expected the game to border DLC content similar to Forces' episode Shadow, but it's way more than that and worth buying for. The new abilities you gain are fun to play around with and satisfying to master. Shadow himself also controls really well.The Sonic part though? I personally always thought it was mediocre and mostly nostalgia bait and that hasn't changed, mostly because there haven't been many changes to the original content. At least not from what I can tell. I would check, but the original port is rubbish and either doesn't want to launch or the controls mess up despite using 3rd party software, so I will have to trust my memory.They added chao to collect, which is nice after Forces one-upped them with number- and silver moon rings. I also have a weak spot for them so they catered to me well with that one.Both Sonics can now drop-dash, another feature from Forces I loved. Unfortunately the boost and spindash are both instant, unlike in Forces, so the feature is unnecessary. Still found myself pulling off the move as classic Sonic for fun though. The downside is that they added it as a skill for classic Sonic, the one I wanted the feature on, while making it a permanent ability for modern Sonic, the one I DON'T want this feature on because every time I've used it, it was accidental because there's no reason to use it in 3D.The last change is a bunch of dialogue changes which didn't bother me personally, but a lot of people got mad about it. I didn't even notice them until people pointed them out.Meanwhile the Shadow part did everything right that the Sonic part failed to do, and I think it's a shame they didn't go back and change the Sonic part to match the improvement they made on the Shadow part. For example, I keep failing to do homing attacks in the Sonic part that I would have been able to get in any other Sonic game while not having this problem even once in the Shadow part. When on rails you can use the bumpers to hop between parallel rails, but only as Shadow, not as Sonic. As Shadow, you get the double jump from Forces instead of the pathetic momentum-killing mid-air dash Sonic does. I'm sure part of the reason is because it would break the current levels, but I feel like it would have been worth going back and changing because it would improve the game a lot. Then again, too many Gen fans would be mad they changed their beloved game, so I will just have my cake.Nevertheless I mostly enjoyed the game, mostly because the Shadow part was just so good and really lifted the game up.
