_childDocuments_.review: This game is really bad so I'll break this into two versions for those who want more details and those who just want a Tl:Dr.Tl:Dr: Pros:Graphics and framerate is fantastic and does a really great job bringing the game forward.Cons: CENSORSHIPThe rewritten dialogue and cutscenes ruin the story and characters.They do not understand who Shadow is and try to recon his history and character. Chao Collectibles is a pointless addition, same with the keys in stages with Shadow Gen.The powers and way Shadow plays has potential but misses the mark.The total amount of stages for Shadow makes the game feel incomplete.This is supposed to be a celebration of their history, but is used as a means to rewrite it instead. Full Version:Censorship is everywhere here, and I do mean that. The rewrite ultimately ruins Generations as they use it as a excuse to take away the slapstick humor, great dynamic, and who these characters are and were. Leaving them completely different from who they should be. Speaking of blatant character rewritting, Shadow is treated as your stereotypical edgelord who needs to learn how to chill out, instead of being the hero he always was. His history is manipulated to fit the needs of the story instead of the story being done to respect his history and create a means proper to go forward with. Collectibles in this game range from pointless to insulting, as mentionted before the chao collectibles don't really add anything to the mix with the remaster, making it feel more forced than genuine. As for the ones with Shadow, why are the collectibles in the stages just keys that I then have to find the boxes for in the open world. Instead of IDK, just giving me the collectibles via the stages. The Doom powers while a really cool idea feel halfbaked as they either feel over restricted or underwhelming as times, but it does have potential if they wish to revisit it in future games.Shadow Gens leaves you wanting for more, which while normally is a good issue. Here it feels as though it was supposed to have more, but was cut for some reason. Making it feel incomplete and half finished.Ultimately, this game feels more like a means for them to turn the Sonic franchise into something it isn't, instead of a love letter for fans who have followed this franchise for years.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic X Shadow Generations features the original game Sonic Generations and all its DLC as a remaster and a new Shadow game which serves as a new Generations game.Sonic Generations:This remaster holds up to the same graphical quality we see in Shadow Generations and includes new content. Sonic Generations features both Classic 2D gameplay with Classic Sonic as well as Modern 3D gameplay with Modern Sonic. You explore each level recognised from previous Sonic titles with the gameplay styles of both Sonics. It's really cool to see all these levels with modern graphics as well as experiencing 2D Sonic levels in 3D, and 3D Sonic levels in 2D. Each level contains other challenge minigames. There are rival battles and boss battles to challenge as well. One of these rival battles includes Shadow. Eventually you can explore all levels as Classic Super Sonic and as Modern Super Sonic. The DLC from the original game included here has the Casino Night pinball minigame. A very fun and creative spin on pinball featuring Sonic as the ball and a slot machine mechanic. The new content in this remaster encourages you to find and collect many types of Chao found in the Modern levels.Shadow Generations:As Sonic Generations was already considered by most to be one of the best Sonic games, and peoples' love for Shadow, this game serves as just that. Shadow Generations features Shadow being brought into the same time stasis as Sonic. Shadow must conquer more recognisable stages from his past and his future - including levels from Forces and Frontiers - the same as the Sonics did. While Shadow is the only playable character in his story, he is not alone when it comes to facing both 3D and 2D levels. Though unlike Sonics', the hubworld in Shadow Generations is sort of an open area you can explore. Shadow also has new abilities for intreging gameplay use, called Doom Powers. This features Doom Spears, a multi-strike Chaos Spear, Doom Blast, an attack that can send certain enemies flying, Doom Surf, a water-treading ability, Doom Morph, a squid-like creature that allows Shadow to travel along special surfaces and swing, and Doom Wings, a power that allows Shadow to glide. At a certain part, Shadow's interaction with Sonic is reflected to intertwine the stories. This game also includes the same amount of bosses yet a shorter amount of stages. Each boss battle is crazier than the last, with my favourite being the second. Overall, the animations and visuals are very well made. You can tell the jump in graphical quality from Forces to Shadow Generations.Overall both games have incredible music and visuals. There are already plenty of mods for Shadow Generations to try out and there will be more for Sonic Generations in the future.That being said, I don't think this game is better than Sonic Frontiers. It has a lot going for it, but there is a lack of content as a new title. Shadow Generations has six stages while Sonic has nine. The open area also is quite small. While it is made to seem big when it is first revealed and nice to witness the potential of Shadow in an open area, it doesn't feel big when you start moving around. You can get from one side of the map to the other in less than a minute. Frontiers overall has more replayability. And I might be the only one thinking this but I appreciated the boost system from Frontiers much more than Generations. I would put this game at #2, being better than Mania, Forces, and Superstars, but short of Frontiers. I think if they can combine the themes, gameplay elements, and visual effects from this game with an open world adventure like Frontiers, they could make the perfect game.Highly recommended to anyone who likes the original Sonic Generations or Shadow the Hedgehog. This is definitely one of the best Sonic games.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite possibly the best 3D Sonic game ever. Full stop. Sonic Generations was already considered one of the best Sonic games ever, even way back in 2011. This is that same game, upscaled for modern PCs, but *also* with AN ENTIRE NEW CAMPAIGN JUST FOR SHADOW. AND THE SHADOW CAMPAIGN IS JUST AS GOOD! Focusing entirely on the Shadow Generations side...-The gameplay is extremely fun and polished. The levels are on par with OG Generations in terms of layouts and pathways, but then you have an entirely new mechanic added in- *Chaos Control*. Chaos Control isn't used just to save time, like you might expect. It also opens up a ton of new routes and shortcuts in each level! In just the first level, you can use it multiple times to freeze projectiles in place to take faster paths by running along them, or use them to create stairs to get higher up. And every level has creative uses for it, just like that! So cool!-The cutscenes look phenominal. Sonic games have a pretty inconsistent track record with cutscene animations, but this is one of the good ones. All of the characters' faces are super expressive, and the models used are super clean and polished. Possibly the best looking cutscenes in the entire series that aren't CG. -The hub world is fun! Think of it like a micro-Frontiers island. It's not as big and expansive, but it has the same sort of "complete short  platforming challenges and pick up collectibles as you go from level-to-level" design. Just like in OG Generations, some of Shadows friends stand outside the different stages, and instead of regurgitating the same hints over and over, they have unique dialogue that changes based on how far you've progressed in the story!Speaking of story....-the way it ties into Sonic Generations' story is pretty neat and creative! Shadow Gens takes place parallel to Sonic Gens. The stories converge and separate where in makes sense in each game's story, but it very clearly/obviously assumes you played Sonic's side first. In conclusion, It feels damn good to play as Shadow again, and this was the best way they could have brought him back. Solid game. 9/10. To me, this is the best 3D Sonic game ever.

_childDocuments_.review: (SPOILER FREE)TL;DR : Amazing game, especially for hardcore Shadow fans, and ties into the original story of Sonic Generations VERY well, it genuinely fits perfectly imo. I'm only a little over half-way through with Shadow Generations, and it's absolutely AMAZING!!I'm a massive Shadow fangirl and have been for many many years, and Shadow Generations is a love letter to all Shadow fans. It tells an excellent story that builds upon the foundation of Sonic Generations, but adds Shadow along into the same story. It's actually done VERY well, it doesn't feel shoved in, or out of place at all. It's actually very crazy for me to say that despite SEGA's reputation for the past 20 years of Sonic, this franchise finally found what it's been looking for.    However, I literally have one complaint about Shadow Generations...  the boost feels WAY too slow compared to the original Sonic Generations... Sonic Generations is obviously very well known for being the Sonic game with the boost formula perfected. The original game wasn't just a "hold boost and win" game like Sonic Forces, it made you feel extremely fast just like Sonic. However, Shadow Generations' boost feels oddly slow compared to Sonic Generations. When you compare Shadow's max running speed to holding the boost button, you don't really notice a difference...

_childDocuments_.review: This game is VERY good.Base Sonic Generations was already a really good game; granted now, there're a few more graphical issues & bugs in this re-release, but nothing like Colour's Ultimate. They're not game-breaking, just a tad annoying-- easily be patched out. The rewritten cutscenes, though a point of contention, really add to the little story existing Generations had. Plus, some of these characters haven't been in a game in the last few years, so having Sonic interact with them more is always welcome. Though I do wish that the animations got touched up more than they did.Anyhow.Shadow Generations; honestly, one of the best Sonic games in the last few games, and a contender for one of the best Sonic games of all time.The story is neat. It reaffirms any Sonic fans from the early 2000's with characters like Mephiles, or more notably Black Doom. Also reintroducing characters like Gerald and Maria helps to give Shadow more a character than just edgy Sonic, which is always nice.The gameplay in Shadow Generations is, in my opinion, much better than Sonic in Generations. The level designs have so many more branching paths, Shadow controls more like Sonic does in Frontiers but more polished, and really levels just have a nice flow to them.His stages are split into 2 Acts, one 3D and one 2D.Honestly, I've never been a big fan of Modern Sonic 2D stages, but Shadow Generations fixes that. I don't know what happened after Frontiers, but it's clear Sonic Team locked in with this game.Even the Open Hub they made for Shadow is just fun to run around in; and the pop-in, though blatant in Frontiers, is minimal. If there's any, it's cleverly hidden, so props to Sonic Team all around.Bosses are cool. The spectacle they started in Frontiers has been carried over and expanded on, and by God have they made so much better. Speaking of spectacle; the Cutscenes in Shadow Generations are phenomenal. Best in the series hands down. Seeing these characters so expressive is great; they really have built on Frontiers massively for Shadow Generations and I'm so glad.Though the campaign is short, levels are so fun to replay. It's a must for any Sonic fan.

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★★ - Amazing 11.4 Hours 4.4 Hours	• Game consists of a remix\remake of iconic classic and modern 2D and 3D iconic levels all throughout the Sonic and Shadow games.	• Controls are responsive, but some of Modern Sonic and Shadow’s abilities have a steep learning curve.	• Boss fights are dynamic, and end just before they start to feel repetitive.	• Majority of levels have the best feeling of speed and flow that I've felt in any Sonic game in the Franchise.	• The Shadow DLC is a short but great enhancement of everything that Sonic Generations did right. 	• The story is focused on a time frozen multiverse collision, a simple but engaging premise.	• Dialogue captures each character’s personality well, with Shadow’s dry edgy melodrama contrasting Sonic’s unwavering optimism.	• Vibrant visuals with detailed environments that transition smoothly between zones.	• Character design and animations are well polished.	• Music is a standout feature, remixing iconic Sonic tracks with high-energy.	• Sound effects are satisfying, but voice acting can be repetitive and hit-or-miss depending on how much you restart a mission. 	• Strongly suggest playing Sonic Generations before playing Shadow Generations if you haven't already.	• Use a controller for optimal gameplay—keyboard controls feel less intuitive.	• Make sure to set time to explore each level and all its challenges thoroughly. _childDocuments_.review: Since most of us are here for Shadow Generations, that's what I'll focus on.In short, you get one of, if not  best Sonic game ever, for a grand total of $50, with a free copy of Sonic Generations with a few extra bells and whistles.Shadow Generations takes what made Sonic Generations so good - the polished, fun and well-designed levels (except for Planet Wisp), smooth, easy-to-get-used-to and diverse gameplay and egregiously good soundtrack - and builds upon it like no other Sonic sequel has before, ever since S3&K.The game itself doesn't have a huge amount of zones, but it makes up for it tenfold with the sheer length of the acts (which are long enough to make the purchase worth it and not long enough to make the game boring and tedious), the amount of alternate pathways and endgame replayability thanks to the addition of the Doom powers.Speaking of which, the Doom powers feel more like an organic expansion of Shadow's moveset rather than annoying afterthought gimmicks. They're polished and well-implemented, and flow naturally with the level design. You unlock them gradually and can use all of them at once - you don't need to manually equip and replace any of them. You can, however, disable them in act select before you start a stage (only works while replaying the stages).Challenge stages are also present and, in my opinion, are also an improvement compared to Sonic Generations' challenges. Though, unlike Sonic Generations, you must complete all of them in order to be able to complete the game. The post-challenge bell note chases are also a lot more engaging, which isn't really that important, but still is a nice improvement.In both story and challenge stages, there are three medallions in each; They act as an alternative Sonic Generations' red rings and are used as keys for chests in the white space, which unlock collectibles - artworks, soundtracks and story recaps of Shadow's previous game appearances. You can also gradually unlock a digital version of Gerald Robotnik's journal and view it along with the rest of collectibles in the collection room (accessible through the pause menu in the white space).Speaking of the white space - It's now in 3D, with massive amounts of explorable areas. It can be compared to Sonic Frontiers' open zone gameplay, but much more polished. It gradually expands, giving you more and more space to explore and traverse in many different ways, including all of the Doom powers. The white space also contains various extra challenges which also grant you collectibles.While there isn't much story in this game, it still plays quite an important role. Although it's not as long and complex as, for example, Sonic Adventure 2's or Sonic '06's, but it does a great job portraying Shadow's inner struggles and how his past still haunts him, no matter how much he has tried to leave it behind. In tandem with the Dark Beginnings animated mini-series, which you can find on Youtube, it makes for a great and emotional story - one that Shadow has needed for all this time.Regarding player controls, they are very responsive and, as expected, can be fully customized in the settings, including alternate KB/M bindings. Though, you cannot use some specific keys, such as either of the Shift keys. By default, the homing attack is bound to a separate button, but you can choose legacy controls to bind it to the jump button. Air dash is replaced by double jump, and drop dash is absent.There are three different control modes for Shadow: Act 1 (3D), Act 2 (2D) and white space (3D).Act 1's controls are great - an undeniable improvement compared to Sonic Generations. On controller, as far as I'm aware, there are no issues whatsoever. On KBM, however, there's one issue that can be a bit of a pace breaker. Attempting to turn/change direction with WASD while not boosting will reset your speed to the base speed - same as when you just start moving. However, you'll quickly get used to avoiding this issue, and it is only really a problem while you're getting used to the game and in one specific challenge stage. Even with this little drawback, the controls feel great.Act 2's 2D controls are simply 3D controls limited to a 2D plain. Classic Sonic with the Modern moveset and physics.White space controls are perfect - free camera controls, mouse steering and seamless turning, complete freedom of movement.If you bought the Deluxe edition, you'll receive a digital artbook and soundtrack, as well as some extra soundtracks to select in-game, as well as an optional skin for shadow - Terios, based off one of his concept designs. Said skin only replaces Shadow's model - animations, VFX and skills are identical.The Sonic Generations part shouldn't be ignored either - as one of the best Sonic games of all time, it is a must-play. Despite not much having changed compared to the initial release, I can still confidently say that this is the definitive way to play this game. This time, it's a proper PC port with fully customizable controls and up-to-date settings. Some dialogues have been rewritten and re-voiced (although not re-animated), but otherwise, the game mostly remains the same - aside from the addition of collectible Chao spread throughout the levels. There is, however, no Chao garden in the game, but you can view the Chao in the collection room.In conclusion, Sonic x Shadow generations is as close to a perfect package as it gets. You get two great games for less than a full price tag, with great replayability and barely any cons. The only complaint I could possibly have towards Shadow Generations is that it's just so good that it leaves you wanting more. 10/10, if you're considering getting this game(s), absolutely do it.Now be real, you can't tell me that Shadow with those wings isn't the rawest ♥♥♥♥ ever

_childDocuments_.review: Without a shadow of a doubt, this is one of (if not) the best 3D Sonic game in recent years. Sonic Generations itself is practically untouched in terms of gameplay, the only additions include the extra hidden Chao and Drop Dash ability added to both Sonic's movesets which are incredibly welcome additions. The rewritten story, while ultimately a little meaningless, gives the game more references and tidbits for long time fans to sink their teeth into. And the game felt great with 60 fps and 4k resolution, it gives you so much more time to react accordingly to the level's challenges. Complaints about this remaster is, again, the rewrite felt a little superfluous to me. The story, while it had no stakes or anything like that, was completely inoffensive and the same can be said about this rewrite. Some of the actors playing these characters are really starting to show their age from the jump from 2011 to 2024. And I'm not sure what caused this, but there were a handful of times where I came across minor hiccups when it came to collision, camera movement, and other things that weren't present in the original release. Nothing game-breaking, just a small nitpick as someone who's spent way too long playing this game over the years. Regardless, it's always nice to come back to this masterclass of a game.But the real highlight of this game is Shadow's campaign bar none. The movement feels like a great blend of the loose controls of Frontiers while maintaining that breakneck speed you've come to love in Generations and other Boost titles. The level design is incredibly well thought out, offering those who'll go out of their way to explore and take different paths rewards. Whether it be through the Collection Keys, ways to shave time off of speedruns, or anything else. The graphics of the levels themselves look amazing, it's so great to see levels like Rail Canyon and Kingdom Valley in such beautiful high definition. The story in Shadow's campaign is one of the best in Sonic history, offering flashy and downright awesome moments with strong emotions to boot. And you already know it's a Sonic game, so the music is going to be amazing no matter what, and this game is no exception. My only complaints with this portion of the game is the map the tedium of collecting the gears for Orbot and Cubot. The map only offers where the level and challenge gates are, boss gates, and collection box locations which sounds useful, but for some odd reason, the boxes that weren't collected didn't always appear right away. Some only showed up after being collected, which one hand incentivizes learning the map's nooks and crannies, but it's also just unintuitive since you can't mark locations like in Frontiers' map. And those machine parts were such a CHORE to deal with. They don't have an icon on the map so you can't track them down like the boxes, and some of them are either in the most obvious spot in the world or somewhere you would NEVER think to look. But regardless, finding everything and eventually 100% completing this game was an amazing experience through and through. Sonic Generations by itself was already an amazing experience and now with Shadow Generations to go along with it makes this one of my all time favorite Sonic games ever. I'll surely be coming back to this to speedrun all the levels to get a new personal best, look at the hours of concept artwork in both game's galleries, mess with mods, and so much more.If you're either a hardcore or new Sonic fan, I still highly recommend this game. It is the best offering the series has to offer to date. Bow your heads low, all hail Shadow.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is specifically for Shadow Generations which I get to try out early and I'm happy to say that it is truly fantastic.This game is like a sequel to three different games:- Sonic Generations for following up on the concept of revisiting stages throughout the series' history.- Shadow the Hedgehog for continuing up on the titular protagonist's story.- Sonic Frontiers for polishing up on the latest Open Zone formula.The gameplay is incredibly polished with engaging level designs that have multiple routes you could take, Doom Powers that naturally complements Shadow's playstyle, and a hub world that is fun to explore, full of collectibles to get, and challenges to complete. It's essentially the Open Zone from Sonic Frontiers but more refined.Sonic Team has nailed the presentation with amazing cinematics, setpieces, and a story that is much more interesting than Sonic Generations which only had a basic excuse plot. Anyone who's invested in Shadow's storyline will get a kick out of this, perhaps even more so when you find all pages of Prof. Gerald's Journal which builds up on the lore.The aesthetics is absolutely gorgeous too. Playing some of the stages and the first boss feels like I'm taking a peek into what a modern remake of Adventure 2 and Heroes could look like. The visual fidelity has definitely been given a step up since Sonic Forces and the environment is now fully-fledged and integrated with the stages again compared to the Cyber Space levels in Sonic Frontiers where everything looked spacious with floating structures.Shadow's campaign might be too short though for a casual playthrough. I think people have only finished it in like 3-4 hours. However, if you're interested in completing the game 100%, the game could actually last you for like 9-10 hours. Combine that with Sonic Generations which I already thought was terrific and you got yourself a good deal of two great games to play.Sonic Team has definitely improved a lot since Sonic Frontiers and especially since Sonic Forces. As much as I really enjoy Frontiers, I wouldn't say it's quite up there yet. Shadow Generations however is up there, it's really an impressive great game, and I could only hope that Sonic Team and Sega keeps it up for the next major Sonic game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm loving it.Edit: I'll add (addition:) under the segments for the new stuff. I have completed Shadow Generations and gotten every collectable, all S ranks on normal and challenge stages, no hit the final boss, did the hard mode bosses w/ S rank, and got all hub challenges with a GREAT completion (gotten by have at least 10 seconds to spare when completing them).The abilities engage the player in the levels to utilize them and abuse them correctly to find alternate paths and easier ways to get through sections of the levels. The star platinum style time stop is very good in this regard, turning an object that damages you even when boosting into a platform that allows you to get to a higher route or just a 4 second time save.Addition: the extra morphs that are unlocked add another level of both difficulty and engaging gameplay. When beating the final boss you can activate Doom Mode, it just adds more challenge stages, new hub challenges, and hard mode bosses. The hub challenges REALLY put the knowledge of the hub and your abilities/morphs to get those GREAT finishers. One boss was a real test. Biolizard is mostly the same, just you need to beat him hitless, and same for Mephiles. As for Metal Overlord, it is a true test to your knowledge of the beginning section and movement to get those direct hits with the ramps. For S rank it really makes you good at the fight. Same goes with beating the final boss hitless for the achievement.There are sadly 2D stages, BUT they are very short in comparison to the 4-8 minute (depending on pace and stage) 3D ones. They are just as good as the 3D ones, and they really don't impede on the journey through the game.The hub on the other hand isn't 2D, and is actually a sizeable 3D area to explore as you unlock the transformations and abilities. It definitely is a better try at what they went for in Frontiers, and I'm very happy they didn't just dust the interesting concept under the rug and are actually TRYING to get better with the concept. (I'm a huge fan of Sunset Overdrive, and this is one step closer to getting half of its awesomeness)The red rings are replaced with tokens between 3 categories(think similar to the sun and moon medallions from Unleashed) artwork, music, and lore. These tokens are used in the hub to unlock the chests with the corresponding icon. They aren't tricky to find in the levels, but there has been one that kicked my butt trying to find. (it was in rail canyon at the VERY END, right after the twisty rails at the end when you fall down, keep boosting forward, it is on the roof of the goal ring area).Addition:The pain does not end here. In the open hub the chests and ship parts really get further as you try searching for them. There is NO help besides guides and pure luck crossing paths with them. There's an amazing guide in the steam guides for the chests. There is a video for the ship parts, but it really is annoying to watch, but it's the only one at the moment. I'd say the map shows you all the unopened chests after beating the game, and there'd be a setting you can turn on for a compass pointing to a rocket part. Those are the only ideas I've got to make it less of a pain in the butt to find.Music good as always, makes me enjoy songs I didn't listen to all that much (biolizard's theme in particular), it gets the blood flowing and really gets you into the game.Story and lore stuff is good. Like how they did in Frontiers how they took the previous games and brought them into a new context they did the same here giving a new understanding of the previous titles that Shadow was in.(also I realized that Big the Cat really hasn't met many other characters really, IDK why this was a surprise when the two meet here as he says "your name is Shadow, right?").Addition: The power scaling mfs will have a field day discussing this story.

As indifferent about Frontiers as I am, one thing I have to give it credit for is that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around and just running aimlessly into collectables is pretty fun. The white space here offers you that same enjoyment as a nice filler in between zones. Shadow's new powers feel a lot like the wisps from previous Sonic games, but are integrated very well with the level design and act like an extension of your moveset. The only honest to god real complaint I have about this game is that I wish it were longer, a sentiment shared among many other players (though the white space certainly helps pad out longer hours.) _childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr: If you like Sonic gameplay both in 2D and 3D, play this. If you like Shadow the Hedgehog (the character), absolutely play this. It is a really good game, I swear. Once again, the Generations game is an absolute gem. (From Edit 3:) If the Sonic part one day stopped working for me, I would not even care if it meant Shadow Generations would still be playable. Shadow's side is just THAT MUCH FUN. I reiterate myself, ABSOLUTELY play this game if you like 3D and 2D Sonic & especially if you like Shadow. You will most likely not be disappointed.I love Shadow the Hedgehog, man. Biased review, because I bought the preorder deluxe lol, but I'll try my best.From the 110 minutes I played in Shadow's portion: S ranks are pretty manageable, or I am just way too good rn. 2D challenges are so-so, I would rather have more 3D ones. I suppose it's fine though. At least the ones I played were pretty short though, so no biggie there. Collectibles are usually easy to spot or require just a little bit of looking around, nothing too difficult. Story seems a bit fast paced, but I am also at the start, so I will hold off on giving that a proper rating. The intermission map is much better than what OG Sonic Generations had.I feel Sonic Frontiers controls are in place, might be wrong. That means that 2D is slower, with emphasis on remembering the layout and jumping (and using Shadow's abilites) well. 3D is pretty nice though, like really chill. Controls are easy to change though & there's an option to use legacy Sonic Generations control scheme.Graphics are very pretty, though nothing to put in a "RTX demo" kind of material. Game is actually really smooth on 60 FPS all the time, except the 30 FPS cutscenes, which I don't mind, but it is a little funny. Audio is also a banger.Collectibles have so far been a joy. Everything is beautiful.Issues: So far only had an audio bug which was fine after restarting my PC: Kinda weird, but didn't happen later.Edit: So, I finished Shadow Generations! It was amazing. Difficulty went up with more Doom Powers to use and yeah, S ranks aren't so easy after all. The ending boss too, so much spectacle, but not the easiest! Only real trouble was the Doom Morph power up - it felt a bit finnicky, though it did get its job done and is pretty cool otherwise.Story was Generations-esque - short, pretty fast-paced, repeated beats from older games, but it was sensible enough thanks to its simplicity - though the ending scene made me cry a little. It is very nice. Only bummer is that some CGs have this weird aspect ratio, so everything is just slightly stretched horizontally. Dunno why.The hub world is honestly absolutely amazing, holy hell, it's so good to roam in itPerformance was always absolutely fine.I am giving this a 9/10, maybe 8.5/10 if I had a bad mood, which I don't, because I got to play as Shadow again!Edit 3: Nah, I think the 9/10 is solid by now. Really fun game and movement with Shadow. Just a very very enjoyable experience.Sonic side is just Sonic Gens with minor changes, the rewritten dialogue I could honestly care less about, though it is unnecessary. And going from Shadow to Sonic made me realize this: I much prefer Shadow over Sonic in this game. Shadow's double jump is just preferrable, his Chaos Control is just awesome. Sonic goes faster, his gameplay is more about speed, while Shadow is about playing a stage gracefully, if that makes any sense. Sonic Gens is like an 8/10. Definitely felt worse after Shadow Gens, but that was to be expected, since the team has advanced their craft. Shadow's challenges are fewer, but don't feel too inflated, unlike what I felt in Sonic Gens (especially since you need to clear just one challenge there, while Shadow needs to clear two for one key).So, I won't be editing this anymore, but I'll say this: I'd buy the game just for the Shadow part only, it is THAT good. Sonic Gens remaster is the one who feels like a DLC to me. Sonic Team made an amazing game with Shadow Generations, they should keep it as one of the best they ever made.

_childDocuments_.review: I have beaten Shadow Generations and replayed every stage a number of times by this point. I have tried to let the recency bias wear off as much as I could, and I have to say; this is far and away the cleanest, slickest, most polished 3D Sonic game EVER made.The gameplay is very much an evolution of Sonic Frontiers' gameplay style, which to me felt somewhat twitchy and hard to manage at times. Not at all the case for this game however. NEVER did I have a single instance where the homing attack locked on to the wrong enemy, or I felt that the control was the reason I died in a level.Which if you know anything about 3D Sonic, is quite the achievement.Shadow Generations boasts some of the best level design in 3D Sonic with TONS of branching paths and ways to play the 6 stages the game offers. meaning you can replay them over and over and still find new paths through the same levels.The animation throughout the game is the best a 3D Sonic game has had up to this point, with gameplay animations being fluid and blending well together. Cutscene animation is a HUGE improvement across the board, you can tell Sonic team has been given the time and money they need to deliver the stunning visuals they've wanted to give us for years.the voice acting is also excellent across the board as well with Kirk Thornton giving his best performance ever as Shadow.The bottom line is the game FEELS GOOD TO PLAY, the jank of learning a wonky control scheme or learning how not to break the game is GONE. _childDocuments_.review: I think the gameplay is fun and the Shadow content lasts about as long as the base game so it's worth buying even if you already have Sonic Generations.  However, Shadow's new lore conflicts with itself and SA2/StH and I'm extremely disappointing in the gaming community's reception of this game.I've played most of the Sonic games excluding 06, Dark Knight, Dream team and Colors.  Many people say that the franchise is washed out and can never compete with Mario for a number of reasons like how the games switch between speed and platforming sections and sometimes you can't tell when they're switching until you fall of the map, performance issues, jank, sometimes sections are too easy and sometimes too hard and so on.  In particular people hate 3D sonic the most because these problems tend to be worse in that game format.  Despite this I keep playing Sonic games because the criticism is valid but I still think the Sonic franchise has a niche of people who find it fun and I'm one of them.  For the people who don't know in 2017 Sega also used the promise of bonus Shadow content in Sonic Forces to get people to pre-purchase the game at full price.  It turns out that content took less than 20 minutes to complete, was just 3 altered levels from the original game and had a garbage story.  On top of that Sonic X Shadow Generations is just a resale of a game that came out 13 years ago.  Meaning that if people were going to hate on a Sonic game this is one of the games they'd rant over.Despite all of this the game has a 97% Steam review score as of 10/31/24.  Again, I find the game enjoyable but there's no way ALL of you do.  The only explanation is that the upcoming movie, Sega's media blitz over the game, and multiple influencer sponsorships was all it took to change all of your minds on the franchise.  Literally, 25 years of mediocre game reviews and "2D Sonic is meh, 3D Sonic is trash" mentality disappeared within a year due to an aggressive ad campaign.  Some of you can be bought for cheap and if you're one of the ones who were easily manipulated I want you to feel bad about it.Now that that's out of the way the base game is fun as it was 13 years ago except there are minor differences here and there like the dialogue.  The only obvious fault I can find is that it's still locked at 60 fps while the Shadow portion of the game caps out at 120.  If there was a change that needed to be done to the base game it's that the game should run at least at 120 fps but perhaps such a change could break the physics so it's unavoidable.The "X Shadow" portion is interesting.  Shadow can slow time, throw spears and do a lot of other things Sonic can't.  You might think this would be hell and they'd force you to use abilities on a seconds notice or fall to your death but this is rare.  Traditionally, Sonic games have alternate routes which can be accessed if you time your jumps well or have certain powerups in certain parts of a stage.  This ends up making some of the levels a little vertical as these routes tend to be on top of each other.  In X Shadow his new moves are sometimes used to open up alternate routes instead of only timed jumps making the levels more horizontal and mixing it up a bit.  On top of that the levels are much larger compared to the base game and have less bonus stages.  For reference It took me about 7 hours to complete the story of X Shadow but 4 hours to complete the base game while doing the minimum number of bonus stages for each.  Steam says I've spent 13 hours on the original Sonic Generations including doing every bonus stage so technically the base game is longer but only if you pad it with the less interesting filler stages.For some reason X Shadow doesn't have a single level from "Shadow the Hedgehog".  I don't consider "The Ark" stage as good enough as it as it's more iconic to SA2 and the music is the SA2 version and not the StH version.  This would have been a great opportunity to add Final haunt or Digital Circuit.  While they're at it they could remember that Shadow's final level in SA2 was Final Chase and not Final Rush.  This is the second time Shadow has had Sonic's music in his Ark stage.  At least they kept the music direction of the base Sonic Generations instead of Sonic Forces/Frontiers repetitive (And IMO low quality) music direction for stages.My biggest gripe with the Shadow portion of the game is that the story conflicts with itself and other Sonic games.  In a bit over a month Sonic 3 the movie will come out and they've already hinted that Shadow's story in the movies will differ from the games meaning Shadow's backstory will become even more of a confusing hellscape due to some important plot points in Shadow the Hedgehog being implied but not stated.  To get the full story you'll still need to play SA2, read between the lines while playing StH at least 6 times and play this game.  To illustrate some of the conflicting plot points I'll give this spoiler example:SA2:  Shadow was created to be a global protector.StH:  Shadow was created to be a global protector and to kill the Black Arms.SXSG (Gerald in cutscenes): Shadow was created so Gerald could find a breakthrough to cure Maria from a disease.SXSG (Gerald in diary): Shadow was primarily created to appease Gerald's G.U.N. backers who wanted more weapons research but also to cure Maria and take out the Black Arms.These story problems aren't a deal breaker but this game's one goal was to make the game's cannon cohesive but instead it fragmented it further.  The game gets a recommendation from me because the gameplay is good but know that the story is all over the place.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't had so much fun playing a game in a long time. Easily one of the top ones I have played this year. I will only be reviewing Shadow Generations, as it was the only reason I bought this and I never played the original Sonic Generations. Sega knows how popular Shadow is, and I fell for it. Since Sonic Adventure 2 came out over 20 years ago (man I'm old), he's been one of my favorite characters of all time and I am not complaining.The story took me about 6 hours to complete, the rest of my gameplay time is from collecting stuff and replaying levels. I didn't have high hopes for the writing since every game I played with Shadow since Sonic Adventure 2 has been disappointing to me, but with what we have here, I was very impressed. Wish there were more cutscenes and there were some missed potential moments, but overall, it wasn't bad at all. There were quite a few times where I was genuinely impressed with the writing. Shadow deserves it, he's a great character.It's been such a long time since I have actually enjoyed boss battles instead of viewing them as a chore to get past. I loved all of them in this game, and the cutscenes during them were amazing.The surfing is fun, and the sound design for it is pretty relaxing. The powers are cool, and collecting stuff in the hub world is fun too. It feels like there's alot of side-things you can do after/during the story.My main complaints are that while the powers are cool, some of them are a little hard to control. Some sections of the levels feel pretty slippery to play as well. The variation of difficulty with gameplay changes drastically sometimes in my opinion. I also feel like the U.I. could be more straightforward with how to fast travel, and there should be a key on the map to explain what the icons mean, because for some of them I had no idea.I am so glad I got this game though in the end even with these issues. If you like Shadow, you need to play this. If you aren't sure, maybe wait for a sale. Either way, I think it is worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: A remaster of Generations was not particularly needed, aside from the awkward way it runs on PC, but it was a fun game with some great music so hearing it was coming back wasn't a bad thing. However, the Shadow half makes this more than worth it. The level design is done in a way that is punishing but fair with a lot of branching path for those with lightning reflexes. The overworld, to me, feels like they jammed all of Frontiers into a Mario 64 Peach's castle and I'm here for it. The new powers are weird... but fun to use and don't feel left behind ever - they all keep getting use beyond their initial reveals so that's really nice. And the music is outstanding, but I mean, obviously. It's Sega, what did you expect?The story, though, is an absolute joy. Original Generations was serviceable, and once again, Shadow's side brings it to a new level. I don't want to spoil it, but it's very touching and has quickly become a favorite. The game is pretty short, but what's there is very solid, which is good because while the story might not take a ton of time, the replayability factor is through the roof. There is so much to do for those who want to 100% everything, or for those who are too bad at games for stuff like that, it's still fun to explore and try new challenges. Or even just pop on Doom Mode and hang out in an apocalypse nightmare, you know, whatever!The controls for the remastered side are still a little on the jankier end. I'm not an expert, but I feel like maybe that wasn't touched up so much. It runs fine, but I found myself getting a little frustrated with some of the movements. Shadow's side has a ton of improvements there, but even then you should expect the occasional surprise you jumped off a cliff ending. Huge improvement from the former, though!If you are new to the series, this isn't a bad place to start! You get a sampling of the whole series to this point in time, but some of the story might not be as fleshed out as it could. It's tough for me to tell, but I think they have enough there you can follow along. For long time fans, what am I even addressing you for? Get it! It's peak! Seriously!! This might be the best "Sonic" game. I don't know. I'm still processing my experience. But it might be!

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10 Overall. (Shadow Generations 9.5/10 and Sonic Generations 8.5/10)Shadow Generations is a true return to form for Sonic in pretty much every way.SHADOW GENERATIONSThe stages are fantastic and show the potential of what peak 3d boosting gameplay could be. The doom powers and chaos control provide replayability in learning to master them to access different routes. The act 2 of the stages show that Sonic team can make brilliant 2d levels, I think it felt way better to have a seperate 3d and 2d act instead of trying to fit 2d segments inside the 3d act. I think the bosses were an upgrade on Sonic generations in every way. I thought the story and presentation was great in doing Shadow justice after it felt like Sonic team had forgotten about him for years. The music was amazing again which didn't surprise me, I always know the sound team will deliver. The open world hub area was a great addition and added some of that frontiers open zone charm to the game which I think fit together nicely. If Sonic team are continuing with the frontiers gameplay model then I think they should focus more on what they did with this game, tune back the open zone a bit in favour for less but longer and more developed cyberspace levels. SONIC GENERATIONSThe only downside to this whole package really was going to Sonic generations after playing the Shadow generations side. Sonic generations just felt a bit outdated in comparison and i feel like they could have given it a bit more love and polish. But still, Sonic generations is a great Sonic game by itself and is nice to have alongside the Shadow portion of the game.CONCLUSIONThis game is a must have for any Sonic fan and is a great jumping on point for anyone wanting to give Sonic a go. We could be entering a grand and exciting era for Sonic, of which hasn't been seen for over a decade and now is as good of a time as any to hop in and join for the ride.

_childDocuments_.review: This is only a review of Shadow Generations since I can't be bothered to play Sonic gens as well, Shadow Gens makes Sonic Gens look like a horrible slog in comparison...and Sonic Gens was considered one of the best Sonic games for a while so that should say a lot.Look man. I am a huge Sonic fan, but I hate playing most of the games. The last time I remember having fun with Sonic was Sonic Unleashed and even I can admit, that wonderful game does has flaws... But Shadow Generations... I honestly think it's the best Sonic game we've had... like... ever? The controls are so polished and satisfying. Usually in Sonic games I find a spot where I end up dying because of clunky controls and it just makes me angry, but every death in Shadow Gens felt justified and deserved. I didn't get mad at this game once. The game also doesn't punish you too hard for small mistakes, which I personally love. You really feel like you are Shadow when you play.The levels are so satisfying and have so many paths you can take. They feel very natural to play and have such fun set pieces in it. Every level was very exciting and satisfying. Now they do have 2d levels, which usually are my most hated thing ever but this game SOMEHOW makes 2d levels fun?! I have no idea how they did it? As for the main event for me... Shadow... omg... I don't even want to say anything and spoil the fun but as a HUGE Shadow fan this game is crack to me. He is freaking adorable and cool as hell in this game and his story was so satisfying. Like as a Shadow fan who's felt like he's been out of character for, like, over 10 years, this... this was it, we are so back. I honestly couldn't be happier. There are so many things I could gush about in this game, there was clearly a lot of love and passion put into this game, which has been missing from this franchise for years. It's not very long to play through, which in my opinion is a good thing because it's repayable as hell but a normal busy adult can actually complete it.Look, just buy this game and play it. _childDocuments_.review: Since I've fully 100%ed the game, I felt I should give the game a review. The best way I can describe this game is "I can't believe they bundled Sonic Generations with the best Sonic game ever made". So far, anyway.I mean, Sonic Generations... is Sonic Generations, but with better dialogue here and there, and the Drop Dash is here too. It's a game I already really enjoyed, and I enjoyed revisiting it just as much. Shadow Generations, on the other hand, quickly has made this 2-in-1 deal my favorite Sonic game of all time. There is SO much to love here, that frankly I would be here ALL day talking about it, so I'll try my best to keep it brief.The story is great, while I think the pacing is a little quick and could've used a bit of extra time to breathe, that's frankly a minor nitpick in this overall great story. It's not as grandiose or interesting lore-wise as Sonic Frontiers's story, but it's a delight nonetheless, and fans of Shadow's character will love it for sure like I have.Like with any game though the most important thing is the gameplay, and this game has an Open Zone-esque White Space to explore, which is really fun with plenty of collectables and side challenges to complete which you can really sink your time into if you want, but of course there's the main levels, and the bosses. On the levels, GOD these have to be some of the best 3D Boost stages the series has to offer so far, they are incredible! So many alternate paths (especially in the final level, I still have yet to see every single path myself), they're pretty lengthy being about 5 minutes on average, but they're fun throughout that entire runtime. And don't misunderstand me, the 2D stages are awesome as well, while not as long or with as many branching paths, they're fast paced and really fun to run through, too! And the bosses... I almost don't want to say anything and just tell you to experience them yourself, they're AWESOME! While not as epic or blood pumping action filled as the Titans from Frontiers, they're really fun to fight, and the optional Hard Modes are no joke, either!The last topic I should bring up is, as you can probably see in the icons in this review, somewhere, I played the entirety of the game on Steam Deck. And it works great! Really smooth experience in both games, although some really dense areas in Shadow Generations caused the framerate to drop a bit (a particular section in Chaos Island comes to mind that just makes the game chug), but it never became unplayable or anything, and felt really smooth.Overall, if you haven't played Sonic Generations, then this game is a mustbuy. If you're a Sonic fan, you already have this game and loved it, be serious with me now. And even if you have played the original Sonic Generations, this is a fun way to re-experience it, along with an incredible new campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow the Hedgehog (シャドウ・ザ・ヘッジホッグ Shadō za Hejjihoggu?) is a character that appears in the Sonic the Hedgehog series. Characterized by his sharp wit and strong sense of purpose, Shadow is a recurrent arch-rival of Sonic the Hedgehog, whom he resembles and shares many abilities. His trademark power is Chaos Control, which allows him to warp spacetime with a Chaos Emerald.[7][8][9]Created over fifty years ago by Professor Gerald Robotnik as part of Project Shadow onboard the Space Colony ARK, Shadow was conceived to achieve immortality and was infused with the DNA of the alien Black Arms. As the "Ultimate Life Form", he possesses several innate talents, including agelessness and formidable combat skills. After his birth, he formed a deep bond with Maria, Gerald's granddaughter. However, the Guardian Units of Nations (G.U.N.) deemed Shadow a threat and raided the ARK, resulting in the capture of Shadow and Gerald, and Maria's death. Driven to madness, Gerald brainwashed Shadow to seek world destruction.Shadow remained in stasis for decades until he was freed by Doctor Eggman, Gerald's grandson, to assist in his plans for world conquest. Although initially motivated by vengeance, Shadow's true memories were eventually restored by Sonic and his friends. He helped save the world from Gerald's doomsday plans, but lost his memories as a result. When the Black Arms invaded Earth shortly after, Shadow uncovered the truth of his past, regained some of his memories, and thwarted the aliens' agenda. He has since then decided to move on from his past life, and committed himself to protecting the planet on his own terms, often joining forces with Sonic and his friends while facing his own adversaries.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Generations is a great game, a decent experience, and a trudge to fully complete (90 challenge stages is absurd). Shadow Generations is a fantastic game, a wonderful, heartfelt experience, especially for long-time fans, and a joy to 100 percent (some of the characters should've helped find the last few collectibles though)! The Music was seller as always, The level design was nearly flawless, and the presentation... THE PRESENTATION! Finally seeing a Sonic Game with fluid animations and Wonderfully composed Cinematography is genuinely heartwarming. The voice acting as well is, bar-none, the best in the series due to the fantastic direction with the line reads; rarely ever did I feel as if a line was given incorrect or stiffly. The stages and Bosses are some of the best the series has to offer. The level design allows for beginners to enjoy a fun, action packed romp, while more advanced players will be inspecting every last inch of the stages for risky routes and corner cuts. The doom abilities allow for these levels to truly Stand out due to their seamless incorporation of platforming and short-cut opportunities. The bosses absolutely blow every other game out of the water game-play and presentation wise (Sonic Frontiers' Titans still win in the hype department though)! The story is simple but allows for Shadow's character and his relationship with Maria to be forefront most of the story. This Game is a must play for any Sonic fans and a strong recommendation for both casual and experienced players! 10/10 (was going to give it a 9/10, but Shadow gave a genuine smile to Maria!)

_childDocuments_.review: I really didn't know what to review this game, since 'ok' isn't an option. But I thought I'd give it a shot anyways, since I have strong thoughts on it despite my mixed feelings. Spoilers ahead.Firstly, the Generations remake is more just a pc port of a pc port. It's lost bugs and gained them, and it's slightly choppy. But the story is slightly better, and all the lines are rerecorded which is trippy as hell, but ultimately a plus I think. You can really hear Ian Flynn's influence in it, a lot subtler than usual despite it's bluntness. A lot of 'this is for my friends', and that's fine. But honestly the changes aren't really that interesting, nor good, they're just there.Planet Wisp Act 2 is still terrible, and the final boss is still ass, that didn't change. But the rest of the game being really fun hasn't either. Both Sonics have the drop dash, and it works for Classic and sucks for Modern. Want to Air Dash but are close to the ground? Roll into a pit. Want jump higher, so you hold the button down? Drop dash into a pit when you land! It's real clunky and annoying, but honestly it didn't rear its head to much.But Sonic Generations is just that, Sonic Generations. New chao collectibles, a drop dash, and that's it as far as I can tell. It's a good game, with a huge drop off at the end, as it always has been.Now, Shadow Generations.... wow, what a doozy. First of all, it has one of the greatest starts of any Sonic game I've ever played. I've never been more excited and happy while playing a game since when I was a kid, honestly. It was amazing. It held up strong for the first few stages. The story starts great, and the writing is a bit on the nose, but still fun. The first three stages were really good!I really want to state here just how good the first half of the game is. It is utterly fantastic, and that's awesome. But... oh boy.Gimmicks are to Sonic what meth is to that one guy under the bridge who speaks in eldritch tongues I can't comprehend. And these 'Doom Powers' are all absolute ass. The chaos spear is fun and fast paced, but the surfboard and... oh, the squid... Shadow the Fish-hog is aaawful to control. But the surfboard is like... okay? It feels super weird, and it's used a LOT.Shadow Generations goes HARD with its gimmicks, and it doesn't give. Each gimmick gets a boss fight, you don't get to do one as just 'Shadow' which really sucks. Biolizard is super fun, but it has an over-reliance on the Chaos Spear, but it was still awesome. Metal Overlord, while ♥♥♥♥♥♥' cool to see, was ENTIRELY on the surfboard. And... oh my god, Mephiles, I love you so much my boy, but your fight was THE SQUID NOOOOO NOT THE SQUID PLEASE GOD ♥♥♥♥ WHY THE SQUIDPoint is, each gimmick isn't just a 'power-up'. Nah, it's an entire different character sometimes. A bogged down, sluggish and clunky different character. It just sucks that these cool moments were bogged down with such ♥♥♥♥♥♥ gimmicks.But that's not my biggest problem with Shadow Generations. That problem is... re-use. It re-uses assets and levels. AGAIN. "Green Hill Again?" No, much worse. Two of the five stages are... FROM GAMES SHADOW WASN'T IMPORTANT IN, AND WERE SUPER RECENT. AND ONE OF THEM IS FROM FRONTIERS, WHICH HE WASN'T EVEN IN AT ALL.What the ♥♥♥♥ were they thinking? I know, and you should too. Money, money, money.Shame on you SEGA, but what's even worse.Shadow Generations, the celebration of Shadow the Hedgehog... HAS NO LEVELS FROM SHADOW THE HEDGEHOG!Are you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ kidding me SEGA? Levels from SONIC FORCES, and SONIC FRONTIERS where SHADOW WASN'T PLAYABLE AT ALL!!! And it was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Chaos Island! You took levels from games where they reused levels from Generations, the cycle continues! It's terrible! And the music just ♥♥♥♥♥ itself when you get to those levels. From cool remixes, kind of Eurobeat-esque in a way, to terrible dubstep that grates on your ears. It really falls off HARD at the Forces level. Then Metal Overlord shows up, and it's like "Yo, sick! It's that guy!" The boss fight kinda sucks, but Crush 40 plays in the background so it's okay. "Man, that Forces Level kinda sucked. Why was it there? Anyway, glad to see we're back on track." Nope. Instead, there aren't even two more levels before the next boss, it's JUST FRONTIERS.But MAN, I was so excited to see that purple goop all over the place. Mephiles is in the game, and I'm very miffed and unsure about my feelings on that. But we'll come back to this.So, we've had The Ark (Final Rush/Chase), Bullet Station, Kingdom Valley, Sunset Heights (♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ City Escape again, mind you.), and Chaos Island (kill me). Black Doom is popping off, what's the final level? They're saving the Shadow the Hedgehog level for last, let's go! It's gotta be Final Haunt, right? Or maybe The Doom? Something really representative of Shadow the Hedgehog (the videogame, the one Black Doom is from).Radical Highway. It's Radical Highway. Which was already in 2 or 3 levels throughout the game.So what I think happened is, they got halfway through the making Shadow Generations and realised something."We just spent loads of time on the Gens Remake, we have no budget or time left! What do we do?" "Oh man, what about those Radical Highway parts in The Ark? Just use those!" "But the game is so short, we have no time left and only three levels ready!""Uh, oh! Shadow was in Forces, right? Use one of those!""But we have another boss after that part!""Oh ♥♥♥♥... uhm, oh! Use the Frontiers one! The one they didn't like, the '2D Island'! Make it 3D""You got it boss!"Seriously, I think they realised they didn't have time to finish it. So they slapped a half-hearted second half of the game together. They say in the game "Oh, you haven't visited those places? Probably means you do in the future" in the same way they make excuses for Sonic visiting Green Hill again in Frontiers. And Neo Devil Doom's design is cool. But the fight sucks, and the fact that it sucks sucks.Anyway, the gameplay is ass whenever a gimmick kicks in, we're used to this. But the story makes no sense either, when you think about it.So, Black Doom is trying to bring back the Black Arms thanks to the time whatever the ♥♥♥♥ is going on. Fine. Why is Mephiles not doing that? He says "I just want to exist!" Which, first of all, he is the MIND of the GOD OF TIME AND SPACE. Why would the GOD OF TIME AND SPACE not be capitalising on the fact that TIME AND SPACE is broke so he's back? He's a manipulator, and he should absolutely be doing what Black Doom is doing. Black Doom... never could do that? His power only ever related to the Black Arms, and he used Chaos Control when he had the seven chaos emeralds to warp the comet to Earth. That's it.Did they think the Snapcube Fandub was canon or some ♥♥♥♥? I'm so confused.OK so I've run out of characters, didn't know there was a limit here. _childDocuments_.review: If you already own Sonic Generations then I can't recommend picking this one up for the current price. Shadow Generations was fun but only lasts 3.5-5 hours long (depending on how many collectibles you go for). I wish they released Shadow Generations as a standalone game and let it cook in the oven a bit longer. It was entertaining for a first run through but I don't feel any strong desire to keep replaying it like I have with other Sonic games. I was kind of disapointed to see that there were no cross unlocks between the two games. After 100% completion (all stages and all collectibles) there were no fun hidden unlocks of any kind other than stuff you can view in the collection area. No Sonic skin over shadow, no Shadow for base Sonic Generations. Just a record tab that says 100% and nothing else. Kinda stung, was hoping that there would be some sort of reward but I suppose not. Sega does what Nintendon't and sells a digital deluxe version with 2 character skins (one for each game) for 10 extra bucks,yet has no other unlockable skins in the game. Sonic Generations feels tacked on and exactly the same as its original pc release, with some cutscene changes and a few new graphical options that I just can't tell if they are making a difference or not. Shadow Generations can run at a solid 100 fps yet Sonic generations is capped at 60 and doesn't feel like its running at 60fps despite what my fps counter says. Textures and models look just like they did when the game originally released, but hey at least now you can find Chao in each level(and the only thing you get for finding them is a fun png in the collectables area showing you what they look like in the level wow so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool thank you Sonic Team!!) If you were a fan of Sonic Frontiers boost levels then you will be in heaven with Shadow generations. If you were not a fan then most of the level design will just be whelming for you like it was for me. Don't get me wrong there was some really cool set pieces in the first few levels but due to the movement physics that come with frontiers boost levels I felt like I was always being held back from actually going fast.tldr of my ramblings, wait for this one to go on sale, especially if you already own and have played Sonic Generations. The price point is way too high for a rerelease of a 13 year old game with barely any additions. Shadow Generations should've been released on its own for 20 bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game.Sonic Generations is one of my favorite games, and seeing it come back with more is great. It does, however, feel like the new port is a bit buggier than the original. I got stuck on a lot more things than I remember.They made lives an option which is really cool. Then there's the drop dash.For Classic Sonic, it's a skill that is automatically applied to your skill set. You can turn it off. YOU CAN NOT TURN IT OFF ON MODERN SONIC. IT ALSO CHARGES IF YOU HOLD A, THE JUMP BUTTON, AFTER JUMPING. This basically leads to you holding the jump button, , and then charging the drop dash for under a second and getting a fully charged spin dash off the side of the stage. There is NO WAY to rebind the control either, so if you stay on legacy controls you're just stuck with it.They've also cut out a bunch of the random stage achievements which is a bit sad but I also didn't want to do them for a third time so I don't mind too much.Almost none of the gameplay improvements from Shadow's campaign made it into this port either. The game opens up a new executable when you choose sonic on the main menu, so I have to assume it's just running a modified version of the old game.All of that being said, the game still very good and worth playing. Definitely one of the best Sonic games to exist. Hope the modding scene is able to move some things over to the new version.I really liked the new story content that came with Shadow. Not only is he peak fiction, but they also made a lot of improvements to the engine and gameplay that make the experience a lot more seamless than regular Generations. Retrying has almost no load time and also keeps the music playing rather than restarting the track. A small touch but it means a lot to me personally.The cinematic and graphical presentation is also fantastic. It's got that sonic flair without it detracting from the gameplay in most cases.The levels are very fun and the movement is great, which makes most of the challenges are satisfying to S rank. I've seen people do some crazy stuff with the chaos spear ability stalling you in the air for example. This game is also way way harder then base Generations. S rank is determined by time alone, rather than just being A Rank without dying. For example, a mechanic you unlock later pretty much doubles the amount of S Ranks you have to go for as well, and the time requirement on the last level doesn't change between these modes, so you need to play perfectly to get the S.The collactible unlocks are really cool. Glad we get to see a lot of shadow related stuff. There's a lot more than I thought there could be.The overworld also has fast travel, which I didn't realize I needed until I used it. Incredible addition.I do have a few issues, namely in the overworld challenges and a specific instance of some boss fights.Some of the overworld timer challenges are a real pain to actually complete. It really just speaks to the fact that this is way harder than base Generations, but I had a lot of trouble trying to get some of these done. The challenge is nice, but the walk back across the entire hub world, even with the fast travel, when you make a mistake makes it take way longer than just having a reset button in the pause menu and makes the grind drag on.To my knowledge, the collectable locations aren't tracked in any way around the map, so all you really have to go off of is the number of the artworks you get. not to mention that there are a bunch of small items  that just add to a number, so you really don't know which ones you missed, even if you were to look up a guide.My last issue lies with a specific attack that two of the bosses have. If you've played it, you most likely know the one. I'm probably just bad, but the telegraphing really really does not help when trying to dodge this attack. It looks like it marks an area, but sometimes it's safe there and other times it isn't. I'm pretty sure that it's not actually marking the spot and just alerting you to the attack. That being said, the depth perception in the fight doesn't really line up with where the attack is going to be, so it's really a toss up as to if you're going to get hit or not.Pair this with the achievement to not get hit at all by the final boss, and said boss using this attack on the last phase with , and it really wastes your time and infuriated me. Only took 45 minutes though :))))Despite the flaws, the game is fantastic and definitely worth playing. There is so much in here to do and most of it is good Sonic fun. Edgy Cringey music, enemies that are just barely in the way that mess you up, and most of all going fast. Really can't recommend this one enough.

_childDocuments_.review: So I think since this is essentially two games bundled together, it would be best to review the Sonic and Shadow chapters separately.I'll be honest, the Shadow Generations portion is the main reason you WANT to have this game in your library. Incredible story, incredible gameplay, and incredible graphics. There were parts of the game where I was floored that the effects were being rendered in-game, and wasn't just a pre-rendered video. I feel like this is the game where Sega finally nailed the design of human characters in Sonic, and I hope this means future games will show more human/mobian interactions in their society. Shadow's input response is incredible. He moves perfectly to the buttons I press. That also means you need to make sure not to panic press every button. A lot of the levels that Shadow's story calls back to play way better here than in the games that they originally featured in. They made  actually good. The Open Zone in this game is an improvement on Frontiers. You still have plenty of freedom of movement, but the space is better used as you're not stuck in the middle of nowhere with nothing to do. The story is probably my favorite part of the game. Shadow's story is predictable, but in a good way, because you know where it's going, as well as the emotions that you'll be feeling by the end. And the ending was perfectly delivered. I would also highly recommend watching the Dark Beginnings episode Trilogy on YouTube before playing Shadow's story, as it bridges everything together, while also setting the mood of what you're getting into. If you've never played the original, and didn't get a chance to buy the original PC version on Steam, don't worry. Playing this will give you more or less the same experience. A fun mashup of Sonic levels from previous games in the series. Each level has two acts: Act one plays out like a classic 2D Sonic Platformer, while the second act plays out in 3D with it's own playstyle. Get to the goals as fast as you can, but remember to watch your step! It's a good introduction to both 2D and 3D Sonic game mechanics if you're new to the franchise. If you've already bought and played the original Sonic Generations, there's not really much different in this remaster, aside from some cleaned up graphics, cleaned up voice lines, and some input changes. A lot of it was just some quick polishing while making sure that the game itself was pretty much exactly as it was in the original. They didn't even patch some of the bugs that I swear were in the original. While that's great for people who want the OG Sonic Generations experience, it does make for a stark contrast compared to the Shadow Story, who's gameplay and graphics are so smooth that you feel like you're playing a much older and clunkier game when you switch to Sonic's story. Because you are. It'll even open Sonic's story in a separate executable than the main game. I experienced that personally when screen-sharing the game to friends in Discord. When it changed executable, it interrupted my screenshare, and I had to restart it. This doesn't make Sonic's part of the game bad, just that it's showing it's age, which makes sense as it originally came out in 2011. That being said, there are reasons to play Sonic's story, if anything, just to spot the differences between this version, and the original. Some cutscenes were altered to better fit the new script, but most of the animations remain the same, for better or for worse:  Overall, Sonic Generations does have some jank, but that's expected out of older games. It still remains one of the best Sonic titles of the 2010s. Full of charm and love for the series, iconic levels and iconic music, including great remixes of the classics.

_childDocuments_.review: This game simply puts a tear in my eye. Not only did you bring back the gameplay to a level comparable to Generations and Unleashed, Shadow Generations even IMPROVES on them in some aspects. Mainly being that Shadow controls so well both while boosting and not boosting, this makes all of the platforming a joy to do. (In Generations and Unleashed Sonic can feel like he is running on ice while accelerating) The second improvement is the level design, (I KNOW, IT'S CRAZY BUT THEY DID IT) it's just straight up better than Sonic Generations. The levels are much longer with a lot more open environments with a beautiful abundance of multiple paths to take. (It just feels excellent to replay all of the levels because of this and is never repetitive) Unleashed is still better when it comes to obstacle placement and fast reaction timing though. Then there's the open zone part of this game. It simply does what Frontiers tried to do but much better. The world feels so much more engaging than Frontiers instead of being a lot of automated platforming and big empty fields of grass. The texture/object pop-in is also reduced compared to Frontiers. (They basically took all of the right lessons, WAY TO GO SEGA)I also want to bring up the boss battles. They are outright fantastic. 3D Sonic bosses tend to be sort of simple with the mechanic just being dodge some obstacles, get close enough to the boss and homing attack. But Shadow Generations takes inspiration from the Frontiers titan fights and combines it with the regular formula, and the result is awesome. The only things I don't like about this game is nr. 1 the homing attack, (But only the version Shadow does while attacking an enemy) it's not as fluid as Unleashed or Generations. But no way near as bad as Frontiers thankfully. (The Frontiers homing attack is super slow and takes away all of your momentum).The other thing I don't like is the EDM Dubstep music. Seriously what is up with this? It does not fit in and is very annoying to listen to. Might be a matter of subjective view, but I think Sonic and organic Rock goes together hand in hand much better as it matches the attitude of Sonic and Shadow.VERDICT: Sonic Team managed to create a truly quality game with Shadow Generations. It honors the Sonic IP with respect and the player's time and money too. If they keep this up we are in for an exciting foreseeable future. (I can't wait for the Keanu Reeves movie DLC!) The only thing that worries me is that Kishimoto is directing the next mainline game. He did not take part in making this. Which is probably why this is actually a good Sonic game.But as they say nowadays, WE ARE SO BACK!!!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This is the best 3D sonic package out there, with the Shadow Generations portion being BETTER than its longer older brother.It feels like every 3d game after Sonic Forces has been leading up to Shadow Generations in a gameplay sense. The evolution from lazy level design, to reused good level design, to now the most solid level design in the series has made sticking with these games a rewarding experience. I already liked frontiers a lot, but it feels like Sonic Team took all the complaints about its controls in cyberspace and lacking length and level design and delivered wholeheartedly with the most passion filled sonic (shadow) game in a while. It pays a lot of respect to the eras of sonic that were looked down on by gaming publications for years with a story that's trying to say something a little more heartfelt than the past few games. It has issues like all of these games do, while I appreciate the effort to tell a moodier story it feels a little rushed at the end, as does the rest of the second half. However purely on the merits of its level design and gameplay, I think sonic team has found their groove here, and makes me super excited for the next, longer, mainline entry.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing this review, I have about 3 hours on the game (2 on the original Generations portion and 1 hour on the new Shadow stuff). So far, it's been phenomenal. The Shadow material is so well-crafted, from gameplay to presentation. The voice acting on Shadow is surprisingly stellar and the animations are so fluid and lively, packed with incredible audio design and some of the most intricate level design the series has seen so far, and it's undeniable that you'll find a great time here.The original Generations portion is familiar and safe, especially if you've played it before, but I've still been having a lot of fun exploring these remastered levels to find the newly added chao's littered throughout the stages. I did run into a few visual bugs on the OG Generations portion; however, the Shadow stuff has been seamless - no game-breaking bugs so far.I woke up at midnight to play this game, and it's currently 5 AM as I'm writing this. I have work in a couple hours, but I couldn't resist the urge to get up and play it as soon as it came out. So far it's been absolutely incredible, and the stuff I was most excited for (the Shadow material) is shaping up to be some of this series' best efforts at making the spectacle, speedy platforming experience that this franchise is known for. _childDocuments_.review: It's a pleasure to navigate the hub world, each stage is pretty well designed, there's a lot of collectables to find, there's a really good soundtrack filled with some very nostalgic songs, and you get Sonic and Shadow Generations in a single package.
