_childDocuments_.review: Full disclosure, I have already 100% the game on another console and the only reason I haven't played much on here yet is because I've been stuck on a laptop that will explode into a mushroom cloud the moment Doom's Eye decides he would like to turn Radical Highway into a kaleidoscope. The Sonic side of this package is a good(if a little disappointing) remaster. The actual gameplay was the exact same as the original, if a little smoother now. The new chao rescue gimmick if kinda mixed to me. Someone at Sonic Team must be going through something, because some of the chao locations were just straight evil. Collecting every chao doesn't really do anything except have them appear in the hub world acting cute. It's kinda neat, but the reward isn't enough to make it worth doing IMO. If this package only consisted of this, I don't feel that it would be worth the price. Fortunately that's not the case.Shadow Generations is if you took Sonic Frontiers(a fun but also objectively kinda ♥♥♥♥ game) and made it into just a good game. The open world design is not ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up anymore, the platforming is actually integrated into the level instead of whatever the hell was going on with Frontiers. The main levels are all pretty damn fun and surprisingly varied and open ended; in fact I would say that these are probably the most open 3D levels since maybe some of the levels of Sonic Adventure and Heroes. The new gimmicks are also very neat. The new time stop mechanic works well and is pretty well integrated with the level design. The new Doom powers are for the most part cool. They are like the wisps of Colors, but I'd argue more interesting. Doom surf is probably my favorite of the bunch, it's fairly intuitive on how it works and is well integrated into the level design. Doom morph has been getting some flak due to being unintuitive and the game doing a bad job explaining it. While I won't argue with that, I will say that once I figured out how it works, it's actually a very fun ability to use; in fact, I would say it would be the best ability, if it wasn't for what I said earlier, and because outside of Chaos Island and the hub, the ability doesn't really come up often. My favorite part of these new abilities is how they all come together to make one of the most complicated time attacks I've seen in the whole series. Most Sonic games I find are fairly simple to start time attacking and getting good times, but with the new abilities, along with the multiple level paths and the quirks of the movement, I find Shadow Generations to be a very fun and challenging one to time attack. Overall, Sonic X Shadow Generations is 100% worth getting for Sonic fans. Even non fans seem to find this title appealing. I'm glad Sonic team proved me wrong on this one. Now how will they manage to ♥♥♥♥ up the next one?

_childDocuments_.review: Not a fan of the changes to Sonic Generations, they were really unnecessary and tacked on for the sake of selling the game again. Shadow Generations is great but I wish it felt more like a full game rather than an amalgamation of ideas and stages. It's quality sure, but it's more to test the waters with Shadow getting a story again within the games.Because why is this the only time Shadow's Doom powers show up, why are events from games that haven't happened yet, present in the game? Why no Shadow the Hedgehog 2005 representation?Overall, a fine enough package but Shadow needs a fully fledged game of his own with this type of gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: SONIC X SHADOW GENERATIONS

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine getting an insanely good sequel to Shadow the Hedgehog and an expansion to Sonic Generations that fixes its issues (better 3D control feel, more balanced 2D/3D ratio, a way better final boss fight) taking notes from some of the best aspects of Frontiers. Now throw in a remaster of the original Sonic Generations with added features like skins, multiple save files, and some new cutscenes more in line with Frontiers and the modern versions of the characters. You don't have to imagine it, it's right here, and it rules.I expected Generations with its own version of Forces' Episode Shadow, something super short and not anything noteworthy. This is not that at all. it is a must play for any fan of the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Controller configuration for the Sonic Generations portion is seemingly bugged right now, but the HD cutscenes are an improvement, as well as some dialogue changes I've heard of. Shadow Generations feels very much like a sequel to Shadow The Hedgehog (2005), but in a very good way. In tandem with the Dark Beginnings anime shorts, the "Shadow's Story" menu selection, and the campaign itself, the game serves to add a lot to Shadow's backstory, and also to the world of Sonic in general. For example, *SLIGHT SPOILER*, when playing Shadow Generations, it is revealed that the Sonic V. Shadow boss fight in Sonic Generations is NOT in fact Sonic fighting PAST Shadow under the ARK, but instead it is the present Shadow who fights Sonic over the Chaos Emerald which Sonic needs to beat the Time Eater. A very fresh change of pace in the franchise, keeping quite a few mechanics and other aspects of Frontiers in Shadow's campaign, while not being an exact copy of the "Island Hub to Cyberspace" formula

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic x shadow generations is a love letter to all sonic fans around the world, it takes an already great game and enhances it by giving us genuinely THE best 3d sonic game ever, im not kidding. lets go more into detail about sonic generations first. sonic gens: so i actually havent played it yet as idk i kinda dont want to rn i will eventually, but ive seen all ive needed to see. its barely really a remaster and moreso a port but that isnt a bad thing, gameplay: gameplay is the same though they did introduce the drop dash for both classic and modern sonic so its a nice little bonus for those who like that move. the extra edditions such as the chao resuce missions seem cool, you can collect chao and view them in the little collection room its kinda cute. no chao garden though obviously. the skins are fine, they dont change anything about sonics base effects or anything which is a shame same as terios but i will get to that later.story: now on to the controversial part. the redubbing, so as we know ian flynn has now become the main sonic writer, he wrote sonic frontiers story and i think in my opinion it was pretty good, not perfect but pretty good. now ive seen a lot of people give this guy hate for redubbing and rewriting base generations. and i have to say, its not a big deal at all. it really doesnt affect anything in the end its sonic generations it wasnt known for having a story at all. overall the gens side of things are pretty yknow nice, its basically just sonic gens you get what you pay for. i think my one issue is the cutscenes werent re animated to fit the redubbed lines.shadow gens: here we go THIS is the main attraction and will be the reason you buy the game or not.gameplay: so gameplay wise it uses the sonic frontiers gameplay formula, instead of having a 2D level select like sonic generations, shadow generations uses the frontiers open world idea but takes it to the next level, theres so much to do in the relatively large map, its not huge but it isnt small either, theres alot of platform challenges, fun gimmicks, AND its all got a very nice aesthetic (looking at you frontiers floating platforms). more of the hub world unlocks when you get more doom powers which is a really cool idea. on top of that shadow feels EVEN better than what sonic felt like in the open zone, he feels way more polished and refined. overall just very fun to mess around with.little thing with the terios skin is i just wish it had a different aura effect and had different animationsThe levels in shadow generations are more akin to the cyber space formula except it actually feels amazing and fun to play, shadows controls unlike cyberspaces feels SOOOO much better, in fact his physics are identical to the ones when hes in his hub world, he turns sharp, hes easy to control, theres barely any homing attack hit stop, its perfect genuinely is the best feeling sonic game ever. the levels themseves are just amazing as well, obviously this has generations in the title so it would follow the same pattern. replaying through past stages shadow has been in (and frontiers cause time eater stuff) and much like generations the level design is FANTASTIC. this game ALONE has more branching paths in levels than any sonic game period. there are so many ways you can go about beating a level especially after you unlock the wings. and also the levels are long again!!! long are the days where we play 2 minute mid stages. a normal shadow gens level takes about 6 to 5 minutes to beat, obviously if you play fast it will take 3 to 4 minutes but its super fun to speed run!now the main gimmick of the game, the doom powers. shadow becomes corrupted by his black arms DNA and taps into his unknown potential known as his doom powers. these powers range from being able to stun multiple enemies at once with the doom spears which enhances your chaos spear, launching enemies in the air and sending them flying teleporting where they land with the new doom blast ability, gaining the ability to surf on the water using the doom surf ability, becoming a damn squid and swimming in purple goop (probably mephiles's) and being able to grapple little orbs to get to higher places, and finally gaining the ability of flight with the doom wings, it uses the boost gauge so you cant fly forever. i almost forgot about one of the most important additions and a main mechanic, chaos control. when you kill a certain amount of enemies your chaos control gauge will fill up and you can literally stop time for 5 seconds, the level design has a lot of uses for chaos control and how it can be used. a cool little tip is chaos control completely refills your boost gauge when activated. it also stops the in game timer, so go out and speed run people!bosses: like generations there are only 4 bosses including the final boss, but these bosses are amazing and are way better than in sonic generations, play for yourself you will see. all i will say is omg the 3rd boss man......hes peak. they all use the doom powers as well each boss requires you to use a certain power to defeat them. but the bosses are super fun and interactive.story: and finally we reach the story, its amazing, its heart felt and made me tear up a couple of times. ian flynn did a fantastic job writing shadows story and going deeper into his past. i wont say much about it but it is one of the best sonic stories in decades, the voice acting is spot on too, kirk did amazing with shadow and is honestly now my favorite shadow voice actor. overall sonic x shadow generations IS the definitive 3d sonic game to get into, its perfect for newcomers and perfect for longtime fans. even if you dont care for sonic you NEED to experience this game at least once in your life. so whats my rating? 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Since this comes with two games, I guess I’ll review both.Sonic Generations:I’ll be quick about this one, since it’s exactly the same as the old version from 2011. I have always loved this game. While it was far from the first Sonic game I played, it was definitely the one that made me a bigger fan of the franchise. I played this game so much as a kid to the point where this is probably the only game I could ever speed-run (maybe RE 4 as-well). Sure the story is overly simple and Classic Sonic’s physics might not be like the Megadrive games. But I have too much fun with the rest of the game to even care. This was a great way to celebrate the franchise back then and it still holds up now.Shadow Generations:Wow, this was a nice surprise. I can’t believe it, but we finally have a boost game that’s not just: "hold X to win". The level design is actually competent and the game overall feels great to control. It makes me want to go back and replay all the stages and improve my time and rankings. I have not had that feeling since the the original release of Generations and it feels so good to actually feel addicted to a Sonic game again. I also loved every single boss in the game. They are filled with so much fan-service and they are actually fun to play as-well. The music is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome, but we all knew that would bang. They added a lot of songs from past games as well for you to listen to while replaying levels and bosses. I can’t really find much wrong with the game. I guess the only thing I noticed was the voice acting being kind of weak. I’ve never really been a fan of the current Shadow voice, and although he has seen improvement over the years, I still feel he sounds off. I guess poor directing was a part of it. I have a feeling a lot of people will enjoy the story in this one. While I think it’s better than Sonic Generation’s story (not a high bar, I know), I think that just comes down to the fact that Shadow as a character is more interesting and has a lot more groundwork for a story. The story in this one is still just about him moving on, which I already thought was the point of the 2005 game? But hey, if a lazy story is an excuse to play reimagined blasts from the past, then I’ll take it! This is the best Sonic game since Mania and is worth your time and I’ll even say your money. Especially if you have not played Sonic Generations before. Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: Not only do you get an already fantastic 3D Sonic with Sonic Generations, a game that still holds up remarkably well, you also get the best 3D Sonic game period with Shadow GenerationsOn the Sonic Generations's end, its probably the best remaster in the Sonic series on the fact that this remaster isn't falling in on itself. the addition of the Drop dash is appreciated, but not as useful as putting the drop dash into the Sonic Origins compilation, and the redone dialog leaves me split like, again, I appreciate it, but some lines don't hit the same compared to the original. at least the Chao rescue stuff was a fun additional side quest. other then that, its Sonic Generations as you remember it.Shadow Generations though, THATS what your buying this for and my biggest complaint is that there's not more of it, cause this is boost Sonic perfected even further. The new open ended white space is also fun to run around in, just be wary that going for everything in white space isn't exactly a fun time due to the map screen seeing a huge downgrade compared to Frontiers's map screen. Also the story is also one of the best in the series, even if I wished we had a little more time with these characters, though maybe this is some god-like play to make us relate to Shadow more lol.If you enjoyed Sonic Generations, or want to experience it for the first time, I'd say $50 is a great asking price, even if you already owned the OG Sonic Generations

_childDocuments_.review: SONIC X SHADOW GENERATIONS is an unpleasant case of tie-in sale. The base game isn't bad so to say, but it holds itself almost solely on fan service (it won't be half as appealing if you haven't played other entries), the final boss is pathetic and the few improvements introduced by this new version feel lazy and buggy. As broken as Sonic Colors: Ultimate is, you can at least fix it all with  and enjoy what I personally consider to be a much better 3D Sonic game.That said, the new Shadow episode is worthwhile, and currently, there's no way to get it other than accepting to give SEGA a bit more of cash for what would otherwise be a shorter and more affordable release. It would've obviously been miles better if SEGA let us skip Generations and buy just this part of the game, especially as it runs on a different engine and is launched separately anyway. If you don't want to give in and if you're not in a hurry to play Shadow Generations right away, just wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Generations:A relatively unchanged rerelease of the original 2011 title, and while that isn't a bad thing, I certainly would not call this a remaster. Aside from the few new collectables in the stages, and the minor dialogue changes which i appreciated, this is the same old amazing experience as it was in 2011.Shadow Generations:Absolutely what the future of the Sonic series should strive to be. The quality and polish on all fronts is at the top of it's game in this entry, and I really hope to see this carry forward. The level design is engaging and endlessly replayable, the open hub world is a joy to run around in, and the characterisation and story is, while limited, very endearing and so fun to see.Overall, this is an amazing package with 2 of the best entries in the Sonic series to date.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic! Love the cutscenes in Shadow Generations. The doom powers are really cool and experimental. The new dialogue in the Sonic Generations portion of the cutscenes might need to grow on me a little bit however. Level design in Shadow Generations is great and the final boss is MILES better than the final boss in Sonic Generations. But a message for Sonic Team and SEGA, for the next main-line Sonic game, no more reusing level themes/level designs. The levels in this game are phenomenal but we do not need anymore nostalgia in the next game. It is proven with Shadow Generations that you can still make amazing level design and creative ideas, but imagine that with original level themes.Anyways, this to me is a 9/10 right now. I might be a little bias since this is recent but my score since it released hasn't changed and probably won't change since it's addicting to replay levels and speedrun them too. I'm also glad that the pop-in is somewhat being ironed out, however it still in some areas is noticeable but not fully. Amazing!

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Generations takes the open world exploration from Sonic Frontiers and builds on it with having Sonic Generations tier level design for the main zones.  If you enjoyed just roaming the world in Frontiers and saying "how do I get that collectable" or "what's up there" you'll like it.  If you enjoyed the tight controls and expansive levels of Sonic Generations, you'll like the main zones.  The design of the overall game shows us just how good a full new Sonic game made in this style could be.  If it has one flaw it's that it's kind of short, but it's bundled with the original Generations to make up for it.  Replaying the original was fun.  Overall a good game and I look forward to where Sega goes from here.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Generations is easily one of the best games in the franchise. Each stage has two acts, both of which are incredibly well-designed and full of insane challenges. I’m not usually a fan of 2D sections, but the 2.5D perspective in this game really helps with visibility, letting you see what’s ahead. Shadow's speed is perfectly balanced in these sections—you can boost without being punished harshly, while still needing to react quickly to shortcuts. Huge win in terms of gameplay design.The bosses? Absolutely insane. Each one is super cool, with unique mechanics that made every battle stand out. The way they incorporated the Doom abilities into each boss fight was next-level and kept things fresh, making each encounter feel distinct and thrilling.I completed every act challenge with an S rank, collecting every item along the way. The challenges are actually challenging, and finding all the collectibles is fun rather than a chore. Every stage offers different routes, with hidden paths leading to keys and collectibles, adding a lot of replayability.The abilities are handled perfectly, feeling essential in many stages and adding depth to the gameplay. The hub world also offers tons of content, and even after all this time, I’m still not done with it. The reappearance of several beloved characters, each with a great introduction and charming cutscenes, is a fantastic nostalgic touch.Overall, Shadow Generations delivers in every aspect. I can’t wait to see more games like this. Absolute banger, 10/10.

Sonic Team cooked, and i'm excited to see them continue to use this gameplay style for future Sonic installments! Oh and Doom Squid is a bit finnicky at times but doesn't boggle the rest of the game down so kudos.

_childDocuments_.review: For Sonic Generations: Massively overpriced considering how old the game is and how many sales and cheap keys there are out there.For just Shadow: Rather short and feels like a big step down in terms of story compared to Frontiers writing. Like an imitation was made but the direction is wooden. New voice actors feel a little off and Shadow "whisper shouting" lines doesn't even have the fun edgyness to it.For those who already own Sonic Generations: Effectively being forced to double dip despite the original still holding up.So already not great and it will probably take a while before a good sale that makes the price tag around what this is actually worth paying for.For those that can ignore the price tag: The game (specifically Shadow, I skipped Sonic) is well made at least, the engine feels improved and there were no technical problems at all. In fact the range of options available was one of the first things I noticed. Wonder if a studio like RGG (Yakuza) is rubbing off on Sonic Team.Shadow gets an experience based on just five (?) games: SA2 (twice?), Sonic Heroes, Sonic 06, Forces and Frontiers. Note that Shadow doesn't even appear in Frontiers and I never played Forces considering its awful reputation, so he didn't get the big treatment Sonic did; somewhat ironic since the game kinda presents "getting to Sonic's Birthday party" to be a goal before the actual goal. In addition while the music remixes are generally great, Frontiers music is just awful, at least you can replace the stage music with actual Frontiers music. Speaking of music, you unlock a LOT of Shadow the Hedgehog music - so bizarre that there are no Shadow stages then.Another thing that makes it feel short is there are in-level cutscenes and neat transitions to teasing the final zone, it does eat up a good chunk of the stage the current zone is supposed to be paying homage to and usually it's for some trippy reality bent ride instead of a SA2 tribute. Replayability will likely suffer for it when it could have been held separate as one of the challenge levels (which are rather simple, easy and short).Boss fights are well done as a tribute act for them. However, Emerl never appears so that's a weird marketing only decision. SA2, Heroes, 06 and Shadow bosses but nope, Battle is still not actually mainline.So overall too expensive for what you get. Considering nobody I know has played let alone appreciate 06 and Forces, for a tribute game there's a big hole where Shadow's story related levels could have gone instead when base Generations already covers 06. Absolutely not worth full price to original Generations owners, this isn't a Yakuza title promising dozens of hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Generations:A good remaster for a game that was already excellent, with lightly rewritten dialogue and cutscenes that benefit going beyond the original bare-bones story from the 2011 release.Shadow Generations:We're so back, a great standalone game with deceptively expansive levels offering multiple routes and secrets that reward repeat playthroughs using new abilities exclusive to Shadow, the best boss fights the series has to offer, and the most stunning in-game cutscenes to date for Sonic games. The whole experience oozes with care and refinement, especially regarding the writing, character interactions, and voice acting. (Seek out the Gerald Robotnik journal entries, simply amazing storytelling and lore to chew on and theorize whats to come for the future)This is the game you would recommend to newcomers and longtime fans. This is the production value that'll set a new standard going forward for the series. A two-for-one deal under full price that offers fulfilling gameplay experiences and tons of replayability.

Voice acting was good as always, this entire game was just so much fun and my only issue with it is... I WISH IT WAS LONGER!!! _childDocuments_.review: Shadow's story is essentially Sonic Frontiers 1.5. It combines the best gameplay from Generations and Frontiers while also trying a few new things. This game features the best level design and the best movement mechanics the series has ever seen. Shadow's story is a bit short, you can beat it within 5 hours and then it takes another few to get 100% completion, but that's still including 6 locations with 12 acts and 4 boss fights. The open world is much more well-designed and impressive than Frontiers' ever was. All this and we also get Sonic Generations itself as a remaster that functions much more smoothly than the previous PC port of the game.It's a small shame that you can only use half the new control scheme in Generations, it would be nice if we could fully unmap the homing attack from the jump button like in Frontiers and Shadow's story. It's also a shame we can't access all the new BGM options from Generations, only Shadow's story.Even with these nitpicks it's still easily the best total package Sonic Team has ever released.

_childDocuments_.review: I know a lot of people were mad that Generations got a remaster before Unleashed, and I get it, but look at what we got. Sonic Team took everything they learned from Frontiers, went back to Generations, and COOKED.The original Sonic Generations isn't much different from the excellent original game from 2011, aside from rewritten cutscenes which give much needed life to this game, new low poly skins (which I will ALWAYS be happy about), and extra collectibles to keep you speed running for hours. On top of being fully re-written and re-dubbed, certain cutscenes have been reanimated. For instance, the opening where Sonic would be holding Amy back with his hand while talking with Tails, Sonic now just kind of ignores Amy who is awkwardly holding a plate of cupcakes. While I do like the original cutscene more, this new one is fine.Now, Shadow Generations on the other hand.... HOLY CRAP. Stunning. Simply stunning. Shadow controls wonderfully, his new powers are a blast to use, and the places he visits, while new to him, aren't new to us. Places like Sunset Heights from Sonic Forces and Chaos Island from Frontiers have been rebuilt to be thrilling roller coaster rides that never stop the excitement from coming. The levels we're given are, while only 5 zones before the finale, split into two acts a piece. Act 1 is always in 3D while Act 2 gives us the 2D platforming that's been fine tuned to near perfection.As Shadow is exploring his White Space, he comes across familiar faces from past and present. Orbot and Cubot appear trying to build an escape rocket to get home, Big shows up after you play Kingdom Valley and does nothing, Omega is the first you come across just as surprised to be there as Shadow, and even Maria and Gerald appear from just before the ARK was raided. Sonic even shows up for a tie in for the original game in an awesome cutscene!Sonic X Shadow Generations is MORE than worth the price of admission! If you never played the original from 2011, now is the PERFECT time to hop in and experience 3D Sonic at his finest and giving Shadow an excellent solo adventure that all fans can be proud of! Just be sure to go into the options and change the control scheme back to the legacy controls for Sonic Generations before you hop into the game.Drop the cash on this game as soon as possible to show Sonic Team that THIS is the golden standard we want to see our favorite hedgehogs running at!

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Generations is the greatest 3D sonic gameplay to date. The level design, the physics and momentum, the new abilities, the soundtrack, the STORY...Everything is incredible.What an emotional rollercoaster this game is - especially if you watched the prequel animation - and its an absolute blast to play from start to finish.I am genuinely beyond all words blown away by how well these levels are designed. Sonic Team finally got their act together after so long and created some fantastic, responsive, good-feeling, challenging sonic gameplay that makes you feel fast and feel awesome. And they know it too, because this entire game just oozes confidence in its environment, spectacle and level design.It's peak, everything about it is peak.Shadow is back and the best he's ever been.Sonic Team PLEASE give us more of this in whatever you do next.10/10As for Sonic Generations... yep this is definitely Sonic Generations.If you liked it back then you'll like it here again, and the script rewrites here and there make the story feel like it cares about itself a little more than the original.But you're not buying this game for Sonic Generations, and part of me wishes that instead of working on its remaster, they should have just made even more content for the other half of the game... cause Shadow Generations absolutely blows the original game and all others that came before it effortlessly out of the water.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent updated version of Sonic Generations, one of the best 'modern' Sonic games (though it's over a decade old), plus a full campaign as Shadow the Edgelord. I'll be honest, I liked Sonic's half much more than Shadow's, but that's probably the nostalgia factor working on me. Sonic's levels are a lot more memorable and visually interesting; Shadow simply doesn't have the history or iconic soundtracks to work with that Sonic does. That said, Shadow's content makes up for this by being a bit more refined, having better boss fights and using some incredible dimension-shifting set pieces. It's also a touch harder than Sonic's content. I appreciate how the devs managed to make Shadow feel distinct from Sonic, with meatier enemy-smashing, teleport attacks, unique abilities and moves to unlock, and not least his power of Chaos Control. Activating this will turn missiles into temporary platforms, which can be used to reach collectibles and different pathways. You'll need your timing to be on point if you want to earn those S-ranks.One thing about Shadow's campaign that I kind of disliked: the treasure hunting in the hub world. If you're looking for everything, you'll probably need a guide at some point, because it gets so dull flying around the map trying to find it yourself.Overall, this is one of a select few games I've purchased on release, without waiting for the price to drop, and I don't regret it. Absolutely recommended for any Sonic fans or Sonic-curious people, especially if Generations passed you by.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Generations Remastered:Overall, a very faithful remaster of the original that's harmless at its worst, and offers a lot of great additions to spice up the experience for anyone who knows the game well already. The only thing that's not 100% faithful would be the redubbed cutscenes, but, seeing as the original barely had a story anyway, it does not personally bother me; hence, harmless at worst.Shadow Generations:Peak. Sonic Team finally seems to have fully found their footing in Hedgehog Engine 2, as everything that was great about Sonic Frontiers' physics and visuals have been improved tenfold, and almost all the kinks that game had are nowhere present in here. Both the Open Zone White Space and the levels feel smooth to play in, unlike the previous game's Cyberspace. The animations in this game, both in levels and in cutscenes are god-tier, they put a lot into this and it shows as the cutscenes and in-level cinematics have the most action seen in a Sonic game since Sonic Unleashed in 2008. As for this game's story, it has great ideas but personally I feel they could have done better in some aspects. Definitely enjoyable through and through though. Overall, I'd give this 2-in-1 package a solid 8/10. Love it, keep it up Sonic Team!

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion, if you like Sonic Frontier's speed and specific mechanics, then yeah, this is an excellent game. As someone who has only played Adventure 1 and 2, Frontiers, Sonic 1, 2, 3 and Knuckles, Sonic the Hedgehog (Sonic 06), that one "3d" Sonic game for the Sega Genesis and is on the Sega Classic Collection for the Xbox 360, and that one Tetris spinoff with Dr. Robotnik, this game is very good compared to them and bares a lot of resemblance to Sonic 06's art style, a few references to it (near the end I even show a poster of Sonic 06 that's in the game), and references Sonic Adventure 1 and 2 (as expected).Do note that you do NOT need to buy the first Generations game to play this as it comes with it, slightly remastered but I am unaware what the original was like outside of the Xbox 360 demo and what the current version is like.

_childDocuments_.review: In my view, this is easily the best experience that 3D Sonic offers: a remaster of what I already considered the best 3D Sonic game combined with what is essentially a sequel with Shadow Generations.I love that Shadow Generations goes into new areas that I wished to see in the original Generations like Space Colony Ark, Rail Canyon, etc. It really fills out the package quite nicely. My favorite Sonic experiences as a kid were the Sonic and Shadow levels in Sonic Adventure 2 (and I played all the 3D ones back then!), so to finally have a game that's just top-tier Sonic and Shadow gameplay is just amazing. I'd go as far to say that this the best "spectacle platformer" I've ever played. Sonic Generations's visuals have aged extraordinarily well. It does not look out of place in 2024.The story I found to be quite nice as well. It's in many ways a sequel to the Shadow the Hedgehog game, but cutting out most of the nonsense of Shadow's messy and confusing canon, and presenting something straightforward for new players and rewarding for those who are familiar with the original games. I was pleasantly surprised by the "inside jokes" the cast around Shadow's hub world would make at times, it almost convinced me that it was worth it to keep Shadow's lore in my brain for 20+ years.I also found the 2D levels in Shadow Generations to be an improvement over the 2D Sonic Generations levels. The 2D levels for Sonic can be a bit "plain" at times compared to the 3D levels, but that's not the case for Shadow. It also helps that Shadow plays pretty much exactly the same between the 2D and 3D levels, just that the 2D levels, well, play in 2D. For Sonic, it's a bit of a shift since 2D and 3D Sonic play and feel so different. Shadow is quite a bit more complex mechanically than either Sonic, so I'm glad I didn't have to learn to play as essentially two different Shadows. That would've been a bit daunting for me personally.Whether you're new to Sonic or not, it doesn't matter. I highly recommend this to anyone who likes platformers. This one is a gem.

_childDocuments_.review: As of writing this I have 100% completed the Sonic Generations portion and will be starting the Shadow Generations section tomorrow. It was an absolute blast going through the game again after such a long time, it felt like it never left. The game still feels timeless and it was really exciting to replay all of these iconic levels and the addition to look for the Chao's where you had to search every nook and cranny of the level; it took me down some routes I haven't been down in YEARS! I would still say this is my absolute favourite Sonic game.The only issues I had was Planet Wisp (I'll never get used to it) and that they Re-Dubbed most, if not all of the voice-lines. I personally think that some of the original lines sounded better but that might just be nostalgia talking. It kind of felt awkward when their mouths weren't synced properly though I do understand why they went with this change. The other issue I have is that they didn't add any of the current Sonic songs, since this game came out after Colours; I was expecting things from Frontiers or Forces so it felt a little bit dated having Splash Hill Zone and Sweet Mountain playing, but it doesn't hinder my experience at all, just a small nitpick.It's basically the same game as when it originally came out in 2011, but still very addictive and fun. I'm VERY excited to try the Shadow portion tomorrow though, I've heard it's far better than generations.

_childDocuments_.review: If you were worried about this being a Sonic Colors Ultimate situation, where it attempts to remaster a good game but completely loses the plot (in more than just the story of that game), leave those worries at the door. This is a straight upgrade from the (now kind of delisted) Sonic Generations from 2011.Sonic's campaign is still just as beautiful as the 2011 release to look at, while stuff like the cutscenes are sharper to look at and some have gone under some re-animation to fit the new script of the game, which I will go into a bit later. Not all of them are winners, as you can tell they were animated around the original script, so you would every now and then see some character gestures not line up with the tone the lines they are speaking are saying, kind of taking you out of the actual story.The actual gameplay of this game is also a step up, at least from the initial PC release. The original felt like it was held back and could not use the resources your PC had, especially if you have had a gaming PC of the past 5 years, where no matter what you did, the game would always find a way to stutter or suffer from pop-in. Largely, the latter of the two would be isolated from the actual gameplay, and only affect background details or cutscenes. It was never like Frontiers where it would pop-in critical bits of the environment that you would need to react to to play efficiently. Framerate problems were constant though. Especially in Chemical Plant. Thankfully, these issues have been ironed out, and it is a smooth 60 fps for Sonics campaign with no compromises.While I am not too deep into Shadow's campaign, I am really pleased with it so far. Levels are longer than Sonics, averaging about 5 minutes rather than Sonics 2-3, but they never overstay their welcome, and the Chaos and Doom Powers are fun to use, and while they take some getting used to, you can tell Shadows levels were really built to use both of these toolkits. Compared to something like Forces where stuff like the Wispons were a complete afterthought, where the one they gave you is practically the best one, and you have very little reason to switch off. Here, you are met with knowledge checks and need good reactions to know what Chaos or Doom Power to use, all while it can feel slightly automated at times, those moments are very few, at least so far. If I had to describe what it is in the simplest way possible, imagine a mix of Generations and Frontiers. Generations because you get two acts you need to complete and needing to get Boss Keys from Challenge Acts, but the hub is an Open-Zone with collectibles and enemies to fight. (There is no combat system in this game though, so take that how you will.)I mentioned a rewrite of Sonic's campaign, as I believe it is for the better. The original was rather self-indulging in the "mystery" of these locations and what they actually are, but the problem was it made Sonic and Tails look not-smart because they should know what these are. Here, the mystery shifted from what they are to why they are grayed out in a white void, which I think is a much better route to take. It raises a question that anyone would reasonably ask themselves if they see their home, or otherwise comfortable and familiar location, suddenly look all drained. I get that this is a touchy subject with rewriting stories of the past, but given how the story was a common criticism of the original Generations, I think this is a net positive for the end user. And while I cannot speak too much on Shadows story itself, I do appreciate how it is recognizing more about his history than just Maria, as that is a common trope in his character and stories that center him. Even making characters like Black Doom, one of his original creators, be the antagonist for him and his runtime. I also like how they showed him "moved on" from Maria. Another trope that is easy to abuse for his character.I have been pretty positive about this game, but that is not to say I think it is perfect. That being said however, my complaints are either exclusive to people like me, or just nitpicks out right, as I do not represent the whole playerbase. One issue I have with the game is how it ties your graphic settings to your save file. This means that if you play on a proper gaming PC, then decide to pick this game back up later on your Steam Deck, the game won't configure the graphics to fit the Steam Deck, insisting that it is just your initial PC like you never left. This isn't a huge deal breaker for the Sonic campaign, because the Steam Deck is well overprepared to run this game at 60 fps, even at max settings, just to be sure to reset your resolution when you go back to your proper 1080p/1440p/4k PC. The problem lies with the Shadow campaign, as that part is way more intense to run on the Deck. Meaning that on each switch off, you have to go out of your way to fix it for your current PC. Yes, if you have just one PC this is not an issue, but it is an inconvenience for people like me who use both. If I want one thing addressed in the future, it is this. I am also ecstatic to report that you can freely swap displays in this game without running into the dreaded "Invalid Graphic Config" error. This was an extra big deal on Steam Deck if you had a dock, as you had to delete the initial Graphic Config file, run the tool again, adjust your settings, and then you can finally play the game. But since this game does not have a dedicated launcher, and can handle swapping displays, this is an error that can stay in the past, and I couldn't be happier.I haven't even gotten to stuff that is an objective upgrade to the original release like implementing proper save files for multiple runs or what the Chao do. I fully believe that SEGA/Sonic Team really did want to treat this game like it deserves the love and attention that it has garnered over the years, bringing it to new hardware while fixing what was broken in the initial release. This is how you do a remaster, people. Honestly the only reason I can think of to even look at the original is if you really want to mess with mods, but even then I would give this game 3-4 years before it catches up to the original's modding potential anyway.If it wasn't clear enough, if you haven't played the original Generations, this will do you wonders, while earning some more bang for your buck like offering hefty QoL fixes and even a whole new campaign that did not even exist. And even if you have played the original (like I have), the Shadow campaign is already earning so much of its keep to justify the price tag, at least as far as I am in now.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Generations is the same game as ever. There are a few changes to the cutscenes, and the drop dash from Mania was added, and a new chao hunting mode. But aside from those small additions, it's all the same as the original version. Which isn't a bad thing; the original game, while not my favorite, was pretty solid and didn't really need much revamping. But the Sonic Generations remaster is really just the side dish to Shadow Generations.Shadow Generations is amazing. The controls feel better than ever, Shadow has some awesome new powers, and the level design is fantastic, being basically as good as Unleashed in my opinion. Shadow also has some cool new powers which help change up the gameplay and make him feel like a distinct character from Sonic, despite their core movesets being the same.The stages in Shadow Generations are fantastic. I love the choices in stages that they brought over (except for Chaos Island -- seems like a weird choice to add a level from Frontiers), and the level design is better than ever. Stages are linear, but pretty wide open with lots of paths to take. They've really refined the boost formula with this game, and it feels better than ever. Control is tight, and it's easy to control Shadow to get him to go in the direction you want, which has been an issue for me in past boost games.The hub world isn't exactly my cup of tea, but I don't think it's bad, per se. I disliked the open-world sections of Sonic Frontiers, and while I do think this is an improvement over them, I still don't love it. I do think the formula works better in a smaller, tighter space like this, but I still don't love the execution. I'd really love them to go back to the style they used in Adventure 1, '06, and Unleashed, where it's mostly just for immersion and connecting the stages together.But despite the few issues I have, I think that this is the best boost formula game Sonic Team has made so far, overtaking Unleashed, with level designs that are just as good as that game, and controls that feel way better to me. To be honest, I've never really been a big fan of the boost formula. I think Unleashed was the best version of it, but even then, I've always preferred the Adventure style gameplay. But Shadow Generations has quickly become my new favorite boost game, and I really think it might overtake Adventure 1 as my favorite 3D Sonic game of all time. If the standard stays as high as it is here, I'm excited for the future of Sonic again.I also want to briefly touch on the story; I know a lot of people don't really care about story in these kinds of games, but I've been invested in the Sonic storyline for practically all my life, so I do care about it. Unlike Sonic Generations' story, which is pretty inconsequential, Shadow Generations actually has some really good development for Shadow's character, which could have an impact on his character in future games. I love that the story takes itself seriously, but doesn't become as melodramatic as Forces and Frontiers' stories do. It feels like it's really very similar to the way Adventure 1, 2, and Heroes tell their stories, albeit the story here is much shorter. I also love how they leaned into the edgy aesthetic again, like they did in Shadow the Hedgehog. I find that over-the-top tryhard edgelord stuff to be really charming when it's pulled off properly, and it is here.I had less-than-amazing feelings about Sonic Frontiers, but Sonic Team has really learned some lessons from that game about what did and didn't work, and they've refined the formula even further. It's taken 16 years, but I think the boost formula is just about perfect at this point. I can't wait to see where the Sonic series goes next, and this is the first time in a long time that I've been able to say that.

_childDocuments_.review: You can definitely tell this was directed by a designer from the original Gens team. Not to trash Morio Kishimoto's recent work, but this is an entirely different league of design quality. Shadow Generations is  good.Level design, boss fights, abilities (yes, Morph is fun when you figure it out), all a joy. Sunset Heights and Chaos Island are way better here than their original incarnations, awesome stuff. Story's mostly a retread of Shadow 05, and the characterization is still not quite perfect, but it has heart, which is great.The Gens remaster included is just the same game with higher res visuals, & some questionable cutscene rewrites + awful VA changes. Hud adjustments are also odd, removing button colors was a bad call.Things of note I'd like to see improved in the future:-Shadow is still rather slow,  in some of the 2D sections. Decision making/reaction pace is decent, just the sense of raw speed is lacking compared to Unleashed/og Gens, albeit vastly better than Frontiers. This is done in large part for the sake of lowering controls difficulty & challenge, but I still think it could be better. There's some dashpad segments that crank the speed up, and I wish the game had more of that kind of speed.-The quickstep isn't actually a quickstep here, it's been replaced by a pseudo-drift spin move that can be held down. In theory this could be interesting, but the game never properly explains it, and doesn't make almost any use of it in the level design. In part because the speed is lower, it feels like it just isn't needed, although the limited application it does have (like in the starting corridor in Sunset Heights) is pretty cool, with a sweet looking animation. I'd like to see this mechanic either expanded, or replaced by the classic quickstep again.-Still miss water running-Wall jumps feel kinda scuffed in how they look & feel compared to SU/og Gens. Just some leftover Frontiers jank lol

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty scummy move for SEGA to remove the OG generations from sale and sell both of these together at a higher price, and as someone, who has put hundreds of hours into the xbox 360 version of generations growing up, I would have most likely bought shadow generations separately, given the chance.Shadow generations could have been released as a standalone 20 euro game, but I guess selling a game for that price nowadays wouldn't do much to please investors. They say they 'remastered' sonic generations, but really, all they did was add some chao for you to collect, a few small minigames, as well as changed some cutscenes... for some reason.  I personally didn't notice improvemens in graphics compared to the original generations.Both games are great, but I'd say, with the amount of content, It's more worth , as the main stories for both games don't take too long to complete. Though I will say, there is a lot of side content in the form of challenge gates to complete, as well as collectibles - mostly concept art and soundtracks from past games.That being said, shadow generations currently, for me, has the best feel for the movement mechanics of any modern sonic game. It is more responsive than any game before this, and I would be happy if they kept this style of movement for future sonic games. Plus, they finally gave us the option to play at 120 fps, without the need of third-party mods, that sometimes break the game mechanics, nor frame generation, which is awesome.Shadow generations didn't impress me quite as much as sonic frontiers, however, the new mechanics for shadow are quite fun to use. The soundtrack is... well it's a sonic game, it would be kind of surprising at this point if it didn't absolutely slap. At it's price, with the amount of content provided, i would say wait for a sale, but otherwise definitely one of the better sonic games.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I want to tell everyone that this game is pretty much a remaster of the Original Sonic Generations. The game is like a two game in 1 type of deal. You cannot get Shadow Generations on its own. The game is very fun and talks about the Origin of Shadow the Hedgehog in addition to all the events going on in the Original Sonic Generations. (Along the way, you understand the "Shadow vs Sonic" Rival battle in "Sonic Generations" with some cut-scenes vs replaying that from Shadow's Point of View. )Shadow Generations is short. You can beat the game in under 10 hours without getting all the collectibles. The Power ups for Shadow are really cool, but the "Doom Wing" is very difficult to control. Also take note while using a PC controller such as an XBOX one, the controls can be a bit taking time to get used to.  I really enjoyed the campaign for Shadow as the game does highlight some of Shadow's Origin points and has a good story-line. The game is really fun and you immediately start with Space Colony Ark, -- Really is just a remaster of Final Chase with some new redesign. Radical Highway is also from SA2 also has a remaster/edited version where the level has Shadow flying and nothing really like the same as the "Original" SA2 level. Music is also remixed and fun to enjoy as well. I do recommend this game to others despite the controls getting some used to. I also want to make note that the tutorials are helpful, but on two of them it took several tries to get it right to move on if your hands are small such as mine. I was able to play this due to the Pre-order Digital Deluxe edition.  You also understand Gerald's and Maria's POV as well in Shadow Generations. The game is really fun and I do recommend this to others despite the controls being difficult at times, the power ups are cool and the last one is hard to control and takes time to get used to as it depletes your rings just like Shadow turning into Super Shadow in the end of SA2.(SA2 - Sonic Adventure 2/SA2-B is Sonic Adventure 2: Battle) The game does play positive tribute to previous games of Shadow. Especially with the level selection for this campaign. Very much a positive experience for me and I do consider replaying this to get 100% completion some other day, but overall I recommend it. If you're a new player to the franchise, this will not disappoint. If you are a returning player, Shadow Generations has the same appeal as Sonic Gens with the whole 2D/3D shift on levels. If you want to play older games to get an understanding of levels between the two, you'd have to play Sonic 1-SA2 and then Sonic (2006), Shadow the Hedgehog to understand the Black Arms, and other games.)  But, you don't have to play those in any particular order to get the gist of Shadow Generations. The only thing I'd change in Shadow's campaign was to make the game side longer in some way. But, overall I'm happy I got to enjoy this thanks to the Steam Digital Deluxe pre-order on my part, and I hope everyone else enjoy's Shadow's Origin like I do.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished both campaigns in about 6 hours.The wait was definitely worth it.If you are honestly waiting to get the OG Generations from the bundle after the delist on a discount, you won’t be missing much, it is still the same short fun game with minor dialogue changes and it’s actually functional (besides the added drop dash on Modern Sonic), so might as well be a good alternative if you missed the chance to get the OG as standalone.The real treat though is Shadow’s Campaign, if base Gens was the appetizer, then this mode is the main course of this whole pack. _childDocuments_.review: When I make this review, I'm speaking specifically about Shadow Generations, as it's the actual new game here, and oh my god did the Sonic team absolutely COOK! This is some of the most fluid and fast-paced gameplay I've ever had the pleasure of experiencing.I will say I was not the biggest Sonic fan beforehand, but over the last few months I've been getting back into the Sonic franchise, and have been very excited and very hyped for this game, learning Shadow's lore and rewatching the Dark Beginnings prologue over and over again. I may be a ♥♥♥♥♥ for this, but the ending left me tearing up, it's just something so sentimental, something so sad yet so beautiful for a Sonic game. My only complaint is that the game could've been a little longer (4 hours including me screwing around and being stupid) but I expected it to be on the shorter side since it was a 2nd campaign to Sonic Generations.I can't believe I'm saying this so many years after my first Sonic phase ended, but I'll say it now, we're so back!!Edit: Forgot to mention; THE SOUNDTRACK IS FIRE!! And I also wanted to go a bit more in depth on the levels themselves. They do an amazing job at being these long set pieces that just look so DAMN cool (And ofc, they're callbacks to older levels and areas related to Shadow), and trying to speed through the levels as fast as possible is such a blast.Each level has many, many separate branches and paths for you as the player to take, which require you to use the new doom powers alongside your own skill to reach, and it makes the first playthrough of each level so exhilarating as you speed your way through, trying to find possible alternative paths to go faster!Speaking of the doom powers, they add quite a lot of variety to the gameplay, to the point where it's no longer just a "Hold forward, jump and press X" game, and that will definitely make me replay this game again because of how well done and unique these abilities are!Again, just want to reiterate that this is peak fiction, and that the Sonic franchise is BACK!!

_childDocuments_.review: I will focus mainly on Shadow Generations portion of this package since its the main selling point and because Shadow is one of the most important characters in all fiction to me. It is recommended that you check out Sonic X Shadow Generations: Dark Beginnings animation that's on youtube and not in the game for some reason before playing.There was a point in time where I lost all hope for this series. Having my favorite characters become a parody of what they used to be, stories that were afraid of taking themselves seriously and embracing what they were, self deprecating humor that showed to me they were embarrassed of what made me love the series in the first place... When Sonic Frontiers released my hope hasn't just been rekindled, it was in flames, and I am happy to say the fire keeps burning in my heart with Shadow Generations.  The game itself took me 5 hours to finish which I fully expected and is okay since there's still bunch of collectables to find and leaderboards to conquer until hackers reach the goal ring in 0 seconds or something. I enjoyed the story and moments that were there, but the ending felt so sudden. It feels like its missing on a conclusion, after credits scene or something and no, original Generations doesn't make up for it. Shadow finally gets a second proper gaming experience dedicated to him and him alone. This time you have a fully explorable hubworld that you can interact with, along with very lengthy main levels that are bursting with visual spectacle and branching paths. For the first time since Sonic 06, Shadow feels different to control and play compared to Sonic, they finally decided to get creative. Speaking of which, there are also new powers Shadow gets, and they're all fun to play except for one which I'll mention later.Boy oh boy the spectacle in bosses was so enjoyable to witness. Aside from Frontiers and now this, there has never been this level of ass whooping and I am all for it. Going full anime, Asura's Wrath style with Shadow is something I always fantasized and now it became a reality. I enjoyed every single fight this game threw at me and I want more.- Trailers showed everything, there's no surprise to be had here minus the dialogue between characters. - Why is Dark Beginnings not included? Why does Playstation get extended cuts while the rest of us have to use Youtube for it? What the hell guys?- Some remixes really don't land, luckily you can pick what song you want in whatever stage you're playing. - Squid. I hate the way it controls, it ruined so many of my good runs, I hate the hook mechanic it has, I don't want to git gud at using it, get it the hell out of here.- The repetitive structure of Generations lives on as you can't go stage to stage but instead have to do side content to obtain keys and it kinda ruins the pacing. These levels aren't bad mind you, I just wish it was optional. Give Shadow more games, please? He deserves them.

_childDocuments_.review: A modest remaster of an enjoyable game, paired with a genuinely excellent new campaign.Sonic Generations holds up as one of the better 3D Sonic titles. The levels are colourful and fun to blast through at the speed of sound, with a good amount of content to tickle the nostalgia glands for longtime fans. Some of the jank of the original release is intact, as you might expect from an older game - the remaster is pretty "light touch", but welcome nonetheless. For example, Classic Sonic still won't feel exactly right for Mega Drive/Genesis fans, but the addition of the drop dash is a lot of fun. Overall though, despite showing its age in some places, it's still a good time.Shadow Generations on the other hand seems to have learned all of the right lessons from both the "Boost Formula" games and from the more recent Sonic Frontiers. Sonic Team has given us a tightly focused, high quality experience. Shadow is a joy to control, both in White Space and in the action stages. Even the 2D "Act 2" stages are an enormous improvement on Classic Sonic's in Sonic Generations (we shall not speak of Sonic Forces). I haven't quite finished Shadow's campaign yet, but it is clearly quite short overall. I never mind this in a Sonic game; not only do I enjoy games which value my time, the joy of the Sonic series is often in coming back to and mastering your favourite levels. I honestly think that this campaign might be as good as the series has ever been, and it's an easy recommendation to fans of any age.If you're not a huge Sonic fan or if you already own Sonic Generations, then you might prefer to wait for a discount.I would note that there seems to be some stuttering in the Sonic Generations remaster while boosting in Modern Sonic levels on an Nvidia 40 series GPU. Tinkering in Nvidia control panel with frame rate caps and forced vsync seem to have helped (if not eliminated) the bad frame pacing.

_childDocuments_.review: So, starting with the Sonic section. The big sticking point seems to be the story rewrites, and it's understandable to be averse to change. Personally, I like the changes. There are mentions to past events here that make this game feel much more like a celebration of Sonic's history compared to the original writing. Otherwise, the game is the same as regular Generations. The addition of the drop dash actually led to more mistakes than anything. It seems useable as Classic Sonic, but it is not helpful as Modern Sonic. The default control changes definitely made it way easier to jump back in after being used to Sonic Frontiers for two years. Overall, an improved Generations with a decent and appreciated slight rewrite.Shadow Generations is an entirely different beast and I love it so much. The story feels like such a small but great love letter to Shadow's history. And since Shadow has fewer games to work with than Sonic, it allows them to write a more deliberate story. So many of the story beats just ooze respect for this character's history. I also love how they've fit it into Sonic Generation's story. Gameplay wise, I was fighting some Frontiers muscle memory the entire time, which is a good thing for the most part. It feels like Frontiers in a lot of ways, but more polished and refined. I sincerely hope this is how Sonic games are laid out in the future. Overall, I love this game and look forward to the 100% grind.This collection is great and I highly recommend. Especially for Sonic fans, it is a must have.

_childDocuments_.review: This is hands down one of the best Sonic packages ever.Sonic Generations:The remaster is a perfect, 4K recreation of the original game. New moves, slightly improved physics, and new collectibles. In terms of game play, this is easily the best version of Sonic Generations, hands down. The story is rewritten, to mixed results. Some changes made are a tad cringe-worthy, but overall the story was never exactly the main draw to Generations so it's not too bad. Overall, this game still aged like a fine wine. Amazing stages with a lot of depth, fun collectibles, and amazing bosses.Shadow Generations:The Shadow side of this collection is easily the highlight, which says a lot when it's paired with *Sonic Generations*. The story is the best in a Sonic game in years, the stages are all super complex and layered whilst still being simple to pick up and play, the bosses are all spectacular, the collectibles are expansive and cover a lot of Shadow's history, and the fan-service is just immaculate.I cannot understate how much of a "must-play" Sonic x Shadow Generations is.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, let's cut the crap here. This is a review of  Sonic Generations is almost 13 years, and if you want to play it, this is the best way. It runs great, plays great and looks better than ever before. Both Sonic's now have the drop dash, for some reason. Some new challenges, some dialog changes. That's about it. OK, time for the real deal.Shadow Generations has, objectively, some of the best level design and gameplay implementation in any Sonic game. Level design has been evolved from base Gens, opening up multiple pathways and skips at almost every turn. Most of these pathways can be accessed through Shadows new Doom powers, all of which, except one (Morph), are a joy to use. The 3D stages feature all the bells and whistles you'd expect, flashy action pieces, high speed platforming and fun new gimmicks every time. That said, there really aren't that many levels. Sonic Team has clearly chosen to put great effort into these select few stages and deliver longer and more meaty levels as a tradeoff. It is up to you to decide if this was a good decision. Having 100% Sonic Forces, I say yes.Bosses are also great and deliver the sceptical you would expect. These also sacrifice numbers for run time, however.Gameplay, predictably, weakens in ACT 2. While still good, playing these fully 2D stages continues to be a real bummer after the treat that is an ACT 1. I understand that it is harder and more expensive to create fully 3D stages, but you start to dread them almost as much as you do in the regular Gens by the end.Now seemingly using Hedgehog Engine 2 and Sonic Frontiers as a base, Shadow Gens is the best looking Sonic game, bar perhaps Unleashed. Every environment is rendered to perfection and cleverly updates level assets to match modern expectations. This is maybe best seen in Kingdom Valley, now given a much clearly visual direction compared to 06. And Sunset Heights is a particular highlight, finally accomplishing the destruction and action Sonic Team... attempted, in Forces. Special shoutout to the Black Doom transitions in most ACT 1's, they are all amazing. Anyway, it looks amazing.I played Shadow Generations on a NVIDIA RTX 3050, a AMD Ryzen 5 4500 6 Core CPU and 8gb of RAM with all settings set to HIGH or above.I experienced a perfect 60fps throughout, with no noticeable framedrops in any scenario. 'Nuff said.Predictably, Shadow Gens sounds amazing.  every music remix sounds great. Space Colony Ark and Kingdom Valley in particular is stellar. Sound effects are crisp and sound exactly how they should. It's not all perfect though, Chaos Island Act 1 is a real stinker, and in my opinion,  the voice acting throughout is notably poor. Gerald just being Mike Pollok again is a bit a cheap out.I've long stopped bothering to care about stories in the Sonic videogames. Any exploration of interesting ideas of concepts can be found exclusively in the Comics (Shoutout IDW Metal Virus Arc). As the name of the game might suggest, this new story follows Shadow's journey through the events of Sonic Generations. I'm not going to go into to much detail (neither does the game), but the story does, frankly, nothing to evolve Shadow as a character. He doesn't get enough time interacting with Maria to facilitate it. That said, the story is serviceable. Just don't expect no Sonic Adventure 2 (unless you expect to just  in which case, the game is sure to shove that games lore down your neck, don't worry).It's not often you can unequivocally recommend a Sonic the Hedgehog game, it's always "a step in the right direction" or "a bold idea executed wrong". This game is neither. Shadow Generations takes a bold new approach in the Sonic franchise, and is just more of the good stuff. I experienced zero glitches, zero grinding, zero artificial roadblocks and zero moments of frustration. It's a short game, yes, but a damn good one from start to finish. It's clear throughout that Sonic Team is no longer set on "reinventing" Sonic. Frontiers gave them the blueprint of what a good Sonic experience could be, and this is the evolution of that game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Sonic Generations on PS3, Xbox360, and PC for so many hours since 2011 and I loved it. I specifically got the PC version to mod it since I had seen so many cool mods. Admittedly, when they revealed this Sonic Generations remaster, I felt it was pointless and wished we were instead getting a remaster of Sonic Unleashed as that game needs it. Then I saw they were gonna add Shadow and give him his own campaign which piqued my interest. Every trailer I've seen made me more and more excited and then the recent Sonic Central solidified my desire, so I preordered the game on PS5 and opted to go digital deluxe for PC so I can play it on my Steam Deck.The Shadow campaign is definitely worth the price if you enjoyed Generations on it's own. I've already completed Shadow's story, but I still have far more to do and I didn't even get all perfect ranks, so I'll be returning to this many times.I haven't touched the base Generations portion of the game because I don't really need to tell you that Sonic Generations is a great game. You already know it is.You're buying this game for the Shadow campaign and they add Frontiers-esque elements to the hub world, making this truly feel like Sega's answer to Super Mario 3D Land + Bowser's Fury. I will say that I wish the Shadow portion of the game was offered as DLC for the original Generations on PC, but I don't make these decisions. Overall, you're definitely paying $50-$60 for Generations plus another Generations length game and it's really about how much you wanna keep returning to the game.I know I plan on returning to Shadow Generations multiple times throughout the rest of this year.

_childDocuments_.review: I seldom write reviews but I want Sega to know that we want more. I want more. I have only completed the story in Shadows side of the game and am planning on doing all of the challenges there.Will you love this as a platformer? Yes absolutely I would say. Shadow controls wonderfully, the stages are very well made and you have multiple ways of clearing them. Some parts of Shadows new kit is a bit iffy to use, but it didn't hinder me too much to take way the fun. Opinions on that may vary. I think people who love Shadow have always wanted the ability to be able to use his whole kit not just him being another Sonic.Using Chaos control to affect the stages in various ways of actually stopping the stage clock (that sweeeeet S-rank yo!), to uncovering new ways to complete objectives in stages. _childDocuments_.review: Sonic Generations has always been one of my favorite games of all time, and I owe much of my love and passion for the franchise to that title alone. As such, I was very interested in this release. Hopeful that this enhanced re-release of the original title would improve upon the original release's flaws and provide even more fun and engaging content, I remained cautiously optimistic. Even in recent years, the quality of Sonic the Hedgehog's latest outings have been haphazard. Thankfully, however, that is not the case here; Sonic x Shadow Generations honors the outstanding quality of the original Sonic Generations and further expands upon it with the Shadow Generations campaign, providing players with an excellent entry into the Sonic the Hedgehog Franchise and a quality 3D platformer overall. After approximately 38 hours spent blasting through expertly crafted levels at the speed of sound and collecting hundreds of rings (among the wide variety of collectibles the title has to offer), I'm happy to say that I really enjoyed my time with this title. This is simply an unmissable entry for newcomers and fans alike, and a great entry point to the franchise too.

_childDocuments_.review: Do I recommend this game? Yes and no. Yes because the Shadow portion of this game is amazing. The story and gameplay, the level design, it's awesome. With Modern Sonic, everything felt alright till I got to Sky Sanctuary, where I entered a 2D section and managed to boost into the background. Somehow, what should have just been a resolution update, and bug FIXES turned into redubbing (which is good, lots of new stuff that makes the interactions better) and bug ADDITIONS. I'm extremely glad I didn't pay for this and played it through the Steam Family. Shadow's portion should have been it's own game with a twice the content, instead it ends quickly due to being a standalone expansion. Fix the Sonic side of the game and maybe I'll bump the score from the 7/10 to a 9/10 like the big journalist scores. _childDocuments_.review: Before starting this review I should say that my favorite 3D sonic game ever was the original Sonic GenerationsAs someone who has PLAYED that game a lot I think I can have a pretty good stance of a review of this game. First off, this game is called Sonic x Shadow Generations, this is not one game, but two. If you have NOT played the original sonic generations, you should buy this. Literally a no brainer, two of the best 3d sonic games ever in one package.Now for people who HAVE played generations before. I still believe this game is worth picking up even if you have zero plans on ever touching the original sonic generations within it. I haven't even finished Shadows campaign and I already have 5 hours logged on this game. I can confidently beat the ORIGINAL game in 5 hours. Granted, I am taking my time with shadows story, but gosh is it hard not to!!The HUB world in this game, oh my gosh. It's literally amazing, the entire hub area is like one giant open world. If you've played Bowser's Fury on the nintendo switch, it's comparable to that. I just have so much fun running around and performing my abilites doing cool stuff that I forget I can play the actual levels too sometimes hahaShadow plays fundamentally different from Sonic. He has new moves and new abilities. I have never in all my years of being a sonic fan felt this in control in game. It's seriously crazy, some sections might have you be able to take a higher path by use chaos control, or by using doom spears, or by electing to glide on the water or etc etc etc. In sonic generations you take the top path often by jumping at the right time! Not a terrible way of doing things but i think that shadow generations just absolutely crushes the original in terms of how you navigate the different paths.Oh BY THE WAY. These zones are soooooo open. I feel like there's so much room to breath, and so many different options for taking different routes in these zones. It's seriously so coolThis game is cinematic as all hell also! Nearly every single act has some crazy dynamic ♥♥♥♥ shadow will be skating around or destroying or dodging etc etc etcI don't know where the sonic team that put out sonic forces is now, but the team that made this must have taken them out back like they took out old yeller cuz it's unrecognizable from that game.Shadow Generations is the most complex sonic game I have ever played and I mean that in the best way possible. If you have played Sonic Generations get this game, if you haven't played Sonic Generations, get this game.Sonic Team are back in their grooveHey btw this is (as of writing this review) the only sonic game on steam with an Overwhelmingly Positive rating. Do with that information as you will!

_childDocuments_.review: This review is meant for the original sonic generations portion of the game. For the shadow part of the game, the TLDR is that its pretty good, not worth 70 dollars but good, get it on sale or something. And for extra context this review was made during the 3 day early release for the deluxe edition.If you are getting this to play sonic generations or it is the decisive factor if you are picking the game up or not, I recommend going back to the original PC release.This remaster adds nothing of value to the original and over all feels very lazy, missing things that would be very easy to add that would be very appreciated, such as new songs or art or being able to use the music unlocked in shadow gens in the original and vice versa or the ability to play as shadow in original generations, even if it were just a skin...Graphically there are no improvement compared to the original PC, and if there are they are truly unnoticeable.The rewritten dialog is very whatever and again, adds nor removes anything of value, both versions of the story are very much nothing burgers, and comes down to personal preference, but most the cutscenes have not been modified for the altered dialog so there are times where its noticeable that the mouths do not match up what was being said.There is also some censorship that twitter as all been over, rouge the bat's model has been censored to remove cleavage and cover up her back, which is a very stupid change, but then again if you are a seasoned fan of the series you already know of other aspects of rouge that have been sanded off with each appearance... ANYWAY The most noticeable thing added in sonic generations is that both modern and classic sonic have been given the drop dash, which ranges from pretty useless for classic like in forces and for modern it is very broken, causing you to clip out of bounds, or more often than not, rocketing off cliff, when it works its pretty underwhelming nothing your boost cant do without the random change of jank.Speaking of jank, I can't really back this up but theres these spots in levels in the remaster where you get caught in geometry some times and you come to a complete stop on them.I've been playing generation since its release all the way back in 2011 to date, and I swear this has never occurred in the original.The original sonic generations also had the option to run at a uncapped frame rate, while sonic x shadow is locked to 60 fps...A minor but missed feature as well is that the dpad is no longer usable which sucks for classic sonic.The cherry on top of the sour is that SEGA decided to delist the original generations, you can still get it if you decide to buy the full sonic collection bundle, which is 100 dollars and is already missing the delisted sonic 1, 2, 3, knuckles and cd thanks to origins, which is another botched port in itself. _childDocuments_.review: Who would've thought that the best 3D sonic game would be a Shadow game?The controls feel responsive, tight, and smooth all at the same time.Levels are decently long, but don't overstay their welcome, with plenty of branching paths.The small open world hub is perfectly sized for the game's length, allowing enough space to find collectables hidden around the world, but it isn't too big that finding all of them is impossible.But man, for me the highlight has to be the boss fights, which is shocking to say for a sonic game (aside from frontiers) without spoiling too much, most boss fights lean heavily into a gimmick, which sounds bad, but the way it's implemented actually works incredibly well.The Sonic Generations portion is also as good as the original, with minimal changes, and the Chao rescue from Sonic Advance 3, which was a fine addition, promoting playing levels in ways you normally wouldn't, such as purposefully taking the lower, slower path to find a Chao.While the highlight is Shadow Generations, revisiting the modern classic of Sonic Generations is never a bad time.At time of writing I have about 30 hours (played some offline on steam deck so it doesnt log properly) and have 100% completed both Sonic and Shadow generations, and I can only say:When your only complaint about a game is that there isn't enough of it? That's a pretty good sign.10/10(and yes, he does find that Damn 4th chaos emerald)
