_childDocuments_.review: I'm sad the original Generations is not 120 fps like Shadow Generations. It needed it, as playing the new updated version of Generations feels so much worse. I feel a lot of hitches too, it isn't as stable as I remember it. It's a minor thing I suppose, but the most jarring thing for me have been the updated physics. Something is definitely off, because I've played so many hours of the original Generations, blast through the original levels, yet I make weird little mistakes with the remastered Generations that I never would before. It feels a little off, but not so much that it kills the experience. I just need to get used to the new physics. The rewritten dialogue is fine, although a bit wonky since they didn't update the animations to match. I don't really notice the graphical updates much personally. It might be a little prettier? but in the same way one might struggle to see the difference between "Medium" and "High" settings in any other game. The improvements are there, but the game doesn't look any different really.As for Shadow Generations, they nailed it. Wow, it feels ultra smooth, 120 fps, no hitches, and the levels are bangers. I'm seriously impressed, and this half alone was worth rebuying Generations. I think what I enjoyed the most so far, is that the level design sacrifices the speed that Generations levels provide, and trades them off for path variety. There's so, so SO many different routes to take sprinkled throughout every level, that it genuinely feels like what 2D Sonic levels in 3D ought to be. I find myself having a lot of fun exploring the new levels because of this. Sure, blasting through levels at insane speeds is addicting in its own way, but it becomes a memory puzzle that once you master, never changes or improves really. Which is fine, I replay Gen levels for the exhilaration of speeding through the levels anyway, not to find new routes. But wow, Shadow's levels feel incredibly well designed, I was worried we'd get the garbage design we did from Forces, or the somewhat improved but mostly stolen design from Frontiers, but no, these levels are fantastic, slower(but still decently fast), and just so great to explore and try many different paths/routes. I think they found a great middle ground with the boost gameplay, and giving you a chance to have control of your character and explore like Heroes or Adventure 2.It's great. If you don't have Generations, this is worth getting to experience that, and an awesome new second half.Edit: I've beaten Shadow Generations, and I'll say.. technically it took as much time as Sonic Gen would've, but that's because of a few reasons. 1. The levels on average are longer than Sonic Gen's Act 2(Modern Sonic) stages. 2. The open world hub isn't very big but it's still 3D explorable like in Frontiers.3. You're forced to do much more challenge stages to get keys to unlock the bosses.That being said, the game has less levels than Sonic Generations. Six total zones, with Seven total 3D Modern stages and 5 2D modern stages. To me, the lack of zones is less content. I kept hearing it had the same amount of Sonic Gen, but it doesn't. I guess they kinda made up for it with the hub world but.. eh? I like stages. Still, it was fun, and the levels are awesome and varied in how you go through them. The bosses are all much better than Sonic Gen bosses, imo. They're pretty fun.

detailed_description: FINAL FANTASY XVI COMPLETE EDITION The COMPLETE EDITION is a bundle containing the following: Game Content: - FINAL FANTASY XVI Base Game - 'Echoes of the Fallen' DLC - 'The Rising Tide' DLC (The products included in this bundle are both available for separate purchase, as well as contained in other bundles. Please be careful to avoid making duplicate purchases.) Redeemable Weapons & Items: - Buster Sword - Curtana - 'Away (1987)' Orchestrion Roll - 'Torn from the Heavens' Orchestrion Roll - 'Through the Maelstrom' Orchestrion Roll FINAL FANTASY XVI Expansion Pass The Expansion Pass set includes FINAL FANTASY XVI DLC “Echoes of the Fallen” and “The Rising Tide” at a discounted price. *To enjoy this DLC content, you must have the FINAL FANTASY XVI base game installed. An internet connection is also required in order to update the base game to the latest version. *Items included in this Expansion Pass are also sold separately. Please be sure that you do not already own either of these DLC before purchasing. FINAL FANTASY XVI Echoes of the Fallen As the sun sets over the land of Valisthea, strange, dark crystals begin to circulate on the black market. Could they be the sinister fruit of a long-slumbering Mothercrystal—one the world never knew existed? Setting out in search of answers, Clive and company encounter a group of suspicious traders. Their trail leads them to a long-abandoned Fallen tower known as the Sagespire and the terrible secrets that await within... New Story Quest Unlock Conditions The new quest will become available after unlocking Origin as a destination on the world map and completing the quests 'Where There's a Will' and 'Priceless.' Special Bonuses - Buster Sword Wield Cloud Strife's iconic weapon from FINAL FANTASY VII. - 'Away (1987)' Orchestrion Roll Liven up the hideaway with a new background music track. *To enjoy this DLC, you must have the FINAL FANTASY XVI base game installed. An internet connection is also required in order to update the base game to the latest version. *Some bundles include this DLC with the base game. Please be sure that you do not already own this DLC before purchasing. FINAL FANTASY XVI The Rising Tide An unmarked letter arrives at the hideaway containing a request most curious: the Dominant of Leviathan, long lost Eikon of Water, is in need of rescue. To heed this call, Clive and his companions must journey to Mysidia—a hidden land under a blue sky—where they will uncover the tragic history of a forgotten people. New Story Quest Unlock Conditions The new quest will become available after unlocking Origin as a destination on the world map and completing the quests 'Where There's a Will' and 'Priceless.' Special Bonuses - Curtana Signature weapon used by the Warrior of Light in FINAL FANTASY XIV, reimagined for FINAL FANTASY XVI. - 'Torn from the Heavens' Orchestrion Roll - 'Through the Maelstrom' Orchestrion Roll Liven up the hideaway with new background music tracks. *To enjoy this DLC, you must have the FINAL FANTASY XVI base game installed. An internet connection is also required in order to update the base game to the latest version. *Some bundles include this DLC with the base game. Please be sure that you do not already own this DLC before purchasing. FINAL FANTASY XVI DEMO Play the opening section of FINAL FANTASY XVI. Save data can be carried over to the full version of the game. After completing the opening section of the story, players can enjoy FINAL FANTASY XVI’s amazing action gameplay in the “Eikonic Challenge” mode made specially for this demo. *Some content in this demo may vary from the final game. *It is not possible to save or load game data for the Eikonic Challenge mode. Data from this mode cannot be carried over to the release version of the game. About the Game The first fully fledged Action RPG in the mainline Final Fantasy series. An epic dark fantasy world where the fate of the land is decided by the mighty Eikons and the Dominants who wield them. This is the tale of Clive Rosfield, a warrior granted the title “First Shield of Rosaria” and sworn to protect his younger brother Joshua, the dominant of the Phoenix. Before long, Clive will be caught up in a great tragedy and swear revenge on the Dark Eikon Ifrit, a mysterious entity that brings calamity in its wake. _childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy XVI has completely blown me away and solidified itself as one of the best entries in the series for me. From the moment the story unfolded, I was captivated by the complex, emotional narrative. The characters feel real, the stakes are high, and the emotional beats hit hard. I cried more than once—it’s that powerful.The relationships between Clive, Joshua, Jill, Cid, and Gav are masterfully developed and form the emotional backbone of the game. Clive and Joshua’s bond as brothers is deeply touching and drives so much of the story’s tension and heart. Watching their connection evolve through moments of tragedy and redemption left me breathless. Clive and Jill’s relationship is equally moving—rooted in childhood friendship, and growing into something more profound as they face overwhelming odds together. It’s one of the most beautifully written and believable love stories I’ve seen in a game.Cid and Gav are also standout characters. Cid’s mentorship and friendship with Clive gave the game so much depth, and Gav’s loyalty and humor were the perfect balance to the more intense moments.When it comes to gameplay, the combat system is nothing short of fantastic. The way FFXVI integrates the different Eikons is not just fun, but also highly creative. Each Eikon fight feels distinct, with its own unique mechanics that push you to experiment and adapt. Every battle is an epic, adrenaline-pumping event, keeping things fresh even after hours of play. The blending of flashy, cinematic moments with player-driven action sequences is truly something to behold.The world is breathtaking, the soundtrack is beautiful, and the attention to detail is mind-blowing. Whether you're a longtime Final Fantasy fan or new to the series, FFXVI is a must-play.

_childDocuments_.review: FF16 a departure from earlier entries with a focus on real-time action combat and a massive sense of scale. It is a polarizing experience, where die-hard fans of past games may not enjoy this style of combat. This is a formula which the FF franchise has been slowly moving towards, and with this game, it feels like it has finally been realized. Although not as dynamic and transformative as other games in the genre, fights are flashy, controls are incredibly tight, and boss battles are thrilling in every way. That being said, the game is relatively easy, with the combat sort of being a delivery system for the story. However, I really don’t see this as a negative, since the story is very gripping, and I always looked forward to the cutscenes and what was happening in the over arching narrative. One thing I must mention is the “Active Time Lore” system, which lets you pause any cutscene you are currently watching and lets the player read about topics that are mentioned in that scene. These topics change as the story advances and as grows and as you learn more about the world of Valisthea. This is an amazing system that keeps you immersed in the world, and I can only hope that other franchises take note of. Overall, Final Fantasy 16 is a masterpiece of a game, with wonderful combat, superb writing, and VO casting that rivals the greats. This is the best FF game I’ve played since FFX, and I hope Square Enix takes what they’ve learned and make FF17 even better. An absolute 10/10 game, and an experience I will remember forever.

_childDocuments_.review: The very definition of wasted potential. The cool moments are really cool but the moments in between are a massive drag. _childDocuments_.review: Its mostly cutscenes, not much gaming. Recommending because it's still enjoyable as a game, but there's a lot of things lacking that could've been expanded on or improved. I feel like even 15 had more exciting lore to it even if it felt unfinished as a whole. This is just my opinion and thoughts so it's not very organized. TL;DR: generic plot with flashy combat. Lacks combat variation, character development, equipment variation, music variation. Interesting Eikon designs and weapon designs. Basic FF story-line of defying gods/fate, felt like a mash between 13 and what 15 probably could've been. I couldn't stop thinking about how Clive and Jill are probably what Noctis and Lunafreya should've been. But while they had more story in their relationship that made it more believable that they were a couple compared to 15,  it was still lacking in interactions that could've made it more meaningful. Most of Clive's companions lacked meaningful interactions, as they're all mostly in the infirmary or sent off somewhere. The story itself, to me, started off strong and interesting but kind of died off the longer it went on, it was just insanely predictable and generic. IMO ambiguous endings are just lazy writing as well. To me the game felt more story heavy vs combat focused, and it lacked in both. I did enjoy the game play, combat mechanics and the music, the main characters are very likable. It's visually stunning, especially the eikon designs. However, the amount of abilities you have are kind of limited...there's no variety, without using eikon abilities you just swing your sword. And you can obliterate everything with your eikon abilities, because of this I not only never really needed to simply attack, but I've also forgot I had the ability to throw fireballs for a majority of the game. I was also bit disappointed by Odin's abilities  that you get to use vs what I expected it would be with how insanely powerful he was shown to be. I feel like that could've been used as the base attack combos and they could've had something else for the eikon ability.A whole lot of gil but nothing really to use it on, Very limited amount of equipment, although I did appreciate the sword designs.The music that plays during each boss battle is the same, I feel like it would've been best used for the first fight or the very last. Speaking of boss battles, every single one had this cinematic QTE fight but it's just 2 buttons, your attack and your dodge. It's cool once in a while, maybe if they added more variation or impact, but it became dull after a while.I didn't bother with sidequests because of the one's I've done they seem to be mainly fetch quests. The game was like, semi open world? But it was dead, kind of like 15. Made me wish Clive or the chocobo walked faster.I started 16 with no expectations, wasn't really excited about it or really looking forward to it, so I'm not literally disappointed by the game or anything but it's not something I would play more than once.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this on Ps5. Got 100% finished and loved every minute. Pc performance is not great and if you don't like cutscene heavy games it is not for you. Also, the rpg elements are limited (basically just getting parts to upgrade swords and gear and the basic slotted items that increase attack, defense, specific special moves etc.) and the turn based combat is not here at all.. if these are deal breakers then no need to read on.Plays a lot like devil may cry 5 with a bayonetta dodge system. The best part of the game has to be the boss fights though. They are some of the most epic fights i've played in an action game. Especially after the bosses are set up so well through the story before hand. Great game and some great characters although, there are a few characters I felt could be more fleshed out but overall its a great game and one of the more engaging stories i've had the pleasure to see unfold. The story is awesome if you pay attention and even more enjoyable if you read the lore around the characters and the world that it takes place in. I love how you can press a button during cutscenes and it gives you lore based on what characters are in the scene and area you are in to familiarize yourself in real time. Reminds me of a game of thrones style story mixed with final fantasy. Basically it felt like a mini series with gameplay. Speaking of gameplay, it is amazing and you can mix and match so many variations of magic abilities as you go through and reset the abilities at any time and its extremely fluid.Highly recommend 8.5/10

The story is pretty damn interesting too. The game seems fairly easy so far, but i'd imagine the difficulty ramps up as it progresses further - those who find juggling the various combat mechanics a bit too much can also equip items that will automatically take care of those systems for you (auto combos, auto heal, companion orders, ect.) I do wish there was some form of transmog system, especially for weapons. I'd love to use some of my DLC/Preorder weapons, but they are extremely OP at the start of the game - im on my 3rd or 4th weapon, fully upgraded and i'm still below the attk lvl of the DLC swords.I bought a ps5 for this game and ghost of tsushima, then sony released them both on steam... i bought both, again. I hope they give us a true collection of the old Uncharted games soon..**TLDR: Highly recommend**

_childDocuments_.review: Review Update: It turns out that this game likes its inbuilt dynamic resolution setting. When this setting is activated, it'll use DLSS/FSR/XeSS (depending on your card I guess) dynamically on demand. All you have to do is leave it on and it'll do its magic while stil keeping the game looking great and steady 60 FPS (I capped at 60) without the abrupt variations I was having before when I had this specific setting off. Seriously, they did a very good job at the way it works without compromising graphic fidelity. I am now using the High preset, but people with a card better than mine could run it on Ultra probably. I have an RTX 3070. Something to note is that you won't be able to alternate between Quality, Balanced, Performance and Ultra Performance modes because the option will be greyed out on Auto despite using upscaling. The  game will decide how to handle it and will deliver very smooth gameplay. Just choose a preset according to your hardware. I have a Ryzen 5800X, RTX 3070 and 32GB RAM @3200 and the High preset delivers smooth 60 FPS at all time. I run the game at 1440p.I also recommend leaving RivaTuner at 0 for this game and only use the ingame cap to avoid messing up the way the dynamic resolution works in this title. Set the Vsync to 120Hz and cap the framerate at 60 ingame while using Nvidia Reflex for really responsive and smooth gameplay.Regarding the game itself, I don't need to add much. It's a great game with great characters, story and music and setting. The tone is very dark, grim and mature, which deviates greatly from what we are used from Final Fantasy games. A very welcoming change. Don't let nostalgic haters tell you otherwise. _childDocuments_.review: I don't usually leave reviews but 76% is a travesty for this game.2 very important points first though:1) This is not an RPG. It has some RPG elements, but it is very much an Action game. It plays like an extremely good Devil May Cry clone, and the RPG elements are surface level at best.2) Performance. This is the big negative: NPC heavy areas and particle effect heavy areas are extremely optimised. You'll need a pretty hardy CPU (my i7-11700k bottlenecked me) to get decent performance, and most areas including almost all of the combat arenas and story mission areas are fine, I was generally between 50 and 70 fps on Mid settings, before I capped at 72, I was getting over 100 in some areas. But, other areas would drop as low as 14fps, and some particle heavy areas such as the  and NPC heavy areas such as the  would sit at ~20fps the entire time I was there. Going through an area like that in an open worldy section can also affect future areas you go to, as it seems they don't despawn things properly once they've spawned in: you can get the performance back by save/quitting or dying outside of the problematic area though. Some cutscenes would have massive issues for me too - honestly the first game I have *ever* had issues with performance in *cutscenes* - but once again seems particle effects are to blame as its always in cutscenes like  and : the cutscene will just freeze and start moving at the speed of a powerpoint whilst the audio played normally behind it, and eventually (usually just before the cutscene would end) it would start back up and fast-forward to the point it should be at. Ironically if you are *only* interested in the story, watching a silent long-play on youtube would be a vastly better experience.Those points out of the way, the remaining game is genuinely incredible. Gameplay is extremely polished. It starts slow but builds up as you progress through the story: each major boss adding to your arsenal and making the gameplay feel more diverse and unique. There are great interactions between skills for different  and the way you switch between them in combat is very sleek and satisfying. Fighting trash mobs early and mid game can get a little repetitive as you settle into a routine (as almost all trash mobs are weak to the first ability set you get) but from the 3rd major power you get, you can get a very easy setup to wipe most trash mob encounters as soon as they start (making them more an annoyance than anything). However it never gets boring. You can skip trash fights if you want (unless they are part of a quest) just by running past them, and they can be useful for trying out new skills and setups.Various "mini-bosses" scatter the maps too, these can be a great experience and fighting them underlevelled is where I found most of my joy with the combat system. Each "mini-boss" (and all of the bosses for that matter) tends to be a unique experience (even with some pallet-swaps they add new mechanics and make the fights more involved and interesting) and tends to fall into an "avoid and punish" souls-like playstyle, however you are well rewarded for mastering the timings of attacks and playing aggressively as there are a good number of attacks (and I believe every single boss has at least one) that can be parried, disrupting the boss and opening a window for big stagger damage or set-up for some "feats". The timings are wildly different from boss to boss and you get punished for failing, so it keeps things interesting. In general there are a lot of moving parts in combat, for example even dodging attacks later in the game goes from a way to avoid damage to a choice between avoiding damage or setting up one of two unique feats. Point being, as the game develops the combat develops with it, and there is always something new or skill-based to try to keep fights interesting.The story is fairly interesting. It starts very character-driven and slowly develops into your standard "save the world" fare, but the personality, character interactions, voice acting etc all work together to ensure it doesn't become boring. I am a very big fan of the voice acting: each character feels unique with a voice well tailored to their personality, and all of the voices (including unimportant NPCs) follow an area-based theme, so they all feel as though they are a part of the world, not just something put there from elsewhere. The world-building is great, especially towards the start: it sets the scene fantastically and there is a lot of attention put into small details, both in cutscenes and in the gameplay areas.Exploration is... lacking. The "open world" areas are some of the worst areas, as they feel very empty and void of anything of substance. Some parts can have decent environmental storytelling, but these are usually tied into quests anyway. They can also feel very slow to move through and it feels far more like a slog than actual exploration. I feel if these areas were smaller or more broken up, or there were faster ways to traverse (yes I have the  but it still feels slow and does not fix the overall issue), or maybe more fast-travel points or just more interesting things along the way, then that would go a long way in helping, but as it stands, there are only so many "wide open plains" and "long canyon paths" you can run through before they start to get tedious, no matter the visual breakups. Quests, especially side-quests and monster hunts, will have you backtracking *a lot*. I very much started dreading seeing those little green marks pop up.Some side-quests can lead you through interesting stories, and are heavily character driven. Others, as noted, are just pure tedium. They very rarely escape the "go here, kill that" format, and most of the time you get virtually nothing (or at least nothing of use) for completing them, so they almost always feels like a waste of time, outside of the occasional character driven one (such as  or ) and very rarely someone referencing a side-quest you completed in the past (only one I can think of off the top of my head is the ). Generally not worth touching them unless you feel the game is too difficult, even then I'd suggest using story-mode over grinding the side-quests.Difficulty-wise, the game starts off very easy. Painfully so. But it does build up from there. You wont ever take much damage, so death is hardly ever a threat, but there were occasionally bosses that made me use a potion or two (like fighting the  as soon as you unlock it, or  boss fights). Haven't ever had to use the Tonics yet. The more difficult encounters are few and far between though, and generally are difficult until you learn the timings at which point they become easy, so I would still say overall the game overall lacks difficulty. For example with , I got my ass handed to me the first time, beat it with some challenge the second time, and as my game crashed after that and I had to re-do that fight, the third time it was absolutely trivial. But as said in a previous segment, the combat is generally engaging enough that even easy fights are still fun and interesting, so I don't think the lack of difficulty is too much of a downside.Overall, I have thoroughly enjoyed (most of) my time with this game, and I think it is a fantastic experience and well worth buying, even at full price..... So long as you can either deal with or look past the performance issues.

_childDocuments_.review: So far I'm finding this game quite boring.To be fair I'm only 13 hours in at the time of writing, and I know these games can be hundreds of hours long but if a game doesn't hook me in the first couple of hours, then it's not a very good game. I shouldn't have to play a game for a hundred hours before I can "appreciate" it. If someone reads this with prior knowledge of the game; at the time of writing I have just met "The Dame" and I'm level 23, I'm playing on "Action" difficulty, no rings.This game is not an RPG. It is an action hack-n-slash in the same vein as Devil May Cry. But it doesn't have the same oomph to the combat that the latest devil may cry game does, in that it's not possible to gib your enemies, there's barely any blood and gore here. One thing is for sure, the old turn based combat of earlier installments,  or real time turn based of FFXII is nowhere to be found. The combat mostly devolves into you mashing two buttons for combo'ing and sometimes evading, jumping and again mashing buttons, you also get some special moves that you can switch between with tab, these can either be focused on doing damage or putting the enemy into a stagger mode where you can really unleash upon them. Later on you get a 'limit-break' meter that can be unleashed with T, this gives you a momentary slight damage boost, and some cool visuals. But they never feel as impactful as some of the moves in Devil May Cry V, precisely because you don't get the sense that you're damaging the enemy, you just look at a HP meter and stagger meter that's decreasing to indicate that you're damaging the enemy.The itemization so far is horrid. There's always only one upgrade path, and if there is some equipment that's better than what you have, the vendor will always have that singular item in stock. For theory building, there's not really anything here, each special set of "skills" have three skills available in their tree which are combat oriented, of which you can equip two of them, with the exception of the fire tree which has six. However the game urges you into specific builds at the time of the story where they're beneficial quite heavily by giving you, as found loot, accessories that boosts those particular skills.You don't have a party, the only character that seems to stick with you for a while is your pet, and you cannot customize any party members, their skills, their gear or anything else.The NPC's, outside of four characters that "accompany you" through your quest, feel very flat and two-dimensional, on more than one occassion I was reminded of Preston Garvey in Fallout 4. When you talked with Preston, there was this awkward silence, your character was standing there looking at him, and he wasn't saying anything, before he would go "And I hope you don't mind, but I have heard from another settlement." You get this situation a lot when talking with characters in Final Fantasy XVI. Which leads into the side quests. They're absolutely cookie cutter and feel like they would be at home in an MMORPG. You get an indicator on the map that shows you exactly where to go, you can just teleport there, then immediately once you've fetched the thing, or killed the thing. You get a little popup that informs you, that you can teleport back to the quest giver, which is generally the best thing to do if you want to save your time. But this removes any sort of potential of the player being waylaid on the way back, or things not being as they appear. There's no imagination here. It's just fetch 4 bear asses and come back, there's no multiple choice, no more than one way to complete any given quest, no way "role play" your character in any way, from dialogue to quest choices, it's all set in stone.To see how to do side quests properly, look at Cyberpunk 2077 or The Witcher 3. There the side quests expand on the universe, it's characters, or the main characters back story, and are contained interesting stories onto themselves, not just busy work, like it is here.The world itself, is so far not that imaginative, it's very much inspired by Game of Thrones, but with traditional Final Fantasy crystal and summons interspersed into medieval age european kingdoms politicking and warmaking. It's filled with characters that are very predictable and stereotypical; if you've seen any recent isekai anime where the character gets reincarnated in a medieval world, you've seen this world before. But while the world looks impressive, and "epic" with it's "mandatory" 'ancient ruins' the world itself is not very well thought out, as an example during your adventures you're given these 'seals' that allows other npc's to recognize you as being one of the good guys. However, you don't get to interact with these npc's without being in posession of these seals, so you never get to see how they would react otherwise; the seals to give you special treatment are always forced onto you before you can talk with anyone in the area. This makes the mechanic of the seals, and the NPCs recognizing them completely pointless. Unlike a game like The Witcher 3 or Baldur's Gate 3, where you can explore the area and find stuff out for yourself, even to the detriment of your own progression. FFXVI never lets go of your hand.Performance wise, this game doesn't perform very well, and requires the use of upscaling technologies to deliver decent frame rates. The load times are very good though, but it has to be said it's installed on a PCI-E 4 NVME. Tested on 7950X3D, 64GB DDR 6000 Mhz, Geforce RTX 4090 @ 4k 240hz monitor.So far I would give this game a 5/10. Unless you're a fan, I would say, stay away, play Devil May Cry V instead, if you've already played that, play the two Nier titles. If you're interested in this universe and really want to get into it, play Final Fantasy XII. And if you're a fan of the series, you've likely already bought it, and I don't know why you're reading this review. If you are a fan however, surely you must lament how simple this has become.

_childDocuments_.review: ABSOLUTE CINEMAA great game in its own right. Everything related to story, characters and worldbuilding would place FF16 among the best games in the franchise.However, when it comes to gameplay it's missing a lot of RPG features from the classics, such as elemental weaknesses and status effects. There were times when I would fight a plant and switch to fire attacks, only to remember that it doesn't deal extra damage.In itself, that wouldn't be a problem if the actual combat was flawless, but that's not the case. FF16 suffers from having only swords as weapons, with Eikons just adding special skills operating on cooldowns. This means that your basic sword combo remains the same from start to finish of this 50+ hour game. Think about it, even Devil May Cry 3, which is around 12 hours long, gives you 5 melee weapons to choose from.The base game has around 8 Eikons +2 in the DLC Rising Tide. Each Eikon has 5 skills, but you can only equip 3 at a time and 1 of them can't be changed. In battle you can circle between 3 Eikons that you had previously equipped, culminating in 9 skills that can be used in the same fight, from the total of 50, so you go to battle with only 18% of your arsenal.In my opinion, a good solution would be to divide the Eikons into skills and different weapons, like spears, daggers and gauntlets, this would expand the player's options to mix and match, breaking the monotony of waiting for a cooldown to end.This issue is agravated because the basic sword attacks deals chip damage, while skills can kill common enemies in one hit, so the fights really boils down to buying time staggering the enemy until you can do real attacks.Magic is extremely boring when compared to previous entries in the series. Yes, even when compared to FF15, which at the very least could interact with the environment.The only battles I really look foward to are the Eikon fights, that's when the game truly shines with its presentation.TL;DR: story is great, gameplay is ok.

_childDocuments_.review: This review covers the PC Port, Gameplay and Story.Segments will be categorized as such.TLDR: Good enough for first time play, bad value for longer-term - expect poor PC performance.Strong 5 - Weak 6/10PC PORT:I don't know what is wrong with modern day gaming but unfortunately this is another port flop of many, as my 7800X3D, RTX 4090 system cannot achieve 100fps natively on a 3440x1440 Ultrawide. (Which is still not 4K and I read a review somewhere that this insanely priced enterprise GPU cannot hold 60FPS on 4K either absolute shame on you Square Enix)I can only achieve this by enabling Frame Generation and even then, sometimes there are cities (particularly Lostwing and other dense forest areas) which force it below the 50-60 recommended baseline FPS to have a good Frame Generation experience.Dropping from DLAA to DLSS-Q however puts the game above a constant 100+ FPS at the cost of significant visual clarity since this game turns into a blurry mess pretty much permanently, which I shouldn't have to endure with a RTX 4090.The textures are incredibly subpar for a modern day title, in Digital Foundry's video you could tell this game has zero improvement from console to PC in this regard.Gameplay:One of the highlights of this game was the Combat and it indeed is a spectacle in every possible sense, however it takes a nose dive immediately once you've achieved all of the Base Game Eikons and the depth of the Combat boils down to having the most optimal Cooldown cycle's for a particular set of Abilities to constantly shuffle inbetween them in fights and stall till they're ready again..It took me 55 Hours to do all of base game, DLC1, DLC2 and 1(+2 tries) full completion of the Gate.I'm currently going through Final Fantasy mode but all I'm seeing is mostly upgraded amulets in compensation for the absolute ridiculous higher new level cap. (60 to 110)Also there's a very particular combo which trivialises the WHOLE game - which is Will o' the Wykes, Lightning Rod, Dancing Steel, Diamond Dust and Gigaflare.Zantetsuken being an even worse offender of the bunch.If you wanna become even more ridiculous - add Berserker Ring and Genji Gloves.I do however appreciate the pushing of the player in Gate content due to the scoring system, it really puts you to the perspective that there's much to learn but not really much reward for it. (except for of course getting S-Rank in all 20 floors, once.)Story:Personally, with all the info that's provided. I think they lost the motivation half-way through to focus on the Combat.The Start of the game is strong but the seeming core gameplay loop really takes you out of the immersion and it pretty much gives you always an idea of what's coming next + the dramatic supposed twists turn redundant because of it and it REALLY, REALLY doesn't help that there are barely any meaningful side quests to add further for the story. It's almost all of it, pretty meaningless content except for completionists.The world practically revolves around Dominants and their Eikons and their ultimate purpose turns out to be so... boring in concept. I really think if they worked on what they started with Echoes of the Fallen, made it a much larger expansion to give more context on what all sorts things you can do with Aether and the Fallen - it could've redeemed the base game story.Ending is pretty much what you'd expect.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: as of right now, i cant even continue to play this. the performance issue made this unplayable. the stuttering in the first half was bearable. but anything past the bahumat fight, my fps dropped to like 12. i dropped the graphics to the lowest setting and it just made the game look even more horrible. didnt do anyhting to fix the fps. im running a 2070 super, which now, isnt the top tier but ive run other higher demanding games with no issue. this is just horrible. unfortunately im not gonna/cant finish the game. ripFor what this game is, its entertaining. buttttt.......idk what performance issues ppl are having (or maybe theyre just being critical?) but i got decent 60fps during gameplay. the CS fps would drop, sure. but nothing that was a deal breaker for me. To call this game a FF game is a bit of a far cry. This is a hack n slash (tbf they do mention that in the description). There is no magic system or party management (any party remember that joins is just passive dmg/aggro). You acquire new abilities that you have to weave in between your one basic combo attack. gets kinda boring if youve played souls, dmc, god of war, or literally any other popular h&s. not really challenging or rewarding. the flashy abilities and battle animations are cool tho.The campaign progression is pretty much on rails. There really isnt any open world exploring (or reward for exploring what little there is).  All i really felt i was ever doing was the main mission. sure theres hunts and side quests but there really wasnt anything else to do in the world to distract you. The world design seemed kinda meh. I think FF has always done a great job at creating these hi-fantasy, breath taking, vistas to view or explore. I know theres a war and blight in game, but still i think they coudlve made something interesting to look at in game or the background. The story itself is basically a Game of Thrones but with Eikons instead of dragons. Its so convoluted they added an npc that breaks down the story thus far, even added a matrix timeline so you can see how relationships and events unfolded. At no point did i ever know what the true goal of this game was. Previous FF games, the ultimate obj was clear. This game, i feel like characters were just reacting to events and happen to push the story forward. The writing for character dialogue was decent but i came to realize i wasnt a fan of the english translation. It was like listening to an episode of peaky blinders. Everyone has an english accent or some raspy, guttural voice. I felt the characters were all sorta bland (except cid, he was cool). The game does a good job at reeling you into feeling for the characters. The backstory and setup is good. However nothing made them unique? Previous FF games, every party member/npc/town had a certain fashion, look/motif, and fighting style that made them interesting. This one, they all have relatively have the same armor/clothes/weapons, just different colors for different nations. There were no real iconic weapons which, i think, is one hallmark that made FF fun. i got tired of EVERYTHING being a cutscene. i think ive spent more time watching CS than i actually did playing. With the lack of exploration and freedom, you just run from one cutscene to another. maybe some fighting here and there. but the game loop is the same. CS>run down corridor>CS>trash mob>CS>boss fight>CS. i feel bad for the time and effort the devs put into doing all this, but dam.  you cant even skip through the dialogue. its skip the entire conversation or sit through it. These are all really just gripes but i felt worth mentioning. If you are a FF fan, this game is kinda a disappointment. With that all being said, the game is worth a go for continuing to play in the series. maybe just not full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic story and great game play. Long time Final Fantasy fan here, and this definitely takes a spot in my top 5. Without going too in depth with a write up, I'll leave it at a 9/10 story and 8/10 gameplay. I plan on playing the DLC now that I've completed the story once through. (I didn't do much for side quests as I don't have much time to game these days) I only wish that Square Enix had released this on PC much earlier. I refuse to buy another console for a single title release.Edit: Now that I've reviewed some of the communities reviews, I've found that with what left most unsatisfied, actually made the game more enjoyable for myself. I'm also incredibly surprised that many of you still think FF's are turn based. LOLOpen World: I dislike the overuse of "open world" games and with how FF16 flowed, I felt like it was a breath of fresh air. I could experience the story at the core without dealing with any fluff or wasted time traveling back and forth across previously explored areas. Why waste time developing an open world when most quick travel anyway? They did a fantastic job making the world feel large without integrating open world. I couldn't be happier with the outcome. Side Quests: Another awesome point is that the side quests are quite literally side quests. You aren't required to complete them. I don't care that a fisherman needs help finding rare bait to catch fish to feed his family. I want a straight to the point story and Square did a great job making that happen without forcing you to run endless quests for the level grind. Yes, some of the main story quests do have you do a few simple material gathering, but what RPG doesn't? They kept it short and sweet.Acting: The voice acting and even character models were incredible. I played on max graphic settings which I feel is a must for this game. If you aren't, you are going to miss out on a good bit of detail. With that being said...Visuals: The visuals are absolutely amazing. (Again, playing on a brand new PC at max graphic settings 4070Ti I9 14k etc) There are no laggy or stuttering bits. The game runs incredible assuming that you have a PC that can handle it. Your 1070 won't cut it this time. They say the minimum is a 1070 with an I5 but what they really mean is an I7 with 2080. Even that might not be enough to run max settings and get the full seamless experience.Story Development: The story starts out small and increases in scale as you progress. If you've ever watched Gurren Lagann, you will see a similar scale progression in FF16. I found this incredible. Yes, there are some slow points in the story. No, it's not 100% action packed. But if you have the patience to appreciate the dialog, character development, and the time to sit through cutscenes, you will most likely enjoy the story. It's not a Call of Duty. It's not Devil May Cry. It's Final Fantasy, and Square Enix kept it classic for this one. I for one greatly appreciate the consistency.

_childDocuments_.review: From what I've played, the story is interesting and engaging, the combat is fun and you continue to get new abilities as the game progresses, and honestly, I've been hooked. EDHere's the big problem though. This game runs like a Special Olympian. I normally wouldn't even write a review but it's so bad I can't continue to play this game. If your rig is a little dated or you are barely making the cut with the minimum requirements, then do not buy this game. This is a huge shame because I love what I've seen so far and I hope it gets fixed soon so I can give it another go. It consistently runs at sub-30 fps with low settings at 1080p, and isn't even stable at 720p. I have a Ryzen 7 3700x, 2060 Super, and 32gb of ram. Normally I can run games with medium to high settings, and at least 1080p, usually higher, with no issues. I've tried all sorts of fiddling and eventually stumbled upon a fix which I will link in this review. With it, I can get a mostly stable frame-rate but the game looks hideous. Maybe I need to upgrade, but this is the only game I've bought in recent memory that has performed this poorly. This is extra frustrating because for the first few hours of the game, the time it's refundable, it ran almost perfectly at 2k. Only after finishing the prologue did the issues start. Had I known this earlier I would have refunded it. Edit:I'm changing my recommendation after upgrading my hardware, I now run a 5700x3d and a 4070 Super and the game runs great at 2k and looks beautiful. I'm happy I can finally enjoy this game and will continue to play it. I still stand by everything I had said previously though, if you are running hardware from previous generations that are edging the minimum requirements, then I strongly suggest you do not buy this game. If you're looking for a modern 3rd person action game, then go buy Wukong or something better optimized instead. If your hardware is newer and has DLSS capabilities, you should be fine after some tinkering with the settings but I would still air on the side of caution if you're on the lower end. The game is excellent when it is working properly though.

_childDocuments_.review: Preliminary review on "mid-tier" PC (RTX 3070/i5-13600K) It is a much smoother experience compared to the demo but it remains a port of a PS5 game that the PS5 itself struggled to run well.I got a stutter-free experience getting to the town of Lostwing (2-3 hours in) on the game's recommended settings with dynamic resolution and DLSS so the shader compilation seems to work. Cutscenes are 30 FPS and there is a mod to unlock them, but they're 20% more demanding than regular gameplay, so I decided to keep it 30 because my GPU can't handle it at 60 FPS.I got a 60 FPS experience 95% of the time, you will get drops when it comes to towns with NPCs and effects like volumetric fog. Fights with multiple enemies will also get me around the 50s, but one-on-one fights and bosses are a solid 60 FPS for me. Frame Generation will take care of these drops, but I also didn't mess with the other settings to see if I could gain performance elsewhere. Any GPUs above mine should be able to get a solid 60 throughout.All in all, it's pretty much behaving like the PS5 version, it's demanding where it was demanding on PS5, but I get much better performance and image quality so I don't think I'll go back on the PS5 now. No more walking around at 40 FPS in performance mode, and 720p resolution during combat.The game is gorgeous especially at night time, I recommend enabling HDR because the game was made for it, and if you don't have HDR, crank up the brightness to a 7 or 8 to see better.You get a practice room in the game and I recommend trying it out at least to get a handle on magic burst (pressing timed magic button between each sword slashes). There is an option there to show burst timing, which will flash red any time you can do it, and there is a timing for virtually every move you make, such as perfect dodging (try doing melee then magic after a dodge, I didn't know about it until way later lol). I also recommend getting your base ability kit like stomp, and mastered charged blade and magic. These moves allow you to chain things together so fluidly and you will work towards getting better at it from the jump.So far, it's pretty good, better than other Square ports but not as fancy as FF15 with all its options. For some reason Square is terrified to include a hard mode from the start, so I recommend to challenge yourself to not use potions and/or to downgrade your equipment if you find it too easy. Waiting for a difficulty mod to fully jump back in. I recommend reading other reviews to get a bigger picture too

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: A playable movie with well-developed characters, an immersive world, and a gripping story that occasionally falls a little flat. Combat is fluid and interesting, though there is little variety in enemies, and no real challenge in the base game. The music is beautiful, and the graphics and animation are incredible. A must buy if you enjoyed the demo and don’t mind constant, long-winded cutscenes. Yes, I beat the whole thing on my 512gb OLED Steam Deck. Cutscenes and combat ran at a low, but stable frame rate for the most part; occasionally I would get significant stuttering. Unfortunately I would see major drops in frame rate whenever I walked into a settlement area such as Lostwing or Martha’s Rest. It seems that they’re just not optimized very well. The biggest problem came from fast travel, where the entire game would sometimes crash. Thankfully, the game’s autosave ensured I never lost more than a minute or two of progress. Overall, the game is playable, but if you hold your games to high standards, you might be disappointed. I put all settings to “Low” and used these mods: I liked the game a lot and would definitely recommend it, though it’s far from perfect. Some things I disliked:- Combat is way too easy and most enemies are just boring HP sponges.- Crafting is an absolute joke. Enemies drop random, often totally unrelated items that you’ll never use.- The victory screen completely undercuts dramatic moments in fights and feels out-of-place even when fighting regular monsters.- No status effects? Seriously? It doesn’t feel right to get hit by a marlboro’s Bad Breath and not have a million debuffs.- No elemental strengths/weaknesses? In a game built around elementally-themed Eikons?! That was even more of a travesty than the lack of status effects.- A lot of characters felt… underutilized. The hideaway sidequests helped flesh some of them out a little more, but so many characters felt disconnected from the main conflict.- I liked Jill, yet I felt that she was so defined by her relationship with Clive that we didn’t really get to see her shine. There were occasional moments where she took the lead, or stepped up, but then she went back to following in Clive’s wake. It’s frustrating because she’s so close to being an incredible character.- While I loved his design, the main villain felt a little lackluster, and a lot of his motivations and connections to Clive were unclear or not explained very well.- The cycle of “pass through town, encounter unexpected roadblock, work with the local leader to resolve the issue before continuing” got tedious very quickly.- Some elements of the story felt either rushed or drawn out too far, and some interesting side content felt like it should’ve taken precedence over filler moments.- I wish that we could have had more downtime moments with the main characters, in the vein of FFXV. - Characters in your party don’t do much. If they had health bars and did something like XV’s link-strikes with Clive they would’ve felt much more present. - I would’ve liked to play as characters other than Clive. There were multiple points through the story where I thought we’d shift the focus away from him for a moment, but I was usually disappointed. Some things I liked:- Disregarding my quibbles with the enemies, combat is flashy and fun. There are lots of possibilities for combos between Eikon abilities.- The Eikon fights are some of the most spectacular things I’ve ever seen in gaming. There’s one that takes place about ⅔ of the way through the game that is just transcendent in every way possible--music, visuals, emotion… Once you play it, you’ll know what I mean.- There are some very good, unexpectedly deep sidequests that do a great job at fleshing out the world and its characters. The ones that pop up in the hideaway right before the final battle are especially worth doing. - While this isn’t everyone’s cup of tea, I appreciated that the game was linear and focused so heavily on story and character development. The “playable movie” style can be hit-or-miss, but I thought it was done quite well here.- I LOVED Clive and his journey from a broken, vengeful soldier to a steadfast, caring leader.- The voice acting is just phenomenal. Can’t think of a single uninspired or bland performance. The most emotional moments of the story wouldn’t have hit nearly so hard if Ben Starr hadn’t put his heart and soul into embodying Clive. Ralph Ineson is also great as Cid, who’s probably the best iteration of the character in the franchise.- The core emotions of the story, such as guilt, grief, and brotherhood, are delivered so achingly well. The ending destroyed me. - The setting and worldbuilding is fantastic. Valisthea was a dark, realistic depiction of a broken world that I felt fully immersed in.- While I’d say that Soken’s work for this game doesn’t quite live up to his work on FFXIV, there are some astounding songs in this game, and of course he uses leitmotifs masterfully. The entire sequence with the final boss was perfectly scored. My favorite songs would have to be Away, Find the Flame, Ascension, and My Star (hard to listen to that one without tears). - Torgal. Good boy!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is definitely a slow burner, looks decent enough, but the combat is quite dull. It wants to be an action game but doesn't have the fluidity (or the difficulty) to be challenging in any real way. It looks flashy, but there's not much more to it than that.In many ways, I don't think there have been any meaningful lessons learned from FF15 (or previous games), either. Both in terms of story and combat. There's a general feeling of an incomplete combat system, and it's so weird that those two games suffer from generally the exact same problems. There's a lot of hand-holding too. And I mean a lot.It is also a game that has a significant amount of side reading required to understand who is who, what is what, and why all those things matter. If you're going into the game cold like I did, you really need to get to the hideout, unlock the library, and then spend some time trying to understand all the puzzle pieces.Overall, the style and presentation is also puzzling. It very much has a veneer of Final Fantasy 14, but somehow doesn't quite have the same charm. There's no sound when levelling up or completing a quest, making it feel incomplete and out of place in this universe. There's voice acting, except when you're doing side quests, where you get the first introductory line and then just classic grunts etc. Which is fine and all, but this is meant to be Square Enix's poster child, the cream of the crop - I don't expect corner cutting here. Again, it weirdly feels like I'm playing FF14 offline with an action combat mod (that's not very good).In some aspects, this game feels like it came out in 2014 - not 2024. It feels like an older game, far older than it actually is.And if I've upset you so far, wait for this next one.It reminds me of Final Fantasy 13.And I finished all three of those games!There's a lot, and I mean a lot, of what boils down to an endless amount of hallways. In a big forest? Actually just a hallway. In the open plains? Hallway. Desert? Hallway. Castle? Hallway. Okay, fine on that last one, but it gets old pretty fast. The movement also feels eerily similar to FF13 too, it's this strange floaty sensation where it feels like there's no weight to anything. Jumping is especially comical. Can't believe that made it to the final production.And don't get me started on the quick time events - this is another reason as to why the game feels way older than it is. They feel so out of place and awkward. Additionally, there's some very clear moments that are designed specifically for the PS5 controller and its original exclusivity. You're not just pressing X to open a door, son, you've gotta press X and then 'force resist' the R2 trigger. This would be fine in moderation, but there's a point where it feels like they're hitting a PlayStation quota.Another mark against this game is the absolute brain-dead AI. Both in terms of your party, and the enemies. Your party will stand around whilst you've staggered an enemy, doing nothing. The enemy will also stand around as you smash their allies, almost if they're stuntmen waiting their turn in a movie. Kind of hilarious that they even give you items that trivialize all combat, too (I immediately discarded them). I wish there was a very hard mode or something to give it a sense of challenge... or, you know, a completely reworked combat system.Performance is kind of a mixed bag. It's mostly fine (RTX 3080) at 4K, but there's definitely room for improvements, which I expect to be released in the next few weeks.Overall, I think this is a decent buy on sale. If you're kind of mixed on whether to get it or not, I'd strongly suggest Black Myth Wukong over this if you want a brand-new action game, and wait for the likely winter sale reduction. A 10-20% price reduction would probably be a good buying point.If I could leave a mixed review rather than a negative one, I would. I think it's just fine, but for Square Enix/Final Fantasy you kind of hope for something more epic. At this point, I think their subteams are actually their best teams, i.e. Team Asano and so on, producing Octopath Traveler and similar games.

_childDocuments_.review: Story line: 9/10Final Fantasy XVI offers a captivating narrative set in the war-torn land of Valisthea. The story follows Clive Rosfield as he navigates themes of duty, sacrifice, and revenge amid political intrigue over the powerful Mothercrystals. The character development is strong, and while the pacing can be uneven at times, the deep lore and emotional engagements keep players invested in the unfolding drama.User Interface: 8/10The user interface is sleek and user-friendly, allowing easy navigation through menus and HUD elements that don’t clutter the screen. However, some sub menus could use better organization, making it occasionally cumbersome to find specific items or skills.Battle System: 9/10The combat system is a standout feature, blending fast-paced action with strategic depth. Players can engage in fluid combos and switch between Eikon abilities, offering a dynamic experience that encourages experimentation. The challenge level is well-balanced, making battles exhilarating and rewarding.Final ThoughtsIn conclusion, after 17 hours, Final Fantasy XVI impresses with its engaging story line, intuitive interface, and thrilling battle system. While minor improvements could be made to the menu organization, the overall experience is compelling. This game is a must-play for fans of the series and newcomers alike.

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10One of the times I would really love a better review system in steam!The game is not bad, the story is amazing BUT...Positive: The story feels a lot more mature than previous FF games, the characters feel a bit more realistic.Graphics are pretty good and the game runs very smooth. No problems in my playthrough!Bonus positiv: Torgal, the best boi!Now the negative points:The game is FAR too easy, even if you stop upgrading your weapon mid game and don't use any trinkets it's easy! After just a few battles you already know when to dodge most enemy attacks. All Eikons have at least some strong and usefull abilities. Exploring the world is just bad! The world is empty, filled with the same 5 types of enemies everywhere and there is absolutely NOTHING to explore! The only things you find at some places are just a few of the currency or more random upgrade materials of which you already have a ton because you never need it. Side quests are extremely boring and just bad fillers. Slay the enemies at x, bring y back to the quest giver. Also the game is filled with thousands of cutscenes for main and side quests which especially for side quests quickly become very annoying! There are basically 0 rpg elements and no customization. _childDocuments_.review: I didn't really know what to expect when people described this game as "linear" or "Devil May Cry-like," which left me a bit worried because I wasn't a particularly big fan of DMC or Bayonetta, however, I think this game does a good job of keeping things moving in such a way that I don't have any issues with it so far. In fact, I was kinda surprised how easy it was to get sucked in to the whole thing. As someone who tends to prefer more open games with a bit more of an RPG focus, I was a bit surprised how much I enjoyed moving from place to place quickly without having to do any obligatory "roam around an area and level up with nonsense fights" kind of stuff.If for some reason it feels like a slog, I'll update with a negative review, but for now, it's really a surprisingly solid experience thus far.UPDATE MANY HOURS LATER: So now that I've had a lot more time with the game, I can really appreciate its approach to the world and how it balances "linearity" and "open world" ideas. In a lot of ways, it feels like XV now because various stages are reused and begin to give the game more of an open-world feeling. The nice part is that there's quite a bit of variation because each of the "stages" is large enough to house quite a bit without feeling like I'm constantly walking across an enormous expanse. Also, the gameplay mechanics do get deeper and more compelling with time, even if they're not the deepest RPG mechanics.The story is strong for a Final Fantasy game and is easily one of the most interesting ones we've had in years.As someone who preordered Metaphor and FFXVI at the same time, I feel like I'm going to get the perfect balance of both new and traditional JRPG goodness in recent years.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who was a fan of the old turn based Final Fantasy games, a part of me wanted to pass on this just to discourage them from going in the action combat direction. But ultimately I decided that was kind of a lost cause, and decided to buy it anyway. What Final Fantasy XVI ended up being to me was an RPG with some rough spots, but ultimately ended up being an incredible experience. I will say up from that this game is not for everyone, so I'll start with the negatives. If you're the kind of person who skips cutscenes and wants to be hitting buttons as often as possible, you'll probably be frustrated with this one. The combat loop is pretty satisfying when you do get to it, but I wouldn't really consider it that special. It's just decent action combat in an RPG, with some decent boss fights. Some of the side quests get pretty tedious, and if you're a completionist, or the kind of person who likes to do these kinds of quests to have more time in the game, some of them can really drag. I also can imagine people having PC performance issues with this one. I used this game to test a new midline 1440p build in 2024, and while the game ran fine for me, I could see people with older hardware having a tough time.What really carries this game is the cinematics, story, characters, and worldbuilding. This is easily one of my favorite Final Fantasy stories to date, and I think I enjoy it more than the Shadowbringers expansion of FF14, FF10, and FF9 (my favorite FF stories before.) I was quite invested early on, and the main story did a great job of making it feel like the world was worth diving into. It tackles some uncomfortable themes, but does it in a way that's ultimately compelling and adds to the experience.This game ended up being something pretty special, and considering the price point, is definitely worth giving a look. Going forward this will be the game I compare other narrative focused RPGs to.

Game really gets heavily carried by its visuals and story and if you can get it in a sale go for it. Full price I would probably not recommend it at all. Also. _childDocuments_.review: Let me get this straight out of the way first, this is a very much action focused game through and through. Alot of people didnt like this game simply because they wanted an old school turn-based JRPG but if you're judging this game for being an JRPG then this game is probably isnt for you because the people designed this game's combat are the same people that made Devil May Cry series. If you're into an action game with Final Fantasy as its main theme then you won't be disappointed, that being said. This game is nowhere perfect because it got its own flaws and inconsistent in the gameplay as well. This game is built FF15 with improvements where 15 lacked, 16 kinda made up for it although there are some things could've done alot better[The Combat]- This is pretty much the bread and butter of this game, if you're into full action, DMC style then you will definitely enjoy the combat in this game, there are so many abilities that you can mix and match to create so many different build depends on your play style. Where other areas of the game lack of, the combat is definitely where the game shines the most.[Story + Sidequest]- The actual main story is pretty good, it's not too groundbreaking or anything too new but it's above average and very enjoyable til the very end. Some of the sidequests will give you more lore and the world of Valesthea if you want to know more about their characters and how you can make an impact for their questline[The Score]- HOLY ♥♥♥♥ this game has BANGERS after BANGERS soundtracks and background music that made me immerse into the game even more whether it's just exploring around or boss battle that giving me that adrenaline rush and sometimes I purposely trying to extend the fight because I want to enjoy the battle just a little longer lol[The Cinematics]- I really don't know much to say, this game probably has the best cinematic cutscenes out of all Final Fantasies I've played, some of them are VERY VERY LONG though, I'd say the cutscenes would take 50% of the entire run of the game itself so just sit back, grab a snack and enjoy the moments as you explore the land of Valesthea[The Boss Fight]- The boss fights are pretty much the main selling point of this game with these crazy big battle between the summons (they call them Eikon in this game), the epic boss fights + the amazing cinematics with these bangers soundtracks = chef kiss[The Gameplay]- This game is a very linear game, if you trying to look at this game as an JRPG then it's probably going to disappoint you. Although I really wish they took their time and input more of those RPG elements into the game and FF16 got the potential to do so with the combat abilities and combination to be limitless but not other things that make it an actual RPG[The Characters]- I really love how the characters interact with each others throughout their journey, they carry with them so much emotions and care about one another with good character development even the side characters[The Open World]- This game is VERY LINEAR, even though the map is big, I really wish there are much more to the open world than the what they have currently developed.[Graphics & Performance]- The graphics is beautiful as always but I think the port is kinda unoptimized, I have a beast PC with 14900k and 4090 but cant even fully run it smooth above 80fps without turning on all the DLSS + frame gen on[My Criticism]- This game is not perfect by any means, there are so many things I wish they took their time longer in the development cycle to improve more about the game itself- My BIGGEST gripe is the lip-sync doesnt match most of the time, if it's not the actual main story cutscene then it's all over the place. Some people might could just ignore it but for me I just cant, even with some main story cutscene the lip-syncing is still terrible. I thought if I switch to Japanese voice over it would solve the issue but that's not the language but the actual animation itself that didnt get a proper care for in development. Horizon Forbidden West got their lip-sync pretty much on point just mainly because they fully did mo-cap on everything, but FF was neglected somehow.- The questing can get boring at time, like even with main quest you're basically doing glorified fetch quests over and over- The open world honestly could have some more life to it, it's very bland just because of how linear the game isThis is my first long form review of a game just because I grew up playing FF as a kid and always loved the franchise ever since, this game holds a special place in my heart just because it dared to be different and it might not be for some people but it is for me, I just wish SE took more time perfecting other aspects of the game and more people giving it the chance it deserve while judging the game for what it is as and action focused game than trying to judge it for trying to be a JRPG

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy XVI is a remarkable addition to the franchise, showcasing breathtaking visuals, an engaging narrative, and a captivating world that draws you in from the start. Set in the enchanting land of Valisthea, the game features stunning landscapes and beautifully designed characters that truly highlight the power of modern gaming.The story is a standout feature, focusing on Clive’s evolution from a young noble to a fierce warrior. The themes of friendship, sacrifice, and political intrigue create a rich narrative tapestry that keeps you invested throughout. The character development is exceptional, making each interaction meaningful and memorable.Combat has taken a bold new direction with a dynamic, action-oriented system that is both thrilling and satisfying. The incorporation of Eikons into battle mechanics adds an epic scale to the encounters, making each fight feel cinematic and intense. This fresh approach revitalizes the series’ combat while maintaining its signature flair.The soundtrack is another triumph, featuring an orchestral score that perfectly complements the game’s emotional beats and sweeping landscapes, enhancing the overall experience.However, it's important to note that the PC version has encountered some performance issues. While the game is visually stunning, players may experience occasional frame rate drops and stuttering, especially during intense combat sequences or in more populated areas. These hiccups can detract from an otherwise immersive experience, but they are not enough to overshadow the game’s many strengths.In conclusion, Final Fantasy XVI is a masterclass in storytelling and gameplay, with a few minor performance issues on PC that can be improved. Whether you're a seasoned fan or a newcomer to the series, this game offers an unforgettable adventure that is well worth experiencing. Don’t let the technical shortcomings deter you from diving into this breathtaking world!

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy 16 is a 7 out of 10 game.The best part is the boss fight, when you transform into a giant monster and fight another giant monster, it’s really cool. It’s so cool, there are few games that can compare to FF16 in terms of epicness.Story is mature and sophisticated, you can clearly see the inspiration from Game Of Thrones, in a good way. But I don’t like the ending, it feels contrived, it seems Final Fantasy must has a sad ending.But that’s it, the good parts of FF16.The bad: Combat, unsatisfying, boring, repetitive. I actually like the action game combat, I think turn-based RPGs are boring. But FF16’s combat feels like FF14 MMO-RPG with free normal attack. It doesn’t have the smoothness of an action game, I don’t know how to say it, just not right.Side missions, COMPLETELY GARBAGE. Basically all fetch quests.And when you talk to NPC, the animation of the character is like a 20 year old game. Very stiff and robotic, let alone facial animation, non-exist. I don’t think there is any motion capture outside of cut scenes where characters actually act like humans.It took me 73 hours to unlock all achievements, which is impressive, but I don't enjoy playing the hardest difficulty in New Game+, because of the boring combat and insanely high HP enemies. I just want to rush through the New game+ and be done with it. And as soon as I unlocked all achievements, I deleted  the game,  I don’t want to play again.All in all, 7/10 game. There are many epic moments in this game, but those epic moments can’t compensate for the bad stuff. FF16 isn’t a bad game, but an OK game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolute art. Settled between a classic RPG franchise and modern gameplay you'll experience hard topics in a black-painted world.The graphics are stunning. Especially the character models feel very lifelike. You'll witness a much more pale Final Fantasy game, but that doesn't even bother me, because everything blends together perfectly.The music is gorgeous. The soundtrack contains 181 tracks. The tracks do their work, from making you feel relaxed and safe to the bombastic battle themes during the battles. Excellent work by Masayoshi Soken.The voice acting is very nice. I play this game in German and the voices are professional at most times.I know that many people think the battle system is problematic and the RPG elements are gaunt. And yes, battles against trash mobs rely heavily on button mashing and are way too easy. The boss battles are staged differently and more impact-heavy. You have to dodge heavy attacks and quick time events bring a cinematic experience.I think the game itself is a masterpiece. One of the biggest plus points is definitely the story. It is well-written, feels dramatic and impactful, leaves you in awe.I had no game crashes yet. The game runs very stable. Also I am not experiencing stuttering and the loading times are fast once you made it into the main menu. Occasional frame drops occur but only rarely.You should definitely buy this game if you like action-oriented RPGs.

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing addition to the series. I thoroughly enjoy playing this game. Everything about it from the setting, the story, the environments and landscapes, the summons, the action scenes, the combat, is extremely fun. The characters have real motivations, some of which are tragic but also realistic. I'm only about 40% through the story but I will see it through to the end because I want to know what happens.While many seem to dislike the combat and say that it's more Devil May Cry than FF, I personally don't see many similarities. For one, there is no combo system in this game. Your moves can be chained into other moves but there's no way you are going to ever have a 200+ hit combo like in DMC. If anything, combat becomes more complex the farther into the game you get as new powers are unlocked and you can switch through them during battle in order to keep your damage output high. The moves are flashy, fun, and keep you entertained which is what a video game is supposed to do. Companions in this game are kind of Meh. Outside of Torgal, the dog, you can't really do much with your third companion. They are kind of just there and do their own thing, which often times makes them seem irrelevant to the overall flow of combat. I don't notice the pace of battle really change if Clive is alone, with Torgal, or with Torgal and another person. Not a huge issue but it's a far cry from the party mechanics provided to players in previous installments. Minimum specs for the game are also insane. This game is very dependent on your GPU. If you don't have a 16GB GPU or higher you will be playing on low graphics. The PS5 has 16GB DDR6 so I'm guessing that's the same benchmark they used for PC min specs. That's a personal issue, not really a flaw on the game, but something to keep in mind. It's clear SquareEnix wants to head in a new direction with its FF games. I enjoy the action RPG style, the story, the Dominants and their Eikons are really freaking cool (All of them are jaw dropping!). The pacing of the game is fine, and the game runs well if you have the proper hardware. I highly recommend it if you are a fan of FF. BTW... Sales for this game are probably not the greatest because the release date wasn't planned well. I'm not sure why this game was released only a few months after a FF14 expansion, the same time as blockbusters like Black Myth Wukong, Warhammer 2, and upcoming games like Dragon Age. Also take into consideration that most of these JRPGs require HOURS upon HOURS to actually beat, and there's your big reason why people are hesitant to purchase. Attention spans are lower than ever and if you don't have hype (Black Myth Wukong) or multiplayer (Warhammer, BG3) behind your game you're not going to get sales. The Marketing/Sales team at SquareEnix should have known this.

_childDocuments_.review: I can easily sum up my experience and thoughts of FFXVI in one word: BORING. I really wanted to like this game but everything about it is average at best, with some elements being down right garbage. The worst of them being the side quests. Every dialogue in this game is a cut scene, which is fine, but the NPCs involved with side quests are so bland and boring that the conversations feel like they last forever. All this just to go run an errand or fetch something or kill something. AND THERE'S AN INSANE AMOUNTS OF SIDE QUESTS IN THIS GAME.The combat system is average at best for an action oriented experience. Abilities are dull and the progression is amateurish and enemies have very little variety. The game eventually opens up (after 20-30 hours of linear maps) but when it does, exploration is dull beyond belief. The loot is pointless and there's no real reason to want and go out and explore. There's no destructible items in the environment either. No barrels or crates or ANYTHING to smash as you explore.The main story is fine and the cinematics involved with the main story are cool at times but overall this is not a fun game. If you really want to play this game wait for a super sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great medieval fantasy — surprisingly mature, sprinkled with some cosmic horror, crazy boss fights and stunning imagery.The narrative comes first in this one, without question. It's neither a technically nor mechanically deep game. That might turn a lot of people off, but I really liked the characters and setting, including the DLCs.There's definitely an issue with optimization as well. The settings menu is basic, and how well the game runs — seems to wildly differentiate from PC to PC, judging by other people's experience. It ran  well for me, outside a couple of big open areas. Try the demo — and get the mod that unlocks the framerate in cutscenes. The game has a lot of them.
