_childDocuments_.review: I am only 6 hours in. Like every FF gsme since FF XIII it is a mixed bag. Gameplaywise it is extremely simple this time. The fights are in realtime and not hard. The combat system itself has interesting ideas but I would like to see the series go back to turn based combat.Graphics are a mixed bag too, while the scenery is fantastic it is also very limited. The invisible borders seem to be everywhere and again and again the markers on the screen telling you where you can climb, etc. kill all immersion. The characters are not on the same quality level as the terrain but also fine (but not great).The whole game plays more like an interactive movie so far and I do not expect this to change.The story itself is interesting and kept me playing a few hours straight now.This one is tough to judge. The  visuals can be stunning and the gameplay can be satisfying but if you are looking for a JRPG you are definitely wrong here. Think of it more as an action adventure with many many many cutscenes.

_childDocuments_.review: Only a handful of hours into this title and I'm enjoying it a lot. While it does a few things that break away from the usual Final Fantasy genre, I personally feel like this might end up being the new way forward. Between this game, Stranger of Paradise: FFO and Final Fantasy VII: Remake / Rebirth it's obvious that SE has begun to focus more on an action oriented style of game play. I waited quite a while to get to play this game. I avoided spoilers and the temptation to give in and pick up a copy for the PlayStation 5 simply because, I knew that the PC port would be worth the wait -- and boy was I right. While breaking away from traditional Final Fantasy turn based combat FF16 does a a wonderful job of transitioning the series to fluid, reactionary, fast paced combo systems. Dare I say, it -almost- feels like playing a Devil May Cry game, minus the absolutely chaotic juggling abilities. Don't get me wrong, you can still juggle to an extent but you'll find that it isn't as insanely complex as a DMC game. I must admit, I wasn't the biggest fan of the combat for FF7:Remake and after the story changes to one of my top five favorite games of all time, I didn't actually give FF7: Rebirth the time of day. FF16 however, at least at this point in the game has been a great experience from the get-go. At this juncture in time, I have little to no complaints about this title, other than perhaps the fact that the game was ported to the PC without the ability to uncap cinematics from their 30-FPS prison. This can be extremely immersion breaking which is a shame considering it renders its cinematics in engine. The weapons that Clive holds don't magically change into different weapons during them which is extremely refreshing and helps in not jarring you out of the scene. But boy, I'll tell you what -- going from 120HZ in game directly into an in game cinematic that immediately drops down to 30 FPS sucks you right out of it. I strongly suggest you look into picking up a mod that uncaps them before you start the game. Outside of that, be prepared for a wonderful experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Mid. Wait for patches and a discount. 100% the base game in about 55 hours and the total package in about 69 hours. It is shallow as an RPG, an Action Game and an Narrative Game. Don't get me wrong it is decent game, but not a Final Fantasy, especially a main line game; switch the Chocobos for horses and this game can be a normal AAA western game. As I said it's a decent game, but not a magical one, and that it is what I expect when playing a Final Fantasy.The sound of this game is awesome, memorable new themes, recurring songs rearranged and GOOD voice acting (besides a very few NPC where the voice didn't match the person). The cinematics are BEAUTIFUL, but by default locked at 30 fps.The gimmick of this Final Fantasy is the usage of Eikons (Summons) but they don't affect a single element besides combat, There is not a single puzzle in the whole game, no platform jumping and no verticality to access hidden areas. would be nice to use the powers outside combat, specially since it is in the lore of the game. I'm the bearer of the Eikon the Fire, the guardian of this element, but when I need to lit a furnace, I go on a fetch quest????? In my opinion would be fun to use Garuda's power to reach things far away or use Titan's to break entrances to secret passages.The story has a more mature approach this time, but its shallow. In the beginning, it starts to build some scenario of multiple nations, their interests, alliances and enemies. I thought I was about to experience a masterpiece of geopolitical narrative, a new Game of Thrones, but in the about 30% of the game the pace start to go to quickly and all that remains is go from mission to mission; the development of this fabric of narratives stop and only the protagonist's circle continues to evolve. The are A LOT of questions that don't get answers, even on the files and DLCs.I have certain expectations when playing a Final Fantasy game, one of them is a magical story. A journey where a diversity of subjects will be treated in a way that makes me, the player, feel. After playing this game twice, for the achievement, this story didn't convey a single emotion until the very ending cutscene, and was not even for the protagonist, was because a side character that I liked () was crying in mix of good and bad feelings. It was not bad, but the overall feeling that I have is that wasted its potential.Not everything needs to be funny, but if you go on YouTube and search for "Final Fantasy 16 funny moments", there are just 2 moments: A joke about counting to 3 between two characters (I liked) and the other one is about a old man saying a dog was with its head on his nuts. Comparing that with FF7Remake, FF7Rebirth and FF15 I just have a feeling of an OK story without memorable moments that will vanish through the years.As an RPG, its shallow, your choices don't matter, the elements don't matter, your build don't matter. Attacking a fire beast with fire? Same damage when using ice. Equipment is decided with higher number, Yellow Good, Red Bad; there are no situational equipments. The real difference between magics is Damage Damage and Stun Damage.As an Action game is not fun, there are no real combos, no delayed combos, no situational combos, just magic rotations and mash.There are a LOT of elements of MMORPGs, especially Final Fantasy 14 (FF14). By itself, that is not a bad thing, but the way it implemented was a problem. The side quests of this game, are well written and involving, but there is a HUGE drop in quality of animations, and visual fidelity. NPCs, when walking away, will turn their heads, then 180º their bodies, then start to run. You can see exactly the moment when the animations change. Feels extremely like FF14 A Realm Reborn, a 10 year old game. Most side quests are go from point A -> B -> C -> A; again, by itself, its not a problem, but EVERY side quest puts a marker with a round area on your map where you have to interact with a NPC/item/monster with the icon on their head. If it is to hunt a monster, after you slay the beast, the camera will focus on Clive's face for about 0.5 seconds, then he will puts his sword away, then switch to the standing animation, then you will be free again; like FF14, a 10 year on game. When in boss fights, the real ones, there are indicators on the ground for AOEs, and in specific bosses there are elements of bullet hell which is very fun, specially the last boss of the "Echoes of the Fallen" DLC, super fun.The technical side of this game is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. I've played on a 3070, Ryzen 7 5800X, 32GB DDR4 3600 mhz, 1080p using DLSS/FSR (3, not 3.1), dynamic resolution AND frame generation and still had problems. The game didn't crash, at least, but THERE ARE memory leaks and a lot of CPU utilization problems. In longer sessions (+4 hours) the FPS drops to about 15 in certain regions, using upscale and frame generation. I don't know what happens on Martha's rest, but every time I go inside the tavern, my fps goes to sub 10, go outside, 35, take the elevator 60.The graphic settings don't work properly. Using FSR, I had a constant bug where the vignette (that was supposed to be disabled) were draw every other frame; Using DLSS solved the problem, but since I'm using a 3070, I don't have access to DLSS frame generation. The depth of field toggle doesn't work, I had to download a mod (FFXIVfix) to disabled it and unlock the 30 fps cutscenes.There is much more to be said but I'm already ranting about a good game that didn't meet my expectations of a franchise that I love.

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond the narrative, this game really doesn't feel like a Final Fantasy game, even with the recurring elements present such as the Eikons, Chocobos, etc. That in itself doesn't present a problem, aside from its use as a mainline title. But for some I know this might be a turn off.While playing I certainly had a lot of thoughts, so I'll try my best to put them into a scuffed review for now.Tldr;Pros:-Great music and scenery in DLC and final segment;-Incredible quality graphics;-Overall good performance;-Stellar voice acting (second only to Xenoblade Chronicles franchise imo);-Well written and paced story;-Believable characters that are well written;-Good character design;-Some cool and flashy cinema.Cons:-Music placement is often badly placed and can take away from some very serious scenes;-A lot of ugly/bland environments for much of the game;-So much focus on cinema that the combat suffers;-Introduces a lot of names and places at once, drops them and expects you to recall them much later in order to follow events and conversations;-Early eikon battles overstay their welcome;-Side quests while trying to be meaningful are just busy work with endlessly pointless dialogue tacked on;-Equipment upgrades don't feel interesting;-Accessories feel pointless;-Lacks replayability.Music:Music was weird to me; one the one hand, there were some amazing pieces, especially later on and in the Rising Tides DLC. But on the other hand, for the vast majority of the game, the music fell flat, often not fitting. For example, avoiding spoilers, there's a very serious scene that really sets the tone and direction of the story for the rest of the game that for myself was around 10 hours in. This very serious event had the goofiest music imaginable playing in the background which, for me, took away from the scene massively. And it didn't stop there; this kind of thing happened regularly, as well as a lot of the background/ambient music for general exploration often just feeling like it didn't fit for me. This is certainly an odd change as Final Fantasy music is among some of the best used in games in my opinion.The latter section of the game, however, truly delivered on this front, in my opinion.Graphics:It's clear from the moment you boot up the game: this game is first and foremost a cinematic game. That is to say, a lot of works was put into graphical fidelity and it honestly looks great, especially during the eikonic battles that were the main feature marketed toward us during development. Issues arise, however, in that the world often despite this looks ugly; like there was no attempt to create beautiful scenery for much of the game, instead opting to put that effort into flashy designs for eikons and battles. Of course, there is technically a lore reason that you can fall back on as an excuse, but for me it was very noticeable even when said excuse would not fit. The RIsing Tide DLC does fix this and has some of the most stunning scenery I've ever seen in a video game at this level of graphics.Gameplay:Honestly, the battle system overstays its welcome; Eikon battles initially feel gimmicky although eventually evolve into something much more exciting and interesting. It's difficult to talk about combat properly without spoiling how it progresses, but regular combat takes far too long to ever really build up; Clive doesn't really get access to enough abilities to play your own way until late in the game and even then it feels like you're limited to specific abilities because of their stats and cooldowns. Not only that, but combat simply becomes a chore later on when boss enemies are sponges that attack relentlessly, sometimes not even leaving a big enough window to use one of the few abilities that are meant for staggering. And on top of this, it felt like  I was better off just running through the regular trash mobs half of the time.Again, though, this game has a big focus on cinema and it shows in the combat. That, however, is to its detriment. There are almost always so many particles on the screen at one time that you simply can't see what is there, meaning it is frequently difficult to read an enemy's actions and respond accordingly. For an action game, this was an absolutely abysmal decision.Story:From literally the first trailer, I was hooked on the story and the game's opening did nothing to change this. This game's story is incredibly well written and the overall pacing of it is very well done. Most past Final Fantasy games have had big ideas but were unable to execute on them properly - usually characters would make decisions that made no sense just to progress the narrative. Here, however, every person's motives and actions make sense for which I applaud Square Enix.  Voice acting:Wow. Just Wow. Especially by the leading case, this is some of the most phenomenal video game voice acting work I've ever known. To me, it's second only to the Xenoblade Chronicles franchise.It took me by surprise just how many more colloquial accents were chosen for the English voice cast. And the  apparent attention to detail was amazing too; during the DLC, you meet characters from the northeast all with accents hailing from the same region of England, in the northeast. As someone from the region myself, it was quite a nice change to hear such solid vocal work from here.Side content:This is another area that really fell short of the mark. There was a solid attempt to make the side quests interesting by using them in order to develop the arcs of characters introduced during the main story, but just about every quest felt like endless busy work. At first, the quests felt like a nice little break between emotionally charged main plot moments, but as more areas opened up the number of quests that appeared at once, all very similar to each other, was massive to a point that I can see some people being burnt out by the sheer amount of time wasted when completing these quests.In addition to this issue, often the dialogue in these quests can have a very typical JRPG problem of there simply being too much pointless speaking. And for most quests, the rewards don't really do much for the player - thankfully quests that give new upgrades of new crafting recipes will be obvious due to the symbols used on the map and journal.Miscellaneous:-A lot of the names of places in the game were incredibly hard to follow for a long time; their contexts are introduced in an instant and then often disappear for 10s of hours at a time with an expectation that the player recalls a random minute detail so that events make sense.-Character designs for the main cast are mostly solid, although admittedly one or two I felt were just one off side characters due to their generic looks. I actually quite like this change since not every character needs to look interesting if they're well enough written as they were in this case.-I play with a 3070 and had very little issue performance wise; the first time I entered a ruin area the frames lagged for that playthrough until I left the location, however after this most cases of frame drops were minor and short lived.-Weapon and armour upgrades are too incremental to feel worth working for and the damage ceiling never really increases with new abilities or skills earned.-Accessories are meaningless.-Due to the cinema over gameplay nature and overall length of XVI, I can't see this game having replayability for many people. Which is a first for mainline FF games and very rare when it comes to JRPGs.

_childDocuments_.review: Cons:Bad performance/optimization.Predictable story (I have been able to guess how things were going to go with a pretty high degree of accuracy throughout the story so far.)A lot of the major plot points just seem derivative and generic.Cut scene>Cut scene>Cut scene>Linear combat stage>Cut scene>Cut scene>Linear combat stage>Cut scene> Boss Battle>Cut scene>Cut scene>Cut scene>Cut scene>Visit hideout to upgrade 1-6 pieces of equipment>Cut scene>Cut scene>Linear combat stage>Cut scene>Cut scene>Linear combat stage>Cut scene> Boss Battle... etc.No party management to speak of. Can't choose party members, or change their gear/skills/etc.Super linear gameplay, even for Final Fantasy standards. Even gear progression is pretty linear. Just go to the forge every so often, craft newest belt+bracer+weapon, then upgrade it. No brainpower necessary.You also have 3 accessory slots that you either use for the "story mode" items to make the game easier, boost the effectiveness of a certain attack skill, or boost some other stat to a mild degree. So there's some strategy there, but it's bare minimum.Pros:Some of the fights look cool.Action/fighting is pretty snappy and responsive. You can pet the dog.(Edit: Like many other hack and slash games, you can ultimately turn your brain off and mindlessly engage in the combat. Which I suppose is a 'Pro' if you're looking for a Devil May Cry alternative, and a 'Con' if you are looking for a JRPG.  As such, if I'm ever in the mood to do some mindless hack and slash, I'll be putting some more hours into this.Basically, if you REALLY want something akin to DMC, and are an action game fanatic, then I actually WOULD recommend this game. But if you want Final Fantasy... Yeah, this ain't it.)

_childDocuments_.review: Update: Almost 30h in and I think FFXVI is a very good, epic and cinematic action adventure (definitely not an RPG), it would sit well besides all the Sony exclusives from the last decade. It runs well (4070Ti, playing on 4k with DLSS Balanced and FG), besides the occasional hitching. The artwork has an amazing level of detail to it, absolutely gorgeous.With some more improvements it could have been one of the best FFs of all time, if they- had a not so limited (why only 2 abilities/Eikon equip-able? There are 4 front buttons on a controller) combat system with more depths (e.g. stamina instead of all cooldowns, elemental affinities, critical hits, backstabbing,  etc), that would unlock its moves much quicker- hard  difficulty mode available from the beginning. As it is mobs are a joke, you just trigger all your cool downs and they are gone. Bosses are the only, small challenge.- more interesting world exploration, currently when you find a chest its 99% crafting materials, that you dont really need. A deeper combat mechanic would have allowed for much more interesting loot- side quests are mostly just boring chores. They instead should have used them to tell more world-building side stories and to let us know our companions better. The main ones would have deserved to have their own quest line throughout the entire game. Currently we see them talk in cinematics only, which is not the best way to make the player care about them.- let us equip our companions with gear/skills at least, for some customization----- original review after launch ---------Good PC port, game looks beautiful and runs well for what it has to offer. You can check the performance yourself in the available demo. Combat system is decent, I enjoy it more than I did the Nier:Automata combat for example, just don't use the cheat items the game puts in your inventory. Compared to the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ combat mechanics from the FF7:R games it is actually fun, no half-assed compromise trying to include some ATB elements, just pure action.I am glad they went away from the open world design from XV and back to a more traditional, cinematic experience for which FF was always known for best. Without all the bloat and all the walking from a to b and back open world games are usually packed with the story experience is much more focused and well paced with the beats of cinematics and gameplay.The negative reviews at launch are mostly folks crying about missing ultrawide support, but there is already a mod to add it, plus it removes the 30fps lock from the cutscenes and allows you to increase the FOV.This is the best game Square Enix released in a long time, and it is also fair priced at the PC launch.

_childDocuments_.review: Square-Enix pushes the envelope with each entry into this series, and I appreciate them for that. That ambition has led them away from creating JRPG classics. The FINAL FANTASY name is now lent to MMORPGs, open-world games, and RPG-lite spectacle fighters, such as FINAL FANTASY XVI. I'm just going to accept the creative direction, and review the game as it is.There is some controversy about how the game addresses difficulty, but I personally liked it. There's a series of crutches in the form of overpowered items, abilities, and consumables that will allow anyone to clear the game without too many setbacks, but it's also possible to adopt a playstyle with a high skill cap. The gamers coming from Elden Ring may still find it way too easy, but there is arcade and post-game content designed to challenge them also.All the important story and gameplay bits are delivered in highly cinematic chunks, which are unlike anything I've experienced in a video game before. The production values are through the roof. It's fun, immersive, and epic in scale. These scenes make the highs of this game so high that it's impossible for me to hate it. And that's why it earns my recommendation.Now we must speak of the lows. What's supposed to happen in between the climactic scenes? Exploring the world, giving depth to the characters, cultivating your skills, leveling and gearing up your player characters. Sadly, this is where FF16 falls short of the classics in every aspect. I found mostly frustration in these parts of the game. Thankfully, they never lasted long enough to make me want to quit. I will also give props to the excellent English localization and voice acting, which even surpasses the Japanese version in my opinion. This made the fantasy lore interesting to learn about, the drama in the story quite gripping at times, and made listening to the characters bearable, even when they yapped on for far too long.In conclusion, the game is revolutionary in its cinematic quality, but the gameplay is lacking in depth to go down in history as one of the great RPGs or action games. I'm looking forward to the future. Will they excise the series' baggage for good and commit fully to cinematic action? Will they go back to the roots? Or find a new direction altogether? Anyway, I hope I'll be around to play many more entries of Final Fantasy.

_childDocuments_.review: It is kind of weird how this game can make you feel if you are a FF fan:Normally Square enix would make some spin offs that , while bearing the name "Final Fantasy" wouldn't be part of the mainline series (or numbered, like XV,XII, etc. if you will);this because while maybe still maintaining a good story, those games have complete different style of gameplay or combat, like Dissidia, Origins, Type- O, tactics , to say some names, when the main/numbered serie would still maintain some aspects of the original gmaes (even if they may be completely different).An example of what I mean: while FFXV is basically all action, you still have a party with different equpment, skills tree for them, etc. , so a little bit of the original RPG formula is maintaned.In FFXVI, while you still have a "skill tree", the party management is non existent.That is because while XV was an action RPG, XVI goes full action.I believe this is also a reason why some fans are divided on this game: by following the "rules" used until nowthis game shouldn't be a numbered one, so why it is?For starters, this game deserve to be not only on the main series, but also in the top positions of best ff games.The story, the characters, the music especially are something out of this world (I'll explain the gameplay later).Story: after many games with some of those being slightly cringe to tell someone , we have a FF set in a "realistic" meadieval style; it's crude, it's dirty,it's bloody, it's direct; imagine it's a little like a Game of thrones but with Final Fantasy, and I say that in a good way.Add to the mix a a story that is perfectely not too direct but not too convoluted and you will have FFXVI.Character: While it's true that you don't have exactly a party like in other FF games, that does not mean that there are no characters. Of course some may shine more than others, but again, pair those with the story and settigns of the game and you will get a cast worth remembering, both foe heroes and villains.The music is indescribable: I challenge you to listen to it once and not wanting to hear it again.If I recall correctly this game won a game award for its music, and it was deserved.Gameplay: at first it may seems like a Devil May Cry , but less deep, and that could be your first impression if you didn't try to check it deeper; in the beginning the general feeling was that you just had a couple of combo available, but then you may try to be more fancy and discover how to actually chain your different actions, opening new combo possibilities, then try the special moves and see that they are not only damage dealers, but again, new moves to chain, etc.I wouldn't say it's a Devil may cry combat system, but it came close while being different.Wouldn't say that is top notch, but's really enjoyable.Also you have loadouts, so you can try different builds and see how you like it.Basically, if you can stomach a different play combat than the rest of the series you will have one of the best Final Fantasy made, and I mean it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'l start off by saying I am not a big fan of the FF series. Turn based combat isn't my cup of tea, that being said, The combat in this entry was enough for me to keep going and finish the game.Does this mean it was a good experience? Hell no. To put it simply, the game is very mid.I'll start with the positive: Combat is fun and has decent variety with the different abilities. And that's pretty much it for the positive.Now for the negative: Performance is abysmal and pretty much everyone says so, me included. Played the game on high settings with DLSS on an RTX 3080 and had some framedrop here and there and some amount of crashes in the big spectable fights.The graphics are also not very good, especially for how hard it hits your computer when playing. I would like to make clear tho that the game doesn't look bad, just not as good as it should considering the performance.The story isn't good. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR beforehand: 5/5 best non-mmo final fantasy in the better part of 20 years (at least)It will reward attention to detail more than any other FF, well, except FFXIV, but that’s an MMO, it’s kinda cheating. Side quests are the meat and potatoes of character development, I didn't even thought at the beginning that a character like Otto would even stick to my mind enough to remember his name, and yet he was the protagonist of one of the most tear jerking moments in the entire game. Not only that; the cities, or more like towns, are brimming with life, the small talk among the folk lets you peek into their hearts and minds in all their complexity as open books and how the world is affected by your actions. But most of these gold nuggets of world building are extremely easy to miss and only the players that truly pay attention to detail will be fully immersed in this world.Finally, the smart way that the game uses it’s apparently small map is by forcing you to explore it beyond a marker, throw the use of “hunts”, side monsters that appear as you progress into the game and you have to actively look out for them, actual exploration, there will be no flying arrow to guide you to them, only the clues that their poster will provide, and a lot of them are hidden in completely optional zones that a player that went straight into the main story may not even know exist.I was worried that the influence of game of thrones would not mix well with final fantasy, and I say this because Game of thrones is basically celebrity gossip in a fantasy medieval setting, that is, finding satisfaction in watching outstanding individuals being miserable. And listen, I can enjoy GoT as much as the next guy, just like The Crown or Death Note, so long as it is in small dosses, because all of those shows are like alcohol, it’s fine a little bit from time to time but if you take too much too often you end up depressed, angry and cynical, you may like it but you know it doesn’t sit well with your body, or soul. And so, I was worried that it would turn every interaction between characters into a snooze-fest where all dialogue is either a purely utilitarian, taciturn, stoic, dry-as-a-chalkboard interchange forgetting all the emotion, corkiness, levity and spontaneity of the series, or a smug snark-fest, with every character answering with a pun in a very try-hard attempt to not show any type of vulnerability forgetting the honesty and heart-felt moments that really make a dialogue shine.Gladly I can say these fears were unfunded. Since FFXVI, instead of J.R.R. Martin, reminds me more to Brandom Sanderson, yes, it reckons there are different viewpoints in life, and it avoids manickeism, but at the end of the day it accepts that there is an objective good and an objective evil, and also that the world needs heroes, things that GoT is allergic to; for Martin a hero is either a fraud or a looser, for Sanderson (and Final Fantasy XVI) a hero is exactly that, a hero.And my brother in Hydaelyn, there is a reason to why the end of GoT soiled the bed. When it comes to fiction, free will is an illusion but a good author knows how to keep the illusion up. The creator already should know witch character is going to do what, yes he might detour from the original idea when it comes to the details but the end goal of the story has already been decided before it even started. An author that truly doesn’t know how his story is going to end or what his characters are going to do is bound to create, mind my french, a huge pile of caca, be it sooner or later. And because all the aforementioned, A Song of Ice and Fire will never have a satisfying ending, George knows it, and that’s why he doesn’t even bother with it, and that’s also why I’m glad that the Final Fantasy XVI team didn’t take their GoT inspiration too far.It’s everything that assassins creed wishes it could be, specially the newer ones. You really feel like you are fighting the power, but not as a petulant college kid with no real life experience would, but as an grown adult would, by understanding that the people that you’re fighting is the same people that you’re trying to save from themselves, by understanding that the problem is the very system of beliefs and it can’t be solved by killing this one high-ranking individual that is oppressing the rest of the society, because  it is the whole of society, from the most powerful to the most humble, the perpetrator of this dystopia, and also by understanding that you can’t force people to change, change takes time and more often than not, the world is not ready for it, but it will, you must be patient and have a buttload of hope, and hope is for the brave, not for the cynical.It’s not like there’s not such a thing as action JRPGs (Mana series, Nier, the og jakuza, kingdom hearts, star ocean and tales of, just to name a few) and I wouldn't mind that in the future this gameplay was revisited in FF, so long as it doesn’t become the new standard, because I’m of the mind that the turn based format is in itself worth preserving… That being said, if you’re going to break the mold and make a new entry in the series fully action based this is the way to go. I heard that they hired a big name of the DMC series and it shows, when they were revealed in trailers I thought that the skills were too simple and too much of same just with a different color coat… I was wrong. It is hard to explain, you really need to play in order to appreciate it, it is far deeper and more customizable than a video would allow you to see. Quoting the devil: it just works (but for real).

_childDocuments_.review: This is as top tier as they come.  TL:DR, 100% recommended.It is important to know what this game is and what it isn't in order to enjoy it as it was intended.  It is not a traditional turn-based RPG, nor is it a challenging action RPG like Elden Ring or even Wukong.  It is an epic, cinematic experience with gameplay that is a lot of fun, although not very challenging.There are a lot of cutscenes and dialogue, so if that turns you off, be aware.  That said, this game has some of the absolute best visuals (both technically and artistically), voice acting, music, and boss battles seen in a long time.  I am loving the story so far and the excellent performances have me bought into the characters with Cid being the standout.I wish the game had a bit more difficulty- the combat was exciting but I haven't been in danger yet, only coming close to dying once.  It has not lessened my enjoyment though, as it can be a change of pace from the endless souls- and souls-likes out there.I have not experienced any performance issues at all, and I know that was a big thing at launch. _childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, the epitome of "meh".There's a lot of poor design choices that ultimately hinder this experience, and it just shows how boxed in this particular dev team is because of how many of these design choices are also in FFXIV.Pacing is atrocious because for some reason basic exposition that should be done in 2 minutes is somehow lengthened to  hour long segments because of the obsession with mundane fetch quest design. There are parts of the main story where I was actually getting into it, and immediately the momentum is killed because I now have to spend the next hour doing fetch quests to help build a stupid bridge.This game has genuinely the worst side quests I have ever seen in an "RPG". It is actually insulting how they're literally just there to pad your playtime.The combat is fine. It really doesn't evolve at all throughout the game and there is no challenge in any of the combat encounters, even the hunts. It's just super watered down Devil May Cry. I get that the game doesn't aim to be challenging, but maybe at least have a difficulty option for those who want a challenge? I'm not playing through this 40 hour long game twice to do New Game + and sit through the story again.The "RPG Mechanics" are also insulting. There is no actual gear system, but they do shove a loot system down your throat that may as well have been designed by an unpaid intern. It's just stat increases with no effects, no visual changes aside from your sword. The obsession with sprinkling literal 1 gil loot in the environment is also just bizarre. In 2024, from a AAA company, that is a joke.The music and voice acting are good, and I think a few of the characters were decently written, but that's not anywhere near enough for me to recommend a $50 video game.

_childDocuments_.review: Find the gold hay in the needle-stack, truly. Just finished 38 hours with this game and finally hit the ending. Wow. What an underwhelming experience overall. This game could have seriously benefited from cutting down its run time. It feels entirely unfocused, like it wants to be an action game but is too hung up on its tired, outdated RPG mechanics to allow you to play the fun, modernized combat system the game places front and center for more than a few minutes at a time, unless it's forcing you to fight the final boss for a whole hour. If the game had taken cues from some other familiars in the genre, Devil May Cry or Bayonetta for example, they would have realized the scoring system actively incentivizes players to attempt combo variety and to play stylishly. This game lacks any sort of motivation to engage with its systems beyond damage output potential, which while it is rewarding to witness as one progresses boss to boss, does not feel very relevant as the mobs and fodder scale alongside you, essentially doing nothing to the level system except allowing it to render your healing items weaker as you progress through the main story. The skill tree has many awesome powers, but their upgrade and mastery potential is entirely lost and there is no real motivation to combine the powers the way the game lays out, and I found the ability point distribution simply did not lend itself to play this way as one's Eikons prove to be enough to defeat any foe regardless of their designations in your ability shortcuts. the game suffers severely from a lack of challenge and enemy design variety, providing too many enemies with simple attacks and nothing particular or interesting the way we saw in Stranger of Paradise, for example.I tend to form emotional bonds with characters heavily when I play games. Call me a baby if you must, but I admit I am a corny, emotional guy. Kingdom Hearts 1 and 2 made me bawl like a baby. Nine Sols recently tore my heart in two. This game's brotherly relationship seems to be the only thing with any sort of real emotional core or soul and even then the uneven scripting makes it seem ridiculous and cheesy. Not only that, the missions where there is no combat, which come down to fighting fodder enemies between beautifully designed wild corridors that have no further interactivity doing fetch quests for NPCs whose character development is as comparatively interesting as watching paint dry. (Seriously, whoever wrote Mid's arc is genuinely emotionless. She barely even grieves her loving father after he dies. How are we supposed to feel anything for her? Also the way Jill's character has no actual arc besides "Help the man" feels like Disney Star Wars level "strong woman" tokenization. Rey Skywalker much?) The only time during the story these moments had any impact were in the Desert (I forget the name of the area) when you save those children from being trafficked by some bad guys and you essentially just kill them like fodder as well, so the gameplay did not reflect the stakes or impact of the story in that moment. It literally feels like one moment you are a Demigod in a divine conflict with the royal religious monsters that rule over the kingdom, doing battle for control of the very world and its economic resources in the body of agiant, horned monster with countless potent powers, and then a few minutes later you're strolling down the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ beach looking for "seashells" (AKA asset-less glowing items) as your home base's personal errand boy. (In fact, this is what ACTUALLY happens after one of the Eikon fights)Overall I'd say this game is having an identity crisis. Maybe they should have made it another spin-off, maybe they should have given the RPG elements more room to breathe, or at least take them out entirely to give the action game aspects more versatility and consistency. This game falls mediocre somewhere in the middle to the point where by the end, even the visually impressive parts of the story you still might care about feel padded out artificially and insignificant as the game is carrying on for far too long, never ceasing to find new ways to hammer home the same things without a theme or semblance of complexity or maturity in how it addresses them.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm just gonna go ahead and say it: Final Fantasy XVI is my favorite real-time JRPG I've ever played, and I've played A LOT!Spoiler-Free :-)Between the super-fast, flexible, and adaptive combat, FFXVI excels in keeping players on their toes. The story is solid, with some genuine tear-jerking moments — especially if you knock out a few side quests. Seriously, don't skip them. They add a lot of depth, and some even hit harder than you'd expect. It's not just "go here, kill this." The side quests actually contribute to the world and story in meaningful ways, and there's usually only 2-4 of them at a time, so you're not drowning in a to-do list. They're quick, fun, and worth doing for the extra context they give.Now, let's talk combat, because it's easily the best part of the game. The real-time action is next level — fast, fluid, and it evolves as you go. The boss fights? Absolute fire. They’ve got these insane cinematic transitions that make you feel like you're playing a full-on movie, but in a way that keeps the gameplay engaging. Every boss feels epic, and the action just keeps ramping up. Plus, they give you the freedom to reset your skill tree whenever, for FREE, which means you can experiment as much as you want. You don’t have to stress about messing up your build, so you’re really encouraged to just have fun with it.The world is gorgeous and full of detail, and the amount of voiced NPCs is impressive. Most of them have something relevant to say depending on where you’re at in the story, which is a nice touch. Yeah, some lines repeat, but it’s still cool that even random side characters feel like they belong in the world.Speaking of voices, the acting in this game is top-tier. The main cast nailed it, especially the lead actor, who I had to look up because I didn’t recognize him. Turns out, he’s not super famous in the U.S., but man, he crushed it. The villains sound spot-on too, no cartoonish over-the-top stuff here — just solid performances all around.Now, I’ve got to mention the music because it's seriously one of the best parts of the whole experience. During boss fights, the orchestra just goes off — it’s all classical epicness that hits you right in the chest. Then, when you’re chilling in The Hideout, the music is totally different. You get this soft, peaceful harp music that makes you feel like you’re home. It’s calming, and you can just feel the change in atmosphere. And when you’re out in the wild, the music picks up again, giving you that adventurous, “let’s go explore” vibe. It really fits every moment of the game and elevates the whole experience.Now, I’m running this on a Ryzen 3950X, RTX 4090, 64GB DDR4 RAM, and a 4K 120Hz LG monitor with G-Sync enabled and Settings maxed out completely with DLSS on Quality. My CPU is definitely showing its age — looking forward to upgrading to the 9800X3D when it drops — but this setup still works great. At 4K with variable G-Sync, I typically pull 45-90 frames per second depending on where I am. In areas with lots of NPCs or heavy logic, my CPU holds back the frames a bit, especially in big cities with a lot of detail. But when I’m out in the wild or in boss fights, I’m averaging a solid 60 FPS, which is really impressive considering the bottleneck I’ve run into with other games at 4K.What’s really great is that this game is well-optimized. Even with my aging processor, it runs smoothly thanks to DLSS and all the latest features. I've seen a drop of 15-20 frames in other games due to CPU limitations, but FFXVI keeps things steady, which is saying something. I bought the full collection with all the DLC, and I think it’s totally worth the price, though I'd say it depends on how much you’re into the game.Final Thoughts:Final Fantasy XVI hits all the right notes, from its story and combat to the world-building and soundtrack. If you love JRPGs or action games, you need to play this. It respects your time, lets you experiment freely, and delivers an unforgettable, heart-pounding experience. Performance-wise, even with some bottlenecking, it’s incredibly optimized and makes full use of modern features like DLSS. For me, this is a 10/10 all day. Sure, there might be some complaints out there, but I’ve had a flawless experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn’t sure whether I should pick up this FF game, although I’ve played nearly all the others, because I have a strong preference for turn-based RPGs, and this was completely action based.   So, I played the (free) demo and was hooked.  This game nails it in every respect.   The story was good and the voice acting and soundtrack superb.  The game looked and played beautifully even on my aged but still venerable 1080 Ti.   There were a few times during my 69 hours of play (I’m a completionist) that the game froze and had to be restarted, but the auto-saves worked surprisingly well and I lost little progress when this happened.   (There is also a manual save option.)     The fights against the common, and not-so-common, riff raff are good, but the boss fights are incredible; you feel like 2 Gods (or at least 2 Kaijus) are duking it out.   Some of the fights – Bahamut comes to mind - were very intense but you never feel overwhelmed as the level progression is implemented nicely. Unlike some earlier FF games, you don’t need to grind out levels to reach a place where you can win a boss fight.  The normal progression of the game does that for you.  There is a skill tree of sorts, but it is limited to learning, upgrading and mastering spells of your Eikons.If you are even a bit of a fan of CARPGs, this title is a must have.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: Beat game at 66 hours doing I'd say about 75% of the side quests, all the hunts but one (need to go back and finish up Savrog) and ended at level 45. Everything I said below still stands. Excellent action game, and it "feels" like a Final Fantasy - especially in the story beats. The front half of the game is very reminicent of IV. Still, some more enemy variety in the back half of the game would have been nice, and the middle of the game lags a bit. The enjoyment of the gameplay really comes down to how much you like the combat loop and getting better and more efficient. The game DOES NOT punish you for losing in the traditional sense. Got my money's worth and then some. I'll come back to finish up the DLC. Original Thoughts: Incredible, action-packed RPG. The "stylish action" heavy gameplay and huge, cinematic battles won't be to everyone's tastes. If you're looking for a traditional JRPG experience with tons of menu diving, this isn't it. If you're looking for a deep job system, you won't find it here either. Instead, you have an excellent action RPG that is more Devil May Cry than Secret of Mana. Basically, play the demo and if you like the combat loop (what little you actually play in the demo) then you'll be golden. The pacing picks up tremendously after the demo - there's just a lot of world building and set up at the outset. Sure, sure, native Ultrawide and 60FPS cut scene support would have been nice but it was an easy fix with the mod. The mod for the demo works just fine on the base game as well and it is a game changer for in-engine cut scenes. While the game is well optimized, it is still one of the more demanding games even for my super beefy rig. I can run most modern AAA games without any of the AI driven enhancement support and hit a solid 4k/60. Even with a 4090, super fast CPU, yadda yadda I still had to turn on DLSS3 in Quality mode and enable VRS to hit a smooth 60 at all times. The 60fps cut scenes are wonderful, but they are demanding. Frame gen and the low latency options tend to make the game feel sluggish, imo, but those can further get your performance higher if you prefer. Overall, great port. Played over 10 hours on PS5 and sat the game down to wait for the PC release. Glad I waited to finish the game on Steam. It's incredible so far. Enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Even without performance issues the game is just awkward.It's this weird hybrid of action game and RPG that does neither particularly well, which is weird coming from a company that did KH and FF7R. KH at least always plays well, 7R had fun combat with a fun hard mode.Pacing of the story is completely atrocious, after every peak they take out all of the momentum like they want to make sure you're not having too much fun. I like the cast in general, the minor characters have a lot of personality. Side quests are so mind numbing it gives me physical pain. "Go collect 3 flowers" over and over. The overworld/map feels too close to an MMO, I was just warping around like an idiot and nothing felt cohesive.I don't like giving thumbs down to games I completed but this just isn't it. I thought after 13 and 15 surely it has to get better again but they somehow made a game that barely even functions with its mechanics. Why the ♥♥♥♥ is gear and crafting a thing? Why is Gil a thing if all I can buy is Orchestrion rolls? Abilities are fun at first but eventually it gets stale. Counter moves are very satisfying, the big hitters have these mini-cutscenes which last a little bit too long after a while. Elements have no function, there are no buffs, debuffs or synergies. The Rising Tide DLC gave Leviathan a nice gimmick. Why not change Clives weapon along with the Eikon? Why limit myself to 2 Abilities per Eikon? Why are accessories so boring? -6s Cooldown redaction, % increase in damage? Rising Tide introduced some accessories that alter some of the Eikons abilities and that's the stuff I was hoping to find in the base game. I also much rather have abilities tied to a resource I can manage rather than Cooldowns, that type of design doesn't do it for me. The game had an overall good story premise which then ♥♥♥♥♥ itself through the halfway point. Why hide so much lore behind ♥♥♥♥♥♥ fetch quests that offer nothing? At not a single point did this game feel like an actual journey. 10/10 Set pieces but that's it. A lot of speeches/monologues also feel redundant. I heard this characters reasoning already, I don't need it to be reiterated over and over.I really hope CBU3 never gets to do a single player game again on their own. A lot of the FFXIV "DNA" is in this game and that's for better and for worse. They know how to do spectacle, some tracks in the OST are really good and characters are likable. The game took 40ish hours to finish with all side quests and side content and I much rather it would have taken 20. I will not touch NG+ or Echoes of the Fallen.I'm absolutely butthurt, buttblasted, upset with borderline buyers remorse. It's what I deserve for trying not to spoil myself on anything regarding this game

_childDocuments_.review: Beat it on the PS5, going to beat it again here.Not a perfect JRPG, and certainly different from what most Final Fantasy fans might expect from a game in the series--different, not worse. The action combat system is great and gets better the more options and abilities you unlock (though a bit on the easy side; I wish for this release they'd let you tackle Final Fantasy mode from the start), the soundtrack is as good as you'd expect from Soken and his team (that is: probably my favorite in the series), and the story is compelling with well-written characters and arcs (bar a few important characters, unfortunately).My main gripe with the game is that its implementation of what you'd expect from a JRPG--an item and gear system; party members; leveling up and assigning abilities--is basically window dressing. Gear is a straightforward path that doesn't require much investment from the player other than just playing through the game, with little choice-making aside from accessories which have asinine perks like '+5% damage for this specific ability', and the itemization and loot systems in the game have you finding stuff like chests with 50 gil inside them while at the game's final zones; party members are present but their contributions in battle are hard to measure (you also can't customize or gear them up); and leveling up just gives you improved attributes, with nothing new or playstyle-changing unlocked. They should've either ditched these elements entirely or actually invested some thought into how they're implemented, as it stands it feels like they're there just because genre conventions say these things must exist in a JRPG.Having said that, I still think the game's great, carried by an excellent cast, soundtrack, fun & quick (if a bit easy) action combat and a plotline that manages to be cohesive and interesting in ways some previous Final Fantasy games might have floundered (particularly towards their conclusion).

Also it's super easy.-Side quests are like FFXIV fetch quests. Some later ones are good but I wish they had cut most of them. -You can fast forward the dialogue in some cutscenes but in others you're forced to listen through the whole thing or skip it entirely.-Clive runs at two different speeds outside or inside town and so you're stuck at a snail place in these areas, which truly is baffling to me.-Eikon battles are quite cool.-The writing is actually decent when they don't lore dump a 5 minutes cutscene about some war you don't care much about.-Voice acting is really good and so most of the dialogue.-Some of the battles are quite fun if you like dodging attacks and countering.-Great music and visualsAt the end of the day I'm glad I played this game. I just didn't enjoy playing a sizeable chunk of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing quality in the graphics, soundtrack and characters, except maybe the comically evil mom. Side quests are pretty meh mechanically but I liked how they let us close out the set pieces outside the main story. Combat while being the most simple out of every final fantasy so far (no element differences, no status effects) made up for it with the bombastic animations and effects.I heard it was like an interactive movie before buying so I was predisposed to expecting that and got exactly what I came for and more. Incredible Final Fantasy action scenes and characters that made me sad when the game was finally over. Completing all the side quests, hunts and main story + DLCs netted me about 60 hours and could easily be more if you wanted to do NG+ for the level cap, gear and challenge. I personally liked the story and side quest stories so I didn't really skip much dialogue, helped that it was all voice acted too. I also think the character development for Clive was really good, but wish that more characters got some of that too.I would say if you're interested in bombastic fantasy action, get the game. If you like the Final Fantasy setting in general, get the game. _childDocuments_.review: The performance of this game is abysmal.I have a 3080ti and a 5800x, and even the lowest settings get extremely choppy FPS in the bigger areas (Which you conveniently won't get to until you're well past the 2 hour refund mark)Even ignoring that, the cutscenes are locked to 30 fps.This is just a piss poor port.Edit after more hours:So the performance got a bit better, but this is just a bad Final Fantasy game.Let me be clear: The story is good. The story is the best thing about it. If you like political intrigue, you'll like the story.But every Final Fantasy after 7 (and some before) had something to draw you into the world gameplay-wise. 7 had chocobo breeding, golden saucer, etc. 8 had Triple Triad, 9 had the card game and mini games. 10 had Blitzball. Hell, even 15 had cooking and fishing, and a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ customizable car.16 has nothing. 16 has generic fetch side quests, kill x enemies, etc. 16 has combat, story, combat, story, combat story. 16 has cutscene primal fights with Quick Time Events. They're awesome to watch, and some of the combat is cool. But it's generic, and boring, and that's all there is in the game.And worse yet: Naoki Yoshida decided to make even basic enemies take several minutes of pure non-step beating on them to actually kill them. I installed a mod to increase the MC's damage by 150%, and reduced enemy health by 30%, and it still takes too long to kill some of the enemies. It's insane. This game stands for what not to do with your combat: Artificially jack up enemy HP numbers just to prolong the playtime.It's insane how bad this game is after you get past the pretty scenery/graphics, and the characters and story. It's basically a visual novel with a little more pzazz.If you're someone who can absolutely fall in love with the good things this game has, then you will enjoy it. I'm not saying you won't. But most people are going to want more from a Final Fantasy game. I want to be IN the world and feel like a part of it, with more activities than just combat.

That being said the combat is super fun, fast paced and satisfying, it feels like the devs were trying to make a game where we finally got a chance to experience, in gameplay, the epic cinematic action promised by the summon cutscenes from classic FF. If you're worried that the gameplay doesnt feel like Final Fantasy let me assure you that this story is not just a final fantasy story. It is arguably the best final fantasy story ever told.

_childDocuments_.review: It's tough to decide whether or not I would entirely recommend this game. It's not a bad game, but definitely has its flaws.Created by the same team that worked on FF14, there are obvious similarities. Various story concepts were clearly inspired by Eorzea, and most of the Eikons are similar in design to the primals. Music is also often reminiscent of themes found in the MMO, but I personally don't find that a bad thing as Soken is a fantastic composer. The FF14 team outdid themselves while working on the graphical quality of this game, everything looks fantastic. The only downside is that it then also requires quite a hefty PC build, and a lot of the cutscenes are locked to 30FPS. The latter at least can be fixed with a lightweight mod called FFXVI Fix.Gameplay-wise, it plays more like a hack and slash than an RPG. That's probably no surprise when considering Ryota Suzuki was the battle director, and he previously worked on the Devil May Cry games. While that is in itself not a bad thing, it's quite a departure for Final Fantasy as a series, which even in 13 and 15 (and the 7 remake) had an RPG focus. Skills are obtained and upgraded via a skill grid using currency obtained through battles, and gear can be obtained through chests, vendors, or crafting. Gear is very simple, with the 3 main slots receiving direct upgrades every so often, and the 3 accessory slots allowing you to add small modifiers. Gear and upgrades are also only available for Clive, party members cannot be customized in this way.The star of the game is definitely the Eikon battles, which giants facing off against giants. These deliver high adrenaline moments with epic setpieces and fast action. That also makes it the game's largest drawback. In between each large confrontation, the game can end up feeling like a slog. It's hard to retain tension in a story regardless, but when these are the highs, the lows are really damn low.All in all, I'd say it's an enjoyable experience for the most part, but I would be more likely to recommend it to people that enjoy games like DMC and/or people that like FF14.

_childDocuments_.review: This review has no story spoilers; As a long time Final Fantasy player and fan I got really excited when XVI was first announced. But not being a console player however meant I would have to wait until a PC port was made. I was able to stay in the dark for the many months that has passed, and I am not disappointed! Having finished my first playthrough I can confidently say that XVI IS BEAUTIFUL! Now, yeah, it is not your usual turn based jrpg, but the combat is fun and customizable, with a good dash of easy to learn and hard to master poured into it. Avoid the easy mode rings however, play in action oriented mode and experiment with the abilities, it gets really rewarding. I know the change bothers some people, but Final Fantasy never shied away from experimenting with each new entry, and XVI isn't different, it is just a new approach. And as long as you understand what you are getting into you won't be disappointed. The game is definitely not hard, with the bigger challenges coming from the DLCs, but a new difficulty mode unlocks once you beat the game once, and one that is meant to bring a higher challenge. I haven't started on it yet, but I can't wait to. Now with that out the way, let's get into the meat of the game, the story! It is great, it is beautiful even, and a rollercoaster of emotions! Often time reminding me of Matsuno's writing for Final Fantasy Tactics. The world is very well woven and put together, and the sidequests while simple, give you a good perspective on the motivations, difficulties and relations of the people living in that world, really making the world feel lived in and you being an active part of it. The game is very dense however, not in a bad way, but it has long cutscenes and dialogue which shouldn't be skipped, so I would suggest taking it easy to let things soak in as you won't have a good grasp of things until around 20 hours in. It is basically a very long prologue, but it sets things in motion nicely before taking off the training wheels. So don't rush it, savor it! The main cast is stellar, Ben Starr really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ delivers his role, and so does Ralph Ineson, Nina Yndis, Jonathan Case, Christopher York and more, they really bring their respective characters to life for me. Sadly small NPCs don't hold up as well, but it is not aggravating or bothersome. The other main star of this game is Soken, the music is just... ♥♥♥♥! A banger after banger, and building the hype or the emotional moments as needed. Dude really went ham with it, and I am thankful he did. With all the praises I can give to the game out of the way, there are some things I wish it could have been done better. They are not game breaking issues or anything that diminishes my overall experience, but things that I feel were somewhat lacking. The main gear you get is very linear. You just get things that are better in numbers than the previous one you had. I wish that had a bit more influence into the gameplay aside big numbers, giving way to customization options through the gear, with weapons having affinities with some abilities or whatnot, so I could actually work out builds with it. You can do that with the accessory slots, but having that option also on weapons and armor would expand it tenfold. My second complaint would be for enemy variety. There is quite a bit of different enemies, but also a lot of recoloring. We do get a lot of the classic creatures from the franchise, but there's also quite a few missing, with some being referenced in the game but never showing up, like Cactuars and Magic Pots. But there's also no Zu or Catoblepas, or even my boy, Gilgamesh. Now, some of these being omitted may have been deliberate as they would be unfit to the game's setting, and that on itself is alright, but I definitely feel we needed more enemy variety.With that said tho, the bosses are exceptional, and the Eikon fights are nothing short of a cinematic spectacle!   I only encountered one single bug in the game, and it is just visual. There is a specific sidequest that will have its icon still in the map and without ways to interact with it. Just progress one step of the main scenario and it will solve itself, allowing for completion. The game is great, and after finishing it I am gladly putting it up top with some of my favorites in the franchise, the story is really something and it really leaves a mark. I can't wait to 100% this one, and then wait patiently for the PC port of Rebirth.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit after completing the game:A masterfully woven tapestry of loss, sacrifice, love, tyranny, gods, hardship, redemption, and perseverance. Ignore what I say below about the story deviating into nonsense territory. They thread the needle so well and keep the story engaging, emotional, and important throughout. My only issue with the game is now that I've completed it I will miss these characters and guiding them through their struggle dearly. Up there with Final Fantasy 6 and 4 in terms of greatness. This game deserves all the praise and accolades it gets and then some. I wish more people would play it. Resume first impressions review:While completely upending the formula for Final Fantasy -- 16 feels more like the SNES Final Fantasy 4 than any game in the series. For fans of that unsung classic, this is a very good thing. It mixes the best parts of mature storytelling with the least anime story (at least for the first half -- until you get to the mystical nonsense later in the game) in ages. People who have stuck with the series through 13 on know what I mean. It's just nonsensical garbage -- this story feels grounded and not a single character speaks in an annoying squeaky child's voice. It's just wonderful.Combat slaps, and once you start unlocking new builds and powers you can really flex on enemies in fun and satisfying ways. I'm on a 4090 and Ryzen 9 7950X so obviously I'm not having any performance  issues, and the widescreen mod still allows for achievements, so if you're on a 21:9, install it. It's worth it. So is this game -- for $50 you're getting a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ steal for this fantastic game.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying I was not affected by the performance issues many say they suffer from despite many of them having better or equal rigs to mine. I have played every FF game since the second one and until now FF7 was my favorite (shocker, I know) but I am very divided between FF16 and FF7 as my favorite now.The story is exceptional, the combat is well done (albeit, slow to get to a "well done" point) and it looks stunning. This is easily the most epic FF so far. From the depiction of the eikons as raw elemental powers to the scope of the story. It's incredible and deserves all the praises it gets. That's not to say it's without flaws. No game is after all. For example, the story often veers into massive plot twists but they've been building up so much towards these twists that you see them coming from a mile away. The combat, as previously mentioned is incredible but starts off very slow and repetitive until you unlock more of the skill tree. The itemization is lacking and you end up with more money than you could possibly count. Crafting is basic and could have been done away with entirely. Some bosses fight extend their welcome way past it's time. There are more minor negatives but that's all they are, minor issues.No game is flawless and the measure of a great game is how easy it makes it for you to ignore these flaws and FF16 succeeds at this.I hope we get more of this.

_childDocuments_.review: The good:- So far the story is pretty engaging. Obviously subjective, but the setting and conflict are interesting- Combat against smaller enemies feels pretty good. It's very simple, but chaining abilities together feels impactful- Music is always a highlight of FF games for me, and it doesn't disappoint hereThe bad:- Some of the plot is a bit hard to follow- The active time lore feature is neat, allowing you to reference things being discussed for more context, but there doesn't seem to be a way to look things up later. I missed an important detail early on and to wait until it was referenced again so that I could look it up in the active lore- Some of the characters feel really out of place- Combat against large enemies/bosses is pretty dull in my opinionThe Ugly- This is a terribly optimized game. In some places I get really smooth gameplay, then I move to the next area and the frame rate falls through the floor- Battle speed seems to be tied to FPS, so in those horribly optimized areas fights are literally in slow motion- The world so far feels pretty empty. There are a handful of sidequests, but almost all of them are literally just on the way to the next main quest. There doesn't seem to be much motivation to talk to people around the various towns, doesn't seem to be much purpose in grinding out levels, etc.Conclusion:After 10 hours the game itself is pretty decent. It scratches the itch for a new Final Fantasy experience. But this version of the game is badly made and needs some serious work to get it playing acceptably. If patches fix performance I will update the review, but as it is at launch I would say pass on it.

_childDocuments_.review: Post Game Edit: I have now beaten the game. I don't want to go on a tirade, I'll just say this. This game aimed to to get a B rating, and it got it. It aimed no higher, took no risks, it was not brave or bold or special. It exists as an above average game that did not try to be great and it did just that. This is not a Final Fantasy.___________________________________I've been an FF fan for over 20 years and am about 1/4th of the way through the game, after the return to Rosaria/Phoenix Gate. Don't know how it ends, but I see where it's going. This game is really good, but not great. I put this game at about 7th place (14, 6, 9, 7, 10, 12, -16-, 8), I put it over 8 mostly due to gameplay.GameplayTL;DR A good action-rpg held back by long stretches of being drip fed adequate MMO-like quests, new abilities and good boss fights. This game feels like a Dragon's Dogma world, with an MMO-like structure mixed with pretty good Kingdom Hearts combat on top.- Very good integration of Devil May Cry like combat with RPG elements (but it does not hold a candle to DMC5)- Combat can be repetitive, especially with the slow exp rate and long stretches between getting new Eikons. I recommend testing out different ability mixes often by resetting points in skills to keep things fresh.- The sidequests have been mostly superfluous fetch/rescue quests usually with monetary not very valuable rewards that have only been passable to me because of some very small story rewards that add to the setting a little. There are mercifully few of them so far.- The bosses are the highlight of this game- I like how they added noticeable area attacks like in FF14 that you can anticipate while fighting midbosses and bosses. It's one of my favorite parts of FF14's combat.- I personally don't like QTEs but they are here and at least add a cinematic quality to bosses- You can feel how slow the game is sometimes like the; tutorials for simple things (yes you can turn them off, but they also turn off tutorials for necessary/new info), strange door opening QTEs and the oddly slow quest transitions. Yet the loading screens are pretty quick.Story (light spoilers)TL;DR The worst thing I can say about this game's story so far is "missed opportunities". I came in thinking I'd get an FFT or 12 or 14 styled deep plot with a big setting and if not a large at least a colorful cast. Everything story-wise is just adequate, above par, save the setting itself which is very fascinating. It's like a primer for FF14.- Characters - They're fine if not flat. Clive's main trait is his vengeance/guilt and brooding on dark aspects of his life and I desperately wish there's more to him later which seems to be sparking where I am. The Cid of this game is up there as one of the most charismatic Cids of the franchise. Jill's fine, a nice supportive young woman to take in Clive's dark. The supporting cast is inoffensive to decent.- Plot - A mostly straightforward revenge plot in the midst of deep political struggle sparked by resource problems that develops into more later as you deal with each nation's intertwining issues.- Setting - Fascinating. The world of Valisthea is not as detailed as most FF worlds, but I can tell it will open up more as things get more dire with mysteries like the ruins and Aether. The spreading Blight is a threat they make apparent to pull you in. The dependence on the Mothercrystals for blessings and power is intriguing. The flip on Bearers (mages) being slaves is fresh and gave me Dragon Age vibes. Though the theme of slavery comes across as convenient with how often you meet people against it personally but are told discrimination's a deep problem. The function of Dominants for the world and Clive's power's relationship to them is a good mystery.- Towns - None are memorable; they feel a bit better than Dragon's Dogma with at least some interesting elements like a nice field or crashed airship as a town square and more character with the little things like seeing how magic works in normal society or talks of local/current events. Each usually has one to three strong supporting characters.- Dialogue - This one hurts the most. The voice actors are really good, but the script is shallow. The characters don't talk about absolutely nothing, but it gets close. There are so many opportunities to add context and subtext in interactions between characters parting, reuniting, catching up on what's happened, the setting, using things that have been brought up to motivate or harm, etc. I'm not asking for more conversation, I'm asking for what's there to be deeper. Really examine the dialogue and acting in Vagrant Story, FF12, FFT and FF14 to see what I mean about giving you context and subtext. Just the opening of Vagrant Story and 12 (plus directorial choices) should give you what you need to see how well dialogue and setup can be made in a semi-action game's opening even with a relatively simple plot.- Pacing - In the end this game feels like it was intended to be long form, but had to be made short form. It uses slow plot beats and quests mixed with fast actiony moments that create a little dissonance. Yet that's the most confusing part is how slow it feels even though I know it's shorter than most FFs, and the lack of subtext does not help. I wish it were either longer with more dialogue depth, or shorter with less attempts at having depth, it's in a strange in-between.- Art Design - Good. The world is mostly classical medieval in look, but this game is missing that FF charm of outlandishly designed places and people. That is not true for the main characters, Eikons, enemies and ancient relics though; those are all well designed with complex clothes/looks that aren't too hard too complicated like some FFs can be. There's a hard cut separation between the simple medieval look and the fantastical magitech and character designs that has its own charm. The most prominent design motif is the "Repetitious, incomplete circle" seen mostly in ruins, very thematic.- Music - Great. Soken's work for FF14 is far better due to years of work on that game's expansive OST with many hits and misses, but this game's OST is still great. The area music adds a lot to Valisthea's semi-realistic medieval fantasy, wonder and culture. His use of leit motif is always excellent and helps connect ideas, themes, characters and groups to moments. Sometimes I swear I you can almost feel how a plot point is going to change or come up just because you heard its melody elsewhere. When you're in an ancient mystical forest or a military fortress infiltration the music makes you feel it. My favorite thing about the music is that the transition from areal music to battle music is seamless and uses the same melodies as the area to keep you in the feeling of that area while fighting; like FF13-2, Nier, KH3, etc. does.- Some early mysteries/setup/buildup are not hinted at well with scenes and bread crumbs to figure them out for yourself. For instance Clive's 13 year timeskip is only talked about, not shown. We don't get to see his striving, struggles and killing which makes its mention later a little hollow. Also the opening feels like the "pancakes" moment of a certain other rpg. And the scenes at the end of the return to Phoenix Gate confuse me, not in terms of plot and mystery, but more motivation and how the characters understand what's going on or not.I get the feeling this game is very back-loaded. As in the highlights, strong points and heavy lifting are going to be in the last 3rd. Despite my problems there's a slow, progressive buildup that I just wish had a better filling out. This game has a good strong start, but due to the poor dialogue and semi-repetitive combat after the second dungeon up to the return to Rosaria I have not been enjoying it as much as I'd like. Yet I still think this is a very good game.If I had to give it a number right now it's somewhere around a 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a ton that I could say about this game. From its musical score to the combat and skill expression, to the narrative body as a whole. This is a game for both fans of the series and newcomers wanting to get a taste of what the Final Fantasy universe is like and all of the joy it can bring. And this title certainly delivers. Despite a few flaws here and there and perhaps -a controversial topic- the preference of the uncapped frame rate mod, this is a title worth picking up~The sensation of combat feels akin to that of Devil May Cry where you have multiple abilities and can string combos together. Mastering such abilities allows for further customization and skill expression and the enemies you're using these combos against pack a punch too. Worthy of that of a protagonist in this game. Coming off of FF15 and the remake of FF7, the combat has a lot to draw similarities to, and all combine to make the fun action sequences all the more thrilling. From bosses to regular enemies, it feels great. Slow at first as your skills are limited at the beginning, but as you grow and explore the more you unlock and the stronger you become.Gods, where do I even begin? The writing is fantastic, the characters are relatable in terms of personalities, and each of them have their own personal goals and challenges that they're facing. Even as we grow in the story, these characters evolve and change around us as well due to the story and the things that we encounter within. It can feel like the pacing may be long for some (Average completion time is around 30-ish hours and a little less if you're speed running the game) but most games in the franchise are long. Its what makes these RPG's what they are.With a New Game+ mode and a unique difficulty that is only an option there, this game is as easy or as hard as you make it out to be. The quests do a good job leveling you up to where you need to be to handle just about anything the game can throw at you. And the DLC content is also a challenge too! I never felt stuck unless I "accidentally" went to challenge a boss that was around 15-20 levels above me. *cough cough fighting a dragon cough couch*I haven't played a solo game in a long time. With so many multiplayer games out there and so much to try and keep up with, its good to have a game that will be here when you get here rather than a live service or online game where keeping up is always key. After a long day of classes or even doubling a shift at work, I coudl always come back home and enjoy the story and gameplay that is Final Fantasy 15. If I were to give one complaint, its just the side quests lengths/quantity. There are a lot and can pile up quick if you let them linger on without touching them. You will laugh, you will cry, you will have relatable moments and feel sympathy for characters. You'll cheer for victories, feel defeats when you fall, and have moments of triumph when you hear that fan fair theme play. (Du du du dun, dun dun dun da dun) This game is fantastic from start to finish. And for the price of a average AAA title, you get a full game AND the DLC's. And I believe thats a win. Went into this game blind ever since it was announced, and i'm so glad I waited for it to arrive on pc."No matter how bitter the truth that awaits me, I will press on."10/10. Would, and will be, playing again.
