_childDocuments_.review: Questionable. 7/10 overall, at best. Parts of a 10/10 game are here, but they're squished between a 6/10 game that takes up 90% of the runtime, and that's not accounting for the literal 11 hours of main story cutscenes.FFXVI has...Epic highs in the form of climactic boss fights, music, voice acting, and some emotionally resonant plot and character moments.General mids in the form of... - the simplistic, limiting battle system; - 11 hours of main story quest cutscenes that often go on for far too long - a dour, bleak, and depressing world that only grows more so as the plot moves forward- open-zone environments that look pretty yet generic while being largely devoid of reason to explore- linear dungeons that look incredible, but feel particularly predictable and straightforwardAnd a ton of lows in the form of...- trash mobs fights being 95% of the gameplay, as none are threats that require more than half a brain cell to be active at a given time as you run through your combat rotation- FFXIV's influence at its worst via its exact quest structure (Main Story Quests and sidequests) and low production quality sidequest animations (there's a clear difference between the animations used in these instances and when they actually bothered to animate the characters)- padding between set pieces and moments of interest. If you're up for a fast-paced narrative, this ain't it- repetition in general. You've seen all the game has to offer after the 2nd boss fight; there's just more of ittely, FFXVI doesn't feel like a Final Fantasy game beyond the usual trappings of FF (summons; chocobos; magic). Whether you'll like it or not depends on how much patience you have for the slow-paced plot and the lows between the climactic highs, as the game experiments with leaving behind party systems and RPG elements while sacrificing complexity to optimize for accessibility. As far as gameplay goes, FFXVI opts for style over substance even as it comes nowhere close to being an equivalent action game to, say, Bayonetta or Devil May Cry V, and that is sure to chafe at many who appreciate past FF entries.Overall: FFXVI is okay, but it tested my patience and I fully understand why others don't like it and didn't finish it.

_childDocuments_.review: Currently 9.5hrs into this game. You can eat a 3 course meal and play this game at the same time. There is an overwhelming abundance of cutscenes. Seldomly there will be a cutscene that you can fast read the subtitles and skip line by line. It would’ve been nice to have interaction take place in 3rd person gameplay and not be a cutscene. Not a lot of roaming around like FFX or FFVII. The gameplay is very linear. It’s like watching a movie that you get to interact with from time to time. Really feeling like this game is 70% cutscenes and 30% gameplay. Just hoping it flips that ratio as the game progresses because it’s frustrating right now. On the positive, it’s a beautiful game visually; The fighting has a Wukong-like feel to it once you field through the extensive cutscenes and eventually get to those parts of the game; and if you are patient enough to treat this game like a movie that you occasionally have to interact with to make it progress, it’s got a decent plot with okay “actors.” Took me 6hrs to finally stop skipping cutscenes and accept my fate. 5/10 rating strictly because it’s a labor of patience just to get to a part where I get to actually play the friggin game.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game overall. Fast-paced gameplay and engaging story. A rollercoaster of emotions.Would give an 8 to 9/10.Gameplay+ Combat is fluid, responsive, and engaging similar to the Devil May Cry series. It's probably not as polished as DMC5 for example but it still holds it's own. They're not really the same, I think both games distinguish themselves apart enough.+ Variety of moves is quite good, the pacing of it is nice, it gives you enough time to get used to your options. I personally wish you could of equipped more than just 2 moves for each Eikons but as I went through the game I think I understood why they did it this way. Switching through Eikons might have been really confusing for some people if it was possible to equip more than a few moves.+ The big bombastic combat scenes were just an adrenaline rush, really amazing stuff. I won't spoil any of them because that would just rob people of the experience but if you like over the top like DMC or Bayonetta, you'll like this, I sure did.- The camera could use some improving. It is a little hard to understand what's going on at times with the amount of particles and such on screen, especially as you progress through the game with more ennemies at once, etc.- I think the worst thing about the game are the side quests. I've done them all and some of them are honestly pretty boring. A lot of them are fetch quests: talk to person, kill monster, gather this and that, etc. I found myself skipping dialogue for some of them.Story+ Cinematics and cutscenes are pretty good. It's not The Last of Us level but there's way worse out there.+ Voice acting is top notch, I honestly can't remember any character that sounded off, everyone is giving a good performance. The main characters are especially amazing.+ Characters are relatable, which I think adds a lot to the story. For that reason, I got emotional on some cutscenes and laughed at some others.- Cutscenes are 30 fps by default. Thankfully, this is fixable with FFXVIfix mod and 60-fps cutscenes mods but I still feel like I had to put this here. I find this baffling how in today's age, they STILL do 30 fps cutscenes. There's no reason for this. If anything, just put the damn option for people! If modders can do it, why not the developpers?Audio+ The music/soundtrack is one of the best part of the game, every track is just fantastic. I found myself often humming at songs in and out of the game. I can see myself listening to the music outside the game which I find pretty rare these days.+ Combat music and audio is just chef's kiss. It just elevates everything on screen and pumps you up. The chorus soundtracks for the big fights are just so epic, it fits perfectly.+ Sound effects are punchy and weighty but I wouldn't say it's anything otherworldly in terms of quality. Overall they're still good.Visuals+ Graphics are very good. Sure, it's not up to par with certain recent games but it's honestly amazing still.+ Particle effects like the elements and energy are just fantastic. Square Enix usually excels on that and they don't disappoint here.- Not sure if this is a sort of bug with the unlocked fps cutscenes mod but if you have DLSS on, some of them will show huge amounts of trails/ghosting during some parts. It's quite bizarre as it seems to be happening only on certain parts of cutscenes, not even the whole thing.Performance+ Ran great for me on a 4090 with DLSS quality and frame generation, 100+ fps most of the time, sometimes up to 180. But then again, it's a 4090, you could say that about almost any games though the state of pc ports these days leave a lot to be desired.- There is stuttering though it's definitely nowhere near as bad as some other games like Jedi Survivor or Dragon's Dogma 2 for example.Not sure how well the game scales on the performance side of things but it is a heavy game to run.I think this game was a really great and fun experience overall. The highlights for me were the bombastic boss fights, the soundtrack, and the cinematics. The only big negative I can think of are the side quests. In my opinion, the rest of the negatives aren't too bad or are not distracting enough to be a deal breaker.Took me over 80 hours to beat the game with all sidequests. And there's still a new game plus after that which I'm sure I'll get to at some point.8-9/10

_childDocuments_.review: This review does not factor in any PC-exclusive technical aspects, as I have only played through it in full on PS5 as of this writing. It also does not factor in anything from the DLCs, as I have not played through them in full.Pros:+ FANTASTIC soundtrack. Easily Masayoshi Soken's best work so far, and one of the best  soundtracks to date+ Gorgeous art direction and visuals+ Satisfying combat that only gets better the further in you get as you unlock more moves+ Some of the most spectacular and frenetic boss fights you will see in any game+ Layered and complex characters supported by great voice acting+ Despite its more mature influences, the game still feels like  at its heart in regards to its characters, stories, world, and lore+ The  influence adds unique political drama flavor to this game that isn't seen in most other  games...Cons:- ... but the game pushes most of that influence aside the further in you get, eventually becoming "just another"  story that doesn't entirely resolve some of the more mature themes or topics raised earlier in its story- Exploration is very limited even when you're given the chance to wander- Clive is the only playable character for the majority of the story; party members are 100% NPC-controlled besides some Torgal commands- Side quests are generally MMO-like and repetitive / boring, with their stories (mostly) only getting interesting near the end of the game- Weapon upgrading, and character customization in general, is very basic. The RPG nature of this action RPG is more light than some may want- Enabling the game's combat accessibility options is done by equipping certain accessories rather than being toggled in the game's settings, meaning your precious equipment slots get taken up if you use themOverall, the game is absolutely worth playing if you're a fan of action RPGs and looking for a  with a more mature flair. While the story was a bit of a letdown for me in some regards, I loved the game's characters, and I can't stress enough just how spectacular the music and boss fights are.

_childDocuments_.review: Although I enjoyed Final Fantasy XVI, I cannot recommend it to others with its current price. Technical IssuesThroughout the game I was have problems with the audio for my speakers. The audio is very quiet and you have to turn it up much higher than normal, I tried several options online but none worked and the only solution would be to use a headset. For some reason there is an open steam store on the main menu and a purchase on steam in the pause menu, its been a month since the release and they haven't changed it. The game does have denuvo drm which can be seen as a downside to many. The gameplay ran smooth for me but when it transitioned into a pre-rendered cutscene the start of the cutscene was very choppy. Sometimes when playing, applications on other monitor screens would go black or blank.GameplayMy biggest complaint of gameplay is the combat, this game your either watching a cutscene to further the story or fight for you but when you get to fight you just spam the exact same button for a minute or so in a usual battle then 10+ minutes for a boss battle. Most basic battles revolve around 1-2 mini boss and several minions, the minions die very quickly and you’re usually left slowly chipping away at the mini bosses health for a minute or so.There is a lot of walking and jogging around the place, the game has a sprint but it only allows you to use it in certain situations and you cannot activate it yourself. It takes about 15+ hours to get a mount but that comes from a side quest and you can only use the mount in specific locations. There is a lot of hold button to open door and QTE it makes me feel like this game was made in 2000-2010 era. A lot of cool scenes and finishing blows don't have a QTE which is weird since they use QTE plenty throughout boss battles for a lot of other scenes.The dodging in this came can be a bit of a hit and miss, the better version of dodging is activated with one of your power ups though. About halfway through or so you unlock something called the hunt board which is implemented poorly, the hunt board tells you the general location of the beast but there is no menu for it or a way to check the general location when you are in the field searching so if you forget you have to fast travel all the way back to base then walk all the way back to the hunt board then go back to the general location. The second main base is a pain to navigate since your fastest movement is a jog, my nan jogs faster than that and shes dead. The game is partially open world so it doesnt have as much wonder of exploration as the previous title.The Eikon abilities are a bit of a hit and miss, most of the abilities are used for groups of weak enemies or mini bosses but when used against an actual boss can get you killed since some abilities have you stand in place letting the boss eat you alive. You gain a new eikon every 5-10 mission but 1 of these eikons is 6 missions before the final mission and the another eikon is 3 missions before the final fight, by then most people have already decided on their favourite abilities, you will be at the final boss by the time you unlock/upgrade one of these new abilities.StoryThere is a lot of cutscenes in this game and they can be very long. You can watch the first minute of a cutscene and usually skip the rest and you will still know whats going on. The story isnt groundbreaking and has the usual twists. The game has a couple nude scenes and some kiss scenes between between man/woman man/man, I don not really care much about the relationships in this game since most of them only get a few cutscenes in game. The final fight and cutscene was really well done, if the entire game had this writing and fighting it would have been more enjoyable. The game wants you to care about the relationships and the people of this world but they dont give us a chance, you can’t interact with your friends at all in this game and final fantasy XV is the winner in making bonds. The only bonding you see in this game is through cutscenes and nothing you decide unlike final fantasy XV, although XV wasnt the best game it did a good job on making you care about the characters and forming the brotherly bond between them. Meanwhile this game just shows you a scene and expects you to feel it.All in all the game is okay, there is enjoyable bits and I did have fun but I think the purchase price is too steepEdit: After 9-10 hrs both dlc are completed. Although the game tells you which sidequests you must do to unlock the dlc, IT does NOT tell you of the sidequests you need to do to unlock the sidequests that unlock the dlc quests. both dlc are harder than the base game, if you are under leveled you will struggle in the the rising tide dlc. the dlc stories were quite nice and I wish they brought the same energy to the base game

_childDocuments_.review: PERFORMANCE: Dunno if the updates have helped, but at least for me on my pc (13900k and RTX4080), the game is running splendidly, around 80 fps at 4k, and then turn on Frame Gen, and i get 120fps or more at 4k max settings. I would recommend taking a minute to install the FFXVIfix mod to fix any strange hiccups with cut-scenes and to unlock some extra settings. GAMEPLAY: Now performance aside, this is a REALLY good game the combat is a somewhat more streamlined version of Devil May Cry 5, it might be a bit sad that there is only one playable character, but with how the game goes its something you can get passed, the giant monster fights are EPIC BEYOND EPIC! seriously worth the price of admission, the story is great, the dialogue is really good, and graphics are beautiful. so really the only mild complaints is that other than some optional quests and fights, the game is rather linear so while the world is rich you might be left wanting for some more adventuring. OVERALL: I think this game and FF7 Rebirth are a return to form for the FF franchise despite the game play differences, the dialog is good again, the story is fleshed out, the fights are epic, and the characters are likable (and unlikable if they are meant to be) this particular entry is fairly grim with themes of slavery and a land that's formed around exploiting others for convenience or religion. not to mention a pretty high death count relative the series for named characters. also pro tip while many of the side quests are rather mundane, a few of them are pretty good, and none of them take too long. so give em a go. 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: It's waaaaaay too long and 60% of the cutscenes are "walk three steps, say two words, end of cutscene" (honestly would cut down at least two or three hours of game time if removed). And don't get me started on the boss "cutscene armour" in fights...Why do we need levels in this game? They just up the HP, stats do nothing, they mean nothing, just a number that goes up, no gear in the game has stat requirements. why even show me how much strength I have if it doesn't do nothing. (And if it does, I didn't feel any difference because all of the fights take the same amount of time and no I never fought lvl 10 enemies when I was lvl 40 because I there was no point in doing so :P )Side quests are incredibly inconsistent, at one point of the story you get 3, on another you get 15, a lot of them are fetch/kill type, so tedious and rarely worth it.Combat is fine, if the fps doesn't drop, but most of the icon abilities are kind of weak, compared to others, and the time it takes to charge some of them just makes them even more silly to use, even if they might be more powerful.Moving around the map is incredibly slow, even with the mount, it feels like sprint and mount speeds are the same, so why even have a mount, other than for the novelty of having one.Also, why the F**K are cutscenes locked to 30 FPS?! At this point the game is just an interactive movie, why even have the player play the game, just make the whole game into one big cutscene and be done with it.If You really like the franchise it's a fun game here and there, but don't expect to have great performance, stutters and other performance related issues are frequent so try out the demo first.

_childDocuments_.review: It plays like a simpler DMC/Bayonetta rather than your slower-paced FF RPG. However, in a game that encourages style with constant bombardment of colorful points popping up on the right of my screen, it feels very counter intuitive, especially when provided with two additional dlc eikons.  Other than that, the game could've used party members, a longer bloody palace and a harder difficulty mode.  The Story is good but kinda felt too "JRPGish" and anime  toward the latter half of the game.  If that is your taste, then by all means yknow, but when I first played the demo, I had the impression that it was going to be super dark, but nah.I had performance issues with a rtx 3080, but that was because I had stuff running on my 2nd monitor.  As soon as I closed everything, my fps was 70-90 on ultra with no dlss.  Before that, I had 10–30 fps, so make sure to close everything out before playing.

_childDocuments_.review: I know I am only about 14 hours in at the time of writing this, but I absolutely love this game. I love to play these type of games and get fully engrosed in the story, starting to care for the characters and the world. I also really love Clive, he is not this stoic "doesn't-speak-much-and-just-looks-menacing" but he has character, he has empathy, he is caring and his voice actor did an amazing job capturing the hurt he went through, you can hear the absolute anguish in his voice in some scenes that just had me hold back some tears. _childDocuments_.review: GameplayThe strong point of the game, it does well what FFXV did poorly but despite that the magic system is still inferior to the rest of the series, not as bad as the one in FF XV but VII Remake and Lightning Returns are better action FFs in their magic system, if you liked DMC V and likes FF you're still going to like the gameplay.MapsNoting really impressive, the game is actually better in the corridor sections than in their multiple big areas, but nothing  quite as good as the secrets or freedom that you have in FF XII, it doesn't help that there are fell dungeons and that they are locked behind the story(you can replay them at any moment).StoryDespite the good start the story is probably the worst I have experienced in a FF game, it tries to be too serious but the western style storytelling doesn't fit with the themes of a FF story, Clive is an adult that acts like a depressive teenager, the game tries to make you fell sympathy for what the characters had to go through but it just fell forced, like the fact the protagonist was "forced" into slavery for 13 years, and it's not just slavery that felt forced, one moment you are invading a country and another you are helping a ♥♥♥♥♥ protect a city? there is a good lore to make things interesting but they didn't know what to focus and ended up half-assing everything.If the game didn't have so many side stories and focused more on the main cast like FF XV did it would had been a lot better but it ends up taking the story too serious for what it is.I would recommend the game if there was less story but because the game has so many cutscenes it's hard to separate it from the game, there are good moments but the bad ones are really bad, at least we the gameplay carries the game for me.

_childDocuments_.review: the game is alright...but being alright isnt enough with so many games on the market, even the FF7 remake which i consider way inferior to the original FF7 is way better than this gameIt can be an enjoyable game, even amazing at times, but half the game also feels like a slog. that is because the exploration of the world and the side quests suck. and half the main quests also feel like useless side quests. It doesn't help that the characters and story itself also feel pretty mid. the main appeal of the game is in its graphics. without good graphics this game would be nothing. The actual big story fights of the game are a spectacle which you dont really see in other games at all. it feels like epic anime fights, but without feeling cheap. I would prefer a good story instead but nowadays with modern gaming we dont really get this that often anymore. Back in the day companies needed to catch our attention with well written stories and being creative, because graphics and animations were too bad to do much else. nowadays its sadly the opposite.all in all pretty midif you are new to FF or didnt play the beloved classics yet... then definitely play FF10 or the original FF7 instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. It goes back to making Summons aka Eikons a big part of the world, sort of like how the story in FFX made them out to be. The story has comparable moments and situations in the style of a Game of Thrones show. The story is darker and personal one focusing on our main character Clive.Many people will not like controlling one character instead of a party , like you would in past Final Fantasy entries. Personally, I like this attempt to tell a Solo character FF story. It feels immersive, and cinematic to follow Clives journey and be part of it.Since this is a solo , personal story centered on Clive, the game play is developed around this, focusing on  real time action combat, reactive quick time cinematic moments, adventure and linear traversal. Occasionally you have NPC's that assist Clive in the game, but for the most part  the Eikons abilities and your dog are your only controllable "party members". The graphics are well done, and very cinematic throughout, the music is some of the best original music ive heard since FFX imo.The Graphics are not optimized enough to run well on PC, as I have plenty of better looking games that perform alot better than this. (Just look at the forums and reviews suggesting the optimization needs some work)Game works fine with mouse and keyboard, especially when you set the bindings the  way you want it to. The target switch currently can not use scroll mouse wheel up or down, which is a bummer.I use the FF16 Fix and play in ultrawide 21:9 1440p. I use a 3080ti and 10700k processor, 32gb ram and run the game from a SSD, and run the game using recommended settings which is ULTRA/ DLSS and dynamic resolution.   Certain areas like hub towns with candle lighting get 40 fps, while in cutscenes and world traversal (exploration and combat), pretty much anywhere away from hub towns get about 60-70fps)   I recommend this game. The game is still a great choice on the PS5 , and runs stable on there , while looking great , as well if you are shopping around.

_childDocuments_.review: So without spoilers: Music: 11/10 the music was so well crafted that it enhanced the experience of every encounter and it made me feel so many emotionsStory: 9.5/10 The beginning was a fantastic introduction to any game I've ever played, it did kinda fall off a little at the end but it was still such a beautiful story, one of the best that I've played however I haven't played many final fantasy games so take from that what you will, as someone who reads a lot I definitely enjoyed the story despite some of the hiccups/ambiguities that plague it. Characters: 10/10 the game did a fantastic job of getting you invested in the characters, I loved, and hated with such strong emotions Combat: 7/10 I like the combat but it feels a little clunky at times despite having a consistent 200 fps while running the game, the combos that you can make and the feel of the combat is good though, if you like a devil may cry type of combat then you would like it. Visuals 10/10: The game is beautiful, the screenshots that you can take are full of potential, the beauty of the world and character models is just chefs kiss, if you love stunning visuals and want to make many cool desktop backgrounds this is definitely a good choice. Gameplay/RPG elements 4/10: ngl I wasn't the biggest fan of this, there wasn't a lot of loot, item upgrading felt pointless, and many things that were just there just to be there or just a lack of things that would make some of the best rpgs. The world isn't open world which is fine but it is pretty restrictive on where you can go unlike ff15, to me the world felt kinda dead but I think that's what they were going for, spoilers if I explain what I mean by that. the next part is a pseudo spoiler so please skip this if you don't want to get an idea of what the ending is like:  Overall I give this game an 8.6/10 if you want a story that will make you feel a myriad of emotions while having decent combat that makes you feel as if you're kicking ass, then I recommend it, personally though I would probably wait for a sale as there are probably much better games for your dollar. But the dollar aside, I enjoyed the game and was definitely worth the years I spent waiting for this to come to pc.

_childDocuments_.review: Having grown up with the FF series, I do understand some of the complaints over lacking the in-depth RPG combat systems, skill customization and mechanics. Still a great deal of customizing your combat style that makes this addition to the franchise a nice treat for longtime fans, but also accessible to new fans that might be looking for a different take on the genre. Very strong recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: For a person who has played these games since the very first game on NES, I am loving this game already.  It reminds me of FF3 (SNES), which was one of my absolute favorites of the series.  Hopefully I'm not the only one that sees the correlation. Main Points:1. The story so far is engaging to the point my wife is asking me to not play when she isn't around.  If you are not a fan of long cinematic sequences, this game probably isn't for you.  My wireless controller actually shuts itself off often waiting for sequences to end.2. The combat mechanics start a bit repetitive but as the story progresses so does the combat.  it has a souls-like feel but the difficulty can be adjusted by using certain optional "Timely" accessories.3. I am running the game on full tilt and streaming through Steam from my primary desktop (i9-9900/RTX 4070 TI Super/ethernet) to my laptop with almost no issues and even those seem to be network hiccups.Bottom Line:  As of right now, this is well on its way to the top three of my favorite games of the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay: Kind of like DMC with a touch of God of War  but you have to wait quite a while until you get the cool stuff so it can feel more boring at first but if you think about it, you only start with Attack in other FFs which is even more boring and it only gets fun later on. Difficulty is somewhere in the middle of Easy and Normal in a DMC game. DLC bosses are hard for some reason but I liked it.Main quest:Pure, absolute, unfiltered, undiluted, unadulterated KINO. Some completely shameless references to other media but they couldn't have been used better than they were.Side quests: I just experienced one of the most hype fights in gaming and now you want me to care about your wine bottles or whatever?Granted, there are some interesting side quests few and far between (and the hunt board is a cool side activity where you can bounty hunt dangerous monsters) but most of the time they feel like a waste of time, were it not for the EXP. It deserves 8.5/10 but I give it a 7 because of the overall rather lame side quest padding which is unfortunate but I totally recommend the game.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY XVI

_childDocuments_.review: A great modern take on the Final Fantasy series: - the story and the characters are very interesting, you will grow attached to them and feel joy and sadness-the gameplay is smooth and responsive, albeit a bit basic. The best part, without going into spoilers, is switching between powers- The voice acting is awesome, they chose some random brits which unironically sound great and add a lot of character to everyone- The graphics are amazing, on top of it the presentation is excellent, making it one of the best looking games I have ever played.All in all, it is a great action RPG with a great story and fun combat. _childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best Final Fantasy games of all time and definitely the best one since FFX.Buy this game. Its a great mix of Lord Of The Rings and Game Of Thrones in terms of world building and plot and Devil May Cry in terms of game play/combat. The music is great, but even though it's maybe not the best or as catchy as past FF games I still find it hauntingly beautiful and some of the music feels like a warm breezy day laying in the grass among fire lilies while dragonflies dance in the sun rays.This game is unlike any FF game that has been released before it, but still manages to feel all familiar. The world is beautiful and the characters are amazing. I'm not too big on the main character I like his backstory and abilities, but I can't get past the fact that hes literally one of the ugliest MC's FF has ever had it might be the fact that he slightly resembles a dog to me and I just don't like his face also his Imperial outfit is atrocious. In terms of party members I love this rendition of [REDACTED] its honestly my favorite version of him/her hes such a bad ass and just a really honest character. I also think Jill is really cool and love how shes there from the beginning helps that shes also extremely pretty and has one of the best outfits in FF history! There's also Torgal the dog he's such a nice addition. FFXV also had a dog(s), but they didn't really do much and weren't incorporated into the game play. The story is great and the world building is incredibly deep with so much lore added into the game that really enriches the game very similar to Mass Effect, but maybe not as grand of scale. And while the side quests are mundane the story centered around those quests are actually really good and makes finishing them well worth it, I find many of them deepen the story, world, and characters so even if they're not the best game play wise the stories they bring are done very well and worth experiencing.This is quite possibly one of the greatest games of the generation. If not one of the greatest games of all time. As you progress through the game you are constantly unlocking new things  The fact that the game manages to touch on social issues like slavery or intolerance while still managing to be a great high fantasy game puts it above similar titles that are at the end of the day just fantasy fluff. Even though the game play switch to a DMC style might throw off some long time fans because it's is so different game play wise I strongly encourage you to buy this game its incredibly good and really something special that I think all FF fans will appreciate. This is truly a "Final Fantasy for fans and first timers". 10/10(mini rant)Every single Final Fantasy game that has been released in the past decade and a half has been a near disappointment and almost everything Square Enix has put out in the past 2 decades has been literal rage bait bad, but this, this is good. Square Enix is 2 for 2 with Final Fantasy Remake and FFXVI if Life Is Strange Double Exposure turns out to be good then they will be back on my good side.Final edit:  This game is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ masterpiece a literal masterclass of it's own. Video games like this don't come around often it is literally up there with one of the greatest video games of all time. I don't see a FF game topping this one in a long time. It's that good. I'll go so far as to say this is the best AAA game of the generation, the best that were going to get. It is truly lightning in a bottle for this gen of gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserved to be GOTYSo that in and of itself is my TLDR review. However, for those looking for more, let me first start off with how I came to play this game to begin with. I had pre-ordered Dragon Age: The Veilguard, and refunded the pre-order. Had used money I had earmarked for my dog Joby...who died at 10 weeks. My father was in the hospital, and I wanted something to distract me - something story driven. Veilguard wouldn't be out soon enough, so I looked at what new was already out. Final Fantasy has always been hit or miss for me. I adored FFIX, but despise FFXI've beaten the original FF7, but barely made it past the beginning area in FF15So to say I was iffy about this game is an understatement. Especially since the change to action combat, and that I had heard it was pretty much on rails. Still, I watched a youtube video by the "Before you buy" guys. Falcon, eagle, whatever his name is. Anyways, he described the game as Final Fantasy's attempt at Game of Thrones, which intrigued me. Had they finally went a more ...mature route? So that was my getting here. For the last month I've gotten a few hours in here, a few there, and during which my father died. However, each day I looked forward to seeing more and more of Clive Rosfield, who, in my appraisal, is the best voice-acted character since Geralt of Rivia. Not only that, he's believable and well written. The story itself was a JOY to experience. I'd say the story was better than that of Witcher 3, and I loved Witcher 3. Only reason I'd say it's BETTER is because it flows so much smoother than that of the Witcher games. Yes, the game is on rails a lot of the time, but that isn't a bad thing here. Side quests exist, and later on become important, but there are always just enough to give you a break between main story entries and then it's back on. The pacing feels like Mass Effect 2, but again, even better. Oh and Square don't hold back either. They do go mature and without being overtly gory or relying on nudity. Not that I mind either, but to see a game stand on it's feet without them, and still feel like it's keyed to adults - that I am amazed by in the current market. FFIX was my first FF game and will always be my sentimental favorite, but if I am to be honest, I'd say this game has become my favorite in the series and has made it onto my top 5 of all time favorite RPGs, period. The combat feels somewhat similar to Monster Hunter and Soulslike games, just in terms of timing your dodges or your parries. You've abilities that slow down or stop time which do help, and all of it is very flashy and very satisfying in a "I'm a dragon ball z fan, here is a big bang or kamehameha" kind of way. But I wasn't in this for the finish because of the combat. I was here for the story. I had to see what came next, and I had to experience it first hand, not see it spoiled. When a story is able to grip you in that way...it has love and care put into it by the writer(s).This game is worth buying if you love a good story. It will be one you remember long after you've finished it. 9.9/10 What would have made it a 10 is if a certain outlaw had made an appearance at the very end. Those who know, know.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a cinematic masterpiece with some combat sprinkled in. Genuinely worth it, very Final Fantasy.I'll jump into pro and cons:Pros: -Combat is actually really fun, fast paced and the companions aren't set pieces who do nothing. The options to expand and change your play-style as you progress the game are good. The  fights are hype and really climactic. -The story is really good, nothing revolutionary, but a lot better than most games nowadays. -The world is beautiful. -Travel doesn't feel like a slog, there are enough fast travel points and the maps are just the right size for mounted traversal.-Side quests: rather than feeling like quests, they are little diversions that reveal more of the lore and character motivations for the supporting cast. (I really liked this approach, but ymmv)Cons:  -Story bosses ALL have a %HP threshold where they stop taking damage for a phase change/qte. You will always hit this threshold while unloading on the staggered boss, the phase change/qte does not activate until the stagger ends. This feels bad.Overall worth every penny I spent. The DLC is also really good, adding more challenging boss fights and a really good bit of extra content for the price point.Note: they have an easy mode that trivializes all the combat by giving you accessories that do most of the fighting for you (ie: There is one that makes all your combos perfect timing, one that auto dodges for you, etc.) Great for people who aren't super good at these games. But also some people have said the game is too easy or un-engaging combat wise while using them, as if they aren't optional.

_childDocuments_.review: This is easily the hardest game I've ever wrote a review for.I'm 36 and have been playing FF games since 1997. I have beaten every single main title Final Fantasy game. This game is NOT a Final Fantasy game. I would say this is closer to a God of War or DMC game, than Final Fantasy. Calling it a RPG is dishonest IMO. That doesn't make this game a bad one by default however.Exactly who is this game made for? This is the most "mature" FF, they swear, there is lots of blood, clearly they are targeting an older audience which, I as an older fan, think is a great idea. However this game is so painstakingly SIMPLE and BRAINDEAD to play. You mash the X button, and you win. I thought they would have learned something with FF15 but I guess the bean counters at Square decided to make another overly simple action game that anyone with an IQ lower than 80 can beat. I don't blame Square for the state of my beloved video game series as much as I do the people who play the games now. After all Square is in the business of making money, and they are listening to the people who demand they make this kind of game. Just how braindead is the vast majority of people? I beat FF7 when I was in 4th grade and its a million times more challenging and complex than this game, and this game is targeting freaking adults. I am ashamed to be rated along with all of you who find this to be challenging. I guess I'm just sad that my favorite video game series is dead. It's clear that it's not coming back. Not as long as video games remain as popular as they are today. I blame all the morons who think this is challenging or demand every game be an action game now. I have more to say but adult life demands more from me. After it is all said and done, this is not a "bad" game. I recommend it only on the basis of it telling a good story with high quality production values and a fair price. However I do NOT recommend this as a Final Fantasy game or even an RPG.RIP Final Fantasy. I will miss you. Hopefully we will meet again one day.

_childDocuments_.review: 4/10The music, sound design, and voice acting are incredible, and the game itself is visually stunning. The large-scale mecha-kaiju battles (though more cinematic than interactive) are thrilling to watch. Unfortunately, the rest of the game falls flat.The gameplay feels like a stripped-down version of mechanics we’ve seen done better elsewhere. Even classic turn-based RPGs offer more freedom and fluidity than what’s found here. Final Fantasy XV delivered a more satisfying combat experience, and it doesn't come close to the level of Devil May Cry V—even the fourth installment. There’s zero choice in gear, no stats to customize, and companions feel identical and uninspired.So maybe the story saves it? Unfortunately, no. It feels like someone tried to blend the worst parts of Game of Thrones with Marvel-style dialogue. The characters lack depth, coming across as hollow or puppet-like, with only one or two exceptions. You finish the game feeling like they’re action figures with voices, lacking any defining traits.For a game aiming for a mature tone, the only “mature” aspect is the repetitive use of a single slur, which quickly loses any impact. Where Game of Thrones (which the game feels most inspired by) offers complex characters, schemes, and motivations, this game offers nothing beyond partial nudity and cursing, never venturing deeper than a puddle.I love the Final Fantasy series and always will, but this entry feels like a step down—even compared to Final Fantasy XV.

_childDocuments_.review: Played this on ps5 already and I'm glad it finally arrived on PC.The port is pretty good so far, lots of extra graphics and configuration options for PC, also ran pretty well the 2 hours I already played, no crashes, bugs or anything, very solid.As for the game itself: well it's an absolute spectacle. Combat is fun and the boss fights start pretty over the top already, but only ramp up even more the further you progress. The Bahamuth fight is probably the absolute peak of all boss battles.There are only 2 things that bothered me personally:1. the overwhelming majority of the sidequests are very boring and tedious fetch quests and not really worth the time, which is a bit of a shame.And 2. the plot is extremely (and I mean extremely extremely) contrived. You won't notice until the end tho, but when all pieces fall into place it's pretty dumb how many completely absurd coincidences had to happen for the villain's scheme to unfold.Those 2 things aside the game is really fun, but I wouldn't call it an RPG whatsoever, both the plot as well as gear progression are very linear, it goes from weaker to stronger, that's pretty much it. Haven't played the DLC yet tho, so maybe that changes a few things.Anyway, it's a great, very cinematic action game and despite its shortcomings still worth picking up.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally beat the game and all the hunts after 65 hours. I played it with a 14700K and 4080 Super in 4K and it was a fantastic experience. No issues, no crashes. My favorite Final Fantasy to date. The combat system is really fun, but takes a while to feel fluid and cohesive. Once it gets going though you won't want to set it down. Dodges and parries are super satisfying, and combining all your newly acquired abilities makes you want to continue further and unlock more. The story is where this shines. A Final Fantasy take on Game of Thrones of sorts. Very political, war, the greed of man, and humanity. You have to mentally piece together all the different factions and nations but it all starts to make sense the more you play. There's an npc that summarizes the story so far, so you can catch up if you've been away from the game or want to keep up if things didn't make sense.Clive is a bad-ass protagonist one of the best in FF. Keep an open mind and enjoy the ride. "We fight, we survive, we endure, we don't need a reason"

_childDocuments_.review: Fast-paced combat that makes you feel like a god once you mix-and-match your perfect set of Eikonic abilities, real grabber of a story, and top-notch cinematics and visuals. Soundtrack is full of orchestral bangers that suit the utterly EPIC & legendary battles you will encounter.I personally only have a few minor gripes with XVI - the static maps with no weather or day/night cycles gets a little barren after hour 30 or so. Unfortunately, there's no ultrawide monitor support either which I was expecting to see on the PC release, and the base difficulty of the game personally speaking is a bit lacking. There are mods to up the difficulty a wee-bit before you reach NG+, but otherwise it's hard to not love this game and the oddly-exciting lore between Bearers, Dominants and looking forward to a world of change.Try the demo. - If you hate a game with cutscenes and deep stories, go find another game.  Regardless of what you think it is, this is an amazing Final Fantasy game, and I'd buy it a third time.

Grand, epic, awe-inspiring laced with perfect music, lore and emotion battles that makes your skin crawl.Now, im off to new game plus. The lack of "american" censorship is refreshing and welcome.3. The game looks good, runs great and sounds fantastic. _childDocuments_.review: After almost 70+ hours and completing both DLC, Final Fantasy XVI is a great action, adventure game filled with great characters to accompany with you along your journey with amazing, fun combat. Not a perfect game by any means, however. I do have a few issues such as repetitive side quests, some pacing issues, and the absence of RPG elements. Again,  (even though the game-play changes every installment past FF X). Pretty much what you see in game-play videos, it's literally Devil May Cry meets Final Fantasy. If you're a DMC fan, you'll probably enjoy this game. As for FF fans, it is a departure from the traditional FF games, but I still think you'll have a lot of fun with it once you get settled with three Eikons.  I feel at times I didn't even try and still won.  I think SE/Creative Studio III listened to feedback from the base game and really upped the difficulty in the two expansions. I actually felt I was challenged in those two expansions and had fun with it.  Story is good overall. Love the tone of it with being more "mature" and dark. Maybe not the best story out of all the FF games, since there is some pacing issues where some characters are not "fleshed out" as they should be and some story elements not being explained well where you can get lost and confused. There is a feature called active time lore where you can pause and see some background information on characters, setting, etc. related to the current cutscene you are watching that can explain it to you; a bit handy at times. The main villain was okay in my opinion. The dominant villains who held the eikon's power were more interesting.  10/10. Don't think I need to go any further. Just listen to it on Spotify or Youtube Music and you'll know why almost every FF16 fan obsess over it.  I have mixed feelings with side quests. One half they can be good if you are invested in the world and its characters. On the other, it is reptitive and a grind fest. With the game coming from the team behind FF14, the quests are structured from MMO games. 'Go here', 'kill/fetch/talk/etc.), come back to the initial NPC, complete, and repeat. Maybe it is my fault since I did try to force myself to do as many as I can before I do the main quests. But how it is presented does at times bore me and make me feel exhausted. With that said, there are times I do get engaged with the characters when they reveal their dark pasts in this troubling world . I just think unless you are invested in the world of FF16, you can skip them. The important side quests are with the '+' icons where they can give you new equipment to craft, increase your inventory slots, and potion potency.  The game isn't open world but similar to FF12 where they have a batch of handcrafted maps; you can say its an "open-area" game more or less. While the areas have purpose, there isn't much exploration. There aren't any big cities for you to get lost and explore or secret mines or dungeons (besides the ones related to the main quests). I believe this is due to hardware limitations and/or ran out resources and time during development.  Performance and graphics can vary. There are times it looks magnificent and there are times it just looks mushy and frames would drop significantly. I want to think there is just too much detail at times the game can handle with NPCs and buildings that SE didn't bother making the capitol cities explorable knowing it would require a lot of system resources. Game play at least was smooth to me. Otherwise, it's a good PC port.Despite all of the issues, I still got past it and had an amazing experience with Final Fantasy XVI and I consider of my favorite FFs so far.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Beautiful game with smooth combat that should not be called Final Fantasy because they have left abandoned nearly everything genre defining and special about the FF series.Good: the graphics are beautiful both cgi and gameplay, the  music is varied and good, the story is cohesive and enjoyable, and the combat, though completely new and different to the series, is smooth.Bad:  *The game is no longer what I would consider an open world environment. The world is tiny and not explorable in the true sense of the word. You don't interact with the environment, there are NO HIDDEN items or areas I have discoivered as of yet @ 40ish hours in. You walk from point A to point B on these tiny maps designed to be straight roads(hand holding).*There is NO  character development, NONE. You have zero need to gear for special situations like resists or special combat tactics because they have been removed! You can no longer find 1000's of pieces of gear from monsters, hidden chests or areas, etc becauset it no longer exists! You are given every little upgrade as part of the main quest with very few examples found in side quests( a lot of which being useless by the time they are achievable) so I am up to a dozen? weapons I can use and they are all exactly the same with exception only of their skin. No special's talents, boosts, stats, different weapon types, etc. Stats have just been reduced to attack and defense essentially(hand holding to the extreme).*The new combat system , while very smoothly implemented, is just boring after your first few fights because you realize you can basically stand in one place and hit attack or evade, that's it! Your eikons don't actually matter, their elements don't matter, your gear doesn't matter because there is no complexity or difficulty to the fights any longer.*While the CGIs are great, there is no longer any choice of what you want to do or where to go to do it! The entire game is linearly mapped out for you with no RPG type choices of consequence built in. The side quests are absolutely boring. There really aren't a lot of REAL sidequests either when you compare to older games or other games of the genre. Most of the sidequests are literal "hey teleport here, run 200ft, kill this monster(don't worry zero challenge) and the game teleports you back to turn it in in exchange for....some gold. No prizes, special items, gear upgrades, nothing because they have removed the need for anything special in the game! The Main quests are not much better. There is a bug as of this writing they have yet to fix to my knowledge. IF your screen times out during a CGI the game crashes. Why is this important? Because the main quests go like this most of the time: Teleport to new place, watch 10 minutes of CGI(amazing looking, cool) but try not to forget to play with your mouse or controller during this time when you are SUPPOSED to be enjoying the CGI, then take control for 10 minutes to fight the EXACT same fight over and over about 8 times, 10 more minutes of CGI(controller, screen timeout, crash, etc)then kill the boss, 10 more minutes of CGI and done! It is extremely boring aside from the lovely CGI's. THis is supposed to be an RPG though right? *The game is no longer an RPG. It is a Story with a little combat in between, combat that a 5 year old could complete because all complexity and difficulty has been thrown away, all of it! The entire game is a Hand Holding event with lots of pretty picture, no choices, no development, no suprises, it's all gone. I personally will no longer be purchasing anything close to FF16 that Sony produces in the future. It's a great game but it is NOT an open-world RPG as they claim. It is an casual story game whatever you call that.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge fan of Final Fantasy. I fell in love with the series from the first time I played FFVII on my old PC. Back in the day, I bought a PS2 and PS3 just to play the games from FFVIII to FFXIII-2. What I really like are the graphics and the story. I haven't played through the whole game yet, but so far there haven’t been too many twists I didn’t see coming, though there are some surprises that I’ve really enjoyed.The things I don’t like are that it isn’t an open-world game. It feels very linear, and I’m not just referring to the story, but the entire world. There are just paths you follow—nothing to explore, nothing new to discover. I also don’t like that I can’t choose my party members (at least, not up until now—maybe it changes later in the game). For me, that’s a key part of what makes Final Fantasy great: the huge, engaging story, the music, the Eikons, and of course, the ability to choose your party members.Another thing I don’t enjoy is the gameplay itself. I feel like I’m just mashing buttons, occasionally prompted to press something specific. I don’t really have to think or make choices about how to play. I also can't choose when to summon my Eikon. So far, it only happens in Eikon vs. Eikon fights.Things I like:* The graphics* The story* The music* The EikonsThings I don't like:* The game feels too linear; there’s no open world to explore.* You can’t choose your party members (so far).* The gameplay feels too simple; button-mashing without strategy.* Eikon summoning is restricted to specific battles.I’m giving it a positive review just because I’m a huge fan, and I want to see Final Fantasy continue to release on PC.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty good and definitely has a good take on combat for a final fantasy game compared to older titles. There are also some fights in the game that feel absolutely epic and are a lot of fun.I have been playing the FF series for many years and my main issue with this game are some of the mechanics are known for are not there. Such as the variability in the gear you equip seems to have a very minimal effect so far. Also no status effects such as poison or confusion, also elements are almost meaningless besides a visual difference. Basically the RPG elements of the game are not very refined. Another thing that bugs me is I have 3060ti, 16 gb of ram and 11700 cpu and still cant play 60fps on 2k for this game. The game feels unplayable for me at times and 4K is completely unplayable.TLDR; Great game but not the best final fantasy game I have played. Also square could do some optimizing on the game to allow it to run better imo.

_childDocuments_.review: FF16 is a strange game. On the one hand, it has serious issues with tonal inconsistency (somewhat of a mainstay in modern FF games it seems), the more "mature" and "grounded" storytelling and worldbuilding absolutely falls flat, the RPG elements feel pointless, and it has some of the worst padding and pacing I've ever seen in a game.On the other hand, bits of the story and dialogue definitely shine through, the combat and magic systems are solid, and the boss battles (particularly the ones involving giant monsters) are positively ace.The difference in quality between FF16's highs and lows cannot be understated. When the game is good, it's amazing. When the game is bad, it is insufferable. Ultimately, I don't regret my time with it, but this definitely wasn't the game-changer that the series was looking for. I think its worth picking up to try and to engage with the combat and boss fights, but likely not at full price despite its frankly unnecessary 100-hour playtime.It also bears mentioning that the game is incredibly poorly optimized for PC. If you do pick it up, highly recommend downloading FF16fix, which installs surprisingly easily, though this does not fix all of the optimization problems.

Thus I purchased this.But simply put, this is like the Resident Evil 6 of FF series.The hope of something awesome might happened is the one that keeps me tried playing enthusiastically up until the end. And it kinda did, the VERY end game moments are great (THANK YOU). But that's it.So please, my dear SQUARE ENIX, you can change the battle mechanism, the party system, exploration system, etc as you like. But don't change the very identity of an FF game. I don't have to explain it, you've made the previous ones all great. You know what it is. I juts really hope your next Final Fantasy can make up for this, just like RE7 shines after RE6.Just some notes to you, Square Enix, PLEASE:- More RPGs. Less Button-Mashing-Actions- Don't make our beloved Summons be gay. Whatever their forms- Hell don't make any creatures be gay- You want to put some romance then put romance...EFFECTIVELY. Not the unnecessary ones. You've done great job before (Cloud & Tifa/Aerith moments, Tidus & Yuna, etc), I don't know why you flopped at this one- You already being a good guy by hiring some "DIVERSE" teams. That already done them a great favor. Now you don't have to let them make the story become "DIVERSE" too.Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: ➤ 𝐓𝐋𝐃𝐑▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔Embody the brooding Avatar of Burning Godzilla as he Megamans his way through a Rogues Gallery of Final Fantasy's most Classic Summons.⚠️ 𝐄𝐕𝐎𝐋𝐕𝐈𝐍𝐆 𝐈𝐌𝐏𝐑𝐄𝐒𝐒𝐈𝐎𝐍𝐒 ⚠️▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔ᴅɪsᴄʟᴀɪᴍᴇʀ -- ɪ ᴅɪᴅ ɴᴏᴛ ᴘʟᴀʏ ᴛʜᴇ ᴘs𝟻 ᴠᴇʀsɪᴏɴ        sᴘᴇᴄs --  ɪɴᴛᴇʟ ɢᴇɴ𝟷𝟸 i𝟽                      ɢᴇғᴏʀᴄᴇ ʀᴛx 𝟹𝟶𝟼𝟶                      sᴀᴍsᴜɴɢ 𝟿𝟾𝟶 ᴘʀᴏ ssᴅ 𝟸ᴛʙ ᴘᴄɪᴇ ɴᴠᴍᴇ ɢᴇɴ 𝟺 ɢᴀᴍɪɴɢ ᴍ.𝟸➤ 𝐀𝐒𝐒𝐄𝐓𝐒 𝐂𝐎𝐌𝐏𝐈𝐋𝐄 𝐃𝐔𝐑𝐈𝐍𝐆 𝐆𝐀𝐌𝐄𝐏𝐋𝐀𝐘▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔    While cutscenes are not entirely pre-rendered, they are 'pre-processed'; what do I mean by that? Certain assets are exclusive to these scenes; such as models, particle effects, shaders, animations, cameras, the list goes on. When these scenes render in realtime, the game will hard-lock itself at 30 FPS (with Denovo it dips to 29 / 28).    Because of this, there is noticeable Stutter; at least at first. While the game does 'Compile Shaders' before launching, the Stutters players may experience are performance dips as new assets are loaded for the FIRST time -- basically compiling additional Shaders during gameplay. These assets can include facial and character animations during the 'pre-processed' scenes. To clarify -- if you were to go back and replay the scenes later, you should not experience these Stutters a SECOND time.    These dips are purely graphical, so if you experience enough in one scene the Audio will eventually get out of sync due to all the momentary pauses. This will persist throughout the entire 30 FPS lock; and only snap back to normal when the game relinquishes control back to the player.    Note, that the more the play the LESS this will occur, but when you first turn on the game it will be impossible overlook and may give the user the impression the game is not performing optimally. ➤ 𝐂𝐎𝐌𝐁𝐀𝐓 𝐈𝐒 𝐅𝐔𝐍, 𝐁𝐔𝐓...▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔    While still Early Game; I'm currently restricted to very short skirmishes and tight spaces. I hope this does not persist for much longer. The game's combat system shines best in larger environments with enemies with large amounts of HP. If you're familiar with combat from Final Fantasy XIV -- you will see a lot familiar here. While there are no big orange telegraphs, the enemy animation tells are remarkably similar and easy to follow if you pay attention.    I enjoy fighting when I get the opportunity to. I am sure the game will open up, but I haven't gotten there yet. I remind I'm not too far in, but I already have an itch to be 'let off the leash' to go about and play the game at my leisure. For the time being I am trapped on a linear rail taking me from one combat arena to the next via a series of elaborate hallways. I will mostly keep track of how long it takes to actually REACH the point where I'm permitted the Freedom the NPCs in the story keep barking about.➤ 𝐏𝐑𝐀𝐂𝐓𝐈𝐂𝐀𝐋 𝐑𝐄𝐂𝐎𝐌𝐌𝐄𝐍𝐃𝐀𝐓𝐈𝐎𝐍𝐒▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔• Activate Toggle Walk/Run   (Keyboard Settings has no Hotkey for this)   - This game is very atmospheric and genuinely is quite comfortable to RP Walk around; even between combat. It paces things well and allows me to absorb all of the surrounding NPC chatter without it all turning into a noisy clutter.• Disable Player Follow (Movement)   (Found under Camera Settings)   - While doing said RP Walk, I got tired of the Camera constantly fighting me. Disable this feature so you can look around at your leisure.

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy 16 is an epic journey with a compelling main cast, gorgeous environments, tight action combat, engaging main story, and meticulously thought out lore. All of that is unfortunately undercut by low-effort padding* and glaring pacing issues**,  which first rear their head after the game's superb opening hours and only get progressively worse. I still loved the game, and I totally recommend it for the amazing highs, but it's a very uneven experience that would've benefitted from a more condensed approach and a better qualified dialogue editor (if the game even had one to begin with).   * Most (not all) of the diversions and side quests are mind-numbing filler too mundane for your character to be tasked with in the first place.  ** The dialogue tends to get pointlessly long-winded, killing all sense of urgency because characters keep standing and rambling without actually adding anything substantial minutes after it was time to get moving

_childDocuments_.review: Update: Changing the review to not recommended. When I enter the open world, the performance is just gone. During combat in the open world, I am down to 50 - 70 FPS with the below specs and settings turned on. Additionally, the stuttering is worse. Even the fix mod, there is not much change with the game other than uncapped cutscenes and widescreen support (We shouldnt need a mod for it anyways). This truly feels like another Playstation port shaft for PC gamers. I'm saying recommended simply because its a very good final fantasy entry. Music and Story are amazing. Combat is satisfying but very different (More than 13 and 15). HOWEVER, the game ran like ass on performance mode on PS5 and it looks like its a struggle on PC as well. _childDocuments_.review: After spending a hundred hours on games like Persona 4/5 and Like A Dragon: Infinite Wealth, I have have come to accept that Final Fantasy games aren't really JRPGs any longer.  This game is 152 GB of emo/whiney cutscenes, with strongly linear storytelling, and combat that can generally be won with button-mashing.  The accessories you get from the DLC are proof positive of my theory.  Accessories that make it so you auto-dodge are like putting easy mode on easier mode.  On a scale of 1-10 I'd give this a U.  A U for uninstall, because I'd rather go play FF12, FF6, FF4 with their Active Time Battles, rather than FF16s Actively Toomuch Boringness.  Heck, I'd rather go play "OUTSIDE"(wtf, I know right?)     I just don't get the whole Eikon summoning thing being a part of warfare.  2 or more people transforming into skyscraper sized creatures on a battlefield, where they literally walk on your own soldiers or burn them alive, all while your comrades are cheering 100 meters away from also being fried/stepped on. Also, these Eikon battles when handled by the player, are less enjoyable than Panzer Dragoon rail shooters on Sega Saturn (Team Andromeda name drop.)     I guess if SQE wants a game to do well, they'll just change a few elements, add some crystals to the story and call it a Final Fantasy game. SQE out here using crystals to justify anything like that one lady you work with, you know who I'm talking about.      One good takeaway from this mid game is that some of the voice acting is quite good. Cid and Clive's voice actors were the only thing keeping me in it for 8 hours.. That and the intro is just longer than the refund time.. coincidentaly.

_childDocuments_.review: Upscale Fantasy 10801440Love the game, the setting and Clive! I'm an FF player from its very inception on the NES. I played every mainline FF and my personal favourites are VI and IV. Now, XVI is undoubtedly very different than my favourites and all of the previous ones. But while many will argue that this isn't FF, it is in my humble opinion a true FF. The series has always been about reinventing itself and trying new things in its formula. But, the things that FF has always stuck to are its story-centric approach and its themes . And in that regard, FFXVI makes no exception. Heck, for all the purists out there, look no further than the first FF movie that many disliked for not being 'FF' enough. Now whether reinventing the wheel with every iteration is successful is another debate. With that said, why am I not recommending the game? One word: optimization. The game's performance is all over the place. I get into fights and walk/run in most areas at a decent framerate (mostly 60 fps and rarely under 45.) But in a few particular areas, the game tanks my rig for no apparent reason. Or worse, every time I open the local map, my FPS dips by 20 or more at any point in the game. And by many accounts, a top of the line gpu isn't immune to these... phenomena?So until the game is patched, spend your money elsewhere. EDIT: Please Square-Enix, fix the game. It's a damn shame it can't run well without upscaling (and even then), super resolution, and other tweaks done through Nvidia/AMD software. I'll be turning this review to positive once fixed, because I REALLY love this game. Best single-player FF since 12, that is in nearly 2 decades.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish Steam would give more options for reviewing, but oh well. I've clocked quite a bit of time in the game and I've definitely been having a lot of fun with it, but. but. BUT. It has a huge, glaring problem and it's the same problem that plagues almost 85% of JRPGs. And that's being GENEROUS because the actual number is probably way higher. That problem is its localization. Which .. is.. screamingly, obnoxiously bad. Most localization issues I'll deal with are typos, or rearranging words a LITTLE, but this masterful mess of garbage that is called 'localization' is embarrassingly bad. It's like they took an entirely different script and decided to use what they thought was better  than doing their damn job and translating/localizing the correct script. Unfortunately this means that the characters are portrayed completely differently, the English version makes the characters out to be more ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ than the Japanese script does, and I know this because I know JUST enough Japanese to pick out the errors.I'm also going to jump the gun and shut down the "if you don't like it play it in Japanese" arguments, which are probably the stupidest arguments dub purists can use. If I could play the game in Japanese, I WOULD BE. I wouldn't be forced to endure the unnecessary changes because certain people think they know better. The "you can't translate 1:1" argument is another stupid one, because  no one is asking for 1:1 translation they are asking for ACCURACY.  Why they make everyone talk in Old English I genuinely don't know. I would rant further on the absolute garbage job localizers do and I for one, welcome the arrival of AI translation/localization and the end of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ human localizers who can't do their job, but I'm not going to.  I will instead praise the game for its story, which keeps me engaged and ready for the next chapter, the graphics - which are absolutely gorgeous even if my poor potato of a computer does chug a bit during the more intense kaiju scenes, and oh boy the COMBAT, it's so much fun and flashy, exactly what I love out of a game. The villains are actual pieces of human garbage male or female, and none of them have pulled a 'feel sorry for me' asspull yet. That said, I highly HIGHLY encourage getting the game, if you play it in Japanese with subs, just brace yourself for the terrible job they did; if you play it in English with dubs (which I will never do because I hate English dubs), enjoy your ignorance and have fun with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Story and Gameplay: The story starts strong but develops slowly and feels a bit shallow. It reminded me of Devil May Cry and the Tales series. I later learned that a developer from DMC worked on this game, but it feels like a simpler version. If you enjoy this style, you might prefer DMC4 or DMC5 for more complex combos.Performance Issues: If you’re playing on PC, be cautious about system requirements. A decent gaming laptop may struggle; I’ve experienced significant frame rate drops during cutscenes, which makes it hard to enjoy the game. I hope for performance patches soon.Combat Experience: The combat feels too easy, with fights often dragging on. You have to save your skills for takedowns, but the gameplay could use more excitement while building up to those moments.Overall Recommendation: I wouldn't recommend this game unless your PC is top-tier, ideally costing over 1500 euros.

_childDocuments_.review: So - this game is long. Too long. Let me explain.Graphics - these are good. Mostly. Environs and especially lighting is great. In Eikon battles the light effects are way too much though. Faces and Hair is not good. Animations in dialogue are non existant.Music - mostly servicable, with a few exceptions.Gameplay - this is what really draged this game down for me.  The combat may be fun the first 15 hours or so, afterwards it starts to overstay its welcome. Getting new eikon abilities makes it fun again. For an hour or so. Then it's the same old.Quests - get boring fast. Mostly go to x, kill y or collect z. Not much variety.Progression - non existant. You get to choose equipped abilities, that's it. No character building to speak of.Itemization & crafting - might as well not exist. I am still wondering why i collected all those crafting materials and money I can barely do anything with.Story - is what carried the game for me. It's a bit too cheesy, but still very entertaining until the end.In sum it's a mediocre game that I cannot recommend because it is just too long for what it offers. Maybe if you like the slight anime influences or are a hard core Final Fantasy fan.

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy XVI, the latest installment in the beloved franchise, takes players on an unforgettable adventure through the enchanting world of Valisthea. From its gripping narrative to its immersive gameplay and stunning visuals, FFXVI delivers an experience that both captivates and impresses.The story of Final Fantasy XVI revolves around the tale of Clive Rosfield, a protagonist driven by a compelling dual purpose. As players embark on Clive's journey, they are immediately drawn into a realm fraught with political strife and ancient conflicts. The narrative unfolds with intricacy, weaving together elements of revenge, redemption, and the destiny of nations. With morally grey choices and complex character relationships, the storyline keeps players engaged and eager to uncover the secrets of Valisthea.Combat in FFXVI takes a departure from the turn-based mechanics of past entries, introducing a real-time system that is both dynamic and exhilarating. The seamless transitions between exploration and battles create a sense of immersion, allowing players to feel fully engrossed in the world. The ability to switch between characters with distinct play styles adds strategic depth and keeps combat encounters fresh and engaging.Visually, Final Fantasy XVI is a feast for the eyes. The graphics showcase a meticulous attention to detail, bringing the world of Valisthea to life with breathtaking environments, intricately designed cities, and character models that exhibit a level of realism rarely seen in the series. The darker and more mature art style complements the narrative tone, immersing players in a visually striking and atmospheric world.Behind the scenes, the development team, led by the talented Naoki Yoshida and Hiroshi Takai, has crafted an experience that honors the Final Fantasy legacy while pushing the boundaries of innovation. The result is a game that stays true to the series' roots while offering fresh and exciting elements that both longtime fans and newcomers will appreciate.Final Fantasy XVI is a triumphant addition to the acclaimed franchise. With its captivating story, thrilling combat system, and breathtaking visuals, it successfully transports players to a fantastical realm filled with adventure and intrigue. FFXVI proves that the Final Fantasy series continues to evolve and delight, promising an experience that will leave a lasting impression on players.
