_childDocuments_.review: A well-made action game with Final Fantasy-esque storytelling and references, it will please some open-minded FF fans and action gamers new to the franchise but may turn off those not into the action genre. Context – I’ve played most of the recent mainline FF games including 7, Tactics, 7 Remake, 8, 10, 10-2, 12, 13, 13-2, 13-3, and 15. Completed 16 twice; the second time on Final Fantasy mode (hard mode). Played for 88 hours, obtained all skills, Clive’s ultimate weapon, and completed all side-quests and hunts. Did not play the DLC. PC specs: Ryzen 7800x3d CPU and RTX 4070 GPU. Monitor: 1440p and 165hz. Detailed Review –[Performance on PC]I do not have a PS5, but as a long-time FF player, I got the demo and then the full game on day one of its PC release. The developers released a patch at the demo phase to smoothen performance for day one. They released another patch sometime later. As a result, the game runs beautifully, at over 120 fps with my rig (described above) on virtually everything set to the maximum with DLSS and Frame Generation on.The game benefits from PC builds, able to stretch its legs and sprint rather than hobble on the base PS5 with lowered resolution and sub-60 fps. Load times are virtually non-existent. There is, however, some traversal stutter. The developers have minimized its impact with patches. While some stutter remains in the form of jankiness when sprinting/riding chocobos, it should not be a game-breaking experience unless you’re used to silky-smooth traversal.  [Graphics] The developers have used their own internally developed engine for FF16, and it rivals some of the greats such as Decima, Frostbite, UE4&5, Fox, Dunia, etc. The visuals, down to clothing fabrics, facial hair, etc., are meticulously detailed; and the larger effects e.g., Eikon battles and action sequences are similarly stunning to behold. The one thing that let down the visual presentation of the game for me was its medieval-type setting and serious tone. To achieve the darker tone of the narrative, many set pieces featured dull or broken apart buildings juxtaposed against a dreary landscape. While beautifully rendered, they became monotonous, and the neutral color tones did not help. E.g., compared to the saturated and pastel-colored visuals of Granblue Fantasy: Relink, FF16 is far more grayscale and monotonous.[Narrative] As with any Final Fantasy game worth its salt, FF16 comes with the full narrative package: cinematic cutscenes, and spoken dialogue (i.e., no speech bubbles), just like watching a film. This format allows for the grand telling of an intricate story about conflict between nations, dominants, bearers, eikons, and antagonistic beings bent on destroying humanity for their own gain.While the overarching narrative is grand, the story itself centers on one person, or a group of people who are pushing against the current to create a better life for all, and in particular those subjugated for selfish gain. It starts tragically and ends rather tragically as well, even if the protagonists manage to achieve their goals. This is not a lighthearted tale. One thing that took some getting used to was the length of the cutscenes. Being a fully fleshed-out FF experience, narrative sequences can be very long with no indication when they would end or whether they will be followed with another lengthy narrative sequence. In the past, some of these sequences would be told in speech bubble format, which players could view at their preferred pace. It would have been good, perhaps, if the developers had included certain QOL features such as showing cutscene summaries if they are skipped, or indicating how long a scene might be with a progress bar (like on Netflix or YouTube). Perhaps the cutscenes could also have been faster-paced and better animated (e.g., Horizon Forbidden West’s cutscenes). They seemed rather draggy at times, especially for scenes that were not animated in a cinematic way, i.e., characters standing still and talking to each other with minimal body movement or facial expression.               Two good QOL measures they include are the ability to pause cutscenes and read contextual information related to the cutscene on the fly and the option to view the history of the conflict from a bird’s eye view, helping the player understand what has happened between the two large time-skips in the game. Overall, the story is ambitious and moderately well-told with thoughtful QOL features that indicate the developer’s keen interest for players to appreciate it. [Music] As with FF games, the music was very good throughout, setting appropriate moods that befit the grand narrative and gameplay elements. Signature FF pieces were played at pivotal moments, adding joy to long time fans. It starts strong, so just playing the free demo on Steam will give you a flavor of the music. [Gameplay] Unlike other FF titles, this is an action game with very few RPG elements. Think Devil May Cry (DMC) with companions you mostly can’t control. Because the action director is the same as DMC, it plays like DMC. The only person you can control, Clive, plays like a combination of Dante and Nero. If you do not like action games, you probably don’t want to play a 40-hour action game. FF16 is not like the party-based RPGs of FF history. It requires paying attention to enemy attack patterns in real-time and having the reflexes to dodge, parry, teleport, time your abilities, and combo your way to victory.The variety of eikonic abilities that the game slowly bestows the main character allows you to play the way you want, e.g., as more of a ranged magic user that handles enemies from afar and closes in only when the enemy is staggered, or someone who focuses on unleashing close-range attacks to deal damage and stagger.You cannot control any other character, and, apart from your dog, you cannot issue commands to them either. Your companions will fight as their AI has programmed them to, typically distracting smaller opponents while you engage the biggest one/s.Enemies, particularly on the harder difficulty settings, are quite spongy, needing many hits to stagger and kill. This can be off-putting if you are used to dispatching enemies quickly. The game went for a quality over quantity fighting experience, trading the joy of dispatching many enemies in succession with hacks and slashes (e.g., Dynasty Warriors) for the rewarding activity of precise technical execution to overcome a small number of enemies who are hard to kill.     At the easier / standard difficulty level, players may find the game too simplistic: slash and shoot magic, use abilities, wait for ability cooldown while slashing and shooting magic, use abilities, repeat (while dodging). The game mechanics, however, reward complex actions (like comboing normal attacks with abilities and timing counterattacks) that may only be apparent at the harder difficulty levels, like Final Fantasy mode where DPS checks and other mechanisms require the use of such complex actions. It is a game, therefore, that is easy to get into as a casual gamer but has hidden mechanics at higher difficulty levels that reward strategic gameplay and precise reflexes, which is attractive to gamers who enjoy challenging action games, e.g., DMC. Watch some YouTube videos of good players executing cool combos at the hardest difficulty level. Eikonic battles are the showstoppers. They get more intense and visually impressive as the game goes on. While not challenging to play, they are a fun ride. The only drawback is that they can take a long time. Steam calls them “spectacle fights”, so sit back and enjoy the spectacle.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello everyone! o/ Hope your day goes well!Final Fantasy 16 has been a PS5 exclusive for quite a while and recently has gotten a PC port due to Square Enix's efforts of going multiplatform.It is important to mention that I have already played the game on the PS5 but got it again on PC for the better experienceWithout further ado, Let's take a look at the PC version of FF16 and the game by itselfIt's not a secret that each Final Fantasy game is very different by its own. that also comes at the genre that it represents and FF16 is a perfect example of this. the FF community often does look at XVI as a FF game but with Devil May Cry gameplay and feel attached to it and I think it's a very accurate point of view. However, that doesn't mean that the game is flawed and instead I will be looking at the game with its own merits insteadThe story of the game is all focused around Clive Rosefield from start to finish with the game also giving us all of the details about during the main story right away. Making it easy to form a connection and relation while also introducing more characters and background stories which all seem to be connected very to the main point without taking our focus away or messing around with it. in terms of emotions and stakes, We are talking a roller coaster with that as the game constantly plays around that aspect which keeps the player constantly engaged and curious. every moment of the story is well designed and only made me more hooked to the realm of Valisthea. I strongly recommend getting the DLCs too as they do add more context towards the ending of the story while introducing more on their ownSo gameplay.. As I mentioned, This is a Devil May Cry but with FF theme on it which isn't a bad thing and I personally approve of but old timers might be disappointed with the lack of RPG elements as XVI did reduce that aspect to the very bare minimum compared to previous entiries.Combat is great and if I had to use a word to describe it then that will be "satisfying". Visually and feeling wise its great but the game shares a similar problem to FFXIV that the game by at its normal difficulty is very easy that the game is few steps away from including an autoplay feature. to truly experience and enjoy the combat then you have to go through New Game+ for that or otherwise it will feel as a visual novel/interactive movie to say the least due to the insane amount of cutscenes that the game has. It's very clear that CBU3 did use XIV as their baseline for the quest design and how the game represents itselfGraphics and port? It was a PS5 exclusive at first so it did aim at high standards within that aspect and the game does look amazing across all fronts and if anything. It's say that XVI has mastered the act of presentation wellHowever that also brings us to performance which weren't great on the PS5 already with constant slowdowns and FPS going down to as low as 15 or less and the problem keeps on going with PC as well. the performance of the game are rather incredibly inconsistent for no real reason. frame rate goes down for no real reason while in some scenes its more than perfect with all of the visual effects.Sometimes the game does have small micro shutters out of nowhere which can go through the entire game until you restart the computer (and no, even when VRAM, RAM or CPU aren't maxed out). Not to mention the lack of Ultrawide support or the game limiting the FPS to 30 in cutscenes. If you decide to play the game, I suggest looking at FFXVIFix which is a mod that does correct some of the shortcomings of the portWhat are my overall thoughts on FF16 and should you buy it? FF16 has been an amazing experience to me during the play-through of both platforms and genuinely I enjoyed the game and maxed all of the value I could get out of it. It's a great game by its own right and I would suggest people to at least try out the demo to see if it's for their liking. However, the port is plain and simple. Bad... and I do hope that the game will get more patches to improve the experienceAs far as my rating goes? FF16 by itself is a 8/10 game and I would recommend it. Just be aware that the port does have issues and a lot of them.

_childDocuments_.review: Setting aside the myriad of performance issues (thanks Denuvo), this is boring, uninspired and every element of this game has been done better in other games. The idea that society and culture depend on the mountains called Mothercrystals, but they themselves are the problem, is just cliche and done to death in JPRGs. The locations and dungeons are small, simple and lacking in any form of meaningful exploration. The combat is probably the best part of this game, but honestly, I am not very good at it to judge. The story and characters are bland, uninspired, checklist-driven more than anything. Any kind of human-like ambiguity, gets resolved easily because plot tends to happen to it. The story simply doesn't let the characters out of their leashes. The characters don't have room to breathe, to be other than their past and their duties and whatever the ♥♥♥♥ they are. The quests are also repetitive, and a chore to complete. Go there fight these monsters, go there search for this item. Even bloody main quests are fairly similar.Meanwhile, the story is said to tackle themes of slavery (I THINK SLAVERY BAD), racism(DIFFERENT NOT BAD), etc. Honestly, the themes are really surface level lacking in any meaningful depth. This game is deep, if puddle is deep. If you want a quality RPG with great world building, story, characters and quests, I suggest play The Witcher 3, this one just isn't worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic.For life long fan, this game felt like the series finally grew up along with its fans. It manages to hold true to the series, but purges the more childish anime tropes that kept into the series. Its very much along the lines of Game of Thrones, and the Witcher, but with a Final Fantasy flair. The game runs pretty well, provided its on a more modern system. At the high end, the game is an absolute spectacle at 4k with a high frame rate. The size and scale of the Eikon battles are on another level.  The music seems more about enhancing the on screen action, a bit of a change compared to the more character-focused themes in past games. The series has always been about mixing things up, and this is a full on action game. Stats and equipment won't matter much as player ability. The only real downside I experienced was a design choice that makes the game less visually appealing for far too long. The side quests get brought up often, but for the most part its fairly controlled up until late point when a large number are opened at once.The two DLCs are pretty good. The first is real short, and basically amounts to a couple boss battle ending in one of the hypest ones in the game. The other is much more meaty, but did contain a really annoying boss mechanic. Still quite good. Overall, the wait was worth it. FF16 is one of the best in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: By Square Enix standards, this is a pretty good port. There are lots of graphical settings and it takes advantage of all the upscaling tech from the various GPU manufacturers. If you've got substantial hardware, then you'll definitely see a noticeable improvement over the PS5 version. It is missing Ultrawide and uncapped FPS cutscenes, however. Though the folks over at Nexus Mods have already remedied that so download that fix before you even get started if those things are important to you. As for the game itself, I'll give a brief review. Although at time of writing you may see a small amount of hours, I have completed this game on PS5 and even went so far as to obtain Platinum (not overly difficult admittedly). The game is fantastic. It has all the rich story telling elements and character depth you'd expect from a Final Fantasy game. The villain is quite mysterious and keeps you wanting to play more to find out more about them. The Active Time Lore mechanic of the game allows you to pause at any time, during cutscenes or general gameplay, and learn more about the world, characters, key phrases you might have heard, and more. Lore junkies will love it. Admittedly, the final fantasy franchise has not always done well in explaining its story and some games, like XIII, horribly hide the most interesting parts of the story behind datalogs. Active Time Lore eliminates the barrier to entry of digging through menus to find out more about the world and dishes it out clean and concisely.The combat is unlike anything fans of the franchise have seen before. If you've played Devil May Cry, you'll feel right at home with the combat of this game. What Final Fantasy has always done well is taking an established gameplay style and perfecting it. It's fluid, dynamic, though at times formulaic. Do yourself a favor and challenge yourself. Hard mode makes this game quite interesting, but even on the 1st playthrough, experiment with different abilities and combos. In a game like this, it can be easy to fall into a singular way of playing for the entire playthrough. Eikon battles are huge cinematic setpieces that are sure to leave you haw dropped. Each one is unique. While not particularly challenging, that's okay because clearly they are trying more to put on a show and game over screens would get in the way of that.The music is just what you'd expect from Final Fantasy, it even won a Game of the Year award for it, so wear headphones or crank those speakers up!Graphically the game is a masterpiece. Most cutscenes in this game are rendered in game, and you'll have a fairly hard time distinguishing them unless you're a keen observer. It's quite impressive what they've done with this engine.Overall, this is a fantastic game and well worth your $50. The DLC are great as well , particularly Rising Tides. The Echoes of the Fallen DLC is mainly an excuse for a badass boss battle, but otherwise not entirely compelling on its own. You save $10 by buying the bundle so might as well go for it. Though if it is too steep for your budget, the base game is satisfying enough on its own. Perhaps next spring during Square Enix's sale (I think it usually happens in March), you can snatch the DLC for a discount.PS: This game does support Direct Storage. So if you have a PCIE Gen 4 NVME SSD, be sure to install this game on there for ultra fast loading.

_childDocuments_.review: A good game that misses greatness due to its pacing issues and far too many fetch-or-kill side quests. If you like action-focused games with emotional storytelling and huge spectacle, I would recommend FF16.FF16 continues the series new direction of fast-paced action combat, improving on what was accomplished before by expanding the available abilities and playstyles available to you as you progress through the story. This however comes at the compromise of incredibly limited roleplay elements, removing things like status effects and turning treasure chests from exciting discoveries into boxes filled almost entirely with useless crafting materials. Clive is the only character you can customize outside of cosmetics, with equipment remaining as nothing more than number sticks with no interesting effects to change up gameplay, the only variety coming from the accessories, very few of which do more than increase the damage or reduce the cooldowns of abilities.One of the better additions, however, are the Eikon fights. Giant spectacles against kaiju-esque creatures, all classic summons from prior entries. These I would consider the highlights of the game, with your fights against  and  being the greatest examples of this.The story is solid, dragging along during the 3/4 mark with unnecessary padding, and adding a dozen more side quests right before the finale before picking back up with an emotional final fight. While worth experiencing, the side content drags out the story about 20 hours longer than it needs to be, the optional storylines feeling mandatory to fully appreciate the world and people within it while keeping a fairly poor and uninteresting presentation and quest structure throughout. Due to this, playing through a second time, especially on a fresh save, becomes a hard sell, as has been the case with many prior Final Fantasy games.

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy XVI finished!The Combat system are the best in the series for me. It remind me of DMC style ARPG combat. Story-wises it's magnificent.Boss Fight (especially when u choose action focused) is the best thing this game has to offers combined with masterpieces BGM and story wrapped around it, it's a chef kiss.The DLC--especially Echoes of the Fallen-- should be initially on the game due to how short and less additional lore added. After completing the game, Echoes of the Fallen and part of Rising Tide, Ive decided to give this game a negative review.  Visually, the game is stunning, looks great, plays great, there arent any bugs or anything that I can remember, but the meat of the game is just garbage.  After watching my friend play 15 for a bit after playing, I realized how bad it really is in comparison.  For example, in 15 (as well as pretty much every other FF game) your party members matter, and hold a pretty significant weight when it comes to battles, in 16 you do not care who is in your party, they hardly do anything, and it would be just fine if they werent even there.  The battle system, once you get a few abilities, become very redundant, and you will do pretty much the exact same thing over and over regardless of who you are fighting which brings me to another point, elemental damage, which is pretty much non existent.  OH you are fighting a bomb and hit it with fire damage?  Yea thats fine, no one cares.  The main story itself is completely forgettable,  Cecil and Kain's story in FF2 or Terra and all the other people in FF3 had much more compelling stories and that ♥♥♥♥ was on snes....I mean cmon.  The sidequests are absolute garbage, and only a handful are worth doing as they give you something that you need or permanent upgrades, I actually ended up about 3/4s through the game just skipping all dialogue on anything other than the main quest because...who tf gave a ♥♥♥♥?  This is just touching on the core part of the game, not even mentioning the small things that really made no sense, like the badges you get from people so that the townsfolk would talk to you? The "crafting" in the game, which...isnt really.  In 15 at least you could cook or upgrade a plethora of weapons, change your car color or something, in 16, you beat a boss, 100 bloody hides, COOL DUDE, not like I already have a billion of these things.  Speaking of which, a boss would drop a rare crafting item so that you could get the next weapon...when they could have just dropped it, or had it in a chest or something, the crafting is really like the bare bones of a crafting system and should be scrapped.  There is literally no system or mechanic in this game that is done better than any previous FF, its like they got the pro visual team to make it look as great as possible, but then got all the interns to finish the rest of the game.  Seriously, I don't know who thought this game was a good idea the way its made, but it is really really ♥♥♥♥, and they should be fired.  Additionally, if people LIKE this FF and say this is how they want games to be, I really wish they would go play some other game and give good reviews there, so that the devs dont think they did a good job, this isnt the way i want this franchise to go.

_childDocuments_.review: Instead of reusing popular formulas,  FFXVI builds their hack & slash based on their popular RPG assets (iconic bosses, summons, magic, and skills). Don't have to wait for an obvious 'turn' after my opponent spam combos after combos. Opening comes fairly often, and worth a player to maximize their combo to fight back.  3. The protagonist won't get stagger/flinch like a soccer player. 4. Move sets are clean, flexible, and interact well with enemies. _childDocuments_.review: I almost passed on this one, thinking "last I loved a FF game was FFX" and most reviews I saw were luke warm for this entry. I'm glad I gave the demo a shot; it made me buy the game about half way in and FFXVI is now sky rocketing into being a contender for the spot of my favourite FF (still too early to say though). The old FF RPG style is long gone, this is an action game with RPG elements, but it still drips of that final fantasy vibe.The atmosphere have a more mature tone where heavy topics, such as slavery, are ingrained in the world. The dialogue and the decisions being made are leaning more to the realistic fantasy side - they are nuanced and often relatable.The combat is silky smooth and really nails those dopamine hits with timed combos, dodges and parries - it reminds me of Devil May Cry. You have ways around it if you don't enjoy the action parts so much: you can choose story mode and equip rings that automate your selected pain point (not recommended imo).The set pieces, world building and boss fights... ermagerd, it's a unique and spectacular experience - my jaw have dropped many times. Try the demo and you'll know what I mean within 15 minutes, and if you keep playing and watch the culmination... just chef's kiss.

_childDocuments_.review: First things first:   Despite the games massive filesizes, I regularly see subpar texture work and there is no Raytracing. At highest settings the game is pretty but nothing revolutionary. As such, there is NO REASON for it to be this taxing. I'm seeing a 7800X3D and a 4080 being brought to their knees (with fast ram to spare and running from an NVME drive) to sometimes sub 60 fps at 1440p ultra. On a game with NO RAYTRACING. What the heck, Square. Second: The game has three pillars for my money. Story, combat and spectacle. And so far only the third is holding its weightThe plot so far is engaging enough (it's no FF 6 or 9) but in keeping with the tradition of 15, it's hampered to hell and forth by dismal pacing. At least they didnt chop bits off of it and put them in media outside the game this time. However the story wastes its opening on a battle we will see in better context later, then jumps to what should have been the intro, diverts from it to introduce antagonists and their politics, then jumps back in time, then forth again, then into a super implausible double childhood reunion Dickensian coincidence...Look, I get it. You have to deliver a lot of exposition to set the stage but frankly you fumbled harded than Skyrim. The game makes you think the tutorial is finally over after the Title Drop but HOURS after that you are Sidenote: I really like the Acitve Time Lore and how much effort when into editing it for almost every line during a cutscene. The in game wikia is also cool since it uses several to the point articles and invites you to pile on Tabs from the "See More" section, much like a real life Wiki dive you get lost in.Next problems, however:The combat. It seems to be based on Forspoken's system of collecting sets of powers to spam in real time as you swap sets you acquire from big bosses.However it inherits Forspoken's problem of making the combat feel super dull until you get the first boss' power set, and introduces new ones.Unlike Forspoken, your character isnt nimble at all. You are slow as ♥♥♥♥. You have a magic dash but IT GIVES NO IFRAMES AND CANT BE USED FOR DODGING.  You dodge with a crappy slow sidestep. You cant even roll. Parrying is a joke. It has no dedicated button, you have to line you animation with an enemies and hope the planets magically aligned to give you one. You cant block either. Since the game assumes powers spamming will be constant almost every enemy is either a push over or has too much health. The combat does get more fun when you become powerful enough to overcome the spongy nature of enemies. But you will mostly be mashing and stunlocking with the occational dodge or jump-to-dodge. There's barely any build variety and your full set of actions is so limited its all about waiting for the powers to charge to spam.Im playing in Action Mode by the way. I wanted to give the combat a chance on its terms. Its mediocreNuiscances pile up with UX and the overworld, thousand papercuts style:YOU ARE SO. EFFIN. SLOW. There is no run button. You hold a direction and after an eternity you start dashing. Your default moving speed is dismal and running doesnt help that much. You cant double jump or climb or crouch. It's one of those games where any enviromental movement interaction is predetermined and everything else is an invisible wall.Did I mention there is no Parry button? i'm still mad at that oneThe game constantly stops to show a fullscreen Title Card for every quest that starts. Just put it on the side ffs. Some cutscenes are locked to 30 fps and its really jarring when it constantly jumps framerates back and forth since only some parts of a whole sequence are considered "Detailed Cutscenes" and locked to 30.You cant give orders to any party member except the dog, nor change their looks or gear.The sidequests are filler garbage.The spectacle sequences of the fights are smeared by fullscreen distortion effects when I need to mash. Just put the prompt by itself instead of flashing crap all over and let me see the animations you worked so hard on clearlyI probbaly will keep at it now that I'm past the worse, but

_childDocuments_.review: Update: after 2 patches frame rate issues still persist.I'd love to give this game a medium voting but considering the high praise this game receives and does not deserve, I feel obliged to give a negative rather than a positive rating.The good:- likeable protagonist- overarching story feels promising- gameplay and fighting is funThe bad:- the much critizised performance issues. I tried all the mods and am running everything at the lowest settings (my rig: GTX 3070, Intel i9 9900KF 3.6GHz, 32gb Memory). I have huge frame drops especially in combat and cut scenes. Running any other modern game on high settings was never an issue.- nearly all dialogues feel shallow. There is no depth or bigger meaning to what is being said and it just comes across as superficial. Characters seem to have a past but you never learn more details, they just act as if something happened between them but you learn no concrete details. - Characters make stupid decisions like staying behind to cover a retreat when they are incognito at the moment and could simply leave without being noticed altogether. - The people who are dominants (meaning they are able to transform into one of the godlike creatures) are everywhere. They don't feel like a rarity but basically every character with more screen time than 30 minutes seems to be a dominant. It feels unnatural.- I wonder why people go to war at all. Every faction seems to have 1 to 2 dominants. Why bother sending your foot soldiers who die in masses as soon as the other dominant arrives when you could just fight it out with the dominants solely?- Every dominant seems to have healing powers of a certain degree as soon as they turn into these gods. It negatively impacts the tension when the big god fights happen.- All the leaders appear to be simply evil or fans of war with no deeper reason. Just for the fun of it. I often feel like there is no depth to most of the characters. Jill as another example seems to have been with our protagonist for a very long time and they seem to have a connection but I do not know anything about her. She is just always there. Reading two lines of background story in the wiki gave me more understanding of her than playing the game for over 20 hours. - Side quests and "filler" main quests (that kind of get in the way on your path to actual bigger and interesting goals) are with little depth. It is not comparable with the unique mission design of a "Witcher 3" where twists and surprises motivated you intrinsically to move forward and learn more. It is always as expected: Go from point a to b, maybe kill something and return. It feels like finishing a to do list.Conclusion:It is a solid game and does deserve a rating of 7/10 depending on your expectations. But It definitely does not deserve the high praise it receives.I like the game and will play it to the end. _childDocuments_.review: The story, cinematics, characters, and music are amazing. This is definitely a more maturely-themed game that explores the political and ethical strife in a dying land at war with itself. My experience with the FF IP is mainly with FF14, so I can't really speak on behalf of other FF media - but I would say this game takes a different direction than most others. The game  is clearly rooted in Final Fantasy with the familiar creatures, crystals, magicks, and monsters - but finds a way to set itself apart by exploring darker themes and twisting the FF formula in some areas, mainly Eikons and Mothercrystals. There is no Warrior of Light in this story.The gameplay is fun and gives you a lot of abilties to work with to keep combat fresh. I found myself trying to maximize Stagger Damage on enemies and bosses, which led to experimentation with ability upgrades and what-not. There are quite a few Quick Time Events in major story battles, but otherwise I can't really complain, it's a lot of fun to play.The main story take its time to set the chess board. It does a really good job grounding the developing warring landscape across the continent with the various battles and factions. The characters are well-written, have great VAs, animations, cinematography, all of it. It's the whole package. It's filled with intrigue, mystery, and balances well with the everyday struggle of mankind dependent on magicked crystals and slaves.I spent just shy of 70 hours with the game after playing the DLCs, the final encounter, and *nearly all* of the sidequests. My biggest gripe with the game is the quantity and quality of the side quests and other side content. Yes, it's optional - they're even clearly marked with (!) for standard side quests, (+) for side quests with buffs/unlocks, and (chest) for collectibles. If I ever go back to play this game again I will 100% be skipping all side quest content except for the (+) quests. Most of them are talk, run, fetch, kill quests that are only there to waste your time (Surprise! an MMORPG developer made this game). The problem is they gatekeep the ability point currency, so when you're towards the end of the game and need 6,000 AP to master a skill - you're really going to wish you did those extra quests. My suggestion: get a mod that allows you to unlock the abilities you want to use.The side questing dialogue and animations are also a far cry from the quality of the main quests and cutscenes. Expressions are blank, lip syncing is laughable, and they cycle through the same 5 animations for all of them. It's very clear where the developers spent their time and it was not in the side quest content. All quest dialogue has full VA which is a plus, even if the dialogue can be somewhat generic at times.There is a Hunt Board where marks are added throughout the game, which give you crafting materials for better weapons. They're essentially mini boss fights ranging in difficulty class. I played on the Normal difficulty and only ever had one fight that was truly challenging (the dragon...). One mild annoyance I had was the Hunt marks give you information on where you can find them, but you can't mark you map and you can't view the marks from the setting screen, so if you go out looking for marks and forget where it was, you have to travel back to the Hideaway and read the Hunt Board again. I found myself taking pictures of the marks on my phone so I could reference those later.All the side content in the game seems to dump on you in the middle of or before a story/battle mission, which also kills the pacing and momentum in the main story. Both of the DLCs do this too. Right before the final battle sequence both DLCs become available, which again kills the buildup to the final mission.Echoes of the Fallen is a shorter DLC that unlocks a dungeon. Between 1.5-3 hrs. It's paced well with mini-boss fights sprinkled throughout, and is capped with my favorite fight in the whole game. Could not recommend this one more. Jam packed with fights, story, and *music*.Rising Tide is more meh. A new area is unlocked that follows the same formula of the main game. Unlock a new area, get side quests dumped on you, go back to main story, rinse and repeat. New characters are forgettable. This one was slightly longer at about 5-6 hours for me. You get new abilities you can use for the final mission in the main game if you want, but I did not find these abilities compelling to use. After completing Rising Tide, where you are expect to go straight for the final battle in the game, 4 more side quests are dumped on you. This was my breaking point and are the only side quest missions I did not complete in the game.Overall as a package, the game is a 7/10 for me. If I skipped the throwaway (!) side quests it's an 8.5/10.Did I mention side quests?

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a 10/10 for me. But it is definitely a pure subjective opinion. I acknowledge that this game is not perfect, it has many flaws that would understandably turn people off from the game. However, the best advice I could give is that if you know what you're expecting for when playing this game, you will have one of the best experiences in gaming. I came to play FF16 initially because I was not only a final fantasy fan, I also love the devil may cry series. Not only that, I'm a big sucker for crazy spectacle boss fights which I fully knew I was gonna get coming into FF16, and I can say that it far exceeded my already high expectations. ------COMBAT------ 10/10For a combative review, yes it is a more streamlined devil may cry. It is definitely easier, and doesn't pose much of a challenge. I understand that the combat system is not as in-depth and fundamentally heavy as devil may cry, but it doesn't have to be. However, even with the streamlining of the heavily influenced DMC style combat, it is nonetheless still a great combat system that not many games have. You can play this game mindlessly and just button mash, but the game actually gives you the chance to play it like a DMC game if you want to. It does limit your options to only 3 slots to switch eikons from (Basically ability types), causing a seemingly big limitation to player creativity in tackling the combat of the game. But it must be said that if we were given more options, the game would DEFINITELY be too easy. That being said, for fellow combat enthusiasts like me, there is a specific game mode dedicated to test your player skill. It is actually a proper challenge for most people and is worth investing into if you love combat like this. (Also, yes there is ng+ with an option for a harder difficulty.)------STORY------ 10/10I didn't really know what I was diving into at first going into the story. But I am glad to say that they have done an astounding job. The story is indeed very long, but for me the story didn't feel like a chore. It was well written and well paced, if you ignore the tedious "RPG" elements of the game. The characters are well written (at least the important ones, side characters are kinda ass), the story was done beautifully, and the voice acting is some of the best. Clive's voice acting is probably some of the best voice acting ever done. Not only does his dialogue feel realistic relative to the world, his battle grunts and cries are just chefs kiss. It is not mentioned often but the voices he makes when fighting, you can feel the sheer force and power in it, which really helps give you that immersive feeling of just how much of a badass he is and how strong it feels. Without mentioning any spoilers, I can confidently say that most people would probably love the story, given how the story itself is not too complicated, but not too simple in a way that its boring and generic. Everything done in the story up from the beginning to the end to me was done amazingly.-----The RPG Elements---- 0/10Yes, as much as I praise this game, i do hate the RPG elements. It has a lot of useless mechanics in the game and it feels like a chore often times. The fetch quests and the constant back and forth walking of just talking to an NPC is... well, tedious. And i know it sucks. I hate it too. But because of how strongly i love the combat and the story, this was a sin i was 100% okay with looking over, because at the end of the day, i dont think every game has to be perfect to be enjoyed. But if you are someone who doesn't have the patience to go through this tedious chores from the RPG elements of FF16, I must say that i cant really recommend this for you. ----Performance----I have a GTX 3060 and for me, it ran perfectly fine on medium to high settings on a 1080p monitor. I say the game is well optimized for what its worth and I ran into no troubles. -----World-building/Exploration----- 5/10The world is not all connected. It is separated into different sections you can fast-travel to, with no option to walk there directly. The world is big, yes. But i do see the flaw in that it feels very disconnected and could potentially ruin immersion. However, for me personally I was never much of the exploring type anyway. I just wanted to enjoy a good story and I love me some of that DMC style combat. So this was never much of an issue for me. But, the design of the world itself is spectacular. The world design for each region you can travel to is designed very well and beautifully. Each environment feels very unique to the world and the graphics and artstyle are spectacular, truly an eye candy. But if you are a fan of exploring wide open world maps, this could potentially a bummer for you. -------Soundtrack-------- 11/10Every boss soundtrack fits the fight so very very well and is insanely hype. The music was done spectacularly to match every scene and moment in the game. The fights were epic, the villages and towns had their distinct soundtracks that gave you a sense of peace and clarity as you would expect from a peaceful village, tense or tragic moments had soundtracks that helped elevate the scene, you name it. There are many split opinions on this game, but this game's soundtrack is undeniably spectacular. For me personally, FF16 has some of the best soundtracks in a video game, ever. -----OVERALL----- subjectively;10/10 // Objectively; probably 6-8/10This game has its flaws. The RPG aspects of it are done poorly, the sidequests suck and they feel like a chore. But if you are a fan of fast paced combat, good and long stories, *insane* boss fights, then this game is definitely for you. That being said, I personally hope that their next entry would adapt the same kind of combat system while improving upon the mentioned flaws FF16 has. I understand that this combat is not for everyone, but that is why FF16's combat was streamlined in order to be accessible to those unfamiliar with this type of combat. For me personally, it would be a miracle if FF17 would follow FF16's footsteps, but better.

_childDocuments_.review: Gonna write an early review and will update this later, to give my impressions so far:TL;DRCombat 8 | Gameplay 7 | RPG Elements 4 | Story 7 | English Voice Acting 6 | Visuals 9 | Music 10I would rate this game a solid 7.5/10, which isn't bad at all, it just isn't a masterpiece in my opinion.Don't go into this expecting an RPG with deep character progression, view this more like Final Fantasy goes God Of War and then you'll definitely enjoy it.Long version:Combat is fun, it's definitely a lot more slow and tactical than pure hack&slash (like if you just brainlessly spam attacks you're inevitably gonna lose and die), it's very different from either FFVII Remake and FFXV. But I personally like it this way, it's a lot less messy and less all over the place, a lot more controlled and clean and it does make it more satisfying to eventually win the big fights. Overall I would say the combat is on the easier side, but some specific battles are definitely big difficulty spikes, so that keeps the flow interesting.The actual combat mechanics and system (Eikon system) seems messy at first and takes some getting used to, especially weaving combos while swapping Eikons in the middle of it can feel a little clunky, but after you get a flow going with it and get used to it, it starts feeling a lot more fluid and satisfying. The upgrading system ('RPG' system I guess is what people call it) is unfortunately very simple and straight-lined. So if you're looking for deep character progression and choices, this isn't the game for you, this is definitely more for the people that like solid action games as opposed to people that like deep RPGs with 1000 character choices. Equipment system is almost non-existent.Story so far is good, generally the English voice acting is fine, especially between main characters during main events.But I will say that the banter between side characters during less important events sometimes really make me raise my eyebrows with how cheap and terrible the voice acting is. So quite a bit of inconsistency there for sure.Main characters are very likeable, I love Cid and Tolga, Clive is okay.Side quests so far are forgettable, but at least they're very short and quick.Graphics and musical score are exactly what you would expect from Squeenix and Final Fantasy: absolutely top notch.

_childDocuments_.review: has fun combat and a mature story, but as an RPG, the exploration is limited, the gear system is weak, and the simple map design may disappoint fans.+ The combat is exciting, with battles that feel like you're watching an anime, especially the Eikon fights, which are stunning.+ The story is mature, dealing with serious themes like murder, betrayal, and safe nudity, making the narrative very engaging.+ Playing as Clive gives you flexibility with his abilities, keeping the gameplay fun for longer.+ The game offers helpful features for less experienced players, like automatic dodging and easy combos.+ The soundtrack is impressive and adds an epic feeling to the game.+ The cutscenes are beautifully animated and directed.+ Hunting tough monsters is a fun challenge that rewards you with materials.+ Having Clive's loyal dog as a companion is a great addition to both gameplay and the story.- The game has limited exploration, with maps that feel more like straightforward paths from point A to B.- On PC, the game can be tough on hardware, with some areas (like those involving Leviathan) causing performance issues.- As an RPG, the equipment system is weak, with few chances to upgrade gear, and crafting doesn’t feel rewarding.- While some side quests are good, many are repetitive and involve too much running back and forth between NPCs.- In Final Fantasy mode, enemies don’t get smarter, they just take longer to defeat, making battles feel drawn out.- You can’t equip or manage any other characters besides Clive, taking away from the team management aspect of the game.- The jump button is mostly useless, as dodging is a much more effective option.- The crafting system feels underdeveloped, with only a few moments where equipment upgrades actually matter.- Important story details are hidden in the glossary, and reading through it interrupts the flow of the game.- Combos start to feel repetitive after a while, reducing the excitement of combat.- The game doesn’t have interesting minigames.*Rating from lowest to highest: C, B, A, S.

_childDocuments_.review: **Final Fantasy XVI (Steam) Review: A Bold and Epic Evolution***Final Fantasy XVI* marks a bold new chapter in the legendary series, and on Steam, it absolutely shines. This entry takes the franchise into darker, more mature territory while maintaining the iconic elements that fans have come to love: grand storytelling, deep lore, and unforgettable characters.From the moment the game starts, it’s clear that *Final Fantasy XVI* is going to be something special. The story is gripping, featuring a medieval-inspired setting where political intrigue, massive wars, and ancient magic come together in a sprawling narrative. The tone is darker than previous entries, filled with mature themes, but it never loses that signature *Final Fantasy* heart and emotional depth. Clive, the protagonist, is a character you genuinely root for, and his journey is full of emotional highs and lows that keep you invested.Visually, *FFXVI* is nothing short of breathtaking. The detailed character designs, stunning environments, and jaw-dropping cinematics elevate the experience to new heights. Whether you're wandering through lush forests, desolate landscapes, or towering castles, the world feels alive and richly detailed. The particle effects during battles and the epic Eikon fights are spectacular, giving every encounter an unforgettable, cinematic flair.The combat system is another highlight. Gone are the turn-based mechanics of old, replaced by a fast-paced, action-packed system that feels fluid and rewarding. Every fight feels impactful, with smooth combos, dodge mechanics, and devastating special abilities that make you feel powerful. Yet, it retains enough RPG elements to allow for customization and strategy, giving players control over how they approach battles. The Eikon battles, in particular, are jaw-dropping set pieces that feel both massive in scale and thrilling to play.In terms of performance on Steam, *Final Fantasy XVI* runs beautifully. The optimization is solid, with smooth framerates and crisp graphics even on mid-range PCs. Whether you're playing on a high-end rig or a more modest setup, the game looks fantastic and plays smoothly. Controller support is seamless, and the keyboard and mouse controls are well-implemented, making for a comfortable experience no matter how you prefer to play.Additionally, the soundtrack is classic *Final Fantasy*—sweeping orchestral scores that perfectly match the game's epic scale. The music enhances every scene, whether it’s a quiet, emotional moment or a bombastic battle.Overall, *Final Fantasy XVI* on Steam is a triumphant evolution of the series. It dares to take risks with its darker tone and action-oriented gameplay, but it never loses sight of what makes *Final Fantasy* great: epic stories, deep characters, and stunning visuals. Whether you're a longtime fan or new to the series, this is a must-play RPG that will leave a lasting impression.

_childDocuments_.review: Man... I absolutely adored my experience with this game. The only negative of any substance i can think of off the top of my head is that the game does tend to stutter now and then. Especially during its action packed QTE infused Eikonic battle sequences / cut scenes. I play on a Lenovo Legion laptop with an RTX 4080 and an I9 processor with 32 GBs of Ram. I had to play the game on medium for a smooth experience. Anything higher and the game would constantly stutter, that being said, the game is absolutely gorgeous on medium settings anyways, anything more is overkill. Apart from the performance issues, any other negatives are just nit-picky stuff that while annoying, are not glaring enough issues as to ruin the experience.      Now, the reasons i love this game:1. The game world is absolutely stunning. The devs crafted an incredibly beautiful fantasy world for you to visually consume, i found myself panning the camera slowly around my character many times just to take it all in. I did this in every new location, without fail.2. I love the story of the game's characters and the world they inhabit. Down to the supporting staff that liter each of the various town hubs you'll visit. Martha, Quinten, Isabelle, Lubor, they all had interesting backstories if you took the time to complete all of their side quests. Speaking of side quests, i know many see them as boring busy work, but i had another view. I did at first find them to be on the lame side but as the game progressed and the side quests began to delve deeper into the livelihoods and stories of the aforementioned beloved supporting cast, i began to eagerly seek them out as i loved learning more about the world and it's inhabitants.3. The action combat this game offers is not as deep as something as Devil May Cry, but i dont need it to be, i dont play those games really. The combat is fun, smooth, employs creative abilities that bleed seamlessly into one another and is backed up by an absolutely glorious, foot stamping, head bobbing soundtrack. The eikonic battles are a visual and audio feast. One of the most exhilarating game play experiences I've had in a while.4. As mentioned before the soundtrack is stunning, not only in combat, but while traversing the open zones and towns of the world. This is nothing new for the Final Fantasy series, they never miss in this department. Standout tracks are "no risk no reward" and "Away".5. The voice acting is stellar, for the main cast, supporting cast and down to the run of the mill npcs littered throughout the game's towns/hubs. The game oozes big budget energy in its overall presentation.This game's combat may not be the deepest, there are no elemental weaknesses to exploit nor meaningful gear upgrades to acquire, and for me, that's ok. Not every game needs to have the materia system from FF7 or the elemental exploitation system from Persona. Final Fantasy is a series that evolves and adapts from iteration to iteration and i believe that 16 is a bonafide home run.Dont get this game if: *You are looking for a deep rpg experience*You need your games to have meaningful experience, progressions system or extremely deep combat mechanicsGet this game if: * you are looking for an excellent fantasy story told with sublime music, visuals and voice acting* You love action combat games with beautifully animated combat* You love Final fantasy storytelling This game is a 9.5 out of 10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Long time FF fan -- probably my favorite gaming franchise of all time.Unfortunately, this game just isn't it. There is more movie than game. When there is actually game to play, there is no challenge. You are never short on resources, never required to deviate from the pre-planned corridor the entire game exists within, and constantly waiting for your next opportunity to actually enjoy the game's decent combat system, even if it is a bit basic. The cinematic battling / QTEs are cool, but the window you have for completing these events is SO long -- you legit have ALL WEEK to press the right button. Why even have it there?This should have been an anime, not a game. Or, if it had to be shipped as a game, 90% of the NPC back-and-forths / straight-line-field-traversing should have been totally stripped away. The game-to-non-game ratio in this game's current state is just so insanely terrible. The story so far has been solid, but I'm not that far into the game yet and am honestly not sure if I can get through it. From the little I've read of others' experiences with this game, the story gets worse, not better. I was really excited to see this come out for PC, and that makes me even more disappointed with how mediocre this experience has been. For me, this is a 5 or 6 out of 10 at best. Truly disappointing. The only gripe I have is that the attacks in the beginning are kind of clunky. You only have two combos really in the beginning. X, X, X, X, Y or X, X, X, X, X. name: 7 Days to Die
detailed_description: HOW LONG WILL YOU SURVIVE? With over 18 million copies sold, 7 Days has defined the survival genre, with unrivaled crafting and world-building content. Set in a brutally unforgiving post-apocalyptic world overrun by the undead, 7 Days is an open-world game that is a unique combination of first-person shooter, survival horror, tower defense, and role-playing games. It presents combat, crafting, looting, mining, exploration, and character growth, in a way that has seen a rapturous response from fans worldwide. Play the definitive zombie survival sandbox RPG that came first. Navezgane awaits! GAME FEATURES Explore - Huge, unique and rich environments, offering the freedom to play the game any way you want, featuring 5 unique biomes and worlds up to 100 square kilometers in size. Craft – Handcraft and repair weapons, clothes, armor, tools, vehicles, and more with over 500 recipes. Learn more powerful recipes by finding schematics. Build – Design your fort to include traps, electric power, auto turrets, automated doors, gadgets and defensive positions to survive the undead in a fully destructible and moldable world. Cooperate or Compete – Work together to build settlements or against each other raiding other player’s bases, it’s really up to you in a wasteland where zombies and outlaws rule the land. Create – Unleash your creativity with access to over 800 in-game items, and over 1,300 unique building blocks and a painting system that offers infinite possibilities. Improve – Increase your skills with a multitude of perks under 5 main attributes. Gain additional skills by reading over 100 books. 7 Days to Die is the only true survival RPG. Choose – Play the campaign world, or dive back in a randomly-generated world with cities, towns, lakes, mountains, valleys, roads, caves and over 700 unique locations. Combat – Encounter nearly 60 unique zombie archetypes including special infected with unique behaviors and attacks progressing in difficulty to provide an infinite challenge. Survive – Experience real hardcore survival mechanics with nearly 50 buffs, boosts and ailments that will impact the gameplay in ways that can both challenge and aid in your survival. Destroy – Buildings and terrain formations can collapse under their own weight from structural damage or poor building design with real structural stability. Loot – Scavenge the world for the best weapons, tools, and armor with 6 quality ranges providing thousands of permutations. Augment items with a multitude of mods. Quest – Meet several Trader NPCs who buy and sell goods and offer quest jobs for rewards. Enjoy many unique quest types supported by over 700 locations. Customize – Create your own character and customize your character further in-game with a huge selection of clothing and armor you can craft or loot in the world. Drive – Enjoy the badass vehicle system where you find all the parts, learn the recipes, craft and customize your own bicycle, minibike, motorcycle, 4x4 or gyrocopters and ride with friends. Farm or Hunt – Plant and grow gardens for sustainable resources or head out into the wilderness and hunt over a dozen unique wild animals.

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst not revolutionary (minecraft with guns, zombie hordes, and some basic block physics), that mix is pretty solid. I nearly gave this a positive review, even. And you can forgive an early access game a fair few flaws. (Also, please note that I played a fair while offline on steam, so... I do have more hours in this than it seems).But the unfortunate issue that's really hurt the playability of this game is how the dev's problem solve. Players are creative, and rather good at solving problems. So, they would slow zombies to a crawl with water, and wait for them to lose the ability to sense them on bloodmoon nights by just staying safe until dawn, and then letting the horde wander off. They would build bases half-way down cliffs; zeds at the bottom couldn't see you or get to you, zeds at the top would fall and splatter. They would use the penalties to mining underwater to fortify structures. They would, in short, win.The dev's, rather than add new content that would complicate these strategies, instead decided to just do things like remove zombie fall damage. To make zombies ALWAYS move full-speed through water.  To remove zombies suffering the same debuffs as players.As such, the game shoehorns you into playing in some very limited ways, and really tries to steer you towards a house/fort, walls, and spike traps. Which would be okay if that wasn't so godawfully boring.Mine forever to keep up your supplies of iron an concrete. Which, staring at low-res stone walls directly in your face is just boring. Place spikes on the ground, because ones on walls won't hurt them (they'll just attack them from outside the damage radius), and watch zombies just stand there and kind of explode bits off, randomly (which gets old fast) whilst you drop ammo into clumps of idiots with a bad tendency to spin wildly in circles.It just gets tedious, and I personally resented being forced to play in the most energy inefficient possible way. I've also yet to experience a breach. A couple got past the outer perimeter on the 28th night, but they quickly died in the bailey. I'd like to be able to automate dealing with zombies much more, because again, they're tedious, not challenging to deal with by... Two to three days in. At the end of the day, it basically boils down to not being a particularly clever game, that has started to punish clever strategies rather than grow in depth.

_childDocuments_.review: I actually love 7 Days to Die. It's a strong zombie survival game, and after a while you can focus on just rebuilding your base and growing. Pros:- Strong crafting- Diverse enemies- Decent graphics- Seems like it's being updated hereCons:- No story or lore anywhere, unless you count a newspaper that says "virus outbreak" or the random challenges you find.- Multiplayer needs work. I'd freaking love it if they had dedicated servers. that you could build on. I understand the challenges. World of Warcraft does a good job because you can't keep a base, but Fallout76 actually (surprisingly) is one they should look at for how to incorporate base building on consistent servers. - Building off of that, the lack of a steady server is why most of the multiplayer is lacking. There's no community and it's downright lonely. You can play with friends, and start on servers together... but unless you keep your game running, you can't play unless the host is available. Makes it something you start on and stop on fairly quickly.- Crafting can get overwhelming. While it's strong, it's a bit too strong and too indepth. It makes organizing things and creating what's necessary obnoxiously tedious at times. Suggestions (that will probably be ignored):- Run dedicated servers.    - You can solve the problem of time by making the enemies you face in an area dictated by the highest level player within 500 meters. i.e., don't spawn super strong, Day 60 zombies against a Day 1 player, unless they're playing with someone nearby who is that far along.   - You can solve the problem of base population with a first come/first served rule. i.e., if Player 1 is on the server and has a base at the Bear Den, and Player 2 joins  the same server but also had a base at the Bear Den, alert them that their base will not populate on this map and prompt them to join a different server/realm.  World of Warcraft does a good job with Realms, where you keep your progress on each map and can ensure you play with friends. Fo76 lets you play with friends, but keeps your base itself static rather than the server, and alerts you if the server you want to join would make spawning your base impossible. - You could also make it so that bases built remain after the player signs off, however that opens the player up to griefing while they sleep or don't play, which would make the game less enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start this review by stating that I have purchased into alot of early access games. By alot I mean at least 50+ games in early access state. One of the common tennants that I have noticed in these games from small developers is that they bite off way more than they can chew and fail to deliver communication on how thier studio is effectively tackling the challenges presented by thier intial overly ambitious goals. This studio is not one of those studios, this game is not one of those games. I have supported this game since it's kickstarter campaign and I have to say its one of the top investments I have made into the early Access game sales model.Reasons why I recommend this game:Updates: Are frequent.Bugs: When found are fixed promptly.Crafting: Many recipies in the initial bucket with tons more custom recipies if you decide to play multiplayerScalable difficulty: The amount of options that you are able to adjust for singleplayer make your experience playing the game as challenging or as easy as you would prefer.Multiplayer: There are some amazing PVP and PVE servers out therePersonal Experience: I play alot of games when I have the oppurtunity to do so. You can tell by the amount of hours I have into this game that it is definitely worth the price tag.Reasons why I would not recommend this game:None.If you are on the fence, and considering buying this game, buy it. If you love the genre of either sandbox games, zombie games, or survival games, buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game for a long time, but today my patience is exhausted.It was a really great game and you could spend days on end.I started playing long before it appeared in Steam.And I, like everyone, waited a very long time and watched its development.But now it's dead like the zeds that walk in it - still moving, but without life.And do you know when it happened?This game have a lot of things and improvements that it needs.There is only one weapon of each type and there are no alternatives.Shooting and weapon behavior, to put it mildly, is not impressive.The light passes through the floors and walls and acts where there is none, or vice versa.Temperature and getting wet work like in Disney cartoons.The concepts "inside" and "outside" work as in constructors for a mentally challenged.The movement is so primitive that you still can't get into a car-sized hole.There is absolutely no support for the workshop and other modding tools when games like Kenshi, KSP, Project Zomboid have long acquired thousands of mods and a strong community.This game has a very weak interface that starts to slow down as soon as you try to do something with it.And tons and tons of what else in this game is wrong or annoying.And a couple of trains of bugs on the siding.And you will say that this is only alpha stage, it's early access and still is not complete.And for 5 or 6 years (from 2013 or 2014, I don’t remember exactly), I always agreed and never said a bad word.But now I can answer the question when this game became dead.This game became dead when devs, instead of doing what the game really needs, began to CHANGE. WHAT. IS. ALREADY. WORKING.Over the past year or two, there is ABSOLUTELY nothing new.Over the last couple of years, several new buttons have appeared in the menu.Instead of this, disappeared several biomes, the type of soil, many buildings (including the largest ones) and the once huge world that was not seen possible to pass now could be crossed in one day.There is no longer a large open water and no rivers and mountain systems.There is practically no water at all anymore.I once said: "Wow, here is a really smooth quality system, not like in Diablo with 7 types of stuff".Here it is not anymore.I once said: "Wow, here is a clever skill system that grow when you do something, and not like in stupid games where you can learn to trade by killing frogs".Here it is not anymore.Nothing new happens here, only changed what already worked.And the hard truth is that this game is NO LONGER in development.Just devs do some ♥♥♥♥ in it.Do not buy this game, it no longer develops.

_childDocuments_.review: 7 Days to Die is a Zombie Survival, Voxel Based Game. Do not let the trailer on the steam store page turn you off, it is extremely outdated, atleast more than two years ago. The game has changed drastically. This game started out as a voxel based, blocky, survival hode crafting game. It has turned into a voxel based, randomly generated, smooth terrained, amazing visuals, and overall VERY fun and hardcore game. (You can choose between Random Gen Map & Premade Navezgane)UI: 7/10 (Relatively easy to understand)Graphics: 7/10Animations: 6/10 (First person is fine, third person needs work)Crafting: 9.6/10 (Fun and engaging)Singleplayer: 7.9/10 (You don't NEED friends, but they are always fun)Multiplayer: 8.4/10 (The game is just as fun with friends, and is more of a co-op experience rather than PvP)Content Amount: 8/10Hardcore Features: 10/10Overall Rating: 9.3/10The reason I give it an 9.3 is because not that many of the flaws in the game are because of the fact it is in Early Access. Sure, the animations and things like that will be improved, but I feel like the way the game is going now is not the way it was originally going, and this may be for the worse. I'm not saying to not buy this game, because it is truly a magnificent game. Definately worth a buy.How many hours will you get out of this game no matter who you are? Between 40-2,000Thank you for reading my review. If you would like to see more of my reviews, check out my profile.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game across a good 4-5 alphas and it still lacks so many quality of life things and has nonsensical choices the devs make because "it's what we want." Twitch integration being the biggest one. Enemies still clip through walls, doors and even sometimes still fall through the floor and hit you through it! I had a zombie clipped through the floor where I couldn't see it and it was hitting me repeatedly, so I'm slapping the floor thinking, "wow this is a first invisible enemies!" nah it's just a crawler in the floor for a quest, which by the way, i couldn't get him to clip out of the floor and the prospect of day 1 destroying a floor tile with 5khp sounds as dismal as it would've felt to do. If you click in your crafting menu to craft anything too quickly it'll instead craft one of whatever you last chose. Sometimes things just... disappear for no real reason. My husband and I on multiple occasions have randomly lost glasses if we swap between them? I could actually go through and rattle off a few other bugs we've seen while playing over the years that still occur to this day, but that's enough of that for now.Next we'll talk about optimization or what you would call optimization if you were a first year college student. Sorry, frankly I couldn't care less that you guys think your game, which has all the visual flair and effort of a juiced up minecraft server, doesn't need to run well on higher rigs, but most people pay money so their games won't run poorly. It was cute in a16, (not really though) but maybe instead of making excuses you guys could make an effort to not have memory leaks and a myriad of optimization issues this many years in. Now, if you're still here and reading and think, "ya know, I can handle all of the things you've mentioned I wanna buy it!" Don't. The game lacks any type of replay value realistically past building big bases or running around willynilly killing things. You can do quests for traders that go from tier 1 to tier 5. Now I know most people aren't going to play like they're a seals team six and get to tier 5 quests in the first 10 days, but even after that there's nothing to do but the same thing over and over and over. Loot, kill.... uhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh don't die? You can try different weapons but ultimately it's the equation with a different variable that has little effect. Speaking of weapons... they add garbage like "twitch integration!" to a almost purely single player game and spears still ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ suck. They've never felt good once in the entire time I've played and not because they aren't my preferred weapon they have zero going for them outside of range. Btw alpha 20 tho, so maybe they'll add a way for me to use zoom calls integration or something? Who knows with these people.Edit: so apparently they added gamespark in a19 and it'll be here till the game releases. It collects specific data about gameplay stats like what skills you took at certain levels, what killed you, etc. That in and of itself isn't a problem, but there's no way to opt in or out. Zero transparency is bad enough, but things like this have become common place in video games and it's bad imo either way you cut it.

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to do this, it really does. I have nearly 4,000 hours in this game. Yes you read that correctly, I suffered from a chronic illness that immobilized me, as a former workaholic it was easy to do. I could actually move, build, and go on adventures, it was an awesome release... until now. I doubt I'll ever hit the 4k hour mark because, quite frankly, it's not fun anymore. And that is not because I lost interest, I would LOVE to keep playing. But over the past few years of development the gameplay itself, the sense of immersion and adventure, has suffered, greatly. It does indeed look better, much better, but it's lost it's mojo.What changed that caused this? A ton of little things really. Removal of Learning By Doing being a huge one, actions no longer mean anything. Instead of fixing exploits, like other games do, they just replaced ALL of it with RNG based magazines. Lame, mods found a compromise by mixing it up at least. Skill improves with use, but crafting up needs mags, that works well enough. But the vanilla just doesn't get it. They removed E for picking things up, now you have to punch crops to get them, also dumb. Farming, also ruined, used to be fun, organic, and useful. But one thing that seriously ruins each new game almost immediately is loot containers becoming static unusable objects once looted. Like wtf, at least give us an option. I hate looting now, and they force you to do more of it. Ugh.I used to take over existing buildings and fix them up, loved to do it, because who in the F would build a house from scratch in a world full of empty buildings. And I love building, so usually I'd make a horder base at least. But with fixer-upper buildings one of my fav things was getting to the point where I made a generator and wired up it's existing lights to work. It was a huge milestone in each playthrough... can't anymore. Again, wtf. How do you dev a game backwards like this.I didn't even mention the new armor system because I can't suffer through a playthrough long enough to get to that point. Especially being FORCED to deal with Rekt, can't stand that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and we have no choice, progression is so overly linked to them now, it no longer feels like a sandbox, I no longer feel independent.Wrapping it up, again I hate doing this, I have gotten far more than my moneys worth, no doubt, and I deeply appreciate what this game once was. But now I cannot in good faith recommend the polished turd it has become. I am hoping mods will save it, I really am. Regardless I owe a deep Thank You to the Fun Pimps for giving me way over 3k hours of good times, alas those times have ended.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great survival game that has a smoothly connected world, the houses look realistic, tunnels in the ground actually look like tunnels, there's many things to craft, books to teach you more crafting recipes. There's hunger, stamina, thirst, and health. You can sprint, you  can cook food on fires if you have cooking pots or a grill. There's a fair amount of fire arms, and you can even craft the bullets for them. You can construct quite a fottress, barricade existing structures, repair damage on structures, upgrade parts of your structures to withstand more damage, grow food, hunt, and the longer you stay in one area, the stronger your scent gets in that area, increasing the chance of an invasion occuring, there's many types of zombies, most look standard, but there's a few special ones, and more are going to be added, not only can you eventually craft standard digging tools and cutting tools, you can find an Auger to dig faster, and a chainsaw to cut tree's down swiftly, multiplayer works fine too, the player sync seems to be perfect even if ping is around 100-150 levels. There are many clothing pieces you can find as you scavenge, head, chest, hands, legs, feet, and they have armor value against attacks, you can even use hides from animals you've hunted to make leather, and then leather armor with the proper knowledge. They recently added the random world generation, which i've been testing, it is done quite well, biomes seperated by rivers, if you look enough you'll find roads, and there's even generated structures to be found, you can also mine a tunnel down anywhere to find yourself some metal ores to make whatever tools, bullet casings, or bullet tips you need and coal, as well as nitrate, to make gunpowder. You can make torches, there's a few ways, and you can find flashlights, there isn't anything that can't be destroyed by you, or the zombies, everything has a different durability depending on what it is made of. The options for playing either on single player or multiplayer are fairy customizable, you can increase drop rates of all items, durability of all blocks, amount of zombies that spawn, how long days last, and how large of percentage of each day is night time, you can also decrease all of these options as well. I'd strongly recommend getting this game if you like a good survival, or action game with an extensive crafting system.
