_childDocuments_.review: Day 21 AftermathCome nightfall, I lasted for less than an hour before the zombies got me.  They clustered on the north wall until they broke through, climbing over each other's corpses.  At least I could see them better this time with the torches I'd placed.  I picked off some with arrows, but I should've used my meager supply of bullets.  In the end they surrounded me from the inner staircase and the 2nd floor balcony.  They chewed through the wall, the doors, and even halfway into the foundation, though the building's still structurally sound.Goals for next week: forge a pickaxe and start an escape tunnel from my base to the natural cavern I found earlier.  Mine for iron in the process.  Add another layer of spikes around the base and repair/strengthen the walls.  Stretch goal: start a garden with the corn & potatoes I've scavenged.***Here's the thing.  The zombies are coming in 7 days, and every week they get stronger.  So while there's a big world to explore and it may seem downright tranquil now, you'd better be one focused taskmasker if you're going to be prepared in time.You'll go back and forth between nomadic and sedentary life.  You'll start out punching grass, and charring that pig you clubbed to death over a campfire (if you don't have to devour it raw that is).  You'll progress, hopefully, until you're sitting pretty in your reinforced bunker, dining on bear stew and blueberry pie.You'll likely always be desperate for something, be it clean water, medicine, building material, metals, or that one part you need to make a gun.  Missing any one of these for long can be fatal, because everything connects with everything else.  The crafting is intuitive, and makes good use of the materials available.  For instance, when you kill an animal, you can get meat, fat, bone, and hide.  Each of these is useful for something very different, and while you may have an excess of some stuff, you'll be wise to never throw things away if you have the space.The game is forgiving enough without being too forgiving.  By default, when you die you can respawn on or near your bed, and all your stuff is in your backpack where you died.  However, once in a while my backpack disappears and I lose some of my best stuff (bug?).  In multiplayer you'll have to defend yourself from other survivors, who are craftier at getting to you and your stuff.  But land claim blocks and locks are meant to alleviate this.  I've only played single player and with friends, so I can't say how good or bad PvP may be.

_childDocuments_.review: In all seriousness though, where to start. After nearly 2.5k hours as of writing this review, I finally decided to sit down and write about my one of my favorite games and quite possibly favorite survival game of all time. The basic gist of this game if that you have 7(or whatever you set) days to collect resources and build a base to defend from a zombie horde, which sounds simple but gets oh so much more fun and indepth. From stronger zombies, to larger hordes, better weapons, automated turrets, and need for a larger base will always keep you looking after the base. But don't fear, this isn't a collect and upgrade simulator, you will have plenty of time to spice up your base, roam the lands slaughtering the undead, or just growing your own drug empire in the basement with a chemistry station. -Massive crafting, building, and upgrading system; enough to keep builders and hoarders busy for years-Large amount of settings to customize each world to your liking-Major updates every year-Large amounts of unique zombie models-Many high population servers to play with others-Modding capabilities-Peer to peer hosting-Large amount of skills to customize your own play style-Large amount of different weapons-Very in-depth crafting system to keep you engaged-Major updates take a year-The game is taxing on your pc, might be hard to run it at highest graphic possibilities, since the world generation will tax your ram-Can be hard to get into solo, definitely better with friendsGet this game, it is worth full price and if you can convince a friend to pick it up as well even better, this game gets exponentially better when you can bring someone else into the wastelands alongside yourself. It does go on sale often both on steam and humble bundle for 7.99$, which is an absolute steal and even more worth it. Message me with any questions I'm happy to help!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard review to write because I do enjoy elements of this game and the overall concept was fun and exciting when it was first released in early-access (way back in 2013). I've owned and played this game since December, 2014. I've been playing since A10 of the game. Just to put this into perspective so that my review makes sense, this game (which is still in alpha) is almost 7 years old in a few months.For 6 of those 7 years, I have been a fan of the potential of this game. In the early years, the formula was simple. start with nothing, craft tools, build bases, survive zombie encounters. The game had bugs, glitches, and other issues, but I'll leave those alone as that's expected. What ruins this game for me are the following in no particular order:1) The leveling, RPG element of the game has been constantly fiddled with, to the point in A19 that it has progressively turned into a chore. It's not fun. It excludes players who do not have hours per day to invest in playing the game. Through each update, the devs seem to have made it a priority to piss off players with ridiculous skill tree grinds.2) The schematics. Skills in the game can be advanced purely by grinding them out through XP or reading books and schematics. These are generally fine, but the developers can't seem the leave this feature alone without ever addressing a major issue that's been with the game forever: You can burn books and schematics by reading the same ones repeatedly. This literally does nothing for your character, save for a few XP points. What's most obnoxious about it is constantly having to check your player stats to see which ones you have read or haven't read. For schematics, you can't even check this. You have to simply look up recipes in your personal inventory, or the work stations, and see which ones are locked. It's a mess. It's never been fixed. It's only been messed with, to the point where it got so bad (the devs made them expire at one point, to force you to keep finding and reading the same ones until you leveled up high enough to just "know" them) that players essentially forced the devs to go back to the original mechanism.3) Optimization. It needs to be stated again that this game is almost 7 years old. I run an i9-9900K paired with an RTX 2080 Super, playing on a 1920x1080 display. Maxed out, I'm lucky if the game runs at 80fps. During horde nights (which increase in scale as the player levels up), the frame drops are easily in the low 20's. It essentially becomes unplayable. They've chosen to focus 7 years of development on assets, content tweaks, bug fixes (which is acceptable) and constant gameplay meddling where stuff isn't broken, instead of optimizing the game. The graphics aren't at all anything special, not even by 2013 standards. There's no reason for this game to run like ♥♥♥♥ other than laziness and/or lack of interest in optimization.4) Stability. This game runs rampant with instability issues. Every patch seems to fix some issues, or not fix listed issues that say "fixed", or introduce entirely new issues that we must wait patiently to be patched in order to "enjoy" the next update. Again, 7 years in alpha. 7 years of community testing and feedback. The "early-access" excuse isn't acceptable at this point.5) Gameplay meddling. It used to be fun and interesting building bases and creating ways to survive horde night. Throughout that last four or five updates, it's just gotten worse. Bases are utterly pointless, as the time and resources it takes to build anything by day 7 and the horde nights that follow, result in structures that might as well be made out of paper. Most annoying is that I've always seen the traders in the game as examples of what a truly 'fortified' position should look like. While I understand that horde night is intended to keep the game intense and interesting and give the player a true sense of purpose and survival, what the prevailing emotion is for me is that the devs are sitting back like, "No matter what they build, let's ♥♥♥♥ with them. Let's destroy their bases with impossibly vicious AI that tears through concrete with flesh and bone, like it's cardboard." It's not fun. It's just plain stupid, and removes the fun and satisfaction of building what would truly be a survivable compound in real life. It makes the player's efforts worthless and rewards them with nothing for taking the time to think out and build a defensible position. The only way I have found to make horde night manageable and entertaining is to turn on creative mode and lay turrets with 360 degrees of coverage, cheating the ammo in to keep them fed. Without them, your base is pointless.6) Structural integrity. I'm a mechanical engineer, so physics and structural mechanics are like second nature to me. This game has had very fundamentally flawed structural physics from the beginning and it continues to this day. I commend the effort to add it to a game like this, but if you can't do it right, or at least well enough to be believable, it's best not to do it at all. Gussets (angled supports between a vertical pillar and horizontal beam) are particularly broken. You can build a pillar, extend out horizontally with blocks until collapse, then rebuild with a single wedge block as a gusset and get a longer horizontal beam. Great! Now, logically, the physical laws that govern a gusset should dictate that if you expand that diagonal structure between your column and beam, you should be able to also expand your horizontal support. Not in this game. A 10-block long gusset has the exact same effect as a single wedge in the corner of your column and beam. Worse, you also have to account for caves or voids under ground, even in areas where no actual support is needed. The way the physics in this game functions is that any void directly impacts the structural stability of ALL the blocks above it, even if they are adequately laterally supported. It doesn't make any sense.7) Lastly is time. In the beginning, time wasn't an issue, as TFP was small, consisting of three guys with day jobs that had a fun idea and plan to make a game. Now they've have over 25 full and part-time employees since 2018 and still have not released a final product. The game isn't even in Beta yet people...The problem that plagues these early-access games, and why I can't recommend them in good consciousness, is because these indie developers have grown accustomed to taking people's money up front, delivering spoon fulls of sub-par product under the guise of "early-access" and the player base has become complacent and accepting of this practice. This game has sold over 2.5 million copies as of 2018. At $25 a copy, that's 62.5 million USD. As of 2020, it's nearly 10 million copies. That's 250 million USD. Where is all of this money going? "The average 7 Days to Die Team member has over 14 years of experience in Game and Software Development working with or for many AAA Video Game Companies." This comes from their original kickstarter... Why am I expected to accept a 7 year old alpha as a fair exchange for my money with AAA "experts" spending 7 years on an alpha? Why am I expected to accept waiting for a final product that I will have long gotten bored of and moved on from in a 7 year time frame, before ever seeing a finished release? The "promise" of a good game to me was worth $25.00 back in 2014. Today, the guarantee of a never finished, poorly optimized, constantly messed with, glitchy, old-looking mess for new players, is not worth $25.00.Yes, I have fun in the game, for what it is. Yes, I still find general entertainment value in it. No, I cannot recommend spending money on it today. These guys have a quarter billion dollars from people buying an alpha. I'll recommend this title when it's finished.

_childDocuments_.review: I can not say for sure if anyone will like something or not only what my experience is/was. Therefore, I suggest you watch a video of game play footage but make sure the video is on the newer pc version (sort/filter by date for game play videos).After playing again for the first time in a while I can no longer call the game a complete waste of money if you only paid 30 bucks for it but I also should mention that this is completely different game from some of the older versions (less survival more looter shooter now).I would not pay over 30 bucks for the game (devs took forever to release updates/fixes and often do not deliver everything they proposed or they delay for years).Although some aspects of the older version are better if you compare the two side by side the newer versions have slightly more going for it (most of that is the fact that they fixed most the bugs and added new content)What the fun pimps screw up you can always fix with mods but it is stupid that you have to resort to that. I also feel it important to mention that just because the developers say they plan to or are trying to put something in that does not mean it will ever actually be added on time if at all. Zip lines were mentioned forever ago and were never added because they deemed it impossible or too difficult after they announced it for 1 example but there are also other times when they would announce something only to delay afterwards for what seems like forever (bandits were supposed to be released several alphas ago and keep getting "delayed").I understand just because you want to do something does not make it possible (sometimes the manpower/resources are a problem and other times what you are trying is simply not possible to do) but not doing the research to see if something was possible before you announce it to the public is a mistake the devs make repeatedly. Furthermore, the fact that the game was in beta so long and still isn't complete enough for official release after 10+ years of beta should be noted (in a bad way).So, taking everything into consideration and judging the new version of the game as if it were a completely different game (which it is) I would recommend this for anyone who is a fan of this kind of game right now if its under $30 USD  but do yourself a favor by not trusting the tags and lookup a game play vid for the newest version to see for yourself especially if there has been another patch/update since may 5 2024 (sort/filter by date to make it easier).Farming is trash even maxed (not usually worth it anymore when food is easily/often found in loot). You can no longer boil or collect water with jars or anything anymore (you gotta buy something to drink, loot something, or use a rain collector (an item you can only get late game). Game cycle is you get quest, complete quest, loot poi, and keep in mind that you gotta build up blood moon base defenses. You have many maze like houses to explore making it less boring but only slightly.You can not simply learn how to craft an item better by crafting it repeatedly anymore and you need to loot the books to get better crafting skills (was another difference in an older version).Honestly, I would not play the game without mods even if we do not take lack of content into account because I want survival not the glorified looter shooter. So, I use mods that revert the changes made to the game which I dislike such as farming and the water collection by the devs along with lots of others. This change does make bookstores more valuable and with the changes they made which changes things you looted into un-lootable objects means if you were not the 1st one to discover the bookstore you missed out on the books until/unless you can reset the area completely (like when you get a quest).However, do not think you can take it easy just because there is not a blood moon happening for a few days since zombie hordes can attack at random especially if you are making allot of noise or you have the fires/torches going.The zombies in the places you explore will be asleep till they hear/see you making looting the place difficult and do not think any wall can protect you for long since they can break those down.Building a base up high may sound like a great plan but unless it has structural support it will fall (no floating bases without an exploit/glitch/mod) and zombies love noting more than to break your support pillars to watch you fall.There are several different zombie types from your average walkers, ones that can fly, ones that will spit acid at you, ones that can jump/climb walls, one which calls in hordes of other zombies, 1 that will try to use suicide bombs to blow up large portions of your base, and more.Not to mention that you can get sick or injured which can cause problems in itself with survival (colds may seem like no big deal but think of coughing/sneezing in a house full of sleeping zombies).As with all games there is a bit of a learning curve.So, I recommend trying to learn the basics by watching some videos, reading posts, or playing with someone who knows how to play and is willing to teach.Keep in mind these zombies are not mindless though and so the basic moat/pitfall traps you see in most zombie movies will not be as effective as you would think (plan your defenses well).As mentioned, I personally think that that for 30 bucks this game is worth it but it is not worth a higher price yet and might not ever be. The devs have claimed they plan to add things to make it more worthwhile but not 100% confident in there ability to deliver on time if at all anymore (they let many horrid bugs stay for so long in the past and proposed features that they either could not deliver or keep delaying repeatedly while claiming it will happen next time). The recent road map for the game says they are working on the bandits that they mentioned years ago and have that set for release next year atm (I would count on more delays based on past experience with these devs).

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game whose developers can't decide what they want to make.Every way YOU decide to deal with zombies is WRONG - unless it's shooting them in the head straight on.Build a fortified base? - WRONG! - They made zombies 100x stronger than the HULKBuild intricate mazes to get to your front door? - WRONG! - They made the zombies smarter than tony starkBuild an underground base? - WRONG! - They made the zombies able to detect you from a half mile away through solid stone.Build pit traps to trap and kill "stupid" zombies? - WRONG! - The made it so the zombies won't die no matter how far they fall, and will use their scientific skills to avoid them anyway. Unless you exploit it of course.Any of these should be viable, but it seems the devs have decided that the game is a zombie shooter game with a hint of survival. Any other player could avoid doing any of the things mentioned and just play it as a zombie hunting game, but they seem determined that any gameplay other than what THEY want is not valid and should not be allowed.Skills are all level gated now which I'm not a 100% against, but when zombies are psychic, genius, hulk level power with pinpoint accuracy from the very start having to wait until level 40+ to make some items seems stupid. Of course you can change some zombie block damage, but it doesn't change the psychic genius AI.It is as someone else on the forums said "a base building arms race between the players and the devs". Any base the players find can defeat the zombie AI the devs attempt to patch out so it's no longer viable.Mention any of this on their forums and their personal attack dog Roland will insult you, tell you that you're wrong, insinuate that you're stupid, lazy, not creative, etc. Roland alone is reason enough to not want to post on the official forums as any criticism of the game or TFP is met with disdain, condescension, and vitriol thinly veiled in "civil language".If you are looking for an open world sandbox zombie survival game DO NOT PURCHASE THIS GAME. By their own admission the devs do not want to make that sort of game. They have their very own narrow idea of what the game shoudl be, and it is NOT open world sandbox survival.

_childDocuments_.review: After having watched some old lets plays from 2013, I was pretty psyched about this game. There's crafting and zombies, two of my favorite elements! I have tried other zombie/craft games that were fairly hyped up when they came, but this looked way cooler. I decided to look it up on steam, and to my surprise my brother whom I have always partnered up with in multiplayer games had it. After asking him if he wanted to do some zombiekilling, I suddenly had something in my inbox. My bro gifted it to me and told me to get my ass on his server, where several of his friends were as well. When I entered the world, I was pretty freaked out. I was in my underwear in a desert. All alone. Even though it was sunny and in the middle of the day, the sounds combined with the scenery made me incredibly uneasy. After checking the map I saw that I really couldn't be further away from their base. I freaked and ran towards them, and died about five times. (never claimed to be good) I finally spawned well within range,  and after a few minutes I found their base. Now, this was some next level fortification. After breaking a few bones trying to get in and not really managing to get anyones attention, a massive zombiehorde came towards me. I finally called my brother on the phone and forced him to show me how to get in. Upon entering they handed me full armor, guns, medkits, a place to put out a bed and showed me around. They really outdid themselves. There were common spaces and everything. After some time we moved up to the roof and started killing some zombones while they bolted past our fort. The next ingame day I was sent out on a scavenging mission (bro takes these kinda games really srsly), and it made me freak out. I had to deal with zombones all by my lonesome and be far away from camp, well until night time. And I still hadn't really learned anything useful about the game, seeing as they had provided me with everything before I could start asking questions. Being by yourself at night in this game without a proper base and proper knowledge is downright terrifying. Now, this was right before Alpha 11. The next time we ganged up to play our server was outdated and saves had been deleted. We had to do everything from scratch, and I finally really got to learn how to do crafting because I would die pretty fast if I didn't. I did get infected several times, broke several legs, and got dysentery more than I would like to admit. And I was loving every minute, while simultaneously ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ my pants. I mean, I love their swagger but zombies are still terrifying.We are still trying to rebuild what we once had, but sitting at night and actually being scared because you could die at any moment is actually way more fun (and gruesome) than being safe and sound inside a fortress. This also goes for having to actually go out and gather/make every last little thing you need too. I still haven't been able to put in that many hours since I refuse to play it alone, but I love it!And after that long boring story; on to the game itself!As I stated, I have tried other games with the same elements. None of these have lived up to my expectations. I was terrified at the start of every last one of them, but that soon wore off. It just gets worse with 7d2d. The atmosphere created by the amazing sounds, the massive landscape with concealed valleys and mountains blocking your view, and the terrifying night/day shifts is just simply amazing. I wanna ♥♥♥♥ my pants when I play these kinda games. And I keep on doing that. There were some complications after Alpha 11 came out, but it is an early access after all. And from what I gather the pimps are pretty involved with their community and active as well, so in time this will probably be one of the greatest zombie mmos out there. Greatest game i've played for a long time, by far.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game in the sale and i can honestly say its my most played and enjoyable game I own.There are people that complain that the zombies are too hard or too easy, or that they shouldnt be able to path around objects to get to you or or dig, or spit at you...... ITS A ZOMBIE GAME! ZOMBIES DONT EXIST IN REAL LIFE! ZOMBIES ARE WHATEVER THE DEV WANT THEM TO BE..... *Ahem*... What i mean to say is, there are different types of zombies like in "I am Legend", "Resident Evil", "The Walking Dead", "World war Z", "Left 4 Dead", etc. Depending on what you prefer to play against, you can change your difficulty. Yes you can even make them walk all the time or run.So to give you my review of the current A17.At first I didnt like the path finding to the Zombie AI, but then i remembered that the pathing in A16 was broken becuase you would get Zombies running around in circles for no reason. The new pathing is a welcome addition, becuase it fixes the running circle bug, and it brings in another element of danger. You not only have to think about where you are going, but also where you have been, you need to check behind you  to make sure nothing is creeping up on you... becuase they can.The building remains largly the same, there are some new addition to blocks and some changes. For example you can no longer craft reinforced steel blocks but this is not game breaking. In A16 people used to build bases that were just behind a 3 block think wall, or just tunnel undergound hide (hide). No longer can you do this and cheese the night away, you now need to change your approach and your base building designs to accomodate for the New zombie AI. People that are complaining that they cant do their bunkers and thick walled bases are unwilling to adapt to a game that is in Alpha which by definition is subject to change until release. I for one enjoy the challenge of building a brand new base design becuase I'm a creative person that like sandbox games, I like creating new bases to solve problems. Zombies digging? ok, no underground bunker. Zombies go through walls quickly? Fine I let them come into my base on my own terms, through traps and turrets. If there a problem, theres always a solution in this game.They also  added XP sharing which was a nice addition.With the above being said, there are things that need balancing. A prime example is the scaling of game stage. After a certain point (about Gamestage  120), there is no real reason to go into a house anymore, becuase the risk of pulling a house full of irradiated for the loot you might get is too great. Its easier just to go to the traders.In addition, If you dont like the base game, you can even mod/ change it to your liking. Want more powerful guns, change the XML yourself or download the modlet. Want the zombies to hit less? Drop the block damage down. Want them harder up it to Nigtmare. To hard? Drop it to Nomad. Dont want them running, Make them walk all the time. Dont want to lose your stuff when you die? Drop nothing. Your choice.As a final note. I bought this game for less that $10/ £8.99 and ive got over 1300 hrs into this game. Ive paid £50 for a AAA game and played less that 100 hours of *cough* Destiny 2 *cough*I will admit that its not a finished product and there are bugs, but for the price I paid for the amount of play time ive gotton out of it PLUS the great community that comes with it.... Its worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: 7 Days to Die is one of those games that you want to share with friends who have never played before, and let them experience its' awesomeness with you. It's a voxel based survival crafting tower defense game that touches on gameplay similar to Minecraft and Fallout 3. At first I was quite apprehensive about this game, mostly because of it's poor reviews and, at that time, the price. I nabbed it when it was on sale, then learned that the developers had lowered the price indefinitely. As I played, exploring immense landscapes, learning crafting recipies, and adapting nighttime survival strategies, I began to wonder why this game had gotten such poor reviews. I know now that I should have bought this game long ago, even at its high price. I have enjoyed watching 7 Days to Die's progress more than any other early access game I have played up to this point. I've found myself on more than one occasion reading players' conflicting suggestions and complaints, then come next update realize that the developers had actually listened to that constructive criticism and developed a method to try to satisfy everybody. You can adjust different settings to cater to your specific preferences and difficulty, even after you have started your game. If it gets too easy, just bump up the zombie spawn rate, or vice versa. I wouldn't recommend this one to gamers who have no patience for early access bugs. Don't expect glitch free bliss with this one. But the pros highly outweigh the cons. Judging by what I've seen the game progress to, I have a good feeling that for us patient gamers who appreciate meaningful development...the end product will be well worth it!

_childDocuments_.review: 7 Days to die is an amazing open world survival game, You must scavenge the wastelands for anything that you can use to craft and cook. You can build bases and then see how they survive the night.In the game you spawn at a random position on the map, you are naked, you have nothing, and you start by punching some plants, some trees, some rocks and you craft your first axe some clothing and a bedroll, Then it is time to look for a safe place, just pick an abandoned building and place your bedroll. Then you should scavenge for some food, water and other supplies. You can mine, And you can go deep, you can go high, there is no limit to building your dreamhouse in the wastelands.Don't get to attached to your new home because zombies will come and destroy it if you remain inside. Zombies walk at day, and run at night, Once every 7 days there is a Bloodmoon, here Zombies are able to sniff you from miles away, and the hordes are bigger, There are lots of different kind of zombies and they all have their abilities.You have to freedom to do what you want, as long as you drink eat and survive. when you die you lose everything, but you could go back for your bag. You have the freedom to just roam forever and kill everything on your path, or just build a house close to water, and just go out for food every once in a while, Or you could build a underground city, where it is safe, but still you would need food and water. I prefer to mine at night and scavenge at day, that way i do not really have to protect my house.The game is designed as a Online experience where you can work together or kill other players for their resources, Ofcourse I would not recommend the latter, Because working together makes the game a whole lot better. Many things are customizable, If the zombies run or not, How much resources you can find, how big the map is, etc.I prefer the original map, It is not too small, not too big, It has a lot of interesting locations and a lot of big buildings to clear, I mostly go for the bank, It is a great place to hold out, The Police Station is also very popular, But there are tons of places to claim as your own, and renovate into the ultimate zombie bunker.I used to have problems with frame drops in this game, But they seem to be fixed. Which is great ofcourse, It is still in Early Access, but slowly it is taking on its final shape and it is great, It might be the ultimate zombie survival game.I do miss more modes of transportation, A mini bike is not the best way to get around, Gas is also very rare, I also wish there where more weapons to take down the zombies, But who knows, The game is not done yetOverall 7DTD is a great game, I think everyone can enjoy this game, Some like the building, some like the surviving, Some like the scavenging or the hunting, But if you like them all, then this game is certainly for you. I give it a solid 8.Follow my Curator Page:
_childDocuments_.name: 7 Days to Die

_childDocuments_.review: Nine years ago today, I purchased 7DTD and have put many hours into it, so I figure it's about time to review the game since it's about to go to 1.0. First off, I don't like zombie movies. They bore me. The only zombie movie I've enjoyed was "Shaun of the Dead". That being said, I was skeptical about the game from the start, but it looked interesting, and I enjoyed it. In those nine years, the game has become my most played game of any. I may look away for a couple weeks if a new game catches my attention, but I always come back here. I have other games of the genre without the zombies, but this blows them away. The game is immersive to a point where you do not want to play it when someone is sleeping nearby, unless you don't mind waking them with your "startled exclamations". Seriously. I speak from experience. Now, like all games, this one has some things which will not appeal to some folks . . . it's inevitable. Fortunately, 7DTD was built with great modding capabilities, and if you don't like something, odds are a modder didn't like it either. The only thing of which I can think that I dislike, I changed with a mod. Excellent. I like them. The artwork pulls you in where details abound which help to create a world able to suspend disbelief. Computer is a few years old, but running 5760 x 1080 > 60 fps @ max settings.  Very enjoyable. Many options available to find your desired game style. Define "complete" and look at my time played.Overall, I really like the game, including the zombies. I would recommend this game to anyone that likes the Sandbox/Survival genre, even if you don't like zombies. They work in the game, and I've come to enjoy them in their role. Thanks for your work, TFP.
_childDocuments_.name: 7 Days to Die

_childDocuments_.review: I think I have played this far more than most but can honestly say every single alpha has been getting worse. The pimps are not fixing their code and instead releasing their experimental versions as stable even though the game wont work for a lot of people. Not sure what most people define as stable but the game loading in would be one. The game engine not seizing due to a single bad chunk not loading. A system when it detects a bad chunk and asked you to remove it, you actually have a tool that allows this hahaha or who'd of thunk it, maybe it would auto repair / delete the chunk so it could reload instead of seizing the game engine and requiring admins to randomly teleport around the world in hope of finding it. Or using commands not meant for detecting chunk errors but forced to use unlockall command to discover how many are corrupted. How in two years of dev time do you still have world corrupt themselves. Servers have to store over 20 gigs of data per world backup. That is around double the installation space of the entire game. Everything about this is a no right now. Stop selling it as a multiplayer game when it doesnt function. You are designing for single player and tell us that every single video you show us but sell it on steam as multiplayer ? Its false advertisement at this point. 12 of the top servers all crashing right now constantly and rebooting dozens of time a day to even run for 15 minute intervals. 2 years+ for this. Two man dev teams do a better job on average with the early access principle.Edit* After some patch work to Alpha 16 we now have servers that will run but still crash due to chunk errors. On server restarts, your items might disappear, or the batteries and engines in your electric machines will vanish. Minibikes still disappear or fall through the world. Players now desync making them invisible to others. We can paint though...Edit* They are finally getting things together in a16.3 stable version. Been fun to play again but some glaring bugs still exist that have needed fixes for over a year. Looking forward to see where they take things from here. Also looking forward to putting this to a positive review.Edit* A18 "stable"  I have been coding ServerTools for game management and not playing for 1.5 years. I finally thought it would be a good time to play. Nope. I had not put down a bed yet, died, spawn on someone else bed in their base that is being attacked. I die from an auger and respawn automatically on the same bed I dont own. When I look at the code, they dont assign the block owner but rather just a list is formed. Some bug is putting other players spawn points on the list despite never placing a bed yet. 5 years of dev time for this.Edit* A19 Stable: This was released very rough again and needed a few major patches to be playable without major breaking bugs. There are some really nice improvements to the game over all. Some glaring optimisation issues are still needed such as water, zombie ai, weather changes, model clipping and bounding boxes. It is a better path now and the devs seem to have an idea of what they want to do with the game. A20 may get a positive review. We'll seeEdit* A20 Stable: Getting better. The game cohesion is off between art assets and game play interaction but you can see a direction for the game. Many of the most obvious bugs have finally been squashed. The content is a little bit lack luster simply because it does not feel cohesive. Leaving some elements ignored or not needed during game play as they serve little purpose or due to bad balance, can be detrimental to use. Modding potential has doubled if not tripled from earlier alphas which really brings a tremendous amount of content and potential to the over all game. I feel this deserves a positive review now but with some apprehension. Many gamers will not like this style of game in its current state and it requires mods to bring out the most from it. If you are looking for a survival game, the mods will help achieve it but the base game has become a bit more of an adventure, exploration, crafting, zombie game. Combat itself is still a little bit clunky but improving

_childDocuments_.review: Fun with friends. Pretty good zombie game.The newest update, A21, has taken the game in a strange direction. I wouldn't call it good. The extreme scarcity of water is actually rather annoyingly implemented. The game's resource economy still seems to expect that you have access to as much water as you could want, which was previously the case for established bases. But no, can't have nice things, can we? Why is my bucket of water from a nearby lake useless? Why can't I boil it on a fire just like I do with every jar of poo water I find in the toilets to get clean water?The dew collector is simultaneously too slow and expensive, somehow draws zombies (a completely silent and inanimate object draws zombies constantly), and it takes up a ton of space. It also doesn't seem to collect water from rainfall. What?, there is now only one way to play the game: You have to find "crafting magazines". Literally every single piece of equipment, every weapon, all armor, and each tool that you need to survive are locked behind finding an arbitrary number of books.How do you find the books? Two options. You either loot or buy them. Buying is incredibly limited in selection and prohibitively expensive, so that leaves us with looting. Easy, right? That's the game already, isn't it? No, it wasn't like that before, and it really shouldn't be this way now.To build the things you want and need, you have to find X crafting magazines to unlock them. To find the books, you are forced to put skill points into skills relevant to the item you want to build. No big deal... Except if you happen to have 2 levels in Skill A, and only 1 level in Skill B, can you guess which flavor the crafting magazines you find will be? That's right, no way to know, you just gotta hope RNG is on your side today. Even once you max out a particular crafting magazine, you continue to find them everywhere, useless and worthless, instead of the ones you still need. Because you have points in that skill.I put 1 point in Cooking, and 3 points into archery, for instance, among other skill choices. I have 100/100 in the cooking skill at this point, and the game seems to think I may have missed a recipe somewhere because it keeps shoveling cookbooks at me instead of anything else.Trying to figure out how to build a workbench? Well, did you put points into Lockpicking? No? Well  you can't figure out how to build a workbench, one of the most important items in the game, without putting points into  you silly goose! Why would you think otherwise?They didn't just drop the ball on this one. They catapulted it into a spike wall.

_childDocuments_.review: Building on survivalist and horror themes, players in 7 Days to Die can scavenge the abandoned cities of the buildable and destructable voxel world for supplies or explore the wilderness to gather raw materials to build their own tools, weapons, traps, fortifications and shelters.

name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra
detailed_description: Cobra rears its ugly head yet again and it's up to G.I. JOE to save the world! Embracing the 1980s era of the iconic universe, Wrath of Cobra is a retro side-scrolling beat 'em up. Play as one of the legendary G.I. JOE characters, including Duke, Scarlett, Roadblock, Snake Eyes, and more. Defeat hordes of Cobra troopers, Vipers, Crimson Guards and more of Cobra’s malevolent machinations. Bring Cobra down, striking back at the likes of Destro, Serpentor, Baroness, and Cobra Commander himself! Fight your own way: Rely on your fists and get up close and personal using each character's unique combos and special moves or keep your foes at a distance with a variety of weapons! Retro Gameplay in a Modern Era: Wrath of Cobra takes the classic arcade beat 'em up and brings it into the modern age: Easy to play, hard to master, and smoother than a ride in a H.I.S.S. Want to play with your friends? The game supports local multiplayer (eg. from your couch)! Play as Classic Heroes: Fight Cobra as your favorite G.I. JOE heroes, painstakingly recreated in beautiful pixel art. The differences between characters aren’t just cosmetic: Each hero has different movesets and unique abilities. From the fast and nimble Snake Eyes to the rough and tumble Roadblock, each character is true to form! Battle Iconic Villains: Cobra isn't just the Cobra Commander, it's also its legions! Face hordes of troopers, armored Alley Vipers, artificial B.A.T.s, armed with some of the most iconic weapon systems in the franchise, including the H.I.S.S., C.L.A.W., and the notorious Trubble Bubble. Retro-Infused Soundtrack: Foil the Commander's plot to the beat of classic G.I. JOE themes, reimagined by industry veterans at Kid Katana Records, bringing a modern twist to classic arcade music! Post-Launch Support: Like Destro's plots, Wrath of Cobra will continue with extensive post-launch support, bringing more G.I. JOE heroes into the fray, adding new game modes, levels, and more to keep the G.I. JOE legacy alive!

short_description: Yo Joe! Cobra returns once again with its most fiendish plot yet and it's up to G.I. Joe to defeat them once more! Pick one of the real American heroes, gear up, and get straight into the fight in this retro side-scrolling beat 'em up - and make Cobra RETREAT yet again!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of the worst beat-em-ups I have ever played.The combat is about as sparse and boring as you can get with only small handful of moves per character that aren't that satisfying to use. Stage design is utterly boring, despite a decent amount of enemy variety almost every stage feels exactly the same with the pacing and the enemy encounters making everything blend together. Occasionally it throws a big mid boss style enemy at you that provide at least something of interest breaking these boring stages up, but they have a huge amount of HP and have to be dealt with using the most tedious techniques making them become an incredible drag.Character balance is non existent, I played through the game as Duke that was an unbelievably tedious and annoying ordeal, but Snake Eyes makes everything much easier. The game is also amazingly buggy, the game would consistently crash after the opening cutscene for me and playing through it I encountered an endless string of bugs and glitches.The game also does absolutely nothing of interest with an IP as cool as GI JOE. The first 4 or so of the previously mentioned bland stages are generic facility looking areas, and once you get into the middle of the game you get a string of like 5 or 6 boring suburban street levels that look like they would be more fitting for a Simpsons game than GI JOE.The Bosses are just mindboggling terrible as well. Every boss in the game just appears with barely any fanfare suddenly at the end of whatever of the 12 boring long corridor levels you're in, and what follows is tedious fights against super armour bosses with enormous amount of health. Many of the bosses have the same AI, many of the bosses are just palette swaps or sprite edits of existing sprites, and all of them are completely uninteresting to both look at and to fight. Only the final boss has elements of being some kind of interesting setpiece.To summarise, the game is terrible both in terms of gameplay and presentation. The combat is very basic, unsatisfying, and tedious with barely any of the satisfying aspects of good beat-em-ups. The stages look bland, plain, have no pacing or any cool or interesting moments, and lead to equally bland bosses. The GI JOE license is not being used to even any of it's potential here.For modern beat-em-ups, Streets of Rage 4 is million times better. TMNT Shredders Revenge is a million times better. Fight 'n Rage is a million times better. Final Vendetta is a million times better. Even the extremely flawed and very recently released Karate Kid Street Rumble (which is currently very overpriced and should only be bought once it's on sale or has its price lowered) is filled with infinitely more charm and highlights than GI JOE Wrath of Cobra.Or you could just get the Capcom Beat-em-up Collection that contains many of the old arcade titles that remain as some of the best beat-em-ups ever made.
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

_childDocuments_.review: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra is by far the worst retro side-scrolling beat 'em up I've played so far on steam. In all honestly I haven't played a beat'em up this bad in a long long time. In fact, I can't even think of one that is worse... and I've played a lot. I was a huge fan of Ninja Turtles, Double Dragon, Golden Axe, Streets of Rage, Final Fight, The Simpsons, The Punisher, Battletoads and many others. Every one of those games is more fun than this one.The only thing going for this game is the 16 bit nostalgic retro style, the music, the license, and... that's it. The gameplay is awful. After playing halfway through a mission, you will want to quit playing. The moves are extremely repetitive. You just punch, kick, throw, and jump. There are no new moves you learn, or anything. Yes, you can pick up weapons, but they barely help.How about multiplayer and co-op? There is local co-op, but you can't play with friends online on steam. What a bummer.What else... the bosses. I fought the Baroness, and I think something went wrong with the game. I just couldn't move anymore. I was super slow, couldn't move, and ended up losing all my health. After fighting her, I almost gave up playing the game. It just wasn't fun. Maybe I need to give it more time or need to get better. But seriously I feel miserable playing this game.I really hope they improve this game. If I could give any recommendations to the developers, it would be to add interesting move lists. Almost every beat-em up I've played has better gameplay. The new double dragon game is just sooo fun, as is Streets of Rage 4. The move lists in those games are amazing. The gameplay and combat is so addictive and fun. You can do sooo many different combos and moves.... That is something that completely lacks in this G.I. Joe game.I've got fond memories of G.I. Joe and used to play the hell out of the old G.I. Joe 3rd person arcade shooter back in the day. That game was extremely impressive for the time and is still a better game than this.I paid a lot more for this game than it is currently worth. But I hope the developers add more content and somehow improve the gameplay and make it more enjoyable. Add some combos! Do a little research and see why those other games are addictive.As is it is right now, this game is more of a bore and a chore than fun. If anything I'd give it a 4 out of 10. But I'd totally bump up the score if the gameplay gets better and more modes are added in the future. I'm a huge GI Joe fan and have positive hopes this game improves in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Graphics are nice. Feels like GI Joe. The different characters special attacks are unique. Characters feel different to play. Bonus features and characters to unlock. Couch Co-Op mode. Check mark system between levels so you don't have to start at the beginning every time.Cons: The combat is pretty bare bones for the variety of attacks. The characters are unbalanced. For instance, Snake Eyes is much, much easier to use than Scarlet. Expect to burn through pretty much every life each level; even on the easy setting. Enemies can gang up on you, essentially juggling you.The Ugly: This issue right here is what will give you absolute frustration and a resulting thumbs down. Normally in any game, you press twice in one direction to dash. Not so in this game as 2 different movements will trigger a dash, including quickly moving in the opposite direction when trying to turn around and attack someone from behind. Instead of doing a normal attack, you end up with a dash attack that puts you run right into the line of fire. This especially happens frequently when using the analog stick instead of the game pad to where you spend more effort trying not have that happen than actually attacking. This is a brain dead decision and should have never been implemented this way. I'd give it a thumbs up if it wasn't for this problem, even with all the other flaws. Let's hope a future patch fixes this.
