_childDocuments_.review: Okay, less than an hour on this but if you think that's not enough time to get the handle of a beat 'em up, then take this review with a grain of salt.This is a 5/10, do not recommend.How it plays:The controls work well enough, but there definitely feels a like a little bit of stiffness, as if you don't have as much control as you want. Every character has their typical light punch combo string, a heavy attack that can be charged, two different run attack for light and heavy, one jumping attack that is essentially a dive kick for everyone but Scarlett, a taunt that just seems to taunt and show how great you are, a block button, and finally a special move that is charged up based on your combo. Characters have different "stats", which seem to affect how fast they attack and how much damage they take, but really the difference come down to their attack animations and, most importantly, their specials.The key techniques the game is demanding of you is to maintain your combo string while balancing a block here and there to keep you alive - and the block absolutely is paramount, as you can block *anything*, punch? Rifle shot? HISS tank cannon shell? Just hold that block button; that said, enemies can too and there is no conventional "grab" mechanic in this one, rather you have to knock down an enemy then you can grab them, but if an enemy is blocking you just have to kind of wail on them - it seems like a charged heavy would do the trick, but I've seen them blocked too.The special, unlike most beat 'em ups, doesn't drain any of your life away and given generally skilled gameplay you'll fill it up about every other screen of enemies, sometimes every screen if enough enemies are spawned. Duke has the best special by far as it is a full screen attack; Roadblock's might be the coolest as he gets his trademark chain gun with the trigger apparently glued down, but it has to be aimed at enemies; Snake Eyes calls out Timber to passively attack enemies for a short time (attacks which can also be blocked), and Scarlett stuns all the enemies on the screen without doing damage to them - she can run around and smack most of them around, but it's just a far less useful special than Duke's, in my opinion.The enemies here are typical fare both in terms of beat 'em ups and G.I. Joe, the A.I. is not great at times as I've seen a half dozen COBRA troopers just hug the top left fo the screen several screens in a row. There aren't a lot of frames to telegraph the attacks of the normal grunts, so they pose the biggest threat, meanwhile the big thugs, mid-level bosses, and end level bosses ending up being a breeze even on the hardest mode thanks to the "block to end all blocks" abilities - they all feature the same heavily telegraphed attacks as other beat 'em up bosses, but now you can just hold that block button and go back to wailing away on them, rinse, repeat.And that's it, it's a beat 'em up, a not particularly good one by today's standards, but if it were released in the early 90s it'd be fondly remembered today of course.How it Runs:"How it runs?" you say, looking at this 16-bit presentation; Well, not the best.  The opening cinematic was skipped when I first started Story Mode - suspecting it was weird I was given NOTHING for context, I returned to the main menu and started again and sure enough got the opening cut-scene.  While fighting one of the end-level bosses as Duke, hit his special and all the frames for the characters (including me) on screen slowed down to less than 1 fps - I say "all the on the screen" because soon some more enemies were spawned that were running at normal speed... I'm not even sure how that possibly happens, and I tested video games for almost a decade. Didn't crash in the hour that I played though.How its presented:As said, there is an opening cartoon with decent animation and pretty bad voice acting; Sounds like a few guys and a girl in with a bad set-up and mediocre voice acting chops. From there, we're given short paragraphs between levels as the Joes beat back Cobra and, well, it's presented exactly like you might suspect a straight-forward G.I. Joe game would be, there are no surprises there. As you play, floppy disks will drop from KO'd enemies, these disks are actually currency used in the frontend "Shop" where a few QoL features can be purchased as well as two additional characters: Gung Ho and Ripcord. I'd tell you how they play, but earning enough disks to unlock ONE of them might require a full story mode playthrough, and they are not the only unlockables here - yeah, disks are earned at a painfully slow pace.There are 4 different difficulties, but to be honest I saw no difference between them, maybe an increase to enemy health?  I played on the hardest difficulty a couple levels in a row and seemed to be doing just as good, if not better (because I had gotten the hang of balancing blocks vs. specials) than I had in the early levels; Really the difficulty is in which character you choose, as with Scarlett you get a somewhat less useful special AND a jumping attack that leaves you pretty vulnerable to enemies, so go that route if you're looking for a challenge.Overall this is a fun novelty, but don't expect the level of consideration that was put into TMNT: Shredder's Revenge, this is a linear level system, scant story points, purely left-to-right scrolling, and unbalanced playable characters which is a shame when you consider this is a franchise that people will heavily favor a specific Joe over others.If it ran fine, it'd be a 6 or 6.5/10, but the technical issues have to bring those points down at least a bit, and I would not recommend it at the current or even intro sale price of $22; maybe if it dips down to $9.99 in its current state.
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

_childDocuments_.review: Easily what I have been wanting for and from GI Joe forever. It plays smooth, the nods to the lore and toys and cartoons all hit, and the amount of care in here as a Joe fan is remarkable.More than anything, it is just *fun.* No, it isn't anything revolutionary, but nostalgic beat'em-ups are not supposed to be. They just need to be fun, and engaging, and I am enthralled. Top to bottom, if you are a GI Joe fan, or a fan of old arcade games, I cannot, at all, recommend this enough.Play it, and have fun.
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

_childDocuments_.review: A must have for G.I. Joe fans.  This is the arcade game we've been waiting for since the eighties.  Of course there's not much story-line, simplistic action and the game itself is bug-city.  But this is what those old side-scrolling beat'em-up games were all about.  Most fans of the franchise are old enough to remember what I mean.  The game doesn't just include the must-have Cobra boss villain lot.  They also added some real obscure baddies as well.  Like Night Stalkers, Ninja Vipers and Inferno BATs.  Plenty of room for improvement but have to commend the makers for doing their homework.  I have two young nephews who don't know jack about Joe and they both love the game as well.
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly basic beat 'em up. Stylistically (visuals) chasing TMNT Shredder's Revenge. Gameplay is VERY classic and boring. Your choices for attacks are basically regular weak attack combos (three hits), a charge power attack cuz apparently everyone needs one to deal with blocking enemies, or two weak and one power for a situational thing. You've also got a jump attack and a normal and heavy running attack. You can pick up enemies from the ground. Most weapons suck. Music is also pretty meh.Basically, game coulda done with a whole lot more time in the oven. As it is, it's baby's first beat 'em up, kinda feels like some dude's Beats of Rage amateur effort with some decent visuals some places and bad in others. Castle/mountain stage... no parallax scrolling? in 2024? Come on. If they don't do anything else to it, this is a 5 dollar game. Go buy Fight'n Rage instead.
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

_childDocuments_.review: ⚠️ Recommended, but wait for bug fixes and maybe a sale.On the positive side, it has good visuals and representation of the G.I. Joe franchise. It has serviceable beat'em up mechanics that I had fun with overall. It has most of the staple mechanics of the genre you would expect. Blocking and countering aren't common though, so that was a nice change. I think people sometimes forget how basic some of the most beloved classic beat'em ups are. It's not as well done as other notable recent games like SoR4 or Shredders Revenge, but it has more to it than a lot of the classics (coming from a hug beat'em up fan). I do also appreciate they added some unlockables and some alternate modes to try, although it seems to take more effort than it should to unlock stuff.The biggest issue with the game are bugs and missing features. I played most of the game with 3 players , but also did a bit solo as well.Main issues I ran into:- characters would get locked in animations, which would sometimes self resolve or require restarting. This happened more often in multiplayer, but did happen in single player too- Played the entire story mode without cutscenes because there's a bug where they don't play when using a controller. Found out after the fact and verified with a keyboard. - At one point enemies all disappeared, including the boss. Then it softlocked when we beat him.- Bosses repeat the same attack over and over, rarely doing one of their other attacks. Some can also get completely stun locked when ganged up on.- Difficulty doesn't properly scale for player numbers. The game was incredibly easy with 3 players on Normal. When I tried single player, it seemed like the exact same number of enemies. Because of this, the achievements are much easier to get in multiplayer (which is sadly local only at the moment, but they said it's coming in a free update)Because of these issues, I'd recommend waiting before picking it up unless you really can't wait.
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a beat em up vet. I love the resurgence of the genre lately and have poured a decent amount of hours in all the new games. I was greatly looking forward to this game as I was a huge fan of GI Joe as a kid. The trailers made this seem basically like Shredder's Revenge with the GI Joe license. I can tell you it is not. Gameplay is boring. I scored more damage with the light attack combo than the hard attack single move even charged up, and the heavy attacks need to be faster. Too much delay. I ended up just not bothering with them. The special moves are worthless in some cases (snake eyes' special just useless). There's no way to earn an extra life (as is the case in most of these games). Enemy difficulty is way off balance.The boss fights are too easy even on the hardest difficulty. I had more trouble with basic enemies (looking at you blue scythe throwers). You can cheese the bosses by trapping them in a corner and spamming light attack or flat out stunlocking them with combos. They're not programmed to have "get away" moves if you cross their hitbox (like Shredders Revenge or most competent beat em ups).The levels feel half baked. Certain levels have what appear to be secret areas or even elevations to them, and in some cases it appears that you CAN go into these areas (shipping containers on level 4) but nothing happens and nothing's there. The glitches are beyond annoying. While doing coop play with a friend, one of our characters just stopped animating, refusing to take inputs. Unplugging the controller and reconnecting it fixed it for a moment but it happened again a few screens later in the level. On another level, after we defeated the boss, the game soft locked on the victory screen and never took us to the next level.The quality is low. Voice Acting is atrocious. The animated cutscenes are low-tier Newgrounds quality level. The audio mix on the cutscenes is +12db over the rest of the game. The music is uninteresting. This all just feels like it was either rushed or licensed to the lowest bidder so Hasbro could take advantage of the retro nostalgia beat em up boom. They saw TMNT Shredders Revenge and decided to half-a$$ a release to cash in.I refunded and used the money to buy Iron Meat. Mmm well done Contra-likes...
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I think it is a fun game and I am recommending it.But yes, it has flaws. To start with, we are looking at an old school beat'em up. It doesn't bring anything new or interesting to the genre: this game could have been released in the early 1990s. Recent games like Shredder's Revenge and Double Dragon Gaiden did much better to bring interesting twists to a classic beat'em up style.  There is a bit of replayability however; many game modes that provide alterations to the game can be unlocked by collecting floppies. It takes a ton though; you will most definitely not unlock everything on a given day.But the controls are responsive, and I have no issue with the gameplay. There is enough variety and stages considering the price. Some enemy units do seem a bit overtured. The Cobra Ferret ATV comes to mind. But overall, it is a solid game.I think it is a great game to enjoy with some friends, especially if you are nostalgic of the early 90s and GI Joe. Otherwise, there are better titles in this genre to pick up first.
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

_childDocuments_.review: Not as deep or as polished as Fight N Rage, SOR4, Final Vendetta, Shredder's Revenge, and Mayhem Brawler, but we are living through the Second Golden Age of Beat 'em ups and we are spoiled for choice.The one thing the game has going for it is it has the GI Joe vibe down pat, but beyond that it's a very mediocre beat em up in most regards. Buy it on a deep discount for nostalgia trip, but I can't see many people logging a ton of hours here because there's just many more satisfying beat em ups out there to be played. I wish I could give it a neutral recommendation, and I don't really like leaving negative reviews, so let's call it a tentative recommendation on a 75% discount.
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay isn't bad. The concept isn't bad either. But the big issue is how buggy the game is.The discs I collected didn't add up by the end of level 4. Not only that, but I couldn't progress and had to turn off the game, then turn it back onBy level 5, I made it to a coliseum like area and I literally couldn't progress. I was soft locked into a position where no progress could be made and I couldn't move forward.
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

_childDocuments_.review: I just don't really understand so many of the decisions made for this game.I'm going to go into spoilers about the "story" and such below, so if you just want my opinion..  If you are a fan of G.I. Joe there is fun to be had here, especially if you have another friend who is into G.I. Joe as well.  If you are a fan of the beat em' up genre and coming off Shredders Revenge, or Streets of Rage 4 and are looking for the next good side scrolling beat em' up.. This isn't it.There is fun to be had if you are a Joe fan.  I certainly haven't laughed as hard as I laughed at this game for a long time. My friend and I are eager to play it again. It was worth the $22 I paid for it. I probably got $22 of enjoyment out of it. But I Probably wouldn't have gotten that same enjoyment without another G.I. Joe loving friend near me.  My kids who love Shredder's revenge didn't like this game.  My Joe loving friend and I talked about this as I write this review and we feel satisfied for $22, but if this was not attached to the G.I. Joe IP then $22 would have felt like way too much.  It's not even a good "mediocre" beat em' up.  I really don't understand why you'd bother putting in the effort with the G.I. Joe license.. I don't get why this company released a demo over 6 months ago got a bunch of feedback and changed absolutely nothing about it.  It took my friend and I about 2 hours to beat the game.  We're probably going to go back try to beat the harder modes unlock everything but after that.. I don't know I don't see coming back to this like I do Shredders Revenge or SoR.	In the end.. For the Joe fan.. It's probably "good enough," but the honest truth is this game isn't going to pull in any beat em' up fans into sticking around to check out G.I. Joe later.. Which is such a shame.. Because this was a chance to make something truly special here and someone either the devs or Hasbro or both failed the fans.  Unfortunately, this means the best G.I. Joe game remains the NES games or the 2015 fan game attack on cobra island.You can read a FULL review here:
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the best GI Joe games out there, though if you're not a fan of arcadey beat 'em up experiences, probably not for you.Pros: In-Game art direction is well done, the characters all play very differently and are fun to experiment with. Nice and short experience for the price, great replay-ability, and the backgrond music is an absolute bop.Cons: While I can tell what they were going for with the opening cinematic, the animation just...doesn't work for me.
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

_childDocuments_.review: Don't fall for the nostalgia baitOf all these new wave of beat'em ups, G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra is the most painfully meh. It doesn't do anything to elevate the genre. It's the most bare bones, basic game possible. The game has no story (EDIT: apparently, the game has a story. There are a few cutscenes that play, but for some reason they didn't play for me on first playthrough, maybe because I changed the language to brazilian portuguese. Either way, it doesn't matter much because the game always softlock after a cutscene, so I have to skip it anyway), no stage transitions, no alternative paths. Characters have different stats but play very similarly. Stages don't offer much in terms of variety, and boss battles are laughable, they barely put up a fight. After beating the last boss it just jumps straight to the credits, and you feel like you accomplished nothing. There is an "extras" session where you can buy stuff like new modes and characters, but after beating the game once I still couldn't afford anything, so they really want you to grind for it. Another thing that should be mentioned, the game is plagued with bugs. More than once I had to restart the game cause it softlocked after a cutscene, and if you don't play the game in English, the text won't fit the dialog box, and is presented on a very ugly font that doesn't fit the game at all. Overall, feels like a very amatour work. You may think it is worth it for a good for a nostalgic trip and some laughs with friends, and to be honest it can serve this purpose, but G.I. Joe deserved better. Makes me angry to see good IPs being exploited for a quick buck like this.
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

_childDocuments_.review: It´s not the game Gijoe deserves, but It still manages to not soil Its legacy, and I respect that.Its just ok, playable, enjoyable to a certain point, but not as smooth and satisfying as should be.Anyway I have to rate this game positively because the OST is fantastic and the game itself scratches some nostalgia itches.I suggest supporting It if you are a Gijoe fan. Its a start. Functional. I think the developers could do more if they improve the whole gameplay, for example the attack animations of enemies should be a bit more complex so counters and parry are a viable strategy, and not just a blurry blink so frustrating.Anyway, I recommend playing with Snake Eyes, its just the most satisfying character.
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

_childDocuments_.review: The game is the worst beat em-up I've ever played on Steam. Shame on the game developer for releasing a buggy mess of a game. Dumb design choices and overall a bland game. I beat it but I had to force myself to just because I didn't want my money wasted. Never buy a game on impulse like I did before reading the reviews and for those interested in buying it - don't because "knowing is half the battle".
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

_childDocuments_.review: I was hyped for this game and I had a blast so far. Nice little time waster for sure. I am, however, not a huge fan of the new theme, or the janky animation. The voice acting is also laughable. But, once inside the game, it is a nice retro brawler that has a lot to offer. I may be wrong, but I don't remember hearing anything resembling the classic theme in the soundtrack of the game. That is very disappointing. Anyways, regardless of my nostalgia nitpicks, the game-play is solid. I do recommend it if you are looking for a fun side-scrolling experience much in the vain of old titles like Turtles in time and such.Update: I have passed the 2 hour refund play time and plan on playing more. I am using this game to relax. The differences in character play-style is great. My main concern is how much currency you get per stage being rather small. For a player like me, it's not that big an issue, but to a casual player, it might be a bit daunting to get the unlockable content. Just a thought to the devs.UPDATE: Be careful about some of the reviews. I have caught a number of them lying or misrepresenting the game.
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a huge G.I. Joe fan, you may like it. If you are a huge fan of beat em ups, and don't care from G.I. Joe, you will probably be disappointed. It is a mediocre beat em up. Each character has a different special attack, and move sets. Blocking negates 100% of damage, with a 'perfect parry' system, or whatever you want to call it when you block just before the attack hits. The animations look amateurish and the sounds/music aren't from the cartoon. The level themes are enemy types are from the old cartoon, and that is fun to see the old vehicles in the background and stuff. I appreciate that the character designs are as they were back in the day, and not some unrecognizable redesign.
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I wanted a more of a SOR,  TMNT beat em up, but this is ok. It's fun, graphics are great, but just needs a little more. I did have some bugs I hope get fixed when fighting, for instance there was a boss fight where I couldn't damage them at all. But is it worth it, sort of, I wish there was more GIJoe sounds and music. I don't understand why all the guys explode into machine parts only the B.A.T's were robots. But this does scratch a certain old school itch, I played with so many of these toys, watched so many of the cartoons, read so many of the comics and books, I just wanted a little bit more.
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

_childDocuments_.review: I really like beat 'em ups, and especially ones that are based on properties that were popular during my childhood. This one is not so great. Hit detection is rough, controls are a little too simple and twitchy, and enemies have that traditional quarter munching behavior with several being ranged attack spammers that come in swarms. It's not an incompetent game but it's definitely one that has way too many rough edges when we have modern versions of these types of games like Streets of Rage 4 and TMNT Shredder's Revenge to compare it against.By stage 8 I found myself aggravated there were 4 more levels to go for an ending and the possibility of character unlocks, at which point I also realized I didn't care to keep going to the end for character unlocks. This isn't a bad game necessarily, but it's pretty mediocre in the genre and isn't especially high on the nostalgia angle since out of a veritable toybox of options, you'll fight about a dozen enemy types.  People have been asking for a middle option for games between yes/no recommendation and that is specifically for games like this.
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I love G.I. Joe, this game just isn't all that fun in its present state. Snake Eyes is the only decent character out of the main 4, but you can unlock a few more later on if you have the patience to do so, along with other unlockable options. Maybe those extra characters or options make the game more fun but i don't think I have the patience to find out.The game does have some glitches right now where some of the bosses just slow down completely. If you encounter this issue, try doing a jump kick at them to speed things up again. Levels seem to take about 10 minutes to clear on average and there are 12 of them. On some of these levels you'll probably expect certain enemies to show up but will be greeted with the same enemies from previous one. There was a chance to really showcase all the different Cobra troops but it's not to be unfortunately.I guess the other nostalgic beat'em up games have spoiled us to the point that this game just feels like a chore. The best part of this game was the animated homage to the cartoon.
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

_childDocuments_.review: The game captures the property of GI Joe in only so much as the characters go. The game itself is buggy such as getting stuck in midair and can't complete a level. The boss design is lack luster for a beat 'em up. The overall quality of this game leaves much to be desired. Do not pick this up at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

_childDocuments_.review: Yo Joe?No. It's "So-So Joe!"As a 90s brawler style it is not bad, but doesn't have a whole lot of options to it. There are two attacks and a special, and three hit combos...but nothing really more than that. If you love brawlers and just bashing things to death...or a fan of GI Joe, I am sure you will get enjoyment. But if you don't check those boxes...there are better fighters out there.The art style in the story isn't exactly the 80s style that most fans feel comfortable with and love. It is a mix of old style and modern cartoons. Just wanted to get that out if that is a big deal to you.I like the weapon use. Guns aren't new in brawlers, but there is a good assortment of them in this. However when the enemies have weapons, it can be frustrating. There really aren't invincibility frames when hit, so it is very easy to get knocked around back and forth with no way to prevent it.But I will say, for what it comes with....the price might asking too much. I would recommend a sale of at least $20 or less before picking it up.....unless you have friends handy that are down to plow through it a few times to unlock everything. I recommend it, but only on sale....and only when you have burned yourself out of all the other great ones out there. This one is priced like Shredder's Revenge...and as much as it sounds like beating a dead horse....SR is better.
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

_childDocuments_.review: Glitch, buggy, boring. Even as a GiJoe fan, it's not worth it. No rewards as thr 'extras' are not only expensive but not worth the grind. No replay value. Sometimes I got stuck in the background. Watching a cutscene always results in a hard game freeze which you have to exit the game. On top of all that very imbalanced levels and bosses. Somebody can literally stand in one spot and spam 1 button. Skills are useless, your characters don't evolve, don't get additional lives as items or as score rewards and for some reason they ran out of ideas for bosses so they use dark versions of the good guys 🤷‍♂️
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

_childDocuments_.review: It's an okay beat 'em up game. But not quite as polished as SoR or Shredder's revenge. Had fun playing it in co-op. If you want to unlock new play modes or characters you better get used to some grinding. There were also a few bugs.Not quite wort the full price. I recommend waiting till it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

_childDocuments_.review: So excited this game is finally out! For fans of 80's nostalgia, this is a can't miss. I played through it all on Steam and really enjoyed seeing the different bosses and fun animation with tons of Joe and Cobra bits represented through enemies and background easter eggs.Although not as deep as Shredder's Revenge, I still had a blast playing and am doubly looking forward to online co-op being added in. A few things stood out such as base enemies taking many levels before variety was added in, no way to earn extra lives while playing, and some enemies being just way too tedious and unforgiving (I'm looking at you teal ninjas and the Cobra Quads).Not sure if there was a problem with cut scenes and an ending (rumblings in the forums about it being a bug when using controller) but it was quiet in between levels. As an older gamer that leans more towards "pop-in" games than mega hour excursions, this really lived up to my year long hype!
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

_childDocuments_.review:
Cobra rears its ugly head yet again and it's up to G.I. JOE to save the world! Embracing the 1980s era of the iconic universe, Wrath of Cobra is a retro side-scrolling beat 'em up. Play as one of the legendary G.I. JOE characters, including Duke, Scarlett, Roadblock, Snake Eyes, and more. Defeat hordes of Cobra troopers, Vipers, Crimson Guards and more of Cobra's malevolent machinations.

Bring Cobra down, striking back at the likes of Destro, Serpentor, Baroness, and Cobra Commander himself! Fight your own way: Rely on your fists and get up close and personal using each character's unique combos and special moves or keep your foes at a distance with a variety of weapons!
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Wrath of Cobra

name: The Legend of Legacy HD Remastered
detailed_description: The Legend of Legacy HD Remastered Purchase Options About the Game RPG fans rejoice as the classic adventure, The Legend of Legacy is remastered in HD and debuting on Steam! INTRODUCTION Many have come, seeking riches, glory, and legendary treasure, but in the end, they all vanish, swallowed up by the darkness. None have seen into the heart of this island, now awakened from its eternal slumber—the mythical land known as Avalon. Do its depths hide a stairway to paradise or the gates to the abyss? This is the tale of some yet unknown truth, spun from the legacies of the ancient gods. HD REMASTER'S FEATURES Beautifully improved graphics and image quality shine in HD! The new guidebook function makes it easy for newcomers to get started, and the addition of detailed functions allow all players intuitive gameplay options and ease of access. KEY POINTS Explore a world map bursting with story-book charm. When characters move, the surrounding terrain springs to life like a pop-up picture book. Grow your adventure with each step you take and discover more of the map. As your character moves, the map will be drawn and filled in. This unique feature is called Cartograph. Legend of Legacy features seven main characters and limitless adventures! Choose from one of the seven characters to lead your adventure and challenge the legend of Avalon! Legend of Legacy features no set route in the story allowing players the ability to fully and freely control their destinies. Join forces with the spirits of Avalon to harness the elemental attributes of the battlefield and overcome mighty enemies! The Fusion World View System by Kyoji Koizumi, creator of multiple innovative battle systems, allows players a unique and exciting combat experience. In addition there are four types of spirits–water, wind, fire, and darkness. Compete with your foes to claim the elementals’ power and dominate the battlefield. Players can also utilize spirit arts by making contracts with spirits during battle. When used, the power of a spirit and the associated technique will gain strength allowing you to decimate powerful enemies. This struggle for power is performed simultaneously with a single command, called a Two-Dimensional Battle. The sound design of Legend of Legacy shines with a BGM that pursues quality game music with thoughtfully created environmental sounds that spare no attention to detail. Wind, waves, monster cries, changes in footsteps, and echoes within buildings can all be clearly heard in an effort to enhance your experience within the vast expanse of the world! The music was created with the goal of expressing emotions, touching heartstrings, and engraving to memory a one-of-a-kind RPG experience. Legend of Legacy HD Remastered brings classic RPG charm with new and exciting twists to the HD era! With vast gameplay options, thoughtful sound design and beautiful music this RPG adventure is a must add to your wishlist!

name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster
detailed_description: Digital Deluxe *The contents of this pack are also sold individually. Please be careful not to buy the same content twice. Contents: - Main Game - Costumes & BGM: Willamette Parkview Mall Pack - Costumes & BGM: Resident Evil Heroes Pack - Costumes & BGM: Resident Evil Villains Pack - Costumes & BGM: Mega Man Pack - Costumes & BGM: Capcom Fighters Pack *Costumes can be changed at the closet in the Security Room in the game. *BGM can be changed via 'Change Mall BGM' on the Options screen. About the Game Dead Rising returns with modern graphics! More than just a remaster, this Deluxe Remaster is a full graphical overhaul of the first game in zombie-slaughtering action game series 'Dead Rising.' This remaster has also been fully voiced, supports auto-saves, and has various other quality-of-life features. Witness the unmatched mayhem and freedom for yourself! - Story: One day, the peaceful town of Willamette, Colorado, found itself put under quarantine by the U.S. army. Frank West, a freelance journalist, smells a scoop and finds his way into the only shopping mall in town. Unfortunately, the mall had turned into a living hell, crawling with countless zombies. Help will arrive in 72 hours, so it's up to him to find out the truth behind this incident before it's too late! - Realistic graphics reborn through RE ENGINE! All of the graphics, including the characters and environments, have been renewed, and greatly improved over the original. Character's facial expressions, material textures, and blood spatter all look much more realistic. Overwhelming hordes of zombies fill the screen with completely remade graphics! - Smoother and friendlier to play! The gameplay of the original remains intact, but there are various quality-of-life improvements, such as auto-saving, revamped controls, improved UI, and many other details. The game is now also fully voiced for improved immersion. - Spend 72 hours the way you want! The game takes place in a giant shopping mall. Use regular weapons like guns and baseball bats, or use daily household objects. Anything goes when it comes to survival! Rescue other survivors, and try out some new clothes while you're at it. Just remember that under these extreme circumstances, it's not just zombies, but psychopaths you'll have to deal with as well. Who poses the biggest threat, zombies or humans!?

_childDocuments_.review: This is overall a great way to experience dead rising 1, but there are a few caveats I personally wouldn't call these deal-breakers though.Pros:-Visuals (duh)-Better controls-Weapon durability is more easily visible-Survivor AI has been reworked and are much more co-operative, with some added mechanics for extra flavour-Can fast-forward the timer in the safe room- You can move while shooting- Several books have been reworked to be more useful- Can change clothes in the safe room as long as you’ve picked up these clothes in the shop beforehand, you also aren’t locked into an animation when picking up clothes- All survivor interactions (and Otis) have voice acting now- Otis is a lot less annoying- Thomas can be spared, albeit he can't be rescued- The mini-chainsaws have been nerfed, which helps to slightly counterbalance how much easier the game is now.- All of the licensed music has been preservedCons:- There’s no longer an indicator for when survivors are able to enter a new area- A lot of censorship, and the erotica tag for photos has been removed- The voice acting is worse across the board- No option of a classic mode with reduced PP gain and disabled auto-saving.Listing cons like this may make them seem worse than they actually are, but overall I do recommend this remake. I imagine mods will fix a number of these issues.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: After fixing my performance issues I gotta say, I've been extremely addicted to this remaster, its super fun, super investing, the graphics are not in the same level as Dragons Dogma 2 or RE4 remake but, if this is the way Capcom wants to handle remastering games they are not so sure about making a full Remake for I'm super down to see more.8.8 out of 10!

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster could have gone wrong, in many ways but luckily the creators of this remaster admire the original as much as it's fans do. The inclusion of so many of the game's positives without basically any of the annoyances of the original mean that it's a game that is essentially Dead Rising 1 but more of what you love and almost spotless of what you don't. It's a great stepping on point for series newcomers or people who have never tried the original and a great romp if you're a veteran. I'll be reviewing this from my own personal standpoint as a returning player, you might not get some of this as a newbie.Dead Rising was infamous for it's difficulty at certain spikes during the game and while some can be mitigated some were serious pain points either left completely out of your control, due to the eccentricities of it's control scheme, the first person camera aiming when using ranged weapons and a mix of all of the above in regards to the game's boss fights. All have been dealt with. Aiming in Dead Rising 1 is no longer a complete pain in the ass, it took us 18 years folks but we finally did it! You can even auto aim if you aren't directly aiming, which acts as a good way of giving you some space from you and some annoying zombies. The control scheme has been revamped and it's a generally much more approachable game from that standpoint. You can opt for classic controls if you really want that, which for veterans with muscle memory.. it's appreciated but i found the newer controls better than the originals even if it took brainhacking my mind to do so.  Holy god, i need to talk about survivors. They aren't perfect but we've finally done it boys. They actively do not constantly get into trouble or constantly do the most hairbrained things imaginable. They aren't a complete nightmare to ferry around the mall, unless you make it that way. 8 Survivors and a tight corridor come to mind. I have never been so happy to set a set of stairs in my entire life as i had when i stepped out the saferoom as a veteran of the first. There is a new mechanic with character affinity and their AI working better with some weapons as opposed to others but it's very barebones and the can give some unintentionally hilarious dialogue when they try to point out something useful as you're swamped in a zombie horde. Yeah, i think i'll live without getting that 5k pp bonus photo shoot you just mentioned while we're surrounded by ZOMBIES TRYING TO RIP US APART. Nevertheless, the changes to survivors is appreciated like capcom offered me a cold glass of water on a hot day.Boss Fights in Dead Rising 1 were just simply ballbusters unless you came prepared with good weapons and with forward knowledge or had simply been through the raw pain of beating them before. They have been slightly nerfed, at least some of them have and progressively get more difficult as you get through the game. Probably a good idea of onboarding players  instead of throwing them at early game bosses that usually were the bane of early players existences. A single boss has had a significant redesign and frankly, it's actually leagues better than the original game. If you're a vet, you'll know who when you run up on them.The original game has seriously shown it's age in recent years and while we got a re-release that did give some of the older graphics a bit more life. It does look dated. Deluxe Remaster gives it a massive new breath of life, some areas have a flair that wasn't there before. The game just looks way way better and at the fidelity you can expect from a game nowadays. You can probably nitpick a few things here or there but they are so inconsequential to the overall experience that i think you would have to actively look for them in order to actually notice them. This applies also to the voice acting. I'm going to be honest, i love TJ rotolo's voice acting as Frank West in the originals and his VA's absence is seriously felt here but his replacement Jas Patrick does a fantastic job of projecting the tone of the original. There were seriously times i thought it would be messed up here or there but the performance is a great emulation of rotolos. I warmed up to it quick and i went in pretty unsure off the back of the announcement trailer. The rest of the cast is the same, you can really tell they trained their performances on the original performances. The smaller more subtle inflections are taken into account in the new VA work. The whole game is also voiced, random ass NPC 231? He's not relegated to the phantom zone of text box with no dialogue. He actually has a voice now, i cannot tell you how much my mind melted to hear old man Otis Washington actually speak on the transceiver after being stuck to a text box FOR 18 YEARS!Right, do you have any legitimate critique mr.freakingoutaboutstairs? Yep. An enemy type later in the game. They are a lot more deadly than the original, take them seriously. And use that first person mode and a machine gun like your life depends on it. If you're fighting more than 2, prepare for a bad time. *SPOILER* Mode is too easy and it's solely down to how often and easy it is to find a certain resource as opposed to the original. That's all i'll add to that for risking spoilers.The game has crashing issues, i crashed maybe a total of 3 times but the game aggressively autosaves and i barely lost any progress so that's kinda a boon. I wouldn't recommend the game on weaker hardware right now and if you're paranoid about that maybe wait for awhile so these crashes can be patched out currently.Overall, Capcom has once again knocked it out of the park in regards to it's remasters and i've already established this is perfect for first timers. However there are a few critiques that this Remaster doesn't have a lot of offer a veteran of the series. I disagree, the changes made here are significant and directly effect pacing. Being able to skip time alone kills huge stretches of just.. killing time in the original. I cannot tell you the magic of finding the exact same weapon spawn from 18 years ago, remembered by whoever put it there or wanting to know what Otis Washington would sound like or STAIRS, I DON'T HAVE TO WAIT FOR EVERY SURVIVOR TO SINGLE FILE CLIMB UP A LEDGE. As a fan of the original, it's like christmas morning and i still highly recommend it if you're looking for a replay. You'll get to experience things in a unique way that newcomers will just simply not be able to appreciate and for a good reason. In terms of value, i understand if it's pushing it a little for some people but to me the price was about worth it for what i got out of it as a returning player but you'll get more bang for your buck as a newbie. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? It certainly was one, in 2006. The original Dead Rising from 2006 was supposed to be a successor to the mediocre Shadow of Rome (PS 2). However, after Shadow of Rome was not particularly successful, the developers at Capcom came up with a different setting and relocated the game to the present day and a huge American shopping center. This worked well for George A. Romero's cult classic Dawn of the Dead, and Ubisoft's very first game (Zombie, 1986) also made use of this scenario. Capcom also had a resounding success with it and founded a new series that has four major parts to date. The first part, which was only ported (quite competently) to the PC in 2016, was no longer a graphic marvel. Now there is a much more elaborate remaster that brings the graphics up to a reasonably up-to-date standard. Plus full voice acting, automatic saves - and, above all, lots of new costumes. You can dress up your hero, Frank West, in a variety of really funny costumes right from the start (in the changing room of the shopping center employees). The gameplay is still as fun as the original, but the basic design comes from the PlayStation 2 hit from 2006. Nevertheless, it's still a lot of fun to eliminate tons of zombies in different ways. Be creative in how you dispose of the slow and stupid zombies. The game doesn't really take itself seriously, it's not a horror game but a fun zombie massacre. And it also looks better graphically now!

I don't have any issues with new voice actors, and to be fully honest, the censorship on some voicelines from the original is kinda dumb, but not really a problem at all.Frank's design in Dead Rising 4 was really good, he had a few extra years since DR1 and THAT'S OK!But why is he so old now in Dead Rising 1? It looks as if DR4 Frank travelled back in time to relive his experience at the mall again.Luckly for us, one of the first mods released in Nexus is a Young Frank V2 mod that makes him look PERFECT. So I highly recomend anyone to download that and play with it.Capcom, if you're reading this, consider making Frank look young again, that change alone would make this remaster a 10/10.Anyway, really good work regardless!

_childDocuments_.review: There's a part of me that wishes I could give a "hand laid flat and tilted left and right" rating to this game in particular.I love the Dead Rising games, The first and second entries are extremely fun, with the Off The Record version of Dead Rising 2 being one of my favorite games of all time. (Although a solid chunk of that is definitely sentimental value.) The third one is also a pretty enjoyable ride, even if the psychopath battles are infinitely less inspired than 1 or 2. There was also a fourth one... anyway! Basically what I'm saying is that I'm a big fan of the franchise. I've played through all of them at least twice, and I know what works for me and what doesn't. Needless to say, when they announced a remaster of the first one, I was cautiously excited. I mean, I adore the first one a lot. For 2006, it was damn revolutionary, and more than that a lot of it has held up pretty well gameplay-wise. HOWEVER, there's a lot of stuff that could use a bit of polishing. The hit-stop for blunt weapons is jarring, Overtime mode is both boring AND infuriating, and there are glitches aplenty that could be buffed out. As time passed, we were made aware of some of the censorship done, and if I'm being frank (no, not that Frank), none of it really bothered me much. Like do I think anyone was truly up in arms about the existence of Erotica shots? No. Do I understand why they got rid of them? Yeah, pretty much. Does removing them from the game make the experience worse in any way shape or form? In theory, no, not really. The censorship was kind of the least of my concerns. No, where my concerns were truly placed was the voice acting. Another new voice for Frank West, huh? That didn't pan out so well last time. In fact, it panned out horribly considering Dead Rising 4's Frank West was some kind of Bazinga Quiplord as opposed to a character that was written. At least this dude was just handed the script that T.J. Rotolo read the first time around, giving him more of a fighting chance. Nevertheless, it was still a bad portend, one I firmly ignored due to my love of this franchise and generally questionable financial decisions. I bought this pretty much as soon as it came out, but only got around to finishing it now. How did it shake out? Well...THE GOOD:1. GENERAL FEEL OF COMBATI think the thing this remaster... remake... thing gets right above anything else is how the game feels to play. No longer does the game pause every time you hit someone with a blunt weapon. No, you can actually hit them without it doing that. And Jesus H. Christ if it doesn't feel better than the original in that regard. Combat feels so smooth, and the actual act of mowing down zombies is inherently more satisfying. I struggle to find anything bad to say about the game in that regard.2. SURVIVOR AI*Thanks to the survivors being dumber than a bucket of spit in the original Dead Rising, there were a lot more times where they died due to something that was their own stupid fault. That never happened in this one. They all followed directions, and thanks to the handy introduction of stairs, I didn't have to give myself an aneurysm trying to make them climb the ledge to the safehouse. You might notice the asterisk, and that's for one simple reason: they don't shut up. You could be walking to the safehouse and one of them will chime in with something like "Wow, Frank! Take a picture of that, it looks important! Winkity-wink, nudgity nudge!" like you're too stupid to see the florescent yellow PP sticker on something. That was firmly an unnecessary addition, but it isn't make or break.THE BAD/THE UGLY:1. VOICE ACTINGThe voice acting in the original Dead Rising wasn't Oscar-worthy or anything, but it had infinite charm, and T.J. Rotolo's performance as Frank West is iconic for a reason. He's the perfect voice for Frank West. Campy, yet normal. The voice acting in this remaster is a two pack of ass. Oddly enough, I was somewhat fine with new Frank West by the end of the game, but almost everyone else is an immediate downgrade to the original. Lines are delivered with the conviction of an elementary school play. Intonation all around is awkward, and only some of the new blood does their job correctly. (major props to the voice actor for Sean Kennan for bringing the perfect amount of PS2-era camp to his lines. I have nothing but praise for his performance.) It's just an absolute shame, if I'm being honest.2. AI-UPSCALED TEXTURESMuch like the disastrous texturework done in the Definitive Edition GTA games, a lot of the texture work in this is AI upscaled. The thing about compression is that AI doesn't know how to decompress things sometimes. Leading to absolute nonsense textures sometimes. Whether it be faces, text, or general outlines, you're sure to find plenty of mistakes if you're looking for them. A prime example is the sign in the CD store in the Entrance Plaza that simply reads "NEW RELEASRS" [sic] It's extremely disappointing to see, especially considering how they made entirely new character models but couldn't be made to give a single damn about the texturework. 3. CENSORSHIP CHOICESNow, I already stated my stance on the Erotica category. I think removing it removes nothing... from the gameplay. It's an entirely different story for making Kent look like more of a creep. Having him change from saying "and this... heh... this is my  shot." to "and this... heh... this is my  shot." removes a lot from making him seem not all there. I mean the dude was shooting creepshots of women in the middle of the literal actual apocalypse. If he's just taking goofy pictures of zombies in hats, there's not really much danger. Generally odd choices are made in the censorship of psychopaths in general. Cliff is no longer a Vietnam vet with PTSD going on insane paranoid rants about the Viet Cong, he's just some guy who was in some non-specific war calling you a non-specific mole. What the hell made him crack then? It's nothing truly dealbreaking, but messy replacements like that are just sprinkled throughout. 4. DIFFICULTYNow, I don't think the first Dead Rising is always fair difficulty-wise. I think it's less unforgiving difficulty-wise than a lot of people suggest, but there are parts that make me want to rip off my wang with the other side of a hammer. You may expect this section to be me complaining about how easy it is now, but it's only HALF about that. No, there are parts that are a little too easy now. I think I only died to a psychopath once, and as where the  fights at the end of Overtime Mode were entirely unfair in the original, they took me less than 3 minutes to beat in this new version. HOWEVER, the special forces you fight in Overtime Mode are unforgiving now, often getting you stuck in a loop of getting shot to death, where reloading is preferable to the "Frank West Escapes" QTE where you lose everything. It's a lopsided dichotomy. They didn't balance anything, and so it just feels annoying to play.5. GENERAL PERFORMANCE AND CRASHINGFor reference: I'm running on a GTX 1080 with 16GB of RAM. This is a rig that can run most modern games without breaking much of a sweat. This game ranges from running at 144 FPS to 35 at any given moment. This is on any setting configuration. It also has a fun habit of crashing, which consistently happened when I tried to get the generator to Isabela. Needless to say, this soured the mood quite a bit. There have also been no updates since release so... cool! Thanks!BOTTOM LINE:I enjoyed my time here... kind of. I think there's a lot this remaster does right in the actual realm of gameplay. However, there are a lot of things keeping me from wholeheartedly recommending this to anyone who wants to play Dead Rising. In my opinion, wait for a sale or play the original. This one needed a bit more time in the oven.

_childDocuments_.review: The ambiance of zombie moans being extremely quiet/basically mute and the fact that they noticeably ignore you and other survivors more often are the only things that really, truly bother me.  Otherwise, this game definitely feels like a worthwhile experience especially if you're a fan of the original, with new voice actors, higher quality model work, different and easier to understand gameplay elements, and higher quality environments across the entire game.Much of the 'issues' people have been getting hopped up on only really boils down to three things: a minor dialogue change to one boss, the removal of "Erotica", and the change of a late-game boss design.  I admit I was a bit worried some other stuff might have changed, but I can confidently tell you that everything else remains the same.  The characters are the same, the story is the same, the layout is the same.  None of the changes are detrimental or world-ending to the overall experience.Totally a good time, and plenty of potential hours to sink into it if you want to see and get everything over multiple playthrough.  I would still recommend that you try the original at some point too, as I believe it ultimately posseses a different identity from this version.

_childDocuments_.review: Its the same great game from 2006, just with a few added bells and whistles. As is the case with Capcom's recent remakes, the game is both easier and harder than the original. Its difficult to describe. A lot of the more frustrating elements from the original game have been either removed entirely or toned down to make them more tolerable (survivor AI being chief among them). The bosses and military soldiers towards the end of the game are a lot tougher now and will kill you very quickly if not properly prepared.The ability to fast-forward the in-game clock is honestly such a game changer. It adds to the fast pace the game has and once you know what you're doing, it cuts out a bunch of downtime. I do have some minor gripes with the game, mainly the sound design in some areas (voice work is fine. guns sound strangely weak when compared to the original game). There were also a handful of odd visual bugs I kept noticing as I played, but nothing to really ruin the experience.One of the greatest zombie games of all time has straight up just been made better and I cannot applaud Capcom enough for it. I only hope Dead Rising 2 gets similar treatment down the road.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a 1:1 remake of the original. As someone who loves the 360 original and the 2016 PC port, this is about as faithful as you could ask for.The only big difference is the lack of returning voice talent. I find it strange that they made shot for shot remakes of the original cutscenes while giving the entire cast new voices. Why not take the chance to rework the scenes a bit? If not that, why not just use the original voices or give us an option to? They clearly still exist in the 2016 game. That all said, it's worth noting that EVERY line in the game is now voiced, including Otis on the radio and all the other survivors. It's a nice bit of polish the original lacked, but the survivors getting to spout off about things while escorting them is mostly unwelcome. This character just sobbed to me about how she watched her daughter be eaten by zombies, but then halfway back to the Security Room she says 'lol at least i have something that will finally go viral on social media!'.The game is also slightly censored, notably in the way 'Erotica' is no longer factored into photos taken. Most of the points I got from that classification were incidental anyways, so the game doesn't really feel lacking without it. Otherwise, the graphics, gameplay and quality of life, atmosphere and overall fun factor is at it's best here. It's hard not to recommend it to fans of the original or someone wanting an offbeat open world adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: Very much a "warts and all" style of remake, for better or worse.The original came out in 2006, and this game absolutely still plays like a game that is 18 years old (holy crap, I'm old). Luckily, Dead Rising is a really solid game at its core. Unluckily, this also means that it feels extremely barebones by even the standards of Dead Rising 2, and very little actual content was added other than a few quality of life changes, like advancing time in safe rooms and being able to skip Otis calling you on the phone instead of just answering it and waiting for a zombie to chew out your childhood memories. No new non-DLC clothing options, the mall is the exact same, no new boss fights or game modes, no new weapons or skills. This is, effectively Dead Rising from the Xbox 360 with a new coat of paint and still has most of the issues that the original had. Bosses and special forces enemies can still stunlock you to death, the machete and small chainsaw are still violently overpowered (although the small chainsaw was nerfed slightly, it's still busted), the majority of weapons are still gimmicky (as in, there is no reason to beat a zombie to death with a bench unless it's just to be funny, so if you're actually trying to live, you're going to be relying on hunting knives, katanas, and psychopath weapons, just because they're strong and easy to get), the missions can still refuse to show up because Otis just decided he doesn't feel like calling you about them, and the survivors are still dumb as a bag of hammers and will regularly forget to follow you if you aren't mashing the FOLLOW ME, OVER HERE button like you have Type 3 Diabetes and that's the only way to get your insulin.But, like I said before, the jank of Dead Rising is kind of part of the charm, and it is interesting to see a game with 360 era game design choices copy-pasted into the modern day with very few changes. If you're like me and enjoy Dead Rising for what it is, then this is Dead Rising and it'll tickle that nostalgia part of your brain that makes you think that Grabbed By The Ghoulies still holds up. If you feel like the franchise is overrated or that the original is clunky and kind of annoying, then DRDR isn't going to change your mind.Short version: Do you like Dead Rising? Buy it. Do you dislike Dead Rising? Don't buy it. Have you never played Dead Rising? Pick up Dead Rising 2, play that, then answer the previous questions.

_childDocuments_.review: In a world where remasters are usually garbage, I'm glad to say this one was done very well!During my 27 hours of playing, the game ran smooth with very minimal issues. I can only hope that the team who remastered this will work on a remaster for Dead Rising 2 next. I recommend this to anyone who is a fan of the series or anyone who just likes zombie games!

_childDocuments_.review: It's faaaaaaaaaaantastic! Incredible refresher of one of Capcom's best games. There's minor things you could nitpick about when it comes to changes from the original, but for the most part it's the game you remember but with way more detailed graphics and tighter gameplay. In particular I'm really happy that the survivors are just a bit smarter and less prone to getting stuck in random places, that was always one of my biggest problems with the original. I was worried about the new voice cast but for the most part they're all great, I'm especially impressed with the new voice for Frank as I never thought someone could live up to TJ Rotolo's performance, but Jas Patrick does a phenomenal job. Still sad that no one from the OG cast returned, but at least what we have here mostly sounds great.Whether you're a fan of the original or someone who's always been curious about Dead Rising, the Deluxe Remaster is very much worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster is truly something special. I'm glad CapCom decided to take a childhood favorite of mine and give it the remaster it deserved 18 years later. There is something about the first Dead Rising that made it special among the others. It wasn't overly complicated and the appeal of characters and the mall had a nostalgic feeling that it left with me since the release in 06'. With the use of the RE Engine, the deluxe remaster has breathed new life into the game with everything feeling smooth, crisp, and clean. From the controls and audio improvements, To the visuals of characters and atmosphere of the mall, Everything is fantastic. _childDocuments_.review: I love the original Dead Rising, and I was incredibly excited when this "Deluxe Remaster" was announced...and it delivered, big time.I already find the original to be quite enjoyable, however I understand that it can feel more...foreign to a modern audience, this remaster adds the QOL improvements to make the game more fitted for the modern gaming space, while leaving in options in case players want something more akin to the original experience from 2006. The graphics, as expected, look absolutely gorgeous. I already thought the original game looked pretty good, but the remake looks amazing. The new facial animations especially brings new life into these characters, especially Frank. The lighting and textures look absolutely beautiful as well. In terms of audio, all the music from the first game is here, licensed and all, plus some extra tracks to play in the mall if you buy the DLC, so the game is still a champ in the music department. I found the voice acting though...to be a little hit or miss. Some voice lines sound really good, while others...honestly sound terrible, it's a very mixed bag.I don't have many issues this this remaster, my only cons being the sometimes less than amazing voice acting, and some of the bosses and enemies (looking at you Special Forces) are far more obnoxious than in the original, which makes auto saves an absolute GOD SEND.Overall, this is a really fun, enjoyable remaster that I think will succeed in catering to both old fans and new comers alike. Hopefully we get a deluxe remaster of DR2, because the team behind this one knew what they were doing. Excellent job, Capcom!

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine screaming because you don't get trivial exp for being a pervert IRLTL;DR As a long time DR1 fan I'll literally never play the original again. Please remake 2 PLEASE.Survivor AI is better, but swung into the opposite direction with survivors going far out of their way to commit suicide via unarmed combat. Survivors still get stuck constantly but they can sort of jump now so that's cool. Saint is monumentally easier because ANY AI that's functionally different than the original is an upgrade. FFS we had better AI a decade before DR1 released, even by 2006 standards it was a disgrace.Survivors must be armed in order to secure your sanity, any unarmed survivor will run meters away from the group (slowly) to spend 5+ seconds winding back to shove a zombie, over and over dealing next to no damage with the full intent of killing it before moving to Frank or your waypoint. Bosses have been nerfed substantially, but too much since most bosses (especially Carlito encounters) can be oneshot without being able to see all their phases. Backup for Brad no longer feels like you signed up for the 10 man Firelands and everyone else logged out, but he dies in about 1-4 hits. Moving while aiming is GREAT but compounds this issue as boss fights no longer require any intelligent positioning whatsoever and you can bob and weave behind cover in all ranged fights.I find absolutely zero issue with the "Censorship" that a very very small, loud minority is arguing over. Larry Chaing's new model is far more interesting, plus he actually looks like a mall employee, not a slave kept in the butcher's shop. Characters like Jo are just as horny as ever. I saw a thread screaming that Frank no longer has a shirt with a nude woman on it, uhh what else. The whole now has a slightly less revealing outfit. You no longer need to struggle to get an Erotica photo worth 500pp so that's much better, you can turn Kent into a Psychopath just from showing him a picture of a fat man burping instead of Zombussy (best change.)New controls are so much easier than the old ones, it's great to not die over and over because holding the stick doesn't = mashing it for dodge roll spams. Mouse+Keyboard is still the best way to play every DR anyway.New magazines are really fun, the Toy Modding magazine makes toys VIABLE and STRONG, it's a shame there's only Megabuster, Bear, Laser Sword, Frisbee and Ratstick that really get value out of it. Call me a Woke Army Normie, I would have loved a few new items from Dead Rising 2 (especially toys) to synergise with these new mags.I never cared for the Real Mega Buster and the Laser Sword, and getting a REAL reward for the Saint achievement makes it VERY enticing for veteran players looking for new ways to goof off.-Three things that disappoint me is zombie grabs are 100x worse, during the day zombies grab like they're night zombies, and the first frame you gain access to your character out of any i-frame animation you WILL be grabbed if a zombie is within a foot or two. Dodge rolling is very inconvenient since zombies are guaranteed to grab you if you end your anim near one, jumping through zombies no longer works (for the better) and zombies will absolutely grab you out of your attacks (so attacking a group of zombies with a swinging weapon like a bat or the mini chainsaw is a really bad ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ idea?) This means the best strategy for your sanity is beelining to the Juice magazine and filling your inventory completely full of Untouchables every chance you get. Even skateboarding through/over zombies is a risk because the zombie you're heelflipping into will just grab you out of the air and pin you down. Okay but if anything, survivors don't get pinned to death, they're pretty competent running through the map thank god.-Survivor AI is still bad, but bearable. The Cult Leader magazine that empowers survivors is more cult-leader than ever since your survivors just attempt suicide into the largest pack of zombies with their fists and run far away from you to do so. The best strategy for survivors is still to farm King Salmon for them and that's kinda lame.-Survivors don't have any personal space, they constantly kill each other if you have more than 3 in a party. I wanted to get a full party of Shotgun chads but had to end that pipe dream after I got a party of six, had them waypoint to a safe open area and watched them swing their arms around and beat each other nonstop. One of them charged through ALL the survivors and brought them ALL down to half health in one unarmed blow. They just all try and run to the exact waypoint location lmao. If I could have one single balance change, just disable survivor-on-survivor friendly fire. It should not be in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Sure do wish Steam had a neutral/mixed option instead of just flat out yes/no.Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster (DRDR) is a 1:1(ish) remake of Dead Rising 1. Now running on the more modern RE engine instead of the old MT Framework engine. Gameplay wise its *largely* the same though now featuring some pretty neat (and mixed) quality of life features.Starting with the visuals - I really *really* think this is the biggest issue I have with the remake outside of some minor gameplay changes I'll get to later. Visually *at times* the game does look pretty decent, I like the new decor, foliage (interior) and lights scattered across the mall, some character models look pretty good though others didn't fare too well with the modernisation (Frank being the biggest one.) But at the same time, I really REALLY think this game looks worse than the original, lighting's flat, inconsistent, shadows barely work (very noticeable on enemies as 80% of the time shadows will just pop in two feet from you) same for enemies, props and textures. It feels like RE engine's incapable of rendering what they're going for, SF6's world tour mode feels like a technical mess, Dragon's Dogma 2 has a lot of performance issues and the recent patch barely did anything on my end and now DRDR. Either the engine needs some heavy work when it comes to wider, open maps/games, or Capcom just doesn't know how to optimise open-ended experiences well enough through laziness, lack of care, etc. But man, does the game feel super rushed at times - there's a bunch of cutscenes or sections which just look awful - I think the courtyard's some of the worst looking environments I've seen Capcom release in recent memory, the introduction helicopter ride had zombies just popping in out of the blue (so does the main game) and even the entirely new mountain was stuck at what could best be described as 240p. So yeah, visually this 'remake' is a mixed bag and for the most part, I don't like the visuals. Gameplay wise - its DR1.5 but slightly better and worse all at the same time. Improved survivor AI is great, the original is notorious for wonky, annoying and inconsistent friendly AI and for the most part that's solved here. Being able to move and shoot's nice, but... Man do I not enjoy how easy DRDR feels in comparison to the original game, PP gain is increased across the board leading to you getting a lot of buffs early on, Zombies feel far more passive and basically ignore survivors leading to you just being able to run across a zone and never needing to defend your allies which was a key component of the original game, same for autosaves - I get it not everyone likes lost progress but... honestly the original release feels unique because of its silly restrictive nature - the risk reward of making a lot of progress and losing it because you didn't save/didn't want to waste time, zombies easily wiping out your survivors, etc. It made DR1 unique and gave rise to the games popularity, but to me it feels like it dumbs an already easy *version* of the game even further. I ain't going to go on too much more, but gameplay wise I do think some of the QOL changes are great, but I'm not sold on this being a "deluxe remaster/remake" I think Capcom can and should do better because this just isn't it in my opinion. I wouldn't be so bothered if the game was far more visually consistent or included customisable difficulty sliders so I can try and get the original difficulty back.

_childDocuments_.review: The original Dead Rising on the Xbox 360 is one of my favorite games of all time. I played the junk out of it back in 2006 and got all the achievements (except for 7 Day Survivor, unfortunately), so I have a lot of time clocked on that game. The remaster mostly does a good job of recapturing the idiosyncrasies of the original while toning down some of the mechanics that made it punishingly difficult at points.Frank levels up way quicker in the remake so you'll probably see the True Ending on your first run, autosave points are more generous, survivors very rarely get caught by zombies, it seems like the cases are spread further apart or the 72 hour mode goes by slower (not sure which) so there's less pressure and of course you can skip conversations on the radio. All of these are definitely good things for players who are new to Dead Rising. You can still get the OP mini chainsaws with the book combo, so I'm glad they didn't balance the game's more ridiculous weapons when tweaking the difficulty.The game has lots of pop in and the draw distance is short. In my memory, the zombie crowds in the original Dead Rising stretched forever; in the remake you'll often not see the hordes until you're pretty close when they will suddenly appear. Frank's new voice actor is fine and if you don't have a fondness for TJ Rotolo's performance you won't be able to discern too much of a difference.I enjoy that the remaster was mostly able to capture the spirit of the original game while also making minor changes to introduce it to a new audience.And I don't give two hoots that they removed the "Erotic" photo bonus, get a life you perverts (or go play the other remake which is just a straight-up port).

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good but not great. It did not completely satisfy my zombie killing needs. I've been thinking about this game for the past couple weeks and need to vent.I appreciate the quality of life improvements such as, checkpoints when zoning to other areas; the ability to move while aiming with firearms is great; survivors are less stupid and for the most part are easier to escort to the Security Office; weapons feel fluid and good to use; and the game has a fresh coat of paint and generally looks pretty good.As for the bad things about the game: I feel like Capcom again missed the opportunity to make this remaster amazing. I would have liked to have extra game modes like Dead Rising 2: Off The Record which had a sandbox mode with a lot of challenges. Also the first game supposedly had other parts of the town modelled / rendered but it was never used. This would have been awesome to include to have an additional story and to have something more to do.With every good decision Capcom makes, they make an equally baffling one. Like Resident Evil 3 Remake which was short. A lot of people wanted DLC for more to do and they did nothing for some reason. Then there was Resident Evil 4 Remake which was infinitely better, with tons to do and a great DLC. I doubt there will be any DLC story or game modes coming down the line for DRDR.If you're new to the Dead Rising franchise, you're mostly likely going to breeze through this game. Veterans will most definitely get through it faster. I tried to take my time and I beat this game in 3 days, but I could it done in 2. So in closing I would recommend waiting for a sale before picking the game up.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Dead Rising. It's one of the most memorable games I have ever played. This remaster does a great job of bringing this classic game to modern hardware. If you’ve never played the 2006 original I highly recommend this game. My opinion has always been that the first is the best entry in the franchise. Something about the weirdness and jankness of this game comes together in a perfect way that was never replicated in later games. (Although 2 is close.) I also recommend this remaster for fans of the OG. Just having the game run in better fidelity, small upgrades like additional voice acting, and more quality-of-life options make this upgrade worth it for fans.However, there are two main issues I want to point out. First and foremost, why is Capcom determined to change who Frank is a character? Frank's appearance and voice in the OG game are Iconic and are a huge part of the nostalgia for the game. Capcom’s quest to retcon Frank’s character has always been confusing but now feels even more out of place in a remaster of this iconic game. Secondly, game performance is pretty shotty sometimes. It's rarely game-breaking, but there are notable FPS dips while areas and enemies load in. These performance issues point to the new engine being ill-suited for this game or this remaster being a rushed and/or underfunded job. The latter is more likely as proven by a few incomprehensible AI-upscaled signs. It is disappointing and somewhat insulating to this IP and its fans.On a final note let's talk about censorship. They have removed the ‘Erotic’ category of picture scoring. I hate censorship. In the same breath, however, I must say: never did miss this feature. It just simply doesn't matter.I get being against the removal as a principle issue. And if it means that much to you then you’re already not going to buy the game. For new players, they won't miss it. Would you really tell someone not to play this because you can’t laugh at sexy zombie pictures? Like really? Yes, it's funny, and yeah it's a part of what makes the OG quirky, but it’s not important. Preach if you want to preach, play the game if you want to enjoy a game.TLDR: Great game. Note to Capcom: stop being lazy and weird with this IP.

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down the best way to experience a classic game in the modern day.Since the moment I got my hands on it, I have been completely amazed. The game sticks to the original material extremely well, and has an incredible level of detail that was just not possible with the original hardware back in 2006.The graphics are spectacular, the survivor AI changes are spectacular, being able to move while aiming is SPECTACULAR. Even the modest changes to the camera like giving us filters, attachable parts, and adding tilt controls are all amazing additions that don't subtract from the original experience in the slightest.Playing through this remaster has revitalized my love for the original, and has genuinely restored my faith in CAPCOM to do good by this series and make up for the 4th game. This game is definitely worth it if you're a fan of the original, or even if you've never played a DR game before!I'm still working to 100% all of the achievements, but from what I've seen so far- this is by far worth your time and you won't be disappointed.
