_childDocuments_.review: Until they release a patch to fix the rampant crashing in Infinity Mode, I cannot in good faith recommend this game. I shouldn't have to quit out and make backup copies of my save every 12 in-game hours because I can't even get through a full in-game day before hitting a crash.Even the crash reporting tool that comes up when Infinity Mode crashes is very slow and itself prone to crashing and requiring a forced quit via Task Manager.UPDATE: I was also having problems keeping the Infinity Mode rewards in future playthroughs. It's supposed to ask you to save after you die, but it was not giving me that prompt. However, I figured out a work around. Once you unlock the items, ** DO NOT DIE!! ** Instead go into the pause menu and Suspend your game. Then you can start a new 72 Hour Mode game, and you should find your Suspended Infinity Mode save in the list of saves to pull Frank's stats and rewards from.Much like the crashes, I shouldn't have to do work arounds. The game should just work properly. I don't know how Infinity Mode ended up so riddled with problems in this version. Until they release some patches and get all of this mess cleaned up, I cannot recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster? Zombie Mayhem Meets Modern Gaming! (ฅ'ω'ฅ)Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster brings back the iconic zombie-slaughtering mayhem, now rebuilt using the powerful RE Engine. The game takes place in the chaotic Willamette mall, where Frank West, a determined journalist, must uncover the truth behind a zombie outbreak while battling hordes of the undead. With improved graphics, modern controls, and a host of quality-of-life upgrades, this remaster aims to enhance everything that made the original special, while smoothing out some of the rougher edges.Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster preserves the sandbox-style zombie-slaying fun of the original while adding some much-needed modern conveniences. The improved graphics are the most obvious enhancement—textures are sharper, environments more detailed, and the sheer number of zombies on-screen is impressive, adding to the game's chaotic atmosphere. Character models, particularly Frank's, look fantastic, and his wardrobe options feel more varied and responsive than before.The game also overhauls the control system, making combat smoother and more intuitive. The dodge mechanic is now far more useful and survivability has increased due to revamped controls that allow more freedom when using the vast array of improvised weapons. The inclusion of auto-saves, alongside updated UI and controls, reduces the frustration found in the original game, especially during high-tension moments where any misstep could lead to disaster.One of the most notable improvements is the vastly better survivor AI. In the original, escorting survivors was a major source of frustration, as they often got stuck or overwhelmed by zombies. This time, survivors are far more capable of defending themselves and following Frank's lead, making rescue missions much more enjoyable. However, the AI isn't foolproof and still suffers from occasional quirks, such as inconsistent pathfinding and combat decisions.Despite these improvements, not everything is perfect. Technical issues persist, with random crashes and frame drops occurring frequently in areas crowded with zombies, breaking immersion and potentially losing progress. The Infinity Mode, a fan-favorite, has been rendered almost unplayable due to frequent crashes after hours of gameplay, making it impossible to complete in its current state.Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster is a visual and mechanical upgrade to a beloved classic that delivers on its promise of zombie-slaying chaos while improving many of the original's frustrating elements. However, lingering technical issues and some questionable design choices prevent it from being the definitive version. For newcomers, this remaster is the best way to experience Frank West’s bloody mall adventure, while returning players will appreciate the smoother controls and quality-of-life improvements—if they can overlook the game's technical flaws.If you enjoyed this review and want to stay updated on the latest game remasters, be sure to follow our  for more deep dives into gaming classics! _childDocuments_.review: It's a shame that a lot of the discussion about this title is centered around "censorship." If you're still mentally a 13 year old boy in 2006 and can't bring yourself to cope with the fact that the game is not going to reward you for taking a photo of a dead woman's cleavage anymore, then I don't really know what to tell you except go to therapy. The world is changing around you and if you can't adapt like the rest of us do with ACTUAL problems, you look like a mumbling knuckle-dragger, drooling all over yourself and rambling on about "wokeness." No one is interested, go back to playing with blocks or something idk.The game looks great. There is a high attention to detail and the environment feels more alive than it has ever been. It's widely apparent that this is more than just a fresh coat of paint and the hard work the devs put into rebuilding the game should be recognized and appreciated.It feels measurably nicer to play with more intuitive controls once you shake the habits of the original control scheme. However there are still some short-comings in this area, for example having to either take your left thumb off the analog stick and stop moving or use your right thumb and stretch it all the way across the controller just to switch an item in your inventory. Overall, its a major improvement and there is very little to complain about.I've noticed the game is easier in a lot of different aspects. The improved control scheme plays a large part, but there are other things like lower ceilings for achievements and unlockable items that used to take an unnecessary amount of grinding to achieve.Some may complain about this, but it's not an issue for me. The game still poses enough of a challenge to warrant multiple playthroughs if you're trying to get all the achievements. Despite the popularity of the Souls series and the spawn of it saturating the market, not every game needs to a tooth and nail fight for your sanity. It's okay to play video games to unwind. If you liked the original, there's no reason why you shouldn't have a great time with this version.

_childDocuments_.review: If Capcom go on to do more Dead Rising like they have done with this? I'll 100% be there for it.I consider myself a pretty big fan of Dead Rising so when Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster was first shown off, I laughed, got excited and concerned all at the same time. Entirely rebuilt on the RE Engine? Sweet! No TJ Rotolo? (Frank's original VA) I don't like the sound of that. But as time went on and Capcom showed some more footage, excitement took over and I pre-ordered and now after a few playthroughs and close to 100%'ing the game I can safely say I don't regret it one bit and would do it again for Dead Rising 2.DRDR is a weird one to me because it's the only game that comes to mind where I actually can't place where I'd put it in terms of 'Remaster' and 'Remake'. Because it IS essentially the 2006 version converted to a modern engine. All the bells and whistles of the RE Engine while still maintaining the same old story, characters, animations, cutscenes etc.However, that is not the say there hasn't been some changes which seem to have taken a spotlight on the overall talk of the game. A huge spotlight has been cast on the 'negative' changes which I think is a shame because personally I think the positive changes greatly overshadow these.The biggest I've seen is the removal of the 'erotica' photo category that would grant you extra points if you snapped a photo containing things like cleavage or upskirt of Jessie or Cheryl's sexy poses during her side quest. While I always saw the erotica category as something that added to the comical side of the game, I also don't REALLY care all that much that it's now not present. As far as I can tell, the extra points you would have earned are still covered as I think it still accounts for that and these changes didn't alter Jessie's appearance or remove Cheryl's sexy photoshooting quest meaning really all that I can tell that's changed is there are no more pink circles to mark the areas? The other two of note are the changes to Cheryl's dress and the shirt with the nude woman that Frank can wear have now been changed which have already started to see mods restore.Now, in terms of positive changes there are tones of them. Some DR1 purists might not enjoy all of them but I personally am happy with them. Some of the big changes I have noticed are the game now including an optional modernised control scheme (no more accidental dodge rolling!), all dialogue is now completely voice acted, new camera features, PP sticker tracker which I believe wasn't in the first game?, better survivor AI that can assist Frank in finding collectibles and useful items (a lot like the pawns in Dragon's Dogma 2), some small map changes like stairs added to the vent on the rooftop to prevent survivors from getting stuck and an overhaul to the overall theme of Paradise Plaza, some changes to Infinity Mode to make surviving longer a bit easier, the ability to advance time to keep the player in the action rather than stood around waiting needlessly and a better day/night cycle making the mall feel almost welcoming in the day compared to the dark and scary silence at night. There is also an autosave feature which may make the consequences of the players riskier actions less severe but I do appreciate the idea of not having to play catch up every now and then because of the death of either myself or a survivor.And for arguably the biggest change. The voice acting. I think this one is entirely down to the individual. I think TJ Rotolo's performance in the original was one of the biggest factors in what made Frank West such an iconic character. But that isn't to say the new voice actor (Jas Patrick) is bad. Initially I found it quite strange not hearing TJ's voice coming from Frank but it quickly grew on me and I found that it was a refreshing new rendition that also managed to kept Frank feeling like Frank. An example for me was the infamous "I've covered wars, you know." line. I was eager to see how the new voice held up and I was pleasantly surprised to hear it delivered better than I had hoped. As for everyone else, I think they sound great. They still sound how I remember them and fit great. My one and only issue with the game so far is the performance. Although I imagine these will get ironed out soon, I feel it is only right to mention on a 4070 Super and 5800X3D, fps is great but there are in some cases micro-stutters that I believe might be due to the amount of zombies in one given location. They haven't stopped me from playing the game but have in some cases threw me off a little. Stability-wise, the game also needs a patch or two. I have lost 2 attempts at the 7-Day Survivor challenge due to a crash after alt-tabbing a few times and the other was moving between locations under the effect of Quickstep/Fleetfoot. Normally I would be okay with a rare hiccup like that due to it now having an autosave feature but as that challenge doesn't, I think it's very important that is fixed immediately.To bring my yapping to a conclusion. Overall, I think this is an easy one for Dead Rising fans to decide on when it comes to whether or not it is worth it. If you're not a huge fan, have already played it or didn't like some of the clunky/arcade-y feel, be aware that although I feel this version is a lot more accessible, it is same game at it's core.I think it's great that Dead Rising is getting some attention again and I only hope that continues. I would have never thought that we would see Dead Rising on the RE Engine and I pray that one day we see Dead Rising 2 and all of it's additional content get the same treatment.

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster was a giant surprise this year developed by Capcom and NeoBard as a quite literal remaster/remake to one of my favorite games of all time. I believed that I missed when they were having the Capcom showcase this summer (for which I remember them announcing Resident Evil 7 for the phone??) but I certainly remember my feelings when I first heard about the remaster: cautiously optimistic. This is one of, if not my favorite, games of all time and as such when anyone says “Remaster” it could mean one of three things: absolute dumpster fire (aka Kingpin: Reloaded), bare minimum (most remasters out there) or could be absolute gold (like the Nightdive Remasters) and as such, I knew there was a ⅔ of a chance to which this could absolutely blow fat d i c k. My hopes for there being more for the Dead Rising franchise went limp under the absolute clusterf u c k of Dead Rising 4 (review for that below) and as such, I figured that playing Chop Till' You Drop on the Wii and 4 would be the last that I would play of Dead Rising for quite some time. Over the months I would see inside developer previews of the game but I didn’t really tune in much then but would still remain semi-optimistic, so much that I PRE-ORDERED the digital copy to play Day 1 (which I didn’t do anyways cause I got so busy so no more of that) and since the failure of Dead Rising 4 I don’t really pre-order games unless I go into it for collectible purposes (aka every Playstation Exclusive ever except Concord and certain others). This is also in spite of the many criticisms that I’ve heard/seen (and agreed on some) for the game like the lack of TJ Rotolo as Frank West, how goofy some of the character models look, and the removal of certain things (will get into later). Recently over the past month I’ve played it on and off as a sort of “chill out and vibe” game after I beat Batman: Arkham Origins and just in time for the Halloween season, I decided to beat this game and review it.(For the rest of the review, go here:  )The gameplay for the remaster remains largely the same, though with a few changes to certain mechanics as well. Starting with the actual camera (since Frank is a photographer), you can actually choose to turn on and off the flash or create dutch camera angles. Some of these upgrades of course you’ll have to find around the mall as an added little collectible, but I think that it’s pretty damn cool that they added that in. However, on the flip side, they removed the Erotica points system in photography too. What’s that? In the original game you can take photos of things and there will be an added category depending on what's in the pic (Funny is putting stupid helmets, Brutality for the really violent scenes, Erotica for the more perverted photos, etc). They removed Erotica entirely so anytime you take a pic of someone posing in a seductive manner (like Cheryl in one of her quests), it’s replaced with the Drama category. I personally don’t hate this but I don’t enjoy it; this I can understand that nowadays things are a lot different to things back twenty years ago, but I also wanted as much of the original in there as humanly possible. This also affects a side quest in the sense that Kent, a psychotic photographer, wanted you to show him your best Erotic picture in the original and it basically gave him a characterization as an unhinged freak. In the remaster, it feels a bit less unhinged but I also suppose it didn’t really affect it too much anyways considering he still tries to infect a guy later.The actual combat itself feels fine for the most part, it still feels the same and/or better due to several layout changes but admittedly I felt that it lost a bit of the “oomph” that the original Dead Rising had, at least at the beginning. In fact, a whole lot of the game feels a lot easier with the combat: the beginning boss with Carlito used to take a whole lot more in the original while in this version? A lot easier. Later on while the Special Forces invaded, I took down a helicopter with two assault rifle shots while it took a lot more in the original. Now I also had a skill book with me (for which they added a whole bunch of new ones) that increased firepower, but even in the original I didn’t feel like it did this. According to the TVTropes page, your fists do three times the damage from the original; like there are changes like this that make the game fundamentally way easier than the original ever did. Hell, about the only complaint I really have with the difficulty here is that the Small Chainsaw you get from Adam was nerfed a decent bit and it disappoints me. _childDocuments_.review: Dead Rising: Deluxe Remaster is a faithful remake of the Original 2006 XBox launch title. You play as Frank West, wartime photo journalist. After receiving a tip of events in the town of Willamette, Colorado. You have 72 hours (6 real-time) to solve the mystery behind the Willamette incident and how it connects to Santa Cabeza.If you liked the original Dead Rising and believed all it needed where some touch ups, you will be happy with Capcom's re-release. It took the core heart and soul of DR and sanded the rough edges while retaining that since of difficulty and urgency. That said: some of the difficulty is lost with the improved control scheme. In regards to the controversy of the removal of the "Erotica" category, Larry's model change, and Cliff's Dialogue: I can confidentially say that it doesn't take away from the core package as a whole. These changes are silly, but don't negatively affect the player experience. This is only a problem for content purists. Speaking of content purists: This game does change things and is NOT the same experience as the 2006 release. If you want the game with all its janky, difficult charm, I earnestly recommend sticking to the 2016 re-release or the original 2006 Console release. On a 100 point scale, I rank this game a 95 out of 100. Wonderful work Capcom. I hope to see Dead Rising 2 get this deluxe treatment.

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid remaster! While I don't personally like that they censored a few things in this release, I find that the changes are minimally intrusive for vets at their worst and I think the backlash over it is way overtuned for the scale of things that were actually changed. Criticizing the game for making those changes is definitely valid, though.I think the majority of the new voice cast is very good, too, including Frank's new VA. I still would have preferred TJ, but his replacement does a very solid job.Overall, just a fun as the original with less rough edges!

I wouldn't be putting to much hope on that. this game is significantly easier then its predecessor, with better survivor AI (no more having to baby sit nick every inch of the way), Faster pp gains and just overall a more casual experience. This in my opinion doesn't take away from the game as much, but definitely leaves some want for a challenge later in the play through. The bosses also feel a bit easier, but that could very from person to person so I wont talk to much on that. 2nd thing I would like to touch on is how good the game looks. (if you care about that sort of stuff) The RE engine didn't do my boy frank no favors but damn does the rest of the game look great. The lighting in particular is just stunning in some places like the food court in the morning or oddly enough Carlito's hideout. Now I will say the game is a bit.. buggy at times with the textures which tbh is expected at this point With new releases but I do feel they will patch this stuff out in time so i'm not that pressed about it. And the voice acting tbh isn't as bad as people are saying. (I 100% would have rather had the OG frank voice actor) Id say like 95% of the voices match the characters pretty soundly and franks voice actor I believe does a decent job in portraying the character. So I guess to wrap this up this game is a solid addition to the series and is a great way for people that maybe haven't played the OG 2 games to see just a tad of what made dead rising such a great game in the past. would recommend picking this up.

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster is an effective way of introducing new fans to the series while welcoming old fans with a fresh start after the series' long hiatus and a couple bad apples.It includes many quality-of-life improvements to the original including a wardrobe in the security room, allowing you to try on any item you've found in the mall; survivors with fully voice-acted lines and improved AI, an autosave feature (which proved to be very useful for me by the time the military arrived), and even some new items such as the Rocket Launcher, which was planned to be in the original game but scrapped.Despite these enhancements, the groundwork and clunky mechanics from the 2006 game are still present in many places. Small areas such as the grocery store, theater, and warehouse still have to be rendered separately as opposed to being connected to their greater regions. Survivors have slightly improved AI but are still prone to jumping into danger and getting killed immediately. Zombies still spawn in the warehouse elevator every time you use it, something that the devs felt was vital enough to keep in the game.To conclude, Deluxe Remaster holds many of the same issues as the original, but it delivers an experience that the franchise has been missing for so long, and it leaves me optimistic that someday a remaster of Dead Rising 2 will occur.

_childDocuments_.review: The developers for Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster made sure to keep the game as close as possible to the original Dead Rising. This is great. It plays like the original to a T. Theres tons of quality of life improvements to make the game more intuitive for today's standards. Some features have been added in the form of new items or unlocks that add to the game as well.     However, there are bugs that weren't present in the original game. Things like boss and other human enemy AI getting really wonky. Enemies spawning inside walls, getting stuck, or just being completely unaware of their surroundings. Items sometimes falling through the floor or disappearing. None of these were gamebreaking in my time playing so far. Solid performance and no crashes either.     The best comparison I can make here is the Resident Evil 4 Remaster. RE4 Remaster was a bigger undertaking, a reimagining, and almost an entirely different game from the original RE4. But this is still 95% the original game.      Some minor things were changed to be more acceptable for the modern day. The erotica photography tag, which is the main controversy, was removed. I don't see how you couldn't feel weird about taking these pictures. I don't miss this whatsoever. Several lines of dialogue and a character or two were modified, but nothing memorable or major to the game or story.     I heard a sentiment about Resident Evil 4 not needing a remaster and I kinda feel the same about Dead Rising. I'm happy to play more Dead Rising personally and I don't feel the original game was done wrong at all, except for maybe the bugs. I feel comfortable recommending this at $50 or less if you liked the original Dead Rising or haven't and are interested in this.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm loving most of the changes and improvements they've made with this remake so far, but there's a few glaring problems that compel me not to recommend it to anyone at its current state or price point:1. A ton of ambient sound is broken or missing. Zombies make absolutely no noises unless you're very close to them. There's no echo or reverb in the mall--especially during cutscenes. The Wonderland Plaza rollercoaster makes zero sounds unless you're right in front of the ride entrance. The list goes on, and it really drains the atmosphere and immersion out of the game, making everything just completely lifeless and a lot less fun. It seems like this is an issue lots of people are having across all platforms, and it was something plenty of YouTubers discussed when they got their hands on the preview build of the game a month ago. The fact that it's still like this leads me to believe it was a creative choice and not a technical problem, and if so, this is a huge blunder.2. The game is way too easy.PP gain (haha) is out of control. Perfectly framed stickers now give out five times the amount of experience that they used to, and photography in general just gives you way too many points. Having only rescued the two tutorial survivors and messed around in Paradise Plaza, I was able to reach level 12 before the first boss fight (out of 50 total levels!)With this much experience being handed out, players will have no incentive to ever restart the game with a leveled character. Worse, they will have no mechanical reason to rescue survivors--which is a real shame, because the improvements to survivors are all fantastic. I wish I could say the same about the zombie AI, but I can't. It seems like they've been tuned to become less aggressive, and in some cases, will outright ignore the player that's standing inches from their faces.3. Technical problems.Some stuttering. Lots of texture and LOD pop-in during cutscenes. Zombies stuck inside trees or pillars. Zombie pop-in is really bad in several areas, and it just feels like there's significantly less zombies on screen at a time compared to the original. If the awful sound design is simply broken, then that belongs here too. Perhaps it can be blamed on Denuvo, or maybe it's just launch day jitters. Either way, there's enough problems here that it's worth mentioning.If Capcom fixes these problems, I would recommend the game in good conscience--and I really wish I could! Because, with these issues aside, there's so many fantastic quality-of-life improvements and new additions that this could be the definitive way to play Dead Rising in the way that Resident Evil 1's remake is the de facto RE1 experience.

All the pain points, the janky interactions such as responding to Otis on the radio or escorting a survivor are tidied up and features such as using the camera are expanded upon with the option to pick up camera parts. The downloadable content included with the digital deluxe edition is also a lot of fun, who doesn't want to walk around Willamette in a Nemesis costume whilst his BGM plays around the mall? 10/10 - fantastic remaster.

_childDocuments_.review: Capcom has set the gold standard for remakes with their latest reimagining of the legendary *Dead Rising*. This beloved classic, originally released in 2006, has received a fresh coat of paint and a slew of new gameplay features that make it a must-play for both veterans and newcomers alike.One of the most exciting aspects of this remaster is the opportunity to experience the stunning visuals powered by the RE Engine in the new version. The thrill of wielding that iconic Rocket Launcher feels even more satisfying this time around, bringing a sense of realism that enhances the overall experience.However, it's essential to clarify that this is a remaster, not a full remake. While the game has its fair share of technical hiccups—bugs that can occasionally detract from the fun—the core gameplay remains as exhilarating as it was in 2006. For those willing to overlook these issues, *Dead Rising* retains its charm and intensity.One of the standout improvements is the new control scheme. Players can opt for the classic controls reminiscent of the original or take advantage of the updated layout inspired by *Resident Evil*, which makes for a smoother and more intuitive gaming experience. This thoughtful addition opens the door for new players to jump in without feeling overwhelmed.Yet, not all changes hit the mark. The game suffers from a lack of ambience and sound effects at times, leaving certain areas feeling a bit empty and soulless. However, the most significant upgrades lie in the AI improvements. Gone are the days of frustratingly incompetent characters; the new and improved AI enhances the overall experience, making objectives feel less tedious and more engaging. Otis, in particular, is less of a nuisance, allowing players to enjoy the game’s flow without unnecessary interruptions.While some old dialogue and character interactions have been altered, the remaster successfully strikes a balance between nostalgia and modernization. It’s a thrilling time to be a *Dead Rising* fan, as this version breathes new life into the classic formula while honoring what made the original special.In summary, *Dead Rising Remaster* is a fantastic homage to its predecessor, and I highly recommend it for both long-time fans and those new to the franchise. Despite its bugs and occasional sound issues, the fun factor remains high, and it's clear that Capcom has put considerable effort into enhancing this iconic title. Whether you’re reliving the past or discovering it for the first time, this game promises a wild ride through the zombie apocalypse. Don’t miss out!

_childDocuments_.review: Speaking as a long term fan of the franchise, Dead Rising Remastered is a fantastic renewal of the original game in Capcom's new RE Engine. It's something I enjoyed for beginning to end, but there are a few things that are worth considering.Dead Rising Remastered (DRR) is a partial remake of the original game (also available on Steam), that brings the shopping mall and its hordes of zombies into the modern RE Engine that Capcom has used to great success since the release of Resident Evil 7. It's also a re-release that has a slew of quality of life and balance changes, even if some of the quirks and rough parts of the original title are left unchanged. The most significant reason for picking up this title is that the quality of life changes bring a great deal to the game. Don't get me wrong, I really enjoyed the original game on Xbox 360, but there are certain elements with the user interface and how the game is balanced that haven't aged well, or have ultimately become points of frustration. The ability to answer your walkie talkie on the fly, the changed mission tracking/waypoint system, and the improved survivor AI are all welcome changes that add a lot to the experience. I remember acutely how the spinning arrow of the original release and survivors getting stuck on walls added a deal of frustration on revisits. By large, these changes smooth out the experience, even if some of the jankier elements (such as trying to fight Special Forces) remain as they were in the original release.Connected to this are various changes to overall balance and progression in the game. Compared to the original release, DRR has a faster levelling up system, and is a little kinder in terms of some objectives, and collection of items specific to certain missions. I still used the 'Start over' trick at the end of the first day to buff Frank a bit (which was essential in the original game), and on that 2nd cycle, I was able to almost max out my level, and was well prepared for the horrors of Willamette Mall. There are also a few balance aspects with human psychopaths that makes things a bit more forgiving. For some, this might make the game seem a bit easier, but I feel it added to the experience. Speaking of which, Wilamette Mall and its hordes of zombies are still fantastic. It's still a great deal of fun to navigate the various areas and tackle the unending waves of undead. It's still highly enjoyable to experiment/hack/slash away with the array of items and weapons available in the game. DRR feels like the best, most polished version of the gameplay loop of Dead Rising in terms of exploration, missions, rescuing survivors and making it back to the safe room. Likewise, as a huge fan of the George A. Romero films that inspired Dead Rising, it's just lovely to have this game in its shiny new package and its faithful tributes to many elements. A point of contention for some is that some elements have been changed/edited, and honestly, if that is a deal breaker, there's always the original release on Steam. One key change that might bother some is that while you CAN get a wide range of clothes in stores, a lot of items are gated behind achievements, which does add to replay-ability, but might feel restrictive to some players. Likewise, for what is a fairly close remaster/remake hybrid, some may find the full price a contentious point, which is a fair matter you need to decide on your own. I loved this release for what it was.I will flag, however, is that there's a texture setting bug that impacts the frame rate/introduces stutter heavily. If you set it to 4GB or below, the game still looks great and runs very fluidly, but there are stutters if it is above this. A patch for this has yet to come, as of early October. To sum things up, I loved my time with Dead Rising Remastered, and subjectively, with the quality of life changes, this has become my preferred version. If you crave the original's specifics, there's still that version, but if this sounds appealing and you do love the original game, you can pick that one up on Steam as well. Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing the original dead rising for 14 years. I've spent almost 25 hours with this game (maxed out Frank, completed main story and infinity mode, still working on finishing the achievements). Here's my review.This remaster is great. It has its problems, but the good outweighs the bad.Accessibility is one of the best new features of this game. However, it also comes at a cost. The game is much easier. Leveling up is a much quicker process, moving while aiming broke a few of the fights, and the new control scheme is much more intuitive. The ability to now skip time has been a god send for, not just the main game - but, the infinity mode. No longer do you have to spend 14 hours of real time to complete it. The loss of challenge is a balancing issue which could be fixed via patch. As it stands, the sense of helplessness and hopelessness you get from being miles away from a bathroom after a boss fight with no healing items is gone. There are a lot of new features that are great. There is a lot more camera customization. You can get a bunch of brand new upgrades to dig into the photography mechanic. The AI has drastically improved with new survivor mechanics that, while I didn't pay much attention to, were still cool. Every NPC is now voiced which adds a new level of immersion. Graphically the game looks fantastic. Costume selection has been streamlined and it's less of a hassle to try on new clothing pieces. I also appreciated that the original soundtrack stayed in tact. There's probably more, but generally speaking the quality of life changes have been a god send for a veteran of this game.This game does have its issues. While Frank West's voice and look grew on me, I can't say the same for a lot of the cast. Many of the models look about the same, yet the voice cast is completely different from 2006. The main voice that sticks out is Brad. His VA sounds like a 19 year old trying to do their best Samuel Jackson impression. It's rough. There were times where this game dropped frames on me during intensive moments but otherwise I didn't have many technical issues. They changed some of the dialogue for seemingly no reason. Frank no longer says "what in the world" when watching the security camera near the beginning of the game, all of the detail is taken from Clint's dialogue as he no longer is specifically a Vietnam vet (we know he is, but 'communist' is replace with 'mole' and his entire PTSD attack is way too vague to be believable now), and they white washed the butcher. That's pretty much all I can think of off the top of my head. If you're looking to get into DR, this is a great introduction for newer players. Yippee!

_childDocuments_.review: This remaster is, at the moment, very rushed feeling. So much so that I felt the need to list all the grievances I have with it in hopes of them being noticed and fixed by Capcom, or modders down the line. Before I get into that stupid long list though, I should mention that this game is still incredibly fun. It's still mostly Dead Rising 1, and that alone makes it a great time.When compared to the original 2006 version, however, there are just too many problems -- either from bugs or weird decisions -- that I can't recommend it at full price. Getting the original at 1/6th of the price is a much better deal, with a much more cohesive experience.So with all that being said, here's a giant list of all the weirdness I've encountered thus far, in no particular order:--------------------------------------------------------------------In the beginning chopper scene, you can see objects spawning in on the side of the screen if you have the camera zoomed all the way out. This doesn't make a very good first impressionTutorial images show an unfinished build of the game, missing lighting and assets. This makes for a very *bad* first impressionFrank can be grabbed while attacking, meaning you get grabbed a lot more, especially when trying to use slower weapons like the sledgehammerYou can no longer jump on boxes to break them, likely due to the fact that objects can now be pushed by walking into themAlso due to the ability to push objects, the hunk of meat is now insanely powerful, as zombies will continually kick it away from them while trying to pick it up, resulting in large groups swarming around it for a long time, moving with it as it gets kicked until one of them finally gets itThey added yellow paint in the food court for Carlito's fight that's both unnecessary and also persists for the entire duration of the game despite only being useful in that one instanceKicking trash cans no longer breaks them consistentlyFrank no longer plays his fatigued animation after being attackedFrank feels much floatier than the original gameZombies constantly despawn or pop inPP is awarded way too generously (I got to level 6 in the very first encounter before the safe room was locked, with up to 6,000 PP in a single image. I went back to the original and the highest I could get here was 800 (without stickers in the mix)Speaking of PP Stickers, they now glow bright yellow, and are called out by survivors, making them painfully obvious and removing a lot of the fun of searching for them as you explore the mall (They're also barely worth it when you can get the same amount of PP they give you in two photos easily)Frank can't get blood on him from zombiesBlood splatter happens immediately, instead of being delayed to simulate the travel time of the liquid as it was beforeThe skateboard is like 3x too big for some reason, and feels 3x as fast (seriously, what the hell)Ambient sounds are missing, most noticably the low zombie growl that's supposed to constantly play. This makes areas feel incredibly empty, which isn't helped by the lack of zombiesVoice acting is worse than the original in nearly every instance, and things like reverb are missing from the voice lines. Also, I will forever be salty about no TJ RotoloThe boxes showing the survivors on your HUD are now just dots, making it more difficult to tell when they're in danger or stuck; especially since they constantly bump into each other and make sounds like they're being grabbed because of itCop zombies being able to shoot means your movement is constantly interrupted by random gunshots hitting you. I imagine this is why it was removed from the original game.Mirrors *only* function in bathrooms, with any other mirrors still present only using cubemaps and screenspace reflections, and some (like the gym one) being outright removedGates were added in-between areas for some reason, making the mall feel even more disconnected than beforeSome textures are just poorly upscaled, or didn't receive proper care (like the door behind Jessie reading "NATAlieS GateO FimPrisOnmentK FimPrisOnmentK NATAlieS GateO", when in the original game it was just too blurry to make out)You can now take 100 photos before having to recharge instead of 30, making it easy to abuse the camera (they tried adding a progressively longer cooldown if you spam it, but with the amount of PP awarded it really doesn't matter)Aligning the servbot head is now a pain, as it's harder to make contact with and spins way further from a single punchErotica was removed, but none of the sexualized angles in cutscenes were changed, nor was the side quest in which Cheryl requests Frank take literal erotica pictures of her (the picture is just considered "drama" or "no genre" now)Item health is now not only visible at all times, but is also overly generous. (Seriously, the regular Chainsaws now last for ages without books and allow you to just clear a path through like three areas)Lots of small details are now worse, like the belt on the treadmill no longer giving the illusion of spinning properly, and moving you back in "steps" when you stand still on it instead of smoothly sliding you offThe dialogue from survivors while exploring with them is awful, and they say the weirdest things, including mentioning posting on "social media" despite the game taking place in 2006Frank's character model is not only unappealing to look at, but is wider than the original by quite a good bit while still using the same rig, resulting in some animations looking strange or being less readableLighting in cutscenes feels very poorly done, which is weird since the lighting in the mall itself looks great. The maintenance room in particular suffers from gross dim bathroom lightingFrank doesn't hold the transceiver properly, his fingers clip through it while he makes a closed fistThe game sometimes stutters when you enter a new area as it loads all the objectsIn general the character models don't look great, especially in comparison to the mallThe Chuck Greene pre-order skin (that I can't get due to not pre-ordering) has errors all over it, including the word "Racing" missing on the back, the "4" being on both of his shoulders instead of one with a logo on the other, and having the number be the wrong color as wellFor me in particular, I killed the convicts, then loaded my game to before I did so and killed them again. The first time I was awarded the prisoner outfit, the second time I was not, and I can no longer seem to obtain it in my playthroughThey didn't change the scoop chances with saved survivors being immediately lost if you enter and exit the safe room, which I find odd as that seems like one of the biggest QoL changes you could make (next to tweaking the AI)The cult's new "eye" pose is kinda cool, but the lack of animation transitions to/from it make it looks like an unfinished mod. It's also just a weird idle animation. Having them pray makes much more sense.Frank goes like a full 6 feet up in the air before dropping back down when he does the knee drop now and it looks insane----------------------------------------------------------------------------------And that's all the stuff I've found so far. Haven't beaten the game yet, but I'd imagine that covers most of the important (and some nitpicky) stuff. Like I said, I'm still enjoying the hell out of the game, and it's worth noting I haven't mentioned a lot of the *good* QoL stuff they added (like survivors not dropping their weapons after you give them food)I just felt it was worth mentioning that while this game is fun, it has a plethora of issues that, until they're addressed, make this the worse version of Dead Rising on PC by a good bit. I very much hope that the team that put this together is able to continue polishing it until it's at least equal to the original, but if not then we at least have a great framework for modders to work with.

_childDocuments_.review: Specs:-CPU: Intel Core i7-11700K - 8 cores - 3.6GHz (5.0GHz)-GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Ti FE 12GB-1440p Ultrawide MonitorUltrawide Users:Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster has full ultrawide support from Day 1, something still few and far between for modern games for some reason. Personally, the vignette that comes standard with the RE Engine feels especially oppressive on ultrawide, so I'd highly recommend REFramework for the best experience possible.I took a Capcom survey around Christmas time last year, where the studio asked a bunch of questions about their franchises and what gamers feel about the current selection, and even what they want to see for the future. I think I was in a minority when I wrote that I would love a full remake/remaster of Dead Rising, a real contender for my favorite IP under Capcom's belt. Imagine my surprise 6 months later when they announce the exact thing I wanted! And coming out just a few months later! So, is it everything I wanted it to be, and more importantly, everything it needs to be?Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster (DRDR) takes the "soul" of the 2006 release and packages it up to modern audiences without losing a single important detail. From the reusing of a majority of animations, to keeping the same story beats and plot points of the original, the overall experience is a great one. It's a strange feeling to start playing a brand new game and to already be going through it as though I've beaten it a thousand times, but I think that really attests to how much of the original game is still here almost 2 decades later.Bringing DRDR to the RE Engine is something I never knew I needed, but seeing Resident Evil 2/3/4 Remake-quality level zombies in Willamette's shopping mall is incredible! Despite the vast number of zombies on screen, if you slow down and actually observe them on a singular level, you can make out the same deformities, blemishes, and injuries you would see playing as Leon or Jill in Raccoon City. Zombie models are unquestionably repeated, but that's no different from the 2006 version, so those who are returning to the game all these years later probably won't feel amiss at all. The world around you doesn't miss this treatment either, with incredible detail given to Frank's surroundings, with new lighting effects and objects placed in every scene of the mall, really bringing the whole package together. It's been a long time since Dead Rising was able to give me a bit of dread with just its environments!Mechanically, this might as well be the same game! All the small little tips and tricks from the original are still present, making any skills you learned from playing the original work just as well in this version! But that's not to say this was purely a copy+paste job by Capcom's team. Many QoL features have been added to the experience, such as a brand-new control scheme for actually moving while aiming, multiple new features for your camera, and a clothing collection in the safe room that keeps every single clothing item you've put on once for future customization. No more running back to Entrance Plaza for a pair of shoes! Combat also feels identical, with a ton of fighting animations feeling like the original with small differences here and there. But new content doesn't stop at QoL, and certainly not just DLC, but the dev team has added multiple new magazines that drastically change certain mechanics, even making some joke items very lethal! There's even  and new attacks from zombies, as well as having Frank's learnable skills now bound to buttons, allowing you to execute them at your leisure!Now, is there a catch? Well, sort of, actually. I'm not sure whether it's optimization, limits of the engine, or my own setup, but initial boot of a save file or new game certainly comes with jitters and stutters, but smooth out after a few minutes tops (at least for me). There's also the occasional zombie-clipping, with zombies ending up in places that are impossible to get to, such as inside a window display or a column. I've also noticed that some enemies will have a "cooldown" of some kind when getting hit by attacks, which was present in the first game, but has been turned up to a degree that leaves me questioning. For example, a survivor died to a psychopath that was tasing them that I was physically unable to stop despite dealing 75% of their health bar in damage while it was happening, which frankly didn't feel fair. But these instances are few and far between, so they felt more like one-offs rather than things that impact the whole experience.I also feel like I should give my 2 cents on complaints I've been seeing around the internet about DRDR, because us gamers sure do love to complain.Listen, I love TJ Rotolo as much as the next guy, but the original game was 18 years ago! Honestly, there's half a chance that a large portion of the original cast don't do VA work anymore, or may not even be alive. Thinking we could get a big family reunion almost 2 decades later is a bit much.Yes, a specific psychopath won't call you Vietcong anymore, and you can't get free PP just by taking pictures of Jessie's chest, but if we can be perfectly honest with ourselves, these aren't the features of the original we needed, it was everything else! I can't even confirm if any of the original dev team worked on DRDR, but even if it was the exact same team, we should expect some touch-ups after all this time.This is a video game. In 2024. You're gonna find yellow paint in your 2024 video game.Jokes aside, and if we're willing to be honest, none of these things are deal breakers. Not to mention this is an RE Engine game, there's going to be mods that likely fix all your grievances. Overall, this is a fantastic experience and well worth the full price. Don't agree? That's fine! Capcom still has you covered. At the time of this review (9/21/2024), the original is still on Steam for a full price of $10. That's less than lunch! There's no way you can't find a way to enjoy Dead Rising if it's something you're genuinely interested it, and I feel DRDR is the best way to do it!

_childDocuments_.review: for about as long as i can remember now, dead rising has pretty much always been my favorite game. i instantly fell in love with it when i was a kid playing it on the 360 and have continued to play it pretty regularly ever since. so safe to say when i heard there was a remaster coming out it had a lot of expectations to live up to me for me and honestly it's surpassed all of them. dead rising deluxe remaster takes what was so special and amazing about the original game and translates it perfectly into the modern age of gaming. for one the graphics are incredible, they brought the original up to date and made the mall look beyond fantastic and even very pretty at times with some of the new lighting stuff they have going on. just seeing my childhood game look this incredible is a dream come true in itself but even beyond that this remaster excels. the updates to gameplay keep the spirit of the original while taking away the jank and allowing for this game to actually control pretty well for the first time. frank's movement is much smoother and his set of different skill attacks are a lot easier to use and allow you to use moves that 99% of the time you would've just never used naturally before. there's a couple tweaks to certain things difficulty level, i found some stuff was easier and some was harder. i was worried they were gonna make this game too baby mode but honestly even i was struggling with certain things even after almost 2 decades of playing this game. i do think this game is more inviting to new comers but it does it in ways that doesn't really compromise difficulty and more-so just negate the archaic old game mechanics. the few new additions also were really cool, i especially loved how thomas surrenders now, the return of the cut rocket launcher weapon and the new magazines are a blast to play around with, especially the one you get for doing a saint run. the only real kinda negative about this game is probably the voice acting. it's not bad but let's be honest the original actors are both super iconic, and all did a better job than the new guys (looking at you frank and brad) but i also don't think they're effects nothing. they also removed the photography category erotica, which for some reason has proven to be somewhat controversial. it's literally just a useless minor feature that only is used for one side mission that most people i've seen play this game miss anyways and the only people that are upset about that being gone are weird perverts who have never spoken to a women before. honestly tho i just don't understand how anyone who liked the original could dislike this without just being blinded by rose tinted goggles. what actually makes this game so special and fun to the point that It's a great example of how a remaster should be handled, respecting the source material while modernizing the experience for today's players.

There must be something wrong with his pc because my pc is old and it has been running absolutely fine.The survivors work a little better now. However I did encounter 1 bug. _childDocuments_.review: Firstly as a lifelong fan of this series, i truly cannot believe this game exists in this day and age after Dead Rising 4. This was a dream in the back of my head that i never thought would come true, and my god am i happy that this became real.DRDR in my honest opinion on a gameplay front improves on the original in almost every conceivable way.The quality of life changes and tweaks make playing through the Willamette mall an absolute blast. No more headache inducing brain dead survivor AI, the rate at which you level up is dramatically increased making every run feel very rewarding and less sluggish, PP stickers give a significant amount of points compared to the original where they didn't offer much and weren't worth going after unless you're a achievement completionist.Psychopath health has been buffed to make their fights much more challenging, Kent specifically is very tough and damaging in the remake. New magazines upon certain unlocks that offer brand new bonuses like explosive throwables or even unlimited item durability upon getting Saint completed. As well as cut content removed from the original game like cop zombies firing off their handguns and obtaining a rocket launcher from the special forces soldiers.The core game is kept nearly identical to the original, down to the same animations and sounds. However there are some things that aren't perfect.In my playthrough at around day 2 and 3 crashes became annoyingly constant when entering different areas, i'm sure this will be addressed and fixed with time, but i would be lying if i said it didn't get to me after a while. Thankfully the newly added autosave feature saved my run on more than one occasion so it wasn't nearly as bad to deal with.Certain characters have been changed or censored, Specifically Larry and Cliff. Certain lines of dialogue and Larry's design have been altered from the original, which to some will be a disappointment. But i personally do not have any issue with them as the game stays virtually the same, the Erotica genre from picture taking has been removed as well.The new voice cast is certainly a mixed bag, some performances rival the original in quality such as Adam the Clown and Jo. Frank's new voice has definitely grown on me and i quite enjoy his new take. I cannot say the same for Brad however, his line delivery in the beginning is rough lolAll in all i believe that if you want to revisit the Dead Rising 1 experience in a beautiful new engine with loads of QOL additions and fixes, on top of brand new never before seen items that reward you for finishing each achievement, this is absolutely worth your time and cash. It's a love letter to the original Dead Rising and the fans, and shows a very bright future for the series if this game performs well.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite some performance issues and making the game easier in some ways this is a very close to being a direct upgrade to the original Dead Rising. Like others I was initially bothered by how easy it was to level up but I came to the realization that the bulk of playtime on DR has always been at level 50 anyway.I'm typically skeptical of QoL updates and feel they often take away from the experience, but being able to skip time genuinely just prevents you from having to AFK to do so many things in this game. Other fantastic additions include being able to change into any clothes you've previously worn from the safe room and voice acting for all survivors.I will say that streamlining the game to this point has taken this from a fairly daunting and time consuming 100% to something I pretty much did in a weekend and some change in just under 30 hours. Granted I have a lot of experience with the game and do know what I'm doing as I have 100%'d it on the 360 and revisited the 2016 port.For first time players this is a strong recommend, this is a classic that has been modernized in all the right ways, and yet kept things the same when they needed to be to have the integrity of what makes dead rising a unique experience. Existing fans will also find this a treat to revisit, well, at least I did. There are some nitpicks and nostalgia factors that I still prefer the original for but overall this is mostly the better version of the game at this point. Here's hoping to the dead rising franchise having a prosperous future.

_childDocuments_.review: There were so many QOL changes and improvements I just wasn't expecting, and I love it!If you liked Dead Rising 1, you'll love Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster... UNLESS you let nostalgia dictate every emotion you have, and always say things like "The orginal is ALWAYS better than the remake". No sir, everything has an opportunity for improvement, and these devs saw that :) Pros--Fast forwarding time, in 72hr and infinity mode, is so perfect-Skateboards were improved in almost every way -Motorcycles can go room to room, now.-AI aren't completely braindead anymore-The new magazines they added gives more game play options.-PP stickers and zombie kills give a lot more exp now, so you actually use your camera to level up now.-Walking while aiming, and gunslinger mags actually make gun builds more enjoyable-Rolling is a nice combat feature now since you become invulnerable in the beginning of the animation. Fighting bosses kinda feels like a very easy souls game since you can dodge attack based on enemy motions. I don't remember ever using the roll in DR1 since it didn't really help, and you couldn't predict attacks from animations being too fast.-Changing from a locker in the safe house is awesome!-Everyone has a voice actor, so no more reading dialogue to break the immersion.-Survivor tips have been surprisingly helpful in the first playthroughCons- -Brads voice sucked. Hard lol. He sounds like he was recording from his moms basement and didn't want to wake up her from a nap.-Stun locks from special forces are insane.It only takes 2 to get you in a nasty stunlock for at LEAST half your HP.-AI fixation on targets is annoying. They won't stop attacking their targets until it dies, and won't just through zombies anymore.-Tank fight at the end was WAY too easy. Tank has never even made an attempt to attack in any playthroughs, and the fight lasts about 15 seconds, now.Pro OR con?-For my fellow achievement hunters, for better or worse, achievements have become a LOT easier to manage. You don't have to kill 1000 zombies barehanded anymore, replay the whole game if you missed just a single call from Otis, or try one of every food in the game lmao.-The  game is being labeled as 'woke' now? I guess from making some dialogue less offensive and removing erotica. I personally don't understand WHY they changed it, but the changes aren't bad. It sounds like these changes offended more people then the original ever offended lmao-You can SPARE Thomas now. It'd be cool to be able to bring him back to the safe house but this still works, I guess.(I'll try to keep updating the list as I remember some of the other changes.)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure what's happening with remasters lately. First of all, I understand this game is running on a brand new engine so it can't be the exact same experience as the original. However, something about this remaster feels clunky. I have no problem getting the game to run at whatever frame cap I set with graphics at max. The game looks great, but something is definitely off with the in game audio. I am personally not a fan of the new Frank voice, but that's a matter of personal preference. Leveling up through PP bonuses is completely broken. It's far too easy to become OP early on in the game just by taking pictures, whether that is intentional or not. I hope that gets patched as it makes the game much easier than it should be. This game as a whole seems more forgiving than it originally was. At least the option for the classic controls is still there. One annoying and consistent bug I encountered was in changing clothes at a store. After the initial switch I was not able to switch back or change to a different item in the store. Instead the game would just swap between a return and change prompt. I should mention this was after using the OG Frank DLC skin which would unfortunately also swap the model to new Frank. There also seems to be less places to change clothes than in the original game. I'm not sure if the visual facelift and censorship has given this now 18 year old game new life especially since the original is still for sale on here and ripe with a community of modders. Still I'm glad to see the series is getting the right kind of attention again from Capcom after DR4 and an abandoned DR5 seemed to kill the series. If you haven't played the series before, this modernized deluxe remaster is a great place to start, but wait for a sale and for the bugs to be ironed out. If you're playing this as a fan of the original game like myself, you may be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd score this game an 85/100.The first game I bought when I got an Xbox 360 was Dead Rising. I remember the creepy mall commercial that played late at night on Cartoon Network for Dead Rising. I've 100%'d Dead Rising on Steam. I even like four-fifths of the series (looking at you, Dead Rising 4. Nobody likes you. You get played by completionists for the sake of finishing the series).THE GOOD I was hesitant with the reveal of the new models for Frank and the gang, along with their new voice actors, but after an S tier playthrough (All Survivors, PP Stickers, Overtime etc) I am content with the direction Capcom took them. Sure, I miss old Frank, but this new Frank is LEAGUES better then DR4 Frank. Others have stated issues with Brad's VA, but that seem's to be mostly subjective. Old Brad was iconic, but New Brad does his job. The same goes for the rest of the VA's as well. I have no complaints. In fact, every voiceless survivor (and Otis!) getting lines was an awesome addition. The updated graphics are beautiful. I love that the mall actually looks used in places that were pristine (un-decorated) in the original. Leisure Park actually has grass and other flora, a feature very toned down in the 2006-era of Dead Rising. The zombies look appropriately gory and rotted while still keeping true to their original design. The costumes for the Deluxe Edition are fun! Capcom used to be very liberal with character crossovers in it's games. You used to always have a skin from Street Fighter, Resident Evil, Dino Crisis, etc. etc. to choose from. They stopped that for a while, but I hope they continue to do it since they've gone so full hog with it here.The controls feel better, but if you want that full nostalgia send, there are classic controls as well. Strafing while shooting a firearm just feels great as opposed to original method of move -> aim -> shoot -> repeat,THE BADImproved Survivor AI was a marketing point for this remaster, but I didn't really notice any difference. I will say I don't use NPC's like a gang though. I rescue them and bring them back to the safehouse. On the rare occasions that they did join me in Psycopath battles, I found them to still be VERY squishy. Also, it always seemed like one survivor was always lagging behind the others, to the point where I'd go back to them just standing by the door we came in. Arming them is also a pain point, as arming them is the same prompt as opening the door. I don't know how many times I tried to open the elevator only to have someone take my Mini-Chainsaws.Despite having a setting for enemy density, and setting it to max, I feel like there were times when I had less zombies around me then I did at the same part in the original game. Also, gone are the days where the game would load enemies in low pixelated groups that enhance the closer you get to give the illusion of density. Instead, zombies would just spawn in out of thin air. They also have an issue with spawning in walls and half clipping through objects. I even had this happen during cut scenes which was very un-immersive. A lot of players are reporting crashes. My play through was fine 99% of the time. I had one crash in Overtime Mode. In the end, I wholeheartedly recommend the Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster for both new and original fans. It's just fun to be in a mall stuck with zombies and everything is a weapon. Hopefully, with enough support Capcom will continue this trend with Dead Rising 2, Dead Rising 2: Off The Record, Dead Rising 3 and finally make Dead Rising 4 *cough, cough*.

_childDocuments_.review: Where Capcom's Resident Evil 2 Remake felt like it was trying to introduce the game to new people, DRDR feels like it isn't trying to garner a new audience or rejuvenate the franchise.Despite the game running on a whole new engine with a new voice cast, the game feels shockingly similar to its 2006 counterpart, so much so that I'm not sure if it's worth the price tag for people (like me) who are intimately familiar with the original.I was sure that - at least - a lot of the original's jankiness and balancing issues would be fixed, but to my surprise, the chainsaw-three-magazine combo is still here and as strong as ever, and the AI is still as dumb as ever (At least in my first playthrough. Even in the original, AI behaviour is very inconsistent).In terms of the changes it does make, the ones that stand out the most are the myriad quality of life changes, including, but not limited to:*The ability to skip time (although it can occasionally affect the pacing negatively.)*Having full control of Frank during radio transmissions*Blender in the security room*Multiple missions can be tracked at once*Skills are simpler to useA big change I've left out is the autosave system and that's because I think it actually harms the game. I'm not opposed to an autosave in DR, but this one feels overly aggressive in the way it saves the game after every single zone transition. This removes a lot of the tension in your treks through the mall as you almost always have a save to revert to from just a few minutes earlier (given how many zone transitions are throughout the mall) if anything goes wrong. I think what confuses me most is that there isn't an option to turn autosaving off for those who don't want to use it.To touch on the new voice cast, I think it's a downgrade in every capacity. At best, you get somebody doing a very good impression of the original character. At worst, you get a performance with the emotional range of Siri. Whether these issues are due to the actors themselves or the direction they were given, I'm not sure, but they're present regardless. There's also the censoring in this version. Most prominently, the 'erotica' photography genre has been removed, and a character's line about communism has been removed.To those with zero media literacy, this is the woke mob in full force ruining a video game. For others, it's the game removing outdated elements. For me, I find it a tad bothersome because I considered these to be aspects of the game's social commentary - the former, a commentary on the male gaze and the objectification of women, particularly as it pertains to the p*rn industry (admittedly, there are much better and more tactful ways of handling this kind of commentary), and the latter, a commentary on the bogey-man-like mentality most Americans harbour towards communism. Whether or not these were the intended interpretations, I'm not sure, but they certainly fall in line with the game's other themes (American consumerism being the big one).TL;DR /// Here's my verdict:If you're a fan of the original, you'll most likely enjoy DRDR given how closely its genetic makeup matches the 2006 classic. You'll most certainly appreciate the plethora of QoL improvements the game makes, although some changes (such as the new voice cast) might not be so appreciated. If you're new to the franchise, there's absolutely nothing wrong with starting here, but personally, unless you absolutely need modern visuals and some improved accessibility, I would recommend the 2016 remaster for the original voice acting alone.It's obvious why they chose to market this as a 'deluxe remaster' rather than a full on remake - it mostly is the same (great) game.

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Rising with a fresh coat of paint but all of the jank left intact. For reference I haven’t played the original in a very long time so my memories of it are a bit hazy, and felt like I might as well revisit with this instead of just replaying. The visuals are clearly the main justification for this “deluxe remaster” so I’ll mention that first, it’s cool to see DR redone in RE Engine and the cutscenes generally get a nice bump comparable to the RE remakes, though overall it’s a bit odd on a technical level. For one the black levels always look washed out to me, I’m not sure why or if it’s intentional on Capcom’s part but it’s like a grey filter is over the screen all the time. There’s a lot of noticeable texture issues also, and feel like the character models don’t translate quite as well from the original style to a more realistic look. The mall itself is a nice upgrade, though I feel it highlights a lack of potential with how it could’ve been more seamless instead of still being segmented with loading screensAside for that, it’s the same game from what I remember with some added QoL improvements. Killing zombies is fun, backtracking and escorting survivors less so. The AI is still not good but I’d assume improved from before, they stick close to you most of the time and didn’t have as much of an issue there. You can move while aiming (though guns are annoying to use), and there’s autosaves with time skipping which are actually great additions since they help speed the game up a lot. There’s also new voice acting which will probably be hit or miss for most, though I’m kinda indifferent to it and the story in general same as before

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing the Dead Rising franchise since I was a child. For a long while I have held this game series close to my heart as the thing that got me into playing video games as a whole - I have 100% completed all games on console, and have bought them all for PC, with the exception of 4. While I write this review while playing my infinity mode run, the last, and fifth playthrough I require to 100% the game and have all achievements, I feel like I have the right to voice my opinion on this game. It's going to probably be long.This is the best way to play Dead Rising 1 right now, bar none. I know for a fact a vocal group of players will flay me alive for this, but that is my view. The game looks *great*. The effort put in to every detail, from the mall itself, to items on the shelves, to the characters, I am blown away by it in so many ways. It's stunning, really, to see the characters given their actualized form. Some characters, such as Frank West, Jessica "Jessie" Mccarney, Isabela, and Brad Garrison have had their appearances altered with the upgrade, however with higher definition and the changes they far more closely resemble their concept art appearances, which in my eyes look far better, but that is entirely subjective on the viewer. The voice actors have changed, however if you let go of nostalgia and give them a chance or are a new player entirely, they all do well, with the only exception being Brad in the beginning, but he eases into the role overtime. Each of them, their appearances and voices are great.The mall's upgrades are a nice touch. If you are a first time player or do not recall what it looked like in the original, you may not 100% realize the changes. Locations such as Paradise Plaza and Wonderland Plaza have had additions for flavor in the decor. Despite what others say about colors feeling washed out, I just don't feel that and i'm going to assume that it is just a case of graphical settings and monitors. Gameplay has had a major uplift. AI has been improved and they are no longer dense as a brick and twice as thick, and are actually competent. Escorting them is less of an agonizing pain, which is a huge boon to the player. Moving around is quicker, and has more oomph to your movement instead of being sluggishly slow, making navigating the mall far smoother than the original 2006 and 2016 release, and when you add in the upgraded AI that isn't mentally deficient, it's great. Psychopaths are a real threat now too. Your skills are actually no longer clunky to use, having their own specific inputs to use them, making your skill moves you unlock through leveling actually easy to use instead of fumbling through them. You cannot just small chainsaw your way through all of them anymore like you used to, with need to actually put some thought into it. In all honesty, the buffs to them make me use more than just the small chainsaw. Infinity mode has had some uplifts too, with enemies occasionally dropping weapons and food items, the addition  of cultists and special forces, and new scheduling for survivors and psychopath spawning. Being able to move while aiming is really, really nice, tooThere are some bugs and jank, like the occasional crash and pop-in at times, which is at it's most glaringly obvious with Leisure Park and in the beginning intro sequence. With Autosaving being a thing now as one of the quality of life change that occurs every time you go through a zone change, if it does occur you won't lose as much progress. I admit with my high-end computer I may just not encounter the vast majority of them, but even with that I have only encountered about three crashes over the course of 32 hours as of writing this review, and those were all extremely early on. I feel a need to cover one last thing before closing, before some people rip on me in the comments. Some players of the original may complain about the removal or adjustment of some things. For example, the Erotica tag from the original game being removed. Honestly? I fail to see how no longer being rewarded for snapping horny pictures (often of zombies, too) is that impactful on the experience, at all, and it doesn't matter too much in the grand scheme of things. The adjustment of a particular psychopath's dialogue I disagree with, but it also doesn't 'remove from his story', you still capture what it was that set them off. All in all though, in the end I believe that this is genuinely the best option for playing Dead Rising's first entry into the series, especially for new players, and i'm glad a friend gifted it to me. I am hoping for remasters of the other titles, Dead Rising 2 and 3, and hopefully an entirely new title for this series to breathe new life into it.

Unfortunately, they didn't do that, but at the end of the day capcom is deciding to call this a remaster for the fact that it is incredibly faithful to the original in terms of the map and the writing (for the most part), but I would have to say that the game is made too easy by one item. The Firearms book, this book is so incredibly overpowered that it made most Psychopaths pretty easy. Another thing that is a gripe is the autosaves. I was hoping that it would maybe autosave after every case or every sub-case, but nope. It saves every time you enter a new area. Which makes the game far too forgiving. Apart from the fact that all I've done is complain, I would say that you should give this game a chance if it's on sale or if you really like the Dead Rising franchise, Because the Graphics and new gameplay additions make this nearly 20 year old game, a lot more accessible for the newer generation. Solid 8/10,  Too much firearm books
