This remake did not personally strike a chord with me, and overall I felt very apathetic to a lot of the design changes. It just was not a vibe for me. It's not a particularly bad remake, and for anyone interested, I would pick up the original on Steam in case Capcom decides to delist it. I don't think they have any particular reason to, but you never know.Sound design for weapons, and impacts got heavily nerfed. Anything from Throwing CD's or plates at zombies, or even pounding them with a sledgehammer. Weapons just sound so weak and pitiful, a lot of weapon feel and sounds like they are made out of cardboard or plastic. The new dialogue feels wooden, and not in a charming way, more in like a every line of dialogue they just went with the first take, and called it a wrap. Character movement and jumping around as just feels floaty, and overall just off.Of course it launched with Denuvo DRM, and there is traversal stutter (that is immediately noticeable when you decide to use skateboards in particular). I don't know if the traversal stutter is due to shader compilation stutter, but that does seem to be a very common problem in newer games. And there is no shader compiling on startup, so I'm kind of assuming that's what the problem is.So much of the original games charm, or what made it stand out, has been changed or altered in destructive ways for my taste. The new voice cast isn't even particularly bad, it's just mainly the soulless line delivery. It's like they couldn't be bothered.Most character models are pretty faithful to the originals, which sort of creates an uncanny valley effect with most characters, where in the original they had a very stylized look, and implementing this together with RE Engine's ultra-photorealistic aesthetic creates this very ugly, and uncanny look that I'm honestly just not a fan of.I really wanted this remake to be the ultimate way to play the original Dead Rising, but in most ways it does not feel that way. It's not particularly bad, but then again I don't think anything will ever be as bad as Dead Rising 4 was. It makes me extremely happy to see that Capcom is not giving up on this franchise. But overall this remake just, isn't it. At least for me. I just feel so mixed on it overall. Wanting to love it, but feeling so disappointed with a lot of the changes made.The most egregious is the change to one of the psychopaths (Psychopaths in Dead Rising are boss encounters, that are usually crazy survivors you meet in different locations). One of them in the original is supposed to be a Vietnam War Veteran, suffering from PTSD.Now with the change that has been made to his dialogue, he could be just a veteran of *any* war. It is an absolutely ridiculous change.Overall RE Engine is an incredibly well optimized engine, but I'm genuinely so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sick of Capcom shipping every new game release with Denuvo DRM, so for at least the first 6 months it has overall worse performance. Until they eventually strip the DRM out of the game, and then it starts running like it should have at launch. (We seen this with Resident Evil Remake 2, 3, and I don't personally know if it was a problem with 4).Shader compilation stutter may also be an issue, as there is no shader compiling on startup. And I'm not going to lie I am borderline sick of games not launching with shader compilation on startup. When is this just going to be a standard feature to launch with your game. This should be standard on PC by now.Overall as someone who was a massive fan of the two original Dead Rising games, this remake has me feeling mixed and sort of put off. As a newcomer, it's probably worth a buy at least at a 30% discount or more once they fix the performance issues. Myself this remake is not for me, and I don't have interest in picking it up again.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original Dead Rising when I was quite young, and somehow even more imbecilic than I am now. I managed to beat it, but the experience was quite an abrasive one; my child mind couldn't grip the idea that following routes outside of quest markers could be optimal, or that guns wouldn't be the best solution for every possible scenario. It was a game I ultimately walked away from not understanding neither the love surrounding it nor even its most basic structural design. Having played this remaster, I safely and definitively say I was wrong. This game rules, and almost all of its best bits trace back to that original release, and many of its weaknesses are contingent on this iteration. A title that encourages creativity, environmental awareness, and arcadey replayfulness supercharged to the max is a welcome delight in the modern era of gaming. Throwing cardboard boxes at a zombie to stun them, then running up and suplexing them into half a dozen other zombies never once failed to make me smile. The athletic abilities you unlock for Frank are almost all handily useful, and just simply fun to employ. The final stretch of the game is relatively far less imaginative, with its most obvious desire to showcase a strength in rendering hundreds of zombies having been long outdone by the march of time, but that, and that alone, is the only sore point I could nail down in the original design document. For this release specifically, I don't like Erotica's removal, I don't like the absurd speed with which you can level, I love the changes to survivor AI and responsiveness, the graphical overhaul was almost always an improvement- sans lighting- and the modern control scheme worked quite a treat for me. I considered DRDR well worth the $50 I paid for, almost specifically for its reserved length, but the fact that it's so replayable means that value will only get drawn from me again and again. It gets a very strong recommendation from me if you also dislike modern design's focus on accessibility over all.

_childDocuments_.review: Eighteen years on, the original  gets a remake, or rather a "deluxe remaster" out of absolutely nowhere. I have had, let's call it, fleeting experiences with the franchise, but mostly by way of the Blue Castle Games-made sequels, which are very different games. I skipped the original, not out of hate for it, but rather that it was a super early seventh-gen game that I missed. Never got the hype for the franchise, didn't love the sequels, and forgot about it. But this re-release gave me the perfect opportunity to acquaint myself with a cult classic. Turns out they were right to praise it. , in its earliest hours, walks the line between fascinating and frustrating, dropping you into a semi-sandbox environment with the very vague aim of uncovering the truth about Willamette's sudden zombie outbreak. As a kid, the idea of being dropped into an endless parade of the undead, and finding new ways to kill them sounds pretty fun. But to adult me, it was an immediate wall of me not getting it. Only after a few hours did I truly begin to appreciate the game's unwavering commitment to player agency, and learning to find the fun in it. You have seventy-two hours until the helicopter returns, seventy-two hours to find the truth, and seventy-two hours to rescue survivors, saving them from deranged psychopaths a little too committed to the bit. Miss a survivor? Oops, dead. Miss a story beat? Oops, the truth vanishes into darkness. Can't beat a psychopath? Oops, you're dead. Want to spend seventy-two hours doing nothing at all? We can accommodate that. The brilliance of  lies in a tightly designed environment in which you have almost complete freedom. I say almost because of the timer, which can seem a little primitive to begin with. But you realise shortly that without it, a lack of tension, of will, desire even, will fill up inside you and, without realising, you'd slip back into the aimless stupor. It is the game's single most defining trait. It throws you head first into discovery whether you like it or not, forces you to make use of your very limited time as efficiently as possible, and forces you to acclimate yourself with every food drop, weapon drop and area of significance within the mall.  The game simply doesn't exist without it. This cycle of saving survivors, and returning to the security room became super addicting for me, beyond reason. I think a lot of it is owed to the dynamic nature of the environment's inhabitants. Randomly, you'll run into a band of escaped convicts, or cult members dedicated to... something. On their own, just more obstacles, but with survivors trailing you? Now it's serious. Because those survivors are frail and stupid (unless you read some books on the subject), and you will have to go the extra mile, lend a shoulder, carry them even, if you want them to see the light of day. The story is something only a Japanese team could write, with its satirical critique of corporate culture, the American citizen's psychotic dedication to the flag along with their excessive, self-indulgent lifestyle and the cover-ups that ensue in the name of patriotism. It teaches you to fear, not the individuals responsible, but the collective that forgives and forgets daily atrocities in a need for personal comfort. Mind, it does all this in a much sillier way than I describe. A very wide man convinced he's still in Nam will try and kill you, another very wide man dressed as a clown will also try to kill you at some point, and another very wide man (seriously, why is everyone so wide?) will kill you for trespassing in his store, careless to the apocalypse happening right outside his door. All acting in the function of their jobs, way past the point of reason. It's all very stupid, and not all that serious. What I love most of all, is Frank's nonchalant, eye-rolling reactions to all of it. I like the idea that despite the severity of everything, this is just another day in his life. I just realised I forgot to say how much of a blast it is to mow down hordes of the undead! With an endless list of items to brandish as weapons, and an array of neck-breaking, gut-wrenching combos from our big ugly protagonist. It's the main draw of the game, and what most will find memorable. In closing, , like many seventh-generation games has aged spectacularly, and this Deluxe Remaster is a great way to play it, retaining the foundations, and adding some necessary QoL features along the way (like auto-save and time skip). If you are new, like me, or returning, this is still a bunch of fun. Highly recommended. It's a Capcom world, we're just living in it.

_childDocuments_.review: [No story spoilers, but, maybe other kinds so be cautious if you want to go in fresh]TL:DR - Yeah, if you really love the original's story and game play, you should feel right at home IF you NEED a reason to hop into Willamette 2.0. Otherwise the original is still there (and cheaper) with all it's wonderful charm right in tact.   Taking into account how much time I've spent with the original across multiple platforms, I have a lot to say about the original, both good and bad. To me it is a special game (my first solo purchase!) and possibly my favorite series in any game media. It is not, and never has been, a 10/10 game, objectively. Regardless I've had a 10/10 experience with the original for over 10 years now (and honestly the 2nd or OTR pick whatever.)    This "Deluxe Remaster" is mildly involved in bringing some beta/ alpha mechanics and designs, and removing some, that a lot of people have grown to love. Erotica is gone, but I never really interacted with it outside it's required usage because I only ever interacted with the camera when it was useful to my situation (PP Stickers, brutality/ horror/ drama/ outtake/ ~erotica~,  and the legendary no genre shots,) so this did not bother me much. The camera angles during some cut-scenes are seemingly "closer to the action" and while that is fine for the wide panned out shots, it is not for the close up personal ones. Heads get cut off and well I would appreciate an FOV slider I'll say that much. Personally I think the graphics (when bugs and errors are not present) are fine, the volumetric lighting is a cool edition but nighttime lacks that "video game" kinda vibe with the more realistic lighting.  Characters feel "just as" expressive as the original because they kind of weren't as finely animated (hair follicles/ body language/ eye/ mouth/ head movement) and now they do. (Irrelevant)   The voice acting is removable, should I ever get tired of hearing it, and overall is fine, but it would be great if some characters had better direction on their delivery.  TJ Rotolo made Frank work really well, too well even, so of course the new guy pales in comparison but he still did a good job of giving Frank a new breath of life, if only just this once. The most notable downgrades are Brad and Adam because the original VA's really put their damn feet in it. Nobody really got "upgraded" unless they didn't have a voice in the first place.   All of the areas now have gates attached to their loading zones, traversing the mall is UBER FAST now like skateboards are faster than the dang cars. Weapons have status bars, the durability of items has been adjusted and the animations have been adjusted for a more hit and run style of game play which means you do have to think just a touch more about your weapon arc and damage. Melee combos are easier to pull off in the modern control scheme, and after a few button swaps my brain adjusted just fine and I felt no loss in skill compared to the original (which to be honest was only challenging until I learned of the mini chainsaws.) Juice blenders have 1 more function and you can just make a quickste... "Fleetfoot" in the safe room.  You may also do a little "timeskip" if you want, it's just in the game now.Survivor AI is slightly more dependable, but once you've done a saint play through you should know the way to keep them safe every time regardless of if you give them supplies or not.  Some survivor interactions has been altered and none of it really effects the main story, just interpersonal dialogue. The comments YOUR survivors make will be more like "very unavoidable hints" and you may feel as if you're playing LAD 7/8 with how often they make them. The Boss fights AKA the Psychopaths/ Maniacs/ etc. are somewhat more challenging overall, and scale in a more linear fashion compared to the original. I was using abilities I never really wanted to before because it was just fun to pull of a good combo with snappier controls. It wasn't impossible to use abilities in the original, but they at least feel a bit more intuitive now. They removed some terminology and MASSIVELY redesigned a certain boss-fight, but I'm not really qualified to comment on that, nor do I want to use it as a wedge to insert politics into this game about exposing a massive government conspiracy while putting funny horse masks on zombies and dressing up in whatever outfit I want to so the cut-scenes look funny. (you can still ogle the pretty girls, son, you just don't get the pink circle.)   The game is just as difficult to get off the ground as ever if you really don't know how to level your Frank. Running the cycle I've always run in the beginning (as many PP stickers in the entrance/ paradise as I can and the plates/ treadmills etc) and while you do gain levels really quickly, bosses scale differently, and don't (easily) die in one shot. I'd recommend just playing casually your first time and seeing how far you can go before you reset if you even want to.   As a long time fan I really hope this is the breath of life that Dead Rising needs to maybe get a new game, with a new cast just doing what Dead Rising does best. This remake deserves the chance to stand on it's own legs via game-play merit alone. I recognize this is a long shot, but a true remaster like this also felt like a long shot for over a decade now. All in all this delivers almost everything I can ask for, and what it didn't, I can probably get with mod support, should mod makers be so kind and creative as they are known to be. No it's not a 10/10 because Dead Rising never was a 10/10. This remake was never going to change that no matter how successful it was. I enjoyed my time, if you don't like what they've done, then enjoy the OG to your heart's content.    The changes to infinity mode are actually really fun. Survivors and Bosses seem to spawn at random, certain NPC's and zombies will give you random drops from time to time. They cut the experience down by a LANDSLIDE as the skip time option is available, but no saving. Only built in suspending. A far cry from what Capcom asked of you on the 360/ PC ports (14 hours or more of your machine being on and running if there's no rest mode option and even then, the port crashes at certain points so you have to route around that.) Though if you don't want to use the timeskip, and you'd like to sit around in the Mall for 14 hours, go on ahead. It's a good way to get some challenges done without a hard time restriction. Just HP. It feels MUCH harder to not die in this mode, especially around the 3 day mark. I did not experience any crashes (except for my own skill issue) in the 6 Days and 18ish hours I survived for.   I'm glad I can give a genuine recommendation  (I have before, warts and all) this game to my friends and family now because I don't have to do the whole "well it's a bit tough and jank but it's got a lot of really cool ideas" song and dance because they have auto-save and some stairs by the vent. Not everyone is going to like this game, not everyone has to. I do, and I think this Remaster does a good job at being Dead Rising, not a perfect job, but a pretty damn good one.

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Rising's remaster delivers exactly what I hoped for: a graphical boost that stays true to its art style, and it runs surprisingly well even on the Steam Deck.Gameplay tweaks like autosaves, time skips, and new magazines are welcome additions, though they don’t drastically change the core experience. The game’s quirks remain intact, and while some dialogue changes might bug die-hard purists, they’re barely noticeable (unless you're the type to obsess over tiny details or follow certain YouTubers a bit too closely).After 18 years, Dead Rising still holds up remarkably well. Mowing down hordes with cars and chainsaws is just as satisfying now as it was back then. The somewhat tense time management mechanics and variety of psychopaths keep things interesting, and honestly, this remaster might be a great entry point for newcomers. Plus, you’re bound to have those "Oh, it’s definitely a Japanese game" moments — the creativity and sheer absurdity are unmistakable.That said, I do have two gripes. First, the weird change to Isabela’s face — she now looks more like Megan Fox, which kind of strips away her original charm. And second, the game crashed once during my infinite mode playthrough on day 6 out of 7, causing me to lose all my progress. That was pretty frustrating, but thankfully it only happened once.

_childDocuments_.review: As you play this game, the seemingly clumsy controls of Frank will become second nature. You will learn the mall like the back of your hand. You will begin to immediately recall what store spawns your favorite weapon or where the closest orange juice is located.The Willamette Mall might be an all-timer video game location and the constantly ticking clock will be all the incentive you need to master it. Between the deliberately confined location, the constantly ticking clock, and the fact that you need to keep looking out for good photo ops because you are a photographer/reporter, Dead Rising is not just another zombie action game.This game gets better with multiple playthroughs and I am higher on it now after getting all the achievements than I was when I rolled credits for the first time.The story/cutscenes were nothing special but I really like the zombies "origin story" that gets revealed throughout the game. Infinity mode provides even more replayability and challenge as well. I think some of the characters and moments in this game are extremely memorable and I am so glad to have gotten to experience this game.

_childDocuments_.review: More downgrades than improvements. Lots of missing effects like blood effects, dismemberment effects, mirror reflections, unrefined audio. The voice acting is not as good as it once was in the 2006 version. There are missing animations, missing or altered lines of dialogue. The game is way easier than it should be. Lots of additions to the game give you too many hints. You level up way faster, removing a lot of the challenge. Any management you had to do in the original game to survive is pretty much gone or just made pointless. Moving place to place is now way faster so you never feel like you're tight on time, removing more tension. Zombies, which are the most common enemy in the game, are less aggressive and way less of an obstacle, making the main threat not threatening at all. The path finding for the NPCs is at times just as bad as they were in the 2006 version. Often times escorted survivors and enemies get stuck on props easily. The auto saves make manual saves in save areas redundant and also makes it easy to undo any punishment the game had, like getting captured. The only thing this game really has to boast is its new graphics and even that is unpolished. Anyone with dark hair now looks like they have gray hair because of how weird the lighting reflects off it. This game feels cheaply produced and it's pretty obvious seeing how it's outsourced to a Chinese developer and how this game was not even marketed that much. I would say, just play the 2006 version that's still available on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: Here is my honest review of the game:- The game is ABSOLUTELY fantastic! As far as remasters go this is definitely one of the best I have ever played. The amount of quality of life changes made in this version is astounding. I was worried that time skipping would make the game too easy but to my surprise the way the game is made the fact you can time skip really doesn't change much in the grand scheme of things and definitely made infinity mode an actually fun mode to play not having to wait 14 real hours.- PP stickers having picture clues makes them so much easier to find and that's not a bad thing as a don't have to look up a 30 minute guide on how to find them all and can actually look for myself.- The achievement challenges are an amazing addition as well actually giving an incentive to 100% the game (Which I myself did within 3 days of release lol) as well as of course adding the closet where you can keep all the clothes you find and earn throughout the mall which is much better than running around the entire mall to assemble your favorite outfit.- The voice acting is good despite everyone's complaints, the only real reason I can think that people hate on it so much is because the love the original's voice acting which I personally agree is a lot better but that doesn't make the remakes voice acting "bad" by any means (though I am personally not a fan of Brad's voice in this version).My complaints about this remake:- Leveling is much too easy in this version.. I found myself at a much higher level in this version than the original at some points making the game feel a lot easier and hurting the replayability a bit.- Another complaint is of course the censorship.. and while I understand why the changes were made I do think that it did take away from the personality of the game a small amount.- The final (small) complaint I have is that the dlc costs an extra 10 bucks because I didn't buy the deluxe edition which a lot of companies seem to do but I still dislike, I don't think the extra costumes are worth another 20 bucks so I will sadly have to wait for a sale.BUT all in all I love this remaster and I really REALLY hope that capcom see's all these positives reviews left (I was worried it would get review bombed but thankfully not) and consider making a remake for the second game, I'd love to play it with a friend!

_childDocuments_.review: I was absolutely obsessed with the original Dead Rising back in high school. I poured over every inch of the mall, worked tirelessly to unlock that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ real Mega Buster, and spent countless hours in infinity mode. When this remake was revealed, I was initially super hesitant, but damn. This might be Capcom's best remake yet. Everything has been faithfully restored. All the little secrets. _childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: Has some bugs and took a while to get used to the new control scheme. It also has some changes I question, like adding doors between every zone (You used to be able to just walk into the movie theatre, idk why it needs a gate toggle) Or changing Franks voice actor. (Terence Rotolo will always be the real Frank West!)Other changes I like, the leveling system is much easier, (Was able to hit level 49 by the time i finished overtime mode) I remember the original being a lot harder, and while this is no cakewalk, it can be finished in one playthrough.Overall, I like this remaster. If you havent played the original in a long while, is a fun excuse to go back to, and if you've never played Dead Rising, then this is a good way to play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: I just wrapped up 100% completing the game, so I'll keep this very short and simple: Then you'll appreciate all of the great quality of life features, including the ability to fast forward time, vastly improved survivor AI, new unlockables, restored cut content, and more! It might not be worth full price, but I'd say you're the intended audience for this game. And if you ever had a dreaded Xbox 360 Red Ring happen in your attempt to achieve 7 Day Survivor, I've got great news: The new fast forward feature works in that as well, along with the ability to suspend save! Then you'll love the improved controls and really grow to love all of the above changes. Some of the jank is still there, but it's the kind of jank you grow to appreciate after a while of playing. Then while I'll definitely say this is currently the best way to play it, there are some things here and there that got lost in translation (Some of them intentional), so while I do recommend you give this a playthrough, I'd also suggest playing the original right afterwards so you too can appreciate all of the new changes. The new voice cast is more hit than miss, and while Frank's new actor really grew on me the longer I played it (But just as David Hayter will always be Snake, TJ will always be Frank West), Stephen and Brad and definite downgrades. I'm also not one to harp on the other changes made, as they seem to be more for selling the game in other countries than anything else. You can still buy and play the original game if they do personally bother you, though.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure what's up with this one but can't get it to play nice with my PC at all with Ryzen 7 5800x and 4070ti. I went back to Re4 remake which runs like a dream but no matter what settings I try in DRDR (texture quality settings, dlss on or off) I get stuttering every time I enter an area and just regularly running around the mall as well with huge dips in Wonderland Plaza and several other areas. Even though the framerate itself doesn't always tank, it is always choppy, except in cutscenes.I think removing the Erotica photo type was probably a good idea but some other changes are just patronising and odd like the Vietnam vet. The faces are not expressive like in the REmakes and some of the voice acting is considerably worse than the original (Brad is terrible for example and TJ Rotolo is sincerely missed even though I don't totally hate the new guy) As a big fan of the original, I'm pretty disappointed with this so far and it feels like a waste of money. Hoping they patch and optimise it as I might just drop it without finishing since it's frustrating to look at.

_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: Another great modern remake of a classic Capcom title! This feels astronomically easier to play by comparison to the 2006 release. The QoL improvements make a night and day difference. It's still clunky but intentionally so. _childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing the game I fully recommend Deluxe Remaster. It is mechanically improved over the original in every meaningful way. Being able to move while aiming, having autosaves, and the much better survivor AI make a big impact on how enjoyable the entire experience is. I didn't have trouble with performance issues or crashes like other reviews mention, my setup is a 5700X3D CPU, 6800XT GPU, and 32GB of RAM.The new voices are definitely not bad, and at moments I found they had better direction for the VAs than the original game. The only negative is Brad's new voice not being as good as his original. He just doesn't have the same cool attitude or emotional impact, but every other voice is just as good as the original cast and sometimes better. I really enjoyed Jessie's and Adam the Clown's performances for this game. We also have Dave Fennoy coming in to finally give Otis a voice, and it makes him instantly lovable.I would definitely recommend this game to both long time Dead Rising fans and newcomers. This is the best way to get into the series, or re-experience this classic.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: DR was already an amazing game, everything has their flaws show more and more with age and the original's AI is a great example of this with how miserably clunky replays can be.So far this remake makes the AI far more responsive, adds bits content here and there, and overall spruces up the player experience to leave nothing but positives and smoother gameplay. Really hope we see 2 get the same treatment someday.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: I gotta admit this is an absolute GODSEND of a remaster. I have played the original Dead Rising, and this version delivers not only the classic story I absolutely love but improves upon the original gameplay by so much. The ability to side strafe while aiming doesn't sound like a big deal until you weave out of the way of a big ol Hummer. The camera got a huge buff, making taking pictures actually viable for level-ups. They also introduced camera add-ons allowing you to upgrade the camera giving you more camera.... who doesn't love more camera. The graphical improvements are obvious, don't need to talk about that. I don't understand why people are complaining about CAPCOM removing stuff like erotica and the big Asian guy. I felt like they weren't needed to begin with, so it never felt like anything was lost.Bottom line this game feels like it was made by actual Dead Rising fans. The amount of viable effort put into this remaster is astonishing and should not be over looked.I'm giving this a Smokin' Sexy Style!! out of Smokin' Sexy Style!!... definitely not cause Dante is holding a gun to my head.

It becomes super satisfying once you get the hang of things.The story? It’s alright, nothing mind-blowing. But if you collect all the cases, the ending is actually pretty fun.The graphics are solid—like, if you pushed an Xbox 360 game to the max, this is what you’d get. Looks great for a remaster.The first playthrough was frustrating as hell. I didn’t know where to go or what to do. But once you figure out where the skateboard and tunnel keys are, everything starts to click, and it becomes a lot smoother.All in all, this game has ended up in my top 5 this year. It might be a bit rough at the start, but stick with it, and it gets really addicting.Don't be afraid to start over. Makes the game much better if you treat as a roguelike.

_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: This ain't it chief.The game as a whole is just not great, the OG is by miles better.Visually it's kind of a cluster♥♥♥♥, with great lighting and reflections, updated to look like what you would expect from current tech, but other details are poor. Shadows and effects such as smoke and fire look extremely bad with low draw distance, textures are mostly blurry or low res except the floors and the zombies themselves which do look great, but things like clothing and objects barely seem touched. What this does is give the game an uncanny feel as you have realistic lighting and reflections along the terrible effects and textures. Every graphical option is set to the max available mind you, so unless I have something bugged within the game I just don't see why would I choose this over the OG, at least the OG was visually consistent according to its limitations.Animations are not great either, I know the OG and even DR 2 and 3 were clunky and stiff, however, here most attacks send the zombies flying in a weird angle, even if you punch them. As I recall and noticed from playing DR 2 this past week, even that game had varied and somewhat more grounded animations, funny, yes but then again not uncanny as they are in this remaster. Hell even when you jump Frank floats for a good 2-3 seconds in the air for no reason.What frustrates me the most is that Capcom had been putting out great remakes with Resident Evil, I can't fault any of them, but this one feels cheap, like no time or detailing was put into it. It rubs me the wrong way as if most of the work was done by AI, and looking at the inconsistencies it might very well have been an AI putting this remaster together. This is nowhere near the quality of the recent RE remakes. Even more baffling is why there was time to remove parts of the original game and change characters for people who won't even buy your game, but there wasn't to polish the textures, the animations, you know, ♥♥♥♥ that we are going to look at for the entirety of it?If this is the kind of effort Capcom is going to put from now on, don't even bother remaking or remastering anything else, let the other franchises rest in peace.Edit: While continuing to endure it, I noticed a few more things worth mentioning. While using 1440p resolution, I upped the texture resolution slider in the game options to 200%, textures look slightly better but still blurry enough to be unacceptable, for instance the first time you get out of the vents, the vent door texture still looks like ♥♥♥♥.The depth of field effect is also terrible, instead of providing a proper sense of depth, it just blurries everything that is about 4 to 5 steps away from you, if I wanted to feel like my sight is going bad, I would just stop wearing glasses instead.Zombies cast shadows only when they feel like it. Some do cast, some others don't cast a shadow regardless of how far or close to them I am, some others only cast a shadow of their head, so the shadow looks like there is just a head floating around. Overall my only feeling about the game right now is disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: A very faithful remaster to the original 2006 game, it's clear that a lot of time and dedication was put into this game. There is some changes to the game. However they are very minimal and understandable as Capcom want's to appeal to other markets then just the american one this time. [Larry's new design looks very good] The Gameplay story is exactly the same as the original with no alterations made to it. The game is more easy going in the beginning then the original however certain twists in the game can trick up even the most veteran of players and the game gets a lot harder then it previously did in the endgame stage even for higher levels giving it a more fun experienceIf your a big fan of the classic version its 100% worth checking out this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: a lot of quality of life improvements for first time players, Some minor censorship that isn't at all a big deal and while I still prefer the original/remastered versions more this is still a solid way to play Dead Rising I hope Capcom remasters Dead Rising 2 along with both Case Zero and Case West and the "what if" senario  Dead Rising 2: Off the Record
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: It's quite good, a pretty faithful remaster with a ton of QOL improvements. The biggest one by far is that survivors will for the most part just bob and weave when moving through zombies, which makes it MUCH easier to actually save them. The game looks good and even the new voice lines from different voice actors feel pretty faithful to the original. I'll admit, it was odd at first not hearing the voices I'm used to, but the actual voice acting is way better than the first go around.The only real issue I've had is stuttering. It's not so bad now that I've capped the VRAM to 4GB, but I've got a 3080Ti so I know that by itself shouldn't be a problem. Overall though it runs well and I'm having a great time playing through this fantastic game with a fresh coat of paint on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing Dead Rising since 2006 back on the Xbox 360.This is everything a remaster should be.Visuals look awesome, and I haven't had any performance dips. In the original Dead Rising, there's a significant amount of hitstop when using melee weapons. It's incredibly noticeable when playing at high refresh rates, and never felt natural to me. There's no hitstop in the remaster.My only complaint is the voice acting. I think it's fine here, but doesn't match up to the original game. Brad's, Jessie's, and Frank's voices were iconic.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good remaster despite all the changes (eg. infamous "mole" scene, Brad conveying less emotion in his speech, no "What in the world...").I like re-addition of beta content from original DR (eg. handgun officer zombies, some zombie models) and new mechanics (eg. blocking Carlito's shots with a barrel).I would recommend playing. It doesn't change the game from the original too much (I'm looking at you RE3), but keeps it faithful - I guess?
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: A great remaster that is extremely faithful to the original while adding some well needed QoL improvements.  The gameplay is modernized a fair bit, but still retains the good kind of "jank" the OG Dead Rising had.  Game looks stellar in the graphical department, and the full voice acting adds a whole new layer of immersion to the game.  My biggest (and really only) complaint is the performance.  There were a couple times, mainly in Wonderland Plaza, I had a noticeable drop in framerates.  But it was nothing that made the game unplayable.  And for some reason, the amount of zombies that can be on the screen at once seems to have been HEAVILY reduced.  There is substantial pop-in across the entire game for hordes and environmental objects.  I don't understand how the original (which is almost 20 years old at this point) was able to manage bigger zombie crowds.  The game would have benefited from a few more months in the oven, and it feels like they rushed a bit to meet the September 18th release date to line up with the date the game take place.All in all if you're a fan of the original or a newcomer to the series, this is without a doubt the definitive way to play Dead Rising.  Holding out hope for remaster of Dead Rising 2!
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: I think it isssss alright, but i refunded it. The game looks nice, puts a smile on my face to see the mall remastered. but capcom, i would only repurchase this game if there was some sort of setting to have it be EXACTLY like the OG. I KNOW a remaster is supposed to change and update some things, you can still have the controls be different/handle a lil different (while aimming etc) but they simply made it wayyyy too easy. you are totally spoiled with the blender right at home base giving you quickstep (now fleetfoot). LOTS more PP stickers and that's fine i guess, but they also give you 5000 XP as opposed to 1000 XP in the original.Now i want to say.... the rest of these changes that make the game easier, definitely come from a lot of JANK that the game had, or whatever you might call it. It was pretty much a nightmare to fight most bosses "legit" AKA not just sniping them down or using adam's small chainsaw. It makes a lot more diversity to playing the game possible. It also irritated a lot of folks that its impossible to get all survivors on your first run (maybe it's possible if you're a freakish speedrunner or something lol) and it seems like you could/come close to getting them all. I'm sitting here being an old man yelling up at the cloud going "KIDS THESE DAYS DIDN'T GET TO EXPERIENCE OUR SUFFERING, THEY'LL NEVER KNOW TRUE GAMING!"But there really is a good point to that. At first, i'm sure back in 2006 it pissed so many people off. But once you know what you gotta do, failed so many times. you know that mall like the damn back of your hand. The blenders you wanna hit for quickstep to get around, bikes and vehicles, skateboards in the shops. The mall is truly fighting you while you're using everything you can to fight back against it and race the clock to beat everything and bring it together just PERFECT.............. except for the AI being idiots, wasting your damn time, and getting chowed down on lolbut it is an AMAZING and fun/funny game, even if it is frustrating at times. But the remaster seems to COMPLETELY remove that IMO.So for better or worse, if you like it thats fine, enjoy it. But that's my opinion on why I refunded it. Love to play Dead Rising 1 with a modern look but they simply made it too easy for me, really wish there was an option to ENGAGE THE SUFFERING! Really wouldn't be so bad with the modern AI i feel but who knows lol.And hey, i still have the original on steam, which they DID NOT remove unlike SOME OTHER DEFINITIVE EDITIONS AND REMASTERS
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time Dead Rising fan: This is as close to how (and why) remakes should be done, with some quirks.First off, if you've never played Dead Rising I 100% recommend this as the starting point now. You can always check out the original after the fact (as of writing it's still available)Pros:RE Engine made this game look PRETTY. Everything looks great hear, the posters, the zombies, the mall, almost all of the character models (looking at you Frank). The lighting is spectacular.Survivor AI has been upgrade ALMOST too much. I don't need to spam the call button every step I take toward the security room and the addition of stairs leading up to the vent is *chef's kiss*They kept the core of the game play intact, but polished with modern tools not available in 2006 and they've provided the option for classic controls and modern controls. I haven't bothered switching to the OG controls because the modern controls are so smooth.One of the most impressive parts of the OG is the sound design and this is a glow up I didn't even know I needed. Cons:There have been a few moments of me skipping dialogue and getting ahead of myself and ruining a survivor prompt. I can't tell if this is a bug that could be triggered in the OG, but it's a bit frustrating.Frank has been aged up visually but nothing in the narrative indicates that this is not supposed to be the same nearly 30 year old man. He now looks just shy of 50. He literally looks closer to his OG Dead Rising model in DR4. Fortunately the OG cosmetic is available. So far every other model has been upgraded very well.This isn't necessarily a con, but it feels like XP gain is cranked to 1000x. In the OG it took a good handful of playthroughs to max out your level. In this it only takes barely 2 playthroughs. While great for increasing the pacing as the story and quests get more busy, it does feel like it makes the game TOO easy in some regards. Regardless the cons that I have are negligible and honestly subjective. I would love not only DR2 remastered in the same fashion but a Resident Evil Outbreak style game would also be great fun. Definitely worth the pick up.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: I had my doubts about this to be honest, Every change worried me, from VA's to designs to features being removed. And despite all that the game feels GREAT! I do wish the difficulty of the original was still here, You can literally be lvl 10+ from the helicopter ride at the beginning and you can easily hit lvl 50 in your first playthrough without really meaning too. The new movement system (aiming and walking at the same time) Makes bosses WAY to easy as they're clearly not designed for that. Game graphically looks great, There's a bit of pop in especially outside, and sometimes i prefer how the original looks. If you have any doubts sure wait for a sale, but I was honestly pleasantly surprised and have struggled to put it down at times. I've played both on steamdeck and my PC and had a playable experience on both except some of my playtime and achievements aren't tracking on steamdeck but oh well gives me more reason to play again!
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: while i do wholeheartedly recommend this game to anyone who played this on the 360 back in the day, after the time i spent with DR2 and its awesome crafting system this game just feels .. meh. a huge layer of the wackiness and fun i got from the dead rising series growing up was making absolutely insane weapons at the crafting tables, and DR1 just never had that. if thats not a huge issue for you and you can look past the barebones nature of the combat than grab this one for nostalgia sake, unfortunately its a refund for me as i just dont see myself playing through the whole thing with no crafting.Awesome updated graphics, typical beefy Capcom graphics options, and i honestly like franks new voice acting here. I would offer more insight into the positives (which im sure theres PLENTY more of) but I only put about an hour in so I'll just leave it at what I personally was able to see myself in the short time i played.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: I wont say this is a phenomenal remaster, but its very close to it! The foundation of the game is there; the gameplay, the music, everything that makes it a Dead Rising game is there but upgraded and better, some might say the game is a little too ‘Easy’ but i think the word is more ‘Accessibile’, especially if we’re talking about the infamous Infinite Mode, now that you can suspend progress and fast forward timeI have finished the story, overtime and 7 Day Survivor Infinite Mode try and give a lowdown so far in my experiencePros;+ Graphics are fantastic! It may shoo people away like me, especially the facial models of characters, but it sorta.. fit in with the Dead Rising style+ Controls/Gameplay feel improved, especially in the skill moves aspect, they are easy to pull off now than they were in the original, you can run and gun, theres more features for your camera+ You can still use skill moves on Survivors and Subboss Enemies, a detail that stands out to me which brought me great nostalgia seeing Frank West disembowel Special Forces, Cultists and even allied survivors lmao+ A little bit of items, theres some weapons like the rocket launcher, theres more magazines that provide unique buffs, like being able to use any item on a blender ANY ITEM, i combined a cardboard box with a fire extinguisher and got a Spitfire drink, and theres more magazines to find while exploring+ Survivor AI is massively improved! They wont get stuck too much many more, but i have noticed i think depending on their personality they’ll be more aggressive to zombies, can always do the classic spam of saying ‘Follow me’ to unstuck them+ More Accessibility! Enough said, games more accessible with a variety of optiond+ Some bosses are easier Some are much more harderNeutral. _childDocuments_.review: When this game was first announced, I was incredibly happy, as the franchise had all but been abandoned since around 2018 with the closing of Capcom Vancouver, leaving fans depressed as the main Capcom franchises like RE & Street Fighter stole the spotlight with successful games. I would've preferred a new game, but a remake is a safe bet, and I'm just happy to see Dead Rising again. Hang on, it's not a remake, it's a "Deluxe Remaster". That is the stupidest thing I've ever heard in my life. Until I actually played it, then I realised "Deluxe Remaster" is the perfect way to describe this. It's very much the same game at it's core, but with completely redone visuals, necessary quality of life features that make the original hard to go back to, and a complete reshuffle of the voice cast, along with pretty much every line of dialogue fully voiced by someone. The ability to fast forward the in-game clock when at a save point is far more useful than you'd think, as there's more than a few times in the game where you don't really have any main objective to do for about twenty real life minutes. The autosave behaves just like in DR2:OtR, except you can exit the game and resume from it. Don't rely on it though, use manual saves, in fact they give you 20 slots, up from the 2016 remaster's 5 and 2006's NONE. Escorting survivors, while certainly not stress-free by any means, is tremendously easier. The survivors have a simple affinity system where generally looking after them by giving them things (each have a set of favourite items too) and ensuring they don't die improves their morale, making them supposedly more competent and more effective if they have a weapon. I absolutely LOVE that the survivors will randomly tell you game tips, point out powerful weapon locations nearby, and tell you where PP stickers are, it's genuinely adorable. In fact escorting survivors is so much easier I ended up getting the Saint achievement to rescue basically all of them on my first run from Level 1. It's not free by any means though and there were some serious close calls when it came to time, you still need to know what you're doing.Which leads nicely into the overall difficulty, which I'm happy with but a little unsatisfied too. The game is definitely easier in subtle ways, I'd say in a typical area there's about 20-30% less zombies clumped together, but you're going to be getting grabbed the same amount, don't worry. You also level up ridiculously fast. I ended up finishing the game at Level 47, but that was with saving everyone, and honestly? These changes are a good thing, because the original can feel like a frustrating stressful chore, and I mean that in the nicest way possible. I saw somewhere on the internet recently in an article or a video or something describe the original game as being made by aliens and you just have to accept it's strange frustrating mechanics to get anywhere (paraphrasing) and I couldn't agree more. However, while these changes make the game easier, this game is still Dead Rising. It's still very weird and does dumb things like going from having loads of free time to being severely crunched, throwing boss fights at you that you couldn't have possibly known about, and toward the end, allowing you to be relentlessly stunlocked. Someone who finished the original is gonna have a lot of fun, but ultimately breeze through this. My fear is that someone who didn't play the original, who doesn't have the patience to sit through those Dead Risingisms™, is still going to give up just as fast and forever look at this franchise with an "eugh" face, and that makes me quite sad. How do I propose making it more palatable for newer players? I don't know, add an easy mode, where there's way more food around, and it does more, or the player has a flat damage reduction bonus. Why not make it like classic RE4 and have some dynamic difficulty going on, or make zombies drop actually good weapons sometimes (police dropping pistols do not count. pistols are not good.). Hell, even having like 3 autosaves instead of 1 could help people who severely messed up their time management. Just throwing out ideas here, it's not too late. Probably.Anyway in lighter news, it looks and runs like a dream on PC. Defaulted to generally high settings on my painfully average system and it stuck to 1080p60, dropping frames exactly once in Wonderland Plaza, where it was only for about 3 seconds, and by about 5-10FPS. As a modern Capcom game it has a downright nauseating amount of graphics options and supports FSR, DLSS & XeSS like you'd hope. It also only crashed once, annoyingly right near the end, but the autosave stops any potential heartbreak. Unless it crashes while autosaving. There's also some noticeable pop-in, distractingly so in cutscenes, but I'm just going to assume that'll be patched.As a final note, some very loud & annoying people on the internet complain that this game has been censored. The censorship in question? The game doesn't acknowledge when you take creep photos, a boss toward the end of the game was redesigned to not be weirdly and blatantly racist, and one line of dialogue from another boss was reworded to not mention the Vietnam war. That's literally it. The changes fit in very well and a new player would be none the wiser. Everything else is the same. If you're upset by these, I don't know what to say, you look at the internet too much and don't actually enjoy enough games.Overall, if you played the original and liked it, you'll enjoy playing it again with this much more tolerable version. If you didn't like the original, you won't like this because it is still Dead Rising. If you haven't played the original, mentally prepare yourself for some jank, save in different slots and prepare to potentially have to restart the game over (with your levels at least) if you really mess up. But if you get through it, you might find a really charming game underneath it all, a game so wonderfully inconsistent in its tone you can't help but remember it years and years later, and you'll see why there are so many fans of this franchise. I hope we get a new game if this does well.

_childDocuments_.review: This "Deluxe Remaster" is appropriately named because it's both a light-remake and remaster. This review is going to act more as a comparison to the original rather than a review of the core game because they are very similar.The game plays mostly the same as it did 18 years ago, but with a more modern, updated control scheme. With the modern controls the game will control as expected for a 3rd person action game in 2024. This control scheme also gives the skills that Frank learns more intuitive commands, such as dodge rolling being circle/B on the controller rather than a double forward motion on the left-stick. Frank feels weightier in DRDR and less responsive as a result, almost as if there is built-in input delay. This causes the combat and movement to feel noticeably sluggish when compared with the original. DRDR allows for the use of the original control scheme if preferred, so overall the new controls are a fine addition and completely optional. In DRDR you will be killing zombies, taking pictures, and doing time-gated cases, which are story-related main-quests, survivor rescuing side-quests, and psychopath boss fights. When doing these you gain experience called "PP" or "Prestige Points" which levels Frank up, giving him access to new skills, increased carry capacity, damage, and health.Zombie killing in this game is  the same as in the original. There seems to either be a bug, oversight, or for whatever reason, a deliberate choice, to remove Frank's i-frames when mid-attack. Frank can now be hit, or grabbed out of all of his attacks. This was immediately noticeable and completely disrupts the flow of the combat. This also applies to all psychopath boss fights. This may sound like a good thing to some, because it does make the combat harder, but because the overall game logic is the same as the original, it can, and often does, result in Frank being infinitely stun-locked until he dies, which is incredibly frustrating. Police zombies with handguns can now shoot their guns, which is actually something from one of the many beta versions of the original game, so that's a neat addition, though a little annoying at times.Taking pictures with Franks camera is the second most common mechanic, and it's both better and worse in DRDR. Mechanically the camera is better; there are new camera items found in the mall such as flash, focus, and brightness which add a level of depth to the the camera the original did not have. The original game had "PP" stickers on points of interest scattered around the mall that garnered huge experience bonuses and that has been expanded in DRDR with more POI's in the mall to find. The PP gained from taking pictures has been significantly increased and the erotica category has been removed, which may be upsetting to purists or people generally opposed to censorship. Overall the mechanic works the same way but with a missing category and higher experience rewards.Cases work the same way as the original. They are time-gated and thus can only be accessed during specific times. Apart from the story cases, most of them are survivor escort quests. The survivor AI has been improved and they are far less frustrating to save. They have a "happiness" system and a preferred food that will increase their happiness, which makes them more efficient in combat and more likely to follow orders. They will also point out PP stickers, hidden weapons and give general tutorial-style advice such as how to cook food or make the various power-up drinks from the blender. Speaking of the blender, one was added to the safe room, which is nice. You can also have more survivors at once than in the original. Psychopath boss fights are the next most common, and work mostly the same, though with the changes to Franks i-frames they are harder to deal with. I also noticed that bosses with high mobility such as Adam and Sean will often get stuck on objects and behave erratically compared to the original. The story missions are unchanged.You can now speed up time at save-points which is a welcome change to those that want to experience the story but would rather not wait in real time for new cases to be available.PP Gains have been increased across the board, making leveling up significantly faster. This could be seen as good change to some, but to others this disrupts the balance of the game. Frank being fairly weak at the beginning, and then ridiculously strong by the end was a core part of the balancing of the original game. Leveling up too quick makes this game significantly easier and throws most of the challenge out the window. Capcom should've offered a setting that allowed the original PP gain to alleviate this. They also added new magazines in this game, some of which are absolutely broken, such as one that gives you access to all of Franks skills immediately. For some odd reason, there are far less zombies in the maintenance tunnels, which makes that area far easier to traverse; zombies will also "pop-in" quite noticeably in this area. Overall, the balancing of this game makes it incredibly easy, which is disappointing to me.This game visually looks great. The map geometry hasn't been updated much, if at all though, so sometimes it can look a little strange if you're paying a lot of attention. Character models have been heavily improved in detail (RIP Frank's hairline), and have significant improvements to facial animations. Zombie models are much higher quality and even include updated versions of unused beta models from the original game. They removed the sexually suggestive zombie models from this game. The improved lighting adds to the atmosphere and better sells what time of day it is, which is a welcome improvement to a game with a heavy emphasis on time management. The caveat to this is the game runs pretty bad in some locations on PC, namely Leisure Park and Wonderland Plaza. If I had to guess, this is mostly due to the new dynamic lighting. The game micro-stutters in these areas pretty significantly on my system. I also have recurring low frame-rate when first loading into an area for around 3-5 seconds. These performance issues are odd because I have a fairly powerful PC (3090, i7 10700K, 32GB RAM) and the game is on a fast NVME SSD. DLSS does not help, and these issues persist regardless of screen resolution or graphics settings. The voice acting has been entirely redone down to the zombie moans and groans. Most of the performances sound fine, though it is odd hearing the same lines ("I've covered wars ya know") performed in the exact same way, but with different actors. Frank's new voice is fine, though I prefer the original. The actor for Brad sounds very forced and is by far the worst recast in this game. Everyone else I could take or leave. Zombie ambiance in the mall sounds very quiet to almost non-extent which hurts the atmosphere, especially at night when the mall music is off. The foley sounds such as footsteps, weapon attacks, and blood sprays sound unchanged but remastered. The soundtrack has stayed the same but the songs sound like they have been remastered, or have higher quality files. This remaster has been censored in several different areas. Like I mentioned before, the erotica category has been removed from the camera mechanic, which rewarded you for taking lewd photos of female characters and zombies. Lewd models are now gone, one character was race-swapped from Chinese to White, and another character no longer references the Vietnam war. To some these are positive changes, to others it's a deal breaker, so it really depends on the person.

_childDocuments_.review: A Fresh Coat of Blood – Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster ReviewOverall Rating: 8.5/10Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster brings Frank West’s wild zombie escapade back to life with upgraded graphics, quality-of-life improvements, and a few new surprises for fans of the original. Capcom has taken this iconic 2006 classic and given it the polished, modern feel it deserves without losing the chaotic charm that made it so beloved. While the remaster maintains the original’s focus on creativity and open-world freedom, some dated mechanics hold it back slightly from achieving perfection in the remaster space.Visuals and Graphics : 9/10The Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster gives the game a stunning visual update, taking full advantage of modern hardware. The textures are noticeably sharper, with detailed character models and dynamic lighting that breathe life into the bustling, zombie-filled Willamette Parkview Mall. Frank’s camera now captures even more detail, letting players appreciate the upgraded environment and the sheer madness of zombie hordes. The increased frame rate also means the action runs more smoothly, and the new lighting effects make the mall feel both more alive and more threatening than ever.The graphical overhaul is impressive, and the enhanced visuals make exploring the mall a more immersive experience, highlighting the wild, unpredictable nature of the zombie outbreak and the gritty industrial backdrop of the mall itself.Gameplay and Combat : 8/10The remaster preserves Dead Rising's signature blend of horror, humor, and creativity, with the combo weapons system updated to be more accessible and less cumbersome. The freedom to experiment with everyday objects—from benches to mannequins and garden tools—is as fun and absurd as ever. The game’s weapon variety remains a joy to explore, allowing players to experiment with everything from chainsaws to golf clubs in taking down hordes of zombies in increasingly bizarre ways.Capcom has made some quality-of-life improvements, like smoother aiming controls and more forgiving hit detection, which help the game feel less clunky by modern standards. The save system has also been reworked, allowing for more flexible saving options, a welcome change from the original game’s stricter mechanics. While the classic time-sensitive structure remains, the remaster includes a more relaxed “Sandbox Mode” for players who prefer exploring the mall without the constant pressure of a ticking clock.Story and Characters : 6/10The story of Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster remains true to the original, following photojournalist Frank West as he documents the zombie outbreak in Willamette. The narrative is mostly unchanged, sticking to its mix of horror and satire, with Frank’s deadpan humor shining as he navigates the chaos.That said, the character interactions and voice acting retain the charm of the original but may feel a bit dated. Frank’s cheesy one-liners and exaggerated dialogue add to the game’s dark humor, though some scenes lack the polish and emotional depth players may expect from a modern game. Still, fans will appreciate the iconic moments and hilarious exchanges that have become part of Dead Rising’s legacy.Sound and Music : 8/10The sound design has been improved to enhance immersion, with clearer audio effects and re-recorded lines that add a crispness to the experience. Zombie moans, weapon sounds, and mall ambiance all contribute to a more immersive experience, helping the remaster feel both modern and true to its roots. The updated soundtrack blends tense themes with more whimsical, jazzy tracks, providing a unique tone that bridges horror and dark humor.Replayability and New Features : 10/10Replayability has always been a strength of Dead Rising, and the Deluxe Remaster stays true to that legacy with both the main story and Sandbox Mode offering players plenty to do. The remaster also introduces new challenges and optional objectives, adding extra layers of challenge for players who want to fully explore and survive everything the mall has to offer.All DLC is bundled into the Digital Deluxe package with unique outfits and Background Music. These additions provide new ways to customize and experiment in the game, allowing players to approach the chaos of Willamette with a fresh sense of style and creativity.Conclusion : 8.5/10Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster successfully revitalizes a cult classic, merging nostalgic gameplay with modern enhancements that make it enjoyable for both returning fans and new players. The polished visuals, quality-of-life upgrades, and additional content make it the definitive way to experience Frank West’s unforgettable first encounter with the undead.While the core mechanics still feel slightly dated, and some character interactions may seem simplistic, these minor drawbacks don’t overshadow the thrill and humor at the heart of Dead Rising. It’s a bloody good time and a wonderful return to the chaotic, satirical world of zombie-infested Willamette. Whether you’re wielding unusual weapons or simply surviving against the odds, Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster offers a reimagined classic that’s more entertaining than ever.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome! I had wanted to play Dead Rising, but due to its age, I was hesitant to get into it. Now, I can finally play it. The mall is full of things to explore, and the environment is just great, especially at night when things tend to be a bit creepier. I had a lot of fun trying to save survivors who might be just a bunch of crybabies, but who really cares when it's literally a mall packed with zombies? Anyone would act like that given the situation. But not the GOAT, Frank West—a man determined to find the truth amidst the zombie apocalypse. A reminder for everyone: remember to save often. I found myself in a situation where I was escorting two NPCs who were low on health, and I had only one health bar left. I repeated that scenario about ten times (not even kidding). It's a hassle, but I enjoyed every bit of it. It's stressful, but not in a way that makes it less fun—it just makes you find solutions where possible, like taking a different route or stockpiling a bunch of wine in your inventory. The game runs well most of the time, but not when there are a lot of zombies around. I highly recommend playing this game!

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has been quite the Dead Rising fan since the original, It feels like I've been waiting forever for something to come around, after the disaster that DR4 was for the series I was thinking it might never return, then we got news of the remake, honestly going in I was concerned, but mostly, those fears didn't come to be.First the few negatives: Although most of the new voice cast is grand, the odd person sounds bad but seems more like a voice direction issue (On that front, although he's not THEE Frank West, the new dude does a grand job, just takes a little getting used to at first)The game has poor optimisation on it's settings, despite my specs being far and away above what the recommendations are, it needed me to turn down graphics by quite a bit (a common issue I've seen browsing discussions) and I'm sure Denuvo is having an affect on all of us as it normally does.A few crashes here and there, although mostly ONLY when the graphics were not adjusted for myself, once I toned it down it only crashed a single time and I had been playing for about 6 hours straight, so I can't fully blame it happening.Now onto the positives:Despite the graphic issues, the game still looks wonderful, the cast, suriviors, zombies & world all look great, the RE engine is very much a good thing for Capcom!Combat is updated enough to feel great but still keep a small bit of the OG Dead Rising "clunkiness", loads of weapons to pick from, with even the Rocket Launcher, that was cut from the OG getting in.The voice cast! Although as stated that we have a few bad apples, on the overall, they do great! all lines are now properly voice acted, you can skip through to save any hassle from Zombies trying to force convos to restart and it all just helps add to the experience.The story is mostly untouched and is what the OG was, most lines are the exact same, with the odd change for censorship here or there (get over it, it's not big stuff) leading to it feeling like a trip down memory lane, even if it turns out I forgot bits of the story or thought they happened in DR2.The updated endless mode is much better, allowing you to suspend your run, although you still need to do 7 in-game days, you can make a save that quits you out the game, allowing you to return when you have time, no more leaving your machine on overnight or trying to do a 14 hour IRL straight run!Overall, DRDR is a grand revisit to the Willamette Mall and our favourite War Journalist, hopefully Capcom patch the few bugs and annoyances and this will then become a perfect entry point for new fans & a modern feeling experience for us old folk.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: Make no mistake; Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster is a *Remaster*, not a Remake ala Resident Evil 2,3,4, et cetera. Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster (DRDR) is still Dead Rising 1, but with a new, shiny coat of paint on it. Yes, its a dozen-hour long escort mission. Yes, it's still a goofy game, yes, its still janky on the psychopath fights. However, I can confidently state that if you enjoy Dead Rising, or have wanted to see what people were talking about it, this is a great place to jump on the franchise, it's a wonderful game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent remaster, or remake rather. Before I get to the review, a bit of a PSA on the performance.I was a bit put off by the performance initially, and I think many people will be as well. RE Engine, if you're not familiar, is a bit weird with its graphics setting. While I don't know what the VRAM allocation setting actually does, setting it too high causes horrific stutters, hard locks, low FPS, and severe object pop in. Remember that VRAM fluctuates based on what is going on on screen. If you're on, say a 8GB RTX 4060, and you set all the graphics options to max and the menu is reading 4.51GB of with DLSS Quality, that does not mean you have 3.5GB of free space and can set the textures to High (3GB). Too much VRAM being used will caused massive instability. For reference, I'm on a 10GB RTX 3080 and, without DLSS, the menu VRAM use was at 5.01GB. Setting the VRAM on my rig to High (4GB) gave me so many performance issues. Once I set it to High (2GB) it was fine. It's generally a good idea to always try and leave 20% of your VRAM open for fluctuations. Since the game doesn't tell you, you'll have to do just a little bit of simple math to work that out.Now, onto the review.Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster is partly a remaster, and partly a remake maybe leaning more towards the remake side. Although it's genuinely hard to say because a lot in a lot of ways it feels like a port with all of the original's little quirks, jank, and nuances that made the 2006 release so damn charming. But on the other hand you can tell its built from the ground up on an entirely new engine. I have to give kudos to the developers for being able to replicate that because, in a lot of ways, that really is part of what made Dead Rising 1 such a cult classic and replicating mistakes on purpose is no easy feat. This does mean that, despite the QoL improvements made to the gameplay, the game is still quite frustrating at times which many people will find to be a good thing.Some of the OG jankness I noticed includes:As far the removed content goes, I'm sorry, but if you're the kind of loser that is so up in arms because you can't take creepshots of women for points, maybe you should try getting a girlfriend and real problems? The game's cutscenes still feature Frank ogling at women.  Jessica's cleavage is still very much in plain view, purposely, at all times and there's even the shot from Frank's POV where he stares at her ass first before looking at her face. You all are crying censorship over nothing. Please, just grow up. The yuppies who yap at you through YouTube do not have your best interest at heart. They are manufacturing outrage for you to get mad at in order to garner views, grift for your attention, and some are even funded by the Russian government for the sake of spreading an agenda. The wokies are not after your games. The changes made to Larry is not censorship. Get over yourselves.The new actors are a little jarring at first, especially Frank, but as you see the remake's cutscenes unfold this new VA offers the same if not better delivery on a lot of Frank's iconic lines. The visual overhaul is gorgeous in a lot of ways, but can lack in some. I think my biggest gripe is the game's lighting. Sometimes it looks really good. Sometimes it looks really washed out. I was worried the shooting while moving would made the game too easy but, thankfully, it's actually really not that all that different from the original. You can only move while aiming, not while actively shooting, so you have to still sit still to actually fire off rounds continuously. The AI improvements to the survivors is actually pretty solid overall. They're not the smartest, still, but if you beeline through zombies they're capable of keeping up without taking any damage or only taking a very minuscule amount of damage. There's still a bit of babysitting you have to do, but it's definitely  frustrating than it was in the original.My only real big complaint is leveling up. It does feel like it goes by too quickly. I've only just finished the first Psychopath, and all the survivors before 6AM on the first day and I'm already level 15. I think Capcom needs to dial back the leveling by about half and this remaster would be perfect.One addition I really like is that now all interactions outside of cutscenes are fully voiced, even Otis's dislogue. And these survivors can now make call outs pointing out various points of interest, helpful hints, and even pointing out effective weaponry nearby as you're escorting them back to the saferoom.Overall, this remaster/remake/whatever you want to call it is a perfect way to enjoy the classic that started it all. The combat is the same, the physics and jank are the same, everything feels new but familiar at the same time and it's quite comforting.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: After 5 hours of playing the game, I can say the game feels very similar to the original game but it is missing something.This game is very casual now compared to the original. In the original you had a clunky A.I that constantly got grabbed by zombies, Zombies latching onto frank every minute or so and a tougher game overall. In the remaster/remake, the A.I actually works well, zombies aren't on your ass, overall its an easier experience and when i say easier i mean it. I left the vent for the first time and i was already level 10. In the OG game you wouldn't even be Level 4 by that pointGraphically, the game is an improvement. Everything looks nice and depth is added to certain areas that felt empty with random litter or rubbish placed around. Lighting is another issue though. The lighting in this game looks really sloppy at some points and puts you off, especially in the outdoor area where everything looks muddled and saturated.    My only big issue with this game is the "VOICE ACTING" and the character models. Some character models look good and actually represent the original models they're designed after, however there are certain characters who look just uncanny. They don't look human or at least don't look like their original models. The voice acting in this game is just bad. I have yet to come across a good voice actor in this game that wasn't Adam the clown, Otis or the woman who was looking for her dog. These two (Not including Otis) almost felt identical to their original counterpart.In my opinion, this is just an acceptable remaster. It doesn't change alot while staying true to the original game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is literally a perfect remake. It's faithful enough that they called it a deluxe remaster instead of just a remake, and just- I can't describe how good this game is.
