_childDocuments_.review: I have limited experience with the original game, so this is coming from someone who's using this version of the game as basically my first experience. I really enjoy this game. It has a certain charm to it that I absolutely love. It feels campy, but also takes the situation they're in seriously. Capcom has done really well with remakes in the past, RE4 being probably my favorite, and this is up there with some of the best. Now for the stuff I can compare to the original, there's really only one aspect I see as an all around downgrade, and that's of course the new VAs. Most of the new VA's work, but Brad's especially is a huge step down. Frank is fine to me, it's clear since the remake was making him a bit older they wanted an older sounding guy, and the guy who replaced him replicates the original VA well enough that it doesn't bother me. Just about every character I've encountered so far stacks up well against the original, while admittedly slightly worse, except Brad who is an all around downgrade. He sounds absolutely nothing like the original VA and I'm really curious as to why they didn't just reuse the original audio for him. Other than that, I have no gripes really. The QoL changes are really nice and are what actually keep me playing now. Autosave is really nice as now when I die I don't have to fully restart from my last manual save. Shooting mechanics are better while still retaining part of the original feel, and probably best of all, this is an outstanding PC port. It may not be the most visually impressive thing in the world, but man it runs like a dream on every computer I've seen it run on. Capcom has been doing really well lately, especially with their remakes. I think this being only $50 is great and totally worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who played this game a bit as a kid, I still remember it somewhat fondly. Capcom has done a phenomenal job with the remake, capturing much of what made the original special. However, there are a few issues that I can't overlook.For starters, the improved graphics are a massive step up from what we saw in the early 2000s. The game looks absolutely stunning, especially when you hit a zombie and see the blood splatter in vivid detail.Gameplay has been streamlined as well. No more restarting at your last save if you die, you can pick up exactly where you left off. While this feature adds convenience, it might frustrate some of the more hardcore players looking for a tougher challenge.A cool feature that was added is the ability to switch between the original and updated controls. For those who prefer the more sluggish, nostalgic movement, it's still available. At the same time, newer players can enjoy modernised controls, like being able to move while shooting. In the classic mode, you're restricted when shooting or throwing objects, which adds a nice touch for fans of the original gameplay style.Many of you will be glad to hear that survivors have finally been made more useful. While they can still be a bit useless at times, they now actively try to assist you rather than just standing around like rocks. So far, with the exception of one, nearly all the survivors have made genuine efforts to keep me alive, a vast improvement over the originalThe story remains unchanged, staying true to the original, the psychos are far more terrifying this time around. Thanks to the new graphics, they've been made significantly creepier, adding a fresh layer of horror to their encounters.  This time around, from what I remember, there definitely seems to be fewer zombies compared to the original, which was a bit disappointing. I was hoping Capcom would take a bigger leap and increase the zombie count, but unfortunately, it feels like there are fewer this time.Unfortunately, the boss fights haven't been updated, so all the frustrating mechanics from the original are still there. Psychos like Steven Chapman nearly killed me multiple times with his shotgun, firing at me from across the entire store, which makes no sense.It also feels like zombies can grab you more frequently, which can get really frustrating, especially when it seems like they shouldn’t be able to reach you.And then there's Otis, still the most annoying character ever. During my fight with Carlito, he called me roughly 50 times, and hearing that constant 'beep, beep, beep' while trying to focus was infuriating. There really should be a way to mute him. Sure, I can answer him while fighting now, but come on, Otis, I get it, some survivors are dead!And finally, the worst change by far is Frank’s voice. The new actor sounds awful—like he's AI-generated, emotionless, and bored. In the original, Frank’s journey from 'I’m here for pictures' to becoming the savior of Willamette was amazing to witness. Now, he just sounds robotic, completely stripping away the personality that made his character so memorable. You should have brought T.J Rotolo back.    >Better Graphics> More refined while staying true to the original> you can choose between Newer movement or classic movement> Survivors are more useful  > Frank's new voice is terrible> Otis is still annoying> Psycho fights are still tedious (shotguns can still kill you from miles away) >  fewer zombies than the original > zombies can grab you far more frequently and from bizarre angles  If you get the Licker outfit, make sure to use it during cut scenes, it’s absolutely hilarious!
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: From what I've played, it's pretty accurate to the original while adding a lot of QoL and cute additions!My favorite new addition are the EXTREMELY improved survivors. While escorting and not being eaten alive, they'll make comments about the area and may give tips. And with better pathing, I have a lot less trouble escorting them.My main two negatives so far are small ones. First, I noticed quickly that the loading screens are very minimalist, with only the time and a loading bar. This is fine and can actually dramatize the tense moments when you might be late to save somebody, but I prefer the photos and film reels of the original. The second is the modern controls, which are ALMOST perfect. However, I wish there were a way to use Dead Rising 2: OTR's camera controls (aim down sides + right bumper), because I'd love to use the bumpers to switch weapons, but don't want to deal with the original game's terrible roll input. (not hard, just annoying)Even with those small issues, I've gotten used to the D-pad for switching pretty quick, and all the new additions have me smiling and enjoying this return to Dead Rising 1. I hope this game will bring us to a new era of the series that sticks to the charm of the first and second game!

_childDocuments_.review: Some nice QoL improvements over the original but lacking polish in many areas. The new voice acting suffers from very poor sound mixing, it sounds like they've capped the volume so when people shout it isn't loud at all and sounds very flat. New voice actors are generally fine but there is absolutely no reason why the original voice actors had to be replaced. Frank and Brad deliver excellent performances in the original game, but in this version Frank sounds decent while lacking a bit of personality but Brad's acting is just plain bad at times. Also censoring Cliff's dialogue about viet cong is just stupid.As for the lack of polish, it is very apparent. - The vehicle physics are absolutely terrible. They weren't great in the original but they somehow made them even worse. You will get caught on absolutely nothing and the car will come to a complete stop. There will also be times when the vehicle just doesn't move at all for no apparent reason. - Another annoyance is that now you can get grabbed a lot easier than in the original. You'll get grabbed while on the skateboard, which I don't remember ever happening in the original. You'll also be often grabbed while mid weapon swing which can be pretty irritating. Also the zombie ride is pretty broken, you'll last about 3 seconds and then just randomly get staggered and fall off which makes it almost useless. - Additionally, zombie spawns work a lot differently and they now pop in a lot which looks very bad, this is especially apparent in the maintenance tunnels. - There's more little things like the skateboard not adjusting to slopes which looks very jank, and the item physics in general are erratic, they will just randomly fall through the floor at times. And the 30 second loop of music playing when the military arrive gets old quick, this one feels like a bug. Also, you can no longer jump on cardboard boxes which is annoying. - Lip sync is terrible at times too, sometimes lips will move while nothing is being said. It made me think the audio went out of sync a couple timesHopefully at least some of these issues will be fixed.Another gripe I have: the additional survivor dialogue during gameplay is a terrible addition. It's very gamey and breaks immersion. Also poorly implemented in general - for example one of the survivors is near death and it's reflected in their dialogue in the mission, but then 10 seconds later they speak like nothing is wrong saying ♥♥♥♥ like 'If you loot trash cans you'll find items!' like bruh you are about to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ die. The worst offender of this is the guy near the beginning who is stuck in a shop for 2 days and has no idea about the zombies. You rescue him and he's like what the hell is going on and you explain to him about there being zombies. Then about a minute later he said 'Zombies get more violent in the night time'. How the ♥♥♥♥ does he know??On a technical level there are some issues too. Game is very CPU limited at times and it is liable to randomly crash. It does generally look nice at least but there is also some strange flickering in the screen space reflections. There is also a very noticeable FPS drop after area transitions.Survivor AI is definitely improved which is nice. It does take away a bit of the challenge but they were just plain dumb in the original which was more annoying than challenging. They have way better pathfinding now which makes a huge difference. They will still randomly get stuck on objects and start charging towards zombies but they are much easier to manage. I do wish they kept in the little view box that showed the survivor though so you could see if they were being grabbed or not, it was pretty useful in the original.I do like the QoL changes after playing the original so much. Now the more grindy tasks like getting all the PP stickers carries over across playthroughs. You can argue that the zombie kill count carrying over between playthroughs for zombie genocider takes away the challenge for that but deep down no one enjoys dedicating a whole playthrough to running over zombies for 4 hours. Time speed up is also really nice as now you don't have to suffer through standing around for 14 hours in infinity mode doing basically nothing to get the achievement. I also really like how you no longer have to finish the current playthrough to get certain rewards like the mega buster.Would also be nice if they added an original difficulty mode to get the original PP gain as you earn way too much PP at the start of the game. At least they kinda balanced it out by making the late game a lot harder.I also miss the original UI, the new one has lost the character that the original had. And Frank looks stupid in his default outfit because the jacket makes him look absolutely huge. Overall it is pretty good, my main complaint really is the new voice actors as there is NO reason to replace them. I kinda would've preferred a total remake if they were gonna change the voice actors and stuff. Feels a bit like they're pissing on the original acting by just recording over the original dialogue while still using the original motion capture.

_childDocuments_.review: After getting all the achievements I can safely say that this is probably the funnest DR up-to-date due to the updated models, physics, game-play, ect. My only gripe about it I guess is it feels a bit more easier this time around as it practically hands you OP items after your first or second run which makes your infinity mode an absolute cake walk. tbh, I kinda missed the old gimmicks the first DR had. It made the game much more challenging but it made me appreciate those items a lot more.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster (unsure why they didn't call it a remake) is a great facelift as well as upgrade and really works on what makes it a little more challenging today. With yet another new Frank and the Willamette Park View mall looking better than ever, zombie slaying and psychopath killing has never been more fun in this wonderful throwback.PRO- The game looks and runs really nice which is hardly surprising as it's on the RE Engine.- The quality of life improvements really help make the game much more enjoyable and up to date.- Frank has another new look and voice and honestly, this one I think suits him the most. You can play as the original Frank though if you prefer him.- You can choose different music for the mall which is a really nice touch.- There is a lot of extra costumes added including from other Capcom franchises.- AI has been massively improved and you can even somewhat "upgrade" survivors to make them more useful and less of a hindrance.- All NPC's are now voiced which is a lot better than reading text boxes all the time.- You can skip Otis' transceiver messages without him making a fuss.- There is now a checkpoint system that auto-saves your progress when entering a new area. Some may say it makes it easier but it helps with a lot of annoying backtracking.NEUTRAL- Certain aspects of this game have been changed due to "modern standards" such as no erotica photo genre, no mention of communism or Vietcong and an entire character changing race. I'm only putting this because I don't agree with changing how games are to suit new viewers. I will make it very clear, it does not change the enjoyment of the game as nothing about the game itself changes.- Due to a boost in PP, the game seemed pretty easy and I rarely ran into trouble. Psychopaths were no problem and I felt like I was getting so many skills so quickly which kinda lost the whole challenge aspect.CON- On many occasions I found myself swinging a weapon only to have a zombie ignore it and grapple me instead to which I had to take damage and fight my way out of when it should have been dead.- There were quite a number of glitches (which should hopefully be patched). These included zombies popping in and out, zombies grabbing me through objects and Steven picking up Isabella and the trolley and swinging it with one hand.- Certain things did take a downgrade like water splashing and glass smashing.- There are more PP stickers for experience boosts but if you're not in the perfect angle they want (even though it's clearly in frame from different angles) then it won't count so you have to try repeatedly to get that shot right.- It did crash quite a few times. Luckily the auto save system is there...If you're someone who has yet to play a Dead Rising game or someone who is a great fan of the first one then the Deluxe Remaster is definitely worth a play through. And seriously, don't listen to the people saying the censorship ruins it, it makes such a miniscule difference in how you will enjoy the game. Yes, it sucks but don't let that put you off a great game.Here's hoping that Capcom goes onto make Dead Rising 2 Deluxe Remaster next!
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn’t planning to buy the Dead Rising remaster, especially not at launch, but something inside me wanted to give it a try. And unexpectedly for myself, I ended up playing a game I hadn’t been waiting for at all. I haven’t played the original, but I’ve heard from friends and others that the remaster had some content cut and some censorship added in certain places. It sounds sad, but I find it hard to feel strongly negative about it because I never tried the original and decided to jump straight into the remaster.I want to say that I liked it — it turned out to be fun, absurd, and stylish. I enjoyed the leveling and skill acquisition mechanics, the variety of weapons, the photography, and the concept that time is always passing. You’re given 72 hours to do everything, and some rescue missions are very time-limited, making them truly challenging. There aren’t many bosses in the game, but they are funny and memorable. I managed to save exactly half of the people I could, as I didn’t want to save scum and just accepted it when someone died during the escape to the safe room.I also liked that the game allows you to fail the main story quests (though here I did reload). I enjoyed the game a lot, but judging by the weak sales, Capcom won’t be releasing new remasters for Dead Rising anytime soon, if at all. Perhaps they should have lowered the price for this specific remaster, but I’m not sure that would have changed the overall sales picture for the game (Dragon’s Dogma says hi).
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: A soulless watered down remake that doesn't live up to the essence of the original game. Still boggles my mind on how the devs were able to mess up and censor most of the zombie's mechanics and gore, which are arguably the most integral part of a game... a sandbox game that takes place in a ZOMBIE-infested mall, but whatever. Even the difficulty has been toned down significantly which makes the game feel too easy and ultimately less enjoyable.On a better note, I personally don't mind the new VA cast. Frank's new VA ultimately grew on me, along with the talented performances behind the psychopaths and main characters, so I have no complaints in that department. Overall, get this remake on sale for $20 or less. OR, better yet, play the original game where the devs actually cared about what they were presenting towards their audience. This remake needed wayyyy more time in the oven, but I think its too late for it now either way.TLDR: I feel like the vfx artists were sleeping during the production of this game lmao
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: DRDR was definitely a lot of fun to play through and I greatly enjoyed many of the quality of life features the game brings to the original. I know a lot of people aren't fans of the voice acting for this game because Frank's original VA didn't return, but I honestly enjoyed most of the vocal performances. One of my most favorite bits about the game were the extra costumes you can get as DLC because they will make every scene hilarious to watch. And another great feature is definitely the ability to speed up time when you are waiting and aren't doing anything.The only issues I encountered with this game were performance-wise where sometimes Frank would just full-on send himself to the other side of the map or outside of a room for no reason. It only happened maybe 2 or 3 times, but it was honestly more funny to watch happen rather than be annoying. One other issue might be with some of the textures loading in, but that was also a bit of a rare instance.Overall though, DRDR was a lot of fun and a great visual enhancement of the original Dead Rising. I don't think I would mind it if Capcom did this same treatment for Dead Rising 2.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: Conceptually, theoretically, and as far as core mechanics go, it's a great remake, but the PC port suffers from the usual 'we don't care about PC, use a controller' mindset that seems to come most often from Japanese game developers. On top of this, the game sorely needs optimisation and bug fixes, the pop-in and random frame plummeting ruins the experience of an otherwise fun, and much-desired, modern revamp of this blast from the past.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: A great upgrade to a great game that plays unlike anything else released to this day - mostly for the better, sometimes for the worse. Some find the time pressure overwhelming, not realizing that the game is designed to be played at least twice.Even if you fail your first run, you carry your stats over into the next. Don't worry about trying to do the entire main story on your first try.Runs playably on Steam Deck if you make some concessions in settings. Lock to 30 for best experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: It feels like the classic game but with so many QoL improvements. Most bosses are harder except for one which was a dramatic improvement. Special Forces are much harder but not impossible. With the exception of the zombie population in the tunnels, this game is an overall improvement pretty much all the way around. Achievements are much easier to obtain. While the game retains its nostalgic niche feel, the added improvements give the game a much more casual feel. If you liked the OG, you'll love this one!

_childDocuments_.review: Competent video game, modern gameplay, pretty graphics. The heart and soul of the Original's voice acting, comedy, and wacky tone are gone. For this I find that Capcom has failed to deliver an actual "Remaster" of a beloved and classic game.EDIT: I beat the game, it is an enjoyable experience, but still not as fun or funny as the original. _childDocuments_.review: If you've played the original, you've played this. Its not like the Resident Evil 4 Remaster where it feels like a completely different game. Aside from the fresh new look, everything more or less feels the same. The game has been considerably re-balanced so that things aren't as tedious or difficult. Examples include: - Guns feel like they pack a heavier punch now, making them much more useful than before IMO.- Survivor AI is SO MUCH BETTER. Only once or twice did I have a survivor that got stubborn and wanted to punch every zombie they stood near.Being able to advance time at any save point makes the game so much quicker in the latter half. Its now one of those games that you can complete in a single sitting and still enjoy the rest of your day.Sure the game is pricey considering the amount of content. It hasn't changed since the original aside from a few enhancements here and there, but is priced like a new original release. I enjoyed playing the original so I knew going into this I was going to have a good time, but I can see how someone would want to skip this title based on price alone, and it's certainly warranted. Regardless, I still think this is "moderately" fun to play. Not exactly great, certainly not stellar, but a reasonably enjoyable time.Side note: I love the choice for Jas Patrick as Frank West. I am not entirely sure why they opted to get all fresh new voice actors when the dialogue in cutscenes is pretty much untouched, which translates to the same lines being repeated by new voices outside of changing Cliff's dialogue and some of Kent's. I do think Dead Rising has some really good bones, so I get wanting to keep a large majority in tact, but I think the original had room to improve and they didn't try to do so here.All-in-all, I do recommend the Deluxe Remaster, but I think Capcom played it a little too safe to the point where if you played the original the most you're getting here are new graphics and some QOL changes.

_childDocuments_.review: So this is my comprehensive review of Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster after a little over 13-14 hours of gameplay and all achievements unlocked aside from the 5 and 7 day survivor achievements which I am working on now. I will likely talk about the story a little bit so expect spoilers. Not sure why I should care about spoilers as the story itself is going on 20 years old, but I might as well put it out there to avoid some complaining.- GraphicsSo the game has been updated with the RE engine and has been given a serious touch up in the graphics department. The changes are VERY noticeable in the mall itself and especially in Leisure Park. Foliage as far as the eye can see in the park, and lots of smaller details added into the whole mall to really bring the Willamette Parkview Mall to life. I think it is a very impressive update to the original's already good looking setting. My one complaints would be with 2 things: the gore and the character's face models. Now let me say that the gore looks absolutely amazing. Blood looks super real and it is an absolute mess after slaughter. My complaint is that blood doesn't really get onto Frank at all. You'd think after taking a battle axe I found in an antique shop to 50 zombies or so, that I'd get some blood on me. Nope, my outfit is just as clean as it was before I even jumped out of the helicopter. Blood on your character is something that literally EVERY other entry in the series had, including the atrocity that was Dead Rising 4. Maybe this is something that can be added in a future update (assuming they do anything else with this game). As for the character face models, it's very much a mixed bag. There's a lot of detail added into all of the faces that make them look more real, but they still seem...ugly compared to the admittedly already ugly-looking faces the original Dead Rising had. It's hard to explain. To me, Frank especially looks much older than he was in the original. Whether this was intentional or not, I don't know. But it just doesn't click with me very well. Not the biggest deal though, and it doesn't take away from all of the graphical fidelity added to the rest of the game.- GameplayGameplay, for the most part, is still just as solid as in the original. Zombies are still super fun to take...whatever you can find to. That's the beauty of Dead Rising, if you can pick it up, you can use it as a weapon, and that very much still holds true to this game. There have even been some improvements to gameplay, like the option to fast forward time at safe places to get rid of some of the downtime people would run into with the original. It's not required by any means, and if people still prefer waiting out the time doing...whatever, they can just avoid the option. There have been a few tweaks to difficulty overall with a few aspects, but I will touch on those more later in the review.- AudioAudio is probably the thing that was altered the least out of everything from the original game. All of the original music from the OST of Dead Rising to the added in tracks for Pyschopath fights are still present in this version of the game. The developers even added a streamer mode so that streamers and content creators can safely play through the game without worry about copyright strikes. Very welcome change! Now personally, the original Dead Rising tracks were never really my favorite in gaming. However, that is definitely a personal preference. The soundtrack is still very well done!- DifficultySo based on what I've seen from other reviewers, this section has been a pretty controversial set of changes from the original. The game has definitely seen some changes, mostly QoL that make the game significantly more accessible for players. Now, a lot of people say that the original game was "so much harder" than this version. I'm going to have to respectfully disagree. The original Dead Rising definitely had a lot more outdated game mechanics to it that made the game more...frustrating to play in my opinion. The survivor AI is a particular stand out one to me. In the original game, survivor NPC AI would CONSTANTLY get stuck on objects, zombies, and each other. Often times, this would lead to you having to babysit them incredibly close and kill every zombie in the immediate area or you risk them getting swarmed super easily and promptly killed. This would cost you valuable PP (the XP for this game) and the Saint achievement if you were going for that. The survivor AI in the remaster has seen a serious improvement. They are not by any means easy mode though. In my first playthrough, I had a couple of occasions where they would run into each other and make a lot of noise, or would get hit by one zombie and go into, what I can only describe as a rage, and start attacking every zombie around them and you would have to kill the zombies yourself to stop this rage. This is reminiscent to what they would do in the original game, however to a much lesser extent. Now, while survivors are definitely more intelligent in this game and receive less friendly fire damage from you (thank god), they are much more squishy to zombie attacks. I had a survivor get stuck in a relatively small swarm of zombies for only roughly 10-15 seconds, and they had almost died on me and costing me my Saint run. That being said, it is definitely and improvement overall and I got the Saint achievement first run from level 0 which is a lot harder in the original.Infinity mode is another thing that was changed a little. They added a change for zombies to drop random items whether it be weapons or even small food items. However, this is a very small chance for food and it is not usually going to save you from dying. However, the ability to save in infinity mode is SO nice. I despised having to do my original 7 day run in one go for 14 hours which most of which is spent waiting. This wasn't fun, or even satisfying when I did do it. And yes, you can skip time in infinity mode too which is also super nice. Just keep an eye on your health bar. - GrindThe grind honestly felt about the same overall. However, the first few levels seemed to come INCREDIBLY fast. I got to level 15 before I even finished the first case. However, it levels out around level 20 where you have to get a lot PP in order to level up. So it took me about the same amount of time to hit level 50 as the original. I imagine the first few levels were for newer players which is okay if you ask me.- StoryThe story is the same, so I'll take this time to give my opinion on the voice actor changes. There is no doubt that the acting is a step down from the original game. However, I don't think it is quite as bad as people make it out to be. Nobody will be winning any Emmys for this but it's not horrendous like people say. Even Frank's new voice actor grew on me a little more as I progressed. However, I do miss old voice actor, TJ Storm a lot. That one was a hard change.- Game TimeI managed to get all but the Infinity mode achievements in roughly 14 hours. A lot of achievements have changed or were removed and are easier to get. Got mixed feelings on that.- PriceHonestly, I'd wait for a sale. $50 is pretty steep for an 18 year old game with a graphical update.- BugsI ran into a quite a few shuddering problems and a 3 crashes in my first run. Nothing game breaking but hopefully these get smoothed out with updates. Final Rating & Conclusion: It's a very solid remake/remaster of Dead Rising. For the most part, it respects everything the original game did while adding nice QoL changes to make the game more accessible for new players. It's definitely the best way to play Dead Rising now in my opinion. However, I still think people should check out the original and judge that for themselves.* 7/10 *

_childDocuments_.review: ___________________________________________________________if you have never played this game before, this is definitely A way to play dead rising. you are playing dead rising, just not THE dead rising and thats something to keep in mind. if you have played dead rising before, there is actually no good reason to play this over the original. for every good change they make, theres another 2 bad. it doesnt bring enough to the table like RE4 Remake did and it just ends up as a subpar version of something great that still holds up nearly 20 years later. it really makes you wonder why we even needed a remake beyond bringing new people into the game and testing to see if there is still interest in this series after dead rising 4. i love that people who have never heard of dead rising before are now getting to experience this for the first time but it sucks to think that some people's first experience is going to be this instead of the original as they are missing out on some stuff. i like that they added voice acting for the in game dialogue that would usually be text boxes. it really makes it alot more interesting to listen to this people and really should've been there in the original. i also love the additional lines where they will tell you about cool places and things to check out in the mall that you'd only find if you went and explored yourself instead of doing the scoops. the only issue is that in order to make this possible, they had to redo the voice acting and since some voice actors could not be recasted, do those voices again or in frank's case, capcom did not want to recast, it was decided that the entire game's voice acting would be recasted. this would be fine if it werent for the fact that so many of these just... dont fit well. there are some good ones dont get me wrong. jessie, adam and especially the voice for otis who had never had a voice to begin with are exceptional examples and even the survivors are fine too.the issue comes when you have misses on such crucial roles like FRANK, the main character or brad who is a critical role to the story and probably the character you hear the most from, second to frank. frank's just doesnt really fit and brad's is just a bad performance. i feel like these performances dont hit as they are trying to replicate the original performances exactly 1:1 when they just dont have the voice for it. brad doesnt have a low enough voice atleast not one that has enought texture and his performances can come off a bit flat too since he's looking at the original performance and not try to replicate the emotion and character in it. one such example is right after you beat carlito and frank is holding info hostage that brad needs, he spells out what he thinks frank is:"You're one hell of a journalist aren't you, Frank? A hotheaded, underhanded, hotshot paparazzi with nothing better to do than to invade people's privacy."and during this line, you can really feel how frustrated he is with his situation and how much disdain he has for these underhanded journalists (that he definitely he has encountered before in his line of work that have gotten in his way) but he still tries to keep his cool. feels kinda just feels lost in the remake's performance. same with franks personality in this same cutscene. its really hard to describe but trust me, this isnt a nostalgia thing, i only played this game for the first time a month ago in preparation for this game and i genuinely think the original casting is better in every way. it feels movie-like. this remake just falls flat. they definitely could've picked better casting if they couldn't get the original.moving away from the topic of the voice acting, lets talk visuals. this is yet another somewhat subjective thing (this moreso than the previous topic). i think the original visuals are better. whilst this is, in a technical sense, way better and has great graphical fidelity, it really misses the character, readability and style of the original. the redesign of frank completely misrepresents his character as he looks way older and uglier to the point of looking cartoonish whilst the original was... just a guy. he wasnt too good looking but not ugly either. the mall whilst getting a fresh coat of paint and having tones more detail, i feel like im seeing less. theres so much clutter and the new lighting adding tones of detail ontop that via shadows and more point lights, it ends up being too much and feels like it has no balance. if i try and remember off the top of my head what the mall looks like in the remake, it just comes out as a soup. it really poses a question we should be asking our selves in this new age of gaming where photorealism is so easy to attain now: "how much detail is too much?" "how realistic is too realistic". this is more so a preference thing and ive always had an appreciation for old graphics which i know some types of people just cant do the same but as i never grow up on this game and it came out at a time in gaming where i was probably 1 years of age, i dont think this is nostalgia or anything talking.now to a more objective issue with the visuals, the game has a colour problem (or more so, the engine). the RE engine has always struggled with contrast. i dont know why but blacks in the RE engine come out as a gray instead of a black. it wasnt too big of an issue in re4 remake as it was always lit very well and whatever was supposed to be unlit was still lit with the blue light of the moon/fog but in this game, when the mall is supposed to get really dark or the outside park at night it looks really bad. re2 remake had the same issue due to also being very dark. it just looks plain ugly. this could be fixed with a mod or reshade but those always have their downsides and the fact that this still needs to be fixed all these years later into the engine is just silly.alot of the game's effects aswell rely on the the bluring of the screen that comes with anti-aliasing. i notice alot of dithering for some shadows or something (honestly not quite sure what it was for) in some cutscenes and i just wonder... why? i have my graphics cranked up to nearly max and you still have to rely on blurring the screen. this is more an issue with modern gaming than just with this game but i still detest it. its a backwards solution that worsens the visual experience and gives me a headache when using it. its like wearing some elses glasses that arent meant for you. if thats not good for my eyes, why is this any better? this issue would be solved by not having such minute details or thin lines ORRR having a higher resolution since theres more pixels to show this detail which would remove the jagged edges but we're still far too early in gaming tech to have that be standard and usable. enough about my AA rant though, just thought i'd mention itnow my review was way too big for steam reviews (15000 characters or something over the limit) so continue below

_childDocuments_.review: Another quality remake from Capcom. The survivor AI is also greatly improved making escorting survivors much less of a chore.Overall I would definitely recommend to anyone playing for the first time and long time fans alike. There's something for everyone here.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished 72 Hour Mode...My takeaway from all this: the devs love the first game but totally miss the point. The entirety of the 72 Hour Mode was a tension-filled romp through the Willamette Parkview Mall with only a bit of time in-between to relax. You were battling the clock as much as you were zombies. You were in a blitz a majority of the time, going at insane lengths to get to where you needed to be at any cost. You planned a lot in your head, almost meticulously. You balanced your inventory, your read the map, you remembered a nice shortcut to cut time and limit your engagements against zombies, you were ready. Here, you can just run right through without much thought. Yes, there are some difficult bits still but with how powerful they make the player early on and throughout, it almost becomes a stroll through the game, not the crazed mad dash it had become. Every second mattered, every decision you made cost you time, the most valuable resource in the game and taking just a second off made the difference. Every time you went to another part of the mall, the clock showed up right in front of your face. The countdown started as soon as you stepped onto the rooftop of Willamette Parkview Mall. By the time you survived your first encounter with the undead, the clock went down to 71 Hours. Already an hour burnt.It's disappointing not to feel the adrenaline as much. The original game made you feel as though you were going through the experience. You had Scoops to cover, people to rescue, weapons to gather, food to eat and carry; everything is against you and you have to make due. Even at your most powerful, zombies are dangerous. Time is your worst enemy. Your decision making made much more of an impact. Instead, here, it feels less punishing and much more forgiving. Time almost feels generous. 72 Hour Mode here didn't bite as much as I wanted it to. I wanted to be down to the wire, challenged. I wanted to be in a mad dash through the Mall, being smart with my decision making and route-taking. I wanted to feel like I had to take a risk just to make it to the bathroom. I wanted to feel like my journey to the North Plaza was dangerous. I wanted the race to retrieve the time bombs to be just as nail-biting and dangerous as it was in the original. Now, it's as easy as ever as to find them and complete a mission that felt simplified when it didn't need to be.I'm moving onto Overtime Mode soon but, so far... this game isn't the definitive Dead Rising experience. If you want to experience the intensity of fighting the clock, the undead and psychopathic survivors in a scrap to the finish, play 2016 re-release first. It's $10. It's intense. It's the Dead Rising game we wanted DR4 to be. It's what DRDR had to be... It isn't. It's not without fun, but it's not the Deluxe Remaster it's advertised to be. The vast array of weird glitches that range from slight annoyance to game breaking, the gameplay that's been made even easier, weird design changes and choices for the remake etc. I've covered my journey in detail in the Discussions. I plan on playing Overtime Mode and Infinity Mode. But, for those wondering if this game is the Deluxe Remaster we've been waiting for. It isn't. It's a nice game to add to your DR collection but it doesn't seem to fully understand its roots besides the details on the surface level. We have yet to wait for a true DR title that goes back to its roots, essence and all.

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster is an incredible faithful reconstruction of the original title.  Almost everything that made the original good is present & accounted for here.  From the arcade fun of finding the variety of weapons in the mall, to entertaining & terrifying psychopaths scattered about.  Aspects of the setting have been fleshed out more in this title, with many areas of the mall feeling more alive than the original.  The RE Engine has been utilized to a horrifying degree as the undead look more realistically gruesome than before.  The visuals received an improvement all around, & it actually shows the best with the little details throughout the mall.  PP stickers are now more visible, making it possible to hunt them down without utilizing a guide.  On top of that, all survivors have their own audio rather than just text boxes, with a few even having cues that alert the player to their presence.  On audio, the game's entire soundtrack is still here.  Control wise, the only noticeable change is the ability to move while aiming, a welcome feature that makes the gunplay a little more useful.  They even added scrapped elements from the original title this time around.  The AI has undergone the biggest change, not only with survivors.  Yes, survivors now follow orders & play around zombies far better than before, but enemy AI also interacts better as well with the special forces soldiers becoming a challenging enemy to overcome.  The best addition for repeated playthroughs has to be the new ability to fast forward time at any save point.  This is even available in infinity mode, making a waiting slog into a more frantic survivor hunt.  Unfortunately, a few of the voice acting roles feel worse than the original.  Considering the original only had voice acting for a select few, this is an issue due to them appearing in many of the game's cutscenes.  On that note, along with a follow up from the game's soundtrack, the original cast was not brought back for this title, & many musicians stated the tracks were used without them being contacted (contracts & all that, but it's still something that should be mentioned).  Visually, there's some noticeable pop in for all zombies in the distance, something that does take one out of the experience whenever it happens.  Frank's movement in this game feels a little stiffer than the original.  In order to balance out the new gun controls, it feels like guns fire slower, especially the real mega buster (which now has a charged shot to attempt to make up for it).  Amusingly enough, with exception to the psychopaths & soldiers, the entire game feels easier thanks to all the changes.  It's interesting looking at both this & the original release, because the lists are very similar.  Many achievements have had their grind reduced, such as Transmissionary dropping from all calls to only 30.  Several middle of the road & severely grind based achievements have been removed & replaced with a few task based ones instead.  Noticeably, Zombie Annihilator (previously Genocider) & 7 Day survivor are still here, but all of the achievement based rewards are there as well, giving incentive to go for them.  All of the improvements & removal of most heavy grind achievements makes this list far easier to go for, though still requiring a few playthroughs to net them all.  Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster is exactly what should be wanted from a title like this.  Everything from the previous game is still present & accounted for (unless you're someone seethingly upset that the erotica option was removed from taking pictures).  The change in the voice actor team & behind the scenes audio stuff will turn a few people off, & it's reasonable to be.  Overall, the game stands out, & deserves a recommendation in my book.

_childDocuments_.review: As a massive Dead Rising 1 fan who's been playing the first game well over 15 years now. I was beyond floored when I saw the reveal for the Deluxe Remaster, now with it finally here I am overall very impressed with it. Now for starters, this remaster does have issues. For the most part the game is great! So many great additions and fixes to the original its a joy to play on newer hardware. While I am not the biggest fan of having an auto save feature. It has 100% saved me from losing tons of progress from crashes. Which happened more than 5 times throughout my first playthrough. The aiming feels much better now and far more streamlined to newer releases now. Survivor AI though still feels rough. The only change that I can see personally is that they don't get targeted or grappled nearly as much as they used to.  They still feel pretty dumb 80% of the time so I guess it's a slight upgrade.Graphics look fantastic however, the RE Engine truly brings this game to life as a whole. Every area has gotten a pretty face lift and looks great!One of the biggest issues by far is pop in. I don't know if its just my PC/Specs but it felt like every 20 or so feet zombies were popping in like crazy. It felt jarring every time it happened. In much denser areas it's not as bad but open ones? It looks horrible.Now lets get the biggest issue out and about. The voice and dialogue changes. I know its been a huge talked about aspect of the remaster and while some changes didn't make much sense. *Like the change where Frank doesn't say "What in the world?" anymore.* To Cliffs changes too. I don't have the biggest issues with these. While it does suck to see them get changed it wasn't a massive deal breaker by any means. Most of the original lines have stayed in the game and I'd go as far to say nearly 99% have been kept while adding extra ones. Speaking of extra voice lines, every character now has voice lines. Even Otis! It's such a nice change and breathes new life into the game. It's all around a lovely touch.But so far I enjoyed my time with the game itself despite the some of the issues. It's a great way to play one of the greatest games from the 360 era and even better for long time fans!7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Some mixed feelings, partially due to some heavy bias towards the original, but overall I feel this is a good remaster. Lots of positive changes, though also a some negative ones, with many negatives being a matter of personal opinion.Overall though, when playing with classic controls, it managed to preserve the experience of playing the original game for the most part. I had a blast playing through the game again, and there were some great QoL changes that will likely make the game a lot more approachable to new players.There are way too many little changes to go over, but the things that stood out most to me were the difficulty and infinity mode changes.In terms of difficulty, they made the game as a whole a lot easier. Levelling happens much faster, and escorting survivors is significantly easier (Maybe even a bit too easy). Some psychopaths also seemed to have balance changes, making some easier and others harder, which is also a welcome change. My biggest issues are some of the changes to Infinity Mode though. It really took the wind out of my sails when I realized how much easier 7 Day Survivor became due to the ability to fast forward time at save points (which is a new mechanic in 72 hour mode as well, but I appreciate a lot more there). The survivor/psychopath locations being randomized at set intervals each day is a good change as well, though having their locations marked on the map kind of spoils the fun of that. Being able to suspend your session for infinity mode is really nice though as it can be a bit daunting to set aside roughly 14 hours in a single day just to attempt 7 Day Survivor mode in the original.I'd recommend turning some settings such as Survivor's being able to give you hints off though, as they'll tell you hidden item locations, which can take away some of the mystique you feel when finding little hidden places in each area on your own. I don't see myself coming back to the remaster very much and will probably just go back to the original game again whenever I want to replay Dead Rising, but I definitely really enjoyed playing this and felt it was worth my time.

_childDocuments_.review: Another great game updated for modern hardware with a few quality of life improvements tossed in to even out the package. If you're the sort who wished the Resident Evil Remakes were more 1:1 in trying to preserve the original gameplay and mechanics then this is definitely what you want to be looking at. This does include some of the jank from the original too when it comes to animations, getting stun locked, and things like that but that's also part of the unique charm to the series which helps it stand out among a rather crowded zombie market these days. I will say it is a little pricey for what is on offer here. I feel like $40 at release would have been better in-line with what you get given that there's nothing really new, content wise, being added here. The original story returns along with Overtime and Infinite Mode as well as the multiple game runs to keep leveling up Frank while trying to save all the survivors. Performance wise it runs incredibly well for me pretty much staying locked 120 with some dips down to the 90's/80's in more open areas when first loading in. There is some pop-in in places like the park and maintenance tunnels too as the RE Engine is really being pushed here in terms of zombie count and all that. Still nothing that ruins the experience or leaves you wanting for more zombies. Had no problem racking up thousands upon thousands of kill during a single run. Only had one crash early on during the Father/Sons sniper fight. Picked up a rifle, game froze for a moment, and then just closed. Autosave put me right back at the start of the fight so didn't really lose anything, just a bit annoying. Outside of that zero issues from start to finish. I have heard Infinite Mode has some bugs but I haven't spent a great deal of time with it at the time of writing this review. If I do encounter any issues I'll update this with the necessary information. Really hoping we see Dead Rising 2 get this treatment.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game fun? Yes.Is this game good? Yes.Is this Dead Rising? Yes.Is it better than the last Dead Rising game? Oh definitely.Then why is this review negative? Well... If steam had a "neutral" option, I would've chose that for this review. This is Dead Rising. It's that same Dead Rising we played on the Xbox 360, and later here on PC with the original remastered release. Sure some things here have been changed and at least one very core feature removed, but don't get it wrong. This is Dead Rising down to every little intricate detail. It even has the same bugs as the original. Don't believe me? Go into day six of infinity mode and try to enter the Food Court and see what happens. I had fun with this game. I had fun showing it off to all my friends and talking about all the little cool things you can do in it. It is a fun game... but. It's the same exact game as the one currently available here on Steam for $9.99. I understand this is a "Deluxe Remaster" and not a "Remake" but I didn't expect this to be a 97% carbon copy for $49.99. I only have 3 major gripes about this game and you just heard me talk about my first one. The second is the "light" censorship present in this version. I've heard that the Erotica tag for photos was removed because of a couple of new laws in Japan. If this is truly the case, I understand. The Psycho, Larry Chiang, was made to resemble more a normal guy than the original's. I can see the reasoning for that as well, his character in the original was a laughably racist stereotype. The last one however is the one I have the most problem with, Clint. Clint is portrayed as a Vietnam War Veteran suffering a PTSD Flashback after seeing his granddaughter be eaten by zombies. As such he believes that everyone, including Frank, is "Viet Cong" and "Filthy Communist". This was changed to "Mole" and "Filthy Animal" in this remaster. This, in my opinion as someone who is the son of a Vietnam War Veteran and was one of their caretakers, is distasteful. It downplays on the emotions that these men feel, and felt by plowing over it with verbal AstroTurf. You might say they did that as to not offend anyone of Vietnamese descent... I don't care. This one is the most far-fetched censorship out of them all, and it leaves a bitter taste in my mouth. I think now I should move on to the final criticism I have for DRDR before people begin to think that one thing influenced this review. My final criticism is the voice acting. Holy. God. This is some of the worst voice acting I've heard in a while. Out of all the main characters Brad is by very very VERY far the worst. It's so bad that it is beyond laughable bad. He sounds like the voice that everyone makes when they're trying to mock someone with an authoritative tone. Jessie, Isabela, and Carlito are all different levels of average to good, but oh my god did the VA for Brad phone this one in. Now Frank's... I was really hesitant and went into the game with a negative opinion for Frank's new VA, but in complete honesty. I really like the new VA for Frank. This new guy sounds like he is really putting the effort into properly portraying Frank in this remaster, and it grows on you as you make your way through the game. I respect and admire the effort, good job.So we're at the end. Thanks for reading all this if you did. There is a lot more I could talk about, like the quality of life changes. For example, you only need 5 queens instead of 10 like in the original. The amount of PP you get is much higher than the original, which in turn makes the whole game way less stressful. I think I'm gonna leave it at those two, and finish writing this review. So what is my final verdict? It's alright... buy it on sale, or something idk. I'm gonna go play Space Marine 2 now.

_childDocuments_.review: It's Dead Rising improved imo.  Somehow just as fun as it always was. I got it just to check out and I've already put in 9 hours and I'm having a blast. There isn't much original to say. I loved Dead Rising at launch and I revisit it every 5 years or so since then.  I just want to address some of the talking points about this release.1) Censorship - I understand being annoyed by censorship in a game, but the things they took out are negligible in my opinion. I don't care all that much about the photo mode to begin with. It's pretty boring and shallow.  So for me the removal of erotic photos does nothing.  I do think it's probably the most uncalled for removal though, considering its a comedic game from the perspective of a sleazy photo journalist.    The race change on the butcher feels unnecessary, but also doesn't make that big of a deal to me. I didn't find the original to be exceptionally racist or anything, especially considering all of the characters are kind of parody or caricatures to begin with, but I like the new aesthetic for the butcher so it's fine with me considering the original didn't blow my socks off or anything. He's kind of a throw away boss fight that never shined to begin with.  The stuff about Viet Cong being removed feels like a right move. Not because it's offensive, but because this is a remaster made for new players to some degree and the joke or parody just doesn't feel all that relevant anymore. I'd have even been okay with them changing the character to an Iraq vet considering this.  Honestly I think considering that's about all of the censorship there's not much to cry about.  It's still a pervy, gory, trashy horror show full of grotesque schizo obese villains, and hot skanky survivors(exaggerating to make a point. That point being the game could still be seen as offensive).  Graphics - Not much for me to complain about here. There are a few new character models like Carlito that look a little plastic to me, but overall it's an improvement and looks about as good as I'd expect a modern remaster of a game this old to look. Some people are divided on the textures, I really don't mind. Some things could be improved like the glass shattering effects, some questionable FPS drops in new environments(really doesn't impact gameplay for me), and reflections.  I'm liking the polish for the most part though.  It's very true to the original while being improved.Voice acting - Brad and Carlito aside I actually love all of the new voie actors. I don't like new Frank any more than the old one, but I also don't like him any less. I think he's great and still feels like the character I love.  Remaster or Remake - Definitely remaster, no doubt, the title says it, and by definition it's exactly that. Not sure how they implimented the old game engine, but it's clear some things were ported over.  As for whether it was necessary. I'm not sure. I'm happy to have great remaster, but I gladly would've taken a complete remake.  I loved all 3 of the recent Resident Evil Remakes and they all felt much more dramatic than this. Would've loved to see something on the same level as RE4.  Gameplay - Its improved where it needs to be and the same otherwise.  I feel like I'm playing the exact same game, but the survivor AI is better, the aiming is better with guns, and moving feels smoother.  They also added stairs to the entrance to the safehouse which was much needed. Really the AI improvement is game changing though. The survivors felt like a real burden in the original to the degree that I'd often just kill them, but now I'm actually changing my play style and trying to save as many as possible.  I've even found them handy in battle and I've brought back groups as large as 7 people. That's mostly all I have to say.  I hope to see a remake of this or Dead Rising 2 some day with totally modern game physics, controls, and mechanics, but I'm just as happy to see this happen.  I do think the price is steep. Had I not felt splurgy I would've waited and I have a hard time recommending this for $50 or even $40 to a friend, especially one with no nostalgia for the game.  The most I'd recommend it at is $30 and I really think $20-$25 is a fair asking price for a remaster today.  I'll be on the lookout for DR2. Hoping for even bigger visual and gameplay improvements for that one if it happens.  Thanks Capcom for making this a refreshing experience again in 2024. Just please stop robbing wallets. SF6 dlc still has me really sour.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, Capcom fanboys are cancerous. They are so desperate to support sugar daddy Capcom, no matter how controversial they have been with the last couple of games.Dead Rising Reluxe Demaster, where shall I start? I am a fan of DR and have played all their games, starting from DR 1 on Xbox 360. I racked up many hours on both DR 1 and DR 2 games. This game feels fan-made and cheap—as if it was made to ease Capcom's erectile dysfunction and consistent boner when impulsively thinking about money.Every conversation in the game is now voiced! This is the only change I really dig with the "remaster." It makes the game feel more immersive than quiet text-only conversations between the protagonist and NPCs.So far, I have recognised obvious survivor AI improvements - they no longer seem to pick a fight with zombies, cowardly cry in the middle of a horde of zombies, or ignore Frankie's commands. The survivors have favourites, too, which you can see while escorting them. Check your watch, and you will see their favourite items and food.Capcom has a history of not leaving things alone, especially things that did not need to be changed. Thankfully, the story events remain untouched. Good boy, Capcom.Original Dead Rising was more vibrant and bright without washing the colours out. The colours are ruined in the remastered, where everything looks grey and almost looks like there is some weird filter on top.While I liked the environmental changes, such as the added foliage to the outdoor environment, there were downgrades. For example, Capcom seems inspired by modern Mortal Kombat by making blood/gore all gooey and fake. VFXs like Smoke and Fire are rendered at 30fps at low resolution.Water reflections and shadows were also heavily reduced — even with the maximum shadow quality, zombies are missing shadows, and most shadows are jagged. Reflections suffer heavily from shimmering artefacts.The graphics are "meh" for an RE engine-powered game. The lighting and Textures look great, except the lighting during the evening looks awful outdoors. The game's presentation is one whole blurry mess but it can be fixed if you turn off Motion Blur and enable upscaling tech like DLSS. TAA should be avoided.The game's optimisation is disappointing and feels rushed. All the mall locations are filled with stutters and weird frame pacing issues. It was pretty impossible to reach a consistent 120fps. Finally, the actor models—why does Frank look like a demented humanoid toad? Capcom managed to make him look so much older than he is. The same applies to most NPCs and Brad, who look older than their OG counterparts.The QoL changes made are undoubtedly great and appreciated, but there are changes made to DRDE that are controversial.First, performing melee skills feels difficult. They were easier in the OG, when Frank would perform a grab animation before performing grab-based attacks.Levelling up is so much easier. It didn't take much effort to level up, making the game easy to play. Escorting survivors to the safe room can earn you a lot of experience.While the Survivor AI is mostly improved, some criticisms must be made. For example, in my game, one of the survivors Rachael jumped from the first floor onto the ground and was cowardly crawling. Thanks a lot, Rachael.There were a few instances where Survivors would randomly freeze in place until I returned to them and gave them a little smack.Overall, the game was easy to play. While annoying in groups, the special forces are easier to deal with than the OG. _childDocuments_.review: The original Dead Rising is my favorite game, so I had some pretty high expectations for this remaster. I want to start off saying the graphics are amazing, their was some obvious care put into the way the game looked. With added set pieces to make the mall look more alive, to retroactively adding cut content back into the game like the rocket launcher and the police zombies shooting their guns. Being able to skip time is a god send for infinity mode and something I never realized I needed until I had it. They kept the original animations for the zombies and survivors so the charm of the original is still there. I noticed a few issues with zombies glitching into the walls when I went into the maintenance tunnel to get the 53 thousand kills but other than that the game was visually stunning. There's some obvious issues with lag and crashes but i'm not sure if that's an issue on my end or the games. They did take out the erotica photo category, but if i'm being honest it was kinda weird and I'm not missing it. I do miss cliff mentioning Vietnam, but it was still clear to me he was a veteran. Larry definitely needed a remodel, I can see how some people would be upset at the change with wanting the game to be as pure to the original as possible, but og Larry was a walking stereotype. Obviously I miss the original voice actor for Frank but I didn't feel like anyone of the new actors did a bad job, some did worse, some did better, it's just how it goes. I'd recommend this game to anyone looking for a fun zombie sandbox with a compelling story that doesn't take it self too seriously.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start off by saying I've NEVER played any other Dead Rising games in the franchise, this is my first entry. I've heard of it before, but it wasn't much of a buzz to me back then. For what it's worth, I'm a die-hard fan of Resident Evil - I've played all mainline games front and back. After playing the RE4 Remake, I found there was nothing else that was as enjoyable until this game dropped OUT OF NOWHERE. I can't say much about the discrepancies, I know people have their gripes with the changes Capcom has made to the game in comparison to the original - I don't really understand them, but I'd imagine it's how us Resident Evil fans felt when Capcom did what they did to Chris, or the many times they made changes for no reason at all.That out of the way, I now want to say that: never in my 2 decades of living and gaming have I sunk 54 hours into the game after JUST picking it up.This review isn't for the die-hard Dead Rising fan, but this is MOST DEFINITELY for the average Jane or Joe surfing steam for a nice game to pick up in today's unfathomably over saturated and under achieving market.Its for the "Aw man, why don't they don't make games like they used to" folks - this DOES it.I want to say that any resentment for the game from die-hard fans is probably valid - I plan to play the old ones too to see how they hold up, but SHOULDN'T rob people the insane experience this has given me so far.I'm SO proud that this is my entry to the franchise. Capcom did this game abundantly well, and I don't think I'll ever retract this statement. I always thought the zombie survival game genre was dead, I've never looked back until now. There is a STUPID AMOUNT OF FUN in this game, it's still UNBELIEVABLY replayable. I've never had this much fun since Left 4 Dead and Resident Evil.P.S: I know I'm the last to talk - seeing as I've never played the other ones. But I'm unbelievably happy with this version of Frank West, he's just awesome.P.S^2: I've seen the videos about the censorship. I understand people have their frustrations with it, but I want to clarify once and for all: THEY DON'T retract ANY enjoyment from the game - and you can 100% pick up on the references the original insinuates without any direct mention, so it's perfectly fine.

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster is a testament to how well Capcom treat their fans. We didn't ask for it, yet we got it. Not a complete "from the ground up remake" as it uses all of the old animation data from the original 2006 version of the game (and that's okay!)Calling it a remaster though I feel is gravely undervaluing what it is we are getting here. You can tell the team have put a lot of effort into every other aspect of the game & I personally would go as far as to say that the game is a remake. It's faithful, yet adds new controls to bring it into the modern age of gaming. It's worthy of that prestige & I think fans & newcomers alike will appreciate what they have done. The new VA is great as well, with more emotion & sarcasm on offer with each scene that plays out. Pretty neat! Apart from the same animation bugs that plagued the original there really isn't a lot to complain about. Made in the RE Engine, this game runs perfectly. I have had no issues running it at 1440p, 60fps with everything maxed out & my 4060ti 16GB barely breaks a sweat. But we all know just how great this engine is & how well they optimize their games. Especially with being able to tweak the game in so many ways as well, this game really can run on older hardware despite stating 1060 minimum. (Also tested this on my 1050 (non ti) laptop with 4gb of VRAM. I wish other devs did this level of fan service & listened to their customers as much as Capcom did. Anyway, will stop ♥♥♥♥-riding now & let you buy the game & play it for yourself. Highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid fan of the Dead Rising series, I'd be hard pressed to recommend this over the original release version.That being said, if you've already played the original and are looking for something with a new coat of paint, some tweaks and QOL improvements then this might be for you, though I'm sure the latest Crowbcat has me agreeing there were definitely corners cut and unnecessary changes made.The addition of the time skip mechanic is okay, not something I think should be available from the start as I think it would make a first time player miss out on some of the content of the game. Traversing the mall during the downtime between cases, finding new survivors or just mowing down the undead with whatever was to hand was. All in all, I would recommend this really only to people who have played the original release and want an updated; graphically and game play wise, version of Dead rising. However, to a new player I would wholeheartedly recommend the original release. Though it may feel a little outdated, you simply cannot replicate the feel it has. _childDocuments_.review: Dead Rising is one of those zombies games where you can just pop it on, enjoy walking around and throwing random objects at zombies.  Coming back to the deluxe remaster i realise that it wasn't just my nostalgia but the game itself holds up incredibly well. Now obviously it has had a "remaster" which drastically improves upon things you've already read like AI or aiming but a lot of the charm is still there. The characters are still goofy even with new voice actors and now with every character having a voice outside of "FRANK" really goes a long way. However that said I wish they didn't give so many hints all the time. Like if I'm fighting a boss just to have "Frank you're a photographer? Maybe you should photography that" - No I'm good some psychopath is trying to kill you. Oh and the lighting is amazing, particularly the flashlights on the rifles really give it a resident evil feel. I know some people have voiced their complaints around the censorship of the game, but to be honest it hasn't really impacted the game. The only thing that was slightly mishandled was a boss fight including a PTSD psychopath. They removed references to the Vietnam war and replaced with with something generic. While I don't mind the removal it might have been better to tie it in with something to do with a plot element (i won't spoil here) but I don't think it's the end of the world. I also have to say that the cut content return was a treat and really adds to the overall experience without negating the legacy of this game. Overall I think this is a solid package and anyone who is either a fan of DR already, fan of zombies or just want a sandbox to play around in should try dead rising. It was a hit in 2006, classic in 2016 and now a legendary classic in 2024. If Capcom wants to I would 100% love to see Dead Rising 2 and it's and all of it's expansions  come out as a remaster. It took me 19 hours to 100% baring in mind that I have already done this in the 2016 release back on console. 7 Day survivor is actually fun now. It took around 3 hours of play time but you are constantly moving with the new time mechanic which is still optional to engage with.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Rising is EASILY my favorite Capcom game, hell, my favorite zombie game. I won't be leaving a review for the original on steam (It's got a lot of issues and just isn't the full OG Dead Rising Experience) But to say the least, amazing game. Now, on to DRDR. Amazing but flawed. More than anything, I was so excited to see Dead Rising built up from scratch in the RE Engine, and I can say they delivered. The game looks wonderful, the mall is beautiful and welcoming, the characters look amazing, and most item/weapon models are neat and improved. I PERSONALLY, think they did a wonderful job taking the mall from the original, and just making it prettier.The gameplay feels fresh, but still the same. I don't really have much to say about gameplay, it feels the same, while still feeling somewhat fresh. Though, a few things I was hoping they'd add to this. Moving while aiming is nice, but feels pointless when you have to stop to shoot?? And I know it was a long shot, but I was hoping for the item system from DR3, being able to pick up items while moving and use consumables felt so nice and always kept you on your feet, but It's not a huge issue to not see it here.AI is really improved, there's this new "Affinity" system which is kinda nice, you can see what weapons or food items Survivors prefer, and upon receiving them, they're more effective in combat. (Some survivors still got stuck on geometry though) Story is the same, I dunno. The hud is kinda ugly in my opinion it just feels like a prototype, but the pause menu and map are beautiful. I love the added challenge list and PP Sticker album, makes keeping track of stuff a lot easier. I'm a sucker for menus. The "Level Up" pop-up is really nice too.The costumes and outfits are really nice. Bringing the DR3 outfit locker mechanic was a great idea, I love collecting all the outfits around the mall and just switching to whatever I want whenever I want.There's a few new items also, nothing major. The Rocket Launcher is here after being cut from the OG, We got a couple new Books, and the camera has some Upgrades you can find too.Some items apparently have new move sets? I personally haven't noticed any of them yet though.I did, however, notice that it seems to me like some items just can't be picked up now?? Like, maybe it's just me, but I never found a store sign I could pick up like in the OG, which was odd.AND the only major bug I think I saw, was that the Cutscene for zombie Jessie never played for me, and thus I never got to find her in the Safehouse.Really, I do recommend this for die hard Dead Rising fans, a lot of the same Dead Rising jank is intact, while adding some new issues sadly, but I can't complain too much. Was this a cash grab by capcom? Yes, easily. But, it wasn't so poorly done that I feel like 0 love went into making this. I hope this sparks new life into the Franchise and we get more Dead Rising stories. Leave frank alone though, dudes been through enough, and DR4 did him DIRTY. Let's just forget that game all together, hopefully they use this Remaster/Remake to wipe the slate clean and fix some mistakes they made in later entries.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a step above from a regular remaster, but does not qualify to be called a remake. Basically what they did was simply move the old game to the new RE Engine. There are some QOL improvements, new voice acting but unfortunately, it still retains the old game jank and some of the finer details of the game was lost.It's a different thing playing janky old game compared to playing janky "new" 2024 game. You will wonder, why don't they fix the janks, improve it, but then you will remember Capcom calls this one a remaster, not a remake. I believe the original intention was to do a remake, but they decided it was far too demanding project and cut it short.Playing the old version and this one side by side, it's hard to recommend this one over the 2006 version. _childDocuments_.review: all 50 achievements in 21 hours of playtime.this remaster is great.the voice acting i only really found rough during the entrance plaza scene in the intro but everything else past that is good. really impressed with the new Frank VA aswell.movement is great and the more responsive control scheme makes the game feel so much better. Rolling is attached to one button and all of the moves you can feel like you're intentionally doing now unlike in the original where some moves were assigned to very similar buttons and you'd end up getting the wrong thing. On screen prompts for some of the moves like giant swing and neck twist also are good QoL improvements. Although I do wish Capcom added keybinding for KB+MThe survivors do feel better but they still have that "dead rising charm" of being agitating at times. There's affinity levels now. Give a survivor a weapon they like, they do more damage, give a survivor a food they like, they fully heal up. The higher the affinity the more they'll help you & other survivors out of grabs and also find you hidden items & PP Stickers.The advance time feature is a treat to have, I appreciate the devs for putting it in. You can advance time in ∞ Mode (Infinity Mode) aswell which does make it easier to achieve 5 day & 7 day survivor but you can also make a save state in ∞ Mode aswell which I appreciate since not everyone will have the time to keep the game running and focus on healing for 14 hours straight.The way they went with the new challenges were very good. All of the previous costumes in the security room in the original are now put with challenges. The OG challenges are still present (Transmissionary has been made easier though) and some even give you different rewards now (saint for example, no longer gives you the police hat; instead another challenge gives you the police hat now)im fine with the censorship, erotica category missing is the only thing in the game that's been completely removed from what i know (besides you currently cant break boxes by jumping on them but thats more of an oversight rather than intentional) every other censorship is just changed lines & clothing like on Cheryl for example which brings me to the final side-scoop of the game being Cheryl's request. It doesn't necessarily fit into the game anymore mostly since there is no erotica category & some people would complain about Cheryl's redesign being less sexualized. I'm glad its still here since cutting things out would be bad but it definitely feels out-of-place now. All in all, Capcom did a good job with the remaster. I had no issues with performance except I did feel like I needed DLSS Quality on. I got 0 crashes however I have heard of people getting crashes.Would recommended, definitely pick it up on sale especially if you've never played before.
