_childDocuments_.review: I love the Dead Rising series, and especially the first game. However, I just can't recommend the game in its current state. I have encountered multiple bugs which range from re-spawning one of the convicts upon entering the park each time, to Jo's captured survivors just not appearing (apart from Kay).Also, several times I've been walking along when suddenly I get hit by an invisible enemy again and again until death. While that can be kind of funny, I think I'd prefer to have a properly functioning remaster instead.Beyond that, the sound design is not good. The moaning and groaning of the zombies is toned down, if not non-existent, most of the time. The game is far less atmospheric in terms of its audio than the original, which is sad.I will gladly update my review if/when the game receives a patch to address these issues, but until then, I have to stop playing it for now.P.S. I don't know if Capcom would do anything about this, but in terms of difficulty, the game is much easier than the original. Part of that is because you level up as such an insane pace, and I wish they would tone that down a bit. Also, while I appreciate the quality-of-life update that strafing while shooting provides, it also makes some of the boss fights a bit trivial. I sincerely hope that they add difficulty modifiers into the game to bring back some of the challenge and increase its re-playability.

_childDocuments_.review: If there was a neutral option for review, I'd probably use it. So far, this remaster has done nothing to justify its existence.The graphical upgrades are cool for the mall itself (characters not so much) but some areas, like outside in the park during certain times of day look terrible and washed out as they did in the trailers. In fact, a lot of areas look really washed out, I imagine some LUT mods and reshades will start popping up soon if they haven't already. They somehow couldn't replicate the almost perfect mirror reflections from the original either which is alarming.Voice acting just doesn't hold a candle to the original. If you're a first-time DR player this wouldn't mean anything but for the ones who grew up on the original, I'm sure some will agree that a lot of the voices feel off and don't have the same effect.I also can't get over what they did to Frank. He looks like Munch from Oddworld and is built like a vending machine.The game is way too easy. The iconic prisoner bosses are somehow more idiotic than before. I also took the 50. cal from the prisoner's vehicle and used it alongside the firearm magazine to kill Adam the clown in 4 seconds (literally). He didn't even have a chance to move from his starting spot.Escorting survivors is better, they don't run head-first into a zombie's clutches anymore. The suggestions given by survivors while escorting feels out of place though, like Capcom sprinkled some Dragon's Dogma 2 on top.Zombies are also phasing in within view. Same goes for if you've just cleared an area, look away then look back again. Boom, zombies are back. Understandable for 2006, not really for 2024.Just a few things I've picked up on in the 2 hours I've played so far. Giving it a positive review for now because Dead Rising in itself in a fun game and newcomers to the franchise is always a good thing. There's just some strange design choices, particularly with the characters and voice acting that make me shake my head.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; If you are debating whether to play this version or the original, play the original first. I'll talk about the positive and then the negative.For positives, this game plays a whole lot smoother and better than the previous version. The PC port of the original is fantastic but you can feel the clunky design that Dead Risings first version had, especially when it came to inputting special attacks. The AI is improved and functions more autonomously without need for 100% babysitting, especially when armed. This is actually probably one of the most important things in the game to get right, so I am glad they did it.There is also new content added, with nice things like new books like one for fist damage and extra skills, skateboarding tricks, probably some I missed as well. Challenges also now exist which add more cosmetics and give you intensives to try new things.The graphical quality is significantly improved as well, with modern day lighting quality that big budget games tend to have. Nothing stuck me as "amazing" but it all just looked good. The ability to move and shoot, as well as the bullets coming from the center of the screen and not from franks gun does lead itself to some cheese, more on that later. The new versions of the music are good, as well as the sound effects for most things felt fine. The new menus and UI, for the most part, are also an improvement and a lot of quality of life changes were made. Honestly, as far as gameplay goes, it all just felt good and that's a good thing. Another really nice touch is that every NPC is fully voice acted in this, which I really appreciate. But onto the negatives, lets start with that same point. The voice acting is an almost universal downgrade and many of the tones of moments were lost due to this. Many main characters lacked character due to these issues. While many of the main cast try to do a good job, you definitely notice the ones who don't when you play the original. While Franks voice is alright, he does a good job, but unfortunately he just doesn't really sound like Frank. The main offender is probably Brad, who's voice actor completely misses the mark in every moment that it would matter. This is generally the trend you'll notice throughout, where Brad is definitely saying the same lines, but without the intensity, passion or emotion. I found some better voice acting from some of the minor NPCs that you escort back to the safe room. The grocery store clerk was another good example, where the iconic screaming was just not present at all as the VA could not even match half of the intensity of the original.But that's not all, there were some unnecessary changes to things that are now censored. Now I actually don't have an issue with some of it. Larry the Butcher's original model and VA from the OG Dead Rising might be one of the most racist portrayals of a Chinese man I've ever seen and came from an era where Japan really didn't like China, which has since improved as time has gone on. I understand the censorship of this character, however I do kind of wish they were still noticeably Chinese. Other changes are the removal of the Erotica stat when taking photos, which on it's own is understandable even if I don't agree with it, but then in the police officer Jo psychopath fight, they kept all the erotic material in that, even the sexual assault implications, as well as many of the in-cutscene ass/chest shots. It seems rather odd to be picky and choosy about what material is acceptable in the same umbrella. The last censorship thing I noticed was the removal of the Vietnamese war veterans lines about the Vietcong and communists. I do not see any reason this should have been removed, it was unnecessary and I cannot imagine who would be offended by this. On top of it, it's removal was half-assed and the replacement is flat and comes across as much less impactful as a result. It just feels really strange to do that.Onto other issues, difficulty. The original game is rather hard, with aggressive lunge-heavy zombies and a very slow level up system. Survivor AI was especially challenging to manage which both added charm and added more frustration. The AI in this game is remarkably easier, but it also tends to remove some of the difficulty as a result and isn't replaced by something else. On top of that, you level up anywhere between 2x to 3x faster in the Remake. This resulted in me hitting Level 50, the max level, in the last few stretches of the game which was probably their intent. But in the original, you would likely have to do a second playthrough to get to level 50, with people probably reaching about 25 to 30 if they complete the entire game in one playthrough. On top of this, it makes the game even easier as I had access to very useful tools and a lot of health and inventory space right off the bat. This also compounded with speed upgrades, which made time management easier and made the PP gains easier as well, in a self fulfilling cycle. I don't think this is wrong, but the game was very easy as a result. The guns also trivialize the game, with the damage being especially strong if you pick up the new "firearm damage" skill book, combined with the ability to shoot around corners due to the bullets coming out of the center of the gun, instead of the gun itself. And even if you die a lot, new autosaves will generally save you.Some of the graphics did not get the same love as the original game. The gas station explosion in the beginning actually looks better in the original despite being an xbox 360 launch title, with heat waves and much more smoke and fire. The new explosion looks very very cheap by comparison. Brads disembowelment in the parking garage looked way less gruesome and way less impactful, with a lot of the horror of the moment being lost. The lighting especially ruins some of the moments with much more brightly lit environments when it shouldn't be. The mall was very dark, in a good way, at night.And lastly, the biggest issue of the remake so far and the one that will likely be fixed, is the crashing. My playthrough of Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster (which is a Remake) had actually crashed over 15 times in my 12 or so hour session. The crashes reduced when I deleted "Crash Handler" exe and dll from the games files. The fact this exists at all is embarrassing, but even without it, crashed plenty of times. Luckily the autosave at least managed to reduce progress lost when it occurred, but this is still unacceptable. Zombie pop-in was very high and framerates were uneven and a little poor, but mostly ran okay.To conclude the review, ill tldr it.This remake (despite being called a remaster) is very good where it counts as far as gameplay improvements and the like, but it does remove a bit too much from the original in terms of content and difficulty.The original is still on steam and still very good and I recommend playing that over this, despite all the nice things this has going for it, as I feel this version of the game is inferior to the original, but is a treat for returning players who won't mind the poor voice acting and easier difficulty. If you are debating whether to play this version or the original, play the original first.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of the 2006 original, and for good reason! It's an absolute classic and, for the time, a really innovating game in the semi open-world zombie games genre. So, how does the remaster hold up? Pretty good actually! The story is the same as the original, sadly Frank's OG voice actor didn't reprise his role for the remaster, but I don't mind that much. The main complaint I got is that the game is way less clunky, which makes it very easy, mainly the survivors don't struggle so much anymore in escort side missions, which takes away a lot of the challenge from the original. The difficulty spike at the end portion of the game is ridiculous tho, you can get stun locked very easily and that can make the experience pretty frustrating, but nothing a well-timed dodge roll can't fix!In conclusion, it's a fun, modern day introduction to the Dead Rising franchise, I wouldn't rank it above the original, but it's an excellent way to experience the game!

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing Overtime Mode and doing some of infinite mode I think I've seen enough to give my true thoughts as someone who loves the original.This game is worse than the original.There are definitely some good things, autosave/timeskip etc is a lifesaver and lifts the game up massively. Not to mention a tonne of other positive changes that you've probably all seen in other reviews. However, there's way more bad than good:- Abysmal PC performance (1070 recommended GPU and I can't keep 60 fps on low with a 2080ti is a complete joke)- Frequent crashes- certain things like fire + explosions look awful even on max settings- Frequent input drops/delays- Vehicles are terrible, they drive extremely slow, get stuck on every little thing, and the animations constantly bug out- Driving controls are defaulted to LMB to drive instead of W for some dumb reason- Skateboards are 10x the size of a normal skateboard for some dumb reason- AI is worse than the original (several times I had survivors just glitch out and die instantly, or not respond to any commands at all, frozen in place until they also died)- Special forces are now absurdly broken, they infinitely stunlock you if two or more at once come at you- Guns are now useless (5+ shotgun blasts to kill a single special forces agent)- Every enemy has absurd iframes after being attacked (if you shoot a special forces with a shotgun, and shoot again immediately, the second blast goes right through them and does no damage)- They somehow made the Brock fight worse (almost every attack phases right through him, hitboxes are ridiculous)- The timeskip mechanic doesn't work as advertised (it tells you that if you skip forward you'll be alerted when the next event happens, I wasn't notified for anything, failed all the cases without a single tell that anything was happening, great feature)- many more, this is just from the top of my headPlay the OG, or wait for patches. Either way it's pathetic that yet another modern game is released in a clearly unfinished state, and still gets 80% positive reviews

_childDocuments_.review: The same BS Anti-Tamper that was present in Dragon's Dogma 2 is alive and well in the Dead Rising Remaster. Any attempts to inject ReShade, Special K or any other popular PC tool is met with swift game crashes. For a strictly single player title this move is utterly baffling and moronic.I paid for this game and own it but it doesn't feel like its mine to do with what I want. Feels more like I'm borrowing something from a friend. For this reason alone I will be leaving a negative review and I hope my fellow PC Gamers will do the same. Do not support this trend. It shouldn't be up to Capcom to police loyal paying customers on how they choose to engage with their game, especially one that is single player only.UPDATE: praydog who is responsible for ReFramework has now released a version that can hook into Dead Rising. Why should you care? Because it bypasses Capcom's anti-tamper protections, granting you access to reshade and the sort. He did it for Dragon's Dogma 2 and has done it again for RDR.Here's the link : You want to download DD2.zip under Assets and extract the contents. Then locate dinput8.dll and drag it to your game's directory where the executable is and nothing more. If you did it correctly you will be greeted with the reframework gui on your next boot up. Press INSERT key to summon the menu and tweak to your hearts content.There are toggles to remove black bars present in ultrawide cut-scenes, vignette and sliders to adjust the fov.Here's my game running with the aforementioned settings. Its legit.Both special K and Reshade are present in-game along with Reframework, all working in harmony. Been playing for the past couple of hours and it's been perfect. No weird glitches or oddities to speak of.Praise praydog!

_childDocuments_.review: Saying "Dead Rising is back" would be wrong, because Dead Rising never left.This game gives you both the option to use modernized controls and classic controls. I played with classic controls, and true enough, I did not have the luxury of aiming while moving, lol.But playing through the game, I was INCREDIBLY impressed with how true to the original the deluxe remaster is while simultaneously feeling better and smoother. There's lots of quality-of-life stuff added, but in no way do they take away from the difficulty. There's tiny additions sprinkled about like new skill magazines which are fun!That's not to say there aren't changes. Obviously there's the graphics, which look great. I LOVE the updated character and zombie models. However, I don't think the visuals are an objective upgrade from the original. I prefer the colour grading in the original game, and the stylistic choice of having intentional frame drops in cutscenes during dramatic moments was unfortunately done away with in favour of simple slow-mo.But man, playing through this was so much fun, just like the original. It's nice to play a game that encourages you to interact with its rules and quirks. There's not a lot of games where using a hockey stick to shoot around corners to outsnipe a sniper is one of the more viable methods.When it simply comes to *playing* it, definitely go for the deluxe remaster over the original. However, when taking *everything* into consideration, I honestly think both the original and the deluxe remaster are worth playing. Dead Rising is simply that good.

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Rising the original title is one of my favorite games of all time, and this remake made the game much much much easier, and whether or not you think that is a good thing or not, is up to you i guess. In my opinion this remake was fun to see so many of the mall details and new design choices in higher quality. The survivor pathing is a lot easier to manage than the original.  The remake is buggier, and you can tell that many corners were skipped, when zombies ragdolls fly through the wall, you cannot pick up some health items on shelves even though there are prompts, many of the variety of clothing is not available in various stores, and some fun items were also missing/taken out. I never played the newer DR games because I felt they lost the point of the series, but I could imagine several of the new mechanics they added were probably already in DR4. THE DARK SOULS ROLL?!? Capcom why did you give Frank such an easy dodge roll, I basically steam rolled all the bosses because you can just greed hits and dodge easily unlike the roll the original had. Some of the voice acting was TERRIBLE and I have to wonder if they even knew the original character they were playing, as well as some audio recording issues in lines in overtime. This remake lacked a lot of the love put into the original, and I think a lot of the "modern audience" changes take a good bit of the charm out of it, but they still did a decent job on other parts. I think they could have released this later and polished it up more, but this is what we got, I hope they continue to work on it. TLDR: This game was noobified and normiefied, but if the original was too hard for you, or you're just a big fan of the original, it might be worth checking out, BUT it is 100% inferior in almost every way to the original, except for the quality of life changes, but they honestly almost make this game TOO easy.

_childDocuments_.review: The long awaited Dead Rising Remaster is a decent remaster that takes all of the same events from the original, and makes its own tweaks, graphical improvements, and spins on different aspects of the original game. Starting with the story and game play, which has pretty much stayed the same aside from the remaster's graphical improvements, sound changes including new voice actors, and so on. It gives some and takes a bit, leaving it basically somewhere in the more positive middle ground for me along with most people I believe.While I could go on in much further detail regarding the list of changes the Dead Rising Remaster brings to the table, I'll just stick with pointing out some of the main ones. First off, new graphical improvements; the big obvious one. They are for the most part, pretty well done in my honest opinion and the mall can look quite sinister especially at night time with the help of the RE Engine's rendering capabilities. Some areas are hit or miss depending on the time of day, but it's mostly a very enjoyable step up from the original in terms of both the environment and the characters (which, with the characters I would call it more of a different take than an improvement, especially for characters like Frank). It took me a while to get used to the new Frank in terms of both voice acting and looks, but eventually he kinda stuck as I played more through the game where in the end I actually quite liked his new character in this remaster. The rest of the voice actors do what I would call ok, with some such as Brad being a little strange at some points. Otis now also has a voice and so that was kinda neat what they did with his character here, even the subtle note you can find at some point in the story was a neat little touch. The game play is much, much easier as well as accessible for new players, and the survivor AI is a little less stupid, with the new auto-save system playing a huge role in getting rid of the common frustration of death that those of use who played the original game are very familiar with. Although if you are a hardcore difficulty nerd, this version of the game is probably is not for you. When I say the survivor AI is a "little" less stupid, I mean for the most part, yes - but some of them still very well managed to have pissed me off to the point where I wanted to run them over with a motorcycle and then beat them with a baseball bat.You level up waaay quicker in the remaster, which I am not personally a fan of at all, but it's all part of the major changes to make the game that much easier for some reason. A lot of the limitations such as the photo amounts you can take at one time are also increased by over three times the original's so that just goes to show the extent of the changes made to the difficulty aspect of the game.There was a lot of stuff taken out of the game from the original such as breakable boxes (when you jump on them), and various other features that many players loved, but it did not impact me *as much personally.Then of course, the other bit that's not so positive and that is of course the censorship of some things in the game from the original that are no longer here. A lot of people have commented on some of them, such as the Erotica filter, the Vietnam psychopath censoring, etc. But honestly it's mostly minor stuff unless you want to get deeper into that subject. All in all, the changes made to the remaster make it stand out a lot from the original, but not necessarily in terms of general improvements as much as it feeling more like a different experience overall, just with the same story and events taking place coupled with the same game play formula from the original we all know and love.It's a good remaster. Not perfect at all, buggy in some areas and a lot of glitches with certain features of the game that may bother others more than the next guy (I did experience my share of crashes), and not a hit for every fan of the original especially when comparing the cost between the games at this point in time, but as a huge fan of the original game from way back then, it was quite enjoyable for me. I would give it 8/10 beef franks, had a blast going back and playing this one all the way through. I am looking forward to my infinite mode run and then getting all the achievements like a psychopath, I'm a little over halfway there. I would say pick it up if you absolutely love Dead Rising or are a new player who has heard of the original and tried it at least once. If you are really on the fence about it, I would recommend picking it up on sale in the future and just going that route. Honestly, it was worth it for me though and I enjoyed it for what I paid for it, where going in I didn't think I would at all. Pretty decent remaster overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty great remake with some good changes (you can now not kill Thomas) and some bad changes... Overall though I'd say it leans way more into the good with the bad and I'm just going to assume you already know about most of the changes at this point, if that's something you can't get over then fair enough, but personally it hasn't lowered my enjoyment of this remake. It runs pretty well on my 3070, I keep above 60fps with it sometimes dropping to 70 when there's a ton of zombies on screen, I have everything maxed out with DLSS on Quality. The most jarring thing for me is the animations, I understand they kept them the same to keep the feel of the original game, but they just look a bit weird sometimes with the new visuals, I think I would have preferred a full makeover to the animations along with the visuals, but again it doesn't really hinder my enjoyment. The biggest downside I think this remake has is that it's just that, a remake. There aren't any new modes, psychos or stories present here, it's the same game you played in 2006, and on one hand it's a bloody good game so that's fine, but I would have liked to have seen some new things here. Maybe some new psychos, survivors or even the sandbox mode from OTR with challenges and stuff to complete with your friends, that would have been cool! Speaking of co-op I'm pretty sad it isn't here, can you just imagine if they built a new campaign maybe based on a "what if?" scenario that was fully co-op? So you'd have the original game to play normally and then an extra brand new coop campaign, that would've been really cool. I'm getting ahead of myself but yeah, I would've liked to have seen some new stuff here beyond a rocket launcher and outfits, but that's really my only big disappointment, everything else I'm very happy with! If you haven't played the original, this might be a good place to start. If you have played the original, did you like it? If so, you should probably pick this up.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: If you've never played a Dead Rising game before, buy it and play it - I highly recommend you experience this type of game and it's mechanics, all the things that make the original game great are present in their entirety here, and Dead Rising is a really fun and unique experience - even if the amazing RE engine isn't quite as 'charming' and oldschool as the original game.If you've played the original, read onnnnn:---------A very genuine remaster of an all time classic. Be aware the difference between a remaster like this and a reMAKE like Capcom's resi 2/3/4 - DRDR holds true to the original mechanics and gameplay far more than the RE remakes do.As a die-hard fan of the original Dead Rising, to play a near identical copy of it with the new RE Engine's lighting and shadows is just everything I dreamed it could look like 20 years ago. It straight up feels like the original with a lot of QOL updates and good lighting/shadows. Most importantly the SURVIVOR AI IS WORKING NOW!I almost wish the AI was as dreadful as the original game, purely for the immense challenge of getting the achievements like Transmissionary and Saint, but ultimately I imagine the OG game now feels unplayable with the new improved survivor AI it's that well improved.There's a few things that aren't great, erotic photo types are gone but the sub-quests referring to them exist (yet a third quest IS changed to a new photo type? weird). Also of course the original voice actor for Frank wasn't brought back which is such a shame, but the new VA does the job well, kudos too as it's an iconic role to try take up.The new content is good, there's not a tonne which honestly I think is a good thing - a handful of interesting and useful books to upgrade Frank, a few new weapons to play with including the rocket launcher which is a capcom classic. The DLCs look good, they're cosmetics to support Capcom and the team who worked on Dead Rising so pick them up if you enjoy.Highly recommend, especially if you have never played a Dead Rising Game before.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to write a review for this. The thing is I did not play any of the Dead Rising trilogy because it was entirely banned in my country. I only played Dead Rising 4 which many people hated. But it was the first of the franchise to release in 2017 that was available to me. I even replayed Dead Rising 4 right before going to Dead Rising Deluxe Remastered. And while DR4 really isn't a very good game I still like it a lot more than this one. DRDR might have a better story or whatever but it's less fun. The first issue is the constant loading screens. That's the most horrible thing I've ever seen in a game. The gameplay gets interrupted by 30 seconds of black screen with loading bar every 5 minutes. It's a joke. Photography is also even more annyoing than in DR4. Inventory management is more annoying than DR. Movement speed is also extremly slow. I know you get more speed and more inventory slots by leveling up but it's not supposed to be intentionally bad just to make leveling up more rewarding. In conclusion I really do not like the pacing of the game ... you move extremly slow ... then you watch tons of loading screens and cutscenes ... then you stop to take photos and have to try 100 times because it's just trial and error ... where is the action? where is the fun?
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: A completely faithful recreation of the original game, despite very minor narrative revisions and gameplay tweaks. Modernized controls, updated visuals and a ton of quality-of-life updates bring the 2006 classic into the modern era free from the burdens of modern game trends. Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster feels good to play simply because it is fun at its core, and in an era where games increasingly feel like part-time jobs gunning for your time, that's the highest praise I can give.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: Update: Getting 100% of the achievements was fun, EVEN INFINITY MODE! Just goes to show how well the quality-of-life changes have taken this game. The effort put into the remaster comes from genuine care for the franchise, and is definitely worth the price.Fantastic versions for fans of the original, as well as newcomers. I will say though, difficulty-wise it's much easier compared to the OG. Most of the time I just don't worry about escorting survivors, they're incredibly efficient on their own, and most follow you very closely. Quality-of-Life changes are very appreciated, but I think Psychopath battles needed a bit more difficulty or added elements to make up for how easily you can dodge, or even just tank hits like nothing.Overall though, there are more positives compared to negatives, and it's a great stepping-stone for future Dead Rising remasters/remakes. I'll wait patiently for Off the Record Remake, PLEASE CAPCOM!
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: So To preface this, I played 2, OTR, 3 and (unfortunately) 4 but I just never got into 1 as it just didn't feel comfortable after going from newer games mechanics and QOL features.This remaster remedies them and builds upon the other gamesAI, As said in another review, is good now. They will help you out, save other survivors and point out secrets such as PP stickers and caches. Protip, Do the halo strat and give them nearly unloaded firearms to maximise their effectiveness.The controls are now smooth and are rebindable in the new control scheme, although you can access the old control scheme if you prefer.The only downside I've found right now, besides frank's original VA not being here and some questionable choices when it comes to censorship, is the optimisation is currently awful. That's the only thing however!A solid way to play Deadrising 1 if you don't want to play the original due to age or QOL issues!

_childDocuments_.review: After 100 percent completing the game and getting all the achievements i can say this is a wonderful remake of the 2006 classic that's worth your time especially if you're new to the dead rising franchise between the game play improvements graphic enhancements and added content i more fun with this version of the game then the revisit i had to the original when i replayed it in preparation for the game. A few things to note1. Zombie density in 72 hour mode and overtime mode is way lower then the original though it seems in infinity mode this isn't an issue.2. Performance is great other then in the maintenance tunnels and wonderland plaza it could be better its not unplayable but framerate dips and pop in are noticeable.3. The recasts are fairly strong with Frank suprisingly being one of the standouts although TJ Rotolo will always be Frank to me Jas Patrick does a great job filling his shoes in most line delivery though nostalgia will prevent me from accepting him fully Isabella and Dr Barnaby are also notable performances with a few others i could name but there is some where its noticeably a downgrade such as Brad Cliff and Steven.4. The censorship controversy is completely blown out proportion, erotica is gone and only one game play moment where it was necessary was replaced being Kent's "Photo Challenge"  the other being "Cheryl's Request" is still in the game and gives more pp then it did in the original. The only dialogue replaced was cliffs communist and viet cong lines while it feels unnecessary it doesn't effect the game or his character at all. Larry's redesign is the only one of its kind in the game and is probably one of the more necessary of the changes turning him from a caricature into a more appealing design other then that the game is just a prettier better playing version of the game you bought for your xbox 360

_childDocuments_.review: Disclosure: My friend gifted me this game, so as I did not pay $30 myself, the sting of the sparse content doesn't bother me as much.You can tell the quality of a licensed game by how surface level references and character inclusions are tied in. For example; yet another TMNT game lacking Casey Jones. Seriously, not even as an assist power-up? You added two new levels in to this port but couldn't bother to get one of the main staples of TMNT?If you, like me, are a reclusive shut-in that never ventures outside, and also enjoy Ninja Turtles like any self-respecting manchild, the release of this former arcade cabinet-exclusive likely caught your interest. A 2017 arcade machine being ported to home devices seven years after the fact? Interesting.That aside, this is a by the numbers and fairly unpredictable, but enjoyable, beat-em-up. It's yet another brawler chasing the dragon that is Turtles in Time, and while it doesn't come close to meeting the goal it aims for, it's still a fun time. The story is barebones and follows as thus: Go fight through New York to get to Shredder. Why? Because it's an arcade game, dummy.The levels are standard side-scrolling fare with dozens of enemies leaping onto the screen from various angles, VERY often shooting at you from off-screen (I'm assuming this is a leftover from the arcade cabinet version where it was likely intended to screw you over to drain more quarters out of your wallet) -- as enemies filter in from all corners. It can get hectic, but thankfully you have ways to even the odds with frequent objects to grab and throw, explosive barrels to set off, special pick-ups that will cause you to spin around on the back of your shell as you 1-hit KO enemies for a short period of time, and even Ally Tokens that will spawn the likes of Metalhead and Leatherhead (AGAIN, seriously-- where the hell is Casey Jones? Or Splinter, for that matter?) which will do screen-clearing waves of attacks that kill any and everything currently on screen.Each level has two boss battles, some of which are peculiar deep cuts from the 2012 version of the series, and all voiced by the 2012 cast. The bosses all sound great, but the turtles themselves... well. You can tell they were called in to do voices on their days off, AND it sounds like they were ony allowed to do one take. I don't know if Greg Cipes was sick the day of this recording, but he sounds incredibly off as Mikey- AND irritating. The game has the most obnoxious, three repeating high-pitched wails from Mikey and Donnie that repeat ad nauseum any time you press the attack button. Seriously, for the love of God-- don't pick Mikey unless you have the game on mute. That aside, the turtles DO all have unique voice-lines for each boss, giving it just the slightest touch of novel effort that other TMNT beat-em-ups don't have.The visuals themselves are fine, but... flat? It's a strange mix. The turtle shells look incredible and have a glowing sheen on their shells, but other models seem... off. Shredder, for instance, looks like he's been fasting for several decades and is very lanky. Some stages look like they've jumped right off the screen of the 2012 series, while others are flat and lacking shadows or the tone that made the '12 series what it was. I'm not sure which is which as I've never played the original arcade cabinet.However, there are little touches that surprised me. When destroying one of the Krang robot suits, the Krang themselves will climb out of the suit and attemple to scuttle away. You can smack it to get extra points/Turtle Power (your own, less powerful screen-clearing super attack) or sometimes fling it towards the screen, Turtles in Time style. It caught my friend and I off guard and made us laugh when we managed to do so. On one level, the 80's Krang will destroy a wall and shoot electric beams through the giant gap into the arena, ripped straight from Turtles in Time. On the New York level, vans will burst onto the screen from the backdrop, swerving into the foreground as Krang robots pile out onto the street in frront of you. Another particularly cool moment is in the sewers where a subway car gets derailed right in front of you and crashes into a wall, only for the Xenomorph-esque squirrel mutants to kick the doors open and come piling out in a screeching fury. These are small touches, of which the game needs WAY more of, but they're still appreciated. (I'm also aware the aliens are called Utroms, but we're going with 2012 terminology.)There is no V-Sync as of this writing, so prepare for notable screen tearing. Aside from that, I had zero issue with performance, the game had no crashes or hitches. I played through Remote Play with a friend and we had a good time despite some of the oddities with the voice performances.The game took about 55~ minutes to beat with a friend on Normal. I plan to play through it at least a few more times over the coming weeks, but your mileage will absolutely vary. The content IS incredibly sparse, and it lacks any of Shredder's Revenge replay value.This is no Shredder's Revenge, but if you were always curious how the arcade cabinet played and you wanted to try it for yourself, this is a surprisingly competent game- just, seriously, don't expect anything on the level of Shredder's Revenge. It's not even close.Personal favorite moment: During the Karai miniboss, she teleports and taunts with a "Catch me if you can!" - before she finished her taunt, she got an explosive crate to the face and flopped over. Made my friend and I burst out laughing.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like that, as someone who has NOT played the arcade version, this port feels bareboned. Don't get me wrong, it's fun for the first few stages, but once you just complete all of them in under an hour or two, you're just left with nothing.If in the future, mods and/or workshop related features come into play, then I wouldn't mind at all, let the community have some fun making level designs, or even some more new, original content by the developers themselves, but for now it isn't it.No online features, either, which for a multiplayer game in 2024 is so surreal. I get it's an arcade port, but you can do more than the bare minimum.Voice acting feels wrong too, like they just cherry picked from the show and just placed into the game, it's only the English voice actors too, which sound like they're voicing an anime dub really poorly with zero effort, repeating phrases more than three times.All in all, you're best waiting for this game to be on sale (15% off still doesn't feel worth it), while I will still play this game every once in a while, it isn't all that good.

_childDocuments_.review: Completed the game on normal in 74 minutes. It was a decent way to pass the time, but offered no story, extremely basic gameplay, and a very subpar experience for $29.99. Sure, I could refund the game since it's under the 2 hour threshold set by Steam, but I played it and so I'll keep it. There are 6 stages with 2 bosses per stage. Using an Xbox controller, your attacks consist of smashing the X button, pressing A+X to do a spin AoE attack, or jumping and pressing A or X for an aerial. There is no dodge or reflect, the latter of which would have made a great addition the the spin attack AoE.

_childDocuments_.review: TMNT Wrath of the Mutants. Now, this is a game where it's highly recommended you know what you're getting into before buying. Mainly, that this is a home port of the 2017 arcade game with some extra content. That being two new levels based on Dimension X and an Amusement Park. There are also some new bosses as well as other bosses that were swapped around. But does that make this port worth it? One way to find outGameplay: This game, like many TMNT beat 'em ups, takes inspiration from the old Konami beat 'em ups. Meaning you have stuff like screen throws and slam attacks. However, there are some unique things this game does like circle attacks that attack all around you, and a screen nuke called Turtle Power that is charged through dealing damage and finding powerups. Said powerups are another addition to separate itself from the 80s beat 'em ups, and include different abilities like more Turtle Power, Health increase, or weapons/assists from the series that do damage to enemies. However, there is also the shell powerup that is basically the Bomb Pizza from the old games. Besides that, it doesn't really get more complex than that, it's a surprisingly simple game. Almost too simple as combat can get repetitive at times, and all the turtles basically play the same, barring their screen nuke... Which is also just more visual flair. It's kinda disappointing that the Turtles don't even get their own stats. Still, the main appeal in these games is the multiplayer, so, I assume everything is more fun there.Another weird thing is that the difficulty is a weird middleground of easy and hard. Even though you do have selectable difficulties, you do get reminders that this was originally an arcade game, so you will often get stuff like enemies with huge reach, enemies with impossible reaction times, or sometimes the enemies will just delete your health bar. But there are also times where you just completely demolish the enemies, and the game already gives you plenty of lives and continues that refresh each stage, so even with these difficulties, you'll still have an easy time playing.That leaves the new stages, the Amusement Park and Dimension X. They're alright, they don't have the most intense gimmicks, but they were still pretty fun to play through. Overall, this game gets an alright 7/10 for gameplayGraphics, Presentation, and Sound: This part is weird. Since it was originally released in 2017, it's based on the 2012 series, so the character designs, locations, and other details are based on that version of the Turtles. This is the closest we will get to 2012 content in the modern age after Nick got obsessed with the 87 designs. Overall, the game does look fine for a 2017 arcade game in most parts, while other parts look... Bad. It's clear that this game didn't receive too many visual upgrades when it was being brought home, which is kind of disappointing. Although the new content does look nice and fits in perfectly with the original arcade stages, stuff like the ending scene that looks like complete crap, and oddly enough, isn't voiced at all. Despite them getting the original voice cast for this game. Speaking of, yes, they were able to get the original voice cast to voice the characters, but for some reason the Turtles themselves sound... Off. It seems that they weren't properly prepared when doing voices for the arcade release, and not much else for the home port (Although in the case of the home port, it was probably years since they did voices for these characters, although Rob Paulsen had the benefit of voicing 87 Raphael so his Donnie here sounded on brand). The rest of the characters sound fine, even if most of them were just reused from the arcade original, including Nolan North, Kevin Michael Richardson, and the late Gilbert Gotfried.Although staying on the sound, the game had issues with sound balancing. Despite the music sounding fine, it was way too quiet to properly hear, causing all the tunes to be less memorable than they should. Same with the sound effects, they're way too quiet and not punchy enough. They really needed more work on this part. 6/10Steam Deck Compatibility: Despite it being listed as unknown, this game worked on Steam Deck with 0 issues whatsoever. 10/10Replayability: After you beat the game, you get the option to replay on hard mode, but after that, nothing. I get it, this was meant to just be a port of the arcade game, but with basically nothing to work for, at best you would only replay this to play with friends, or to practice for a session on the actual arcade cabinet. Not even something as basic as a survival mode. That's... Sad. 2/10Final Thoughts: Again, you have to know what you're getting into with this. I feel if you know that this is a port of the 2017 arcade game, and it's something you're looking for, I'd say go for it. It helps that the game is a somewhat generous 30 bucks, and right now it's on sale. And since it's a GameMill game, it'll go on sale every 2 seconds. However, if you aren't interested in a near direct port with minimal additions to the original game, I'd say pass. Personally however, I found this a very fine game, so I think it deserves a fine rating of a 7/10 with a side of a plain cheese pizza. If nothing else, there is one undeniable fact on one thing this game does well: Preservation. Raw Thrills is absolutely horrible at making their games accessible. In the modern age, you really cannot rely on arcade exclusives, so we are really lucky that GameMill is porting their games over to console. Why GameMill? I dunno. But still, it's good that Raw Thrills' games are being properly preserved on consoles instead of being stuck on arcade jail. Now... Can we get Dirty Drivin' next? Or maybe Nicktoons Nitro if they're gonna keep doing Nick arcade games (Maybe with a fully voiced cast this time).If you're looking for other platforms to play this on, it's on every other modern platform: PS4, PS5, Switch, XBONE, and XBOX SeX/SeS including physical copies, so you won't have trouble finding it

_childDocuments_.review: I am enjoying this so far. Yes, the game is much shorter than Shredder's revenge but it doesn't have to - Wrath of the Mutants was initially an arcade game. I feel that a number of folks these days have never experienced an arcade game and expect games to take 10+ hours to be worth their money, except that most folks would not be spending 10+ hours at an arcade to play a game. Shorter games can be very entertaining, and this is a good example. This is also based on the 2012 cartoon series, not the more recent iterations.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Steam Deck review.  At the time of this review, this game runs smoothly and easy to play on the handheld.  There’s no cloud saves in case you delete and redownload, but the content of the game isn’t heavy or needing to unlock much besides the last level or hard mode.The game plays like a 90’s TMNT game which is fine if that’s all you want.  That also means the controls are limited to move, jump, and attack.  And I wish it was just a jump.  The jump button also lunges at an opponent in proximity, which doesn’t help when an explosive is near.  Maybe there’s workarounds for this.  It’s pretty straightforward and doesn’t require a lot of time, so this is good in between things or other games.  Cathartic gaming at the end of a day.  This is really only for your hardcore TMNT base, or if you have a group that wants to play arcade beat em up ports.  This should be bought at a discount, around $5-20 - five dollars for every player you expect to play with you.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an enhanced version of a 2017 arcade game, with-- according to the description-- three extra stages and six extra boss fights. I never played the original arcade game, so I can't compare the two; however, it feels fairly seamless to me. I have no idea which are the new stages and which are the old, so nothing feels out of place.As for the game itself, it is about what you would expect. It is a side-scrolling beat 'em up that is obviously inspired by the older TMNT arcade games (available on Steam as part of the Cowabunga Collection). You can choose between the four turtles, and it has four-player local co-op as well. There are three difficulty levels, and finishing it on hard was challenging for me. That said, it is on the short side, and you will probably finish it on easy or normal in less than an hour. Getting the achievements adds some replayability, though.I'm glad to see this game getting another chance outside of the arcades. I enjoyed it, and recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember playing the original arcade game back in either 2017 or 2018 and I was hyped after seeing that the game was coming back better than ever on PC and other platforms. NYC, Sewer, and T.C.R.I. brought me back to the good old days while Dimension X and Amusement Park were perfect additions to the game. I could tell that the developers tried hard on this game and put heart into it. A lot of the other players got mad because the game took 1 hour to beat, in the game's defense, that's just how it was. The thing that made the older arcade game feel like it took forever to beat was the fact that you had put in more money for each time you ran out of continues, you don't have to do that anymore now that you've paid $29.99 for it here on whatever platform you're playing on which makes the game feel shorter despite the new levels. Although, it's not gonna feel like it took 1 hour to beat if you're playing on hard mode. Overall, I love this game and I don't care what other people think.Likes: The boss fights are fun and you might get some funny dialog from one of the turtles when the boss fight starts or when it ends. It has an excellent usage of other characters who can help you like Leatherhead, Metalhead, and Ice Cream Kitty. I'm surprised and glad that they were able to get all of the voice actors back just so that they could get some new lines from them. Dislikes: It's possible for the blue Foot Soldiers and the Kraang to shoot you off screen with their laser gun, it's hard to dodge the lasers when they're off screen, especially since you can't see them and know if they're about to shoot lasers at you or not. It's also hard to evade attacks, there are times where opponents can hit you without warning, enough time to react, or in other unfair ways like glitches for example; which is a becomes a big issue if you're playing in hard mode. During the Karai boss fight, I knocked Karai down and jumped next to her (because opponents getting up will kick you if you're in the way) and she got up while I was in mid air, and while I was next to her hitting her, she just suddenly stood still in a different position and it dealt damage even though she already got up like 3 seconds ago and she didn't even do anything to hit me. Things that I would do if I could change the game: I would make it so that you could evade attacks, have opponents attack with time for you to react, and also make it so that opponents getting up after being knocked down doesn't deal damage. I was kind of disappointed that Michelangelo didn't shout "Leatherhead" or "Ice Cream Kitty" when they came to help you, so I would've made Michelangelo shout one of those things depending on who came to help you. I would also make it so having more players would benefit you because there were some extra opponents when I was playing the game with my dad. Another thing that I would do is make it so that the Shredder boss fight and the Super Shredder boss fight weren't combined, I would make Karai and Shredder the only boss fights in "Shredder" and add a bonus level called "Owari" where you fight Shredder on the roof of the hidden mansion in the woods and each turtle is in their Owari outfit and you can only play it if you beat easy, normal, and hard mode (the difficulty would be optional no matter what mode you beat the game in). I hope that we get a sequel to this game; there are so many boss fights that we could get like Captain Mozar, Lord Dregg, Ho Chan, Savanti Romero, Oroku Saki (before he became Shredder), Hattori Tatsu, Newtralizer, Mom-Thing, Spider Bytez, etc. Thank you to whoever made this game available on more platforms so that we don't have to let the game drain our wallets at the arcade anymore (even though I'm still willing to play the older arcade again) and thank you for adding all of these cool levels, this game is awesome. My rating: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun! So glad Raw Thrills made the effort to update and release commercially. My kids love it. It is simple, sharp and short. That’s exactly what you should expect from an arcade port, this isn’t a console game. Doesn’t try to be. Visuals are solid, and it has a unique spin on the series. If you want more depth/longevity go for Shredder’s Revenge. If you want straight up turtles arcade action, pick this up. Fans are spoilt for choice at the moment, keep ‘em coming!
